#include <LibWakeLock/DisplaySleepInhibitor.h>

#include <AK/StdLibExtras.h>
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <IOKit/pwr_mgt/IOPMLib.h>

namespace WakeLock {

namespace Detail {

struct DisplaySleepInhibitorImpl {
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    explicit DisplaySleepInhibitorImpl(IOPMAssertionID assertion_id)
        : assertion_id(assertion_id)
    {
    }

    ~DisplaySleepInhibitorImpl()
    {
        IOPMAssertionRelease(assertion_id);
    }

    IOPMAssertionID assertion_id { 0 };
};

}

ErrorOr<DisplaySleepInhibitor> DisplaySleepInhibitor::create(StringView reason)
{
    auto const* reason_string = CFStringCreateWithBytes(nullptr, reinterpret_cast<u8 const*>(reason.characters_without_null_termination()), reason.length(), kCFStringEncodingUTF8, false);
    if (!reason_string)
        return Error::from_string_literal("Failed to create display sleep inhibition reason");

    IOPMAssertionID assertion_id = 0;
    auto result = IOPMAssertionCreateWithName(kIOPMAssertPreventUserIdleDisplaySleep, kIOPMAssertionLevelOn, reason_string, &assertion_id);
    CFRelease(reason_string);
    if (result != kIOReturnSuccess)
        return Error::from_string_literal("Failed to inhibit display sleep");

    return DisplaySleepInhibitor { make<Detail::DisplaySleepInhibitorImpl>(assertion_id) };
}

DisplaySleepInhibitor::DisplaySleepInhibitor(NonnullOwnPtr<Detail::DisplaySleepInhibitorImpl> impl)
    : m_impl(move(impl))
{
}

DisplaySleepInhibitor::DisplaySleepInhibitor(DisplaySleepInhibitor&&) = default;

DisplaySleepInhibitor& DisplaySleepInhibitor::operator=(DisplaySleepInhibitor&&) = default;

DisplaySleepInhibitor::~DisplaySleepInhibitor() = default;

}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Engine/build.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Compiles the interpreter, Libraries/LibWasm/Interpreter/interpreter.flap, against the layout constants of
//! ../Module/src/abi.rs, and assembles it into the crate. Also generates the C++ header of the C ABI in src/capi.rs.

use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::path::PathBuf;

#[path = "../Module/src/abi.rs"]
mod abi;

fn write_if_changed(path: &PathBuf, contents: &str) {
    if fs::read_to_string(path).is_ok_and(|existing| existing == contents) {
        return;
    }
    fs::write(path, contents).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("write {}: {error}", path.display()));
}

fn main() {
    let manifest_directory = PathBuf::from(env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").expect("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
    let output_directory = PathBuf::from(env::var("OUT_DIR").expect("OUT_DIR"));
    let interpreter_source = manifest_directory.join("../Interpreter/interpreter.flap");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=../Module/src/abi.rs");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", interpreter_source.display());
    println!("cargo::rustc-check-cfg=cfg(wasm_interpreter)");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=cbindgen.toml");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=src/capi.rs");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=src/runtime/heap.rs");

    // The bindings only cover the C ABI, so they are generated from that file alone.
    let bindings = cbindgen::Builder::new()
        .with_config(cbindgen::Config::from_file(manifest_directory.join("cbindgen.toml")).expect("read cbindgen.toml"))
        .with_src(manifest_directory.join("src/capi.rs"))
        .with_src(manifest_directory.join("src/runtime/heap.rs"))
        .generate()
        .expect("generate the C ABI header");
    bindings.write_to_file(output_directory.join("RustFFI.h"));

    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET");
    let architecture = env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ARCH").expect("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ARCH");
    let os = env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").expect("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS");
    let object_format = match os.as_str() {
        "macos" | "ios" => flapc::ObjectFormat::MachO,
        "windows" => flapc::ObjectFormat::Coff,
        _ => flapc::ObjectFormat::Elf,
    };
    let architecture = match architecture.as_str() {
        "x86_64" => flapc::Architecture::X86_64,
        // FIXME: Port the interpreter's entry and exit to the Windows AArch64 calling convention.
        "aarch64" if object_format != flapc::ObjectFormat::Coff => flapc::Architecture::Aarch64,
        _ => return,
    };
    println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=wasm_interpreter");

    let layout = abi::layout_constants();
    let layout_path = output_directory.join("layout.conf");
    write_if_changed(&layout_path, &layout);

    // The interpreter counts zeros with LZCNT and TZCNT where the build targets CPUs that have them (see
    // `check_cpu_features()`), and with bit scans everywhere else.
    let target_features = env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_FEATURE").unwrap_or_default();
    let has_target_feature = |feature: &str| target_features.split(',').any(|candidate| candidate == feature);
    let has_lzcnt = architecture == flapc::Architecture::X86_64 && has_target_feature("lzcnt");
    let has_bmi1 = architecture == flapc::Architecture::X86_64 && has_target_feature("bmi1");

    let source = fs::read_to_string(&interpreter_source).expect("read interpreter.flap");
    let source_name = interpreter_source.display().to_string();
    let compiler = flapc::Compiler::new(flapc::CompileOptions {
        target: flapc::Target {
            architecture,
            object_format,
        },
        has_jscvt: false,
        has_lzcnt,
        has_bmi1,
        enable_assertions: true,
        profiling: false,
        profile: flapc::Profile::WebAssembly,
    });
    let assembly = compiler
        .compile(flapc::CompilationUnit {
            source: flapc::SourceInput {
                name: &source_name,
                contents: &source,
            },
            constants: Some(flapc::SourceInput {
                name: "layout.conf",
                contents: &layout,
            }),
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("flapc failed to compile the interpreter:\n{error}"));
    let assembly_path = output_directory.join("interpreter.S");
    write_if_changed(&assembly_path, assembly.as_str());

    let mut build = cc::Build::new();
    build.file(&assembly_path);
    if os == "macos"
        && let Some(deployment_target) = rust_macos_deployment_target()
    {
        build.flag(format!("-mmacosx-version-min={deployment_target}"));
    }
    if env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ENV").is_ok_and(|environment| environment == "msvc") {
        // flapc writes GNU assembly, which MSVC's cl.exe cannot assemble. Ladybird builds for Windows with clang-cl.
        if !build
            .try_get_compiler()
            .is_ok_and(|compiler| compiler.is_like_clang_cl())
        {
            build.compiler("clang-cl");
        }
        // Given -Fo, clang-cl writes the preprocessed assembly to the working directory, which cargo makes the source
        // directory of the crate.
        env::set_current_dir(&output_directory)
            .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("enter {}: {error}", output_directory.display()));
    }
    if architecture == flapc::Architecture::X86_64 {
        build.flag_if_supported("-malign-branch-boundary=32");
        build.flag_if_supported("-malign-branch=fused,jcc");
    }
    build.compile("libwasm_interpreter");
}

/// The minimum macOS version rustc builds the crate's own code for, which the assembled interpreter has to match.
fn rust_macos_deployment_target() -> Option<String> {
    if let Ok(target) = env::var("MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET") {
        return Some(target);
    }
    let rustc = env::var("RUSTC").unwrap_or_else(|_| "rustc".to_string());
    let target = env::var("TARGET").ok()?;
    let output = std::process::Command::new(rustc)
        .args(["--print", "deployment-target", "--target", &target])
        .output()
        .ok()?;
    String::from_utf8(output.stdout)
        .ok()?
        .trim()
        .strip_prefix("MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=")
        .map(str::to_string)
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Print whether each module named on stdin decodes and validates, one `path<TAB>verdict` line per module, for
//! comparing verdicts with other implementations. With `--stats`, valid modules also report the size of their code
//! and of what validation keeps for running it.

use std::io::BufRead;

fn main() {
    let stats = std::env::args().any(|argument| argument == "--stats");
    for line in std::io::stdin().lock().lines() {
        let path = line.expect("read a path");
        let verdict = match std::fs::read(&path) {
            Err(error) => format!("unreadable: {error}"),
            Ok(bytes) => match libwasm_engine::compile(&bytes) {
                Ok(module) if stats => {
                    let code: u32 = module.code.iter().map(|body| body.code.end - body.code.start).sum();
                    let entries: usize = module.function_infos.iter().map(|info| info.side_table.len()).sum();
                    let metadata: usize = module.function_infos.iter().map(|info| info.metadata_size()).sum();
                    format!(
                        "valid functions={} code_bytes={code} side_table_entries={entries} metadata_bytes={metadata}",
                        module.code.len()
                    )
                }
                Ok(_) => "valid".to_string(),
                Err(error) => format!("error:{error}"),
            },
        };
        println!("{path}\t{verdict}");
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Engine/src/capi.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The C ABI the embedders use: compiling modules, and a store to instantiate them in, call their functions, and
//! access their memories, tables, and globals.
//!
//! Modules are reference counted and immutable, so they can be shared across threads. A store and everything in it
//! belongs to one thread. Entities (functions, tables, memories, globals, tags, and instances) are the addresses of
//! their cells.

use crate::module::{ImportDescription, Module};
use crate::runtime::entity::{Entity, Handle};
use crate::runtime::heap::{GcInterface, TRACE_NONE, Visitor};
use crate::runtime::{ExternValue, HostFunction, InstantiationError, Store, Trap, Value};
use crate::types::{AddressType, FuncType, GlobalType, HeapType, Limits, MemoryType, RefType, TableType, ValType};
use core::ffi::c_void;
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// An owned string, which the embedder releases with `wasm_string_release()`.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct WasmString {
    pub data: *mut u8,
    pub length: usize,
}

/// A string borrowed from a module or store, valid while it is.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct WasmStringView {
    pub data: *const u8,
    pub length: usize,
}

impl WasmStringView {
    fn of(text: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            data: text.as_ptr(),
            length: text.len(),
        }
    }
}

fn write_string(destination: *mut WasmString, text: &str) {
    if destination.is_null() {
        return;
    }
    let bytes: Box<[u8]> = text.as_bytes().into();
    let length = bytes.len();
    unsafe {
        *destination = WasmString {
            data: Box::into_raw(bytes).cast(),
            length,
        };
    }
}

/// Create a string the engine takes ownership of, as a host function's error message.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `data` must point at `length` readable bytes, and `string` must be writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_string_create(data: *const u8, length: usize, string: *mut WasmString) {
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(data, length) }).into_owned();
    write_string(string, &text);
}

/// Release a string the engine returned.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The string must come from the engine and not have been released.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_string_release(string: WasmString) {
    if string.data.is_null() {
        return;
    }
    unsafe {
        drop(Box::from_raw(std::ptr::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(
            string.data,
            string.length,
        )));
    }
}

#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WasmValueKind {
    I32,
    I64,
    F32,
    F64,
    V128,
    Reference,
}

#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WasmHeapKind {
    Function,
    NoFunction,
    Extern,
    NoExtern,
    Any,
    Eq,
    I31,
    Struct,
    Array,
    None,
    Exception,
    NoException,
    /// A type the module defines; `type_index` is its index in the module, or its identity in the store for the types
    /// of the store's functions and globals, and those of a host function.
    Concrete,
}

/// A value type. `heap`, `nullable`, and `type_index` only matter for references.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct WasmValueType {
    pub kind: WasmValueKind,
    pub heap: WasmHeapKind,
    pub nullable: bool,
    pub type_index: u32,
}

impl WasmValueType {
    fn of(ty: ValType) -> Self {
        let scalar = |kind| Self {
            kind,
            heap: WasmHeapKind::Function,
            nullable: false,
            type_index: 0,
        };
        match ty {
            ValType::I32 => scalar(WasmValueKind::I32),
            ValType::I64 => scalar(WasmValueKind::I64),
            ValType::F32 => scalar(WasmValueKind::F32),
            ValType::F64 => scalar(WasmValueKind::F64),
            ValType::V128 => scalar(WasmValueKind::V128),
            ValType::Ref(reference) => {
                let (heap, type_index) = match reference.heap {
                    HeapType::Func => (WasmHeapKind::Function, 0),
                    HeapType::NoFunc => (WasmHeapKind::NoFunction, 0),
                    HeapType::Extern => (WasmHeapKind::Extern, 0),
                    HeapType::NoExtern => (WasmHeapKind::NoExtern, 0),
                    HeapType::Any => (WasmHeapKind::Any, 0),
                    HeapType::Eq => (WasmHeapKind::Eq, 0),
                    HeapType::I31 => (WasmHeapKind::I31, 0),
                    HeapType::Struct => (WasmHeapKind::Struct, 0),
                    HeapType::Array => (WasmHeapKind::Array, 0),
                    HeapType::None | HeapType::Bottom => (WasmHeapKind::None, 0),
                    HeapType::Exn => (WasmHeapKind::Exception, 0),
                    HeapType::NoExn => (WasmHeapKind::NoException, 0),
                    HeapType::Concrete(index) => (WasmHeapKind::Concrete, index),
                };
                Self {
                    kind: WasmValueKind::Reference,
                    heap,
                    nullable: reference.nullable,
                    type_index,
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn to_value_type(self) -> ValType {
        match self.kind {
            WasmValueKind::I32 => ValType::I32,
            WasmValueKind::I64 => ValType::I64,
            WasmValueKind::F32 => ValType::F32,
            WasmValueKind::F64 => ValType::F64,
            WasmValueKind::V128 => ValType::V128,
            WasmValueKind::Reference => ValType::Ref(RefType {
                nullable: self.nullable,
                heap: match self.heap {
                    WasmHeapKind::Function => HeapType::Func,
                    WasmHeapKind::NoFunction => HeapType::NoFunc,
                    WasmHeapKind::Extern => HeapType::Extern,
                    WasmHeapKind::NoExtern => HeapType::NoExtern,
                    WasmHeapKind::Any => HeapType::Any,
                    WasmHeapKind::Eq => HeapType::Eq,
                    WasmHeapKind::I31 => HeapType::I31,
                    WasmHeapKind::Struct => HeapType::Struct,
                    WasmHeapKind::Array => HeapType::Array,
                    WasmHeapKind::None => HeapType::None,
                    WasmHeapKind::Exception => HeapType::Exn,
                    WasmHeapKind::NoException => HeapType::NoExn,
                    WasmHeapKind::Concrete => HeapType::Concrete(self.type_index),
                },
            }),
        }
    }
}

/// A value: i32 and f32 bits in the low 32 bits of `low`, v128 in `low` and `high`, references as their bits (zero
/// for null). `trace` says how the collector follows the value, as one of the TRACE_* kinds, which only a reference
/// needs: a function reference points into its function's cell, while other references are the addresses of cells.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct WasmValue {
    pub kind: WasmValueKind,
    pub trace: u8,
    pub low: u64,
    pub high: u64,
}

impl WasmValue {
    fn of(value: Value, trace: u8) -> Self {
        let (kind, low, high) = match value {
            Value::I32(value) => (WasmValueKind::I32, u64::from(value as u32), 0),
            Value::I64(value) => (WasmValueKind::I64, value as u64, 0),
            Value::F32(bits) => (WasmValueKind::F32, u64::from(bits), 0),
            Value::F64(bits) => (WasmValueKind::F64, bits, 0),
            Value::V128(bits) => (WasmValueKind::V128, bits as u64, (bits >> 64) as u64),
            Value::Ref(bits) => (WasmValueKind::Reference, bits, 0),
        };
        Self { kind, trace, low, high }
    }

    fn to_value(self) -> Value {
        match self.kind {
            WasmValueKind::I32 => Value::I32(self.low as u32 as i32),
            WasmValueKind::I64 => Value::I64(self.low as i64),
            WasmValueKind::F32 => Value::F32(self.low as u32),
            WasmValueKind::F64 => Value::F64(self.low),
            WasmValueKind::V128 => Value::V128(u128::from(self.low) | (u128::from(self.high) << 64)),
            WasmValueKind::Reference => Value::Ref(self.low),
        }
    }
}

#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WasmExternKind {
    Function,
    Table,
    Memory,
    Global,
    Tag,
}

/// A function, table, memory, global, or tag of a store.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct WasmExtern {
    pub kind: WasmExternKind,
    /// The entity's cell.
    pub entity: *mut c_void,
}

impl WasmExtern {
    fn of(value: ExternValue) -> Self {
        let (kind, entity) = match value {
            ExternValue::Function(address) => (WasmExternKind::Function, address.cell().cast()),
            ExternValue::Table(address) => (WasmExternKind::Table, address.cell().cast()),
            ExternValue::Memory(address) => (WasmExternKind::Memory, address.cell().cast()),
            ExternValue::Global(address) => (WasmExternKind::Global, address.cell().cast()),
            ExternValue::Tag(address) => (WasmExternKind::Tag, address.cell().cast()),
        };
        Self { kind, entity }
    }

    fn to_extern_value(self) -> ExternValue {
        match self.kind {
            WasmExternKind::Function => ExternValue::Function(entity(self.entity)),
            WasmExternKind::Table => ExternValue::Table(entity(self.entity)),
            WasmExternKind::Memory => ExternValue::Memory(entity(self.entity)),
            WasmExternKind::Global => ExternValue::Global(entity(self.entity)),
            WasmExternKind::Tag => ExternValue::Tag(entity(self.entity)),
        }
    }
}

/// The limits of a memory or table. `maximum` only matters if `has_maximum` is set.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct WasmLimits {
    pub minimum: u64,
    pub maximum: u64,
    pub has_maximum: bool,
    pub address64: bool,
    pub shared: bool,
}

impl WasmLimits {
    fn of(limits: &Limits) -> Self {
        Self {
            minimum: limits.min,
            maximum: limits.max.unwrap_or(0),
            has_maximum: limits.max.is_some(),
            address64: limits.address_type == AddressType::I64,
            shared: limits.shared,
        }
    }

    fn to_limits(self) -> Limits {
        Limits {
            min: self.minimum,
            max: self.has_maximum.then_some(self.maximum),
            address_type: if self.address64 {
                AddressType::I64
            } else {
                AddressType::I32
            },
            shared: self.shared,
        }
    }
}

/// What an import or export is, beyond its kind: the type index of a function or tag, the limits of a memory or
/// table, the element type of a table, and the value type and mutability of a global.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct WasmExternType {
    pub kind: WasmExternKind,
    pub type_index: u32,
    pub limits: WasmLimits,
    pub value_type: WasmValueType,
    pub mutable: bool,
}

fn extern_type_of_import(description: &ImportDescription) -> WasmExternType {
    let mut ty = WasmExternType {
        kind: WasmExternKind::Function,
        type_index: 0,
        limits: WasmLimits::of(&Limits {
            min: 0,
            max: None,
            address_type: AddressType::I32,
            shared: false,
        }),
        value_type: WasmValueType::of(ValType::I32),
        mutable: false,
    };
    match description {
        ImportDescription::Function(index) => ty.type_index = *index,
        ImportDescription::Table(table) => {
            ty.kind = WasmExternKind::Table;
            ty.limits = WasmLimits::of(&table.limits);
            ty.value_type = WasmValueType::of(ValType::Ref(table.element));
        }
        ImportDescription::Memory(memory) => {
            ty.kind = WasmExternKind::Memory;
            ty.limits = WasmLimits::of(&memory.limits);
        }
        ImportDescription::Global(global) => {
            ty.kind = WasmExternKind::Global;
            ty.value_type = WasmValueType::of(global.value);
            ty.mutable = global.mutable;
        }
        ImportDescription::Tag(tag) => {
            ty.kind = WasmExternKind::Tag;
            ty.type_index = tag.type_index;
        }
    }
    ty
}

// Modules.

/// A compiled module, which the embedder holds a reference to until it calls `wasm_module_release()`. Its pointer is
/// that of an `Arc<Module>`, and it is never dereferenced as itself.
pub struct WasmModule {
    _opaque: [u8; 0],
}

/// Decode and validate a module. Returns null and sets `error` if the module is malformed or invalid.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `bytes` must point at `length` readable bytes, and `error` must be null or writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_module_compile(
    bytes: *const u8,
    length: usize,
    error: *mut WasmString,
) -> *const WasmModule {
    let bytes = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(bytes, length) };
    match crate::compile(bytes) {
        Ok(module) => Arc::into_raw(Arc::new(module)).cast(),
        Err(compile_error) => {
            write_string(error, &compile_error.to_string());
            std::ptr::null()
        }
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `module` must be a live module, which this releases one reference to.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_module_release(module: *const WasmModule) {
    unsafe { Arc::decrement_strong_count(module.cast::<Module>()) };
}

fn module_of<'a>(module: *const WasmModule) -> &'a Module {
    unsafe { &*module.cast::<Module>() }
}

/// A reference of our own to the module of `module`.
fn module_arc(module: *const WasmModule) -> Arc<Module> {
    let module = module.cast::<Module>();
    unsafe {
        Arc::increment_strong_count(module);
        Arc::from_raw(module)
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `module` must be a live module.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_module_import_count(module: *const WasmModule) -> usize {
    module_of(module).imports.len()
}

/// The names and type of an import.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `module` must be a live module with an import at `index`, and the out parameters must be writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_module_import(
    module: *const WasmModule,
    index: usize,
    module_name: *mut WasmStringView,
    name: *mut WasmStringView,
    ty: *mut WasmExternType,
) {
    let import = &module_of(module).imports[index];
    unsafe {
        *module_name = WasmStringView::of(&import.module);
        *name = WasmStringView::of(&import.name);
        *ty = extern_type_of_import(&import.description);
    }
}

/// The parameter and result counts of the function type at `type_index`, or false if it is not a function type.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `module` must be a live module, and the out parameters must be writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_module_function_type(
    module: *const WasmModule,
    type_index: u32,
    parameter_count: *mut usize,
    result_count: *mut usize,
) -> bool {
    let Some(function) = module_of(module)
        .types
        .get(type_index as usize)
        .and_then(|ty| ty.as_func())
    else {
        return false;
    };
    unsafe {
        *parameter_count = function.params.len();
        *result_count = function.results.len();
    }
    true
}

/// Copy the parameter and result types of the function type at `type_index`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `module` must be a live module with a function type at `type_index`, and the out arrays must have room for its
/// parameters and results.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_module_function_type_values(
    module: *const WasmModule,
    type_index: u32,
    parameters: *mut WasmValueType,
    results: *mut WasmValueType,
) {
    let function = module_of(module).types[type_index as usize]
        .as_func()
        .expect("the embedder checks for a function type");
    unsafe { write_function_type(function, parameters, results) };
}

/// Write the parameter and result types of `function`; a null `results` skips the results.
unsafe fn write_function_type(function: &FuncType, parameters: *mut WasmValueType, results: *mut WasmValueType) {
    for (index, &ty) in function.params.iter().enumerate() {
        unsafe { *parameters.add(index) = WasmValueType::of(ty) };
    }
    if results.is_null() {
        return;
    }
    for (index, &ty) in function.results.iter().enumerate() {
        unsafe { *results.add(index) = WasmValueType::of(ty) };
    }
}

// Stores.

/// A store, which belongs to the thread that created it.
pub struct WasmStore(Store);

/// Create a store for the current thread, whose entities, GC objects, and memories live in the LibGC heap and
/// primitive storage of `interface`. The store keeps no entity alive: its embedder visits or roots the cells of those
/// it uses (see `WasmExtern`).
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `interface` must hold the functions of LibGC's C interface and a heap of the current thread, which outlives the
/// store.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_create(interface: *const GcInterface) -> *mut WasmStore {
    let interface = unsafe { *interface };
    let store = Box::into_raw(Box::new(WasmStore(Store::with_heap(Some(interface)))));
    unsafe { (*store).0.attach_to_heap() };
    store
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store that no call is running in.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_destroy(store: *mut WasmStore) {
    unsafe { drop(Box::from_raw(store)) };
}

/// The entity of a cell an embedder passed in. Panics if the cell is not a live entity of the kind.
fn entity<T: Entity>(cell: *mut c_void) -> Handle<T> {
    unsafe { Handle::from_cell(cell) }.expect("the embedder passes a live entity of the right kind")
}

fn store_of<'a>(store: *mut WasmStore) -> &'a mut Store {
    unsafe { &mut (*store).0 }
}

#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WasmStatus {
    Ok,
    /// Linking failed: an import is missing or has the wrong type.
    LinkError,
    /// Execution trapped.
    Trap,
    /// An exception was thrown and not caught.
    Exception,
    /// Execution ran out of stack.
    StackExhausted,
}

impl WasmStatus {
    /// The status of a trap, with what the embedder needs to know of it in `error` and `exception`.
    fn of_trap(trap: &Trap, error: *mut WasmString, exception: *mut u64) -> Self {
        match trap {
            Trap::UncaughtException(reference) => {
                if !exception.is_null() {
                    unsafe { *exception = *reference };
                }
                write_string(error, &trap.message());
                Self::Exception
            }
            Trap::StackExhausted => {
                write_string(error, &trap.message());
                Self::StackExhausted
            }
            _ => {
                write_string(error, &trap.message());
                Self::Trap
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A function the embedder implements. It reads the arguments and writes the results, in the order of the function
/// type, and returns `Ok`. It traps by returning `Trap` with a message in `error`, and throws an exception by
/// returning `Exception` with the exception's reference in `exception`.
pub type WasmHostCallback = unsafe extern "C" fn(
    user_data: *mut std::ffi::c_void,
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    arguments: *const WasmValue,
    argument_count: usize,
    results: *mut WasmValue,
    result_count: usize,
    error: *mut WasmString,
    exception: *mut u64,
) -> WasmStatus;

/// Visits the cells the user data of a host function refers to, with a LibGC visitor.
pub type WasmVisitCallback = unsafe extern "C" fn(user_data: *mut std::ffi::c_void, visitor: *mut std::ffi::c_void);

/// Releases the user data of a host function when its function goes away.
pub type WasmReleaseCallback = unsafe extern "C" fn(user_data: *mut std::ffi::c_void);

struct HostFunctionData {
    callback: WasmHostCallback,
    visit: WasmVisitCallback,
    release: WasmReleaseCallback,
    user_data: *mut std::ffi::c_void,
    /// The store the function belongs to, which its calls get.
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    /// The types of the arguments, which say how the collector follows them.
    parameter_types: Vec<ValType>,
    result_count: usize,
}

impl Drop for HostFunctionData {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        unsafe { (self.release)(self.user_data) };
    }
}

impl HostFunction for HostFunctionData {
    fn call(&self, store: &mut Store, arguments: &[Value]) -> Result<Vec<Value>, Trap> {
        let arguments: Vec<WasmValue> = arguments
            .iter()
            .zip(&self.parameter_types)
            .map(|(&value, &ty)| WasmValue::of(value, store.trace_of(ty)))
            .collect();
        let mut results = vec![
            WasmValue {
                kind: WasmValueKind::I32,
                trace: TRACE_NONE,
                low: 0,
                high: 0,
            };
            self.result_count
        ];
        let mut error = WasmString {
            data: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            length: 0,
        };
        let mut exception = 0u64;
        let status = unsafe {
            (self.callback)(
                self.user_data,
                self.store,
                arguments.as_ptr(),
                arguments.len(),
                results.as_mut_ptr(),
                results.len(),
                &raw mut error,
                &raw mut exception,
            )
        };
        let message = if error.data.is_null() {
            String::new()
        } else {
            let bytes = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(error.data, error.length) };
            let message = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).into_owned();
            unsafe { wasm_string_release(error) };
            message
        };
        match status {
            WasmStatus::Ok => Ok(results.into_iter().map(WasmValue::to_value).collect()),
            WasmStatus::Exception => Err(Trap::UncaughtException(exception)),
            _ => Err(Trap::Host(message)),
        }
    }

    fn visit_edges(&self, visitor: &Visitor) {
        unsafe { (self.visit)(self.user_data, visitor.raw()) };
    }

    fn user_data(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.user_data
    }
}

/// Add a host function of the given type to the store, and return its cell. The function visits what its user data
/// refers to with `visit`, and releases the user data with `release` when it goes away. The concrete types among its
/// types must be identities of the store, which is how the collector tells what its values are, or the runtime aborts.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store, and the type arrays must hold the given numbers of types.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_allocate_host_function(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    parameters: *const WasmValueType,
    parameter_count: usize,
    results: *const WasmValueType,
    result_count: usize,
    callback: WasmHostCallback,
    visit: WasmVisitCallback,
    release: WasmReleaseCallback,
    user_data: *mut std::ffi::c_void,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let to_types = |types: *const WasmValueType, count: usize| -> Vec<ValType> {
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(types, count) }
            .iter()
            .map(|ty| ty.to_value_type())
            .collect()
    };
    let ty = FuncType {
        params: to_types(parameters, parameter_count),
        results: to_types(results, result_count),
    };
    assert!(
        ty.params
            .iter()
            .chain(&ty.results)
            .all(|&ty| store_of(store).knows_type(ty)),
        "a host function's concrete types must be identities of the store"
    );
    let data = Rc::new(HostFunctionData {
        callback,
        visit,
        release,
        user_data,
        store,
        parameter_types: ty.params.clone(),
        result_count: ty.results.len(),
    });
    store_of(store).allocate_host_function(ty, data).cell().cast()
}

/// Add a memory to the store. Returns false if it cannot be allocated.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store, and `address` writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_allocate_memory(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    limits: WasmLimits,
    address: *mut *mut c_void,
) -> bool {
    let Some(allocated) = store_of(store).allocate_memory(MemoryType {
        limits: limits.to_limits(),
    }) else {
        return false;
    };
    unsafe { *address = allocated.cell().cast() };
    true
}

/// Add a table to the store, with every element set to `initial`. Returns false if it would be too large.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store, and `address` writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_allocate_table(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    element: WasmValueType,
    limits: WasmLimits,
    initial: u64,
    address: *mut *mut c_void,
) -> bool {
    let ValType::Ref(element) = element.to_value_type() else {
        panic!("table elements are references");
    };
    let Some(allocated) = store_of(store).allocate_table(
        TableType {
            element,
            limits: limits.to_limits(),
        },
        initial,
    ) else {
        return false;
    };
    unsafe { *address = allocated.cell().cast() };
    true
}

/// Add a global to the store.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_allocate_global(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    ty: WasmValueType,
    mutable: bool,
    value: WasmValue,
) -> *mut c_void {
    store_of(store)
        .allocate_global(
            GlobalType {
                value: ty.to_value_type(),
                mutable,
            },
            value.to_value(),
        )
        .cell()
        .cast()
}

/// Instantiate `module` with `imports`, one for each of its imports in order. On success, writes the instance's
/// address; otherwise writes a message to `error`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` and `module` must be live, `imports` must hold `import_count` externs, and the out parameters must be
/// writable (`error` and `exception` may be null).
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_instantiate(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    module: *const WasmModule,
    imports: *const WasmExtern,
    import_count: usize,
    instance: *mut *mut c_void,
    error: *mut WasmString,
    exception: *mut u64,
) -> WasmStatus {
    let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(import_count);
    for import in unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(imports, import_count) } {
        values.push(import.to_extern_value());
    }
    let module = module_arc(module);
    match store_of(store).instantiate(module, &values) {
        Ok(address) => {
            unsafe { *instance = address.cell().cast() };
            WasmStatus::Ok
        }
        Err(InstantiationError::Link(message)) => {
            write_string(error, &message);
            WasmStatus::LinkError
        }
        Err(InstantiationError::Trap(trap)) => WasmStatus::of_trap(&trap, error, exception),
    }
}

/// The number of exports of an instance.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store with an instance at `instance`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_instance_export_count(store: *mut WasmStore, instance: *mut c_void) -> usize {
    store_of(store).instance(entity(instance)).module.exports.len()
}

/// The name and value of an instance's export, in the module's order.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store with an instance at `instance` that has an export at `index`, and the out parameters
/// must be writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_instance_export(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    instance: *mut c_void,
    index: usize,
    name: *mut WasmStringView,
    value: *mut WasmExtern,
) -> bool {
    let instance = store_of(store).instance(entity(instance));
    let export = &instance.module.exports[index];
    unsafe { *name = WasmStringView::of(&export.name) };
    let Some(extern_value) = instance.export(&export.name) else {
        return false;
    };
    unsafe { *value = WasmExtern::of(extern_value) };
    true
}

/// Find an instance's export by name.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store with an instance at `instance`, `name` must hold `length` bytes, and `value` must be
/// writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_instance_find_export(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    instance: *mut c_void,
    name: *const u8,
    length: usize,
    value: *mut WasmExtern,
) -> bool {
    let name = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(name, length) };
    let Ok(name) = std::str::from_utf8(name) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Some(extern_value) = store_of(store).instance(entity(instance)).export(name) else {
        return false;
    };
    unsafe { *value = WasmExtern::of(extern_value) };
    true
}

/// The parameter and result counts of a function.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store with a function at `function`, and the out parameters must be writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_function_type(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    function: *mut c_void,
    parameter_count: *mut usize,
    result_count: *mut usize,
) {
    let ty = &store_of(store).function(entity(function)).ty;
    unsafe {
        *parameter_count = ty.params.len();
        *result_count = ty.results.len();
    }
}

/// Copy the parameter and result types of a function.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store with a function at `function`, and the out arrays must have room for its parameters
/// and results.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_function_type_values(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    function: *mut c_void,
    parameters: *mut WasmValueType,
    results: *mut WasmValueType,
) {
    let ty = &store_of(store).function(entity(function)).ty;
    unsafe { write_function_type(ty, parameters, results) };
}

/// Call a function. On a trap, writes its message to `error`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store with a function at `function`, `arguments` must hold one value for each parameter,
/// `results` must have room for one value for each result, and `error` and `exception` must be null or writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_invoke(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    function: *mut c_void,
    arguments: *const WasmValue,
    argument_count: usize,
    results: *mut WasmValue,
    result_count: usize,
    error: *mut WasmString,
    exception: *mut u64,
) -> WasmStatus {
    let arguments: Vec<Value> = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(arguments, argument_count) }
        .iter()
        .map(|value| value.to_value())
        .collect();
    let store = store_of(store);
    match store.invoke(entity(function), &arguments) {
        Ok(values) => {
            let types = &store.function(entity(function)).ty.results;
            for (index, (value, &ty)) in values.into_iter().zip(types).take(result_count).enumerate() {
                unsafe { *results.add(index) = WasmValue::of(value, store.trace_of(ty)) };
            }
            WasmStatus::Ok
        }
        Err(trap) => WasmStatus::of_trap(&trap, error, exception),
    }
}

/// Visits a value of a store with a LibGC visitor, which keeps the cell a reference refers to alive.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `visitor` must be the LibGC visitor a cell's visit_edges was given, and `value` a value of a store.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_visitor_visit_value(visitor: *mut c_void, value: WasmValue) {
    if value.kind == WasmValueKind::Reference {
        Visitor::new(visitor).visit_value(value.low, value.trace);
    }
}

/// The reference to a function, as tables and reference values hold it.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store with a function at `function`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_function_reference(store: *mut WasmStore, function: *mut c_void) -> u64 {
    store_of(store).function_reference(entity(function))
}

/// The function a function reference refers to. Returns false for null.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store, `reference` a function reference of it, and `function` writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_function_from_reference(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    reference: u64,
    function: *mut *mut c_void,
) -> bool {
    let Some(address) = store_of(store).function_from_reference(reference) else {
        return false;
    };
    unsafe { *function = address.cell().cast() };
    true
}

/// The type of a global.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store with a global at `global`, and `mutable` writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_global_type(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    global: *mut c_void,
    mutable: *mut bool,
) -> WasmValueType {
    let ty = store_of(store).global(entity(global)).ty;
    unsafe { *mutable = ty.mutable };
    WasmValueType::of(ty.value)
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `store` must be a live store with a global at `global`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_store_global_get(store: *mut WasmStore, global: *mut c_void) -> WasmValue {
    let global = store_of(store).global(entity(global));
    WasmValue::of(global.get(), global.trace)
}

// WASI.

/// The state of a WASI command, whose functions a store gets with `wasm_wasi_allocate_function()`.
pub struct WasmWasi(Rc<crate::wasi::Wasi>);

fn strings_of(strings: *const WasmStringView, count: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    if count == 0 {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(strings, count) }
        .iter()
        .map(|string| {
            String::from_utf8_lossy(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(string.data, string.length) }).into_owned()
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Create the state of a WASI command with its arguments, its environment (as `NAME=value` strings), and the host
/// directories it sees at the guest paths of the same index.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Each array must hold its count of strings.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_wasi_create(
    arguments: *const WasmStringView,
    argument_count: usize,
    environment: *const WasmStringView,
    environment_count: usize,
    host_paths: *const WasmStringView,
    guest_paths: *const WasmStringView,
    preopen_count: usize,
) -> *mut WasmWasi {
    let preopens = strings_of(host_paths, preopen_count)
        .into_iter()
        .zip(strings_of(guest_paths, preopen_count))
        .map(|(host, guest)| crate::wasi::Preopen::new(host, guest))
        .collect();
    let wasi = crate::wasi::Wasi::new(
        strings_of(arguments, argument_count),
        strings_of(environment, environment_count),
        preopens,
    );
    Box::into_raw(Box::new(WasmWasi(Rc::new(wasi))))
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `wasi` must come from `wasm_wasi_create()`. The functions made from it keep what they need.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_wasi_destroy(wasi: *mut WasmWasi) {
    unsafe { drop(Box::from_raw(wasi)) };
}

/// Add the WASI function `name` (of `wasi_snapshot_preview1`) to the store, and write its cell to `function`.
/// Returns false if there is no such function.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `store` and `wasi` must be live, `name` must hold `length` bytes, and `function` must be writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_wasi_allocate_function(
    store: *mut WasmStore,
    wasi: *mut WasmWasi,
    name: *const u8,
    length: usize,
    function: *mut *mut c_void,
) -> bool {
    let Ok(name) = std::str::from_utf8(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(name, length) }) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Some(address) = unsafe { &(*wasi).0 }.allocate_function(store_of(store), name) else {
        return false;
    };
    unsafe { *function = address.cell().cast() };
    true
}

/// Have the WASI functions work on `memory`, which is usually the memory the command exports. The memory must live
/// while they run, as the command's instance makes it.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `wasi` must be live, and `memory` a memory's cell.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_wasi_set_memory(wasi: *mut WasmWasi, memory: *mut c_void) {
    unsafe { &(*wasi).0 }.set_memory(entity(memory));
}

/// Whether the command called proc_exit, and with which code.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `wasi` must be live, and `code` writable.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn wasm_wasi_exit_code(wasi: *mut WasmWasi, code: *mut i32) -> bool {
    let Some(exit_code) = unsafe { &(*wasi).0 }.exit_code() else {
        return false;
    };
    unsafe { *code = exit_code };
    true
}

//! Evaluating the constant expressions that initialize globals, tables, and segments.

use super::{FunctionAddress, GlobalAddress, Store, Trap, Value};
use crate::module::{ConstantExpression, Module};
use crate::opcode;
use crate::parser::parse_heap_type;
use crate::reader::Reader;
use crate::types::CompositeType;

pub fn evaluate(
    store: &mut Store,
    globals: &[GlobalAddress],
    functions: &[FunctionAddress],
    type_identities: &[u32],
    module: &Module,
    expression: &ConstantExpression,
) -> Result<Value, Trap> {
    let mut reader = Reader::with_range(
        &module.bytes,
        expression.code.start as usize,
        expression.code.end as usize,
    );
    let mut stack: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    let malformed = || Trap::Host("malformed constant expression".to_string());
    let read = |result: crate::Result<u64>| result.map_err(|_| malformed());
    loop {
        let opcode = reader.read_u8().map_err(|_| malformed())?;
        match opcode {
            opcode::END => break,
            opcode::I32_CONST => stack.push(Value::I32(reader.read_i32().map_err(|_| malformed())?)),
            opcode::I64_CONST => stack.push(Value::I64(reader.read_i64().map_err(|_| malformed())?)),
            opcode::F32_CONST => stack.push(Value::F32(reader.read_fixed_u32().map_err(|_| malformed())?)),
            opcode::F64_CONST => stack.push(Value::F64(reader.read_fixed_u64().map_err(|_| malformed())?)),
            opcode::REF_NULL => {
                parse_heap_type(&mut reader).map_err(|_| malformed())?;
                stack.push(Value::Ref(0));
            }
            opcode::REF_FUNC => {
                let index = read(reader.read_u32().map(u64::from))?;
                stack.push(Value::Ref(store.function_reference(functions[index as usize])));
            }
            opcode::GLOBAL_GET => {
                let index = read(reader.read_u32().map(u64::from))?;
                stack.push(store.global(globals[index as usize]).get());
            }
            opcode::I32_ADD | opcode::I32_SUB | opcode::I32_MUL => {
                let (Some(Value::I32(rhs)), Some(Value::I32(lhs))) = (stack.pop(), stack.pop()) else {
                    return Err(malformed());
                };
                stack.push(Value::I32(match opcode {
                    opcode::I32_ADD => lhs.wrapping_add(rhs),
                    opcode::I32_SUB => lhs.wrapping_sub(rhs),
                    _ => lhs.wrapping_mul(rhs),
                }));
            }
            opcode::I64_ADD | opcode::I64_SUB | opcode::I64_MUL => {
                let (Some(Value::I64(rhs)), Some(Value::I64(lhs))) = (stack.pop(), stack.pop()) else {
                    return Err(malformed());
                };
                stack.push(Value::I64(match opcode {
                    opcode::I64_ADD => lhs.wrapping_add(rhs),
                    opcode::I64_SUB => lhs.wrapping_sub(rhs),
                    _ => lhs.wrapping_mul(rhs),
                }));
            }
            opcode::PREFIX_SIMD => {
                read(reader.read_u32().map(u64::from))?;
                let bytes = reader.read_bytes(16).map_err(|_| malformed())?;
                let mut array = [0u8; 16];
                array.copy_from_slice(bytes);
                stack.push(Value::V128(u128::from_le_bytes(array)));
            }
            opcode::PREFIX_GC => {
                let sub_opcode = reader.read_u32().map_err(|_| malformed())?;
                let mut immediate = || reader.read_u32().map_err(|_| malformed());
                match sub_opcode {
                    opcode::gc::STRUCT_NEW | opcode::gc::STRUCT_NEW_DEFAULT => {
                        let type_index = immediate()?;
                        let identity = type_identities[type_index as usize];
                        let CompositeType::Struct(fields) = &store.types[identity as usize].composite else {
                            return Err(malformed());
                        };
                        let count = fields.len();
                        let values = if sub_opcode == opcode::gc::STRUCT_NEW {
                            stack.split_off(stack.len().checked_sub(count).ok_or_else(malformed)?)
                        } else {
                            fields
                                .iter()
                                .map(|field| Value::default_for(field.storage.unpacked()))
                                .collect()
                        };
                        let object = store.allocate_struct(identity, &values);
                        if object == 0 {
                            return Err(Trap::Host("out of memory".to_string()));
                        }
                        stack.push(Value::Ref(object));
                    }
                    opcode::gc::ARRAY_NEW | opcode::gc::ARRAY_NEW_DEFAULT | opcode::gc::ARRAY_NEW_FIXED => {
                        let type_index = immediate()?;
                        let identity = type_identities[type_index as usize];
                        let CompositeType::Array(element) = &store.types[identity as usize].composite else {
                            return Err(malformed());
                        };
                        let element = element.storage.unpacked();
                        // NB: The length of array.new is any u32, so its elements go into the array directly, which
                        //     checks its size first, rather than into a vector of that length.
                        let array = match sub_opcode {
                            opcode::gc::ARRAY_NEW_FIXED => {
                                let count = immediate()? as usize;
                                let values = stack.split_off(stack.len().checked_sub(count).ok_or_else(malformed)?);
                                store.allocate_array(identity, &values)
                            }
                            _ => {
                                let Some(Value::I32(length)) = stack.pop() else {
                                    return Err(malformed());
                                };
                                let value = if sub_opcode == opcode::gc::ARRAY_NEW {
                                    stack.pop().ok_or_else(malformed)?
                                } else {
                                    Value::default_for(element)
                                };
                                store.allocate_filled_array(identity, value, length as u32)
                            }
                        };
                        if array == 0 {
                            return Err(Trap::Host("out of memory".to_string()));
                        }
                        stack.push(Value::Ref(array));
                    }
                    opcode::gc::REF_I31 => {
                        let Some(Value::I32(value)) = stack.pop() else {
                            return Err(malformed());
                        };
                        stack.push(Value::Ref(super::gc::i31_reference(value)));
                    }
                    // A reference keeps its bits when it moves between the any and extern hierarchies.
                    opcode::gc::ANY_CONVERT_EXTERN | opcode::gc::EXTERN_CONVERT_ANY => {}
                    _ => return Err(malformed()),
                }
            }
            _ => return Err(Trap::Host("unsupported constant expression".to_string())),
        }
    }
    stack.pop().ok_or_else(malformed)
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! The entities of the runtime: functions, tables, memories, globals, tags, and instances. Each is a cell of the heap,
//! with the entity right after the cell header, and lives while something refers to it: an embedder's cell, another
//! entity (an instance refers to everything it defines and imports, a function to its instance), or an interpreter
//! frame, whose function pointer the conservative scan of the stack finds. The store refers to none of them.
//!
//! The first word of an entity's cell says what it is, so that a handle an embedder passes in can be checked.

use super::heap::{CELL_HEADER_SIZE, CellType, Heap, Visitor, forget_host_object, visit_host_object};
use super::memory::MemoryInstance;
use super::{FunctionInstance, FunctionKind, GlobalInstance, Instance, TableInstance, TagInstance};
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

pub const ENTITY_FUNCTION: usize = 0;
pub const ENTITY_TABLE: usize = 1;
pub const ENTITY_MEMORY: usize = 2;
pub const ENTITY_GLOBAL: usize = 3;
pub const ENTITY_TAG: usize = 4;
pub const ENTITY_INSTANCE: usize = 5;
pub const ENTITY_KIND_COUNT: usize = 6;

pub const ENTITY_NAMES: [&str; ENTITY_KIND_COUNT] = [
    "WebAssembly function",
    "WebAssembly table",
    "WebAssembly memory",
    "WebAssembly global",
    "WebAssembly tag",
    "WebAssembly instance",
];

/// What the first word of an entity's cell holds, besides its kind.
const ENTITY_MAGIC: u64 = 0x5741_534d_0000_0000;

pub trait Entity: Sized {
    const KIND: usize;

    /// Visit the cells the entity refers to.
    fn visit_edges(&self, visitor: &Visitor);
}

/// An entity, as the address of the entity in its cell. Function references and tag identities are the handles of
/// their functions and tags, and the interpreter's views of instances, tables, memories, and globals are the first
/// fields of theirs, so the interpreter's pointers are handles too, and a slice of handles is an array of them.
#[repr(transparent)]
pub struct Handle<T>(NonNull<T>);

impl<T> Clone for Handle<T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        *self
    }
}

impl<T> Copy for Handle<T> {}

impl<T> PartialEq for Handle<T> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.0 == other.0
    }
}

impl<T> Eq for Handle<T> {}

impl<T> core::hash::Hash for Handle<T> {
    fn hash<H: core::hash::Hasher>(&self, state: &mut H) {
        self.0.hash(state);
    }
}

impl<T> core::fmt::Debug for Handle<T> {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        write!(formatter, "{:p}", self.0)
    }
}

impl<T: Entity> Handle<T> {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `pointer` must be the address of a live entity of this kind.
    pub unsafe fn from_ptr(pointer: *const T) -> Self {
        Self(NonNull::new(pointer.cast_mut()).expect("an entity is never null"))
    }

    /// The entity of a cell, if the cell is an entity of this kind.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `cell` must be a live cell of the runtime.
    pub unsafe fn from_cell(cell: *mut c_void) -> Option<Self> {
        if cell.is_null() || unsafe { cell.cast::<u64>().read() } != ENTITY_MAGIC | T::KIND as u64 {
            return None;
        }
        Some(Self(unsafe {
            NonNull::new_unchecked(cell.cast::<u8>().add(CELL_HEADER_SIZE).cast())
        }))
    }

    pub fn as_ptr(self) -> *mut T {
        self.0.as_ptr()
    }

    pub fn cell(self) -> *mut u8 {
        self.0.as_ptr().cast::<u8>().wrapping_sub(CELL_HEADER_SIZE)
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The entity must be alive for `'a`, and not be mutated meanwhile.
    pub unsafe fn get<'a>(self) -> &'a T {
        unsafe { self.0.as_ref() }
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The entity must be alive for `'a`, and not be accessed otherwise meanwhile.
    pub unsafe fn get_mut<'a>(mut self) -> &'a mut T {
        unsafe { self.0.as_mut() }
    }
}

/// The size of the cell of an entity kind.
pub fn entity_cell_size(kind: usize) -> usize {
    let size = match kind {
        ENTITY_FUNCTION => size_of::<FunctionInstance>(),
        ENTITY_TABLE => size_of::<TableInstance>(),
        ENTITY_MEMORY => size_of::<MemoryInstance>(),
        ENTITY_GLOBAL => size_of::<GlobalInstance>(),
        ENTITY_TAG => size_of::<TagInstance>(),
        ENTITY_INSTANCE => size_of::<Instance>(),
        _ => unreachable!("there are {ENTITY_KIND_COUNT} entity kinds"),
    };
    (CELL_HEADER_SIZE + size).next_multiple_of(16)
}

/// Make `entity` a cell of `heap`. Garbage is not collected until the entity is in place, but may be right after, so
/// the caller keeps the handle where the collector looks: on the stack, or in a cell it reaches.
pub fn allocate<T: Entity>(heap: &Heap, entity: T) -> Handle<T> {
    const { assert!(align_of::<T>() <= 16, "cells are 16-byte aligned") };
    heap.defer_gc();
    let cell = heap.allocate_cell(CellType::Entity(T::KIND));
    let handle = unsafe {
        cell.cast::<u64>().write(ENTITY_MAGIC | T::KIND as u64);
        let pointer = cell.add(CELL_HEADER_SIZE).cast::<T>();
        pointer.write(entity);
        Handle::from_ptr(pointer)
    };
    heap.undefer_gc();
    handle
}

unsafe fn kind_of(cell: *mut c_void) -> usize {
    let word = unsafe { cell.cast::<u64>().read() };
    debug_assert_eq!(word & !0xffff, ENTITY_MAGIC);
    (word & 0xffff) as usize
}

/// # Safety
///
/// Only LibGC calls this, with a live entity's cell.
pub unsafe extern "C" fn entity_visit_edges(cell: *mut c_void, visitor: *mut c_void) {
    unsafe fn visit<T: Entity>(cell: *mut c_void, visitor: *mut c_void) {
        let handle = unsafe { Handle::<T>::from_cell(cell) }.expect("the cell is an entity of its kind");
        unsafe { handle.get() }.visit_edges(&Visitor::new(visitor));
    }
    unsafe {
        visit_host_object(cell, &Visitor::new(visitor));
        match kind_of(cell) {
            ENTITY_FUNCTION => visit::<FunctionInstance>(cell, visitor),
            ENTITY_TABLE => visit::<TableInstance>(cell, visitor),
            ENTITY_MEMORY => visit::<MemoryInstance>(cell, visitor),
            ENTITY_GLOBAL => visit::<GlobalInstance>(cell, visitor),
            ENTITY_TAG => visit::<TagInstance>(cell, visitor),
            ENTITY_INSTANCE => visit::<Instance>(cell, visitor),
            _ => unreachable!("there are {ENTITY_KIND_COUNT} entity kinds"),
        }
    }
}

/// Drop the entity of a cell, which is going away.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be an entity's cell, which nothing uses afterwards.
pub unsafe extern "C" fn destroy_entity(cell: *mut u8) {
    unsafe fn destroy<T: Entity>(cell: *mut u8) {
        let handle = unsafe { Handle::<T>::from_cell(cell.cast()) }.expect("the cell is an entity of its kind");
        unsafe {
            core::ptr::drop_in_place(handle.as_ptr());
            // A dead cell is no entity, so a stale handle to it is rejected.
            cell.cast::<u64>().write(0);
        }
    }
    unsafe {
        forget_host_object(cell.cast());
        match kind_of(cell.cast()) {
            ENTITY_FUNCTION => destroy::<FunctionInstance>(cell),
            ENTITY_TABLE => destroy::<TableInstance>(cell),
            ENTITY_MEMORY => destroy::<MemoryInstance>(cell),
            ENTITY_GLOBAL => destroy::<GlobalInstance>(cell),
            ENTITY_TAG => destroy::<TagInstance>(cell),
            ENTITY_INSTANCE => destroy::<Instance>(cell),
            _ => unreachable!("there are {ENTITY_KIND_COUNT} entity kinds"),
        }
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// Only LibGC calls this, with an entity's cell that is going away.
pub unsafe extern "C" fn entity_destroy(cell: *mut c_void) {
    unsafe { destroy_entity(cell.cast()) };
}

impl Entity for FunctionInstance {
    const KIND: usize = ENTITY_FUNCTION;

    fn visit_edges(&self, visitor: &Visitor) {
        match &self.kind {
            FunctionKind::Wasm { instance, .. } => visitor.visit_cell(instance.cell()),
            FunctionKind::Host(host) => host.visit_edges(visitor),
        }
    }
}

impl Entity for TableInstance {
    const KIND: usize = ENTITY_TABLE;

    fn visit_edges(&self, visitor: &Visitor) {
        for &element in &self.elements {
            visitor.visit_value(element, self.trace);
        }
    }
}

impl Entity for MemoryInstance {
    const KIND: usize = ENTITY_MEMORY;

    fn visit_edges(&self, _: &Visitor) {}
}

impl Entity for GlobalInstance {
    const KIND: usize = ENTITY_GLOBAL;

    fn visit_edges(&self, visitor: &Visitor) {
        visitor.visit_value(self.value[0], self.trace);
    }
}

impl Entity for TagInstance {
    const KIND: usize = ENTITY_TAG;

    fn visit_edges(&self, _: &Visitor) {}
}

impl Entity for Instance {
    const KIND: usize = ENTITY_INSTANCE;

    fn visit_edges(&self, visitor: &Visitor) {
        for function in &self.functions {
            visitor.visit_cell(function.cell());
        }
        for table in &self.tables {
            visitor.visit_cell(table.cell());
        }
        for memory in &self.memories {
            visitor.visit_cell(memory.cell());
        }
        for global in &self.globals {
            visitor.visit_cell(global.cell());
        }
        for tag in &self.tags {
            visitor.visit_cell(tag.cell());
        }
        for (segment, &trace) in self.element_storage.iter().zip(&self.element_traces) {
            for &value in segment {
                visitor.visit_value(value, trace);
            }
        }
    }
}

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
