//! GC objects, exceptions, and runtime types, as cells of the heap (see heap.rs), and how the collector traces them.
//!
//! References in the any hierarchy are encoded so that their kind shows in their low bits: zero is null, an i31 has
//! bit 0 set (its value is in the bits above), a host value converted from an externref has bits 1:0 equal to 0b10,
//! and GC objects and exceptions are the addresses of their cells. Converting between externref and anyref keeps the
//! bits. An embedder's host values must be the addresses of its cells with bit 1 set, which the collector follows as
//! it does any other cell.

use super::heap::{
    CELL_HEADER_SIZE, CellType, Heap, TRACE_FUNCTION, TRACE_NONE, TRACE_REFERENCE, Visitor, forget_host_object,
    object_size_class, visit_host_object,
};
use super::{Store, TagAddress, Value};
pub use crate::abi::EXCEPTION_CELL_SIZE;
use crate::abi::{
    ARRAY_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET, EXCEPTION_KINDS_OFFSET, EXCEPTION_LENGTH_OFFSET, EXCEPTION_PAYLOAD_OFFSET,
    EXCEPTION_TAG_OFFSET, MAX_INLINE_DATA_SIZE, OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET, OBJECT_LENGTH_OFFSET, RTT_KIND_ARRAY,
    RTT_KIND_FUNCTION, RTT_KIND_STRUCT, Rtt, STORAGE_32, STORAGE_64, STORAGE_FUNCTION_REFERENCE, STORAGE_I8,
    STORAGE_I16, STORAGE_REFERENCE, STORAGE_V128, STRUCT_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET,
};
use crate::types::{CompositeType, HeapType, StorageType, SubType, ValType, struct_layout};
use core::ffi::c_void;

const STORE_ROOT_STORE_OFFSET: usize = 16;

/// The largest data an object can have.
const MAX_OBJECT_DATA_SIZE: u64 = 1 << 31;

unsafe fn read<T: Copy>(cell: *const c_void, offset: usize) -> T {
    unsafe { cell.cast::<u8>().add(offset).cast::<T>().read() }
}

unsafe fn write<T>(cell: *mut u8, offset: usize, value: T) {
    unsafe { cell.add(offset).cast::<T>().write(value) };
}

/// How the collector follows values of `ty` (TRACE_*). Concrete heap types are identities of `types`.
pub fn trace_of(ty: ValType, types: &[SubType]) -> u8 {
    let ValType::Ref(reference) = ty else {
        return TRACE_NONE;
    };
    match reference.heap {
        HeapType::Func | HeapType::NoFunc => TRACE_FUNCTION,
        HeapType::Concrete(identity) => match types.get(identity as usize).map(|ty| &ty.composite) {
            Some(CompositeType::Func(_)) => TRACE_FUNCTION,
            Some(_) => TRACE_REFERENCE,
            None => panic!("concrete heap types are identities of the store"),
        },
        _ => TRACE_REFERENCE,
    }
}

pub fn storage_kind(storage: StorageType, types: &[SubType]) -> u8 {
    match storage {
        StorageType::I8 => STORAGE_I8,
        StorageType::I16 => STORAGE_I16,
        StorageType::Val(ValType::V128) => STORAGE_V128,
        StorageType::Val(ValType::I32 | ValType::F32) => STORAGE_32,
        StorageType::Val(value) => match trace_of(value, types) {
            TRACE_REFERENCE => STORAGE_REFERENCE,
            TRACE_FUNCTION => STORAGE_FUNCTION_REFERENCE,
            _ => STORAGE_64,
        },
    }
}

/// How the collector follows a field of storage `kind`.
fn trace_of_storage(kind: u8) -> u8 {
    match kind {
        STORAGE_REFERENCE => TRACE_REFERENCE,
        STORAGE_FUNCTION_REFERENCE => TRACE_FUNCTION,
        _ => TRACE_NONE,
    }
}

fn leak<T>(values: Vec<T>) -> *const T {
    Box::leak(values.into_boxed_slice()).as_ptr()
}

unsafe fn free<T>(pointer: *const T, length: usize) {
    if length != 0 {
        unsafe {
            drop(Box::from_raw(core::ptr::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(
                pointer.cast_mut(),
                length,
            )));
        };
    }
}

/// The Rtt of a cell that holds one.
fn rtt_of_cell(cell: *mut u8) -> *mut Rtt {
    cell.wrapping_add(CELL_HEADER_SIZE).cast()
}

fn cell_of_rtt(rtt: *const Rtt) -> *mut u8 {
    rtt.cast::<u8>().cast_mut().wrapping_sub(CELL_HEADER_SIZE)
}

/// Allocate the runtime type of the store type `identity`, whose supertypes have runtime types already.
pub fn allocate_rtt(store: &Store, identity: u32) -> *const Rtt {
    let sub_type = &store.types[identity as usize];
    let mut display = match sub_type.supertypes.first() {
        Some(&supertype) => {
            let parent = store.rtt(supertype);
            unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(parent.display, parent.depth as usize + 1) }.to_vec()
        }
        None => Vec::new(),
    };
    display.push(identity);
    let (kind, field_kinds, field_offsets, size) = match &sub_type.composite {
        CompositeType::Func(_) => (RTT_KIND_FUNCTION, Vec::new(), Vec::new(), 0),
        CompositeType::Struct(fields) => {
            let kinds: Vec<u8> = fields
                .iter()
                .map(|field| storage_kind(field.storage, &store.types))
                .collect();
            let (offsets, size) = struct_layout(fields);
            (RTT_KIND_STRUCT, kinds, offsets, size)
        }
        CompositeType::Array(element) => {
            let kind = storage_kind(element.storage, &store.types);
            let size = element.storage.object_field_size();
            (RTT_KIND_ARRAY, vec![kind], Vec::new(), size)
        }
    };
    let depth = display.len() as u32 - 1;
    let field_count = field_offsets.len() as u32;
    let kind_count = field_kinds.len();
    let cell = store.heap.allocate_cell(CellType::Rtt);
    let rtt = rtt_of_cell(cell);
    unsafe {
        rtt.write(Rtt {
            kind,
            depth,
            display: leak(display),
            field_offsets: leak(field_offsets),
            field_kinds: leak(field_kinds),
            size,
            field_count: kind_count as u32,
        });
        // The count of offsets and kinds differs for arrays, which have one kind and no offsets.
        debug_assert!(field_count as usize <= kind_count);
    }
    rtt
}

pub(super) unsafe extern "C" fn rtt_visit_edges(_: *mut c_void, _: *mut c_void) {}

pub(super) unsafe extern "C" fn rtt_destroy(cell: *mut c_void) {
    unsafe {
        let rtt = &*rtt_of_cell(cell.cast());
        free(rtt.display, rtt.depth as usize + 1);
        let kind_count = if rtt.kind == RTT_KIND_ARRAY {
            1
        } else {
            rtt.field_count as usize
        };
        free(rtt.field_kinds, kind_count);
        let offset_count = if rtt.kind == RTT_KIND_STRUCT {
            rtt.field_count as usize
        } else {
            0
        };
        free(rtt.field_offsets, offset_count);
    }
}

/// Allocate a zeroed object of the type `rtt` with `data_size` bytes of data and, for an array, `length` elements.
/// Returns zero if the data is too large, or if there is no memory for it.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `rtt` must be the runtime type of a struct or array type of the heap's store.
pub unsafe fn allocate_object(heap: &Heap, rtt: *const Rtt, data_size: u64, length: u64) -> u64 {
    if data_size > MAX_OBJECT_DATA_SIZE {
        return 0;
    }
    let is_array = unsafe { (*rtt).kind } == RTT_KIND_ARRAY;
    let inline_data_offset = if is_array {
        ARRAY_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET
    } else {
        STRUCT_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET
    };
    let (cell, data) = if data_size as usize <= MAX_INLINE_DATA_SIZE {
        let class = object_size_class(inline_data_offset + data_size as usize);
        let cell = heap.allocate_cell(CellType::Object(class));
        (cell, unsafe { cell.add(inline_data_offset) })
    } else {
        // The data lives outside the heap, after a word that holds the number of words after it. It counts towards
        // the next collection before the cell is allocated, which may collect.
        let words = data_size.div_ceil(8) as usize;
        let mut block = Vec::new();
        if block.try_reserve_exact(words + 1).is_err() {
            return 0;
        }
        block.resize(words + 1, 0u64);
        heap.did_allocate_external_memory((words + 1) * 8);
        let block = Box::leak(block.into_boxed_slice());
        block[0] = words as u64;
        let data = unsafe { block.as_mut_ptr().add(1) }.cast::<u8>();
        let cell = heap.allocate_cell(CellType::Object(object_size_class(inline_data_offset)));
        (cell, data)
    };
    unsafe {
        write(cell, 0, rtt as u64);
        write(cell, OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET, data as u64);
        if is_array {
            write(cell, OBJECT_LENGTH_OFFSET, length);
        }
    }
    cell as u64
}

/// The out-of-line data of an object and its size in words, if it has some.
unsafe fn out_of_line_data(cell: *const c_void) -> Option<(*mut u64, usize)> {
    unsafe {
        let data: *mut u64 = read(cell, OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET);
        // NB: The object's type may be gone already while the heap is destroyed, so this cannot ask whether it is an
        //     array. Data outside the heap is never right after the cell header.
        let data_address = data.cast::<u8>().cast_const();
        let cell = cell.cast::<u8>();
        if data_address == cell.add(STRUCT_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET) || data_address == cell.add(ARRAY_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET) {
            return None;
        }
        let block = data.sub(1);
        Some((block, *block as usize + 1))
    }
}

pub(super) unsafe extern "C" fn object_visit_edges(cell: *mut c_void, visitor: *mut c_void) {
    let visitor = Visitor::new(visitor);
    unsafe {
        visit_host_object(cell, &visitor);
        let rtt: *const Rtt = read(cell, 0);
        visitor.visit_cell(cell_of_rtt(rtt));
        let rtt = &*rtt;
        let data: *const u8 = read(cell, OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET);
        if rtt.kind == RTT_KIND_STRUCT {
            for index in 0..rtt.field_count as usize {
                let trace = trace_of_storage(*rtt.field_kinds.add(index));
                if trace != TRACE_NONE {
                    let field = data.add(*rtt.field_offsets.add(index) as usize).cast::<u64>().read();
                    visitor.visit_value(field, trace);
                }
            }
        } else {
            let trace = trace_of_storage(*rtt.field_kinds);
            if trace != TRACE_NONE {
                let length: u64 = read(cell, OBJECT_LENGTH_OFFSET);
                for index in 0..length as usize {
                    visitor.visit_value(data.cast::<u64>().add(index).read(), trace);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

pub(super) unsafe extern "C" fn object_destroy(cell: *mut c_void) {
    unsafe {
        forget_host_object(cell);
        if let Some((block, words)) = out_of_line_data(cell) {
            free(block, words);
        }
    }
}

pub(super) unsafe extern "C" fn object_external_memory_size(cell: *const c_void) -> usize {
    unsafe { out_of_line_data(cell).map_or(0, |(_, words)| words * 8) }
}

/// The number of elements of an array.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `array` must be a live array reference.
pub unsafe fn array_length(array: u64) -> u32 {
    unsafe { read::<u64>(array as *const c_void, OBJECT_LENGTH_OFFSET) as u32 }
}

/// The address and storage kind of the element at `index` of an array of numbers (whose elements are neither
/// references nor v128s).
unsafe fn numeric_array_element(array: u64, index: u32) -> (*mut u8, u8) {
    unsafe {
        let cell = array as *const c_void;
        let rtt = &*read::<*const Rtt>(cell, 0);
        assert_eq!(rtt.kind, RTT_KIND_ARRAY, "the object is an array");
        let kind = *rtt.field_kinds;
        assert!(
            matches!(kind, STORAGE_I8 | STORAGE_I16 | STORAGE_32 | STORAGE_64),
            "the array's elements are numbers"
        );
        assert!(index < array_length(array), "the index is in bounds");
        let data: *mut u8 = read(cell, OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET);
        (data.add(index as usize * rtt.size as usize), kind)
    }
}

/// The bits of the element at `index` of an array of numbers, with packed elements zero-extended.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `array` must be a live array reference.
pub unsafe fn array_element(array: u64, index: u32) -> u64 {
    unsafe {
        let (address, kind) = numeric_array_element(array, index);
        read_number(address, kind)
    }
}

/// Set the element at `index` of an array of numbers to `bits`, which packed elements wrap.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `array` must be a live array reference.
pub unsafe fn set_array_element(array: u64, index: u32, bits: u64) {
    unsafe {
        let (address, kind) = numeric_array_element(array, index);
        write_number(address, kind, bits);
    }
}

/// The bits of the number of storage `kind` (neither a reference nor a v128) at `address`, zero-extended.
unsafe fn read_number(address: *const u8, kind: u8) -> u64 {
    unsafe {
        match kind {
            STORAGE_I8 => u64::from(address.read()),
            STORAGE_I16 => u64::from(address.cast::<u16>().read()),
            STORAGE_32 => u64::from(address.cast::<u32>().read()),
            _ => address.cast::<u64>().read(),
        }
    }
}

/// Store the low bits of `bits` that a field or element of storage `kind` (not a v128) holds at `address`.
unsafe fn write_number(address: *mut u8, kind: u8, bits: u64) {
    unsafe {
        match kind {
            STORAGE_I8 => address.write(bits as u8),
            STORAGE_I16 => address.cast::<u16>().write(bits as u16),
            STORAGE_32 => address.cast::<u32>().write(bits as u32),
            _ => address.cast::<u64>().write(bits),
        }
    }
}

/// An exception: a tag and the values thrown with it, in operand stack order (the last value in the lowest slot).
pub struct Exception {
    pub tag: TagAddress,
    pub payload: &'static [u64],
}

/// Allocate an exception with the tag `tag` and the slots of `payload`, which the collector follows as `traces` says
/// (TRACE_*).
pub fn allocate_exception(heap: &Heap, tag: TagAddress, payload: &[u64], traces: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    let cell = heap.allocate_cell(CellType::Exception);
    let kinds: Vec<u8> = traces.to_vec();
    unsafe {
        write(cell, EXCEPTION_TAG_OFFSET, tag.as_ptr() as u64);
        write(cell, EXCEPTION_PAYLOAD_OFFSET, leak(payload.to_vec()) as u64);
        write(cell, EXCEPTION_LENGTH_OFFSET, payload.len() as u64);
        write(cell, EXCEPTION_KINDS_OFFSET, leak(kinds) as u64);
    }
    cell as u64
}

/// The exception an exception reference refers to.
pub fn exception(reference: u64) -> Exception {
    let cell = reference as *const c_void;
    unsafe {
        let tag: u64 = read(cell, EXCEPTION_TAG_OFFSET);
        let payload: *const u64 = read(cell, EXCEPTION_PAYLOAD_OFFSET);
        let length: u64 = read(cell, EXCEPTION_LENGTH_OFFSET);
        Exception {
            tag: TagAddress::from_ptr(tag as *const super::TagInstance),
            payload: if length == 0 {
                &[]
            } else {
                ak::slice_from_raw_parts(payload, length as usize)
            },
        }
    }
}

pub(super) unsafe extern "C" fn exception_visit_edges(cell: *mut c_void, visitor: *mut c_void) {
    let visitor = Visitor::new(visitor);
    unsafe {
        visit_host_object(cell, &visitor);
        let payload: *const u64 = read(cell, EXCEPTION_PAYLOAD_OFFSET);
        let length: u64 = read(cell, EXCEPTION_LENGTH_OFFSET);
        let kinds: *const u8 = read(cell, EXCEPTION_KINDS_OFFSET);
        let tag: *const super::TagInstance = read(cell, EXCEPTION_TAG_OFFSET);
        visitor.visit_cell(TagAddress::from_ptr(tag).cell());
        for index in 0..length as usize {
            visitor.visit_value(*payload.add(index), *kinds.add(index));
        }
    }
}

pub(super) unsafe extern "C" fn exception_destroy(cell: *mut c_void) {
    unsafe {
        forget_host_object(cell);
        let length: u64 = read(cell, EXCEPTION_LENGTH_OFFSET);
        free(read::<*const u64>(cell, EXCEPTION_PAYLOAD_OFFSET), length as usize);
        free(read::<*const u8>(cell, EXCEPTION_KINDS_OFFSET), length as usize);
    }
}

/// Allocate the cell through which the collector reaches what a store refers to.
pub(crate) fn allocate_store_root(heap: &Heap, store: *const Store) -> *mut u8 {
    let cell = heap.allocate_cell(CellType::StoreRoot);
    unsafe { write(cell, STORE_ROOT_STORE_OFFSET, store as u64) };
    cell
}

/// Detach a store's root cell from the store, which is going away, so that the collector no longer reaches it.
pub(crate) fn detach_store_root(cell: *mut u8) {
    unsafe { write(cell, STORE_ROOT_STORE_OFFSET, 0u64) };
}

pub(super) unsafe extern "C" fn store_root_destroy(cell: *mut c_void) {
    unsafe {
        let store: *mut Store = read(cell, STORE_ROOT_STORE_OFFSET);
        if let Some(store) = store.as_mut() {
            store.root_cell = std::ptr::null_mut();
        }
    }
}

pub(super) unsafe extern "C" fn store_root_visit_edges(cell: *mut c_void, visitor: *mut c_void) {
    unsafe {
        let store: *const Store = read(cell, STORE_ROOT_STORE_OFFSET);
        if let Some(store) = store.as_ref() {
            store.trace(&Visitor::new(visitor));
        }
    }
}

impl Store {
    pub fn rtt(&self, identity: u32) -> &Rtt {
        unsafe { &*self.rtt_pointers[identity as usize] }
    }

    /// Allocate a zeroed object of `data_size` bytes whose type is `rtt`, or return zero if it is too large.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `rtt` must be the runtime type of a struct or array type of the store.
    pub unsafe fn allocate_object(&mut self, rtt: *const Rtt, data_size: u64, length: u64) -> u64 {
        unsafe { allocate_object(&self.heap, rtt, data_size, length) }
    }

    /// Allocate a struct of the type `identity` with the given field values, or return zero if there is no memory
    /// for it.
    pub fn allocate_struct(&mut self, identity: u32, fields: &[Value]) -> u64 {
        let rtt: *const Rtt = self.rtt(identity);
        let size = u64::from(unsafe { (*rtt).size });
        let object = unsafe { self.allocate_object(rtt, size, 0) };
        if object == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        let data = unsafe { read::<*mut u8>(object as *const c_void, OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET) };
        for (index, value) in fields.iter().enumerate() {
            unsafe {
                let offset = *(*rtt).field_offsets.add(index);
                let kind = *(*rtt).field_kinds.add(index);
                store_field(data.add(offset as usize), kind, *value);
            }
        }
        object
    }

    /// Allocate an array of the type `identity` with `values` as its elements, or return zero if it is too large.
    pub fn allocate_array(&mut self, identity: u32, values: &[Value]) -> u64 {
        let rtt: *const Rtt = self.rtt(identity);
        let (element_size, kind) = unsafe { (u64::from((*rtt).size), *(*rtt).field_kinds) };
        let object = unsafe { self.allocate_object(rtt, values.len() as u64 * element_size, values.len() as u64) };
        if object == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        let data = unsafe { read::<*mut u8>(object as *const c_void, OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET) };
        for (index, value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
            unsafe { store_field(data.add(index * element_size as usize), kind, *value) };
        }
        object
    }

    /// Allocate an array of the type `identity` with `length` elements of `value`, or return zero if it is too large
    /// or there is no memory for it.
    pub fn allocate_filled_array(&mut self, identity: u32, value: Value, length: u32) -> u64 {
        let rtt: *const Rtt = self.rtt(identity);
        let (element_size, kind) = unsafe { (u64::from((*rtt).size), *(*rtt).field_kinds) };
        let object = unsafe { self.allocate_object(rtt, u64::from(length) * element_size, u64::from(length)) };
        if object == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        let data = unsafe { read::<*mut u8>(object as *const c_void, OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET) };
        for index in 0..length as usize {
            unsafe { store_field(data.add(index * element_size as usize), kind, value) };
        }
        object
    }

    /// Make an exception with `tag` and the values of `payload` (in operand stack order), and return its reference.
    pub fn allocate_exception(&mut self, tag: TagAddress, payload: &[u64]) -> u64 {
        let mut traces = Vec::with_capacity(payload.len());
        // The slots are in operand stack order, the last parameter first.
        for &param in self.tag(tag).ty.params.iter().rev() {
            traces.push(trace_of(param, &self.types));
            traces.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(TRACE_NONE, param.slot_count() as usize - 1));
        }
        // NB: The collector follows the payload and frees it as long as the tag's parameters say it is.
        assert_eq!(
            payload.len(),
            traces.len(),
            "an exception's payload has the slots of its tag's parameters"
        );
        allocate_exception(&self.heap, tag, payload, &traces)
    }

    /// The exception an exception reference refers to.
    pub fn exception(&self, reference: u64) -> Exception {
        exception(reference)
    }

    /// Visit what the store keeps: its runtime types, and the exception of a trap that is on its way out.
    pub fn trace(&self, visitor: &Visitor) {
        for &rtt in &self.rtt_pointers {
            visitor.visit_cell(cell_of_rtt(rtt));
        }
        if let Some(super::Trap::UncaughtException(exception)) = &self.pending_trap {
            visitor.visit_cell(*exception as *mut u8);
        }
    }
}

unsafe fn store_field(address: *mut u8, kind: u8, value: Value) {
    let (slots, _) = value.to_slots();
    unsafe {
        if kind == STORAGE_V128 {
            address.cast::<u64>().write(slots[0]);
            address.cast::<u64>().add(1).write(slots[1]);
        } else {
            write_number(address, kind, slots[0]);
        }
    }
}

/// The i31 reference of a value.
pub fn i31_reference(value: i32) -> u64 {
    (u64::from(value as u32 & 0x7fff_ffff) << 1) | 1
}

/*

 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! Where the runtime's garbage-collected objects and linear memories live: in the embedder's LibGC heap and primitive
//! storage, reached through the functions of Libraries/LibGC/CAPI.h that the embedder hands over in a `GcInterface`,
//! or, for a store without one (as in this crate's tests), in plain allocations that are never freed and mappings of
//! their own.
//!
//! Cells start with a word that belongs to the runtime and a word that holds LibGC's mark, state, and kind. GC objects
//! (see gc.rs) are cells; so are runtime types, exceptions, and the cell that roots a store. The embedder's thread
//! stack, which holds the interpreter's frames, is scanned conservatively, and LibGC recognizes pointers into a cell,
//! so references with tags in their low bits keep their cells alive there too.

use core::ffi::{c_char, c_void};
use std::sync::OnceLock;

/// Mirrors GCCellTypeInfo.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct CellTypeInfo {
    pub cell_size: u32,
    pub alignment: u32,
    pub kind: u8,
    pub visit_edges: unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *mut c_void, visitor: *mut c_void),
    pub finalize: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *mut c_void)>,
    pub destroy: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *mut c_void)>,
    pub external_memory_size: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *const c_void) -> usize>,
    pub class_name: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *const c_void, length: *mut usize) -> *const c_char>,
}

/// Mirrors GCLayout.
#[derive(Default, Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct GcLayout {
    pub cell_state_offset: u32,
    pub cell_kind_offset: u32,
    pub min_cell_size: u32,
    pub max_cell_size: u32,
    pub max_cell_alignment: u32,
    pub cell_type_info_size: u32,
    pub weak_impl_pointer_offset: u32,
    pub free_cell_next_offset: u32,
    pub free_cell_link_mask: u32,
    pub local_cursor_offset: u32,
    pub local_end_offset: u32,
    pub local_cell_size_offset: u32,
    pub heap_allocated_bytes_since_last_gc_offset: u32,
    pub heap_gc_bytes_threshold_offset: u32,
    pub heap_total_allocated_bytes_offset: u32,
    pub block_size: u32,
    pub block_foreign_type_offset: u32,
    pub heap_region_offset_mask: u64,
    pub primitive_storage_cage_offset_mask: u64,
    pub visitor_marker_offset: u32,
    pub identity_hash_state_offset: u32,
    pub identity_hash_hashed: u8,
    pub identity_hash_moved: u8,
}

/// Mirrors GCPrimitiveStorageLayout.
#[derive(Default, Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct PrimitiveStorageLayout {
    pub offset: usize,
    pub size: usize,
    pub capacity: usize,
}

/// The functions of LibGC's C interface the runtime uses, and the heap to use them with. An embedder fills it in with
/// the functions of Libraries/LibGC/CAPI.h of the same names.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct GcInterface {
    pub heap: *mut c_void,
    pub gc_get_layout: unsafe extern "C" fn(layout: *mut GcLayout, layout_size: usize),
    pub gc_allocator_create: unsafe extern "C" fn(
        type_info: *const CellTypeInfo,
        name: *const c_char,
        name_length: usize,
        foreign_type: *const c_void,
    ) -> *mut c_void,
    pub gc_allocator_set_traced_on_owner_thread_only: unsafe extern "C" fn(allocator: *mut c_void),
    pub gc_heap_allocate_cell: unsafe extern "C" fn(heap: *mut c_void, allocator: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void,
    pub gc_heap_defer_gc: unsafe extern "C" fn(heap: *mut c_void),
    pub gc_heap_undefer_gc: unsafe extern "C" fn(heap: *mut c_void),
    pub gc_heap_collect_garbage: unsafe extern "C" fn(heap: *mut c_void, collection_type: i32, print_report: bool),
    pub gc_heap_did_allocate_external_memory: unsafe extern "C" fn(heap: *mut c_void, size: usize),
    pub gc_root_create: unsafe extern "C" fn(cell: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void,
    pub gc_root_destroy: unsafe extern "C" fn(root: *mut c_void),
    pub gc_visitor_visit_cell: unsafe extern "C" fn(visitor: *mut c_void, cell: *mut c_void),
    pub gc_primitive_storage_reserve: unsafe extern "C" fn(
        size: usize,
        capacity: usize,
        zero_fill: bool,
        guard_size: usize,
        out_handle: *mut u64,
        out_layout: *mut PrimitiveStorageLayout,
    ) -> bool,
    pub gc_primitive_storage_resize: unsafe extern "C" fn(
        handle: u64,
        new_size: usize,
        zero_fill: bool,
        out_layout: *mut PrimitiveStorageLayout,
    ) -> bool,
    pub gc_primitive_storage_free: unsafe extern "C" fn(handle: u64),
    pub gc_primitive_storage_data: unsafe extern "C" fn(handle: u64) -> *mut u8,
}

/// The size of the words every cell starts with: one of the runtime's and one of LibGC's.
pub const CELL_HEADER_SIZE: usize = 16;

const CELL_STATE_LIVE: u8 = 0;
const CELL_KIND_OTHER: u8 = 0;

/// The byte after LibGC's in a cell, which holds the runtime's flags for the cell.
const CELL_FLAGS_OFFSET: usize = 11;
/// The cell keeps an object of the embedder's alive (see set_host_object()).
const CELL_FLAG_HOST_OBJECT: u8 = 1;

thread_local! {
    /// The object of the embedder's each cell of this thread's heap keeps alive, by cell.
    static HOST_OBJECTS: core::cell::RefCell<std::collections::HashMap<usize, *mut c_void>> = Default::default();
}

/// Have `cell` keep the embedder's cell `object` alive for as long as it lives itself, as an edge the collector follows
/// from it. An embedder's object that stands for `cell` and refers to it then stays the same object while `cell` lives,
/// and goes away with it.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be a live cell of the runtime, and `object` a cell of the same LibGC heap.
pub unsafe fn set_host_object(cell: *mut u8, object: *mut c_void) {
    HOST_OBJECTS.with_borrow_mut(|objects| objects.insert(cell.addr(), object));
    unsafe { *cell.add(CELL_FLAGS_OFFSET) |= CELL_FLAG_HOST_OBJECT };
}

/// The object `cell` keeps alive, or null if it keeps none.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be a live cell of the runtime.
pub unsafe fn host_object(cell: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void {
    if unsafe { *cell.cast::<u8>().add(CELL_FLAGS_OFFSET) } & CELL_FLAG_HOST_OBJECT == 0 {
        return core::ptr::null_mut();
    }
    HOST_OBJECTS.with_borrow(|objects| objects.get(&cell.addr()).copied().unwrap_or(core::ptr::null_mut()))
}

/// Visit the object `cell` keeps alive, if it keeps one.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be a live cell of the runtime.
pub unsafe fn visit_host_object(cell: *mut c_void, visitor: &Visitor) {
    let object = unsafe { host_object(cell) };
    if !object.is_null() {
        visitor.visit_cell(object.cast());
    }
}

/// Forget the object `cell` keeps alive, as `cell` is going away.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be a cell of the runtime.
pub unsafe fn forget_host_object(cell: *mut c_void) {
    let flags = unsafe { &mut *cell.cast::<u8>().add(CELL_FLAGS_OFFSET) };
    if *flags & CELL_FLAG_HOST_OBJECT == 0 {
        return;
    }
    *flags &= !CELL_FLAG_HOST_OBJECT;
    // NB: A thread's cells are destroyed on the thread, unless it is exiting, when its table is gone already.
    let _ = HOST_OBJECTS.try_with(|objects| objects.borrow_mut().remove(&cell.addr()));
}

/// The cell types of the runtime, in the order of their allocators.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum CellType {
    /// A GC object whose inline data has the size of the given size class.
    Object(usize),
    Rtt,
    Exception,
    StoreRoot,
    /// A function, table, memory, global, tag, or instance (see entity.rs), by its ENTITY_* kind.
    Entity(usize),
}

pub use crate::abi::OBJECT_CELL_SIZE_CLASSES;

/// The size class of object cells of at least `size` bytes, which is at most the largest class.
pub fn object_size_class(size: usize) -> usize {
    OBJECT_CELL_SIZE_CLASSES
        .iter()
        .position(|&class| class >= size)
        .expect("object cells are at most the largest class")
}

/// The allocators of the runtime's cell types, which LibGC requires to outlive every heap, so there is one set of
/// them for the process, made with the first interface.
struct Allocators {
    objects: Vec<*mut c_void>,
    rtt: *mut c_void,
    exception: *mut c_void,
    store_root: *mut c_void,
    entities: Vec<*mut c_void>,
}

// The allocators are only handles: LibGC never changes them, and keeps what it allocates with in each heap.
unsafe impl Send for Allocators {}
unsafe impl Sync for Allocators {}

static ALLOCATORS: OnceLock<Allocators> = OnceLock::new();

/// The functions of the first interface, which every heap's cells are visited with: they are the same functions of
/// LibGC whichever heap a store uses.
struct Functions(GcInterface);

// Only the function pointers are used, never the heap.
unsafe impl Send for Functions {}
unsafe impl Sync for Functions {}

static FUNCTIONS: OnceLock<Functions> = OnceLock::new();

unsafe extern "C" fn class_name(_: *const c_void, length: *mut usize) -> *const c_char {
    const NAME: &str = "WebAssembly cell";
    unsafe { length.write(NAME.len()) };
    NAME.as_ptr().cast()
}

/// What LibGC knows each cell type by: its size and name, and the functions it visits and destroys cells with.
fn type_info(cell_type: CellType) -> (&'static CellTypeInfo, &'static str) {
    use super::{entity, gc};
    type VisitEdges = unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void);
    type Destroy = unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void);
    type ExternalMemorySize = unsafe extern "C" fn(*const c_void) -> usize;
    let (visit_edges, destroy, external_memory_size, name): (VisitEdges, Destroy, Option<ExternalMemorySize>, _) =
        match cell_type {
            CellType::Object(_) => (
                gc::object_visit_edges,
                gc::object_destroy,
                Some(gc::object_external_memory_size),
                "WebAssembly object",
            ),
            CellType::Rtt => (gc::rtt_visit_edges, gc::rtt_destroy, None, "WebAssembly runtime type"),
            CellType::Exception => (
                gc::exception_visit_edges,
                gc::exception_destroy,
                None,
                "WebAssembly exception",
            ),
            CellType::StoreRoot => (
                gc::store_root_visit_edges,
                gc::store_root_destroy,
                None,
                "WebAssembly store",
            ),
            CellType::Entity(kind) => (
                entity::entity_visit_edges,
                entity::entity_destroy,
                None,
                entity::ENTITY_NAMES[kind],
            ),
        };
    let info = Box::leak(Box::new(CellTypeInfo {
        cell_size: cell_size(cell_type) as u32,
        // NB: Objects come in sizes 8 bytes apart, and their fields are aligned to at most 8 bytes.
        alignment: if matches!(cell_type, CellType::Object(_)) {
            8
        } else {
            16
        },
        kind: CELL_KIND_OTHER,
        visit_edges,
        finalize: None,
        destroy: Some(destroy),
        external_memory_size,
        class_name: Some(class_name),
    }));
    (info, name)
}

impl Allocators {
    fn new(interface: &GcInterface) -> Self {
        let create = |cell_type: CellType| {
            let (info, name) = type_info(cell_type);
            let allocator =
                unsafe { (interface.gc_allocator_create)(info, name.as_ptr().cast(), name.len(), core::ptr::null()) };
            // NB: Tracing reaches the host objects of the thread that owns the heap (see HOST_OBJECTS), and the
            //     embedder's visit callbacks, so the cells of these allocators are only traced on that thread.
            unsafe { (interface.gc_allocator_set_traced_on_owner_thread_only)(allocator) };
            allocator
        };
        Self {
            objects: (0..OBJECT_CELL_SIZE_CLASSES.len())
                .map(|class| create(CellType::Object(class)))
                .collect(),
            rtt: create(CellType::Rtt),
            exception: create(CellType::Exception),
            store_root: create(CellType::StoreRoot),
            entities: (0..super::entity::ENTITY_KIND_COUNT)
                .map(|kind| create(CellType::Entity(kind)))
                .collect(),
        }
    }

    fn of(&self, cell_type: CellType) -> *mut c_void {
        match cell_type {
            CellType::Object(class) => self.objects[class],
            CellType::Rtt => self.rtt,
            CellType::Exception => self.exception,
            CellType::StoreRoot => self.store_root,
            CellType::Entity(kind) => self.entities[kind],
        }
    }
}

/// The size of a cell of a type.
pub fn cell_size(cell_type: CellType) -> usize {
    match cell_type {
        CellType::Object(class) => OBJECT_CELL_SIZE_CLASSES[class],
        CellType::Rtt => CELL_HEADER_SIZE + size_of::<crate::abi::Rtt>().next_multiple_of(16),
        CellType::Exception => super::gc::EXCEPTION_CELL_SIZE,
        CellType::StoreRoot => 32,
        CellType::Entity(kind) => super::entity::entity_cell_size(kind),
    }
}

/// A LibGC heap.
pub struct GcHeap {
    pub interface: GcInterface,
    layout: GcLayout,
    allocators: &'static Allocators,
    /// How many defer_gc() calls have no matching undefer_gc() yet.
    deferrals: core::cell::Cell<u32>,
}

pub enum Heap {
    /// Cells are plain allocations, which the store's entities are freed with, and memories are mappings of their own.
    Standalone(core::cell::RefCell<Vec<*mut u8>>),
    Gc(Box<GcHeap>),
}

impl Heap {
    pub fn new(interface: Option<GcInterface>) -> Self {
        let Some(interface) = interface else {
            return Self::Standalone(core::cell::RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
        };
        let mut layout = GcLayout::default();
        unsafe { (interface.gc_get_layout)(&raw mut layout, size_of::<GcLayout>()) };
        assert!(
            layout.cell_state_offset as usize >= 8 && (layout.cell_kind_offset as usize) < CELL_HEADER_SIZE,
            "LibGC keeps its cell header in the second word"
        );
        assert!(
            [layout.cell_state_offset, layout.cell_kind_offset]
                .iter()
                .all(|&offset| (offset as usize) < CELL_FLAGS_OFFSET),
            "the runtime's flags follow LibGC's cell header"
        );
        let allocators = ALLOCATORS.get_or_init(|| Allocators::new(&interface));
        FUNCTIONS.get_or_init(|| Functions(interface));
        Self::Gc(Box::new(GcHeap {
            interface,
            layout,
            allocators,
            deferrals: core::cell::Cell::new(0),
        }))
    }

    pub fn gc(&self) -> Option<&GcHeap> {
        match self {
            Self::Standalone(_) => None,
            Self::Gc(heap) => Some(heap),
        }
    }

    /// Allocate a zero-filled cell. Garbage may be collected first, so every reference the caller holds outside of
    /// the stack and the cells the store reaches must be in a deferred section.
    pub fn allocate_cell(&self, cell_type: CellType) -> *mut u8 {
        let size = cell_size(cell_type);
        match self {
            Self::Standalone(entities) => {
                // NB: Standalone stores never free their cells, but drop their entities when they go away.
                let words = vec![0u128; size.div_ceil(16)].into_boxed_slice();
                let cell: *mut u8 = Box::leak(words).as_mut_ptr().cast();
                if matches!(cell_type, CellType::Entity(_)) {
                    entities.borrow_mut().push(cell);
                }
                cell
            }
            Self::Gc(heap) => unsafe {
                let cell: *mut u8 =
                    (heap.interface.gc_heap_allocate_cell)(heap.interface.heap, heap.allocators.of(cell_type)).cast();
                assert!(!cell.is_null(), "LibGC allocates the cell");
                core::ptr::write_bytes(cell, 0, size);
                *cell.add(heap.layout.cell_state_offset as usize) = CELL_STATE_LIVE;
                *cell.add(heap.layout.cell_kind_offset as usize) = CELL_KIND_OTHER;
                cell
            },
        }
    }

    /// Drop the entities of a standalone heap, whose store is going away.
    pub(crate) fn drop_standalone_entities(&self) {
        if let Self::Standalone(entities) = self {
            for cell in entities.take() {
                unsafe { super::entity::destroy_entity(cell) };
            }
        }
    }

    /// Count memory a cell owns outside of the heap towards the next collection.
    pub fn did_allocate_external_memory(&self, size: usize) {
        if let Self::Gc(heap) = self {
            unsafe { (heap.interface.gc_heap_did_allocate_external_memory)(heap.interface.heap, size) };
        }
    }

    /// Stop collecting garbage until the matching undefer_gc(), for code that keeps references where the collector
    /// does not look.
    pub fn defer_gc(&self) {
        if let Self::Gc(heap) = self {
            heap.deferrals.set(heap.deferrals.get() + 1);
            unsafe { (heap.interface.gc_heap_defer_gc)(heap.interface.heap) };
        }
    }

    pub fn undefer_gc(&self) {
        if let Self::Gc(heap) = self {
            heap.deferrals.set(heap.deferrals.get() - 1);
            unsafe { (heap.interface.gc_heap_undefer_gc)(heap.interface.heap) };
        }
    }

    /// Whether this runtime deferred garbage collection, with defer_gc().
    pub fn is_gc_deferred(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Gc(heap) if heap.deferrals.get() != 0)
    }
}

impl GcHeap {
    /// Keep the cell alive until the root is destroyed.
    pub(crate) fn root(&self, cell: *mut u8) -> *mut c_void {
        unsafe { (self.interface.gc_root_create)(cell.cast()) }
    }

    pub(crate) fn unroot(&self, root: *mut c_void) {
        unsafe { (self.interface.gc_root_destroy)(root) };
    }
}

/// How the collector follows a value: not at all, as a reference in the any, extern, or exn hierarchy, or as a
/// function reference, which points into its function's cell.
pub const TRACE_NONE: u8 = 0;
pub const TRACE_REFERENCE: u8 = 1;
pub const TRACE_FUNCTION: u8 = 2;

/// A visitor LibGC passes to the cells' visit_edges, with the functions to visit cells with.
pub struct Visitor {
    raw: *mut c_void,
    interface: *const GcInterface,
}

impl Visitor {
    /// The visitor LibGC passed to a cell's visit_edges. Only cells of a LibGC heap are visited, so there is an
    /// interface by then.
    pub fn new(raw: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        let functions = FUNCTIONS.get().expect("cells are only visited once a heap exists");
        Self {
            raw,
            interface: &raw const functions.0,
        }
    }

    /// The LibGC visitor itself, for an embedder to visit its cells with.
    pub fn raw(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.raw
    }

    pub(crate) fn visit_cell(&self, cell: *mut u8) {
        unsafe { ((*self.interface).gc_visitor_visit_cell)(self.raw, cell.cast()) };
    }

    /// Visit a value of a type whose TRACE_* kind is `trace`.
    pub fn visit_value(&self, value: u64, trace: u8) {
        match trace {
            TRACE_REFERENCE => self.visit_reference(value),
            TRACE_FUNCTION if value != 0 => self.visit_cell((value as *mut u8).wrapping_sub(CELL_HEADER_SIZE)),
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    /// Visit a reference in the any, extern, or exn hierarchy, whose kind is in its low bits (see gc.rs).
    pub fn visit_reference(&self, reference: u64) {
        if reference == 0 || reference & 1 != 0 {
            return;
        }
        // NB: An embedder's host value is the address of one of its cells, with bit 1 set.
        self.visit_cell((reference & !3) as *mut u8);
    }
}

//! The runtime services the interpreter calls for what needs the runtime: growing memories and tables, and calling
//! host functions. Each takes the execution context, whose `arguments` hold the operands.

use super::memory::SharedMemory;
use super::{FunctionAddress, FunctionInstance, FunctionKind, MemoryAddress, Store, TableAddress, Trap};
use crate::abi::{
    ExecutionContext, FRAME_FUNCTION, FRAME_HEADER_SIZE, FRAME_INSTANCE, FRAME_RETURN_IP, FRAME_SAVED_FP, MemoryData,
    TableData,
};
use crate::validator::{CatchKind, NO_EXCEPTION_LOCAL, NOT_DELEGATED};
use ak::waiter_list::{self, AgentWaiter, AtomicWaitResult, WaitWord};

export_runtime_functions! {
    wasm_runtime_memory_grow => memory_grow,
    wasm_runtime_table_grow => table_grow,
    wasm_runtime_call_host => call_host,
    wasm_runtime_allocate => allocate,
    wasm_runtime_throw => throw,
    wasm_runtime_wait => wait,
    wasm_runtime_notify => notify,
}

unsafe fn store_of(context: *mut ExecutionContext) -> &'static mut Store {
    unsafe { &mut *(*context).store.cast::<Store>() }
}

/// Grow the memory of `arguments[0]` (a `MemoryData`) by `arguments[1]` pages. Returns the previous size in pages, or
/// u64::MAX if the memory cannot grow.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only the interpreter calls this, with the context of the store it runs in.
unsafe fn memory_grow(context: *mut ExecutionContext) -> u64 {
    unsafe {
        let data = (*context).arguments[0] as *const MemoryData;
        let delta = (*context).arguments[1];
        if (*data).shared != 0 {
            // NB: Nothing is told that the memory grew: an agent finds the size where it finds the bytes, and the
            //     embedder gives each of them a buffer of the new size once it is asked for one.
            return SharedMemory::from_data(data).grow(delta).unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
        }
        let store = store_of(context);
        // The data of a memory that is not shared is at the memory's handle, see MemoryInstance::data().
        let memory = MemoryAddress::from_ptr(data.cast());
        let Some(previous) = store.memory_mut(memory).grow(delta) else {
            return u64::MAX;
        };
        if let Some(callback) = store.memory_grow_callback.clone() {
            callback(memory);
        }
        previous
    }
}

/// Grow the table of `arguments[0]` (a `TableData`) by `arguments[1]` elements initialized to `arguments[2]`. Returns
/// the previous size, or u64::MAX if the table cannot grow.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only the interpreter calls this, with the context of the store it runs in.
unsafe fn table_grow(context: *mut ExecutionContext) -> u64 {
    unsafe {
        let data = (*context).arguments[0] as *const TableData;
        let delta = (*context).arguments[1];
        let initial = (*context).arguments[2];
        let store = store_of(context);
        // The data is at the table's handle.
        store
            .table_mut(TableAddress::from_ptr(data.cast()))
            .grow(delta, initial)
            .unwrap_or(u64::MAX)
    }
}

/// Call the host function whose header is `arguments[0]` with the arguments on the operand stack at `arguments[1]`,
/// replacing them with its results. `arguments[2]` is the address the call returns to and `arguments[3]` the caller's
/// frame, which an exception the host function throws unwinds from. Returns the new top of the operand stack, 1 if
/// the call threw an exception that a handler caught (see `wasm_runtime_throw`), or 0 if it trapped.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only the interpreter calls this, with the context of the store it runs in.
unsafe fn call_host(context: *mut ExecutionContext) -> u64 {
    unsafe {
        let function = &*((*context).arguments[0] as *const FunctionInstance);
        let top = (*context).arguments[1] as *mut u64;
        let return_ip = (*context).arguments[2];
        let frame = (*context).arguments[3];
        let store = store_of(context);
        let address = FunctionAddress::from_ptr(function);
        // The results replace the arguments, at the bottom of the arguments' slots.
        let return_top = top
            .add(function.header.param_slots as usize)
            .sub(function.header.result_slots as usize);
        match store.call_host_slots(address, top, return_top) {
            Ok(()) => return_top as u64,
            Err(Trap::UncaughtException(exception)) => {
                // The exception continues in the caller, as if the call instruction had thrown it.
                if unwind(context, store, exception, frame, return_ip - 1) {
                    return 1;
                }
                store.pending_trap = Some(Trap::UncaughtException(exception));
                0
            }
            Err(trap) => {
                store.pending_trap = Some(trap);
                0
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Allocate a GC object whose runtime type is `arguments[0]`, with `arguments[1]` bytes of zeroed data and, for an
/// array, `arguments[2]` elements. Returns zero if it is too large.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only the interpreter calls this, with the context of the store it runs in.
unsafe fn allocate(context: *mut ExecutionContext) -> u64 {
    unsafe {
        let store = store_of(context);
        let rtt = (*context).arguments[0] as *const crate::abi::Rtt;
        let size = (*context).arguments[1];
        let length = (*context).arguments[2];
        let object = store.allocate_object(rtt, size, length);
        if object == 0 {
            store.pending_trap = Some(Trap::Host("out of memory".to_string()));
        }
        object
    }
}

/// Throw an exception: a new one with the tag whose identity is `arguments[0]` and the values on the operand stack
/// at `arguments[1]`, or the existing one `arguments[4]` refers to if that is not zero. `arguments[2]` is the
/// throwing instruction and `arguments[3]` its frame. Returns 1 if a handler caught the exception, with the frame,
/// instruction pointer, side-table pointer, and operand stack top to continue with in `arguments[0..4]`, or 0 if it
/// left the interpreter uncaught.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only the interpreter calls this, with the context of the store it runs in.
unsafe fn throw(context: *mut ExecutionContext) -> u64 {
    unsafe {
        let store = store_of(context);
        let pc = (*context).arguments[2];
        let frame = (*context).arguments[3];
        let mut exception = (*context).arguments[4];
        if exception == 0 {
            let tag = store.tag_from_identity((*context).arguments[0]);
            let slot_count: u32 = store.tag(tag).ty.params.iter().map(|param| param.slot_count()).sum();
            let top = (*context).arguments[1] as *const u64;
            let payload = ak::slice_from_raw_parts(top, slot_count as usize).to_vec();
            exception = store.allocate_exception(tag, &payload);
        }
        if unwind(context, store, exception, frame, pc) {
            return 1;
        }
        store.pending_trap = Some(Trap::UncaughtException(exception));
        0
    }
}

/// Find the handler of `exception`, thrown by the instruction at `pc` in the frame `frame`, in that frame or the ones
/// it was called from, up to where the runtime entered the interpreter. If there is one, push what the handler
/// receives and put where it continues into the context's arguments.
pub(crate) unsafe fn unwind(
    context: *mut ExecutionContext,
    store: &Store,
    exception: u64,
    mut frame: u64,
    mut pc: u64,
) -> bool {
    let read = |address: u64| unsafe { *(address as *const u64) };
    let thrown_tag = store.exception(exception).tag;
    loop {
        // The frame the runtime enters the interpreter with has no instance.
        if read(frame.wrapping_add_signed(FRAME_INSTANCE as i64)) == 0 {
            return false;
        }
        let function = unsafe { &*(read(frame.wrapping_add_signed(FRAME_FUNCTION as i64)) as *const FunctionInstance) };
        if let FunctionKind::Wasm {
            module,
            index,
            instance,
        } = &function.kind
        {
            let info = &module.function_infos[(*index - module.imported_function_count) as usize];
            let offset = pc.wrapping_sub(module.bytes.as_ptr() as u64);
            // Regions are in instruction order, inner ones after the regions they are in. A legacy `delegate` leaves
            // out the regions that start after its bound.
            let mut bound = u32::MAX;
            for region in info.try_regions.iter().rev() {
                if offset < u64::from(region.start) || offset >= u64::from(region.end) || region.start > bound {
                    continue;
                }
                if region.delegate_bound != NOT_DELEGATED {
                    bound = region.delegate_bound;
                    continue;
                }
                let clauses = &info.catch_clauses
                    [region.first_clause as usize..(region.first_clause + region.clause_count) as usize];
                for clause in clauses {
                    let catches = match clause.kind {
                        CatchKind::Catch | CatchKind::CatchRef => {
                            store.instance(*instance).tags[clause.tag as usize] == thrown_tag
                        }
                        CatchKind::CatchAll | CatchKind::CatchAllRef => true,
                    };
                    if !catches {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let payload: &[u64] = match clause.kind {
                        CatchKind::Catch | CatchKind::CatchRef => store.exception(exception).payload,
                        CatchKind::CatchAll | CatchKind::CatchAllRef => &[],
                    };
                    let pushes_reference = matches!(clause.kind, CatchKind::CatchRef | CatchKind::CatchAllRef);
                    let pushed = payload.len() as u64 + u64::from(pushes_reference);
                    let empty_stack = frame - FRAME_HEADER_SIZE as u64;
                    let top = empty_stack - (u64::from(clause.height) + pushed) * 8;
                    let mut slot = top as *mut u64;
                    unsafe {
                        if clause.exception_local != NO_EXCEPTION_LOCAL {
                            *((frame + u64::from(clause.exception_local) * 8) as *mut u64) = exception;
                        }
                        if pushes_reference {
                            *slot = exception;
                            slot = slot.add(1);
                        }
                        for &value in payload {
                            *slot = value;
                            slot = slot.add(1);
                        }
                        (*context).arguments[0] = frame;
                        (*context).arguments[1] = module.bytes.as_ptr() as u64 + u64::from(clause.target_pc);
                        (*context).arguments[2] = info.side_table.as_ptr() as u64 + u64::from(clause.target_stp) * 16;
                        (*context).arguments[3] = top;
                    }
                    return true;
                }
            }
        }
        // Continue in the caller, inside the call instruction this frame returns past.
        pc = read(frame.wrapping_add_signed(FRAME_RETURN_IP as i64)) - 1;
        frame = read(frame.wrapping_add_signed(FRAME_SAVED_FP as i64));
    }
}

/// Wait on the shared memory location at address `arguments[0]` while it holds `arguments[1]` (compared at
/// `arguments[3]` bytes), for at most `arguments[2]` nanoseconds if that is not negative. Returns 0 when woken, 1 if
/// the location held another value, and 2 when the time ran out, or WAIT_CANNOT_BLOCK with the trap in the store if
/// the store's agent cannot block.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only the interpreter calls this, with an address it checked.
unsafe fn wait(context: *mut ExecutionContext) -> u64 {
    let (address, expected, timeout, size) = unsafe {
        (
            (*context).arguments[0],
            (*context).arguments[1],
            (*context).arguments[2] as i64,
            (*context).arguments[3],
        )
    };
    let store = unsafe { store_of(context) };
    if !store.can_block {
        store.pending_trap = Some(Trap::Host(
            "memory.atomic.wait in an agent that cannot block".to_string(),
        ));
        return crate::abi::WAIT_CANNOT_BLOCK;
    }
    // NB: The waits and wakes are those of Atomics.wait and Atomics.notify, in the waiter lists of the process, per
    //     address: JavaScript and WebAssembly wake each other, as the memory model's single WaiterList per location
    //     requires.
    let word = unsafe {
        if size == 4 {
            WaitWord::Word32(&*(address as *const std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32))
        } else {
            WaitWord::Word64(&*(address as *const std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64))
        }
    };
    let timeout = (timeout >= 0).then(|| std::time::Duration::from_nanos(timeout as u64));
    // NB: A store without an agent has nothing to interrupt it, as a test's has not.
    let waiter = store.agent_waiter.clone().unwrap_or_else(AgentWaiter::new);
    match waiter_list::atomic_wait(word, expected, timeout, &waiter) {
        AtomicWaitResult::Woken => 0,
        AtomicWaitResult::NotEqual => 1,
        AtomicWaitResult::TimedOut => 2,
        AtomicWaitResult::Interrupted => {
            store.pending_trap = Some(Trap::StackExhausted);
            crate::abi::WAIT_CANNOT_BLOCK
        }
    }
}

/// Wake at most `arguments[1]` of the threads waiting on the shared memory location at address `arguments[0]`, and
/// return how many it woke.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only the interpreter calls this.
unsafe fn notify(context: *mut ExecutionContext) -> u64 {
    let (address, count) = unsafe { ((*context).arguments[0], (*context).arguments[1]) };
    let word = unsafe { &*(address as *const std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32) };
    waiter_list::atomic_notify(word, usize::try_from(count).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)) as u64
}

//! Entering the interpreter, and turning faulting memory accesses inside it into traps.

use crate::abi::{EntryRecord, OPCODE_CALL_ENTRY, OPCODE_CALL_PENDING, OPCODE_ENTER, OPCODE_EXIT};

/// The code the runtime enters the interpreter at (see `OPCODE_ENTER`).
static ENTRY_CODE: [u8; 3] = [OPCODE_ENTER, OPCODE_CALL_ENTRY, OPCODE_EXIT];

/// The code the interpreter continues at to call a pending tail call (see `OPCODE_CALL_PENDING`).
static CALL_PENDING_CODE: [u8; 1] = [OPCODE_CALL_PENDING];

pub fn call_pending_code() -> u64 {
    CALL_PENDING_CODE.as_ptr() as u64
}

// The interpreter uses the System V calling convention on every x86-64 target, Windows included.
#[cfg(all(wasm_interpreter, not(all(target_arch = "x86_64", windows))))]
unsafe extern "C" {
    fn wasm_interpreter(ip: *const u8, argument: u64);
}

#[cfg(all(wasm_interpreter, target_arch = "x86_64", windows))]
unsafe extern "sysv64" {
    fn wasm_interpreter(ip: *const u8, argument: u64);
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    static wasm_interpreter_end: u8;
    static wasm_interpreter_dispatch_table: [usize; 256];
}

/// Run the function of `record` in the interpreter.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The record must describe a function of a live instance, its arguments, and room for its results.
pub unsafe fn enter(record: &mut EntryRecord) {
    #[cfg(wasm_interpreter)]
    unsafe {
        wasm_interpreter(ENTRY_CODE.as_ptr(), (record as *mut EntryRecord) as u64);
    }
    #[cfg(not(wasm_interpreter))]
    {
        let _ = &ENTRY_CODE;
        record.trap = crate::abi::TRAP_RUNTIME;
    }
}

#[cfg(wasm_interpreter)]
fn interpreter_code_range() -> (usize, usize) {
    (
        wasm_interpreter as *const () as usize,
        &raw const wasm_interpreter_end as usize,
    )
}

/// The handler of a primary opcode.
#[cfg(wasm_interpreter)]
pub fn dispatch_table_entry(opcode: u8) -> usize {
    unsafe { wasm_interpreter_dispatch_table[usize::from(opcode)] }
}

#[cfg(wasm_interpreter)]
fn memory_fault_handler() -> usize {
    dispatch_table_entry(crate::abi::OPCODE_MEMORY_FAULT)
}

/// The CPU features the interpreter's code uses: SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2 and POPCNT, and LZCNT and BMI1 where the build
/// targets them (see build.rs), on x86-64, and NEON, LSE and RDM on AArch64. A CPU without them would not fault but compute wrong results (lzcnt
/// runs as bsr on older CPUs), so the engine refuses to start instead.
pub fn check_cpu_features() {
    let missing = missing_interpreter_cpu_features();
    assert!(
        missing.is_empty(),
        "The WebAssembly engine needs CPU features this machine lacks: {}",
        missing.join(", ")
    );
}

/// Whether the CPU has the JIT's baseline features. On x86-64, optional AVX, BMI and LZCNT instructions are selected
/// at runtime; SSE4.2 and POPCNT suffice for both tiers. AArch64 uses the interpreter's features.
pub fn cpu_supports_jit() -> bool {
    missing_jit_cpu_features().is_empty()
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
use std::arch::is_x86_feature_detected as is_cpu_feature_detected;

#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
use std::arch::is_aarch64_feature_detected as is_cpu_feature_detected;

#[cfg(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
macro_rules! missing_cpu_features {
    ($($feature:tt),+) => {{
        let mut missing = Vec::new();
        $(if !is_cpu_feature_detected!($feature) {
            missing.push($feature);
        })+
        missing
    }};
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
fn missing_interpreter_cpu_features() -> Vec<&'static str> {
    let mut missing = missing_cpu_features!("ssse3", "sse4.1", "sse4.2", "popcnt");
    if cfg!(target_feature = "lzcnt") {
        missing.extend(missing_cpu_features!("lzcnt"));
    }
    if cfg!(target_feature = "bmi1") {
        missing.extend(missing_cpu_features!("bmi1"));
    }
    missing
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
fn missing_jit_cpu_features() -> Vec<&'static str> {
    missing_cpu_features!("ssse3", "sse4.1", "sse4.2", "popcnt")
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
fn missing_interpreter_cpu_features() -> Vec<&'static str> {
    missing_cpu_features!("neon", "lse", "rdm")
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
fn missing_jit_cpu_features() -> Vec<&'static str> {
    missing_interpreter_cpu_features()
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]
fn missing_interpreter_cpu_features() -> Vec<&'static str> {
    Vec::new()
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]
fn missing_jit_cpu_features() -> Vec<&'static str> {
    Vec::new()
}

/// The lowest address the interpreter's frames may use on the current thread, leaving `reserve` bytes below it.
pub fn stack_limit(reserve: usize) -> u64 {
    // OPTIMIZATION: Finding where a thread's stack ends can mean reading /proc/self/maps (glibc does for the main
    //               thread), which took over half a millisecond per call from JavaScript into WebAssembly, so each
    //               thread finds it once.
    thread_local! {
        static LOWEST: std::cell::Cell<usize> = const { std::cell::Cell::new(0) };
    }
    let lowest = LOWEST.with(|lowest| {
        if lowest.get() == 0
            && let Some(address) = thread_stack_lowest_address()
        {
            lowest.set(address);
        }
        lowest.get()
    });
    if lowest != 0 {
        return (lowest + reserve) as u64;
    }
    // NB: Without the stack's bounds, the limit is a mebibyte below wherever this is called from, which depends on the
    //     caller, so it is not cached.
    let marker = 0u8;
    let current = &raw const marker as usize;
    (current.saturating_sub(1024 * 1024) + reserve) as u64
}

#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
fn thread_stack_lowest_address() -> Option<usize> {
    unsafe {
        let mut attributes: libc::pthread_attr_t = std::mem::zeroed();
        if libc::pthread_getattr_np(libc::pthread_self(), &raw mut attributes) != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let mut address = std::ptr::null_mut();
        let mut size = 0;
        let result = libc::pthread_attr_getstack(&raw const attributes, &raw mut address, &raw mut size);
        libc::pthread_attr_destroy(&raw mut attributes);
        (result == 0).then_some(address as usize)
    }
}

#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
#[allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps)] // The other platforms' versions can fail.
fn thread_stack_lowest_address() -> Option<usize> {
    unsafe {
        let thread = libc::pthread_self();
        let top = libc::pthread_get_stackaddr_np(thread) as usize;
        Some(top - libc::pthread_get_stacksize_np(thread))
    }
}

#[cfg(windows)]
#[allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps)] // The other platforms' versions can fail.
fn thread_stack_lowest_address() -> Option<usize> {
    unsafe extern "system" {
        fn GetCurrentThreadStackLimits(low: *mut usize, high: *mut usize);
    }
    let (mut low, mut high) = (0, 0);
    unsafe { GetCurrentThreadStackLimits(&raw mut low, &raw mut high) };
    Some(low)
}

#[cfg(not(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "macos", windows)))]
fn thread_stack_lowest_address() -> Option<usize> {
    None
}

#[cfg(all(wasm_interpreter, unix))]
mod fault {
    use super::{interpreter_code_range, memory_fault_handler};
    use crate::runtime::memory::is_in_any_reservation;
    use std::sync::Once;

    static INSTALL: Once = Once::new();
    static mut PREVIOUS_SIGSEGV: libc::sigaction = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    static mut PREVIOUS_SIGBUS: libc::sigaction = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };

    #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "x86_64"))]
    unsafe fn instruction_pointer(context: *mut libc::c_void) -> *mut usize {
        unsafe {
            let context = context.cast::<libc::ucontext_t>();
            (&raw mut (*context).uc_mcontext.gregs[libc::REG_RIP as usize]).cast()
        }
    }

    #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
    unsafe fn instruction_pointer(context: *mut libc::c_void) -> *mut usize {
        unsafe {
            let context = context.cast::<libc::ucontext_t>();
            (&raw mut (*context).uc_mcontext.pc).cast()
        }
    }

    #[cfg(all(target_os = "macos", target_arch = "x86_64"))]
    unsafe fn instruction_pointer(context: *mut libc::c_void) -> *mut usize {
        unsafe {
            let context = context.cast::<libc::ucontext_t>();
            (&raw mut (*(*context).uc_mcontext).__ss.__rip).cast()
        }
    }

    #[cfg(all(target_os = "macos", target_arch = "aarch64"))]
    unsafe fn instruction_pointer(context: *mut libc::c_void) -> *mut usize {
        unsafe {
            let context = context.cast::<libc::ucontext_t>();
            (&raw mut (*(*context).uc_mcontext).__ss.__pc).cast()
        }
    }

    unsafe fn forward(signal: i32, info: *mut libc::siginfo_t, context: *mut libc::c_void) {
        unsafe {
            let previous = if signal == libc::SIGSEGV {
                &raw const PREVIOUS_SIGSEGV
            } else {
                &raw const PREVIOUS_SIGBUS
            };
            let previous = &*previous;
            if previous.sa_flags & libc::SA_SIGINFO != 0 && previous.sa_sigaction > libc::SIG_IGN {
                let handler: extern "C" fn(i32, *mut libc::siginfo_t, *mut libc::c_void) =
                    std::mem::transmute(previous.sa_sigaction);
                handler(signal, info, context);
                return;
            }
            if previous.sa_sigaction > libc::SIG_IGN {
                let handler: extern "C" fn(i32) = std::mem::transmute(previous.sa_sigaction);
                handler(signal);
                return;
            }
            // Return with the default action in place, so that the faulting access faults again and kills the
            // process as it would have without us.
            libc::signal(signal, libc::SIG_DFL);
        }
    }

    extern "C" fn handle_fault(signal: i32, info: *mut libc::siginfo_t, context: *mut libc::c_void) {
        unsafe {
            let pc = instruction_pointer(context);
            let (start, end) = interpreter_code_range();
            let address = (*info).si_addr() as usize;
            if (start..end).contains(&*pc) && is_in_any_reservation(address) {
                // The handlers keep their frame in the pinned registers, so the trap handler can find the
                // execution context of the access from the frame pointer.
                *pc = memory_fault_handler();
                return;
            }
            if is_in_any_reservation(address) && crate::runtime::jit::redirect_fault(context) {
                return;
            }
            forward(signal, info, context);
        }
    }

    pub fn install() {
        INSTALL.call_once(|| unsafe {
            let mut action: libc::sigaction = std::mem::zeroed();
            action.sa_sigaction = handle_fault as *const () as usize;
            action.sa_flags = libc::SA_SIGINFO | libc::SA_ONSTACK;
            libc::sigemptyset(&raw mut action.sa_mask);
            libc::sigaction(libc::SIGSEGV, &raw const action, &raw mut PREVIOUS_SIGSEGV);
            libc::sigaction(libc::SIGBUS, &raw const action, &raw mut PREVIOUS_SIGBUS);
        });
    }
}

/// Windows reports faults to vectored exception handlers before it looks for handlers in the faulting thread's frames.
#[cfg(all(wasm_interpreter, windows))]
mod fault {
    use super::{interpreter_code_range, memory_fault_handler};
    use crate::runtime::memory::is_in_any_reservation;
    use std::ffi::c_void;
    use std::sync::Once;

    const EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION: u32 = 0xc000_0005;
    const EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION: i32 = -1;
    const EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH: i32 = 0;
    /// Where Rip is in the x86-64 CONTEXT structure.
    const CONTEXT_RIP_OFFSET: usize = 0xf8;

    #[repr(C)]
    struct ExceptionRecord {
        code: u32,
        flags: u32,
        record: *mut ExceptionRecord,
        address: *mut c_void,
        parameter_count: u32,
        /// For access violations, whether the access was a write, and the address it accessed.
        information: [usize; 15],
    }

    #[repr(C)]
    struct ExceptionPointers {
        record: *mut ExceptionRecord,
        context: *mut u8,
    }

    unsafe extern "system" {
        fn AddVectoredExceptionHandler(
            first: u32,
            handler: unsafe extern "system" fn(*mut ExceptionPointers) -> i32,
        ) -> *mut c_void;
    }

    static INSTALL: Once = Once::new();

    unsafe extern "system" fn handle_exception(pointers: *mut ExceptionPointers) -> i32 {
        unsafe {
            let record = &*(*pointers).record;
            if record.code != EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION || record.parameter_count < 2 {
                return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH;
            }
            let pc = (*pointers).context.add(CONTEXT_RIP_OFFSET).cast::<usize>();
            let (start, end) = interpreter_code_range();
            if (start..end).contains(&*pc) && is_in_any_reservation(record.information[1]) {
                // The handlers keep their frame in the pinned registers, so the trap handler can find the
                // execution context of the access from the frame pointer.
                *pc = memory_fault_handler();
                return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION;
            }
            if is_in_any_reservation(record.information[1])
                && crate::runtime::jit::redirect_fault((*pointers).context.cast())
            {
                return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION;
            }
            EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH
        }
    }

    pub fn install() {
        INSTALL.call_once(|| unsafe {
            AddVectoredExceptionHandler(1, handle_exception);
        });
    }
}

pub fn install_fault_handler() {
    #[cfg(wasm_interpreter)]
    fault::install();
}

/*
