/// The guest's memory, which every access checks the bounds of.
struct Memory<'a>(&'a mut [u8]);

impl Memory<'_> {
    fn slice(&mut self, address: u32, length: u32) -> Result<&mut [u8], Errno> {
        let start = address as usize;
        let end = start.checked_add(length as usize).ok_or(ERRNO_FAULT)?;
        self.0.get_mut(start..end).ok_or(ERRNO_FAULT)
    }

    fn read_u32(&mut self, address: u32) -> Result<u32, Errno> {
        let bytes = self.slice(address, 4)?;
        Ok(u32::from_le_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]]))
    }

    fn write(&mut self, address: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Errno> {
        self.slice(address, bytes.len() as u32)?.copy_from_slice(bytes);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn write_u8(&mut self, address: u32, value: u8) -> Result<(), Errno> {
        self.write(address, &[value])
    }

    fn write_u16(&mut self, address: u32, value: u16) -> Result<(), Errno> {
        self.write(address, &value.to_le_bytes())
    }

    fn write_u32(&mut self, address: u32, value: u32) -> Result<(), Errno> {
        self.write(address, &value.to_le_bytes())
    }

    fn write_u64(&mut self, address: u32, value: u64) -> Result<(), Errno> {
        self.write(address, &value.to_le_bytes())
    }
}

/// Write the pointers to `strings` at `pointers`, and the strings, each followed by a null byte, at `buffer`.
fn write_strings(memory: &mut Memory, strings: &[String], pointers: u32, buffer: u32) -> Result<(), Errno> {
    let mut offset = buffer;
    for (index, string) in strings.iter().enumerate() {
        memory.write_u32(pointers.wrapping_add(index as u32 * 4), offset)?;
        memory.write(offset, string.as_bytes())?;
        memory.write_u8(offset.wrapping_add(string.len() as u32), 0)?;
        offset = offset.wrapping_add(string.len() as u32 + 1);
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn write_string_sizes(memory: &mut Memory, strings: &[String], count: u32, size: u32) -> Result<(), Errno> {
    memory.write_u32(count, strings.len() as u32)?;
    let total: usize = strings.iter().map(|string| string.len() + 1).sum();
    memory.write_u32(size, total as u32)
}

/// What fd_filestat_get and path_filestat_get return.
pub struct FileStatus {
    device: u64,
    inode: u64,
    filetype: u8,
    link_count: u64,
    size: u64,
    access_time: u64,
    modification_time: u64,
    status_change_time: u64,
}

fn write_filestat(memory: &mut Memory, address: u32, status: &FileStatus) -> Result<(), Errno> {
    memory.write_u64(address, status.device)?;
    memory.write_u64(address.wrapping_add(8), status.inode)?;
    memory.write_u8(address.wrapping_add(16), status.filetype)?;
    memory.write_u64(address.wrapping_add(24), status.link_count)?;
    memory.write_u64(address.wrapping_add(32), status.size)?;
    memory.write_u64(address.wrapping_add(40), status.access_time)?;
    memory.write_u64(address.wrapping_add(48), status.modification_time)?;
    memory.write_u64(address.wrapping_add(56), status.status_change_time)
}

#[cfg(unix)]
mod platform {
    use super::{ERRNO_INVAL, ERRNO_IO, ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE, Errno, FileStatus, OpenOptions};
    use std::collections::VecDeque;
    use std::ffi::CString;

    pub const WHENCE_CURRENT: u32 = 1;

    /// The most symbolic links one path resolution follows, as Linux's.
    const MAX_SYMLINKS: u32 = 40;

    /// A path resolved beneath a directory: the directory its last component is in, and that component, which is
    /// neither `..` nor a symbolic link that the resolution was to follow.
    struct Beneath {
        directory: i32,
        /// Whether `directory` is a descriptor of the resolution's own, which it closes.
        owned: bool,
        name: CString,
        /// Whether the path ended in a slash, which only a directory may be named with.
        must_be_directory: bool,
    }

    impl Drop for Beneath {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            if self.owned {
                unsafe { libc::close(self.directory) };
            }
        }
    }

    fn components(path: &[u8]) -> impl DoubleEndedIterator<Item = &[u8]> {
        path.split(|byte| *byte == b'/')
            .filter(|component| !component.is_empty() && *component != b".")
    }

    /// The symbolic link `name` in `directory` points to, or None if it is not one.
    fn link_target(directory: i32, name: &CString) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, Errno> {
        let mut status = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed::<libc::stat>() };
        if unsafe { libc::fstatat(directory, name.as_ptr(), &raw mut status, libc::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) } != 0
            || status.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT != libc::S_IFLNK
        {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut target = vec![0u8; libc::PATH_MAX as usize];
        let length = unsafe { libc::readlinkat(directory, name.as_ptr(), target.as_mut_ptr().cast(), target.len()) };
        if length < 0 {
            return Err(last_errno());
        }
        // NB: readlinkat() truncates a target that does not fit without saying so.
        if length as usize == target.len() {
            return Err(errno_of(libc::ENAMETOOLONG));
        }
        target.truncate(length as usize);
        Ok(Some(target))
    }

    /// Resolves `path` beneath the directory `base`, one component at a time, so that it never leaves it: absolute
    /// paths and symbolic links, and `..` above `base`, are not capable. Symbolic links in the middle are followed
    /// (beneath `base`), and the last one too if `follow_last`, or if the path ends in a slash, as POSIX resolves it.
    fn resolve_beneath(base: i32, path: &[u8], follow_last: bool) -> Result<Beneath, Errno> {
        if path.is_empty() {
            return Err(errno_of(libc::ENOENT));
        }
        if path[0] == b'/' {
            return Err(ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE);
        }
        // The directories below `base` the resolution is in, innermost last, which it owns.
        let mut directories: Vec<i32> = Vec::new();
        let close_all = |directories: &mut Vec<i32>| {
            for fd in directories.drain(..) {
                unsafe { libc::close(fd) };
            }
        };
        let mut queue: VecDeque<Vec<u8>> = components(path).map(<[u8]>::to_vec).collect();
        let mut must_be_directory = path.last() == Some(&b'/');
        let mut links = 0;
        let result = loop {
            let Some(component) = queue.pop_front() else {
                break Ok(c".".to_owned());
            };
            let current = *directories.last().unwrap_or(&base);
            if component == b".." {
                match directories.pop() {
                    Some(fd) => unsafe {
                        libc::close(fd);
                    },
                    None => break Err(ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE),
                }
                continue;
            }
            let name = match path_of(&component) {
                Ok(name) => name,
                Err(errno) => break Err(errno),
            };
            let last = queue.is_empty();
            if !last || follow_last || must_be_directory {
                match link_target(current, &name) {
                    Ok(Some(target)) => {
                        links += 1;
                        if links > MAX_SYMLINKS {
                            break Err(errno_of(libc::ELOOP));
                        }
                        if target.first() == Some(&b'/') {
                            break Err(ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE);
                        }
                        if last && target.last() == Some(&b'/') {
                            must_be_directory = true;
                        }
                        for component in components(&target).rev() {
                            queue.push_front(component.to_vec());
                        }
                        continue;
                    }
                    Ok(None) => {}
                    Err(errno) => break Err(errno),
                }
            }
            if last {
                break Ok(name);
            }
            let fd = unsafe {
                libc::openat(
                    current,
                    name.as_ptr(),
                    libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_NOFOLLOW | libc::O_RDONLY | libc::O_CLOEXEC,
                )
            };
            if fd < 0 {
                break Err(last_errno());
            }
            directories.push(fd);
        };
        match result {
            Ok(name) => {
                let directory = directories.pop();
                close_all(&mut directories);
                Ok(Beneath {
                    directory: directory.unwrap_or(base),
                    owned: directory.is_some(),
                    name,
                    must_be_directory,
                })
            }
            Err(errno) => {
                close_all(&mut directories);
                Err(errno)
            }
        }
    }

    const NANOSECONDS_PER_SECOND: u64 = 1_000_000_000;

    fn last_errno() -> Errno {
        errno_of(std::io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error().unwrap_or(0))
    }

    /// The WASI errno of a host errno.
    fn errno_of(host: i32) -> Errno {
        match host {
            libc::E2BIG => 1,
            libc::EACCES => 2,
            libc::EADDRINUSE => 3,
            libc::EADDRNOTAVAIL => 4,
            libc::EAFNOSUPPORT => 5,
            libc::EAGAIN => 6,
            libc::EALREADY => 7,
            libc::EBADF => 8,
            libc::EBUSY => 10,
            libc::ECHILD => 12,
            libc::ECONNREFUSED => 14,
            libc::ECONNRESET => 15,
            libc::EDEADLK => 16,
            libc::EDOM => 18,
            libc::EEXIST => 20,
            libc::EFAULT => 21,
            libc::EFBIG => 22,
            libc::EINTR => 27,
            libc::EINVAL => 28,
            libc::EIO => 29,
            libc::EISDIR => 31,
            libc::ELOOP => 32,
            libc::EMFILE => 33,
            libc::EMLINK => 34,
            libc::ENAMETOOLONG => 37,
            libc::ENFILE => 41,
            libc::ENOBUFS => 42,
            libc::ENODEV => 43,
            libc::ENOENT => 44,
            libc::ENOEXEC => 45,
            libc::ENOMEM => 48,
            libc::ENOSPC => 51,
            libc::ENOSYS => 52,
            libc::ENOTDIR => 54,
            libc::ENOTEMPTY => 55,
            libc::ENOTSUP => 58,
            libc::ENOTTY => 59,
            libc::ENXIO => 60,
            libc::EOVERFLOW => 61,
            libc::EPERM => 63,
            libc::EPIPE => 64,
            libc::ERANGE => 68,
            libc::EROFS => 69,
            libc::ESPIPE => 70,
            libc::ESRCH => 71,
            libc::ETIMEDOUT => 73,
            libc::EXDEV => 75,
            _ => ERRNO_IO,
        }
    }

    fn path_of(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<CString, Errno> {
        CString::new(bytes).map_err(|_| ERRNO_INVAL)
    }

    pub fn open_directory(path: &str) -> Result<i32, Errno> {
        let path = path_of(path.as_bytes())?;
        let fd = unsafe { libc::open(path.as_ptr(), libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_RDONLY | libc::O_CLOEXEC) };
        if fd < 0 { Err(last_errno()) } else { Ok(fd) }
    }

    pub fn open_at(directory: i32, path: &[u8], options: &OpenOptions) -> Result<i32, Errno> {
        const OFLAGS_CREAT: u16 = 1;
        const OFLAGS_DIRECTORY: u16 = 2;
        const OFLAGS_EXCL: u16 = 4;
        const OFLAGS_TRUNC: u16 = 8;
        const FDFLAGS_APPEND: u16 = 1;
        const FDFLAGS_NONBLOCK: u16 = 4;
        const FDFLAGS_SYNC: u16 = 16;
        const RIGHTS_FD_READ: u64 = 1 << 1;
        const RIGHTS_FD_WRITE: u64 = 1 << 6;

        let resolved = resolve_beneath(directory, path, options.follow_symlinks)?;
        let readable = options.rights & RIGHTS_FD_READ != 0;
        let writable = options.rights & RIGHTS_FD_WRITE != 0;
        let mut flags = match (readable, writable) {
            (_, false) => libc::O_RDONLY,
            (false, true) => libc::O_WRONLY,
            (true, true) => libc::O_RDWR,
        };
        flags |= libc::O_CLOEXEC;
        if options.open_flags & OFLAGS_DIRECTORY != 0 {
            flags = libc::O_RDONLY | libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_CLOEXEC;
        }
        if resolved.must_be_directory {
            // NB: As on Linux, a file cannot be created with a name that ends in a slash.
            if options.open_flags & OFLAGS_CREAT != 0 {
                return Err(errno_of(libc::EISDIR));
            }
            flags |= libc::O_DIRECTORY;
        }
        if options.open_flags & OFLAGS_CREAT != 0 {
            flags |= libc::O_CREAT;
        }
        if options.open_flags & OFLAGS_EXCL != 0 {
            flags |= libc::O_EXCL;
        }
        if options.open_flags & OFLAGS_TRUNC != 0 {
            flags |= libc::O_TRUNC;
        }
        if options.fd_flags & FDFLAGS_APPEND != 0 {
            flags |= libc::O_APPEND;
        }
        if options.fd_flags & FDFLAGS_NONBLOCK != 0 {
            flags |= libc::O_NONBLOCK;
        }
        if options.fd_flags & FDFLAGS_SYNC != 0 {
            flags |= libc::O_SYNC;
        }
        // NB: The resolution followed the symbolic links it was to follow: a link in the last place now is one that
        //     appeared since, which must not be followed out.
        flags |= libc::O_NOFOLLOW;
        let fd = unsafe { libc::openat(resolved.directory, resolved.name.as_ptr(), flags, 0o644 as libc::c_uint) };
        if fd < 0 { Err(last_errno()) } else { Ok(fd) }
    }

    pub fn close(fd: i32) -> Result<(), Errno> {
        if unsafe { libc::close(fd) } != 0 {
            return Err(last_errno());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn read(fd: i32, bytes: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, Errno> {
        let result = unsafe { libc::read(fd, bytes.as_mut_ptr().cast(), bytes.len()) };
        if result < 0 {
            Err(last_errno())
        } else {
            Ok(result as usize)
        }
    }

    pub fn write(fd: i32, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, Errno> {
        let result = unsafe { libc::write(fd, bytes.as_ptr().cast(), bytes.len()) };
        if result < 0 {
            Err(last_errno())
        } else {
            Ok(result as usize)
        }
    }

    pub fn seek(fd: i32, offset: i64, whence: u32) -> Result<u64, Errno> {
        let whence = match whence {
            0 => libc::SEEK_SET,
            1 => libc::SEEK_CUR,
            2 => libc::SEEK_END,
            _ => return Err(ERRNO_INVAL),
        };
        let result = unsafe { libc::lseek(fd, offset as libc::off_t, whence) };
        if result < 0 {
            Err(last_errno())
        } else {
            Ok(result as u64)
        }
    }

    pub fn create_directory(directory: i32, path: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Errno> {
        let resolved = resolve_beneath(directory, path, false)?;
        if unsafe { libc::mkdirat(resolved.directory, resolved.name.as_ptr(), 0o755) } != 0 {
            return Err(last_errno());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn filetype_of(mode: libc::mode_t) -> u8 {
        match mode & libc::S_IFMT {
            libc::S_IFBLK => 1,
            libc::S_IFCHR => 2,
            libc::S_IFDIR => 3,
            libc::S_IFREG => 4,
            libc::S_IFSOCK => 6,
            libc::S_IFLNK => 7,
            _ => 0,
        }
    }

    // NB: The types of stat's fields differ between hosts.
    #[allow(clippy::unnecessary_cast)]
    fn status_of(status: &libc::stat) -> FileStatus {
        let time = |seconds: i64, nanoseconds: i64| -> u64 {
            (seconds as u64)
                .wrapping_mul(NANOSECONDS_PER_SECOND)
                .wrapping_add(nanoseconds as u64)
        };
        FileStatus {
            device: status.st_dev as u64,
            inode: status.st_ino as u64,
            filetype: filetype_of(status.st_mode),
            link_count: status.st_nlink as u64,
            size: status.st_size as u64,
            access_time: time(status.st_atime as i64, status.st_atime_nsec as i64),
            modification_time: time(status.st_mtime as i64, status.st_mtime_nsec as i64),
            status_change_time: time(status.st_ctime as i64, status.st_ctime_nsec as i64),
        }
    }

    pub fn fstat(fd: i32) -> Result<FileStatus, Errno> {
        let mut status = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed::<libc::stat>() };
        if unsafe { libc::fstat(fd, &raw mut status) } != 0 {
            return Err(last_errno());
        }
        Ok(status_of(&status))
    }

    pub fn stat_at(directory: i32, path: &[u8], follow_symlinks: bool) -> Result<FileStatus, Errno> {
        let resolved = resolve_beneath(directory, path, follow_symlinks)?;
        let mut status = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed::<libc::stat>() };
        let (directory, name) = (resolved.directory, resolved.name.as_ptr());
        if unsafe { libc::fstatat(directory, name, &raw mut status, libc::AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) } != 0 {
            return Err(last_errno());
        }
        if resolved.must_be_directory && status.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT != libc::S_IFDIR {
            return Err(errno_of(libc::ENOTDIR));
        }
        Ok(status_of(&status))
    }

    /// The filetype and fdflags of a descriptor.
    pub fn fd_status(fd: i32) -> Result<(u8, u16), Errno> {
        let status = fstat(fd)?;
        let flags = unsafe { libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_GETFL) };
        if flags < 0 {
            return Err(last_errno());
        }
        let mut fd_flags = 0;
        if flags & libc::O_APPEND != 0 {
            fd_flags |= 1;
        }
        if flags & libc::O_NONBLOCK != 0 {
            fd_flags |= 4;
        }
        if flags & libc::O_SYNC == libc::O_SYNC {
            fd_flags |= 16;
        }
        Ok((status.filetype, fd_flags))
    }

    fn clock_of(id: u32) -> Result<libc::clockid_t, Errno> {
        match id {
            0 => Ok(libc::CLOCK_REALTIME),
            1 => Ok(libc::CLOCK_MONOTONIC),
            2 => Ok(libc::CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID),
            3 => Ok(libc::CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID),
            _ => Err(ERRNO_INVAL),
        }
    }

    fn nanoseconds_of(time: &libc::timespec) -> u64 {
        (time.tv_sec as u64)
            .wrapping_mul(NANOSECONDS_PER_SECOND)
            .wrapping_add(time.tv_nsec as u64)
    }

    pub fn clock_time(id: u32) -> Result<u64, Errno> {
        let mut time = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed::<libc::timespec>() };
        if unsafe { libc::clock_gettime(clock_of(id)?, &raw mut time) } != 0 {
            return Err(last_errno());
        }
        Ok(nanoseconds_of(&time))
    }

    pub fn clock_resolution(id: u32) -> Result<u64, Errno> {
        let mut time = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed::<libc::timespec>() };
        if unsafe { libc::clock_getres(clock_of(id)?, &raw mut time) } != 0 {
            return Err(last_errno());
        }
        Ok(nanoseconds_of(&time))
    }

    // NB: The libc crate does not bind getentropy() for musl, whose C library has it.
    #[cfg(target_env = "musl")]
    unsafe extern "C" {
        fn getentropy(buffer: *mut libc::c_void, length: libc::size_t) -> libc::c_int;
    }
    #[cfg(not(target_env = "musl"))]
    use libc::getentropy;

    pub fn fill_with_random(bytes: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Errno> {
        // getentropy() fills at most 256 bytes at a time.
        for chunk in bytes.chunks_mut(256) {
            if unsafe { getentropy(chunk.as_mut_ptr().cast(), chunk.len()) } != 0 {
                return Err(last_errno());
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

#![cfg(any(target_arch = "x86_64", all(target_arch = "aarch64", not(windows))))]

use libwasm_engine::runtime::{ExternValue, InstanceAddress, Store, Trap, Value};
use std::sync::Arc;

fn instantiate(store: &mut Store, name: &str) -> InstanceAddress {
    let path = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("tests/fixtures")
        .join(name);
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).unwrap();
    let module = libwasm_engine::compile(&bytes).unwrap();
    store.instantiate(Arc::new(module), &[]).unwrap()
}

fn call(store: &mut Store, instance: InstanceAddress, name: &str, arguments: &[Value]) -> Result<Vec<Value>, Trap> {
    let Some(ExternValue::Function(function)) = store.instance(instance).export(name) else {
        panic!("no function export {name}");
    };
    store.invoke(function, arguments)
}

#[test]
fn runs_control_flow_locals_calls_and_memory() {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "basics.wasm");
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "add", &[Value::I32(40), Value::I32(2)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(42)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "fib", &[Value::I64(20)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I64(6765)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "sum_to", &[Value::I32(100)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(5050)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(
            &mut store,
            instance,
            "store_and_load",
            &[Value::I32(16), Value::I32(0x1234_5678)]
        ),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(0x56)])
    );
    for (input, output) in [(0, 100), (1, 200), (2, 300), (7, 300)] {
        assert_eq!(
            call(&mut store, instance, "classify", &[Value::I32(input)]),
            Ok(vec![Value::I32(output)])
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(call(&mut store, instance, "bump", &[]), Ok(vec![Value::I32(15)]));
    assert_eq!(call(&mut store, instance, "bump", &[]), Ok(vec![Value::I32(20)]));
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "multi", &[]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(1), Value::I64(2), Value::I32(3)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "select", &[Value::I32(1)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(11)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "select", &[Value::I32(0)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(22)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "drop_in_block", &[]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(3)])
    );
}

#[test]
fn recurses_with_frames_larger_than_a_page() {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "big_frames.wasm");
    // Each frame reaches more than a page below the previous one, which Windows only commits if the interpreter probes
    // the pages in between.
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "deep", &[Value::I32(100)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(101)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "deep", &[Value::I32(1_000_000)]),
        Err(Trap::StackExhausted)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "deep", &[Value::I32(10)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(11)])
    );
}

#[test]
fn traps() {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "basics.wasm");
    assert_eq!(call(&mut store, instance, "trap", &[]), Err(Trap::Unreachable));
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "out_of_bounds", &[]),
        Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "recurse", &[Value::I32(0)]),
        Err(Trap::StackExhausted)
    );
    // The store still works after a trap.
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "add", &[Value::I32(1), Value::I32(2)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(3)])
    );
}

#[test]
fn checks_bounds_of_other_memories_and_memory64() {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "checked_memories.wasm");
    assert_eq!(
        call(
            &mut store,
            instance,
            "store_other",
            &[Value::I32(100), Value::I32(0x1234)]
        ),
        Ok(vec![])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "load_other", &[Value::I32(100)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(0x1234)])
    );
    // The store went to the other memory, not to memory 0.
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "load_small", &[Value::I32(100)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(0)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "load_other", &[Value::I32(65533)]),
        Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "store_wide", &[Value::I64(16), Value::I64(-5)]),
        Ok(vec![])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "load_wide", &[Value::I64(16)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I64(-5)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "load_wide", &[Value::I64(1 << 40)]),
        Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
    );
    // An address and offset that wrap around 2^64 are out of bounds too.
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "load_wide", &[Value::I64(-4)]),
        Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "splat_other", &[Value::I32(100)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(0x1234)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "splat_other", &[Value::I32(65535)]),
        Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "lane_wide", &[Value::I64(24)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(-5)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "lane_wide", &[Value::I64(65533)]),
        Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "grow_wide", &[Value::I64(1)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I64(1)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "grow_wide", &[Value::I64(1 << 40)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I64(-1)])
    );
}

#[test]
fn catches_exceptions_from_webassembly_and_host_functions() {
    use libwasm_engine::types::{FuncType, ValType};
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let tag = store.allocate_tag(FuncType {
        params: vec![ValType::I32],
        results: vec![],
    });
    let thrower = store.allocate_host_function(
        FuncType {
            params: vec![ValType::I32],
            results: vec![],
        },
        std::rc::Rc::new(move |store: &mut Store, arguments: &[Value]| {
            let Value::I32(value) = arguments[0] else {
                unreachable!();
            };
            let exception = store.allocate_exception(tag, &[u64::from((value * 2) as u32)]);
            Err(Trap::UncaughtException(exception))
        }),
    );
    let path = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("tests/fixtures/exceptions.wasm");
    let module = libwasm_engine::compile(&std::fs::read(path).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let instance = store
        .instantiate(
            Arc::new(module),
            &[ExternValue::Tag(tag), ExternValue::Function(thrower)],
        )
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "catch_own", &[Value::I32(7)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(7)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "catch_host", &[Value::I32(7)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(14)])
    );
    let Err(Trap::UncaughtException(exception)) = call(&mut store, instance, "uncaught", &[Value::I32(5)]) else {
        panic!("the exception should leave the interpreter");
    };
    assert_eq!(store.exception(exception).tag, tag);
    assert_eq!(store.exception(exception).payload, &[5]);
}

#[test]
fn checks_values_from_the_host_against_function_types() {
    use libwasm_engine::types::{FuncType, HeapType, RefType, ValType};
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let any = ValType::Ref(RefType {
        nullable: true,
        heap: HeapType::Any,
    });
    let reference = store.allocate_host_function(
        FuncType {
            params: vec![],
            results: vec![any],
        },
        std::rc::Rc::new(|_: &mut Store, _: &[Value]| Ok(vec![Value::I64(0x4141)])),
    );
    let path = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("tests/fixtures/host_values.wasm");
    let module = libwasm_engine::compile(&std::fs::read(path).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let instance = store
        .instantiate(Arc::new(module), &[ExternValue::Function(reference)])
        .unwrap();
    let is_host_trap = |result: Result<Vec<Value>, Trap>| matches!(result, Err(Trap::Host(_)));
    let traps =
        |store: &mut Store, name: &str, arguments: &[Value]| is_host_trap(call(store, instance, name, arguments));

    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "is_null", &[Value::Ref(0)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(1)])
    );
    assert!(traps(&mut store, "is_null", &[Value::I64(0x4141)]));
    assert!(traps(&mut store, "take_non_null", &[Value::Ref(0)]));
    assert!(traps(&mut store, "host_is_null", &[]));
    assert!(is_host_trap(store.invoke(reference, &[])));

    let takes_an_argument = store.allocate_host_function(
        FuncType {
            params: vec![ValType::I32],
            results: vec![],
        },
        std::rc::Rc::new(|_: &mut Store, arguments: &[Value]| {
            assert_eq!(arguments.len(), 1);
            Ok(vec![])
        }),
    );
    assert!(is_host_trap(store.invoke(takes_an_argument, &[])));
    assert!(is_host_trap(store.invoke(takes_an_argument, &[Value::I64(1)])));
    assert_eq!(store.invoke(takes_an_argument, &[Value::I32(1)]), Ok(vec![]));
}

#[test]
fn waits_on_shared_memory() {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "shared_waits.wasm");
    // The location holds 0, not 1.
    assert_eq!(
        call(
            &mut store,
            instance,
            "wait",
            &[Value::I32(0), Value::I32(1), Value::I64(-1)]
        ),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(1)])
    );
    // Nobody notifies, so the wait times out after a millisecond.
    assert_eq!(
        call(
            &mut store,
            instance,
            "wait",
            &[Value::I32(0), Value::I32(0), Value::I64(1_000_000)]
        ),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(2)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "notify", &[Value::I32(0)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(0)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "or", &[Value::I32(8), Value::I32(6)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(0)])
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "or", &[Value::I32(8), Value::I32(9)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(6)])
    );
}

#[test]
fn wait_traps_in_an_agent_that_cannot_block() {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    store.can_block = false;
    let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "shared_waits.wasm");
    // Even where the value differs and nothing would block.
    for expected in [0, 1] {
        assert!(matches!(
            call(
                &mut store,
                instance,
                "wait",
                &[Value::I32(0), Value::I32(expected), Value::I64(0)]
            ),
            Err(Trap::Host(_))
        ));
    }
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "notify", &[Value::I32(0)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(0)])
    );
}

#[test]
fn active_element_segments_point_nowhere_after_instantiation() {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "element_segments.wasm");
    // The active segment's values went into the table and the segment was dropped: nothing points at its storage.
    let segments = &store.instance(instance).element_segments;
    assert!(segments[0].contents.is_null());
    assert_eq!(segments[0].length, 0);
    assert!(!segments[1].contents.is_null());
    assert_eq!(segments[1].length, 2);
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "call", &[Value::I32(1)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(7)])
    );
    assert_eq!(call(&mut store, instance, "init", &[Value::I32(2)]), Ok(vec![]));
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "call", &[Value::I32(3)]),
        Ok(vec![Value::I32(7)])
    );
}

#[test]
fn constant_arrays_too_large_for_memory_trap() {
    for name in ["huge_constant_arrays.wasm", "huge_constant_arrays_new.wasm"] {
        let path = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
            .join("tests/fixtures")
            .join(name);
        let module = libwasm_engine::compile(&std::fs::read(path).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let mut store = Store::new();
        // The length is 2^32 - 1: building the elements first aborted the process.
        assert!(store.instantiate(Arc::new(module), &[]).is_err(), "{name}");
    }
}

/// memory.atomic.wait waits where Atomics.wait does, on the waiter lists of the process, so that a notify of the address
/// from outside WebAssembly, as Atomics.notify does it, ends it.
#[test]
fn waits_end_with_wakes_from_outside_webassembly() {
    let (sender, receiver) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
    let waiter = std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let mut store = Store::new();
        let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "shared_memory_export.wasm");
        let Some(ExternValue::Memory(memory)) = store.instance(instance).export("memory") else {
            panic!("no memory export");
        };
        sender.send(store.memory(memory).bytes().as_ptr() as usize).unwrap();
        // Ten seconds, which only a wake cuts short.
        call(
            &mut store,
            instance,
            "wait",
            &[Value::I32(8), Value::I32(0), Value::I64(10_000_000_000)],
        )
    });
    let address = receiver.recv().unwrap() + 8;
    let start = std::time::Instant::now();
    loop {
        // Until the wait has started: a wake before it wakes nobody.
        // SAFETY: The word is in the memory of the store, which lives until the wait is over.
        let woken = ak::waiter_list::atomic_notify(unsafe { &*(address as *const std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32) }, 1);
        if woken == 1 {
            break;
        }
        assert!(
            start.elapsed() < std::time::Duration::from_secs(5),
            "the wait never started"
        );
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(1));
    }
    assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), Ok(vec![Value::I32(0)]));
}

#[test]
fn traps_on_ranges_that_wrap_around() {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "wrapping_ranges.wasm");
    let wrapping_start = Value::I64(-256);
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "fill", &[wrapping_start, Value::I64(512)]),
        Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(
            &mut store,
            instance,
            "copy",
            &[wrapping_start, Value::I64(0), Value::I64(512)]
        ),
        Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(
            &mut store,
            instance,
            "copy",
            &[Value::I64(0), wrapping_start, Value::I64(512)]
        ),
        Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "table_fill", &[Value::I64(-2), Value::I64(4)]),
        Err(Trap::TableOutOfBounds)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        call(&mut store, instance, "fill", &[Value::I64(16), Value::I64(16)]),
        Ok(vec![])
    );
}

#[test]
fn calls_between_the_tiers_with_many_values() {
    let run = |interpreted: bool| {
        let mut store = Store::new();
        if interpreted {
            store.disable_jit();
        }
        let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "wide_calls.wasm");
        call(&mut store, instance, "run", &[]).unwrap()
    };
    assert_eq!(run(false), run(true));
}

/// (func (export "spin") (loop (br 0)))
const LOOP_FOREVER: &[u8] = &[
    0x00, 0x61, 0x73, 0x6d, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x04, 0x01, 0x60, 0x00, 0x00, 0x03, 0x02, 0x01, 0x00, 0x07,
    0x08, 0x01, 0x04, 0x73, 0x70, 0x69, 0x6e, 0x00, 0x00, 0x0a, 0x09, 0x01, 0x07, 0x00, 0x03, 0x40, 0x0c, 0x00, 0x0b,
    0x0b,
];

/// Runs LOOP_FOREVER in `store` while another thread interrupts the store.
fn interrupt_a_loop(mut store: Store, delay: std::time::Duration) {
    let module = libwasm_engine::compile(LOOP_FOREVER).unwrap();
    let instance = store.instantiate(Arc::new(module), &[]).unwrap();
    let word = store.stack_limit_word() as usize;
    let interrupter = std::thread::spawn(move || {
        std::thread::sleep(delay);
        // SAFETY: The store outlives this thread.
        let word = unsafe { &*(word as *const std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64) };
        word.store(
            libwasm_engine::abi::STACK_LIMIT_INTERRUPTED,
            std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed,
        );
    });
    assert_eq!(call(&mut store, instance, "spin", &[]), Err(Trap::StackExhausted));
    interrupter.join().unwrap();

    // NB: It stays that way.
    assert_eq!(call(&mut store, instance, "spin", &[]), Err(Trap::StackExhausted));
}

#[test]
fn another_thread_interrupts_an_interpreted_loop() {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    store.disable_jit();
    interrupt_a_loop(store, std::time::Duration::from_millis(50));
}

#[test]
fn another_thread_interrupts_a_compiled_loop() {
    // NB: The loop tiers up on the way there, wherever the JIT runs.
    interrupt_a_loop(Store::new(), std::time::Duration::from_millis(500));
}

/// Starts a memory.atomic.wait on a thread of its own, which `interrupt` can end, and returns the address of its word.
fn start_wait(
    timeout: i64,
    interrupt: Arc<ak::waiter_list::AgentWaiter>,
    disable_jit: bool,
) -> (usize, std::thread::JoinHandle<Result<Vec<Value>, Trap>>) {
    let (sender, receiver) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
    let waiter = std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let mut store = Store::new();
        if disable_jit {
            store.disable_jit();
        }
        store.agent_waiter = Some(interrupt);
        let instance = instantiate(&mut store, "shared_memory_export.wasm");
        let Some(ExternValue::Memory(memory)) = store.instance(instance).export("memory") else {
            panic!("no memory export");
        };
        sender.send(store.memory(memory).bytes().as_ptr() as usize).unwrap();
        call(
            &mut store,
            instance,
            "wait",
            &[Value::I32(8), Value::I32(0), Value::I64(timeout)],
        )
    });
    (receiver.recv().unwrap() + 8, waiter)
}

#[test]
fn another_thread_interrupts_a_wait() {
    for disable_jit in [false, true] {
        // No timeout, and ten minutes.
        for timeout in [-1, 600_000_000_000] {
            let interrupt = ak::waiter_list::AgentWaiter::new();
            let (_, waiter) = start_wait(timeout, interrupt.clone(), disable_jit);
            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50));
            interrupt.interrupt();
            assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), Err(Trap::StackExhausted));
        }
    }
}

/// Only a wake ends a wait: it does not look at the word again.
#[test]
fn a_change_of_the_word_does_not_end_a_wait() {
    let interrupt = ak::waiter_list::AgentWaiter::new();
    let (address, waiter) = start_wait(300_000_000, interrupt, false);
    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
    // SAFETY: The word is in the memory of the store, which lives until the wait is over.
    unsafe { &*(address as *const std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32) }.store(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
    assert_eq!(waiter.join().unwrap(), Ok(vec![Value::I32(2)]));
}

#[test]
fn knows_the_types_of_its_own_identities() {
    use libwasm_engine::types::{FuncType, HeapType, RefType, ValType};
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let reference_to = |identity| {
        ValType::Ref(RefType {
            nullable: true,
            heap: HeapType::Concrete(identity),
        })
    };
    assert!(store.knows_type(ValType::I32));
    assert!(!store.knows_type(reference_to(0)));

    store.allocate_host_function(
        FuncType {
            params: vec![],
            results: vec![],
        },
        std::rc::Rc::new(|_: &mut Store, _: &[Value]| Ok(vec![])),
    );
    assert!(store.knows_type(reference_to(0)));
    assert!(!store.knows_type(reference_to(1)));
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Engine/tests/fault_stress.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#![cfg(any(target_arch = "x86_64", all(target_arch = "aarch64", not(windows))))]

//! Out-of-bounds accesses trap while another thread reserves, grows, and releases memories, which changes the set of
//! reservations the fault handler looks addresses up in.

use libwasm_engine::runtime::{ExternValue, Store, Trap, Value};
use libwasm_engine::types::{AddressType, Limits, MemoryType};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

#[test]
fn out_of_bounds_accesses_trap_while_memories_come_and_go() {
    let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
    let churn = {
        let stop = stop.clone();
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut rounds = 0u64;
            while !stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
                let mut store = Store::new();
                for _ in 0..8 {
                    let memory = store
                        .allocate_memory(MemoryType {
                            limits: Limits {
                                min: 1,
                                max: Some(4),
                                address_type: AddressType::I32,
                                shared: false,
                            },
                        })
                        .expect("the memory is allocated");
                    let _ = store.memory_mut(memory).grow(1);
                }
                // Dropping the store releases its memories.
                drop(store);
                rounds += 1;
            }
            rounds
        })
    };

    let bytes =
        std::fs::read(std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("tests/fixtures/out-of-bounds.wasm"))
            .unwrap();
    let module = Arc::new(libwasm_engine::compile(&bytes).unwrap());
    let mut store = Store::new();
    let instance = store.instantiate(module, &[]).unwrap();
    let export = |name: &str| match store.instance(instance).export(name) {
        Some(ExternValue::Function(function)) => function,
        _ => panic!("no function export {name}"),
    };
    let (load, store_function) = (export("load"), export("store"));
    for iteration in 0..20_000u32 {
        let address = 65536 + (iteration % 1024) * 4096;
        assert_eq!(
            store.invoke(load, &[Value::I32(address as i32)]),
            Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            store.invoke(store_function, &[Value::I32(iteration as i32)]),
            Err(Trap::MemoryOutOfBounds)
        );
    }
    stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    let rounds = churn.join().unwrap();
    assert!(rounds > 0);
}

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

fn fixtures() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let root = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../..");
    let mut paths = Vec::new();
    for directory in [
        "Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Fixtures/Modules",
        "Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/CI",
        "Tests/LibWasm/Fixtures",
    ] {
        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(root.join(directory)).unwrap() {
            let path = entry.unwrap().path();
            if path.extension().is_some_and(|extension| extension == "wasm") {
                paths.push(path);
            }
        }
    }
    paths.sort();
    paths
}

#[test]
fn validates_the_fixture_modules() {
    let paths = fixtures();
    assert!(paths.len() >= 20);
    for path in paths {
        let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
        let result = libwasm_engine::compile(&bytes);
        let name = path.file_name().unwrap().to_str().unwrap();
        if name == "atomics-misaligned.wasm" {
            assert_eq!(
                result.unwrap_err(),
                libwasm_engine::Error::invalid("atomic memory op alignment must be equal to natural")
            );
        } else {
            result.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{name}: {error}"));
        }
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Engine/tests/side_table.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

use libwasm_engine::validator::{CatchKind, SideTableEntry};
use libwasm_engine::{Error, Module, compile};

fn leb(mut value: u32, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    loop {
        let byte = (value & 0x7f) as u8;
        value >>= 7;
        if value == 0 {
            out.push(byte);
            return;
        }
        out.push(byte | 0x80);
    }
}

fn section(id: u8, contents: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    out.push(id);
    leb(contents.len() as u32, out);
    out.extend_from_slice(contents);
}

/// A module with one function of type `params -> results` (value type bytes), with no declared locals and the given
/// instructions, which must end with the function's `end`. Tag 0 has type [i32] -> [].
fn module(params: &[u8], results: &[u8], code: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = b"\0asm\x01\0\0\0".to_vec();
    let mut types = vec![2, 0x60];
    leb(params.len() as u32, &mut types);
    types.extend_from_slice(params);
    leb(results.len() as u32, &mut types);
    types.extend_from_slice(results);
    types.extend_from_slice(&[0x60, 1, 0x7f, 0]);
    section(1, &types, &mut bytes);
    section(3, &[1, 0], &mut bytes);
    section(13, &[1, 0, 1], &mut bytes);
    let mut body = vec![0];
    body.extend_from_slice(code);
    let mut function = Vec::new();
    leb(body.len() as u32, &mut function);
    function.extend_from_slice(&body);
    let mut code_section = vec![1];
    code_section.extend_from_slice(&function);
    section(10, &code_section, &mut bytes);
    bytes
}

fn compile_function(params: &[u8], results: &[u8], code: &[u8]) -> (Module, u32) {
    let bytes = module(params, results, code);
    let module = compile(&bytes).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{error}"));
    let start = module.code[0].code.start;
    (module, start)
}

fn entries(module: &Module) -> &[SideTableEntry] {
    &module.function_infos[0].side_table
}

const I32: u8 = 0x7f;

#[test]
fn branches_out_of_blocks_past_their_end() {
    // block (result i32) i32.const 1 i32.const 2 br 0 end drop end
    let code = [0x02, I32, 0x41, 1, 0x41, 2, 0x0c, 0, 0x0b, 0x1a, 0x0b];
    let (module, start) = compile_function(&[], &[], &code);
    let branch = 6;
    let after_end = 9;
    assert_eq!(
        entries(&module),
        [SideTableEntry {
            pc_delta: after_end - branch,
            stp_delta: 1,
            keep: 1,
            drop: 1,
        }]
    );
    assert_eq!(module.function_infos[0].max_stack_slots, 2);
    assert_eq!(module.bytes[(start as usize) + after_end as usize], 0x1a);
}

#[test]
fn branches_back_to_the_loop_instruction() {
    // loop local.get 0 br_if 0 end end, with param i32
    let code = [0x03, 0x40, 0x20, 0, 0x0d, 0, 0x0b, 0x0b];
    let (module, _) = compile_function(&[I32], &[], &code);
    assert_eq!(
        entries(&module),
        [SideTableEntry {
            pc_delta: -4,
            stp_delta: 0,
            keep: 0,
            drop: 0,
        }]
    );
}

#[test]
fn if_jumps_to_its_else_arm_and_the_first_arm_jumps_past_the_end() {
    // local.get 0 if (result i32) i32.const 1 else i32.const 2 end drop end
    let code = [0x20, 0, 0x04, I32, 0x41, 1, 0x05, 0x41, 2, 0x0b, 0x1a, 0x0b];
    let (module, _) = compile_function(&[I32], &[], &code);
    let if_pc = 2;
    let else_pc = 6;
    let end_pc = 9;
    assert_eq!(
        entries(&module),
        [
            SideTableEntry {
                pc_delta: else_pc + 1 - if_pc,
                stp_delta: 2,
                keep: 0,
                drop: 0,
            },
            SideTableEntry {
                pc_delta: end_pc + 1 - else_pc,
                stp_delta: 1,
                keep: 1,
                drop: 0,
            },
        ]
    );
}

#[test]
fn if_without_else_jumps_past_its_end() {
    // local.get 0 if nop end end
    let code = [0x20, 0, 0x04, 0x40, 0x01, 0x0b, 0x0b];
    let (module, _) = compile_function(&[I32], &[], &code);
    assert_eq!(entries(&module)[0].pc_delta, 6 - 2);
    assert_eq!(entries(&module)[0].stp_delta, 1);
}

#[test]
fn br_table_has_an_entry_per_label_with_the_default_last() {
    // block block local.get 0 br_table 0 1 0 end end end
    let code = [0x02, 0x40, 0x02, 0x40, 0x20, 0, 0x0e, 2, 0, 1, 0, 0x0b, 0x0b, 0x0b];
    let (module, _) = compile_function(&[I32], &[], &code);
    let branch = 6;
    let inner_end = 11;
    let outer_end = 12;
    let table = entries(&module);
    assert_eq!(table.len(), 3);
    assert_eq!(table[0].pc_delta, inner_end + 1 - branch);
    assert_eq!(table[1].pc_delta, outer_end + 1 - branch);
    assert_eq!(table[2].pc_delta, inner_end + 1 - branch);
    for (index, entry) in table.iter().enumerate() {
        assert_eq!(entry.stp_delta, 3 - index as i32);
    }
}

#[test]
fn branches_to_the_function_label_target_its_final_end() {
    // i32.const 7 br 0 end, returning i32
    let code = [0x41, 7, 0x0c, 0, 0x0b];
    let (module, _) = compile_function(&[], &[I32], &code);
    assert_eq!(
        entries(&module),
        [SideTableEntry {
            pc_delta: 2,
            stp_delta: 1,
            keep: 1,
            drop: 0,
        }]
    );
}

#[test]
fn counts_vector_values_as_two_slots() {
    // v128.const 0 v128.const 0 drop drop end
    let mut code = vec![0xfd, 0x0c];
    code.extend_from_slice(&[0; 16]);
    code.extend_from_slice(&[0xfd, 0x0c]);
    code.extend_from_slice(&[0; 16]);
    code.extend_from_slice(&[0x1a, 0x1a, 0x0b]);
    let (module, _) = compile_function(&[], &[], &code);
    assert_eq!(module.function_infos[0].max_stack_slots, 4);
}

#[test]
fn records_try_table_handlers() {
    // block (result i32) try_table (catch 0 0) i32.const 1 throw 0 end unreachable end drop end
    let code = [
        0x02, I32, 0x1f, 0x40, 1, 0x00, 0, 0, 0x41, 1, 0x08, 0, 0x0b, 0x00, 0x0b, 0x1a, 0x0b,
    ];
    let (module, start) = compile_function(&[], &[], &code);
    let info = &module.function_infos[0];
    assert_eq!(info.try_regions.len(), 1);
    let region = info.try_regions[0];
    assert_eq!(region.start - start, 8);
    assert_eq!(region.end - start, 12);
    assert_eq!(region.clause_count, 1);
    let clause = info.catch_clauses[0];
    assert_eq!(clause.kind, CatchKind::Catch);
    assert_eq!(clause.tag, 0);
    assert_eq!(clause.target_pc - start, 15);
    assert_eq!(clause.height, 0);
}

#[test]
fn rejects_malformed_and_invalid_functions() {
    // i32.add on an empty stack
    let error = compile(&module(&[], &[], &[0x6a, 0x0b])).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(error, Error::invalid("type mismatch"));
    // a missing end
    let error = compile(&module(&[], &[], &[0x01])).unwrap_err();
    assert!(error.is_malformed(), "{error}");
    // br to a label that does not exist
    let error = compile(&module(&[], &[], &[0x0c, 1, 0x0b])).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(error, Error::invalid("unknown label"));
}

/*

use libwasm_engine::compile;

fn leb(mut value: u32, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    loop {
        let byte = (value & 0x7f) as u8;
        value >>= 7;
        if value == 0 {
            out.push(byte);
            return;
        }
        out.push(byte | 0x80);
    }
}

fn section(id: u8, contents: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    out.push(id);
    leb(contents.len() as u32, out);
    out.extend_from_slice(contents);
}

/// A module with type 0 `(array (mut i32))` and one function of type `[] -> [(ref 0)]` with the given code, which
/// must end with the function's `end`.
fn array_module(code: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = b"\0asm\x01\0\0\0".to_vec();
    section(1, &[2, 0x5e, 0x7f, 0x01, 0x60, 0, 1, 0x64, 0], &mut bytes);
    section(3, &[1, 1], &mut bytes);
    let mut body = vec![0];
    body.extend_from_slice(code);
    let mut contents = vec![1];
    leb(body.len() as u32, &mut contents);
    contents.extend_from_slice(&body);
    section(10, &contents, &mut bytes);
    bytes
}

fn array_new_fixed(count: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut code = vec![0xfb, 0x08, 0];
    leb(count, &mut code);
    code
}

#[test]
fn array_new_fixed_in_unreachable_code_takes_any_count_at_once() {
    // Each of the 2^32 - 1 operands would be a pop of the polymorphic stack, which took seconds.
    let mut code = vec![0x00];
    code.extend(array_new_fixed(u32::MAX));
    code.push(0x0b);
    let start = std::time::Instant::now();
    assert!(compile(&array_module(&code)).is_ok());
    assert!(start.elapsed() < std::time::Duration::from_secs(1));

    // The operands that are on the stack are still checked.
    let mut code = vec![0x00, 0x42, 0x00];
    code.extend(array_new_fixed(u32::MAX));
    code.push(0x0b);
    assert!(compile(&array_module(&code)).is_err());
}

#[test]
fn array_new_fixed_needs_its_operands_in_reachable_code() {
    let mut code = vec![0x41, 0x01, 0x41, 0x02];
    code.extend(array_new_fixed(2));
    code.push(0x0b);
    assert!(compile(&array_module(&code)).is_ok());

    let mut code = vec![0x41, 0x01];
    code.extend(array_new_fixed(2));
    code.push(0x0b);
    assert!(compile(&array_module(&code)).is_err());
}

/*

//! WASI's descriptors and its capability model, through the functions a guest imports.

#![cfg(unix)]

use libwasm_engine::runtime::{ExternValue, InstanceAddress, Store, Value};
use libwasm_engine::wasi::{MODULE_NAME, Preopen, Wasi};
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::Arc;

const ERRNO_SUCCESS: i32 = 0;
const ERRNO_BADF: i32 = 8;

struct Guest {
    store: Store,
    instance: InstanceAddress,
}

impl Guest {
    fn new(preopens: Vec<Preopen>) -> Self {
        let path = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("tests/fixtures/wasi_calls.wasm");
        let module = Arc::new(libwasm_engine::compile(&std::fs::read(path).unwrap()).unwrap());
        let mut store = Store::new();
        let wasi = Rc::new(Wasi::new(Vec::new(), Vec::new(), preopens));
        let mut imports = Vec::new();
        for import in &module.imports {
            assert_eq!(import.module, MODULE_NAME);
            let function = wasi.allocate_function(&mut store, &import.name).unwrap();
            imports.push(ExternValue::Function(function));
        }
        let instance = store.instantiate(module, &imports).unwrap();
        let Some(ExternValue::Memory(memory)) = store.instance(instance).export("memory") else {
            panic!("no memory export");
        };
        wasi.set_memory(memory);
        Self { store, instance }
    }

    fn call(&mut self, name: &str, arguments: &[Value]) -> i32 {
        let Some(ExternValue::Function(function)) = self.store.instance(self.instance).export(name) else {
            panic!("no function export {name}");
        };
        match self.store.invoke(function, arguments).unwrap()[..] {
            [Value::I32(errno)] => errno,
            ref other => panic!("{name} returned {other:?}"),
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn closing_standard_streams_keeps_the_hosts_open() {
    let mut guest = Guest::new(Vec::new());
    assert_eq!(guest.call("fd_close", &[Value::I32(1)]), ERRNO_SUCCESS);
    // The guest's descriptor is gone, the host's standard output is not.
    assert_eq!(guest.call("fd_close", &[Value::I32(1)]), ERRNO_BADF);
    assert_eq!(
        guest.call(
            "fd_write",
            &[Value::I32(1), Value::I32(0), Value::I32(0), Value::I32(64)]
        ),
        ERRNO_BADF
    );
    assert!(unsafe { libc::fcntl(1, libc::F_GETFD) } >= 0);
}

const ERRNO_LOOP: i32 = 32;
const ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE: i32 = 76;
const LOOKUP_SYMLINK_FOLLOW: i32 = 1;
const OFLAGS_CREAT: i32 = 1;
const RIGHTS_FD_READ: i64 = 1 << 1;

/// A directory tree for sandbox tests, removed afterwards:
///   root/secret.txt
///   root/sandbox/inside.txt, sub/, link_in -> inside.txt, link_out -> ../secret.txt, link_absolute -> <secret.txt>,
///   sub/link_up -> ../inside.txt, sub/link_out -> ../../secret.txt
struct Tree(std::path::PathBuf);

impl Tree {
    fn new(name: &str) -> Self {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("libwasm-wasi-{name}-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
        let sandbox = root.join("sandbox");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(sandbox.join("sub")).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(root.join("secret.txt"), "secret").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(sandbox.join("inside.txt"), "inside").unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink("inside.txt", sandbox.join("link_in")).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink("../secret.txt", sandbox.join("link_out")).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(root.join("secret.txt"), sandbox.join("link_absolute")).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink("../inside.txt", sandbox.join("sub/link_up")).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink("../../secret.txt", sandbox.join("sub/link_out")).unwrap();
        Self(root)
    }

    fn guest(&self) -> Guest {
        let sandbox = self.0.join("sandbox").to_str().unwrap().to_string();
        Guest::new(vec![Preopen::new(sandbox, "/sandbox".to_string())])
    }
}

impl Drop for Tree {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
    }
}

impl Guest {
    /// Writes `path` at address 16, and returns its length.
    fn path(&mut self, path: &str) -> i32 {
        let Some(ExternValue::Memory(memory)) = self.store.instance(self.instance).export("memory") else {
            panic!("no memory export");
        };
        self.store.memory_mut(memory).bytes_mut()[16..16 + path.len()].copy_from_slice(path.as_bytes());
        path.len() as i32
    }

    fn open(&mut self, fd: i32, path: &str, follow: bool, oflags: i32) -> i32 {
        let length = self.path(path);
        let lookup = if follow { LOOKUP_SYMLINK_FOLLOW } else { 0 };
        self.call(
            "path_open",
            &[
                Value::I32(fd),
                Value::I32(lookup),
                Value::I32(16),
                Value::I32(length),
                Value::I32(oflags),
                Value::I64(RIGHTS_FD_READ),
                Value::I64(0),
                Value::I32(0),
                Value::I32(0),
            ],
        )
    }
}

#[test]
fn paths_stay_beneath_their_preopen() {
    let tree = Tree::new("open");
    let mut guest = tree.guest();
    for path in [
        "inside.txt",
        "./inside.txt",
        "sub/../inside.txt",
        "sub/",
        "sub/link_up",
        "link_in",
    ] {
        assert_eq!(guest.open(3, path, true, 0), ERRNO_SUCCESS, "{path}");
    }
    for path in [
        "../secret.txt",
        "sub/../../secret.txt",
        "..",
        "/etc/passwd",
        &tree.0.join("secret.txt").to_string_lossy(),
        "link_out",
        "link_absolute",
        "sub/link_out",
        "link_out/../sandbox/inside.txt",
    ] {
        assert_eq!(guest.open(3, path, true, 0), ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE, "{path}");
    }
    // Without following, a symbolic link in the last place is not opened.
    assert_eq!(guest.open(3, "link_out", false, 0), ERRNO_LOOP);
    // A link in the middle is followed, but not out.
    assert_eq!(guest.open(3, "link_out/x", false, 0), ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE);
    // Nothing is created outside either.
    assert_eq!(guest.open(3, "../created.txt", false, OFLAGS_CREAT), ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE);
    assert!(!tree.0.join("created.txt").exists());
}

#[test]
fn descriptors_the_guest_does_not_have_resolve_nothing() {
    let tree = Tree::new("badf");
    let mut guest = tree.guest();
    // These resolved against the host's working directory before.
    assert_eq!(guest.open(99, "inside.txt", true, 0), ERRNO_BADF);
    let length = guest.path("created");
    assert_eq!(
        guest.call(
            "path_create_directory",
            &[Value::I32(99), Value::I32(16), Value::I32(length)]
        ),
        ERRNO_BADF
    );
}

#[test]
fn directories_and_status_stay_beneath_their_preopen() {
    let tree = Tree::new("other");
    let mut guest = tree.guest();
    let length = guest.path("../escaped");
    assert_eq!(
        guest.call(
            "path_create_directory",
            &[Value::I32(3), Value::I32(16), Value::I32(length)]
        ),
        ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE
    );
    assert!(!tree.0.join("escaped").exists());
    let length = guest.path("sub/made");
    assert_eq!(
        guest.call(
            "path_create_directory",
            &[Value::I32(3), Value::I32(16), Value::I32(length)]
        ),
        ERRNO_SUCCESS
    );
    assert!(tree.0.join("sandbox/sub/made").is_dir());
    for (path, follow, errno) in [
        ("inside.txt", true, ERRNO_SUCCESS),
        ("link_in", true, ERRNO_SUCCESS),
        ("link_out", false, ERRNO_SUCCESS),
        ("link_out", true, ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE),
        ("../secret.txt", false, ERRNO_NOTCAPABLE),
    ] {
        let length = guest.path(path);
        let lookup = if follow { LOOKUP_SYMLINK_FOLLOW } else { 0 };
        let arguments = [
            Value::I32(3),
            Value::I32(lookup),
            Value::I32(16),
            Value::I32(length),
            Value::I32(1024),
        ];
        assert_eq!(guest.call("path_filestat_get", &arguments), errno, "{path}");
    }
}
