//! Runs a module's entry function in two stores, one interpreted and one where the runtime compiles every function
//! (`LIBWASM_JIT=eager` unless set otherwise), and compares the results, traps, exit codes, memories, tables and
//! globals afterwards. The imports are deterministic: WASI, with `clock_time_get` and `random_get` replaced by
//! counters, and any other function import returns a clock in milliseconds of its result type, 100 * calls^2, so that
//! both stores see the same. A case that runs longer than `--timeout SECONDS` (300) ends the process with a failure.
//! `--compiled-only` runs and times only the compiled store, for timing.
//!
//! ```text
//! bench_check [--timeout SECONDS] [--compiled-only] MODULE ENTRY [MODULE ENTRY]...
//! ```

#[path = "../tests/harness/mod.rs"]
mod harness;

use harness::script::{outcome, same_outcome, state_difference};
use libwasm_engine::module::ImportDescription;
use libwasm_engine::runtime::{ExternValue, HostCallback, InstanceAddress, MemoryAddress, Store, Value};
use libwasm_engine::types::ValType;
use libwasm_engine::wasi::Wasi;
use std::cell::Cell;
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

struct Instance {
    store: Store,
    instance: InstanceAddress,
    wasi: Rc<Wasi>,
}

fn instantiate(module: &Arc<libwasm_engine::Module>, interpreted: bool) -> Option<Instance> {
    let mut store = Store::new();
    if interpreted {
        store.disable_jit();
    }
    let wasi = Rc::new(Wasi::new(vec!["bench".to_string()], Vec::new(), Vec::new()));
    let memory: Rc<Cell<Option<MemoryAddress>>> = Rc::new(Cell::new(None));
    let counter = Rc::new(Cell::new(0u64));
    let mut imports = Vec::new();
    for import in &module.imports {
        let ImportDescription::Function(type_index) = import.description else {
            eprintln!("{}.{}: only function imports are provided", import.module, import.name);
            return None;
        };
        let ty = module.types[type_index as usize].as_func()?.clone();
        let function = match (import.module.as_str(), import.name.as_str()) {
            ("wasi_snapshot_preview1", "clock_time_get" | "random_get") => {
                let (memory, counter, name) = (memory.clone(), counter.clone(), import.name.clone());
                let callback: HostCallback = Rc::new(move |store: &mut Store, arguments: &[Value]| {
                    let Some(memory) = memory.get() else {
                        return Ok(vec![Value::I32(8)]);
                    };
                    let bytes = store.memory_mut(memory).bytes_mut();
                    let argument = |index: usize| match arguments[index] {
                        Value::I32(value) => value as u32 as usize,
                        _ => 0,
                    };
                    counter.set(counter.get() + 1_000_000);
                    if name == "clock_time_get" {
                        let at = argument(2);
                        bytes[at..at + 8].copy_from_slice(&counter.get().to_le_bytes());
                    } else {
                        for (offset, byte) in bytes[argument(0)..argument(0) + argument(1)].iter_mut().enumerate() {
                            *byte = offset as u8;
                        }
                    }
                    Ok(vec![Value::I32(0)])
                });
                store.allocate_host_function(ty, callback)
            }
            ("wasi_snapshot_preview1", name) => wasi.allocate_function(&mut store, name)?,
            _ => {
                let results = ty.results.clone();
                let calls = Rc::new(Cell::new(0u64));
                let callback: HostCallback = Rc::new(move |_: &mut Store, _: &[Value]| {
                    // NB: A clock that advances more with every call, so that a benchmark that runs until enough
                    //     time has passed, like coremark, stops after a few rounds.
                    calls.set(calls.get() + 1);
                    let now = 100 * calls.get() * calls.get();
                    Ok(results
                        .iter()
                        .map(|result| match result {
                            ValType::I32 => Value::I32(now as i32),
                            ValType::I64 => Value::I64(now as i64),
                            ValType::F32 => Value::F32((now as f32).to_bits()),
                            ValType::F64 => Value::F64((now as f64).to_bits()),
                            other => Value::default_for(*other),
                        })
                        .collect())
                });
                store.allocate_host_function(ty, callback)
            }
        };
        imports.push(ExternValue::Function(function));
    }
    let instance = match store.instantiate(module.clone(), &imports) {
        Ok(instance) => instance,
        Err(error) => {
            eprintln!("instantiation failed: {error:?}");
            return None;
        }
    };
    if let Some(ExternValue::Memory(exported)) = store.instance(instance).export("memory") {
        wasi.set_memory(exported);
        memory.set(Some(exported));
    }
    Some(Instance { store, instance, wasi })
}

fn main() {
    harness::run_main(checked_main);
}

fn checked_main() {
    if std::env::var_os("LIBWASM_JIT").is_none() {
        // SAFETY: Nothing else runs yet.
        unsafe { std::env::set_var("LIBWASM_JIT", "eager") };
    }
    let mut arguments = std::env::args().skip(1).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let mut timeout = 300;
    if arguments.first().is_some_and(|argument| argument == "--timeout") {
        timeout = arguments[1].parse().expect("--timeout SECONDS");
        arguments.drain(..2);
    }
    // For timing: runs only the compiled store, and compares nothing.
    let compiled_only = arguments.first().is_some_and(|argument| argument == "--compiled-only");
    if compiled_only {
        arguments.drain(..1);
    }
    // A watchdog, so that a case that hangs cannot hold the machine.
    static DEADLINE: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(u64::MAX);
    static CURRENT: Mutex<String> = Mutex::new(String::new());
    std::thread::spawn(|| {
        loop {
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1));
            let now = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs();
            if now > DEADLINE.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
                println!("TIMEOUT   {}", CURRENT.lock().unwrap());
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
    });
    let mut failures = 0;
    for pair in arguments.chunks(2) {
        let [path, entry] = pair else {
            eprintln!("usage: bench_check MODULE ENTRY [MODULE ENTRY]...");
            std::process::exit(2);
        };
        *CURRENT.lock().unwrap() = path.clone();
        let now = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs();
        DEADLINE.store(now + timeout, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let bytes = std::fs::read(path).expect("the module can be read");
        let module = Arc::new(libwasm_engine::compile(&bytes).expect("the module validates"));
        let (Some(mut interpreted), Some(mut jit)) = (instantiate(&module, true), instantiate(&module, false)) else {
            failures += 1;
            continue;
        };
        let run = |instance: &mut Instance| {
            let Some(ExternValue::Function(function)) = instance.store.instance(instance.instance).export(entry) else {
                panic!("{path} exports no function {entry}");
            };
            let start = std::time::Instant::now();
            let outcome = outcome(instance.store.invoke(function, &[]));
            (outcome, start.elapsed())
        };
        let name = std::path::Path::new(path)
            .file_name()
            .unwrap()
            .to_string_lossy()
            .into_owned();
        if compiled_only {
            let (actual, jit_time) = run(&mut jit);
            println!(
                "timed     {name} ({actual:?}; {:.3} s compiled)",
                jit_time.as_secs_f64()
            );
            continue;
        }
        let (expected, interpreted_time) = run(&mut interpreted);
        let (actual, jit_time) = run(&mut jit);
        let mut problems = Vec::new();
        if !same_outcome(&expected, &actual) {
            problems.push(format!("interpreter {expected:?}, JIT {actual:?}"));
        }
        if interpreted.wasi.exit_code() != jit.wasi.exit_code() {
            problems.push(format!(
                "exit codes {:?} and {:?}",
                interpreted.wasi.exit_code(),
                jit.wasi.exit_code()
            ));
        }
        if let Some(difference) = state_difference(&interpreted.store, interpreted.instance, &jit.store, jit.instance) {
            problems.push(difference);
        }
        if problems.is_empty() {
            println!(
                "same      {name} ({expected:?}, exit {:?}; {:.2} s interpreted, {:.2} s compiled)",
                jit.wasi.exit_code(),
                interpreted_time.as_secs_f64(),
                jit_time.as_secs_f64()
            );
        } else {
            failures += 1;
            println!("DIFFERENT {name}: {}", problems.join("; "));
        }
    }
    if failures > 0 {
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/JIT/examples/compile_all.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Compiles every function of WebAssembly modules and reports how long it took.
//!
//! ```text
//! compile_all [--threads N] [--runs N] [--verify] [--stress-registers] [--no-licm] [--quiet]
//!             [--dump-ir FUNCTION [--osr PC]] [--dump-asm] MODULE|DIRECTORY...
//! ```
//!
//! A first pass finds the functions the JIT compiles; every measurement after it compiles only those, so that time
//! spent on functions that fail does not count. CPU time is the sum of every compile thread's own CPU time
//! (CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID), taken once per thread after its last compile, the best of `--runs` runs, on one thread and on
//! `--threads`. A pass with phase timers (time stamp counter ticks) gives the time of each phase, the slowest
//! function per byte among those of at least 1 KiB, the cost of the smallest functions, and the nodes, stack slots
//! and moves per byte. Module decoding and validation are not included.

use libwasm_jit::{CompileContext, CompileRequest, Options, PHASES, RuntimeInfo, Stats};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

/// A runtime for code that never runs.
const RUNTIME: RuntimeInfo = RuntimeInfo {
    trap_exit: 0x7fff_0000_1000,
    memory_grow: 0x7fff_0000_2000,
    table_grow: 0x7fff_0000_3000,
    call_host: 0x7fff_0000_4000,
    allocate: 0x7fff_0000_5000,
    wait: 0x7fff_0000_6000,
    notify: 0x7fff_0000_7000,
    allocate_exception: 0x7fff_0000_8000,
    throw: 0x7fff_0000_9000,
};

/// Functions at least this big count for the slowest function per byte.
const LARGE_FUNCTION: u32 = 1024;
/// Functions at most this big count for the cost per function.
const SMALL_FUNCTION: u32 = 32;

fn thread_cpu_ns() -> u64 {
    let mut time = libc::timespec { tv_sec: 0, tv_nsec: 0 };
    unsafe { libc::clock_gettime(libc::CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID, &raw mut time) };
    time.tv_sec as u64 * 1_000_000_000 + time.tv_nsec as u64
}

/// Time stamp counter ticks per nanosecond.
fn ticks_per_ns() -> f64 {
    let (start, start_ticks) = (Instant::now(), libwasm_jit::ticks());
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
    let ticks = libwasm_jit::ticks() - start_ticks;
    ticks as f64 / start.elapsed().as_nanos() as f64
}

struct Arguments {
    threads: usize,
    runs: usize,
    options: Options,
    dump: Option<u32>,
    /// With --dump-ir, the OSR compile at the loop at this module offset.
    osr: Option<u32>,
    quiet: bool,
    paths: Vec<String>,
}

fn parse_arguments() -> Arguments {
    let mut arguments = Arguments {
        threads: 1,
        runs: 3,
        options: Options::default(),
        dump: None,
        osr: None,
        quiet: false,
        paths: Vec::new(),
    };
    let mut iterator = std::env::args().skip(1);
    while let Some(argument) = iterator.next() {
        match argument.as_str() {
            "--threads" => arguments.threads = iterator.next().and_then(|n| n.parse().ok()).expect("--threads N"),
            "--runs" => arguments.runs = iterator.next().and_then(|n| n.parse().ok()).expect("--runs N"),
            "--verify" => arguments.options.verify_ir = true,
            "--stress-registers" => arguments.options.stress_registers = true,
            "--no-licm" => arguments.options.no_licm = true,
            "--quiet" => arguments.quiet = true,
            "--dump-asm" => arguments.options.dump_asm = true,
            "--osr" => arguments.osr = Some(iterator.next().and_then(|n| n.parse().ok()).expect("--osr PC")),
            "--dump-ir" => {
                arguments.dump = Some(
                    iterator
                        .next()
                        .and_then(|n| n.parse().ok())
                        .expect("--dump-ir FUNCTION"),
                );
            }
            _ => arguments.paths.push(argument),
        }
    }
    arguments
}

fn module_paths(paths: &[String]) -> Vec<std::path::PathBuf> {
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    for path in paths {
        let path = std::path::PathBuf::from(path);
        if path.is_dir() {
            let mut entries = std::fs::read_dir(&path)
                .expect("a readable directory")
                .filter_map(|entry| entry.ok().map(|entry| entry.path()))
                .filter(|path| path.extension().is_some_and(|extension| extension == "wasm"))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
            entries.sort();
            result.extend(entries);
        } else {
            result.push(path);
        }
    }
    result
}

/// Compiles `functions` (counting imports) of `module` on `threads` threads and returns the CPU time they took.
fn timed_compile(module: &Arc<libwasm_engine::Module>, functions: &[u32], threads: usize, options: Options) -> u64 {
    let next = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    std::thread::scope(|scope| {
        let handles = (0..threads)
            .map(|_| {
                scope.spawn(|| {
                    let mut context = CompileContext::default();
                    let start = thread_cpu_ns();
                    loop {
                        let index = next.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                        let Some(&function) = functions.get(index) else {
                            break;
                        };
                        let request = CompileRequest {
                            stack_limit: 0,
                            osr: None,
                            module: module.clone(),
                            function,
                            runtime: RUNTIME,
                            options,
                        };
                        libwasm_jit::compile(&mut context, &request).expect("it compiled before");
                    }
                    thread_cpu_ns() - start
                })
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        handles.into_iter().map(|handle| handle.join().unwrap()).sum()
    })
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Totals {
    functions: usize,
    compiled: usize,
    code_bytes: u64,
    compiled_bytes: u64,
    cpu_ns: u64,
    threaded_cpu_ns: u64,
    failures: BTreeMap<&'static str, usize>,
}

fn main() {
    let arguments = parse_arguments();
    let ticks_per_ns = ticks_per_ns();
    let mut totals = Totals::default();
    for path in module_paths(&arguments.paths) {
        let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(&path) else {
            continue;
        };
        let Ok(module) = libwasm_engine::compile(&bytes) else {
            continue;
        };
        let module = Arc::new(module);
        let first = module.imported_function_count;
        if let Some(function) = arguments.dump {
            let mut context = CompileContext::default();
            let mut options = arguments.options;
            options.dump_ir = !arguments.quiet;
            options.stats = true;
            let request = CompileRequest {
                stack_limit: 0,
                osr: arguments.osr,
                module: module.clone(),
                function,
                runtime: RUNTIME,
                options,
            };
            // NB: The phases are the best of `--runs` compiles, the first of which also dumps.
            let mut best = None::<Vec<u64>>;
            for _ in 1..arguments.runs {
                let quiet = CompileRequest {
                    stack_limit: 0,
                    osr: None,
                    module: module.clone(),
                    function,
                    runtime: RUNTIME,
                    options: Options {
                        dump_ir: false,
                        ..options
                    },
                };
                if let Ok(compiled) = libwasm_jit::compile(&mut context, &quiet) {
                    let ticks = compiled.stats.ticks.to_vec();
                    best = Some(match best {
                        Some(best) => best.iter().zip(&ticks).map(|(a, b)| *a.min(b)).collect(),
                        None => ticks,
                    });
                }
            }
            match libwasm_jit::compile(&mut context, &request) {
                Ok(compiled) => {
                    let body = &module.code[(function - first) as usize];
                    let bytes = f64::from(body.code.end - body.code.start);
                    let ticks = match best {
                        Some(best) => best.iter().zip(compiled.stats.ticks).map(|(a, b)| *a.min(&b)).collect(),
                        None => compiled.stats.ticks.to_vec(),
                    };
                    let phases = libwasm_jit::PHASES
                        .iter()
                        .zip(ticks)
                        .map(|(phase, ticks)| format!("{phase} {:.1}", ticks as f64 / ticks_per_ns / bytes))
                        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                    println!(
                        "function {function}: {bytes} bytes; phases (ns/byte): {}; {} nodes, {} slots, {} moves",
                        phases.join(", "),
                        compiled.stats.nodes,
                        compiled.stats.slots,
                        compiled.stats.moves
                    );
                    println!("{}", compiled.dump.unwrap_or_default());
                }
                Err(failure) => println!("{failure:?}"),
            }
            continue;
        }

        // Which functions compile.
        let mut context = CompileContext::default();
        let mut compiled = Vec::new();
        let mut failures: BTreeMap<&'static str, usize> = BTreeMap::new();
        for index in 0..module.code.len() as u32 {
            let request = CompileRequest {
                stack_limit: 0,
                osr: None,
                module: module.clone(),
                function: first + index,
                runtime: RUNTIME,
                options: arguments.options,
            };
            match libwasm_jit::compile(&mut context, &request) {
                Ok(_) => compiled.push(first + index),
                Err(failure) => *failures.entry(failure.reason()).or_default() += 1,
            }
        }
        let size = |function: u32| {
            let body = &module.code[(function - first) as usize].code;
            body.end - body.start
        };

        // The phase timers, the slowest functions and the counts. Each function's time is its best of the runs, so
        // that a preemption does not make it the slowest.
        let mut stats = Stats::default();
        let mut best_ns = vec![f64::MAX; compiled.len()];
        let options = Options {
            stats: true,
            ..arguments.options
        };
        for run in 0..arguments.runs.max(1) {
            for (position, &function) in compiled.iter().enumerate() {
                let request = CompileRequest {
                    stack_limit: 0,
                    osr: None,
                    module: module.clone(),
                    function,
                    runtime: RUNTIME,
                    options,
                };
                let start = libwasm_jit::ticks();
                let result = libwasm_jit::compile(&mut context, &request).expect("it compiled before");
                let ns = (libwasm_jit::ticks() - start) as f64 / ticks_per_ns;
                best_ns[position] = best_ns[position].min(ns);
                if run > 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                for (total, phase) in stats.ticks.iter_mut().zip(result.stats.ticks) {
                    *total += phase;
                }
                stats.nodes += result.stats.nodes;
                stats.slots += result.stats.slots;
                stats.moves += result.stats.moves;
                stats.hoisted += result.stats.hoisted;
            }
        }
        let mut worst = (0.0, 0, 0);
        let mut small = Vec::new();
        for (position, &function) in compiled.iter().enumerate() {
            let (bytes, ns) = (size(function), best_ns[position]);
            if bytes >= LARGE_FUNCTION && ns / f64::from(bytes) > worst.0 {
                worst = (ns / f64::from(bytes), function, bytes);
            }
            if bytes <= SMALL_FUNCTION {
                small.push(ns);
            }
        }
        small.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);

        // CPU time.
        let best = |threads: usize| {
            (0..arguments.runs)
                .map(|_| timed_compile(&module, &compiled, threads, arguments.options))
                .min()
                .unwrap_or(0)
        };
        let cpu = best(1);
        let threaded = if arguments.threads > 1 {
            best(arguments.threads)
        } else {
            cpu
        };

        let code_bytes = module
            .code
            .iter()
            .map(|body| u64::from(body.code.end - body.code.start))
            .sum::<u64>();
        let compiled_bytes = compiled.iter().map(|function| u64::from(size(*function))).sum::<u64>();
        totals.functions += module.code.len();
        totals.compiled += compiled.len();
        totals.code_bytes += code_bytes;
        totals.compiled_bytes += compiled_bytes;
        totals.cpu_ns += cpu;
        totals.threaded_cpu_ns += threaded;
        for (what, count) in &failures {
            *totals.failures.entry(what).or_default() += count;
        }
        if arguments.quiet {
            continue;
        }
        let per_byte = |ns: f64| ns / compiled_bytes.max(1) as f64;
        println!("{}", path.display());
        println!(
            "  compiled: {}/{} functions ({:.1}%), {}/{} bytes ({:.1}%)",
            compiled.len(),
            module.code.len(),
            100.0 * compiled.len() as f64 / module.code.len().max(1) as f64,
            compiled_bytes,
            code_bytes,
            100.0 * compiled_bytes as f64 / code_bytes.max(1) as f64
        );
        println!(
            "  CPU: {:.3} ms on 1 thread, {:.1} ns/byte; {:.3} ms on {} threads, {:.1} ns/byte",
            cpu as f64 / 1e6,
            per_byte(cpu as f64),
            threaded as f64 / 1e6,
            arguments.threads,
            per_byte(threaded as f64)
        );
        let phases = PHASES
            .iter()
            .zip(stats.ticks)
            .map(|(name, ticks)| format!("{name} {:.1}", per_byte(ticks as f64 / ticks_per_ns)))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        println!("  phases (ns/byte): {}", phases.join(", "));
        if worst.2 > 0 {
            println!(
                "  slowest function of {LARGE_FUNCTION}+ bytes: {:.1} ns/byte (function {}, {} bytes)",
                worst.0, worst.1, worst.2
            );
        }
        if !small.is_empty() {
            println!(
                "  functions of up to {SMALL_FUNCTION} bytes: {:.0} ns median, {} of them",
                small[small.len() / 2],
                small.len()
            );
        }
        println!(
            "  per byte: {:.2} nodes, {:.3} slots, {:.3} moves; {} nodes hoisted out of loops",
            stats.nodes as f64 / compiled_bytes.max(1) as f64,
            stats.slots as f64 / compiled_bytes.max(1) as f64,
            stats.moves as f64 / compiled_bytes.max(1) as f64,
            stats.hoisted
        );
        for (what, count) in &failures {
            println!("  unsupported: {count} x {what}");
        }
    }
    println!(
        "total: {}/{} functions, {}/{} bytes compiled, {:.3} ms CPU on 1 thread ({:.1} ns/byte), {:.3} ms on {}",
        totals.compiled,
        totals.functions,
        totals.compiled_bytes,
        totals.code_bytes,
        totals.cpu_ns as f64 / 1e6,
        totals.cpu_ns as f64 / totals.compiled_bytes.max(1) as f64,
        totals.threaded_cpu_ns as f64 / 1e6,
        arguments.threads
    );
    for (what, count) in &totals.failures {
        println!("  unsupported: {count} x {what}");
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/JIT/examples/osr_check.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Compiles every function of modules as an OSR continuation at each of its loops, with the IR and register
//! allocation verified, and reports what fails. Loops that cannot be OSR entries (see `CompileFailure::NoOsrEntry`) are
//! skipped.
//!
//! ```text
//! osr_check [--threads N] [--stress-registers] [--dump FUNCTION:PC] MODULE...
//! ```

use libwasm_jit::decode::{Decoder, Instruction};
use libwasm_jit::{CompileContext, CompileFailure, CompileRequest, Options, RuntimeInfo};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};

const RUNTIME: RuntimeInfo = RuntimeInfo {
    trap_exit: 0x7fff_0000_1000,
    memory_grow: 0x7fff_0000_2000,
    table_grow: 0x7fff_0000_3000,
    call_host: 0x7fff_0000_4000,
    allocate: 0x7fff_0000_5000,
    wait: 0x7fff_0000_6000,
    notify: 0x7fff_0000_7000,
    allocate_exception: 0x7fff_0000_8000,
    throw: 0x7fff_0000_9000,
};

fn main() {
    let mut threads = 1;
    let mut options = Options {
        verify_ir: true,
        ..Options::default()
    };
    let mut dump = None;
    let mut paths = Vec::new();
    let mut arguments = std::env::args().skip(1);
    while let Some(argument) = arguments.next() {
        match argument.as_str() {
            "--threads" => threads = arguments.next().and_then(|n| n.parse().ok()).expect("--threads N"),
            "--stress-registers" => options.stress_registers = true,
            "--dump" => {
                let value = arguments.next().expect("--dump FUNCTION:PC");
                let (function, pc) = value.split_once(':').expect("--dump FUNCTION:PC");
                dump = Some((
                    function.parse::<u32>().expect("a function index"),
                    pc.parse::<u32>().expect("a module offset"),
                ));
            }
            _ => paths.push(argument),
        }
    }
    let mut failures = 0;
    for path in &paths {
        let bytes = std::fs::read(path).expect("a readable module");
        let module = Arc::new(libwasm_engine::compile(&bytes).expect("a valid module"));
        if let Some((function, pc)) = dump {
            let mut context = CompileContext::default();
            let request = CompileRequest {
                stack_limit: 0,
                module: module.clone(),
                function,
                runtime: RUNTIME,
                options: Options {
                    dump_ir: true,
                    dump_asm: true,
                    ..options
                },
                osr: Some(pc),
            };
            match libwasm_jit::compile(&mut context, &request) {
                Ok(compiled) => println!("{}", compiled.dump.unwrap_or_default()),
                Err(failure) => println!("{failure:?}"),
            }
            continue;
        }
        let first = module.imported_function_count;
        let count = module.code.len() as u32;
        let next = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let compiled = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let failed = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            for _ in 0..threads {
                scope.spawn(|| {
                    let mut context = CompileContext::default();
                    loop {
                        let index = next.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) as u32;
                        if index >= count {
                            break;
                        }
                        let body = &module.code[index as usize];
                        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&module.bytes, body.code.start as usize, body.code.end as usize);
                        let mut loops = Vec::new();
                        while !decoder.is_at_end() {
                            let pc = decoder.position() as u32;
                            if let Instruction::Loop(_) = decoder.decode() {
                                loops.push(pc);
                            }
                        }
                        for pc in loops {
                            let request = CompileRequest {
                                stack_limit: 0,
                                module: module.clone(),
                                function: first + index,
                                runtime: RUNTIME,
                                options,
                                osr: Some(pc),
                            };
                            let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
                                libwasm_jit::compile(&mut context, &request)
                            }));
                            match result {
                                Ok(Ok(_)) => {
                                    compiled.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                                }
                                Ok(Err(CompileFailure::NoOsrEntry { .. })) => {}
                                Ok(Err(failure)) => {
                                    failed.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                                    println!("FAIL {path} function {}:{pc}: {failure:?}", first + index);
                                }
                                Err(_) => {
                                    failed.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                                    println!("FAIL {path} function {}:{pc}: panicked", first + index);
                                    context = CompileContext::default();
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                });
            }
        });
        let failed = failed.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
        failures += failed;
        println!(
            "{path}: {} OSR compiles, {failed} failures",
            compiled.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
        );
    }
    if failures > 0 {
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/JIT/examples/smith_check.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Generates random modules in the subset the JIT compiles with `wasm-tools smith`, calls every exported function
//! the JIT compiled with random arguments, and compares results, traps, memories and globals with the interpreter.
//!
//! ```text
//! smith_check [--count N] [--seed S] [--keep DIRECTORY] [--wasm-tools PATH] [--stress-registers] [--no-licm]
//!     [--simd] [--features gc,threads,memory64,multi-memory]
//! ```
//!
//! `--features` turns on proposals besides the default ones, in every module. Modules that wait on shared memory are
//! skipped, since nothing would wake them. With GC, modules get less fuel, since the stores never free objects.

#[path = "../tests/harness/mod.rs"]
mod harness;

use harness::{CompiledModule, Outcome, TestBinding, function_index};
use libwasm_engine::runtime::{ExternValue, Store, Trap, Value};
use libwasm_engine::types::ValType;
use libwasm_jit::Options;
use std::io::Write;
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::sync::Arc;

// NB: NaN payloads may differ between implementations, and reinterpreting them makes the difference visible, so
//     the modules canonicalize them.
const SMITH_FLAGS: &[&str] = &[
    "--ensure-termination",
    "--canonicalize-nans",
    "true",
    "--fuel",
    "1000000",
    "--max-imports",
    "0",
    "--max-tables",
    "4",
    "--max-memories",
    "1",
    "--max-memory32-bytes",
    "262144",
    "--max-memory64-bytes",
    "262144",
    "--bulk-memory-enabled",
    "true",
    "--reference-types-enabled",
    "true",
    "--exceptions-enabled",
    "false",
    "--gc-enabled",
    "false",
    "--tail-call-enabled",
    "true",
    "--threads-enabled",
    "false",
    "--memory64-enabled",
    "false",
    "--custom-page-sizes-enabled",
    "false",
    "--wide-arithmetic-enabled",
    "false",
    "--multi-value-enabled",
    "true",
    "--saturating-float-to-int-enabled",
    "true",
    "--sign-extension-ops-enabled",
    "true",
    "--export-everything",
    "true",
    "--min-funcs",
    "4",
    "--max-funcs",
    "40",
];

/// xorshift64*.
struct Random(u64);

impl Random {
    fn next(&mut self) -> u64 {
        self.0 ^= self.0 >> 12;
        self.0 ^= self.0 << 25;
        self.0 ^= self.0 >> 27;
        self.0.wrapping_mul(0x2545_f491_4f6c_dd1d)
    }

    fn below(&mut self, bound: u64) -> u64 {
        self.next() % bound
    }

    fn bits(&mut self, width: u32) -> u64 {
        const SPECIAL: [u64; 8] = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 0xff, 0x7fff_ffff, 0x8000_0000];
        let bits = match self.below(4) {
            0 => SPECIAL[self.below(SPECIAL.len() as u64) as usize],
            1 => self.below(64),
            2 => self.next().wrapping_neg() & 0xffff,
            _ => self.next(),
        };
        if width == 32 { bits & 0xffff_ffff } else { bits }
    }

    fn argument(&mut self, ty: ValType) -> Option<Value> {
        Some(match ty {
            ValType::I32 => Value::I32(self.bits(32) as u32 as i32),
            ValType::I64 => Value::I64(self.bits(64) as i64),
            ValType::F32 => {
                const VALUES: [f32; 8] = [0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.5, 2147483648.0, f32::INFINITY, f32::NAN, 1e30];
                Value::F32(match self.below(3) {
                    0 => VALUES[self.below(8) as usize].to_bits(),
                    1 => (self.below(2000) as f32 - 1000.0).to_bits(),
                    _ => self.next() as u32,
                })
            }
            ValType::F64 => {
                const VALUES: [f64; 8] = [0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.5, 9.3e18, f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::NAN, 4294967296.0];
                Value::F64(match self.below(3) {
                    0 => VALUES[self.below(8) as usize].to_bits(),
                    1 => (self.below(2000) as f64 - 1000.0).to_bits(),
                    _ => self.next(),
                })
            }
            ValType::V128 => Value::V128(u128::from(self.bits(64)) | (u128::from(self.bits(64)) << 64)),
            ValType::Ref(reference) if reference.nullable => Value::Ref(0),
            ValType::Ref(_) => return None,
        })
    }
}

fn outcome(result: Result<Vec<Value>, Trap>) -> Outcome {
    match result {
        Ok(values) => Outcome::Values(values),
        Err(trap) => Outcome::Trap(trap.code()),
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Totals {
    modules: usize,
    functions: usize,
    compiled: usize,
    runnable: usize,
    cases: usize,
    failures: usize,
    not_compiled: usize,
    /// Why functions were not compiled, and how often.
    unsupported: std::collections::BTreeMap<&'static str, usize>,
}

fn main() {
    harness::run_main(checked_main);
}

fn checked_main() {
    let mut count = 100;
    let mut seed = 1u64;
    let mut keep = None;
    let mut stress_registers = false;
    let mut no_licm = false;
    let mut simd = false;
    let mut features: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut wasm_tools = std::env::var("HOME")
        .map(|home| format!("{home}/.cargo/bin/wasm-tools"))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let mut arguments = std::env::args().skip(1);
    while let Some(argument) = arguments.next() {
        match argument.as_str() {
            "--count" => {
                count = arguments
                    .next()
                    .and_then(|value| value.parse().ok())
                    .expect("--count N");
            }
            "--seed" => seed = arguments.next().and_then(|value| value.parse().ok()).expect("--seed S"),
            "--keep" => keep = arguments.next(),
            "--wasm-tools" => wasm_tools = arguments.next().expect("--wasm-tools PATH"),
            "--stress-registers" => stress_registers = true,
            "--no-licm" => no_licm = true,
            "--simd" => simd = true,
            "--features" => {
                features = arguments
                    .next()
                    .expect("--features LIST")
                    .split(',')
                    .map(str::to_string)
                    .collect();
            }
            _ => panic!("unknown argument {argument}"),
        }
    }
    let simd_flag = |iteration: usize| {
        if simd || iteration.is_multiple_of(2) {
            "true"
        } else {
            "false"
        }
    };
    let mut flags: Vec<&str> = SMITH_FLAGS.to_vec();
    let mut set_flag = |name: &str, value: &'static str| {
        let position = flags.iter().position(|flag| *flag == name).expect("a known flag");
        flags[position + 1] = value;
    };
    for feature in &features {
        match feature.as_str() {
            "gc" => {
                set_flag("--gc-enabled", "true");
                // NB: The stores of these tests never free GC objects, so allocating loops run out of memory with
                //     the usual fuel.
                set_flag("--fuel", "20000");
            }
            "threads" => set_flag("--threads-enabled", "true"),
            "memory64" => set_flag("--memory64-enabled", "true"),
            "multi-memory" => set_flag("--max-memories", "4"),
            _ => panic!("unknown feature {feature}"),
        }
    }
    let mut random = Random(seed.wrapping_mul(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15) | 1);
    let mut totals = Totals::default();
    for iteration in 0..count {
        let input = (0..1000 + random.below(30000))
            .map(|_| random.next() as u8)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let mut child = Command::new(&wasm_tools)
            .arg("smith")
            .args(&flags)
            // NB: Every other module without SIMD, unless --simd says otherwise.
            .args(["--simd-enabled", simd_flag(iteration)])
            .args(["--relaxed-simd-enabled", simd_flag(iteration)])
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .spawn()
            .expect("wasm-tools runs");
        child.stdin.take().unwrap().write_all(&input).unwrap();
        let output = child.wait_with_output().unwrap();
        if !output.status.success() {
            continue;
        }
        let bytes = output.stdout;
        let Ok(module) = libwasm_engine::compile(&bytes) else {
            continue;
        };
        if waits(&module) {
            continue;
        }
        let module = Arc::new(module);
        let mut interpreted = Store::new();
        let mut jit = Store::new();
        let (Ok(interpreted_instance), Ok(jit_instance)) = (
            interpreted.instantiate(module.clone(), &[]),
            jit.instantiate(module.clone(), &[]),
        ) else {
            continue;
        };
        if let Some(directory) = &keep {
            // NB: Where a crash leaves it.
            std::fs::write(format!("{directory}/current.wasm"), &bytes).unwrap();
        }
        let compiled = CompiledModule::compile(
            module.clone(),
            Options {
                verify_ir: true,
                stress_registers,
                no_licm,
                ..Options::default()
            },
        );
        let mut binding = TestBinding::new(&compiled, &jit, jit_instance);
        totals.modules += 1;
        totals.functions += module.code.len();
        let first = module.imported_function_count as usize;
        totals.compiled += compiled.entries[first..].iter().filter(|entry| **entry != 0).count();
        totals.runnable += compiled.runnable[first..].iter().filter(|runnable| **runnable).count();
        for failure in compiled.failures.iter().flatten() {
            let what = failure.reason();
            *totals.unsupported.entry(what).or_default() += 1;
        }
        let mut exports = interpreted
            .instance(interpreted_instance)
            .exports
            .iter()
            .map(|(name, export)| (name.clone(), *export))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        exports.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));
        let mut failed = false;
        let mut stop = false;
        for (name, export) in exports {
            let ExternValue::Function(interpreted_function) = export else {
                continue;
            };
            let Some(ExternValue::Function(jit_function)) = jit.instance(jit_instance).export(&name) else {
                continue;
            };
            let Some(index) = function_index(&jit, jit_function, jit_instance) else {
                continue;
            };
            let ty = interpreted.function(interpreted_function).ty.clone();
            for _ in 0..4 {
                let Some(arguments) = ty
                    .params
                    .iter()
                    .map(|ty| random.argument(*ty))
                    .collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()
                else {
                    break;
                };
                let expected = outcome(interpreted.invoke(interpreted_function, &arguments));
                if !compiled.runnable[index as usize] {
                    let _ = jit.invoke(jit_function, &arguments);
                    continue;
                }
                totals.cases += 1;
                let actual = binding.call(&mut jit, &compiled, index, &arguments);
                if actual == Outcome::Trap(harness::TRAP_NOT_COMPILED) {
                    totals.not_compiled += 1;
                    stop = true;
                    break;
                }
                let exhausted = Outcome::Trap(libwasm_engine::abi::TRAP_STACK_EXHAUSTED);
                if expected == exhausted || actual == exhausted {
                    // NB: How deep the stack gets before it is exhausted differs between the tiers, and so does what
                    //     the code did on the way there, like how much of a fuel global it used. The stores differ
                    //     from here on.
                    stop = true;
                    break;
                }
                let mut problem = None;
                if !harness::script::same_outcome(&expected, &actual) {
                    problem = Some(format!("{name}{arguments:?}: interpreter {expected:?}, JIT {actual:?}"));
                } else if let Some(difference) =
                    harness::script::state_difference(&interpreted, interpreted_instance, &jit, jit_instance)
                {
                    problem = Some(format!("{name}{arguments:?}: {difference}"));
                }
                if let Some(problem) = problem {
                    totals.failures += 1;
                    failed = true;
                    println!("FAIL module {iteration}: {problem}");
                    break;
                }
            }
            if failed || stop {
                break;
            }
        }
        if failed && let Some(directory) = &keep {
            let path = format!("{directory}/smith-{seed}-{iteration}.wasm");
            std::fs::write(&path, &bytes).unwrap();
            println!("  kept {path}");
        }
    }
    println!(
        "{} modules, {} functions: {} compiled, {} runnable; {} cases, {} failures, {} reached uncompiled code",
        totals.modules,
        totals.functions,
        totals.compiled,
        totals.runnable,
        totals.cases,
        totals.failures,
        totals.not_compiled
    );
    for (what, count) in &totals.unsupported {
        println!("{count:>8} not compiled: {what}");
    }
    if totals.failures > 0 {
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

/// Whether a function of the module waits on shared memory (`memory.atomic.wait32` and `wait64`).
fn waits(module: &libwasm_engine::module::Module) -> bool {
    use libwasm_jit::decode::{Decoder, Instruction};
    module.code.iter().any(|body| {
        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&module.bytes, body.code.start as usize, body.code.end as usize);
        while !decoder.is_at_end() {
            if let Instruction::Atomic(1 | 2) = decoder.decode() {
                return true;
            }
        }
        false
    })
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/JIT/examples/spec_check.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Runs spec testsuite scripts with calls into compiled functions running compiled code, and compares everything
//! with the interpreter (see `tests/harness/script.rs`).
//!
//! ```text
//! spec_check [--verbose] [--stress-registers] [--no-licm] [--runtime] [--dump FILE] DIRECTORY|SCRIPT.json...
//! ```
//!
//! `--dump FILE` writes what the interpreter did in every action to FILE, which should be the same on every
//! architecture: with `--runtime` and `LIBWASM_JIT=off`, comparing the files of two architectures checks one's
//! interpreter against the other's.

#[path = "../tests/harness/mod.rs"]
mod harness;

fn main() {
    harness::run_main(checked_main);
}

fn checked_main() {
    let mut verbose = false;
    let mut runtime = false;
    let mut paths = Vec::new();
    let mut dump_path = None;
    let mut arguments = std::env::args().skip(1);
    let mut options = libwasm_jit::Options {
        verify_ir: true,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    while let Some(argument) = arguments.next() {
        match argument.as_str() {
            "--dump" => dump_path = arguments.next(),
            "--verbose" => verbose = true,
            "--stress-registers" => options.stress_registers = true,
            "--no-licm" => options.no_licm = true,
            "--runtime" => runtime = true,
            _ => paths.push(argument),
        }
    }
    if runtime && std::env::var_os("LIBWASM_JIT").is_none() {
        // SAFETY: Nothing else runs yet.
        unsafe { std::env::set_var("LIBWASM_JIT", "eager") };
    }
    let mut dump = dump_path.map(|path| {
        std::io::BufWriter::new(std::fs::File::create(&path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("create {path}: {error}")))
    });
    let totals = harness::script::run_with_dump(
        &paths,
        verbose,
        options,
        runtime,
        dump.as_mut().map(|dump| dump as &mut dyn std::io::Write),
    );
    if let Some(mut dump) = dump {
        std::io::Write::flush(&mut dump).expect("write the dump");
    }
    println!(
        "{} scripts, {} modules, {} functions: {} compiled, {} runnable, {} exercised; {} cases, {} failures, {} reached uncompiled code",
        totals.scripts,
        totals.modules,
        totals.functions,
        totals.compiled,
        totals.runnable,
        totals.exercised,
        totals.cases,
        totals.failures,
        totals.not_compiled
    );
    if totals.failures > 0 {
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/JIT/src/builder/calls.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Calls, and the instance data they and tables reach.
//!
//! Every call goes through the callee's `FunctionHeader`. A direct call of one of the module's own functions passes
//! the caller's instance and memory base; any other call (of an import, or through a table or reference) passes
//! the callee's instance, found from its header, and that instance's memory base. Host functions have no instance;
//! they get the caller's, through which their stub finds the runtime.

use super::{Builder, instance_offset, ir_type};
use crate::ir::{FLAG_NOT_NULL, Func, NONE, Node, Op, Type, Value};
use libwasm_module::Module;
use libwasm_module::abi::{InstanceData, TRAP_NULL_REFERENCE, TRAP_UNDEFINED_ELEMENT, TRAP_UNINITIALIZED_ELEMENT};
use libwasm_module::types::FuncType;
use std::mem::offset_of;

/// How a call ends the code that makes it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum CallKind {
    Normal,
    Tail,
}

impl Builder {
    /// A pointer field of the instance that never changes once it is instantiated.
    pub(super) fn instance_field(&mut self, func: &mut Func, offset: usize) -> Value {
        self.pure(
            func,
            Node::new(
                Op::InstanceField,
                Type::Pointer,
                0,
                [self.instance, instance_offset(offset), 0],
            ),
        )
    }

    /// Element `index` of the pointer array of the instance at `offset`, which never changes either.
    pub(super) fn instance_pointer(&mut self, func: &mut Func, offset: usize, index: u32, ty: Type) -> Value {
        let array = self.instance_field(func, offset);
        self.pure(func, Node::new(Op::LoadPointer, ty, 0, [array, index * 8, 0]))
    }

    /// The store-wide identity of the module's type `type_index`.
    pub(super) fn type_identity(&mut self, func: &mut Func, type_index: u32) -> Value {
        let identities = self.instance_field(func, offset_of!(InstanceData, type_identities));
        self.pure(
            func,
            Node::new(Op::LoadPointer, Type::I32, 4, [identities, type_index * 4, 0]),
        )
    }

    /// The `TableData` of table `table`.
    pub(super) fn table_data(&mut self, func: &mut Func, table: u32) -> Value {
        self.instance_pointer(func, offset_of!(InstanceData, tables), table, Type::Pointer)
    }

    /// The `MemoryData` of memory `memory`.
    pub(super) fn memory_data(&mut self, func: &mut Func, memory: u32) -> Value {
        self.instance_pointer(func, offset_of!(InstanceData, memories), memory, Type::Pointer)
    }

    /// `ref.func`: the function's header, which is what a funcref is.
    pub(super) fn function_reference(&mut self, func: &mut Func, function: u32) -> Value {
        self.instance_pointer(func, offset_of!(InstanceData, functions), function, Type::Ref)
    }

    pub(super) fn call(&mut self, func: &mut Func, module: &Module, function: u32, kind: CallKind) {
        let ty = module.function_type(function).expect("functions have function types");
        let header = self.instance_pointer(func, offset_of!(InstanceData, functions), function, Type::Pointer);
        let (instance, memory_base) = if function < module.imported_function_count {
            self.callee_instance(func, header, true)
        } else {
            (self.instance, self.memory_base)
        };
        self.emit_call(func, ty, [header, instance, memory_base], function, kind);
    }

    pub(super) fn call_indirect(
        &mut self,
        func: &mut Func,
        module: &Module,
        type_index: u32,
        table: u32,
        kind: CallKind,
    ) {
        let ty = module.types[type_index as usize]
            .as_func()
            .expect("call_indirect has a function type");
        let index = func.resolve(self.pop());
        let table = self.table_data(func, table);
        let element = Self::append(
            func,
            Node::new(
                Op::TableElement,
                Type::Ref,
                TRAP_UNDEFINED_ELEMENT as u8,
                [table, index, 0],
            ),
        );
        let identity = self.type_identity(func, type_index);
        Self::append(
            func,
            Node::new(
                Op::CheckFunction,
                Type::None,
                TRAP_UNINITIALIZED_ELEMENT as u8,
                [element, identity, 0],
            ),
        );
        let (instance, memory_base) = self.callee_instance(func, element, false);
        self.emit_call(func, ty, [element, instance, memory_base], NONE, kind);
    }

    pub(super) fn call_ref(&mut self, func: &mut Func, module: &Module, type_index: u32, kind: CallKind) {
        let ty = module.types[type_index as usize]
            .as_func()
            .expect("call_ref has a function type");
        let reference = func.resolve(self.pop());
        Self::append(
            func,
            Node::new(Op::CheckNull, Type::None, TRAP_NULL_REFERENCE as u8, [reference, 0, 0]),
        );
        let (instance, memory_base) = self.callee_instance(func, reference, false);
        self.emit_call(func, ty, [reference, instance, memory_base], NONE, kind);
    }

    /// The instance and memory base a call of the function whose header is `header` passes. Only a header that is
    /// never null is value numbered: any other is read where the call's null check guards it.
    fn callee_instance(&mut self, func: &mut Func, header: Value, not_null: bool) -> (Value, Value) {
        let node = Node::new(
            Op::CalleeInstance,
            Type::Pointer,
            if not_null { FLAG_NOT_NULL } else { 0 },
            [header, self.instance, 0],
        );
        let instance = if not_null {
            self.pure(func, node)
        } else {
            Self::append(func, node)
        };
        let memory_base = self.pure(
            func,
            Node::new(
                Op::InstanceField,
                Type::Pointer,
                0,
                [instance, instance_offset(offset_of!(InstanceData, memory0_base)), 0],
            ),
        );
        (instance, memory_base)
    }

    fn emit_call(
        &mut self,
        func: &mut Func,
        ty: &FuncType,
        [header, instance, memory_base]: [Value; 3],
        function: u32,
        kind: CallKind,
    ) {
        let argument_count = ty.params.len();
        let start = func.operands.len() as u32;
        func.operands.extend_from_slice(&[header, instance, memory_base]);
        let top = self.stack.len() - argument_count;
        for position in top..self.stack.len() {
            let value = func.resolve(self.stack[position]);
            func.operands.push(value);
        }
        self.stack.truncate(top);
        let first_result = ty
            .results
            .first()
            .and_then(|result| ir_type(*result))
            .unwrap_or(Type::None);
        let node = Node::new(Op::Call, first_result, 0, [start, 3 + argument_count as u32, function]);
        if kind == CallKind::Tail {
            self.terminate(
                func,
                Node {
                    op: Op::TailCall,
                    ty: Type::None,
                    ..node
                },
                &[],
            );
            self.set_unreachable();
            return;
        }
        let call = Self::append(func, node);
        if !ty.results.is_empty() {
            self.push(call);
        }
        for (index, &result) in ty.results.iter().enumerate().skip(1) {
            let result_type = ir_type(result).expect("the results' types were checked");
            let value = Self::append(func, Node::new(Op::CallResult, result_type, 0, [call, index as u32, 0]));
            self.push(value);
        }
        self.call_epoch += 1;
        self.check_exception(func, call);
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/JIT/src/builder/exceptions.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Exception handling, in the IR of the function.
//!
//! A handler is a `try_table`, or the body of a legacy `try`. Every way an exception comes up in a handler's region
//! is an edge to the handler's dispatch, carrying the exception: a throw branches there, and a call checks the
//! context's `exception` when it returns, which the runtime sets when it unwinds an exception to the call (a call
//! with `FLAG_CHECKS_EXCEPTION` is an exception site). The dispatch is a block of its own, made where the region ends,
//! which tests the clauses in order: the first that catches the exception gets what it pushes, and an exception none
//! catches goes on to the handler around, or leaves the function through `Op::Throw`, which has the runtime unwind it
//! to the callers.
//!
//! The clauses of a `try_table` branch to labels around it. Those of a legacy `try` branch to its handlers, the
//! `catch` and `catch_all` blocks that follow its body, which run outside the region and keep the exception for
//! `rethrow`. A body that ends with `delegate` has no clauses, and its exceptions go to the handler that the label is,
//! or is in.

use super::{Builder, ControlKind, Edge};
use crate::ir::{BlockId, FLAG_CHECKS_EXCEPTION, Func, Helper, IntCondition, NONE, Node, Op, Type, Value};
use libwasm_module::Module;
use libwasm_module::abi::{EXCEPTION_PAYLOAD_OFFSET, EXCEPTION_TAG_OFFSET, ExecutionContext, InstanceData};
use libwasm_module::types::ValType;
use std::mem::offset_of;

/// A clause of a handler: catch (0), catch_ref (1), catch_all (2) or catch_all_ref (3), its tag, and for `try_table`
/// its label. For a legacy `try`, once the dispatch is made, the block and successor slot of its edge to the handler,
/// or NONE.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(super) struct Clause {
    pub kind: u32,
    pub tag: u32,
    pub label: u32,
    pub block: BlockId,
}

const CATCH_ALL: u32 = 2;

fn pushes_reference(kind: u32) -> bool {
    kind == 1 || kind == 3
}

impl Builder {
    /// The parameter types of tag `tag`.
    fn tag_params(module: &Module, tag: u32) -> &[ValType] {
        let type_index = module.tag_space[tag as usize].type_index;
        &module.types[type_index as usize]
            .as_func()
            .expect("tags have function types")
            .params
    }

    /// Makes the construct just pushed a handler, with the clauses from `clauses` on.
    fn begin_handler(&mut self, clauses: usize) {
        let index = self.controls.len() - 1;
        let control = &mut self.controls[index];
        control.clauses = (clauses as u32, (self.clauses.len() - clauses) as u32);
        control.outer_handler = self.handler;
        self.handler = index as u32;
    }

    pub(super) fn begin_try_table(&mut self, params: (u32, u32), results: (u32, u32), clauses: &[[u32; 3]]) {
        let start = self.clauses.len();
        self.clauses.extend(clauses.iter().map(|&[kind, tag, label]| Clause {
            kind,
            tag,
            label,
            block: NONE,
        }));
        self.push_control(ControlKind::TryTable, params, results, NONE);
        self.begin_handler(start);
    }

    /// A legacy `try` whose body starts at module offset `body`.
    pub(super) fn begin_try(&mut self, module: &Module, params: (u32, u32), results: (u32, u32), body: usize) {
        let info = &module.function_infos[self.defined as usize];
        // NB: The regions are in the order their instructions appear, and the builder meets them in that order (but
        //     for those in unreachable code, which it skips), so the region is at or after the cursor.
        let regions = &info.try_regions;
        while (regions[self.try_region_cursor].start as usize) < body {
            self.try_region_cursor += 1;
        }
        let region = &regions[self.try_region_cursor];
        assert_eq!(region.start as usize, body, "validation made a region of every try");
        self.try_region_cursor += 1;
        let start = self.clauses.len();
        let clauses =
            &info.catch_clauses[region.first_clause as usize..(region.first_clause + region.clause_count) as usize];
        for clause in clauses {
            let kind = match clause.kind {
                libwasm_module::validator::CatchKind::Catch => 0,
                _ => CATCH_ALL,
            };
            self.clauses.push(Clause {
                kind,
                tag: clause.tag,
                label: NONE,
                block: NONE,
            });
        }
        self.push_control(ControlKind::Try, params, results, NONE);
        self.begin_handler(start);
    }

    /// Records an edge from the current block, through the successor `slot`, to the dispatch of the handler
    /// `controls[handler]`, carrying `exception`.
    fn add_throw_edge(&mut self, handler: u32, slot: u32, exception: Value) {
        let values = self.edge_values.len() as u32;
        self.edge_values.push(exception);
        let control = &mut self.controls[handler as usize];
        self.edges.push(Edge {
            block: self.current_block,
            slot,
            values,
            next: control.throws,
        });
        control.throws = self.edges.len() as u32 - 1;
    }

    /// Ends the current block by throwing `exception` to the handler `handler`, or out of the function if it is NONE.
    fn throw_to(&mut self, func: &mut Func, handler: u32, exception: Value) {
        if handler == NONE {
            self.terminate(func, Node::new(Op::Throw, Type::None, 0, [exception, 0, 0]), &[]);
        } else {
            let slot = self.jump(func, NONE);
            self.add_throw_edge(handler, slot, exception);
        }
    }

    /// Throws `exception` from the current position, and makes what follows unreachable.
    pub(super) fn throw_exception(&mut self, func: &mut Func, exception: Value) {
        let handler = self.handler;
        self.throw_to(func, handler, exception);
        self.set_unreachable();
    }

    /// `throw tag`: a new exception with the tag and the values on the stack.
    pub(super) fn throw_tag(&mut self, func: &mut Func, module: &Module, tag: u32) {
        let identity = self.instance_pointer(func, offset_of!(InstanceData, tags), tag, Type::Pointer);
        let exception = self.helper(func, Helper::AllocateException, &[identity], Type::Ref);
        let payload = self.read_field(func, exception, EXCEPTION_PAYLOAD_OFFSET, Type::Pointer);
        let params = Self::tag_params(module, tag);
        // The payload is in operand stack order: the last value in the lowest slot.
        let mut slot = 0;
        for &param in params.iter().rev() {
            let value = func.resolve(self.pop());
            self.write_payload(func, payload, slot, param, value);
            slot += param.slot_count();
        }
        self.throw_exception(func, exception);
    }

    fn read_field(&mut self, func: &mut Func, pointer: Value, offset: usize, ty: Type) -> Value {
        let bytes = if ty == Type::I32 { 4 } else { 8 };
        Self::append(func, Node::new(Op::ReadField, ty, bytes, [pointer, offset as u32, 0]))
    }

    fn write_field(func: &mut Func, pointer: Value, offset: u32, value: Value) {
        let bytes = if func.node(value).ty == Type::I32 { 4 } else { 8 };
        Self::append(
            func,
            Node::new(Op::WriteField, Type::None, bytes, [pointer, value, offset]),
        );
    }

    /// Stores `value`, of type `ty`, in the payload at `payload` from `slot` on.
    fn write_payload(&mut self, func: &mut Func, payload: Value, slot: u32, ty: ValType, value: Value) {
        let offset = 8 * slot;
        match ty {
            ValType::I32 | ValType::I64 | ValType::Ref(_) => Self::write_field(func, payload, offset, value),
            ValType::F32 | ValType::F64 => {
                let bits = if ty == ValType::F32 { Type::I32 } else { Type::I64 };
                let bits = self.unary(func, Op::Reinterpret, bits, value);
                Self::write_field(func, payload, offset, bits);
            }
            ValType::V128 => {
                for lane in 0..2 {
                    let half = self.pure(
                        func,
                        Node::new(Op::ExtractLane, Type::I64, 0, [value, I64X2_EXTRACT_LANE, lane]),
                    );
                    Self::write_field(func, payload, offset + 8 * lane, half);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The value of type `ty` in the payload at `payload` from `slot` on.
    fn read_payload(&mut self, func: &mut Func, payload: Value, slot: u32, ty: ValType) -> Value {
        let offset = 8 * slot as usize;
        match ty {
            ValType::I32 => self.read_field(func, payload, offset, Type::I32),
            ValType::I64 => self.read_field(func, payload, offset, Type::I64),
            ValType::Ref(_) => self.read_field(func, payload, offset, Type::Ref),
            ValType::F32 => {
                let bits = self.read_field(func, payload, offset, Type::I32);
                self.unary(func, Op::Reinterpret, Type::F32, bits)
            }
            ValType::F64 => {
                let bits = self.read_field(func, payload, offset, Type::I64);
                self.unary(func, Op::Reinterpret, Type::F64, bits)
            }
            ValType::V128 => {
                let low = self.read_field(func, payload, offset, Type::I64);
                let high = self.read_field(func, payload, offset + 8, Type::I64);
                let vector = self.pure(func, Node::new(Op::VectorUnary, Type::V128, 0, [low, I64X2_SPLAT, 0]));
                self.pure(
                    func,
                    Node::new(
                        Op::ReplaceLane,
                        Type::V128,
                        0,
                        [vector, high, I64X2_REPLACE_LANE | (1 << 16)],
                    ),
                )
            }
        }
    }

    /// Pushes what a clause of `kind` with tag `tag` pushes for `exception`.
    fn push_caught(&mut self, func: &mut Func, module: &Module, kind: u32, tag: u32, exception: Value) {
        if kind < CATCH_ALL {
            let params = Self::tag_params(module, tag);
            let payload = self.read_field(func, exception, EXCEPTION_PAYLOAD_OFFSET, Type::Pointer);
            let mut slot: u32 = params.iter().map(|param| param.slot_count()).sum();
            for &param in params {
                slot -= param.slot_count();
                let value = self.read_payload(func, payload, slot, param);
                self.push(value);
            }
        }
        if pushes_reference(kind) {
            self.push(exception);
        }
    }

    /// After a call in a handler's region: continues at the handler's dispatch if the call threw.
    pub(super) fn check_exception(&mut self, func: &mut Func, call: Value) {
        let handler = self.handler;
        if handler == NONE {
            return;
        }
        func.nodes[call as usize].flags |= FLAG_CHECKS_EXCEPTION;
        let context = self.instance_field(func, offset_of!(InstanceData, context));
        let exception = self.read_field(func, context, offset_of!(ExecutionContext, exception), Type::Ref);
        let zero = self.constant(func, Type::Ref, 0);
        let slot = self.terminate(
            func,
            Node::new(
                Op::BranchCompare,
                Type::None,
                IntCondition::Ne as u8,
                [exception, zero, 0],
            ),
            &[NONE, NONE],
        );
        self.add_throw_edge(handler, slot, exception);
        self.continue_after(func, slot + 1);
    }

    /// Starts a block whose only predecessor is the current block, through its successor `slot`.
    fn continue_after(&mut self, func: &mut Func, slot: u32) {
        let block = self.current_block;
        self.continue_from(func, block, slot);
    }

    /// Starts a block whose only predecessor is `predecessor`, through its successor `slot`.
    fn continue_from(&mut self, func: &mut Func, predecessor: BlockId, slot: u32) {
        let block = self.new_block(func);
        Self::set_predecessors(func, block, &[predecessor]);
        func.successors[slot as usize] = block;
        self.start_block(func, block);
    }

    /// Makes the dispatch of the handler `controls[index]`, if anything throws to it, and returns the exception it
    /// starts with, in its block, which is current then. Clears the context's `exception`, which a call that threw
    /// left there.
    fn begin_dispatch(&mut self, func: &mut Func, index: usize) -> Option<Value> {
        let control = self.controls[index];
        if control.throws == NONE {
            return None;
        }
        self.collect_edges(control.throws);
        let block = self.new_block(func);
        let predecessors = std::mem::take(&mut self.scratch_blocks);
        Self::set_predecessors(func, block, &predecessors);
        self.scratch_blocks = predecessors;
        for &edge in &self.scratch_values {
            func.successors[self.edges[edge as usize].slot as usize] = block;
        }
        self.start_block(func, block);
        let exception = self.merge_edge_values(func, block, Type::Ref, 0);
        let context = self.instance_field(func, offset_of!(InstanceData, context));
        let zero = self.constant(func, Type::I64, 0);
        Self::append(
            func,
            Node::new(
                Op::WriteField,
                Type::None,
                8,
                [context, zero, offset_of!(ExecutionContext, exception) as u32],
            ),
        );
        Some(exception)
    }

    /// Ends the current block with a test of whether `exception` has tag `tag`, whose first successor is the match,
    /// and returns the block and the slot of that successor.
    fn test_tag(&mut self, func: &mut Func, tag: u32, exception: Value) -> (BlockId, u32) {
        let identity = self.instance_pointer(func, offset_of!(InstanceData, tags), tag, Type::Pointer);
        let thrown = self.read_field(func, exception, EXCEPTION_TAG_OFFSET, Type::Pointer);
        let slot = self.terminate(
            func,
            Node::new(
                Op::BranchCompare,
                Type::None,
                IntCondition::Eq as u8,
                [thrown, identity, 0],
            ),
            &[NONE, NONE],
        );
        (self.current_block, slot)
    }

    /// Ends the body of the handler `controls[index]`: the fallthrough goes to the end of the construct, and the
    /// handler stops being the current one.
    fn end_region(&mut self, func: &mut Func, index: usize) {
        let control = self.controls[index];
        if !control.unreachable {
            let slot = self.jump(func, NONE);
            self.add_edge(index, slot);
            self.controls[index].unreachable = true;
        }
        self.unnumber(control.numbering_mark);
        self.stack.truncate(control.height as usize);
        self.handler = control.outer_handler;
    }

    /// The `end` of a `try_table`.
    pub(super) fn end_try_table(&mut self, func: &mut Func, module: &Module, index: usize) {
        let control = self.controls[index];
        if control.throws == NONE {
            self.handler = control.outer_handler;
            self.end_block(func, index);
            return;
        }
        self.end_region(func, index);
        let exception = self.begin_dispatch(func, index).expect("something throws");
        let mut caught_all = false;
        for clause_index in control.clauses.0..control.clauses.0 + control.clauses.1 {
            let clause = self.clauses[clause_index as usize];
            let otherwise = if clause.kind < CATCH_ALL {
                let (test, slot) = self.test_tag(func, clause.tag, exception);
                self.continue_from(func, test, slot);
                Some((test, slot + 1))
            } else {
                None
            };
            self.push_caught(func, module, clause.kind, clause.tag, exception);
            // NB: The labels are counted from outside the try_table, whose own construct is still open.
            self.branch(func, clause.label + 1);
            self.stack.truncate(control.height as usize);
            match otherwise {
                Some((test, slot)) => self.continue_from(func, test, slot),
                None => {
                    caught_all = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if !caught_all {
            self.throw_to(func, control.outer_handler, exception);
        }
        self.end_block(func, index);
    }

    /// `catch` or `catch_all` of a legacy `try`: ends the body or the previous handler, and starts the next handler.
    pub(super) fn begin_catch(&mut self, func: &mut Func, module: &Module) {
        let index = self.controls.len() - 1;
        let control = self.controls[index];
        if control.kind == ControlKind::Try {
            self.end_region(func, index);
            // The dispatch branches to each handler that catches, in order; the handlers' blocks come later.
            let exception = self.begin_dispatch(func, index);
            let mut caught_all = false;
            if let Some(exception) = exception {
                for clause_index in control.clauses.0..control.clauses.0 + control.clauses.1 {
                    let clause = self.clauses[clause_index as usize];
                    let (block, slot) = if clause.kind == CATCH_ALL {
                        let slot = self.jump(func, NONE);
                        (self.current_block, slot)
                    } else {
                        self.test_tag(func, clause.tag, exception)
                    };
                    self.clauses[clause_index as usize].label = slot;
                    self.clauses[clause_index as usize].block = block;
                    if clause.kind == CATCH_ALL {
                        caught_all = true;
                        break;
                    }
                    self.continue_from(func, block, slot + 1);
                }
                if !caught_all {
                    self.throw_to(func, control.outer_handler, exception);
                }
            }
            let control = &mut self.controls[index];
            control.kind = ControlKind::Catch;
            control.exception = exception.unwrap_or(NONE);
            control.next_clause = control.clauses.0;
        } else {
            // The end of the previous handler.
            if !control.unreachable {
                let slot = self.jump(func, NONE);
                self.add_edge(index, slot);
            }
            self.unnumber(control.numbering_mark);
            self.stack.truncate(control.height as usize);
        }
        let control = self.controls[index];
        let clause_index = control.next_clause;
        self.controls[index].next_clause += 1;
        let clause = self.clauses[clause_index as usize];
        if control.exception == NONE || clause.label == NONE {
            // Nothing throws to the try, or an earlier catch_all catches everything: the handler is unreachable.
            self.controls[index].unreachable = true;
            return;
        }
        // The dispatch's edge to this handler: the first successor of the test's block, or the jump of catch_all.
        self.continue_from(func, clause.block, clause.label);
        self.controls[index].unreachable = false;
        self.push_caught(func, module, clause.kind, clause.tag, control.exception);
    }

    /// The `end` of a legacy `try`, after its body or a handler.
    pub(super) fn end_try(&mut self, func: &mut Func, index: usize) {
        let control = self.controls[index];
        if control.kind == ControlKind::Try {
            // A try without handlers: what its body throws goes on to the handler around it.
            if control.throws == NONE {
                self.handler = control.outer_handler;
                self.end_block(func, index);
                return;
            }
            self.end_region(func, index);
            let exception = self.begin_dispatch(func, index).expect("something throws");
            self.throw_to(func, control.outer_handler, exception);
        }
        self.end_block(func, index);
    }

    /// `delegate label` of a legacy `try`: its body ends, and what it throws goes to the handler that the label is,
    /// or the one around it.
    pub(super) fn delegate(&mut self, func: &mut Func, label: u32) {
        let index = self.controls.len() - 1;
        let control = self.controls[index];
        self.handler = control.outer_handler;
        if control.throws != NONE {
            // The label is counted from outside the try. A legacy try whose body is open catches what is delegated to
            // its label; any other construct passes it on to the handler around it.
            let target = index - 1 - label as usize;
            let mut handler = control.outer_handler;
            while handler != NONE
                && !(handler as usize == target && self.controls[target].kind == ControlKind::Try)
                && handler as usize >= target
            {
                handler = self.controls[handler as usize].outer_handler;
            }
            if !control.unreachable {
                let slot = self.jump(func, NONE);
                self.add_edge(index, slot);
                self.controls[index].unreachable = true;
            }
            self.unnumber(control.numbering_mark);
            self.stack.truncate(control.height as usize);
            let exception = self.begin_dispatch(func, index).expect("something throws");
            self.throw_to(func, handler, exception);
        }
        self.end_block(func, index);
    }

    /// `rethrow label`: throws the exception the legacy handler `label` caught again.
    pub(super) fn rethrow(&mut self, func: &mut Func, label: u32) {
        let index = self.controls.len() - 1 - label as usize;
        let exception = self.controls[index].exception;
        debug_assert_ne!(
            exception, NONE,
            "a reachable rethrow is in a handler that caught something"
        );
        self.throw_exception(func, exception);
    }
}

const I64X2_SPLAT: u32 = 0x12;
const I64X2_EXTRACT_LANE: u32 = 0x1d;
const I64X2_REPLACE_LANE: u32 = 0x1e;
