//! Local folding: constant folding and algebraic simplification of a node about to be created, from its inputs
//! alone. Floats are left alone: their results depend on NaN payloads the code may observe.

use crate::ir::{FLAG_CANNOT_TRAP, Func, IntCondition, Op, Type, Value};

/// What a node about to be created simplifies to.
pub enum Folded {
    /// An existing value.
    Value(Value),
    /// A constant of the node's type.
    Constant(u64),
    /// The node, possibly with its inputs swapped or its flags changed.
    Node { op: Op, flags: u8, a: Value, b: Value },
}

fn mask(ty: Type, bits: u64) -> u64 {
    if ty == Type::I32 { bits & 0xffff_ffff } else { bits }
}

fn width(ty: Type) -> u32 {
    if ty == Type::I32 { 32 } else { 64 }
}

/// The signed value of `bits` of type `ty`.
fn signed(ty: Type, bits: u64) -> i64 {
    if ty == Type::I32 {
        i64::from(bits as u32 as i32)
    } else {
        bits as i64
    }
}

fn evaluate_binary(op: Op, ty: Type, a: u64, b: u64, flags: u8) -> Option<u64> {
    let bits = width(ty);
    let shift = (b as u32) & (bits - 1);
    let result = match op {
        Op::Add => a.wrapping_add(b),
        Op::Sub => a.wrapping_sub(b),
        Op::Mul => a.wrapping_mul(b),
        Op::And => a & b,
        Op::Or => a | b,
        Op::Xor => a ^ b,
        Op::Shl => a << shift,
        Op::ShrS => (signed(ty, a) >> shift) as u64,
        Op::ShrU => mask(ty, a) >> shift,
        Op::Rotl if ty == Type::I32 => u64::from((a as u32).rotate_left(shift)),
        Op::Rotl => a.rotate_left(shift),
        Op::Rotr if ty == Type::I32 => u64::from((a as u32).rotate_right(shift)),
        Op::Rotr => a.rotate_right(shift),
        Op::DivU | Op::RemU | Op::DivS | Op::RemS if mask(ty, b) == 0 => return None,
        Op::DivU => mask(ty, a) / mask(ty, b),
        Op::RemU => mask(ty, a) % mask(ty, b),
        Op::DivS => {
            let (a, b) = (signed(ty, a), signed(ty, b));
            if b == -1 && a == signed(ty, 1 << (bits - 1)) {
                return None;
            }
            (a / b) as u64
        }
        Op::RemS => {
            let (a, b) = (signed(ty, a), signed(ty, b));
            if b == -1 { 0 } else { (a % b) as u64 }
        }
        Op::Compare => u64::from(IntCondition::from_flags(flags).evaluate(a, b, ty.is_64())),
        _ => return None,
    };
    Some(mask(ty, result))
}

/// Folds an integer binary op of type `ty` (for `Compare`, the operands' type) on `a` and `b`.
pub fn binary(func: &Func, op: Op, ty: Type, flags: u8, a: Value, b: Value) -> Folded {
    let constant_a = func.node(a).constant();
    let constant_b = func.node(b).constant();
    if let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (constant_a, constant_b)
        && let Some(result) = evaluate_binary(op, ty, x, y, flags)
    {
        return Folded::Constant(result);
    }
    // Constants go to the right.
    if constant_a.is_some() && constant_b.is_none() {
        if op.is_commutative() {
            return binary(func, op, ty, flags, b, a);
        }
        if op == Op::Compare {
            let swapped = IntCondition::from_flags(flags).swap() as u8;
            return binary(func, op, ty, swapped, b, a);
        }
    }
    let all_ones = mask(ty, u64::MAX);
    if let Some(y) = constant_b {
        let shift = (y as u32) & (width(ty) - 1);
        match op {
            Op::Add | Op::Sub | Op::Or | Op::Xor if y == 0 => return Folded::Value(a),
            Op::Shl | Op::ShrS | Op::ShrU | Op::Rotl | Op::Rotr if shift == 0 => return Folded::Value(a),
            Op::Mul | Op::DivS | Op::DivU if y == 1 => return Folded::Value(a),
            Op::Mul | Op::And if y == 0 => return Folded::Constant(0),
            Op::And if y == all_ones => return Folded::Value(a),
            Op::Or if y == all_ones => return Folded::Constant(all_ones),
            Op::RemU if y == 1 => return Folded::Constant(0),
            Op::RemS if y == 1 || y == all_ones => return Folded::Constant(0),
            Op::DivU | Op::RemU if y != 0 => {
                return Folded::Node {
                    op,
                    flags: flags | FLAG_CANNOT_TRAP,
                    a,
                    b,
                };
            }
            Op::DivS | Op::RemS if y != 0 && y != all_ones => {
                return Folded::Node {
                    op,
                    flags: flags | FLAG_CANNOT_TRAP,
                    a,
                    b,
                };
            }
            Op::Compare if y == 0 => match IntCondition::from_flags(flags) {
                IntCondition::LtU => return Folded::Constant(0),
                IntCondition::GeU => return Folded::Constant(1),
                _ => {}
            },
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    if a == b {
        match op {
            Op::Sub | Op::Xor => return Folded::Constant(0),
            Op::And | Op::Or => return Folded::Value(a),
            Op::Compare => {
                let holds = matches!(
                    IntCondition::from_flags(flags),
                    IntCondition::Eq | IntCondition::LeS | IntCondition::LeU | IntCondition::GeS | IntCondition::GeU
                );
                return Folded::Constant(u64::from(holds));
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    Folded::Node { op, flags, a, b }
}

/// Folds an integer unary op producing `ty` on `a`.
pub fn unary(func: &Func, op: Op, ty: Type, a: Value) -> Option<Folded> {
    let input = func.node(a);
    if let Some(x) = input.constant() {
        let input_type = input.ty;
        let result = match op {
            Op::Clz if ty == Type::I32 => u64::from((x as u32).leading_zeros()),
            Op::Clz => u64::from(x.leading_zeros()),
            Op::Ctz if ty == Type::I32 => u64::from((x as u32).trailing_zeros()),
            Op::Ctz => u64::from(x.trailing_zeros()),
            Op::Popcnt => u64::from(x.count_ones()),
            Op::Eqz => u64::from(mask(input_type, x) == 0),
            Op::Extend8S => x as u8 as i8 as i64 as u64,
            Op::Extend16S => x as u16 as i16 as i64 as u64,
            Op::Extend32S | Op::ExtendI32S => x as u32 as i32 as i64 as u64,
            Op::ExtendI32U => u64::from(x as u32),
            Op::Wrap => x,
            _ => return None,
        };
        return Some(Folded::Constant(mask(ty, result)));
    }
    match (op, input.op) {
        (Op::Eqz, Op::Compare) => Some(Folded::Node {
            op: Op::Compare,
            flags: IntCondition::from_flags(input.flags).invert() as u8,
            a: input.args[0],
            b: input.args[1],
        }),
        (Op::Wrap, Op::ExtendI32S | Op::ExtendI32U) => Some(Folded::Value(input.args[0])),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/*

//! The GC instructions (the `0xFB` prefix): structs, arrays, i31 references, and tests and casts of references.
//!
//! Objects are cells of the runtime's heap (see `abi::Rtt`): the Rtt first, the data's address at OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET
//! and an array's length at OBJECT_LENGTH_OFFSET. Data of up to `MAX_INLINE_DATA_SIZE` bytes is inline, at
//! STRUCT_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET or ARRAY_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET, so a struct's fields are at constant offsets from the object
//! where the struct is small enough and its type is final. Fields take `StorageType::object_field_size()` bytes, at
//! the offsets `struct_layout` gives them: the runtime's layout, which `abi` and `types` define for both.
//!
//! GC references in compiled frames need nothing special: the collector scans the stack conservatively and recognizes
//! pointers into cells, and every allocation is a call of the runtime, around which values live in stack slots or in
//! registers the runtime saves. The data of a large object lives outside the heap, so its address does not keep the
//! object alive; that address is read where the access is (`ReadField` and `ElementAddress` are not pure), so the
//! object is live up to there.

use super::Builder;
use crate::ir::{Func, HeapTest, Helper, LoadKind, Node, Op, REF_TEST_CAST, REF_TEST_NULLABLE, Type, Value};
use libwasm_module::Module;
use libwasm_module::abi::{
    ARRAY_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET, InstanceData, MAX_INLINE_DATA_SIZE, OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET, OBJECT_LENGTH_OFFSET,
    STRUCT_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET, TRAP_MEMORY_OUT_OF_BOUNDS, TRAP_NULL_REFERENCE, TRAP_TABLE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS,
};
use libwasm_module::opcode::gc::*;
use libwasm_module::opcode::simd::I64X2_EXTRACT_LANE;
use libwasm_module::types::{CompositeType, HeapType, StorageType, ValType, struct_layout};
use std::mem::offset_of;

/// The log2 of the bytes a field or element of `storage` takes, which its stores write.
fn size_log2(storage: StorageType) -> u8 {
    storage.object_field_size().trailing_zeros() as u8
}

fn struct_fields(module: &Module, type_index: u32) -> &[libwasm_module::types::FieldType] {
    match &module.types[type_index as usize].composite {
        CompositeType::Struct(fields) => fields,
        _ => unreachable!("validated code accesses fields of struct types"),
    }
}

fn array_storage(module: &Module, type_index: u32) -> StorageType {
    match &module.types[type_index as usize].composite {
        CompositeType::Array(element) => element.storage,
        _ => unreachable!("validated code accesses elements of array types"),
    }
}

/// The number of supertypes above the module's type `type_index`.
fn type_depth(module: &Module, mut type_index: u32) -> u32 {
    let mut depth = 0;
    while let Some(&supertype) = module.types[type_index as usize].supertypes.first() {
        type_index = supertype;
        depth += 1;
    }
    depth
}

impl Builder {
    /// The byte offset of field `field` in the data of a struct of the module's type `type_index`, or with `field`
    /// equal to the field count, the size of its data.
    fn field_offset(&mut self, module: &Module, type_index: u32, field: u32) -> u32 {
        let key = (u64::from(type_index) << 32) | u64::from(field);
        if let Some(offset) = self.field_offsets.get(key) {
            return offset;
        }
        let (offsets, size) = struct_layout(struct_fields(module, type_index));
        for (index, offset) in offsets.into_iter().enumerate() {
            self.field_offsets
                .insert((u64::from(type_index) << 32) | index as u64, offset);
        }
        let count = struct_fields(module, type_index).len() as u64;
        self.field_offsets.insert((u64::from(type_index) << 32) | count, size);
        self.field_offsets.get(key).expect("every field has an offset")
    }

    /// The runtime type of the module's type `type_index`.
    fn rtt(&mut self, func: &mut Func, type_index: u32) -> Value {
        self.pure(
            func,
            Node::new(Op::Rtt, Type::Pointer, 0, [self.instance, type_index, 0]),
        )
    }

    /// The size of the data of every struct that a reference to the module's struct type `type_index` can refer to.
    fn struct_data_size(&mut self, module: &Module, type_index: u32) -> Option<u32> {
        if !module.types[type_index as usize].is_final {
            return None;
        }
        let count = struct_fields(module, type_index).len() as u32;
        Some(self.field_offset(module, type_index, count))
    }

    /// Where the data of an object with `size` bytes of it is, with `inline_data_offset` where it would be inline: the
    /// object and the offset of its inline data, or the address of its data.
    fn object_data(func: &mut Func, object: Value, size: Option<u32>, inline_data_offset: usize) -> (Value, u32) {
        if size.is_some_and(|size| size as usize <= MAX_INLINE_DATA_SIZE) {
            return (object, inline_data_offset as u32);
        }
        let data = Self::append(
            func,
            Node::new(Op::ReadField, Type::Pointer, 8, [object, OBJECT_DATA_OFFSET as u32, 0]),
        );
        (data, 0)
    }

    /// A field or element of `storage` at `base` + `offset`, sign-extended if it is packed and `signed`.
    fn load_field(&mut self, func: &mut Func, base: Value, offset: u32, storage: StorageType, signed: bool) -> Value {
        let (kind, ty) = match storage {
            StorageType::I8 if signed => (LoadKind::I32S8, Type::I32),
            StorageType::I8 => (LoadKind::I32U8, Type::I32),
            StorageType::I16 if signed => (LoadKind::I32S16, Type::I32),
            StorageType::I16 => (LoadKind::I32U16, Type::I32),
            StorageType::Val(ValType::I32) => (LoadKind::I32, Type::I32),
            StorageType::Val(ValType::F32) => (LoadKind::F32, Type::F32),
            StorageType::Val(ValType::F64) => (LoadKind::F64, Type::F64),
            StorageType::Val(ValType::I64) => (LoadKind::I64, Type::I64),
            StorageType::Val(ValType::Ref(_)) => (LoadKind::I64, Type::Ref),
            StorageType::Val(ValType::V128) => {
                let zero = self.constant(func, Type::I32, 0);
                // NB: The flags are the sub-opcode of `v128.load`, which is 0.
                return Self::append(func, Node::new(Op::VectorLoad, Type::V128, 0, [base, zero, offset]));
            }
        };
        self.load_at(func, kind, ty, base, offset)
    }

    fn check_null(func: &mut Func, reference: Value) {
        Self::append(
            func,
            Node::new(Op::CheckNull, Type::None, TRAP_NULL_REFERENCE as u8, [reference, 0, 0]),
        );
    }

    /// A call of the runtime that allocates an object of the module's type `type_index` with `size` bytes of zeroed
    /// data and, for an array, `length` elements (both i64 values).
    fn allocate(&mut self, func: &mut Func, type_index: u32, size: Value, length: Value) -> Value {
        let rtt = self.rtt(func, type_index);
        self.helper(func, Helper::Allocate, &[rtt, size, length], Type::Ref)
    }

    /// The bits of an element's value as the runtime's functions take them: the low and the high 64 bits.
    fn value_bits(&mut self, func: &mut Func, value: Value, storage: StorageType) -> (Value, Value) {
        let value = func.resolve(value);
        let zero = self.constant(func, Type::I64, 0);
        match storage {
            StorageType::Val(ValType::F32) => {
                let bits = self.pure(func, Node::new(Op::Reinterpret, Type::I32, 0, [value, 0, 0]));
                (bits, zero)
            }
            StorageType::Val(ValType::F64) => {
                let bits = self.pure(func, Node::new(Op::Reinterpret, Type::I64, 0, [value, 0, 0]));
                (bits, zero)
            }
            StorageType::Val(ValType::V128) => {
                let low = self.pure(
                    func,
                    Node::new(Op::ExtractLane, Type::I64, 0, [value, I64X2_EXTRACT_LANE, 0]),
                );
                let high = self.pure(
                    func,
                    Node::new(Op::ExtractLane, Type::I64, 0, [value, I64X2_EXTRACT_LANE, 1]),
                );
                (low, high)
            }
            _ => (value, zero),
        }
    }

    /// Whether `value` is the zero of its type, which every new object's fields start as.
    fn is_zero(&self, func: &Func, value: Value) -> bool {
        let value = func.resolve(value);
        func.node(value).constant() == Some(0) || (value == self.vector_zero && value != crate::ir::NONE)
    }

    /// The test of `reference` against `heap`, as an i32, or for a cast, a check that traps.
    fn ref_test(
        &mut self,
        func: &mut Func,
        module: &Module,
        reference: Value,
        heap: HeapType,
        nullable: bool,
        cast: bool,
    ) -> Value {
        let reference = func.resolve(reference);
        let (test, identity, depth) = match heap {
            HeapType::Any | HeapType::Func | HeapType::Extern | HeapType::Exn => (HeapTest::NonNull, None, 0),
            HeapType::Eq => (HeapTest::Eq, None, 0),
            HeapType::I31 => (HeapTest::I31, None, 0),
            HeapType::Struct => (HeapTest::Struct, None, 0),
            HeapType::Array => (HeapTest::Array, None, 0),
            HeapType::None | HeapType::NoFunc | HeapType::NoExtern | HeapType::NoExn | HeapType::Bottom => {
                (HeapTest::Nothing, None, 0)
            }
            HeapType::Concrete(type_index) => {
                let test = match module.types[type_index as usize].composite {
                    CompositeType::Func(_) => HeapTest::ConcreteFunction,
                    _ => HeapTest::ConcreteObject,
                };
                (
                    test,
                    Some(self.type_identity(func, type_index)),
                    type_depth(module, type_index),
                )
            }
        };
        let identity = match identity {
            Some(identity) => identity,
            None => self.constant(func, Type::I32, 0),
        };
        let mut flags = test as u8;
        if nullable {
            flags |= REF_TEST_NULLABLE;
        }
        if cast {
            flags |= REF_TEST_CAST;
            return Self::append(
                func,
                Node::new(Op::RefTest, Type::None, flags, [reference, identity, depth]),
            );
        }
        self.pure(
            func,
            Node::new(Op::RefTest, Type::I32, flags, [reference, identity, depth]),
        )
    }

    /// The instructions of the `0xFB` prefix, with the immediates the decoder kept.
    pub(super) fn gc(
        &mut self,
        func: &mut Func,
        module: &Module,
        sub_opcode: u32,
        [first, second]: [u32; 2],
        heap_types: [HeapType; 2],
        cast_flags: u8,
    ) {
        match sub_opcode {
            STRUCT_NEW | STRUCT_NEW_DEFAULT => {
                let count = struct_fields(module, first).len();
                let size = self.field_offset(module, first, count as u32);
                let mut values = Vec::new();
                if sub_opcode == STRUCT_NEW {
                    values = self.stack.split_off(self.stack.len() - count);
                }
                let size_value = self.constant(func, Type::I64, u64::from(size));
                let zero = self.constant(func, Type::I64, 0);
                let object = self.allocate(func, first, size_value, zero);
                if !values.is_empty() {
                    let (base, data_offset) = Self::object_data(func, object, Some(size), STRUCT_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET);
                    for (index, &value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
                        if self.is_zero(func, value) {
                            continue;
                        }
                        let storage = struct_fields(module, first)[index].storage;
                        let offset = data_offset + self.field_offset(module, first, index as u32);
                        self.store_at(func, size_log2(storage), base, offset, value);
                    }
                }
                self.push(object);
            }
            STRUCT_GET | STRUCT_GET_S | STRUCT_GET_U => {
                let object = func.resolve(self.pop());
                Self::check_null(func, object);
                let size = self.struct_data_size(module, first);
                let (base, data_offset) = Self::object_data(func, object, size, STRUCT_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET);
                let offset = data_offset + self.field_offset(module, first, second);
                let storage = struct_fields(module, first)[second as usize].storage;
                let value = self.load_field(func, base, offset, storage, sub_opcode == STRUCT_GET_S);
                self.push(value);
            }
            STRUCT_SET => {
                let value = self.pop();
                let object = func.resolve(self.pop());
                Self::check_null(func, object);
                let size = self.struct_data_size(module, first);
                let (base, data_offset) = Self::object_data(func, object, size, STRUCT_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET);
                let offset = data_offset + self.field_offset(module, first, second);
                let storage = struct_fields(module, first)[second as usize].storage;
                self.store_at(func, size_log2(storage), base, offset, value);
            }
            ARRAY_NEW | ARRAY_NEW_DEFAULT => {
                let count = self.pop();
                let storage = array_storage(module, first);
                let length = self.unary(func, Op::ExtendI32U, Type::I64, count);
                let element_size = self.constant(func, Type::I64, u64::from(storage.object_field_size()));
                let size = self.binary(func, Op::Mul, Type::I64, length, element_size);
                let array = if sub_opcode == ARRAY_NEW {
                    let value = self.pop();
                    let array = self.allocate(func, first, size, length);
                    if !self.is_zero(func, value) {
                        let (low, high) = self.value_bits(func, value, storage);
                        let zero = self.constant(func, Type::I64, 0);
                        self.helper(func, Helper::ArrayFill, &[array, zero, low, high, length], Type::None);
                    }
                    array
                } else {
                    self.allocate(func, first, size, length)
                };
                self.push(array);
            }
            ARRAY_NEW_FIXED => {
                let storage = array_storage(module, first);
                let values = self.stack.split_off(self.stack.len() - second as usize);
                let element_size = storage.object_field_size();
                let data_size = second * element_size;
                let size = self.constant(func, Type::I64, u64::from(data_size));
                let length = self.constant(func, Type::I64, u64::from(second));
                let array = self.allocate(func, first, size, length);
                let (base, data_offset) = Self::object_data(func, array, Some(data_size), ARRAY_INLINE_DATA_OFFSET);
                for (index, &value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
                    if self.is_zero(func, value) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let offset = data_offset + index as u32 * element_size;
                    self.store_at(func, size_log2(storage), base, offset, value);
                }
                self.push(array);
            }
            ARRAY_NEW_DATA | ARRAY_NEW_ELEM => {
                let count = self.pop();
                let source = self.pop();
                let storage = array_storage(module, first);
                let (segments, unit, trap, init) = if sub_opcode == ARRAY_NEW_DATA {
                    (
                        offset_of!(InstanceData, data_segments),
                        u64::from(storage.object_field_size()),
                        TRAP_MEMORY_OUT_OF_BOUNDS,
                        Helper::ArrayInitData,
                    )
                } else {
                    (
                        offset_of!(InstanceData, element_segments),
                        1,
                        TRAP_TABLE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS,
                        Helper::ArrayInitElem,
                    )
                };
                let segment = self.segment(func, segments, second);
                // The segment's range is checked first, before the array is allocated.
                let unit = self.constant(func, Type::I64, unit);
                let trap = self.constant(func, Type::I64, u64::from(trap));
                self.helper(
                    func,
                    Helper::SegmentRange,
                    &[segment, source, count, unit, trap],
                    Type::None,
                );
                let length = self.unary(func, Op::ExtendI32U, Type::I64, count);
                let element_size = self.constant(func, Type::I64, u64::from(storage.object_field_size()));
                let size = self.binary(func, Op::Mul, Type::I64, length, element_size);
                let array = self.allocate(func, first, size, length);
                let zero = self.constant(func, Type::I64, 0);
                self.helper(func, init, &[array, segment, zero, source, count], Type::None);
                self.push(array);
            }
            ARRAY_GET | ARRAY_GET_S | ARRAY_GET_U => {
                let index = func.resolve(self.pop());
                let array = func.resolve(self.pop());
                let storage = array_storage(module, first);
                let shift = size_log2(storage);
                let address = Self::append(
                    func,
                    Node::new(Op::ElementAddress, Type::Pointer, shift, [array, index, 0]),
                );
                let value = self.load_field(func, address, 0, storage, sub_opcode == ARRAY_GET_S);
                self.push(value);
            }
            ARRAY_SET => {
                let value = self.pop();
                let index = func.resolve(self.pop());
                let array = func.resolve(self.pop());
                let storage = array_storage(module, first);
                let shift = size_log2(storage);
                let address = Self::append(
                    func,
                    Node::new(Op::ElementAddress, Type::Pointer, shift, [array, index, 0]),
                );
                self.store_at(func, shift, address, 0, value);
            }
            ARRAY_LEN => {
                let array = func.resolve(self.pop());
                Self::check_null(func, array);
                let length = Self::append(
                    func,
                    Node::new(Op::ReadField, Type::I32, 4, [array, OBJECT_LENGTH_OFFSET as u32, 0]),
                );
                self.push(length);
            }
            ARRAY_FILL => {
                let count = self.pop();
                let value = self.pop();
                let start = self.pop();
                let array = self.pop();
                let (low, high) = self.value_bits(func, value, array_storage(module, first));
                self.helper(func, Helper::ArrayFill, &[array, start, low, high, count], Type::None);
            }
            ARRAY_COPY => {
                let count = self.pop();
                let source_start = self.pop();
                let source = self.pop();
                let destination_start = self.pop();
                let destination = self.pop();
                self.helper(
                    func,
                    Helper::ArrayCopy,
                    &[destination, destination_start, source, source_start, count],
                    Type::None,
                );
            }
            ARRAY_INIT_DATA | ARRAY_INIT_ELEM => {
                let count = self.pop();
                let source = self.pop();
                let destination = self.pop();
                let array = self.pop();
                let (segments, init) = if sub_opcode == ARRAY_INIT_DATA {
                    (offset_of!(InstanceData, data_segments), Helper::ArrayInitData)
                } else {
                    (offset_of!(InstanceData, element_segments), Helper::ArrayInitElem)
                };
                let segment = self.segment(func, segments, second);
                self.helper(func, init, &[array, segment, destination, source, count], Type::None);
            }
            REF_TEST | REF_TEST_NULL => {
                let reference = self.pop();
                let value = self.ref_test(
                    func,
                    module,
                    reference,
                    heap_types[0],
                    sub_opcode == REF_TEST_NULL,
                    false,
                );
                self.push(value);
            }
            REF_CAST | REF_CAST_NULL => {
                let reference = func.resolve(self.pop());
                self.ref_test(
                    func,
                    module,
                    reference,
                    heap_types[0],
                    sub_opcode == REF_CAST_NULL,
                    true,
                );
                self.push(reference);
            }
            BR_ON_CAST | BR_ON_CAST_FAIL => {
                let reference = *self.stack.last().expect("br_on_cast has an operand");
                let nullable = cast_flags & 2 != 0;
                let matches = self.ref_test(func, module, reference, heap_types[1], nullable, false);
                let condition = if sub_opcode == BR_ON_CAST {
                    matches
                } else {
                    self.unary(func, Op::Eqz, Type::I32, matches)
                };
                self.conditional_branch(func, first, condition);
            }
            ANY_CONVERT_EXTERN | EXTERN_CONVERT_ANY => {
                // References keep their bits between the any and extern hierarchies.
            }
            REF_I31 => {
                let value = self.pop();
                let reference = self.unary(func, Op::I31New, Type::Ref, value);
                self.push(reference);
            }
            I31_GET_S | I31_GET_U => {
                let reference = func.resolve(self.pop());
                Self::check_null(func, reference);
                let flags = u8::from(sub_opcode == I31_GET_S);
                let value = self.pure(func, Node::new(Op::I31Get, Type::I32, flags, [reference, 0, 0]));
                self.push(value);
            }
            _ => unreachable!("validated code has no unknown 0xFB instruction {sub_opcode:#x}"),
        }
    }
}

//! Accesses of memories without guard pages (memory64, and memories other than memory 0), and atomics. Both access
//! the memory at a `CheckedAddress`, which checks the access against the memory's current size; atomic accesses are
//! checked for alignment too, whatever memory they access.

use super::{Builder, load_kind, store_size_log2};
use crate::decode::{Decoder, MemoryArgument};
use crate::ir::{
    AtomicOp, CHECKED_ATOMIC, CHECKED_MEMORY64, Func, Helper, LOAD_ATOMIC, LoadKind, Node, Op, Type, Value,
};
use libwasm_module::Module;
use libwasm_module::abi::TRAP_EXPECTED_SHARED_MEMORY;
use libwasm_module::instruction_tables::{AtomicKind, atomic_kind};
use libwasm_module::opcode::atomic;
use libwasm_module::types::{AddressType, ValType};

impl Builder {
    /// The address of an access of `1 << size_log2` bytes at `index` + `argument.offset` in `argument.memory`, after
    /// checking it (`Op::CheckedAddress`).
    pub(super) fn checked_address(
        &mut self,
        func: &mut Func,
        module: &Module,
        argument: MemoryArgument,
        index: Value,
        size_log2: u8,
        atomic: bool,
    ) -> Value {
        let memory64 = module.memory_space[argument.memory as usize].limits.address_type == AddressType::I64;
        let index = func.resolve(index);
        let data = self.memory_data(func, argument.memory);
        let offset = self.constant(func, Type::I64, argument.offset);
        let mut flags = size_log2;
        if atomic {
            flags |= CHECKED_ATOMIC;
        }
        if memory64 {
            flags |= CHECKED_MEMORY64;
        }
        Self::append(
            func,
            Node::new(Op::CheckedAddress, Type::Pointer, flags, [data, index, offset]),
        )
    }

    /// A load of `kind` at `address`, a pointer.
    pub(super) fn load_at(&mut self, func: &mut Func, kind: LoadKind, ty: Type, address: Value, offset: u32) -> Value {
        let zero = self.constant(func, Type::I32, 0);
        Self::append(func, Node::new(Op::Load, ty, kind as u8, [address, zero, offset]))
    }

    /// A store of `1 << size_log2` bytes of `value` at `address`, a pointer.
    pub(super) fn store_at(&mut self, func: &mut Func, size_log2: u8, address: Value, offset: u32, value: Value) {
        let zero = self.constant(func, Type::I32, 0);
        let value = func.resolve(value);
        let start = func.operands.len() as u32;
        func.operands.extend_from_slice(&[address, zero, value]);
        Self::append(func, Node::new(Op::Store, Type::None, size_log2, [start, 3, offset]));
    }

    /// A core load or store in its bounds-checked form (quickening rule 1).
    pub(super) fn checked_access(&mut self, func: &mut Func, module: &Module, opcode: u8, argument: MemoryArgument) {
        if opcode <= libwasm_module::opcode::I64_LOAD32_U {
            let (kind, ty) = load_kind(opcode);
            let index = self.pop();
            let size_log2 = kind.size().trailing_zeros() as u8;
            let address = self.checked_address(func, module, argument, index, size_log2, false);
            let value = self.load_at(func, kind, ty, address, 0);
            self.push(value);
        } else {
            let value = self.pop();
            let index = self.pop();
            let size_log2 = store_size_log2(opcode);
            let address = self.checked_address(func, module, argument, index, size_log2, false);
            self.store_at(func, size_log2, address, 0, value);
        }
    }

    /// The instructions of the `0xFE` prefix.
    pub(super) fn atomic(&mut self, func: &mut Func, module: &Module, sub_opcode: u32, decoder: &Decoder<'_>) {
        let argument = decoder.atomic_argument();
        let kind = atomic_kind(sub_opcode).expect("validated code has no unknown atomic instructions");
        let ir = |value: ValType| if value == ValType::I64 { Type::I64 } else { Type::I32 };
        match kind {
            AtomicKind::Fence => {
                Self::append(func, Node::new(Op::AtomicFence, Type::None, 0, [0; 3]));
            }
            AtomicKind::Notify => {
                let count = self.pop();
                let index = self.pop();
                let address = self.checked_address(func, module, argument, index, 2, true);
                // Only a shared memory can have threads waiting on it.
                let woken = if module.memory_space[argument.memory as usize].limits.shared {
                    self.helper(func, Helper::AtomicNotify, &[address, count], Type::I32)
                } else {
                    self.constant(func, Type::I32, 0)
                };
                self.push(woken);
            }
            AtomicKind::Wait { value } => {
                let timeout = self.pop();
                let expected = self.pop();
                let index = self.pop();
                let size_log2 = if value == ValType::I64 { 3 } else { 2 };
                let address = self.checked_address(func, module, argument, index, size_log2, true);
                if !module.memory_space[argument.memory as usize].limits.shared {
                    self.terminate(
                        func,
                        Node::new(Op::Trap, Type::None, 0, [TRAP_EXPECTED_SHARED_MEMORY, 0, 0]),
                        &[],
                    );
                    self.set_unreachable();
                    return;
                }
                let size = self.constant(func, Type::I64, 1 << size_log2);
                let result = self.helper(func, Helper::AtomicWait, &[address, expected, timeout, size], Type::I32);
                self.push(result);
            }
            AtomicKind::Load { value, size } => {
                let index = self.pop();
                let size_log2 = size.trailing_zeros() as u8;
                let address = self.checked_address(func, module, argument, index, size_log2, true);
                let kind = match (value, size) {
                    (ValType::I64, 8) => LoadKind::I64,
                    (ValType::I64, 4) => LoadKind::I64U32,
                    (ValType::I64, 2) => LoadKind::I64U16,
                    (ValType::I64, _) => LoadKind::I64U8,
                    (_, 4) => LoadKind::I32,
                    (_, 2) => LoadKind::I32U16,
                    _ => LoadKind::I32U8,
                };
                // NB: Plain loads are sequentially consistent on x86-64, where stores are locked exchanges; AArch64
                //     loads them with acquire semantics.
                let zero = self.constant(func, Type::I32, 0);
                let loaded = Self::append(
                    func,
                    Node::new(Op::Load, ir(value), kind as u8 | LOAD_ATOMIC, [address, zero, 0]),
                );
                self.push(loaded);
            }
            AtomicKind::Store { value, size } => {
                let stored = func.resolve(self.pop());
                let index = self.pop();
                let size_log2 = size.trailing_zeros() as u8;
                let address = self.checked_address(func, module, argument, index, size_log2, true);
                // An exchange is a sequentially consistent store.
                Self::append(
                    func,
                    Node::new(
                        Op::AtomicRmw,
                        ir(value),
                        size_log2,
                        [address, stored, AtomicOp::Exchange as u32],
                    ),
                );
            }
            AtomicKind::ReadModifyWrite { value, size } => {
                let operand = func.resolve(self.pop());
                let index = self.pop();
                let size_log2 = size.trailing_zeros() as u8;
                let address = self.checked_address(func, module, argument, index, size_log2, true);
                let op = AtomicOp::from_index((sub_opcode - atomic::I32_ATOMIC_RMW_ADD) / 7);
                let old = Self::append(
                    func,
                    Node::new(Op::AtomicRmw, ir(value), size_log2, [address, operand, op as u32]),
                );
                self.push(old);
            }
            AtomicKind::CompareExchange { value, size } => {
                let replacement = func.resolve(self.pop());
                let expected = func.resolve(self.pop());
                let index = self.pop();
                let size_log2 = size.trailing_zeros() as u8;
                let address = self.checked_address(func, module, argument, index, size_log2, true);
                let old = Self::append(
                    func,
                    Node::new(
                        Op::AtomicCompareExchange,
                        ir(value),
                        size_log2,
                        [address, expected, replacement],
                    ),
                );
                self.push(old);
            }
        }
    }
}

/*

//! The builder: one forward pass over a validated, quickened function body that produces typed SSA.
//!
//! Locals become SSA values with the algorithm of Braun et al. ("Simple and Efficient Construction of SSA Form"),
//! specialized for structured control flow:
//!
//! - The merge block of a `block` or `if` is created at its `end`, when every branch to it is known, so it is sealed
//!   from the start. Only loop headers are unsealed while their body is built: their back edges are the branches to
//!   the loop inside it, and the loop's `end` seals them.
//! - Reading a local first looks at a dense per-local cache of the last definition, tagged with its block. Older
//!   definitions move into function-wide chunks of a block's locals when the cache entry is overwritten.
//!   A read that finds neither walks the predecessors, with an explicit stack, memoizing what it finds; reads in an
//!   unsealed loop header make incomplete phis.
//! - Phis that turn out trivial become `Forward` nodes. Cleanup removes the rest of them, to a fixed point.
//!
//! The operand stack holds values; values flowing into merges become explicit phis, as the block types say.
//! Unreachable code is skipped, only tracking nesting. Nodes fold as they are created (`fold`), and pure nodes are
//! value numbered in a table whose entries are undone when the construct that made them ends, so that every hit
//! dominates its use. Global values are numbered too, keyed by epochs that `global.set` and calls advance.

mod calls;
mod exceptions;
pub mod fold;
pub mod gc;
mod memories;
mod simd;
mod tables;

use crate::decode::{BlockType, Decoder, Instruction};
use crate::ir::{BlockId, Func, IntCondition, LoadKind, Loop, NONE, Node, Op, Type, Value};
use crate::ir::{FLAG_IMMUTABLE, FloatCondition};
use crate::table::Table;
use calls::CallKind;
use fold::Folded;
use libwasm_module::Module;
use libwasm_module::abi::{InstanceData, TRAP_NULL_REFERENCE};
use libwasm_module::opcode;
use libwasm_module::quickening;
use libwasm_module::types::{FuncType, ValType};
use std::mem::offset_of;

/// The IR type of a WebAssembly value type, if the JIT compiles values of it.
pub fn ir_type(value: ValType) -> Option<Type> {
    match value {
        ValType::I32 => Some(Type::I32),
        ValType::I64 => Some(Type::I64),
        ValType::F32 => Some(Type::F32),
        ValType::F64 => Some(Type::F64),
        ValType::V128 => Some(Type::V128),
        ValType::Ref(_) => Some(Type::Ref),
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum ControlKind {
    Function,
    Block,
    Loop,
    If,
    Else,
    /// A `try_table`, the body of a legacy `try`, and a legacy `catch` or `catch_all` handler.
    TryTable,
    Try,
    Catch,
}

/// The parameter and result types of a block, as ranges of `Builder::types`.
type Signature = ((u32, u32), (u32, u32));

/// A construct whose `end` is still ahead.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Control {
    kind: ControlKind,
    /// The types of its parameters and results, in `Builder::types`.
    params: (u32, u32),
    results: (u32, u32),
    /// The height of the operand stack below its parameters.
    height: u32,
    /// The loop's header, or for `if` the block that branches on the condition.
    block: BlockId,
    /// The `else` edge of an `if`: its slot in `Func::successors`, or NONE once taken care of.
    else_slot: u32,
    /// For `if`, where its parameters start in `Builder::edge_values`, for the second arm.
    if_params: u32,
    /// The branches to the label, as a list through `Builder::edges`.
    edges: u32,
    /// The block that branched to the label last, so that a `br_table` adds one edge per block.
    last_edge_block: BlockId,
    /// Whether the rest of the construct is unreachable.
    unreachable: bool,
    /// Where the construct's entries start in the value numbering log.
    numbering_mark: u32,
    /// For loops, their index in `Func::loops` and the start of their incomplete phis.
    loop_index: u32,
    incomplete_start: u32,
    /// For a handler (see `exceptions.rs`): the exceptions thrown in its region, as a list through `Builder::edges`
    /// of edges carrying the exception, and the handler around it in `Builder::controls`, or NONE.
    throws: u32,
    outer_handler: u32,
    /// For `try_table` and legacy `try`: the start and count of its clauses in `Builder::clauses`.
    clauses: (u32, u32),
    /// For a legacy handler: the exception it caught, or NONE if nothing throws to it, and its next clause.
    exception: Value,
    next_clause: u32,
}

impl Control {
    fn label_arity(&self) -> (u32, u32) {
        if self.kind == ControlKind::Loop {
            self.params
        } else {
            self.results
        }
    }
}

/// A branch to a label whose block may not exist yet: its source, the successor slot to fill, and the values it
/// carries, in `Builder::edge_values`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Edge {
    block: BlockId,
    slot: u32,
    values: u32,
    next: u32,
}

/// The key of a value numbering entry: a node's op, type and flags, then its arguments.
type NumberingKey = [u32; 4];

fn numbering_key(node: &Node) -> NumberingKey {
    [
        node.op as u32 | ((node.ty as u32) << 16) | (u32::from(node.flags) << 24),
        node.args[0],
        node.args[1],
        node.args[2],
    ]
}

/// A node of the explicit stack that `read_local_slow` walks predecessors with.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct ReadFrame {
    block: BlockId,
    /// The phi whose inputs are being read, or NONE.
    phi: Value,
    /// Where in `read_values` the values of the predecessors read so far start, for a merge whose phi is only made
    /// if they differ, or NONE.
    collected: u32,
    next_predecessor: u32,
}

/// The builder's state, kept between compiles so that its storage is reused.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Builder {
    local_types: Vec<Type>,
    /// The last definition of each local and its block.
    current: Vec<(BlockId, Value)>,
    /// The value of each local at the end of each block, where known, in chunks of `DEFINITION_CHUNK` locals of a
    /// block: `definition_chunks` maps (block, chunk index) to where the chunk starts in `definitions`, in chunks. A
    /// block has the chunks of the locals it knows only, and a local it does not know is NONE in its chunk.
    ///
    /// OPTIMIZATION: Reads memoize in every block they walk through, so most blocks end up knowing most locals. A map
    /// from (block, local) to value took several times the memory of this, hundreds of megabytes for the largest
    /// functions.
    definition_chunks: Table<u64>,
    definitions: Vec<Value>,
    /// The locals each loop writes, itself or in loops in it: keyed by (loop, local), and as a list per loop of
    /// (local, next entry) from its entry in `loop_write_heads`.
    loop_writes: Table<u64>,
    loop_write_list: Vec<(u32, u32)>,
    loop_write_heads: Vec<u32>,
    sealed: Vec<bool>,
    /// (header, phi, local) of every incomplete phi of an unsealed loop header.
    incomplete: Vec<(BlockId, Value, u32)>,
    stack: Vec<Value>,
    controls: Vec<Control>,
    edges: Vec<Edge>,
    edge_values: Vec<Value>,
    types: Vec<Type>,
    /// Value numbers, and constants, which are never undone. A value of NONE is no entry.
    numbering: Table<NumberingKey>,
    numbering_log: Vec<(NumberingKey, Value)>,
    global_epochs: Vec<u32>,
    call_epoch: u32,
    read_stack: Vec<ReadFrame>,
    read_values: Vec<Value>,
    scratch_values: Vec<Value>,
    scratch_blocks: Vec<BlockId>,
    params: Vec<Value>,
    current_block: BlockId,
    instance: Value,
    memory_base: Value,
    /// The zero vector, which every v128 local starts as, once made.
    vector_zero: Value,
    /// The next of the function's `try_regions` a legacy `try` may be (see `begin_try`).
    try_region_cursor: usize,
    /// The byte offsets of struct fields, by (type index, field index); the field count gives the size.
    field_offsets: Table<u64>,
    /// What an OSR compile needs (see `build_osr`), or what probing for one found.
    osr: Option<Osr>,
    /// The innermost handler whose region the code is in, as an index into `controls`, or NONE.
    handler: u32,
    clauses: Vec<exceptions::Clause>,
    /// The function, among the module's defined ones.
    defined: u32,
}

/// An OSR compile: the function as a continuation of an interpreter frame at a loop.
///
/// Its only parameter is the frame's fp. Its entry block branches, on a constant, to a block that loads the frame's
/// locals and operand stack and jumps to the header of the outermost loop around the frame's position, and to the
/// function's code as it starts, which never runs. That keeps the entry block dominating everything. Every loop
/// entered this way has a second way in, from the frame, besides its entry and back edges, and every value on the
/// operand stack at its header becomes a phi of them.
///
/// A loop in other loops is entered through them, so that each loop keeps a single header: each loop around it starts
/// with a branch on a flag (a local of its own, which only the way in from the frame sets), which goes from the header
/// to the next loop in, through a block that loads the operand stack at that loop from the frame.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Osr {
    /// The module offset of the loop instruction.
    pc: u32,
    /// The types of the operand stack at the loop, from bottom to top, parameters included.
    stack_types: Vec<Type>,
    /// The module offsets of the loops around it, outermost first, and how many of them have been entered.
    around: Vec<u32>,
    entered: usize,
    /// While probing: whether the loop was found and reachable, and the loops open where the probe is.
    found: bool,
    probing: bool,
    open_loops: Vec<u32>,
    /// The frame's fp, and the local that flags the way in from the frame (see above).
    frame: Value,
    flag: u32,
    /// The block that jumps to the next loop to enter from the frame, the slot of that jump, and the values the
    /// operand stack has at that loop's header, from the frame.
    block: BlockId,
    slot: u32,
    stack: Vec<Value>,
    /// The loops entered from the frame.
    entries: Vec<OsrEntry>,
}

/// A loop an OSR compile enters from the frame: its index, the indices of its entry edge and its edge from the frame,
/// and the phis of the values below its parameters (phi, value from the entry, value from the frame).
struct OsrEntry {
    loop_index: u32,
    entry_edge: u32,
    edge: u32,
    below: Vec<(Value, Value, Value)>,
}

/// Where an OSR compile enters a function: the types of the operand stack at the loop, and the loops around it.
pub type OsrEntryPoint = (Vec<Type>, Vec<u32>);

/// The fp offset of the local slot `local` of an interpreter frame.
fn frame_local_offset(local: u32) -> i32 {
    8 * local as i32
}

/// How many locals a chunk of `Builder::definitions` holds.
const DEFINITION_CHUNK: u32 = 32;

fn key(block: BlockId, local: u32) -> u64 {
    (u64::from(block) << 32) | u64::from(local)
}

fn instance_offset(offset: usize) -> u32 {
    offset as u32
}

impl Builder {
    fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.local_types.clear();
        self.current.clear();
        self.definition_chunks.clear();
        self.definitions.clear();
        self.loop_writes.clear();
        self.loop_write_list.clear();
        self.loop_write_heads.clear();
        self.sealed.clear();
        self.incomplete.clear();
        self.stack.clear();
        self.controls.clear();
        self.edges.clear();
        self.edge_values.clear();
        self.types.clear();
        self.numbering.clear();
        self.numbering_log.clear();
        self.global_epochs.clear();
        self.call_epoch = 0;
        self.read_stack.clear();
        self.read_values.clear();
        self.params.clear();
        self.vector_zero = NONE;
        self.try_region_cursor = 0;
        self.field_offsets.clear();
        self.handler = NONE;
        self.clauses.clear();
    }

    /// Builds the IR of the defined function `index` (counting imports) of `module` into `func`.
    pub fn build(&mut self, module: &Module, index: u32, func: &mut Func) {
        self.osr = None;
        self.build_function(module, index, func);
    }

    /// The types of the operand stack at the loop at module offset `pc`, and the loops around it, if an OSR compile
    /// can enter it: if it is reachable and in no legacy handler. Builds the function into `func` to find out.
    pub fn probe_osr(&mut self, module: &Module, index: u32, pc: u32, func: &mut Func) -> Option<OsrEntryPoint> {
        self.osr = Some(Osr {
            pc,
            probing: true,
            ..Osr::default()
        });
        self.build_function(module, index, func);
        let osr = self.osr.take().expect("the probe is there");
        osr.found.then_some((osr.stack_types, osr.around))
    }

    /// Builds the OSR compile of the function at the loop at `pc`, whose operand stack has `stack_types` there (see
    /// `probe_osr`).
    pub fn build_osr(
        &mut self,
        module: &Module,
        index: u32,
        pc: u32,
        (stack_types, around): OsrEntryPoint,
        func: &mut Func,
    ) {
        self.osr = Some(Osr {
            pc,
            stack_types,
            around,
            ..Osr::default()
        });
        self.build_function(module, index, func);
        self.osr = None;
    }

    fn is_osr_compile(&self) -> bool {
        self.osr.as_ref().is_some_and(|osr| !osr.probing)
    }

    fn build_function(&mut self, module: &Module, index: u32, func: &mut Func) {
        self.clear();
        func.clear();
        let defined = (index - module.imported_function_count) as usize;
        self.defined = defined as u32;
        let body = &module.code[defined];
        let ty = module.function_type(index).expect("functions have function types");
        let start = body.code.start as usize;
        for &param in &ty.params {
            let param = ir_type(param).expect("the JIT has a type for every value");
            func.params.push(param);
            self.local_types.push(param);
        }
        for &result in &ty.results {
            let result = ir_type(result).expect("the JIT has a type for every value");
            func.results.push(result);
        }
        for &(count, local) in &body.locals {
            let local = ir_type(local).expect("the JIT has a type for every value");
            self.local_types.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(local, count as usize));
        }
        self.current.resize(self.local_types.len(), (NONE, NONE));
        self.global_epochs.resize(module.global_space.len(), 0);

        let mut entry = self.new_block(func);
        self.start_block(func, entry);
        self.sealed[entry as usize] = true;
        self.instance = self.entry_value(func, Op::Instance, Type::Pointer, 0);
        self.memory_base = self.entry_value(func, Op::MemoryBase, Type::Pointer, 0);
        if self.is_osr_compile() {
            entry = self.enter_osr(func);
        } else {
            for (param_index, &param) in func.params.clone().iter().enumerate() {
                let value = self.entry_value(func, Op::Param, param, param_index as u32);
                self.params.push(value);
            }
        }
        let results = self.push_types(&ty.results);
        self.controls.push(Control {
            kind: ControlKind::Function,
            params: (0, 0),
            results,
            height: 0,
            block: entry,
            else_slot: NONE,
            if_params: 0,
            edges: NONE,
            last_edge_block: NONE,
            unreachable: false,
            numbering_mark: 0,
            loop_index: NONE,
            incomplete_start: 0,
            throws: NONE,
            outer_handler: NONE,
            clauses: (0, 0),
            exception: NONE,
            next_clause: 0,
        });

        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&module.bytes, start, body.code.end as usize);
        while !self.controls.is_empty() {
            let pc = decoder.position();
            let instruction = decoder.decode();
            if self.controls.last().expect("there is a construct").unreachable {
                self.skip(func, module, &instruction, &mut decoder, pc);
                continue;
            }
            self.instruction(func, module, instruction, &decoder, pc);
        }
    }

    // Blocks.

    /// Makes the entry of an OSR compile (see `Osr`) and returns the block the function's code starts in.
    /// Loads the bottom values of the operand stack of the interpreter frame at `frame`, of types `types`.
    fn load_frame_stack(func: &mut Func, frame: Value, types: &[Type]) -> Vec<Value> {
        let mut offset = -(libwasm_module::abi::FRAME_HEADER_SIZE as i32);
        let mut stack = Vec::with_capacity(types.len());
        for &ty in types {
            // The operand stack grows down from the frame header; a value's lowest slot is its first.
            offset -= 8 * ty.slots() as i32;
            stack.push(Self::append(
                func,
                Node::new(Op::FrameLoad, ty, 0, [frame, offset as u32, 0]),
            ));
        }
        stack
    }

    fn enter_osr(&mut self, func: &mut Func) -> BlockId {
        let param_types = std::mem::take(&mut func.params);
        func.params.push(Type::Pointer);
        let frame = self.entry_value(func, Op::Param, Type::Pointer, 0);
        // The function's own code never runs, but it must build as it would, so its parameters are not constants
        // there.
        for (local, &ty) in param_types.iter().enumerate() {
            let indirect = u8::from(ty == Type::V128);
            let value = Self::append(
                func,
                Node::new(
                    Op::FrameLoad,
                    ty,
                    indirect,
                    [frame, frame_local_offset(local as u32) as u32, 0],
                ),
            );
            self.params.push(value);
        }
        let from_frame = self.new_block(func);
        let start = self.new_block(func);
        let always = self.constant(func, Type::I32, 1);
        let entry = self.current_block;
        self.terminate(
            func,
            Node::new(Op::Branch, Type::None, 0, [always, 0, 0]),
            &[from_frame, start],
        );
        Self::set_predecessors(func, from_frame, &[entry]);
        Self::set_predecessors(func, start, &[entry]);
        self.start_block(func, from_frame);
        for local in 0..self.local_types.len() as u32 {
            let ty = self.local_types[local as usize];
            let indirect = u8::from(ty == Type::V128);
            let value = Self::append(
                func,
                Node::new(
                    Op::FrameLoad,
                    ty,
                    indirect,
                    [frame, frame_local_offset(local) as u32, 0],
                ),
            );
            self.write_local(local, value);
        }
        let flag = self.local_types.len() as u32;
        self.local_types.push(Type::I32);
        self.current.push((NONE, NONE));
        let one = self.constant(func, Type::I32, 1);
        self.write_local(flag, one);
        let stack_types = std::mem::take(&mut self.osr.as_mut().expect("this is an OSR compile").stack_types);
        let stack = Self::load_frame_stack(func, frame, &stack_types);
        let slot = self.jump(func, NONE);
        let osr = self.osr.as_mut().expect("this is an OSR compile");
        osr.frame = frame;
        osr.flag = flag;
        osr.block = from_frame;
        osr.slot = slot;
        osr.stack = stack;
        osr.stack_types = stack_types;
        self.start_block(func, start);
        start
    }

    fn new_block(&mut self, func: &mut Func) -> BlockId {
        let block = func.blocks.len() as BlockId;
        let loop_index = self
            .controls
            .iter()
            .rev()
            .find(|control| control.kind == ControlKind::Loop)
            .map_or(NONE, |control| control.loop_index);
        func.blocks.push(crate::ir::Block {
            loop_index,
            ..Default::default()
        });
        self.sealed.push(true);
        block
    }

    fn start_block(&mut self, func: &mut Func, block: BlockId) {
        func.blocks[block as usize].start = func.nodes.len() as u32;
        self.current_block = block;
    }

    fn set_predecessors(func: &mut Func, block: BlockId, predecessors: &[BlockId]) {
        let data = &mut func.blocks[block as usize];
        data.predecessors_start = func.predecessors.len() as u32;
        data.predecessor_count = predecessors.len() as u32;
        func.predecessors.extend_from_slice(predecessors);
    }

    /// Ends the current block with `node`, whose successors are `successors` (NONE for those not known yet).
    /// Returns the slot of the first successor.
    fn terminate(&mut self, func: &mut Func, node: Node, successors: &[BlockId]) -> u32 {
        func.nodes.push(node);
        let slot = func.successors.len() as u32;
        let block = &mut func.blocks[self.current_block as usize];
        block.end = func.nodes.len() as u32;
        block.successors_start = slot;
        block.successor_count = successors.len() as u32;
        func.successors.extend_from_slice(successors);
        slot
    }

    // Nodes.

    fn append(func: &mut Func, node: Node) -> Value {
        func.nodes.push(node);
        func.nodes.len() as Value - 1
    }

    fn entry_value(&mut self, func: &mut Func, op: Op, ty: Type, argument: u32) -> Value {
        Self::append(func, Node::new(op, ty, 0, [argument, 0, 0]))
    }

    fn constant(&mut self, func: &mut Func, ty: Type, bits: u64) -> Value {
        if ty == Type::V128 {
            if self.vector_zero == NONE {
                self.vector_zero = self.vector_constant(func, u128::from(bits));
            }
            debug_assert_eq!(bits, 0);
            return self.vector_zero;
        }
        let node = if ty.is_64() {
            Node::new(Op::Const64, ty, 0, [bits as u32, (bits >> 32) as u32, 0])
        } else {
            Node::new(Op::Const32, ty, 0, [bits as u32, 0, 0])
        };
        let key = numbering_key(&node);
        if let Some(value) = self.numbering.get(key) {
            return value;
        }
        let value = Self::append(func, node);
        // NB: Constants have no position, so they are never undone.
        self.numbering.insert(key, value);
        value
    }

    /// A pure node, or the value of an equal one that dominates the current position.
    fn pure(&mut self, func: &mut Func, node: Node) -> Value {
        let key = numbering_key(&node);
        if let Some(value) = self.numbering.get(key)
            && value != NONE
        {
            return value;
        }
        let value = Self::append(func, node);
        self.number(key, value);
        value
    }

    fn number(&mut self, key: NumberingKey, value: Value) {
        let previous = self.numbering.insert(key, value).unwrap_or(NONE);
        self.numbering_log.push((key, previous));
    }

    /// Undoes the value numbering entries made since `mark`.
    fn unnumber(&mut self, mark: u32) {
        while self.numbering_log.len() > mark as usize {
            let (key, previous) = self.numbering_log.pop().expect("the log is longer than the mark");
            self.numbering.insert(key, previous);
        }
    }

    fn binary(&mut self, func: &mut Func, op: Op, ty: Type, a: Value, b: Value) -> Value {
        self.binary_with_flags(func, op, ty, 0, a, b)
    }

    fn binary_with_flags(&mut self, func: &mut Func, op: Op, ty: Type, flags: u8, a: Value, b: Value) -> Value {
        let (a, b) = (func.resolve(a), func.resolve(b));
        let result_type = if op == Op::Compare { Type::I32 } else { ty };
        match fold::binary(func, op, ty, flags, a, b) {
            Folded::Value(value) => value,
            Folded::Constant(bits) => self.constant(func, result_type, bits),
            Folded::Node { op, flags, a, b } => {
                let node = Node::new(op, result_type, flags, [a, b, 0]);
                if node.effect() == crate::ir::Effect::Pure {
                    self.pure(func, node)
                } else {
                    Self::append(func, node)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn unary(&mut self, func: &mut Func, op: Op, ty: Type, a: Value) -> Value {
        let a = func.resolve(a);
        match fold::unary(func, op, ty, a) {
            Some(Folded::Value(value)) => value,
            Some(Folded::Constant(bits)) => self.constant(func, ty, bits),
            Some(Folded::Node { op, flags, a, b }) => self.pure(func, Node::new(op, ty, flags, [a, b, 0])),
            None => {
                let node = Node::new(op, ty, 0, [a, 0, 0]);
                if node.effect() == crate::ir::Effect::Pure {
                    self.pure(func, node)
                } else {
                    Self::append(func, node)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Locals (see the module documentation).

    fn write_local(&mut self, local: u32, value: Value) {
        let (block, previous) = self.current[local as usize];
        if block != self.current_block && block != NONE {
            self.define(block, local, previous);
        }
        self.current[local as usize] = (self.current_block, value);
    }

    fn note_loop_write(&mut self, loop_index: u32, local: u32) {
        if loop_index == NONE || self.loop_writes.insert(key(loop_index, local), 1).is_some() {
            return;
        }
        if self.loop_write_heads.len() <= loop_index as usize {
            self.loop_write_heads.resize(loop_index as usize + 1, NONE);
        }
        let next = self.loop_write_heads[loop_index as usize];
        self.loop_write_heads[loop_index as usize] = self.loop_write_list.len() as u32;
        self.loop_write_list.push((local, next));
    }

    /// Counts the locals a loop that has ended writes as written by the loop around it.
    fn propagate_loop_writes(&mut self, func: &Func, loop_index: u32) {
        let parent = func.loops[loop_index as usize].parent;
        let mut entry = self.loop_write_heads.get(loop_index as usize).copied().unwrap_or(NONE);
        while entry != NONE && parent != NONE {
            let (local, next) = self.loop_write_list[entry as usize];
            self.note_loop_write(parent, local);
            entry = next;
        }
    }

    /// Records `value` as the value of `local` at the end of `block`.
    fn memoize(&mut self, block: BlockId, local: u32, value: Value) {
        if block == self.current_block {
            self.write_local(local, value);
        } else {
            self.define(block, local, value);
        }
    }

    fn define(&mut self, block: BlockId, local: u32, value: Value) {
        let chunk_key = key(block, local / DEFINITION_CHUNK);
        let start = match self.definition_chunks.get(chunk_key) {
            Some(start) => start,
            None => {
                let start = u32::try_from(self.definitions.len() / DEFINITION_CHUNK as usize)
                    .expect("the chunks of a function fit in memory");
                self.definition_chunks.insert(chunk_key, start);
                self.definitions
                    .resize(self.definitions.len() + DEFINITION_CHUNK as usize, NONE);
                start
            }
        };
        self.definitions[start as usize * DEFINITION_CHUNK as usize + (local % DEFINITION_CHUNK) as usize] = value;
    }

    fn lookup(&self, func: &Func, block: BlockId, local: u32) -> Option<Value> {
        let (cached_block, value) = self.current[local as usize];
        if cached_block == block {
            return Some(func.resolve(value));
        }
        let start = self.definition_chunks.get(key(block, local / DEFINITION_CHUNK))?;
        let value = self.definitions[start as usize * DEFINITION_CHUNK as usize + (local % DEFINITION_CHUNK) as usize];
        (value != NONE).then(|| func.resolve(value))
    }

    fn read_local(&mut self, func: &mut Func, block: BlockId, local: u32) -> Value {
        if let Some(value) = self.lookup(func, block, local) {
            return value;
        }
        self.read_local_slow(func, block, local)
    }

    fn new_phi(func: &mut Func, block: BlockId, ty: Type) -> Value {
        let first = func.blocks[block as usize].first_phi;
        let phi = Self::append(func, Node::new(Op::Phi, ty, 0, [0, 0, first]));
        func.blocks[block as usize].first_phi = phi;
        phi
    }

    /// The value of a local that a block is entered with: a parameter, or zero.
    fn initial_value(&mut self, func: &mut Func, local: u32) -> Value {
        if (local as usize) < self.params.len() {
            return self.params[local as usize];
        }
        let ty = self.local_types[local as usize];
        self.constant(func, ty, 0)
    }

    /// Whether a read of a local can be on a cycle through `block`: only if the block is in a loop whose header is
    /// sealed, so that reads go around the back edges.
    fn may_be_on_cycle(&self, func: &Func, block: BlockId) -> bool {
        let loop_index = func.blocks[block as usize].loop_index;
        loop_index != NONE && self.sealed[func.loops[loop_index as usize].header as usize]
    }

    fn read_local_slow(&mut self, func: &mut Func, block: BlockId, local: u32) -> Value {
        let ty = self.local_types[local as usize];
        let base = self.read_stack.len();
        self.read_stack.push(ReadFrame {
            block,
            phi: NONE,
            collected: NONE,
            next_predecessor: 0,
        });
        // The value the frame on top of the stack delivers, if it is done.
        let mut delivered: Option<Value> = None;
        loop {
            let top = self.read_stack.len() - 1;
            if let Some(value) = delivered.take() {
                let frame = &mut self.read_stack[top];
                if frame.collected != NONE {
                    self.read_values.push(value);
                    frame.next_predecessor += 1;
                } else if frame.phi != NONE {
                    let phi = func.nodes[frame.phi as usize];
                    func.operands[(phi.args[0] + frame.next_predecessor) as usize] = value;
                    frame.next_predecessor += 1;
                } else {
                    let frame_block = frame.block;
                    self.read_stack.pop();
                    self.memoize(frame_block, local, value);
                    if self.read_stack.len() == base {
                        return value;
                    }
                    delivered = Some(value);
                    continue;
                }
            }
            let frame = self.read_stack[top];
            if frame.phi != NONE || frame.collected != NONE {
                let predecessors = func.predecessors(frame.block);
                if (frame.next_predecessor as usize) < predecessors.len() {
                    let predecessor = predecessors[frame.next_predecessor as usize];
                    if let Some(value) = self.lookup(func, predecessor, local) {
                        delivered = Some(value);
                    } else {
                        self.read_stack.push(ReadFrame {
                            block: predecessor,
                            phi: NONE,
                            collected: NONE,
                            next_predecessor: 0,
                        });
                    }
                    continue;
                }
                self.read_stack.pop();
                let value = if frame.phi != NONE {
                    let value = Self::try_remove_trivial_phi(func, frame.phi);
                    if value != frame.phi {
                        self.memoize(frame.block, local, value);
                    }
                    value
                } else {
                    let value = self.merge_collected(func, frame.block, ty, frame.collected);
                    self.memoize(frame.block, local, value);
                    value
                };
                if self.read_stack.len() == base {
                    return value;
                }
                delivered = Some(value);
                continue;
            }
            // A frame visited for the first time.
            if let Some(value) = self.lookup(func, frame.block, local) {
                delivered = Some(value);
                continue;
            }
            if !self.sealed[frame.block as usize] {
                let phi = Self::new_phi(func, frame.block, ty);
                self.incomplete.push((frame.block, phi, local));
                delivered = Some(phi);
                continue;
            }
            let loop_index = func.blocks[frame.block as usize].loop_index;
            let entered_from_frame = self
                .osr
                .as_ref()
                .is_some_and(|osr| osr.entries.iter().any(|entry| entry.loop_index == loop_index));
            if self.may_be_on_cycle(func, frame.block)
                && !entered_from_frame
                && self.loop_writes.get(key(loop_index, local)).is_none()
            {
                // OPTIMIZATION: Everywhere in a loop that does not write the local, it has the value it entered
                // the loop with. Reads after a loop would otherwise go around all of it.
                let header = func.loops[loop_index as usize].header;
                let entry = func.predecessors(header)[0];
                if let Some(value) = self.lookup(func, entry, local) {
                    delivered = Some(value);
                } else {
                    self.read_stack.push(ReadFrame {
                        block: entry,
                        phi: NONE,
                        collected: NONE,
                        next_predecessor: 0,
                    });
                }
                continue;
            }
            let predecessors = func.predecessors(frame.block);
            match predecessors.len() {
                0 => {
                    let value = self.initial_value(func, local);
                    delivered = Some(value);
                }
                1 => {
                    let predecessor = predecessors[0];
                    if let Some(value) = self.lookup(func, predecessor, local) {
                        delivered = Some(value);
                    } else {
                        self.read_stack.push(ReadFrame {
                            block: predecessor,
                            phi: NONE,
                            collected: NONE,
                            next_predecessor: 0,
                        });
                    }
                }
                // OPTIMIZATION: Where no read can come back around to the block, its phi is only made if the
                // predecessors' values differ. Most merges of large functions need no phi for most locals, and
                // making and forwarding them took most of the build time of such functions.
                _ if !self.may_be_on_cycle(func, frame.block) => {
                    self.read_stack[top].collected = self.read_values.len() as u32;
                }
                count => {
                    let phi = Self::new_phi(func, frame.block, ty);
                    let start = func.operands.len() as u32;
                    func.operands.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(phi, count));
                    func.nodes[phi as usize].args[0] = start;
                    func.nodes[phi as usize].args[1] = count as u32;
                    // NB: Memoized before its inputs are read, so that cycles through it end at it.
                    self.memoize(frame.block, local, phi);
                    self.read_stack[top].phi = phi;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The value of a local at the start of `block`, given its predecessors' values in `read_values` from `start`
    /// on, which it removes: their value if they are all the same, else a new phi of them.
    fn merge_collected(&mut self, func: &mut Func, block: BlockId, ty: Type, start: u32) -> Value {
        let values = &self.read_values[start as usize..];
        let first = func.resolve(values[0]);
        let value = if values[1..].iter().all(|value| func.resolve(*value) == first) {
            first
        } else {
            let phi = Self::new_phi(func, block, ty);
            let operands = func.operands.len() as u32;
            func.operands.extend_from_slice(values);
            func.nodes[phi as usize].args[0] = operands;
            func.nodes[phi as usize].args[1] = values.len() as u32;
            phi
        };
        self.read_values.truncate(start as usize);
        value
    }

    /// Value `index` of each of the edges `collect_edges()` collected, merged at the start of `block`.
    fn merge_edge_values(&mut self, func: &mut Func, block: BlockId, ty: Type, index: usize) -> Value {
        let start = self.read_values.len() as u32;
        for position in 0..self.scratch_values.len() {
            let edge = self.scratch_values[position];
            let value = self.edge_values[self.edges[edge as usize].values as usize + index];
            self.read_values.push(value);
        }
        self.merge_collected(func, block, ty, start)
    }

    /// Forwards `phi` if its inputs are only itself and one other value, which it returns; returns `phi` otherwise.
    fn try_remove_trivial_phi(func: &mut Func, phi: Value) -> Value {
        // NB: A phi with no other input is only reachable through itself: the loop is never entered with a value for
        //     it, and the phi stays.
        let Some(same) = func.trivial_phi_input(phi) else {
            return phi;
        };
        func.forward(phi, same);
        same
    }

    // Types and labels.

    fn push_types(&mut self, types: &[ValType]) -> (u32, u32) {
        let start = self.types.len() as u32;
        for &ty in types {
            let ty = ir_type(ty).expect("the JIT has a type for every value");
            self.types.push(ty);
        }
        (start, types.len() as u32)
    }

    fn block_signature(&mut self, module: &Module, block_type: BlockType) -> Signature {
        match block_type {
            BlockType::Empty => ((0, 0), (0, 0)),
            BlockType::Value(value) => ((0, 0), self.push_types(&[value])),
            BlockType::Function(index) => {
                let function: &FuncType = module.types[index as usize]
                    .as_func()
                    .expect("block types are functions");
                let params = self.push_types(&function.params);
                let results = self.push_types(&function.results);
                (params, results)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Ends the current block with a jump to `target`, or to a block the caller sets later if it is NONE, and returns
    /// the jump's successor slot.
    fn jump(&mut self, func: &mut Func, target: BlockId) -> u32 {
        self.terminate(func, Node::new(Op::Jump, Type::None, 0, [0; 3]), &[target])
    }

    /// Records a branch from the current block to the label of `controls[index]`, carrying the top values of the
    /// stack, through the successor `slot`.
    fn add_edge(&mut self, index: usize, slot: u32) {
        let control = self.controls[index];
        let (_, arity) = control.label_arity();
        let values = self.edge_values.len() as u32;
        let top = self.stack.len() - arity as usize;
        self.edge_values.extend_from_slice(&self.stack[top..]);
        self.edges.push(Edge {
            block: self.current_block,
            slot,
            values,
            next: control.edges,
        });
        let control = &mut self.controls[index];
        control.edges = self.edges.len() as u32 - 1;
        control.last_edge_block = self.current_block;
    }

    /// Collects the edges of a label in the order they were made, which is linear order, into `scratch_blocks`
    /// (their blocks) and returns the edges' indices in `scratch_values`.
    fn collect_edges(&mut self, head: u32) {
        self.scratch_blocks.clear();
        self.scratch_values.clear();
        let mut edge = head;
        while edge != NONE {
            self.scratch_values.push(edge);
            edge = self.edges[edge as usize].next;
        }
        self.scratch_values.reverse();
        for &edge in &self.scratch_values {
            self.scratch_blocks.push(self.edges[edge as usize].block);
        }
    }

    fn is_unreachable(&self) -> bool {
        self.controls.last().is_some_and(|control| control.unreachable)
    }

    fn set_unreachable(&mut self) {
        let control = self.controls.last_mut().expect("there is a construct");
        control.unreachable = true;
        self.stack.truncate(control.height as usize);
    }

    // Instructions.

    fn pop(&mut self) -> Value {
        self.stack.pop().expect("validated code does not underflow the stack")
    }

    fn push(&mut self, value: Value) {
        self.stack.push(value);
    }

    fn skip(
        &mut self,
        func: &mut Func,
        module: &Module,
        instruction: &Instruction,
        decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>,
        pc: usize,
    ) {
        match instruction {
            Instruction::Else
            | Instruction::End
            | Instruction::Catch(_)
            | Instruction::CatchAll
