/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The registers of the calling convention on x86-64.
//!
//! - Parameters of integer types go in rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8 and r9, in order, and those of float and vector types
//!   in xmm0 to xmm7. Results of integer types come back in rax and rdx, and those of float and vector types in xmm0
//!   and xmm1.
//! - r14 holds the callee's instance and r15 the base of its memory 0 at the call, and r10 its `FunctionHeader`.
//! - Every register but rsp and rbp is caller-saved. rsp is 16-byte aligned at the call.

use super::{Register, RegisterMask};

pub const FPR_BASE: Register = 16;

pub const RAX: Register = 0;
pub const RCX: Register = 1;
pub const RDX: Register = 2;
pub const RBX: Register = 3;
pub const RSP: Register = 4;
pub const RBP: Register = 5;
pub const RSI: Register = 6;
pub const RDI: Register = 7;
pub const R8: Register = 8;
pub const R9: Register = 9;
pub const R10: Register = 10;
pub const R11: Register = 11;
pub const R12: Register = 12;
pub const R13: Register = 13;
pub const R14: Register = 14;
pub const R15: Register = 15;

pub const fn xmm(index: u8) -> Register {
    FPR_BASE + index
}

pub const GPR_ARGUMENTS: [Register; 6] = [RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9];
pub const FPR_ARGUMENTS: [Register; 8] = [xmm(0), xmm(1), xmm(2), xmm(3), xmm(4), xmm(5), xmm(6), xmm(7)];
pub const GPR_RESULTS: [Register; 2] = [RAX, RDX];
pub const FPR_RESULTS: [Register; 2] = [xmm(0), xmm(1)];

pub const INSTANCE_REGISTER: Register = R14;
pub const MEMORY_BASE_REGISTER: Register = R15;
pub const CALLEE_REGISTER: Register = R10;

/// Never allocated: moves between memory locations go through them, and lowerings may clobber them.
pub const SCRATCH_GPR: Register = R11;
pub const SCRATCH_FPR: Register = xmm(15);

/// The registers values may live in, in the order the allocator prefers them.
pub const ALLOCATABLE_GPRS: [Register; 13] = [RAX, RCX, RDX, RSI, RDI, R8, R9, R10, RBX, R12, R13, R14, R15];
pub const ALLOCATABLE_FPRS: [Register; 15] = [
    xmm(0),
    xmm(1),
    xmm(2),
    xmm(3),
    xmm(4),
    xmm(5),
    xmm(6),
    xmm(7),
    xmm(8),
    xmm(9),
    xmm(10),
    xmm(11),
    xmm(12),
    xmm(13),
    xmm(14),
];

/// Every allocatable register, as a mask.
pub const ALLOCATABLE: RegisterMask = {
    let mut mask = 0;
    let mut index = 0;
    while index < ALLOCATABLE_GPRS.len() {
        mask |= 1 << ALLOCATABLE_GPRS[index];
        index += 1;
    }
    index = 0;
    while index < ALLOCATABLE_FPRS.len() {
        mask |= 1 << ALLOCATABLE_FPRS[index];
        index += 1;
    }
    mask
};

/// Where a call of a function of the runtime (`Op::Helper`) takes its operands: the instance, from which it finds the
/// context, then the operands, which it stores in the context's `arguments`.
pub const HELPER_REGISTERS: [Register; 7] = [RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9, R10];

/// The registers a call of a function of the runtime overwrites: those the host ABI does not preserve.
pub const HOST_CLOBBERS: RegisterMask = {
    let preserved = (1 << RBX) | (1 << RSP) | (1 << RBP) | (1 << R12) | (1 << R13) | (1 << R14) | (1 << R15);
    !preserved
};

/// With `stress-registers`, the registers values get besides those of fixed constraints: few enough that most
/// values spill.
pub const STRESS_GPRS: [Register; 3] = [RAX, RBX, R12];
pub const STRESS_FPRS: [Register; 2] = [xmm(8), xmm(9)];

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/JIT/src/decode.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The decoder: one instruction at a time from a validated, quickened function body (see
//! `libwasm_module::quickening`).
//!
//! Validation already checked every immediate, so decoding does not check them again. It reads every instruction of
//! every proposal the engine supports, including the quickened forms, so that the builder can skip the immediates of
//! instructions it does not compile in unreachable code. Instructions the JIT does not compile come out as coarse
//! variants that only tell how they nest.

use libwasm_module::instruction_tables::{AtomicKind, SimdKind, atomic_kind, simd_kind};
use libwasm_module::opcode;
use libwasm_module::quickening;
use libwasm_module::types::{HeapType, RefType, ValType};

/// The type of a block, loop, if or try_table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BlockType {
    Empty,
    Value(ValType),
    /// The type index of a function type, whose parameters the block takes and whose results it produces.
    Function(u32),
}

/// The memory immediate of a load or store.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MemoryArgument {
    pub memory: u32,
    pub offset: u64,
}

/// A decoded instruction. Numeric instructions without immediates are `Numeric` with their opcode.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Instruction {
    Unreachable,
    Nop,
    Block(BlockType),
    Loop(BlockType),
    If(BlockType),
    Else,
    End,
    Br(u32),
    BrIf(u32),
    /// `br_table` with `count` labels before the default; the decoder keeps the labels (see `Decoder::targets()`).
    BrTable {
        count: u32,
    },
    Return,
    Call(u32),
    CallIndirect {
        type_index: u32,
        table: u32,
    },
    ReturnCall(u32),
    ReturnCallIndirect {
        type_index: u32,
        table: u32,
    },
    CallRef(u32),
    ReturnCallRef(u32),
    Throw(u32),
    ThrowRef,
    /// A `try_table`, whose catch clauses the decoder skipped.
    TryTable(BlockType),
    /// The legacy exception handling instructions: `try`, `catch` and its tag, `catch_all`, `delegate` and its
    /// label, and `rethrow` and its label.
    Try(BlockType),
    Catch(u32),
    CatchAll,
    Delegate(u32),
    Rethrow(u32),
    Drop,
    Select,
    SelectTyped(ValType),
    LocalGet(u32),
    LocalSet(u32),
    LocalTee(u32),
    GlobalGet(u32),
    GlobalSet(u32),
    TableGet(u32),
    TableSet(u32),
    /// A core load or store (`opcode` from `I32_LOAD` to `I64_STORE32`) of memory 0, which is a memory32 with guard
    /// pages.
    Access {
        opcode: u8,
        argument: MemoryArgument,
    },
    /// The explicitly bounds-checked form of a core load or store (quickening rule 1).
    CheckedAccess {
        opcode: u8,
        argument: MemoryArgument,
    },
    MemorySize(u32),
    MemoryGrow(u32),
    I32Const(i32),
    I64Const(i64),
    /// The bits of an f32 constant.
    F32Const(u32),
    /// The bits of an f64 constant.
    F64Const(u64),
    /// An instruction from `I32_EQZ` to `I64_EXTEND32_S`, none of which has immediates.
    Numeric(u8),
    RefNull(HeapType),
    RefIsNull,
    RefFunc(u32),
    RefEq,
    RefAsNonNull,
    BrOnNull(u32),
    BrOnNonNull(u32),
    /// A `0xFC` instruction. The decoder keeps its index immediates (see `Decoder::misc_indices()`).
    Misc(u32),
    /// A `0xFB` instruction. The decoder keeps its immediates (see `Decoder::gc_indices()`, `gc_heap_types()` and
    /// `gc_flags()`).
    Gc(u32),
    /// A `0xFD` instruction. `checked` for the bounds-checked forms of accesses. The decoder keeps its immediates
    /// (see `Decoder::simd_argument()`, `simd_lane()` and `simd_bytes()`).
    Simd {
        sub_opcode: u32,
        checked: bool,
    },
    /// A `0xFE` instruction. The decoder keeps its memory immediate (see `Decoder::atomic_argument()`).
    Atomic(u32),
    /// A v128 form of `local.get`, `local.set`, `local.tee`, `global.get`, `global.set`, `drop` or `select`
    /// (quickening rule 2), and its index immediate if it has one.
    Vector {
        opcode: u8,
        index: u32,
    },
}

/// The last fixed-width form of `i64.const` (quickening rule 3), for 10 bytes.
const I64_CONST_FIXED_LAST: u8 = quickening::I64_CONST_FIXED + 8;

/// A cursor over a function body.
pub struct Decoder<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    position: usize,
    end: usize,
    targets: Vec<u32>,
    simd_argument: MemoryArgument,
    simd_lane: u8,
    simd_bytes: [u8; 16],
    misc_indices: [u32; 2],
    gc_indices: [u32; 2],
    gc_heap_types: [HeapType; 2],
    gc_flags: u8,
    atomic_argument: MemoryArgument,
}

impl<'a> Decoder<'a> {
    /// A decoder over `bytes[start..end]`, which must be a validated function body (or its instructions).
    pub fn new(bytes: &'a [u8], start: usize, end: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            bytes,
            position: start,
            end,
            targets: Vec::new(),
            simd_argument: MemoryArgument { memory: 0, offset: 0 },
            simd_lane: 0,
            simd_bytes: [0; 16],
            misc_indices: [0; 2],
            gc_indices: [0; 2],
            gc_heap_types: [HeapType::Any; 2],
            gc_flags: 0,
            atomic_argument: MemoryArgument { memory: 0, offset: 0 },
        }
    }

    /// Reuses the decoder's storage for another body.
    pub fn reset(&mut self, bytes: &'a [u8], start: usize, end: usize) {
        self.bytes = bytes;
        self.position = start;
        self.end = end;
    }

    /// The module offset of the next instruction.
    pub fn position(&self) -> usize {
        self.position
    }

    pub fn is_at_end(&self) -> bool {
        self.position >= self.end
    }

    /// The labels of the last `br_table`, the default last.
    pub fn targets(&self) -> &[u32] {
        &self.targets
    }

    /// The catch clauses of the last `try_table`, as its encoding has them: the kind (0 for catch, 1 catch_ref, 2
    /// catch_all, 3 catch_all_ref), the tag and the label of each.
    pub fn catch_clauses(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = [u32; 3]> + '_ {
        self.targets.as_chunks::<3>().0.iter().copied()
    }

    /// The memory immediate of the last SIMD load or store.
    pub fn simd_argument(&self) -> MemoryArgument {
        self.simd_argument
    }

    /// The lane immediate of the last SIMD instruction with one.
    pub fn simd_lane(&self) -> u8 {
        self.simd_lane
    }

    /// The index immediates of the last `0xFC` instruction with any, in order: one, or two for memory.init,
    /// memory.copy, table.init and table.copy.
    pub fn misc_indices(&self) -> [u32; 2] {
        self.misc_indices
    }

    /// The index immediates of the last `0xFB` instruction with any, in order: a type index, then a field index, a
    /// count, or a data or element segment index; for `array.copy`, the two type indices; for `br_on_cast` and
    /// `br_on_cast_fail`, the label first.
    pub fn gc_indices(&self) -> [u32; 2] {
        self.gc_indices
    }

    /// The heap types of the last `ref.test`, `ref.cast` (the first only), `br_on_cast` or `br_on_cast_fail` (source,
    /// then target).
    pub fn gc_heap_types(&self) -> [HeapType; 2] {
        self.gc_heap_types
    }

    /// The flags byte of the last `br_on_cast` or `br_on_cast_fail`: bit 0 for a nullable source, bit 1 for a
    /// nullable target.
    pub fn gc_flags(&self) -> u8 {
        self.gc_flags
    }

    /// The memory immediate of the last atomic access.
    pub fn atomic_argument(&self) -> MemoryArgument {
        self.atomic_argument
    }

    /// The 16 bytes of the last `v128.const` or `i8x16.shuffle`.
    pub fn simd_bytes(&self) -> [u8; 16] {
        self.simd_bytes
    }

    #[inline]
    fn byte(&mut self) -> u8 {
        let byte = self.bytes[self.position];
        self.position += 1;
        byte
    }

    #[inline]
    fn u32(&mut self) -> u32 {
        let byte = self.byte();
        if byte < 0x80 {
            return u32::from(byte);
        }
        self.u64_continued(byte) as u32
    }

    fn u64_continued(&mut self, first: u8) -> u64 {
        let mut result = u64::from(first & 0x7f);
        let mut shift = 7;
        loop {
            let byte = self.byte();
            result |= u64::from(byte & 0x7f) << shift;
            if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
                return result;
            }
            shift += 7;
        }
    }

    fn u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
        let byte = self.byte();
        if byte < 0x80 {
            return u64::from(byte);
        }
        self.u64_continued(byte)
    }

    fn signed(&mut self) -> i64 {
        let mut result = 0i64;
        let mut shift = 0;
        loop {
            let byte = self.byte();
            result |= i64::from(byte & 0x7f) << shift;
            shift += 7;
            if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
                if shift < 64 && byte & 0x40 != 0 {
                    result |= -1i64 << shift;
                }
                return result;
            }
        }
    }

    /// The value of a fixed-width constant (quickening rule 3) of `length` bytes, for a type of `size` bytes: sign
    /// extended from its bytes, or its first `size` bytes where it has more.
    fn fixed_constant(&mut self, length: usize, size: usize) -> i64 {
        let bytes = &self.bytes[self.position..self.position + length];
        self.position += length;
        let stored = length.min(size);
        let mut value = 0u64;
        for (index, byte) in bytes[..stored].iter().enumerate() {
            value |= u64::from(*byte) << (8 * index);
        }
        let bits = 8 * stored as u32;
        if bits < 64 {
            let shift = 64 - bits;
            ((value << shift) as i64) >> shift
        } else {
            value as i64
        }
    }

    fn fixed_u32(&mut self) -> u32 {
        let bytes = &self.bytes[self.position..self.position + 4];
        self.position += 4;
        u32::from_le_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]])
    }

    fn fixed_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
        let mut bytes = [0; 8];
        bytes.copy_from_slice(&self.bytes[self.position..self.position + 8]);
        self.position += 8;
        u64::from_le_bytes(bytes)
    }

    fn heap_type(&mut self) -> HeapType {
        let byte = self.bytes[self.position];
        let heap = match byte {
            0x70 => HeapType::Func,
            0x73 => HeapType::NoFunc,
            0x6f => HeapType::Extern,
            0x72 => HeapType::NoExtern,
            0x6e => HeapType::Any,
            0x6d => HeapType::Eq,
            0x6c => HeapType::I31,
            0x6b => HeapType::Struct,
            0x6a => HeapType::Array,
            0x71 => HeapType::None,
            0x69 => HeapType::Exn,
            0x74 => HeapType::NoExn,
            _ => return HeapType::Concrete(self.signed() as u32),
        };
        self.position += 1;
        heap
    }

    fn value_type(&mut self) -> ValType {
        let value = match self.bytes[self.position] {
            0x7f => ValType::I32,
            0x7e => ValType::I64,
            0x7d => ValType::F32,
            0x7c => ValType::F64,
            0x7b => ValType::V128,
            0x63 => {
                self.position += 1;
                return ValType::Ref(RefType::new(true, self.heap_type()));
            }
            0x64 => {
                self.position += 1;
                return ValType::Ref(RefType::new(false, self.heap_type()));
            }
            _ => return ValType::Ref(RefType::new(true, self.heap_type())),
        };
        self.position += 1;
        value
    }

    fn block_type(&mut self) -> BlockType {
        match self.bytes[self.position] {
            0x40 => {
                self.position += 1;
                BlockType::Empty
            }
            0x7f | 0x7e | 0x7d | 0x7c | 0x7b | 0x63 | 0x64 | 0x70 | 0x6f | 0x6e | 0x6d | 0x6c | 0x6b | 0x6a | 0x69
            | 0x71 | 0x72 | 0x73 | 0x74 => BlockType::Value(self.value_type()),
            _ => BlockType::Function(self.signed() as u32),
        }
    }

    fn memory_argument(&mut self) -> MemoryArgument {
        let alignment = self.u32();
        let memory = if alignment & 0x40 != 0 { self.u32() } else { 0 };
        MemoryArgument {
            memory,
            offset: self.u64(),
        }
    }

    /// Decodes the next instruction.
    pub fn decode(&mut self) -> Instruction {
        let opcode = self.byte();
        match opcode {
            opcode::UNREACHABLE => Instruction::Unreachable,
            opcode::NOP => Instruction::Nop,
            opcode::BLOCK => Instruction::Block(self.block_type()),
            opcode::LOOP => Instruction::Loop(self.block_type()),
            opcode::IF => Instruction::If(self.block_type()),
            opcode::ELSE => Instruction::Else,
            opcode::END => Instruction::End,
            opcode::BR => Instruction::Br(self.u32()),
            opcode::BR_IF => Instruction::BrIf(self.u32()),
            opcode::BR_TABLE => {
                let count = self.u32();
                self.targets.clear();
                for _ in 0..=count {
                    let target = self.u32();
                    self.targets.push(target);
                }
                Instruction::BrTable { count }
            }
            opcode::RETURN => Instruction::Return,
            opcode::CALL => Instruction::Call(self.u32()),
            opcode::CALL_INDIRECT => {
                let type_index = self.u32();
                Instruction::CallIndirect {
                    type_index,
                    table: self.u32(),
                }
            }
            opcode::RETURN_CALL => Instruction::ReturnCall(self.u32()),
            opcode::RETURN_CALL_INDIRECT => {
                let type_index = self.u32();
                Instruction::ReturnCallIndirect {
                    type_index,
                    table: self.u32(),
                }
            }
            opcode::CALL_REF => Instruction::CallRef(self.u32()),
            opcode::RETURN_CALL_REF => Instruction::ReturnCallRef(self.u32()),
            opcode::THROW => Instruction::Throw(self.u32()),
            opcode::THROW_REF => Instruction::ThrowRef,
            opcode::TRY => Instruction::Try(self.block_type()),
            opcode::CATCH => Instruction::Catch(self.u32()),
            opcode::CATCH_ALL => Instruction::CatchAll,
            opcode::DELEGATE => Instruction::Delegate(self.u32()),
            opcode::RETHROW => Instruction::Rethrow(self.u32()),
            opcode::TRY_TABLE => {
                let block_type = self.block_type();
                let count = self.u32();
                self.targets.clear();
                for _ in 0..count {
                    let kind = self.byte();
                    let tag = if kind < 2 { self.u32() } else { 0 };
                    let label = self.u32();
                    self.targets.extend_from_slice(&[u32::from(kind), tag, label]);
                }
                Instruction::TryTable(block_type)
            }
            opcode::DROP => Instruction::Drop,
            opcode::SELECT => Instruction::Select,
            opcode::SELECT_TYPED => {
                self.u32();
                Instruction::SelectTyped(self.value_type())
            }
            opcode::LOCAL_GET => Instruction::LocalGet(self.u32()),
            opcode::LOCAL_SET => Instruction::LocalSet(self.u32()),
            opcode::LOCAL_TEE => Instruction::LocalTee(self.u32()),
            opcode::GLOBAL_GET => Instruction::GlobalGet(self.u32()),
            opcode::GLOBAL_SET => Instruction::GlobalSet(self.u32()),
            opcode::TABLE_GET => Instruction::TableGet(self.u32()),
            opcode::TABLE_SET => Instruction::TableSet(self.u32()),
            opcode::I32_LOAD..=opcode::I64_STORE32 => Instruction::Access {
                opcode,
                argument: self.memory_argument(),
            },
            opcode::MEMORY_SIZE => Instruction::MemorySize(self.u32()),
            opcode::MEMORY_GROW => Instruction::MemoryGrow(self.u32()),
            opcode::I32_CONST => Instruction::I32Const(self.signed() as i32),
            opcode::I64_CONST => Instruction::I64Const(self.signed()),
            opcode::F32_CONST => Instruction::F32Const(self.fixed_u32()),
            opcode::F64_CONST => Instruction::F64Const(self.fixed_u64()),
            opcode::I32_EQZ..=opcode::I64_EXTEND32_S => Instruction::Numeric(opcode),
            opcode::REF_NULL => Instruction::RefNull(self.heap_type()),
            opcode::REF_IS_NULL => Instruction::RefIsNull,
            opcode::REF_FUNC => Instruction::RefFunc(self.u32()),
            opcode::REF_EQ => Instruction::RefEq,
            opcode::REF_AS_NON_NULL => Instruction::RefAsNonNull,
            opcode::BR_ON_NULL => Instruction::BrOnNull(self.u32()),
            opcode::BR_ON_NON_NULL => Instruction::BrOnNonNull(self.u32()),
            opcode::PREFIX_MISC => self.misc(),
            opcode::PREFIX_GC => self.gc(),
            opcode::PREFIX_SIMD => {
                let sub_opcode = self.u32();
                self.simd_immediates(sub_opcode);
                Instruction::Simd {
                    sub_opcode,
                    checked: false,
                }
            }
            opcode::PREFIX_ATOMIC => {
                let sub_opcode = self.u32();
                match atomic_kind(sub_opcode) {
                    Some(AtomicKind::Fence) => {
                        self.byte();
                    }
                    Some(_) => {
                        self.atomic_argument = self.memory_argument();
                    }
                    None => unreachable!("validated code has no unknown atomic instructions"),
                }
                Instruction::Atomic(sub_opcode)
            }
            quickening::QUICK_PREFIX => self.quickened(),
            quickening::I32_CONST_FIXED..quickening::I64_CONST_FIXED => {
                let length = usize::from(opcode - quickening::I32_CONST_FIXED) + 2;
                Instruction::I32Const(self.fixed_constant(length, 4) as i32)
            }
            quickening::I64_CONST_FIXED..=I64_CONST_FIXED_LAST => {
                let length = usize::from(opcode - quickening::I64_CONST_FIXED) + 2;
                Instruction::I64Const(self.fixed_constant(length, 8))
            }
            quickening::LOCAL_GET_V128..=quickening::GLOBAL_SET_V128 => Instruction::Vector {
                opcode,
                index: self.u32(),
            },
            quickening::DROP_V128 | quickening::SELECT_V128 => Instruction::Vector { opcode, index: 0 },
            _ => unreachable!("validated code has no unknown opcode {opcode:#x}"),
        }
    }

    fn misc(&mut self) -> Instruction {
        let sub_opcode = self.u32();
        match sub_opcode {
            opcode::misc::I32_TRUNC_SAT_F32_S..=opcode::misc::I64_TRUNC_SAT_F64_U => {}
            // memory.init, memory.copy, table.init and table.copy take two indices.
            opcode::misc::MEMORY_INIT
            | opcode::misc::MEMORY_COPY
            | opcode::misc::TABLE_INIT
            | opcode::misc::TABLE_COPY => {
                self.misc_indices = [self.u32(), self.u32()];
            }
            _ => {
                self.misc_indices = [self.u32(), 0];
            }
        }
        Instruction::Misc(sub_opcode)
    }

    fn gc(&mut self) -> Instruction {
        use opcode::gc::*;
        let sub_opcode = self.u32();
        match sub_opcode {
            STRUCT_NEW | STRUCT_NEW_DEFAULT | ARRAY_NEW | ARRAY_NEW_DEFAULT | ARRAY_GET | ARRAY_GET_S | ARRAY_GET_U
            | ARRAY_SET | ARRAY_FILL => {
                self.gc_indices = [self.u32(), 0];
            }
            STRUCT_GET | STRUCT_GET_S | STRUCT_GET_U | STRUCT_SET | ARRAY_NEW_FIXED | ARRAY_NEW_DATA
            | ARRAY_NEW_ELEM | ARRAY_COPY | ARRAY_INIT_DATA | ARRAY_INIT_ELEM => {
                self.gc_indices = [self.u32(), self.u32()];
            }
            REF_TEST | REF_TEST_NULL | REF_CAST | REF_CAST_NULL => {
                self.gc_heap_types[0] = self.heap_type();
            }
            BR_ON_CAST | BR_ON_CAST_FAIL => {
                self.gc_flags = self.byte();
                self.gc_indices[0] = self.u32();
                self.gc_heap_types = [self.heap_type(), self.heap_type()];
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        Instruction::Gc(sub_opcode)
    }

    fn simd_immediates(&mut self, sub_opcode: u32) {
        match simd_kind(sub_opcode) {
            Some(SimdKind::Load { .. } | SimdKind::Store { .. }) => {
                self.simd_argument = self.memory_argument();
            }
            Some(SimdKind::LoadLane { .. } | SimdKind::StoreLane { .. }) => {
                self.simd_argument = self.memory_argument();
                self.simd_lane = self.byte();
            }
            Some(SimdKind::Const | SimdKind::Shuffle) => {
                self.simd_bytes
                    .copy_from_slice(&self.bytes[self.position..self.position + 16]);
                self.position += 16;
            }
            Some(SimdKind::ExtractLane { .. } | SimdKind::ReplaceLane { .. }) => {
                self.simd_lane = self.byte();
            }
            Some(_) => {}
            None => unreachable!("validated code has no unknown SIMD instructions"),
        }
    }

    fn quickened(&mut self) -> Instruction {
        let sub_opcode = self.byte();
        if sub_opcode < quickening::CHECKED_SIMD_ACCESS {
            let memory = if sub_opcode & quickening::CHECKED_ACCESS_HAS_MEMORY_INDEX != 0 {
                self.u32()
            } else {
                0
            };
            return Instruction::CheckedAccess {
                opcode: sub_opcode & !quickening::CHECKED_ACCESS_HAS_MEMORY_INDEX,
                argument: MemoryArgument {
                    memory,
                    offset: self.u64(),
                },
            };
        }
        let index = sub_opcode - quickening::CHECKED_SIMD_ACCESS;
        let has_memory = index & quickening::CHECKED_SIMD_ACCESS_HAS_MEMORY_INDEX != 0;
        let simd = quickening::SIMD_ACCESSES[(index & !quickening::CHECKED_SIMD_ACCESS_HAS_MEMORY_INDEX) as usize];
        let memory = if has_memory { self.u32() } else { 0 };
        self.simd_argument = MemoryArgument {
            memory,
            offset: self.u64(),
        };
        if matches!(
            simd_kind(simd),
            Some(SimdKind::LoadLane { .. } | SimdKind::StoreLane { .. })
        ) {
            self.simd_lane = self.byte();
        }
        Instruction::Simd {
            sub_opcode: simd,
            checked: true,
        }
    }
}

/// How an instruction changes the nesting of blocks: +1 for those that open one, -1 for `end`.
pub fn nesting_change(instruction: &Instruction) -> i32 {
    match instruction {
        Instruction::Block(_)
        | Instruction::Loop(_)
        | Instruction::If(_)
        | Instruction::TryTable(_)
        | Instruction::Try(_) => 1,
        // NB: `catch` and `catch_all` continue the `try` they are in, like `else`.
        Instruction::End | Instruction::Delegate(_) => -1,
        _ => 0,
    }
}

//! A vector of copyable values that keeps up to `N` of them inline, for small lists that mostly need no heap
//! allocation.

/// Up to `N` values inline; more spill to the heap.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct InlineVec<T: Copy + Default, const N: usize> {
    len: usize,
    inline: [T; N],
    heap: Vec<T>,
}

impl<T: Copy + Default, const N: usize> InlineVec<T, N> {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            len: 0,
            inline: [T::default(); N],
            heap: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// `count` copies of `value`.
    pub fn from_elem(value: T, count: usize) -> Self {
        let mut vec = Self::new();
        for _ in 0..count {
            vec.push(value);
        }
        vec
    }

    pub fn push(&mut self, value: T) {
        if self.len < N {
            self.inline[self.len] = value;
        } else {
            if self.heap.is_empty() {
                self.heap.extend_from_slice(&self.inline);
            }
            self.heap.push(value);
        }
        self.len += 1;
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default, const N: usize> Default for InlineVec<T, N> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default, const N: usize> std::ops::Deref for InlineVec<T, N> {
    type Target = [T];

    fn deref(&self) -> &[T] {
        if self.len <= N {
            &self.inline[..self.len]
        } else {
            &self.heap
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default, const N: usize> std::ops::DerefMut for InlineVec<T, N> {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [T] {
        if self.len <= N {
            &mut self.inline[..self.len]
        } else {
            &mut self.heap
        }
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default + std::fmt::Debug, const N: usize> std::fmt::Debug for InlineVec<T, N> {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter.debug_list().entries(self.iter()).finish()
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default + PartialEq, const N: usize> PartialEq for InlineVec<T, N> {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        **self == **other
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default + Eq, const N: usize> Eq for InlineVec<T, N> {}

impl<'a, T: Copy + Default, const N: usize> IntoIterator for &'a InlineVec<T, N> {
    type Item = &'a T;
    type IntoIter = std::slice::Iter<'a, T>;

    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        self.iter()
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default, const N: usize> FromIterator<T> for InlineVec<T, N> {
    fn from_iter<I: IntoIterator<Item = T>>(iterator: I) -> Self {
        let mut vec = Self::new();
        for value in iterator {
            vec.push(value);
        }
        vec
    }
}

impl<T: Copy + Default, const N: usize> Extend<T> for InlineVec<T, N> {
    fn extend<I: IntoIterator<Item = T>>(&mut self, iterator: I) {
        for value in iterator {
            self.push(value);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::InlineVec;

    #[test]
    fn values_stay_inline_until_they_spill() {
        let mut vec = InlineVec::<u32, 2>::new();
        vec.push(1);
        vec.push(2);
        assert_eq!(&*vec, &[1, 2]);
        vec.push(3);
        vec[0] = 7;
        assert_eq!(&*vec, &[7, 2, 3]);
        assert_eq!(InlineVec::<u8, 4>::from_elem(5, 3).len(), 3);
        assert_eq!((0..6).collect::<InlineVec<u32, 2>>().iter().sum::<u32>(), 15);
    }
}

//! The text form of the IR, for `dump-ir` and the IR tests.

use super::{FloatCondition, Func, IntCondition, LoadKind, Op, Shape, Type, Value};
use std::fmt::Write;

/// The value as text: a constant's value, or `vN`.
fn operand(func: &Func, value: Value) -> String {
    let node = func.node(value);
    match node.op {
        Op::Const32 if node.ty == Type::F32 => format!("{}f32", f32::from_bits(node.args[0])),
        Op::Const32 => format!("{}", node.args[0] as i32),
        Op::Const64 if node.ty == Type::F64 => {
            format!("{}f64", f64::from_bits(node.constant().expect("a constant")))
        }
        Op::Const64 => format!("{}i64", node.constant().expect("a constant") as i64),
        Op::Const128 => format!("{:#034x}v128", func.constants[node.args[0] as usize]),
        _ => format!("v{value}"),
    }
}

/// One node as text, without its value name.
pub fn node_text(func: &Func, value: Value) -> String {
    let node = func.node(value);
    let mut text = String::from(node.op.name());
    if node.ty != Type::None {
        write!(text, ".{}", node.ty.name()).unwrap();
    }
    match node.op {
        Op::Compare | Op::BranchCompare => write!(text, " {}", IntCondition::from_flags(node.flags).name()).unwrap(),
        Op::FloatCompare | Op::BranchFloatCompare => {
            write!(text, " {}", FloatCondition::from_flags(node.flags).name()).unwrap();
        }
        Op::Load => write!(text, " {}", LoadKind::from_flags(node.flags).name()).unwrap(),
        Op::Store => write!(text, " {}", 8 << node.flags).unwrap(),
        _ => {}
    }
    let inputs = func.inputs(value);
    if !inputs.is_empty() && node.op != Op::BrTable {
        let inputs = inputs.iter().map(|input| operand(func, *input)).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        write!(text, " {}", inputs.join(", ")).unwrap();
    }
    match node.op {
        Op::Const32 | Op::Const64 | Op::Const128 => write!(text, " {}", operand(func, value)).unwrap(),
        Op::VectorUnary | Op::ExtractLane => write!(text, " simd {:#x}", node.args[1]).unwrap(),
        Op::VectorBinary => write!(text, " simd {:#x}", node.args[2]).unwrap(),
        Op::ReplaceLane => write!(text, " simd {:#x} lane {}", node.args[2] & 0xffff, node.args[2] >> 16).unwrap(),
        Op::Shuffle => write!(text, " {:#034x}", func.constants[node.args[2] as usize]).unwrap(),
        Op::VectorLoad => write!(text, " simd {:#x} +{}", node.flags, node.args[2]).unwrap(),
        Op::VectorTernary => write!(text, " simd {:#x}", node.flags).unwrap(),
        Op::Param => write!(text, " {}", node.args[0]).unwrap(),
        Op::Forward => write!(text, " v{}", node.args[0]).unwrap(),
        Op::InstanceField | Op::LoadPointer => write!(text, " +{}", node.args[1]).unwrap(),
        Op::GlobalGet => write!(text, " global {}", node.args[1]).unwrap(),
        Op::GlobalSet => write!(text, " global {}", node.args[2]).unwrap(),
        Op::Load => write!(text, " +{}", node.args[2]).unwrap(),
        Op::Store => write!(text, " +{}", node.args[2]).unwrap(),
        Op::Call | Op::TailCall if node.args[2] != crate::ir::NONE => {
            write!(text, " function {}", node.args[2]).unwrap();
        }
        Op::Offset | Op::ReadField => write!(text, " +{}", node.args[1]).unwrap(),
        Op::FrameLoad => write!(text, " {:+}", node.args[1] as i32).unwrap(),
        Op::WriteField => write!(text, " +{}", node.args[2]).unwrap(),
        Op::Helper => write!(text, " {}", crate::ir::Helper::from_index(node.args[2]).name()).unwrap(),
        Op::CallResult => write!(text, " v{} #{}", node.args[0], node.args[1]).unwrap(),
        Op::Trap => write!(text, " {}", node.args[0]).unwrap(),
        Op::CheckedAddress => write!(text, " size {} flags {:#x}", 1 << (node.flags & 7), node.flags & !7).unwrap(),
        Op::AtomicRmw => write!(
            text,
            " {} size {}",
            crate::ir::AtomicOp::from_index(node.args[2]).name(),
            1 << node.flags
        )
        .unwrap(),
        Op::AtomicCompareExchange | Op::ElementAddress => write!(text, " size {}", 1 << node.flags).unwrap(),
        Op::Rtt => write!(text, " type {}", node.args[1]).unwrap(),
        Op::I31Get if node.flags != 0 => text.push_str(" signed"),
        Op::RefTest => write!(
            text,
            " {}{}{} depth {}",
            crate::ir::HeapTest::from_flags(node.flags).name(),
            if node.flags & crate::ir::REF_TEST_NULLABLE != 0 {
                " null"
            } else {
                ""
            },
            if node.flags & crate::ir::REF_TEST_CAST != 0 {
                " cast"
            } else {
                ""
            },
            node.args[2]
        )
        .unwrap(),
        Op::BrTable => {
            let block = func
                .blocks
                .iter()
                .position(|block| block.end == value + 1)
                .expect("a br_table ends a block") as u32;
            let successors = func.successors(block);
            let targets = func
                .table_targets(value)
                .iter()
                .map(|target| format!("b{}", successors[*target as usize]))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
            write!(text, " {} [{}]", operand(func, node.args[0]), targets.join(", ")).unwrap();
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    if matches!(node.op.shape(), Shape::Fixed(_)) && node.flags & super::FLAG_CANNOT_TRAP != 0 {
        text.push_str(" (cannot trap)");
    }
    text
}

/// The whole function as text.
pub fn dump(func: &Func) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    let types = |types: &[Type]| types.iter().map(|ty| ty.name()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
    writeln!(out, "function ({}) -> ({})", types(&func.params), types(&func.results)).unwrap();
    for (index, block) in func.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        let block_id = index as u32;
        let list = |blocks: &[u32]| {
            blocks
                .iter()
                .map(|block| format!("b{block}"))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ")
        };
        write!(out, "b{index}:").unwrap();
        if !func.predecessors(block_id).is_empty() {
            write!(out, " <- {}", list(func.predecessors(block_id))).unwrap();
        }
        if block.loop_index != super::NONE {
            let loop_ = &func.loops[block.loop_index as usize];
            if loop_.header == block_id {
                write!(out, " (loop to b{})", loop_.last).unwrap();
            }
        }
        out.push('\n');
        for phi in func.phis(block_id) {
            if func.node(phi).op == Op::Phi {
                writeln!(out, "  v{phi} = {}", node_text(func, phi)).unwrap();
            }
        }
        for value in block.start..block.end {
            let node = func.node(value);
            if (node.op.is_entry_value() && node.op != Op::Param) || matches!(node.op, Op::Phi | Op::Forward) {
                continue;
            }
            if node.op.is_terminator() {
                write!(out, "  {}", node_text(func, value)).unwrap();
                if !func.successors(block_id).is_empty() && node.op != Op::BrTable {
                    write!(out, " -> {}", list(func.successors(block_id))).unwrap();
                }
                out.push('\n');
            } else if node.ty == Type::None {
                writeln!(out, "  {}", node_text(func, value)).unwrap();
            } else {
                writeln!(out, "  v{value} = {}", node_text(func, value)).unwrap();
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! The IR: typed SSA in flat arenas.
//!
//! A `Func` is a list of blocks in linear order, which is the order of the WebAssembly code: every forward edge goes
//! to a later block, and every loop is a contiguous range of blocks that only its header is entered at. Nodes live in
//! one arena and are named by their index (`Value`). Each block owns a contiguous range of nodes, its body, which
//! ends with its terminator, and a list of phis. Nodes are created in order, so a body node's index is also its
//! position in linear order.
//!
//! A `Node` is 16 bytes: an op, a type, eight bits of flags and three 32-bit arguments, which are inputs or immediates
//! as the op says (`Op::shape()`). Ops with more inputs keep them in `Func::operands`.
//!
//! Constants, parameters, the instance and the memory base are values without code at their position: constants are
//! rematerialized at every use, and the others arrive in registers or slots at the entry.

pub mod dump;
pub mod verify;

/// A node, by its index in `Func::nodes`.
pub type Value = u32;

/// A block, by its index in `Func::blocks`.
pub type BlockId = u32;

/// No value or block.
pub const NONE: u32 = u32::MAX;

/// The type of a value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum Type {
    #[default]
    None,
    I32,
    I64,
    F32,
    F64,
    V128,
    /// A reference: zero for null, else what the runtime encodes it as (a `FunctionHeader` for funcref).
    Ref,
    /// A machine pointer, for addresses the code computes (the memory base, instance data).
    Pointer,
}

impl Type {
    pub fn is_float(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Type::F32 | Type::F64)
    }

    /// Whether values of this type live in xmm registers: floats and vectors.
    pub fn uses_xmm(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Type::F32 | Type::F64 | Type::V128)
    }

    /// The 8-byte slots a value of this type takes in memory.
    pub fn slots(self) -> u32 {
        if self == Type::V128 { 2 } else { 1 }
    }

    pub fn is_64(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Type::I64 | Type::F64 | Type::Ref | Type::Pointer)
    }

    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Type::None => "none",
            Type::I32 => "i32",
            Type::I64 => "i64",
            Type::F32 => "f32",
            Type::F64 => "f64",
            Type::V128 => "v128",
            Type::Ref => "ref",
            Type::Pointer => "ptr",
        }
    }
}

/// Where an op finds its inputs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Shape {
    /// The first `n` arguments are inputs; the others are immediates.
    Fixed(u8),
    /// `args[0]` is the start and `args[1]` the count of the inputs in `Func::operands`.
    Variadic,
}

/// What an op may do besides computing its value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Effect {
    /// Nothing: equal nodes compute equal values anywhere their inputs are available, and unused ones go away.
    Pure,
    /// Reads state that stores and calls may change; may trap where it reads memory.
    Read,
    /// Writes state, or traps where its inputs say so (division, truncation): never removed or moved.
    Write,
    /// Ends a block.
    Terminator,
}

/// An integer comparison, in `Node::flags` of `Compare` and `BranchCompare`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum IntCondition {
    Eq,
    Ne,
    LtS,
    LtU,
    GtS,
    GtU,
    LeS,
    LeU,
    GeS,
    GeU,
}

impl IntCondition {
    pub const ALL: [IntCondition; 10] = [
        IntCondition::Eq,
        IntCondition::Ne,
        IntCondition::LtS,
        IntCondition::LtU,
        IntCondition::GtS,
        IntCondition::GtU,
        IntCondition::LeS,
        IntCondition::LeU,
        IntCondition::GeS,
        IntCondition::GeU,
    ];

    pub fn from_flags(flags: u8) -> Self {
        Self::ALL[flags as usize]
    }

    pub fn invert(self) -> Self {
        match self {
            IntCondition::Eq => IntCondition::Ne,
            IntCondition::Ne => IntCondition::Eq,
            IntCondition::LtS => IntCondition::GeS,
            IntCondition::LtU => IntCondition::GeU,
            IntCondition::GtS => IntCondition::LeS,
            IntCondition::GtU => IntCondition::LeU,
            IntCondition::LeS => IntCondition::GtS,
            IntCondition::LeU => IntCondition::GtU,
            IntCondition::GeS => IntCondition::LtS,
            IntCondition::GeU => IntCondition::LtU,
        }
    }

    /// The condition with the operands swapped.
    pub fn swap(self) -> Self {
        match self {
            IntCondition::Eq => IntCondition::Eq,
            IntCondition::Ne => IntCondition::Ne,
            IntCondition::LtS => IntCondition::GtS,
            IntCondition::LtU => IntCondition::GtU,
            IntCondition::GtS => IntCondition::LtS,
            IntCondition::GtU => IntCondition::LtU,
            IntCondition::LeS => IntCondition::GeS,
            IntCondition::LeU => IntCondition::GeU,
            IntCondition::GeS => IntCondition::LeS,
            IntCondition::GeU => IntCondition::LeU,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate(self, lhs: u64, rhs: u64, is_64: bool) -> bool {
        let (signed_lhs, signed_rhs) = if is_64 {
            (lhs as i64, rhs as i64)
        } else {
            (i64::from(lhs as u32 as i32), i64::from(rhs as u32 as i32))
        };
        let (lhs, rhs) = if is_64 {
            (lhs, rhs)
        } else {
            (u64::from(lhs as u32), u64::from(rhs as u32))
        };
        match self {
            IntCondition::Eq => lhs == rhs,
            IntCondition::Ne => lhs != rhs,
            IntCondition::LtS => signed_lhs < signed_rhs,
            IntCondition::LtU => lhs < rhs,
            IntCondition::GtS => signed_lhs > signed_rhs,
            IntCondition::GtU => lhs > rhs,
            IntCondition::LeS => signed_lhs <= signed_rhs,
            IntCondition::LeU => lhs <= rhs,
            IntCondition::GeS => signed_lhs >= signed_rhs,
            IntCondition::GeU => lhs >= rhs,
        }
    }

    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            IntCondition::Eq => "eq",
            IntCondition::Ne => "ne",
            IntCondition::LtS => "lt_s",
            IntCondition::LtU => "lt_u",
            IntCondition::GtS => "gt_s",
            IntCondition::GtU => "gt_u",
            IntCondition::LeS => "le_s",
            IntCondition::LeU => "le_u",
            IntCondition::GeS => "ge_s",
            IntCondition::GeU => "ge_u",
        }
    }
}

/// A float comparison, in `Node::flags` of `FloatCompare` and `BranchFloatCompare`. All are false for NaN but `Ne`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum FloatCondition {
    Eq,
    Ne,
    Lt,
    Gt,
    Le,
    Ge,
}

impl FloatCondition {
    pub const ALL: [FloatCondition; 6] = [
        FloatCondition::Eq,
        FloatCondition::Ne,
        FloatCondition::Lt,
        FloatCondition::Gt,
        FloatCondition::Le,
        FloatCondition::Ge,
    ];

    pub fn from_flags(flags: u8) -> Self {
        Self::ALL[flags as usize]
    }

    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            FloatCondition::Eq => "eq",
            FloatCondition::Ne => "ne",
            FloatCondition::Lt => "lt",
            FloatCondition::Gt => "gt",
            FloatCondition::Le => "le",
            FloatCondition::Ge => "ge",
        }
    }
}

/// In `Node::flags` of a `Load`, besides its `LoadKind`: the load of an atomic access, which has to be ordered with the
/// others where plain loads are not (on AArch64).
pub const LOAD_ATOMIC: u8 = 0x80;

/// How a load reads memory, in `Node::flags` of `Load`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum LoadKind {
    I32,
    I64,
    F32,
    F64,
    I32S8,
    I32U8,
    I32S16,
    I32U16,
    I64S8,
    I64U8,
    I64S16,
    I64U16,
    I64S32,
    I64U32,
}

impl LoadKind {
    pub const ALL: [LoadKind; 14] = [
        LoadKind::I32,
        LoadKind::I64,
        LoadKind::F32,
        LoadKind::F64,
        LoadKind::I32S8,
        LoadKind::I32U8,
        LoadKind::I32S16,
        LoadKind::I32U16,
        LoadKind::I64S8,
        LoadKind::I64U8,
        LoadKind::I64S16,
        LoadKind::I64U16,
        LoadKind::I64S32,
        LoadKind::I64U32,
    ];

    pub fn from_flags(flags: u8) -> Self {
        Self::ALL[(flags & !LOAD_ATOMIC) as usize]
    }

    pub fn size(self) -> u32 {
        match self {
            LoadKind::I32S8 | LoadKind::I32U8 | LoadKind::I64S8 | LoadKind::I64U8 => 1,
            LoadKind::I32S16 | LoadKind::I32U16 | LoadKind::I64S16 | LoadKind::I64U16 => 2,
            LoadKind::I32 | LoadKind::F32 | LoadKind::I64S32 | LoadKind::I64U32 => 4,
            LoadKind::I64 | LoadKind::F64 => 8,
        }
    }

    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            LoadKind::I32 => "i32",
            LoadKind::I64 => "i64",
            LoadKind::F32 => "f32",
            LoadKind::F64 => "f64",
            LoadKind::I32S8 => "i32.s8",
            LoadKind::I32U8 => "i32.u8",
            LoadKind::I32S16 => "i32.s16",
            LoadKind::I32U16 => "i32.u16",
            LoadKind::I64S8 => "i64.s8",
            LoadKind::I64U8 => "i64.u8",
            LoadKind::I64S16 => "i64.s16",
            LoadKind::I64U16 => "i64.u16",
            LoadKind::I64S32 => "i64.s32",
            LoadKind::I64U32 => "i64.u32",
        }
    }
}

/// The runtime functions `Helper` calls, and their operands.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u32)]
pub enum Helper {
    /// memory data, delta in pages: the previous size, or u64::MAX.
    MemoryGrow,
    /// table data, delta, initial element: the previous size, or u64::MAX.
    TableGrow,
    /// memory data, destination, value, count.
    MemoryFill,
    /// destination memory data, source memory data, destination, source, count.
    MemoryCopy,
    /// memory data, segment, destination, source, count.
    MemoryInit,
    /// table data, destination, value, count.
    TableFill,
    /// destination table data, source table data, destination, source, count.
    TableCopy,
    /// table data, segment, destination, source, count.
    TableInit,
    /// address, expected value, timeout in nanoseconds, size: 0 when woken, 1 if the value differed, 2 on timeout,
    /// or WAIT_CANNOT_BLOCK when the runtime has the trap.
    AtomicWait,
    /// address, count: how many waiters it woke.
    AtomicNotify,
    /// rtt, data size in bytes, array length: the new zeroed GC object, or zero (when the runtime has the trap).
    Allocate,
    /// array, start, the low and high 64 bits of the value, count.
    ArrayFill,
    /// destination array, destination start, source array, source start, count.
    ArrayCopy,
    /// array, data segment, destination, source, count.
    ArrayInitData,
    /// array, element segment, destination, source, count.
    ArrayInitElem,
    /// segment, start, count, bytes per item, TRAP_* code: traps with the code unless the items are in the segment.
    SegmentRange,
    /// tag identity: a new exception with that tag and a zeroed payload, for the code to fill in.
    AllocateException,
}

impl Helper {
    pub const ALL: [Helper; 17] = [
        Helper::MemoryGrow,
        Helper::TableGrow,
        Helper::MemoryFill,
        Helper::MemoryCopy,
        Helper::MemoryInit,
        Helper::TableFill,
        Helper::TableCopy,
        Helper::TableInit,
        Helper::AtomicWait,
        Helper::AtomicNotify,
        Helper::Allocate,
        Helper::ArrayFill,
        Helper::ArrayCopy,
        Helper::ArrayInitData,
        Helper::ArrayInitElem,
        Helper::SegmentRange,
        Helper::AllocateException,
    ];

    pub fn from_index(index: u32) -> Self {
        Self::ALL[index as usize]
    }

    /// Whether the helper returns 0 or the TRAP_* code to trap with, rather than a value.
    pub fn may_trap(self) -> bool {
        !matches!(
            self,
            Helper::MemoryGrow
                | Helper::TableGrow
                | Helper::AtomicWait
                | Helper::AtomicNotify
                | Helper::Allocate
                | Helper::AllocateException
        )
    }

    /// Whether a value of zero means the runtime trapped, with TRAP_RUNTIME.
    pub fn traps_on_zero(self) -> bool {
        self == Helper::Allocate
    }

    /// The value, besides zero for `traps_on_zero()`, that means the runtime trapped, with TRAP_RUNTIME.
    pub fn trap_value(self) -> Option<u64> {
        (self == Helper::AtomicWait).then_some(libwasm_module::abi::WAIT_CANNOT_BLOCK)
    }

    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Helper::MemoryGrow => "memory_grow",
            Helper::TableGrow => "table_grow",
            Helper::MemoryFill => "memory_fill",
            Helper::MemoryCopy => "memory_copy",
            Helper::MemoryInit => "memory_init",
            Helper::TableFill => "table_fill",
            Helper::TableCopy => "table_copy",
            Helper::TableInit => "table_init",
            Helper::AtomicWait => "atomic_wait",
            Helper::AtomicNotify => "atomic_notify",
            Helper::Allocate => "allocate",
            Helper::ArrayFill => "array_fill",
            Helper::ArrayCopy => "array_copy",
            Helper::ArrayInitData => "array_init_data",
            Helper::ArrayInitElem => "array_init_elem",
            Helper::SegmentRange => "segment_range",
            Helper::AllocateException => "allocate_exception",
        }
    }
}

/// How many bytes a store writes, in `Node::flags` of `Store`. The value's type says the rest.
pub fn store_size(flags: u8) -> u32 {
    1 << flags
}

/// `Node::flags` bit of ops that may trap (division, truncation) once their inputs show they cannot.
pub const FLAG_CANNOT_TRAP: u8 = 0x80;

/// `Node::flags` bit of `GlobalGet` for globals no code can change.
pub const FLAG_IMMUTABLE: u8 = 0x40;

/// `Node::flags` bit of `CalleeInstance` for a header that is never null, like an imported function's.
pub const FLAG_NOT_NULL: u8 = 0x40;

/// `Node::flags` bits of `CheckedAddress`, besides log2 of the access size in the low bits: an atomic access, which
/// must be aligned, and an access of a memory64, whose index and offset may add up past 2^64.
pub const CHECKED_ATOMIC: u8 = 0x08;
pub const CHECKED_MEMORY64: u8 = 0x10;

/// The read-modify-write operations of `AtomicRmw`, in its args[2].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u32)]
pub enum AtomicOp {
    Add,
    Sub,
    And,
    Or,
    Xor,
    Exchange,
}

impl AtomicOp {
    pub const ALL: [AtomicOp; 6] = [
        AtomicOp::Add,
        AtomicOp::Sub,
        AtomicOp::And,
        AtomicOp::Or,
        AtomicOp::Xor,
        AtomicOp::Exchange,
    ];

    pub fn from_index(index: u32) -> Self {
        Self::ALL[index as usize]
    }

    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            AtomicOp::Add => "add",
            AtomicOp::Sub => "sub",
            AtomicOp::And => "and",
            AtomicOp::Or => "or",
            AtomicOp::Xor => "xor",
            AtomicOp::Exchange => "xchg",
        }
    }
}

/// What `RefTest` checks a reference against, in the low bits of its flags.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum HeapTest {
    /// Every reference but null: any, func, extern and exn.
    NonNull,
    /// An i31 or a GC object: eq.
    Eq,
    I31,
    /// A GC object of a struct type.
    Struct,
    /// A GC object of an array type.
    Array,
    /// Only null: none, nofunc, noextern and noexn.
    Nothing,
    /// A GC object whose type is the identity input or one of its subtypes, which are args[2] deep.
    ConcreteObject,
    /// A function whose type is the identity input or one of its subtypes, which are args[2] deep.
    ConcreteFunction,
}

impl HeapTest {
    pub const ALL: [HeapTest; 8] = [
        HeapTest::NonNull,
        HeapTest::Eq,
        HeapTest::I31,
        HeapTest::Struct,
        HeapTest::Array,
        HeapTest::Nothing,
        HeapTest::ConcreteObject,
        HeapTest::ConcreteFunction,
    ];

    pub fn from_flags(flags: u8) -> Self {
        Self::ALL[(flags & 0xf) as usize]
    }

    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            HeapTest::NonNull => "non_null",
            HeapTest::Eq => "eq",
            HeapTest::I31 => "i31",
            HeapTest::Struct => "struct",
            HeapTest::Array => "array",
            HeapTest::Nothing => "nothing",
            HeapTest::ConcreteObject => "object",
            HeapTest::ConcreteFunction => "function",
        }
    }
}

/// `Node::flags` bits of `RefTest`, besides the `HeapTest`: null matches too; and the test is a cast, which traps
/// where the reference does not match and has no value.
pub const REF_TEST_NULLABLE: u8 = 0x10;
pub const REF_TEST_CAST: u8 = 0x80;
/// `Node::flags` bit of a `Call` in a region of an exception handler, which checks the context's `exception` once
/// it returns (see `builder/exceptions.rs`).
pub const FLAG_CHECKS_EXCEPTION: u8 = 0x01;

macro_rules! ops {
    ($($(#[$meta:meta])* $name:ident: $shape:expr, $effect:ident, $text:literal;)*) => {
        /// The operation of a node. See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for what each one does.
        #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
        #[repr(u16)]
        pub enum Op {
            $($(#[$meta])* $name,)*
        }

        const SHAPES: &[Shape] = &[$($shape,)*];
        const EFFECTS: &[Effect] = &[$(Effect::$effect,)*];

        impl Op {
            #[inline]
            pub fn shape(self) -> Shape {
                SHAPES[self as usize]
            }

            #[inline]
            pub fn base_effect(self) -> Effect {
                EFFECTS[self as usize]
            }

            pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
                match self {
                    $(Op::$name => $text,)*
                }
            }
        }
    };
}

use Shape::{Fixed, Variadic};

ops! {
    // Values without code at their position.
    Const32: Fixed(0), Pure, "const";
    Const64: Fixed(0), Pure, "const";
    /// args[0]: the index of the constant in `Func::constants`.
    Const128: Fixed(0), Pure, "const";
    Param: Fixed(0), Pure, "param";
    Instance: Fixed(0), Pure, "instance";
    MemoryBase: Fixed(0), Pure, "memory_base";
    Phi: Variadic, Pure, "phi";
    /// A phi that turned out trivial, forwarding to args[0]. Gone after cleanup.
    Forward: Fixed(0), Pure, "forward";

    // Integer arithmetic, on I32 or I64 as the node's type says.
    Add: Fixed(2), Pure, "add";
    Sub: Fixed(2), Pure, "sub";
    Mul: Fixed(2), Pure, "mul";
    And: Fixed(2), Pure, "and";
    Or: Fixed(2), Pure, "or";
    Xor: Fixed(2), Pure, "xor";
    Shl: Fixed(2), Pure, "shl";
    ShrS: Fixed(2), Pure, "shr_s";
    ShrU: Fixed(2), Pure, "shr_u";
    Rotl: Fixed(2), Pure, "rotl";
    Rotr: Fixed(2), Pure, "rotr";
    DivS: Fixed(2), Write, "div_s";
    DivU: Fixed(2), Write, "div_u";
    RemS: Fixed(2), Write, "rem_s";
    RemU: Fixed(2), Write, "rem_u";
    Clz: Fixed(1), Pure, "clz";
    Ctz: Fixed(1), Pure, "ctz";
    Popcnt: Fixed(1), Pure, "popcnt";
    Eqz: Fixed(1), Pure, "eqz";
    Extend8S: Fixed(1), Pure, "extend8_s";
    Extend16S: Fixed(1), Pure, "extend16_s";
    Extend32S: Fixed(1), Pure, "extend32_s";
    ExtendI32S: Fixed(1), Pure, "extend_i32_s";
    ExtendI32U: Fixed(1), Pure, "extend_i32_u";
    Wrap: Fixed(1), Pure, "wrap";
    Compare: Fixed(2), Pure, "compare";

    // Float arithmetic, on F32 or F64.
    FAdd: Fixed(2), Pure, "fadd";
    FSub: Fixed(2), Pure, "fsub";
    FMul: Fixed(2), Pure, "fmul";
    FDiv: Fixed(2), Pure, "fdiv";
    FMin: Fixed(2), Pure, "fmin";
    FMax: Fixed(2), Pure, "fmax";
    FCopysign: Fixed(2), Pure, "fcopysign";
    FAbs: Fixed(1), Pure, "fabs";
    FNeg: Fixed(1), Pure, "fneg";
    FSqrt: Fixed(1), Pure, "fsqrt";
    FCeil: Fixed(1), Pure, "fceil";
    FFloor: Fixed(1), Pure, "ffloor";
    FTrunc: Fixed(1), Pure, "ftrunc";
    FNearest: Fixed(1), Pure, "fnearest";
    FloatCompare: Fixed(2), Pure, "fcompare";

    // Conversions to the node's type from the input's.
    TruncS: Fixed(1), Write, "trunc_s";
    TruncU: Fixed(1), Write, "trunc_u";
    TruncSatS: Fixed(1), Pure, "trunc_sat_s";
    TruncSatU: Fixed(1), Pure, "trunc_sat_u";
    ConvertS: Fixed(1), Pure, "convert_s";
    ConvertU: Fixed(1), Pure, "convert_u";
    Demote: Fixed(1), Pure, "demote";
    Promote: Fixed(1), Pure, "promote";
    Reinterpret: Fixed(1), Pure, "reinterpret";

    /// args: condition, value if nonzero, value if zero.
    Select: Fixed(3), Pure, "select";

    // Vectors. The SIMD sub-opcode says which operation; the node's type is its result's.
    /// args: operand, sub-opcode. Splats, unary lane operations and the reductions to an i32.
    VectorUnary: Fixed(1), Pure, "vector_unary";
    /// args: lhs, rhs, sub-opcode. Binary lane operations, comparisons, and shifts by an i32.
    VectorBinary: Fixed(2), Pure, "vector_binary";
    /// args: three operands; flags: the sub-opcode's low byte (bitselect, or a relaxed operation from 0x100 on).
    VectorTernary: Fixed(3), Pure, "vector_ternary";
    /// args: vector, sub-opcode, lane.
    ExtractLane: Fixed(1), Pure, "extract_lane";
    /// args: vector, value, sub-opcode and lane << 16.
    ReplaceLane: Fixed(2), Pure, "replace_lane";
    /// args: lhs, rhs, the index of the lane indices in `Func::constants`.
    Shuffle: Fixed(2), Pure, "shuffle";
    /// args: base, index, offset; flags: the load's SIMD sub-opcode.
    VectorLoad: Fixed(2), Read, "vector_load";

    // Instance data.
    /// args: instance, byte offset. A pointer field of the instance data that never changes.
    InstanceField: Fixed(1), Pure, "instance_field";
    /// args: pointer, byte offset; flags: 4 for a u32, else a pointer. Data of the instance that never changes, like
    /// `globals[i]` or a type identity.
    LoadPointer: Fixed(1), Pure, "load_pointer";
    /// args: the global's storage, global index.
    GlobalGet: Fixed(1), Read, "global_get";
    /// args: the global's storage, value, global index.
    GlobalSet: Fixed(2), Write, "global_set";

    // Memory 0, a memory32 with guard pages: the access is at base + zero-extended index + offset.
    /// args: base, index, offset; flags: LoadKind.
    Load: Fixed(2), Read, "load";
    /// operands: base, index, value; args[2]: offset; flags: log2 of the size.
    Store: Variadic, Write, "store";

    /// args: pointer, byte offset. The address that far from the pointer.
    Offset: Fixed(1), Pure, "offset";
    /// args: an interpreter frame's fp, byte offset (a signed 32-bit value); flags: 1 for a v128 local, whose slot
    /// has the address of its storage. A local or operand stack value of the frame an OSR compile continues.
    FrameLoad: Fixed(1), Read, "frame_load";
    /// args: pointer, byte offset; flags: the bytes it reads, 4 or 8. A field of runtime data that may change, like
    /// the size of a memory or table, read where it is.
    ReadField: Fixed(1), Read, "read_field";
    /// args: pointer, value, byte offset; flags: the bytes it writes, 4 or 8.
    WriteField: Fixed(2), Write, "write_field";

    // Tables. A table's `TableData` is a pointer of the instance's that never changes.
    /// args: table data, index; flags: the TRAP_* code for an index out of bounds. Element `index`.
    TableElement: Fixed(2), Read, "table_element";
    /// args: table data, index, value; flags: the TRAP_* code for an index out of bounds.
    TableStore: Fixed(3), Write, "table_store";

    // Memories without guard pages, and atomics.
    /// args: memory data, index (i32, or i64 for a memory64), offset (i64); flags: log2 of the access size,
    /// CHECKED_ATOMIC, CHECKED_MEMORY64. The address of the access at index + offset, after checking that it is in
    /// the memory, and for atomics then that it is aligned.
    CheckedAddress: Fixed(3), Read, "checked_address";
    /// args: address, value, the `AtomicOp`; flags: log2 of the size. Applies the op atomically and returns the old
    /// value, zero-extended.
    AtomicRmw: Fixed(2), Write, "atomic_rmw";
    /// args: address, expected value, replacement; flags: log2 of the size. Returns the old value, zero-extended.
    AtomicCompareExchange: Fixed(3), Write, "atomic_cmpxchg";
    /// A sequentially consistent fence.
    AtomicFence: Fixed(0), Write, "atomic_fence";

    // GC objects. A field or element is accessed with `Load`, `VectorLoad` and `Store` at its address, or at the
    // object with the field's offset where the data is inline.
    /// args: instance, the module's type index. The `Rtt` of the type, which never changes.
    Rtt: Fixed(1), Pure, "rtt";
    /// args: i32. The i31 reference of its low 31 bits.
    I31New: Fixed(1), Pure, "ref_i31";
    /// args: i31 reference (not null); flags: 1 to sign-extend. The i32 value.
    I31Get: Fixed(1), Pure, "i31_get";
    /// args: array, index; flags: log2 of the element size. The address of the element, after checking the array for
    /// null and the index against its length.
    ElementAddress: Fixed(2), Read, "element_address";
    /// args: reference, the type identity it is tested against (a constant for abstract heap types), the depth of
    /// that type; flags: `HeapTest`, REF_TEST_NULLABLE, REF_TEST_CAST. Whether the reference matches, as an i32; a
    /// cast has no value and traps instead where it does not.
    RefTest: Fixed(2), Pure, "ref_test";

    // Calls.
    /// args: callee FunctionHeader, the calling instance. The callee's instance: its function header's, or for a host
    /// function, which has none, the caller's, through which its stub finds the runtime; flags: FLAG_NOT_NULL. Pure
    /// only with FLAG_NOT_NULL: a function reference may be null anywhere the null check that guards its call does
    /// not dominate, and a pure node could be hoisted above that check and fault instead of trapping.
    CalleeInstance: Fixed(2), Read, "callee_instance";
    /// args: function reference, the type identity it must have; flags: the TRAP_* code for null. Traps unless the
    /// reference is not null and of that type or a subtype.
    CheckFunction: Fixed(2), Write, "check_function";
    /// args: reference; flags: the TRAP_* code. Traps if the reference is null.
    CheckNull: Fixed(1), Write, "check_null";
    /// Traps if another thread interrupted the store, which raised the stack limit. In the header of every loop: a
    /// function entry checks the limit anyway, but loops may not call. It finds the limit through the frame, so that it
    /// keeps no register busy across the loop.
    CheckInterrupt: Fixed(0), Write, "check_interrupt";
    /// operands: callee FunctionHeader, its instance, its memory base, arguments; args[2]: the function index, or
    /// NONE for an indirect call. The value is the first result.
    Call: Variadic, Write, "call";
    /// operands: the instance, then up to six operands; args[2]: the `Helper`. A call of a function of the runtime
    /// that takes its operands in the `ExecutionContext`'s `arguments` and returns a u64.
    Helper: Variadic, Write, "helper";
    /// args: call, result index. A further result of the call right before it.
    CallResult: Fixed(0), Pure, "call_result";

    // Terminators. Successors are in the block (`Func::successors()`).
    Jump: Fixed(0), Terminator, "jump";
    /// args: condition. To the first successor if nonzero, else the second.
    Branch: Fixed(1), Terminator, "branch";
    /// args: lhs, rhs; flags: IntCondition. To the first successor if the comparison holds.
    BranchCompare: Fixed(2), Terminator, "branch_compare";
    /// args: lhs, rhs; flags: FloatCondition.
    BranchFloatCompare: Fixed(2), Terminator, "branch_fcompare";
    /// args: index, start of the targets in `Func::operands`, their count before the default (which comes last).
    /// Each target is the index of a successor of the block.
    BrTable: Fixed(1), Terminator, "br_table";
    /// operands: the results.
    Return: Variadic, Terminator, "return";
    /// args: the TRAP_* code.
    Trap: Fixed(0), Terminator, "trap";
    /// operands and args like `Call`. A call whose results are the function's.
    TailCall: Variadic, Terminator, "tail_call";
    /// args: an exception reference, not null. Throws it to the function's callers: the runtime unwinds it to the
    /// first call that handles exceptions, or out of compiled code.
    Throw: Fixed(1), Terminator, "throw";
}

impl Op {
    pub fn is_terminator(self) -> bool {
        self.base_effect() == Effect::Terminator
    }

    /// Whether nodes of this op never have code where they are.
    pub fn is_entry_value(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            Op::Const32 | Op::Const64 | Op::Const128 | Op::Param | Op::Instance | Op::MemoryBase
        )
    }

    pub fn is_constant(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Op::Const32 | Op::Const64 | Op::Const128)
    }

    pub fn is_commutative(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            Op::Add | Op::Mul | Op::And | Op::Or | Op::Xor | Op::FAdd | Op::FMul
        )
    }
}

/// One node: 16 bytes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Node {
    pub op: Op,
    pub ty: Type,
    pub flags: u8,
    pub args: [u32; 3],
}

const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Node>() == 16);

impl Node {
    pub fn new(op: Op, ty: Type, flags: u8, args: [u32; 3]) -> Self {
        Self { op, ty, flags, args }
    }

    /// What this node may do besides computing its value.
    pub fn effect(&self) -> Effect {
        match self.op {
            Op::GlobalGet if self.flags & FLAG_IMMUTABLE != 0 => Effect::Pure,
            Op::CalleeInstance if self.flags & FLAG_NOT_NULL != 0 => Effect::Pure,
            Op::DivS | Op::DivU | Op::RemS | Op::RemU | Op::TruncS | Op::TruncU
                if self.flags & FLAG_CANNOT_TRAP != 0 =>
            {
                Effect::Pure
            }
            Op::RefTest if self.flags & REF_TEST_CAST != 0 => Effect::Write,
            op => op.base_effect(),
        }
    }

    /// The constant bits of a scalar constant node. Vector constants are in `Func::constants`.
    pub fn constant(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        match self.op {
            Op::Const32 => Some(u64::from(self.args[0])),
            Op::Const64 => Some(u64::from(self.args[0]) | (u64::from(self.args[1]) << 32)),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// A block: its phis, its body and its edges.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Block {
    /// The body: nodes `start..end`, the last of which is the terminator.
    pub start: u32,
    pub end: u32,
    /// The first phi; each phi's `args[2]` links to the next one.
    pub first_phi: Value,
    pub predecessors_start: u32,
    pub predecessor_count: u32,
    pub successors_start: u32,
    pub successor_count: u32,
    /// The innermost loop this block is in, as an index into `Func::loops`.
    pub loop_index: u32,
}

impl Default for Block {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            start: 0,
            end: 0,
            first_phi: NONE,
            predecessors_start: 0,
            predecessor_count: 0,
            successors_start: 0,
            successor_count: 0,
            loop_index: NONE,
        }
    }
}

/// A loop: the contiguous blocks `header..=last`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Loop {
    pub header: BlockId,
    pub last: BlockId,
    /// The loop around this one.
    pub parent: u32,
    pub depth: u32,
}

/// A function in the IR.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct Func {
    pub blocks: Vec<Block>,
    pub nodes: Vec<Node>,
    /// The inputs of variadic nodes, and the targets of `BrTable`s.
    pub operands: Vec<u32>,
    /// Vector constants and shuffles' lane indices.
    pub constants: Vec<u128>,
    pub predecessors: Vec<BlockId>,
    pub successors: Vec<BlockId>,
    pub loops: Vec<Loop>,
    /// The type of each parameter and result.
    pub params: Vec<Type>,
    pub results: Vec<Type>,
}

impl Func {
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.blocks.clear();
        self.nodes.clear();
        self.operands.clear();
        self.constants.clear();
        self.predecessors.clear();
        self.successors.clear();
        self.loops.clear();
        self.params.clear();
        self.results.clear();
    }

    pub fn node(&self, value: Value) -> &Node {
        &self.nodes[value as usize]
    }

    /// The inputs of a node.
    #[inline]
    pub fn inputs(&self, value: Value) -> &[u32] {
        let node = &self.nodes[value as usize];
        match node.op.shape() {
            Shape::Fixed(count) => &node.args[..count as usize],
            Shape::Variadic => {
                let start = node.args[0] as usize;
                &self.operands[start..start + node.args[1] as usize]
            }
        }
    }

    /// The value a forwarded phi stands for, or the value itself.
    pub fn resolve(&self, mut value: Value) -> Value {
        while self.nodes[value as usize].op == Op::Forward {
            value = self.nodes[value as usize].args[0];
        }
        value
    }

    /// The value a phi always has, if its inputs are only itself and one other value.
    pub fn trivial_phi_input(&self, phi: Value) -> Option<Value> {
        let mut same = NONE;
        for &input in self.inputs(phi) {
            let input = self.resolve(input);
            if input == phi || input == same {
                continue;
            }
            if same != NONE {
                return None;
            }
            same = input;
        }
        (same != NONE).then_some(same)
    }

    /// Makes `phi` stand for `value` from now on.
    pub fn forward(&mut self, phi: Value, value: Value) {
        let node = &mut self.nodes[phi as usize];
        node.op = Op::Forward;
        node.args[0] = value;
        node.args[1] = 0;
    }

    pub fn predecessors(&self, block: BlockId) -> &[BlockId] {
        let block = &self.blocks[block as usize];
        let start = block.predecessors_start as usize;
        &self.predecessors[start..start + block.predecessor_count as usize]
    }

    pub fn successors(&self, block: BlockId) -> &[BlockId] {
        let block = &self.blocks[block as usize];
        let start = block.successors_start as usize;
        &self.successors[start..start + block.successor_count as usize]
    }

    pub fn terminator(&self, block: BlockId) -> Value {
        self.blocks[block as usize].end - 1
    }

    /// The phis of a block, forwarded ones included.
    pub fn phis(&self, block: BlockId) -> PhiIter<'_> {
        PhiIter {
            func: self,
            next: self.blocks[block as usize].first_phi,
        }
    }

    /// The targets of a `BrTable`, the default last, as indices into the block's successors.
    pub fn table_targets(&self, value: Value) -> &[BlockId] {
        let node = &self.nodes[value as usize];
        debug_assert_eq!(node.op, Op::BrTable);
        let start = node.args[1] as usize;
        &self.operands[start..start + node.args[2] as usize + 1]
    }

    /// Whether `block` is the header of a loop.
    pub fn is_loop_header(&self, block: BlockId) -> bool {
        let loop_index = self.blocks[block as usize].loop_index;
        loop_index != NONE && self.loops[loop_index as usize].header == block
    }
}

pub struct PhiIter<'a> {
    func: &'a Func,
    next: Value,
}

impl Iterator for PhiIter<'_> {
    type Item = Value;

    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Value> {
        if self.next == NONE {
            return None;
        }
        let phi = self.next;
        self.next = self.func.nodes[phi as usize].args[2];
        Some(phi)
    }
}
