//! The IR verifier: checks the invariants every phase relies on. It runs under `verify-ir` and in tests.

use super::{Effect, Func, NONE, Op, Shape, Type, Value};

/// The immediate dominator of each block, with the entry its own. Linear order is a topological order of the
/// forward edges, so one pass over the blocks in it finds them; loops add back edges only.
pub fn immediate_dominators(func: &Func) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut idom = vec![NONE; func.blocks.len()];
    if func.blocks.is_empty() {
        return idom;
    }
    idom[0] = 0;
    for block in 1..func.blocks.len() as u32 {
        let mut dominator = NONE;
        for &predecessor in func.predecessors(block) {
            if predecessor >= block || idom[predecessor as usize] == NONE {
                continue;
            }
            dominator = if dominator == NONE {
                predecessor
            } else {
                intersect(&idom, dominator, predecessor)
            };
        }
        idom[block as usize] = dominator;
    }
    idom
}

fn intersect(idom: &[u32], mut a: u32, mut b: u32) -> u32 {
    while a != b {
        while a > b {
            a = idom[a as usize];
        }
        while b > a {
            b = idom[b as usize];
        }
    }
    a
}

/// Whether block `a` dominates block `b`.
pub fn dominates(idom: &[u32], a: u32, mut b: u32) -> bool {
    loop {
        if a == b {
            return true;
        }
        if b == 0 || idom[b as usize] == NONE || b < a {
            return false;
        }
        b = idom[b as usize];
    }
}

/// Checks the function. `after_cleanup` requires that no forwarded phi is used.
pub fn verify(func: &Func, after_cleanup: bool) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut errors = Vec::new();
    let mut error = |message: String| {
        if errors.len() < 20 {
            errors.push(message);
        }
    };
    let idom = immediate_dominators(func);
    // The block of every body node and phi, to check dominance.
    let mut block_of = vec![NONE; func.nodes.len()];
    for (index, block) in func.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        let block_id = index as u32;
        if block.start >= block.end {
            error(format!("b{index} has no terminator"));
            continue;
        }
        if index > 0 && idom[index] == NONE {
            error(format!("b{index} is unreachable"));
        }
        for value in block.start..block.end {
            let op = func.node(value).op;
            if matches!(op, Op::Phi | Op::Forward) || op.is_entry_value() {
                continue;
            }
            block_of[value as usize] = block_id;
            if op.is_terminator() != (value == block.end - 1) {
                error(format!("v{value} in b{index}: terminators end blocks and only they do"));
            }
        }
        for phi in func.phis(block_id) {
            block_of[phi as usize] = block_id;
            let node = func.node(phi);
            if node.op == Op::Phi && node.args[1] as usize != func.predecessors(block_id).len() {
                error(format!(
                    "phi v{phi} of b{index} has {} inputs for {} predecessors",
                    node.args[1],
                    func.predecessors(block_id).len()
                ));
            }
        }
        for &successor in func.successors(block_id) {
            if successor as usize >= func.blocks.len() {
                error(format!("b{index} has an unknown successor b{successor}"));
                continue;
            }
            let count = func.successors(block_id).iter().filter(|s| **s == successor).count();
            let back = func.predecessors(successor).iter().filter(|p| **p == block_id).count();
            if count != 1 || back != 1 {
                error(format!(
                    "the edge b{index} -> b{successor} is not listed once on each side"
                ));
            }
        }
        for &predecessor in func.predecessors(block_id) {
            if !func.successors(predecessor).contains(&block_id) {
                error(format!(
                    "b{index} lists b{predecessor} as a predecessor, which does not branch to it"
                ));
            }
        }
        let terminator = func.terminator(block_id);
        let expected_successors = match func.node(terminator).op {
            Op::Jump => Some(1),
            Op::Branch | Op::BranchCompare | Op::BranchFloatCompare => Some(2),
            Op::Return | Op::Trap | Op::TailCall | Op::Throw => Some(0),
            _ => None,
        };
        if let Some(expected) = expected_successors
            && func.successors(block_id).len() != expected
        {
            error(format!("b{index} has {} successors", func.successors(block_id).len()));
        }
    }

    let defined_before = |input: Value, block: u32, position: Value| -> bool {
        let node = func.node(input);
        if node.op.is_entry_value() {
            return true;
        }
        let definition = block_of[input as usize];
        if definition == NONE {
            return false;
        }
        if definition == block {
            return node.op == Op::Phi || input < position;
        }
        dominates(&idom, definition, block)
    };
    for (index, block) in func.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
        let block_id = index as u32;
        for value in (block.start..block.end).chain(func.phis(block_id)) {
            let node = func.node(value);
            if node.op.is_entry_value() || block_of[value as usize] != block_id {
                continue;
            }
            if after_cleanup && node.op == Op::Forward {
                continue;
            }
            for (input_index, &input) in func.inputs(value).iter().enumerate() {
                if input as usize >= func.nodes.len() {
                    error(format!("v{value} uses an unknown value {input}"));
                    continue;
                }
                let mut input = input;
                while !after_cleanup && func.node(input).op == Op::Forward {
                    input = func.node(input).args[0];
                }
                let input_node = func.node(input);
                if input_node.ty == Type::None {
                    error(format!("v{value} uses v{input}, which has no value"));
                }
                if after_cleanup && input_node.op == Op::Forward {
                    error(format!("v{value} uses the forwarded phi v{input}"));
                }
                let (use_block, position) = if node.op == Op::Phi {
                    let predecessor = func.predecessors(block_id)[input_index];
                    (predecessor, func.blocks[predecessor as usize].end)
                } else {
                    (block_id, value)
                };
                if !defined_before(input, use_block, position) {
                    error(format!(
                        "v{value} in b{index} uses v{input}, which does not dominate it"
                    ));
                }
            }
            check_types(func, value, &mut error);
        }
    }
    if errors.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(errors.join("\n"))
    }
}

fn check_types(func: &Func, value: Value, error: &mut impl FnMut(String)) {
    let node = func.node(value);
    let inputs = func.inputs(value);
    let input_type = |index: usize| func.node(inputs[index]).ty;
    let same = |ty: Type| inputs.iter().all(|input| func.node(*input).ty == ty);
    let ok = match node.op {
        Op::Add
        | Op::Sub
        | Op::Mul
        | Op::And
        | Op::Or
        | Op::Xor
        | Op::Shl
        | Op::ShrS
        | Op::ShrU
        | Op::Rotl
        | Op::Rotr
        | Op::DivS
        | Op::DivU
        | Op::RemS
        | Op::RemU
        | Op::Clz
        | Op::Ctz
        | Op::Popcnt
        | Op::Extend8S
        | Op::Extend16S
        | Op::Extend32S => matches!(node.ty, Type::I32 | Type::I64) && same(node.ty),
        Op::Eqz => node.ty == Type::I32 && matches!(input_type(0), Type::I32 | Type::I64 | Type::Ref),
        Op::Compare | Op::BranchCompare => {
            matches!(input_type(0), Type::I32 | Type::I64 | Type::Ref | Type::Pointer) && input_type(0) == input_type(1)
        }
        Op::FAdd
        | Op::FSub
        | Op::FMul
        | Op::FDiv
        | Op::FMin
        | Op::FMax
        | Op::FCopysign
        | Op::FAbs
        | Op::FNeg
        | Op::FSqrt
        | Op::FCeil
        | Op::FFloor
        | Op::FTrunc
        | Op::FNearest => node.ty.is_float() && same(node.ty),
        Op::FloatCompare | Op::BranchFloatCompare => input_type(0).is_float() && input_type(0) == input_type(1),
        Op::ExtendI32S | Op::ExtendI32U => node.ty == Type::I64 && input_type(0) == Type::I32,
        Op::Wrap => node.ty == Type::I32 && input_type(0) == Type::I64,
        Op::Select => input_type(0) == Type::I32 && input_type(1) == node.ty && input_type(2) == node.ty,
        Op::Phi => same(node.ty),
        // NB: GC objects' fields are accessed at the object's reference.
        Op::Load | Op::Store => matches!(input_type(0), Type::Pointer | Type::Ref) && input_type(1) == Type::I32,
        Op::Branch => input_type(0) == Type::I32,
        Op::BrTable => input_type(0) == Type::I32,
        Op::InstanceField | Op::LoadPointer | Op::GlobalGet | Op::GlobalSet | Op::Offset | Op::FrameLoad => {
            input_type(0) == Type::Pointer
        }
        // NB: References to runtime objects, like exceptions and GC objects, point at them.
        Op::ReadField | Op::WriteField => matches!(input_type(0), Type::Pointer | Type::Ref),
        Op::CheckedAddress => {
            input_type(0) == Type::Pointer
                && matches!(input_type(1), Type::I32 | Type::I64)
                && input_type(2) == Type::I64
                && node.ty == Type::Pointer
        }
        Op::AtomicRmw | Op::AtomicCompareExchange => {
            input_type(0) == Type::Pointer
                && matches!(node.ty, Type::I32 | Type::I64)
                && inputs[1..].iter().all(|input| func.node(*input).ty == node.ty)
        }
        Op::Rtt => input_type(0) == Type::Pointer && node.ty == Type::Pointer,
        Op::I31New => input_type(0) == Type::I32 && node.ty == Type::Ref,
        Op::I31Get => input_type(0) == Type::Ref && node.ty == Type::I32,
        Op::ElementAddress => input_type(0) == Type::Ref && input_type(1) == Type::I32 && node.ty == Type::Pointer,
        Op::RefTest => input_type(0) == Type::Ref && input_type(1) == Type::I32,
        Op::TableElement => input_type(0) == Type::Pointer && node.ty == Type::Ref,
        Op::TableStore => input_type(0) == Type::Pointer && input_type(2) == Type::Ref,
        Op::CheckFunction => input_type(0) == Type::Ref && input_type(1) == Type::I32,
        Op::CheckNull => input_type(0) == Type::Ref,
        Op::CheckInterrupt => true,
        Op::CalleeInstance => matches!(input_type(0), Type::Ref | Type::Pointer) && input_type(1) == Type::Pointer,
        Op::Call | Op::TailCall => {
            matches!(input_type(0), Type::Ref | Type::Pointer)
                && input_type(1) == Type::Pointer
                && input_type(2) == Type::Pointer
        }
        Op::Helper => input_type(0) == Type::Pointer && inputs.len() <= 7,
        _ => true,
    };
    if !ok {
        error(format!("v{value} ({}) has inputs of the wrong types", node.op.name()));
    }
    if node.op.shape() == Shape::Variadic && node.op != Op::Phi && node.effect() == Effect::Pure {
        error(format!("v{value} is a pure variadic node"));
    }
}

//! The LibWasm optimizing JIT compiler.
//!
//! This crate is a pure compiler: it turns one function of a validated module into machine code and the metadata
//! the runtime needs to install and run it. It touches no heap and no store, so it runs on any thread. See
//! `ARCHITECTURE.md` for how it works.

// NB: The assemblers are libjs_jit's, until both JITs share them from a crate of their own. The test helpers of the
//     assemblers' own tests are for libjs_jit's tests.
#[cfg_attr(test, allow(dead_code))]
#[path = "../../../LibJS/JIT/Rust/src/asm/mod.rs"]
pub mod asm;

pub mod builder;
pub mod codegen;
pub mod convention;
pub mod decode;
pub mod inline_vec;
pub mod ir;
pub mod passes;
pub mod regalloc;
pub mod runtime;
#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
pub mod stubs;
#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
#[path = "stubs_aarch64.rs"]
pub mod stubs;
pub mod table;

use libwasm_module::Module;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// Why a function was not compiled.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CompileFailure {
    /// An OSR compile at a loop it cannot enter, at module offset `pc`: one that is unreachable, or in a legacy
    /// handler, whose exception the interpreter frame has no value for. The frame goes on in the interpreter.
    NoOsrEntry { pc: u32 },
    /// The assembler could not finish the code.
    CodeGeneration,
}

impl CompileFailure {
    pub fn reason(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            CompileFailure::NoOsrEntry { .. } => "no OSR entry at the loop",
            CompileFailure::CodeGeneration => "code generation failed",
        }
    }
}

/// Options of a compile.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Options {
    /// Check the IR and the register allocation after every phase.
    pub verify_ir: bool,
    pub dump_ir: bool,
    pub dump_asm: bool,
    /// Measure the time of every phase (`Stats::ticks`), which includes verification if that is on too.
    pub stats: bool,
    /// Give values only a few registers, so that the allocator spills and reloads all the time.
    pub stress_registers: bool,
    /// Leave loop invariant code in its loop.
    pub no_licm: bool,
    /// Refuse OSR compiles at loops in no other loop, so that tests reach the loops in them.
    pub stress_nested_osr: bool,
}

/// The addresses of the runtime compiled code reaches, which are constants of the process.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RuntimeInfo {
    /// Where code jumps to trap, with the TRAP_* code in edi and rbp the frame pointer of the trapping function.
    pub trap_exit: u64,
    /// The runtime's helpers (`wasm_runtime_memory_grow`, `wasm_runtime_table_grow` and `wasm_runtime_call_host`),
    /// which take the `ExecutionContext` with their operands in its `arguments`.
    pub memory_grow: u64,
    pub table_grow: u64,
    pub call_host: u64,
    /// `wasm_runtime_allocate`, `wasm_runtime_wait` and `wasm_runtime_notify`.
    pub allocate: u64,
    pub wait: u64,
    pub notify: u64,
    /// `wasm_runtime_allocate_exception` (`Helper::AllocateException`), and `wasm_runtime_throw_from_native`, which
    /// takes an exception and the fp of the frame that throws it, unwinds the exception, and returns the context,
    /// whose `resume` says where to continue.
    pub allocate_exception: u64,
    pub throw: u64,
}

/// What to compile.
pub struct CompileRequest {
    pub module: Arc<Module>,
    /// The function, counting imports.
    pub function: u32,
    pub runtime: RuntimeInfo,
    /// The address of the store's `ExecutionContext::stack_limit`, which stays the same for as long as the store lives
    /// (each store has its own code).
    pub stack_limit: u64,
    pub options: Options,
    /// For an OSR compile, the module offset of the loop that it continues an interpreter frame at, in any number of
    /// other loops. Its code takes the frame's fp as its only argument and returns the function's results.
    pub osr: Option<u32>,
}

/// The reusable state of one compile thread: every phase's storage, cleared between compiles.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct CompileContext {
    pub func: ir::Func,
    builder: builder::Builder,
    liveliness: passes::cleanup::Liveliness,
    licm: passes::licm::Licm,
    scheduler: passes::schedule::Scheduler,
    allocator: regalloc::Allocator,
    pub allocation: regalloc::Allocation,
    code_memory: CodeMemory,
}

/// The memory that an assembler works in: the column that it writes the code to, and the zone of its labels and
/// fixups.
pub struct CodeMemory {
    pub code: ak::Column<u8>,
    pub work: ak::Zone,
}

impl CodeMemory {
    /// The most code that one function or stub can have.
    const MAX_CODE_BYTES: usize = 1 << 30;
    /// The most bytes that the work data of the assembler can take. It is address space, which costs nothing before
    /// it is used, and it is far above what the largest function body that the parser accepts (7,654,321 bytes) takes,
    /// even one that is all `br_table` targets.
    const MAX_WORK_BYTES: usize = 1 << 34;

    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            code: ak::Column::new(Self::MAX_CODE_BYTES, c"Wasm JIT code"),
            work: ak::Zone::new(Self::MAX_WORK_BYTES, c"Wasm JIT assembler"),
        }
    }

    /// Drops the code and the data of the assembler that wrote it, and keeps the memory for the next code.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.code.clear();
        self.work.reset();
    }
}

impl Default for CodeMemory {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// The phases of a compile, as `Stats::ticks` counts them.
pub const PHASES: [&str; 5] = ["build", "passes", "liveness", "allocation", "codegen"];

/// What a compile did.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub struct Stats {
    /// The time stamp counter ticks of each phase (see `PHASES`), with `Options::stats`.
    pub ticks: [u64; PHASES.len()],
    /// The nodes the function's IR has, dead ones included.
    pub nodes: u32,
    /// The stack slots of the frame.
    pub slots: u32,
    /// The moves the allocator inserted, on edges and before nodes.
    pub moves: u32,
    /// The nodes loop invariant code motion moved out of loops.
    pub hoisted: u32,
}

/// The time stamp counter, for the phase timers.
pub fn ticks() -> u64 {
    #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
    // SAFETY: rdtsc only reads a counter.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::x86_64::_rdtsc()
    }
    #[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")]
    {
        let counter: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading the virtual counter has no effects.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("mrs {}, cntvct_el0", out(reg) counter, options(nomem, nostack)) };
        counter
    }
    #[cfg(not(any(target_arch = "x86_64", target_arch = "aarch64")))]
    0
}

/// The result of a compile.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct CompiledFunction {
    /// Position-independent machine code; the entry point is its start.
    pub code: Vec<u8>,
    /// The bytes between fp and rsp in the function's frame.
    pub frame_size: u32,
    /// The offsets of the return addresses of the calls that handle exceptions: an exception the runtime unwinds to
    /// one of them continues there, with the context's `exception` set, as if the call had returned.
    pub exception_sites: Vec<u32>,
    pub stats: Stats,
    pub dump: Option<String>,
}

/// Compiles one function of a module.
pub fn compile(context: &mut CompileContext, request: &CompileRequest) -> Result<CompiledFunction, CompileFailure> {
    let module = &*request.module;
    let timed = request.options.stats;
    let mut stats = Stats::default();
    let mut last = if timed { ticks() } else { 0 };
    let mut lap = |phase: usize, stats: &mut Stats| {
        if timed {
            let now = ticks();
            stats.ticks[phase] += now - last;
            last = now;
        }
    };
    match request.osr {
        None => context.builder.build(module, request.function, &mut context.func),
        Some(pc) => {
            let Some(entry) = context
                .builder
                .probe_osr(module, request.function, pc, &mut context.func)
                .filter(|(_, around)| !request.options.stress_nested_osr || !around.is_empty())
            else {
                return Err(CompileFailure::NoOsrEntry { pc });
            };
            context
                .builder
                .build_osr(module, request.function, pc, entry, &mut context.func);
        }
    }
    lap(0, &mut stats);
    if request.options.verify_ir
        && let Err(errors) = ir::verify::verify(&context.func, false)
    {
        panic!(
            "invalid IR after building function {}:\n{errors}\n{}",
            request.function,
            ir::dump::dump(&context.func)
        );
    }
    passes::cleanup::cleanup(&mut context.func, &mut context.liveliness);
    passes::interrupt_checks::run(&context.func, &mut context.liveliness);
    // NB: The loop an OSR compile enters has two ways in, so it has no preheader to hoist into.
    let no_licm = request.options.no_licm || request.osr.is_some();
    if no_licm {
        context.licm.home.clear();
        context.licm.home.resize(context.func.nodes.len(), ir::NONE);
    } else {
        context.licm.run(&context.func, &context.liveliness);
    }
    context
        .scheduler
        .run(&mut context.func, &mut context.liveliness, &context.licm.home);
    lap(1, &mut stats);
    if request.options.verify_ir
        && let Err(errors) = ir::verify::verify(&context.func, true)
    {
        panic!(
            "invalid IR after cleanup and scheduling of function {}:\n{errors}\n{}",
            request.function,
            ir::dump::dump(&context.func)
        );
    }
    context
        .allocator
        .allocate(&context.func, &mut context.allocation, request.options.stress_registers);
    lap(3, &mut stats);
    if timed {
        // NB: Liveness runs first in the allocator, which times it.
        stats.ticks[2] = context.allocator.liveness_ticks;
        stats.ticks[3] = stats.ticks[3].saturating_sub(stats.ticks[2]);
    }
    if request.options.verify_ir
        && let Err(errors) = regalloc::verify::verify(&context.func, &context.allocation)
    {
        panic!(
            "invalid register allocation of function {}:\n{errors}\n{}\n{}",
            request.function,
            ir::dump::dump(&context.func),
            regalloc::verify::dump(&context.func, &context.allocation)
        );
    }
    context.code_memory.clear();
    let generated = codegen::target::generate(
        &context.func,
        &context.allocation,
        &request.runtime,
        request.stack_limit,
        &mut context.code_memory,
    )?;
    lap(4, &mut stats);
    stats.nodes = context.func.nodes.len() as u32;
    stats.slots = context.allocation.slot_count;
    stats.moves = context.allocation.moves.len() as u32;
    stats.hoisted = if no_licm { 0 } else { context.licm.hoisted };
    let mut compiled = CompiledFunction {
        code: generated.code,
        frame_size: generated.frame_size,
        exception_sites: generated.exception_sites,
        stats,
        dump: None,
    };
    if request.options.dump_ir || request.options.dump_asm {
        let mut text = String::new();
        if request.options.dump_ir {
            text.push_str(&ir::dump::dump(&context.func));
            text.push_str(&regalloc::verify::dump(&context.func, &context.allocation));
        }
        if request.options.dump_asm {
            let architecture = if cfg!(target_arch = "aarch64") {
                asm::Architecture::AArch64
            } else {
                asm::Architecture::X86_64
            };
            asm::disassembler::for_each_instruction(architecture, &compiled.code, compiled.code.len(), |line| {
                text.push_str(&format!("{:6x}  {}\n", line.offset, line.text));
            });
        }
        compiled.dump = Some(text);
    }
    Ok(compiled)
}

/*

//! Cleanup after building: removes the phis that turned out trivial, to a fixed point, rewrites every use of a
//! forwarded phi, removes pure nodes nobody uses, and fuses branches with the comparisons only they use.

use crate::ir::{Effect, Func, IntCondition, NONE, Node, Op, Shape, Type, Value};

/// What cleanup leaves for the later phases: which nodes are gone, and how often each value is used.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Liveliness {
    pub dead: Vec<bool>,
    pub uses: Vec<u32>,
    worklist: Vec<Value>,
}

impl Liveliness {
    pub fn is_dead(&self, value: Value) -> bool {
        self.dead[value as usize]
    }
}

pub fn cleanup(func: &mut Func, state: &mut Liveliness) {
    // Trivial phis, to a fixed point over the phis only.
    loop {
        let mut changed = false;
        for block in 0..func.blocks.len() as u32 {
            let mut phi = func.blocks[block as usize].first_phi;
            while phi != NONE {
                let next = func.nodes[phi as usize].args[2];
                if func.nodes[phi as usize].op == Op::Phi
                    && let Some(value) = func.trivial_phi_input(phi)
                {
                    func.forward(phi, value);
                    changed = true;
                }
                phi = next;
            }
        }
        if !changed {
            break;
        }
    }
    // Every use of a forwarded phi becomes a use of its value, and every use is counted.
    let count = func.nodes.len();
    state.dead.clear();
    state.dead.resize(count, false);
    state.uses.clear();
    state.uses.resize(count, 0);
    for index in 0..count {
        let node = func.nodes[index];
        if node.op == Op::Forward {
            state.dead[index] = true;
            continue;
        }
        match node.op.shape() {
            Shape::Fixed(inputs) => {
                for slot in 0..inputs as usize {
                    let input = func.resolve(node.args[slot]);
                    func.nodes[index].args[slot] = input;
                    state.uses[input as usize] += 1;
                }
            }
            Shape::Variadic => {
                let start = node.args[0] as usize;
                for slot in start..start + node.args[1] as usize {
                    let input = func.resolve(func.operands[slot]);
                    func.operands[slot] = input;
                    state.uses[input as usize] += 1;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Dead code: pure nodes without uses.
    state.worklist.clear();
    for index in 0..count {
        // NB: Unused results of calls stay, since they tell how the call returns its results.
        let node = &func.nodes[index];
        if state.uses[index] == 0 && !state.dead[index] && node.effect() == Effect::Pure && node.op != Op::CallResult {
            state.worklist.push(index as Value);
        }
    }
    while let Some(value) = state.worklist.pop() {
        if state.dead[value as usize] {
            continue;
        }
        state.dead[value as usize] = true;
        for input_index in 0..func.inputs(value).len() {
            let input = func.inputs(value)[input_index];
            let uses = &mut state.uses[input as usize];
            *uses -= 1;
            let input_node = &func.nodes[input as usize];
            if *uses == 0 && input_node.effect() == Effect::Pure && input_node.op != Op::CallResult {
                state.worklist.push(input);
            }
        }
    }

    // Forwarded and dead phis leave their blocks.
    for block in 0..func.blocks.len() {
        let mut previous = NONE;
        let mut phi = func.blocks[block].first_phi;
        while phi != NONE {
            let next = func.nodes[phi as usize].args[2];
            if state.dead[phi as usize] {
                if previous == NONE {
                    func.blocks[block].first_phi = next;
                } else {
                    func.nodes[previous as usize].args[2] = next;
                }
            } else {
                previous = phi;
            }
            phi = next;
        }
    }

    fuse_branches(func, state);
}

/// A branch on a comparison that only it uses, in the same block, compares itself.
fn fuse_branches(func: &mut Func, state: &mut Liveliness) {
    for block in 0..func.blocks.len() {
        let terminator = func.blocks[block].end - 1;
        let node = func.nodes[terminator as usize];
        if node.op != Op::Branch {
            continue;
        }
        let condition = node.args[0];
        let condition_node = func.nodes[condition as usize];
        let in_block = condition >= func.blocks[block].start && condition < terminator;
        if !in_block || state.uses[condition as usize] != 1 {
            continue;
        }
        let fused = match condition_node.op {
            Op::Compare => Node::new(
                Op::BranchCompare,
                Type::None,
                condition_node.flags,
                [condition_node.args[0], condition_node.args[1], 0],
            ),
            Op::FloatCompare => Node::new(
                Op::BranchFloatCompare,
                Type::None,
                condition_node.flags,
                [condition_node.args[0], condition_node.args[1], 0],
            ),
            Op::Eqz => {
                let operand = condition_node.args[0];
                let ty = func.nodes[operand as usize].ty;
                let zero = if ty.is_64() {
                    Node::new(Op::Const64, ty, 0, [0, 0, 0])
                } else {
                    Node::new(Op::Const32, Type::I32, 0, [0, 0, 0])
                };
                func.nodes.push(zero);
                state.dead.push(false);
                state.uses.push(1);
                let zero = func.nodes.len() as Value - 1;
                Node::new(
                    Op::BranchCompare,
                    Type::None,
                    IntCondition::Eq as u8,
                    [operand, zero, 0],
                )
            }
            _ => continue,
        };
        func.nodes[terminator as usize] = fused;
        // The comparison's inputs are now the branch's.
        state.dead[condition as usize] = true;
        state.uses[condition as usize] = 0;
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! The dominator tree. Linear order is a topological order of the forward edges and loops are entered at their
//! header only, so one pass over the blocks finds every immediate dominator. The tree is numbered in preorder, so
//! that a dominance query compares two numbers.

use crate::ir::{BlockId, Func, NONE};

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Dominators {
    pub idom: Vec<BlockId>,
    /// The preorder number of each block, and the largest number in its subtree.
    pre: Vec<u32>,
    last: Vec<u32>,
    children_start: Vec<u32>,
    children: Vec<BlockId>,
    stack: Vec<(BlockId, u32)>,
}

impl Dominators {
    pub fn compute(&mut self, func: &Func) {
        let count = func.blocks.len();
        self.idom.clear();
        self.idom.resize(count, NONE);
        if count == 0 {
            return;
        }
        self.idom[0] = 0;
        for block in 1..count as BlockId {
            let mut dominator = NONE;
            for &predecessor in func.predecessors(block) {
                if predecessor >= block || self.idom[predecessor as usize] == NONE {
                    continue;
                }
                dominator = if dominator == NONE {
                    predecessor
                } else {
                    let (mut a, mut b) = (dominator, predecessor);
                    while a != b {
                        while a > b {
                            a = self.idom[a as usize];
                        }
                        while b > a {
                            b = self.idom[b as usize];
                        }
                    }
                    a
                };
            }
            self.idom[block as usize] = dominator;
        }
        // Children lists, then a preorder walk.
        self.children_start.clear();
        self.children_start.resize(count + 1, 0);
        for block in 1..count {
            let parent = self.idom[block];
            if parent != NONE {
                self.children_start[parent as usize + 1] += 1;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..count {
            self.children_start[index + 1] += self.children_start[index];
        }
        self.children.clear();
        self.children.resize(self.children_start[count] as usize, 0);
        let mut cursor = self.children_start.clone();
        for block in 1..count {
            let parent = self.idom[block];
            if parent != NONE {
                self.children[cursor[parent as usize] as usize] = block as BlockId;
                cursor[parent as usize] += 1;
            }
        }
        self.pre.clear();
        self.pre.resize(count, NONE);
        self.last.clear();
        self.last.resize(count, NONE);
        let mut number = 0;
        self.stack.clear();
        self.stack.push((0, self.children_start[0]));
        self.pre[0] = 0;
        while let Some(&mut (block, ref mut next)) = self.stack.last_mut() {
            if *next < self.children_start[block as usize + 1] {
                let child = self.children[*next as usize];
                *next += 1;
                number += 1;
                self.pre[child as usize] = number;
                self.stack.push((child, self.children_start[child as usize]));
            } else {
                self.last[block as usize] = number;
                self.stack.pop();
            }
        }
    }

    /// Whether block `a` dominates block `b`.
    #[inline]
    pub fn dominates(&self, a: BlockId, b: BlockId) -> bool {
        let (pre_a, pre_b) = (self.pre[a as usize], self.pre[b as usize]);
        pre_a <= pre_b && pre_b <= self.last[a as usize]
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/JIT/src/passes/interrupt_checks.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Interrupt check elimination: small counting loops lose their `Op::CheckInterrupt`, as in LibJS's JIT.
//!
//! A check costs a loop of a few instructions a lot of them. It is there so that no code runs forever and an interrupt
//! arrives soon, and both still hold for two kinds of innermost loops. One that is known to run a few thousand times
//! at most stops soon by itself. One that counts towards any other bound ends within 2^32 iterations, and the code then
//! stops at the check of the loop around it. A counting loop without a loop around it keeps its check, or it could run
//! for seconds after an interrupt.
//!
//! An i32 phi of the loop's header counts if every back edge steps it by one in the same direction, and a branch that
//! every iteration passes leaves the loop once it gets to a bound. Everything wraps around in WebAssembly, so the test
//! must be one that a step by one cannot go past: `<` going up, `>` going down, or `!=` of a bound that stays the same
//! and so eventually comes up. A step of any other size can go past all of those.

use crate::ir::{BlockId, Func, IntCondition, NONE, Op, Type, Value};
use crate::passes::cleanup::Liveliness;
use crate::passes::dominators::Dominators;

/// How many nodes a loop may have to lose its check. In larger ones the check costs next to nothing.
const MAX_LOOP_SIZE: u32 = 64;

/// How many iterations a loop may have to lose its check without a loop around it, the bound V8 uses for this.
const MAX_ITERATIONS_WITHOUT_CHECK: i64 = 5000;

struct Loop<'a> {
    header: BlockId,
    /// The blocks that get back to the header. The block after a loop can have the loop's `loop_index`.
    blocks: &'a [BlockId],
}

impl Loop<'_> {
    fn contains(&self, block: BlockId) -> bool {
        self.blocks.contains(&block)
    }

    /// Whether a value is the same in every iteration.
    fn is_invariant(&self, func: &Func, value: Value) -> bool {
        func.node(value).constant().is_some()
            || self.blocks.iter().all(|&block| {
                let data = &func.blocks[block as usize];
                !(data.start..data.end).contains(&value) && !func.phis(block).any(|phi| phi == value)
            })
    }
}

/// What a branch at the end of a block of the loop knows of `counter`: the bound, and the comparison of the counter with
/// it that keeps the loop going.
fn test_of(func: &Func, loop_: &Loop, block: BlockId, counters: [Value; 2]) -> Option<(Value, IntCondition)> {
    let [first, second] = *func.successors(block) else {
        return None;
    };
    let stays_if_true = match (loop_.contains(first), loop_.contains(second)) {
        (true, false) => true,
        (false, true) => false,
        _ => return None,
    };
    let node = func.node(func.terminator(block));
    let (left, right, condition) = match node.op {
        Op::BranchCompare => (node.args[0], node.args[1], IntCondition::from_flags(node.flags)),
        Op::Branch => {
            let tested = func.resolve(node.args[0]);
            let tested_node = func.node(tested);
            match tested_node.op {
                Op::Compare => (
                    tested_node.args[0],
                    tested_node.args[1],
                    IntCondition::from_flags(tested_node.flags),
                ),
                Op::Eqz => (tested_node.args[0], NONE, IntCondition::Eq),
                _ => (tested, NONE, IntCondition::Ne),
            }
        }
        _ => return None,
    };
    let left = func.resolve(left);
    // NB: The zero of a plain branch is a bound that no node holds.
    let right = if right == NONE { NONE } else { func.resolve(right) };
    let (bound, condition) = if counters.contains(&left) {
        (right, condition)
    } else if right != NONE && counters.contains(&right) {
        (left, condition.swap())
    } else {
        return None;
    };
    Some((bound, if stays_if_true { condition } else { condition.invert() }))
}

/// By how much `next` changes `phi`, if that is one up or down.
fn step_of(func: &Func, phi: Value, next: Value) -> Option<i32> {
    let node = func.node(next);
    // NB: Only an addition or a subtraction has two values as its arguments; a constant's first argument is its value.
    if node.ty != Type::I32 || !matches!(node.op, Op::Add | Op::Sub) {
        return None;
    }
    let (left, right) = (func.resolve(node.args[0]), func.resolve(node.args[1]));
    let step = match node.op {
        Op::Add if left == phi => func.node(right).constant()? as u32 as i32,
        Op::Add if right == phi => func.node(left).constant()? as u32 as i32,
        Op::Sub if left == phi => (func.node(right).constant()? as u32 as i32).wrapping_neg(),
        _ => return None,
    };
    (step == 1 || step == -1).then_some(step)
}

/// How far `start` is from `bound` in steps, if the comparison of the two as it says tells that.
fn distance(start: u32, bound: u32, step: i32, condition: IntCondition) -> Option<i64> {
    let (start, bound) = match condition {
        IntCondition::LtU | IntCondition::GtU => (i64::from(start), i64::from(bound)),
        _ => (i64::from(start as i32), i64::from(bound as i32)),
    };
    let distance = (bound - start) * i64::from(step);
    // NB: A test of `!=` that starts past its bound goes all the way around.
    (condition != IntCondition::Ne || distance >= 0).then_some(distance)
}

/// How long a loop that counts with `phi` takes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
enum Trip {
    /// It ends by itself.
    Counted,
    /// It ends within MAX_ITERATIONS_WITHOUT_CHECK iterations.
    Short,
}

fn trip_of(func: &Func, dominators: &Dominators, loop_: &Loop, back_edges: &[usize], phi: Value) -> Option<Trip> {
    let inputs = func.inputs(phi);
    let predecessors = func.predecessors(loop_.header);
    let mut direction = 0;
    let mut next = NONE;
    for &edge in back_edges {
        let input = func.resolve(inputs[edge]);
        let step = step_of(func, phi, input)?;
        if (direction != 0 && step != direction) || (next != NONE && next != input) {
            return None;
        }
        direction = step;
        next = input;
    }
    let test = loop_.blocks.iter().find_map(|&block| {
        if !back_edges
            .iter()
            .all(|&edge| dominators.dominates(block, predecessors[edge]))
        {
            return None;
        }
        let (bound, condition) = test_of(func, loop_, block, [phi, next])?;
        let can_go_past = match (direction, condition) {
            (1, IntCondition::LtS | IntCondition::LtU) | (-1, IntCondition::GtS | IntCondition::GtU) => false,
            (_, IntCondition::Ne) => bound != NONE && !loop_.is_invariant(func, bound),
            _ => true,
        };
        (!can_go_past).then_some((bound, condition))
    });
    let (bound, condition) = test?;
    let bound = if bound == NONE {
        Some(0)
    } else {
        func.node(bound).constant()
    };
    let is_short = bound.is_some_and(|bound| {
        inputs
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(edge, _)| !back_edges.contains(edge))
            .all(|(_, start)| {
                func.node(func.resolve(*start)).constant().is_some_and(|start| {
                    distance(start as u32, bound as u32, direction, condition)
                        .is_some_and(|distance| distance < MAX_ITERATIONS_WITHOUT_CHECK)
                })
            })
    });
    Some(if is_short { Trip::Short } else { Trip::Counted })
}

/// Marks the checks that go as dead, which keeps `schedule` from placing them.
pub fn run(func: &Func, liveliness: &mut Liveliness) {
    if func.loops.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let mut dominators = Dominators::default();
    dominators.compute(func);
    let mut has_loop_inside = vec![false; func.loops.len()];
    for loop_ in &func.loops {
        if loop_.parent != NONE {
            has_loop_inside[loop_.parent as usize] = true;
        }
    }
    let mut blocks = Vec::new();
    let mut back_edges = Vec::new();
    for (index, loop_) in func.loops.iter().enumerate() {
        if has_loop_inside[index] {
            continue;
        }
        back_edges.clear();
        back_edges.extend(
            func.predecessors(loop_.header)
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .filter(|(_, predecessor)| **predecessor >= loop_.header)
                .map(|(edge, _)| edge),
        );
        blocks.clear();
        blocks.push(loop_.header);
        for &edge in &back_edges {
            let source = func.predecessors(loop_.header)[edge];
            if !blocks.contains(&source) {
                blocks.push(source);
            }
        }
        let mut next = 1;
        while next < blocks.len() {
            for &predecessor in func.predecessors(blocks[next]) {
                if !blocks.contains(&predecessor) {
                    blocks.push(predecessor);
                }
            }
            next += 1;
        }
        let mut size = 0;
        let mut calls = false;
        for &block in &blocks {
            let data = &func.blocks[block as usize];
            size += data.end - data.start;
            calls |= (data.start..data.end)
                .any(|value| !liveliness.is_dead(value) && matches!(func.node(value).op, Op::Call | Op::Helper));
        }
        if calls || size > MAX_LOOP_SIZE {
            continue;
        }
        let current = Loop {
            header: loop_.header,
            blocks: &blocks,
        };
        let best_trip = func
            .phis(loop_.header)
            .filter(|phi| !liveliness.is_dead(*phi) && func.node(*phi).op == Op::Phi && func.node(*phi).ty == Type::I32)
            .filter_map(|phi| trip_of(func, &dominators, &current, &back_edges, phi))
            .max();
        let may_lose_check = match best_trip {
            Some(Trip::Short) => true,
            Some(Trip::Counted) => loop_.parent != NONE,
            None => false,
        };
        if !may_lose_check {
            continue;
        }
        let header = &func.blocks[loop_.header as usize];
        for value in header.start..header.end {
            if func.node(value).op == Op::CheckInterrupt {
                liveliness.dead[value as usize] = true;
            }
        }
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/JIT/src/passes/licm.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Loop invariant code motion: finds the nodes of loops that compute the same value in every iteration, and the
//! outermost loop each one is invariant in. `schedule` then moves them to the end of that loop's preheader: the
//! block entering the loop, which always ends in a jump to its header.
//!
//! A pure node is invariant in a loop when none of its inputs is defined in the loop (or each was hoisted out of
//! it). Pure nodes never trap, so computing them where the loop might not have needs no proof that it would have.
//! A global's value is invariant in a loop that does not set it. Memory loads stay where they are, since moving one
//! out of a loop that would not have run it could trap.
//!
//! OPTIMIZATION: Nothing leaves a loop that calls: calls clobber every register, so a hoisted value would be reloaded
//! from its stack slot in every iteration, which costs about what computing it again does. In a loop that calls a
//! leaf 10 million times, hoisting the callee's `FunctionHeader` made it 16% slower.

use crate::ir::{BlockId, Effect, FLAG_IMMUTABLE, Func, NONE, Op, Value};
use crate::passes::cleanup::Liveliness;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Licm {
    /// The block each value moves to, or NONE.
    pub home: Vec<BlockId>,
    /// The block of each body node.
    block_of: Vec<BlockId>,
    /// Per loop: whether it calls, and the globals it sets.
    calls: Vec<bool>,
    globals_set: Vec<Vec<u32>>,
    /// How many nodes moved.
    pub hoisted: u32,
}

impl Licm {
    pub fn run(&mut self, func: &Func, liveliness: &Liveliness) {
        let count = func.nodes.len();
        self.home.clear();
        self.home.resize(count, NONE);
        self.hoisted = 0;
        if func.loops.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        self.block_of.clear();
        self.block_of.resize(count, 0);
        self.calls.clear();
        self.calls.resize(func.loops.len(), false);
        for set in &mut self.globals_set {
            set.clear();
        }
        self.globals_set.resize_with(func.loops.len(), Vec::new);
        for (index, block) in func.blocks.iter().enumerate() {
            for value in block.start..block.end {
                self.block_of[value as usize] = index as BlockId;
                let node = func.node(value);
                if liveliness.is_dead(value) || block.loop_index == NONE {
                    continue;
                }
                let global = match node.op {
                    Op::Call | Op::Helper => None,
                    Op::GlobalSet => Some(node.args[2]),
                    _ => continue,
                };
                let mut loop_index = block.loop_index;
                while loop_index != NONE {
                    match global {
                        None => self.calls[loop_index as usize] = true,
                        Some(global) => self.globals_set[loop_index as usize].push(global),
                    }
                    loop_index = func.loops[loop_index as usize].parent;
                }
            }
        }
        for phi_block in 0..func.blocks.len() as BlockId {
            for phi in func.phis(phi_block) {
                self.block_of[phi as usize] = phi_block;
            }
        }
        for block in &func.blocks {
            if block.loop_index == NONE {
                continue;
            }
            for value in block.start..block.end - 1 {
                let node = func.node(value);
                if liveliness.is_dead(value) || node.op.is_entry_value() || matches!(node.op, Op::Phi | Op::Forward) {
                    continue;
                }
                let global = match node.effect() {
                    Effect::Pure if node.op != Op::CallResult => None,
                    Effect::Read if node.op == Op::GlobalGet && node.flags & FLAG_IMMUTABLE == 0 => Some(node.args[1]),
                    _ => continue,
                };
                let mut target = NONE;
                let mut loop_index = block.loop_index;
                while loop_index != NONE {
                    let loop_ = &func.loops[loop_index as usize];
                    let outside = |input: &Value| {
                        let input_node = func.node(*input);
                        if input_node.op.is_entry_value() {
                            return true;
                        }
                        let home = self.home[*input as usize];
                        let block = if home == NONE {
                            self.block_of[*input as usize]
                        } else {
                            home
                        };
                        block < loop_.header || block > loop_.last
                    };
                    let unwritten =
                        global.is_none_or(|global| !self.globals_set[loop_index as usize].contains(&global));
                    if self.calls[loop_index as usize] || !unwritten || !func.inputs(value).iter().all(outside) {
                        break;
                    }
                    target = loop_index;
                    loop_index = loop_.parent;
                }
                if target != NONE {
                    let header = func.loops[target as usize].header;
                    self.home[value as usize] = func.predecessors(header)[0];
                    self.hoisted += 1;
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

//! Scheduling: rebuilds the node arena in linear order, which leaves out the dead nodes and puts the nodes loop
//! invariant code motion moved (`Licm::home`) at the end of their new block, before its terminator. Every input is
//! renumbered, so a node's index is its position again.
//!
//! The entry values come first, in the range of the entry block, and the phis last, outside every block's range,
//! since they are defined where their block starts wherever they are.

use crate::ir::{Func, NONE, Node, Op, Shape, Value};
use crate::passes::cleanup::Liveliness;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Scheduler {
    order: Vec<Value>,
    renumbered: Vec<Value>,
    nodes: Vec<Node>,
    hoisted: Vec<Vec<Value>>,
}

impl Scheduler {
    /// Schedules `func`, moving nodes as `home` says.
    pub fn run(&mut self, func: &mut Func, liveliness: &mut Liveliness, home: &[u32]) {
        let count = func.nodes.len();
        for list in &mut self.hoisted {
            list.clear();
        }
        self.hoisted.resize_with(func.blocks.len(), Vec::new);
        for (value, &block) in home.iter().enumerate() {
            if block != NONE {
                self.hoisted[block as usize].push(value as Value);
            }
        }
        self.order.clear();
        let live = |value: Value| !liveliness.is_dead(value);
        // The entry values, wherever cleanup or the builder put them.
        for value in 0..count as Value {
            if live(value) && func.nodes[value as usize].op.is_entry_value() {
                self.order.push(value);
            }
        }
        for block in 0..func.blocks.len() {
            let data = func.blocks[block];
            let start = if block == 0 { 0 } else { self.order.len() };
            for value in data.start..data.end - 1 {
                let op = func.nodes[value as usize].op;
                if live(value)
                    && !op.is_entry_value()
                    && !matches!(op, Op::Phi | Op::Forward)
                    && home[value as usize] == NONE
                {
                    self.order.push(value);
                }
            }
            for index in 0..self.hoisted[block].len() {
                self.order.push(self.hoisted[block][index]);
            }
            self.order.push(data.end - 1);
            func.blocks[block].start = start as u32;
            func.blocks[block].end = self.order.len() as u32;
        }
        for block in 0..func.blocks.len() {
            let mut phi = func.blocks[block].first_phi;
            while phi != NONE {
                self.order.push(phi);
                phi = func.nodes[phi as usize].args[2];
            }
        }

        self.renumbered.clear();
        self.renumbered.resize(count, NONE);
        for (index, value) in self.order.iter().enumerate() {
            self.renumbered[*value as usize] = index as Value;
        }
        self.nodes.clear();
        for &value in &self.order {
            let mut node = func.nodes[value as usize];
            match node.op.shape() {
                Shape::Fixed(inputs) => {
                    for slot in 0..inputs as usize {
                        node.args[slot] = self.renumbered[node.args[slot] as usize];
                    }
                }
                Shape::Variadic => {
                    let start = node.args[0] as usize;
                    for slot in start..start + node.args[1] as usize {
                        func.operands[slot] = self.renumbered[func.operands[slot] as usize];
                    }
                }
            }
            match node.op {
                Op::CallResult => node.args[0] = self.renumbered[node.args[0] as usize],
                Op::Phi if node.args[2] != NONE => node.args[2] = self.renumbered[node.args[2] as usize],
                _ => {}
            }
            self.nodes.push(node);
        }
        for block in &mut func.blocks {
            if block.first_phi != NONE {
                block.first_phi = self.renumbered[block.first_phi as usize];
            }
        }
        std::mem::swap(&mut func.nodes, &mut self.nodes);
        liveliness.dead.clear();
        liveliness.dead.resize(func.nodes.len(), false);
    }
}

/*

//! The constraints of nodes on AArch64. Instructions have three operands and no fixed registers, and code generation
//! puts any constant that does not fit an immediate into a scratch register, so constants may be inputs anywhere a
//! lowering takes one.

use super::{Constraints, Input, Output, Temp};
use crate::ir::{Func, Op, Type, Value};

/// Whether constant `value` can be an input of its own: any scalar constant can.
pub fn fits_immediate(func: &Func, value: Value) -> bool {
    func.node(value).constant().is_some()
}

pub(super) fn constraints(func: &Func, value: Value) -> Constraints {
    let node = func.node(value);
    let output = if node.ty == Type::None {
        Output::None
    } else {
        Output::Register
    };
    let mut constraints = Constraints {
        inputs: [Input::Register; 3],
        output,
        temps: [Temp::None; 2],
        clobbers: 0,
        reuse_first: false,
        slot_inputs: 0,
    };
    match node.op {
        Op::Add
        | Op::Sub
        | Op::And
        | Op::Or
        | Op::Xor
        | Op::Mul
        | Op::Shl
        | Op::ShrS
        | Op::ShrU
        | Op::Rotl
        | Op::Rotr
        | Op::Compare
        | Op::BranchCompare
        | Op::Load
        | Op::VectorLoad
        | Op::GlobalSet
        | Op::WriteField
        | Op::RefTest => constraints.inputs[1] = Input::RegisterOrConstant,
        Op::Store => {
            constraints.inputs[1] = Input::RegisterOrConstant;
            constraints.inputs[2] = Input::RegisterOrConstant;
        }
        Op::CheckFunction => constraints.temps = [Temp::Gpr, Temp::Gpr],
        Op::CheckedAddress => {
            let size = 1u64 << (node.flags & 7);
            let offset = func.node(node.args[2]).constant();
            // NB: A memory64's offset can be close enough to 2^64 that adding the size wraps around.
            if offset
                .and_then(|offset| offset.checked_add(size))
                .is_some_and(|end| end <= i32::MAX as u64)
            {
                constraints.inputs[2] = Input::RegisterOrConstant;
            }
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    if node.op == Op::RefTest {
        constraints.temps = match crate::ir::HeapTest::from_flags(node.flags) {
            crate::ir::HeapTest::Struct | crate::ir::HeapTest::Array | crate::ir::HeapTest::ConcreteObject => {
                [Temp::Gpr, Temp::None]
            }
            crate::ir::HeapTest::ConcreteFunction => [Temp::Gpr, Temp::Gpr],
            _ => [Temp::None, Temp::None],
        };
    }
    if matches!(
        node.op,
        Op::Shuffle | Op::VectorUnary | Op::VectorBinary | Op::VectorTernary
    ) {
        let temps = crate::codegen::aarch64::vector_temps(func, value);
        for temp in constraints.temps.iter_mut().take(temps) {
            *temp = Temp::Fpr;
        }
        if node.op == Op::VectorBinary && crate::codegen::aarch64::is_vector_shift(node.args[2]) {
            constraints.inputs[1] = Input::RegisterOrConstant;
        }
    }
    constraints
}
