//! The binary format decoder. It decodes the module structure and leaves function bodies and constant expressions as
//! byte ranges, which validation decodes as it checks them.

use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::module::CustomSection;
use crate::module::{
    ConstantExpression, Data, DataMode, Element, ElementItems, ElementMode, Export, ExternalKind, FunctionBody, Global,
    Import, ImportDescription, Module, RecursionGroup, Table,
};
use crate::opcode;
use crate::reader::Reader;
use crate::types::{
    AddressType, CompositeType, FieldType, FuncType, GlobalType, HeapType, Limits, MemoryType, RefType, StorageType,
    SubType, TableType, TagType, ValType,
};

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#limits
// The maximum size of a function body, including locals declarations, is 7,654,321 bytes.
const MAX_FUNCTION_SIZE: u32 = 7_654_321;

const SECTION_CUSTOM: u8 = 0;
const SECTION_TYPE: u8 = 1;
const SECTION_IMPORT: u8 = 2;
const SECTION_FUNCTION: u8 = 3;
const SECTION_TABLE: u8 = 4;
const SECTION_MEMORY: u8 = 5;
const SECTION_GLOBAL: u8 = 6;
const SECTION_EXPORT: u8 = 7;
const SECTION_START: u8 = 8;
const SECTION_ELEMENT: u8 = 9;
const SECTION_CODE: u8 = 10;
const SECTION_DATA: u8 = 11;
const SECTION_DATA_COUNT: u8 = 12;
const SECTION_TAG: u8 = 13;

/// The position of each non-custom section in the order the binary format requires.
fn section_order(id: u8) -> Option<u8> {
    Some(match id {
        SECTION_TYPE => 1,
        SECTION_IMPORT => 2,
        SECTION_FUNCTION => 3,
        SECTION_TABLE => 4,
        SECTION_MEMORY => 5,
        SECTION_TAG => 6,
        SECTION_GLOBAL => 7,
        SECTION_EXPORT => 8,
        SECTION_START => 9,
        SECTION_ELEMENT => 10,
        SECTION_DATA_COUNT => 11,
        SECTION_CODE => 12,
        SECTION_DATA => 13,
        _ => return None,
    })
}

pub fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Module> {
    let mut module = Module {
        bytes: bytes.into(),
        ..Module::default()
    };
    let mut reader = Reader::new(bytes);
    let magic = reader.read_bytes(4).map_err(|_| Error::malformed("unexpected end"))?;
    if magic != b"\0asm" {
        return Err(Error::malformed("magic header not detected"));
    }
    let version = reader.read_bytes(4).map_err(|_| Error::malformed("unexpected end"))?;
    if version != [1, 0, 0, 0] {
        return Err(Error::malformed("unknown binary version"));
    }

    let mut last_order = 0;
    let mut function_count = None;
    while !reader.is_at_end() {
        let id = reader.read_u8()?;
        let size = reader.read_u32()?;
        let mut section = reader.sub_reader(size as usize)?;
        if id != SECTION_CUSTOM {
            let order = section_order(id).ok_or_else(|| Error::malformed("malformed section id"))?;
            if order <= last_order {
                return Err(Error::malformed("unexpected content after last section"));
            }
            last_order = order;
        }
        match id {
            SECTION_CUSTOM => {
                let name = section.read_name()?.to_string();
                module.custom_sections.push(CustomSection {
                    name,
                    contents: section.position() as u32..section.end() as u32,
                });
                continue;
            }
            SECTION_TYPE => parse_type_section(&mut section, &mut module)?,
            SECTION_IMPORT => parse_import_section(&mut section, &mut module)?,
            SECTION_FUNCTION => {
                let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
                for _ in 0..count {
                    let type_index = section.read_u32()?;
                    module.functions.push(type_index);
                    module.function_space.push(type_index);
                }
                function_count = Some(count);
            }
            SECTION_TABLE => {
                let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
                for _ in 0..count {
                    let table = parse_table(&mut section)?;
                    module.table_space.push(table.ty);
                    module.tables.push(table);
                }
            }
            SECTION_MEMORY => {
                let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
                for _ in 0..count {
                    let memory = parse_memory_type(&mut section)?;
                    module.memory_space.push(memory);
                    module.memories.push(memory);
                }
            }
            SECTION_TAG => {
                let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
                for _ in 0..count {
                    let tag = parse_tag_type(&mut section)?;
                    module.tag_space.push(tag);
                    module.tags.push(tag);
                }
            }
            SECTION_GLOBAL => {
                let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
                for _ in 0..count {
                    let ty = parse_global_type(&mut section)?;
                    let initializer = parse_constant_expression(&mut section)?;
                    module.global_space.push(ty);
                    module.globals.push(Global { ty, initializer });
                }
            }
            SECTION_EXPORT => {
                let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
                for _ in 0..count {
                    let name = section.read_name()?.to_string();
                    let kind = match section.read_u8()? {
                        0x00 => ExternalKind::Function,
                        0x01 => ExternalKind::Table,
                        0x02 => ExternalKind::Memory,
                        0x03 => ExternalKind::Global,
                        0x04 => ExternalKind::Tag,
                        _ => return Err(Error::malformed("malformed export kind")),
                    };
                    let index = section.read_u32()?;
                    module.exports.push(Export { name, kind, index });
                }
            }
            SECTION_START => module.start = Some(section.read_u32()?),
            SECTION_ELEMENT => {
                let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
                for _ in 0..count {
                    module.elements.push(parse_element(&mut section)?);
                }
            }
            SECTION_DATA_COUNT => module.data_count = Some(section.read_u32()?),
            SECTION_CODE => {
                let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
                if function_count.unwrap_or(0) != count {
                    return Err(Error::malformed("function and code section have inconsistent lengths"));
                }
                for _ in 0..count {
                    module.code.push(parse_function_body(&mut section)?);
                }
            }
            SECTION_DATA => {
                let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
                if let Some(data_count) = module.data_count
                    && data_count != count
                {
                    return Err(Error::malformed(
                        "data count and data section have inconsistent lengths",
                    ));
                }
                for _ in 0..count {
                    module.data.push(parse_data(&mut section)?);
                }
            }
            _ => unreachable!("section ids are checked above"),
        }
        if !section.is_at_end() {
            return Err(Error::malformed("section size mismatch"));
        }
    }
    if function_count.unwrap_or(0) != 0 && module.code.is_empty() {
        return Err(Error::malformed("function and code section have inconsistent lengths"));
    }
    if module.data_count.is_some_and(|count| count != 0) && module.data.is_empty() {
        return Err(Error::malformed(
            "data count and data section have inconsistent lengths",
        ));
    }
    Ok(module)
}

fn parse_type_section(section: &mut Reader<'_>, module: &mut Module) -> Result<()> {
    let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
    for _ in 0..count {
        let start = module.types.len() as u32;
        if section.peek_u8()? == 0x4e {
            section.read_u8()?;
            let group_size = section.read_vector_length()?;
            for _ in 0..group_size {
                module.types.push(parse_sub_type(section)?);
            }
        } else {
            module.types.push(parse_sub_type(section)?);
        }
        let count = module.types.len() as u32 - start;
        module.recursion_groups.push(RecursionGroup { start, count });
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn parse_sub_type(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<SubType> {
    let (is_final, supertypes) = match reader.peek_u8()? {
        byte @ (0x50 | 0x4f) => {
            reader.read_u8()?;
            let supertypes = reader.read_vector(Reader::read_u32)?;
            (byte == 0x4f, supertypes)
        }
        _ => (true, Vec::new()),
    };
    let composite = match reader.read_u8()? {
        0x60 => {
            let params = parse_value_types(reader)?;
            let results = parse_value_types(reader)?;
            CompositeType::Func(FuncType { params, results })
        }
        0x5f => CompositeType::Struct(reader.read_vector(parse_field_type)?),
        0x5e => CompositeType::Array(parse_field_type(reader)?),
        _ => return Err(Error::malformed("integer representation too long")),
    };
    Ok(SubType {
        is_final,
        supertypes,
        composite,
    })
}

fn parse_field_type(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<FieldType> {
    let storage = match reader.peek_u8()? {
        0x78 => {
            reader.read_u8()?;
            StorageType::I8
        }
        0x77 => {
            reader.read_u8()?;
            StorageType::I16
        }
        _ => StorageType::Val(parse_value_type(reader)?),
    };
    let mutable = match reader.read_u8()? {
        0 => false,
        1 => true,
        _ => return Err(Error::malformed("malformed mutability")),
    };
    Ok(FieldType { storage, mutable })
}

fn parse_value_types(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<Vec<ValType>> {
    reader.read_vector(parse_value_type)
}

/// The abstract heap type a single byte encodes, both as a shorthand reference type (nullable) and as a heap type.
fn abstract_heap_type(byte: u8) -> Option<HeapType> {
    Some(match byte {
        0x70 => HeapType::Func,
        0x73 => HeapType::NoFunc,
        0x6f => HeapType::Extern,
        0x72 => HeapType::NoExtern,
        0x6e => HeapType::Any,
        0x6d => HeapType::Eq,
        0x6c => HeapType::I31,
        0x6b => HeapType::Struct,
        0x6a => HeapType::Array,
        0x71 => HeapType::None,
        0x69 => HeapType::Exn,
        0x74 => HeapType::NoExn,
        _ => return None,
    })
}

pub fn parse_heap_type(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<HeapType> {
    if let Some(heap) = abstract_heap_type(reader.peek_u8()?) {
        reader.read_u8()?;
        return Ok(heap);
    }
    let index = reader.read_s33()?;
    if index < 0 {
        return Err(Error::malformed("malformed reference type"));
    }
    u32::try_from(index)
        .map(HeapType::Concrete)
        .map_err(|_| Error::malformed("malformed reference type"))
}

pub fn parse_reference_type(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<RefType> {
    let byte = reader.read_u8()?;
    match byte {
        0x63 => Ok(RefType::new(true, parse_heap_type(reader)?)),
        0x64 => Ok(RefType::new(false, parse_heap_type(reader)?)),
        _ => abstract_heap_type(byte)
            .map(|heap| RefType::new(true, heap))
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::malformed("malformed reference type")),
    }
}

pub fn parse_value_type(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<ValType> {
    let value = match reader.peek_u8()? {
        0x7f => ValType::I32,
        0x7e => ValType::I64,
        0x7d => ValType::F32,
        0x7c => ValType::F64,
        0x7b => ValType::V128,
        _ => return Ok(ValType::Ref(parse_reference_type(reader)?)),
    };
    reader.read_u8()?;
    Ok(value)
}

fn parse_limits(reader: &mut Reader<'_>, is_memory: bool) -> Result<Limits> {
    let flags = reader.read_u8()?;
    let valid_flags = if is_memory { 0x07 } else { 0x05 };
    if flags & !valid_flags != 0 {
        return Err(Error::malformed(if is_memory {
            "malformed memory limits flags"
        } else {
            "malformed table limits flags"
        }));
    }
    let address_type = if flags & 0x04 != 0 {
        AddressType::I64
    } else {
        AddressType::I32
    };
    let read = |reader: &mut Reader<'_>| match address_type {
        AddressType::I32 => reader.read_u32().map(u64::from),
        AddressType::I64 => reader.read_u64(),
    };
    let min = read(reader)?;
    let max = if flags & 0x01 != 0 { Some(read(reader)?) } else { None };
    Ok(Limits {
        min,
        max,
        address_type,
        shared: flags & 0x02 != 0,
    })
}

fn parse_table_type(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<TableType> {
    let element = parse_reference_type(reader)?;
    let limits = parse_limits(reader, false)?;
    Ok(TableType { element, limits })
}

fn parse_table(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<Table> {
    if reader.peek_u8()? == 0x40 {
        reader.read_u8()?;
        if reader.read_u8()? != 0x00 {
            return Err(Error::malformed("malformed table"));
        }
        let ty = parse_table_type(reader)?;
        let initializer = parse_constant_expression(reader)?;
        return Ok(Table {
            ty,
            initializer: Some(initializer),
        });
    }
    Ok(Table {
        ty: parse_table_type(reader)?,
        initializer: None,
    })
}

fn parse_memory_type(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<MemoryType> {
    Ok(MemoryType {
        limits: parse_limits(reader, true)?,
    })
}

fn parse_global_type(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<GlobalType> {
    let value = parse_value_type(reader)?;
    let mutable = match reader.read_u8()? {
        0 => false,
        1 => true,
        _ => return Err(Error::malformed("malformed mutability")),
    };
    Ok(GlobalType { value, mutable })
}

fn parse_tag_type(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<TagType> {
    if reader.read_u8()? != 0x00 {
        return Err(Error::malformed("malformed tag attribute"));
    }
    Ok(TagType {
        type_index: reader.read_u32()?,
    })
}

fn parse_import_section(section: &mut Reader<'_>, module: &mut Module) -> Result<()> {
    let count = section.read_vector_length()?;
    for _ in 0..count {
        let module_name = section.read_name()?.to_string();
        let name = section.read_name()?.to_string();
        let description = match section.read_u8()? {
            0x00 => {
                let type_index = section.read_u32()?;
                module.function_space.push(type_index);
                module.imported_function_count += 1;
                ImportDescription::Function(type_index)
            }
            0x01 => {
                let table = parse_table_type(section)?;
                module.table_space.push(table);
                ImportDescription::Table(table)
            }
            0x02 => {
                let memory = parse_memory_type(section)?;
                module.memory_space.push(memory);
                ImportDescription::Memory(memory)
            }
            0x03 => {
                let global = parse_global_type(section)?;
                module.global_space.push(global);
                module.imported_global_count += 1;
                ImportDescription::Global(global)
            }
            0x04 => {
                let tag = parse_tag_type(section)?;
                module.tag_space.push(tag);
                ImportDescription::Tag(tag)
            }
            _ => return Err(Error::malformed("malformed import kind")),
        };
        module.imports.push(Import {
            module: module_name,
            name,
            description,
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Skip over the instructions of a constant expression up to and including its `end`. Only the instructions a
/// constant expression may contain are decoded; anything else is left for validation to reject.
pub fn parse_constant_expression(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<ConstantExpression> {
    let start = reader.position() as u32;
    loop {
        let opcode = reader.read_u8()?;
        match opcode {
            opcode::END => break,
            opcode::I32_CONST => {
                reader.read_i32()?;
            }
            opcode::I64_CONST => {
                reader.read_i64()?;
            }
            opcode::F32_CONST => {
                reader.read_bytes(4)?;
            }
            opcode::F64_CONST => {
                reader.read_bytes(8)?;
            }
            opcode::REF_NULL => {
                parse_heap_type(reader)?;
            }
            opcode::REF_FUNC | opcode::GLOBAL_GET => {
                reader.read_u32()?;
            }
            opcode::I32_ADD
            | opcode::I32_SUB
            | opcode::I32_MUL
            | opcode::I64_ADD
            | opcode::I64_SUB
            | opcode::I64_MUL => {}
            opcode::PREFIX_SIMD => {
                let sub_opcode = reader.read_u32()?;
                if sub_opcode != opcode::simd::V128_CONST {
                    return Err(Error::invalid("constant expression required"));
                }
                reader.read_bytes(16)?;
            }
            opcode::PREFIX_GC => {
                let sub_opcode = reader.read_u32()?;
                match sub_opcode {
                    opcode::gc::STRUCT_NEW
                    | opcode::gc::STRUCT_NEW_DEFAULT
                    | opcode::gc::ARRAY_NEW
                    | opcode::gc::ARRAY_NEW_DEFAULT => {
                        reader.read_u32()?;
                    }
                    opcode::gc::ARRAY_NEW_FIXED => {
                        reader.read_u32()?;
                        reader.read_u32()?;
                    }
                    opcode::gc::REF_I31 | opcode::gc::ANY_CONVERT_EXTERN | opcode::gc::EXTERN_CONVERT_ANY => {}
                    _ => return Err(Error::invalid("constant expression required")),
                }
            }
            _ => return Err(Error::invalid("constant expression required")),
        }
    }
    Ok(ConstantExpression {
        code: start..reader.position() as u32,
    })
}

fn parse_function_indices(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<ElementItems> {
    Ok(ElementItems::Functions(reader.read_vector(Reader::read_u32)?))
}

fn parse_element_expressions(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<ElementItems> {
    Ok(ElementItems::Expressions(
        reader.read_vector(parse_constant_expression)?,
    ))
}

/// Segments of function indices hold non-null function references.
const FUNCTION_INDEX_ELEMENT_TYPE: RefType = RefType {
    nullable: false,
    heap: HeapType::Func,
};

fn parse_element_kind(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<RefType> {
    if reader.read_u8()? != 0x00 {
        return Err(Error::malformed("malformed element kind"));
    }
    Ok(FUNCTION_INDEX_ELEMENT_TYPE)
}

fn parse_element(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<Element> {
    let flags = reader.read_u32()?;
    let (ty, mode, items) = match flags {
        0 => {
            let offset = parse_constant_expression(reader)?;
            let items = parse_function_indices(reader)?;
            (
                FUNCTION_INDEX_ELEMENT_TYPE,
                ElementMode::Active { table: 0, offset },
                items,
            )
        }
        1 => {
            let ty = parse_element_kind(reader)?;
            (ty, ElementMode::Passive, parse_function_indices(reader)?)
        }
        2 => {
            let table = reader.read_u32()?;
            let offset = parse_constant_expression(reader)?;
            let ty = parse_element_kind(reader)?;
            (
                ty,
                ElementMode::Active { table, offset },
                parse_function_indices(reader)?,
            )
        }
        3 => {
            let ty = parse_element_kind(reader)?;
            (ty, ElementMode::Declarative, parse_function_indices(reader)?)
        }
        4 => {
            let offset = parse_constant_expression(reader)?;
            let items = parse_element_expressions(reader)?;
            (RefType::FUNCREF, ElementMode::Active { table: 0, offset }, items)
        }
        5 => {
            let ty = parse_reference_type(reader)?;
            (ty, ElementMode::Passive, parse_element_expressions(reader)?)
        }
        6 => {
            let table = reader.read_u32()?;
            let offset = parse_constant_expression(reader)?;
            let ty = parse_reference_type(reader)?;
            (
                ty,
                ElementMode::Active { table, offset },
                parse_element_expressions(reader)?,
            )
        }
        7 => {
            let ty = parse_reference_type(reader)?;
            (ty, ElementMode::Declarative, parse_element_expressions(reader)?)
        }
        _ => return Err(Error::malformed("malformed elements segment kind")),
    };
    Ok(Element { ty, mode, items })
}

fn parse_data(reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<Data> {
    let flags = reader.read_u32()?;
    let mode = match flags {
        0 => DataMode::Active {
            memory: 0,
            offset: parse_constant_expression(reader)?,
        },
        1 => DataMode::Passive,
        2 => {
            let memory = reader.read_u32()?;
            DataMode::Active {
                memory,
                offset: parse_constant_expression(reader)?,
            }
        }
        _ => return Err(Error::malformed("malformed data segment kind")),
    };
    let length = reader.read_u32()?;
    let start = reader.position() as u32;
    reader.read_bytes(length as usize)?;
    Ok(Data {
        mode,
        bytes: start..start + length,
    })
}

fn parse_function_body(section: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<FunctionBody> {
    let size = section.read_u32()?;
    let mut body = section.sub_reader(size as usize)?;
    if size > MAX_FUNCTION_SIZE {
        return Err(Error::invalid("function body too large"));
    }
    let run_count = body.read_u32()?;
    let mut locals = Vec::new();
    let mut declared_local_count = 0u32;
    for _ in 0..run_count {
        let count = body.read_u32()?;
        declared_local_count = declared_local_count
            .checked_add(count)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::malformed("too many locals"))?;
        let ty = parse_value_type(&mut body)?;
        locals.push((count, ty));
    }
    let start = body.position() as u32;
    if body.is_at_end() {
        return Err(Error::malformed("unexpected end of section or function"));
    }
    Ok(FunctionBody {
        locals,
        declared_local_count,
        code: start..body.end() as u32,
    })
}

//! Quickening: the validator rewrites some instructions in the engine's own copy of a module's code into forms that
//! say what validation found out about them, so that the interpreter's handlers for the common forms need no checks.
//! These rules are a contract between the validator and everything that executes code: the interpreter and the JIT.
//!
//! A rewrite never changes the length of an instruction or moves any other one, so branch targets and side-table
//! entries stay valid. Quickened forms use bytes WebAssembly leaves unused:
//!
//! - The prefix 0xFF, followed by a one-byte sub-opcode, for instructions with an immediate byte to spare.
//! - Single-byte opcodes from 0xF4 to 0xFA, for instructions with none (0xF0 to 0xF3 are the runtime's entry and exit
//!   pseudo-instructions), and from 0xE0 to 0xEC for constants.
//!
//! The rules:
//!
//! 1. A core load or store (opcodes 0x28 to 0x3E) whose memory argument is not exactly a one-byte alignment followed by
//!    the offset, for memory 0 as a memory32, becomes an explicitly bounds-checked access. That is every access that
//!    cannot use the guard pages of memory 0, because it accesses another memory or memory 0 is a memory64, and also
//!    every access whose alignment is encoded in more than one byte or that names memory 0 with an explicit memory
//!    index, so that the plain handlers can rely on the layout `op align offset`:
//!
//!    `op align [memory] offset` becomes `0xFF sub [memory] offset 0x01*`, where sub is the original opcode, plus 0x40
//!    if a memory index follows. The memory index and offset keep their original encodings. The alignment, which only
//!    matters to validation, is dropped; if it took more than one byte, `nop` instructions (0x01) fill the bytes it
//!    leaves over, after the access.
//!
//!    A SIMD load or store (0xFD followed by sub-opcode 0x00 to 0x0B or 0x54 to 0x5D) with such a memory argument works
//!    the same way, with its own sub-opcode: 0x80 plus the position of its SIMD sub-opcode in `SIMD_ACCESSES`, plus 0x20 if a
//!    memory index follows. A lane index, if the instruction has one, comes after the offset, and `nop` instructions
//!    fill what the SIMD sub-opcode and alignment leave over.
//!
//! 2. An instruction whose operand or local type is v128, where the plain form assumes a single 8-byte slot, becomes
//!    its v128 form with the same immediates (see `V128_FORMS`).
//!
//! 3. An `i32.const` or `i64.const` whose immediate takes n > 1 bytes becomes a fixed-width form, so that executing it
//!    takes a load instead of a decoding loop: `I32_CONST_FIXED + n - 2` (n up to 5) or `I64_CONST_FIXED + n - 2` (n
//!    up to 10), followed by the value in n little-endian bytes, which hold it since a LEB128 integer of n bytes has
//!    at most 7n bits. The value is sign-extended from those 8n bits, except that an i32 of 5 bytes and an i64 of 9 or
//!    10 bytes keep their value in the first 4 or 8 bytes, followed by zeros. Since a function body ends with `end`,
//!    reading the byte after a 3-byte value stays inside the code.
//!
//! Executing code may assume these rules have been applied: plain loads and stores access memory 0, which is a
//! memory32 with guard pages, their alignment takes one byte and no memory index follows it, and the plain forms of
//! the instructions in rule 2 never see v128 values.

pub const QUICK_PREFIX: u8 = 0xff;

/// The sub-opcode bit that says a memory index follows.
pub const CHECKED_ACCESS_HAS_MEMORY_INDEX: u8 = 0x40;

/// The first sub-opcode of checked SIMD accesses, and the bit that says a memory index follows.
pub const CHECKED_SIMD_ACCESS: u8 = 0x80;
pub const CHECKED_SIMD_ACCESS_HAS_MEMORY_INDEX: u8 = 0x20;

/// The SIMD sub-opcodes of the loads and stores, in the order of their checked sub-opcodes.
pub const SIMD_ACCESSES: [u32; 22] = [
    0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x54, 0x55, 0x56, 0x57, 0x58, 0x59, 0x5a,
    0x5b, 0x5c, 0x5d,
];

/// The fixed-width form of an `i32.const` with a 2-byte immediate; those for 3 to 5 bytes follow (rule 3).
pub const I32_CONST_FIXED: u8 = 0xe0;
/// The fixed-width form of an `i64.const` with a 2-byte immediate; those for 3 to 10 bytes follow (rule 3).
pub const I64_CONST_FIXED: u8 = 0xe4;

/// The rewrite of rule 3 for a constant at `position` whose immediate of `length` bytes has the value `value`, or
/// None if the immediate takes one byte.
pub fn fixed_constant(position: usize, length: usize, value: i64, is_i64: bool) -> Option<Rewrite> {
    if length < 2 {
        return None;
    }
    let opcode = if is_i64 { I64_CONST_FIXED } else { I32_CONST_FIXED } + (length - 2) as u8;
    let mut bytes = vec![opcode];
    let stored = if is_i64 { length.min(8) } else { length.min(4) };
    bytes.extend_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes()[..stored]);
    bytes.resize(1 + length, 0);
    Some(Rewrite {
        position: position as u32,
        bytes,
    })
}

pub const LOCAL_GET_V128: u8 = 0xf4;
pub const LOCAL_SET_V128: u8 = 0xf5;
pub const LOCAL_TEE_V128: u8 = 0xf6;
pub const GLOBAL_GET_V128: u8 = 0xf7;
pub const GLOBAL_SET_V128: u8 = 0xf8;
pub const DROP_V128: u8 = 0xf9;
pub const SELECT_V128: u8 = 0xfa;

/// Each plain opcode with a v128 form, and that form.
pub const V128_FORMS: [(u8, u8); 7] = [
    (crate::opcode::LOCAL_GET, LOCAL_GET_V128),
    (crate::opcode::LOCAL_SET, LOCAL_SET_V128),
    (crate::opcode::LOCAL_TEE, LOCAL_TEE_V128),
    (crate::opcode::GLOBAL_GET, GLOBAL_GET_V128),
    (crate::opcode::GLOBAL_SET, GLOBAL_SET_V128),
    (crate::opcode::DROP, DROP_V128),
    (crate::opcode::SELECT, SELECT_V128),
];

/// The v128 form of a plain opcode.
pub fn v128_form(opcode: u8) -> Option<u8> {
    V128_FORMS
        .iter()
        .find_map(|&(plain, quickened)| (plain == opcode).then_some(quickened))
}

/// Bytes to write over a module's code, starting at `position`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Rewrite {
    pub position: u32,
    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
}

/// The rewrite of rule 1, for the access whose opcode is at `position`, with the alignment, memory index (if any),
/// and offset immediates encoded in the given byte ranges of `code`.
pub fn checked_access(
    code: &[u8],
    position: usize,
    alignment: std::ops::Range<usize>,
    memory: Option<std::ops::Range<usize>>,
    offset: std::ops::Range<usize>,
) -> Rewrite {
    let opcode = code[position];
    let mut bytes = vec![
        QUICK_PREFIX,
        opcode
            | if memory.is_some() {
                CHECKED_ACCESS_HAS_MEMORY_INDEX
            } else {
                0
            },
    ];
    if let Some(memory) = memory {
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&code[memory]);
    }
    bytes.extend_from_slice(&code[offset]);
    bytes.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(crate::opcode::NOP, alignment.len() - 1));
    Rewrite {
        position: position as u32,
        bytes,
    }
}

/// The rewrite of rule 1 for the SIMD access whose prefix is at `position`, its sub-opcode `sub_opcode`, its
/// alignment, memory index, and offset immediates in the given ranges of `code`, and a lane index at `lane` if it has
/// one. `end` is where the instruction ends.
pub fn checked_simd_access(
    code: &[u8],
    position: usize,
    sub_opcode: u32,
    memory: Option<std::ops::Range<usize>>,
    offset: std::ops::Range<usize>,
    end: usize,
) -> Rewrite {
    let index = SIMD_ACCESSES
        .iter()
        .position(|&access| access == sub_opcode)
        .expect("only SIMD accesses are rewritten") as u8;
    let mut bytes = vec![
        QUICK_PREFIX,
        CHECKED_SIMD_ACCESS
            + index
            + if memory.is_some() {
                CHECKED_SIMD_ACCESS_HAS_MEMORY_INDEX
            } else {
                0
            },
    ];
    if let Some(memory) = memory {
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&code[memory]);
    }
    bytes.extend_from_slice(&code[offset.start..end]);
    let length = end - position;
    bytes.resize(length, crate::opcode::NOP);
    Rewrite {
        position: position as u32,
        bytes,
    }
}

/// Apply rewrites to a module's code.
pub fn apply(code: &mut [u8], rewrites: &[Rewrite]) {
    for rewrite in rewrites {
        let start = rewrite.position as usize;
        code[start..start + rewrite.bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(&rewrite.bytes);
    }
}

//! A cursor over the bytes of a binary module.

use crate::error::{Error, Result};

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Reader<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    position: usize,
    end: usize,
}

impl<'a> Reader<'a> {
    pub fn new(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
        Self {
            bytes,
            position: 0,
            end: bytes.len(),
        }
    }

    /// A reader over `bytes[start..end]` that reports positions relative to the start of `bytes`.
    pub fn with_range(bytes: &'a [u8], start: usize, end: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            bytes,
            position: start,
            end,
        }
    }

    pub fn bytes(&self) -> &'a [u8] {
        self.bytes
    }

    pub fn position(&self) -> usize {
        self.position
    }

    pub fn end(&self) -> usize {
        self.end
    }

    pub fn is_at_end(&self) -> bool {
        self.position >= self.end
    }

    pub fn remaining(&self) -> usize {
        self.end - self.position
    }

    /// A reader over the next `length` bytes, which this reader skips.
    pub fn sub_reader(&mut self, length: usize) -> Result<Reader<'a>> {
        if length > self.remaining() {
            return Err(Error::malformed("unexpected end of section or function"));
        }
        let reader = Reader::with_range(self.bytes, self.position, self.position + length);
        self.position += length;
        Ok(reader)
    }

    pub fn read_u8(&mut self) -> Result<u8> {
        if self.position >= self.end {
            return Err(Error::malformed("unexpected end"));
        }
        let byte = self.bytes[self.position];
        self.position += 1;
        Ok(byte)
    }

    pub fn peek_u8(&self) -> Result<u8> {
        if self.position >= self.end {
            return Err(Error::malformed("unexpected end"));
        }
        Ok(self.bytes[self.position])
    }

    pub fn read_bytes(&mut self, length: usize) -> Result<&'a [u8]> {
        if length > self.remaining() {
            return Err(Error::malformed("unexpected end"));
        }
        let bytes = &self.bytes[self.position..self.position + length];
        self.position += length;
        Ok(bytes)
    }

    pub fn read_fixed_u32(&mut self) -> Result<u32> {
        let bytes = self.read_bytes(4)?;
        Ok(u32::from_le_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]]))
    }

    pub fn read_fixed_u64(&mut self) -> Result<u64> {
        let bytes = self.read_bytes(8)?;
        let mut array = [0; 8];
        array.copy_from_slice(bytes);
        Ok(u64::from_le_bytes(array))
    }

    fn read_unsigned_leb(&mut self, bits: u32) -> Result<u64> {
        let mut result = 0u64;
        let mut shift = 0;
        loop {
            let byte = self.read_u8().map_err(|_| Error::malformed("unexpected end"))?;
            let payload = u64::from(byte & 0x7f);
            let remaining_bits = bits - shift;
            if remaining_bits < 7 {
                // The final byte may not set bits beyond the integer's width.
                if byte & 0x80 != 0 || payload >> remaining_bits != 0 {
                    return Err(Error::malformed(if byte & 0x80 != 0 {
                        "integer representation too long"
                    } else {
                        "integer too large"
                    }));
                }
            }
            result |= payload << shift;
            if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
                return Ok(result);
            }
            shift += 7;
        }
    }

    fn read_signed_leb(&mut self, bits: u32) -> Result<i64> {
        let mut result = 0i64;
        let mut shift = 0;
        loop {
            let byte = self.read_u8().map_err(|_| Error::malformed("unexpected end"))?;
            let payload = i64::from(byte & 0x7f);
            let remaining_bits = bits - shift;
            if remaining_bits < 7 {
                // The unused bits of the final byte must all equal its sign bit.
                let sign_and_unused = (byte & 0x7f) >> (remaining_bits - 1);
                let expected = if byte & 0x40 != 0 {
                    0x7f >> (remaining_bits - 1)
                } else {
                    0
                };
                if byte & 0x80 != 0 {
                    return Err(Error::malformed("integer representation too long"));
                }
                if sign_and_unused != expected {
                    return Err(Error::malformed("integer too large"));
                }
            }
            result |= payload << shift;
            shift += 7;
            if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
                if shift < 64 && byte & 0x40 != 0 {
                    result |= -1i64 << shift;
                }
                return Ok(result);
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn read_u32(&mut self) -> Result<u32> {
        Ok(self.read_unsigned_leb(32)? as u32)
    }

    pub fn read_u64(&mut self) -> Result<u64> {
        self.read_unsigned_leb(64)
    }

    pub fn read_i32(&mut self) -> Result<i32> {
        Ok(self.read_signed_leb(32)? as i32)
    }

    pub fn read_i64(&mut self) -> Result<i64> {
        self.read_signed_leb(64)
    }

    pub fn read_s33(&mut self) -> Result<i64> {
        self.read_signed_leb(33)
    }

    pub fn read_name(&mut self) -> Result<&'a str> {
        let length = self.read_u32()? as usize;
        let bytes = self.read_bytes(length)?;
        std::str::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| Error::malformed("malformed UTF-8 encoding"))
    }

    /// The length of a vector, rejected early if it cannot fit in the remaining bytes, given that every element
    /// takes at least one byte.
    pub fn read_vector_length(&mut self) -> Result<u32> {
        let length = self.read_u32()?;
        if length as usize > self.remaining() {
            return Err(Error::malformed("unexpected end of section or function"));
        }
        Ok(length)
    }

    /// A vector of elements, each read by `read_element`. Its storage is reserved up front, and a length whose storage
    /// cannot be allocated is an error rather than an abort.
    pub fn read_vector<T>(&mut self, mut read_element: impl FnMut(&mut Self) -> Result<T>) -> Result<Vec<T>> {
        let length = self.read_vector_length()?;
        let mut elements = Vec::new();
        elements
            .try_reserve_exact(length as usize)
            .map_err(|_| Error::malformed("vector too large"))?;
        for _ in 0..length {
            elements.push(read_element(self)?);
        }
        Ok(elements)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn decodes_leb128() {
        assert_eq!(Reader::new(&[0x7f]).read_u32().unwrap(), 127);
        assert_eq!(Reader::new(&[0x80, 0x01]).read_u32().unwrap(), 128);
        assert_eq!(
            Reader::new(&[0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x0f]).read_u32().unwrap(),
            u32::MAX
        );
        assert!(Reader::new(&[0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x1f]).read_u32().is_err());
        assert!(Reader::new(&[0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x00]).read_u32().is_err());
        assert_eq!(Reader::new(&[0x7f]).read_i32().unwrap(), -1);
        assert_eq!(Reader::new(&[0x80, 0x7f]).read_i32().unwrap(), -128);
        assert_eq!(
            Reader::new(&[0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x07]).read_i32().unwrap(),
            i32::MAX
        );
        assert_eq!(
            Reader::new(&[0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x78]).read_i32().unwrap(),
            i32::MIN
        );
        assert!(Reader::new(&[0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x0f]).read_i32().is_err());
        assert!(Reader::new(&[0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x70]).read_i32().is_err());
        assert_eq!(
            Reader::new(&[0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x7f])
                .read_i64()
                .unwrap(),
            i64::MIN
        );
        assert_eq!(Reader::new(&[0x40]).read_s33().unwrap(), -64);
    }
}

/*

 */

//! The WebAssembly type language, and the canonicalization that decides when two type indices denote the same type.

use std::collections::HashMap;

/// A heap type. `Concrete` names a type by its index in the module's type section.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum HeapType {
    Func,
    NoFunc,
    Extern,
    NoExtern,
    Any,
    Eq,
    I31,
    Struct,
    Array,
    None,
    Exn,
    NoExn,
    Concrete(u32),
    /// The bottom of every hierarchy. Validation only produces it for values popped from an unreachable stack.
    Bottom,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct RefType {
    pub nullable: bool,
    pub heap: HeapType,
}

impl RefType {
    pub const FUNCREF: RefType = RefType {
        nullable: true,
        heap: HeapType::Func,
    };
    pub const EXNREF: RefType = RefType {
        nullable: true,
        heap: HeapType::Exn,
    };

    pub fn new(nullable: bool, heap: HeapType) -> Self {
        Self { nullable, heap }
    }

    pub fn as_non_null(self) -> Self {
        Self {
            nullable: false,
            heap: self.heap,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum ValType {
    I32,
    I64,
    F32,
    F64,
    V128,
    Ref(RefType),
}

impl ValType {
    pub const FUNCREF: ValType = ValType::Ref(RefType::FUNCREF);

    pub fn is_reference(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Ref(_))
    }

    pub fn is_numeric(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::I32 | Self::I64 | Self::F32 | Self::F64)
    }

    /// Whether a local of this type has a default value, so that it can be used before it is set.
    pub fn is_defaultable(self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Ref(reference) => reference.nullable,
            _ => true,
        }
    }

    /// The number of 8-byte slots a value of this type takes on the operand stack.
    pub fn slot_count(self) -> u32 {
        match self {
            Self::V128 => 2,
            _ => 1,
        }
    }

    /// This type with the type index of a concrete heap type replaced by `map` of it.
    pub fn map_type_indices(self, map: &impl Fn(u32) -> u32) -> Self {
        match self {
            Self::Ref(RefType {
                nullable,
                heap: HeapType::Concrete(index),
            }) => Self::Ref(RefType {
                nullable,
                heap: HeapType::Concrete(map(index)),
            }),
            other => other,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum StorageType {
    Val(ValType),
    I8,
    I16,
}

impl StorageType {
    /// The bytes a struct field or array element of this storage type takes in a GC object's data (see
    /// `abi::STORAGE_64`): its natural size, with references taking 8.
    pub fn object_field_size(self) -> u32 {
        match self {
            Self::I8 => 1,
            Self::I16 => 2,
            Self::Val(ValType::I32 | ValType::F32) => 4,
            Self::Val(ValType::V128) => 16,
            Self::Val(_) => 8,
        }
    }

    /// The alignment of a struct field of this storage type in a GC object's data, which is at most 8.
    pub fn object_field_alignment(self) -> u32 {
        self.object_field_size().min(8)
    }

    pub fn is_packed(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::I8 | Self::I16)
    }

    /// The type a field of this storage type has once it is read.
    pub fn unpacked(self) -> ValType {
        match self {
            Self::Val(value) => value,
            Self::I8 | Self::I16 => ValType::I32,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct FieldType {
    pub storage: StorageType,
    pub mutable: bool,
}

/// The byte offsets of the fields of a struct in a GC object's data, and the size of the data rounded up to 8 bytes.
/// Each field is aligned, and takes the first gap the fields before it left that it fits in, or else goes at the end.
/// A field's place depends only on the fields before it, so the fields a subtype shares with its supertype are where
/// they are in the supertype.
pub fn struct_layout(fields: &[FieldType]) -> (Vec<u32>, u32) {
    let mut offsets = Vec::with_capacity(fields.len());
    // The gaps alignment has left so far, as (start, end), in order.
    let mut gaps: Vec<(u32, u32)> = Vec::new();
    let mut end: u32 = 0;
    for field in fields {
        let size = field.storage.object_field_size();
        let alignment = field.storage.object_field_alignment();
        let fitting_gap = gaps.iter().enumerate().find_map(|(index, &(start, gap_end))| {
            let offset = start.next_multiple_of(alignment);
            (offset + size <= gap_end).then_some((index, offset))
        });
        let offset = match fitting_gap {
            Some((index, offset)) => {
                let (start, gap_end) = gaps[index];
                gaps.remove(index);
                if offset + size < gap_end {
                    gaps.insert(index, (offset + size, gap_end));
                }
                if start < offset {
                    gaps.insert(index, (start, offset));
                }
                offset
            }
            None => {
                let offset = end.next_multiple_of(alignment);
                if end < offset {
                    gaps.push((end, offset));
                }
                end = offset + size;
                offset
            }
        };
        offsets.push(offset);
    }
    (offsets, end.next_multiple_of(8))
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
pub struct FuncType {
    pub params: Vec<ValType>,
    pub results: Vec<ValType>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum CompositeType {
    Func(FuncType),
    Struct(Vec<FieldType>),
    Array(FieldType),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct SubType {
    pub is_final: bool,
    pub supertypes: Vec<u32>,
    pub composite: CompositeType,
}

impl SubType {
    /// This type with every type index in it replaced by `map` of it.
    pub fn map_type_indices(&self, map: &impl Fn(u32) -> u32) -> Self {
        let storage = |storage: StorageType| match storage {
            StorageType::Val(value) => StorageType::Val(value.map_type_indices(map)),
            packed => packed,
        };
        let field = |field: &FieldType| FieldType {
            storage: storage(field.storage),
            mutable: field.mutable,
        };
        Self {
            is_final: self.is_final,
            supertypes: self.supertypes.iter().map(|&supertype| map(supertype)).collect(),
            composite: match &self.composite {
                CompositeType::Func(function) => CompositeType::Func(FuncType {
                    params: function
                        .params
                        .iter()
                        .map(|param| param.map_type_indices(map))
                        .collect(),
                    results: function
                        .results
                        .iter()
                        .map(|result| result.map_type_indices(map))
                        .collect(),
                }),
                CompositeType::Struct(fields) => CompositeType::Struct(fields.iter().map(field).collect()),
                CompositeType::Array(element) => CompositeType::Array(field(element)),
            },
        }
    }

    pub fn as_func(&self) -> Option<&FuncType> {
        match &self.composite {
            CompositeType::Func(function) => Some(function),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AddressType {
    I32,
    I64,
}

impl AddressType {
    pub fn value_type(self) -> ValType {
        match self {
            Self::I32 => ValType::I32,
            Self::I64 => ValType::I64,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Limits {
    pub min: u64,
    pub max: Option<u64>,
    pub address_type: AddressType,
    pub shared: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MemoryType {
    pub limits: Limits,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TableType {
    pub element: RefType,
    pub limits: Limits,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct GlobalType {
    pub value: ValType,
    pub mutable: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TagType {
    pub type_index: u32,
}

/// A type index inside a canonicalization key: either relative to the start of the recursion group it appears in,
/// or the canonical identity of a type outside of it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum KeyIndex {
    Recursive(u32),
    Canonical(u32),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum KeyHeap {
    Abstract(HeapType),
    Index(KeyIndex),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum KeyValue {
    Plain(ValType),
    Ref(bool, KeyHeap),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum KeyStorage {
    Value(KeyValue),
    I8,
    I16,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum KeyComposite {
    Func(Vec<KeyValue>, Vec<KeyValue>),
    Struct(Vec<(KeyStorage, bool)>),
    Array(KeyStorage, bool),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
struct KeySubType {
    is_final: bool,
    supertypes: Vec<KeyIndex>,
    composite: KeyComposite,
}

/// Assigns every type a canonical identity, such that two types are equal exactly when their identities are. Types are
/// equal when their recursion groups are structurally identical and they sit at the same position in them, so a whole
/// group is canonicalized at once, with references to types of earlier groups replaced by their identities.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct TypeCanonicalizer {
    groups: HashMap<Vec<KeySubType>, u32>,
    next_identity: u32,
}

impl TypeCanonicalizer {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Canonicalize a recursion group whose first type has index `start`. `identity_of` gives the identities of the
    /// types before `start`. Returns the identity of each type in the group.
    pub fn canonicalize_group(&mut self, group: &[SubType], start: u32, identity_of: impl Fn(u32) -> u32) -> Vec<u32> {
        let index = |type_index: u32| {
            if type_index >= start {
                KeyIndex::Recursive(type_index - start)
            } else {
                KeyIndex::Canonical(identity_of(type_index))
            }
        };
        let value = |value: ValType| match value {
            ValType::Ref(reference) => KeyValue::Ref(
                reference.nullable,
                match reference.heap {
                    HeapType::Concrete(type_index) => KeyHeap::Index(index(type_index)),
                    heap => KeyHeap::Abstract(heap),
                },
            ),
            plain => KeyValue::Plain(plain),
        };
        let storage = |storage: StorageType| match storage {
            StorageType::Val(inner) => KeyStorage::Value(value(inner)),
            StorageType::I8 => KeyStorage::I8,
            StorageType::I16 => KeyStorage::I16,
        };
        let key = group
            .iter()
            .map(|sub_type| KeySubType {
                is_final: sub_type.is_final,
                supertypes: sub_type.supertypes.iter().map(|&supertype| index(supertype)).collect(),
                composite: match &sub_type.composite {
                    CompositeType::Func(function) => KeyComposite::Func(
                        function.params.iter().map(|&param| value(param)).collect(),
                        function.results.iter().map(|&result| value(result)).collect(),
                    ),
                    CompositeType::Struct(fields) => KeyComposite::Struct(
                        fields
                            .iter()
                            .map(|field| (storage(field.storage), field.mutable))
                            .collect(),
                    ),
                    CompositeType::Array(field) => KeyComposite::Array(storage(field.storage), field.mutable),
                },
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let count = group.len() as u32;
        let next_identity = &mut self.next_identity;
        let first = *self.groups.entry(key).or_insert_with(|| {
            let first = *next_identity;
            *next_identity += count;
            first
        });
        (first..first + count).collect()
    }
}

//! Module validation. Function bodies are checked in one pass over their bytes, which also builds the side table the
//! in-place interpreter branches with.
//!
//! # Side tables
//!
//! The interpreter executes a function's original bytes, so it cannot find branch targets in the code itself. Every
//! instruction that may transfer control to somewhere other than the next instruction owns entries of the function's
//! side table, in the order the instructions appear. The interpreter keeps a pointer to the next entry (`stp`) next
//! to the instruction pointer and advances it as it executes those instructions, so a branch finds its entry without
//! a search:
//!
//! - `br`, `br_if`, `br_on_null`, `br_on_non_null`, `br_on_cast`, and `br_on_cast_fail` own one entry, for the taken
//!   branch. Not taking a conditional branch steps over it.
//! - `br_table` owns one entry per label, the default last.
//! - `if` owns one entry, for jumping to its `else` arm, or past its `end` if it has none.
//! - `else` owns one entry, for jumping past the `end` of the `if` when its first arm completes.
//! - The legacy `catch` and `catch_all` own one entry each, for jumping past the `end` of their `try` when the body or
//!   handler before them completes, as `else` does.
//! - The legacy `rethrow` owns one entry, whose `keep` is the index of the local that holds the exception to rethrow.
//!
//! An entry holds the distance from the branching instruction to its target, the distance from the entry itself to
//! the entry the target continues with, and how to reshape the operand stack: keep the `keep` slots at its top and
//! drop the `drop` slots below them. Branches to blocks target the instruction after their `end`; branches to loops
//! target the `loop` instruction, which is where back edges are counted; branches to the function's label target its
//! final `end`, which returns.
//!
//! Exceptions are not linear, so `try_table` handlers live in a separate table of the regions they protect.
//!
//! # Legacy exception handling
//!
//! The body of a legacy `try` is a region whose clauses are its `catch` and `catch_all` handlers, in order. A handler
//! starts after its instruction, with the operand stack at the height of the `try`, and the runtime also stores the
//! exception it caught in a local of its own past the function's declared ones, for `rethrow`. A handler nested in
//! the handlers of `n` other tries gets the `n`th such local. The body of a `try` that ends with `delegate` is a region
//! without clauses that names where the search for a handler goes on: only regions that start at or before its
//! `delegate_bound`, which leaves out those inside the block the `delegate` names.

use crate::error::{Error, Result};
use crate::instruction_tables::{AtomicKind, SimdKind, atomic_kind, simd_kind};
use crate::module::{ConstantExpression, DataMode, ElementItems, ElementMode, ExternalKind, ImportDescription, Module};
use crate::opcode;
use crate::parser::{parse_heap_type, parse_value_type};
use crate::quickening::Rewrite;
use crate::reader::Reader;
use crate::types::{
    AddressType, CompositeType, FieldType, FuncType, HeapType, Limits, RefType, StorageType, SubType,
    TypeCanonicalizer, ValType,
};
use std::collections::HashSet;

/// One side-table entry. See the module documentation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct SideTableEntry {
    /// The target's offset from the branching instruction, in bytes.
    pub pc_delta: i32,
    /// The target's next entry's offset from this entry, in entries.
    pub stp_delta: i32,
    /// The number of slots at the top of the operand stack the branch keeps.
    pub keep: u32,
    /// The number of slots below them the branch drops.
    pub drop: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CatchKind {
    Catch,
    CatchRef,
    CatchAll,
    CatchAllRef,
}

/// One catch clause of a `try_table` or a legacy `try`: which exceptions it catches and where the handler continues.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CatchClause {
    pub kind: CatchKind,
    /// The tag index of `catch` and `catch_ref` clauses.
    pub tag: u32,
    /// The module offset of the instruction the handler continues at.
    pub target_pc: u32,
    /// The index of the side-table entry the handler continues with.
    pub target_stp: u32,
    /// The height of the operand stack, in slots, below the values the handler pushes.
    pub height: u32,
    /// The local a legacy handler keeps the exception in, for `rethrow`, or NO_EXCEPTION_LOCAL.
    pub exception_local: u32,
}

pub const NO_EXCEPTION_LOCAL: u32 = u32::MAX;

/// The instructions of one `try_table` or legacy `try` body, by module offset, and the range of its clauses in the
/// catch table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TryRegion {
    pub start: u32,
    pub end: u32,
    pub first_clause: u32,
    pub clause_count: u32,
    /// For the body of a legacy `try` that ends with `delegate`, the latest start of the regions the search for a
    /// handler goes on with, or NOT_DELEGATED.
    pub delegate_bound: u32,
}

pub const NOT_DELEGATED: u32 = u32::MAX;

/// What validation learned about a defined function that running it needs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct FunctionInfo {
    pub side_table: Box<[SideTableEntry]>,
    /// `try_table` regions in the order their instructions appear, so that inner regions come after outer ones.
    pub try_regions: Box<[TryRegion]>,
    pub catch_clauses: Box<[CatchClause]>,
    /// The number of locals, parameters and the locals of legacy handlers included. The types of the others are in
    /// the function's body.
    pub local_count: u32,
    /// The number of locals legacy handlers keep their exceptions in, which come after the declared ones.
    pub exception_local_count: u32,
    /// The most slots the operand stack ever holds.
    pub max_stack_slots: u32,
}

impl FunctionInfo {
    /// The bytes this function's validation results take beyond the module's own bytes.
    pub fn metadata_size(&self) -> usize {
        size_of::<Self>()
            + self.side_table.len() * size_of::<SideTableEntry>()
            + self.try_regions.len() * size_of::<TryRegion>()
            + self.catch_clauses.len() * size_of::<CatchClause>()
    }
}

/// The largest number of pages a memory may declare.
const MEMORY32_MAX_PAGES: u64 = 1 << 16;
const MEMORY64_MAX_PAGES: u64 = 1 << 48;

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#limits

// The maximum depth of a defined subtype hierarchy is 63 (where a type defined with no supertype has depth 0).
const MAX_SUBTYPING_DEPTH: u32 = 63;

// The maximum number of parameters to any function or block is 1,000.
const MAX_FUNCTION_PARAMS: usize = 1_000;

// The maximum number of return values for any function or block is 1,000.
const MAX_FUNCTION_RESULTS: usize = 1_000;

// The maximum number of locals declared in a function, including implicitly declared as parameters, is 50,000.
const MAX_FUNCTION_LOCALS: usize = 50_000;

// The maximum number of fields in a struct is 10,000.
const MAX_STRUCT_FIELDS: usize = 10_000;

// AD-HOC: A function's operand stack lives in its frame, 8 bytes per slot. Its height is capped so the frame size
//         stays far from wrapping a u32 and validation memory stays bounded. A function that needs more than 8 MiB of
//         operand stack could not be entered on a thread stack anyway.
const MAX_FUNCTION_STACK_SLOTS: u32 = 1 << 20;

fn invalid<T>(message: impl Into<String>) -> Result<T> {
    Err(Error::invalid(message))
}

fn type_mismatch<T>() -> Result<T> {
    invalid("type mismatch")
}

/// The type-level view of a module that validation checks against.
pub struct TypeContext<'a> {
    pub types: &'a [SubType],
    /// The identity of each type, or none where the types are identities themselves, as in a store.
    pub identities: Option<&'a [u32]>,
}

impl TypeContext<'_> {
    fn sub_type(&self, index: u32) -> &SubType {
        &self.types[index as usize]
    }

    fn is_func(&self, index: u32) -> bool {
        matches!(self.sub_type(index).composite, CompositeType::Func(_))
    }

    fn top(&self, heap: HeapType) -> HeapType {
        match heap {
            HeapType::Func | HeapType::NoFunc => HeapType::Func,
            HeapType::Extern | HeapType::NoExtern => HeapType::Extern,
            HeapType::Exn | HeapType::NoExn => HeapType::Exn,
            HeapType::Any | HeapType::Eq | HeapType::I31 | HeapType::Struct | HeapType::Array | HeapType::None => {
                HeapType::Any
            }
            HeapType::Concrete(index) => match self.sub_type(index).composite {
                CompositeType::Func(_) => HeapType::Func,
                _ => HeapType::Any,
            },
            HeapType::Bottom => HeapType::Bottom,
        }
    }

    pub fn heap_subtype(&self, sub: HeapType, sup: HeapType) -> bool {
        use HeapType::*;
        if sub == sup || sub == Bottom {
            return true;
        }
        match (sub, sup) {
            (Concrete(a), Concrete(b)) => {
                if self
                    .identities
                    .is_some_and(|identities| identities[a as usize] == identities[b as usize])
                {
                    return true;
                }
                self.sub_type(a)
                    .supertypes
                    .iter()
                    .any(|&supertype| self.heap_subtype(Concrete(supertype), sup))
            }
            (Concrete(a), _) => match self.sub_type(a).composite {
                CompositeType::Func(_) => sup == Func,
                CompositeType::Struct(_) => matches!(sup, Struct | Eq | Any),
                CompositeType::Array(_) => matches!(sup, Array | Eq | Any),
            },
            (None, Concrete(b)) => !self.is_func(b),
            (NoFunc, Concrete(b)) => self.is_func(b),
            (_, Concrete(_)) => false,
            (None, Any | Eq | I31 | Struct | Array) => true,
            (I31 | Struct | Array, Eq | Any) => true,
            (Eq, Any) => true,
            (NoFunc, Func) | (NoExtern, Extern) | (NoExn, Exn) => true,
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    pub fn ref_subtype(&self, sub: RefType, sup: RefType) -> bool {
        (!sub.nullable || sup.nullable) && self.heap_subtype(sub.heap, sup.heap)
    }

    pub fn value_subtype(&self, sub: ValType, sup: ValType) -> bool {
        match (sub, sup) {
            (ValType::Ref(sub), ValType::Ref(sup)) => self.ref_subtype(sub, sup),
            _ => sub == sup,
        }
    }

    fn storage_subtype(&self, sub: StorageType, sup: StorageType) -> bool {
        match (sub, sup) {
            (StorageType::Val(sub), StorageType::Val(sup)) => self.value_subtype(sub, sup),
            _ => sub == sup,
        }
    }

    fn field_subtype(&self, sub: FieldType, sup: FieldType) -> bool {
        if sub.mutable != sup.mutable {
            return false;
        }
        if sub.mutable {
            self.storage_subtype(sub.storage, sup.storage) && self.storage_subtype(sup.storage, sub.storage)
        } else {
            self.storage_subtype(sub.storage, sup.storage)
        }
    }

    fn values_subtype(&self, sub: &[ValType], sup: &[ValType]) -> bool {
        sub.len() == sup.len() && sub.iter().zip(sup).all(|(&sub, &sup)| self.value_subtype(sub, sup))
    }

    fn function_subtype(&self, sub: &FuncType, sup: &FuncType) -> bool {
        self.values_subtype(&sup.params, &sub.params) && self.values_subtype(&sub.results, &sup.results)
    }

    fn composite_subtype(&self, sub: &CompositeType, sup: &CompositeType) -> bool {
        match (sub, sup) {
            (CompositeType::Func(sub), CompositeType::Func(sup)) => self.function_subtype(sub, sup),
            (CompositeType::Struct(sub), CompositeType::Struct(sup)) => {
                sub.len() >= sup.len() && sub.iter().zip(sup).all(|(&sub, &sup)| self.field_subtype(sub, sup))
            }
            (CompositeType::Array(sub), CompositeType::Array(sup)) => self.field_subtype(*sub, *sup),
            _ => false,
        }
    }
}

/// An operand stack entry. `None` is a value of unknown type, which only unreachable code produces.
type Operand = Option<ValType>;

fn operand_slots(operand: Operand) -> u32 {
    operand.map_or(1, ValType::slot_count)
}

fn slots_of(types: &[ValType]) -> u32 {
    types.iter().map(|ty| ty.slot_count()).sum()
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum FrameKind {
    Block,
    Loop,
    If,
    Else,
    TryTable,
    /// The body of a legacy `try`.
    Try,
    /// A legacy `catch` handler.
    Catch,
    /// A legacy `catch_all` handler.
    CatchAll,
    Function,
}

/// A side-table entry or catch clause whose target is the end of a frame that has not been reached yet.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
enum Fixup {
    Entry { entry: usize, branch_pc: u32 },
    Clause(usize),
}

struct Frame {
    kind: FrameKind,
    params: Vec<ValType>,
    results: Vec<ValType>,
    height: usize,
    slot_height: u32,
    unreachable: bool,
    initialization_height: usize,
    /// The module offset of the frame's first instruction: the `loop` instruction of a loop, which back edges target.
    start_pc: u32,
    /// The side-table index a branch to a loop continues with.
    start_stp: u32,
    fixups: Vec<Fixup>,
    /// The entry of an `if` that jumps to its `else` arm.
    if_entry: Option<(usize, u32)>,
    /// The index of the `try_table` region this frame protects.
    try_region: Option<usize>,
    /// The index of the region of a legacy `try`'s body, for the try and its handlers.
    legacy_region: Option<usize>,
    /// The clauses of a legacy `try`'s handlers so far, which go into the catch table together at its `end`.
    legacy_clauses: Vec<CatchClause>,
    /// The local in which a legacy handler keeps its exception.
    exception_local: Option<u32>,
    /// How many legacy handlers this frame is in, itself included: the position among the exception locals, which
    /// come after the declared locals, of the one a handler directly inside it takes. Kept per frame so that a handler
    /// need not count them in every frame around it, which made deeply nested handlers take quadratic time.
    catch_depth: u32,
}

impl Frame {
    fn label_types(&self) -> &[ValType] {
        if self.kind == FrameKind::Loop {
            &self.params
        } else {
            &self.results
        }
    }
}

struct FunctionValidator<'a> {
    module: &'a Module,
    types: TypeContext<'a>,
    declared_functions: &'a HashSet<u32>,
    locals: Vec<ValType>,
    local_initialized: Vec<bool>,
    initialization_log: Vec<u32>,
    operands: Vec<Operand>,
    slot_height: u32,
    max_slot_height: u32,
    frames: Vec<Frame>,
    side_table: Vec<SideTableEntry>,
    try_regions: Vec<TryRegion>,
    catch_clauses: Vec<CatchClause>,
    exception_local_count: u32,
    results: Vec<ValType>,
    /// Where the instruction being validated starts.
    instruction_start: u32,
    /// The quickened forms of this function's instructions (see quickening.rs).
    rewrites: Vec<Rewrite>,
    /// The memory index and offset immediates of the last memory argument read, if its access needs bounds checks.
    checked_access: Option<(Option<std::ops::Range<usize>>, std::ops::Range<usize>)>,
}

impl FunctionValidator<'_> {
    /// Quicken the instruction being validated into its v128 form if its value is a v128.
    fn quicken_for_v128(&mut self, value: Operand) {
        if value != Some(ValType::V128) {
            return;
        }
        let opcode = self.module.bytes[self.instruction_start as usize];
        let quickened = crate::quickening::v128_form(opcode).expect("only instructions with a v128 form get here");
        self.rewrites.push(Rewrite {
            position: self.instruction_start,
            bytes: vec![quickened],
        });
    }

    fn push(&mut self, operand: Operand) {
        self.slot_height += operand_slots(operand);
        self.max_slot_height = self.max_slot_height.max(self.slot_height);
        self.operands.push(operand);
    }

    fn push_value(&mut self, value: ValType) {
        self.push(Some(value));
    }

    fn push_values(&mut self, values: &[ValType]) {
        for &value in values {
            self.push_value(value);
        }
    }

    fn pop(&mut self) -> Result<Operand> {
        let frame = self.frames.last().expect("validation always has a frame");
        if self.operands.len() == frame.height {
            if frame.unreachable {
                return Ok(None);
            }
            return type_mismatch();
        }
        let operand = self.operands.pop().expect("the stack is above the frame's height");
        self.slot_height -= operand_slots(operand);
        Ok(operand)
    }

    fn pop_expecting(&mut self, expected: ValType) -> Result<Operand> {
        let actual = self.pop()?;
        if let Some(actual) = actual
            && !self.types.value_subtype(actual, expected)
        {
            return type_mismatch();
        }
        Ok(actual.or(Some(expected)))
    }

    fn pop_values(&mut self, values: &[ValType]) -> Result<()> {
        for &value in values.iter().rev() {
            self.pop_expecting(value)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Pop a reference of any type, and return it unless it is of unknown type.
    fn pop_reference(&mut self) -> Result<Option<RefType>> {
        match self.pop()? {
            None => Ok(None),
            Some(ValType::Ref(reference)) => Ok(Some(reference)),
            Some(_) => type_mismatch(),
        }
    }

    fn set_unreachable(&mut self) {
        let frame = self.frames.last_mut().expect("validation always has a frame");
        let height = frame.height;
        frame.unreachable = true;
        while self.operands.len() > height {
            let operand = self.operands.pop().expect("the stack is above the frame's height");
            self.slot_height -= operand_slots(operand);
        }
    }

    fn push_frame(&mut self, kind: FrameKind, params: Vec<ValType>, results: Vec<ValType>, start_pc: u32) {
        let height = self.operands.len();
        let slot_height = self.slot_height;
        let catch_depth = self.frames.last().map_or(0, |frame| frame.catch_depth)
            + u32::from(matches!(kind, FrameKind::Catch | FrameKind::CatchAll));
        self.frames.push(Frame {
            kind,
            params: params.clone(),
            results,
            height,
            slot_height,
            unreachable: false,
            initialization_height: self.initialization_log.len(),
            start_pc,
            start_stp: self.side_table.len() as u32,
            fixups: Vec::new(),
            if_entry: None,
            try_region: None,
            legacy_region: None,
            legacy_clauses: Vec::new(),
            exception_local: None,
            catch_depth,
        });
        self.push_values(&params);
    }

    fn pop_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Frame> {
        let frame = self.frames.last().expect("validation always has a frame");
        let results = frame.results.clone();
        self.pop_values(&results)?;
        let frame = self.frames.last().expect("validation always has a frame");
        if self.operands.len() != frame.height {
            return type_mismatch();
        }
        let frame = self.frames.pop().expect("validation always has a frame");
        for local in self.initialization_log.drain(frame.initialization_height..) {
            self.local_initialized[local as usize] = false;
        }
        Ok(frame)
    }

    fn label(&self, depth: u32) -> Result<&Frame> {
        let count = self.frames.len();
        if depth as usize >= count {
            return invalid("unknown label");
        }
        Ok(&self.frames[count - 1 - depth as usize])
    }

    fn label_types(&self, depth: u32) -> Result<Vec<ValType>> {
        Ok(self.label(depth)?.label_types().to_vec())
    }

    /// Add the side-table entry of a branch at `branch_pc` to the label at `depth`, taken with the current operand
    /// stack.
    fn add_branch_entry(&mut self, depth: u32, branch_pc: u32) {
        let entry_index = self.side_table.len();
        let frame_index = self.frames.len() - 1 - depth as usize;
        let frame = &self.frames[frame_index];
        let keep = slots_of(frame.label_types());
        let drop = self.slot_height.saturating_sub(frame.slot_height + keep);
        let reachable = !self.frames.last().expect("validation always has a frame").unreachable;
        let mut entry = SideTableEntry {
            pc_delta: 0,
            stp_delta: 0,
            keep,
            drop: if reachable { drop } else { 0 },
        };
        if frame.kind == FrameKind::Loop {
            entry.pc_delta = frame.start_pc as i32 - branch_pc as i32;
            entry.stp_delta = frame.start_stp as i32 - entry_index as i32;
        } else {
            self.frames[frame_index].fixups.push(Fixup::Entry {
                entry: entry_index,
                branch_pc,
            });
        }
        self.side_table.push(entry);
    }

    /// Point the pending branches of a frame at `target_pc`, continuing with the next side-table entry.
    fn resolve_fixups(&mut self, fixups: &[Fixup], target_pc: u32) {
        let target_stp = self.side_table.len();
        for fixup in fixups {
            match *fixup {
                Fixup::Entry { entry, branch_pc } => {
                    self.side_table[entry].pc_delta = target_pc as i32 - branch_pc as i32;
                    self.side_table[entry].stp_delta = target_stp as i32 - entry as i32;
                }
                Fixup::Clause(clause) => {
                    self.catch_clauses[clause].target_pc = target_pc;
                    self.catch_clauses[clause].target_stp = target_stp as u32;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn local(&self, index: u32) -> Result<ValType> {
        self.locals
            .get(index as usize)
            .copied()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::invalid("unknown local"))
    }

    fn initialize_local(&mut self, index: u32) {
        if !self.local_initialized[index as usize] {
            self.local_initialized[index as usize] = true;
            self.initialization_log.push(index);
        }
    }

    fn global(&self, index: u32) -> Result<crate::types::GlobalType> {
        self.module
            .global_space
            .get(index as usize)
            .copied()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::invalid("unknown global"))
    }

    fn table(&self, index: u32) -> Result<crate::types::TableType> {
        self.module
            .table_space
            .get(index as usize)
            .copied()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::invalid("unknown table"))
    }

    fn memory_address_type(&self, index: u32) -> Result<AddressType> {
        self.module
            .memory_space
            .get(index as usize)
            .map(|memory| memory.limits.address_type)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::invalid("unknown memory"))
    }

    fn function_type(&self, index: u32) -> Result<FuncType> {
        let type_index = *self
            .module
            .function_space
            .get(index as usize)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::invalid("unknown function"))?;
        Ok(self.module.types[type_index as usize]
            .as_func()
            .expect("function types are checked first")
            .clone())
    }

    fn func_type_at(&self, type_index: u32) -> Result<FuncType> {
        match self.module.types.get(type_index as usize) {
            None => invalid("unknown type"),
            Some(sub_type) => sub_type
                .as_func()
                .cloned()
                .ok_or_else(|| Error::invalid("type mismatch")),
        }
    }

    fn struct_type(&self, type_index: u32) -> Result<Vec<FieldType>> {
        match self
            .module
            .types
            .get(type_index as usize)
            .map(|sub_type| &sub_type.composite)
        {
            None => invalid("unknown type"),
            Some(CompositeType::Struct(fields)) => Ok(fields.clone()),
            Some(_) => type_mismatch(),
        }
    }

    fn array_type(&self, type_index: u32) -> Result<FieldType> {
        match self
            .module
            .types
            .get(type_index as usize)
            .map(|sub_type| &sub_type.composite)
        {
            None => invalid("unknown type"),
            Some(CompositeType::Array(field)) => Ok(*field),
            Some(_) => type_mismatch(),
        }
    }

    fn tag_params(&self, index: u32) -> Result<Vec<ValType>> {
        let tag = self
            .module
            .tag_space
            .get(index as usize)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::invalid("unknown tag"))?;
        Ok(self.func_type_at(tag.type_index)?.params)
    }

    fn check_data_index(&self, index: u32) -> Result<()> {
        let Some(count) = self.module.data_count else {
            return invalid("data count section required");
        };
        if index >= count {
            return invalid("unknown data segment");
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn element_type(&self, index: u32) -> Result<RefType> {
        self.module
            .elements
            .get(index as usize)
            .map(|element| element.ty)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::invalid("unknown elem segment"))
    }

    fn check_heap_type(&self, heap: HeapType) -> Result<()> {
        check_heap_type(self.module, heap)
    }

    fn check_value_type(&self, value: ValType) -> Result<()> {
        check_value_type(self.module, value)
    }

    fn read_block_type(&self, reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<(Vec<ValType>, Vec<ValType>)> {
        match reader.peek_u8()? {
            0x40 => {
                reader.read_u8()?;
                Ok((Vec::new(), Vec::new()))
            }
            0x7f | 0x7e | 0x7d | 0x7c | 0x7b | 0x63 | 0x64 | 0x70 | 0x6f | 0x6e | 0x6d | 0x6c | 0x6b | 0x6a | 0x69
            | 0x71 | 0x72 | 0x73 | 0x74 => {
                let value = parse_value_type(reader)?;
                self.check_value_type(value)?;
                Ok((Vec::new(), vec![value]))
            }
            _ => {
                let index = reader.read_s33()?;
                if index < 0 {
                    return Err(Error::malformed("malformed block type"));
                }
                let function = self.func_type_at(u32::try_from(index).map_err(|_| Error::invalid("unknown type"))?)?;
                Ok((function.params, function.results))
            }
        }
    }

    fn read_memory_argument(&mut self, reader: &mut Reader<'_>, natural_size: u32) -> Result<AddressType> {
        let alignment_start = reader.position();
        let mut align = reader.read_u32()?;
        let alignment_end = reader.position();
        let mut memory = 0;
        let mut memory_bytes = None;
        if align & 0x40 != 0 {
            align &= !0x40;
            let start = reader.position();
            memory = reader.read_u32()?;
            memory_bytes = Some(start..reader.position());
        }
        let address_type = self.memory_address_type(memory)?;
        let offset_start = reader.position();
        let offset = reader.read_u64()?;
        let opcode = self.module.bytes[self.instruction_start as usize];
        let is_core_access = (crate::opcode::I32_LOAD..=crate::opcode::I64_STORE32).contains(&opcode);
        self.checked_access = None;
        // The plain handlers only decode `align offset` with a one-byte alignment, for memory 0 as a memory32 (see
        // rule 1 in quickening.rs). Every other encoding, even of the same access, becomes a checked access.
        let is_plain =
            memory_bytes.is_none() && alignment_end - alignment_start == 1 && address_type == AddressType::I32;
        if !is_plain {
            if is_core_access {
                self.rewrites.push(crate::quickening::checked_access(
                    &self.module.bytes,
                    self.instruction_start as usize,
                    alignment_start..alignment_end,
                    memory_bytes,
                    offset_start..reader.position(),
                ));
            } else {
                self.checked_access = Some((memory_bytes, offset_start..reader.position()));
            }
        }
