void Value::visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor) const
{
    // NB: LibGC's C interface passes its Cell::Visitor as the visitor.
    FFI::wasm_visitor_visit_value(&visitor, bit_cast<FFI::WasmValue>(*this));
}

static FFI::WasmValueType to_ffi(ValueType type) { return bit_cast<FFI::WasmValueType>(type); }
static FFI::WasmValue to_ffi(Value value) { return bit_cast<FFI::WasmValue>(value); }
static FFI::WasmLimits to_ffi(Limits limits) { return bit_cast<FFI::WasmLimits>(limits); }
static ValueType from_ffi(FFI::WasmValueType type) { return bit_cast<ValueType>(type); }
static Value from_ffi(FFI::WasmValue value) { return bit_cast<Value>(value); }
static ExternType from_ffi(FFI::WasmExternType type) { return bit_cast<ExternType>(type); }
static StringView from_ffi(FFI::WasmStringView view) { return { reinterpret_cast<char const*>(view.data), view.length }; }

static ByteString take_string(FFI::WasmString string)
{
    if (!string.data)
        return {};
    ByteString result { reinterpret_cast<char const*>(string.data), string.length };
    FFI::wasm_string_release(string);
    return result;
}

static FFI::WasmString make_string(StringView text)
{
    // The engine releases the strings it gets back, so they are allocated the way it allocates its own: as a boxed
    // byte slice, which only the engine can create.
    FFI::WasmString string {};
    FFI::wasm_string_create(reinterpret_cast<u8 const*>(text.characters_without_null_termination()), text.length(), &string);
    return string;
}

ErrorOr<NonnullRefPtr<Module>, ByteString> Module::compile(ReadonlyBytes bytes)
{
    FFI::WasmString error {};
    auto const* module = FFI::wasm_module_compile(bytes.data(), bytes.size(), &error);
    if (!module)
        return take_string(error);
    return adopt_ref(*new Module(module));
}

Module::~Module()
{
    FFI::wasm_module_release(m_module);
}

size_t Module::import_count() const
{
    return FFI::wasm_module_import_count(m_module);
}

Import Module::import(size_t index) const
{
    FFI::WasmStringView module_name {};
    FFI::WasmStringView name {};
    FFI::WasmExternType type {};
    FFI::wasm_module_import(m_module, index, &module_name, &name, &type);
    return { from_ffi(module_name), from_ffi(name), from_ffi(type) };
}

static FunctionType make_function_type(size_t parameter_count, size_t result_count, auto copy)
{
    Vector<FFI::WasmValueType> parameters;
    Vector<FFI::WasmValueType> results;
    parameters.resize(parameter_count);
    results.resize(result_count);
    copy(parameters.data(), results.data());
    FunctionType type;
    type.parameters.ensure_capacity(parameter_count);
    type.results.ensure_capacity(result_count);
    for (auto parameter : parameters)
        type.parameters.unchecked_append(from_ffi(parameter));
    for (auto result : results)
        type.results.unchecked_append(from_ffi(result));
    return type;
}

Optional<FunctionType> Module::function_type(u32 type_index) const
{
    size_t parameter_count = 0;
    size_t result_count = 0;
    if (!FFI::wasm_module_function_type(m_module, type_index, &parameter_count, &result_count))
        return {};
    return make_function_type(parameter_count, result_count, [&](auto* parameters, auto* results) {
        FFI::wasm_module_function_type_values(m_module, type_index, parameters, results);
    });
}

template<typename To, typename From>
static To function_cast(From function)
{
    return reinterpret_cast<To>(function);
}

static FFI::GcInterface gc_interface(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    using Interface = FFI::GcInterface;
    return {
        .heap = &heap,
        .gc_get_layout = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_get_layout)>(gc_get_layout),
        .gc_allocator_create = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_allocator_create)>(gc_allocator_create),
        .gc_allocator_set_traced_on_owner_thread_only = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_allocator_set_traced_on_owner_thread_only)>(gc_allocator_set_traced_on_owner_thread_only),
        .gc_heap_allocate_cell = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_heap_allocate_cell)>(gc_heap_allocate_cell),
        .gc_heap_defer_gc = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_heap_defer_gc)>(gc_heap_defer_gc),
        .gc_heap_undefer_gc = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_heap_undefer_gc)>(gc_heap_undefer_gc),
        .gc_heap_collect_garbage = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_heap_collect_garbage)>(gc_heap_collect_garbage),
        .gc_heap_did_allocate_external_memory = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_heap_did_allocate_external_memory)>(gc_heap_did_allocate_external_memory),
        .gc_root_create = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_root_create)>(gc_root_create),
        .gc_root_destroy = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_root_destroy)>(gc_root_destroy),
        .gc_visitor_visit_cell = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_visitor_visit_cell)>(gc_visitor_visit_cell),
        .gc_primitive_storage_reserve = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_primitive_storage_reserve)>(gc_primitive_storage_reserve),
        .gc_primitive_storage_resize = function_cast<decltype(Interface::gc_primitive_storage_resize)>(gc_primitive_storage_resize),
        .gc_primitive_storage_free = gc_primitive_storage_free,
        .gc_primitive_storage_data = gc_primitive_storage_data,
    };
}

Store::Store(GC::Heap& heap)
{
    auto interface = gc_interface(heap);
    m_store = FFI::wasm_store_create(&interface);
}

Store::~Store()
{
    FFI::wasm_store_destroy(m_store);
}

static void* to_ffi(Entity entity) { return entity; }
static Entity entity_from_ffi(void* cell) { return static_cast<GC::ForeignCell*>(cell); }

namespace {

struct HostFunctionData {
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

    Store& store;
    GC::Ref<Store::HostFunction> function;
};

}

static FFI::WasmStatus call_host_function(void* user_data, FFI::WasmStore*, FFI::WasmValue const* arguments, size_t argument_count, FFI::WasmValue* results, size_t result_count, FFI::WasmString* error, u64*)
{
    auto& data = *static_cast<HostFunctionData*>(user_data);
    ReadonlySpan<Value> argument_span { reinterpret_cast<Value const*>(arguments), argument_count };
    Span<Value> result_span { reinterpret_cast<Value*>(results), result_count };
    auto result = (*data.function)(data.store, argument_span, result_span);
    if (!result.is_error())
        return FFI::WasmStatus::Ok;
    *error = make_string(result.error().message);
    return FFI::WasmStatus::Trap;
}

static void visit_host_function(void* user_data, void* visitor)
{
    // NB: LibGC's C interface passes its Cell::Visitor as the visitor.
    auto& data = *static_cast<HostFunctionData*>(user_data);
    static_cast<GC::Cell::Visitor*>(visitor)->visit(data.function);
}

static void release_host_function(void* user_data)
{
    delete static_cast<HostFunctionData*>(user_data);
}

Entity Store::allocate_host_function(FunctionType const& type, GC::Ref<HostFunction> function)
{
    Vector<FFI::WasmValueType> parameters;
    Vector<FFI::WasmValueType> results;
    for (auto parameter : type.parameters)
        parameters.append(to_ffi(parameter));
    for (auto result : type.results)
        results.append(to_ffi(result));
    auto* data = new HostFunctionData { *this, function };
    // NB: Allocating the function's cell can collect garbage, and only the cell visits the GC::Function once it exists.
    auto function_root = GC::make_root(function);
    return entity_from_ffi(FFI::wasm_store_allocate_host_function(m_store, parameters.data(), parameters.size(), results.data(), results.size(), call_host_function, visit_host_function, release_host_function, data));
}

Optional<Entity> Store::allocate_memory(Limits limits)
{
    void* memory = nullptr;
    if (!FFI::wasm_store_allocate_memory(m_store, to_ffi(limits), &memory))
        return {};
    return entity_from_ffi(memory);
}

Optional<Entity> Store::allocate_table(ValueType element, Limits limits, u64 initial)
{
    void* table = nullptr;
    if (!FFI::wasm_store_allocate_table(m_store, to_ffi(element), to_ffi(limits), initial, &table))
        return {};
    return entity_from_ffi(table);
}

Entity Store::allocate_global(ValueType type, bool is_mutable, Value value)
{
    return entity_from_ffi(FFI::wasm_store_allocate_global(m_store, to_ffi(type), is_mutable, to_ffi(value)));
}

static Failure failure_of(FFI::WasmStatus status, FFI::WasmString error, u64 exception)
{
    switch (status) {
    case FFI::WasmStatus::LinkError:
        return { FailureKind::LinkError, take_string(error) };
    case FFI::WasmStatus::Trap:
        return { FailureKind::Trap, take_string(error) };
    case FFI::WasmStatus::Exception:
        return { FailureKind::Exception, take_string(error), exception };
    case FFI::WasmStatus::StackExhausted:
        return { FailureKind::StackExhausted, take_string(error) };
    case FFI::WasmStatus::Ok:
        break;
    }
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

ErrorOr<Entity, Failure> Store::instantiate(Module const& module, ReadonlySpan<Extern> imports)
{
    static_assert(sizeof(Extern) == sizeof(FFI::WasmExtern));
    void* instance = nullptr;
    FFI::WasmString error {};
    u64 exception = 0;
    auto status = FFI::wasm_store_instantiate(m_store, module.handle(), reinterpret_cast<FFI::WasmExtern const*>(imports.data()), imports.size(), &instance, &error, &exception);
    if (status == FFI::WasmStatus::Ok)
        return entity_from_ffi(instance);
    return failure_of(status, error, exception);
}

Vector<InstanceExport> Store::instance_exports(Entity instance)
{
    auto count = FFI::wasm_store_instance_export_count(m_store, to_ffi(instance));
    Vector<InstanceExport> exports;
    exports.ensure_capacity(count);
    for (size_t index = 0; index < count; ++index) {
        FFI::WasmStringView name {};
        FFI::WasmExtern value {};
        if (!FFI::wasm_store_instance_export(m_store, to_ffi(instance), index, &name, &value))
            continue;
        exports.unchecked_append({ from_ffi(name), bit_cast<Extern>(value) });
    }
    return exports;
}

Optional<Extern> Store::find_export(Entity instance, StringView name)
{
    FFI::WasmExtern value {};
    if (!FFI::wasm_store_instance_find_export(m_store, to_ffi(instance), reinterpret_cast<u8 const*>(name.characters_without_null_termination()), name.length(), &value))
        return {};
    return bit_cast<Extern>(value);
}

FunctionType Store::function_type(Entity function)
{
    size_t parameter_count = 0;
    size_t result_count = 0;
    FFI::wasm_store_function_type(m_store, to_ffi(function), &parameter_count, &result_count);
    return make_function_type(parameter_count, result_count, [&](auto* parameters, auto* results) {
        FFI::wasm_store_function_type_values(m_store, to_ffi(function), parameters, results);
    });
}

ErrorOr<Values, Failure> Store::invoke(Entity function, ReadonlySpan<Value> arguments)
{
    size_t parameter_count = 0;
    size_t result_count = 0;
    FFI::wasm_store_function_type(m_store, to_ffi(function), &parameter_count, &result_count);
    Values results;
    results.resize(result_count);
    FFI::WasmString error {};
    u64 exception = 0;
    auto status = FFI::wasm_store_invoke(m_store, to_ffi(function), reinterpret_cast<FFI::WasmValue const*>(arguments.data()), arguments.size(), reinterpret_cast<FFI::WasmValue*>(results.data()), results.size(), &error, &exception);
    if (status != FFI::WasmStatus::Ok)
        return failure_of(status, error, exception);
    return results;
}

Value Store::function_reference(Entity function)
{
    return { ValueKind::Reference, ValueTrace::FunctionReference, FFI::wasm_store_function_reference(m_store, to_ffi(function)), 0 };
}

Entity Store::function_from_reference(u64 reference)
{
    void* function = nullptr;
    VERIFY(FFI::wasm_store_function_from_reference(m_store, reference, &function));
    return entity_from_ffi(function);
}

ValueType Store::global_type(Entity global, bool& is_mutable)
{
    return from_ffi(FFI::wasm_store_global_type(m_store, to_ffi(global), &is_mutable));
}

Value Store::global_get(Entity global)
{
    return from_ffi(FFI::wasm_store_global_get(m_store, to_ffi(global)));
}

static Vector<FFI::WasmStringView> string_views(ReadonlySpan<ByteString> strings)
{
    Vector<FFI::WasmStringView> views;
    views.ensure_capacity(strings.size());
    for (auto const& string : strings)
        views.unchecked_append({ reinterpret_cast<u8 const*>(string.characters()), string.length() });
    return views;
}

Wasi::Wasi(ReadonlySpan<ByteString> arguments, ReadonlySpan<ByteString> environment, ReadonlySpan<Preopen> preopens)
{
    Vector<ByteString> host_paths;
    Vector<ByteString> guest_paths;
    for (auto const& preopen : preopens) {
        host_paths.append(preopen.host_path);
        guest_paths.append(preopen.guest_path);
    }
    auto argument_views = string_views(arguments);
    auto environment_views = string_views(environment);
    auto host_views = string_views(host_paths);
    auto guest_views = string_views(guest_paths);
    m_wasi = FFI::wasm_wasi_create(argument_views.data(), argument_views.size(), environment_views.data(), environment_views.size(), host_views.data(), guest_views.data(), preopens.size());
}

Wasi::~Wasi()
{
    FFI::wasm_wasi_destroy(m_wasi);
}

Optional<Entity> Wasi::allocate_function(Store& store, StringView name)
{
    void* function = nullptr;
    if (!FFI::wasm_wasi_allocate_function(store.handle(), m_wasi, reinterpret_cast<u8 const*>(name.characters_without_null_termination()), name.length(), &function))
        return {};
    return entity_from_ffi(function);
}

void Wasi::set_memory(Entity memory)
{
    FFI::wasm_wasi_set_memory(m_wasi, to_ffi(memory));
}

Optional<i32> Wasi::exit_code() const
{
    i32 code = 0;
    if (!FFI::wasm_wasi_exit_code(m_wasi, &code))
        return {};
    return code;
}

}

#pragma once

#include <AK/BitCast.h>

// The C++ interface of the WebAssembly engine, which is written in Rust (Libraries/LibWasm/Engine). These types mirror
// the ones of its C ABI (Libraries/LibWasm/Engine/src/capi.rs) exactly.
namespace Wasm::Runtime {

enum class ValueKind : u8 {
    I32,
    I64,
    F32,
    F64,
    V128,
    Reference,
};

enum class HeapKind : u8 {
    Function,
    NoFunction,
    Extern,
    NoExtern,
    Any,
    Eq,
    I31,
    Struct,
    Array,
    None,
    Exception,
    NoException,
    Concrete,
};

// A value type. `heap`, `nullable`, and `type_index` only matter for references; `type_index` indexes the types of
// the module the type comes from.
struct ValueType {
    ValueKind kind { ValueKind::I32 };
    HeapKind heap { HeapKind::Function };
    bool nullable { false };
    u32 type_index { 0 };

    static constexpr ValueType scalar(ValueKind kind) { return { kind, HeapKind::Function, false, 0 }; }
    static constexpr ValueType reference(HeapKind heap, bool nullable = true) { return { ValueKind::Reference, heap, nullable, 0 }; }
};

// How the garbage collector follows a value. A function reference points into its function's cell, while any other
// reference is null, an i31, the address of a cell, or the address of a host value's cell with bit 1 set.
enum class ValueTrace : u8 {
    None,
    Reference,
    FunctionReference,
};

// A value. i32 and f32 bits are zero-extended in `low`, a v128 is `low` and `high`, and a reference is its bits, which
// are zero for null.
struct WASM_API Value {
    ValueKind kind { ValueKind::I32 };
    ValueTrace trace { ValueTrace::None };
    u64 low { 0 };
    u64 high { 0 };

    static Value from_i32(i32 value) { return { ValueKind::I32, ValueTrace::None, static_cast<u32>(value), 0 }; }
    static Value from_i64(i64 value) { return { ValueKind::I64, ValueTrace::None, static_cast<u64>(value), 0 }; }
    static Value from_f32_bits(u32 bits) { return { ValueKind::F32, ValueTrace::None, bits, 0 }; }
    static Value from_f64_bits(u64 bits) { return { ValueKind::F64, ValueTrace::None, bits, 0 }; }
    static Value from_f32(float value) { return from_f32_bits(bit_cast<u32>(value)); }
    static Value from_f64(double value) { return from_f64_bits(bit_cast<u64>(value)); }
    static Value from_v128(u64 low, u64 high) { return { ValueKind::V128, ValueTrace::None, low, high }; }
    // A reference that is not a function reference, which only the store makes (see Store::function_reference()).
    static Value from_reference(u64 bits) { return { ValueKind::Reference, ValueTrace::Reference, bits, 0 }; }
    static Value default_for(ValueType type) { return { type.kind, ValueTrace::None, 0, 0 }; }

    i32 to_i32() const { return static_cast<i32>(static_cast<u32>(low)); }
    i64 to_i64() const { return static_cast<i64>(low); }
    u32 f32_bits() const { return static_cast<u32>(low); }
    u64 f64_bits() const { return low; }
    float to_f32() const { return bit_cast<float>(f32_bits()); }
    double to_f64() const { return bit_cast<double>(f64_bits()); }
    u64 reference_bits() const { return low; }
    bool is_null_reference() const { return low == 0; }

    void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor&) const;
};

enum class ExternKind : u8 {
    Function,
    Table,
    Memory,
    Global,
    Tag,
};

// A function, table, memory, global, tag, or instance: an entity of the store, which is a cell of the store's heap.
// The store keeps no entity alive: an entity lives while something visits or roots its cell, or while another
// entity that refers to it lives (an instance refers to what it defines and imports, a function to its instance).
// Embedders pass the store only entities it made, or the runtime aborts.
using Entity = GC::ForeignCell*;

struct Extern {
    ExternKind kind { ExternKind::Function };
    GC::Ptr<GC::ForeignCell> entity;

    void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor) { visitor.visit(entity.ptr()); }
};

struct Limits {
    u64 minimum { 0 };
    u64 maximum { 0 };
    bool has_maximum { false };
    bool address64 { false };
    bool shared { false };
};

// What an import or export is: the type index of a function or tag, the limits of a memory or table, the element type
// of a table, and the value type and mutability of a global.
struct ExternType {
    ExternKind kind { ExternKind::Function };
    u32 type_index { 0 };
    Limits limits;
    ValueType value_type;
    bool is_mutable { false };
};

struct FunctionType {
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;

    Vector<ValueType> parameters;
    Vector<ValueType> results;
};

struct Import {
    StringView module;
    StringView name;
    ExternType type;
};

struct InstanceExport {
    StringView name;
    Extern value;

    void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor) { value.visit_edges(visitor); }
};

// Values that may be references to cells, which the garbage collector keeps alive while the vector lives.
using Values = GC::RootVector<Value, 8>;

// A compiled module, which can be shared across threads and instantiated in any store.
class WASM_API Module : public AtomicRefCounted<Module> {
public:
    static ErrorOr<NonnullRefPtr<Module>, ByteString> compile(ReadonlyBytes);
    ~Module();

    size_t import_count() const;
    Import import(size_t index) const;
    Optional<FunctionType> function_type(u32 type_index) const;

    FFI::WasmModule const* handle() const { return m_module; }

private:
    explicit Module(FFI::WasmModule const* module)
        : m_module(module)
    {
    }

    FFI::WasmModule const* m_module { nullptr };
};

enum class FailureKind : u8 {
    LinkError,
    Trap,
    // An exception was thrown and not caught: `exception` refers to it.
    Exception,
    StackExhausted,
};

struct Failure {
    FailureKind kind { FailureKind::Trap };
    ByteString message;
    u64 exception { 0 };
};

// How a host function fails: it traps with a message.
struct HostError {
    HostError(ByteString message)
        : message(move(message))
    {
    }

    ByteString message;
};

// What the entities of one thread share: their heap, types, and the interpreter's state. One store serves a whole
// agent.
class WASM_API Store {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(Store);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(Store);
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

public:
    // Entities and GC objects live in the heap, and memories in LibGC's primitive storage.
    explicit Store(GC::Heap&);
    ~Store();

    // A host function writes one result for each result of its type, or returns an error to trap or throw. The
    // function it is made of lives as long as the function is in the store. The concrete types of its type must be
    // identities of the store, or the runtime aborts.
    using HostFunction = GC::Function<ErrorOr<void, HostError>(Store&, ReadonlySpan<Value> arguments, Span<Value> results)>;

    Entity allocate_host_function(FunctionType const&, GC::Ref<HostFunction>);
    Optional<Entity> allocate_memory(Limits);
    Optional<Entity> allocate_table(ValueType element, Limits, u64 initial);
    Entity allocate_global(ValueType, bool is_mutable, Value);

    // Returns the instance.
    ErrorOr<Entity, Failure> instantiate(Module const&, ReadonlySpan<Extern> imports);
    Vector<InstanceExport> instance_exports(Entity instance);
    Optional<Extern> find_export(Entity instance, StringView name);

    FunctionType function_type(Entity function);
    ErrorOr<Values, Failure> invoke(Entity function, ReadonlySpan<Value> arguments);
    // A reference to the function, which the garbage collector follows into the function's cell.
    Value function_reference(Entity function);
    // The function a non-null function reference refers to.
    Entity function_from_reference(u64 reference);

    ValueType global_type(Entity global, bool& is_mutable);
    Value global_get(Entity global);

    FFI::WasmStore* handle() { return m_store; }

private:
    FFI::WasmStore* m_store { nullptr };
};

// The state of a WASI (wasi_snapshot_preview1) command. Its functions only work on Unix hosts.
class WASM_API Wasi {
    AK_MAKE_NONCOPYABLE(Wasi);
    AK_MAKE_NONMOVABLE(Wasi);
    AK_ALLOC_WITH_KMALLOC;

public:
    struct Preopen {
        ByteString host_path;
        ByteString guest_path;
    };

    // The environment is a list of NAME=value strings.
    Wasi(ReadonlySpan<ByteString> arguments, ReadonlySpan<ByteString> environment, ReadonlySpan<Preopen> preopens);
    ~Wasi();

    static constexpr StringView module_name = "wasi_snapshot_preview1"sv;

    // Add the WASI function `name` to the store, if there is one.
    Optional<Entity> allocate_function(Store&, StringView name);
    // Have the functions work on `memory`, usually the one the command exports.
    void set_memory(Entity memory);
    // The code the command passed to proc_exit, if it called it.
    Optional<i32> exit_code() const;

private:
    FFI::WasmWasi* m_wasi { nullptr };
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/differential-fuzz.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Differential fuzzing of the WebAssembly engine against other ones: `wasm-tools smith` generates valid modules, to
# which this script adds, for each exported function, a probe that calls the function with zero arguments and returns
# a hash of its results (floats as their bits, references as whether they are null) and of memory 0. Each engine runs
# each probe; whether it traps and the hash it returns must agree. When the engine under test and the old engine
# disagree, wabt's interpreter (wasm-interp) decides which one is wrong.
#
#   differential-fuzz.py --new Build/release/bin/wasm --old /path/to/old/wasm --cases 500 --out /tmp/fuzz
#
# Each case that the engine under test gets wrong is kept in the output directory with what the engines returned.
# Re-run a single case with --seed. Cases are reproducible from their seed.

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import os
import random
import re
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from reencode import DecodeError  # noqa: E402
from reencode import Reader  # noqa: E402
from reencode import unsigned_leb  # noqa: E402

SMITH_FEATURES = [
    "--ensure-termination",
    "--export-everything",
    "true",
    "--canonicalize-nans",
    "true",
    "--max-imports",
    "0",
    "--min-funcs",
    "1",
    "--max-funcs",
    "8",
    "--max-memory32-bytes",
    str(16 * 65536),
    "--max-memories",
    "1",
    "--max-tables",
    "2",
    "--max-table-elements",
    "100",
    "--max-data-segments",
    "4",
    "--simd-enabled",
    "true",
    "--bulk-memory-enabled",
    "true",
    "--reference-types-enabled",
    "true",
    "--multi-value-enabled",
    "true",
    "--saturating-float-to-int-enabled",
    "true",
    "--sign-extension-ops-enabled",
    "true",
    "--tail-call-enabled",
    "true",
    "--relaxed-simd-enabled",
    "false",
    "--gc-enabled",
    "false",
    "--exceptions-enabled",
    "false",
    "--threads-enabled",
    "false",
    "--memory64-enabled",
    "false",
    "--extended-const-enabled",
    "true",
    "--allow-start-export",
    "false",
]

VALUE_TYPE_ZERO = {
    0x7F: bytes([0x41, 0x00]),
    0x7E: bytes([0x42, 0x00]),
    0x7D: bytes([0x43, 0, 0, 0, 0]),
    0x7C: bytes([0x44, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]),
    0x7B: bytes([0xFD, 0x0C]) + bytes(16),
    0x70: bytes([0xD0, 0x70]),
    0x6F: bytes([0xD0, 0x6F]),
}


def sections_of(data):
    reader = Reader(data, 8)
    sections = []
    while reader.position < reader.end:
        section_id = reader.byte()
        size = reader.unsigned(32)
        sections.append([section_id, bytearray(reader.bytes(size))])
    return sections


def vector_of(contents):
    reader = Reader(bytes(contents))
    return reader, reader.unsigned(32)


def add_probes(data):
    """Add, for each exported function, an exported `__probe_<n>` that calls it with zero arguments, drops its
    results, and returns a hash of memory 0. Returns the new module and the names of the functions probed."""
    sections = sections_of(data)
    by_id = {section_id: contents for section_id, contents in sections}
    if 2 in by_id and vector_of(by_id[2])[1] > 0:
        raise DecodeError("imports are not probed")
    types = []
    reader, count = vector_of(by_id.get(1, b"\0"))
    for _ in range(count):
        if reader.byte() != 0x60:
            raise DecodeError("only function types are probed")
        parameters = [reader.byte() for _ in range(reader.unsigned(32))]
        results = [reader.byte() for _ in range(reader.unsigned(32))]
        if any(t not in VALUE_TYPE_ZERO for t in parameters + results):
            raise DecodeError("unprobed value type")
        types.append((parameters, results))
    reader, count = vector_of(by_id.get(3, b"\0"))
    functions = [reader.unsigned(32) for _ in range(count)]
    reader, count = vector_of(by_id.get(7, b"\0"))
    exports = []
    for _ in range(count):
        name = reader.bytes(reader.unsigned(32)).decode()
        kind = reader.byte()
        index = reader.unsigned(32)
        if kind == 0:
            exports.append((name, index))
    has_memory = 5 in by_id and vector_of(by_id[5])[1] > 0

    probe_type = len(types)
    new_types = bytearray(by_id.get(1, b"\0"))
    reader, count = vector_of(new_types)
    new_types = bytearray(unsigned_leb(count + 1)) + new_types[reader.position :] + bytes([0x60, 0x00, 0x01, 0x7E])

    # Locals: $i (i32), $hash (i64), $vector (v128).
    fold = bytes([0x20, 0x01, 0x42, 0x1F, 0x7E, 0x7C, 0x21, 0x01])
    folds = {
        0x7F: bytes([0xAD]) + fold,
        0x7E: fold,
        0x7D: bytes([0xBC, 0xAD]) + fold,
        0x7C: bytes([0xBD]) + fold,
        0x7B: bytes([0x21, 0x02, 0x20, 0x02, 0xFD, 0x1D, 0x00]) + fold + bytes([0x20, 0x02, 0xFD, 0x1D, 0x01]) + fold,
        0x70: bytes([0xD1, 0xAD]) + fold,
        0x6F: bytes([0xD1, 0xAD]) + fold,
    }
    bodies = []
    for _, function_index in exports:
        parameters, results = types[functions[function_index]]
        code = bytearray()
        for parameter in parameters:
            code += VALUE_TYPE_ZERO[parameter]
        code += bytes([0x10]) + unsigned_leb(function_index)
        # The last result is on top.
        for result in reversed(results):
            code += folds[result]
        if has_memory:
            # block loop
            #   i >= memory.size << 16 -> exit
            #   hash = hash * 31 + i64.load(i); i += 8
            # end end
            code += bytes([0x02, 0x40, 0x03, 0x40])
            code += bytes([0x20, 0x00, 0x3F, 0x00, 0x41, 0x10, 0x74, 0x4F, 0x0D, 0x01])
            code += bytes([0x20, 0x00, 0x29, 0x03, 0x00]) + fold
            code += bytes([0x20, 0x00, 0x41, 0x08, 0x6A, 0x21, 0x00, 0x0C, 0x00])
            code += bytes([0x0B, 0x0B])
        code += bytes([0x20, 0x01, 0x0B])
        body = bytes([0x03, 0x01, 0x7F, 0x01, 0x7E, 0x01, 0x7B]) + bytes(code)
        bodies.append(unsigned_leb(len(body)) + body)

    reader, count = vector_of(by_id.get(3, b"\0"))
    new_functions = bytearray(unsigned_leb(count + len(exports))) + by_id.get(3, b"\0")[reader.position :]
    new_functions += unsigned_leb(probe_type) * len(exports)
    reader, count = vector_of(by_id.get(10, b"\0"))
    new_code = bytearray(unsigned_leb(count + len(exports))) + by_id.get(10, b"\0")[reader.position :]
    for body in bodies:
        new_code += body
    reader, count = vector_of(by_id.get(7, b"\0"))
    # Every function gets a plain name as well, since smith's names may not survive a command line.
    new_exports = bytearray(unsigned_leb(count + 2 * len(exports))) + by_id.get(7, b"\0")[reader.position :]
    for probe, (_, function_index) in enumerate(exports):
        name = f"__function_{probe}".encode()
        new_exports += unsigned_leb(len(name)) + name + bytes([0x00]) + unsigned_leb(function_index)
        name = f"__probe_{probe}".encode()
        new_exports += unsigned_leb(len(name)) + name + bytes([0x00]) + unsigned_leb(len(functions) + probe)

    replaced = {1: new_types, 3: new_functions, 7: new_exports, 10: new_code}
    present = {section_id for section_id, _ in sections}
    order = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 13, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 10, 11]
    out = bytearray(data[:8])
    for section_id in order:
        if section_id in replaced:
            contents = replaced[section_id]
        elif section_id in present:
            contents = by_id[section_id]
        else:
            continue
        out += bytes([section_id]) + unsigned_leb(len(contents)) + contents
    return bytes(out), [name for name, _ in exports]


def outcome_of(process):
    if process.returncode < 0:
        return f"crash {process.returncode}"
    output = process.stdout + process.stderr
    if "trapped" in output or ") => error" in output:
        return "trap"
    if "failed" in output.lower() or "error:" in output:
        return "failed"
    match = re.search(r"(?:  -> |=> i64:)(-?[0-9]+)", output)
    if not match:
        return "failed"
    # Engines print the hash signed or unsigned.
    return f"returned {int(match[1]) % (1 << 64)}"


def run(binary, module, function):
    try:
        process = subprocess.run([binary, "-e", function, module], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return "timeout"
    return outcome_of(process)


def run_wabt(module, function):
    try:
        process = subprocess.run(
            ["wasm-interp", "--enable-all", module, "-r", function], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60
        )
    except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError):
        return "unavailable"
    return outcome_of(process)


def run_case(seed, arguments):
    random.seed(seed)
    entropy = bytes(random.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(arguments.entropy))
    smith = subprocess.run(
        [arguments.wasm_tools, "smith", *SMITH_FEATURES, *arguments.smith_argument],
        input=entropy,
        capture_output=True,
        timeout=60,
    )
    if smith.returncode != 0:
        return seed, "skipped", "smith failed"
    try:
        module, names = add_probes(smith.stdout)
    except (DecodeError, IndexError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:
        return seed, "skipped", str(error)
    path = os.path.join(arguments.out, f"case-{seed}.wasm")
    with open(path, "wb") as file:
        file.write(module)
    differences = []
    verdict = "same"
    for probe in range(len(names)):
        function = f"__probe_{probe}"
        new = run(arguments.new, path, function)
        old = run(arguments.old, path, function)
        if new == old:
            continue
        wabt = run_wabt(path, function)
        if old == "failed" and wabt == "failed" and new != "failed":
            # Neither reference engine can run the module, which is valid (smith only makes valid ones).
            if verdict == "same":
                verdict = "references-fail"
            continue
        if wabt == new:
            # The old engine is wrong, or cannot run the module (smith only makes valid ones).
            if verdict == "same":
                verdict = "old-wrong"
            continue
        verdict = "different"
        differences.append(f"{function}: new {new!r}, old {old!r}, wabt {wabt!r}")
    if differences:
        with open(os.path.join(arguments.out, f"case-{seed}.txt"), "w") as file:
            file.write("\n".join(differences) + "\n")
        return seed, "different", "; ".join(differences[:3])
    os.remove(path)
    return seed, verdict, f"{len(names)} functions"


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--new", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--old", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--wasm-tools", default=os.path.expanduser("~/.cargo/bin/wasm-tools"))
    parser.add_argument("--cases", type=int, default=200)
    parser.add_argument("--first-seed", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--entropy", type=int, default=4096)
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=8)
    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--smith-argument", action="append", default=[], help="More arguments for smith, like --min-uleb-size=5"
    )
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    os.makedirs(arguments.out, exist_ok=True)
    seeds = (
        [arguments.seed]
        if arguments.seed is not None
        else range(arguments.first_seed, arguments.first_seed + arguments.cases)
    )
    counts = {"same": 0, "different": 0, "skipped": 0, "old-wrong": 0, "references-fail": 0}
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=arguments.jobs) as pool:
        for seed, verdict, detail in pool.map(lambda seed: run_case(seed, arguments), seeds):
            counts[verdict] += 1
            if verdict == "different":
                print(f"seed {seed}: {verdict}: {detail}", flush=True)
    print(
        f"{counts['same']} same, {counts['different']} different, {counts['skipped']} skipped, "
        f"{counts['old-wrong']} where only the old engine is wrong (by wabt), "
        f"{counts['references-fail']} that neither the old engine nor wabt can run"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Executor/test-atomics.js
// Threads-proposal atomics on non-shared memory: they behave like plain accesses, except that
// they trap when misaligned, waits always trap, and notifies never have anyone to wake.

function loadAtomics() {
    const bin = readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/atomics.wasm");
    const module = parseWebAssemblyModule(bin);
    const exports = {};
    for (const name of [
        "i32_load",
        "i32_store",
        "i32_load8_u",
        "i32_store8",
        "i32_load16_u",
        "i64_load",
        "i64_store",
        "i64_load32_u",
        "i64_store16",
        "i32_rmw_add",
        "i32_rmw_sub",
        "i32_rmw_and",
        "i32_rmw_or",
        "i32_rmw_xor",
        "i32_rmw_xchg",
        "i32_rmw8_add_u",
        "i32_rmw16_sub_u",
        "i64_rmw_add",
        "i64_rmw16_xchg_u",
        "i64_rmw32_or_u",
        "i32_cmpxchg",
        "i32_cmpxchg8_u",
        "i64_cmpxchg",
        "i64_cmpxchg32_u",
        "notify",
        "wait32",
        "wait64",
        "fence",
        "i32_load_offset",
        "plain_i32_load",
    ]) {
        const fn = module.getExport(name);
        exports[name] = (...args) => module.invoke(fn, ...args);
    }
    return exports;
}

test("atomic loads and stores behave like plain ones", () => {
    const m = loadAtomics();

    m.i32_store(8, 0x12345678);
    expect(m.i32_load(8)).toBe(0x12345678);
    expect(m.plain_i32_load(8)).toBe(0x12345678);
    expect(m.i32_load_offset(4)).toBe(0x12345678);
    expect(m.i32_load8_u(8)).toBe(0x78);
    expect(m.i32_load8_u(11)).toBe(0x12);
    expect(m.i32_load16_u(10)).toBe(0x1234);

    m.i32_store8(16, 0x1ff);
    expect(m.i32_load(16)).toBe(0xff);

    m.i64_store(24, 0x1122334455667788n);
    expect(m.i64_load(24)).toBe(0x1122334455667788n);
    expect(m.i64_load32_u(24)).toBe(0x55667788n);
    expect(m.i64_load32_u(28)).toBe(0x11223344n);

    m.i64_store16(32, 0x1abcdn);
    expect(m.i64_load(32)).toBe(0xabcdn);
});

test("read-modify-write returns the old value and updates memory", () => {
    const m = loadAtomics();

    m.i32_store(0, 10);
    expect(m.i32_rmw_add(0, 5)).toBe(10);
    expect(m.i32_load(0)).toBe(15);
    expect(m.i32_rmw_sub(0, 3)).toBe(15);
    expect(m.i32_load(0)).toBe(12);
    expect(m.i32_rmw_and(0, 0xa)).toBe(12);
    expect(m.i32_load(0)).toBe(8);
    expect(m.i32_rmw_or(0, 3)).toBe(8);
    expect(m.i32_load(0)).toBe(11);
    expect(m.i32_rmw_xor(0, 1)).toBe(11);
    expect(m.i32_load(0)).toBe(10);
    expect(m.i32_rmw_xchg(0, 99)).toBe(10);
    expect(m.i32_load(0)).toBe(99);

    // Narrow operations wrap at the access width and zero-extend their result.
    m.i32_store(4, 0);
    expect(m.i32_rmw8_add_u(4, 0x1ff)).toBe(0);
    expect(m.i32_load(4)).toBe(0xff);
    expect(m.i32_rmw8_add_u(4, 1)).toBe(0xff);
    expect(m.i32_load(4)).toBe(0);
    m.i32_store(4, 0x00010000);
    expect(m.i32_rmw16_sub_u(4, 1)).toBe(0);
    expect(m.i32_load(4)).toBe(0x0001ffff);

    m.i64_store(8, 5n);
    expect(m.i64_rmw_add(8, 0xffffffffn)).toBe(5n);
    expect(m.i64_load(8)).toBe(0x100000004n);
    expect(m.i64_rmw16_xchg_u(8, 0x1abcdn)).toBe(4n);
    expect(m.i64_load(8)).toBe(0x10000abcdn);
    expect(m.i64_rmw32_or_u(12, 0x100000001n)).toBe(1n);
    expect(m.i64_load(8)).toBe(0x10000abcdn);
});

test("cmpxchg compares at the access width", () => {
    const m = loadAtomics();

    m.i32_store(0, 7);
    expect(m.i32_cmpxchg(0, 8, 100)).toBe(7);
    expect(m.i32_load(0)).toBe(7);
    expect(m.i32_cmpxchg(0, 7, 100)).toBe(7);
    expect(m.i32_load(0)).toBe(100);

    m.i32_store(0, 0x1234);
    expect(m.i32_cmpxchg8_u(0, 0x134, 0x99)).toBe(0x34);
    expect(m.i32_load(0)).toBe(0x1299);
    expect(m.i32_cmpxchg8_u(1, 0x99, 0x77)).toBe(0x12);
    expect(m.i32_load(0)).toBe(0x1299);

    m.i64_store(8, 0xffffffffffffffffn);
    expect(m.i64_cmpxchg(8, 0xffffffffffffffffn, 1n)).toBe(-1n);
    expect(m.i64_load(8)).toBe(1n);
    expect(m.i64_cmpxchg32_u(8, 0x100000001n, 2n)).toBe(1n);
    expect(m.i64_load(8)).toBe(2n);
    expect(m.i64_cmpxchg32_u(12, 1n, 3n)).toBe(0n);
    expect(m.i64_load(8)).toBe(2n);
});

test("atomic accesses trap on misaligned or out-of-bounds addresses", () => {
    const m = loadAtomics();
    const unaligned = "Execution trapped: Unaligned atomic memory access";
    const outOfBounds = "Execution trapped: Memory access out of bounds";

    expect(() => m.i32_load(2)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, unaligned);
    expect(() => m.i32_store(1, 0)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, unaligned);
    expect(() => m.i64_load(4)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, unaligned);
    expect(() => m.i64_load32_u(2)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, unaligned);
    expect(() => m.i32_rmw_add(2, 1)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, unaligned);
    expect(() => m.i32_cmpxchg(1, 0, 0)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, unaligned);
    expect(() => m.i32_load_offset(2)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, unaligned);
    expect(m.i32_load8_u(3)).toBe(0);
    expect(m.i32_load16_u(6)).toBe(0);

    expect(() => m.i32_load(65536)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, outOfBounds);
    expect(() => m.i32_load(65534)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, outOfBounds);
    expect(() => m.i32_load(-4)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, outOfBounds);
    expect(() => m.i64_store(65532, 0n)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, outOfBounds);
    expect(() => m.i32_rmw_add(65536, 1)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, outOfBounds);
    expect(() => m.i32_load_offset(65532)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, outOfBounds);
    expect(m.i32_load(65532)).toBe(0);
});

test("waits trap and notifies wake nobody on non-shared memory", () => {
    const m = loadAtomics();
    const unaligned = "Execution trapped: Unaligned atomic memory access";
    const outOfBounds = "Execution trapped: Memory access out of bounds";
    const notShared = "Execution trapped: Expected shared memory";

    expect(m.notify(0, 1)).toBe(0);
    expect(m.notify(4, 0xffffffff)).toBe(0);
    expect(() => m.notify(2, 1)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, unaligned);
    expect(() => m.notify(65536, 1)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, outOfBounds);

    expect(() => m.wait32(0, 0, 0n)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, notShared);
    expect(() => m.wait32(0, 0, -1n)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, notShared);
    expect(() => m.wait32(2, 0, 0n)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, unaligned);
    expect(() => m.wait32(65536, 0, 0n)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, outOfBounds);
    expect(() => m.wait64(8, 0n, 0n)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, notShared);
    expect(() => m.wait64(4, 0n, 0n)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, unaligned);
    expect(() => m.wait64(65532, 0n, 0n)).toThrowWithMessage(TypeError, outOfBounds);

    m.fence();
});

    const module = parseWebAssemblyModule(bin);
    const fn = module.getExport("i32_const_2local_and");

// References that frames hold while the collector runs, whichever tier runs them (see gc-frames.wat). Each round
// allocates enough garbage that collections happen in the middle of the functions.

const module = parseWebAssemblyModule(readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/gc-frames.wasm"));
const call = (name, ...args) => module.invoke(module.getExport(name), ...args);
const before = peakResidentMemorySize();

test("a list held by a local survives collections", () => {
    for (let round = 0; round < 3; ++round) expect(call("list", 200)).toBe(19900n);
});

test("references on the operand stack survive collections", () => {
    for (let round = 0; round < 3; ++round) expect(call("operands", 100)).toBe(4950n + 100000n);
});

test("an array of references outside the heap survives collections", () => {
    for (let round = 0; round < 3; ++round) expect(call("array", 1000)).toBe(499500n);
});

test("a large array of numbers survives collections", () => {
    for (let round = 0; round < 3; ++round) expect(call("wide", 1000)).toBe(499500n + 599n);
});

test("vector, float, i31 and cast references survive collections", () => {
    for (let round = 0; round < 3; ++round) expect(call("mixed", 300)).toBe(3n * 44850n + 1800n);
});

test("the garbage was collected", () => {
    // The rounds above allocate and write more than 2 GiB.
    // The limit leaves room for what a sanitizer adds to the resident memory.
    expect(peakResidentMemorySize() - before).toBeLessThan(1024 * 1024 * 1024);
});

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Executor/test-global-access.js
function loadGlobalModules() {
    const globalsBinary = readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/global-access.wasm");
    const calleeBinary = readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/global-cross-module-callee.wasm");
    const callerBinary = readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/global-cross-module-caller.wasm");

    const globals = parseWebAssemblyModule(globalsBinary);
    const callee = parseWebAssemblyModule(calleeBinary);
    const caller = parseWebAssemblyModule(callerBinary, { callee });
    return { globals, callee, caller };
}

function exerciseGlobalAccess({ globals, callee, caller }) {
    const readImported = globals.getExport("read_imported");
    const i32Roundtrip = globals.getExport("i32_roundtrip");
    const i64Roundtrip = globals.getExport("i64_roundtrip");
    const f32Roundtrip = globals.getExport("f32_roundtrip");
    const f64Roundtrip = globals.getExport("f64_roundtrip");
    const incrementLoop = globals.getExport("increment_loop");
    const callAndRead = caller.getExport("call_and_read");
    const readCallee = callee.getExport("read");

    expect(globals.invoke(readImported, 0)).toBe(666);
    expect(globals.invoke(i32Roundtrip, 0x12345678)).toBe(0x12345678);
    expect(globals.invoke(i64Roundtrip, 0x123456789abcdefn)).toBe(0x123456789abcdefn);
    expect(globals.invoke(f32Roundtrip, 0x7fc12345)).toBe(0x7fc12345);
    expect(globals.invoke(f64Roundtrip, 0x7ff8123456789abcn)).toBe(0x7ff8123456789abcn);
    expect(globals.invoke(incrementLoop, 25)).toBe(25);
    expect(caller.invoke(callAndRead)).toBe(42);
    expect(callee.invoke(readCallee)).toBe(99);
}

test("global access remains interpreter-compatible", () => {
    const modules = loadGlobalModules();
    exerciseGlobalAccess(modules);

    const growthBinary = readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/global-storage-growth.wasm");
    for (let i = 0; i < 64; ++i) parseWebAssemblyModule(growthBinary);

    exerciseGlobalAccess(modules);
});

test("blocks nested across calls", () => {
    // At the deepest point, the blocks of $caller and of $inlinee, which it calls, are open together.
    const bin = readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/inline-label-reservation.wasm");
    const module = parseWebAssemblyModule(bin);

    const run = module.getExport("run");

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Executor/test-memory_fill-order.js
test("memfill executes and returns expected result", () => {
    const bin = readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/memory_fill-order.wasm");
    const module = parseWebAssemblyModule(bin);

    const test_fill = module.getExport("test_fill");
    // memory.fill off=10 value=42 size=5
    module.invoke(test_fill);

    const get_value = module.getExport("get_value");

    // After memory.fill, bytes 10..14 should be filled with value 42
    expect(module.invoke(get_value, 10)).toBe(42);
    expect(module.invoke(get_value, 11)).toBe(42);
    expect(module.invoke(get_value, 12)).toBe(42);
    expect(module.invoke(get_value, 13)).toBe(42);
    expect(module.invoke(get_value, 14)).toBe(42);

    // Byte 9 (before the fill region) should still be 0
    expect(module.invoke(get_value, 9)).toBe(0);

    // Byte 15 (after the fill region) should still be 0
    expect(module.invoke(get_value, 15)).toBe(0);
});

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Executor/test-multi-memory-access.js
test("multi-memory loads, stores, bounds checks, and growth remain interpreter-compatible", () => {
    const binary = readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/multi-memory-access.wasm");
    const module = parseWebAssemblyModule(binary);
    const roundtrip = module.getExport("roundtrip");
    const loadAt = module.getExport("load_at");
    const storeAt = module.getExport("store_at");
    const memoryOneIsDistinct = module.getExport("memory_one_is_distinct");
    const growAndRoundtrip = module.getExport("grow_and_roundtrip");
    const callGrowAndRoundtrip = module.getExport("call_grow_and_roundtrip");

    expect(module.invoke(roundtrip, 0x12345678)).toBe(0x12345678);
    expect(module.invoke(memoryOneIsDistinct)).toBe(0);
    expect(() => module.invoke(loadAt, 65534)).toThrowWithMessage(
        TypeError,
        "Execution trapped: Memory access out of bounds"
    );
    expect(() => module.invoke(storeAt, 65534)).toThrowWithMessage(
        TypeError,
        "Execution trapped: Memory access out of bounds"
    );
    expect(module.invoke(growAndRoundtrip, 0x24681357)).toBe(0x24681357);
    expect(module.invoke(callGrowAndRoundtrip, 0x76543210)).toBe(0x76543210);
});

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Executor/test-return-mid-function.js
test("return mid-function doesn't corrupt caller stack", () => {
    const bin = readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/return-mid-function.wasm");
    const module = parseWebAssemblyModule(bin);

    // Deterministic check: without the fix, the residual 99 from $leaky sits between the caller’s 10 and the result 42,
    // so i32.add yields 141, rather than the correct 52.
    const test_add = module.getExport("test_add");
    expect(module.invoke(test_add)).toBe(52);

    // Stress check: 100 iterations accumulate residuals under the bug; under ASan this overflows the value stack’s
    // inline storage.
    const drive = module.getExport("drive");
    expect(module.invoke(drive)).toBe(100 * 42);
});

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Executor/test-tail-call-label-reservation.js
test("a tail call reserves the callee's labels", () => {
    // A tail call replaces the current frame, but the callee ($deep, 64 nested blocks) can nest deeper than
    // whatever label capacity the replaced frame left behind. The callee pushes its labels unchecked, so
    // without reserving for the callee here this overflows the inline label storage and corrupts the frame
    // stack. Just needs to run to completion without crashing.
    const bin = readBinaryWasmFile("Fixtures/Modules/tail-call-label-reservation.wasm");
    const module = parseWebAssemblyModule(bin);

    const run = module.getExport("run");
    module.invoke(run, 0);
});

;; Allocates objects, large arrays, and exceptions that become garbage right away.
(module
  (type $node (struct (field (mut i64)) (field (ref null $node))))
  (type $bytes (array (mut i32)))
  (tag $thrown (param (ref null $node)))
  (func (export "churn") (param $count i32) (result i64)
    (local $index i32)
    (local $last (ref null $node))
    (loop $again
      (local.set $last (struct.new $node (i64.extend_i32_u (local.get $index)) (ref.null $node)))
      ;; 64 KiB of elements, which live outside the heap.
      (drop (array.new_default $bytes (i32.const 16384)))
      (block $caught (result (ref null $node))
        (try_table (catch $thrown $caught)
          (throw $thrown (local.get $last)))
        (unreachable))
      (drop)
      (local.set $index (i32.add (local.get $index) (i32.const 1)))
      (br_if $again (i32.lt_u (local.get $index) (local.get $count))))
    (struct.get $node 0 (local.get $last)))
)

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Fixtures/Modules/gc-frames.wasm
FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Fixtures/Modules/gc-frames.wat
;; References that live in frames while the collector runs: in locals and on the operand stack across calls that
;; allocate enough to collect, in inline and out-of-line objects, and as i31 values. Every function
;; returns a checksum that is only right if nothing they still refer to was freed or overwritten.
(module
  (type $node (struct (field $value (mut i64)) (field $next (mut (ref null $node)))))
  (type $nodes (array (mut (ref null $node))))
  (type $bytes (array (mut i8)))
  (type $vector (struct (field v128) (field (ref null $node)) (field f64)))
  ;; 600 fields of 8 bytes: data outside the heap.
  (type $wide (array (mut i64)))

  ;; Allocates 32 KB of garbage per count, written so that it takes memory, so that collections happen during the
  ;; calls below.
  (func $churn (param $count i32)
    (local $i i32)
    (loop $again

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Fixtures/Modules/return-mid-function.wasm
FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Fixtures/Modules/return-mid-function.wat
(module
  ;; Regression test for https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/issues/9614
  ;;
  ;; The 'return' instruction must drop intermediate working values from the value stack, keeping only the top .arity()
  ;; values (the return values). The spec validation rule for 'return' doesn’t require the value stack to be otherwise
  ;; empty when return fires. So a function is allowed to leave extras on the stack, provided the top items match the
  ;; result types.
  ;;
  ;; Before the fix for #9614, the interpreter's return_ handler only shrank the label stack and left residual values on
  ;; the shared value stack, leaking them to the caller.

  ;; Pushes residual 99, then returns 42. The residual must be discarded.
  (func $leaky (result i32)
    i32.const 99
    i32.const 42
    return
  )

  ;; Deterministic correctness check: caller pushes 10, calls $leaky, adds. With the fix: value stack after
  ;; call = [10, 42]; i32.add yields 52. Without the fix: residual 99 sits between 10 and 42. So, i32.add consumes
  ;; 99+42=141. Wrong answer, caught immediately without ASan.
  (func (export "test_add") (result i32)
    i32.const 10
    call $leaky
    i32.add
  )

  ;; Pushes three values, then returns the top one. The bottom two are residuals; 'return' is required to discard them.
  (func $return_with_residuals (result i32)
    i32.const 1111
    i32.const 2222
    i32.const 42
    return
  )

  ;; Calls $return_with_residuals 100 times. Without the fix for #9614, each call leaks two residuals into the driver's
  ;; value stack. Under ASan, that eventually overflows the value stack's inline storage as heap-buffer-overflow. With
  ;; the fix, every iteration is net-zero and acc == 100 * 42.
  (func (export "drive") (result i32)
    (local $i i32)
    (local $acc i32)
    (loop $loop
      call $return_with_residuals
      local.get $acc
      i32.add
      local.set $acc

      local.get $i
      i32.const 1
      i32.add
      local.tee $i
      i32.const 100
      i32.lt_s
      br_if $loop
    )
    local.get $acc
  )
)

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/Parser/test-function-type-limits.js
function uleb(value) {
    const bytes = [];
    do {
        const byte = value & 0x7f;
        value >>= 7;
        bytes.push(value ? byte | 0x80 : byte);
    } while (value);
    return bytes;
}

function moduleWithFunctionType(paramCount, resultCount) {
    const i32 = 0x7f;
    const types = [
        1,
        0x60,
        ...uleb(paramCount),
        ...Array(paramCount).fill(i32),
        ...uleb(resultCount),
        ...Array(resultCount).fill(i32),
    ];
    return new Uint8Array([0x00, 0x61, 0x73, 0x6d, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 1, ...uleb(types.length), ...types]);
}

test("a function type has at most 1000 parameters", () => {
    parseWebAssemblyModule(moduleWithFunctionType(1000, 0));
    expect(() => parseWebAssemblyModule(moduleWithFunctionType(1001, 0))).toThrow(SyntaxError);
});

test("a function type has at most 1000 results", () => {
    parseWebAssemblyModule(moduleWithFunctionType(0, 1000));
    expect(() => parseWebAssemblyModule(moduleWithFunctionType(0, 1001))).toThrow(SyntaxError);
});

FILE: Libraries/LibWasm/Tests/reencode.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Re-encode the function bodies of WebAssembly modules, so that the engine's decoding of immediates can be tested on
# every encoding the binary format allows, not only the minimal ones that tools emit.
#
#   reencode.py --mode wide IN OUT       Every LEB128 in a function body takes its maximum width: 5 bytes for u32,
#                                        s32, and s33, 10 for u64 and s64.
#   reencode.py --mode memory-index ...  Every memory argument names its memory, including memory 0.
#   reencode.py --tree SOURCE DEST ...   Re-encode every .wasm under SOURCE into DEST; other files are linked.
#
# Modules this script cannot decode (malformed or invalid ones that the tests expect to be rejected) are copied as
# they are. Sections and bodies get their sizes fixed up.

import argparse
import os
import sys


class DecodeError(Exception):
    pass


class Reader:
    def __init__(self, data, position=0, end=None):
        self.data = data
        self.position = position
        self.end = len(data) if end is None else end

    def byte(self):
        if self.position >= self.end:
            raise DecodeError("unexpected end")
        value = self.data[self.position]
        self.position += 1
        return value

    def bytes(self, count):
        if self.position + count > self.end:
            raise DecodeError("unexpected end")
        value = self.data[self.position : self.position + count]
        self.position += count
        return value

    def unsigned(self, bits):
        # Strict, like the binary format: at most ceil(bits / 7) bytes, and the unused bits of the last one are zero.
        result = 0
        shift = 0
        while True:
            byte = self.byte()
            result |= (byte & 0x7F) << shift
            shift += 7
            if byte & 0x80 == 0:
                break
            if shift >= bits:
                raise DecodeError("integer too long")
        if result >> bits:
            raise DecodeError("integer too large")
        return result

    def signed(self, bits):
        # Strict, like the binary format: at most ceil(bits / 7) bytes, and the unused bits of the last one extend the
        # sign.
        result = 0
        shift = 0
        while True:
            byte = self.byte()
            result |= (byte & 0x7F) << shift
            shift += 7
            if byte & 0x80 == 0:
                break
            if shift >= bits:
                raise DecodeError("integer too long")
        if shift > bits:
            unused = shift - bits
            top = (byte & 0x7F) >> (7 - unused - 1)
            if top not in (0, (1 << (unused + 1)) - 1):
                raise DecodeError("integer too large")
        if result >> (shift - 1):
            result -= 1 << shift
        return result


def unsigned_leb(value, width=None):
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        byte = value & 0x7F
        value >>= 7
        if value == 0 and width is None:
            out.append(byte)
            return bytes(out)
        out.append(byte | 0x80)
        if width is not None and len(out) == width - 1:
            out.append(value & 0x7F)
            return bytes(out)


def signed_leb(value, width=None):
    out = bytearray()
    if width is None:
        while True:
            byte = value & 0x7F
            value >>= 7
            if (value == 0 and byte & 0x40 == 0) or (value == -1 and byte & 0x40):
                out.append(byte)
                return bytes(out)
            out.append(byte | 0x80)
    for _ in range(width - 1):
        out.append((value & 0x7F) | 0x80)
        value >>= 7
    out.append(value & 0x7F)
    return bytes(out)


# Widths of the maximal encodings.
U32 = 5
S32 = 5
S33 = 5
U64 = 10
S64 = 10


class Encoder:
    def __init__(self, mode):
        self.mode = mode
        self.out = bytearray()

    def u32(self, value):
        self.out += unsigned_leb(value, U32 if self.mode == "wide" else None)

    def u64(self, value):
        self.out += unsigned_leb(value, U64 if self.mode == "wide" else None)

    def s32(self, value):
        self.out += signed_leb(value, S32 if self.mode == "wide" else None)

    def s33(self, value):
        self.out += signed_leb(value, S33 if self.mode == "wide" else None)

    def s64(self, value):
        self.out += signed_leb(value, S64 if self.mode == "wide" else None)

    def raw(self, data):
        self.out += data


def copy_heap_type(reader, encoder):
    first = reader.data[reader.position]
    if first & 0x40 and first & 0x80 == 0:
        # An abstract heap type, which is a byte.
        encoder.raw(bytes([reader.byte()]))
        return
    value = reader.signed(33)
    if value < 0:
        raise DecodeError("negative heap type")
    encoder.s33(value)


def copy_value_type(reader, encoder):
    byte = reader.byte()
    encoder.raw(bytes([byte]))
    if byte in (0x63, 0x64):
        copy_heap_type(reader, encoder)


def copy_block_type(reader, encoder):
    first = reader.data[reader.position]
    if first == 0x40:
        encoder.raw(bytes([reader.byte()]))
        return
    if first & 0x40 and first & 0x80 == 0:
        copy_value_type(reader, encoder)
        return
    value = reader.signed(33)
    if value < 0:
        raise DecodeError("negative block type")
    encoder.s33(value)


def copy_memory_argument(reader, encoder):
    flags = reader.unsigned(32)
    has_index = flags & 0x40
    memory = reader.unsigned(32) if has_index else 0
    offset = reader.unsigned(64)
    if encoder.mode == "memory-index":
        has_index = True
    encoder.u32(flags | 0x40 if has_index else flags)
    if has_index:
        encoder.u32(memory)
    encoder.u64(offset)


# Immediates of the single-byte opcodes. "u" is a u32, "b" a block type, "m" a memory argument, "h" a heap type, "l" a
# lane index byte, "z" a zero byte, and "v" sixteen bytes.

    0xD1: "",
    0xD2: "u",
    0xD3: "",
    0xD4: "",

    0xD6: "u",

for opcode in range(0x28, 0x3F):
    PLAIN[opcode] = "m"
for opcode in range(0x45, 0xC5):
    PLAIN[opcode] = ""

# The 0xFB (GC) sub-opcodes. "c" is br_on_cast's flags byte and two heap types after a label.
GC = {
    0: "u",
    1: "u",
    2: "uu",
    3: "uu",
    4: "uu",

MISC = {
    0: "",
    1: "",
    2: "",
    3: "",
    4: "",
    5: "",

    9: "u",

def simd_immediates(sub):
    if sub <= 0x0B or sub in (0x5C, 0x5D):
        return "m"
    if 0x54 <= sub <= 0x5B:
        return "ml"
    if sub == 0x0C:
        return "v"
    if sub == 0x0D:
        return "v"
    if 0x15 <= sub <= 0x22:
        return "l"
    return ""


def atomic_immediates(sub):
    if sub == 0x03:
        return "z"
    return "m"


def copy_immediates(reader, encoder, kinds):
    index = 0
    while index < len(kinds):
        kind = kinds[index]
        if kind == "u":
            encoder.u32(reader.unsigned(32))
        elif kind == "b":
            copy_block_type(reader, encoder)
        elif kind == "m":
            copy_memory_argument(reader, encoder)
        elif kind == "h":
            copy_heap_type(reader, encoder)
        elif kind == "l" or kind == "z":
            encoder.raw(bytes([reader.byte()]))
        elif kind == "v":
            # A v128 constant or a shuffle's sixteen lanes.
            encoder.raw(reader.bytes(16))
        elif kind == "c":
            encoder.raw(bytes([reader.byte()]))
            encoder.u32(reader.unsigned(32))
            copy_heap_type(reader, encoder)
            copy_heap_type(reader, encoder)
        else:
            raise DecodeError(f"unknown immediate kind {kind}")
        index += 1


def copy_instruction(reader, encoder):
    opcode = reader.byte()
    encoder.raw(bytes([opcode]))
    if opcode in PLAIN:
        copy_immediates(reader, encoder, PLAIN[opcode])
        return
    if opcode == 0x0E:
        count = reader.unsigned(32)
        encoder.u32(count)
        for _ in range(count + 1):
            encoder.u32(reader.unsigned(32))
        return
    if opcode == 0x1C:
        count = reader.unsigned(32)
        encoder.u32(count)
        for _ in range(count):
            copy_value_type(reader, encoder)
        return
    if opcode == 0x1F:
        copy_block_type(reader, encoder)
        count = reader.unsigned(32)
        encoder.u32(count)
        for _ in range(count):
            kind = reader.byte()
            encoder.raw(bytes([kind]))
            if kind < 2:
                encoder.u32(reader.unsigned(32))
            encoder.u32(reader.unsigned(32))
        return
    if opcode == 0x41:
        encoder.s32(reader.signed(32))
        return
    if opcode == 0x42:
        encoder.s64(reader.signed(64))
        return
    if opcode == 0x43:
        encoder.raw(reader.bytes(4))
        return
    if opcode == 0x44:
        encoder.raw(reader.bytes(8))
        return
    if opcode in (0xFB, 0xFC, 0xFD, 0xFE):
        sub = reader.unsigned(32)
        encoder.u32(sub)
        if opcode == 0xFB:
            kinds = GC.get(sub)
        elif opcode == 0xFC:
            kinds = MISC.get(sub)
        elif opcode == 0xFD:
            kinds = simd_immediates(sub)
        else:
            kinds = atomic_immediates(sub)
        if kinds is None:
            raise DecodeError(f"unknown sub-opcode {opcode:#x} {sub}")
        copy_immediates(reader, encoder, kinds)
        return
    raise DecodeError(f"unknown opcode {opcode:#x}")


def reencode_body(body, mode):
    reader = Reader(body)
    encoder = Encoder(mode)
    groups = reader.unsigned(32)
    encoder.u32(groups)
    for _ in range(groups):
        encoder.u32(reader.unsigned(32))
        copy_value_type(reader, encoder)
    while reader.position < reader.end:
        copy_instruction(reader, encoder)
    return bytes(encoder.out)


def reencode_module(data, mode):
    if data[:8] != b"\0asm\x01\0\0\0":
        raise DecodeError("not a module")
    reader = Reader(data, 8)
    out = bytearray(data[:8])
    while reader.position < reader.end:
        section_id = reader.byte()
        size = reader.unsigned(32)
        contents = reader.bytes(size)
        if section_id != 10:
            out += bytes([section_id]) + unsigned_leb(size) + contents
            continue
        section = Reader(contents)
        count = section.unsigned(32)
        new_contents = bytearray(unsigned_leb(count))
        for _ in range(count):
            body_size = section.unsigned(32)
            body = reencode_body(section.bytes(body_size), mode)
            new_contents += unsigned_leb(len(body)) + body
        if section.position != section.end:
            raise DecodeError("code section has trailing bytes")
        out += bytes([10]) + unsigned_leb(len(new_contents)) + new_contents
    return bytes(out)


def reencode_tree(source, destination, mode):
    rewritten = 0
    kept = 0
    for directory, _, files in os.walk(source):
        relative = os.path.relpath(directory, source)
        target = os.path.join(destination, relative)
        os.makedirs(target, exist_ok=True)
        for name in files:
            source_path = os.path.join(directory, name)
            target_path = os.path.join(target, name)
            if os.path.lexists(target_path):
                os.remove(target_path)
            if not name.endswith(".wasm"):
                os.symlink(os.path.abspath(source_path), target_path)
                continue
            data = open(source_path, "rb").read()
            try:
                new = reencode_module(data, mode)
                rewritten += 1
            except (DecodeError, IndexError):
                new = data
                kept += 1
            open(target_path, "wb").write(new)
    print(f"{rewritten} modules re-encoded, {kept} kept as they were", file=sys.stderr)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=["wide", "memory-index"], required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--tree", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("source")
    parser.add_argument("destination")
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    if arguments.tree:
        reencode_tree(arguments.source, arguments.destination, arguments.mode)
        return
    data = open(arguments.source, "rb").read()
    open(arguments.destination, "wb").write(reencode_module(data, arguments.mode))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

// Called from Bindings/Rust/src/animations/animatable.rs.
void web_animation_for_each_associated_animation(JSObject* node_wrapper, bool subtree, void* context, void (*on_animation)(void* context, RustFFI::AnimationCell const*));
i32 web_animation_compare_elements_in_tree_order(void* first, void* second);
}

// The associated animations of `element`, and of its descendants where `subtree` is set.
static void for_each_associated_animation(DOM::Element const& element, bool subtree, Function<void(AnimationRef const&)> const& callback)
{
    for (auto const& record : element.associated_animations_unordered())
        callback(record);

    if (subtree) {
        element.for_each_child_of_type<DOM::Element>([&](auto const& child) {
            for_each_associated_animation(child, true, callback);
            return IterationDecision::Continue;
        });
    }
}

// NB: The Rust implementations of getAnimations() collect the associated animations of an element, or of the subtree
//     of a node where `subtree` is set, with this, after the pending style changes are applied, and keep the relevant
//     ones and sort them themselves.
void web_animation_for_each_associated_animation(JSObject* node_wrapper, bool subtree, void* context, void (*on_animation)(void* context, RustFFI::AnimationCell const*))
{
    auto& node = *Bindings::impl_from<DOM::Node>(JS::HostABI::object_from_abi(node_wrapper));
    node.document().update_style();
    Function<void(AnimationRef const&)> push = [&](AnimationRef const& animation) { on_animation(context, &animation.record()); };
    if (auto const* element = as_if<DOM::Element>(node)) {
        for_each_associated_animation(*element, subtree, push);
        return;
    }
    VERIFY(subtree);
    as<DOM::ParentNode>(node).for_each_child_of_type<DOM::Element>([&](auto const& child) {
        for_each_associated_animation(child, true, push);
        return IterationDecision::Continue;
    });
}

i32 web_animation_compare_elements_in_tree_order(void* first, void* second)
{
    return compare_elements_in_tree_order_for_composite_order(first, second);
}

Optional<RustFFI::AnimationOwnerSlot> Animatable::owner_slot(Optional<CSS::PseudoElement> pseudo_element)
{
    if (!pseudo_element.has_value())
        return RustFFI::AnimationOwnerSlot { 0 };
    if (!CSS::Selector::PseudoElementSelector::is_known_pseudo_element_type(*pseudo_element))
        return {};
    return RustFFI::AnimationOwnerSlot { static_cast<u8>(to_underlying(*pseudo_element) + 1) };
}

Animatable::~Animatable()
{
    finalize_animations();
}

void Animatable::finalize_animations()
{
    if (auto* animations = exchange(m_animations, nullptr))
        RustFFI::animations_element_animations_destroy(animations, as_if<DOM::Element>(*this));
}

RustFFI::ElementAnimations& Animatable::ensure_animations()
{
    if (!m_animations)
        m_animations = RustFFI::animations_element_animations_create();
    return *m_animations;
}

void Animatable::forget_published_effect_descriptions()
{
    if (m_animations)
        RustFFI::animations_element_animations_forget_published_effect_descriptions(m_animations);
}

ElementAnimationList Animatable::associated_animations_in_composite_order()
{
    if (m_animations)
        RustFFI::animations_element_animations_sort_in_composite_order(m_animations, compare_elements_in_tree_order_for_composite_order);
    return associated_animations_unordered();
}

ElementAnimationList Animatable::associated_animations_unordered() const
{
    return { m_animations, RustFFI::ElementAnimationListKind::Associated, RustFFI::AnimationOwnerSlot { 0 } };
}

void Animatable::invalidate_associated_animation_composite_order()
{
    if (m_animations)
        RustFFI::animations_element_animations_invalidate_composite_order(m_animations);
}

bool Animatable::has_associated_animations() const
{
    return !associated_animations_unordered().is_empty();
}

size_t Animatable::animation_record_memory_size(bool (*first_counted)(void*, RustFFI::KeyframeSet const*), void* context) const
{
    return m_animations ? RustFFI::animations_element_animations_record_memory_size(m_animations, first_counted, context) : 0;
}

void Animatable::associate_with_animation(AnimationRef const& animation)
{
    auto& element = as<DOM::Element>(*this);
    if (!RustFFI::animations_element_animations_associate(&ensure_animations(), &element.document().document_animations(), &animation.record(), element.document().is_in_style_stabilization_epoch()))
        return;
    // The style engine computes no record for an element whose animations compose its style.
    CSS::record_element_animations_changed(element);

    element.change_associated_animation_count_in_subtree(1);
    CSS::record_element_associated_with_animation(element);
}

void Animatable::disassociate_with_animation(AnimationRef const& animation, Optional<EffectRef> const& effect)
{
    auto& element = as<DOM::Element>(*this);
    auto was_associated = RustFFI::animations_element_animations_disassociate(m_animations, &element.document().document_animations(), &animation.record(), effect.has_value() ? &effect->record() : nullptr);
    CSS::record_element_animations_changed(element);

    if (was_associated)
        element.change_associated_animation_count_in_subtree(-1);
}

void Animatable::on_document_changed(DOM::Document& old_document, DOM::Document& new_document)
{
    if (m_animations)
        RustFFI::animations_element_animations_move_to_document(m_animations, &old_document.document_animations(), &new_document.document_animations(), new_document.is_in_style_stabilization_epoch());
}

// The computation of an element's animation definitions matches them against the animations the element already has,
// so the lists publish the name of each and the definition it last had applied to the style engine, which knows the
// element by its identity there, as they change.
static Layout::RustFFI::DocumentHost const* style_engine_host_of(Animatable& animatable)
{
    auto* element = as_if<DOM::Element>(animatable);
    return element ? CSS::style_engine_host_for_identified(*element) : nullptr;
}

static u32 style_node_of(Animatable& animatable)
{
    auto* element = as_if<DOM::Element>(animatable);
    return element ? element->style_node_id().value() : 0;
}

void Animatable::cancel_css_animations_and_transitions()
{
    if (!m_animations)
        return;

    GC::RootVector<AnimationRef> animations;
    RustFFI::animations_element_animations_cancel_css_animations_and_transitions(
        m_animations, style_engine_host_of(*this), style_node_of(*this), keep_animation_alive_in, in_execution_context_of_animation, &animations, web_animation_perform_host_effect);
}

void Animatable::cancel_css_animations_and_transitions_of(CSS::PseudoElement pseudo_element)
{
    auto slot = owner_slot(pseudo_element);
    if (!m_animations || !slot.has_value())
        return;

    GC::RootVector<AnimationRef> animations;
    RustFFI::animations_element_animations_cancel_css_animations_and_transitions_of_owner(
        m_animations, *slot, style_engine_host_of(*this), style_node_of(*this), keep_animation_alive_in, in_execution_context_of_animation, &animations, web_animation_perform_host_effect);
}

void Animatable::play_or_pause_css_animations_as_their_play_state_asks()
{
    if (!m_animations)
        return;

    struct Context {
        GC::RootVector<AnimationRef> animations;
        GC::Ref<DOM::Element> element;
    } context { {}, as<DOM::Element>(*this) };
    RustFFI::animations_element_animations_play_or_pause_css_animations(
        m_animations,
        [](void* context, RustFFI::AnimationCell const* animation) {
            keep_animation_alive_in(&static_cast<Context*>(context)->animations, animation);
        },
        [](void* context, RustFFI::AnimationCell const*, void (*run)(void*), void* run_context) {
            HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext execution_context { static_cast<Context*>(context)->element->document().relevant_settings_object() };
            run(run_context);
        },
        &context, web_animation_perform_host_effect);
}

bool Animatable::has_matching_transition_property_entry(Optional<CSS::PseudoElement> pseudo_element) const
{
    auto const& style = static_cast<DOM::Element const&>(*this).installed_style(pseudo_element);
    if (!style)
        return false;
    auto view = style.view();
    return CSS::StyleEngineFFI::style_engine_view_has_matching_transition_entries(&view, has_existing_transitions(pseudo_element));
}

bool Animatable::has_existing_transitions(Optional<CSS::PseudoElement> pseudo_element) const
{
    auto slot = owner_slot(pseudo_element);
    return m_animations && slot.has_value() && RustFFI::animations_element_animations_count(m_animations, RustFFI::ElementAnimationListKind::Transitions, *slot) != 0;
}

void Animatable::visit_edges(JS::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    if (!m_animations)
        return;
    RustFFI::animations_element_animations_for_each_host_cell(m_animations, &visitor, visit_host_cell);
}

bool Animatable::has_css_animations_or_transitions() const
{
    return m_animations && RustFFI::animations_element_animations_has_css_animations_or_transitions(m_animations);
}

bool Animatable::has_css_defined_animations(Optional<CSS::PseudoElement> pseudo_element) const
{
    auto slot = owner_slot(pseudo_element);
    return m_animations && slot.has_value() && RustFFI::animations_element_animations_count(m_animations, RustFFI::ElementAnimationListKind::CssAnimations, *slot) != 0;
}
