//! Writes the GL constants that the WebGL interfaces define, from the `const` members of their IDL, so that the
//! implementation names a value as the specifications do and cannot disagree with the constant that script reads.

use std::fmt::Write;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Constant {
    pub name: String,
    pub rust_type: &'static str,
    /// The value as the first definition of the constant spells it, which the generated constant keeps.
    pub spelling: String,
    pub value: i128,
}

/// A comment becomes a space, which keeps the words around it apart, and a string literal keeps only its quotes: both
/// can hold a `;` or a `const`, and neither holds a statement.
fn without_comments_and_string_contents(idl: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(idl.len());
    let mut rest = idl;
    while let Some(start) = rest.find(['/', '"']) {
        let (before, found) = rest.split_at(start);
        out.push_str(before);
        rest = if let Some(comment) = found.strip_prefix("//") {
            out.push(' ');
            comment.find('\n').map_or("", |end| &comment[end..])
        } else if let Some(comment) = found.strip_prefix("/*") {
            out.push(' ');
            comment.find("*/").map_or("", |end| &comment[end + 2..])
        } else if let Some(string) = found.strip_prefix('"') {
            out.push_str("\"\"");
            string.find('"').map_or("", |end| &string[end + 1..])
        } else {
            out.push('/');
            &found[1..]
        };
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
    out
}

/// The value of an integer of the IDL, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#prod-integer, whose spelling Rust reads as the
/// same integer: decimal digits without a leading zero, which makes an integer of the IDL octal, or hexadecimal digits
/// after `0x`.
fn integer_value(spelling: &str) -> Option<i128> {
    let digits = spelling.strip_prefix('-').unwrap_or(spelling);
    let magnitude = match digits.strip_prefix("0x") {
        Some(hex_digits) if hex_digits.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_hexdigit()) => {
            i128::from_str_radix(hex_digits, 16).ok()?
        }
        None if digits.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) && (digits == "0" || !digits.starts_with('0')) => {
            digits.parse::<i128>().ok()?
        }
        _ => return None,
    };
    // NB: The spelling is written to Rust as it is, where an unsigned type does not take the sign of -0.
    match (spelling.starts_with('-'), magnitude) {
        (true, 0) => None,
        (true, magnitude) => Some(-magnitude),
        (false, magnitude) => Some(magnitude),
    }
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#prod-ExtendedAttributeList
fn without_leading_extended_attributes(statement: &str) -> &str {
    let statement = statement.trim_start();
    statement
        .strip_prefix('[')
        .and_then(|attributes_and_member| attributes_and_member.split_once(']'))
        .map_or(statement, |(_attributes, member)| member)
}

fn parse_constant(statement: &str) -> Result<Constant, String> {
    let unreadable = || {
        let statement = statement.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
        format!("the WebGL constants cannot be read from the IDL statement {statement:?}")
    };
    let declaration = statement.strip_suffix(';').ok_or_else(unreadable)?;
    let (type_and_name, spelling) = declaration.split_once('=').ok_or_else(unreadable)?;
    let mut words = type_and_name.split_whitespace().skip(1);
    let (Some(idl_type), Some(name), None) = (words.next(), words.next(), words.next()) else {
        return Err(unreadable());
    };
    if !name.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || byte == b'_') {
        return Err(unreadable());
    }
    let (rust_type, values_of_type) = match idl_type {
        "GLenum" => ("u32", 0..=i128::from(u32::MAX)),
        "GLint64" => ("i64", i128::from(i64::MIN)..=i128::from(i64::MAX)),
        _ => {
            return Err(format!(
                "the WebGL constant {name} has the type {idl_type}, which has no Rust type yet"
            ));
        }
    };
    let spelling = spelling.trim();
    let value = integer_value(spelling)
        .filter(|value| values_of_type.contains(value))
        .ok_or_else(unreadable)?;
    Ok(Constant {
        name: name.to_string(),
        rust_type,
        spelling: spelling.to_string(),
        value,
    })
}

/// Several interfaces define the same constant, which then has to have the same value in each, however each spells
/// it.
pub fn collect_constants(idl: &str, constants: &mut Vec<Constant>) -> Result<(), String> {
    // NB: The first member of an interface follows a `{`, and every other one follows the `;` of the member before it.
    for statement in without_comments_and_string_contents(idl).split_inclusive([';', '{', '}']) {
        let statement = without_leading_extended_attributes(statement);
        if statement.split_whitespace().next() != Some("const") {
            continue;
        }
        let constant = parse_constant(statement)?;
        match constants.iter().find(|existing| existing.name == constant.name) {
            None => constants.push(constant),
            Some(existing) if existing.rust_type == constant.rust_type && existing.value == constant.value => {}
            Some(existing) => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "the WebGL constant {} is defined as the {} {} and as the {} {}",
                    constant.name, existing.rust_type, existing.spelling, constant.rust_type, constant.spelling
                ));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn write_constants(constants: &[Constant]) -> String {
    let mut out =
        String::from("// Generated by build.rs from the constants of the IDL files of Libraries/LibWeb/WebGL.\n\n");
    for constant in constants {
        writeln!(
            out,
            "pub(crate) const GL_{}: {} = {};",
            constant.name, constant.rust_type, constant.spelling
        )
        .unwrap();
    }
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn written_constants(idl_files: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
        let mut constants = Vec::new();
        for idl in idl_files {
            collect_constants(idl, &mut constants)?;
        }
        let written = write_constants(&constants);
        Ok(written.lines().skip(2).map(str::to_string).collect())
    }

    fn unreadable(statement: &str) -> String {
        format!("the WebGL constants cannot be read from the IDL statement {statement:?}")
    }

    #[test]
    fn constants_are_collected_once() {
        let idl_files = [
            "interface mixin A {\n    const GLenum DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT = 0x00000100;\n    const GLenum ZERO = 0;\n\
             // const GLenum NOT_THIS = 1;\n    const GLint64 TIMEOUT_IGNORED = -1; // forever\n    undefined f();\n};\n",
            "interface B {\n    const GLenum   ZERO   = 0;\n};\n",
        ];
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&idl_files).unwrap(),
            [
                "pub(crate) const GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT: u32 = 0x00000100;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_ZERO: u32 = 0;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_TIMEOUT_IGNORED: i64 = -1;",
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_constant_keeps_its_first_spelling_whatever_the_later_ones_are() {
        let idl_files = [
            "interface A { const GLenum DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT = 0x0100; };",
            "interface B { const GLenum DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT = 256; };",
            "interface C { const GLenum DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT = 0x00000100; };",
        ];
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&idl_files).unwrap(),
            ["pub(crate) const GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT: u32 = 0x0100;"]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_constant_has_one_value_and_one_type() {
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&["const GLenum ONE = 1;", "const GLenum ONE = 0x2;"]).unwrap_err(),
            "the WebGL constant ONE is defined as the u32 1 and as the u32 0x2"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&["const GLenum ONE = 1;", "const GLint64 ONE = 1;"]).unwrap_err(),
            "the WebGL constant ONE is defined as the u32 1 and as the i64 1"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn constants_are_read_by_statement_and_not_by_line() {
        let idl = "interface A { const GLenum ONE = 1; const GLenum TWO = 2;\n    const GLenum\n        THREE\n        =\n\
                   3;const GLenum FOUR=4;\n    undefined f(); const GLenum FIVE = 5 ; };";
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&[idl]).unwrap(),
            [
                "pub(crate) const GL_ONE: u32 = 1;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_TWO: u32 = 2;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_THREE: u32 = 3;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_FOUR: u32 = 4;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_FIVE: u32 = 5;",
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_constant_can_follow_extended_attributes() {
        let idl = "interface A {\n    [Exposed=Window] const GLenum ON_THE_SAME_LINE = 1;\n    \
                   [Exposed=(Window,Worker)]\n    const GLenum ON_THE_NEXT_LINE = 2;\n    \
                   [Exposed=Window]const GLenum WITHOUT_A_SPACE = 3;\n    \
                   [Exposed=Window] undefined f(long const);\n};";
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&[idl]).unwrap(),
            [
                "pub(crate) const GL_ON_THE_SAME_LINE: u32 = 1;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_ON_THE_NEXT_LINE: u32 = 2;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_WITHOUT_A_SPACE: u32 = 3;",
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&["interface A { [Exposed=Window] const GLenum NAMED = OTHER; };"]).unwrap_err(),
            unreadable("const GLenum NAMED = OTHER;")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn braces_that_are_not_of_an_interface_end_a_statement_too() {
        let idl = "dictionary D { long member = 1; };\ninterface A {\n    \
                   undefined f(optional D d = {}); const GLenum AFTER_A_DEFAULT_VALUE = 1;\n};\n\
                   namespace N { const GLenum IN_A_NAMESPACE = 2; };";
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&[idl]).unwrap(),
            [
                "pub(crate) const GL_AFTER_A_DEFAULT_VALUE: u32 = 1;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_IN_A_NAMESPACE: u32 = 2;",
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_line_can_end_with_a_carriage_return_before_its_line_feed() {
        let idl = "interface A {\r\n    const GLenum BEFORE = 0x10;\r\n    // const GLenum IN_A_LINE = 1;\r\n    \
                   const GLenum AFTER = 2;\r\n};\r\n";
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&[idl]).unwrap(),
            [
                "pub(crate) const GL_BEFORE: u32 = 0x10;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_AFTER: u32 = 2;",
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn comments_and_string_literals_define_no_constants() {
        let idl = "interface A {\n    /* const GLenum IN_A_BLOCK = 1; */\n    /*\n    const GLenum IN_A_LONG_BLOCK = 2;\n\
                   */\n    // const GLenum IN_A_LINE = 3;\n    const GLenum /* between */ KEPT = 4; // const GLenum AFTER = 5;\n\
                   attribute DOMString a = \"; const GLenum IN_A_STRING = 6;\"; const GLenum AFTER_A_STRING = 7;\n\
                   attribute DOMString b = \"//\"; const GLenum AFTER_A_STRING_WITH_SLASHES = 8;\n\
                   [Reflect=a/b] attribute DOMString c; const GLenum AFTER_A_SLASH = 9;\n};\n\
                   /* const GLenum IN_A_BLOCK_WITHOUT_AN_END = 10;";
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&[idl]).unwrap(),
            [
                "pub(crate) const GL_KEPT: u32 = 4;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_AFTER_A_STRING: u32 = 7;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_AFTER_A_STRING_WITH_SLASHES: u32 = 8;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_AFTER_A_SLASH: u32 = 9;",
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_value_is_within_the_range_of_its_type() {
        let idl = "const GLenum HIGHEST = 0xFFFFFFFF; const GLenum HIGHEST_IN_DECIMAL = 4294967295;\n\
                   const GLint64 LOWEST_OF_64_BITS = -9223372036854775808;\n\
                   const GLint64 LOWEST_OF_64_BITS_IN_HEXADECIMAL = -0x8000000000000000;\n\
                   const GLint64 HIGHEST_OF_64_BITS = 0x7fffffffffffffff;";
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&[idl]).unwrap(),
            [
                "pub(crate) const GL_HIGHEST: u32 = 0xFFFFFFFF;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_HIGHEST_IN_DECIMAL: u32 = 4294967295;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_LOWEST_OF_64_BITS: i64 = -9223372036854775808;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_LOWEST_OF_64_BITS_IN_HEXADECIMAL: i64 = -0x8000000000000000;",
                "pub(crate) const GL_HIGHEST_OF_64_BITS: i64 = 0x7fffffffffffffff;",
            ]
        );
        for statement in [
            "const GLenum TOO_HIGH = 0x100000000;",
            "const GLenum TOO_HIGH = 4294967296;",
            "const GLenum NEGATIVE = -1;",
            "const GLenum NEGATIVE_ZERO = -0;",
            "const GLint64 TOO_LOW = -9223372036854775809;",
            "const GLint64 TOO_LOW = -0x8000000000000001;",
            "const GLint64 TOO_HIGH = 9223372036854775808;",
            "const GLint64 TOO_HIGH_FOR_ANY_TYPE = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF;",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(written_constants(&[statement]).unwrap_err(), unreadable(statement));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_statement_that_cannot_be_read_is_named() {
        for statement in [
            "const GLenum NAMED = OTHER;",
            "const GLenum OCTAL = 010;",
            "const GLenum UPPER_CASE_PREFIX = 0X10;",
            "const GLenum WITHOUT_DIGITS = 0x;",
            "const GLenum SIGN_AFTER_PREFIX = 0x-1;",
            "const GLenum PLUS = +1;",
            "const GLenum WITHOUT_VALUE = ;",
            "const GLenum WITHOUT_VALUE;",
            "const GLenum = 1;",
            "const unsigned long TYPE_OF_TWO_WORDS = 1;",
            "const GLenum NOT-A-NAME = 1;",
            "const GLenum UNFINISHED = 1",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(written_constants(&[statement]).unwrap_err(), unreadable(statement));
        }
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&["interface A {\n    const GLenum UNFINISHED = 1\n};"]).unwrap_err(),
            unreadable("const GLenum UNFINISHED = 1 }")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&["interface A {\n    const GLenum\n        FIRST = 1,\n        SECOND = 2;\n};"])
                .unwrap_err(),
            unreadable("const GLenum FIRST = 1, SECOND = 2;")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            written_constants(&["const GLfloat HALF = 0.5;"]).unwrap_err(),
            "the WebGL constant HALF has the type GLfloat, which has no Rust type yet"
        );
    }
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Bindings/Rust/generate/webgl_proxy.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Writes the methods of the WebGL command recorder that follow from the signature of a GL function, which
//! src/web_gl/proxy/generated.rs includes: one per command, per object creation and per synchronous call of
//! GLFunctions.json. A method has the name and the arguments of the GL function, records the struct of the command
//! or makes the round trip of the call, and returns what the function returns.

use std::fmt::Write;

use crate::webgl_wire_model::{
    Argument, Category, FieldSpec, Function, PayloadFactor, WireStruct, WireType, rust_identifier,
    title_case_to_snake_case, wire_struct,
};

fn parameter_name(argument: &Argument) -> String {
    rust_identifier(&title_case_to_snake_case(&argument.name))
}

fn inline_data_name(argument: &Argument) -> String {
    format!("{}_inline_data", title_case_to_snake_case(&argument.name))
}

fn unsupported(function: &Function, argument: &Argument, what: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "the recorder has no method for {}, whose argument {} {what}",
        function.name, argument.name
    )
}

fn scalar_parameter_type(function: &Function, argument: &Argument) -> Result<&'static str, String> {
    match WireType::of(&argument.cpp_type) {
        // A GLboolean.
        Some(WireType::U8) => Ok("bool"),
        Some(WireType::DataSpan) | None => Err(unsupported(function, argument, "is not a plain value")),
        Some(wire_type) => Ok(wire_type.rust_type()),
    }
}

fn payload_size_expression(function: &Function, argument: &Argument) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut factors = Vec::new();
    for factor in function.payload_size(argument)? {
        match factor {
            PayloadFactor::Constant(constant) => factors.push(constant.to_string()),
            PayloadFactor::ColorBufferComponents(index) => factors.push(format!(
                "if {} == GL_COLOR {{ 4 }} else {{ 1 }}",
                parameter_name(&function.arguments[index])
            )),
            PayloadFactor::Argument(index) => {
                let counted_by = &function.arguments[index];
                let name = parameter_name(counted_by);
                match WireType::of(&counted_by.cpp_type) {
                    Some(WireType::I32) => factors.push(format!("i64::from({name})")),
                    Some(WireType::I64) => factors.push(name),
                    _ => {
                        return Err(unsupported(
                            function,
                            argument,
                            &format!("is counted by {}", counted_by.name),
                        ));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(format!("payload_size(&[{}])", factors.join(", ")))
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Inputs {
    parameters: Vec<String>,
    statements: Vec<String>,
    inline_data: Option<String>,
    /// `None` for a field that has the name of the parameter it is from.
    field_values: Vec<(String, Option<String>)>,
}

impl Inputs {
    fn add_inline_data(&mut self, function: &Function, argument: &Argument, data: String) -> Result<(), String> {
        if self.inline_data.is_some() {
            return Err(unsupported(function, argument, "is a second one that points at data"));
        }
        let name = inline_data_name(argument);
        self.statements.push(format!("let {name} = {data};"));
        self.inline_data = Some(name);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn inline_data(&self) -> &str {
        self.inline_data.as_deref().unwrap_or("InlineData::NONE")
    }

    fn parameter_list(&self) -> String {
        self.parameters
            .iter()
            .map(|parameter| format!(", {parameter}"))
            .collect()
    }
}

fn inputs(function: &Function, struct_path: &str, fields: &[FieldSpec]) -> Result<Inputs, String> {
    let mut inputs = Inputs::default();
    for (index, argument) in function.arguments.iter().enumerate() {
        if argument.is_out {
            continue;
        }
        let name = parameter_name(argument);
        let span = format!("DataSpan::following::<{struct_path}>({})", inline_data_name(argument));
        let fields_of_argument = fields.iter().filter(|field| field.argument == Some(index));
        if argument.is_string {
            inputs.parameters.push(format!("{name}: &[u8]"));
            inputs.add_inline_data(
                function,
                argument,
                format!("InlineData::NulTerminated(until_nul({name}))"),
            )?;
            inputs.field_values.push((name, Some(span)));
        } else if argument.is_offset {
            inputs.parameters.push(format!("{name}: i64"));
            inputs.field_values.push((name, None));
        } else if argument.is_object && !argument.is_pointer() {
            inputs.parameters.push(format!("{name}: u32"));
            inputs.field_values.push((name, None));
        } else if argument.payload.is_some() {
            if !argument.is_const_pointer() {
                return Err(unsupported(function, argument, "points at data that is not const"));
            }
            let size = payload_size_expression(function, argument)?;
            let data = if argument.is_object {
                inputs.parameters.push(format!("{name}: &[u32]"));
                format!("leading_bytes(bytes_of({name}), {size})")
            } else if argument.is_nullable {
                inputs.parameters.push(format!("{name}: Option<&[u8]>"));
                format!("{name}.map(|{name}| leading_bytes({name}, {size})).unwrap_or_default()")
            } else {
                inputs.parameters.push(format!("{name}: &[u8]"));
                format!("leading_bytes({name}, {size})")
            };
            inputs.add_inline_data(function, argument, format!("InlineData::Bytes({data})"))?;
            for field in fields_of_argument {
                if field.cpp_type == "bool" {
                    inputs
                        .field_values
                        .push((rust_identifier(&field.name), Some(format!("{name}.is_some()"))));
                }
            }
            inputs.field_values.push((name, Some(span)));
        } else if argument.is_pointer() {
            return Err(unsupported(function, argument, "is a pointer without a size"));
        } else {
            let parameter_type = scalar_parameter_type(function, argument)?;
            inputs.parameters.push(format!("{name}: {parameter_type}"));
            let value = (argument.cpp_type == "GLboolean").then(|| format!("u8::from({name})"));
            inputs.field_values.push((name, value));
        }
    }
    Ok(inputs)
}

fn struct_expression(struct_path: &str, layout: &WireStruct, field_values: &[(String, Option<String>)]) -> String {
    if layout.fields.is_empty() {
        return format!("{struct_path}::ZEROED");
    }
    let mut expression = format!("{struct_path} {{ ");
    for (name, value) in field_values {
        match value {
            Some(value) => write!(expression, "{name}: {value}, ").unwrap(),
            None => write!(expression, "{name}, ").unwrap(),
        }
    }
    if layout.has_unused_bytes() {
        write!(expression, "..{struct_path}::ZEROED ").unwrap();
    }
    expression.push('}');
    expression
}

fn check_fields_have_values(
    function: &Function,
    layout: &WireStruct,
    field_values: &[(String, Option<String>)],
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut field_names: Vec<String> = layout
        .fields
        .iter()
        .map(|field| rust_identifier(&field.spec.name))
        .collect();
    let mut value_names: Vec<String> = field_values.iter().map(|(name, _)| name.clone()).collect();
    field_names.sort();
    value_names.sort();
    if field_names == value_names {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(format!(
            "the recorder would fill the fields {value_names:?} of {}, which has the fields {field_names:?}",
            function.name
        ))
    }
}

fn write_statements(out: &mut String, statements: &[String]) {
    for statement in statements {
        writeln!(out, "        {statement}").unwrap();
    }
}

fn write_command_method(out: &mut String, function: &Function) -> Result<(), String> {
    let name = function.command_name();
    let struct_path = format!("commands::{name}");
    let fields = function.command_fields()?;
    let layout = wire_struct(format!("Commands::{name}"), fields.clone())?;
    let inputs = inputs(function, &struct_path, &fields)?;
    check_fields_have_values(function, &layout, &inputs.field_values)?;

    writeln!(
        out,
        "    pub(crate) fn {}(&self{}) {{",
        function.method_name(),
        inputs.parameter_list()
    )
    .unwrap();
    write_statements(out, &inputs.statements);
    let command = struct_expression(&struct_path, &layout, &inputs.field_values);
    match &inputs.inline_data {
        Some(inline_data) => writeln!(out, "        self.record_with_data(&{command}, {inline_data});").unwrap(),
        None => writeln!(out, "        self.record(&{command});").unwrap(),
    }
    out.push_str("    }\n\n");
    Ok(())
}

/// The recorder allocates the ids of the objects, so that it does not have to wait for the replayer to create them.
fn write_gen_method(out: &mut String, function: &Function) -> Result<(), String> {
    let name = function.command_name();
    let struct_path = format!("commands::{name}");
    let fields = function.command_fields()?;
    let layout = wire_struct(format!("Commands::{name}"), fields.clone())?;
    let method_name = function.method_name();

    if !function.returns_void() {
        let mut inputs = inputs(function, &struct_path, &fields)?;
        if inputs.inline_data.is_some() {
            return Err(format!(
                "the recorder has no method for {}, which creates an object from data",
                function.name
            ));
        }
        inputs.field_values.insert(0, ("id".to_string(), None));
        check_fields_have_values(function, &layout, &inputs.field_values)?;
        writeln!(
            out,
            "    pub(crate) fn {method_name}(&self{}) -> u32 {{",
            inputs.parameter_list()
        )
        .unwrap();
        out.push_str("        let id = self.allocate_object_id();\n");
        let command = struct_expression(&struct_path, &layout, &inputs.field_values);
        writeln!(out, "        self.record(&{command});").unwrap();
        out.push_str("        id\n    }\n\n");
        return Ok(());
    }

    let [count, ids] = function.arguments.as_slice() else {
        return Err(format!(
            "the recorder has no method for {}, which is not a count and ids",
            function.name
        ));
    };
    if WireType::of(&count.cpp_type) != Some(WireType::I32) || ids.cpp_type != "GLuint*" {
        return Err(format!(
            "the recorder has no method for {}, which is not a count and ids",
            function.name
        ));
    }
    let count_name = parameter_name(count);
    let ids_name = parameter_name(ids);
    let inline_data = inline_data_name(ids);
    let field_values = [
        (count_name, Some(format!("gen_count({ids_name})"))),
        (
            ids_name.clone(),
            Some(format!("DataSpan::following::<{struct_path}>({inline_data})")),
        ),
    ];
    check_fields_have_values(function, &layout, &field_values)?;
    writeln!(out, "    pub(crate) fn {method_name}(&self, {ids_name}: &mut [u32]) {{").unwrap();
    writeln!(out, "        if {ids_name}.is_empty() {{").unwrap();
    out.push_str("            return;\n        }\n");
    writeln!(out, "        for id in &mut *{ids_name} {{").unwrap();
    out.push_str("            *id = self.allocate_object_id();\n        }\n");
    writeln!(
        out,
        "        let {inline_data} = InlineData::Bytes(bytes_of({ids_name}));"
    )
    .unwrap();
    let command = struct_expression(&struct_path, &layout, &field_values);
    writeln!(out, "        self.record_with_data(&{command}, {inline_data});").unwrap();
    out.push_str("    }\n\n");
    Ok(())
}

fn output_element_type(function: &Function, argument: &Argument) -> Result<&'static str, String> {
    match argument.pointee_cpp_type().as_str() {
        "GLchar" | "GLboolean" => Ok("u8"),
        "GLint" | "GLsizei" => Ok("i32"),
        "GLuint" | "GLenum" => Ok("u32"),
        "GLfloat" => Ok("f32"),
        "GLint64" => Ok("i64"),
        other => Err(unsupported(function, argument, &format!("is a buffer of {other}"))),
    }
}

/// A value that a synchronous call returns: the return value of the GL function, or what it stores through a
/// pointer to one value.
struct ScalarOutput {
    name: String,
    rust_type: &'static str,
    value: String,
}

fn scalar_output(function: &Function, field: &FieldSpec) -> Result<ScalarOutput, String> {
    let name = rust_identifier(&field.name);
    let no_rust_type = || {
        format!(
            "the recorder has no method for {}, which returns a {}",
            function.name, field.cpp_type
        )
    };
    let (rust_type, value) = match WireType::of(&field.cpp_type).ok_or_else(no_rust_type)? {
        WireType::DataSpan | WireType::Bool => return Err(no_rust_type()),
        // A GLboolean.
        WireType::U8 => ("bool", format!("reply.{name} != 0")),
        wire_type => (wire_type.rust_type(), format!("reply.{name}")),
    };
    Ok(ScalarOutput { name, rust_type, value })
}

fn write_sync_method(out: &mut String, output_structs: &mut String, function: &Function) -> Result<(), String> {
    let name = function.command_name();
    let struct_path = format!("sync_calls::{name}Request");
    let request_fields = function.sync_request_fields()?;
    let request_layout = wire_struct(format!("SyncCalls::{name}::Request"), request_fields.clone())?;
    let mut inputs = inputs(function, &struct_path, &request_fields)?;
    check_fields_have_values(function, &request_layout, &inputs.field_values)?;

    let mut scalar_outputs = Vec::new();
    let mut copies = Vec::new();
    for field in function.sync_reply_fields() {
        let argument = field.argument.map(|index| &function.arguments[index]);
        match argument {
            Some(argument) if argument.payload.is_some() => {
                let parameter = parameter_name(argument);
                let element_type = output_element_type(function, argument)?;
                inputs.parameters.push(format!("{parameter}: &mut [{element_type}]"));
                let size = payload_size_expression(function, argument)?;
                copies.push(format!(
                    "copy_reply_data(reply_bytes, reply.{}, leading_bytes_mut(bytes_of_mut({parameter}), {size}));",
                    rust_identifier(&field.name)
                ));
            }
            _ => scalar_outputs.push(scalar_output(function, &field)?),
        }
    }

    let (return_type, output) = match scalar_outputs.as_slice() {
        [] => (String::new(), None),
        [output] => (format!(" -> {}", output.rust_type), Some(output.value.clone())),
        outputs => {
            let struct_name = format!("{name}Outputs");
            writeln!(output_structs, "/// What `{}` returns.", function.name).unwrap();
            output_structs.push_str("#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]\n");
            writeln!(output_structs, "pub(crate) struct {struct_name} {{").unwrap();
            let mut values = String::new();
            for output in outputs {
                writeln!(output_structs, "    pub(crate) {}: {},", output.name, output.rust_type).unwrap();
                write!(values, "{}: {}, ", output.name, output.value).unwrap();
            }
            output_structs.push_str("}\n\n");
            (
                format!(" -> {struct_name}"),
                Some(format!("{struct_name} {{ {values}}}")),
            )
        }
    };

    writeln!(
        out,
        "    pub(crate) fn {}(&self{}){return_type} {{",
        function.method_name(),
        inputs.parameter_list()
    )
    .unwrap();
    write_statements(out, &inputs.statements);
    let request = struct_expression(&struct_path, &request_layout, &inputs.field_values);
    writeln!(out, "        let request = {request};").unwrap();
    let reply = if output.is_some() || !copies.is_empty() {
        "reply"
    } else {
        "_reply"
    };
    let reply_bytes = if copies.is_empty() {
        "_reply_bytes"
    } else {
        "reply_bytes"
    };
    writeln!(
        out,
        "        self.sync_call(&request, {}, |{reply}, {reply_bytes}| {{",
        inputs.inline_data()
    )
    .unwrap();
    for copy in &copies {
        writeln!(out, "            {copy}").unwrap();
    }
    if let Some(output) = &output {
        writeln!(out, "            {output}").unwrap();
    }
    // NB: Without a reply, which is when the context is lost, a call returns zeros and leaves the buffers alone.
    out.push_str(if output.is_some() {
        "        })\n        .unwrap_or_default()\n"
    } else {
        "        });\n"
    });
    out.push_str("    }\n\n");
    Ok(())
}

pub fn write_proxy(functions: &[Function]) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut methods = String::new();
    let mut output_structs = String::new();
    for function in functions {
        match function.category {
            Category::Command => write_command_method(&mut methods, function)?,
            Category::Gen => write_gen_method(&mut methods, function)?,
            Category::Sync => write_sync_method(&mut methods, &mut output_structs, function)?,
            // Written by hand in src/web_gl/proxy/custom.rs.
            Category::Custom | Category::BuiltinCommand => {}
        }
    }

    let mut out = String::from("// Generated by build.rs from Libraries/LibCompositing/WebGL/GLFunctions.json.\n\n");
    out.push_str(&output_structs);
    out.push_str(
        "#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = \"the methods have the arguments of the GL functions\")]\n",
    );
    out.push_str("impl<T: Transport> Proxy<T> {\n");
    out.push_str(methods.trim_end());
    out.push_str("\n}\n");
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::webgl_wire_model::parse_functions;

    fn proxy_for(function_json: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        write_proxy(&parse_functions(&format!("[{function_json}]")).unwrap())
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_size_of_a_payload_is_the_product_that_the_json_gives() {
        let proxy = proxy_for(
            r#"{"name": "glUniformMatrix4fv", "return": "void", "category": "command", "args": [
                {"type": "GLint", "name": "location"},
                {"type": "GLsizei", "name": "count"},
                {"type": "GLboolean", "name": "transpose"},
                {"type": "GLfloat const*", "name": "value", "payload": "count * 16 * sizeof(GLfloat)"}]}"#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(proxy.contains(
            "pub(crate) fn uniform_matrix4fv(&self, location: i32, count: i32, transpose: bool, value: &[u8]) {"
        ));
        assert!(proxy.contains("leading_bytes(value, payload_size(&[i64::from(count), 16, 4]))"));
        assert!(proxy.contains("transpose: u8::from(transpose), value: DataSpan::following::<"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_synchronous_call_returns_its_outputs_and_fills_its_buffers() {
        let proxy = proxy_for(
            r#"{"name": "glGetActiveAttrib", "return": "void", "category": "sync", "args": [
                {"type": "GLuint", "name": "program", "object": true},
                {"type": "GLsizei", "name": "bufSize"},
                {"type": "GLsizei*", "name": "length", "out": true},
                {"type": "GLenum*", "name": "type", "out": true},
                {"type": "GLchar*", "name": "name", "out": true, "payload": "bufSize * sizeof(GLchar)"}]}"#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(proxy.contains(
            "pub(crate) struct GetActiveAttribOutputs {\n    pub(crate) length: i32,\n    pub(crate) r#type: u32,\n}"
        ));
        assert!(proxy.contains(
            "pub(crate) fn get_active_attrib(&self, program: u32, buf_size: i32, name: &mut [u8]) -> GetActiveAttribOutputs {"
        ));
        assert!(proxy.contains("copy_reply_data(reply_bytes, reply.name, leading_bytes_mut(bytes_of_mut(name), payload_size(&[i64::from(buf_size), 1])));"));
        assert!(proxy.contains("GetActiveAttribOutputs { length: reply.length, r#type: reply.r#type, }"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn what_the_recorder_cannot_serialize_is_rejected() {
        let two_payloads = proxy_for(
            r#"{"name": "glTwo", "return": "void", "category": "command", "args": [
                {"type": "GLsizei", "name": "n"},
                {"type": "GLint const*", "name": "a", "payload": "n * sizeof(GLint)"},
                {"type": "GLint const*", "name": "b", "payload": "n * sizeof(GLint)"}]}"#,
        );
        assert!(
            two_payloads
                .unwrap_err()
                .contains("is a second one that points at data")
        );
        let unknown_size = proxy_for(
            r#"{"name": "glSized", "return": "void", "category": "command", "args": [
                {"type": "GLint const*", "name": "a", "payload": "strlen(a)"}]}"#,
        );
        assert!(unknown_size.unwrap_err().contains("the size \"strlen(a)\""));
        let unknown_element = proxy_for(
            r#"{"name": "glGetDoubles", "return": "void", "category": "sync", "args": [
                {"type": "GLsizei", "name": "n"},
                {"type": "GLdouble*", "name": "values", "out": true, "payload": "n * sizeof(GLint64)"}]}"#,
        );
        assert!(unknown_element.unwrap_err().contains("is a buffer of GLdouble"));
    }
}

//! Numbers in the messages of exceptions, written as LibWeb's C++ wrote them.

use core::fmt::LowerExp;

/// The number as AK's formatter writes it for "{}", which the messages of the C++ had: the shortest digits that
/// read back as the number, in the notation of Number::toString() of ECMAScript.
pub(crate) fn ak_formatted(number: impl LowerExp) -> String {
    let scientific = format!("{number:e}");
    let (sign, scientific) = match scientific.strip_prefix('-') {
        Some(magnitude) => ("-", magnitude),
        None => ("", scientific.as_str()),
    };
    let (mantissa, exponent) = scientific
        .split_once('e')
        .expect("a number in scientific notation has an exponent");
    let exponent: i32 = exponent.parse().expect("the exponent is an integer");
    let digits: String = mantissa.chars().filter(|character| *character != '.').collect();
    let digit_count = i32::try_from(digits.len()).expect("a number has few digits");
    let zeros = |count: i32| "0".repeat(usize::try_from(count).expect("the count is not negative"));

    let unsigned = if !(-6..=20).contains(&exponent) {
        let (first, rest) = digits.split_at(1);
        let fraction = if rest.is_empty() {
            String::new()
        } else {
            format!(".{rest}")
        };
        let exponent_sign = if exponent < 0 { '-' } else { '+' };
        format!("{first}{fraction}e{exponent_sign}{}", exponent.unsigned_abs())
    } else if exponent < 0 {
        format!("0.{}{digits}", zeros(-exponent - 1))
    } else if digit_count <= exponent + 1 {
        format!("{digits}{}", zeros(exponent + 1 - digit_count))
    } else {
        let (integer, fraction) = digits.split_at(usize::try_from(exponent + 1).expect("the exponent is not negative"));
        format!("{integer}.{fraction}")
    };
    format!("{sign}{unsigned}")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::ak_formatted;

    #[test]
    fn numbers_are_formatted_as_ak_formats_them() {
        // NB: What AK's "{}" wrote for these numbers, which a C++ program printed.
        let floats: [(f32, &str); 14] = [
            (-1.0, "-1"),
            (-0.5, "-0.5"),
            (-0.1, "-0.1"),
            (-1e30, "-1e+30"),
            (-1e-7, "-1e-7"),
            (-123_456_789.0, "-123456790"),
            (-3.402_823_5e38, "-3.4028235e+38"),
            (-1.175_494_4e-38, "-1.1754944e-38"),
            (-0.333_333_3, "-0.3333333"),
            (-16_777_217.0, "-16777216"),
            (-1e7, "-10000000"),
            (-1e16, "-10000000000000000"),
            (-100_000.0, "-100000"),
            (-0.0001, "-0.0001"),
        ];
        for (number, formatted) in floats {
            assert_eq!(ak_formatted(number), formatted);
        }
        let doubles: [(f64, &str); 10] = [
            (-1.0, "-1"),
            (-0.1, "-0.1"),
            (-1e300, "-1e+300"),
            (-1e-7, "-1e-7"),
            (-123_456_789.123, "-123456789.123"),
            (-1e21, "-1e+21"),
            (-1e22, "-1e+22"),
            (-0.0001, "-0.0001"),
            (-1e16, "-10000000000000000"),
            (-1e17, "-100000000000000000"),
        ];
        for (number, formatted) in doubles {
            assert_eq!(ak_formatted(number), formatted);
        }
    }
}

//! https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#the-animatable-interface-mixin

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, MarkedVec, Object};
use libweb_rust::AnimationRecordRef;
use libweb_rust::web_animations::{
    element_node_document, sort_in_composite_order, web_animation_compare_elements_in_tree_order,
};

use super::animation::{
    AnyAnimation, TimelineRangeValue, animation_object, parse_timeline_range_edge, perform_host_effect,
    realm_of_element,
};
use super::animation_timeline::{AnyAnimationTimeline, element_of_wrapper};
use super::keyframe_effect::{
    KeyframeEffect, KeyframeEffectOptions, KeyframesArgument, UnrestrictedDoubleOrKeyframeEffectOptions,
    process_a_keyframes_argument, pseudo_element_parsing,
};
use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_animation_for_each_associated_animation(
        node_wrapper: *mut c_void,
        subtree: bool,
        context: *mut c_void,
        on_animation: unsafe extern "C" fn(context: *mut c_void, animation: *const c_void),
    );
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#dictdef-keyframeanimationoptions
pub(crate) struct KeyframeAnimationOptions {
    pub(crate) parent: KeyframeEffectOptions,
    pub(crate) id: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) timeline: Option<Option<AnyAnimationTimeline>>,
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-keyframeanimationoptions-rangestart
    pub(crate) range_start: TimelineRangeValue,
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-keyframeanimationoptions-rangeend
    pub(crate) range_end: TimelineRangeValue,
}

/// The union (unrestricted double or KeyframeAnimationOptions) of the options of Animatable.animate().
pub(crate) enum UnrestrictedDoubleOrKeyframeAnimationOptions {
    UnrestrictedDouble(f64),
    KeyframeAnimationOptions(KeyframeAnimationOptions),
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#dom-animatable-animate
pub(crate) fn animate(
    this: &CppInterface,
    cx: &mut CallContext,
    keyframes: Option<Gc<Object>>,
    options: UnrestrictedDoubleOrKeyframeAnimationOptions,
) -> WebIdlResult<AnyAnimation> {
    let vm = cx.vm();

    // 1. Let target be the object on which this method was called.
    let target = element_of_wrapper(*this);

    // INTEROP: Like Chrome, the keyframes are processed before the range is parsed, so the keyframes' getters run first.
    let keyframes = process_a_keyframes_argument(vm, keyframes)?;

    // NB: The getters of the keyframes can move the target to another document, whose default document timeline the
    //     animation then gets.
    let document = element_node_document(target);
    let realm = realm_of_element(target);

    let (effect_options, animation_options) = match options {
        UnrestrictedDoubleOrKeyframeAnimationOptions::UnrestrictedDouble(duration) => (
            UnrestrictedDoubleOrKeyframeEffectOptions::UnrestrictedDouble(duration),
            None,
        ),
        UnrestrictedDoubleOrKeyframeAnimationOptions::KeyframeAnimationOptions(options) => (
            UnrestrictedDoubleOrKeyframeEffectOptions::KeyframeEffectOptions(options.parent),
            Some((options.id, options.timeline, options.range_start, options.range_end)),
        ),
    };

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-keyframeanimationoptions-rangestart
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-keyframeanimationoptions-rangeend
    let mut timeline_option = None;
    let mut id = None;
    let mut range = None;
    if let Some((options_id, options_timeline, range_start, range_end)) = animation_options {
        range = Some((
            parse_timeline_range_edge(document, range_start, false)?,
            parse_timeline_range_edge(document, range_end, true)?,
        ));
        timeline_option = options_timeline;
        id = Some(options_id);
    }

    // 2. Construct a new KeyframeEffect object, effect, in the relevant Realm of target by using the same procedure as
    //    the KeyframeEffect(target, keyframes, options) constructor, passing target as the target argument, and the
    //    keyframes and options arguments as supplied.
    //
    //    If the above procedure causes an exception to be thrown, propagate the exception and abort this procedure.
    let mut effect_cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);
    let effect = KeyframeEffect::construct_for_target(
        &mut effect_cx,
        target.as_ptr(),
        KeyframesArgument::Processed(keyframes),
        effect_options,
    )?;

    // 3. If options is a KeyframeAnimationOptions object, let timeline be the timeline member of options or, if
    //    timeline member of options is missing, the default document timeline of the node document of the element on
    //    which this method was called.
    let timeline = match timeline_option {
        Some(timeline) => timeline.map(|timeline| timeline.record().clone()),
        None => Some(libweb_rust::web_animations::TimelineRecordRef::default_of_document(
            document,
        )),
    };

    // 4. Construct a new Animation object, animation, in the relevant Realm of target by using the same procedure as
    //    the Animation() constructor, passing effect and timeline as arguments of the same name.
    let animation = super::animation::Animation::create(vm, realm, Some(effect.effect().record()), timeline.as_ref());

    // 5. If options is a KeyframeAnimationOptions object, assign the value of the id member of options to animation’s
    //    id attribute.
    if let Some(id) = id {
        animation.record().set_dom_id(&id);
    }

    // 6. Run the procedure to play an animation for animation with the auto-rewind flag set to true.
    animation
        .record()
        .play_an_animation(perform_host_effect)
        .map_err(|exception| match exception {
            libweb_rust::web_animations::AnimationException::InvalidState(message) => {
                Exception::Dom("InvalidStateError", Utf16String::from_utf8(message))
            }
            libweb_rust::web_animations::AnimationException::TypeError(message) => Exception::type_error(message),
        })?;

    if let Some((start, end)) = range {
        animation.record().set_range_edge(false, start, perform_host_effect);
        animation.record().set_range_edge(true, end, perform_host_effect);
    }

    // 7. Return animation.
    Ok(AnyAnimation::Animation(animation))
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#dictdef-getanimationsoptions
pub(crate) struct GetAnimationsOptions {
    pub(crate) subtree: bool,
    pub(crate) pseudo_element: Option<Utf16String>,
}

/// https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#dom-animatable-getanimations
pub(crate) fn get_animations<'vm>(
    this: &CppInterface,
    cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
    options: GetAnimationsOptions,
) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, AnyAnimation>> {
    // 1. Let object be the object on which this method was called.
    // 2. Let pseudoElement be the result of pseudo-element parsing applied to pseudoElement of options, or null if
    //    options is not passed.
    let _pseudo_element = pseudo_element_parsing(options.pseudo_element.as_ref())?;

    // 3. If pseudoElement is not null, then let target be the pseudo-element identified by pseudoElement with object
    //    as the originating element. Otherwise, let target be object.
    // FIXME: We can't refer to pseudo-elements directly, and they also can't be animated yet.

    // 4. If options is passed with subtree set to true, then return the set of relevant animations for a subtree of
    //    target. Otherwise, return the set of relevant animations for target.
    // The list returned by the above algorithm is sorted using the composite order described for the associated
    // animations of effects in § 5.4.2 The effect stack.
    Ok(sorted_relevant_animations(this, options.subtree, cx))
}

/// The relevant animations of the element or the document or shadow root `node`, and those of its subtree where
/// `subtree` is set, after the pending style changes are applied, sorted in composite order.
pub(super) fn sorted_relevant_animations<'vm>(
    node: &CppInterface,
    subtree: bool,
    cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
) -> MarkedVec<'vm, AnyAnimation> {
    unsafe extern "C" fn on_animation(context: *mut c_void, animation: *const c_void) {
        // SAFETY: The context is the list below, and LibWeb passes animations that it holds references to.
        let animations = unsafe { &mut *context.cast::<Vec<AnimationRecordRef>>() };
        animations.push(unsafe { AnimationRecordRef::retained_from_host(animation) });
    }
    let mut relevant_animations: Vec<AnimationRecordRef> = Vec::new();
    // SAFETY: The wrapper is live, and the callback receives the list for as long as the call runs.
    unsafe {
        web_animation_for_each_associated_animation(
            node.wrapper().as_ptr().cast(),
            subtree,
            (&raw mut relevant_animations).cast(),
            on_animation,
        );
    }
    relevant_animations.retain(AnimationRecordRef::is_exposed_relevant);

    sort_in_composite_order(&mut relevant_animations, web_animation_compare_elements_in_tree_order);

    let vm = cx.vm();
    let animations = MarkedVec::new(vm);
    for animation in &relevant_animations {
        animations.push(animation_object(vm, animation));
    }
    animations
}

//! AnimationEffect, https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#the-animationeffect-interface

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
pub(crate) use libcompositing_rust::animation_timing::{FillMode, PlaybackDirection};
use libcompositing_rust::animation_timing::{SpecifiedIterationDuration, TimeValue};
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Trace, Visitor};

    animation_relevant_realm, current_time_for_observation, effect_timing_changed, update_style_if_needed,

use super::keyframe_effect::KeyframeEffect;
use crate::bindings::conversions::ToJs;

use crate::css::css_numeric_value::{AnyCSSNumericValue, CSSNumberish};
use core::ops::Deref;
use libjs_rust::api::{ThrowCompletionOr, Value, Vm};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_animation_effect_visit_host_cells(effect: *const c_void, visitor: *mut c_void);
}

/// The union (unrestricted double or CSSNumericValue or DOMString) of the duration member of EffectTiming.
pub(crate) enum UnrestrictedDoubleOrCSSNumericValueOrDOMString {
    UnrestrictedDouble(f64),
    CSSNumericValue(AnyCSSNumericValue),
    DOMString(Utf16String),
}

/// The union (unrestricted double or DOMString) of the duration member of OptionalEffectTiming.
pub(crate) enum UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMString {
    UnrestrictedDouble(f64),
    DOMString(Utf16String),
}

// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#dictdef-effecttiming
pub(crate) struct EffectTiming {
    pub(crate) delay: f64,
    pub(crate) direction: PlaybackDirection,
    pub(crate) duration: UnrestrictedDoubleOrCSSNumericValueOrDOMString,
    pub(crate) easing: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) end_delay: f64,
    pub(crate) fill: FillMode,
    pub(crate) iteration_start: f64,
    pub(crate) iterations: f64,
}

// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#dictdef-computedeffecttiming
pub(crate) struct ComputedEffectTiming {
    pub(crate) parent: EffectTiming,
    pub(crate) active_duration: Option<CSSNumberish>,
    pub(crate) current_iteration: Option<Option<f64>>,
    pub(crate) end_time: Option<CSSNumberish>,
    pub(crate) local_time: Option<Option<CSSNumberish>>,
    pub(crate) progress: Option<Option<f64>>,
}

// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#dictdef-optionaleffecttiming
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct OptionalEffectTiming {
    pub(crate) delay: Option<f64>,
    pub(crate) direction: Option<PlaybackDirection>,
    pub(crate) duration: Option<UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMString>,
    pub(crate) easing: Option<Utf16String>,
    pub(crate) end_delay: Option<f64>,
    pub(crate) fill: Option<FillMode>,
    pub(crate) iteration_start: Option<f64>,
    pub(crate) iterations: Option<f64>,
}

/// Whether the UTF-16 code units are the ASCII text.
pub(crate) fn units_equal(units: &[u16], text: &str) -> bool {
    units.iter().copied().eq(text.encode_utf16())
}

// https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#the-animationeffect-interface
pub(crate) struct AnimationEffect {
    record: EffectRecordRef,
}

// SAFETY: Visits the cells of the host that keep the record's associated animation and target element alive, as the
//         host visits them.
unsafe impl Trace for AnimationEffect {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        // SAFETY: The effect holds a reference to the record, and the visitor is one LibGC passed in.
        unsafe { web_animation_effect_visit_host_cells(self.record.as_host_ptr(), visitor.as_raw().cast()) };
    }
}

impl Wrappable for AnimationEffect {
    const TRACED_ON_OWNER_THREAD_ONLY: bool = true;
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        self.relevant_realm()
    }
}

impl AnimationEffect {
    /// The part as an AnimationEffect of the object of the effect whose state `record` holds.
    pub(crate) fn from_record(record: EffectRecordRef) -> Self {
        Self { record }
    }

    /// The effect's state, which lives as long as the effect.
    pub(crate) fn record(&self) -> &EffectRecordRef {
        &self.record
    }

    /// The realm of the relevant global object of the associated animation, if there is one.
    pub(crate) fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        animation_relevant_realm(&self.record.associated_animation()?)
    }

    pub(crate) fn update_style_if_needed(&self) {
        if let Some(animation) = self.record.associated_animation() {
            update_style_if_needed(&animation);
        }
    }

    fn associated_animation(&self) -> Option<AnimationRecordRef> {
        self.record.associated_animation()
    }

    // https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#dom-animationeffect-gettiming
    pub(crate) fn get_timing(&self, _cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<EffectTiming> {
        self.update_style_if_needed();

        // Returns the specified timing properties for this animation effect.
        let specified = self.record.specified_timing();
        let timing = self.record.timing();
        Ok(EffectTiming {
            delay: specified.start_delay,
            direction: timing.playback_direction,
            duration: if specified.iteration_duration.is_auto {
                UnrestrictedDoubleOrCSSNumericValueOrDOMString::DOMString(Utf16String::from_ascii(b"auto"))
            } else {
                UnrestrictedDoubleOrCSSNumericValueOrDOMString::UnrestrictedDouble(
                    specified.iteration_duration.milliseconds,
                )
            },
            easing: self.record.timing_function_serialization(),
            end_delay: specified.end_delay,
            fill: timing.fill_mode,
            iteration_start: specified.iteration_start,
            iterations: specified.iteration_count,
        })
    }

    // https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#dom-animationeffect-getcomputedtiming
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-animationeffect-getcomputedtiming
    pub(crate) fn get_computed_timing(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<ComputedEffectTiming> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        self.update_style_if_needed();

        // NB: The local time is the current time of the associated animation as script observes it.
        let local_time = self
            .associated_animation()
            .and_then(|animation| current_time_for_observation(&animation));

        // Returns the calculated timing properties for this animation effect.

        // Although some of the attributes of the object returned by getTiming() and getComputedTiming() are common,
        // their values can differ in the following ways:

        //     - duration: while getTiming() can return the string auto, getComputedTiming() must return a number
        //       corresponding to the calculated value of the iteration duration as defined in the description of the
        //       duration member of the EffectTiming interface.
        //
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-animationeffect-getcomputedtiming
        // The description of the duration attribute of the object needs to indicate that if timing.duration is the
        // string auto, this attribute will return the current calculated value of the intrinsic iteration duration,
        // which may be a expressed as a double representing the duration in milliseconds or a percentage when the
        // effect is associated with a progress-based timeline.
        let timing_properties = self.record.timing();
        let duration = match time_value_as_css_numberish(vm, timing_properties.iteration_duration) {
            CSSNumberish::Double(value) => UnrestrictedDoubleOrCSSNumericValueOrDOMString::UnrestrictedDouble(value),
            CSSNumberish::CSSNumericValue(value) => {
                UnrestrictedDoubleOrCSSNumericValueOrDOMString::CSSNumericValue(value)
            }
        };

        //     - fill: likewise, while getTiming() can return the string auto, getComputedTiming() must return the
        //       specific FillMode used for timing calculations as defined in the description of the fill member of the
        //       EffectTiming interface.
        //
        //       In this level of the specification, that simply means that an auto value is replaced by the none
        //       FillMode.
        let specified_fill_mode = timing_properties.fill_mode;
        let fill = if specified_fill_mode == FillMode::Auto {
            FillMode::None
        } else {
            specified_fill_mode
        };

        let specified = self.record.specified_timing();
        let timing = self.record.resolve_timing(local_time, specified_fill_mode, true);
        let as_css_numberish = |time: TimeValue| time_value_as_css_numberish(vm, time);
        Ok(ComputedEffectTiming {
            parent: EffectTiming {
                delay: specified.start_delay,
                direction: timing_properties.playback_direction,
                duration,
                easing: self.record.timing_function_serialization(),
                end_delay: specified.end_delay,
                fill,
                iteration_start: timing_properties.iteration_start,
                iterations: timing_properties.iteration_count,
            },
            active_duration: Some(as_css_numberish(timing.active_duration)),
            current_iteration: Some(timing.current_iteration),
            end_time: Some(as_css_numberish(timing.end_time)),
            local_time: Some(local_time.map(as_css_numberish)),
            progress: Some(timing.transformed_progress),
        })
    }

    // https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#dom-animationeffect-updatetiming
    pub(crate) fn update_timing(&self, _cx: &mut CallContext, timing: OptionalEffectTiming) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.update_the_timing_properties(timing)
    }

    // https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#update-the-timing-properties-of-an-animation-effect
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#updating-animationeffect-timing
    pub(crate) fn update_the_timing_properties(&self, timing: OptionalEffectTiming) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If the iterationStart member of input exists and is less than zero, throw a TypeError and abort this
        //    procedure.
        if timing
            .iteration_start
            .is_some_and(|iteration_start| iteration_start < 0.0)
        {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Invalid iteration start value"));
        }

        // 2. If the iterations member of input exists, and is less than zero or is the value NaN, throw a TypeError
        //    and abort this procedure.
        if timing
            .iterations
            .is_some_and(|iterations| iterations < 0.0 || iterations.is_nan())
        {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Invalid iteration count value"));
        }

        // 3. If the duration member of input exists, and is less than zero, is the value NaN, or is a string other than
        //    the lowercase auto, throw a TypeError and abort this procedure.
        let has_valid_duration_value = match &timing.duration {
            None => true,
            Some(UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMString::UnrestrictedDouble(duration)) => {
                !(*duration < 0.0 || duration.is_nan())
            }
            Some(UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMString::DOMString(duration)) => units_equal(&duration.to_utf16(), "auto"),
        };
        if !has_valid_duration_value {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Invalid duration value"));
        }

        // 4. If the easing member of input exists but cannot be parsed using the <easing-function> production
        //    [CSS-EASING-1], throw a TypeError and abort this procedure.
        let easing_value: Option<ParsedEasing> = match &timing.easing {
            Some(easing) => {
                Some(parse_easing_function(easing).ok_or_else(|| Exception::type_error("Invalid easing function"))?)
            }
            None => None,
        };

        // 5. Assign each member that exists in input to the corresponding timing property of effect as follows:
        let mut specified = self.record.specified_timing();

        //    - delay → specified start delay
        if let Some(delay) = timing.delay {
            specified.start_delay = delay;
        }

        //    - endDelay → specified end delay
        if let Some(end_delay) = timing.end_delay {
            specified.end_delay = end_delay;
        }

        //    - fill → fill mode
        if let Some(fill) = timing.fill {
            specified.fill_mode = fill;
        }

        //    - iterationStart → iteration start
        if let Some(iteration_start) = timing.iteration_start {
            specified.iteration_start = iteration_start;
        }

        //    - iterations → iteration count
        if let Some(iterations) = timing.iterations {
            specified.iteration_count = iterations;
        }

        //    - duration → specified iteration duration
        // NB: "auto" is the only string an iteration duration can be.
        match timing.duration {
            Some(UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMString::UnrestrictedDouble(duration)) => {
                specified.iteration_duration = SpecifiedIterationDuration::milliseconds(duration);
            }
            Some(UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMString::DOMString(_)) => {
                specified.iteration_duration = SpecifiedIterationDuration::AUTO;
            }
            None => {}
        }

        //    - direction → playback direction
        if let Some(direction) = timing.direction {
            specified.playback_direction = direction;
        }
        self.record.set_specified_timing(specified);

        //    - easing → timing function
        if let Some(easing_value) = &easing_value {
            self.record.set_timing_function(easing_value);
        }

        // 6. Follow the procedure to normalize specified timing.
        self.record.normalize_specified_timing();

        // AD-HOC: Notify the associated animation that the effect timing has changed.
        if let Some(animation) = self.associated_animation() {
            effect_timing_changed(&animation);
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}

/// An EffectTiming as the OptionalEffectTiming with each of its members, which the procedure to update the timing
/// properties of an animation effect takes; none of its durations is a CSSNumericValue.
pub(crate) fn to_optional_effect_timing(effect_timing: EffectTiming) -> OptionalEffectTiming {
    OptionalEffectTiming {
        delay: Some(effect_timing.delay),
        direction: Some(effect_timing.direction),
        duration: Some(match effect_timing.duration {
            UnrestrictedDoubleOrCSSNumericValueOrDOMString::UnrestrictedDouble(value) => {
                UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMString::UnrestrictedDouble(value)
            }
            UnrestrictedDoubleOrCSSNumericValueOrDOMString::DOMString(value) => {
                UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMString::DOMString(value)
            }
            // NB: We check that this isn't the case in the caller
            UnrestrictedDoubleOrCSSNumericValueOrDOMString::CSSNumericValue(_) => {
                unreachable!("the caller rejects a CSSNumericValue duration")
            }
        }),
        easing: Some(effect_timing.easing),
        end_delay: Some(effect_timing.end_delay),
        fill: Some(effect_timing.fill),
        iteration_start: Some(effect_timing.iteration_start),
        iterations: Some(effect_timing.iterations),
    }
}

/// An object script sees of an effect, of the interface that inherits from AnimationEffect it is of.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
#[allow(clippy::enum_variant_names, reason = "the variants have the interfaces’ names")]
pub(crate) enum AnyAnimationEffect {
    AnimationEffect(Ref<AnimationEffect>),
    KeyframeEffect(Ref<KeyframeEffect>),
}

impl Deref for AnyAnimationEffect {
    type Target = AnimationEffect;

    fn deref(&self) -> &AnimationEffect {
        match self {
            Self::AnimationEffect(effect) => effect,
            Self::KeyframeEffect(effect) => effect.parent(),
        }
    }
}

impl ToJs for AnyAnimationEffect {
    fn to_js(self, cx: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        match self {
            Self::AnimationEffect(effect) => effect.to_js(cx),
            Self::KeyframeEffect(effect) => effect.to_js(cx),
        }
    }
}

impl AnyAnimationEffect {
    /// The bytes the object of the effect holds.
    pub(crate) fn memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::AnimationEffect(_) => size_of::<AnimationEffect>(),
            Self::KeyframeEffect(effect) => effect.memory_size(),
        }
    }
}

/// The object of the effect, if it has one.
pub(crate) fn existing_effect_object(effect: &EffectRecordRef) -> Option<AnyAnimationEffect> {
    let cell = effect.object_cell()?;
    // SAFETY: The object cell of an effect is the live cell of its object, a KeyframeEffect, the only AnimationEffect there
    //         is.
    Some(AnyAnimationEffect::KeyframeEffect(unsafe {
        cell_from_abi(cell.as_ptr())
    }))
}

/// The object script sees of the effect, a KeyframeEffect, which the effect of a CSS animation or transition gets as
/// script first asks for it.
pub(crate) fn effect_object(vm: &Vm, effect: &EffectRecordRef) -> AnyAnimationEffect {
    if let Some(object) = existing_effect_object(effect) {
        return object;
    }
    let object = KeyframeEffect::create_for_record(vm, effect.clone());
    effect.set_object_cell(NonNull::new(cell_into_abi(object)));
    AnyAnimationEffect::KeyframeEffect(object)
}

//! AnimationPlaybackEvent, https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#animationplaybackevent

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libcompositing_rust::animation_timing::{TimeValue, TimeValueType};
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::event_target::CppEvent;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::css::css_numeric_value::{AnyCSSNumericValue, CSSNumberish};
use crate::css::css_unit_value::CSSUnitValue;
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;

/// The dictionary AnimationPlaybackEventInit of Animations/AnimationPlaybackEvent.idl.
pub(crate) struct AnimationPlaybackEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) current_time: Option<CSSNumberish>,
    pub(crate) timeline_time: Option<CSSNumberish>,
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#animationplaybackevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct AnimationPlaybackEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-animationplaybackevent-currenttime
    current_time: Option<CSSNumberish>,
    // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-animationplaybackevent-timelinetime
    timeline_time: Option<CSSNumberish>,
}

impl Wrappable for AnimationPlaybackEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

/// A time value as the CSSNumberish that the attributes of the event expose: a double for milliseconds and a
/// CSSUnitValue for a percentage.
pub(crate) fn time_value_as_css_numberish(vm: &Vm, time: TimeValue) -> CSSNumberish {
    match time.r#type {
        TimeValueType::Milliseconds => CSSNumberish::Double(time.value),
        TimeValueType::Percentage => CSSNumberish::CSSNumericValue(AnyCSSNumericValue::CSSUnitValue(
            CSSUnitValue::create(vm, time.value, "percent"),
        )),
    }
}

impl AnimationPlaybackEvent {
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: AnimationPlaybackEventInit,
    ) -> Ref<AnimationPlaybackEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.parent.bubbles,
            event_init.parent.cancelable,
            event_init.parent.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| AnimationPlaybackEvent {
            event,
            current_time: event_init.current_time,
            timeline_time: event_init.timeline_time,
        });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: AnimationPlaybackEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<AnimationPlaybackEvent>> {
        Ok(Self::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &r#type, event_init_dict))
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    pub(crate) fn current_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CSSNumberish>> {
        Ok(self.current_time)
    }

    pub(crate) fn timeline_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CSSNumberish>> {
        Ok(self.timeline_time)
    }
}

//! AnimationTimeline, https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#the-animationtimeline-interface

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Object, Trace, Visitor, Vm};
use libjs_rust::api::{ThrowCompletionOr, Value};
use libweb_rust::web_animations::{TimelineInterfaceKind, TimelineRecordRef};

use super::animation_playback_event::time_value_as_css_numberish;
use super::document_timeline::DocumentTimeline;
use super::scroll_timeline::ScrollTimeline;
use super::view_timeline::ViewTimeline;
use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use core::ops::Deref;

use crate::bindings::conversions::ToJs;
use crate::bindings::interface::{
    Inherits, Interface, InterfaceCell, Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_if_abi, cell_into_abi,
};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::css::css_numeric_value::CSSNumberish;
use crate::internals::internal_animation_timeline::InternalAnimationTimeline;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_animation_wrap_element(realm: *mut c_void, element: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_animation_element_of_wrapper(wrapper: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
}

// https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#the-animationtimeline-interface
pub(crate) struct AnimationTimeline {
    record: TimelineRecordRef,
}

// SAFETY: Visits the cells of the host that the record names: the document the timeline is associated with, and the
//         element a scroll timeline finds its scroller from.
unsafe impl Trace for AnimationTimeline {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.record.for_each_host_cell(|cell| {
            // SAFETY: The record names live cells of the host, which this keeps alive.
            visitor.visit(unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(cell) });
        });
    }
}

impl Wrappable for AnimationTimeline {
    const TRACED_ON_OWNER_THREAD_ONLY: bool = true;
}

impl AnimationTimeline {
    /// The timeline's state, which lives as long as the timeline.
    pub(crate) fn record(&self) -> &TimelineRecordRef {
        &self.record
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-animationtimeline-currenttime
    pub(crate) fn current_time(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CSSNumberish>> {
        // Returns the current time for this timeline or null if this timeline is inactive. The value is expressed as a
        // percentage for a progress-based timeline, or as a double in milliseconds otherwise.
        // NB: Script observes the current time as the timeline is sampled for observation.
        Ok(self
            .record
            .current_time_for_observation()
            .map(|time| time_value_as_css_numberish(cx.vm(), time)))
    }

    // https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-2/#dom-animationtimeline-duration
    pub(crate) fn duration(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CSSNumberish>> {
        // Returns the duration for this timeline.
        Ok(self
            .record
            .duration()
            .map(|time| time_value_as_css_numberish(cx.vm(), time)))
    }
}

/// Finalizes a timeline: the record can outlive the timeline until what holds the record is swept.
pub(crate) fn finalize_timeline(timeline: &AnimationTimeline) {
    timeline.record.set_object_cell(None);
}

impl AnimationTimeline {
    pub(crate) fn new(record: TimelineRecordRef) -> Self {
        Self { record }
    }
}

/// Notes the cell of a new object of a timeline, which its record then reaches it through.
pub(crate) fn did_create_timeline(cell: *mut c_void) {
    // SAFETY: The cell is that of a new timeline.
    let timeline = unsafe { timeline_of_cell(cell) }.expect("the cell is that of a timeline");
    timeline.record.set_object_cell(NonNull::new(cell));
}

/// The object script sees of the timeline of `record`, which is made as script first asks for it, of the interface the
/// kind of the record picks.
pub(crate) fn timeline_object_of_record(vm: &Vm, record: &TimelineRecordRef) -> AnyAnimationTimeline {
    if let Some(cell) = record.object_cell() {
        // SAFETY: The object cell of a record is the live cell of its object.
        return unsafe { timeline_object(InterfaceCell::from_raw(cell.as_ptr())) };
    }
    let timeline = AnimationTimeline::new(record.clone());
    let cell = match record.kind() {
        TimelineInterfaceKind::Document => cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| DocumentTimeline::from_timeline(timeline))),
        TimelineInterfaceKind::Scroll => cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| ScrollTimeline::from_timeline(timeline))),
        TimelineInterfaceKind::View => cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| ViewTimeline::from_timeline(timeline))),
        TimelineInterfaceKind::Internal => {
            cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| InternalAnimationTimeline::from_timeline(timeline)))
        }
    };
    did_create_timeline(cell);
    // SAFETY: The cell is that of the new object.
    unsafe { timeline_object(InterfaceCell::from_raw(cell)) }
}

/// The part as an AnimationTimeline of the timeline whose cell the host names.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be a live cell.
pub(crate) unsafe fn timeline_of_cell<'a>(cell: *mut c_void) -> Option<&'a AnimationTimeline> {
    // NB: The cells live while the host names them, which outlives the reference the caller uses.
    fn extend<'a, T: Interface>(object: Ref<T>, timeline: impl Fn(&T) -> &AnimationTimeline) -> &'a AnimationTimeline {
        let timeline: *const AnimationTimeline = timeline(&object);
        // SAFETY: The cell lives while the host names it.
        unsafe { &*timeline }
    }
    // SAFETY: Guaranteed by the caller.
    unsafe {
        if let Some(object) = cell_if_abi::<DocumentTimeline>(cell) {
            return Some(extend(object, |object| object.timeline()));
        }
        if let Some(object) = cell_if_abi::<ScrollTimeline>(cell) {
            return Some(extend(object, |object| object.timeline()));
        }
        if let Some(object) = cell_if_abi::<ViewTimeline>(cell) {
            return Some(extend(object, |object| object.scroll_timeline().timeline()));
        }
        if let Some(object) = cell_if_abi::<InternalAnimationTimeline>(cell) {
            return Some(extend(object, |object| object.timeline()));
        }
        if let Some(object) = cell_if_abi::<AnimationTimeline>(cell) {
            return Some(extend(object, |object| object));
        }
    }
    None
}

/// The wrapper of the host's `DOM::Element` in the realm of the call.
pub(crate) fn element_wrapper(cx: &CallContext, element: NonNull<c_void>) -> CppInterface {
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the element is a live element.
    let wrapper = unsafe { web_animation_wrap_element(cx.realm().as_ptr().cast(), element.as_ptr()) };
    let wrapper = NonNull::new(wrapper.cast::<Object>()).expect("LibWeb returns the wrapper of the element");
    // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live wrapper of an Element.
    unsafe { CppInterface::from_wrapper(Gc::from_non_null(wrapper)) }
}

/// The host's `DOM::Element` of a wrapper of an Element.
pub(crate) fn element_of_wrapper(element: CppInterface) -> NonNull<c_void> {
    // SAFETY: The wrapper is that of a live Element.
    NonNull::new(unsafe { web_animation_element_of_wrapper(element.wrapper().as_ptr().cast()) })
        .expect("a wrapper of an Element wraps an element")
}

/// An object script sees of a timeline, of the interface that inherits from AnimationTimeline it is of.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
#[allow(clippy::enum_variant_names, reason = "the variants have the interfaces’ names")]
pub(crate) enum AnyAnimationTimeline {
    AnimationTimeline(Ref<AnimationTimeline>),
    DocumentTimeline(Ref<DocumentTimeline>),
    ScrollTimeline(Ref<ScrollTimeline>),
    ViewTimeline(Ref<ViewTimeline>),
    InternalAnimationTimeline(Ref<InternalAnimationTimeline>),
}

impl Deref for AnyAnimationTimeline {
    type Target = AnimationTimeline;

    fn deref(&self) -> &AnimationTimeline {
        match self {
            Self::AnimationTimeline(timeline) => timeline,
            Self::DocumentTimeline(timeline) => timeline.parent(),
            Self::ScrollTimeline(timeline) => timeline.parent(),
            Self::ViewTimeline(timeline) => timeline.parent().parent(),
            Self::InternalAnimationTimeline(timeline) => timeline.parent(),
        }
    }
}

impl ToJs for AnyAnimationTimeline {
    fn to_js(self, cx: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        match self {
            Self::AnimationTimeline(timeline) => timeline.to_js(cx),
            Self::DocumentTimeline(timeline) => timeline.to_js(cx),
            Self::ScrollTimeline(timeline) => timeline.to_js(cx),
            Self::ViewTimeline(timeline) => timeline.to_js(cx),
            Self::InternalAnimationTimeline(timeline) => timeline.to_js(cx),
        }
    }
}

/// The object of the timeline whose cell the host names.
pub(crate) fn timeline_object(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> AnyAnimationTimeline {
    if let Some(object) = cell.object_if::<DocumentTimeline>() {
        return AnyAnimationTimeline::DocumentTimeline(object);
    }
    if let Some(object) = cell.object_if::<ViewTimeline>() {
        return AnyAnimationTimeline::ViewTimeline(object);
    }
    if let Some(object) = cell.object_if::<ScrollTimeline>() {
        return AnyAnimationTimeline::ScrollTimeline(object);
    }
    if let Some(object) = cell.object_if::<InternalAnimationTimeline>() {
        return AnyAnimationTimeline::InternalAnimationTimeline(object);
    }
    AnyAnimationTimeline::AnimationTimeline(cell.object::<AnimationTimeline>())
}
