//! The asynchronous iterators of the interfaces implemented in Rust, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-async-iterable,
//! for a value asynchronously iterable declaration.

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    Attribute, EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, ErrorKind, ErrorType, Gc, HostObject, JSHostClass, Must,
    NativeFunction, Object, Promise, PropertyAttributes, PropertyKey, RawNativeFunctionPointer, Realm, Throw,
    ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value, Vm, call, create_iterator_result_object, host_data_of, is_host_instance_of,
};

use crate::bindings::CallContext;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Interface, SecurityCheckType, define_operation, perform_a_security_check};
use crate::bindings::promise::{NativeSteps, WebIdlPromise, create_promise};
use crate::bindings::services::web_bindings_ensure_web_iterator_prototype;

/// What the steps that get the next iteration result fulfill their promise with at the end of the iteration,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#end-of-iteration
pub(crate) const END_OF_ITERATION: Value = Value::EMPTY;

/// What the implementation of an interface with a value asynchronously iterable declaration implements, for a default
/// asynchronous iterator object of the interface whose state its asynchronous iterator initialization steps created.
pub(crate) trait AsyncIterable: Interface {
    type IteratorState: Trace + 'static;

    /// The steps to get the next iteration result, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-get-the-next-iteration-result,
    /// which return a promise fulfilled with the next value or END_OF_ITERATION.
    fn get_the_next_iteration_result(cx: &CallContext, state: &Self::IteratorState) -> WebIdlPromise;

    /// The asynchronous iterator return algorithm, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#asynchronous-iterator-return, of an
    /// interface whose IDL marks it [DefinesAsyncIteratorReturn].
    fn asynchronous_iterator_return(cx: &CallContext, state: &Self::IteratorState, value: Value) -> WebIdlPromise;
}

/// What the generated bindings of an interface with an asynchronously iterable declaration define: the classes of its
/// default asynchronous iterator objects.
pub(crate) trait DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses: AsyncIterable {
    /// The class of the cells of the default asynchronous iterator objects of the interface.
    const ASYNC_ITERATOR_CELL_CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<DefaultAsyncIterator<Self>>;

    /// The class of the default asynchronous iterator objects of the interface.
    fn async_iterator_class() -> &'static JSHostClass;
}

/// A default asynchronous iterator object, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#default-asynchronous-iterator-object,
/// which is the host data of a host object of the asynchronous iterator class of its interface.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct DefaultAsyncIterator<T: AsyncIterable> {
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    state: T::IteratorState,
    ongoing_promise: Cell<Option<Gc<Promise>>>,
    is_finished: Cell<bool>,
}

impl<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses> EmbedderValue for DefaultAsyncIterator<T> {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = T::ASYNC_ITERATOR_CELL_CLASS;
}

type IteratorCell<T> = Gc<EmbedderCell<DefaultAsyncIterator<T>>>;

/// Defines the "values" and %Symbol.asyncIterator% methods of an interface with a value asynchronously iterable
/// declaration on its interface prototype object, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#define-the-asynchronous-iteration-methods
pub(crate) fn define_async_iterator_properties(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    prototype: Gc<Object>,
    values: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    length: i32,
) {
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "values", values, length);
    prototype.define_direct_property(
        vm,
        &PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().async_iterator),
        prototype.get_without_side_effects(vm, &vm.names.values),
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE | Attribute::WRITABLE),
    );
}

/// A newly created default asynchronous iterator object for the interface in the realm of the call context, with the
/// state that the asynchronous iterator initialization steps of the interface created.
pub(crate) fn create_default_async_iterator<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses>(
    cx: &CallContext,
    state: T::IteratorState,
) -> Value {
    let vm = cx.vm();
    let realm = cx.realm();
    let iterator = T::ASYNC_ITERATOR_CELL_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| DefaultAsyncIterator {
        realm,
        state,
        ongoing_promise: Cell::new(None),
        is_finished: Cell::new(false),
    });
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the interface is asynchronously iterable.
    let prototype = unsafe { web_bindings_ensure_web_iterator_prototype(realm.as_ptr().cast(), T::INTERFACE_NAME) };
    let prototype = NonNull::new(prototype.cast::<Object>()).expect("LibWeb returns the iterator prototype object");
    // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live object, the iterator class has no hooks, and the host data is a live cell.
    let object = unsafe {
        HostObject::create(
            vm,
            realm,
            T::async_iterator_class(),
            Some(Gc::from_non_null(prototype)),
            None,
            Some(iterator.as_non_null().cast()),
        )
    };
    Value::from_object(object.upcast::<Object>())
}

/// Validates the this value of the "next" and "return" methods of the asynchronous iterator prototype object, steps
/// 3 to 7: the default asynchronous iterator object, or the promise of thisValidationPromiseCapability, which it
/// rejected.
fn validate_this<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses>(
    vm: &Vm,
    identifier: &str,
    this_validation_promise_capability: WebIdlPromise,
) -> Result<IteratorCell<T>, Value> {
    let reject = |error: Value| {
        call(
            vm,
            Value::from_object(this_validation_promise_capability.reject().upcast::<Object>()),
            Value::UNDEFINED,
            &[error],
        )
        .must();
        Value::from_object(this_validation_promise_capability.promise())
    };

    // 3. Let thisValue be the this value.
    let this_value = vm.this_value();

    // 4. Let object be Completion(ToObject(thisValue)).
    // 5. IfAbruptRejectPromise(object, thisValidationPromiseCapability).
    let object = this_value.to_object(vm).map_err(|throw| reject(throw.value()))?;

    // 6. If object is a platform object, then perform a security check, passing:
    //     * the platform object object,
    //     * the identifier "next", and
    //     * the type "method".
    //
    //    If this threw an exception e, then:
    //        1. Perform ! Call(thisValidationPromiseCapability.[[Reject]], undefined, « e »).
    //        2. Return thisValidationPromiseCapability.[[Promise]].
    // NB: The "return" method passes the identifier "return".
    // 7. If object is not a default asynchronous iterator object for interface, then:
    let Some(iterator) = default_async_iterator_of::<T>(object) else {
        // NB: This runs after the check above, which no Window or Location object passes.
        perform_a_security_check(vm, Value::from_object(object), identifier, SecurityCheckType::Method)
            .map_err(|throw| reject(throw.value()))?;

        // 1. Let error be a new TypeError.
        let name = format!("{}AsyncIterator", T::NAME);
        let error = vm
            .throw_completion::<()>(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&name])
            .expect_err("throwing a completion throws");

        // 2. Perform ! Call(thisValidationPromiseCapability.[[Reject]], undefined, « error »).
        // 3. Return thisValidationPromiseCapability.[[Promise]].
        return Err(reject(error.value()));
    };
    Ok(iterator)
}

fn default_async_iterator_of<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses>(object: Gc<Object>) -> Option<IteratorCell<T>> {
    if !is_host_instance_of(&object, T::async_iterator_class()) {
        return None;
    }
    let host_data = host_data_of(&object).expect("a default asynchronous iterator object holds its cell");
    // SAFETY: The object is a host object of the asynchronous iterator class, whose host data is the cell of a default
    //         asynchronous iterator.
    unsafe { T::ASYNC_ITERATOR_CELL_CLASS.downcast(host_data) }
}

/// The steps of a built-in function that the iterator creates, given its captures.
type BuiltinSteps<C> = fn(&Vm, C) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value>;

fn native_function<C: Trace + Copy + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    captures: C,
    behaviour: BuiltinSteps<C>,
) -> Value {
    let function = NativeFunction::create(
        vm,
        NativeSteps {
            captures,
            steps: behaviour,
        },
        |vm: &Vm, function: &NativeSteps<C, BuiltinSteps<C>>| (function.steps)(vm, function.captures),
        0,
        &PropertyKey::from_utf8(""),
        Some(realm),
        None,
        None,
    );
    Value::from_object(function.upcast::<Object>())
}

/// Runs the steps after the ongoing promise of the iterator settles, or now if it has none, and makes their promise
/// the ongoing promise, steps 9 to 11 of the "next" and "return" methods.
fn chain_onto_ongoing_promise<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses, C: Trace + Copy + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    iterator: IteratorCell<T>,
    captures: C,
    steps: BuiltinSteps<C>,
) {
    let realm = iterator.realm;

    // 9. Let ongoingPromise be object’s ongoing promise.
    // 10. If ongoingPromise is not null, then:
    if let Some(ongoing_promise) = iterator.ongoing_promise.get() {
        // 1. Let afterOngoingPromiseCapability be ! NewPromiseCapability(%Promise%).
        let after_ongoing_promise_capability = create_promise(vm, realm);

        // 2. Let onSettled be CreateBuiltinFunction(steps, « »).
        let on_settled = native_function(vm, realm, captures, steps);

        // 3. Perform PerformPromiseThen(ongoingPromise, onSettled, onSettled, afterOngoingPromiseCapability).
        ongoing_promise.perform_then(vm, on_settled, on_settled, Some(after_ongoing_promise_capability));

        // 4. Set object’s ongoing promise to afterOngoingPromiseCapability.[[Promise]].
        iterator
            .ongoing_promise
            .set(Some(promise_of(after_ongoing_promise_capability.promise())));
    }
    // 11. Otherwise:
    else {
        // 1. Set object’s ongoing promise to the result of running steps.
        let result = steps(vm, captures).must();
        iterator.ongoing_promise.set(Some(promise_of(result.as_object())));
    }
}

fn promise_of(object: Gc<Object>) -> Gc<Promise> {
    object.downcast::<Promise>().expect("the steps return a promise")
}

/// The "next" method of the asynchronous iterator prototype object of the interface,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-asynchronous-iterator-prototype-object
pub(crate) fn async_iterator_next<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let interface be the interface for which the asynchronous iterator prototype object exists.
    // 2. Let thisValidationPromiseCapability be ! NewPromiseCapability(%Promise%).
    let this_validation_promise_capability =
        create_promise(vm, vm.current_realm().expect("a native function runs in a realm"));

    // 3. Let thisValue be the this value.
    // 4. Let object be Completion(ToObject(thisValue)).
    // 5. IfAbruptRejectPromise(object, thisValidationPromiseCapability).
    // 6. If object is a platform object, then perform a security check, passing:
    // 7. If object is not a default asynchronous iterator object for interface, then:
    let iterator = match validate_this::<T>(vm, "next", this_validation_promise_capability) {
        Ok(iterator) => iterator,
        Err(promise) => return Ok(promise),
    };

    // 8. Let nextSteps be the following steps:
    fn next_steps<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses>(vm: &Vm, iterator: IteratorCell<T>) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let realm = iterator.realm;

        // 1. Let nextPromiseCapability be ! NewPromiseCapability(%Promise%).
        let next_promise_capability = create_promise(vm, realm);

        // 2. If object’s is finished is true, then:
        if iterator.is_finished.get() {
            // 1. Let result be CreateIteratorResultObject(undefined, true).
            let result = create_iterator_result_object(vm, realm, Value::UNDEFINED, true);

            // 2. Perform ! Call(nextPromiseCapability.[[Resolve]], undefined, « result »).
            call(
                vm,
                Value::from_object(next_promise_capability.resolve().upcast::<Object>()),
                Value::UNDEFINED,
                &[Value::from_object(result)],
            )
            .must();

            // 3. Return nextPromiseCapability.[[Promise]].
            return Ok(Value::from_object(next_promise_capability.promise()));
        }

        // 3. Let kind be object’s kind.
        // 4. Let nextPromise be the result of getting the next iteration result with object’s target and object.
        let next_promise = T::get_the_next_iteration_result(&CallContext::new(vm, realm), &iterator.state);

        // 5. Let fulfillSteps be the following steps, given next:
        fn fulfill_steps<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses>(
            vm: &Vm,
            iterator: IteratorCell<T>,
        ) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
            let next = vm.argument(0);

            // 1. Set object’s ongoing promise to null.
            iterator.ongoing_promise.set(None);

            // 2. If next is end of iteration, then:
            if next == END_OF_ITERATION {
                // 1. Set object’s is finished to true.
                iterator.is_finished.set(true);

                // 2. Return CreateIteratorResultObject(undefined, true).
                return Ok(Value::from_object(create_iterator_result_object(
                    vm,
                    iterator.realm,
                    Value::UNDEFINED,
                    true,
                )));
            }

            // 3. Otherwise, if interface has a pair asynchronously iterable declaration:
            // NB: The bindings only handle a value asynchronously iterable declaration.

            // 4. Otherwise:
            //    1. Assert: interface has a value asynchronously iterable declaration.
            //    2. Assert: next is a value of the type that appears in the declaration.
            //    3. Let value be next, converted to a JavaScript value.
            //    4. Return CreateIteratorResultObject(value, false).
            Ok(Value::from_object(create_iterator_result_object(
                vm,
                iterator.realm,
                next,
                false,
            )))
        }

        // 6. Let onFulfilled be CreateBuiltinFunction(fulfillSteps, « »).
        let on_fulfilled = native_function(vm, realm, iterator, fulfill_steps::<T>);

        // 7. Let rejectSteps be the following steps, given reason:
        fn reject_steps<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses>(
            vm: &Vm,
            iterator: IteratorCell<T>,
        ) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
            // 1. Set object’s ongoing promise to null.
            iterator.ongoing_promise.set(None);

            // 2. Set object’s is finished to true.
            iterator.is_finished.set(true);

            // 3. Throw reason.
            Err(Throw::new(vm.argument(0)))
        }

        // 8. Let onRejected be CreateBuiltinFunction(rejectSteps, « »).
        let on_rejected = native_function(vm, realm, iterator, reject_steps::<T>);

        // 9. Perform PerformPromiseThen(nextPromise, onFulfilled, onRejected, nextPromiseCapability).
        promise_of(next_promise.promise()).perform_then(vm, on_fulfilled, on_rejected, Some(next_promise_capability));

        // 10. Return nextPromiseCapability.[[Promise]].
        Ok(Value::from_object(next_promise_capability.promise()))
    }

    // 9. Let ongoingPromise be object’s ongoing promise.
    // 10. If ongoingPromise is not null, then:
    // 11. Otherwise:
    chain_onto_ongoing_promise(vm, iterator, iterator, next_steps::<T>);

    // 12. Return object’s ongoing promise.
    let ongoing_promise = iterator
        .ongoing_promise
        .get()
        .expect("the iterator has an ongoing promise");
    Ok(Value::from_object(ongoing_promise.upcast::<Object>()))
}

/// The "return" method of the asynchronous iterator prototype object of an interface whose IDL marks it
/// [DefinesAsyncIteratorReturn], https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-asynchronous-iterator-prototype-object
pub(crate) fn async_iterator_return<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    let value = vm.argument(0);

    // 1. Let interface be the interface for which the asynchronous iterator prototype object exists.
    // 2. Let returnPromiseCapability be ! NewPromiseCapability(%Promise%).
    let return_promise_capability = create_promise(vm, vm.current_realm().expect("a native function runs in a realm"));

    // 3. Let thisValue be the this value.
    // 4. Let object be Completion(ToObject(thisValue)).
    // 5. IfAbruptRejectPromise(object, returnPromiseCapability).
    // 6. If object is a platform object, then perform a security check, passing:
    // 7. If object is not a default asynchronous iterator object for interface, then:
    let iterator = match validate_this::<T>(vm, "return", return_promise_capability) {
        Ok(iterator) => iterator,
        Err(promise) => return Ok(promise),
    };
    let realm = iterator.realm;

    // 8. Let returnSteps be the following steps:
    fn return_steps<T: DefaultAsyncIteratorClasses>(
        vm: &Vm,
        (iterator, value): (IteratorCell<T>, Value),
    ) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let realm = iterator.realm;

        // 1. Let returnPromiseCapability be ! NewPromiseCapability(%Promise%).
        let return_promise_capability = create_promise(vm, realm);

        // 2. If object’s is finished is true, then:
        if iterator.is_finished.get() {
            // 1. Let result be CreateIteratorResultObject(value, true).
            let result = create_iterator_result_object(vm, realm, value, true);

            // 2. Perform ! Call(returnPromiseCapability.[[Resolve]], undefined, « result »).
            call(
                vm,
                Value::from_object(return_promise_capability.resolve().upcast::<Object>()),
                Value::UNDEFINED,
                &[Value::from_object(result)],
            )
            .must();

            // 3. Return returnPromiseCapability.[[Promise]].
            return Ok(Value::from_object(return_promise_capability.promise()));
        }

        // 3. Set object’s is finished to true.
        iterator.is_finished.set(true);

        // 4. Return the result of running the asynchronous iterator return algorithm for interface, given object’s
        //    target, object, and value.
        let promise = T::asynchronous_iterator_return(&CallContext::new(vm, realm), &iterator.state, value);
        Ok(Value::from_object(promise.promise()))
    }

    // 9. Let ongoingPromise be object’s ongoing promise.
    // 10. If ongoingPromise is not null, then:
    // 11. Otherwise:
    chain_onto_ongoing_promise(vm, iterator, (iterator, value), return_steps::<T>);

    // 12. Let fulfillSteps be the following steps:
    fn fulfill_steps(vm: &Vm, (realm, value): (Gc<Realm>, Value)) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        // 1. Return CreateIteratorResultObject(value, true).
        Ok(Value::from_object(create_iterator_result_object(
            vm, realm, value, true,
        )))
    }

    // 13. Let onFulfilled be CreateBuiltinFunction(fulfillSteps, « »).
    let on_fulfilled = native_function(vm, realm, (realm, value), fulfill_steps);

    // 14. Perform PerformPromiseThen(object’s ongoing promise, onFulfilled, undefined, returnPromiseCapability).
    let ongoing_promise = iterator
        .ongoing_promise
        .get()
        .expect("the iterator has an ongoing promise");
    ongoing_promise.perform_then(vm, on_fulfilled, Value::UNDEFINED, Some(return_promise_capability));

    // 15. Return returnPromiseCapability.[[Promise]].
    Ok(Value::from_object(return_promise_capability.promise()))
}

/*

//! Callback function values, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-callback-function, and callback interface values,
//! https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-callback-interface, which LibWeb's C++ code represents as a WebIDL::CallbackType:
//! the object and its callback context.

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    ErrorKind, ErrorType, ForeignCellSlot, Gc, Object, RawNativeFunctionResult, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value,
    Vm,
};

use crate::bindings::promise::{WebIdlPromise, promise_from_abi};

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// A new WebIDL::CallbackType of the object, whose callback context is the incumbent settings object.
    fn web_bindings_create_callback_function(callable: *mut c_void, returns_promise: bool) -> *mut c_void;

    /// WebIDL::invoke_callback() of the WebIDL::CallbackType with the this value, if `has_this_value`, and the
    /// arguments.
    fn web_bindings_invoke_callback_function(
        callback: *mut c_void,
        has_this_value: bool,
        this_value: u64,
        arguments: ak::Span<'_, Value>,
    ) -> RawNativeFunctionResult;

    /// WebIDL::invoke_callback() of the WebIDL::CallbackType with the arguments and the "report" exception behavior.
    fn web_bindings_invoke_callback_function_and_report(callback: *mut c_void, arguments: ak::Span<'_, Value>);

    /// The callback function object of the WebIDL::CallbackType.
    fn web_bindings_callback_function_callback(callback: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;

    /// WebIDL::invoke_promise_callback() of the WebIDL::CallbackType, whose return type is a promise type, with the this
    /// value, if `has_this_value`, and the arguments.
    fn web_bindings_invoke_promise_callback_function(
        callback: *mut c_void,
        has_this_value: bool,
        this_value: u64,
        arguments: ak::Span<'_, Value>,
    ) -> *mut c_void;
}

/// A callback function value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-callback-function
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CallbackFunction(CallbackType);

/// A callback function value whose return type is a promise type.
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PromiseCallbackFunction(CallbackType);

/// A callback interface value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-callback-interface
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CallbackInterface(CallbackType);

/// The WebIDL::CallbackType of a callback function value or a callback interface value.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct CallbackType(ForeignCellSlot);

impl Clone for CallbackType {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The slot keeps the callback alive.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw(self.0.as_ptr()) }
    }
}

impl CallbackType {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `callback` must be a live WebIDL::CallbackType.
    unsafe fn from_raw(callback: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        let slot = ForeignCellSlot::empty();
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live WebIDL::CallbackType, a cell of the heap.
        unsafe { slot.set(Some(NonNull::new(callback).expect("LibWeb passes a callback"))) };
        Self(slot)
    }

    // https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-callback-function
    fn from_js(vm: &Vm, value: Value, returns_promise: bool) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Self> {
        // 1. If the result of calling IsCallable(V) is false and the conversion to an IDL value is not being performed
        //    due to V being assigned to an attribute whose type is a nullable callback function that is annotated with
        //    [LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull], then throw a TypeError.
        if !value.is_function() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAFunction, &[&value]);
        }

        // 2. Return the IDL callback function type value that represents a reference to the same object that V
        //    represents, with the incumbent realm as the callback context.
        // SAFETY: The value is a live object.
        Ok(unsafe {
            Self::from_raw(web_bindings_create_callback_function(
                value.as_object().as_ptr().cast(),
                returns_promise,
            ))
        })
    }
}

impl CallbackFunction {
    pub(crate) fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.0.as_ptr()
    }

    /// The callback function value of a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-callback-function
    pub(crate) fn from_js(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Self> {
        CallbackType::from_js(vm, value, false).map(Self)
    }

    /// Invokes the callback function with the this value and the arguments, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function
    pub(crate) fn invoke(&self, this_value: Option<Value>, arguments: &[Value]) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        // SAFETY: The slot keeps the callback alive, and the values are live for the call.
        unsafe {
            web_bindings_invoke_callback_function(
                self.0.0.as_ptr(),
                this_value.is_some(),
                this_value.unwrap_or(Value::UNDEFINED).to_raw(),
                ak::Span::new(arguments),
            )
        }
        .into_completion()
    }

    /// Invokes the callback function with the arguments and "report", https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function
    pub(crate) fn invoke_and_report(&self, arguments: &[Value]) {
        // SAFETY: The slot keeps the callback alive, and the values are live for the call.
        unsafe { web_bindings_invoke_callback_function_and_report(self.0.0.as_ptr(), ak::Span::new(arguments)) };
    }

    pub(crate) fn callback_realm(&self) -> Gc<Realm> {
        // SAFETY: The slot keeps the callback alive, and LibWeb returns its live callback function object.
        let callback = unsafe { web_bindings_callback_function_callback(self.0.0.as_ptr()) };
        // SAFETY: The callback function object is live.
        let callback: Gc<Object> =
            unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(callback.cast()).expect("a callback has a function object")) };
        callback.shape().realm()
    }
}

impl CallbackInterface {
    // https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-callback-interface
    pub(crate) fn from_js(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Self> {
        // 1. If V is not an Object, then throw a TypeError.
        if !value.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&value]);
        }

        // 2. Return the IDL callback interface type value that represents a reference to V, with the incumbent realm
        //    as the callback context.
        // SAFETY: The value is a live object.
        Ok(Self(unsafe {
            CallbackType::from_raw(web_bindings_create_callback_function(
                value.as_object().as_ptr().cast(),
                false,
            ))
        }))
    }

    /// The WebIDL::CallbackType, which this keeps alive.
    pub(crate) fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.0.as_ptr()
    }
}

impl PromiseCallbackFunction {
    pub(crate) fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.0.as_ptr()
    }

    /// The callback function value of a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-callback-function
    pub(crate) fn from_js(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Self> {
        CallbackType::from_js(vm, value, true).map(Self)
    }

    /// Invokes the callback function with the this value and the arguments, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function:
    /// the promise that it returns, or one rejected with what it throws.
    pub(crate) fn invoke(&self, this_value: Option<Value>, arguments: &[Value]) -> WebIdlPromise {
        // SAFETY: The slot keeps the callback alive, and the values are live for the call.
        //         LibWeb returns a live promise.
        unsafe {
            promise_from_abi(web_bindings_invoke_promise_callback_function(
                self.0.0.as_ptr(),
                this_value.is_some(),
                this_value.unwrap_or(Value::UNDEFINED).to_raw(),
                ak::Span::new(arguments),
            ))
        }
    }
}

/// A USVString, a string without lone surrogates. Its UTF-16 code units are always well-formed.
#[derive(Clone, Eq, PartialEq, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct UsvString(Utf16String);

impl UsvString {
    pub(crate) fn from_ascii(string: &[u8]) -> Self {
        Self(Utf16String::from_ascii(string))
    }

    pub(crate) fn units(&self) -> Utf16StringUnits<'_> {
        self.0.as_units()
    }

    pub(crate) fn length_in_code_units(&self) -> usize {
        self.0.length_in_code_units()
    }

    pub(crate) fn utf8_length(&self) -> usize {
        match self.units() {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(bytes) => bytes.len(),
            Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(bytes) => bytes.len() + bytes.iter().filter(|&&byte| byte >= 0x80).count(),
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => utf8_length_from_valid_utf16(code_units),
        }
    }

    /// Writes the string's UTF-8 encoding to the start of `output`, which need not be initialized, and returns the
    /// number of bytes written.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `output` must have room for the encoding: utf8_length() bytes, or three bytes per code unit. The encoding is
    /// written without checking that, as measuring it first would cost a pass over the string.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn encode_utf8(&self, output: &mut [MaybeUninit<u8>]) -> usize {
        match self.units() {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(bytes) => {
                output[..bytes.len()].write_copy_of_slice(bytes);
                bytes.len()
            }
            Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(bytes) => {
                let mut length = 0;
                for &byte in bytes {
                    let mut buffer = [0; 2];
                    let encoded = char::from(byte).encode_utf8(&mut buffer).as_bytes();
                    output[length..length + encoded.len()].write_copy_of_slice(encoded);
                    length += encoded.len();
                }
                length
            }
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => {
                debug_assert!(output.len() >= utf8_length_from_valid_utf16(code_units));
                // SAFETY: A USVString is well-formed, and the caller gives the output room for its encoding.
                unsafe { convert_valid_utf16_to_utf8(code_units, output) }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The string without its first code unit, if that is the ASCII character.
    pub(crate) fn strip_ascii_prefix(&self, prefix: u8) -> Option<Self> {
        match self.units() {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(bytes) => bytes.strip_prefix(&[prefix]).map(Self::from_ascii),
            Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(bytes) => bytes.strip_prefix(&[prefix]).map(|rest| {
                Self(Utf16String::from_utf16(
                    &rest.iter().map(|&byte| u16::from(byte)).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
                ))
            }),
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => code_units
                .strip_prefix(&[u16::from(prefix)])
                .map(|rest| Self(Utf16String::from_utf16(rest))),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn into_utf16_string(self) -> Utf16String {
        self.0
    }

    pub(crate) fn as_utf16_string(&self) -> &Utf16String {
        &self.0
    }

    /// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-string-convert
    pub(crate) fn from_utf16_string(string: &Utf16String) -> Self {
        Self(to_well_formed(string))
    }

    pub(crate) fn to_utf16(&self) -> std::borrow::Cow<'_, [u16]> {
        self.0.to_utf16()
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_utf8(string: &str) -> Self {
        Self(Utf16String::from_utf8(string))
    }

    pub(crate) fn to_utf8(&self) -> String {
        match self.units() {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(bytes) => String::from_utf8(bytes.to_vec()),
            Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(bytes) => Ok(bytes.iter().map(|&byte| char::from(byte)).collect()),
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => String::from_utf16(code_units).map_err(|_| unreachable!()),
        }
        .expect("a USVString is well-formed")
    }

    /// The string of the code units, with U+FFFD in place of every surrogate that is not part of a pair.
    pub(crate) fn from_utf16_replacing_lone_surrogates(code_units: &[u16]) -> Self {
        Self(to_well_formed(&Utf16String::from_utf16(code_units)))
    }
}

impl From<UsvString> for Utf16String {
    fn from(string: UsvString) -> Self {
        string.0
    }
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ByteString
#[derive(Clone, Eq, PartialEq, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct ByteString(Vec<u8>);

impl ByteString {
    pub(crate) fn from_bytes(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Self {
        Self(bytes)
    }

    pub(crate) fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.0
    }

    pub(crate) fn into_bytes(self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.0
    }
}

/// A JS value converted to a DOMString, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-DOMString
pub(crate) fn to_dom_string(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Utf16String> {
    value.to_utf16_string(vm)
}

/// A JS value converted to a DOMString with [LegacyNullToEmptyString], https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-DOMString
pub(crate) fn to_dom_string_treating_null_as_empty(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Utf16String> {
    // 1. If V is null and the conversion is to an IDL type associated with the [LegacyNullToEmptyString] extended
    //    attribute, then return the DOMString value that represents the empty string.
    if value.is_null() {
        return Ok(Utf16String::default());
    }
    to_dom_string(vm, value)
}

/// A JS value converted to a USVString, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-USVString
pub(crate) fn to_usv_string(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<UsvString> {
    // 1. Let string be the result of converting V to a DOMString.
    let string = to_dom_string(vm, value)?;

    // 2. Return an IDL USVString value that is the result of converting string to a sequence of scalar values.
    Ok(UsvString(to_well_formed(&string)))
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-ByteString
pub(crate) fn to_byte_string(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<ByteString> {
    // 1. Let x be ? ToString(V).
    let x = value.to_utf16_string(vm)?;

    let code_units = match x.as_units() {
        Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(bytes) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(bytes) => return Ok(ByteString(bytes.to_vec())),
        Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => code_units,
    };

    // 2. If the value of any element of x is greater than 255, then throw a TypeError.
    if let Some((index, code_unit)) = code_units.iter().enumerate().find(|(_, code_unit)| **code_unit > 0xFF) {
        let message = format!(
            "Invalid byte 0x{code_unit:X} at index {index}, must be an integer no less than 0 and no greater than 0xFF"
        );
        return vm.throw_completion_with_utf16_message(ErrorKind::TypeError, Utf16String::from_utf8(&message));
    }

    // 3. Return an IDL ByteString value whose length is the length of x, and where the value of each element is the
    //    value of the corresponding element of x.
    Ok(ByteString(
        code_units.iter().map(|code_unit| *code_unit as u8).collect(),
    ))
}

/// The value of an enumeration that a JS value names, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-enumeration: the index of
/// the string that the value converts to among the values of the enumeration, which are ASCII.
pub(crate) fn to_enumeration_value(
    vm: &Vm,
    value: Value,
    enumeration_name: &str,
    enumeration_values: &[&str],
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<usize> {
    // 1. Let S be the result of calling ? ToString(V).
    let string = value.to_utf16_string(vm)?;

    // 2. If S is not one of E's enumeration values, then throw a TypeError.
    // 3. Return the enumeration value of type E that is equal to S.
    let index = enumeration_values
        .iter()
        .position(|enumeration_value| match string.as_units() {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units) => units == enumeration_value.as_bytes(),
            // NB: Every enumeration value is ASCII.
            Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(_) => false,
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => units.iter().copied().eq(enumeration_value.bytes().map(u16::from)),
        });
    match index {
        Some(index) => Ok(index),
        None => vm.throw_completion(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            ErrorType::InvalidEnumerationValue,
            &[&string, &enumeration_name],
        ),
    }
}

/// A value of an enumeration converted to a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-enumeration
pub(crate) fn enumeration_value_to_js(cx: &CallContext, enumeration_value: &str) -> Value {
    Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create_from_ascii(
        cx.vm(),
        enumeration_value.as_bytes(),
    ))
}

/// An object converted from a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-object
pub(crate) fn to_object(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<Object>> {
    // 1. If V is not an Object, then throw a TypeError.
    if !value.is_object() {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&value]);
    }

    // 2. Return the IDL object value that is a reference to the same object as V.
    Ok(value.as_object())
}

/// A JS value converted to a boolean, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-boolean
#[expect(
    clippy::unnecessary_wraps,
    reason = "the generated bindings convert every type with an expression that can throw"
)]
pub(crate) fn to_boolean(value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<bool> {
    // 1. Let x be the result of computing ToBoolean(V).
    // 2. Return the IDL boolean value that is the one that represents the same truth value as the JavaScript Boolean
    //    value x.
    Ok(value.to_boolean())
}

/// A JS value converted to a long, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-long
pub(crate) fn to_long(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<i32> {
    // 1. Let x be ? ConvertToInt(V, 32, "signed").
    // 2. Return the IDL long value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    value.to_i32(vm)
}

/// A JS value converted to an unsigned short, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unsigned-short
pub(crate) fn to_unsigned_short(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<u16> {
    // 1. Let x be ? ConvertToInt(V, 16, "unsigned").
    // 2. Return the IDL unsigned short value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    value.to_u16(vm)
}

/// A JS value converted to an unsigned long, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unsigned-long
pub(crate) fn to_unsigned_long(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<u32> {
    // 1. Let x be ? ConvertToInt(V, 32, "unsigned").
    // 2. Return the IDL unsigned long value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    value.to_u32(vm)
}

/// A JS value converted to an integer of the IDL type with [EnforceRange], whose bounds those are: steps 4 to 6 of
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-converttoint, which throw the errors that WebIDL::convert_to_int()
/// of the C++ bindings throws.
fn to_integer_enforcing_range(vm: &Vm, value: Value, lower_bound: f64, upper_bound: f64) -> ThrowCompletionOr<f64> {
    // 4. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    // 5. If x is −0, then set x to +0.
    let x = value.to_double(vm)? + 0.0;

    // 6. If the conversion is to an IDL type associated with the [EnforceRange] extended attribute, then:
    //     1. If x is NaN, +∞, or −∞, then throw a TypeError.
    if !x.is_finite() {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NumberIsNaNOrInfinity, &[]);
    }

    //     2. Set x to IntegerPart(x).
    let x = x.trunc() + 0.0;

    //     3. If x < lowerBound or x > upperBound, then throw a TypeError.
    if x < lower_bound || x > upper_bound {
        let message = format!(
            "Number '{}' is outside of allowed range of {} to {}",
            ak_formatted(x),
            ak_formatted(lower_bound),
            ak_formatted(upper_bound)
        );
        return vm.throw_completion_with_utf16_message(ErrorKind::TypeError, Utf16String::from_utf8(&message));
    }

    //     4. Return x.
    Ok(x)
}

/// The largest integer that a JS number represents unambiguously, the upper bound of a 64-bit integer type with
/// [EnforceRange] or [Clamp].
const MAX_SAFE_INTEGER: f64 = 9_007_199_254_740_991.0;

/// A JS value converted to an octet with [EnforceRange], https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-octet
#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    clippy::cast_sign_loss,
    reason = "the value is an integer within the bounds of the type"
)]
pub(crate) fn to_octet_enforcing_range(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<u8> {
    Ok(to_integer_enforcing_range(vm, value, 0.0, f64::from(u8::MAX))? as u8)
}

/// A JS value converted to an unsigned short with [EnforceRange], https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unsigned-short
#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    clippy::cast_sign_loss,
    reason = "the value is an integer within the bounds of the type"
)]
pub(crate) fn to_unsigned_short_enforcing_range(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<u16> {
    Ok(to_integer_enforcing_range(vm, value, 0.0, f64::from(u16::MAX))? as u16)
}

/// A JS value converted to a long with [EnforceRange], https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-long
#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    reason = "the value is an integer within the bounds of the type"
)]
pub(crate) fn to_long_enforcing_range(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<i32> {
    Ok(to_integer_enforcing_range(vm, value, f64::from(i32::MIN), f64::from(i32::MAX))? as i32)
}

/// A JS value converted to an unsigned long with [EnforceRange], https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unsigned-long
#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    clippy::cast_sign_loss,
    reason = "the value is an integer within the bounds of the type"
)]
pub(crate) fn to_unsigned_long_enforcing_range(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<u32> {
    Ok(to_integer_enforcing_range(vm, value, 0.0, f64::from(u32::MAX))? as u32)
}

/// A JS value converted to a long long with [EnforceRange], https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-long-long
#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    reason = "the value is an integer within the bounds of the type"
)]
pub(crate) fn to_long_long_enforcing_range(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<i64> {
    Ok(to_integer_enforcing_range(vm, value, -MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)? as i64)
}

/// A JS value converted to an unsigned long long with [EnforceRange],
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unsigned-long-long
#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    clippy::cast_sign_loss,
    reason = "the value is an integer within the bounds of the type"
)]
pub(crate) fn to_unsigned_long_long_enforcing_range(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<u64> {
    Ok(to_integer_enforcing_range(vm, value, 0.0, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)? as u64)
}

/// A JS value converted to an integer of the IDL type with [Clamp], whose bounds those are: steps 4, 5, 7 and 8 of
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-converttoint
fn to_integer_clamping(vm: &Vm, value: Value, lower_bound: f64, upper_bound: f64) -> ThrowCompletionOr<f64> {
    // 4. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    // 5. If x is −0, then set x to +0.
    let x = value.to_double(vm)? + 0.0;

    // 7. If x is not NaN and the conversion is to an IDL type associated with the [Clamp] extended attribute, then:
    if !x.is_nan() {
        //     1. Set x to min(max(x, lowerBound), upperBound).
        //     2. Round x to the nearest integer, choosing the even integer if it lies halfway between two, and
        //        choosing +0 rather than −0.
        //     3. Return x.
        return Ok(x.clamp(lower_bound, upper_bound).round_ties_even() + 0.0);
    }

    // 8. If x is NaN, +0, +∞, or −∞, then return +0.
    Ok(0.0)
}

/// A JS value converted to a long long with [Clamp], https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-long-long
#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    reason = "the value is an integer within the bounds of the type"
)]
pub(crate) fn to_long_long_clamping(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<i64> {
    Ok(to_integer_clamping(vm, value, -MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)? as i64)
}

/// A JS value converted to an unsigned long with [Clamp], https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unsigned-long
#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    clippy::cast_sign_loss,
    reason = "the value is an integer within the bounds of the type"
)]
pub(crate) fn to_unsigned_long_clamping(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<u32> {
    Ok(to_integer_clamping(vm, value, 0.0, f64::from(u32::MAX))? as u32)
}

/// The integer that https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-converttoint has after step 10 for a bit length of
/// 64.
#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    clippy::cast_sign_loss,
    reason = "the remainder is an integer whose magnitude is below 2^64"
)]
fn to_integer_modulo_two_to_the_64(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<u64> {
    const TWO_TO_THE_64: f64 = 18_446_744_073_709_551_616.0;

    // 4. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    // 5. If x is −0, then set x to +0.
    let x = value.to_double(vm)?;

    // 8. If x is NaN, +0, +∞, or −∞, then return +0.
    if x.is_nan() || x == 0.0 || x.is_infinite() {
        return Ok(0);
    }

    // 9. Set x to IntegerPart(x).
    let x = x.trunc();

    // 10. Set x to x modulo 2^bitLength.
    // NB: The remainder of % is exact, an integer of the sign of x whose magnitude is below 2^64, which a u64 holds. But
    //     an f64 holds few integers near 2^64, so adding 2^64 to a negative remainder in one would round (and -1 would
    //     become 2^64). So the wrap around to a non-negative x is done in a u64 instead.
    let remainder = x % TWO_TO_THE_64;
    Ok(if remainder < 0.0 {
        0u64.wrapping_sub((-remainder) as u64)
    } else {
        remainder as u64
    })
}

/// A JS value converted to a long long, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-long-long
pub(crate) fn to_long_long(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<i64> {
    // 1. Let x be ? ConvertToInt(V, 64, "signed").
    let x = to_integer_modulo_two_to_the_64(vm, value)?;

    // 11. If signedness is "signed" and x ≥ 2^(bitLength − 1), then return x − 2^(bitLength).
    // 2. Return the IDL long long value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    // NB: Reinterpreting the bits of x as an i64 does just that.
    #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_wrap, reason = "the wrap is step 11")]
    Ok(x as i64)
}

/// A JS value converted to an unsigned long long, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unsigned-long-long
pub(crate) fn to_unsigned_long_long(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<u64> {
    // 1. Let x be ? ConvertToInt(V, 64, "unsigned").
    // 2. Return the IDL unsigned long long value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    to_integer_modulo_two_to_the_64(vm, value)
}

/// A JS value converted to a float, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-float
///
/// The identifier is the name of the parameter or member that the value is of, which the error names.
pub(crate) fn to_float(vm: &Vm, value: Value, identifier: &str) -> ThrowCompletionOr<f32> {
    // 1. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    let x = value.to_double(vm)?;

    // 2. If x is NaN, +∞, or −∞, then throw a TypeError.
    // 3. Let S be the set of finite IEEE 754 single-precision floating point values except −0, but with two special
    //    values added: 2^128 and −2^128.
    // 4. Let y be the number in S that is closest to x, selecting the number with an even significand if there are two
    //    equally close values. (The two special values 2^128 and −2^128 are considered to have even significands for
    //    this purpose.)
    // 5. If y is 2^128 or −2^128, then throw a TypeError.
    // 6. If y is +0 and x is negative, return −0.
    // 7. Return y.
    // NB: Rounding x to the nearest float gives an infinity where step 4 gives one of the two special values.
    #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, reason = "the spec rounds to the closest float")]
    let y = x as f32;
    if !y.is_finite() {
        return vm.throw_completion(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            ErrorType::InvalidRestrictedFloatingPointParameter,
            &[&identifier],
        );
    }
    Ok(y)
}

/// A JS value converted to an unrestricted float, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unrestricted-float
pub(crate) fn to_unrestricted_float(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<f32> {
    // 1. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    let x = value.to_double(vm)?;

    // 2. If x is NaN, then return the IDL unrestricted float value that represents the IEEE 754 NaN value with the
    //    bit pattern 0x7fc00000.
    // 3. Let S be the set of finite IEEE 754 single-precision floating point values except −0, but with two special
    //    values added: 2^128 and −2^128.
    // 4. Let y be the number in S that is closest to x, selecting the number with an even significand if there are two
    //    equally close values. (The two special values 2^128 and −2^128 are considered to have even significands for
    //    this purpose.)
    // 5. If y is 2^128, return +∞.
    // 6. If y is −2^128, return −∞.
    // 7. If y is +0 and x is negative, return −0.
    // 8. Return y.
    // NB: Rounding x to the nearest float gives an infinity where step 4 gives one of the two special values.
    #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, reason = "the spec rounds to the closest float")]
    Ok(x as f32)
}

/// A JS value converted to a double, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-double
///
/// The identifier is the name of the parameter or member that the value is of, which the error names.
pub(crate) fn to_double(vm: &Vm, value: Value, identifier: &str) -> ThrowCompletionOr<f64> {
    // 1. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    let x = value.to_double(vm)?;

    // 2. If x is NaN, +∞, or −∞, then throw a TypeError.
    if !x.is_finite() {
        return vm.throw_completion(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            ErrorType::InvalidRestrictedFloatingPointParameter,
            &[&identifier],
        );
    }

    // 3. Return the IDL double value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    Ok(x)
}

/// A JS value converted to an unrestricted double, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-unrestricted-double
pub(crate) fn to_unrestricted_double(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<f64> {
    // 1. Let x be ? ToNumber(V).
    // 2. If x is NaN, then return the IDL unrestricted double value that represents the IEEE 754 NaN value with the
    //    bit pattern 0x7ff8000000000000.
    // 3. Return the IDL unrestricted double value that represents the same numeric value as x.
    value.to_double(vm)
}

/// What the extended attributes of a buffer source type allow, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-buffer-source-types
pub(crate) struct BufferSourceRules {
    pub(crate) allow_shared: bool,
    pub(crate) allow_resizable: bool,
}

/// The buffer source types included in a union and their conversion rules.
pub(crate) struct BufferSourceTypes<'a> {
    pub(crate) array_buffer_type: Option<&'a BufferSourceRules>,
    pub(crate) shared_array_buffer_type: Option<&'a BufferSourceRules>,
    pub(crate) array_buffer_view_type: Option<&'a BufferSourceRules>,
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-ArrayBuffer
pub(crate) fn to_array_buffer(vm: &Vm, value: Value, rules: &BufferSourceRules) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
    // 1. If V is not an Object, or V does not have an [[ArrayBufferData]] internal slot, then throw a TypeError.
    let buffer = value
        .is_object()
        .then(|| value.as_object().downcast::<ArrayBuffer>())
        .flatten();
    let Some(buffer) = buffer else {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&"ArrayBuffer"]);
    };
    // 2. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(V) is true, then throw a TypeError.
    if buffer.is_shared_array_buffer() {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::SharedArrayBuffer, &[]);
    }
    // 3. If the conversion is not to an IDL type associated with the [AllowResizable] extended attribute, and IsFixedLengthArrayBuffer(V) is false, then throw a TypeError.
    if !rules.allow_resizable && !buffer.is_fixed_length() {
        return vm.throw_completion(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType,
            &[&"fixed-length ArrayBuffer"],
        );
    }
    // 4. Return the IDL ArrayBuffer value that is a reference to the same object as V.
    Ok(buffer)
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-buffer-source-types
pub(crate) fn to_shared_array_buffer(
    vm: &Vm,
    value: Value,
    rules: &BufferSourceRules,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
    // 1. If V is not an Object, or V does not have an [[ArrayBufferData]] internal slot, then throw a TypeError.
    let buffer = value
        .is_object()
        .then(|| value.as_object().downcast::<ArrayBuffer>())
        .flatten();
    let Some(buffer) = buffer else {
        return vm.throw_completion(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType,
            &[&"SharedArrayBuffer"],
        );
    };
    // 2. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(V) is false, then throw a TypeError.
    if !buffer.is_shared_array_buffer() {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotASharedArrayBuffer, &[]);
    }
    // 3. If the conversion is not to an IDL type associated with the [AllowResizable] extended attribute, and
    //    IsFixedLengthArrayBuffer(V) is false, then throw a TypeError.
    if !rules.allow_resizable && !buffer.is_fixed_length() {
        return vm.throw_completion(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType,
            &[&"fixed-length SharedArrayBuffer"],
        );
    }
    // 4. Return the IDL SharedArrayBuffer value that is a reference to the same object as V.
    Ok(buffer)
}

/// A JS value converted to an IDL typed array value of the kind, whose name is the type's name.
pub(crate) fn to_typed_array(
    vm: &Vm,
    value: Value,
    kind: TypedArrayKind,
    name: &str,
    rules: &BufferSourceRules,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<TypedArrayBase>> {
    // 1. Let T be the IDL type V is being converted to.
    // 2. If V is not an Object, or V does not have a [[TypedArrayName]] internal slot with a value equal to T's name,
    //    then throw a TypeError.
    let typed_array = value
        .is_object()
        .then(|| value.as_object().downcast::<TypedArrayBase>())
        .flatten()
        .filter(|typed_array| typed_array.kind() == kind);
    let Some(typed_array) = typed_array else {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&name]);
    };
    check_buffer_of_buffer_source(vm, &typed_array.viewed_array_buffer(), name, rules)?;

    // 5. Return the IDL value of type T that is a reference to the same object as V.
    Ok(typed_array)
}

/// The steps that the conversions to the buffer source types share, which check the buffer of the value against the
/// extended attributes of the type whose name is given.
fn check_buffer_of_buffer_source(
    vm: &Vm,
    buffer: &ArrayBuffer,
    type_name: &str,
    rules: &BufferSourceRules,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()> {
    // If the conversion is not to an IDL type associated with the [AllowShared] extended attribute, and
    // IsSharedArrayBuffer(V.[[ViewedArrayBuffer]]) is true, then throw a TypeError.
    if !rules.allow_shared && buffer.is_shared_array_buffer() {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::SharedArrayBuffer, &[]);
    }

    // If the conversion is not to an IDL type associated with the [AllowResizable] extended attribute, and
    // IsFixedLengthArrayBuffer(V.[[ViewedArrayBuffer]]) is false, then throw a TypeError.
    if !rules.allow_resizable && !buffer.is_fixed_length() {
        return vm.throw_completion(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType,
            &[&format!("fixed-length {type_name}")],
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// An IDL BufferSource value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#BufferSource
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum BufferSource {
    ArrayBuffer(Gc<ArrayBuffer>),
    DataView(Gc<DataView>),
    TypedArray(Gc<TypedArrayBase>),
}

/// An IDL ArrayBufferView value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#ArrayBufferView
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum ArrayBufferView {
    DataView(Gc<DataView>),
    TypedArray(Gc<TypedArrayBase>),
}

impl From<ArrayBufferView> for BufferSource {
    fn from(view: ArrayBufferView) -> Self {
        match view {
            ArrayBufferView::DataView(view) => Self::DataView(view),
            ArrayBufferView::TypedArray(typed_array) => Self::TypedArray(typed_array),
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) struct BufferSourceExtent {
    pub(crate) buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>,
    pub(crate) is_out_of_bounds: bool,
    pub(crate) byte_offset: usize,
    pub(crate) byte_length: usize,
    pub(crate) element_size: usize,
}

impl BufferSource {
    pub(crate) fn extent(&self) -> BufferSourceExtent {
        match self {
            Self::TypedArray(typed_array) => {
                let record = make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record(typed_array, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
                // AD-HOC: The WebIDL spec has not been updated for resizable ArrayBuffer objects. This check follows
                //         the behavior of step 7 of the TypedArray.prototype.buffer getter.
                let is_out_of_bounds = is_typed_array_out_of_bounds(&record);
                let byte_length = if is_out_of_bounds {
                    0
                } else {
                    typed_array_byte_length(&record) as usize
                };
                BufferSourceExtent {
                    buffer: typed_array.viewed_array_buffer(),
                    is_out_of_bounds,
                    byte_offset: typed_array.byte_offset(),
                    byte_length,
                    element_size: typed_array.element_size(),
                }
            }
            Self::DataView(view) => {
                let record = make_data_view_with_buffer_witness_record(*view, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
                // AD-HOC: The WebIDL spec has not been updated for resizable ArrayBuffer objects. This check follows
                //         the behavior of step 7 of the DataView.prototype.buffer getter.
                let is_out_of_bounds = is_view_out_of_bounds(&record);
                let byte_length = if is_out_of_bounds {
                    0
                } else {
                    get_view_byte_length(&record) as usize
                };
                BufferSourceExtent {
                    buffer: view.viewed_array_buffer(),
                    is_out_of_bounds,
                    byte_offset: view.byte_offset(),
                    byte_length,
                    element_size: 1,
                }
            }
            Self::ArrayBuffer(buffer) => BufferSourceExtent {
                buffer: *buffer,
                is_out_of_bounds: false,
                byte_offset: 0,
                byte_length: buffer.byte_length(),
                element_size: 1,
            },
        }
    }

    /// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-get-buffer-source-copy, without copying the bytes unless their buffer is
    /// shared.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The function must not run script or allocate a cell, either of which could detach, resize or free the buffer
    /// that the bytes are in.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn with_bytes<R>(&self, function: impl FnOnce(&[u8]) -> R) -> R {
        let extent = self.extent();
        // 7. If IsDetachedBuffer(jsArrayBuffer) is true, then return the empty byte sequence.
        let held_byte_length = if extent.buffer.is_detached() {
            0
        } else {
            extent.byte_length
        };
        let held_bytes = extent.byte_offset..extent.byte_offset + held_byte_length;
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the function from running script and from allocating.
        unsafe { with_bytes_of_buffer(&extent.buffer, held_bytes, function) }
            .expect("a buffer has the bytes of its views that are in bounds")
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// The function must not run script or allocate a cell, either of which could detach, resize or free the buffer that
/// the bytes are in.
pub(crate) unsafe fn with_bytes_of_buffer<R>(
    buffer: &ArrayBuffer,
    bytes: Range<usize>,
    function: impl FnOnce(&[u8]) -> R,
) -> Option<R> {
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the function from running script and from allocating.
    unsafe { borrowed_or_copied_bytes_of_buffer(buffer, bytes) }.map(|bytes| function(&bytes))
}

/// `None` when the buffer does not have the bytes.
pub(crate) fn copy_of_bytes_of_buffer(buffer: &ArrayBuffer, bytes: Range<usize>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    // SAFETY: The bytes are borrowed only while they are copied, which neither runs script nor allocates a cell.
    unsafe { borrowed_or_copied_bytes_of_buffer(buffer, bytes) }.map(Cow::into_owned)
}

/// # Safety
///
/// Nothing may run script or allocate a cell while the bytes are borrowed, either of which could detach, resize or
/// free the buffer that they are in.
unsafe fn borrowed_or_copied_bytes_of_buffer(buffer: &ArrayBuffer, bytes: Range<usize>) -> Option<Cow<'_, [u8]>> {
    if bytes.is_empty() {
        return Some(Cow::Borrowed(&[]));
    }
    if buffer.is_detached() || bytes.end > buffer.byte_length() {
        return None;
    }

    // NB: Another thread can write the bytes of a shared buffer at any time, so they are copied.
    if buffer.is_shared_array_buffer() {
        return Some(Cow::Owned(buffer.copy_to_byte_buffer(bytes.start, bytes.len())));
    }
    let data = buffer.with_data_block(|data_block| data_block.data_at(bytes.start));
    assert!(!data.is_null());
    // SAFETY: The buffer is not detached and has the bytes, which nothing writes while they are borrowed, as the
    //         buffer is not shared and the caller keeps script from running.
    Some(Cow::Borrowed(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(data, bytes.len()) }))
}

/// A promise converted from a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-promise
#[allow(
    clippy::unnecessary_wraps,
    reason = "the bindings convert every argument with a conversion that can throw"
)]
pub(crate) fn to_promise(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<WebIdlPromise> {
    // 1. Let promiseCapability be ? NewPromiseCapability(%Promise%).
    let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a conversion runs in a realm");
    let promise = crate::bindings::promise::create_promise(vm, realm);

    // 2. Perform ? Call(promiseCapability.[[Resolve]], undefined, « V »).
    crate::bindings::promise::resolve_promise(vm, promise, value);

    // 3. Return promiseCapability.
    Ok(promise)
}

/// The value as a BufferSource, if it is an ArrayBuffer, a DataView or a typed array, without the checks of a
/// conversion to the type.
pub(crate) fn buffer_source_type_of(value: Value) -> Option<BufferSource> {
    if !value.is_object() {
        return None;
    }
    let object = value.as_object();
    object
        .downcast::<ArrayBuffer>()
        .map(BufferSource::ArrayBuffer)
        .or_else(|| object.downcast::<DataView>().map(BufferSource::DataView))
        .or_else(|| object.downcast::<TypedArrayBase>().map(BufferSource::TypedArray))
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#arraybufferview-create, for a Uint8Array in the realm of the call context.
pub(crate) fn create_uint8_array(cx: &CallContext, bytes: &[u8]) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<Object>> {
    let buffer =
        ArrayBuffer::try_create_written_by(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), bytes.len(), ArrayBufferShared::No, |output| {
            for (byte, value) in output.iter_mut().zip(bytes) {
                byte.write(*value);
            }
            bytes.len()
        })?;
    Ok(create_typed_array_on_buffer(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), TypedArrayKind::Uint8Array, bytes.len(), buffer).upcast())
}

impl ArrayBufferView {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The function must not run script or allocate a cell, either of which could detach, resize or free the buffer
    /// that the bytes are in.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn with_bytes<R>(&self, function: impl FnOnce(&[u8]) -> R) -> R {
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the function from running script and from allocating.
        unsafe { BufferSource::from(*self).with_bytes(function) }
    }
}

/// A JS value converted to a BufferSource, with the steps of the conversion to a union type that apply to the buffer
/// source types, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-union
pub(crate) fn to_buffer_source(vm: &Vm, value: Value, rules: &BufferSourceRules) -> ThrowCompletionOr<BufferSource> {
    let types = BufferSourceTypes {
        array_buffer_type: Some(rules),
        shared_array_buffer_type: rules.allow_shared.then_some(rules),
        array_buffer_view_type: Some(rules),
    };
    if value.is_object()
        && let Some(buffer_source) = buffer_source_if(vm, value.as_object(), types)?
    {
        return Ok(buffer_source);
    }

    // 20. Throw a TypeError.
    throw_no_union_types_matched(vm)
}

/// An object converted to a BufferSource if it is one, with the steps of the conversion to a union type that apply
/// to the buffer source types, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-union
pub(crate) fn buffer_source_if(
    vm: &Vm,
    object: Gc<Object>,
    types: BufferSourceTypes<'_>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Option<BufferSource>> {
    // 6. If V is an Object, V has an [[ArrayBufferData]] internal slot, and IsSharedArrayBuffer(V) is false, then:
    //     1. If types includes ArrayBuffer, then return the result of converting V to ArrayBuffer.
    if let Some(buffer) = object.downcast::<ArrayBuffer>()
        && !buffer.is_shared_array_buffer()
        && let Some(rules) = types.array_buffer_type
    {
        check_buffer_of_buffer_source(vm, &buffer, "ArrayBuffer", rules)?;
        return Ok(Some(BufferSource::ArrayBuffer(buffer)));
    }

    // 7. If V is an Object, V, has an [[ArrayBufferData]] internal slot, and IsSharedArrayBuffer(V) is true, then:
    //     1. If types includes SharedArrayBuffer, then return the result of converting V to SharedArrayBuffer.
    if let Some(buffer) = object.downcast::<ArrayBuffer>()
        && buffer.is_shared_array_buffer()
        && let Some(rules) = types.shared_array_buffer_type
    {
        let buffer = to_shared_array_buffer(vm, Value::from_object(object), rules)?;
        return Ok(Some(BufferSource::ArrayBuffer(buffer)));
    }

    // 8. If V is an Object and V has a [[DataView]] internal slot, then:
    //     1. If types includes DataView, then return the result of converting V to DataView.
    if let Some(view) = object.downcast::<DataView>()
        && let Some(rules) = types.array_buffer_view_type
    {
        check_buffer_of_buffer_source(vm, &view.viewed_array_buffer(), "DataView", rules)?;
        return Ok(Some(BufferSource::DataView(view)));
    }

    // 9. If V is an Object and V has a [[TypedArrayName]] internal slot, then:
    //     1. If types includes a typed array type whose name is the value of V's [[TypedArrayName]] internal slot,
    //        then return the result of converting V to that type.
    if let Some(typed_array) = object.downcast::<TypedArrayBase>()
        && let Some(rules) = types.array_buffer_view_type
    {
        let type_name = format!("{:?}", typed_array.kind());
        check_buffer_of_buffer_source(vm, &typed_array.viewed_array_buffer(), &type_name, rules)?;
        return Ok(Some(BufferSource::TypedArray(typed_array)));
    }

    Ok(None)
}

/// A JS value converted to an ArrayBufferView, with the steps of the conversion to a union type that apply to the
/// types of the views, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-union
pub(crate) fn to_array_buffer_view(
    vm: &Vm,
    value: Value,
    rules: &BufferSourceRules,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<ArrayBufferView> {
    if value.is_object() {
        let object = value.as_object();

        // 8. If V is an Object and V has a [[DataView]] internal slot, then:
        //     1. If types includes DataView, then return the result of converting V to DataView.
        if let Some(view) = object.downcast::<DataView>() {
            check_buffer_of_buffer_source(vm, &view.viewed_array_buffer(), "DataView", rules)?;
            return Ok(ArrayBufferView::DataView(view));
        }

        // 9. If V is an Object and V has a [[TypedArrayName]] internal slot, then:
        //     1. If types includes a typed array type whose name is the value of V's [[TypedArrayName]] internal slot,
        //        then return the result of converting V to that type.
        if let Some(typed_array) = object.downcast::<TypedArrayBase>() {
            let type_name = format!("{:?}", typed_array.kind());
            check_buffer_of_buffer_source(vm, &typed_array.viewed_array_buffer(), &type_name, rules)?;
            return Ok(ArrayBufferView::TypedArray(typed_array));
        }
    }

    // 20. Throw a TypeError.
    throw_no_union_types_matched(vm)
}

/// The last step of the conversion of a JS value to a union type, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-union, with
/// the message of the C++ bindings.
pub(crate) fn throw_no_union_types_matched<T>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T> {
    // 20. Throw a TypeError.
    vm.throw_completion_with_message(ErrorKind::TypeError, "No union types matched".to_string())
}

/// Where an IDL sequence keeps its elements: a Vec, which hides cells from the collector, so its elements hold none,
/// or a MarkedVec, which keeps them alive while the rest are converted and for as long as the sequence lives.
pub(crate) trait SequenceStorage<T> {
    fn append(&mut self, value: T);
}

impl<T> SequenceStorage<T> for Vec<T> {
    fn append(&mut self, value: T) {
        self.push(value);
    }
}

impl<T: Trace + Clone + 'static> SequenceStorage<T> for MarkedVec<'_, T> {
    fn append(&mut self, value: T) {
        self.push(value);
    }
}

/// A JS value converted to an IDL sequence in `sequence`, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-sequence, with the
/// conversion of its elements.
pub(crate) fn sequence_from_js<T, S: SequenceStorage<T>>(
    vm: &Vm,
    value: Value,
    sequence: S,
    element_from_js: impl FnMut(Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<S> {
    // 1. If V is not an Object, throw a TypeError.
    if !value.is_object() {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&value]);
    }

    // 2. Let method be ? GetMethod(V, %Symbol.iterator%).
    // 3. If method is undefined, throw a TypeError.
    let Some(method) = iterator_method(vm, value)? else {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotIterable, &[&value]);
    };

    // 4. Return the result of creating a sequence from V and method.
    sequence_from_iterable(vm, value, method, sequence, element_from_js)
}

/// ? GetMethod(V, %Symbol.iterator%), which decides whether a JS value converts to a sequence type.
pub(crate) fn iterator_method(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Option<Gc<FunctionObject>>> {
    value.get_method(vm, &PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().iterator))
}

/// An IDL sequence in `sequence` created from an iterable and its iterator getter method,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#create-sequence-from-iterable
pub(crate) fn sequence_from_iterable<T, S: SequenceStorage<T>>(
    vm: &Vm,
    iterable: Value,
    method: Gc<FunctionObject>,
    mut sequence: S,
    mut element_from_js: impl FnMut(Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<S> {
    // 1. Let iteratorRecord be ? GetIteratorFromMethod(iterable, method).
    let iterator_record = get_iterator_from_method_impl(vm, iterable, method)?;

    // 2. Initialize i to be 0.
    // 3. Repeat
    //     1. Let next be ? IteratorStepValue(iteratorRecord).
    //     2. If next is done, then return an IDL sequence value of type sequence<T> of length i, where the value of the
    //        element at index j is Sj.
    while let Some(next) = iterator_step_value(vm, &iterator_record)? {
        //     3. Initialize Si to the result of converting next to an IDL value of type T.
        //     4. Set i to i + 1.
        sequence.append(element_from_js(next)?);
    }
    Ok(sequence)
}

pub(crate) trait RecordStorage<K, V> {
    /// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set
    fn set(&mut self, key: K, value: V);
}

impl<K: PartialEq, V> RecordStorage<K, V> for Vec<(K, V)> {
    fn set(&mut self, key: K, value: V) {
        match self.iter_mut().find(|(existing_key, _)| *existing_key == key) {
            Some(entry) => entry.1 = value,
            None => self.push((key, value)),
        }
    }
}

impl<K: PartialEq + Trace + Clone + 'static, V: Trace + Clone + 'static> RecordStorage<K, V> for MarkedVec<'_, (K, V)> {
    fn set(&mut self, key: K, value: V) {
        let index = self.values().iter().position(|(existing_key, _)| *existing_key == key);
        match index {
            Some(index) => MarkedVec::set(self, index, (key, value)),
            None => self.push((key, value)),
        }
    }
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-record
pub(crate) fn record_from_js<K: PartialEq, V, R: RecordStorage<K, V>>(
    vm: &Vm,
    value: Value,
    storage: R,
    mut key_from_js: impl FnMut(Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<K>,
    mut value_from_js: impl FnMut(Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<V>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<R> {
    // 1. If O is not an Object, throw a TypeError.
    if !value.is_object() {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObject, &[&value]);
    }
    let object = value.as_object();

    // 2. Let result be a new empty instance of record<K, V>.
    let mut result = storage;

    // 3. Let keys be ? O.[[OwnPropertyKeys]]().
    let keys = object.internal_own_property_keys(vm)?;

    // 4. For each key of keys:
    for index in 0..keys.len() {
        let key = keys.get(index).expect("the index is in bounds");
        let property_key = PropertyKey::from_value(vm, key).must();

        // 1. Let desc be ? O.[[GetOwnProperty]](key).
        let descriptor = object.internal_get_own_property(vm, &property_key)?;

        // 2. If desc is not undefined and desc.[[Enumerable]] is true:
        if !descriptor.is_some_and(|descriptor| descriptor.enumerable == Some(true)) {
            continue;
        }

        // 1. Let typedKey be key converted to an IDL value of type K.
        let typed_key = key_from_js(key)?;

        // 2. Let value be ? Get(O, key).
        let value = object.get(vm, &property_key)?;

        // 3. Let typedValue be value converted to an IDL value of type V.
        let typed_value = value_from_js(value)?;

        // 4. Set result[typedKey] to typedValue.
        result.set(typed_key, typed_value);
    }

    // 5. Return result.
    Ok(result)
}

/// The types of the IDL definitions that a JS value converts to, with the conversions that the generated bindings
/// write for them.
pub(crate) trait FromJs: Sized {
    fn from_js(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Self>;
}

/// A dictionary without required members, which has a value that no JS value was converted to: the default value
/// `{}` of a parameter.
pub(crate) trait EmptyDictionary {
    fn empty() -> Self;
}

/// The object that the members of a dictionary are read from, step 1 of https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-dictionary.
/// It is None for undefined and null, which convert to a dictionary without reading a member.
pub(crate) fn dictionary_object(vm: &Vm, value: Value, dictionary_name: &str) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Option<Gc<Object>>> {
    // 1. If V is not Undefined, Null, or an Object, then throw a TypeError.
    if value.is_object() {
        return Ok(Some(value.as_object()));
    }
    if value.is_nullish() {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&dictionary_name])
}

/// The value of a member of a dictionary, if the object it is read from has one that is not undefined, steps 4.1.2
/// and 4.1.3 of https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-dictionary
pub(crate) fn dictionary_member(
    vm: &Vm,
    object: Option<Gc<Object>>,
    key: &PropertyKey,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Option<Value>> {
    // 2. If V is Undefined or Null, then let jsMemberValue be undefined.
    let Some(object) = object else {
        return Ok(None);
    };

    // 3. Otherwise, let jsMemberValue be ? Get(V, key).
    let value = object.get(vm, key)?;
    Ok((!value.is_undefined()).then_some(value))
}

/// An IDL value converted to a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-type-mapping
pub(crate) trait ToJs {
    fn to_js(self, cx: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value>;
}

impl ToJs for () {
    fn to_js(self, _: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
    }
}

impl ToJs for bool {
    fn to_js(self, _: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::from_bool(self))
    }
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-any
impl ToJs for Value {
    fn to_js(self, _: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(self)
    }
}

/// An object converted to a JS value: https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-object, and what an implementation returns
/// for a promise type, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-promise, which is the promise object.
impl ToJs for Gc<Object> {
    fn to_js(self, _: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::from_object(self))
    }
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-promise
impl ToJs for WebIdlPromise {
    fn to_js(self, _: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::from_object(self.promise()))
    }
}

    }
