/// A callback function converted to a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-callback-function
impl ToJs for Gc<FunctionObject> {
    fn to_js(self, _: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::from_object(self))
    }
}

impl ToJs for Utf16String {
    fn to_js(self, cx: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(cx.vm(), self)))
    }
}

impl ToJs for UsvString {
    fn to_js(self, cx: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        self.into_utf16_string().to_js(cx)
    }
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-ByteString
impl ToJs for ByteString {
    fn to_js(self, cx: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        // The result of converting an IDL ByteString value to a JavaScript value is a String value whose length is the
        // length of the ByteString, and the value of each element of which is the value of the corresponding element
        // of the ByteString.
        let string = if self.0.is_ascii() {
            Utf16String::from_ascii(&self.0)
        } else {
            Utf16String::from_utf16(&self.0.iter().map(|byte| u16::from(*byte)).collect::<Vec<_>>())
        };
        string.to_js(cx)
    }
}

impl ToJs for Gc<TypedArrayBase> {
    fn to_js(self, _: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::from_object(self))
    }
}

impl ToJs for ArrayBufferView {
    fn to_js(self, _: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(match self {
            Self::DataView(view) => Value::from_object(view),
            Self::TypedArray(array) => Value::from_object(array),
        })
    }
}

impl ToJs for Gc<ArrayBuffer> {
    fn to_js(self, _: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::from_object(self))
    }
}

/// An object of an interface converted to a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-interface
impl<T: Interface> ToJs for Ref<T> {
    fn to_js(self, cx: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::from_object(wrap(cx, self)))
    }
}

/// (DOMString or sequence<DOMString>), which more than one interface's IDL names without a typedef.
pub(crate) enum DOMStringOrDOMStringSequence {
    DOMString(Utf16String),
    Sequence(Vec<Utf16String>),
}

/// An object of an interface that LibWeb implements in C++, as its wrapper. Only the C++ code knows the object
/// behind the wrapper, so an implementation hands the wrapper to a service of LibWeb to have something done with it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CppInterface(Gc<Object>);

impl CppInterface {
    /// The object whose wrapper a service of LibWeb returned.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `wrapper` must be a wrapper of an object of the interface that the IDL names where the value is used.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_wrapper(wrapper: Gc<Object>) -> Self {
        Self(wrapper)
    }

    pub(crate) fn wrapper(self) -> Gc<Object> {
        self.0
    }

    pub(crate) fn cell(self) -> CppCell {
        // SAFETY: The wrapper is live, and LibWeb returns the live cell of the object that it wraps.
        unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(web_bindings_cell_of_wrapper(self.0.as_ptr().cast())) }
    }
}

/// Whether the object is a wrapper of an object that implements the interface, which LibWeb implements in C++ and
/// knows by the value of its Web::Bindings::InterfaceName.
pub(crate) fn implements_cpp_interface(object: Gc<Object>, interface_name: u16) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: The object is live.
    object.is_platform_object()
        && unsafe { web_bindings_object_implements_interface(object.as_ptr().cast(), interface_name) }
}

/// An object of an interface that LibWeb implements in C++ converted from a JS value,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-interface
pub(crate) fn to_cpp_interface(
    vm: &Vm,
    value: Value,
    interface_name: u16,
    name: &str,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<CppInterface> {
    // 1. If V implements I, then return the IDL interface type value that represents a reference to that platform
    //    object.
    if value.is_object() && implements_cpp_interface(value.as_object(), interface_name) {
        return Ok(CppInterface(value.as_object()));
    }
    // 2. Throw a TypeError.
    vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&name])
}

/// A JS value converted to a union of interfaces that LibWeb implements in C++, which the values of their
/// Web::Bindings::InterfaceName name, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-union
pub(crate) fn to_cpp_interface_in_union(
    vm: &Vm,
    value: Value,
    interface_names: &[u16],
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<CppInterface> {
    // 5. If V is a platform object, then:
    //     1. If types includes an interface type that V implements, then return the IDL value that is a reference to
    //        the object V.
    if value.is_object()
        && interface_names
            .iter()
            .any(|interface_name| implements_cpp_interface(value.as_object(), *interface_name))
    {
        return Ok(CppInterface(value.as_object()));
    }
    throw_no_union_types_matched(vm)
}

/// The WindowProxy whose exotic object this is, if any.
pub(crate) fn window_proxy_from_object(object: Gc<Object>) -> Option<CppInterface> {
    // SAFETY: The object is live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_object_is_window_proxy(object.as_ptr().cast()) }.then_some(CppInterface(object))
}

/// A WindowProxy converted from a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-interface
pub(crate) fn to_window_proxy(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<CppInterface> {
    // 1. If V implements I, then return the IDL interface type value that represents a reference to that platform
    //    object.
    if value.is_object()
        && let Some(window_proxy) = window_proxy_from_object(value.as_object())
    {
        return Ok(window_proxy);
    }
    // 2. Throw a TypeError.
    vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&"WindowProxy"])
}

/// A WindowProxy converted to a JS value, as the object that scripts of the realm see for it.
pub(crate) fn window_proxy_to_js(cx: &CallContext, window_proxy: CppInterface) -> Value {
    // SAFETY: The object and the realm are live.
    let object = unsafe {
        web_bindings_window_proxy_object_in_realm(window_proxy.0.as_ptr().cast(), cx.realm().as_ptr().cast())
    };
    let object = NonNull::new(object.cast::<Object>()).expect("a WindowProxy has an object");
    // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live object.
    Value::from_object(unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(object) })
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-interface
impl ToJs for CppInterface {
    fn to_js(self, _: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::from_object(self.0))
    }
}

/// An IDL sequence converted to a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-sequence, with the conversion of its
/// elements.
pub(crate) fn sequence_to_js<T>(
    cx: &CallContext,
    sequence: Vec<T>,
    mut element_to_js: impl FnMut(T) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let n be the length of S.
    // 2. Let A be a new Array object created as if by the expression [].
    let array = Array::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), sequence.len() as u64, None)?;

    // 3. Initialize i to be 0.
    // 4. While i < n:
    for (index, element) in sequence.into_iter().enumerate() {
        // 1. Let V be the value in S at index i.
        // 2. Let E be the result of converting V to a JavaScript value.
        let element = element_to_js(element)?;

        // 3. Let P be the result of calling ! ToString(i).
        // 4. Perform ! CreateDataPropertyOrThrow(A, P, E).
        // 5. Set i to i + 1.
        let index = u32::try_from(index).expect("an array of the length of the sequence was created");
        array.create_data_property(cx.vm(), &PropertyKey::from(index), element, None, None)?;
    }

    // 5. Return A.
    Ok(Value::from_object(array))
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-frozen-array
pub(crate) fn frozen_array_to_js(cx: &CallContext, array: ThrowCompletionOr<Value>) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let array be the result of converting the sequence of type T to a JavaScript value.
    let array = array?;

    // 2. Perform ! SetIntegrityLevel(array, "frozen").
    array
        .as_object()
        .set_integrity_level(cx.vm(), IntegrityLevel::Frozen)
        .must();

    // 3. Return array.
    Ok(array)
}

/// sequence_to_js() for a sequence of cells, which stay rooted while converting an element allocates.
pub(crate) fn rooted_sequence_to_js<T: Trace + Clone + 'static>(
    cx: &CallContext,
    sequence: MarkedVec<'_, T>,
    mut element_to_js: impl FnMut(&T) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    let array = Array::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), sequence.len() as u64, None)?;
    for (index, element) in sequence.values().iter().enumerate() {
        let element = element_to_js(element)?;
        let index = u32::try_from(index).expect("an array of the length of the sequence was created");
        array.create_data_property(cx.vm(), &PropertyKey::from(index), element, None, None)?;
    }
    Ok(Value::from_object(array))
}

/// The elements of a sequence of a dictionary in a MarkedVec, which keeps them alive while the dictionary is converted.
pub(crate) fn mark_sequence<'vm, T: Trace + Clone + 'static>(
    cx: &CallContext<'vm>,
    sequence: &[T],
) -> MarkedVec<'vm, T> {
    let marked = MarkedVec::with_capacity(cx.vm(), sequence.len());
    marked.extend_from_slice(sequence);
    marked
}

/// An IDL record converted to a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-record, with the conversion of its
/// values. The entries of the record are in the order of the Vec.
pub(crate) fn record_to_js<K: Into<Utf16String>, V>(
    cx: &CallContext,
    record: Vec<(K, V)>,
    mut value_to_js: impl FnMut(V) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let result be OrdinaryObjectCreate(%Object.prototype%).
    let result = create_dictionary_object(cx);

    // 2. For each key → value of D:
    for (key, value) in record {
        // 1. Let jsKey be key converted to a JavaScript value.
        let key = PropertyKey::from_utf16_string(&key.into());

        // 2. Let jsValue be value converted to a JavaScript value.
        let value = value_to_js(value)?;

        // 3. Let created be ! CreateDataProperty(result, jsKey, jsValue).
        // 4. Assert: created is true.
        result.create_data_property(cx.vm(), &key, value, None, None)?;
    }

    // 3. Return result.
    Ok(Value::from_object(result))
}

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{ForeignCellSlot, Gc, GcWeak, Trace, Vm};

/// A cell of LibWeb's C++ code, which this keeps alive.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CppCell(ForeignCellSlot);

impl Clone for CppCell {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The slot keeps the cell alive.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw(self.0.as_ptr()) }
    }
}

/// The C++ classes of the cells that LibWeb's C++ code lends the exports of the crate, which name the class of a
/// LentCppCell.
pub(crate) mod cpp_class {
    /// A GC::Cell of any class, which the code that the export hands it to does not rely on.
    pub(crate) enum Cell {}

    /// A GC::Function<void()> that runs an abort algorithm.
    pub(crate) enum AbortAlgorithm {}
    /// A GC::Function<void(ByteBuffer)>, a Streams::ReadableStreamDefaultReader::SuccessSteps.
    pub(crate) enum BytesSteps {}
    /// A CSS::CSSRule.
    pub(crate) enum CSSRule {}
    /// A CSS::CSSStyleDeclaration.
    pub(crate) enum CSSStyleDeclaration {}
    /// A CSS::CSSStyleProperties.
    pub(crate) enum CSSStyleProperties {}
    /// A CSS::CSSStyleSheet.
    pub(crate) enum CSSStyleSheet {}
    /// A DOM::Document.
    pub(crate) enum Document {}
    /// A DOM::Element.
    pub(crate) enum Element {}
    /// An HTML::EnvironmentSettingsObject.
    pub(crate) enum EnvironmentSettingsObject {}
    /// A DOM::Event.
    pub(crate) enum Event {}
    /// An HTML::EventLoop.
    pub(crate) enum EventLoop {}
    /// A DOM::EventTarget.
    pub(crate) enum EventTarget {}
    /// A Fetch::Infrastructure::FetchController.
    pub(crate) enum FetchController {}
    /// A DOM::Node.
    pub(crate) enum Node {}
    /// A GC::Function<GC::Ref<WebIDL::Promise>()>, a Streams::PullAlgorithm or a Streams::FlushAlgorithm.
    pub(crate) enum PromiseAlgorithm {}
    /// A GC::Function<GC::Ref<WebIDL::Promise>(JS::Value)>, a Streams::CancelAlgorithm, a Streams::TransformAlgorithm
    /// or a Streams::WriteAlgorithm.
    pub(crate) enum PromiseAlgorithmWithArgument {}
    /// A Streams::ReadRequest.
    pub(crate) enum ReadRequest {}
    /// A Fetch::Infrastructure::ResponseView.
    pub(crate) enum ResponseView {}
    /// A CSS::StyleSheetImportCell.
    pub(crate) enum StyleSheetImportCell {}
    /// A CSS::StyleSheetStateCell.
    pub(crate) enum StyleSheetStateCell {}
    /// An HTML::TextTrack.
    pub(crate) enum TextTrack {}
    /// A GC::Function<void(JS::Value)>, a Streams::ReadableStreamDefaultReader::FailureSteps.
    pub(crate) enum ValueSteps {}
    /// An HTML::Window.
    pub(crate) enum Window {}
}

/// A cell of LibWeb's C++ code, of the C++ class that `Class` names, which C++ lends the exports of the crate for as
/// long as they run. The exports take a `&LentCppCell<Class>` where C++ passes such a cell, as they take a `&Vm` where
/// it passes the VM, so a reference to one is always a live cell of that class. The wrappers of the cells of a class
/// make themselves only of a cell lent as one of that class; CppCell, which assumes no class, of any.
#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct LentCppCell<Class> {
    // NB: The cell is mutable behind a shared reference, and bigger than Rust sees, so a reference to one must not tell
    //     the compiler that the memory behind it is read only or unaliased.
    _opaque: core::cell::UnsafeCell<[u8; 0]>,
    _not_send_sync_or_unpin: core::marker::PhantomData<(*const (), core::marker::PhantomPinned)>,
    _class: core::marker::PhantomData<Class>,
}

impl CppCell {
    /// Keeps alive the cell that C++ lends, whatever its class.
    pub(crate) fn from_lent<Class>(cell: &LentCppCell<Class>) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: A LentCppCell is a live cell.
        unsafe { Self::from_raw(NonNull::from(cell).as_ptr().cast()) }
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `cell` must be a live cell of LibWeb's C++ code.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_raw(cell: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        let slot = ForeignCellSlot::empty();
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell.
        unsafe { slot.set(Some(NonNull::new(cell).expect("C++ passes a cell"))) };
        Self(slot)
    }

    pub(crate) fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.as_ptr()
    }
}

/// A cell of LibWeb's C++ code, which this does not keep alive.
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct WeakCppCell(GcWeak<c_void>);

impl WeakCppCell {
    pub(crate) fn new(vm: &Vm, cell: &CppCell) -> Self {
        let cell = NonNull::new(cell.as_ptr()).expect("a CppCell holds a cell");
        // SAFETY: The CppCell keeps the cell alive.
        Self(GcWeak::new(vm.heap(), unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(cell) }))
    }

    pub(crate) fn get(&self) -> Option<CppCell> {
        // SAFETY: A cell that the weak reference still has is live.
        self.0.get().map(|cell| unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(cell.as_ptr()) })
    }
}

use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_bindings_relevant_settings_object(global_object: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_bindings_principal_realm_settings_object(realm: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_global_object(settings_object: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_realm(settings_object: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_time_origin(settings_object: *mut c_void) -> f64;
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_is_secure_context(settings_object: *mut c_void) -> bool;
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_top_level_origin(
        settings_object: *mut c_void,
        origin: *mut c_void,
        on_origin: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const FfiOrigin),
    ) -> bool;
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_api_base_url(
        settings_object: *mut c_void,
        url: *mut c_void,
        on_url: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const RustUrl),
    );
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_current_wall_time(settings_object: *mut c_void) -> f64;
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_id(
        settings_object: *mut c_void,
        id: *mut c_void,
        on_id: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, ak::Span<'_, u8>),
    );
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_origin(
        settings_object: *mut c_void,
        origin: *mut c_void,
        on_origin: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const FfiOrigin),
    );
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_creation_url(
        settings_object: *mut c_void,
        url: *mut c_void,
        on_url: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const RustUrl),
    );
    fn web_bindings_environment_settings_object_encoding_parse_url(
        settings_object: *mut c_void,
        url: usize,
        parsed_url: *mut c_void,
        on_url: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const RustUrl),
    );
}

unsafe extern "C" fn on_url(parsed_url: *mut c_void, url: *const RustUrl) {
    // SAFETY: parsed_url is the URL of the caller, and LibWeb lends the URL for the call.
    unsafe { *parsed_url.cast::<Option<Url>>() = Some((*url).to_url()) };
}

unsafe extern "C" fn on_origin(origin: *mut c_void, ffi_origin: *const FfiOrigin) {
    // SAFETY: origin is the origin of the caller, and LibWeb lends the origin for the call.
    unsafe { *origin.cast::<Option<Origin>>() = Some((*ffi_origin).to_origin()) };
}

unsafe extern "C" fn on_id(id: *mut c_void, bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>) {
    // SAFETY: id is the string of the caller, and LibWeb lends the id, which is ASCII, for the call.
    unsafe { *id.cast::<String>() = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes.as_slice()).into_owned() };
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#environment-settings-object
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CppEnvironmentSettingsObject(CppCell);

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#relevant-settings-object
pub(crate) fn relevant_settings_object(global_object: Gc<Object>) -> CppEnvironmentSettingsObject {
    // SAFETY: The global object is live, and LibWeb returns its live environment settings object.
    CppEnvironmentSettingsObject(unsafe {
        CppCell::from_raw(web_bindings_relevant_settings_object(global_object.as_ptr().cast()))
    })
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#current-settings-object
pub(crate) fn current_settings_object(vm: &Vm) -> CppEnvironmentSettingsObject {
    // Then, the current settings object is the environment settings object of the current realm.
    let current_realm = vm.current_realm().expect("there is a current realm");
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and LibWeb returns its live environment settings object.
    CppEnvironmentSettingsObject(unsafe {
        CppCell::from_raw(web_bindings_principal_realm_settings_object(
            current_realm.as_ptr().cast(),
        ))
    })
}

impl CppEnvironmentSettingsObject {
    pub(crate) fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.as_ptr()
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-environment-id
    pub(crate) fn id(&self) -> String {
        let mut id = String::new();
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live, and the id outlives the call.
        unsafe { web_bindings_environment_settings_object_id(self.as_ptr(), (&raw mut id).cast(), on_id) };
        id
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-settings-object-global
    pub(crate) fn global_object(&self) -> Gc<Object> {
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live, and LibWeb returns its live global object.
        let global_object = unsafe { web_bindings_environment_settings_object_global_object(self.as_ptr()) };
        // SAFETY: The global object is live.
        unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(global_object.cast()).expect("a settings object has a global object")) }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#environment-settings-object's-realm
    pub(crate) fn realm(&self) -> Gc<Realm> {
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live, and LibWeb returns its live realm.
        let realm = unsafe { web_bindings_environment_settings_object_realm(self.as_ptr()) };
        // SAFETY: The realm is live.
        unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(realm.cast()).expect("a settings object has a realm")) }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#secure-context
    pub(crate) fn is_secure_context(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_environment_settings_object_is_secure_context(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-settings-object-time-origin
    pub(crate) fn time_origin(&self) -> f64 {
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_environment_settings_object_time_origin(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-settings-object-origin
    pub(crate) fn origin(&self) -> Origin {
        let mut origin = None;
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live, and the origin outlives the call.
        unsafe { web_bindings_environment_settings_object_origin(self.as_ptr(), (&raw mut origin).cast(), on_origin) };
        origin.expect("LibWeb lends the origin")
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-environment-creation-url
    pub(crate) fn creation_url(&self) -> Url {
        let mut url = None;
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live, and the URL outlives the call.
        unsafe { web_bindings_environment_settings_object_creation_url(self.as_ptr(), (&raw mut url).cast(), on_url) };
        url.expect("LibWeb lends the creation URL")
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-environment-top-level-origin
    pub(crate) fn top_level_origin(&self) -> Option<Origin> {
        let mut origin = None;
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live, and the origin outlives the call.
        unsafe {
            web_bindings_environment_settings_object_top_level_origin(
                self.as_ptr(),
                (&raw mut origin).cast(),
                on_origin,
            )
        };
        origin
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#api-base-url
    pub(crate) fn api_base_url(&self) -> Url {
        let mut url = None;
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live, and the URL outlives the call.
        unsafe { web_bindings_environment_settings_object_api_base_url(self.as_ptr(), (&raw mut url).cast(), on_url) };
        url.expect("LibWeb lends the API base URL")
    }

    /// https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-wall-time
    pub(crate) fn current_wall_time(&self) -> f64 {
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_environment_settings_object_current_wall_time(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/urls-and-fetching.html#encoding-parsing-a-url
    pub(crate) fn encoding_parse_url(&self, url: &Utf16String) -> Option<Url> {
        let mut parsed_url = None;
        // SAFETY: The settings object is live, the URL is lent for the call, and the parsed URL outlives it.
        unsafe {
            web_bindings_environment_settings_object_encoding_parse_url(
                self.as_ptr(),
                url.raw_identity(),
                (&raw mut parsed_url).cast(),
                on_url,
            );
        }
        parsed_url
    }

//! The EventTarget or Event that an object of an interface implemented in Rust owns when its interface inherits from
//! one of them, which LibWeb implements in C++ (Libraries/LibWeb/Bindings/RustEventTarget.h). The object's wrappers
//! hold it as their wrappable, so that the C++ bindings of EventTarget and Event run on it, and its wrappers are the

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{FunctionObject, Gc, Realm, Trace, Value};

/// The EventTarget that an object owns.
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CppEventTarget(CppCell);

/// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#get-the-parent
pub(crate) trait GetTheParent: Interface {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget>;
}

/// The steps that run whenever an event listener is added to or removed from the EventTarget of an owner.
pub(crate) trait EventListenerListChanged: Interface {
    fn event_listener_list_changed(this: Ref<Self>);
}

impl CppEventTarget {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
        // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a new, live EventTarget.
        Self(unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(web_bindings_create_event_target()) })
    }

    /// An EventTarget of LibWeb's C++ code, which this keeps alive.
    pub(crate) fn from_lent(event_target: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::EventTarget>) -> Self {
        Self(CppCell::from_lent(event_target))
    }

    /// An EventTarget of LibWeb's C++ code, which this keeps alive.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `event_target` must be a live EventTarget.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_raw(event_target: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live EventTarget.
        Self(unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(event_target) })
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_owner<T: GetTheParent>(&self, owner: Ref<T>) {
        unsafe extern "C" fn get_the_parent<T: GetTheParent>(owner: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void {
            // SAFETY: LibWeb passes the owner that set_owner() gave it, which is the live cell of an object of T.
            let owner = unsafe { cell_from_abi::<T>(owner) };
            owner
                .get_the_parent()
                .map_or(core::ptr::null_mut(), |parent| parent.as_ptr())
        }
        // SAFETY: The EventTarget and the owner are live, and the owner keeps the EventTarget alive.
        unsafe {
            web_bindings_set_event_target_owner(
                self.as_ptr(),
                T::INTERFACE_NAME,
                cell_into_abi(owner),
                get_the_parent::<T>,
            );
        }
    }

    /// Runs the owner's event_listener_list_changed() whenever the event listener list changes. The owner must be the
    /// one that set_owner() gave.
    pub(crate) fn set_event_listener_list_changed_steps<T: EventListenerListChanged>(&self) {
        unsafe extern "C" fn event_listener_list_changed<T: EventListenerListChanged>(owner: *mut c_void) {
            // SAFETY: LibWeb passes the owner that set_owner() gave it, which is the live cell of an object of T.
            T::event_listener_list_changed(unsafe { cell_from_abi::<T>(owner) });
        }
        // SAFETY: The EventTarget is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_set_event_listener_list_changed_steps(self.as_ptr(), event_listener_list_changed::<T>) };
    }

    pub(crate) fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.as_ptr()
    }

    /// Whether the event listener list has a listener for the event type.
    pub(crate) fn has_event_listener(&self, event_type: &str) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The EventTarget is live, and the type is lent for the call.
        unsafe { web_bindings_has_event_listener(self.as_ptr(), ak::Span::new(event_type.as_bytes())) }
    }

    pub(crate) fn has_event_listeners(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The EventTarget is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_has_event_listeners(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// Adds an event listener for the event type whose callback is the function, with no options,
    /// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#add-an-event-listener
    pub(crate) fn add_event_listener(&self, cx: &CallContext, event_type: &str, callback: Gc<FunctionObject>) {
        // SAFETY: The realm, the EventTarget and the callback are live, and the type is lent for the call.
        unsafe {
            web_bindings_add_event_listener(
                cx.realm().as_ptr().cast(),
                self.as_ptr(),
                ak::Span::new(event_type.as_bytes()),
                callback.as_ptr().cast(),
            );
        }
    }

    /// Adds an event listener for the event type whose callback is the EventListener, with no options,
    /// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#add-an-event-listener
    pub(crate) fn add_event_listener_without_options(&self, event_type: &str, callback: &CallbackInterface) {
        // SAFETY: The EventTarget and the callback are live, and the type is lent for the call.
        unsafe {
            web_bindings_add_event_listener_without_options(
                self.as_ptr(),
                ak::Span::new(event_type.as_bytes()),
                callback.as_ptr(),
            );
        }
    }

    /// Removes the event listener for the event type whose callback is the EventListener and whose capture is false,
    /// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#remove-an-event-listener
    pub(crate) fn remove_event_listener_without_options(&self, event_type: &str, callback: &CallbackInterface) {
        // SAFETY: The EventTarget and the callback are live, and the type is lent for the call.
        unsafe {
            web_bindings_remove_event_listener_without_options(
                self.as_ptr(),
                ak::Span::new(event_type.as_bytes()),
                callback.as_ptr(),
            );
        }
    }

    /// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch
    pub(crate) fn dispatch_event(&self, event: &CppEvent) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The EventTarget and the event are live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_dispatch_event(self.as_ptr(), event.as_ptr()) }
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_has_pending_activity(&self, realm: Gc<Realm>, has_pending_activity: bool) {
        // SAFETY: The realm and the EventTarget are live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_set_has_pending_activity(realm.as_ptr().cast(), self.as_ptr(), has_pending_activity) };
    }

    /// Returns the legacyOutputDidListenersThrowFlag.
    pub(crate) fn dispatch_event_with_legacy_output_did_listeners_throw_flag(&self, event: &CppEvent) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The EventTarget and the event are live.
        unsafe {
            web_bindings_dispatch_event_with_legacy_output_did_listeners_throw_flag(self.as_ptr(), event.as_ptr())
        }
    }
}

/// An Event: a plain one, or the one that an object owns.
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CppEvent(CppCell);

impl CppEvent {

        Self(CppCell::from_lent(event))
    }

    pub(crate) fn create(realm: Gc<Realm>, r#type: &str, bubbles: bool, cancelable: bool, composed: bool) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The realm is live, the type is lent for the call, and LibWeb returns a live event.
        Self(unsafe {
            CppCell::from_raw(web_bindings_create_event(
                realm.as_ptr().cast(),
                ak::Span::new(r#type.as_bytes()),
                bubbles,
                cancelable,
                composed,
            ))
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_for_owner(
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        r#type: &Utf16String,
        bubbles: bool,
        cancelable: bool,
        composed: bool,
    ) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The realm is live, the type is lent for the call, and LibWeb returns a live event.
        Self(unsafe {
            CppCell::from_raw(web_bindings_create_rust_event(
                realm.as_ptr().cast(),
                r#type.raw_identity(),
                bubbles,
                cancelable,
                composed,
            ))
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_owner<T: Interface>(&self, owner: Ref<T>) {
        // SAFETY: The event and the owner are live, and the owner keeps the event alive.
        unsafe { web_bindings_set_event_owner(self.as_ptr(), T::INTERFACE_NAME, cell_into_abi(owner)) };
    }

    pub(crate) fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.as_ptr()
    }

    /// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-istrusted
    pub(crate) fn set_is_trusted(&self, is_trusted: bool) {
        // SAFETY: The event is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_event_set_is_trusted(self.as_ptr(), is_trusted) };
    }

        unsafe { Utf16FlyString::from_raw_borrowed(web_bindings_event_type(self.as_ptr())) }.into()
    }

    }

    }

    /// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-cancelable
    pub(crate) fn cancelable(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The event is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_event_cancelable(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// The result of retargeting the object, an EventTarget, against the event's currentTarget,
    /// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#retarget
    pub(crate) fn retarget_against_current_target(&self, object: &CppCell) -> CppCell {

        unsafe {

                self.as_ptr(),

            ))
        }
    }

    }

fn event_target_of(object: &impl Wrappable) -> *mut c_void {
    object
        .cpp_parent()
        .expect("an object with event handler IDL attributes owns an EventTarget")
        .as_ptr()
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-handler-idl-attributes
pub(crate) fn event_handler_attribute(object: &impl Wrappable, event_type: &str) -> Value {
    // SAFETY: The EventTarget is live, and the name is lent for the call.
    let value =
        unsafe { web_bindings_event_handler_attribute(event_target_of(object), ak::Span::new(event_type.as_bytes())) };
    // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live value.
    unsafe { Value::from_raw(value) }
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-handler-idl-attributes
pub(crate) fn set_event_handler_attribute(object: &impl Wrappable, event_type: &str, value: Value) {
    // SAFETY: The EventTarget and the value are live, and the name is lent for the call.
    unsafe {
        web_bindings_set_event_handler_attribute(
            event_target_of(object),
            ak::Span::new(event_type.as_bytes()),
            value.to_raw(),
        );
    }
}

    }
}

        NonNull::new(self.as_ptr())
    }

    fn web_bindings_for_each_active_window(ctx: *mut c_void, on_window: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void));

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CppWindow(CppCell);

/// The cell of a C++ object that LibWeb returns, or None for a null pointer.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be null or a live cell of LibWeb's C++ code.
unsafe fn cell_if_not_null(cell: *mut c_void) -> Option<CppCell> {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell.
    NonNull::new(cell).map(|cell| unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(cell.as_ptr()) })
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-relevant-global
pub(crate) fn relevant_global_object<T: Wrappable>(object: &T) -> Gc<Object> {
    object
        .relevant_realm()
        .expect("the implementation knows the realm of the relevant global object")
        .global_object()
}

/// The Window that the global object is, if it is one.
pub(crate) fn window_from_global_object(global_object: Gc<Object>) -> Option<CppWindow> {
    // SAFETY: The global object is live, and LibWeb returns null or the live Window that it is.
    unsafe { cell_if_not_null(web_bindings_window_from_global_object(global_object.as_ptr().cast())) }.map(CppWindow)
}

/// The WorkerGlobalScope that the global object is, if it is one.
pub(crate) fn worker_global_scope_from_global_object(global_object: Gc<Object>) -> Option<CppWorkerGlobalScope> {
    // SAFETY: The global object is live, and LibWeb returns null or the live WorkerGlobalScope that it is.
    unsafe {
        cell_if_not_null(web_bindings_worker_global_scope_from_global_object(
            global_object.as_ptr().cast(),
        ))
    }
    .map(CppWorkerGlobalScope)
}

pub(crate) fn is_service_worker_global_scope(global_object: Gc<Object>) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: The global object is live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_is_service_worker_global_scope(global_object.as_ptr().cast()) }
}

pub(crate) fn window_or_worker_global_scope_from_global_object(
    global_object: Gc<Object>,
) -> Option<CppWindowOrWorkerGlobalScope> {
    if window_from_global_object(global_object).is_some()
        || worker_global_scope_from_global_object(global_object).is_some()
    {
        return Some(CppWindowOrWorkerGlobalScope(global_object));
    }
    None
}

unsafe extern "C" fn on_active_window(windows: *mut c_void, window: *mut c_void) {
    // SAFETY: windows is the list of the caller, and LibWeb passes a live Window.
    unsafe { &*windows.cast::<MarkedVec<'_, CppWindow>>() }.push(CppWindow(unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(window) }));
}

/// Every Window of this process whose associated Document is fully active.
pub(crate) fn active_windows(vm: &Vm) -> MarkedVec<'_, CppWindow> {
    let windows = MarkedVec::new(vm);
    // SAFETY: The list outlives the call.
    unsafe { web_bindings_for_each_active_window((&raw const windows).cast_mut().cast(), on_active_window) };
    windows
}

impl CppWindow {
    pub(crate) fn from_lent(window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>) -> Self {
        Self(CppCell::from_lent(window))
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `window` must be a live Window.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_raw(window: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live Window.
        Self(unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(window) })
    }

    pub(crate) fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.as_ptr()
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#sec-modifications-HTML
    pub(crate) fn event_timing_state(&self, vm: &Vm) -> WindowEventTimingStateRef {
        let data = realm_data(vm, self.realm());
        if let Some(state) = data.event_timing_state.get() {
            return state;
        }
        let state = WindowEventTimingState::create(vm);
        data.event_timing_state.set(Some(state));
        state
    }

    pub(crate) fn realm(&self) -> Gc<Realm> {
        // SAFETY: The Window is live, and LibWeb returns its live relevant realm.
        let realm = unsafe { web_bindings_window_realm(self.0.as_ptr()) };
        // SAFETY: The realm is live.
        unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(realm.cast()).expect("a Window has a relevant realm")) }
    }

    /// The Window as an EventTarget.
    pub(crate) fn as_event_target(&self) -> CppEventTarget {
        // SAFETY: The Window is live, and LibWeb returns it as an EventTarget.
        unsafe { CppEventTarget::from_raw(web_bindings_window_as_event_target(self.0.as_ptr())) }
    }

    /// The id of the page whose traversable navigable the Window's navigable belongs to.

        // SAFETY: The Window is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_window_page_id(self.0.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#pdf-viewer-supported
    pub(crate) fn pdf_viewer_supported(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The Window is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_window_pdf_viewer_supported(self.0.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#transient-activation
    pub(crate) fn has_transient_activation(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The Window is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_window_has_transient_activation(self.0.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#consume-user-activation
    pub(crate) fn consume_user_activation(&self) {
        // SAFETY: The Window is live.
        unsafe { web_bindings_window_consume_user_activation(self.0.as_ptr()) };
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#transient-activation
    pub(crate) fn give_transient_activation(&self) {

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! What the generated bindings of an interface do with its wrappers, its interface object and its interface prototype
//! object, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-interfaces
//!
//! An object of an interface implemented in Rust is a cell that holds the implementation, a `Ref<T>`, which is what
//! implementations hold and pass each other. A wrapper of such an object is a platform object of the interface's
//! wrapper class, which LibWeb's C++ bindings define. Its host data is the cell, and its wrappable slot stays empty,
//! so the C++ bindings treat it like a platform object without a wrappable.
//!
//! An object has one wrapper per wrapper world, as an implementation object of the C++ bindings has
//! (Documentation/WrapperArchitecture.md), and wrap() finds or creates it.

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ops::Deref;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16FlyString;
use libjs_rust::api::{
    Attribute, DeferGc, EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, ErrorKind, ErrorType, ExternalMemorySize,
    FunctionObject, Gc, HostObject, JSHostClass, Object, PrimitiveString, PropertyAttributes, PropertyKey,
    RawNativeFunction, RawNativeFunctionPointer, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value, Vm, get_function_realm,
    host_class_of, host_data_of, is_host_instance_of,
};

use crate::bindings::CallContext;
use crate::bindings::conversions::implements_cpp_interface;
use crate::bindings::realm_data::wrapper_world_of;
use crate::bindings::services::{
    web_bindings_define_unforgeable_attributes, web_bindings_ensure_web_constructor, web_bindings_ensure_web_prototype,
    web_bindings_perform_a_security_check, web_bindings_realm_is_secure_context, web_bindings_realm_is_window,
    web_bindings_report_an_exception, web_bindings_rust_wrapper_for, web_bindings_set_rust_wrapper,
    web_bindings_with_temporary_execution_context,
};

/// What an implementation can tell the bindings about its objects, as a C++ implementation object does by overriding
/// the virtual functions of Web::Bindings::Wrappable.
pub(crate) trait Wrappable {
    /// The realm of the relevant global object of the object, which the wrapper of the object in the main world is
    /// created in, as Wrappable::relevant_global_impl() decides for a C++ implementation object. Without one, the
    /// wrapper is created in the realm that first asks for it.
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        None
    }

    /// Whether the object owns memory outside the heap, which LibGC then asks external_memory_size() for while it
    /// sweeps and counts towards the bytes that make it collect, as Cell::external_memory_size() of a C++
    /// implementation object.
    const OWNS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY: bool = false;

    /// Whether the memory outside the heap that the object owns was made with it, so that allocating the object counts
    /// it towards the next collection. Not so for an object that reports memory another object holds as well, as a CSS
    /// rule does the rule its style sheet holds: counting it each time a new one is made would start collections that
    /// free none of it.
    const COUNTS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_WHEN_ALLOCATED: bool = false;

    /// How much memory outside the heap the object owns, which LibGC asks for if OWNS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY is true.
    fn external_memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        0
    }

    /// Whether LibGC may only trace the object, and ask for its external_memory_size(), on the thread that owns its heap,
    /// as it does C++ objects. LibGC traces other objects on several threads at once while that thread is stopped, so
    /// this must be true for an object whose tracing reaches C++ objects, thread-local state, or state that it shares
    /// with other objects without synchronization.
    const TRACED_ON_OWNER_THREAD_ONLY: bool = false;

    /// Whether LibGC finalizes the object before it destroys it, which it does through finalize(), as it does a C++
    /// implementation object that overrides Cell::finalize().
    const FINALIZES: bool = false;

    /// What the object does when LibGC finalizes it, while every cell that dies in the collection is still intact.
    /// It must not allocate.
    fn finalize(_object: Ref<Self>)
    where
        Self: Trace + Sized,
    {
    }

    /// The C++ EventTarget or Event that the object owns, which its wrappers hold as their wrappable
    /// (bindings::event_target).
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        None
    }
}

/// The value of the cell of an object of an interface: its implementation, and its wrapper in the main world.
///
/// The cell keeps that wrapper alive, and the wrapper keeps the cell alive through its host data, so the two live and
/// die together: the object has the same wrapper in the main world for as long as it lives. A C++ implementation
/// object holds its wrapper weakly until script makes the wrapper observable, which the wrapper of an interface
/// implemented in Rust has no hooks to tell.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Wrapped<T: Trace> {
    main_world_wrapper: Cell<Option<Gc<HostObject>>>,
    implementation: T,
}

impl<T: Trace> Deref for Wrapped<T> {
    type Target = T;

    fn deref(&self) -> &T {
        &self.implementation
    }
}

/// An object of the interface that `T` implements.
pub(crate) type Ref<T> = Gc<EmbedderCell<Wrapped<T>>>;

/// What the implementation of an interface that inherits from another implements, for the implementation of that
/// interface: where an object of the interface keeps what it is as an object of the inherited interface. The
/// attributes and operations of the inherited interface run on that.
pub(crate) trait Inherits<Parent> {
    fn parent(&self) -> &Parent;
}

/// An implementation of an interface, as the generated bindings of the interface describe it.
pub(crate) trait Interface: Wrappable + Trace + Sized + 'static {
    /// The class of the cells of the objects of the interface.
    const CELL_CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Wrapped<Self>>;
    /// Web::Bindings::InterfaceName of the interface.
    const INTERFACE_NAME: u16;
    /// The name that errors call the interface.
    const NAME: &'static str;
    /// The interface implemented in C++ that the interface inherits from, if it has unforgeable attributes, which are
    /// properties of each wrapper.
    const UNFORGEABLE_ATTRIBUTES_INTERFACE: Option<u16> = None;

    /// The class of the wrappers of the objects of the interface.
    fn wrapper_class() -> &'static JSHostClass;
}

impl<T: Interface> EmbedderValue for Wrapped<T> {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = T::CELL_CLASS;
}

impl<T: Wrappable + Trace> ExternalMemorySize for Wrapped<T> {
    fn external_memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.implementation.external_memory_size()
    }
}

/// The class of the cells of the objects of an interface, which the generated bindings of the interface define once.
pub(crate) const fn cell_class<T: Wrappable + Trace + 'static>(name: &'static str) -> EmbedderClass<Wrapped<T>> {
    let class = if T::OWNS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY {
        EmbedderClass::new_with_external_memory_size(name)
    } else {
        EmbedderClass::new(name)
    };
    let class = if T::TRACED_ON_OWNER_THREAD_ONLY {
        class.traced_on_owner_thread_only()
    } else {
        class
    };
    if T::FINALIZES {
        class.with_finalize(finalize_object::<T>)
    } else {
        class
    }
}

/// The finalize entry of the class of the cells of an interface whose implementation finalizes its objects.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Only LibGC calls it, with a dead cell of the class.
unsafe extern "C" fn finalize_object<T: Wrappable + Trace + 'static>(cell: *mut c_void) {
    let cell = NonNull::new(cell.cast::<EmbedderCell<Wrapped<T>>>()).expect("LibGC passes a cell");
    // SAFETY: LibGC passes a dead cell of the class, which stays intact while it finalizes.
    T::finalize(unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(cell) });
}

/// Without the generated bindings, which a build of the crate on its own leaves out, nothing creates or wraps an
/// object, but the implementations still name each other's objects. This stands in for the bindings of every
/// interface so that they compile.
#[cfg(not(web_idl_bindings))]
impl<T: Wrappable + Trace + Sized + 'static> Interface for T {
    const CELL_CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Wrapped<Self>> = &EmbedderClass::new("");
    const INTERFACE_NAME: u16 = 0;
    const NAME: &'static str = "";

    fn wrapper_class() -> &'static JSHostClass {
        unreachable!("an interface has no wrappers without its bindings")
    }
}

/// A new object of the interface, built as Heap::allocate() builds a cell.
pub(crate) fn allocate<T: Interface>(vm: &Vm, build: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> T) -> Ref<T> {
    let object = T::CELL_CLASS.allocate(vm, |defer_gc| Wrapped {
        main_world_wrapper: Cell::new(None),
        implementation: build(defer_gc),
    });
    // NB: The memory the object owns outside the heap counts towards the next collection too, or a page could make
    //     many objects that each own a lot of it, and keep the dead ones until its other allocations started one.
    if T::OWNS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY && T::COUNTS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_WHEN_ALLOCATED {
        let size = object.external_memory_size();
        if size != 0 {
            vm.heap().did_allocate_external_memory(size);
        }
    }
    object
}

/// What the constructor steps or the transfer-receiving steps of an interface create: the implementation of the new
/// object, which the bindings allocate, or the new object itself, for steps that hand the object to something else
/// before they finish, as the constructor of ReadableStream gives it to its controller.
pub(crate) trait ConstructedObject<T: Interface> {
    fn into_object(self, vm: &Vm) -> Ref<T>;
}

impl<T: Interface> ConstructedObject<T> for T {
    fn into_object(self, vm: &Vm) -> Ref<T> {
        allocate(vm, |_| self)
    }
}

impl<T: Interface> ConstructedObject<T> for Ref<T> {
    fn into_object(self, _: &Vm) -> Ref<T> {
        self
    }
}

/// HTML::SecurityCheckType.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub(crate) enum SecurityCheckType {
    Method,
    Getter,
    Setter,
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-perform-a-security-check
pub(crate) fn perform_a_security_check(
    vm: &Vm,
    platform_object: Value,
    identifier: &str,
    check_type: SecurityCheckType,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()> {
    let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a native function runs in a realm");
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, the value is live while the native function runs, and the identifier is lent for the
    //         call.
    unsafe {
        web_bindings_perform_a_security_check(
            realm.as_ptr().cast(),
            platform_object.to_raw(),
            ak::Span::new(identifier.as_bytes()),
            check_type as u8,
        )
    }
    .into_completion()
    .map(|_| ())
}

/// The object an attribute or an operation of an interface runs on, if it is a wrapper of the interface or of an
/// interface that inherits from it, with the object's realm. A nullish this value stands for the global object of
/// the current realm. https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-check-an-object
pub(crate) fn this_object(
    vm: &Vm,
    wrapper_class: &'static JSHostClass,
    interface_name: &str,
    identifier: &str,
    check_type: SecurityCheckType,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<(Gc<Object>, Gc<Realm>)> {
    let mut this_value = vm.this_value();
    if this_value.is_nullish() {
        let current_realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a native function runs in a realm");
        this_value = Value::from_object(current_realm.global_object());
    }
    if this_value.is_object() {
        let object = this_value.as_object();
        if is_host_instance_of(&object, wrapper_class) {
            return Ok((object, object.shape().realm()));
        }
    }
    // NB: This runs after the check above, which no Window or Location object passes.
    perform_a_security_check(vm, this_value, identifier, check_type)?;
    vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&interface_name])
}

/// The object an attribute or an operation of an interface implemented in C++ runs on, if it is a wrapper of an object
/// that implements the interface, which the value of its Web::Bindings::InterfaceName names, with the object's realm.
/// A nullish this value stands for the global object of the current realm.
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-check-an-object
pub(crate) fn this_cpp_object(
    vm: &Vm,
    interface_name: u16,
    name: &str,
    identifier: &str,
    check_type: SecurityCheckType,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<(Gc<Object>, Gc<Realm>)> {
    let mut this_value = vm.this_value();
    if this_value.is_nullish() {
        let current_realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a native function runs in a realm");
        this_value = Value::from_object(current_realm.global_object());
    }
    if this_value.is_object() {
        let object = this_value.as_object();
        if implements_cpp_interface(object, interface_name) {
            return Ok((object, object.shape().realm()));
        }
    }
    // NB: This runs after the check above, which no Window or Location object passes.
    perform_a_security_check(vm, this_value, identifier, check_type)?;
    vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&name])
}

/// The object that a wrapper of exactly the interface wraps.
pub(crate) fn implementation_of<T: Interface>(wrapper: Gc<Object>) -> Ref<T> {
    implementation_if(wrapper).expect("a wrapper holds the cell of its object")
}

/// The object that the wrapper of an interface implemented in Rust wraps, if it is an object of exactly this
/// interface and not of one that inherits from it.
pub(crate) fn implementation_if<T: Interface>(wrapper: Gc<Object>) -> Option<Ref<T>> {
    let host_data = host_data_of(&wrapper).expect("a wrapper holds the cell of its object");
    // SAFETY: The wrapper is a host object of the wrapper class of an interface implemented in Rust, whose host data
    //         the bindings set to the cell of an object of such an interface.
    unsafe { T::CELL_CLASS.downcast(host_data) }
}

/// The object of the interface that the object is a wrapper of, if it is one.
pub(crate) fn implementation_if_wrapper<T: Interface>(object: Gc<Object>) -> Option<Ref<T>> {
    is_host_instance_of(&object, T::wrapper_class()).then(|| implementation_of(object))
}

/// Whether the object is a wrapper of exactly this interface, and not of one that inherits from it.
pub(crate) fn is_exact_wrapper<T: Interface>(object: Gc<Object>) -> bool {
    host_class_of(&object).is_some_and(|class| core::ptr::eq(class, T::wrapper_class()))
}

/// An object of the interface converted from a JS value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-interface
pub(crate) fn to_interface<T: Interface>(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Ref<T>> {
    // 1. If V implements I, then return the IDL interface type value that represents a reference to that platform
    //    object.
    if value.is_object()
        && let Some(object) = implementation_if_wrapper(value.as_object())
    {
        return Ok(object);
    }
    // 2. Throw a TypeError.
    vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&T::NAME])
}

/// The `this` value of an operation of a setlike or maplike, its implementation, and the context of its realm.
pub(crate) fn this_implementation<'vm, T: Interface>(
    vm: &'vm Vm,
    identifier: &str,
    check_type: SecurityCheckType,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<(Gc<Object>, Ref<T>, CallContext<'vm>)> {
    let (wrapper, realm) = this_object(vm, T::wrapper_class(), T::NAME, identifier, check_type)?;
    Ok((wrapper, implementation_of(wrapper), CallContext::new(vm, realm)))
}

/// The wrapper of the object in the wrapper world of the realm of the call context, which the first call for that
/// world creates, as Web::Bindings::wrap() does for a C++ implementation object.
pub(crate) fn wrap<T: Interface>(cx: &CallContext, object: Ref<T>) -> Gc<Object> {
    let vm = cx.vm();
    let realm = cx.realm();
    let main_world_wrapper = object.main_world_wrapper.get();
    if let Some(wrapper) = main_world_wrapper
        && wrapper.shape().realm() == realm
    {
        return wrapper.upcast();
    }

    let wrapper_world = wrapper_world_of(vm, realm);
    if wrapper_world.is_main_world() {
        if let Some(wrapper) = main_world_wrapper {
            // NB: An agent has one main world, which the realms of the agent share, and objects do not cross agents.
            assert!(
                wrapper_world_of(vm, wrapper.shape().realm()) == wrapper_world,
                "an object has a wrapper in the main world of another agent"
            );
            return wrapper.upcast();
        }
        let wrapper_realm = object
            .relevant_realm()
            .filter(|relevant_realm| wrapper_world_of(vm, *relevant_realm) == wrapper_world)
            .unwrap_or(realm);
        let wrapper = create_wrapper(vm, wrapper_realm, object);
        object.main_world_wrapper.set(Some(wrapper));
        return wrapper.upcast();
    }

    // SAFETY: The realm and the cell are live.
    let wrapper = unsafe { web_bindings_rust_wrapper_for(realm.as_ptr().cast(), object.as_ptr().cast()) };
    if let Some(wrapper) = NonNull::new(wrapper.cast::<Object>()) {
        // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live wrapper.
        return unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(wrapper) };
    }
    let wrapper = create_wrapper(vm, realm, object);
    register_wrapper_outside_main_world(realm, object, wrapper);
    wrapper.upcast()
}

/// The wrapper that a construction creates for the new object of the interface, with the prototype that the new
/// target of the construction decides.
pub(crate) fn construct_wrapper<T: Interface>(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    prototype: Gc<Object>,
    object: impl ConstructedObject<T>,
) -> Gc<HostObject> {
    let object = object.into_object(vm);
    assert!(
        object.main_world_wrapper.get().is_none(),
        "the constructor steps create no wrapper of the new object"
    );
    let wrapper = create_wrapper(vm, realm, object);
    wrapper.set_prototype(vm, Some(prototype));
    if wrapper_world_of(vm, realm).is_main_world() {
        object.main_world_wrapper.set(Some(wrapper));
    } else {
        register_wrapper_outside_main_world(realm, object, wrapper);
    }
    wrapper
}

fn register_wrapper_outside_main_world<T: Interface>(realm: Gc<Realm>, object: Ref<T>, wrapper: Gc<HostObject>) {
    // SAFETY: The realm, the cell and the wrapper are live, and the wrapper is in the realm.
    unsafe {
        web_bindings_set_rust_wrapper(realm.as_ptr().cast(), object.as_ptr().cast(), wrapper.as_ptr().cast());
    }
}

/// A new wrapper of the object, which always starts from the interface's own prototype. Shapes do not know the class of
/// their objects, so a wrapper created directly with the prototype of another interface would share the shape of that
/// interface's wrappers, and a direct getter validated on those would read a field of the other interface out of this
/// wrapper's implementation.
fn create_wrapper<T: Interface>(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, object: Ref<T>) -> Gc<HostObject> {
    let prototype = interface_prototype_object(realm, T::INTERFACE_NAME);
    // SAFETY: The wrapper class's hooks expect a wrappable exactly for an interface that inherits from an interface
    //         implemented in C++, whose objects own one, and the wrappable and the host data are live cells.
    let wrapper = unsafe {
        HostObject::create(
            vm,
            realm,
            T::wrapper_class(),
            Some(prototype),
            object.cpp_parent(),
            Some(object.as_non_null().cast()),
        )
    };
    if let Some(interface_name) = T::UNFORGEABLE_ATTRIBUTES_INTERFACE {
        // SAFETY: The realm and the wrapper are live, and the interface is one the wrapper's interface inherits from.
        unsafe {
            web_bindings_define_unforgeable_attributes(realm.as_ptr().cast(), wrapper.as_ptr().cast(), interface_name);
        }
    }
    wrapper
}

/// The cell of an object of the interface, as LibWeb's C++ code holds it: a pointer to a class that derives from
/// Web::Bindings::RustInterfaceCell.
pub(crate) fn cell_into_abi<T: Interface>(object: Ref<T>) -> *mut c_void {
    object.as_ptr().cast()
}

/// The cell of an object of an interface implemented in Rust, which LibWeb's C++ code holds as a pointer to a class that
/// derives from Web::Bindings::RustInterfaceCell, and lends the exports of the crate for as long as they run. The
/// exports take a `&InterfaceCell` where C++ passes such a cell, as they take a `&Vm` where it passes the VM, so a
/// reference to one is always a live cell of an embedder class.
#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct InterfaceCell {
    // NB: The cell is mutable behind a shared reference, and bigger than Rust sees, so a reference to one must not tell
    //     the compiler that the memory behind it is read only or unaliased.
    _opaque: core::cell::UnsafeCell<[u8; 0]>,
    _not_send_sync_or_unpin: core::marker::PhantomData<(*const (), core::marker::PhantomPinned)>,
}

impl InterfaceCell {
    /// The cell behind the pointer that C++ passes.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `cell` must be a live cell of an object of an interface implemented in Rust, which stays live for `'a`.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_raw<'a>(cell: *mut c_void) -> &'a Self {
        let cell = NonNull::new(cell.cast::<Self>()).expect("C++ passes the cell of an object");
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell.
        unsafe { cell.as_ref() }
    }

    /// The object of the interface whose cell this is.
    pub(crate) fn object<T: Interface>(&self) -> Ref<T> {
        self.object_if()
            .expect("C++ passes the cell of an object of the interface")
    }

    /// The object of the interface whose cell this is, if the cell is that of an object of exactly the interface: C++
    /// names an object of an interface that others inherit from by that interface, whichever it is.
    pub(crate) fn object_if<T: Interface>(&self) -> Option<Ref<T>> {
        // SAFETY: An InterfaceCell is a live cell of an embedder class.
        unsafe { T::CELL_CLASS.downcast(NonNull::from(self).cast()) }
    }

    /// The implementation of the object whose cell this is, for as long as the cell is lent.
    pub(crate) fn implementation<T: Interface>(&self) -> &T {
        self.implementation_if()
            .expect("C++ passes the cell of an object of the interface")
    }

    /// The implementation of the object whose cell this is, if it is an object of exactly the interface, as
    /// object_if() finds it.
    pub(crate) fn implementation_if<T: Interface>(&self) -> Option<&T> {
        let object = self.object_if::<T>()?;
        // SAFETY: The cell is live for as long as the reference to it.
        Some(unsafe { &*object.as_ptr() })
    }
}

/// The object of the interface whose cell LibWeb's C++ code holds.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be a live cell of an object of an interface implemented in Rust.
pub(crate) unsafe fn cell_from_abi<T: Interface>(cell: *mut c_void) -> Ref<T> {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell of an embedder class.
    unsafe { InterfaceCell::from_raw(cell) }.object()
}

/// The object of the interface whose cell LibWeb's C++ code holds, if the cell is that of an object of exactly the
/// interface, as InterfaceCell::object_if() finds it.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be a live cell of an object of an interface implemented in Rust.
pub(crate) unsafe fn cell_if_abi<T: Interface>(cell: *mut c_void) -> Option<Ref<T>> {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell of an embedder class.
    unsafe { InterfaceCell::from_raw(cell) }.object_if()
}

/// Whether the global object of the realm is a Window, which the members that only a Window has, [Exposed=Window] on
/// an interface exposed elsewhere as well, are defined for.
pub(crate) fn realm_is_window(realm: Gc<Realm>) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: The realm is live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_realm_is_window(realm.as_ptr().cast()) }
}

/// Whether the realm is a secure context, which the [SecureContext] members are defined for.
pub(crate) fn realm_is_secure_context(realm: Gc<Realm>) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: The realm is live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_realm_is_secure_context(realm.as_ptr().cast()) }
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#report-an-exception
pub(crate) fn report_an_exception(realm: Gc<Realm>, exception: Value) {
    // SAFETY: The realm and the exception are live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_report_an_exception(realm.as_ptr().cast(), exception.to_raw()) }
}

/// Runs the steps while an execution context of the realm is on the stack, for steps that can run script but that do not
/// run on behalf of script, as an HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext does for C++.
pub(crate) fn with_temporary_execution_context<F: FnOnce() -> R, R>(realm: Gc<Realm>, steps: F) -> R {
    run_with_temporary_execution_context(realm, false, steps)
}

/// Runs the steps as with_temporary_execution_context() does, with the realm prepared to run callbacks as well, as an
/// HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext with CallbacksEnabled::Yes does for C++.
pub(crate) fn with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks<F: FnOnce() -> R, R>(realm: Gc<Realm>, steps: F) -> R {
    run_with_temporary_execution_context(realm, true, steps)
}

fn run_with_temporary_execution_context<F: FnOnce() -> R, R>(realm: Gc<Realm>, callbacks_enabled: bool, steps: F) -> R {
    unsafe extern "C" fn run_steps<F: FnOnce() -> R, R>(context: *mut c_void) {
        // SAFETY: The context is the steps and the slot for their result, which outlive the call.
        let (steps, result) = unsafe { &mut *context.cast::<(Option<F>, Option<R>)>() };
        *result = Some(steps.take().expect("LibWeb runs the steps once")());
    }

    let mut context = (Some(steps), None);
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the context outlives the call, which runs the steps once.
    unsafe {
        web_bindings_with_temporary_execution_context(
            realm.as_ptr().cast(),
            callbacks_enabled,
            (&raw mut context).cast(),
            run_steps::<F, R>,
        );
    }
    context.1.expect("LibWeb runs the steps")
}

/// The interface prototype object of the interface in the realm.
pub(crate) fn interface_prototype_object(realm: Gc<Realm>, interface_name: u16) -> Gc<Object> {
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the interface is implemented in Rust.
    let prototype = unsafe { web_bindings_ensure_web_prototype(realm.as_ptr().cast(), interface_name) };
    let prototype = NonNull::new(prototype.cast::<Object>()).expect("the realm has the interface prototype object");
    // SAFETY: LibWeb returns the live prototype.
    unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(prototype) }
}

/// The prototype of an object that newTarget constructs, steps 3.2 and 3.3 of internally creating a new object
/// implementing the interface, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#internally-create-a-new-object-implementing-the-interface
pub(crate) fn prototype_from_new_target(
    vm: &Vm,
    new_target: Gc<Object>,
    interface_name: u16,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<Object>> {
    // 3.2. Let prototype be ? Get(newTarget, "prototype").
    let prototype = new_target.get(vm, &vm.names.prototype)?;

    // 3.3. If Type(prototype) is not Object, then:
    if prototype.is_object() {
        return Ok(prototype.as_object());
    }
    // 1. Let targetRealm be ? GetFunctionRealm(newTarget).
    let new_target = new_target
        .downcast::<FunctionObject>()
        .expect("the new target of a construction is a constructor");
    let target_realm = get_function_realm(vm, new_target)?;
    // 2. Set prototype to the interface prototype object for interface in targetRealm.
    Ok(interface_prototype_object(target_realm, interface_name))
}

/// Unwraps the raw arguments that LibWeb's C++ bindings pass the entry points that initialize the interface object and
/// the interface prototype object, which run before any binding of the interface. The C++ bindings pass the runtime's
/// VM and cells, as JS::HostABI::vm_to_abi() and object_to_abi() do.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the live VM, a live realm and a live object.
pub(crate) unsafe fn entry_point_arguments<'vm>(
    vm: *mut c_void,
    realm: *mut c_void,
    object: *mut c_void,
) -> (&'vm Vm, Gc<Realm>, Gc<Object>) {
    let realm = NonNull::new(realm.cast::<Realm>()).expect("C++ passes a realm");
    let object = NonNull::new(object.cast::<Object>()).expect("C++ passes an object");
    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that the pointers are live.
    unsafe { (&*vm.cast::<Vm>(), Gc::from_non_null(realm), Gc::from_non_null(object)) }
}

/// Unwraps the VM and the realm that LibWeb's C++ bindings pass an entry point.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the live VM and a live realm.
pub(crate) unsafe fn realm_arguments<'vm>(vm: *mut c_void, realm: *mut c_void) -> (&'vm Vm, Gc<Realm>) {
    let realm = NonNull::new(realm.cast::<Realm>()).expect("C++ passes a realm");
    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that the pointers are live.
    unsafe { (&*vm.cast::<Vm>(), Gc::from_non_null(realm)) }
}

/// Unwraps the raw arguments that LibWeb's C++ bindings pass the entry point that constructs an object.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the live VM and the live new target of a construction.
pub(crate) unsafe fn construct_arguments<'vm>(vm: *mut c_void, new_target: *mut c_void) -> (&'vm Vm, Gc<Object>) {
    let new_target = NonNull::new(new_target.cast::<Object>()).expect("a construction has a new target");
    // SAFETY: The caller guarantees that the pointers are live.
    unsafe { (&*vm.cast::<Vm>(), Gc::from_non_null(new_target)) }
}

/// Gives the interface prototype object its [[Prototype]]: the interface prototype object of the interface that the
/// interface inherits from, or %Object.prototype%, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-prototype-object
pub(crate) fn set_interface_prototype_object_prototype(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    prototype: Gc<Object>,
    inherited_interface_name: Option<u16>,
) {
    let parent = match inherited_interface_name {
        Some(inherited_interface_name) => interface_prototype_object(realm, inherited_interface_name),
        None => realm.intrinsics().object_prototype(vm),
    };
    prototype.set_prototype(vm, Some(parent));
}

/// Defines a regular attribute on the interface prototype object, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-attributes
pub(crate) fn define_attribute(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    prototype: Gc<Object>,
    name: &str,
    getter: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    setter: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
) {
    prototype.define_native_accessor(
        vm,
        realm,
        &PropertyKey::from_utf8(name),
        getter,
        setter,
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::ENUMERABLE | Attribute::CONFIGURABLE),
    );
}

/// Defines a regular attribute that is read only and [CachedAccessor] on the interface prototype object: its getter
/// returns the same value for as long as the object lives, so the engine keeps the value on the object after the first
/// get and does not call the getter again, as LibWeb's C++ bindings define such an attribute.
pub(crate) fn define_cached_attribute(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    prototype: Gc<Object>,
    name: &str,
    getter: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
) {
    let property_key = PropertyKey::from_utf8(name);
    let getter = RawNativeFunction::create(vm, getter, 0, &property_key, Some(realm), Some("get"), None);
    prototype.define_direct_cached_accessor(
        vm,
        &property_key,
        Some(getter.upcast()),
        None,
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::ENUMERABLE | Attribute::CONFIGURABLE),
        true,
    );
}

/// Defines a regular operation on the interface prototype object, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-operations
pub(crate) fn define_operation(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    prototype: Gc<Object>,
    name: &str,
    behaviour: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    length: i32,
) {
    prototype.define_native_function(
        vm,
        realm,
        &PropertyKey::from_utf8(name),
        behaviour,
        length,
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::WRITABLE | Attribute::ENUMERABLE | Attribute::CONFIGURABLE),
        None,
    );
}

/// Defines the @@iterator property of the interface prototype object of an interface that supports indexed properties,
/// which is %Array.prototype.values%, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-iterator
pub(crate) fn define_indexed_properties_iterator(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, prototype: Gc<Object>) {
    let array_prototype = realm.intrinsics().array_prototype(vm);
    prototype.define_direct_property(
        vm,
        &PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().iterator),
        array_prototype.get_without_side_effects(vm, &vm.names.values),
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE | Attribute::WRITABLE),
    );
}

/// Defines the properties of a value iterator on the interface prototype object of an interface that supports indexed
/// properties, which are those of %Array.prototype%, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#define-the-iteration-methods
pub(crate) fn define_value_iterator_properties(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, prototype: Gc<Object>) {
    let array_prototype = realm.intrinsics().array_prototype(vm);
    let names = &vm.names;
    for name in [&names.entries, &names.keys, &names.values, &names.forEach] {
        prototype.define_direct_property(
            vm,
            name,
            array_prototype.get_without_side_effects(vm, name),
            PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::WRITABLE | Attribute::ENUMERABLE | Attribute::CONFIGURABLE),
        );
    }
}

/// Records a regular attribute or operation that the interface does not implement on the interface prototype object,
/// so that a read of it is reported, without the property being there for script.
pub(crate) fn define_unimplemented_property(vm: &Vm, prototype: Gc<Object>, name: &str) {
    prototype.define_unimplemented_property(vm, Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(name));
}

/// Defines the constants of an interface on its interface object or its interface prototype object,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#define-the-constants
pub(crate) fn define_constants(vm: &Vm, target: Gc<Object>, constants: &[(&str, f64)]) {
    // 1. For each constant const that is a member of definition:
    for (identifier, value) in constants {
        // 2. Let value be the result of converting const's IDL value to a JavaScript value.
        // 3. Let desc be the PropertyDescriptor{[[Writable]]: false, [[Enumerable]]: true, [[Configurable]]: false,
        //    [[Value]]: value}.
        // 4. Let id be const's identifier.
        // 5. Perform ! DefinePropertyOrThrow(target, id, desc).
        target.define_direct_property(
            vm,
            &PropertyKey::from_utf8(identifier),
            Value::from_f64(*value),
            PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::ENUMERABLE),
        );
    }
}

/// Defines @@toStringTag on the interface prototype object, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-interface-prototype-object
pub(crate) fn define_to_string_tag(vm: &Vm, prototype: Gc<Object>, name: &str) {
    prototype.define_direct_property(
        vm,
        &PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().to_string_tag),
        ascii_string(vm, name),
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE),
    );
}

/// Gives the interface object its [[Prototype]], if the interface inherits from another: the interface object of that
/// interface. Then defines the "length", "name" and "prototype" properties of the interface object,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-object
pub(crate) fn define_interface_object_properties(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    constructor: Gc<Object>,
    name: &str,
    length: i32,
    interface_name: u16,
    inherited_interface_name: Option<u16>,
) {
    if let Some(inherited_interface_name) = inherited_interface_name {
        // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the interface is implemented in Rust.
        let parent = unsafe { web_bindings_ensure_web_constructor(realm.as_ptr().cast(), inherited_interface_name) };
        let parent = NonNull::new(parent.cast::<Object>()).expect("the realm has the interface object");
        // SAFETY: LibWeb returns the live interface object.
        constructor.set_prototype(vm, Some(unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(parent) }));
    }
    constructor.define_direct_property(
        vm,
        &vm.names.length,
        Value::from_f64(f64::from(length)),
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE),
    );
    constructor.define_direct_property(
        vm,
        &vm.names.name,
        ascii_string(vm, name),
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE),
    );
    let prototype = interface_prototype_object(realm, interface_name);
    constructor.define_direct_property(
        vm,
        &vm.names.prototype,
        Value::from_object(prototype),
        PropertyAttributes::new(0),
    );
}

fn ascii_string(vm: &Vm, string: &str) -> Value {
    Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create_from_ascii(vm, string.as_bytes()))
}

/// A new object for a dictionary value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-dictionary
pub(crate) fn create_dictionary_object(cx: &CallContext) -> Gc<Object> {
    // 1. Let O be OrdinaryObjectCreate(%Object.prototype%).
    let object_prototype = cx.realm().intrinsics().object_prototype(cx.vm());
    Object::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), Some(object_prototype))
}

/// Stores a member of a dictionary value in its object, step 3.2.3 of https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-dictionary
pub(crate) fn set_dictionary_member(
    cx: &CallContext,
    object: Gc<Object>,
    key: &PropertyKey,
    value: Value,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()> {
    // 3. Perform ! CreateDataPropertyOrThrow(O, key, value).
    object.create_data_property(cx.vm(), key, value, None, None)?;
    Ok(())
}
