//! The pair iterators of the interfaces implemented in Rust, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-iterable

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ops::Deref;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    Array, Attribute, EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, ErrorKind, ErrorType, Gc, HostObject, JSHostClass,
    Object, PropertyAttributes, PropertyKey, RawNativeFunctionPointer, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value, Vm,
    call, create_iterator_result_object, host_data_of, is_host_instance_of,
};

use crate::bindings::CallContext;
use crate::bindings::conversions::ToJs;
use crate::bindings::interface::{
    Interface, SecurityCheckType, define_operation, perform_a_security_check, this_object,
};
use crate::bindings::services::web_bindings_ensure_web_iterator_prototype;

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#default-iterator-object-kind
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum IterationKind {
    Key,
    Value,
    KeyAndValue,
}

/// A default iterator object, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-default-iterator-object, which is the host data of
/// a host object of the iterator class of its interface.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct DefaultIterator<T: PairIterable> {
    target: T::Target,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    kind: IterationKind,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    index: Cell<usize>,
}

/// What the implementation of an interface with a pair iterator implements: its value pairs to iterate over, with
/// Rust types that convert to the key and value types of the iterable declaration.
pub(crate) trait PairIterable: Interface {
    type Key: ToJs + Clone;
    type Value: ToJs + Clone;

    /// What an iteration reads its value pairs from: normally the object, or what the object looked like when the
    /// iteration started, for an interface that does not follow the changes of the object during an iteration.
    type Target: Trace + 'static;

    /// The target of an iteration of the kind over the object that the wrapper wraps.
    fn iteration_target(cx: &CallContext, wrapper: Gc<Object>, kind: IterationKind) -> Self::Target;

    // https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-value-pairs-to-iterate-over
    fn value_pairs_to_iterate_over(target: &Self::Target) -> impl Deref<Target = [(Self::Key, Self::Value)]> + '_;
}

/// What the generated bindings of an interface with a pair iterator define: the classes of its default iterator
/// objects.
pub(crate) trait DefaultIteratorClasses: PairIterable {
    /// The class of the cells of the default iterator objects of the interface.
    const ITERATOR_CELL_CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<DefaultIterator<Self>>;

    /// The class of the default iterator objects of the interface.
    fn iterator_class() -> &'static JSHostClass;
}

impl<T: DefaultIteratorClasses> EmbedderValue for DefaultIterator<T> {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = T::ITERATOR_CELL_CLASS;
}

/// Defines the iteration methods of an interface with a pair iterator on its interface prototype object,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#define-the-iteration-methods
pub(crate) fn define_pair_iterator_properties(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    prototype: Gc<Object>,
    entries: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    for_each: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    keys: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    values: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
) {
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "entries", entries, 0);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "forEach", for_each, 1);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "keys", keys, 0);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "values", values, 0);

    // https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-iterator
    prototype.define_direct_property(
        vm,
        &PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().iterator),
        prototype.get_without_side_effects(vm, &vm.names.entries),
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE | Attribute::WRITABLE),
    );
}

/// A newly created default iterator object for the interface, with the object as its target, the kind, and index set
/// to 0, in the realm of the call context.
pub(crate) fn create_default_iterator<T: DefaultIteratorClasses>(
    cx: &CallContext,
    wrapper: Gc<Object>,
    kind: IterationKind,
) -> Value {
    let vm = cx.vm();
    let realm = cx.realm();
    let target = T::iteration_target(cx, wrapper, kind);
    let iterator = T::ITERATOR_CELL_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| DefaultIterator {
        target,
        kind,
        index: Cell::new(0),
    });
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the interface has a pair iterator.
    let prototype = unsafe { web_bindings_ensure_web_iterator_prototype(realm.as_ptr().cast(), T::INTERFACE_NAME) };
    let prototype = NonNull::new(prototype.cast::<Object>()).expect("LibWeb returns the iterator prototype object");
    // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live object, the iterator class has no hooks, and the host data is a live cell.
    let object = unsafe {
        HostObject::create(
            vm,
            realm,
            T::iterator_class(),
            Some(Gc::from_non_null(prototype)),
            None,
            Some(iterator.as_non_null().cast()),
        )
    };
    Value::from_object(object.upcast::<Object>())
}

/// The "next" method of the iterator prototype object of the interface,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-iterator-prototype-object
pub(crate) fn iterator_next<T: DefaultIteratorClasses>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let interface be the interface for which the iterator prototype object exists.
    // 2. Let thisValue be the this value.
    // 3. Let object be ? ToObject(thisValue).
    let object = vm.this_value().to_object(vm)?;

    // 4. If object is a platform object, then perform a security check, passing:
    //     * the platform object object,
    //     * the identifier "next", and
    //     * the type "method".
    // 5. If object is not a default iterator object for interface, then throw a TypeError.
    let Some(iterator) = default_iterator_of::<T>(object) else {
        // NB: This runs after the check above, which no Window or Location object passes.
        perform_a_security_check(vm, Value::from_object(object), "next", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;
        let name = format!("{}Iterator", T::NAME);
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&name]);
    };
    let realm = object.shape().realm();

    // 6. Let index be object's index.
    let index = iterator.index.get();

    // 7. Let kind be object's kind.
    let kind = iterator.kind;

    let pair = {
        // 8. Let values be object's target's value pairs to iterate over.
        let values = T::value_pairs_to_iterate_over(&iterator.target);

        // 9. Let len be the length of values.
        let len = values.len();

        // 10. If index is greater than or equal to len, then return CreateIteratorResultObject(undefined, true).
        if index >= len {
            return Ok(Value::from_object(create_iterator_result_object(
                vm,
                realm,
                Value::UNDEFINED,
                true,
            )));
        }

        // 11. Let pair be the entry in values at index index.
        values[index].clone()
    };

    // 12. Set object's index to index + 1.
    iterator.index.set(index + 1);

    // 13. Return the iterator result for pair and kind.
    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);
    iterator_result(&cx, pair, kind)
}

fn default_iterator_of<T: DefaultIteratorClasses>(object: Gc<Object>) -> Option<Gc<EmbedderCell<DefaultIterator<T>>>> {
    if !is_host_instance_of(&object, T::iterator_class()) {
        return None;
    }
    let host_data = host_data_of(&object).expect("a default iterator object holds its cell");
    // SAFETY: The object is a host object of the iterator class, whose host data is the cell of a default iterator.
    unsafe { T::ITERATOR_CELL_CLASS.downcast(host_data) }
}

/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#iterator-result
fn iterator_result<K: ToJs, V: ToJs>(cx: &CallContext, pair: (K, V), kind: IterationKind) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    let (key, value) = pair;
    let result = match kind {
        // 1. Let result be a value determined by the value of kind:
        // -> "key"
        //     1. Let idlKey be pair's key.
        //     2. Let key be the result of converting idlKey to a JavaScript value.
        //     3. result is key.
        IterationKind::Key => key.to_js(cx)?,
        // -> "value"
        //     1. Let idlValue be pair's value.
        //     2. Let value be the result of converting idlValue to a JavaScript value.
        //     3. result is value.
        IterationKind::Value => value.to_js(cx)?,
        // -> "key+value"
        //     1. Let idlKey be pair's key.
        //     2. Let idlValue be pair's value.
        //     3. Let key be the result of converting idlKey to a JavaScript value.
        //     4. Let value be the result of converting idlValue to a JavaScript value.
        //     5. Let array be ! ArrayCreate(2).
        //     6. Perform ! CreateDataPropertyOrThrow(array, "0", key).
        //     7. Perform ! CreateDataPropertyOrThrow(array, "1", value).
        //     8. result is array.
        IterationKind::KeyAndValue => {
            let key = key.to_js(cx)?;
            let value = value.to_js(cx)?;
            Value::from_object(Array::create_from(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &[key, value]).upcast::<Object>())
        }
    };

    // 2. Return CreateIteratorResultObject(result, false).
    Ok(Value::from_object(create_iterator_result_object(
        cx.vm(),
        cx.realm(),
        result,
        false,
    )))
}

/// The steps of the %Symbol.iterator% and "entries" methods of the interface prototype object,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#define-the-iteration-methods
pub(crate) fn entries<T: DefaultIteratorClasses>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let jsValue be ? ToObject(this value).
    // 2. If jsValue is a platform object, then perform a security check, passing jsValue, "%Symbol.iterator%", and
    //    "method".
    // 3. If jsValue does not implement definition, then throw a TypeError.
    let (js_value, realm) = this_object(
        vm,
        T::wrapper_class(),
        T::NAME,
        "%Symbol.iterator%",
        SecurityCheckType::Method,
    )?;

    // 4. Return a newly created default iterator object for definition, with jsValue as its target, "key+value" as its
    //    kind, and index set to 0.
    Ok(create_default_iterator::<T>(
        &CallContext::new(vm, realm),
        js_value,
        IterationKind::KeyAndValue,
    ))
}

/// The steps of the "keys" method of the interface prototype object,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#define-the-iteration-methods
pub(crate) fn keys<T: DefaultIteratorClasses>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let jsValue be ? ToObject(this value).
    // 2. If jsValue is a platform object, then perform a security check, passing jsValue, "keys", and "method".
    // 3. If jsValue does not implement definition, then throw a TypeError.
    let (js_value, realm) = this_object(vm, T::wrapper_class(), T::NAME, "keys", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 4. Return a newly created default iterator object for definition, with jsValue as its target, "key" as its kind,
    //    and index set to 0.
    Ok(create_default_iterator::<T>(
        &CallContext::new(vm, realm),
        js_value,
        IterationKind::Key,
    ))
}

/// The steps of the "values" method of the interface prototype object,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#define-the-iteration-methods
pub(crate) fn values<T: DefaultIteratorClasses>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let jsValue be ? ToObject(this value).
    // 2. If jsValue is a platform object, then perform a security check, passing jsValue, "values", and "method".
    // 3. If jsValue does not implement definition, then throw a TypeError.
    let (js_value, realm) = this_object(vm, T::wrapper_class(), T::NAME, "values", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 4. Return a newly created default iterator object for definition, with jsValue as its target, "value" as its
    //    kind, and index set to 0.
    Ok(create_default_iterator::<T>(
        &CallContext::new(vm, realm),
        js_value,
        IterationKind::Value,
    ))
}

/// The steps of the "forEach" method of the interface prototype object,
/// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#define-the-iteration-methods
pub(crate) fn for_each<T: DefaultIteratorClasses>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    let callback = vm.argument(0);
    let this_arg = vm.argument(1);

    // 1. Let jsValue be ? ToObject(this value).
    // 2. If jsValue is a platform object, then perform a security check, passing jsValue, "forEach", and "method".
    // 3. If jsValue does not implement definition, then throw a TypeError.
    let (js_value, realm) = this_object(vm, T::wrapper_class(), T::NAME, "forEach", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;
    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);

    // 4. Let idlCallback be callback, converted to a Function.
    if !callback.is_function() {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAFunction, &[&callback]);
    }

    // 5. Let idlObject be the IDL interface type value that represents a reference to jsValue.
    let idl_object = T::iteration_target(&cx, js_value, IterationKind::KeyAndValue);

    // 6. Let pairs be idlObject's list of value pairs to iterate over.
    // 7. Let i be 0.
    let mut i = 0;

    // 8. While i < pairs's size:
    while i < T::value_pairs_to_iterate_over(&idl_object).len() {
        // 1. Let pair be pairs[i].
        let (key, value) = T::value_pairs_to_iterate_over(&idl_object)[i].clone();

        // 2. Invoke idlCallback with « pair's value, pair's key, idlObject » and with thisArg as the callback this
        //    value.
        let value = value.to_js(&cx)?;
        let key = key.to_js(&cx)?;
        call(vm, callback, this_arg, &[value, key, Value::from_object(js_value)])?;

        // 3. Set pairs to idlObject's current list of value pairs to iterate over. (It might have changed.)
        // 4. Set i to i + 1.
        i += 1;
    }

    Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
}

//! The strings that LibWeb's C++ code lends the exports of the crate for as long as they run, as the raw
//! representation of an AK::Utf16String or an AK::Utf16FlyString. An export takes one of these where C++ passes such a
//! string, as it takes a `&Vm` where C++ passes the VM, so a value of one is always a live string. Its lifetime is that
//! of the call, which keeps the string from outliving it.

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::num::NonZeroUsize;

use ak::{Utf16FlyString, Utf16String};

/// An AK::Utf16String that C++ lends for the call.
#[repr(transparent)]
pub(crate) struct LentUtf16String<'a>(NonZeroUsize, PhantomData<&'a ()>);

impl LentUtf16String<'_> {
    /// The string, with a reference of its own.
    pub(crate) fn to_utf16_string(&self) -> Utf16String {
        // SAFETY: A LentUtf16String is a live string.
        unsafe { Utf16String::from_raw_borrowed(self.0.get()) }
    }
}

/// An AK::Utf16FlyString that C++ lends for the call.
#[repr(transparent)]
pub(crate) struct LentUtf16FlyString<'a>(NonZeroUsize, PhantomData<&'a ()>);

impl LentUtf16FlyString<'_> {
    /// The string, with a reference of its own.
    pub(crate) fn to_utf16_fly_string(&self) -> Utf16FlyString {
        // SAFETY: A LentUtf16FlyString is a live fly string.
        unsafe { Utf16FlyString::from_raw_borrowed(self.0.get()) }
    }
}

//! The maplike declarations of the interfaces implemented in Rust, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-maplike

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{
    Attribute, ErrorKind, ErrorType, Gc, Map, MapIterator, Object, PropertyAttributes, PropertyKey, PropertyKind,
    RawNativeFunctionPointer, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr, Value, Vm, call,
};

use crate::bindings::CallContext;
use crate::bindings::conversions::{ToJs, to_dom_string};
use crate::bindings::interface::{
    Interface, SecurityCheckType, define_attribute, define_operation, this_implementation,
};

/// What the implementation of an interface with a maplike declaration, whose keys are strings, implements.
pub(crate) trait Maplike: Interface {
    fn has(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        map_has::<Self>(vm)
    }

    // https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-map-entries
    fn map_entries(&self, cx: &CallContext) -> Gc<Map>;

    /// The value of the entry of the key, converted to a JS value, if there is one.
    fn map_value(&self, cx: &CallContext, key: &Utf16String) -> Option<Value> {
        let key = key.clone().to_js(cx).expect("a string converts to a JS value");
        self.map_entries(cx).map_get(key)
    }
}

/// What the implementation of an interface with a read-write maplike declaration implements, for the operations that
/// the interface does not declare itself.
pub(crate) trait WritableMaplike: Maplike {
    /// Sets the entry of the key to a value that the bindings converted to the value type.
    fn map_set(&self, cx: &CallContext, key: Utf16String, value: Value);
    fn map_remove(&self, cx: &CallContext, key: &Utf16String) -> bool;
    fn map_clear(&self, cx: &CallContext);
}

/// What the generated bindings of a maplike declaration with operations of the bindings define.
pub(crate) trait MaplikeDeclaration: Maplike {
    /// Throws unless the JS value converts to the value type of the declaration.
    fn check_value(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()>;
}

/// Defines the properties that every maplike declaration has, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-maplike
#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "these are the functions of the declaration")]
pub(crate) fn define_maplike_properties(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    prototype: Gc<Object>,
    size: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    entries: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    keys: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    values: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    for_each: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    get: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    has: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
) {
    define_attribute(vm, realm, prototype, "size", size, None);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "entries", entries, 0);
    prototype.define_direct_property(
        vm,
        &PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().iterator),
        prototype.get_without_side_effects(vm, &vm.names.entries),
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE | Attribute::WRITABLE),
    );
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "keys", keys, 0);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "values", values, 0);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "forEach", for_each, 1);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "get", get, 1);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "has", has, 1);
}

/// The call context of the realm that a collection of a wrapper world lives in.
pub(crate) fn context_of_map<'vm>(cx: &CallContext<'vm>, map: Gc<Map>) -> CallContext<'vm> {
    CallContext::new(cx.vm(), map.upcast::<Object>().shape().realm())
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-map-size
pub(crate) fn map_size<T: Maplike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "size" and type "getter".
    let (_, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "size", SecurityCheckType::Getter)?;

    // 2. Let map be the map entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    let map = implementation.map_entries(&cx);

    // 3. Return map's size, converted to a JavaScript value.
    Ok(Value::from_f64(map.map_size() as f64))
}

fn create_map_iterator<T: Maplike>(vm: &Vm, identifier: &str, kind: PropertyKind) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    let (_, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, identifier, SecurityCheckType::Method)?;
    let map = implementation.map_entries(&cx);
    Ok(Value::from_object(
        MapIterator::create(vm, cx.realm(), map, kind).upcast::<Object>(),
    ))
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-map-entries
pub(crate) fn map_iterator_entries<T: Maplike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "entries" and type "method".
    // 2. Let map be the map entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    // 3. Return the result of creating a map iterator from map with kind "key+value".
    create_map_iterator::<T>(vm, "entries", PropertyKind::KeyAndValue)
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-map-keys
pub(crate) fn map_iterator_keys<T: Maplike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "keys" and type "method".
    // 2. Let map be the map entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    // 3. Return the result of creating a map iterator from map with kind "key".
    create_map_iterator::<T>(vm, "keys", PropertyKind::Key)
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-map-values
pub(crate) fn map_iterator_values<T: Maplike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "values" and type "method".
    // 2. Let map be the map entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    // 3. Return the result of creating a map iterator from map with kind "value".
    create_map_iterator::<T>(vm, "values", PropertyKind::Value)
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-map-forEach
pub(crate) fn map_for_each<T: Maplike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "forEach" and type "method".
    let (wrapper, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "forEach", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 2. Let map be the map entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    let map = implementation.map_entries(&cx);

    // 3. Let callbackFn be the first argument passed to the function, or undefined if not supplied.
    // 4. If IsCallable(callbackFn) is false, throw a TypeError.
    let callback = vm.argument(0);
    if !callback.is_function() {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAFunction, &[&callback]);
    }

    // 5. Let thisArg be the second argument passed to the function, or undefined if not supplied.
    let this_arg = vm.argument(1);

    // 6. For each key → value of map:
    let iterator = map.begin();
    while !iterator.is_end() {
        // 1. Let jsKey be key converted to a JavaScript value.
        // 2. Let jsValue be value converted to a JavaScript value.
        let entry = iterator.current();

        // 3. Perform ? Call(callbackFn, thisArg, « jsValue, jsKey, O »).
        call(
            vm,
            callback,
            this_arg,
            &[entry.value, entry.key, Value::from_object(wrapper)],
        )?;
        iterator.advance();
    }

    // 7. Return undefined.
    Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
}

/// The map entries of the this value, and the key argument converted to the key type and back to a JS value.
fn entries_and_key<T: Maplike>(vm: &Vm, identifier: &str) -> ThrowCompletionOr<(Gc<Map>, Value)> {
    let (_, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, identifier, SecurityCheckType::Method)?;
    let map = implementation.map_entries(&cx);
    let key = to_dom_string(vm, vm.argument(0))?;
    Ok((map, key.to_js(&cx)?))
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-map-get
pub(crate) fn map_get<T: Maplike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "get" and type "method".
    let (_, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "get", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 3. Let keyType be the key type specified in the maplike declaration.
    // 4. Let keyArg be the first argument passed to this function, or undefined if not supplied.
    // 5. Let key be keyArg converted to an IDL value of type keyType.
    let key = to_dom_string(vm, vm.argument(0))?;

    // 7. If map[key] exists, then return map[key], converted to a JavaScript value.
    // 8. Return undefined.
    Ok(implementation.map_value(&cx, &key).unwrap_or(Value::UNDEFINED))
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-map-has
pub(crate) fn map_has<T: Maplike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "has" and type "method".
    // 2. Let map be the map entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    // 3. Let keyType be the key type specified in the maplike declaration.
    // 4. Let keyArg be the first argument passed to this function, or undefined if not supplied.
    // 5. Let key be keyArg converted to an IDL value of type keyType.
    let (map, key) = entries_and_key::<T>(vm, "has")?;

    // 7. If map[key] exists, then return true, otherwise return false.
    Ok(Value::from_bool(map.map_has(key)))
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-map-set
pub(crate) fn map_set<T: MaplikeDeclaration + WritableMaplike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "set" and type "method".
    let (wrapper, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "set", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 3. Let keyType be the key type specified in the maplike declaration, and valueType be the value type.
    // 4. Let keyArg be the first argument passed to this function, or undefined if not supplied.
    // 5. Let key be keyArg converted to an IDL value of type keyType.
    let key = to_dom_string(vm, vm.argument(0))?;

    // 7. Let valueArg be the second argument passed to this function, or undefined if not supplied.
    // 8. Let value be valueArg converted to an IDL value of type valueType.
    let value = vm.argument(1);
    T::check_value(vm, value)?;

    // 9. Set map[key] to value.
    implementation.map_set(&cx, key, value);

    // 10. Return O.
    Ok(Value::from_object(wrapper))
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-map-delete
pub(crate) fn map_delete<T: WritableMaplike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "delete" and type "method".
    let (_, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "delete", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 3. Let keyType be the key type specified in the maplike declaration.
    // 4. Let keyArg be the first argument passed to this function, or undefined if not supplied.
    // 5. Let key be keyArg converted to an IDL value of type keyType.
    let key = to_dom_string(vm, vm.argument(0))?;

    // 7. Let retVal be true if map[key] exists, or else false.
    // 8. Remove map[key].
    // 9. Return retVal.
    Ok(Value::from_bool(implementation.map_remove(&cx, &key)))
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-map-clear
pub(crate) fn map_clear<T: WritableMaplike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "clear" and type "method".
    let (_, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "clear", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 3. Clear map.
    // NOTE: The map is preserved because there may be existing iterators, currently suspended, iterating over it.
    implementation.map_clear(&cx);

    // 4. Return undefined.
    Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
}

//! The runtime of the WebIDL bindings that Meta/Generators/generate_libweb_bindings.py writes in Rust, for the
//! interfaces that their IDL marks [ImplementedIn=Rust]. The bindings of such an interface are the native functions,
//! constructor and prototype of the interface, which call the methods of the interface's implementation in this
//! crate: one per constructor, attribute and operation, whose signatures the generated bindings document. A dictionary
//! of the interface's IDL is a struct next to the implementation, whose fields are the dictionary's members; the
//! bindings convert it.
//!
//! Values and cells live in locals while a binding runs, which the collector scans; a binding that gathers values in
//! a container keeps them in a MarkedVec.

#[allow(
    clippy::unnecessary_wraps,
    reason = "the asynchronous iterator steps are built-in functions, which can throw"
)]
pub(crate) mod async_iterable;
pub(crate) mod callback;
pub(crate) mod conversions;
pub(crate) mod cpp_cell;
pub(crate) mod environment_settings_object;
pub(crate) mod event_target;
#[cfg(web_idl_bindings)]
pub(crate) mod generated;
pub(crate) mod global_object;
pub(crate) mod interface;
pub(crate) mod iterable;
pub(crate) mod lent_string;
pub(crate) mod maplike;
pub(crate) mod new_global_object;
pub(crate) mod promise;
pub(crate) mod realm_data;
pub(crate) mod services;
pub(crate) mod setlike;
pub(crate) mod structured_data;

use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{ErrorKind, Gc, Object, Realm, Throw, ThrowCompletionOr, Value, Vm};

use crate::bindings::services::{
    web_bindings_create_dom_exception, web_bindings_pop_element_queue_and_invoke_reactions,
    web_bindings_push_element_queue,
};

/// Runs the steps of a [CEReactions] construct, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#cereactions
/// An exception of the steps is in the result, which the caller rethrows after the reactions ran.
#[cfg_attr(
    not(web_idl_bindings),
    allow(dead_code, reason = "only the generated bindings use the function")
)]
pub(crate) fn with_custom_element_reactions<R>(original_steps: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
    // 1. Push a new element queue onto this object's relevant agent's custom element reactions stack.
    // SAFETY: The bindings run on the main thread.
    unsafe { web_bindings_push_element_queue() };

    // 2. Run the originally-specified steps for this construct, catching any exceptions. If the steps return a value,
    //    let value be the returned value. If they throw an exception, let exception be the thrown exception.
    let value_or_exception = original_steps();

    // 3. Let queue be the result of popping from this object's relevant agent's custom element reactions stack.
    // 4. Invoke custom element reactions in queue.
    // SAFETY: The bindings run on the main thread, and the queue is the one this function pushed.
    unsafe { web_bindings_pop_element_queue_and_invoke_reactions() };

    // 5. If an exception exception was thrown by the original steps, rethrow exception.
    // 6. If a value value was returned from the original steps, return value.
    value_or_exception
}

/// What the bindings pass the implementation of an interface: the VM, and the realm that the implementation creates
/// its results in. For an attribute or an operation, that is the realm of the object it runs on; for a constructor,
/// the current realm.
pub(crate) struct CallContext<'vm> {
    vm: &'vm Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
}

impl<'vm> CallContext<'vm> {
    pub(crate) fn new(vm: &'vm Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Self {
        Self { vm, realm }
    }

    pub(crate) fn vm(&self) -> &'vm Vm {
        self.vm
    }

    pub(crate) fn realm(&self) -> Gc<Realm> {
        self.realm
    }
}

/// An exception that the implementation of an interface throws.
pub(crate) enum Exception {
    /// A value that JavaScript code threw.
    Thrown(Throw),
    /// A simple exception with the message, which the bindings create in the current realm.
    TypeError(Utf16String),
    RangeError(Utf16String),
    /// A DOMException with the name, one of https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-error-names-table, and the message.
    Dom(&'static str, Utf16String),
}

impl From<Throw> for Exception {
    fn from(throw: Throw) -> Self {
        Self::Thrown(throw)
    }
}

impl Exception {
    pub(crate) fn type_error(message: &str) -> Self {
        Self::TypeError(Utf16String::from_utf8(message))
    }

    pub(crate) fn range_error(message: &str) -> Self {
        Self::RangeError(Utf16String::from_utf8(message))
    }

    pub(crate) fn index_size_error(message: Utf16String) -> Self {
        Self::Dom("IndexSizeError", message)
    }

    pub(crate) fn syntax_error(message: Utf16String) -> Self {
        Self::Dom("SyntaxError", message)
    }

    /// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-exceptions
    pub(crate) fn throw_in_current_realm(self, vm: &Vm) -> Throw {
        let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a native function runs in a realm");
        self.throw(&CallContext::new(vm, realm))
    }

    pub(crate) fn throw(self, cx: &CallContext) -> Throw {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        match self {
            Self::Thrown(throw) => throw,
            Self::TypeError(message) => thrown(vm.throw_completion_with_utf16_message(ErrorKind::TypeError, message)),
            Self::RangeError(message) => thrown(vm.throw_completion_with_utf16_message(ErrorKind::RangeError, message)),
            Self::Dom(name, message) => {
                // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the name and the message are lent for the call.
                let exception = unsafe {
                    web_bindings_create_dom_exception(
                        cx.realm().as_ptr().cast(),
                        ak::Span::new(name.as_bytes()),
                        message.raw_identity(),
                    )
                };
                let exception = NonNull::new(exception.cast::<Object>()).expect("LibWeb returns the DOMException");
                // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live wrapper.
                Throw::new(Value::from_object(unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(exception) }))
            }
        }
    }
}

fn thrown(completion: ThrowCompletionOr<()>) -> Throw {
    match completion {
        Err(throw) => throw,
        Ok(()) => unreachable!("throwing a completion throws"),
    }
}

pub(crate) type WebIdlResult<T> = Result<T, Exception>;

/// The value of a WebIDL result that cannot be an exception, as `!` asserts of an abstract operation.
pub(crate) trait MustNotThrow<T> {
    fn must(self) -> T;
}

impl<T> MustNotThrow<T> for WebIdlResult<T> {
    #[track_caller]
    fn must(self) -> T {
        match self {
            Ok(value) => value,
            Err(_) => panic!("a step that cannot throw threw"),
        }
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{ErrorKind, Gc, JSONObject, Must, RawNativeFunctionResult, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr, Value, Vm};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_bindings_throw_copy_of_error_in_current_realm(vm: *const c_void, error: u64) -> RawNativeFunctionResult;
}

pub(crate) fn run_in_a_new_global_object<T>(
    vm: &Vm,
    steps: impl FnOnce(Gc<Realm>) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T> {
    let execution_context = Realm::initialize_host_defined_realm(vm, None, None).must();
    let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("the new execution context has a realm");
    let result = steps(realm);
    assert_eq!(vm.pop_execution_context(), execution_context.as_non_null());

    // Recreate any thrown error in the caller's realm before it reaches script.
    result.map_err(|error| {
        // SAFETY: The VM and error are live.
        unsafe {
            web_bindings_throw_copy_of_error_in_current_realm(core::ptr::from_ref(vm).cast(), error.value().to_raw())
        }
        .into_completion()
        .expect_err("throwing a copy of the error returns a throw completion")
    })
}

pub(crate) fn serialize_to_json_in_a_new_global_object(
    vm: &Vm,
    create_value: impl FnOnce(Gc<Realm>) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Utf16String> {
    let json = run_in_a_new_global_object(vm, |realm| {
        JSONObject::stringify_impl(vm, create_value(realm)?, Value::UNDEFINED, Value::UNDEFINED)
    })?;
    let Some(json) = json else {
        return vm.throw_completion_with_message(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            "Result of stringifying value must not be undefined".into(),
        );
    };
    Ok(json)
}

//! Promises as implementations hold them, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-promise: the PromiseCapability records
//! that LibWeb's C++ code calls WebIDL::Promise.

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    Array, EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, Must, NativeFunction, Object, Promise, PromiseCapability,
    PromiseState, PropertyKey, Realm, RejectionOperation, Trace, Value, Visitor, Vm, call, new_promise_capability,
    safe_promise_resolve,
};

use crate::bindings::interface::{with_temporary_execution_context, with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};

/// A Promise<T> value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-promise
pub(crate) type WebIdlPromise = Gc<PromiseCapability>;

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// Queues a microtask that calls the function, a native function with no arguments, while an execution context of
    /// the realm is on the stack, as HTML::queue_a_microtask() queues one without a document.
    fn web_bindings_queue_a_microtask(realm: *mut c_void, function: *mut c_void);

    fn web_bindings_deferred_invoke(cell: *mut c_void, steps: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void));

    /// Calls the steps with the VM and the cell in parallel: later, outside of any task, while an execution context of
    /// the realm is on the stack. The cell lives until then.
    fn web_bindings_run_in_parallel(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        cell: *mut c_void,
        steps: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void),
    );

    /// Queues a task on the task source, an HTML::Task::Source, that calls the steps with the VM and the cell, as
    /// HTML::queue_a_task() queues one without a document. The cell lives until then.
    fn web_bindings_queue_a_task(
        task_source: u8,
        cell: *mut c_void,
        steps: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void),
    );

    /// Queues a global task on the task source, an HTML::Task::Source, with the global object, that calls the steps with
    /// the VM and the cell, as HTML::queue_global_task() queues one. The cell lives until then. Returns the task's
    /// HTML::TaskID.
    fn web_bindings_queue_a_global_task(
        global_object: *mut c_void,
        task_source: u8,
        cell: *mut c_void,
        steps: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void),
    ) -> u64;

    /// Removes the tasks with the HTML::TaskIDs from the task queue of the event loop of the realm's agent.
    fn web_bindings_remove_tasks(realm: *mut c_void, task_ids: ak::Span<'_, u64>);

    /// The HTML::TaskID of the task that the event loop of the realm's agent is running.
    fn web_bindings_currently_running_task(realm: *mut c_void) -> u64;

    /// Spins the event loop until the promise, a Promise, is no longer pending.
    fn web_bindings_spin_until_promise_is_settled(promise: *mut c_void);
}

/// The task sources of HTML::Task::Source that the bindings queue tasks on.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub(crate) enum TaskSource {
    Unspecified = 0,
    DOMManipulation = 1,
    UserInteraction = 2,
    Networking = 3,
    PostedMessage = 6,
    TimerTask = 8,
    Geolocation = 10,
    FileReading = 13,
    PerformanceTimeline = 15,
    Clipboard = 17,
    Permissions = 18,
    FontLoading = 19,
    RemoteEvent = 20,
    Gamepad = 25,
    WebGL = 26,
    Crypto = 27,
    Storage = 29,
}

// SAFETY: A task source holds no cells.
unsafe impl Trace for TaskSource {
    fn trace(&self, _: &mut Visitor) {}
}

/// A task that queue_a_global_task() queued, an HTML::TaskID.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct TaskId(u64);

impl TaskId {
    /// The HTML::TaskID of the task.
    pub(crate) fn host_id(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
}

/// The promise that LibWeb's C++ code returns, a WebIDL::Promise.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `promise` must be a live WebIDL::Promise.
pub(crate) unsafe fn promise_from_abi(promise: *mut c_void) -> WebIdlPromise {
    let promise = NonNull::new(promise.cast::<PromiseCapability>()).expect("LibWeb returns a promise");
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live promise capability.
    unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(promise) }
}

/// A new promise in the realm, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-new-promise
pub(crate) fn create_promise(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Let constructor be realm.[[Intrinsics]].[[%Promise%]].
    let constructor = realm.intrinsics().promise_constructor(vm);

    // 2. Return ? NewPromiseCapability(constructor).
    // NB: When called with %Promise%, NewPromiseCapability can't throw.
    new_promise_capability(vm, Value::from_object(constructor)).must()
}

/// A promise resolved with the value in the realm, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-resolved-with
pub(crate) fn create_resolved_promise(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, value: Value) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Let value be the result of converting x to an ECMAScript value.
    // 2. Let constructor be realm.[[Intrinsics]].[[%Promise%]].
    // 3. Let promiseCapability be ? NewPromiseCapability(constructor).
    let promise = create_promise(vm, realm);

    // 4. Perform ! Call(promiseCapability.[[Resolve]], undefined, « value »).
    resolve_promise(vm, promise, value);

    // 5. Return promiseCapability.
    promise
}

/// A promise rejected with the reason in the realm, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with
pub(crate) fn create_rejected_promise(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, reason: Value) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Let constructor be realm.[[Intrinsics]].[[%Promise%]].
    // 2. Let promiseCapability be ? NewPromiseCapability(constructor).
    let promise = create_promise(vm, realm);

    // 3. Perform ! Call(promiseCapability.[[Reject]], undefined, « r »).
    reject_promise(vm, promise, reason);

    // 4. Return promiseCapability.
    promise
}

/// A promise rejected with the exception, which is created in the realm of the promise.
pub(crate) fn create_rejected_promise_from_exception(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, exception: Exception) -> WebIdlPromise {
    let reason = exception_value(vm, realm, exception);
    create_rejected_promise(vm, realm, reason)
}

/// The value of an exception that is created in the realm.
pub(crate) fn exception_value(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, exception: Exception) -> Value {
    let _type_error_realm = vm.type_error_realm_scope(realm);
    with_temporary_execution_context(realm, || exception.throw(&CallContext::new(vm, realm)).value())
}

/// The realm of the promise's [[Promise]], which its reactions run in.
pub(crate) fn promise_realm(promise: WebIdlPromise) -> Gc<Realm> {
    promise.promise().shape().realm()
}

/// Resolves the promise with the value, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#resolve
pub(crate) fn resolve_promise(vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise, value: Value) {
    // 1. If x is not given, then let it be the undefined value.
    // 2. Let value be the result of converting x to an ECMAScript value.
    // 3. Perform ! Call(p.[[Resolve]], undefined, « value »).
    // AD-HOC: We perform SafePromiseResolve instead, which never runs script.
    //         See https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/pull/1645
    safe_promise_resolve(vm, promise, value).must();
}

/// Rejects the promise with the reason, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#reject
pub(crate) fn reject_promise(vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise, reason: Value) {
    // 1. Perform ! Call(p.[[Reject]], undefined, « r »).
    call(
        vm,
        Value::from_object(promise.reject().upcast::<Object>()),
        Value::UNDEFINED,
        &[reason],
    )
    .must();
}

/// Rejects the promise with the exception, which is created in the realm of the promise.
pub(crate) fn reject_promise_with_exception(vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise, exception: Exception) {
    let reason = exception_value(vm, promise_realm(promise), exception);
    reject_promise(vm, promise, reason);
}

/// The steps that a reaction to a promise performs given what the reaction captures and the value or the reason.
pub(crate) type ReactionSteps<C> = fn(&CallContext, C, Value) -> WebIdlResult<Value>;

/// What a native function that runs steps given by a plain function captures: the state that the steps are given, and
/// the steps, which the native function's behaviour itself cannot capture.
pub(crate) struct NativeSteps<C, S> {
    pub(crate) captures: C,
    pub(crate) steps: S,
}

// SAFETY: The steps are a plain function, which holds no cells.
unsafe impl<C: Trace, S> Trace for NativeSteps<C, S> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.captures.trace(visitor);
    }
}

/// Reacts to the promise with the steps, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-perform-steps-once-promise-is-settled,
/// which are given the captures.
pub(crate) fn react_to_promise<C: Trace + Copy + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    promise: WebIdlPromise,
    captures: C,
    on_fulfilled: Option<ReactionSteps<C>>,
    on_rejected: Option<ReactionSteps<C>>,
) -> WebIdlPromise {
    let realm = promise_realm(promise);
    let name = PropertyKey::from_utf8("");

    // 1. Let onFulfilledSteps be the following steps given argument V:
    let on_fulfilled_steps = |vm: &Vm, function: &NativeSteps<(C, Gc<Realm>), Option<ReactionSteps<C>>>| {
        let (captures, realm) = function.captures;
        let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);

        // 1. Let value be the result of converting V to an IDL value of type T.
        let value = vm.argument(0);

        // 2. If there is a set of steps to be run if the promise was fulfilled, then let result be the result of
        //    performing them, given value if T is not undefined. Otherwise, let result be value.
        let result = match function.steps {
            Some(steps) => steps(&cx, captures, value).map_err(|exception| exception.throw(&cx))?,
            None => value,
        };

        // 3. Return result, converted to an ECMAScript value.
        Ok(result)
    };

    // 2. Let onFulfilled be CreateBuiltinFunction(onFulfilledSteps, 1, "", « »):
    let on_fulfilled_function = NativeFunction::create(
        vm,
        NativeSteps {
            captures: (captures, realm),
            steps: on_fulfilled,
        },
        on_fulfilled_steps,
        1,
        &name,
        Some(realm),
        None,
        None,
    );

    // 3. Let onRejectedSteps be the following steps given argument R:
    let on_rejected_steps = |vm: &Vm, function: &NativeSteps<(C, Gc<Realm>), Option<ReactionSteps<C>>>| {
        let (captures, realm) = function.captures;
        let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);

        // 1. Let reason be the result of converting R to an IDL value of type any.
        let reason = vm.argument(0);

        // 2. If there is a set of steps to be run if the promise was rejected, then let result be the result of
        //    performing them, given reason. Otherwise, let result be a promise rejected with reason.
        let result = match function.steps {
            Some(steps) => steps(&cx, captures, reason).map_err(|exception| exception.throw(&cx))?,
            None => Value::from_object(create_rejected_promise(vm, realm, reason).promise()),
        };

        // 3. Return result, converted to an ECMAScript value.
        Ok(result)
    };

    // 4. Let onRejected be CreateBuiltinFunction(onRejectedSteps, 1, "", « »):
    let on_rejected_function = NativeFunction::create(
        vm,
        NativeSteps {
            captures: (captures, realm),
            steps: on_rejected,
        },
        on_rejected_steps,
        1,
        &name,
        Some(realm),
        None,
        None,
    );

    // 5. Let constructor be promise.[[Promise]].[[Realm]].[[Intrinsics]].[[%Promise%]].
    // 6. Let newCapability be ? NewPromiseCapability(constructor).
    let new_capability = create_promise(vm, realm);

    // 7. Perform PerformPromiseThen(promise.[[Promise]], onFulfilled, onRejected, newCapability).
    promise_object(promise).perform_then(
        vm,
        Value::from_object(on_fulfilled_function.upcast::<Object>()),
        Value::from_object(on_rejected_function.upcast::<Object>()),
        Some(new_capability),
    );

    // 8. Return newCapability.
    new_capability
}

/// Performs the steps upon fulfillment of the promise, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#upon-fulfillment
pub(crate) fn upon_fulfillment<C: Trace + Copy + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    promise: WebIdlPromise,
    captures: C,
    steps: ReactionSteps<C>,
) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Return the result of reacting to promise:
    //    - If promise was fulfilled with value v, then:
    //      1. Perform steps with v.
    react_to_promise(vm, promise, captures, Some(steps), None)
}

/// Performs the steps upon rejection of the promise, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#upon-rejection
pub(crate) fn upon_rejection<C: Trace + Copy + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    promise: WebIdlPromise,
    captures: C,
    steps: ReactionSteps<C>,
) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Return the result of reacting to promise:
    //    - If promise was rejected with reason r, then:
    //      1. Perform steps with r.
    react_to_promise(vm, promise, captures, None, Some(steps))
}

/// Marks the promise as handled, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#mark-a-promise-as-handled
pub(crate) fn mark_promise_as_handled(vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise) {
    // To mark as handled a Promise<T> promise, set promise.[[Promise]].[[PromiseIsHandled]] to true.
    let promise_object = promise_object(promise);

    // AD-HOC: If the promise was already rejected, tell the host it is now handled, matching what
    //         PerformPromiseThen does when a handler is attached to a rejected promise. This pulls the
    //         promise out of the about-to-be-notified rejected promises list, so specs that reject a
    //         promise and then mark it as handled (the Streams API does this on every reader and writer
    //         release) don't leave a trail of queued unhandled-rejection notification tasks behind.
    if promise_object.state() == PromiseState::Rejected && !promise_object.is_handled() {
        vm.host_promise_rejection_tracker()(vm, promise_object, RejectionOperation::Handle);
    }

    promise_object.set_is_handled();
}

pub(crate) fn is_promise_fulfilled(promise: WebIdlPromise) -> bool {
    promise_object(promise).state() == PromiseState::Fulfilled
}

/// A promise that settles once every promise has, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#waiting-for-all-promise
pub(crate) fn get_promise_for_wait_for_all(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, promises: &[WebIdlPromise]) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Let promise be a new promise of type Promise<sequence<T>> in realm.
    let promise = create_promise(vm, realm);

    // 2. Let successSteps be the following steps, given results:
    // 3. Let failureSteps be the following steps, given reason:
    // 4. Wait for all with promises, given successSteps and failureSteps.
    wait_for_all(vm, realm, promises, promise);

    // 5. Return promise.
    promise
}

/// The state of waiting for all of some promises, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#wait-for-all, whose success and
/// failure steps settle `promise`.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct WaitForAll {
    promise: WebIdlPromise,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    rejected: Cell<bool>,
    result: Gc<Array>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    total: usize,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    fulfilled_count: Cell<usize>,
}

static WAIT_FOR_ALL_CLASS: EmbedderClass<WaitForAll> = EmbedderClass::new("WaitForAll");

impl EmbedderValue for WaitForAll {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &WAIT_FOR_ALL_CLASS;
}

impl WaitForAll {
    // 2. Let successSteps be the following steps, given results:
    fn success_steps(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(self.realm, || {
            // 1. Resolve promise with results.
            resolve_promise(vm, self.promise, Value::from_object(self.result.upcast::<Object>()));
        });
    }

    // 3. Let failureSteps be the following steps, given reason:
    fn failure_steps(&self, vm: &Vm, reason: Value) {
        with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(self.realm, || {
            // 1. Reject promise with reason.
            reject_promise(vm, self.promise, reason);
        });
    }
}

/// Waits for all of the promises, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#wait-for-all, with the success and failure steps of
/// getting a promise to wait for all, which settle `promise`.
fn wait_for_all(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, promises: &[WebIdlPromise], promise: WebIdlPromise) {
    let name = PropertyKey::from_utf8("");

    // 1. Let fullfilledCount be 0.
    // 2. Let rejected be false.
    // 5. Let total be promises’s size.
    // 8. Let result be a list containing total null values.
    let total = promises.len();
    let result = Array::create_from(vm, realm, &vec![Value::NULL; total]);
    let state = WAIT_FOR_ALL_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| WaitForAll {
        promise,
        realm,
        rejected: Cell::new(false),
        result,
        total,
        fulfilled_count: Cell::new(0),
    });

    // 3. Let rejectionHandlerSteps be the following steps given arg:
    let rejection_handler_steps = |vm: &Vm, state: &Gc<EmbedderCell<WaitForAll>>| {
        // 1. If rejected is true, abort these steps.
        if state.rejected.get() {
            return Ok(Value::UNDEFINED);
        }

        // 2. Set rejected to true.
        state.rejected.set(true);

        // 3. Perform failureSteps given arg.
        state.failure_steps(vm, vm.argument(0));
        Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
    };

    // 4. Let rejectionHandler be CreateBuiltinFunction(rejectionHandlerSteps, 1, "", « »):
    let rejection_handler =
        NativeFunction::create(vm, state, rejection_handler_steps, 1, &name, Some(realm), None, None);

    // 6. If total is 0, then:
    if total == 0 {
        // 1. Queue a microtask to perform successSteps given « ».
        queue_a_microtask(vm, realm, state, |vm, state| state.success_steps(vm));

        // 2. Return.
        return;
    }

    // 7. Let index be 0.
    // 9. For each promise of promises:
    for (index, each_promise) in promises.iter().enumerate() {
        // 1. Let promiseIndex be index.
        let promise_index = u32::try_from(index).expect("a list of promises fits an array");

        // 2. Let fulfillmentHandler be the following steps given arg:
        let fulfillment_handler_steps = |vm: &Vm, captures: &(Gc<EmbedderCell<WaitForAll>>, u32)| {
            let (state, promise_index) = *captures;

            // 1. Set result[promiseIndex] to arg.
            state
                .result
                .create_data_property(vm, &PropertyKey::from(promise_index), vm.argument(0), None, None)
                .must();

            // 2. Set fullfilledCount to fullfilledCount + 1.
            state.fulfilled_count.set(state.fulfilled_count.get() + 1);

            // 3. If fullfilledCount equals total, then perform successSteps given result.
            if state.fulfilled_count.get() == state.total {
                state.success_steps(vm);
            }
            Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
        };

        // 3. Let fulfillmentHandler be CreateBuiltinFunction(fulfillmentHandler, 1, "", « »):
        let fulfillment_handler = NativeFunction::create(
            vm,
            (state, promise_index),
            fulfillment_handler_steps,
            1,
            &name,
            Some(realm),
            None,
            None,
        );

        // 4. Perform PerformPromiseThen(promise, fulfillmentHandler, rejectionHandler).
        promise_object(*each_promise).perform_then(
            vm,
            Value::from_object(fulfillment_handler.upcast::<Object>()),
            Value::from_object(rejection_handler.upcast::<Object>()),
            None,
        );

        // 5. Set index to index + 1.
    }
}

/// Queues a microtask that performs the steps with the captures,
/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#queue-a-microtask
pub(crate) fn queue_a_microtask<C: Trace + Copy + 'static>(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, captures: C, steps: fn(&Vm, C)) {
    let function = NativeFunction::create(
        vm,
        NativeSteps { captures, steps },
        |vm: &Vm, function: &NativeSteps<C, fn(&Vm, C)>| {
            (function.steps)(vm, function.captures);
            Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
        },
        0,
        &PropertyKey::from_utf8(""),
        Some(realm),
        None,
        None,
    );
    // SAFETY: The realm and the function are live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_queue_a_microtask(realm.as_ptr().cast(), function.as_ptr().cast()) };
}

/// Steps with what they capture, which run once, later, from a task or in parallel. They run as C++ code would, with
/// no function of their own on the stack.
trait DeferredSteps: Trace {
    fn run(&self, vm: &Vm);
}

struct CapturedSteps<C> {
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, C),
}

// SAFETY: The steps are a plain function, which holds no cells.
unsafe impl<C: Trace> Trace for CapturedSteps<C> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.captures.trace(visitor);
    }
}

impl<C: Trace + Clone + 'static> DeferredSteps for CapturedSteps<C> {
    fn run(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        (self.steps)(vm, self.captures.clone());
    }
}

/// The cell that keeps deferred steps and what they capture alive until they run.
struct PendingSteps(RefCell<Option<Box<dyn DeferredSteps>>>);

// SAFETY: The steps that have not run are all the cells this reaches.
unsafe impl Trace for PendingSteps {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        if let Some(steps) = &*self.0.borrow() {
            steps.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

static PENDING_STEPS_CLASS: EmbedderClass<PendingSteps> = EmbedderClass::new("PendingSteps");

impl EmbedderValue for PendingSteps {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &PENDING_STEPS_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) fn pending_steps<C: Trace + Clone + 'static>(vm: &Vm, captures: C, steps: fn(&Vm, C)) -> *mut c_void {
    PENDING_STEPS_CLASS
        .allocate(vm, |_| {
            let steps: Box<dyn DeferredSteps> = Box::new(CapturedSteps { captures, steps });
            PendingSteps(RefCell::new(Some(steps)))
        })
        .as_ptr()
        .cast()
}

pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn run_pending_steps(vm: *mut c_void, cell: *mut c_void) {
    // SAFETY: LibWeb passes the VM and the cell that pending_steps() made, which it kept alive.
    let (vm, cell) = unsafe {
        (
            &*vm.cast::<Vm>(),
            Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new_unchecked(cell.cast::<EmbedderCell<PendingSteps>>())),
        )
    };
    // NB: The cell keeps what the steps capture alive while they run, and lets go of it once they have.
    cell.0.borrow().as_ref().expect("deferred steps run once").run(vm);
    cell.0.take();
}

/// Defers steps to the event loop without pushing an execution context.
pub(crate) fn deferred_invoke<C: Trace + Clone + 'static>(vm: &Vm, captures: C, steps: fn(&Vm, C)) {
    let cell = pending_steps(vm, captures, steps);
    // SAFETY: The cell is live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_deferred_invoke(cell, run_pending_steps) };
}

/// Performs the steps with the captures in parallel, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/infrastructure.html#in-parallel,
/// with an execution context of the realm on the stack.
pub(crate) fn in_parallel<C: Trace + Copy + 'static>(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, captures: C, steps: fn(&Vm, C)) {
    let cell = pending_steps(vm, captures, steps);
    // SAFETY: The realm and the cell are live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_run_in_parallel(realm.as_ptr().cast(), cell, run_pending_steps) };
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#queue-a-task
pub(crate) fn queue_a_task<C: Trace + Clone + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    task_source: TaskSource,
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, C),
) {
    let cell = pending_steps(vm, captures, steps);
    // SAFETY: The cell is live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_queue_a_task(task_source as u8, cell, run_pending_steps) };
}

/// Queues a global task on the task source, given the global object, that performs the steps with the captures,
/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#queue-a-global-task. As with queue_a_task(), the steps run
/// with no execution context of their own on the stack.
pub(crate) fn queue_a_global_task<C: Trace + Clone + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    global: Gc<Object>,
    task_source: TaskSource,
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, C),
) -> TaskId {
    let cell = pending_steps(vm, captures, steps);
    // SAFETY: The global object and the cell are live.
    TaskId(unsafe {
        web_bindings_queue_a_global_task(global.as_ptr().cast(), task_source as u8, cell, run_pending_steps)
    })
}

/// Removes the tasks from the task queue of the event loop of the realm's agent.
pub(crate) fn remove_tasks(realm: Gc<Realm>, tasks: &[TaskId]) {
    let task_ids: Vec<u64> = tasks.iter().map(|task| task.0).collect();
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the task IDs are lent for the call.
    unsafe { web_bindings_remove_tasks(realm.as_ptr().cast(), ak::Span::new(&task_ids)) };
}

/// The task that the event loop of the realm's agent is running.
pub(crate) fn currently_running_task(realm: Gc<Realm>) -> TaskId {
    // SAFETY: The realm is live.
    TaskId(unsafe { web_bindings_currently_running_task(realm.as_ptr().cast()) })
}

/// Spins the event loop until the promise is fulfilled or rejected.
pub(crate) fn spin_until_promise_is_settled(promise: WebIdlPromise) {
    // SAFETY: The promise is live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_spin_until_promise_is_settled(promise_object(promise).as_ptr().cast()) };
}

/// The [[Promise]] of a promise capability that LibWeb created, which is a Promise.
fn promise_object(promise: WebIdlPromise) -> Gc<Promise> {
    promise
        .promise()
        .downcast::<Promise>()
        .expect("the promise of a capability that the bindings create is a Promise")
}

//! What the interfaces implemented in Rust keep for a realm: the objects that a specification has a global object
//! hold, which every object of an interface in the realm of that global returns, and what the bindings ask LibWeb
//! about the realm once.

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, FunctionObject, Gc, GcRefCell, Object, Realm, Trace, Vm,
};

use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;

use crate::bindings::services::web_bindings_wrapper_world;
use crate::event_timing::event_timing::WindowEventTimingStateRef;
use crate::gamepad::navigator_gamepad::NavigatorGamepadRef;
use crate::html::mime_type::MimeType;
use crate::html::plugin::Plugin;
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_timeline::PerformanceTimelineRef;
use crate::web_assembly::tag::Tag;

/// The wrapper world of a realm, Web::Bindings::WrapperWorld, which the realm keeps alive.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct WrapperWorld {
    world: NonNull<c_void>,
    is_main_world: bool,
}

impl WrapperWorld {
    pub(crate) fn is_main_world(self) -> bool {
        self.is_main_world
    }
}

#[derive(Default, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct RealmData {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    wrapper_world: Cell<Option<WrapperWorld>>,
    /// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#count-queuing-strategy-size-function
    pub(crate) count_queuing_strategy_size_function: Cell<Option<Gc<FunctionObject>>>,
    /// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#byte-length-queuing-strategy-size-function
    pub(crate) byte_length_queuing_strategy_size_function: Cell<Option<Gc<FunctionObject>>>,
    /// The NativeError prototypes and constructors of WebAssembly.CompileError, LinkError and RuntimeError,
    /// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#error-objects
    pub(crate) webassembly_error_prototypes: [Cell<Option<Gc<Object>>>; 3],
    pub(crate) webassembly_error_constructors: [Cell<Option<Gc<Object>>>; 3],
    /// The Tag object of the JavaScript exception tag, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#javascript-exception-tag
    pub(crate) webassembly_js_tag: Cell<Option<Ref<Tag>>>,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#performance-timeline
    pub(crate) performance_timeline: Cell<Option<PerformanceTimelineRef>>,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#supportedentrytypes-attribute
    pub(crate) performance_observer_supported_entry_types: Cell<Option<Gc<Object>>>,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#sec-modifications-HTML
    pub(crate) event_timing_state: Cell<Option<WindowEventTimingStateRef>>,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#internal-slots
    pub(crate) navigator_gamepad: Cell<Option<NavigatorGamepadRef>>,
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#pdf-viewer-plugin-objects
    pub(crate) pdf_viewer_plugin_objects: GcRefCell<Vec<Ref<Plugin>>>,
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#pdf-viewer-mime-type-objects
    pub(crate) pdf_viewer_mime_type_objects: GcRefCell<Vec<Ref<MimeType>>>,
}

static REALM_DATA_CLASS: EmbedderClass<RealmData> = EmbedderClass::new("RealmData");

impl EmbedderValue for RealmData {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &REALM_DATA_CLASS;
}

/// The data of the realm, which the first use in a realm creates.
pub(crate) fn realm_data(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Gc<EmbedderCell<RealmData>> {
    if let Some(data) = realm.embedder_data::<RealmData>() {
        return data;
    }
    let data = REALM_DATA_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| RealmData::default());
    realm.set_embedder_data(data);
    data
}

/// The wrapper world of the realm, which LibWeb is asked for once per realm.
pub(crate) fn wrapper_world_of(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> WrapperWorld {
    let data = realm_data(vm, realm);
    if let Some(wrapper_world) = data.wrapper_world.get() {
        return wrapper_world;
    }
    let mut is_main_world = false;
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and LibWeb set its host defined data up before any binding runs in it.
    let world = unsafe { web_bindings_wrapper_world(realm.as_ptr().cast(), &raw mut is_main_world) };
    let wrapper_world = WrapperWorld {
        world: NonNull::new(world).expect("a realm of LibWeb has a wrapper world"),
        is_main_world,
    };
    data.wrapper_world.set(Some(wrapper_world));
    wrapper_world
}

//! The services of LibWeb's C++ bindings that the Rust bindings use, which the bindings generator defines in
//! Bindings/IntrinsicDefinitions.cpp and Bindings/RustBindingsServices.cpp defines by hand.

use core::ffi::c_void;

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// The interface prototype object of the interface in the realm, which the realm's intrinsics create on first use.
    /// The realm and the object are the runtime's cells, and the interface name is a Web::Bindings::InterfaceName of an
    /// interface implemented in Rust.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_ensure_web_prototype(realm: *mut c_void, interface_name: u16) -> *mut c_void;

    /// The interface object of the interface in the realm, likewise.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_ensure_web_constructor(realm: *mut c_void, interface_name: u16) -> *mut c_void;

    /// The iterator prototype object of the interface in the realm, likewise, for an interface with a pair iterator.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_ensure_web_iterator_prototype(realm: *mut c_void, interface_name: u16) -> *mut c_void;

    /// The wrapper world of the realm, a cell that the realm keeps alive, and whether it is the main world of its
    /// agent.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_wrapper_world(realm: *mut c_void, is_main_world: *mut bool) -> *mut c_void;

    /// The wrapper that the world of the realm, which is not a main world, holds for the cell of an object of an
    /// interface implemented in Rust, or null.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_rust_wrapper_for(realm: *mut c_void, cell: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;

    /// Defines the unforgeable attributes of the interface implemented in C++ on the wrapper.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_define_unforgeable_attributes(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        wrapper: *mut c_void,
        interface_name: u16,
    );

    /// Makes `wrapper` the wrapper that the world of its realm, which is not a main world, holds for the cell.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_set_rust_wrapper(realm: *mut c_void, cell: *mut c_void, wrapper: *mut c_void);

    /// Pushes a new element queue onto the custom element reactions stack of the agent of the main thread.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_push_element_queue();

    /// Pops the element queue from that stack and invokes the custom element reactions in it.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_pop_element_queue_and_invoke_reactions();

    /// Whether the global object of the realm is a Window.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_realm_is_window(realm: *mut c_void) -> bool;
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_realm_is_secure_context(realm: *mut c_void) -> bool;

    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_report_an_exception(realm: *mut c_void, exception: u64);

    /// Runs the steps with the context while an execution context of the realm is on the stack, as an
    /// HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext puts it there, with callbacks enabled if `callbacks_enabled`.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_with_temporary_execution_context(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        callbacks_enabled: bool,
        context: *mut c_void,
        steps: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void),
    );

    /// Whether the object is a wrapper of an object that implements the interface, a Web::Bindings::InterfaceName of
    /// an interface that LibWeb implements in C++.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_object_implements_interface(object: *mut c_void, interface_name: u16) -> bool;

    /// The cell of the C++ object that the wrapper wraps.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_cell_of_wrapper(wrapper: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;

    /// Whether the object is the exotic object of a WindowProxy.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_object_is_window_proxy(object: *mut c_void) -> bool;

    /// The object that scripts of the realm see for the WindowProxy whose exotic object this is: that of the
    /// WindowProxy of its browsing context for the wrapper world of the realm, or the object itself if it has none.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_window_proxy_object_in_realm(object: *mut c_void, realm: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;

    /// Runs the extract an origin operation of the object, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#extract-an-origin,
    /// if it is a platform object of an interface implemented in C++ or a WindowProxy, and calls `on_origin` with the
    /// origin, which it lends for the call, if that is not null. Returns whether it called `on_origin`.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_extract_an_origin(
        object: *mut c_void,
        ctx: *mut c_void,
        on_origin: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const liburl_rust::FfiOrigin),
    ) -> bool;

    /// HTML::perform_a_security_check() of the value, with the identifier, which is ASCII, and the
    /// HTML::SecurityCheckType.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_perform_a_security_check(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        platform_object: u64,
        identifier: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
        check_type: u8,
    ) -> libjs_rust::api::RawNativeFunctionResult;

    /// The wrapper in the realm of a new DOMException with the name, which is ASCII, and the message, a borrowed
    /// AK::Utf16String.
    pub(crate) fn web_bindings_create_dom_exception(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        name: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
        message: usize,
    ) -> *mut c_void;
}
