//! The setlike declarations of the interfaces implemented in Rust, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-setlike

use core::cell::RefCell;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    Attribute, ErrorKind, ErrorType, Gc, GcWeak, MarkedVec, Object, PropertyAttributes, PropertyKey, PropertyKind,
    RawNativeFunctionPointer, Realm, Set, SetIterator, ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value, Vm, call,
};

use crate::bindings::CallContext;
use crate::bindings::interface::{
    Interface, SecurityCheckType, define_attribute, define_operation, this_implementation,
};
use crate::bindings::realm_data::{WrapperWorld, wrapper_world_of};

/// The JS collection of an object in each wrapper world that asked for it, as the entries of a collection hold the
/// wrappers of one world. Nothing keeps a collection alive here, so the next use creates it again if it is collected.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct WorldEntries<T: 'static> {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    entries: RefCell<Vec<(WrapperWorld, GcWeak<T>)>>,
}

impl<T> Default for WorldEntries<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            entries: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
        }
    }
}

impl<T> WorldEntries<T> {
    /// The collection of the wrapper world of the call, which `create` makes if there is none.
    pub(crate) fn get_or_create(&self, cx: &CallContext, create: impl FnOnce() -> Gc<T>) -> Gc<T> {
        let wrapper_world = wrapper_world_of(cx.vm(), cx.realm());
        self.entries.borrow_mut().retain(|(_, entries)| entries.get().is_some());
        let existing = self
            .entries
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .find(|(world, _)| *world == wrapper_world)
            .and_then(|(_, entries)| entries.get());
        if let Some(entries) = existing {
            return entries;
        }
        let entries = create();
        self.entries
            .borrow_mut()
            .push((wrapper_world, GcWeak::new(cx.vm().heap(), entries)));
        entries
    }

    /// Forgets the collection of each world.
    pub(crate) fn clear(&self) {
        self.entries.borrow_mut().clear();
    }

    /// Calls back with each live collection, for the caller to update when the object changes. The collections stay
    /// alive through the walk, as updating one can allocate and nothing else holds the rest.
    pub(crate) fn for_each_live(&self, vm: &Vm, mut callback: impl FnMut(Gc<T>)) {
        let live = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        for (_, entries) in self.entries.borrow().iter() {
            if let Some(entries) = entries.get() {
                live.push(entries);
            }
        }
        for entries in live.values().iter() {
            callback(*entries);
        }
    }
}

/// What the implementation of an interface with a setlike declaration implements.
pub(crate) trait Setlike: Interface {
    // https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-set-entries
    fn set_entries(&self, cx: &CallContext) -> Gc<Set>;

    /// The size of the set entries, without creating them and the wrappers they hold.
    fn set_entries_size(&self) -> usize;

    /// Whether the set entries contain the value, which the bindings checked against the value type, without creating
    /// them and the wrappers they hold.
    fn set_entries_contain(&self, value: Value) -> bool;
}

/// What the implementation of an interface with a read-write setlike declaration implements, for the operations that
/// the interface does not declare itself. The value is one that the bindings converted to the value type.
pub(crate) trait WritableSetlike: Setlike {
    fn set_add(&self, cx: &CallContext, value: Value);
    fn set_remove(&self, cx: &CallContext, value: Value) -> bool;
    fn set_clear(&self, cx: &CallContext);
}

/// What the generated bindings of an interface with a setlike declaration define.
pub(crate) trait SetlikeDeclaration: Setlike {
    /// Throws unless the JS value converts to the value type of the declaration.
    fn check_value(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()>;
}

/// Defines the properties that every setlike declaration has, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-setlike
#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "these are the functions of the declaration")]
pub(crate) fn define_setlike_properties(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    prototype: Gc<Object>,
    size: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    entries: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    for_each: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    has: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
    values: RawNativeFunctionPointer,
) {
    define_attribute(vm, realm, prototype, "size", size, None);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "entries", entries, 0);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "keys", values, 0);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "values", values, 0);
    prototype.define_direct_property(
        vm,
        &PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().iterator),
        prototype.get_without_side_effects(vm, &PropertyKey::from_utf8("values")),
        PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE | Attribute::WRITABLE),
    );
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "forEach", for_each, 1);
    define_operation(vm, realm, prototype, "has", has, 1);
}

/// The call context of the realm that a collection of a wrapper world lives in.
pub(crate) fn context_of_set<'vm>(cx: &CallContext<'vm>, set: Gc<Set>) -> CallContext<'vm> {
    CallContext::new(cx.vm(), set.upcast::<Object>().shape().realm())
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-set-size
pub(crate) fn set_size<T: Setlike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "size" and type "getter".
    let (_, implementation, _) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "size", SecurityCheckType::Getter)?;

    // 2. Let set be the set entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    // 3. Return set's size, converted to a JavaScript value.
    // OPTIMIZATION: The implementation knows the size without creating the set entries.
    Ok(Value::from_f64(implementation.set_entries_size() as f64))
}

fn create_set_iterator<T: Setlike>(vm: &Vm, identifier: &str, kind: PropertyKind) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    let (_, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, identifier, SecurityCheckType::Method)?;
    let set = implementation.set_entries(&cx);
    Ok(Value::from_object(
        SetIterator::create(vm, cx.realm(), set, kind).upcast::<Object>(),
    ))
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-set-entries
pub(crate) fn set_iterator_entries<T: Setlike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "entries" and type "method".
    // 2. Let set be the set entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    // 3. Return the result of creating a set iterator from set with kind "key+value".
    create_set_iterator::<T>(vm, "entries", PropertyKind::KeyAndValue)
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-set-values
pub(crate) fn set_iterator_values<T: Setlike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "values" and type "method".
    // 2. Let set be the set entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    // 3. Return the result of creating a set iterator from set with kind "value".
    create_set_iterator::<T>(vm, "values", PropertyKind::Value)
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-set-forEach
pub(crate) fn set_for_each<T: Setlike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "forEach" and type "method".
    let (wrapper, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "forEach", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 2. Let set be the set entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    let set = implementation.set_entries(&cx);

    // 3. Let callbackFn be the first argument passed to the function, or undefined if not supplied.
    // 4. If IsCallable(callbackFn) is false, throw a TypeError.
    let callback = vm.argument(0);
    if !callback.is_function() {
        return vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAFunction, &[&callback]);
    }

    // 5. Let thisArg be the second argument passed to the function, or undefined if not supplied.
    let this_arg = vm.argument(1);

    // 6. For each value of set:
    let iterator = set.begin();
    while !iterator.is_end() {
        // 1. Let jsValue be value converted to a JavaScript value.
        let value = iterator.current();

        // 2. Perform ? Call(callbackFn, thisArg, « jsValue, jsValue, O»).
        call(vm, callback, this_arg, &[value, value, Value::from_object(wrapper)])?;
        iterator.advance();
    }

    // 7. Return undefined.
    Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-set-has
pub(crate) fn set_has<T: SetlikeDeclaration>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "has" and type "method".
    let (_, implementation, _) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "has", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 2. Let set be the set entries of the IDL value that represents a reference to O.
    // 3. Let valueType be the value type specified in the setlike declaration.
    // 4. Let valueArg be the first argument passed to this function, or undefined if not supplied.
    // 5. Let value be valueArg converted to an IDL value of type valueType.
    let value = vm.argument(0);
    T::check_value(vm, value)?;

    // 7. If set contains value, then return true, otherwise return false.
    // OPTIMIZATION: The implementation looks for the value without creating the set entries.
    Ok(Value::from_bool(implementation.set_entries_contain(value)))
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-set-add
pub(crate) fn set_add<T: SetlikeDeclaration + WritableSetlike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "add" and type "method".
    let (wrapper, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "add", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 3. Let valueType be the value type specified in the setlike declaration.
    // 4. Let valueArg be the first argument passed to this function, or undefined if not supplied.
    // 5. Let value be valueArg converted to an IDL value of type valueType.
    let value = vm.argument(0);
    T::check_value(vm, value)?;

    // 7. If set does not contain value, then append value to set.
    implementation.set_add(&cx, value);

    // 8. Return O.
    Ok(Value::from_object(wrapper))
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-set-delete
pub(crate) fn set_delete<T: SetlikeDeclaration + WritableSetlike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "delete" and type "method".
    let (_, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "delete", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 3. Let valueType be the value type specified in the setlike declaration.
    // 4. Let valueArg be the first argument passed to this function, or undefined if not supplied.
    // 5. Let value be valueArg converted to an IDL value of type valueType.
    let value = vm.argument(0);
    T::check_value(vm, value)?;

    // 7. Let retVal be true if set contains value, or else false.
    // 8. Remove value from set.
    // 9. Return retVal.
    Ok(Value::from_bool(implementation.set_remove(&cx, value)))
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#js-set-clear
pub(crate) fn set_clear<T: WritableSetlike>(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let O be the this value, implementation-checked against A with identifier "clear" and type "method".
    let (_, implementation, cx) = this_implementation::<T>(vm, "clear", SecurityCheckType::Method)?;

    // 3. Empty set.
    implementation.set_clear(&cx);

    // 4. Return undefined.
    Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
}

//! What an interface implemented in Rust that is serializable or transferable does in a structured serialization,
//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#serializable-objects and
//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#transferable-objects
//!
//! The algorithms of crate::html::structured_serialize call the steps of such an interface directly through the
//! generated Rust dispatch. Those steps write and read the record of the algorithm.
//! The algorithms run the transfer steps and the transfer-receiving steps themselves, which write and read the Rust
//! data holders of the transfer. Unlike an object of an interface implemented in C++, which is created before its
//! deserialization steps fill it in, an object of an interface implemented in Rust is what its deserialization steps
//! and its transfer-receiving steps return.

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;
use std::collections::VecDeque;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libipc_rust::{Decode, DecodeError, Decoder, Encode};
use libjs_rust::api::{ArrayBuffer, Gc, MarkedVec, Object, Realm, Value, Vm};
use libwebcommon_rust::html::serialization_records::SerializationType;

use crate::bindings::interface::{ConstructedObject, Interface, Ref, implementation_of, wrap};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::html::message_port::{TransferredTransport, TransportHandle};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::cpp::{
    ImageBitmapSharedPixels, SharedPixelBuffers, data_clone_error_from_serialization_error,
};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::reader::StructuredSerializeReader;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::transfer_data_holder::{CarriedChannelEnd, TransferDataHolder, TransferPayload};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::transfer_record::{TransferRecord, TransferRecordRef};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::writer::StructuredSerializeWriter;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::{
    Deserializer, Serializer, decode_serializable_object_header, encode_serializable_object_header,
    structured_deserialize_with_transfer_internal, structured_serialize_with_transfer,
};

/// The record of a structured serialization, which the serialization steps of an object write to, and the serialization
/// that the sub-serializations of the steps run in.
pub(crate) struct SerializationWriter<'a, 'memory> {
    serializer: &'a Serializer<'a, 'a, 'memory>,
}

impl<'a, 'memory> SerializationWriter<'a, 'memory> {
    pub(crate) fn new(serializer: &'a Serializer<'a, 'a, 'memory>) -> Self {
        Self { serializer }
    }

    fn serialized(&self) -> &StructuredSerializeWriter<'memory> {
        self.serializer.serialized()
    }

    /// Sets a field of the serialized form to the sub-serialization of the value,
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#sub-serialization
    pub(crate) fn write_value(&mut self, value: Value) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.serializer.serialize(value)
    }

    /// Writes the record of the shared WebAssembly memory that `id` names, and that `buffer` is a buffer of.
    pub(crate) fn write_shared_web_assembly_memory(&mut self, id: u64, buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.serializer.serialize_shared_web_assembly_memory(id, buffer)
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_u8(&mut self, value: u8) {
        self.serialized().encode_u8(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_i32(&mut self, value: i32) {
        self.serialized().encode_i32(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_u16(&mut self, value: u16) {
        self.serialized().encode_u16(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_u32(&mut self, value: u32) {
        self.serialized().encode_u32(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_u64(&mut self, value: u64) {
        self.serialized().encode_u64(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_f64(&mut self, value: f64) {
        self.serialized().encode_f64(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_bool(&mut self, value: bool) {
        self.serialized().encode_bool(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_i64(&mut self, value: i64) {
        self.serialized().encode_i64(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_optional_u64(&mut self, value: Option<u64>) {
        self.serialized().encode_optional_u64(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_utf16_string(&mut self, string: &Utf16String) {
        self.serialized().encode_utf16_string(string);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_bytes(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        self.serialized().encode_bytes(bytes);
    }

    /// Writes the record of a serializable object in place, as StructuredSerializeInternal writes it, but without
    /// giving the object a position in the memory of the serialization, which a format that predates the
    /// sub-serialization of the object has none for.
    pub(crate) fn write_object_in_place<T: Serializable>(
        &mut self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        object: &T,
        for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        encode_serializable_object_header(self.serialized(), T::INTERFACE_NAME)?;
        object.serialization_steps(cx, self, for_storage)
    }
}

/// The record of a structured deserialization, which the deserialization steps of an object read from, and the
/// deserialization that the sub-deserializations of the steps run in. What it reads that the record does not hold
/// throws a "DataCloneError" DOMException.
pub(crate) struct SerializationReader<'a, 'memory> {
    deserializer: &'a Deserializer<'a, 'a, 'memory>,
}

impl<'a, 'memory> SerializationReader<'a, 'memory> {
    pub(crate) fn new(deserializer: &'a Deserializer<'a, 'a, 'memory>) -> Self {
        Self { deserializer }
    }

    fn serialized(&self) -> &'a StructuredSerializeReader<'a> {
        self.deserializer.serialized()
    }

    /// The value of a field of the serialized form, which is a sub-serialization,
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#sub-deserialization
    pub(crate) fn read_value(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        self.deserializer.deserialize()
    }

    /// The id of the shared WebAssembly memory of a record, which the realm may have the memory of.
    pub(crate) fn read_shared_web_assembly_memory_id(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        self.deserializer.deserialize_agent_cluster()?;
        self.read_u64()
    }

    /// Whether the record is one for storage, rather than for IPC.
    pub(crate) fn is_for_storage(&mut self) -> bool {
        self.serialized().serialization_type() == SerializationType::Storage
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_u8(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<u8> {
        self.serialized().decode_u8()
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_i32(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<i32> {
        self.serialized().decode_i32()
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_u16(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<u16> {
        self.serialized().decode_u16()
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_u32(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        self.serialized().decode_u32()
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_u64(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        self.serialized().decode_u64()
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_f64(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        self.serialized().decode_f64()
    }

    /// Reads what SerializationWriter::write_object_in_place() writes, and returns the new object.
    pub(crate) fn read_object_in_place<T: Serializable>(&mut self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<T>> {
        decode_serializable_object_header(self.serialized(), T::INTERFACE_NAME)?;
        let object = T::deserialization_steps(cx, self)?;
        Ok(object.into_object(cx.vm()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_bool(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        self.serialized().decode_bool()
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_i64(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<i64> {
        self.serialized().decode_i64()
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_optional_u64(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<Option<u64>> {
        self.serialized().decode_optional_u64()
    }

    /// Bytes that the record holds, which it lends for as long as the deserialization runs.
    pub(crate) fn read_borrowed_bytes(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<&'a [u8]> {
        self.serialized().decode_bytes()
    }

    /// A copy of bytes that the record holds. If the copy cannot be allocated, a "DataCloneError" DOMException.
    pub(crate) fn read_bytes(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<u8>> {
        let bytes = self.read_borrowed_bytes()?;
        let mut copy = Vec::new();
        copy.try_reserve_exact(bytes.len()).map_err(|_| {
            data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(
                self.serialized().realm(),
                "Unable to allocate a copy of the bytes",
            )
        })?;
        copy.extend_from_slice(bytes);
        Ok(copy)
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_utf16_string(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        self.serialized().decode_utf16_string()
    }
}

/// An interface that is serializable, [Serializable] in its IDL.
pub(crate) trait Serializable: Interface {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#serialization-steps
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()>;

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#deserialization-steps, which create the object.
    fn deserialization_steps(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationReader,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<impl ConstructedObject<Self> + use<Self>>;
}

/// The data holder of a transferred object, which its transfer steps write to, in the realm of the transfer, which
/// creates what the steps throw.
pub(crate) struct TransferDataWriter<'a> {
    data_holder: &'a TransferDataHolder,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    /// AD-HOC: The shared memory that the transfer gathers the pixels of its ImageBitmaps in, if it has some.
    image_bitmap_pixels: Option<&'a ImageBitmapSharedPixels>,
}

impl<'a> TransferDataWriter<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn new(
        data_holder: &'a TransferDataHolder,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        image_bitmap_pixels: Option<&'a ImageBitmapSharedPixels>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            data_holder,
            realm,
            image_bitmap_pixels,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn realm(&self) -> Gc<Realm> {
        self.realm
    }

    /// The shared pixels as the C ABI of ImageBitmap's C++ code takes them, or null.
    pub(crate) fn image_bitmap_pixels_as_raw(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.image_bitmap_pixels
            .and_then(ImageBitmapSharedPixels::as_raw)
            .map_or(core::ptr::null_mut(), NonNull::as_ptr)
    }

    pub(crate) fn write<T: Encode + ?Sized>(&mut self, value: &T) {
        self.data_holder.encode(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_bool(&mut self, value: bool) {
        self.write(&value);
    }

    /// Writes the records of structured serializations with transfer, as a list.
    pub(crate) fn write_records(&mut self, cx: &CallContext, records: &[TransferRecordRef]) {
        self.data_holder.with_encoder(|encoder| {
            encoder.encode_size(records.len())?;
            for &record in records {
                TransferRecord::encode_into(record, cx.vm(), encoder)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        });
    }

    /// Writes what a MessagePort reaches its peer with, which the data holder takes.
    pub(crate) fn write_transport(&mut self, transport: TransferredTransport) {
        match transport {
            TransferredTransport::Channel(end) => {
                self.write_bool(true);
                self.data_holder.add_channel_end(end);
            }
            TransferredTransport::Socket(handle) => {
                self.write_bool(false);
                self.data_holder.with_encoder(|encoder| handle.encode_into(encoder));
            }
        }
    }

    /// Writes ! StructuredSerializeWithTransfer(value, « value ») as the data holder of value, which is all that the
    /// record holds: its [[Serialized]] is a reference to the transferred value. read_transferred_value() reads it.
    pub(crate) fn write_transferred_value(&mut self, cx: &CallContext, value: Value) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let record = structured_serialize_with_transfer(cx, value, &[value.as_object()])?;
        for holder in record.data_holders.borrow_mut().drain(..) {
            self.data_holder.extend(holder);
        }
        TransferRecord::discard(record);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The data holder of a received object, which its transfer-receiving steps read from, in the realm that the object is
/// created in. What the steps read that the data holder does not hold throws a "DataCloneError" DOMException.
pub(crate) struct TransferDataReader<'a> {
    decoder: Decoder<'a>,
    channel_ends: VecDeque<CarriedChannelEnd>,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    shared_pixels: Option<&'a SharedPixelBuffers<'a>>,
}

impl<'a> TransferDataReader<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn new(payload: &'a mut TransferPayload, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Self {
        Self {
            decoder: Decoder::new(&payload.bytes, core::mem::take(&mut payload.attachments)),
            channel_ends: core::mem::take(&mut payload.channel_ends),
            realm,
            shared_pixels: None,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn with_shared_pixels(
        payload: &'a mut TransferPayload,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        shared_pixels: &'a SharedPixelBuffers<'a>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            shared_pixels: Some(shared_pixels),
            ..Self::new(payload, realm)
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn shared_pixels_as_raw(&self) -> WebIdlResult<*mut c_void> {
        self.shared_pixels
            .and_then(SharedPixelBuffers::as_raw)
            .map(core::ptr::NonNull::as_ptr)
            .ok_or_else(|| data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(self.realm, "Invalid ImageBitmap shared pixels"))
    }

    pub(crate) fn realm(&self) -> Gc<Realm> {
        self.realm
    }

    fn decoded<T>(&mut self, read: impl FnOnce(&mut Decoder<'a>) -> Result<T, DecodeError>) -> WebIdlResult<T> {
        read(&mut self.decoder).map_err(|error| {
            data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(self.realm, &format!("Unable to decode transfer data: {error:?}"))
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn read<T: Decode>(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<T> {
        self.decoded(Decoder::decode)
    }

    /// Reads bytes, which go as their count and then the bytes, as IPC encodes a ByteBuffer.
    pub(crate) fn read_bytes(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<&'a [u8]> {
        self.decoded(|decoder| {
            let size = decoder.decode_size()?;
            decoder.read_bytes(size)
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_bool(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        self.read()
    }

    /// Reads what TransferDataWriter::write_records() writes.
    pub(crate) fn read_records<'vm>(&mut self, vm: &'vm Vm) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, TransferRecordRef>> {
        let records = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        let result = self.decoded(|decoder| {
            let count = decoder.decode_size()?;
            for _ in 0..count {
                records.push(TransferRecord::decode(vm, decoder)?);
            }
            Ok(())
        });
        if let Err(exception) = result {
            for &record in records.values().iter() {
                TransferRecord::discard(record);
            }
            return Err(exception);
        }
        Ok(records)
    }

    /// Reads what TransferDataWriter::write_transport() writes.
    pub(crate) fn read_transport(&mut self) -> WebIdlResult<TransferredTransport> {
        if !self.read::<bool>()? {
            return Ok(TransferredTransport::Socket(self.decoded(TransportHandle::decode)?));
        }
        let end = self.channel_ends.pop_front().ok_or_else(|| {
            data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(self.realm, "Missing channel end in transfer data")
        })?;
        Ok(TransferredTransport::Channel(end.into_end()))
    }

    /// ! StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer(dataHolder, the current Realm).[[Deserialized]] for what
    /// TransferDataWriter::write_transferred_value() wrote: the transferred value, created in the realm.
    pub(crate) fn read_transferred_value(&mut self, cx: &CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        structured_deserialize_with_transfer_internal(cx, self)
    }
}

/// An interface that is transferable, [Transferable] in its IDL.
pub(crate) trait Transferable: Interface {
    /// The [[Detached]] internal slot of the object, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#detached
    fn detached(&self) -> &Cell<bool>;

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#transfer-steps
    fn transfer_steps(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext, data_holder: &mut TransferDataWriter)
    -> WebIdlResult<()>;

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#transfer-receiving-steps, which create the object.
    fn transfer_receiving_steps(cx: &mut CallContext, data_holder: &mut TransferDataReader) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>>;
}

pub(crate) fn serialization_steps<T: Serializable>(
    cx: &CallContext,
    object: Gc<Object>,
    serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
    for_storage: bool,
) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
    let mut cx = CallContext::new(cx.vm(), cx.realm());
    implementation_of::<T>(object)
        .serialization_steps(&mut cx, serialized, for_storage)
        .map_err(|exception| Exception::Thrown(exception.throw(&cx)))
}

pub(crate) fn deserialization_steps<T: Serializable>(
    cx: &CallContext,
    serialized: &mut SerializationReader,
) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    let mut cx = CallContext::new(cx.vm(), cx.realm());
    let object = T::deserialization_steps(&mut cx, serialized)?;
    Ok(Value::from_object(wrap(&cx, object.into_object(cx.vm()))))
}

/// What a CSS value of a context is resolved with besides its canvas: the font of the context, if it has one yet.
/// `FontMetricsSource` of Canvas2DContextBase.cpp mirrors it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct FontMetricsSource {
    /// The Gfx::FontCascadeList of the font, or null for the font that a context starts with.
    cascade: *const c_void,
    /// The computed size of the font in pixels, unrounded, which lengths relative to it scale.
    font_size: f64,
}

impl FontMetricsSource {
    pub(crate) fn of(font: Option<&ResolvedFont>) -> Self {
        match font {
            Some(font) => Self {
                cascade: font.cascade.as_raw(),
                font_size: font.font_size,
            },
            None => Self {
                cascade: core::ptr::null(),
                font_size: 0.0,
            },
        }
    }
}

/// `ResolvedFont` of Canvas2DContextBase.cpp.

    cascade: *const c_void,
    environment_generation: u64,
    font_size: f64,
    /// An AK::Utf16String that the caller takes over.
    serialized: usize,
}

            text_rendering: state.text_rendering,
        }
    }
}

/// A CSS::StyleValue of LibWeb, one reference to which the value owns.
pub(crate) struct StyleValue(NonNull<c_void>);

impl StyleValue {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `style_value` is a CSS::StyleValue with a reference that the value takes over, or null.
    unsafe fn adopt(style_value: *const c_void) -> Option<Self> {
        NonNull::new(style_value.cast_mut()).map(Self)
    }
}

impl Clone for StyleValue {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The value owns a reference to the style value, so it is live.
        unsafe { web_canvas_2d_style_value_ref(self.0.as_ptr()) };
        Self(self.0)
    }
}

impl Drop for StyleValue {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: The value owns a reference to the style value.
        unsafe { web_canvas_2d_style_value_unref(self.0.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct Canvas {
    /// The cell of the canvas, which the context keeps alive through a slot of its own.
    pub(crate) cell: NonNull<c_void>,
    pub(crate) host: NonNull<c_void>,
    pub(crate) is_offscreen: bool,
}

// SAFETY (of every call below): The context that holds the canvas keeps its cell alive, and the host is the same
// object. Strings are lent for the call, and the style values are live.
impl Canvas {
    pub(crate) fn did_change_content(self) {
        unsafe { web_canvas_2d_canvas_did_change_content(self.host.as_ptr()) };
    }

    pub(crate) fn did_create_backing_storage(self) {
        unsafe { web_canvas_2d_canvas_did_create_backing_storage(self.host.as_ptr()) };
    }

    /// A transport to a new context in the Compositor, if the page of the canvas has a Compositor.
    pub(crate) fn create_transport(self) -> Option<CompositorTransport> {
        let mut transport = TransportAbi::default();
        // SAFETY: LibWeb hands over the transport where it answers true.
        unsafe { web_canvas_2d_canvas_create_transport(self.host.as_ptr(), &raw mut transport) }
            .then(|| unsafe { CompositorTransport::adopt(transport) })
    }

    pub(crate) fn wrapper(self, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> CppInterface {
        let wrapper =
            unsafe { web_canvas_2d_canvas_wrapper(self.cell.as_ptr(), self.is_offscreen, realm.as_ptr().cast()) };
        let wrapper = NonNull::new(wrapper.cast::<Object>()).expect("LibWeb returns the wrapper of the canvas");
        // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live wrapper of an HTMLCanvasElement or an OffscreenCanvas.
        unsafe { CppInterface::from_wrapper(Gc::from_non_null(wrapper)) }
    }

    /// The realm of the relevant global object of the canvas, once that global object has a wrapper.
    pub(crate) fn relevant_realm(self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        let realm = unsafe { web_canvas_2d_canvas_relevant_realm(self.host.as_ptr()) };
        // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live realm, or null.
        NonNull::new(realm.cast::<Realm>()).map(|realm| unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(realm) })
    }

    /// The generation of the fonts that the canvas can use, which changes when a font loads.
    pub(crate) fn font_environment_generation(self) -> u64 {
        unsafe { web_canvas_2d_canvas_font_environment_generation(self.host.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// Whether the directionality of a canvas element, or the inherited direction of an OffscreenCanvas, is 'rtl'.
    pub(crate) fn directionality_is_rtl(self) -> bool {
        unsafe { web_canvas_2d_canvas_directionality_is_rtl(self.cell.as_ptr(), self.is_offscreen) }
    }

    /// The font that a value of the font attribute describes, resolved against the canvas, unless the value is not a
    /// CSS font.
    pub(crate) fn resolve_font(self, font: &Utf16String, font_selection: FontSelection) -> Option<ResolvedFont> {
        let mut resolved = ResolvedFontAbi {
            cascade: core::ptr::null(),
            environment_generation: 0,
            font_size: 0.0,
            serialized: 0,
        };
        let is_font = unsafe {
            web_canvas_2d_canvas_resolve_font(
                self.cell.as_ptr(),
                self.is_offscreen,
                font.raw_identity(),
                font_selection,
                &raw mut resolved,
            )
        };
        if !is_font {
            return None;
        }
        Some(ResolvedFont {
            // SAFETY: LibWeb hands over a reference to the cascade.
            cascade: unsafe { FontCascadeListHandle::adopt(resolved.cascade) },
            environment_generation: resolved.environment_generation,
            font_size: resolved.font_size,
            // SAFETY: LibWeb hands over the string.
            serialized: unsafe { Utf16String::from_raw_owned(resolved.serialized) },
        })
    }

    /// The used color of a parsed CSS color, resolved against the canvas, in sRGB and in the color space.
    pub(crate) fn resolve_color(
        self,
        color: &StyleValue,
        font: FontMetricsSource,
        color_space: PredefinedColorSpace,
    ) -> CanvasColor {
        let mut srgb = Color::default();
        let mut in_color_space = Color::default();
        unsafe {
            web_canvas_2d_canvas_resolve_color(
                self.host.as_ptr(),
                color.0.as_ptr(),
                font,
                color_space.into(),
                &raw mut srgb,
                &raw mut in_color_space,
            );
        };
        CanvasColor { srgb, in_color_space }
    }

    /// A parsed CSS length in CSS pixels, resolved against the canvas.
    pub(crate) fn resolve_length(self, length: &StyleValue, font: FontMetricsSource) -> f32 {
        unsafe { web_canvas_2d_canvas_resolve_length(self.host.as_ptr(), length.0.as_ptr(), font) }
    }

    /// The functions of a <filter-value-list>, with their lengths and colors resolved against the canvas, unless the
    /// value is not one.
    pub(crate) fn parse_filter(self, filter: &Utf16String, font: FontMetricsSource) -> Option<Vec<FfiFilterFunction>> {
        unsafe extern "C" fn append_function(functions: *mut c_void, function: *const FfiFilterFunction) {
            // SAFETY: The functions are the vector below, and LibWeb lends the function for the call.
            unsafe { (*functions.cast::<Vec<FfiFilterFunction>>()).push(*function) };
        }
        let mut functions = Vec::new();
        let is_filter = unsafe {
            web_canvas_2d_canvas_parse_filter(
                self.host.as_ptr(),
                filter.raw_identity(),
                font,
                (&raw mut functions).cast(),
                append_function,
            )
        };
        is_filter.then_some(functions)
    }
}

/// A CSS <color>, parsed without a canvas to resolve it against, unless the string is not one.
pub(crate) fn parse_color(color: &Utf16String) -> Option<StyleValue> {
    // SAFETY: The string is lent for the call, and LibWeb hands over a reference to the style value, or null.
    unsafe { StyleValue::adopt(web_canvas_2d_parse_color(color.raw_identity())) }
}

/// A CSS <length>, parsed without a canvas to resolve it against, and its serialization, unless the string is not
/// one.
pub(crate) fn parse_length(length: &Utf16String) -> Option<(StyleValue, Utf16String)> {
    let mut serialized = 0;
    // SAFETY: The string is lent for the call, and LibWeb hands over a reference to the style value, or null.
    let style_value =
        unsafe { StyleValue::adopt(web_canvas_2d_parse_length(length.raw_identity(), &raw mut serialized)) }?;
    // SAFETY: LibWeb hands over the serialization with the style value.
    Some((style_value, unsafe { Utf16String::from_raw_owned(serialized) }))
}

/// A frame of a copy of `height` rows of `width` RGBA8888 pixels that are unpremultiplied, `pitch` bytes apart and in
/// the color space, or None if there is no memory for it.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The rows must be readable, and no script may change them during the call.
pub(crate) unsafe fn image_frame_from_pixels(
    first_row: NonNull<u8>,
    pitch: usize,
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    color_space: ColorSpace,
) -> Option<ImageFrameHandle> {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes readable rows.
    let frame = unsafe { web_canvas_2d_image_frame_from_pixels(first_row.as_ptr(), pitch, width, height, color_space) };
    // SAFETY: LibWeb hands over a frame that it allocated with new, or null.
    (!frame.is_null()).then(|| unsafe { ImageFrameHandle::adopt(frame) })
}

// SAFETY (of every call below): The wrapper is live and of the interface that the kind names.
impl CanvasImageSourceKind {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#check-the-usability-of-the-image-argument
    pub(crate) fn check_usability(self, source: CppInterface) -> Usability {
        let mut message = 0;
        let usability =
            unsafe { web_canvas_2d_check_usability_of_image(source.wrapper().as_ptr().cast(), self, &raw mut message) };
        match usability {
            USABILITY_GOOD => Usability::Good,
            USABILITY_BAD => Usability::Bad,
            // SAFETY: LibWeb hands over the message of the exception.
            USABILITY_INVALID_STATE => Usability::InvalidState(unsafe { Utf16String::from_raw_owned(message) }),
            unknown => unreachable!("LibWeb returned {unknown} for the usability of an image"),
        }
    }

    /// The width and the height of the image, as the operations that do not take its size use them. An image without a
    /// natural size is sized against the default object size, the size of the canvas it is drawn into.
    pub(crate) fn size(self, source: CppInterface, default_object_size: IntSize) -> (i32, i32) {
        let (mut width, mut height) = (0, 0);
        unsafe {
            web_canvas_2d_image_source_size(
                source.wrapper().as_ptr().cast(),
                self,
                default_object_size.width,
                default_object_size.height,
                &raw mut width,
                &raw mut height,
            );
        }
        (width, height)
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#the-image-argument-is-not-origin-clean
    pub(crate) fn is_not_origin_clean(self, source: CppInterface) -> bool {
        unsafe { web_canvas_2d_image_is_not_origin_clean(source.wrapper().as_ptr().cast(), self) }
    }

    /// The id of the canvas that a canvas or an OffscreenCanvas draws into, readied to be drawn, and whether a 2D
    /// context draws into it, if it is drawn by its id.
    pub(crate) fn canvas_id(self, source: CppInterface) -> Option<(u64, bool)> {
        let (mut canvas_id, mut source_is_2d) = (0, false);
        let has_id = unsafe {
            web_canvas_2d_image_source_canvas_id(
                source.wrapper().as_ptr().cast(),
                self,
                &raw mut canvas_id,
                &raw mut source_is_2d,
            )
        };
        has_id.then_some((canvas_id, source_is_2d))
    }

    /// The frame of an image or a canvas, if it has one. This can read a canvas back, which flushes the commands of
    /// every canvas.
    pub(crate) fn frame(self, source: CppInterface) -> Option<ImageFrameHandle> {
        self.frame_rasterized_at(source, 0, 0).map(|(frame, _)| frame)
    }

    /// The frame of an image or a canvas, as frame() returns it, except that a vector image is rasterized at the
    /// given size if it is not empty. Also returns whether it was.
    pub(crate) fn frame_rasterized_at(
        self,
        source: CppInterface,
        raster_width: i32,
        raster_height: i32,
    ) -> Option<(ImageFrameHandle, bool)> {
        let mut rasterized = false;
        let frame = unsafe {
            web_canvas_2d_image_source_frame(
                source.wrapper().as_ptr().cast(),
                self,
                raster_width,
                raster_height,
                &raw mut rasterized,
            )
        };
        // SAFETY: LibWeb hands over a frame that it allocated with new, or null.
        (!frame.is_null()).then(|| (unsafe { ImageFrameHandle::adopt(frame) }, rasterized))
    }
}

/// The frame of the video that its element shows, if it shows one.
pub(crate) fn capture_video_frame(video: CppInterface) -> Option<CapturedVideoFrame> {
    let mut frame = CapturedVideoFrameAbi {
        hold: core::ptr::null_mut(),
        sink_handle: 0,
        generation: 0,
    };
    // SAFETY: The wrapper is a live HTMLVideoElement, and LibWeb hands over a reference to the hold.
    if !unsafe { web_canvas_2d_capture_video_frame(video.wrapper().as_ptr().cast(), &raw mut frame) } {
        return None;
    }
    let hold = NonNull::new(frame.hold).expect("LibWeb passes the hold of the frame");
    Some(CapturedVideoFrame {
        // SAFETY: LibWeb handed over a reference to the hold.
        hold: unsafe { VideoFrameHold::adopt(hold) },
        sink_handle: frame.sink_handle,
        generation: frame.generation,
    })
}

/// A transport to a new context in the Compositor of the page of the video, if the page has a Compositor.
pub(crate) fn video_transport(video: CppInterface) -> Option<CompositorTransport> {
    let mut transport = TransportAbi::default();
    // SAFETY: The wrapper is a live HTMLVideoElement, and LibWeb hands over the transport where it answers true.
    unsafe { web_canvas_2d_video_transport(video.wrapper().as_ptr().cast(), &raw mut transport) }
        .then(|| unsafe { CompositorTransport::adopt(transport) })
}

//! The state that CanvasRenderingContext2D and OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D share: the drawing state, the current
//! default path, and the backing storage, which is a context in the Compositor that the context records commands for.

use core::cell::{Cell, Ref as CellRef, RefCell, RefMut};
use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::ops::Deref;

use ak::Utf16String;
use ak::math;
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::canvas_2d::{Compositing, Paint, Stroke};
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::canvas_2d_recorder::{AlphaType, ColorSpace, Recorder};
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::commands::{Canvas2DShadow, CanvasId};
use libgfx_rust::image_frame::ImageFrameHandle;
use libgfx_rust::path::Path;
use libgfx_rust::{AffineTransform, Color, CompositingAndBlendingOperator, FloatRect, IntRect, IntSize, WindingRule};
use libjs_rust::api::{DeferGc, ForeignCellSlot, Gc, GcRefCell, GcRefMut, Realm, Trace, Visitor, Vm};

pub(crate) type CanvasRecorder = Recorder<CompositorTransport>;

/// What tells the two kinds of 2D context apart: the canvas that each draws for, an HTMLCanvasElement or an
/// OffscreenCanvas. Everything else they share.
pub(crate) trait CanvasKind: 'static {}

/// The kind of a CanvasRenderingContext2D.
pub(crate) struct OnScreen;
/// The kind of an OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D.
pub(crate) struct Offscreen;

impl CanvasKind for OnScreen {}
impl CanvasKind for Offscreen {}

/// The attributes and operations that CanvasRenderingContext2D and OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D share are
/// implemented once, for every `K`.
pub(crate) struct RenderingContext2D<K: CanvasKind> {
    state: ContextState,
    kind: PhantomData<K>,
}

impl<K: CanvasKind> RenderingContext2D<K> {
    pub(crate) fn new(_: &DeferGc<'_>, state: ContextState) -> Self {
        Self {
            state,
            kind: PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

impl<K: CanvasKind> Deref for RenderingContext2D<K> {
    type Target = ContextState;

    fn deref(&self) -> &ContextState {
        &self.state
    }
}

// SAFETY: The state holds every cell that a context can reach.
unsafe impl<K: CanvasKind> Trace for RenderingContext2D<K> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.state.trace(visitor);
    }
}

impl<K: CanvasKind> Wrappable for RenderingContext2D<K> {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        self.state.canvas.relevant_realm()
    }

    const OWNS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY: bool = true;

    fn external_memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.state.external_memory_size()
    }
}

/// The backing storage of a context: the recorder of the commands of its context in the Compositor. Dropping it
/// destroys that context.
struct BackingStorage {
    recorder: CanvasRecorder,
}

impl Drop for BackingStorage {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // Flush the shared stream before destroying the context: it may still hold commands targeting this canvas, and
        // DrawCanvas commands from other canvases referencing it, which must replay while it is alive.
        self.recorder.flush();
        self.recorder.destroy_context();
    }
}

/// A readback of the pixels of a rectangle of the canvas.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct CachedReadback {
    pixels: ImageFrameHandle,
    rect: IntRect,
    alpha_type: AlphaType,
    color_space: ColorSpace,
}

/// A color that a context was given as a string. Context-independent simple colors store a resolved color. Other
/// colors store their parsed style value so they can be resolved against the current canvas context on every use. An
/// entry with neither is a parse failure.
struct ColorCacheEntry {
    input: Utf16String,
    parsed_value: Option<StyleValue>,
    resolved_color: Option<CanvasColor>,
}

const MAX_COLOR_CACHE_SIZE: usize = 8;
const MAX_COLOR_CACHE_INPUT_LENGTH: usize = 128;

/// What a context is created with.
pub(crate) struct ContextParameters {
    pub(crate) canvas: Canvas,
    pub(crate) context_attributes: CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings,
    pub(crate) size: IntSize,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct ContextState {
    canvas_cell: ForeignCellSlot,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    canvas: Canvas,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) context_attributes: CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    size: Cell<IntSize>,
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#concept-canvas-origin-clean
    #[gc(untraced)]
    origin_clean: Cell<bool>,
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#concept-canvas-context-lost
    #[gc(untraced)]
    context_lost: Cell<bool>,
    /// The drawing state stack, with the current drawing state last.
    states: GcRefCell<Vec<DrawingState>>,
    /// The current default path, in the coordinates of the current transformation matrix.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    path: RefCell<Path>,
    /// The matrix in whose coordinates the current default path is.
    ///
    /// NB: This is the current transformation matrix while that matrix is invertible. A path cannot be kept in the
    ///     coordinates of a matrix that is not invertible, so it stays in those of the last matrix that was.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    path_transform: Cell<AffineTransform>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    backing_storage: RefCell<Option<BackingStorage>>,
    /// OPTIMIZATION: A readback requires a synchronous IPC to the Compositor, so its pixels are reused while no
    /// drawing command has changed them.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    cached_readback: RefCell<Option<CachedReadback>>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    color_cache: RefCell<Vec<ColorCacheEntry>>,
}

fn empty_path() -> Path {
    Path::new()
}

/// The paint of a draw with the style in a context of the color space, with the image of a pattern added to the stream
/// of the recorder.
pub(crate) fn paint_of<'a>(
    recorder: &CanvasRecorder,
    style: &'a FillOrStrokeStyle,
    color_space: PredefinedColorSpace,
) -> Paint<'a> {
    match style {
        FillOrStrokeStyle::Color(color) => Paint::Color(color.in_color_space),
        // SAFETY: Nothing adds a stop to the gradient while the recorder records the paint.
        FillOrStrokeStyle::Gradient(gradient) => unsafe { gradient.paint_unguarded(color_space) },
        FillOrStrokeStyle::Pattern(pattern) => Paint::Pattern {
            image: pattern.image().map(|frame| recorder.add_image_frame(frame)),
            repetition: pattern.repetition(),
            transform: pattern.transform(),
        },
    }
}

impl ContextState {
    pub(crate) fn new(_: &DeferGc<'_>, parameters: ContextParameters) -> Self {
        let canvas_cell = ForeignCellSlot::empty();
        // SAFETY: The canvas is a live cell of the heap that the runtime allocates from.
        unsafe { canvas_cell.set(Some(parameters.canvas.cell)) };
        Self {
            canvas_cell,
            canvas: parameters.canvas,
            context_attributes: parameters.context_attributes,
            size: Cell::new(parameters.size),
            origin_clean: Cell::new(true),
            context_lost: Cell::new(false),
            states: GcRefCell::new(vec![DrawingState::default()]),
            path: RefCell::new(empty_path()),
            path_transform: Cell::new(AffineTransform::identity()),
            backing_storage: RefCell::new(None),
            cached_readback: RefCell::new(None),
            color_cache: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
        }
    }

    /// The canvas, which the canvas attribute returns.
    pub(crate) fn canvas_handle(&self) -> Canvas {
        self.canvas
    }

    pub(crate) fn size(&self) -> IntSize {
        self.size.get()
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#concept-canvas-origin-clean
    pub(crate) fn origin_clean(&self) -> bool {
        self.origin_clean.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_origin_clean(&self, origin_clean: bool) {
        self.origin_clean.set(origin_clean);
    }

    pub(crate) fn context_is_lost(&self) -> bool {
        self.context_lost.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_context_lost(&self, context_lost: bool) {
        self.context_lost.set(context_lost);
    }

    /// The current drawing state, which nothing may change while the borrow lasts.
    pub(crate) fn drawing_state(&self) -> CellRef<'_, DrawingState> {
        CellRef::map(self.states.borrow(), |states| {
            states.last().expect("a context has a current drawing state")
        })
    }

    /// The current drawing state, to change it. Nothing may run script while the borrow lasts.
    pub(crate) fn drawing_state_mut<'a>(&'a self, vm: &'a Vm) -> GcRefMut<'a, DrawingState> {
        GcRefMut::map(self.states.borrow_mut(vm), |states| {
            states.last_mut().expect("a context has a current drawing state")
        })
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-save
    pub(crate) fn push_drawing_state(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        let mut states = self.states.borrow_mut(vm);
        let current = states.last().expect("a context has a current drawing state").clone();
        states.push(current);
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-restore
    pub(crate) fn pop_drawing_state(&self, vm: &Vm) -> bool {
        let mut states = self.states.borrow_mut(vm);
        if states.len() == 1 {
            return false;
        }
        states.pop();
        true
    }

    /// The current default path, which nothing may change while the borrow lasts.
    pub(crate) fn path(&self) -> CellRef<'_, Path> {
        self.path.borrow()
    }

    pub(crate) fn path_mut(&self) -> RefMut<'_, Path> {
        self.path.borrow_mut()
    }

    /// Empties the list of subpaths of the current default path.
    pub(crate) fn clear_path(&self) {
        self.path.replace(empty_path());
    }

    /// The matrix in whose coordinates the current default path is.
    pub(crate) fn path_transform(&self) -> AffineTransform {
        self.path_transform.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_path_transform(&self, transform: AffineTransform) {
        self.path_transform.set(transform);
    }

    /// Transforms every point of the current default path.
    pub(crate) fn transform_path(&self, transform: AffineTransform) {
        let transformed = self.path.borrow().copy_transformed(transform.values);
        self.path.replace(transformed);
    }

    fn external_memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        // NB: LibGC asks while it sweeps, when nothing borrows these mutably.
        let mut size = self
            .cached_readback
            .try_borrow()
            .ok()
            .and_then(|readback| readback.as_ref().map(|readback| readback.pixels.size_in_bytes()))
            .unwrap_or(0);
        let has_backing_storage = self
            .backing_storage
            .try_borrow()
            .is_ok_and(|backing_storage| backing_storage.is_some());
        if !has_backing_storage {
            return size;
        }
        let surface_size = self.size.get();
        if surface_size.width <= 0 || surface_size.height <= 0 {
            return size;
        }
        let pixel_size = usize::try_from(surface_size.width)
            .ok()
            .zip(usize::try_from(surface_size.height).ok())
            .and_then(|(width, height)| width.checked_mul(height))
            .and_then(|pixels| pixels.checked_mul(4));
        let Some(pixel_size) = pixel_size else {
            return usize::MAX;
        };
        size = size.saturating_add(pixel_size);
        size
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#concept-canvas-alpha
    pub(crate) fn clear_color(&self) -> Color {
        if self.context_attributes.alpha {
            Color::TRANSPARENT
        } else {
            Color::from_rgb(0, 0, 0)
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn has_backing_storage(&self) -> bool {
        self.backing_storage.borrow().is_some()
    }

    fn ensure_remote_canvas_context(&self) -> bool {
        if self.has_backing_storage() {
            return true;
        }
        let Some(transport) = self.canvas.create_transport() else {
            return false;
        };
        // FIXME: implement context attribute .color_type
        // FIXME: implement context attribute .desynchronized
        let recorder = Recorder::new(transport);
        if !recorder.create_context(
            self.size.get(),
            self.context_attributes.alpha,
            self.context_attributes.will_read_frequently,
            self.context_attributes.color_space.into(),
        ) {
            return false;
        }
        self.backing_storage.replace(Some(BackingStorage { recorder }));
        true
    }

    pub(crate) fn ensure_backing_storage(&self) {
        let size = self.size.get();
        if self.has_backing_storage() || size.width <= 0 || size.height <= 0 {
            return;
        }
        if !self.ensure_remote_canvas_context() {
            return;
        }
        self.canvas.did_create_backing_storage();
    }

    pub(crate) fn discard_backing_storage(&self) {
        self.cached_readback.replace(None);
        let backing_storage = self.backing_storage.take();
        drop(backing_storage);
    }

    /// Readies the recorder of the canvas to record, which it is unless the context is lost or the canvas has no
    /// backing storage. As the steps of a draw call it before each command they record.
    pub(crate) fn recorder_is_ready(&self) -> bool {
        if self.context_lost.get() {
            return false;
        }
        self.ensure_backing_storage();
        let backing_storage = self.backing_storage.borrow();
        let Some(backing_storage) = backing_storage.as_ref() else {
            return false;
        };
        backing_storage.recorder.prepare_to_record();
        true
    }

    /// Records with the recorder, which the caller has readied.
    pub(crate) fn record<R>(&self, record: impl FnOnce(&mut CanvasRecorder) -> R) -> R {
        let mut backing_storage = self.backing_storage.borrow_mut();
        let backing_storage = backing_storage
            .as_mut()
            .expect("the canvas has backing storage while the recorder is ready");
        record(&mut backing_storage.recorder)
    }

    /// Readies the recorder and records with it, unless the canvas cannot draw.
    pub(crate) fn record_if_ready(&self, record: impl FnOnce(&mut CanvasRecorder)) -> bool {
        if !self.recorder_is_ready() {
            return false;
        }
        self.record(record);
        true
    }

    pub(crate) fn did_draw(&self) {
        self.cached_readback.replace(None);
        // FIXME: Make use of the rectangle that changed to reduce the invalidated area when possible.
        self.canvas.did_change_content();
    }

    /// The pixels of the rectangle of the canvas, read back from the Compositor and converted to the color space.
    /// Unpremultiplied pixels come back as RGBA8888, and premultiplied pixels as BGRA8888.
    pub(crate) fn read_pixels(
        &self,
        rect: IntRect,
        alpha_type: AlphaType,
        color_space: ColorSpace,
    ) -> Option<ImageFrameHandle> {
        if !self.has_backing_storage() {
            return None;
        }
        if let Some(readback) = self.cached_readback.borrow().as_ref()
            && readback.rect == rect
            && readback.alpha_type == alpha_type
            && readback.color_space == color_space
        {
            return Some(readback.pixels.clone());
        }
        let pixels = {
            let backing_storage = self.backing_storage.borrow();
            let recorder = &backing_storage
                .as_ref()
                .expect("the canvas has backing storage")
                .recorder;
            recorder.flush();
            recorder.read_back_pixels(rect, alpha_type, color_space)
        };
        if let Some(pixels) = &pixels {
            self.cached_readback.replace(Some(CachedReadback {
                pixels: pixels.clone(),
                rect,
                alpha_type,
                color_space,
            }));
        }
        pixels
    }

    pub(crate) fn drop_cached_readback(&self) {
        self.cached_readback.replace(None);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_size(&self, size: IntSize) {
        if self.size.get() == size {
            return;
        }
        self.size.set(size);
        self.discard_backing_storage();
    }

    pub(crate) fn prepare_for_compositing(&self) {
        if let Some(backing_storage) = self.backing_storage.borrow().as_ref() {
            backing_storage.recorder.present();
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn canvas_id(&self) -> Option<CanvasId> {
        self.backing_storage
            .borrow()
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|backing_storage| backing_storage.recorder.canvas_id())
    }

    fn full_rect(&self) -> FloatRect {
        let size = self.size.get();
        #[allow(
            clippy::cast_precision_loss,
            reason = "the rectangle is in floats, as the C++ had it"
        )]
        FloatRect::new(0.0, 0.0, size.width as f32, size.height as f32)
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#reset-the-rendering-context-to-its-default-state
    pub(crate) fn reset_to_default_state(&self) {
        let has_recorder = self.has_backing_storage() && self.recorder_is_ready();

        // 1. Clear canvas's bitmap to transparent black.
        // NB: The clear is recorded after the reset of the recorder, which happens in step 4. The recorded clear is
        //     then not under the transformation matrix and the clipping region of the drawing state that is reset,
        //     so it clears the whole bitmap.
        if has_recorder {
            let rect = self.full_rect();
            let color = self.clear_color();
            self.record(|recorder| {
                recorder.reset();
                recorder.clear_rect(rect, color);
            });
        }

        // 2. Empty the list of subpaths in the context's current default path.
        self.clear_path();

        // 3. Clear the context's drawing state stack.
        // 4. Reset everything that drawing state consists of to their initial values.
        self.states.replace(vec![DrawingState::default()]);
        self.path_transform.set(AffineTransform::identity());

        if has_recorder {
            self.did_draw();
        }
    }

    /// Clears the bitmap of an OffscreenCanvas when transferToImageBitmap() takes it.
    pub(crate) fn replace_bitmap_with_cleared_bitmap(&self) {
        self.cached_readback.replace(None);
        // NB: The new bitmap is origin-clean, but the fill and stroke styles only taint the context when they are set.
        //     A pattern that is not origin-clean and is still a style of the context, or of a state on the stack,
        //     could then draw onto a clean bitmap, so the flag stays unset while one is.
        let holds_a_tainted_style = self
            .states
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .any(|state| state.fill_style.is_not_origin_clean() || state.stroke_style.is_not_origin_clean());
        self.origin_clean.set(!holds_a_tainted_style);
        if !self.has_backing_storage() {
            return;
        }
        let color = self.clear_color();
        if self.record_if_ready(|recorder| recorder.clear_canvas(color)) {
            self.did_draw();
        }
    }

    /// Sets the transformation matrix of the recorder to the current one.
    pub(crate) fn flush_transform(&self) {
        let transform = self.drawing_state().transform;
        self.record_if_ready(|recorder| recorder.set_transform(transform));
    }

    /// What the font of the current drawing state is resolved with, for the CSS values that are resolved against the
    /// canvas.
    pub(crate) fn font_metrics_source(&self) -> FontMetricsSource {
        FontMetricsSource::of(self.drawing_state().font.as_ref())
    }

    /// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/#parse-a-css-color-value
    /// NB: The color is resolved in sRGB and in the color space of the context.
    pub(crate) fn parse_a_css_color_value(&self, value: &Utf16String) -> Option<CanvasColor> {
        // To parse a CSS <color> value, given a string input, and an optional context element element:

        // 1. Parse input as a <color>. If the result is failure, return failure; otherwise, let color be the result.
        let input_is_cacheable = value.length_in_code_units() <= MAX_COLOR_CACHE_INPUT_LENGTH;
        let mut cached = None;
        if input_is_cacheable {
            let mut color_cache = self.color_cache.borrow_mut();
            if let Some(index) = color_cache.iter().position(|entry| entry.input == *value) {
                let entry = color_cache.remove(index);
                cached = Some((entry.parsed_value.clone(), entry.resolved_color));
                color_cache.push(entry);
            }
        }

        let (color, resolved_color) = match cached {
            Some(cached) => cached,
            None => {
                let resolved_color = match value.as_units() {
                    ak::Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units) => libweb_rust::parse_simple_color_ascii(units),
                    ak::Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(units) => libweb_rust::parse_simple_color_utf16(
                        &units.iter().map(|&unit| u16::from(unit)).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
                    ),
                    ak::Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => libweb_rust::parse_simple_color_utf16(units),
                }
                .map(|srgb| {
                    let color_space = self.context_attributes.color_space as u8;
                    let [red, green, blue, alpha] =
                        libweb_rust::srgb_color_in_predefined_color_space(srgb, color_space);
                    let [srgb_red, srgb_green, srgb_blue, srgb_alpha] = srgb;
                    CanvasColor {
                        srgb: Color::from_rgba(srgb_red, srgb_green, srgb_blue, srgb_alpha),
                        in_color_space: Color::from_rgba(red, green, blue, alpha),
                    }
                });
                let color = if resolved_color.is_none() {
                    parse_color(value)
                } else {
                    None
                };
                if input_is_cacheable {
                    let mut color_cache = self.color_cache.borrow_mut();
                    if color_cache.len() == MAX_COLOR_CACHE_SIZE {
                        color_cache.remove(0);
                    }
                    color_cache.push(ColorCacheEntry {
                        input: value.clone(),
                        parsed_value: color.clone(),
                        resolved_color,
                    });
                }
                (color, resolved_color)
            }
        };

        if resolved_color.is_some() {
            return resolved_color;
        }
        let color = color?;

        // 2. Let used color be the result of resolving color to a used color. If the value of other properties on the
        //    element a <color> is on is required to do the resolution (such as resolving a currentcolor or system
        //    color), use element if it was passed, or the initial values of the properties if not.
        // AD-HOC: The spec tells us to use the element's properties as context but doesn't tell us how to resolve other
        //         context dependent values (e.g. viewport relative lengths). This also differs from how font-relative
        //         lengths are absolutized (i.e. using the canvas' font rather than the element's) in other canvas values
        //         (e.g. letterSpacing) so we instead use a computation context based on the drawing state. See
        //         https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12505.
        let used_color =
            self.canvas
                .resolve_color(&color, self.font_metrics_source(), self.context_attributes.color_space);

        // 3. Return used color.
        Some(used_color)
    }

    /// Sets the font of the current drawing state, unless the value is not a CSS font.
    pub(crate) fn assign_font(&self, vm: &Vm, font: &Utf16String) {
        let font_selection = FontSelection::of(&self.drawing_state());
        if let Some(font) = self.canvas.resolve_font(font, font_selection) {
            self.drawing_state_mut(vm).font = Some(font);
        }
    }

    /// Whether the direction of text is 'rtl', as step 7 of the text preparation algorithm determines it,
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#text-preparation-algorithm
    pub(crate) fn direction_is_rtl(&self) -> bool {
        match self.drawing_state().direction {
            // If the target object's direction attribute has the value "ltr": Let direction be 'ltr'.
            CanvasDirection::Ltr => false,
            // If the target object's direction attribute has the value "rtl": Let direction be 'rtl'.
            CanvasDirection::Rtl => true,
            // If the target object's direction attribute has the value "inherit":
            // 1. Let sourceObject be object's font style source object.
            // 2. If sourceObject is a canvas element, then let direction be sourceObject's directionality.
            // 3. Otherwise:
            //    1. Assert: sourceObject is an OffscreenCanvas object.
            //    2. Let direction be sourceObject's inherited direction.
            CanvasDirection::Inherit => self.canvas.directionality_is_rtl(),
        }
    }

    /// Resolves the font of the current drawing state again, after a change to the text drawing styles that select
    /// its fonts.
    pub(crate) fn font_selection_did_change(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        let font = self.drawing_state().font.as_ref().map(|font| font.serialized.clone());
        if let Some(font) = font {
            self.assign_font(vm, &font);
        }
    }

    /// The word spacing of the current drawing state in CSS pixels.
    pub(crate) fn resolved_word_spacing(&self) -> f32 {
        let word_spacing = self.drawing_state().word_spacing.clone();
        match word_spacing {
            Some(word_spacing) => self
                .canvas
                .resolve_length(&word_spacing.length, self.font_metrics_source()),
            None => 0.0,
        }
    }

    /// The font of the current drawing state, which is resolved the first time the context needs one, and again when
    /// the fonts that the canvas can use change.
    pub(crate) fn current_font(&self, vm: &Vm) -> ResolvedFont {
        // When font style value is empty load default font
        if self.drawing_state().font.is_none() {
            self.assign_font(vm, &Utf16String::from_ascii(b"10px sans-serif"));
        }

        // NB: Drawing states, including saved states, retain their cascades across font loads and font-display
        //     transitions. Refresh them lazily so cached invisible fallback glyphs and metrics cannot outlive the font
        //     environment that selected them.
        let font = self
            .drawing_state()
            .font
            .clone()
            .expect("a context has a font once it is set");
        if font.environment_generation != self.canvas.font_environment_generation() {
            self.assign_font(vm, &font.serialized);
            return self
                .drawing_state()
                .font
                .clone()
                .expect("a context has a font once it is set");
        }
        font
    }

    /// The letter spacing of the current drawing state in CSS pixels.
    pub(crate) fn resolved_letter_spacing(&self) -> f32 {
        let letter_spacing = self.drawing_state().letter_spacing.clone();
        match letter_spacing {
            Some(letter_spacing) => self
                .canvas
                .resolve_length(&letter_spacing.length, self.font_metrics_source()),
            None => 0.0,
        }
    }

    /// How a draw composites under the current drawing state.
    pub(crate) fn compositing(state: &DrawingState) -> Compositing<'_> {
        Compositing {
            filter: state.filter.as_deref(),
            global_alpha: state.global_alpha,
            compositing_and_blending_operator: state.current_compositing_and_blending_operator,
            shadow: Self::shadow_of(state),
        }
    }

    /// The shadow of a draw, unless the draw casts none, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#shadows
    fn shadow_of(state: &DrawingState) -> Option<Canvas2DShadow> {
        // NB: A draw with the copy operator replaces the whole bitmap with its source, which would replace its shadow.
        if state.current_compositing_and_blending_operator == CompositingAndBlendingOperator::Copy {
            return None;
        }

        // Shadows are only drawn if the opacity component of the alpha component of the shadow color is nonzero and
        // either the shadowBlur is nonzero, or the shadowOffsetX is nonzero, or the shadowOffsetY is nonzero.
        if state.shadow_color.alpha() == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        if state.shadow_blur == 0.0 && state.shadow_offset_x == 0.0 && state.shadow_offset_y == 0.0 {
            return None;
        }
        Some(Canvas2DShadow {
            color: state.shadow_color.in_color_space,
            offset_x: state.shadow_offset_x,
            offset_y: state.shadow_offset_y,
            blur: state.shadow_blur,
        })
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#drawing-model
    /// 7. Composite B within the clipping region over the current output bitmap using the current compositing and
    ///    blending operator.
    /// NB: A transparent source paint changes nothing only under source-over.
    fn transparent_source_paint_can_be_ignored(state: &DrawingState) -> bool {
        state.current_compositing_and_blending_operator == CompositingAndBlendingOperator::SourceOver
    }

    pub(crate) fn fill_internal(&self, path: &Path, winding_rule: WindingRule) {
        if !self.recorder_is_ready() {
            return;
        }
        {
            let state = self.drawing_state();
            if !state.fill_style.is_visible() && Self::transparent_source_paint_can_be_ignored(&state) {
                return;
            }
        }

        let path_bytes = path.serialize_to_bytes();
        {
            let state = self.drawing_state();
            self.record(|recorder| {
                let paint = paint_of(recorder, &state.fill_style, self.context_attributes.color_space);
                recorder.fill_path(&path_bytes, &paint, winding_rule, &Self::compositing(&state));
            });
        }
        self.did_draw();
    }

    pub(crate) fn stroke_internal(&self, path: &Path) {
        if !self.recorder_is_ready() {
            return;
        }
        {
            let state = self.drawing_state();
            if !state.stroke_style.is_visible() && Self::transparent_source_paint_can_be_ignored(&state) {
                return;
            }
        }

        let dash_array = self.drawing_state().dash_array();
        let path_bytes = path.serialize_to_bytes();

        {
            let state = self.drawing_state();
            let stroke = Stroke {
                thickness: state.line_width,
                cap_style: state.cap_style(),
                join_style: state.join_style(),
                miter_limit: state.miter_limit,
                dash_array: &dash_array,
                dash_offset: state.line_dash_offset,
            };
            self.record(|recorder| {
                let paint = paint_of(recorder, &state.stroke_style, self.context_attributes.color_space);
                recorder.stroke_path(&path_bytes, &paint, &stroke, &Self::compositing(&state));
            });
        }
        self.did_draw();
    }

    pub(crate) fn clip_internal(&self, path: &Path, winding_rule: WindingRule) {
        if !self.recorder_is_ready() {
            return;
        }
        let path_bytes = path.serialize_to_bytes();
        self.record(|recorder| recorder.clip_path(&path_bytes, winding_rule));
    }
}

/// The transform translated by (x, y) in its own coordinates, as Gfx::AffineTransform::translate().
pub(crate) fn translated(transform: AffineTransform, x: f32, y: f32) -> AffineTransform {
    let [a, b, c, d, e, f] = transform.values;
    if a == 1.0 && b == 0.0 && c == 0.0 && d == 1.0 {
        return AffineTransform::new(a, b, c, d, e + x, f + y);
    }
    AffineTransform::new(a, b, c, d, e + (x * a + y * c), f + (x * b + y * d))
}

/// The transform scaled by (x, y) in its own coordinates, as Gfx::AffineTransform::scale().
pub(crate) fn scaled(transform: AffineTransform, x: f32, y: f32) -> AffineTransform {
    let [a, b, c, d, e, f] = transform.values;
    AffineTransform::new(a * x, b * x, c * y, d * y, e, f)
}

/// The transform multiplied by another, which applies first, as Gfx::AffineTransform::multiply().
pub(crate) fn multiply_transforms(transform: AffineTransform, other: AffineTransform) -> AffineTransform {
    if other.is_identity() {
        return transform;
    }
    let [a, b, c, d, e, f] = transform.values;
    let [oa, ob, oc, od, oe, of] = other.values;
    AffineTransform::new(
        oa * a + ob * c,
        oa * b + ob * d,
        oc * a + od * c,
        oc * b + od * d,
        oe * a + of * c + e,
        oe * b + of * d + f,
    )
}

/// The transform rotated by the angle in radians, as Gfx::AffineTransform::rotate_radians().
pub(crate) fn rotated(transform: AffineTransform, radians: f32) -> AffineTransform {
    let (sin, cos) = math::sincos(radians);
    multiply_transforms(transform, AffineTransform::new(cos, sin, -sin, cos, 0.0, 0.0))
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#drawing-state

use std::rc::Rc;

use ak::Utf16String;

};
