fn cookie_list_item_to_js(cx: &CallContext, item: CookieListItem) -> Value {
    // NB: The generated bindings convert the dictionary, which a build of the crate on its own leaves out.
    #[cfg(web_idl_bindings)]
    return ToJs::to_js(item, cx).expect("a cookie list item converts to a JS value");
    #[cfg(not(web_idl_bindings))]
    {
        let _ = (item, cx);
        unreachable!("only the generated bindings resolve a promise with the dictionary")
    }
}

fn cookie_list_to_js(cx: &CallContext, cookie_list: Vec<CookieListItem>) -> Value {
    #[cfg(web_idl_bindings)]
    return sequence_to_js(cx, cookie_list, |item| ToJs::to_js(item, cx))
        .expect("a cookie list converts to a JS value");
    #[cfg(not(web_idl_bindings))]
    {
        let _ = (cookie_list, cx);
        unreachable!("only the generated bindings resolve a promise with the dictionary")
    }
}

fn resolve_cookie_list_item_or_null_promise(vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise, cookie_list: Vec<CookieListItem>) {
    let Some(first_item) = cookie_list.into_iter().next() else {
        resolve_promise(vm, promise, Value::NULL);
        return;
    };

    let value = cookie_list_item_to_js(&CallContext::new(vm, promise_realm(promise)), first_item);
    resolve_promise(vm, promise, value);
}

fn resolve_cookie_list_promise(vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise, cookie_list: Vec<CookieListItem>) {
    let result = cookie_list_to_js(&CallContext::new(vm, promise_realm(promise)), cookie_list);
    resolve_promise(vm, promise, result);
}

fn validate_cookie_store_get_options(
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    options: &CookieStoreGetOptions,
    empty_options_allowed: EmptyOptionsAllowed,
) -> Result<Url, Exception> {
    // 1. Let settings be this's relevant settings object.
    let settings = relevant_settings_object(realm.global_object());

    // 2. Let origin be settings's origin.
    let origin = settings.origin();

    // 3. If origin is an opaque origin, then return a promise rejected with a "SecurityError" DOMException.
    if origin.is_opaque() {
        return Err(Exception::Dom(
            "SecurityError",
            Utf16String::from_utf8("Document origin is opaque"),
        ));
    }

    // 4. Let url be settings's creation URL.
    let mut url = settings.creation_url();

    // 5. If options is empty, then return a promise rejected with a TypeError.
    if empty_options_allowed == EmptyOptionsAllowed::No && options.name.is_none() && options.url.is_none() {
        return Err(Exception::type_error("CookieStoreGetOptions is empty"));
    }

    // 6. If options["url"] exists:
    if let Some(options_url) = &options.url {
        // 1. Let parsed be the result of parsing options["url"] with settings's API base URL.
        let api_base_url = settings.api_base_url();
        let options_url = options_url.to_utf16();
        let parsed = basic_parse(
            UrlInput::from(&*options_url),
            BasicParseOptions::new().base_url(&api_base_url),
        );

        // 2. If parsed is failure or parsed does not equal url with exclude fragments set to true, then return a promise
        //    rejected with a TypeError.
        let Some(parsed) = parsed else {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("url is invalid"));
        };
        if parsed.serialize(ExcludeFragment::Yes) != url.serialize(ExcludeFragment::Yes) {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("url does not match creation URL"));
        }

        // 3. If parsed's origin and url's origin are not the same origin, then return a promise rejected with a TypeError.
        if !parsed.origin().is_same_origin(&url.origin()) {
            return Err(Exception::type_error(
                "url's origin does not match creation URL's origin",
            ));
        }

        // 4. Set url to parsed.
        url = parsed;
    }

    Ok(url)
}

fn validate_cookie_store_mutation(realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Result<Url, Exception> {
    // 1. Let settings be this's relevant settings object.
    let settings = relevant_settings_object(realm.global_object());

    // 2. Let origin be settings's origin.
    let origin = settings.origin();

    // 3. If origin is an opaque origin, then return a promise rejected with a "SecurityError" DOMException.
    if origin.is_opaque() {
        return Err(Exception::Dom(
            "SecurityError",
            Utf16String::from_utf8("Document origin is opaque"),
        ));
    }

    // 4. Let url be settings's creation URL.
    Ok(settings.creation_url())
}

fn complete_cookie_list_request(vm: &Vm, request: CookieListRequest, cookie_list: Vec<CookieListItem>) {
    // AD-HOC: Queue a global task to perform the next steps
    // Spec issue: https://github.com/whatwg/cookiestore/issues/239
    queue_a_global_task(
        vm,
        request.global,
        TaskSource::Unspecified,
        (
            request.promise,
            CookieListResult { list: cookie_list },
            request.first_item_only == FirstItemOnly::Yes,
        ),
        |vm, (promise, cookie_list, first_item_only)| {
            with_temporary_execution_context(promise_realm(promise), || {
                if first_item_only {
                    resolve_cookie_list_item_or_null_promise(vm, promise, cookie_list.list);
                } else {
                    resolve_cookie_list_promise(vm, promise, cookie_list.list);
                }
            });
        },
    );
}

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct CookieListResult {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    list: Vec<CookieListItem>,
}

fn complete_cookie_mutation(
    vm: &Vm,
    global: Gc<Object>,
    promise: WebIdlPromise,
    failure_message: &'static str,
    result: bool,
) {
    // NB: The UI's notification of this mutation's cookie changes is handled from a deferred invocation scheduled while
    //     waiting for its reply. Queue the task below after that, so the change event is fired first.
    deferred_invoke(
        vm,
        (global, promise, result, failure_message),
        |vm, (global, promise, result, failure_message)| {
            // AD-HOC: Queue a global task to perform the next steps
            // Spec issue: https://github.com/whatwg/cookiestore/issues/239
            queue_a_global_task(
                vm,
                global,
                TaskSource::Unspecified,
                (promise, result, failure_message),
                |vm, (promise, result, failure_message)| {
                    with_temporary_execution_context(promise_realm(promise), || {
                        if !result {
                            reject_promise_with_exception(vm, promise, Exception::type_error(failure_message));
                            return;
                        }

                        resolve_promise(vm, promise, Value::UNDEFINED);
                    });
                },
            );
        },
    );
}

// https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#create-a-cookielistitem
fn create_a_cookie_list_item(name: &str, value: &str) -> CookieListItem {
    // 1. Let name be the result of running UTF-8 decode without BOM on cookie’s name.
    // 2. Let value be the result of running UTF-8 decode without BOM on cookie’s value.
    // 3. Return «[ "name" → name, "value" → value ]».
    CookieListItem {
        name: Some(UsvString::from_utf8(name)),
        value: Some(UsvString::from_utf8(value)),
    }
}

// https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#normalize-a-cookie-name-or-value
fn normalize(input: &str) -> &str {
    // Remove all U+0009 TAB and U+0020 SPACE that are at the start or end of input.
    input.trim_matches(['\t', ' '])
}

// https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#query-cookies
fn query_cookies(environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject, url: &Url, name: Option<&str>) -> Vec<CookieListItem> {
    struct QueriedCookie {
        name: String,
        value: String,
        http_only: bool,
    }

    unsafe extern "C" fn on_cookie(ctx: *mut c_void, name: ak::Span<'_, u8>, value: ak::Span<'_, u8>, http_only: bool) {
        // SAFETY: ctx is the list below, and LibWeb lends the name and the value, which are UTF-8, for the call.
        unsafe { &mut *ctx.cast::<Vec<QueriedCookie>>() }.push(QueriedCookie {
            name: String::from_utf8_lossy(name.as_slice()).into_owned(),
            value: String::from_utf8_lossy(value.as_slice()).into_owned(),
            http_only,
        });
    }

    // 1. Perform the steps defined in Cookies § Retrieval Model to compute the "cookie-string from a given cookie store"
    //    with url as request-uri. The cookie-string itself is ignored, but the intermediate cookie-list is used in subsequent steps.
    //    For the purposes of the steps, the cookie-string is being generated for a "non-HTTP" API.
    let mut cookie_list: Vec<QueriedCookie> = Vec::new();
    let rust_url = RustUrl::from_url(url);
    // SAFETY: The settings object is live, and the URL and the list outlive the call.
    unsafe {
        web_cookie_store_request_all_cookies(
            environment.as_ptr(),
            &raw const rust_url,
            (&raw mut cookie_list).cast(),
            on_cookie,
        );
    }

    // 2. Let list be « ».
    let mut list = Vec::new();

    // 3. For each cookie of cookie-list:
    for cookie in &cookie_list {
        // 1. Assert: cookie’s http-only-flag is false.
        assert!(!cookie.http_only);

        // 2. If name is non-null:
        if let Some(name) = name {
            // 1. Normalize name.
            let normalized_name = normalize(name);

            // 2. Let cookieName be the result of running UTF-8 decode without BOM on cookie’s name.
            // 3. If cookieName does not equal name, then continue.
            if cookie.name != normalized_name {
                continue;
            }
        }

        // 3. Let item be the result of running create a CookieListItem from cookie.
        let item = create_a_cookie_list_item(&cookie.name, &cookie.value);

        // 4. Append item to list.
        list.push(item);
    }

    // 4. Return list.
    list
}

// https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-layered-cookies#name-cookie-default-path
fn cookie_default_path(mut path: Vec<&str>) -> Vec<&str> {
    // 1. Assert: path is a non-empty list.
    assert!(!path.is_empty());

    // 2. If path's size is greater than 1, then remove path's last item.
    if path.len() > 1 {
        path.pop();
    }
    // 3. Otherwise, set path[0] to the empty string.
    else {
        path[0] = "";
    }

    // 4. Return path.
    path
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#serialized-cookie-default-path
fn serialized_cookie_default_path(url: &Url) -> String {
    // 1. Let cloneURL be a clone of url.
    let mut clone_url = url.clone();

    // 2. Set cloneURL’s path to the cookie default path of cloneURL’s path.
    clone_url.set_path(cookie_default_path(url.path_segments().collect()));

    // 3. Return the URL path serialization of cloneURL.
    clone_url.serialize_path().to_owned()
}

const MAXIMUM_NAME_VALUE_PAIR_SIZE: usize = 4096;
const MAXIMUM_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_SIZE: usize = 1024;

/// LibHTTP's MAXIMUM_COOKIE_AGE: 400 days.
const MAXIMUM_COOKIE_AGE_IN_MILLISECONDS: i64 = 400 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

fn unix_now_in_milliseconds() -> i64 {
    let since_epoch = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default();
    i64::try_from(since_epoch.as_millis()).unwrap_or(i64::MAX)
}

// https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#set-a-cookie
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the algorithm has these arguments")]
fn set_a_cookie(
    environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
    url: &Url,
    name: &str,
    value: &str,
    expires: Option<f64>,
    domain: Option<&str>,
    path: &str,
    same_site: CookieSameSite,
    partitioned: bool,
    max_age: Option<i64>,
) -> bool {
    // 1. Normalize name.
    let name = normalize(name);

    // 2. Normalize value.
    let value = normalize(value);

    // 3. If name or value contain U+003B (;), any C0 control character except U+0009 TAB, or U+007F DELETE, then return failure.
    let is_forbidden = |code_point: char| {
        code_point == ';' || (code_point <= '\u{1F}' && code_point != '\t') || code_point == '\u{7F}'
    };
    if name.contains(is_forbidden) || value.contains(is_forbidden) {
        return false;
    }

    // 4. If name contains U+003D (=), then return failure.
    if name.contains('=') {
        return false;
    }

    // 5. If name’s length is 0:
    if name.is_empty() {
        // 1. If value contains U+003D (=), then return failure.
        if value.contains('=') {
            return false;
        }

        // 2. If value’s length is 0, then return failure.
        if value.is_empty() {
            return false;
        }

        // 3. If value, byte-lowercased, starts with `__host-`, `__host-http-`, `__http-`, or `__secure-`, then return failure.
        let value_byte_lowercased = value.to_ascii_lowercase();
        if value_byte_lowercased.starts_with("__host-")
            || value_byte_lowercased.starts_with("__host-http-")
            || value_byte_lowercased.starts_with("__http-")
            || value_byte_lowercased.starts_with("__secure-")
        {
            return false;
        }
    }

    // 6. If name, byte-lowercased, starts with `__host-http-` or `__http-`, then return failure.
    let name_ascii_lowercased = name.to_ascii_lowercase();
    if name_ascii_lowercased.starts_with("__host-http-") || name_ascii_lowercased.starts_with("__http-") {
        return false;
    }

    // 7. Let encodedName be the result of UTF-8 encoding name.
    // 8. Let encodedValue be the result of UTF-8 encoding value.
    let encoded_name = name.as_bytes();
    let encoded_value = value.as_bytes();

    // 9. If the byte sequence length of encodedName plus the byte sequence length of encodedValue is greater than the
    //    maximum name/value pair size, then return failure.
    if encoded_name.len() + encoded_value.len() > MAXIMUM_NAME_VALUE_PAIR_SIZE {
        return false;
    }

    // 10. Let host be url’s host
    let host = url.serialized_host().map(|serialization| Host {
        kind: url.host_kind(),
        serialization: serialization.to_owned(),
    });

    // 11. Let attributes be « ».
    let mut encoded_domain = None;

    // 12. If domain is non-null:
    if let Some(domain) = domain {
        // 1. If domain starts with U+002E (.), then return failure.
        if domain.starts_with('.') {
            return false;
        }

        // 2. If name, byte-lowercased, starts with `__host-`, then return failure.
        if name_ascii_lowercased.starts_with("__host-") {
            return false;
        }

        // 3. If domain is not a registrable domain suffix of and is not equal to host, then return failure.
        let Some(host) = &host else {
            return false;
        };
        if !is_a_registrable_domain_suffix_of_or_is_equal_to(&Utf16String::from_utf8(domain), host) {
            return false;
        }

        // 4. Let parsedDomain be the result of host parsing domain.
        let parsed_domain = parse_host(domain);

        // 5. Assert: parsedDomain is not failure.
        let parsed_domain = parsed_domain.expect("a registrable domain suffix of a host parses");

        // 6. Let encodedDomain be the result of UTF-8 encoding parsedDomain.
        let domain = parsed_domain.serialization;

        // 7. If the byte sequence length of encodedDomain is greater than the maximum attribute value size, then return failure.
        if domain.len() > MAXIMUM_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_SIZE {
            return false;
        }

        // 8. Append (`Domain`, encodedDomain) to attributes.
        encoded_domain = Some(domain);
    }

    let mut expiry_time = None;
    let mut encoded_max_age = None;

    // 13. If expires is non-null:
    if let Some(expires) = expires {
        // 1. If maxAge is non-null, then return failure.
        if max_age.is_some() {
            return false;
        }

        // 2. Append (`Expires`, expires (date serialized)) to attributes.
        #[allow(
            clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
            reason = "a timestamp is milliseconds since the epoch"
        )]
        let mut expires = expires as i64;

        // https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis-15.html#section-5.6.1
        // 3. Let cookie-age-limit be the maximum age of the cookie (which SHOULD be 400 days in the future or sooner, see
        //    Section 5.5).
        let cookie_age_limit = unix_now_in_milliseconds().saturating_add(MAXIMUM_COOKIE_AGE_IN_MILLISECONDS);

        // 4. If the expiry-time is more than cookie-age-limit, the user agent MUST set the expiry time to cookie-age-limit
        //    in seconds.
        if expires.div_euclid(1000) > cookie_age_limit.div_euclid(1000) {
            expires = cookie_age_limit;
        }

        expiry_time = Some(expires);
    }
    // 14. Otherwise, if maxAge is non-null, then append (`Max-Age`, ToString(maxAge)) to attributes.
    else if let Some(max_age) = max_age {
        encoded_max_age = Some(max_age.to_string());
    }

    // 15. If path is the empty string, then set path to the serialized cookie default path of url.
    let path = if path.is_empty() {
        serialized_cookie_default_path(url)
    } else {
        path.to_owned()
    };

    // 16. If path does not start with U+002F (/), then return failure.
    if !path.starts_with('/') {
        return false;
    }

    // 17. If path is not U+002F (/), and name, byte-lowercased, starts with `__host-`, then return failure.
    if path != "/" && name_ascii_lowercased.starts_with("__host-") {
        return false;
    }

    // 18. Let encodedPath be the result of UTF-8 encoding path.
    let encoded_path = path.as_bytes();

    // 19. If the byte sequence length of encodedPath is greater than the maximum attribute value size, then return failure.
    if encoded_path.len() > MAXIMUM_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_SIZE {
        return false;
    }

    // 20. Append (`Path`, encodedPath) to attributes.
    // 21. Append (`Secure`, ``) to attributes.
    let secure_attribute_present = true;

    // 22. Switch on sameSite:
    let same_site_attribute = match same_site {
        // -> "none"
        //    Append (`SameSite`, `None`) to attributes.
        CookieSameSite::None => SAME_SITE_NONE,
        // -> "strict"
        //    Append (`SameSite`, `Strict`) to attributes.
        CookieSameSite::Strict => SAME_SITE_STRICT,
        // -> "lax"
        //    Append (`SameSite`, `Lax`) to attributes.
        CookieSameSite::Lax => SAME_SITE_LAX,
    };

    // FIXME: 23. If partitioned is true, Append (`Partitioned`, ``) to attributes.
    let _ = partitioned;

    // 24. Perform the steps defined in Cookies § Storage Model for when the user agent "receives a cookie" with url as
    //     request-uri, encodedName as cookie-name, encodedValue as cookie-value, and attributes as cookie-attribute-list.
    //     For the purposes of the steps, the newly-created cookie was received from a "non-HTTP" API.
    let attributes = ParsedCookieAbi {
        name: ak::Span::new(encoded_name),
        value: ak::Span::new(encoded_value),
        has_expiry_time: expiry_time.is_some(),
        expiry_time: expiry_time.unwrap_or_default(),
        has_max_age: encoded_max_age.is_some(),
        max_age: ak::Span::new(encoded_max_age.as_deref().unwrap_or_default().as_bytes()),
        has_domain: encoded_domain.is_some(),
        domain: ak::Span::new(encoded_domain.as_deref().unwrap_or_default().as_bytes()),
        path: ak::Span::new(encoded_path),
        secure_attribute_present,
        same_site_attribute,
    };
    let rust_url = RustUrl::from_url(url);
    // SAFETY: The settings object is live, and the URL and the attributes outlive the call.
    unsafe { web_cookie_store_set_cookie(environment.as_ptr(), &raw const rust_url, &raw const attributes) };

    // 25. Return success.
    true
}

// https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#delete-a-cookie
fn delete_a_cookie(
    environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
    url: &Url,
    name: &str,
    domain: Option<&str>,
    path: &str,
    partitioned: bool,
) -> bool {
    // 1. Normalize name.
    let name = normalize(name);

    // 2. Let value be the empty string.
    let mut value = "";

    // 3. If name’s length is 0, then set value to any non-empty implementation-defined string.
    if name.is_empty() {
        value = "ladybird";
    }

    // 4. Return the results of running set a cookie with url, name, value, null, domain, path, "strict", partitioned,
    //    and 0.
    set_a_cookie(
        environment,
        url,
        name,
        value,
        None,
        domain,
        path,
        CookieSameSite::Strict,
        partitioned,
        Some(0),
    )
}

// https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#cookie-change
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct CookieChange {
    cookie: Cookie,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    r#type: CookieChangeType,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum CookieChangeType {
    Changed,
    Deleted,
}

// https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#observable-changes
fn observable_changes(changes: Vec<Cookie>) -> Vec<CookieChange> {
    // The observable changes for url are the set of cookie changes to cookies in a cookie store which meet the
    // requirements in step 1 of Cookies § Retrieval Algorithm’s steps to compute the "cookie-string from a given
    // cookie store" with url as request-uri, for a "non-HTTP" API.
    let now = unix_now_in_milliseconds();

    changes
        .into_iter()
        .map(|cookie| {
            // A cookie change is a cookie and a type (either changed or deleted):
            // - A cookie which is removed due to an insertion of another cookie with the same name, domain, and path is ignored.
            // - A newly-created cookie which is not immediately evicted is considered changed.
            // - A newly-created cookie which is immediately evicted is considered deleted.
            // - A cookie which is otherwise evicted or removed is considered deleted
            let r#type = if cookie.expiry_time_in_milliseconds < now {
                CookieChangeType::Deleted
            } else {
                CookieChangeType::Changed
            };
            CookieChange { cookie, r#type }
        })
        .collect()
}

// https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#prepare-lists
fn prepare_lists(changes: &[CookieChange]) -> (Vec<CookieListItem>, Vec<CookieListItem>) {
    // 1. Let changedList be « ».
    let mut changed_list = Vec::new();

    // 2. Let deletedList be « ».
    let mut deleted_list = Vec::new();

    // 3. For each change in changes, run these steps:
    for change in changes {
        // 1. Let item be the result of running create a CookieListItem from change’s cookie.
        let mut item = create_a_cookie_list_item(&change.cookie.name, &change.cookie.value);

        // 2. If change’s type is changed, then append item to changedList.
        if change.r#type == CookieChangeType::Changed {
            changed_list.push(item);
        }
        // 3. Otherwise, run these steps:
        else {
            // 1. Set item["value"] to undefined.
            item.value = None;

            // 2. Append item to deletedList.
            deleted_list.push(item);
        }
    }

    // 4. Return changedList and deletedList.
    (changed_list, deleted_list)
}

// https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#cookiestore
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CookieStore {
    event_target: CppEventTarget,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
}

impl Wrappable for CookieStore {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.realm)
    }

    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event_target.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for CookieStore {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
}

impl CookieStore {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Ref<Self> {
        let cookie_store = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            event_target: CppEventTarget::new(),
            realm,
        });
        cookie_store.event_target.set_owner(cookie_store);
        cookie_store
    }

    fn request_cookie_list(
        &self,
        vm: &Vm,
        options: &CookieStoreGetOptions,
        empty_options_allowed: EmptyOptionsAllowed,
        first_item_only: FirstItemOnly,
        in_parallel: fn(&Vm, CookieListRequest),
    ) -> WebIdlPromise {
        let url = match validate_cookie_store_get_options(self.realm, options, empty_options_allowed) {
            Ok(url) => url,
            Err(exception) => return create_rejected_promise_from_exception(vm, self.realm, exception),
        };

        let promise = create_promise(vm, self.realm);
        in_parallel(
            vm,
            CookieListRequest {
                environment: relevant_settings_object(self.realm.global_object()),
                url,
                name: options.name.as_ref().map(UsvString::to_utf8),
                global: self.realm.global_object(),
                promise,
                first_item_only,
            },
        );
        promise
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_with_name(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        let options = CookieStoreGetOptions {
            name: Some(name),
            url: None,
        };
        Ok(self.request_cookie_list(
            cx.vm(),
            &options,
            EmptyOptionsAllowed::No,
            FirstItemOnly::Yes,
            Self::get_in_parallel,
        ))
    }

    // https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-cookiestore-get-options
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, options: CookieStoreGetOptions) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        Ok(self.request_cookie_list(
            cx.vm(),
            &options,
            EmptyOptionsAllowed::No,
            FirstItemOnly::Yes,
            Self::get_in_parallel,
        ))
    }

    fn get_in_parallel(vm: &Vm, request: CookieListRequest) {
        // 8. Run the following steps in parallel:
        deferred_invoke(vm, request, |vm, request| {
            // 1. Let list be the results of running query cookies with url and options["name"] with default null.
            let list = query_cookies(&request.environment, &request.url, request.name.as_deref());
            complete_cookie_list_request(vm, request, list);
        });
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_all_with_name(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        let options = CookieStoreGetOptions {
            name: Some(name),
            url: None,
        };
        Ok(self.request_cookie_list(
            cx.vm(),
            &options,
            EmptyOptionsAllowed::Yes,
            FirstItemOnly::No,
            Self::get_all_in_parallel,
        ))
    }

    // https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-cookiestore-getall-options
    pub(crate) fn get_all(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, options: CookieStoreGetOptions) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        Ok(self.request_cookie_list(
            cx.vm(),
            &options,
            EmptyOptionsAllowed::Yes,
            FirstItemOnly::No,
            Self::get_all_in_parallel,
        ))
    }

    fn get_all_in_parallel(vm: &Vm, request: CookieListRequest) {
        // 7. Run the following steps in parallel:
        deferred_invoke(vm, request, |vm, request| {
            // 1. Let list be the results of running query cookies with url and options["name"] with default null.
            let list = query_cookies(&request.environment, &request.url, request.name.as_deref());
            complete_cookie_list_request(vm, request, list);
        });
    }

    fn request_cookie_mutation(&self, vm: &Vm, options: &CookieInit, failure_message: &'static str) -> WebIdlPromise {
        let url = match validate_cookie_store_mutation(self.realm) {
            Ok(url) => url,
            Err(exception) => return create_rejected_promise_from_exception(vm, self.realm, exception),
        };

        let promise = create_promise(vm, self.realm);
        let mutation = CookieMutation {
            environment: relevant_settings_object(self.realm.global_object()),
            url,
            name: options.name.to_utf8(),
            value: options.value.to_utf8(),
            expires: options.expires,
            domain: options.domain.as_ref().map(UsvString::to_utf8),
            path: options.path.to_utf8(),
            same_site: options.same_site,
            partitioned: options.partitioned,
            max_age: options.max_age,
            global: self.realm.global_object(),
            promise,
            failure_message,
        };

        // 6. Run the following steps in parallel:
        deferred_invoke(vm, mutation, |vm, mutation| {
            // 1. Let r be the result of running set a cookie with url, options["name"], options["value"], options["expires"],
            //    options["domain"], options["path"], options["sameSite"], options["partitioned"], and options["maxAge"].
            let result = set_a_cookie(
                &mutation.environment,
                &mutation.url,
                &mutation.name,
                &mutation.value,
                mutation.expires,
                mutation.domain.as_deref(),
                &mutation.path,
                mutation.same_site,
                mutation.partitioned,
                mutation.max_age,
            );
            complete_cookie_mutation(vm, mutation.global, mutation.promise, mutation.failure_message, result);
        });
        promise
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_with_name_and_value(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        name: UsvString,
        value: UsvString,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        let options = CookieInit {
            name,
            value,
            expires: None,
            domain: None,
            path: UsvString::from_ascii(b"/"),
            same_site: CookieSameSite::Strict,
            partitioned: false,
            max_age: None,
        };
        Ok(self.request_cookie_mutation(cx.vm(), &options, "Name or value are malformed"))
    }

    // https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-cookiestore-set-options
    pub(crate) fn set(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, options: CookieInit) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        Ok(self.request_cookie_mutation(cx.vm(), &options, "Name, value, domain or path are malformed"))
    }

    fn request_cookie_deletion(&self, vm: &Vm, options: &CookieStoreDeleteOptions) -> WebIdlPromise {
        let url = match validate_cookie_store_mutation(self.realm) {
            Ok(url) => url,
            Err(exception) => return create_rejected_promise_from_exception(vm, self.realm, exception),
        };

        let promise = create_promise(vm, self.realm);
        let deletion = CookieDeletion {
            environment: relevant_settings_object(self.realm.global_object()),
            url,
            name: options.name.to_utf8(),
            domain: options.domain.as_ref().map(UsvString::to_utf8),
            path: options.path.to_utf8(),
            partitioned: options.partitioned,
            global: self.realm.global_object(),
            promise,
            failure_message: "Name is malformed",
        };

        // 6. Run the following steps in parallel:
        deferred_invoke(vm, deletion, |vm, deletion| {
            // 1. Let r be the result of running delete a cookie with url, options["name"], options["domain"], options["path"],
            //    and options["partitioned"].
            let result = delete_a_cookie(
                &deletion.environment,
                &deletion.url,
                &deletion.name,
                deletion.domain.as_deref(),
                &deletion.path,
                deletion.partitioned,
            );
            complete_cookie_mutation(vm, deletion.global, deletion.promise, deletion.failure_message, result);
        });
        promise
    }

    pub(crate) fn delete_with_name(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        let options = CookieStoreDeleteOptions {
            name,
            domain: None,
            path: UsvString::from_ascii(b"/"),
            partitioned: true,
        };
        Ok(self.request_cookie_deletion(cx.vm(), &options))
    }

    // https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-cookiestore-delete-options
    pub(crate) fn delete(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        options: CookieStoreDeleteOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        Ok(self.request_cookie_deletion(cx.vm(), &options))
    }

    // https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#process-cookie-changes
    pub(crate) fn process_cookie_changes(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm, all_changes: Vec<Cookie>) {
        // 1. Let url be window’s relevant settings object’s creation URL.
        // 2. Let changes be the observable changes for url.
        // 3. If changes is empty, then continue.
        // NB: We perform the URL-based filtering in the UI process so that we don't have to send all changed cookies over
        //     IPC to every tab.
        let changes = observable_changes(all_changes);

        // 4. Queue a global task on the DOM manipulation task source given window to fire a change event named "change"
        //    with changes at window’s CookieStore.
        queue_a_global_task(
            vm,
            this.realm.global_object(),
            TaskSource::DOMManipulation,
            (this, changes),
            |vm, (this, changes)| {
                with_temporary_execution_context(this.realm, || {
                    // https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#fire-a-change-event
                    // 4. Let changedList and deletedList be the result of running prepare lists from changes.
                    let (changed_list, deleted_list) = prepare_lists(&changes);

                    // 1. Let event be the result of creating an Event using CookieChangeEvent.
                    // 2. Set event’s type attribute to type.
                    // 3. Set event’s bubbles and cancelable attributes to false.
                    // 5. Set event’s changed attribute to changedList.
                    // 6. Set event’s deleted attribute to deletedList.
                    let event_init = CookieChangeEventInit {
                        parent: EventInit {
                            bubbles: false,
                            cancelable: false,
                            composed: false,
                        },
                        changed: Some(changed_list),
                        deleted: Some(deleted_list),
                    };
                    let event =
                        CookieChangeEvent::create(vm, this.realm, &Utf16String::from_utf8("change"), event_init);

                    // 7. Dispatch event at target.
                    this.event_target.dispatch_event(event.event());
                });
            },
        );
    }
}

//! The entry points through which LibWeb's C++ code creates a CookieStore and reports cookie changes to it, declared
//! in Libraries/LibWeb/CookieStore/CookieStore.cpp.

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::{InterfaceCell, cell_into_abi};
use crate::cookie_store::cookie_store::{Cookie, CookieStore};

/// A changed cookie, with its name and value in UTF-8 and its expiry time in milliseconds since the epoch.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct CookieAbi<'a> {
    name: ak::Span<'a, u8>,
    value: ak::Span<'a, u8>,
    expiry_time: i64,
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_cookie_store_create_cookie_store(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(CookieStore::create(vm, realm))
}

/// https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#process-cookie-changes
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_cookie_store_process_cookie_changes(
    vm: &Vm,
    cookie_store: &InterfaceCell,
    changes: ak::Span<'_, CookieAbi<'_>>,
) {
    let cookie_store = cookie_store.object::<CookieStore>();
    let changes = changes
        .as_slice()
        .iter()
        .map(|cookie| Cookie {
            name: String::from_utf8_lossy(cookie.name.as_slice()).into_owned(),
            value: String::from_utf8_lossy(cookie.value.as_slice()).into_owned(),
            expiry_time_in_milliseconds: cookie.expiry_time,
        })
        .collect();
    CookieStore::process_cookie_changes(cookie_store, vm, changes);
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CredentialsContainer;

impl Wrappable for CredentialsContainer {}

fn reject_not_implemented_promise(vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise, operation: &str) {
    let throw = vm
        .throw_completion::<()>(ErrorKind::InternalError, ErrorType::NotImplemented, &[&operation])
        .expect_err("throwing a completion throws");
    reject_promise_with_exception(vm, promise, Exception::from(throw));
}

impl CredentialsContainer {
    // https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialscontainer-get
    pub(crate) fn get(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        promise: WebIdlPromise,
        _: CredentialRequestOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        eprintln!("FIXME: Unimplemented CredentialsContainer::get()");
        reject_not_implemented_promise(cx.vm(), promise, "get");
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialscontainer-store
    pub(crate) fn store(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, promise: WebIdlPromise, _: AnyCredential) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        eprintln!("FIXME: Unimplemented CredentialsContainer::store()");

    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialscontainer-create
    pub(crate) fn create(

/// https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#abstract-opdef-create-a-federatedcredential-from-federatedcredentialinit
pub(crate) fn create_federated_credential(
    vm: &Vm,
    init: FederatedCredentialInit,
    origin: Origin,
) -> Ref<FederatedCredential> {
    // 1. Let c be a new FederatedCredential object.
    // 3. Set c’s properties as follows:
    //    - id
    //      - init.id's value
    //    - provider
    //      - init.provider's value
    //    - iconURL
    //      - init.iconURL's value
    //    - name
    //      - init.name's value
    //    - [[origin]]
    //      - init.origin's value.
    //      NOTE: origin is retrieved by parsing the URL from init.provider.
    // 4. Return c.
    allocate(vm, |_| FederatedCredential::new(init, origin))
}

    pub(crate) parent: CredentialData,
    pub(crate) icon_url: Option<UsvString>,
    pub(crate) name: Option<UsvString>,
    pub(crate) protocol: Option<Utf16String>,
    pub(crate) provider: UsvString,

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct FederatedCredential {
    credential: Credential,
    user_data: CredentialUserData,
    provider: UsvString,
    protocol: Option<Utf16String>,
    // https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credential-origin-slot
    #[gc(untraced)]
    #[cfg_attr(web_idl_bindings, expect(dead_code, reason = "no algorithm reads [[origin]] yet"))]
    origin: Origin,
}

impl Wrappable for FederatedCredential {}

impl Inherits<Credential> for FederatedCredential {
    fn parent(&self) -> &Credential {
        &self.credential
    }
}

impl FederatedCredential {
    pub(crate) fn new(init: FederatedCredentialInit, origin: Origin) -> Self {
        Self {
            credential: Credential::new(init.parent.id, "federated"),
            user_data: CredentialUserData::new(
                init.name.unwrap_or_else(|| UsvString::from_ascii(b"")),
                init.icon_url.unwrap_or_else(|| UsvString::from_ascii(b"")),
            ),
            provider: init.provider,
            protocol: init.protocol,
            origin,
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-federatedcredential-federatedcredential
    pub(crate) fn construct(cx: &mut CallContext, data: FederatedCredentialInit) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // 1. Let r be the result of executing Create a FederatedCredential from FederatedCredentialInit on data. If that
        // threw an exception, rethrow that exception.
        // 2. Return r.
        if data.parent.id.as_utf16_string().is_empty() {
            return Err(Exception::TypeError(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"'id' must not be empty.",
            )));
        }
        if data.provider.as_utf16_string().is_empty() {
            return Err(Exception::TypeError(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"'provider' must not be empty.",
            )));
        }

        // AD-HOC: Aligning with how Chromium retrieves the origin by parsing the URL from data.provider.
        let Some(url) = basic_parse(url_input(data.provider.units()), BasicParseOptions::new()) else {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "SyntaxError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"'provider' is not a valid url."),
            ));
        };

        Ok(create_federated_credential(cx.vm(), data, url.origin()))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-federatedcredential-provider
    pub(crate) fn provider(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        Ok(self.provider.clone())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-federatedcredential-protocol
    pub(crate) fn protocol(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Utf16String>> {
        Ok(self.protocol.clone())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialuserdata-name
    pub(crate) fn name(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        Ok(self.user_data.name())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialuserdata-iconurl
    pub(crate) fn icon_url(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        Ok(self.user_data.icon_url())
    }
}

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::Vm;
use liburl_rust::origin::Origin;

use super::credential::CredentialData;
use super::password_credential::{PasswordCredential, PasswordCredentialData};
use crate::bindings::conversions::UsvString;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::html::html_form_element::CppHTMLFormElement;
use crate::xhr::form_data::{FormData, FormDataEntryValue};

/// https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#abstract-opdef-create-a-passwordcredential-from-an-htmlformelement
pub(crate) fn create_password_credential_from_form(
    cx: &mut CallContext,
    form: CppHTMLFormElement,
    origin: Origin,
) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<PasswordCredential>> {
    // 1. Let data be a new PasswordCredentialData dictionary.
    let mut data = PasswordCredentialData {
        parent: CredentialData {
            id: UsvString::from_ascii(b""),
        },
        icon_url: None,
        name: None,
        password: UsvString::from_ascii(b""),
    };

    // 2. Set data’s origin member’s value to origin’s value.

    // 3. Let formData be the result of executing the FormData constructor on form.
    let form_data = FormData::construct(cx, Some(form.interface()), None)?;

    // 4. Let elements be a list of all the submittable elements whose form owner is form, in tree order.
    let elements = form.submittable_elements(cx.vm());

    // 5. Let newPasswordObserved be false.
    let mut new_password_observed = false;

    // 6. For each field in elements, run the following steps:
    for index in 0..elements.len() {
        let field = elements.get(index).expect("the index is in range");

        // 1. If field does not have an autocomplete attribute, then skip to the next field.
        let Some(autocomplete_attribute) = field.attribute("autocomplete").filter(|value| !value.is_empty()) else {
            continue;
        };

        // 2. Let name be the value of field’s name attribute.
        // 3. If formData’s has() method returns false when executed on name, then skip to the next field.
        let Some(name) = field.attribute("name") else {
            continue;
        };
        let name = UsvString::from_utf16_string(&name);
        if !form_data.has(cx, name.clone())? {
            continue;
        }

        let string_value_of = |cx: &mut CallContext| -> WebIdlResult<Option<UsvString>> {
            Ok(match form_data.get(cx, name.clone())? {
                Some(FormDataEntryValue::USVString(value)) => Some(value),
                _ => None,
            })
        };

        // 4. If field’s autocomplete attribute’s value contains one or more autofill detail tokens (tokens), then:
        // 1. For each token in tokens:
        let autocomplete_attribute = String::from_utf16_lossy(&autocomplete_attribute.to_utf16());
        for token in autocomplete_attribute.split(' ').filter(|token| !token.is_empty()) {
            // 1. If token is an ASCII case-insensitive match for one of the following strings, run the associated steps:
            //    - "new-password"
            //       Set data’s password member’s value to the result of executing formData’s get() method on name,
            //       and newPasswordObserved to true.
            if token.eq_ignore_ascii_case("new-password")
                && let Some(password) = string_value_of(cx)?
            {
                data.password = password;
                new_password_observed = true;
            }
            //    - "current-password"
            //       If newPasswordObserved is false, set data’s password member’s value to the result of executing
            //       formData’s get() method on name.
            //       Note: By checking that newPasswordObserved is false, new-password fields take precedence over
            //             current-password fields.
            if !new_password_observed
                && token.eq_ignore_ascii_case("current-password")
                && let Some(password) = string_value_of(cx)?
            {
                data.password = password;
            }
            //    - "photo"
            //      Set data’s iconURL member’s value to the result of executing formData’s get() method on name.
            if token.eq_ignore_ascii_case("photo")
                && let Some(photo) = string_value_of(cx)?
            {
                data.icon_url = Some(photo);
            }
            //    - "name"
            //    - "nickname"
            //      Set data’s name member’s value to the result of executing formData’s get() method on name.
            if token.eq_ignore_ascii_case("name")
                && let Some(name) = string_value_of(cx)?
            {
                data.name = Some(name);
            }
            if token.eq_ignore_ascii_case("nickname")
                && let Some(nickname) = string_value_of(cx)?
            {
                data.name = Some(nickname);
            }
            //    - "username"
            //      Set data’s id member’s value to the result of executing formData’s get() method on name.
            if token.eq_ignore_ascii_case("username")
                && let Some(username) = string_value_of(cx)?
            {
                data.parent.id = username;
            }
        }
    }

    // 7. Let c be the result of executing Create a PasswordCredential from PasswordCredentialData on data.
    //    If that threw an exception, rethrow that exception.
    // 8. Assert: c is a PasswordCredential.
    // 9. Return c.
    create_password_credential_from_data(cx.vm(), data, origin)
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#abstract-opdef-create-a-passwordcredential-from-passwordcredentialdata
pub(crate) fn create_password_credential_from_data(
    vm: &Vm,
    data: PasswordCredentialData,
    origin: Origin,
) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<PasswordCredential>> {
    // 1. Let c be a new PasswordCredential object.
    // 2. If any of the following are the empty string, throw a TypeError exception:
    //    - data’s id member’s value
    //    - data’s origin member’s value
    //      NOTE: origin cannot be an empty string at this time since it is retrieved from the current settings object
    //            in the constructor.
    //    - data’s password member’s value
    if data.parent.id.as_utf16_string().is_empty() {
        return Err(Exception::TypeError(Utf16String::from_ascii(
            b"'id' must not be empty.",
        )));
    }
    if data.password.as_utf16_string().is_empty() {
        return Err(Exception::TypeError(Utf16String::from_ascii(
            b"'password' must not be empty.",
        )));
    }

    // 3. Set c’s properties as follows:
    //    - password
    //      - data’s password member’s value
    //    - id
    //      - data’s id member’s value
    //    - iconUrl
    //      - data’s iconURL member’s value
    //    - name
    //      - data’s name member’s value
    //    - [[origin]]
    //      - data’s origin member’s value.
    //        NOTE: origin is retrieved from the current settings object in the constructor.
    // 4. Return c.
    Ok(allocate(vm, |_| PasswordCredential::new(data, origin)))
}

    relevant_settings_object(cx.realm().global_object()).origin()

impl PasswordCredential {
    pub(crate) fn new(data: PasswordCredentialData, origin: Origin) -> Self {
        Self {
            credential: Credential::new(data.parent.id, "password"),
            user_data: CredentialUserData::new(
                data.name.unwrap_or_else(|| UsvString::from_ascii(b"")),

        // 1. Let origin be the current settings object’s origin.
        let origin = current_settings_object_origin(cx);

        // 2. Let r be the result of executing Create a PasswordCredential from an HTMLFormElement given form and origin.
        // 3. If r is an exception, throw r. Otherwise, return r.
        // SAFETY: The bindings pass the wrapper of an HTMLFormElement.
        let form = unsafe { CppHTMLFormElement::from_interface(form) };

        // 1. Let r be the result of executing Create a PasswordCredential from PasswordCredentialData on data.
        // 2. If r is an exception, throw r.
        create_password_credential_from_data(cx.vm(), data, origin)
    }

    pub(crate) fn icon_url(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        Ok(self.user_data.icon_url())
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#algorithm-overview
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct AlgorithmParams {
    pub(crate) name: Utf16String,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
struct HashAlgorithmIdentifier {
    name: Utf16String,
}

fn hash_algorithm_identifier_from_value(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    hash_value: Value,
    hash_string: Option<Utf16String>,
) -> WebIdlResult<HashAlgorithmIdentifier> {
    let algorithm = if let Some(hash_string) = hash_string {
        AlgorithmIdentifier::DOMString(hash_string)
    } else if hash_value.is_object() {
        AlgorithmIdentifier::Object(hash_value.to_object(vm)?)
    } else if hash_value.is_undefined() {
        return vm
            .throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::MissingRequiredProperty, &[&"hash"])
            .map_err(Into::into);
    } else {
        AlgorithmIdentifier::DOMString(hash_value.to_utf16_string(vm)?)
    };

    let normalized_algorithm = normalize_an_algorithm(vm, realm, &algorithm, "digest")?;
    Ok(HashAlgorithmIdentifier {
        name: normalized_algorithm.parameter.name,
    })
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#concept-usage-intersection
fn usage_intersection(a: &[KeyUsage], b: &[KeyUsage]) -> Vec<KeyUsage> {
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    for &usage in a {
        if b.contains(&usage) && !result.contains(&usage) {
            result.push(usage);
        }
    }
    result.sort_unstable_by_key(|usage| *usage as u8);
    result
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#concept-normalized-usages
pub(crate) fn normalized_key_usages(usages: &[KeyUsage]) -> Vec<KeyUsage> {
    usage_intersection(
        usages,
        &[
            KeyUsage::Encrypt,
            KeyUsage::Decrypt,
            KeyUsage::Sign,
            KeyUsage::Verify,
            KeyUsage::DeriveKey,
            KeyUsage::DeriveBits,
            KeyUsage::WrapKey,
            KeyUsage::UnwrapKey,
            KeyUsage::EncapsulateKey,
            KeyUsage::EncapsulateBits,
            KeyUsage::DecapsulateKey,
            KeyUsage::DecapsulateBits,
        ],
    )
}

// https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7518#section-2
fn base64_url_bytes_encode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Utf16String {
    ak::encode_base64(bytes, ak::Base64Alphabet::Base64Url, true)
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#concept-parse-an-asn1-structure
// NB: The structure is given as its parser, whose errors are reported with `error_format`.
fn parse_an_asn1_structure<'a, T>(
    data: &'a [u8],
    structure: impl FnOnce(&'a [u8]) -> Result<(T, bool), CryptoError>,
    error_format: &str,
    exact_data: bool,
) -> Result<T, Utf16String> {
    // 1. Let data be a sequence of bytes to be parsed.
    // 2. Let structure be the ASN.1 structure to be parsed.
    // 3. Let exactData be an optional boolean value. If it is not supplied, let it be initialized to true.

    // 4. Parse data according to the Distinguished Encoding Rules of [X690], using structure as the ASN.1 structure to be decoded.
    let (value, all_consumed) =
        structure(data).map_err(|detail| libjs_rust::api::utf16_formatted(error_format, &[&detail.message()]))?;

    // 5. If exactData was specified, and all of the bytes of data were not consumed during the parsing phase, then throw a DataError.
    if exact_data && !all_consumed {
        return Err(Utf16String::from_utf8(
            "Not all bytes were consumed during the parsing phase",
        ));
    }

    // 6. Return the parsed ASN.1 structure.
    Ok(value)
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#concept-parse-a-spki
fn parse_a_subject_public_key_info(data: &[u8]) -> WebIdlResult<KeyInfo> {
    // When this specification says to parse a subjectPublicKeyInfo, the user agent must parse an ASN.1 structure,
    // with data set to the sequence of bytes to be parsed, structure as the ASN.1 structure of subjectPublicKeyInfo,
    // as specified in [RFC5280], and exactData set to true.
    parse_an_asn1_structure(
        data,
        libcrypto_rust::parse_subject_public_key_info,
        "Error parsing subjectPublicKeyInfo: {}",
        true,
    )
    .map_err(|message| Exception::Dom("DataError", message))
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#concept-parse-a-privateKeyInfo
fn parse_a_private_key_info(data: &[u8]) -> WebIdlResult<KeyInfo> {
    // When this specification says to parse a PrivateKeyInfo, the user agent must parse an ASN.1 structure
    // with data set to the sequence of bytes to be parsed, structure as the ASN.1 structure of PrivateKeyInfo,
    // as specified in [RFC5208], and exactData set to true.
    parse_an_asn1_structure(
        data,
        libcrypto_rust::parse_private_key_info,
        "Error parsing privateKeyInfo: {}",
        true,
    )
    .map_err(|message| Exception::Dom("DataError", message))
}

        Self(Rc::new(bytes))
    }

        self.0.as_slice()
    }
}

fn get_optional_buffer_source(vm: &Vm, object: Gc<Object>, name: &PropertyKey) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Bytes>> {
    if !object.has_property(vm, name)? {
        return Ok(None);
    }

    let value = object.get(vm, name)?;
    let Some(buffer_source) = buffer_source_type_of(value) else {
        return vm
            .throw_completion(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, &[&"BufferSource"])
            .map_err(Into::into);
    };

    Ok(Some(get_a_copy_of_the_bytes(vm, buffer_source)?))
}

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CShakeParams {
    output_length: u32,
    function_name: Option<Bytes>,
    customization: Option<Bytes>,
}

impl CShakeParams {
    pub(crate) fn from_value(vm: &Vm, object: Gc<Object>) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        let output_length_property = PropertyKey::from_utf8("outputLength");
        if !object.has_property(vm, &output_length_property)? {
            return vm
                .throw_completion(
                    ErrorKind::TypeError,
                    ErrorType::MissingRequiredProperty,
                    &[&"outputLength"],
                )
                .map_err(Into::into);
        }

        let output_length = object.get(vm, &output_length_property)?;

        let length = to_unsigned_long_enforcing_range(vm, output_length)?;

        let function_name = get_optional_buffer_source(vm, object, &PropertyKey::from_utf8("functionName"))?;

        let customization = get_optional_buffer_source(vm, object, &PropertyKey::from_utf8("customization"))?;

        Ok(Self {
            output_length: length,
            function_name,
            customization,
        })
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Sha;

impl AlgorithmMethods for Sha {
    // https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#sha-operations-digest
    fn digest(&self, _: Gc<Realm>, algorithm: &AlgorithmParams, data: &Bytes) -> WebIdlResult<Bytes> {
        let algorithm_name = &algorithm.name;

        let hash_kind = if matches!(algorithm_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-1")) {
            // 1. If the name member of normalizedAlgorithm is a cases-sensitive string match for "SHA-1":
            //    Let result be the result of performing the SHA-1 hash function defined in Section 6.1 of [FIPS-180-4]
            //    using message as the input message, M.
            ShaHashKind::Sha1
        } else if matches!(algorithm_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-256")) {
            // 1. If the name member of normalizedAlgorithm is a cases-sensitive string match for "SHA-256":
            //    Let result be the result of performing the SHA-256 hash function defined in Section 6.2 of
            //    [FIPS-180-4] using message as the input message, M.
            ShaHashKind::Sha256
        } else if matches!(algorithm_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-384")) {
            // 1. If the name member of normalizedAlgorithm is a cases-sensitive string match for "SHA-384":
            //    Let result be the result of performing the SHA-384 hash function defined in Section 6.5 of
            //    [FIPS-180-4] using message as the input message, M.
            ShaHashKind::Sha384
        } else if matches!(algorithm_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-512")) {
            // 1. If the name member of normalizedAlgorithm is a cases-sensitive string match for "SHA-512":
            //    Let result be the result of performing the SHA-512 hash function defined in Section 6.4 of
            //    [FIPS-180-4] using message as the input message, M.
            ShaHashKind::Sha512
        } else if matches!(algorithm_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA3-256")) {
            // https://wicg.github.io/webcrypto-modern-algos/#sha3-operations-digest
            // 1. If the name member of normalizedAlgorithm is a case-sensitive string match for "SHA3-256":
            //    Let result be the result of performing the SHA3-256 hash function defined in Section 6.1 of [FIPS-202]
            //    using the Keccak decoding of message as the input message, M.
            ShaHashKind::Sha3_256
        } else if matches!(algorithm_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA3-384")) {
            // 1. If the name member of normalizedAlgorithm is a case-sensitive string match for "SHA3-384":
            //    Let result be the result of performing the SHA3-384 hash function defined in Section 6.1 of [FIPS-202]
            //    using the Keccak decoding of message as the input message, M.
            ShaHashKind::Sha3_384
        } else if matches!(algorithm_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA3-512")) {
            // 1. If the name member of normalizedAlgorithm is a case-sensitive string match for "SHA3-512":
            //    Let result be the result of performing the SHA3-512 hash function defined in Section 6.1 of [FIPS-202]
            //    using the Keccak decoding of message as the input message, M.
            ShaHashKind::Sha3_512
        } else {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "NotSupportedError",
                libjs_rust::api::utf16_formatted("Invalid hash function '{}'", &[algorithm_name]),
            ));
        };

        let result_buffer = libcrypto_rust::sha_digest(hash_kind, data.as_slice()).map(Bytes::new);
        // 2. If performing the operation results in an error, then throw an OperationError.
        let Ok(result_buffer) = result_buffer else {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "OperationError",
                Utf16String::from_utf8("Failed to create result buffer"),
            ));
        };

        // 3. Return result.
        // https://wicg.github.io/webcrypto-modern-algos/#sha3-operations-digest
        // 3. Return the Keccak encoding of result.
        Ok(result_buffer)
    }
}

impl AlgorithmMethods for CShakeParams {
    // https://wicg.github.io/webcrypto-modern-algos/#cshake-operations-digest
    fn validate_digest_parameters(&self, _: Gc<Realm>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // NB: Step 5 throws an OperationError for the parameters that our cSHAKE does not support.
        let normalized_algorithm = self;

        let result = libcrypto_rust::cshake_validate_parameters(normalized_algorithm.output_length);
        if let Err(detail) = result {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "OperationError",
                libjs_rust::api::utf16_formatted("Hash function failed: {}", &[&detail.message()]),
            ));
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    // https://wicg.github.io/webcrypto-modern-algos/#cshake-operations-digest
    fn digest(&self, _: Gc<Realm>, algorithm: &AlgorithmParams, data: &Bytes) -> WebIdlResult<Bytes> {
        let normalized_algorithm = self;

        // 1. Let outputLength be the outputLength member of normalizedAlgorithm.
        let output_length = normalized_algorithm.output_length;

        // 2. Let functionName be the Keccak decoding of the functionName member of normalizedAlgorithm if present, or
        //    the empty bit string otherwise.
        let function_name = normalized_algorithm.function_name.as_ref();

        // 3. Let customization be the Keccak decoding of the customization member of normalizedAlgorithm if present, or
        //    the empty bit string otherwise.
        let customization = normalized_algorithm.customization.as_ref();

        // 4. If the name member of normalizedAlgorithm is a case-sensitive string match for "cSHAKE128":
        //    Let result be the result of performing the cSHAKE128 function defined in Section 3 of [NIST-SP800-185]
        //    using the Keccak decoding of message as the X input parameter, outputLength as the L input parameter,
        //    functionName as the N input parameter, and customization as the S input parameter.
        let kind = if matches!(algorithm.name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"cSHAKE128")) {
            CShakeKind::CShake128
        // 4. If the name member of normalizedAlgorithm is a case-sensitive string match for "cSHAKE256":
        //    Let result be the result of performing the cSHAKE256 function defined in Section 3 of [NIST-SP800-185]
        //    using the Keccak decoding of message as the X input parameter, outputLength as the L input parameter,
        //    functionName as the N input parameter, and customization as the S input parameter.
        } else if matches!(algorithm.name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"cSHAKE256")) {
            CShakeKind::CShake256
        } else {
            unreachable!("the algorithm is cSHAKE128 or cSHAKE256");
        };

        let result = libcrypto_rust::cshake_digest(
            kind,
            data.as_slice(),
            output_length,
            customization.map(Bytes::as_slice),
            function_name.map(Bytes::as_slice),
        )
        .map(Bytes::new);

        // 5. If performing the operation results in an error, then throw an OperationError.
        let result = result.map_err(|detail| {
            Exception::Dom(
                "OperationError",
                libjs_rust::api::utf16_formatted("Hash function failed: {}", &[&detail.message()]),
            )
        })?;

        // 6. Return the Keccak encoding of result.
        Ok(result)
    }
}

fn key_usage_to_string(usage: KeyUsage) -> &'static str {
    std::str::from_utf8(KEY_USAGES[usage as usize]).expect("a key usage is ASCII")
}

fn parse_jwk_symmetric_key(jwk: &JsonWebKey) -> WebIdlResult<Bytes> {
    let Some(base64_url_string) = &jwk.k else {
        return Err(dom_error("DataError", b"JWK has no 'k' field"));
    };

    base64_url_bytes_decode(base64_url_string)
}

fn base64_url_bytes_decode(base64_url_string: &Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<Bytes> {
    let result = ak::decode_base64(
        base64_url_string.as_units(),
        ak::Base64Alphabet::Base64Url,
        ak::LastChunkHandling::Loose,
        None,
    );
    if result.error.is_some() {
        return Err(dom_error("DataError", b"base64 decode: invalid base64url"));
    }
    Ok(Bytes::new(result.bytes))
}

// https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7517#section-4.3
fn validate_jwk_key_ops(jwk: &JsonWebKey, usages: &[KeyUsage]) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
    // Use of the "key_ops" member is OPTIONAL, unless the application requires its presence.
    let Some(key_operations) = &jwk.key_ops else {
        return Ok(());
    };

    // Duplicate key operation values MUST NOT be present in the array
    let mut seen_operations = HashSet::new();
    for key_operation in key_operations {
        if !seen_operations.insert(key_operation) {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "DataError",
                libjs_rust::api::utf16_formatted("Duplicate key operation: {}", &[key_operation]),
            ));
        }
    }

    // Multiple unrelated key operations SHOULD NOT be specified for a key because of the potential
    // vulnerabilities associated with using the same key with multiple algorithms.  Thus, the
    // combinations "sign" with "verify", "encrypt" with "decrypt", and "wrapKey" with "unwrapKey"
    // are permitted, but other combinations SHOULD NOT be used.
    let is_used_for_signing = seen_operations.contains(&Utf16String::from_ascii(b"sign"))
        || seen_operations.contains(&Utf16String::from_ascii(b"verify"));
    let is_used_for_encryption = seen_operations.contains(&Utf16String::from_ascii(b"encrypt"))
        || seen_operations.contains(&Utf16String::from_ascii(b"decrypt"));
    let is_used_for_wrapping = seen_operations.contains(&Utf16String::from_ascii(b"wrapKey"))
        || seen_operations.contains(&Utf16String::from_ascii(b"unwrapKey"));
    let number_of_operation_types =
        u8::from(is_used_for_signing) + u8::from(is_used_for_encryption) + u8::from(is_used_for_wrapping);
    if number_of_operation_types > 1 {
        return Err(dom_error(
            "DataError",
            b"Multiple unrelated key operations are specified",
        ));
    }

    // The "use" and "key_ops" JWK members SHOULD NOT be used together; however, if both are used,
    // the information they convey MUST be consistent. Applications should specify which of these
    // members they use, if either is to be used by the application.
    if let Some(key_use) = &jwk.r#use {
        for key_operation in key_operations {
            if *key_operation == Utf16String::from_ascii(b"deriveKey")
                || *key_operation == Utf16String::from_ascii(b"deriveBits")
            {
                continue;
            }
            if *key_use == Utf16String::from_ascii(b"sig")
                && *key_operation != Utf16String::from_ascii(b"sign")
                && *key_operation != Utf16String::from_ascii(b"verify")
            {
                return Err(dom_error(
                    "DataError",
                    b"use=sig but key_ops does not contain 'sign' or 'verify'",
                ));
            }
            if *key_use == Utf16String::from_ascii(b"enc")
                && (*key_operation == Utf16String::from_ascii(b"sign")
                    || *key_operation == Utf16String::from_ascii(b"verify"))
            {
                return Err(dom_error(
                    "DataError",
                    b"use=enc but key_ops contains 'sign' or 'verify'",
                ));
            }
        }
    }

    // NOTE: This validation happens in multiple places in the spec, so it is here for convenience.
    for &usage in usages {
        let usage = key_usage_to_string(usage);
        if !seen_operations.contains(&Utf16String::from_utf8(usage)) {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "DataError",
                libjs_rust::api::utf16_formatted("Missing key_ops usage: {}", &[&usage]),
            ));
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}

// NB: Keeps only the bytes that hold the first length_in_bits bits of data, and zeroes the unused low-order bits of
//     the last byte when the length is not a whole number of bytes.
fn keep_first_bits(data: &mut Vec<u8>, length_in_bits: usize) {
    let length_in_bytes = length_in_bits.div_ceil(8);
    assert!(length_in_bytes <= data.len());
    data.truncate(length_in_bytes);

    let remainder_bits = length_in_bits % 8;
    if remainder_bits != 0 {
        data[length_in_bytes - 1] &= !(0xff >> remainder_bits);
    }
}

fn generate_random_key(vm: &Vm, size_in_bits: u32) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<u8>> {
    let size_in_bits = size_in_bits as usize;
    let length_in_bytes = size_in_bits.div_ceil(8);
    let mut key_buffer = Vec::new();
    if key_buffer.try_reserve_exact(length_in_bytes).is_err() {
        return vm
            .throw_completion(ErrorKind::InternalError, ErrorType::OutOfMemory, &[])
            .map_err(Into::into);
    }
    key_buffer.resize(length_in_bytes, 0);

    libcrypto_rust::fill_with_random(&mut key_buffer).expect("OpenSSL produces random bytes");
    keep_first_bits(&mut key_buffer, size_in_bits);
    Ok(key_buffer)
}

// NB: Our KMAC implementation is byte-oriented, so it cannot use keys with a partial last byte. OpenSSL also only
//     accepts KMAC keys of up to 512 bytes.
fn validate_kmac_key_length(length_in_bits: u32) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
    if !length_in_bits.is_multiple_of(8) {
        return Err(dom_error(
            "NotSupportedError",
            b"KMAC key length must be a multiple of 8",
        ));
    }
    if length_in_bits > 512 * 8 {
        return Err(dom_error(
            "NotSupportedError",
            b"KMAC key length must not exceed 4096 bits",
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn hmac_calculate_message_digest(hash_name: &Utf16String, key: &[u8], message: &[u8]) -> WebIdlResult<Bytes> {
    let hash_kind = if matches!(hash_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-1")) {
        ShaHashKind::Sha1
    } else if matches!(hash_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-256")) {
        ShaHashKind::Sha256
    } else if matches!(hash_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-384")) {
        ShaHashKind::Sha384
    } else if matches!(hash_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-512")) {
        ShaHashKind::Sha512
    } else {
        return Err(Exception::Dom(
            "NotSupportedError",
            libjs_rust::api::utf16_formatted("Invalid hash function '{}'", &[hash_name]),
        ));
    };

    let Ok(mac) = libcrypto_rust::hmac_sign(hash_kind, key, message) else {
        return Err(dom_error("OperationError", b"Failed to compute the HMAC"));
    };
    Ok(Bytes::new(mac))
}

fn hmac_hash_block_size(hash: &HashAlgorithmIdentifier) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
    let hash_name = &hash.name;
    if matches!(hash_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-1")) {
        return Ok(64);
    }
    if matches!(hash_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-256")) {
        return Ok(64);
    }
    if matches!(hash_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-384")) {
        return Ok(128);
    }
    if matches!(hash_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"SHA-512")) {
        return Ok(128);
    }
    Err(Exception::Dom(
        "NotSupportedError",
        libjs_rust::api::utf16_formatted("Invalid hash function '{}'", &[hash_name]),
    ))
}

fn kmac_kind_from_algorithm_name(algorithm_name: &Utf16String) -> Option<KmacKind> {
    if matches!(algorithm_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"KMAC128")) {
        return Some(KmacKind::Kmac128);
    }
    if matches!(algorithm_name.as_units(), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"KMAC256")) {
        return Some(KmacKind::Kmac256);
    }
    None
}

fn kmac_calculate_mac(
    algorithm_name: &Utf16String,
    key: &[u8],
    message: &[u8],
    output_length_bits: u32,
    customization: Option<&Bytes>,
) -> WebIdlResult<Bytes> {
    let Some(kind) = kmac_kind_from_algorithm_name(algorithm_name) else {
        return Err(dom_error("OperationError", b"Unsupported KMAC algorithm"));
    };

    let mac = libcrypto_rust::kmac_sign(
        kind,
        key,
        message,
        output_length_bits,
        customization.map(Bytes::as_slice),
    )
    .map(Bytes::new);
    let Ok(mac) = mac else {
        return Err(dom_error("OperationError", b"KMAC operation failed"));
    };
    Ok(mac)
}

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct HmacImportParams {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    hash: HashAlgorithmIdentifier,
    length: Option<u32>,
}

impl HmacImportParams {
    pub(crate) fn from_value(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, object: Gc<Object>) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        let hash_value = object.get(vm, &PropertyKey::from_utf8("hash"))?;
        let hash = hash_algorithm_identifier_from_value(vm, realm, hash_value, None)?;

        let mut length = None;
        let length_property = PropertyKey::from_utf8("length");
        if object.has_property(vm, &length_property)? {
            let length_value = object.get(vm, &length_property)?;
            length = Some(to_unsigned_long_enforcing_range(vm, length_value)?);
        }

        Ok(Self { hash, length })
    }
}
