//! URLSearchParams, https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-urlsearchparams

use core::cell::{self, Cell, RefCell};
use core::ops::Deref;

use ak::{Utf16String, Utf16StringUnits};
use encoding_rs::UTF_8;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Object, Trace};
use liburl_rust::url::form_urlencoded;

use super::url::URL;
use super::url_input;
use crate::bindings::conversions::UsvString;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, implementation_of};
use crate::bindings::iterable::{IterationKind, PairIterable};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};

/// The union (sequence<sequence<USVString>> or record<USVString, USVString> or USVString) of
/// DOMURL/URLSearchParams.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) enum USVStringSequenceSequenceOrUSVStringUSVStringRecordOrUSVString {
    Sequence(Vec<Vec<UsvString>>),
    Record(Vec<(UsvString, UsvString)>),
    USVString(UsvString),
}

type Init = USVStringSequenceSequenceOrUSVStringUSVStringRecordOrUSVString;

/// A name-value tuple.
pub(crate) type Tuple = (UsvString, UsvString);

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct URLSearchParams {
    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlsearchparams-list
    #[gc(untraced)]
    list: RefCell<Vec<Tuple>>,
    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlsearchparams-url-object
    url_object: Cell<Option<Ref<URL>>>,
}

impl Wrappable for URLSearchParams {}

fn code_units(string: &UsvString) -> impl Iterator<Item = u16> + '_ {
    let (ascii, utf16) = match string.units() {
        Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(bytes) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(bytes) => (bytes, &[][..]),
        Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => (&[][..], code_units),
    };
    ascii.iter().map(|byte| u16::from(*byte)).chain(utf16.iter().copied())
}

// https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlencoded-string-parser
pub(crate) fn parse_query(input: &str) -> Vec<Tuple> {
    form_urlencoded::parse(input.as_bytes())
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(name, value)| (UsvString::from_utf8(&name), UsvString::from_utf8(&value)))
        .collect()
}

impl URLSearchParams {
    pub(crate) fn new(list: Vec<Tuple>, url_object: Option<Ref<URL>>) -> Self {
        Self {
            list: RefCell::new(list),
            url_object: Cell::new(url_object),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_list(&self, list: Vec<Tuple>) {
        *self.list.borrow_mut() = list;
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-urlsearchparams-urlsearchparams
    pub(crate) fn construct(_: &mut CallContext, init: Init) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. If init is a string and starts with U+003F (?), then remove the first code point from init.
        let init = match init {
            Init::USVString(string) => Init::USVString(string.strip_ascii_prefix(b'?').unwrap_or(string)),
            init => init,
        };

        // 2. Initialize this with init.
        Ok(Self::new(Self::initialize(init)?, None))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#urlsearchparams-initialize
    fn initialize(init: Init) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<Tuple>> {
        match init {
            // 1. If init is a sequence, then for each innerSequence of init:
            Init::Sequence(sequence) => sequence
                .into_iter()
                .map(|inner_sequence| {
                    // 1. If innerSequence's size is not 2, then throw a TypeError.
                    let [name, value]: [UsvString; 2] = inner_sequence.try_into().map_err(|_| {
                        Exception::TypeError(Utf16String::from_utf8("Expected each pair to contain exactly 2 items"))
                    })?;

                    // 2. Append (innerSequence[0], innerSequence[1]) to query's list.
                    Ok((name, value))
                })
                .collect(),
            // 2. Otherwise, if init is a record, then for each name → value of init, append (name, value) to query's
            //    list.
            Init::Record(record) => Ok(record),
            // 3. Otherwise:
            //     1. Assert: init is a string.
            //     2. Set query's list to the result of parsing init.
            Init::USVString(string) => Ok(parse_query(&string.to_utf8())),
        }
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlsearchparams-update
    fn update(&self) {
        // 1. If query's URL object is null, then return.
        let Some(url_object) = self.url_object.get() else {
            return;
        };

        // 2. Let serializedQuery be the serialization of query's list.
        let serialized_query = self.serialize();

        // 3. If serializedQuery is the empty string, then set serializedQuery to null.
        let serialized_query = (!serialized_query.is_empty()).then_some(serialized_query.as_str());

        // 4. Set query's URL object's URL's query to serializedQuery.
        url_object.set_query(serialized_query);
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlencoded-serializer
    pub(crate) fn serialize(&self) -> String {
        let list = self.list.borrow();
        form_urlencoded::serialize(
            list.iter()
                .map(|(name, value)| (url_input(name.units()), url_input(value.units()))),
            UTF_8,
        )
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-urlsearchparams-size
    pub(crate) fn size(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        // The size getter steps are to return this's list's size.
        Ok(u32::try_from(self.list.borrow().len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-urlsearchparams-append
    pub(crate) fn append(&self, _: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Append (name, value) to this's list.
        self.list.borrow_mut().push((name, value));

        // 2. Update this.
        self.update();
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-urlsearchparams-delete
    pub(crate) fn delete(&self, _: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString, value: Option<UsvString>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        match value {
            // 1. If value is given, then remove all tuples whose name is name and value is value from this's list.
            Some(value) => self
                .list
                .borrow_mut()
                .retain(|(tuple_name, tuple_value)| *tuple_name != name || *tuple_value != value),
            // 2. Otherwise, remove all tuples whose name is name from this's list.
            None => self.list.borrow_mut().retain(|(tuple_name, _)| *tuple_name != name),
        }

        // 3. Update this.
        self.update();
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-urlsearchparams-get
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, _: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<Option<UsvString>> {
        // The get(name) method steps are to return the value of the first tuple whose name is name in this's list, if
        // there is such a tuple; otherwise null.
        Ok(self
            .list
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .find(|(tuple_name, _)| *tuple_name == name)
            .map(|(_, tuple_value)| tuple_value.clone()))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-urlsearchparams-getall
    pub(crate) fn get_all(&self, _: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<UsvString>> {
        // The getAll(name) method steps are to return the values of all tuples whose name is name in this's list, in
        // list order; otherwise the empty sequence.
        Ok(self
            .list
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .filter(|(tuple_name, _)| *tuple_name == name)
            .map(|(_, tuple_value)| tuple_value.clone())
            .collect())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-urlsearchparams-has
    pub(crate) fn has(&self, _: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString, value: Option<UsvString>) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        let list = self.list.borrow();
        match value {
            // 1. If value is given and there is a tuple whose name is name and value is value in this's list, then
            //    return true.
            Some(value)
                if list
                    .iter()
                    .any(|(tuple_name, tuple_value)| *tuple_name == name && *tuple_value == value) =>
            {
                return Ok(true);
            }
            // 2. If value is not given and there is a tuple whose name is name in this's list, then return true.
            None if list.iter().any(|(tuple_name, _)| *tuple_name == name) => return Ok(true),
            _ => {}
        }

        // 3. Return false.
        Ok(false)
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-urlsearchparams-set
    pub(crate) fn set(&self, _: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        {
            let mut list = self.list.borrow_mut();

            // 1. If this's list contains any tuples whose name is name, then set the value of the first such tuple
            //    to value and remove the others.
            if list.iter().any(|(tuple_name, _)| *tuple_name == name) {
                let mut is_first = true;
                list.retain_mut(|(tuple_name, tuple_value)| {
                    if *tuple_name != name {
                        return true;
                    }
                    if is_first {
                        is_first = false;
                        *tuple_value = value.clone();
                        return true;
                    }
                    false
                });
            }
            // 2. Otherwise, append (name, value) to this's list.
            else {
                list.push((name, value));
            }
        }

        // 3. Update this.
        self.update();
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-urlsearchparams-sort
    pub(crate) fn sort(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Set this's list to the result of sorting in ascending order this's list, with a being less than b if a's
        //    name is code unit less than b's name.
        self.list
            .borrow_mut()
            .sort_by(|(a_name, _), (b_name, _)| code_units(a_name).cmp(code_units(b_name)));

        // 2. Update this.
        self.update();
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#urlsearchparams-stringification-behavior
    pub(crate) fn to_string(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The stringification behavior steps are to return the serialization of this's list.
        Ok(Utf16String::from_ascii(self.serialize().as_bytes()))
    }
}

impl PairIterable for URLSearchParams {
    type Key = UsvString;
    type Value = UsvString;
    type Target = Ref<URLSearchParams>;

    fn iteration_target(_: &CallContext, wrapper: Gc<Object>, _: IterationKind) -> Self::Target {
        implementation_of(wrapper)
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-dfn-value-pairs-to-iterate-over
    fn value_pairs_to_iterate_over(target: &Self::Target) -> impl Deref<Target = [(UsvString, UsvString)]> + '_ {
        // The value pairs to iterate over are this's list's tuples with the key being the name and the value being the
        // value.
        cell::Ref::map(target.list.borrow(), Vec::as_slice)
    }
}

//! URL, https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-class

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};
use liburl_rust::origin::Origin;
use liburl_rust::url::{ExcludeFragment, State};
use liburl_rust::{BasicParseOptions, Url, basic_parse, basic_parse_with_state_override};

use super::url_input;
use super::url_search_params::{URLSearchParams, parse_query};
use crate::bindings::conversions::{CppInterface, UsvString};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::file_api::blob::AnyBlob;

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// Adds an entry to the blob URL store for the Blob or File whose cell the call borrows, and returns the URL as a
    /// raw AK::Utf16String that the caller owns.
    fn web_url_create_object_url_for_blob(blob: *mut c_void) -> usize;

    /// Adds an entry to the blob URL store for the MediaSource that the wrapper wraps, and returns the URL as a raw
    /// AK::Utf16String that the caller owns.
    fn web_url_create_object_url_for_media_source(media_source: *mut c_void) -> usize;

    /// Runs the revokeObjectURL(url) steps for the URL, a raw AK::Utf16String that the call borrows.
    fn web_url_revoke_object_url(url: usize);
}

/// The union (Blob or MediaSource) of DOMURL/URL.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) enum BlobOrMediaSource {
    Blob(AnyBlob),
    MediaSource(CppInterface),
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
#[expect(
    clippy::upper_case_acronyms,
    reason = "the bindings name the implementation after the interface"
)]
pub(crate) struct URL {
    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-url
    #[gc(untraced)]
    url: RefCell<Url>,
    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query-object
    query: Cell<Option<Ref<URLSearchParams>>>,
}

impl Wrappable for URL {}

// https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#api-url-parser
fn parse_api_url(url: &UsvString, base: Option<&UsvString>) -> Option<Url> {
    // 1. Let parsedBase be null.
    // 2. If base is non-null:
    let parsed_base = match base {
        // 1. Set parsedBase to the result of running the basic URL parser on base.
        // 2. If parsedBase is failure, then return failure.
        Some(base) => Some(basic_parse(url_input(base.units()), BasicParseOptions::new())?),
        None => None,
    };

    // 3. Return the result of running the basic URL parser on url with parsedBase.
    let mut options = BasicParseOptions::new();
    if let Some(parsed_base) = &parsed_base {
        options = options.base_url(parsed_base);
    }
    basic_parse(url_input(url.units()), options)
}

impl URL {
    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-initialize
    fn initialize(url_record: Url) -> Self {
        // OPTIMIZATION: Defer creating and initializing the query object until searchParams is accessed.
        // 2. Set url's URL to urlRecord.
        Self {
            url: RefCell::new(url_record),
            query: Cell::new(None),
        }
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-initialize
    // NB: The steps of initialize that searchParams defers.
    fn initialize_query_object(this: &Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) -> Ref<URLSearchParams> {
        // 1. Let query be urlRecord's query, if that is non-null; otherwise the empty string.
        let url = this.url.borrow();
        let query = url.query().unwrap_or("");

        // 3. Set url's query object to a new URLSearchParams object.
        // 4. Initialize url's query object with query.
        // 5. Set url's query object's URL object to url.
        let query_object = allocate(vm, |_| URLSearchParams::new(parse_query(query), Some(*this)));
        this.query.set(Some(query_object));
        query_object
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-url
    pub(crate) fn construct(_: &mut CallContext, url: UsvString, base: Option<UsvString>) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Let parsedURL be the result of running the API URL parser on url with base, if given.
        // 2. If parsedURL is failure, then throw a TypeError.
        let parsed_url = parse_api_url(&url, base.as_ref())
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::TypeError(Utf16String::from_utf8("Invalid URL")))?;

        // 3. Initialize this with parsedURL.
        Ok(Self::initialize(parsed_url))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-parse
    pub(crate) fn parse(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        url: UsvString,
        base: Option<UsvString>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<Self>>> {
        // 1. Let parsedURL be the result of running the API URL parser on url with base, if given.
        // 2. If parsedURL is failure, then return null.
        let Some(parsed_url) = parse_api_url(&url, base.as_ref()) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };

        // 3. Let url be a new URL object.
        // 4. Initialize url with parsedURL.
        // 5. Return url.
        Ok(Some(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| Self::initialize(parsed_url))))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-canparse
    pub(crate) fn can_parse(_: &mut CallContext, url: UsvString, base: Option<UsvString>) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let parsedURL be the result of running the API URL parser on url with base, if given.
        // 2. If parsedURL is failure, then return false.
        // 3. Return true.
        Ok(parse_api_url(&url, base.as_ref()).is_some())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-createObjectURL
    pub(crate) fn create_object_url(_: &mut CallContext, obj: BlobOrMediaSource) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The createObjectURL(obj) static method must return the result of adding an entry to the blob URL store for
        // obj.
        // SAFETY: The object is live, and LibWeb returns a string that the caller owns.
        Ok(unsafe {
            Utf16String::from_raw_owned(match obj {
                BlobOrMediaSource::Blob(blob) => web_url_create_object_url_for_blob(blob.cell_into_abi()),
                BlobOrMediaSource::MediaSource(media_source) => {
                    web_url_create_object_url_for_media_source(media_source.wrapper().as_ptr().cast())
                }
            })
        })
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-revokeObjectURL
    pub(crate) fn revoke_object_url(_: &mut CallContext, url: Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // SAFETY: The string outlives the call, which borrows it.
        unsafe { web_url_revoke_object_url(url.raw_identity()) };
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#extract-an-origin
    pub(crate) fn extract_an_origin(&self) -> Origin {
        // Objects implementing the URL interface's extract an origin steps are to return this's URL's origin.
        self.url.borrow().origin()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_query(&self, query: Option<&str>) {
        self.url.borrow_mut().set_query(query);
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-href
    pub(crate) fn href(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // The href getter steps and the toJSON() method steps are to return the serialization of this's URL.
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(
            self.url.borrow().serialize(ExcludeFragment::No).as_bytes(),
        ))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-tojson
    pub(crate) fn to_json(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // The href getter steps and the toJSON() method steps are to return the serialization of this's URL.
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(
            self.url.borrow().serialize(ExcludeFragment::No).as_bytes(),
        ))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-dom-url-href②
    pub(crate) fn set_href(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let parsedURL be the result of running the basic URL parser on the given value.
        // 2. If parsedURL is failure, then throw a TypeError.
        let parsed_url = basic_parse(url_input(value.units()), BasicParseOptions::new())
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::TypeError(Utf16String::from_utf8("Invalid URL")))?;

        // 3. Set this's URL to parsedURL.
        *self.url.borrow_mut() = parsed_url;

        if let Some(query_object) = self.query.get() {
            // 4. Empty this's query object's list.
            // 5. Let query be this's URL's query.
            // 6. If query is non-null, then set this's query object's list to the result of parsing query.
            query_object.set_list(self.url.borrow().query().map(parse_query).unwrap_or_default());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-origin
    pub(crate) fn origin(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // The origin getter steps are to return the serialization of this's URL's origin. [HTML]
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(self.url.borrow().origin().serialize().as_bytes()))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-protocol
    pub(crate) fn protocol(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // The protocol getter steps are to return this's URL's scheme, followed by U+003A (:).
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(
            format!("{}:", self.url.borrow().scheme()).as_bytes(),
        ))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-dom-url-protocol%E2%91%A0
    pub(crate) fn set_protocol(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The protocol setter steps are to basic URL parse the given value, followed by U+003A (:), with this's URL as
        // url and scheme start state as state override.
        let value_with_colon = format!("{}:", value.to_utf8());
        basic_parse_with_state_override(
            value_with_colon.as_str(),
            &mut self.url.borrow_mut(),
            State::SchemeStart,
            None,
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-username
    pub(crate) fn username(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // The username getter steps are to return this's URL's username.
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(self.url.borrow().username().as_bytes()))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-dom-url-username%E2%91%A0
    pub(crate) fn set_username(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let mut url = self.url.borrow_mut();

        // 1. If this's URL cannot have a username/password/port, then return.
        if url.cannot_have_a_username_or_password_or_port() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Set the username given this's URL and the given value.
        url.set_username(url_input(value.units()));
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-password
    pub(crate) fn password(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // The password getter steps are to return this's URL's password.
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(self.url.borrow().password().as_bytes()))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-dom-url-password%E2%91%A0
    pub(crate) fn set_password(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let mut url = self.url.borrow_mut();

        // 1. If this's URL cannot have a username/password/port, then return.
        if url.cannot_have_a_username_or_password_or_port() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Set the password given this's URL and the given value.
        url.set_password(url_input(value.units()));
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-host
    pub(crate) fn host(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // 1. Let url be this's URL.
        let url = self.url.borrow();

        // 2. If url's host is null, then return the empty string.
        let Some(host) = url.serialized_host() else {
            return Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(b""));
        };

        // 3. If url's port is null, return url's host, serialized.
        let Some(port) = url.port() else {
            return Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(host.as_bytes()));
        };

        // 4. Return url's host, serialized, followed by U+003A (:) and url's port, serialized.
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(format!("{host}:{port}").as_bytes()))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-host
    pub(crate) fn set_host(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let mut url = self.url.borrow_mut();

        // 1. If this's URL has an opaque path, then return.
        if url.has_opaque_path() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Basic URL parse the given value with this's URL as url and host state as state override.
        basic_parse_with_state_override(url_input(value.units()), &mut url, State::Host, None);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-hostname
    pub(crate) fn hostname(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // 1. If this's URL's host is null, then return the empty string.
        // 2. Return this's URL's host, serialized.
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(
            self.url.borrow().serialized_host().unwrap_or("").as_bytes(),
        ))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-dom-url-hostname①
    pub(crate) fn set_hostname(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let mut url = self.url.borrow_mut();

        // 1. If this's URL has an opaque path, then return.
        if url.has_opaque_path() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Basic URL parse the given value with this's URL as url and hostname state as state override.
        basic_parse_with_state_override(url_input(value.units()), &mut url, State::Hostname, None);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-port
    pub(crate) fn port(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // 1. If this's URL's port is null, then return the empty string.
        // 2. Return this's URL's port, serialized.
        let port = self
            .url
            .borrow()
            .port()
            .map(|port| port.to_string())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(port.as_bytes()))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-dom-url-port%E2%91%A0
    pub(crate) fn set_port(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let mut url = self.url.borrow_mut();

        // 1. If this's URL cannot have a username/password/port, then return.
        if url.cannot_have_a_username_or_password_or_port() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. If the given value is the empty string, then set this's URL's port to null.
        if value.length_in_code_units() == 0 {
            url.set_port(None);
        }
        // 3. Otherwise, basic URL parse the given value with this's URL as url and port state as state override.
        else {
            basic_parse_with_state_override(url_input(value.units()), &mut url, State::Port, None);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-pathname
    pub(crate) fn pathname(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // The pathname getter steps are to return the result of URL path serializing this's URL.
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(self.url.borrow().serialize_path().as_bytes()))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-dom-url-pathname%E2%91%A0
    pub(crate) fn set_pathname(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let mut url = self.url.borrow_mut();

        // 1. If this's URL has an opaque path, then return.
        if url.has_opaque_path() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Empty this's URL's path.
        url.set_path(core::iter::empty());

        // 3. Basic URL parse the given value with this's URL as url and path start state as state override.
        basic_parse_with_state_override(url_input(value.units()), &mut url, State::PathStart, None);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-search
    pub(crate) fn search(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // 1. If this's URL's query is either null or the empty string, then return the empty string.
        // 2. Return U+003F (?), followed by this's URL's query.
        let query = match self.url.borrow().query() {
            None | Some("") => String::new(),
            Some(query) => format!("?{query}"),
        };
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(query.as_bytes()))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-dom-url-search%E2%91%A0
    pub(crate) fn set_search(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let url be this's URL.
        let mut url = self.url.borrow_mut();

        // 2. If the given value is the empty string, then set url's query to null, empty this's query object's list,
        //    and return.
        if value.length_in_code_units() == 0 {
            url.set_query(None);
            if let Some(query_object) = self.query.get() {
                query_object.set_list(Vec::new());
            }
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 3. Let input be the given value with a single leading U+003F (?) removed, if any.
        let input = value.strip_ascii_prefix(b'?').unwrap_or(value);

        // 4. Set url's query to the empty string.
        url.set_query(Some(""));

        // 5. Basic URL parse input with url as url and query state as state override.
        basic_parse_with_state_override(url_input(input.units()), &mut url, State::Query, None);

        // 6. Set this's query object's list to the result of parsing url's query.
        if let Some(query_object) = self.query.get() {
            query_object.set_list(url.query().map(parse_query).unwrap_or_default());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-searchparams
    pub(crate) fn search_params(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<URLSearchParams>> {
        // The searchParams getter steps are to return this's query object.
        Ok(this
            .query
            .get()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| Self::initialize_query_object(this, cx.vm())))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-hash
    pub(crate) fn hash(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // 1. If this's URL's fragment is either null or the empty string, then return the empty string.
        // 2. Return U+0023 (#), followed by this's URL's fragment.
        let fragment = match self.url.borrow().fragment() {
            None | Some("") => String::new(),
            Some(fragment) => format!("#{fragment}"),
        };
        Ok(UsvString::from_ascii(fragment.as_bytes()))
    }

    // https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-dom-url-hash%E2%91%A0
    pub(crate) fn set_hash(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let mut url = self.url.borrow_mut();

        // 1. If the given value is the empty string, then set this's URL's fragment to null and return.
        if value.length_in_code_units() == 0 {
            url.set_fragment(None);
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Let input be the given value with a single leading U+0023 (#) removed, if any.
        let input = value.strip_ascii_prefix(b'#').unwrap_or(value);

        // 3. Set this's URL's fragment to the empty string.
        url.set_fragment(Some(""));

        // 4. Basic URL parse input with this's URL as url and fragment state as state override.
        basic_parse_with_state_override(url_input(input.units()), &mut url, State::Fragment, None);
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! TextDecoderStream, https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-textdecoderstream

use core::cell::RefCell;

use ak::Utf16String;
use encoding_rs::Encoding;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, PrimitiveString, Trace, Value};
use libtextcodec_rust::{DecodingFailed, StreamingDecoder, encoding_for_label};

use crate::bindings::conversions::{BufferSourceRules, UsvString, to_buffer_source};
use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;
use crate::bindings::interface::Wrappable;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::encoding::text_decoder::TextDecoderOptions;
use crate::streams::generic_transform_stream::{TransformSteps, create_and_set_up};
use crate::streams::readable_stream::ReadableStream;
use crate::streams::transform_stream::TransformStream;
use crate::streams::writable_stream::WritableStream;

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct TextDecoderStream {
    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#textdecoder-encoding
    #[gc(untraced)]
    encoding: &'static Encoding,
    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#textdecoder-error-mode
    fatal: bool,
    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#textdecoder-ignore-bom-flag
    ignore_bom: bool,
    // https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#generictransformstream-transform
    transform: Ref<TransformStream>,
}

impl Wrappable for TextDecoderStream {}

#[expect(
    clippy::unnecessary_wraps,
    reason = "the bindings call every method of an implementation for its WebIDL result, whether or not it can fail"
)]
impl TextDecoderStream {
    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textdecoderstream
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        label: Utf16String,
        options: TextDecoderOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Let encoding be the result of getting an encoding from label.
        // 2. If encoding is failure or replacement, then throw a RangeError.
        let encoding = encoding_for_label(label.as_units())
            .filter(|&encoding| encoding != encoding_rs::REPLACEMENT)
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::RangeError(Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Invalid encoding")))?;

        // 3. Let errorMode be "fatal" if options["fatal"] is true; otherwise "replacement".
        // 4. Set up a text decoder stream with this, encoding, errorMode, and options["ignoreBOM"].
        Ok(Self::set_up(cx, encoding, options.fatal, options.ignore_bom))
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#set-up-a-text-decoder-stream
    pub(crate) fn set_up(cx: &CallContext, encoding: &'static Encoding, fatal: bool, ignore_bom: bool) -> Self {
        // 1. Assert: encoding is not replacement.
        assert!(
            encoding != encoding_rs::REPLACEMENT,
            "a text decoder stream has an encoding with a decoder"
        );

        // 2. Set stream's encoding to encoding.
        // 3. Set stream's error mode to errorMode.
        // 4. Set stream's ignore BOM to ignoreBOM.
        // 5. Set stream's decoder to a new instance of encoding's decoder.
        // 6. Set stream's I/O queue to a new I/O queue.
        // NB: The decoder holds the I/O queue, and whether the BOM was seen.
        let decoder = Decoder {
            decoder: RefCell::new(StreamingDecoder::new(encoding, fatal, ignore_bom)),
        };

        // 7. Let transformAlgorithm be an algorithm which takes a chunk argument and runs the decode and enqueue a
        //    chunk algorithm with stream and chunk.
        // 8. Let flushAlgorithm be an algorithm which takes no arguments and runs the flush and enqueue algorithm with
        //    stream.
        // 9. Let transformStream be a new TransformStream.
        // 10. Set up transformStream with transformAlgorithm set to transformAlgorithm and flushAlgorithm set to
        //     flushAlgorithm.
        // 11. Set stream's transform to transformStream.
        Self {
            encoding,
            fatal,
            ignore_bom,
            transform: create_and_set_up(cx, decoder),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn transform(&self) -> Ref<TransformStream> {
        self.transform
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textdecoder-encoding
    pub(crate) fn encoding(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The encoding getter steps are to return this's encoding's name, ASCII lowercased.
        let name = self.encoding.name().to_ascii_lowercase();
        Ok(Utf16String::from_ascii(name.as_bytes()))
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textdecoder-fatal
    pub(crate) fn fatal(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The fatal getter steps are to return true if this's error mode is "fatal", otherwise false.
        Ok(self.fatal)
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textdecoder-ignorebom
    pub(crate) fn ignore_bom(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The ignoreBOM getter steps are to return this's ignore BOM.
        Ok(self.ignore_bom)
    }

    // https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-generictransformstream-readable
    pub(crate) fn readable(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<ReadableStream>> {
        // The readable getter steps are to return this's transform.[[readable]].
        Ok(self.transform.readable_stream())
    }

    // https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-generictransformstream-writable
    pub(crate) fn writable(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<WritableStream>> {
        // The writable getter steps are to return this's transform.[[writable]].
        Ok(self.transform.writable_stream())
    }
}

/// The decoder of a TextDecoderStream, with its I/O queue, which the algorithms of the stream's transform run on.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct Decoder {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    decoder: RefCell<StreamingDecoder>,
}

static DECODER_CLASS: EmbedderClass<Decoder> = EmbedderClass::new("TextDecoderStreamDecoder");

impl EmbedderValue for Decoder {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &DECODER_CLASS;
}

/// Enqueues the output of the decoder in the transform as a string, unless it is the empty string.
fn enqueue_output_chunk(cx: &CallContext, transform: Ref<TransformStream>, output: &[u16]) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
    let output_chunk = UsvString::from_utf16_replacing_lone_surrogates(output).into_utf16_string();
    if !output_chunk.is_empty() {
        TransformStream::enqueue(
            transform,
            cx.vm(),
            Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(cx.vm(), output_chunk)),
        )?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn decoding_failed(_: DecodingFailed) -> Exception {
    Exception::TypeError(Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Decoding failed"))
}

impl TransformSteps for Decoder {
    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#decode-and-enqueue-a-chunk
    fn transform(&self, cx: &CallContext, transform: Ref<TransformStream>, chunk: Value) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let bufferSource be the result of converting chunk to an AllowSharedBufferSource.
        let rules = BufferSourceRules {
            allow_shared: true,
            allow_resizable: false,
        };
        let buffer_source = to_buffer_source(cx.vm(), chunk, &rules)?;

        // 2. Push a copy of bufferSource to decoder's I/O queue.
        // 3. Let output be the I/O queue of scalar values « end-of-queue ».
        // 4. While true:
        //     1. Let item be the result of reading from decoder's I/O queue.
        //     2. If item is end-of-queue:
        //         1. Let outputChunk be the result of running serialize I/O queue with decoder and output.
        //         2. If outputChunk is not the empty string, then enqueue outputChunk in decoder's transform.
        //         3. Return.
        //     3. Let result be the result of processing an item with item, decoder's decoder, decoder's I/O queue,
        //        output, and decoder's error mode.
        //     4. If result is error, then throw a TypeError.
        // NB: The decoder decodes the bytes as more input to follow, and keeps what it cannot decode yet.
        let mut decoder = self.decoder.borrow_mut();
        // SAFETY: Decoding runs no script and allocates no cell, so nothing detaches, resizes or frees the buffer of
        //         the chunk while its bytes are read.
        let output =
            unsafe { buffer_source.with_bytes(|bytes| decoder.decode(bytes, true)) }.map_err(decoding_failed)?;
        enqueue_output_chunk(cx, transform, &output)
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#flush-and-enqueue
    fn flush(&self, cx: &CallContext, transform: Ref<TransformStream>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let output be the I/O queue of scalar values « end-of-queue ».
        // 2. While true:
        //     1. Let item be the result of reading from decoder's I/O queue.
        //     2. Let result be the result of processing an item with item, decoder's decoder, decoder's I/O queue,
        //        output, and decoder's error mode.
        //     3. If result is finished:
        //         1. Let outputChunk be the result of running serialize I/O queue with decoder and output.
        //         2. If outputChunk is not the empty string, then enqueue outputChunk in decoder's transform.
        //         3. Return.
        //     4. Otherwise, if result is error, throw a TypeError.
        // NB: The decoder's I/O queue holds no more bytes, so the decoder decodes the end of the input.
        let output = self.decoder.borrow_mut().decode(&[], false).map_err(decoding_failed)?;
        enqueue_output_chunk(cx, transform, &output)
    }
}

//! TextDecoder, https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-textdecoder

use core::cell::RefCell;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::Trace;
use libtextcodec_rust::{DecodingFailed, StreamingDecoder, encoding_for_label};

use crate::bindings::conversions::{BufferSource, UsvString};
use crate::bindings::interface::Wrappable;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::webidl::buffers::AllowSharedBufferSource;

/// The dictionary TextDecoderOptions of Encoding/TextDecoder.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) struct TextDecoderOptions {
    pub(crate) fatal: bool,
    pub(crate) ignore_bom: bool,
}

/// The dictionary TextDecodeOptions of Encoding/TextDecoder.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) struct TextDecodeOptions {
    pub(crate) stream: bool,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct TextDecoder {
    /// The encoding, the error mode and the ignore BOM flag of the decoder, with the decoder of the encoding, which
    /// holds the I/O queue of a decode() that asked for more input to follow.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    decoder: RefCell<StreamingDecoder>,
}

impl Wrappable for TextDecoder {}

#[expect(
    clippy::unnecessary_wraps,
    reason = "the bindings call every method of an implementation for its WebIDL result, whether or not it can fail"
)]
impl TextDecoder {
    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textdecoder
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        _: &mut CallContext,
        label: Utf16String,
        options: TextDecoderOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Let encoding be the result of getting an encoding from label.
        // 2. If encoding is failure or replacement, then throw a RangeError.
        let encoding = encoding_for_label(label.as_units())
            .filter(|&encoding| encoding != encoding_rs::REPLACEMENT)
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::RangeError(Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Invalid encoding")))?;

        // 3. Set this's encoding to encoding.
        // 4. If options["fatal"] is true, then set this's error mode to "fatal".
        // 5. Set this's ignore BOM to options["ignoreBOM"].
        Ok(Self {
            decoder: RefCell::new(StreamingDecoder::new(encoding, options.fatal, options.ignore_bom)),
        })
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textdecoder-encoding
    pub(crate) fn encoding(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The encoding getter steps are to return this's encoding's name, ASCII lowercased.
        let name = self.decoder.borrow().encoding().name().to_ascii_lowercase();
        Ok(Utf16String::from_ascii(name.as_bytes()))
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textdecoder-fatal
    pub(crate) fn fatal(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The fatal getter steps are to return true if this's error mode is "fatal", otherwise false.
        Ok(self.decoder.borrow().fatal())
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textdecoder-ignorebom
    pub(crate) fn ignore_bom(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The ignoreBOM getter steps are to return this's ignore BOM.
        Ok(self.decoder.borrow().ignore_bom())
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textdecoder-decode
    pub(crate) fn decode(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        input: Option<AllowSharedBufferSource>,
        options: TextDecodeOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        // 1. If this's do not flush is false, then set this's decoder to a new instance of this's encoding's decoder,
        //    this's I/O queue to the I/O queue of bytes « end-of-queue », and this's BOM seen to false.
        // 2. Set this's do not flush to options["stream"].
        // 3. If input is given, then push a copy of input to this's I/O queue.
        // 4. Let output be the I/O queue of scalar values « end-of-queue ».
        // 5. While true:
        //     1. Let item be the result of reading from this's I/O queue.
        //     2. If item is end-of-queue and this's do not flush is true, then return the result of running
        //        serialize I/O queue with this and output.
        //     3. Let result be the result of processing an item with item, this's decoder, this's I/O queue, output,
        //        and this's error mode.
        //     4. If result is finished, then return the result of running serialize I/O queue with this and output.
        //     5. If result is error:
        //         1. Set this's do not flush to false.
        //         2. Throw a TypeError.
        // NB: The decoder holds the I/O queue and whether the BOM was seen, and is replaced at the end of a call that
        //     does not stream or that throws, where step 1 replaces it in the next call.
        let mut decoder = self.decoder.borrow_mut();
        let input = input.map(BufferSource::from);
        let decoded = match &input {
            // SAFETY: Decoding runs no script and allocates no cell, so nothing detaches, resizes or frees the
            //         buffer of the input while its bytes are read.
            Some(input) => unsafe { input.with_bytes(|bytes| decoder.decode(bytes, options.stream)) },
            None => decoder.decode(&[], options.stream),
        };
        let decoded =
            decoded.map_err(|DecodingFailed| Exception::TypeError(Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Decoding failed")))?;
        Ok(UsvString::from_utf16_replacing_lone_surrogates(&decoded))
    }
}

/// The UTF-8 encoder of a TextEncoderStream, with its leading surrogate, which the algorithms of the stream's
/// transform run on.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct Encoder {
    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#textencoderstream-pending-high-surrogate
    leading_surrogate: Cell<Option<u16>>,
}

static ENCODER_CLASS: EmbedderClass<Encoder> = EmbedderClass::new("TextEncoderStreamEncoder");

impl EmbedderValue for Encoder {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &ENCODER_CLASS;
}

/// The bytes of U+FFFD (�) in UTF-8.
const REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER_UTF8_BYTES: [u8; 3] = [0xEF, 0xBF, 0xBD];

impl Encoder {
    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#convert-code-unit-to-scalar-value
    fn convert_code_unit_to_scalar_value(&self, item: u16, input_position: &mut usize) -> Option<char> {
        // 1. If encoder's leading surrogate is non-null:
        if let Some(leading_surrogate) = self.leading_surrogate.get() {
            // 1. Let leadingSurrogate be encoder's leading surrogate.
            // 2. Set encoder's leading surrogate to null.
            self.leading_surrogate.set(None);

            // 3. If item is a trailing surrogate, then return a scalar value from surrogates given leadingSurrogate
            //    and item.
            if is_trailing_surrogate(item) {
                return Some(scalar_value_from_surrogates(leading_surrogate, item));
            }

            // 4. Restore item to input.
            *input_position -= 1;

            // 5. Return U+FFFD (�).
            return Some(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER);
        }

        // 2. If item is a leading surrogate, then set encoder's leading surrogate to item and return continue.
        if is_leading_surrogate(item) {
            self.leading_surrogate.set(Some(item));
            return None;
        }

        // 3. If item is a trailing surrogate, then return U+FFFD (�).
        if is_trailing_surrogate(item) {
            return Some(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER);
        }

        // 4. Return item.
        Some(char::from_u32(u32::from(item)).expect("a code unit that is not a surrogate is a scalar value"))
    }
}

fn is_leading_surrogate(code_unit: u16) -> bool {
    (0xD800..=0xDBFF).contains(&code_unit)
}

fn is_trailing_surrogate(code_unit: u16) -> bool {
    (0xDC00..=0xDFFF).contains(&code_unit)
}

// https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value-from-surrogates
fn scalar_value_from_surrogates(leading: u16, trailing: u16) -> char {
    // To obtain a scalar value from surrogates, given a leading surrogate leading and a trailing surrogate trailing,
    // return 0x10000 + ((leading − 0xD800) << 10) + (trailing − 0xDC00).
    let scalar_value = 0x10000 + ((u32::from(leading) - 0xD800) << 10) + (u32::from(trailing) - 0xDC00);
    char::from_u32(scalar_value).expect("surrogates make a scalar value")
}

impl TransformSteps for Encoder {
    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encode-and-enqueue-a-chunk
    fn transform(&self, cx: &CallContext, transform: Ref<TransformStream>, chunk: Value) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let input be the result of converting chunk to a DOMString.
        let input = with_temporary_execution_context(cx.realm(), || to_dom_string(cx.vm(), chunk))?;

        // 2. Convert input to an I/O queue of code units.
        let input = input.to_utf16();
        let mut input_position = 0;

        // 3. Let output be the I/O queue of bytes « end-of-queue ».
        let mut output = Vec::new();

        // 4. While true:
        loop {
            // 1. Let item be the result of reading from input.
            let Some(&item) = input.get(input_position) else {
                // 2. If item is end-of-queue:
                // 1. Convert output into a byte sequence.
                // 2. If output is not empty:
                if !output.is_empty() {
                    // 1. Let chunk be the result of creating a Uint8Array object given output and encoder's relevant
                    //    realm.
                    let chunk = create_uint8_array(cx, &output)?;

                    // 2. Enqueue chunk into encoder's transform.
                    TransformStream::enqueue(transform, cx.vm(), Value::from_object(chunk))?;
                }

                // 3. Return.
                return Ok(());
            };
            input_position += 1;

            // 3. Let result be the result of executing the convert code unit to scalar value algorithm with encoder,
            //    item and input.
            // 4. If result is not continue, then process an item with result, encoder's encoder, input, output, and
            //    "fatal".
            if let Some(result) = self.convert_code_unit_to_scalar_value(item, &mut input_position) {
                let mut bytes = [0; 4];
                output.extend_from_slice(result.encode_utf8(&mut bytes).as_bytes());
            }
        }
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encode-and-flush
    fn flush(&self, cx: &CallContext, transform: Ref<TransformStream>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If encoder's leading surrogate is non-null:
        if self.leading_surrogate.get().is_some() {
            // 1. Let chunk be the result of creating a Uint8Array object given « 0xEF, 0xBF, 0xBD » and encoder's
            //    relevant realm.
            // NB: This is U+FFFD (�) in UTF-8 bytes.
            let chunk = create_uint8_array(cx, &REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER_UTF8_BYTES)?;

            // 2. Enqueue chunk into encoder's transform.
            TransformStream::enqueue(transform, cx.vm(), Value::from_object(chunk))?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! TextEncoder, https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-textencoder

use core::mem::MaybeUninit;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{
    ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferOrder, ArrayBufferShared, Gc, Trace, TypedArrayBase, TypedArrayKind,
    create_typed_array_on_buffer, is_typed_array_out_of_bounds, make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record,
    typed_array_byte_length,
};

use crate::bindings::conversions::UsvString;
use crate::bindings::interface::Wrappable;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::encoding::utf8::{self, EncodeIntoProgress};

/// A TextEncoder has no state: it always encodes UTF-8.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct TextEncoder;

impl Wrappable for TextEncoder {}

/// The dictionary TextEncoderEncodeIntoResult of Encoding/TextEncoder.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) struct TextEncoderEncodeIntoResult {
    pub(crate) read: Option<u64>,
    pub(crate) written: Option<u64>,
}

fn encode_into_result(progress: EncodeIntoProgress) -> TextEncoderEncodeIntoResult {
    TextEncoderEncodeIntoResult {
        read: Some(progress.read as u64),
        written: Some(progress.written as u64),
    }
}

/// Every code unit encodes to at most three bytes, so a source of that many bytes fits a destination without the
/// encoding being measured first.
const MAX_UTF8_BYTES_PER_CODE_UNIT: usize = 3;

#[expect(
    clippy::unnecessary_wraps,
    reason = "the bindings call every method of an implementation for its WebIDL result, whether or not it can fail"
)]
impl TextEncoder {
    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textencoder
    pub(crate) fn construct(_: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // The new TextEncoder() constructor steps are to do nothing.
        Ok(Self)
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textencoder-encoding
    pub(crate) fn encoding(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The encoding getter steps are to return "utf-8".
        Ok(Utf16String::from_ascii(b"utf-8"))
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textencoder-encode
    pub(crate) fn encode(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, input: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<TypedArrayBase>> {
        // 1. Convert input to an I/O queue of scalar values.
        // 2. Let output be the I/O queue of bytes « end-of-queue ».
        // 3. While true:
        //     1. Let item be the result of reading from input.
        //     2. Let result be the result of processing an item with item, an instance of the UTF-8 encoder,
        //        input, output, and "fatal".
        //     3. Assert: result is not an error.
        //     4. If result is finished, then convert output into a byte sequence and return a Uint8Array object
        //        wrapping an ArrayBuffer containing output.
        let length = input.utf8_length();
        let buffer =
            ArrayBuffer::try_create_written_by(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), length, ArrayBufferShared::No, |output| {
                // SAFETY: The buffer has the length of the encoding.
                unsafe { input.encode_utf8(output) }
            })?;
        Ok(create_typed_array_on_buffer(
            cx.vm(),
            cx.realm(),
            TypedArrayKind::Uint8Array,
            length,
            buffer,
        ))
    }

    // https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textencoder-encodeinto
    pub(crate) fn encode_into(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        source: UsvString,
        destination: Gc<TypedArrayBase>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<TextEncoderEncodeIntoResult> {
        // AD-HOC: Return early if destination is detached. This is not explicitly handled in the spec, however no
        //         bytes are copied as the destination's size is always zero in this case.
        //         See: https://github.com/whatwg/encoding/issues/324
        let buffer = destination.viewed_array_buffer();
        if buffer.is_detached() {
            return Ok(encode_into_result(EncodeIntoProgress { read: 0, written: 0 }));
        }
        let destination_record = make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record(&destination, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
        if is_typed_array_out_of_bounds(&destination_record) {
            return Ok(encode_into_result(EncodeIntoProgress { read: 0, written: 0 }));
        }
        let destination_byte_length = typed_array_byte_length(&destination_record) as usize;
        if destination_byte_length == 0 {
            return Ok(encode_into_result(EncodeIntoProgress { read: 0, written: 0 }));
        }
        let destination_bytes = buffer.with_data_block(|data_block| data_block.data_at(destination.byte_offset()));
        assert!(!destination_bytes.is_null());

        // OPTIMIZATION: Encode the whole source at once into a destination that is not shared when it fits.
        //               Shared destinations stay on the incremental path, which keeps their writes the same.
        if !buffer.is_shared_array_buffer() {
            let fits = source.length_in_code_units() * MAX_UTF8_BYTES_PER_CODE_UNIT <= destination_byte_length
                || source.utf8_length() <= destination_byte_length;
            if fits {
                // SAFETY: The destination views `destination_byte_length` bytes of the buffer from its byte offset,
                //         which nothing else accesses while this runs, as the buffer is not shared, and which the
                //         encoding fits.
                let written = unsafe {
                    let output = ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(
                        destination_bytes.cast::<MaybeUninit<u8>>(),
                        destination_byte_length,
                    );
                    source.encode_utf8(output)
                };
                return Ok(encode_into_result(EncodeIntoProgress {
                    read: source.length_in_code_units(),
                    written,
                }));
            }
        }

        // 1. Let read be 0.
        // 2. Let written be 0.
        // 3. Let encoder be an instance of the UTF-8 encoder.
        // 4. Let unused be the I/O queue of scalar values « end-of-queue ».
        // 5. Convert source to an I/O queue of scalar values.
        // 6. While true:
        //     1. Let item be the result of reading from source.
        //     2. Let result be the result of running encoder's handler on unused and item.
        //     3. If result is finished, then break.
        //     4. Otherwise:
        //         1. If destination's byte length − written is greater than or equal to the number of bytes in
        //            result, then:
        //             1. If item is greater than U+FFFF, then increment read by 2.
        //             2. Otherwise, increment read by 1.
        //             3. Write the bytes in result into destination, with startingOffset set to written.
        //             4. Increment written by the number of bytes in result.
        //         2. Otherwise, break.
        // 7. Return «[ "read" → read, "written" → written ]».
        let units = source.units();
        let progress = if buffer.is_shared_array_buffer() {
            // WARNING: See the warning for SharedArrayBuffer objects at
            //          https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#sharedarraybuffer-warning. Another thread can access the
            //          bytes at any time, so they are only written through raw copies.
            utf8::encode_into(&units, destination_byte_length, |offset, bytes| {
                // SAFETY: The encoder writes within the destination's byte length.
                unsafe {
                    core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), destination_bytes.add(offset), bytes.len());
                }
            })
        } else {
            // SAFETY: Nothing else accesses the bytes of a buffer that is not shared while this runs.
            let output = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(destination_bytes, destination_byte_length) };
            utf8::encode_into(&units, destination_byte_length, |offset, bytes| {
                output[offset..offset + bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);
            })
        };
        Ok(encode_into_result(progress))
    }
}

//! The UTF-8 encoder, https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-encoder, encoding a string in AK's representation one
//! scalar value at a time.

use ak::Utf16StringUnits;

/// The scalar values of a string with UTF-16 storage, each with the number of code units it takes. A lone surrogate
/// reads as U+FFFD, which takes as many code units.
fn scalar_values(code_units: &[u16]) -> impl Iterator<Item = (char, usize)> + '_ {
    char::decode_utf16(code_units.iter().copied()).map(|scalar_value| match scalar_value {
        Ok(scalar_value) => (scalar_value, scalar_value.len_utf16()),
        Err(_) => (char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER, 1),
    })
}

/// The number of code units read and of bytes written by the encodeInto() algorithm,
/// https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textencoder-encodeinto
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct EncodeIntoProgress {
    pub(crate) read: usize,
    pub(crate) written: usize,
}

/// Encodes the scalar values of the string that fit in `capacity` bytes, in order, and stops at the first one that
/// does not. `write` stores bytes at the offset it is given.
pub(crate) fn encode_into(
    units: &Utf16StringUnits<'_>,
    capacity: usize,
    mut write: impl FnMut(usize, &[u8]),
) -> EncodeIntoProgress {
    match units {
        Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(bytes) => {
            // Every scalar value of ASCII storage is one code unit and one byte.
            let length = bytes.len().min(capacity);
            write(0, &bytes[..length]);
            EncodeIntoProgress {
                read: length,
                written: length,
            }
        }
        Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(latin1) => {
            let mut progress = EncodeIntoProgress { read: 0, written: 0 };
            let mut bytes = [0; 2];
            for &byte in *latin1 {
                let encoded = char::from(byte).encode_utf8(&mut bytes);
                if capacity - progress.written < encoded.len() {
                    break;
                }
                write(progress.written, encoded.as_bytes());
                progress.read += 1;
                progress.written += encoded.len();
            }
            progress
        }
        Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => {
            let mut progress = EncodeIntoProgress { read: 0, written: 0 };
            let mut bytes = [0; 4];
            for (scalar_value, code_unit_count) in scalar_values(code_units) {
                let encoded = scalar_value.encode_utf8(&mut bytes);
                if capacity - progress.written < encoded.len() {
                    break;
                }
                write(progress.written, encoded.as_bytes());
                progress.read += code_unit_count;
                progress.written += encoded.len();
            }
            progress
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn utf16(string: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        string.encode_utf16().collect()
    }

    fn encoded_into(units: &Utf16StringUnits<'_>, capacity: usize) -> (EncodeIntoProgress, Vec<u8>) {
        let mut output = vec![0; capacity];
        let progress = encode_into(units, capacity, |offset, bytes| {
            output[offset..offset + bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);
        });
        (progress, output)
    }

    #[test]
    fn encode_into_encodes_lone_surrogates_as_replacement_characters() {
        let string = [0x61, 0xD800, 0x62, 0xDC00];
        let (progress, output) = encoded_into(&Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(&string), 8);
        assert_eq!(progress, EncodeIntoProgress { read: 4, written: 8 });
        assert_eq!(output, [0x61, 0xEF, 0xBF, 0xBD, 0x62, 0xEF, 0xBF, 0xBD]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn encode_into_stops_before_a_scalar_value_that_does_not_fit() {
        let string = utf16("ab\u{1F600}c");
        let (progress, output) = encoded_into(&Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(&string), 5);
        assert_eq!(progress, EncodeIntoProgress { read: 2, written: 2 });
        assert_eq!(output, [0x61, 0x62, 0, 0, 0]);

        let (progress, output) = encoded_into(&Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(&string), 6);
        assert_eq!(progress, EncodeIntoProgress { read: 4, written: 6 });
        assert_eq!(output, [0x61, 0x62, 0xF0, 0x9F, 0x98, 0x80]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn encode_into_counts_code_units_read() {
        let string = utf16("\u{E9}\u{1F600}");
        let (progress, _) = encoded_into(&Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(&string), 16);
        assert_eq!(progress, EncodeIntoProgress { read: 3, written: 6 });

        let (progress, output) = encoded_into(&Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b"xyz"), 2);
        assert_eq!(progress, EncodeIntoProgress { read: 2, written: 2 });
        assert_eq!(output, b"xy");
    }
}

    // FIXME: Check FFmpeg?
    true

// https://w3c.github.io/encrypted-media/#get-supported-capabilities-for-audio-video-type
pub(crate) fn get_supported_capabilities_for_audio_video_type(
    implementation: &dyn KeySystem,
    r#type: CapabilitiesType,
    requested_capabilities: Vec<MediaKeySystemMediaCapability>,
    config: MediaKeySystemConfiguration,
    restrictions: &MediaKeyRestrictions,
) -> Option<Vec<MediaKeySystemMediaCapability>> {
    // 1. Let local accumulated configuration be a local copy of accumulated configuration.
    let mut accumulated_configuration = config;

    // 2. Let supported media capabilities be an empty sequence of MediaKeySystemMediaCapability dictionaries.
    let mut supported_media_capabilities = Vec::new();

    // 3. For each requested media capability in requested media capabilities:
    for capability in requested_capabilities {
        // 1. Let content type be requested media capability's contentType member.
        let content_type = &capability.content_type;

        // 2. Let encryption scheme be requested media capability’s encryptionScheme member.
        let encryption_scheme = capability.encryption_scheme.as_ref();

        // 3. Let robustness be requested media capability's robustness member.
        let robustness = &capability.robustness;

        // 4. If content type is the empty string, return null.
        if content_type.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }

        // 5. Let mimeType be the result of running parse a MIME type with content type.
        let content_type = char::decode_utf16(content_type.to_utf16().iter().copied())
            .map(|code_point| code_point.unwrap_or(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let mime_type = MimeType::parse(&content_type);

        // 6. If mimeType is failure or is unrecognized, continue to the next iteration.
        let Some(mime_type) = mime_type else {
            continue;
        };

        // 7. Let container be the container type specified by mimeType.
        let essence = mime_type.essence();
        let container = format!("{}/{}", essence.type_, essence.subtype);

        // 8. If the user agent does not support container, continue to the next iteration.
        //    The case-sensitivity of string comparisons is determined by the appropriate RFC.
        if !supports_container(&container) {
            continue;
        }

        // 9. Let parameters be the "codecs" and "profiles" RFC 6381 [RFC6381] parameters, if any, of mimeType.
        let mut parameters = mime_type.parameters();

        // FIXME: 10. If the user agent does not recognize one or more parameters, or
        //            if any parameters are not valid per the relevant specification, continue to the next iteration.

        // 11. Let media types be the set of codecs and codec constraints specified by parameters.
        //     The case-sensitivity of string comparisons is determined by the appropriate RFC or other specification.
        let media_types = parameters
            .find(|(name, _)| *name == "codecs")
            .map_or("", |(_, value)| value);

        // 12. If media types is empty:
        if media_types.is_empty() {
            // FIXME: If container normatively implies a specific set of codecs and codec constraints:
            if false {
                // Let parameters be that set.
            }
            // Otherwise:
            else {
                // Continue to the next iteration.
                continue;
            }
        }

        // 13. If mimeType is not strictly an audio/video type, continue to the next iteration.
        if !essence.is_audio_or_video() {
            continue;
        }

        // 14. If encryption scheme is non-null and is not recognized or not supported by implementation,
        //     continue to the next iteration.
        if encryption_scheme
            .is_some_and(|encryption_scheme| !implementation.supports_encryption_scheme(encryption_scheme))
        {
            continue;
        }

        // 15. If robustness is not the empty string and contains an unrecognized value or a value not supported
        //     by implementation, continue to the next iteration. String comparison is case-sensitive.
        if !robustness.is_empty() && !implementation.supports_robustness(robustness) {
            continue;
        }

        // 16. If the user agent and implementation definitely support playback of encrypted media data for
        //     the combination of container, media types, encryption scheme, robustness and
        //     local accumulated configuration in combination with restrictions:
        if implementation.definitely_supports_playback(
            &container,
            media_types,
            encryption_scheme,
            robustness,
            &accumulated_configuration,
            restrictions,
        ) {
            // 1. Add requested media capability to supported media capabilities.
            supported_media_capabilities.push(capability.clone());

            // 2. If audio/video type is Video:
            if r#type == CapabilitiesType::Video {
                // Add requested media capability to the videoCapabilities member of local accumulated configuration.
                accumulated_configuration.video_capabilities.push(capability.clone());
            }

            // If audio/video type is Audio:
            if r#type == CapabilitiesType::Audio {
                // Add requested media capability to the audioCapabilities member of local accumulated configuration.
                accumulated_configuration.audio_capabilities.push(capability.clone());
            }
        }
    }

    // 4. If supported media capabilities is empty, return null.
    if supported_media_capabilities.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }

    // 5. Return supported media capabilities.
    Some(supported_media_capabilities)
}

// https://w3c.github.io/encrypted-media/#dfn-is-persistent-session-type
pub(crate) fn is_persistent_session_type(session_type: MediaKeySessionType) -> bool {
    // 1. Let the session type be the specified MediaKeySessionType value.

    // 2. Follow the steps for the value of session type from the following list:
    match session_type {
        // * "temporary"
        MediaKeySessionType::Temporary => {
            // Return false.
            false
        }
        // * "persistent-license"
        MediaKeySessionType::PersistentLicense => {
            // Return true.
            true
        }
    }
}
