// https://w3c.github.io/encrypted-media/#get-supported-configuration-and-consent
pub(crate) fn get_supported_configuration_and_consent(
    implementation: &dyn KeySystem,
    candidate_configuration: &MediaKeySystemConfiguration,
    restrictions: &mut MediaKeyRestrictions,
    origin: &Origin,
) -> Option<ConsentConfiguration> {
    // 1. Let accumulated configuration be a new MediaKeySystemConfiguration dictionary.
    // 2. Set the label member of accumulated configuration to equal the label member of candidate configuration.
    let mut accumulated_configuration = MediaKeySystemConfiguration {
        label: candidate_configuration.label.clone(),
        ..Default::default()
    };

    // 3. If the initDataTypes member of candidate configuration is non-empty, run the following steps:
    if !candidate_configuration.init_data_types.is_empty() {
        // 1. Let supported types be an empty sequence of DOMStrings.
        let mut supported_types = Vec::new();

        // 2. For each value in candidate configuration's initDataTypes member:
        for init_data_type in &candidate_configuration.init_data_types {
            // 1. Let initDataType be the value.

            // 2. If the implementation supports generating requests based on initDataType, add initDataType to supported types.
            // String comparison is case-sensitive. The empty string is never supported.
            if implementation.supports_init_data_type(init_data_type) {
                supported_types.push(init_data_type.clone());
            }
        }

        // 3. If supported types is empty, return NotSupported.
        if supported_types.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }

        // 4. Set the initDataTypes member of accumulated configuration to supported types.
        accumulated_configuration.init_data_types = supported_types;
    }

    // 4. Let distinctive identifier requirement be the value of candidate configuration's distinctiveIdentifier member.
    let mut distinctive_identifier_requirement = candidate_configuration.distinctive_identifier;

    // 5. If distinctive identifier requirement is "optional" and Distinctive Identifiers are not allowed according to restrictions,
    //    set distinctive identifier requirement to "not-allowed".
    if distinctive_identifier_requirement == MediaKeysRequirement::Optional && !restrictions.distinctive_identifiers {
        distinctive_identifier_requirement = MediaKeysRequirement::NotAllowed;
    }

    // 6. Follow the steps for distinctive identifier requirement from the following list:
    match distinctive_identifier_requirement {
        MediaKeysRequirement::Required => {
            // FIXME: If the implementation does not support use of Distinctive Identifier(s) in combination
            //        with accumulated configuration and restrictions, return NotSupported.
        }
        MediaKeysRequirement::Optional => {
            // Continue with the following steps.
        }
        MediaKeysRequirement::NotAllowed => {
            // FIXME: If the implementation requires use of Distinctive Identifier(s) or Distinctive Permanent Identifier(s)
            //        in combination with accumulated configuration and restrictions, return NotSupported.
        }
    }

    // 7. Set the distinctiveIdentifier member of accumulated configuration to equal distinctive identifier requirement.
    accumulated_configuration.distinctive_identifier = distinctive_identifier_requirement;

    // 8. Let persistent state requirement be equal to the value of candidate configuration's persistentState member.
    let mut persistent_state_requirement = candidate_configuration.persistent_state;

    // 9. If persistent state requirement is "optional" and persisting state is not allowed according to restrictions,
    //    set persistent state requirement to "not-allowed".
    if persistent_state_requirement == MediaKeysRequirement::Optional && !restrictions.persist_state {
        persistent_state_requirement = MediaKeysRequirement::NotAllowed;
    }

    // 10. Follow the steps for persistent state requirement from the following list:
    match persistent_state_requirement {
        MediaKeysRequirement::Required => {
            // FIXME: If the implementation does not support persisting state in combination with accumulated configuration
            //        and restrictions, return NotSupported.
        }
        MediaKeysRequirement::Optional => {
            // Continue with the following steps.
        }
        MediaKeysRequirement::NotAllowed => {
            // FIXME: If the implementation requires persisting state in combination with accumulated configuration
            //        and restrictions, return NotSupported.
        }
    }

    // 12. Set the persistentState member of accumulated configuration to equal the value of persistent state requirement.
    accumulated_configuration.persistent_state = persistent_state_requirement;

    // 1. Follow the steps for the first matching condition from the following list:
    let session_types = match &candidate_configuration.session_types {
        // * If the sessionTypes member is present in candidate configuration
        Some(session_types) => {
            // Let session types be candidate configuration's sessionTypes member.
            session_types.clone()
        }
        // * Otherwise
        None => {
            // Let session types be [ "temporary" ].
            vec![Utf16String::from_ascii(b"temporary")]
        }
    };

    // 13. For each value in session types:
    for session_type in &session_types {
        // 1. Let session type be the value.
        // AD-HOC: sessionTypes is a sequence of DOMString, but Is persistent session type? takes a MediaKeySessionType
        //         value. A session type that is not one is not supported, so the candidate configuration is not either.
        //         See https://github.com/w3c/encrypted-media/issues/447
        let session_type = MediaKeySessionType::from_string(session_type)?;

        // 2. If accumulated configuration's persistentState value is "not-allowed" and the Is persistent session type? algorithm
        //    returns true for session type return NotSupported.
        if accumulated_configuration.persistent_state == MediaKeysRequirement::NotAllowed
            && is_persistent_session_type(session_type)
        {
            return None;
        }

        // 3. FIXME: If the implementation does not support session type in combination with accumulated configuration and restrictions for other reasons, return NotSupported.

        // 4. If accumulated configuration's persistentState value is "optional" and the result of running the Is persistent session type? algorithm
        //    on session type is true, change accumulated configuration's persistentState value to "required".
        if accumulated_configuration.persistent_state == MediaKeysRequirement::Optional
            && is_persistent_session_type(session_type)
        {
            accumulated_configuration.persistent_state = MediaKeysRequirement::Required;
        }
    }

    // 14. Set the sessionTypes member of accumulated configuration to session types.
    accumulated_configuration.session_types = Some(session_types);

    // 15. If the videoCapabilities and audioCapabilities members in candidate configuration are both empty, return NotSupported.
    if candidate_configuration.video_capabilities.is_empty() && candidate_configuration.audio_capabilities.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }

    // 16. If the videoCapabilities member in candidate configuration is non-empty:
    if !candidate_configuration.video_capabilities.is_empty() {
        // 1. Let video capabilities be the result of executing the Get Supported Capabilities for Audio/Video Type algorithm
        //    on Video, candidate configuration's videoCapabilities member, accumulated configuration, and restrictions.
        let video_capabilities = get_supported_capabilities_for_audio_video_type(
            implementation,
            CapabilitiesType::Video,
            candidate_configuration.video_capabilities.clone(),
            accumulated_configuration.clone(),
            restrictions,
        );

        // 2. If video capabilities is null, return NotSupported.
        let video_capabilities = video_capabilities?;

        // 3. Set the videoCapabilities member of accumulated configuration to video capabilities.
        accumulated_configuration.video_capabilities = video_capabilities;
    }
    // Otherwise:
    else {
        // 1. Set the videoCapabilities member of accumulated configuration to an empty sequence.
        accumulated_configuration.video_capabilities = Vec::new();
    }

    // 1. If the audioCapabilities member in candidate configuration is non-empty:
    if !candidate_configuration.audio_capabilities.is_empty() {
        // 1. Let audio capabilities be the result of executing the Get Supported Capabilities for Audio/Video Type algorithm
        //    on Audio, candidate configuration's audioCapabilities member, accumulated configuration, and restrictions.
        let audio_capabilities = get_supported_capabilities_for_audio_video_type(
            implementation,
            CapabilitiesType::Audio,
            candidate_configuration.audio_capabilities.clone(),
            accumulated_configuration.clone(),
            restrictions,
        );

        // 2. If audio capabilities is null, return NotSupported.
        let audio_capabilities = audio_capabilities?;

        // 3. Set the audioCapabilities member of accumulated configuration to audio capabilities.
        accumulated_configuration.audio_capabilities = audio_capabilities;
    }
    // Otherwise:
    else {
        // 1. Set the audioCapabilities member of accumulated configuration to an empty sequence.
        accumulated_configuration.audio_capabilities = Vec::new();
    }

    // 18. If accumulated configuration's distinctiveIdentifier value is "optional", follow the steps for the first matching condition from the following list:
    if accumulated_configuration.distinctive_identifier == MediaKeysRequirement::Optional {
        // FIXME: 1. If the implementation requires use of Distinctive Identifier(s) or Distinctive Permanent Identifier(s) for any of the combinations in accumulated configuration:
        if false {
            // 1. Change accumulated configuration's distinctiveIdentifier value to "required".
            accumulated_configuration.distinctive_identifier = MediaKeysRequirement::Required;
        }
        // Otherwise
        else {
            // 1. Change accumulated configuration's distinctiveIdentifier value to "not-allowed".
            accumulated_configuration.distinctive_identifier = MediaKeysRequirement::NotAllowed;
        }
    }

    // 19. If accumulated configuration's persistentState value is "optional", follow the steps for the first matching condition from the following list:
    if accumulated_configuration.persistent_state == MediaKeysRequirement::Optional {
        // FIXME: 1. If the implementation requires persisting state for any of the combinations in accumulated configuration
        if false {
            // 1. Change accumulated configuration's persistentState value to "required".
            accumulated_configuration.persistent_state = MediaKeysRequirement::Required;
        }
        // Otherwise
        else {
            // 1. Change accumulated configuration's persistentState value to "not-allowed".
            accumulated_configuration.persistent_state = MediaKeysRequirement::NotAllowed;
        }
    }

    // FIXME: 20. If implementation in the configuration specified by the combination of the values in accumulated configuration
    //            is not supported or not allowed in the origin, return NotSupported.
    // FIXME: 21. If accumulated configuration's distinctiveIdentifier value is "required" and the Distinctive Identifier(s)
    //            associated with accumulated configuration are not unique per origin and profile and clearable:
    // FIXME: 1. Update restrictions to reflect that all configurations described by accumulated configuration do not have user consent.
    // FIXME: 2. Return ConsentDenied and restrictions.

    // 22. Let consent status and updated restrictions be the result of running the Get Consent Status algorithm
    //     on accumulated configuration, restrictions and origin and follow the steps for the value of consent status from the following list:
    let consent_status = get_consent_status(&accumulated_configuration, restrictions, origin);
    match consent_status {
        ConsentStatus::ConsentDenied => {
            // Return ConsentDenied and updated restrictions.
            return None;
        }
        ConsentStatus::InformUser => {
            // FIXME: Inform the user that accumulated configuration is in use in the origin including, specifically,
            //        the information that Distinctive Identifier(s) and/or Distinctive Permanent Identifier(s) as
            //        appropriate will be used if the distinctiveIdentifier member of accumulated configuration is "required".
            //        Continue to the next step.
        }
        ConsentStatus::Allowed => {
            // Continue to the next step.
        }
    }

    // 23. Return accumulated configuration.
    Some(ConsentConfiguration {
        status: consent_status,
        configuration: Some(accumulated_configuration),
    })
}

// https://w3c.github.io/encrypted-media/#get-supported-configuration
pub(crate) fn get_supported_configuration(
    implementation: &dyn KeySystem,
    candidate_configuration: &MediaKeySystemConfiguration,
    origin: &Origin,
) -> Option<ConsentConfiguration> {
    // 1. Let supported configuration be ConsentDenied.
    let mut supported_configuration = Some(ConsentConfiguration {
        status: ConsentStatus::ConsentDenied,
        configuration: None,
    });

    // 2. Initialize restrictions to indicate that no configurations have had user consent denied.
    let mut restrictions = MediaKeyRestrictions::default();

    let mut loop_count = 0;

    // 3. Repeat the following step while supported configuration is ConsentDenied:
    while supported_configuration
        .as_ref()
        .is_some_and(|supported_configuration| supported_configuration.status == ConsentStatus::ConsentDenied)
    {
        // 1. Let supported configuration and, if provided, restrictions be the result of executing
        //    the Get Supported Configuration and Consent algorithm with implementation, candidate configuration, restrictions and origin.
        supported_configuration =
            get_supported_configuration_and_consent(implementation, candidate_configuration, &mut restrictions, origin);

        // AD-HOC: While this is being implemented, we use this to avoid a possible infinite loop
        if loop_count > 5 {
            break;
        }
        loop_count += 1;
    }

    // 4. Return supported configuration.
    supported_configuration
}

// https://w3c.github.io/encrypted-media/#dfn-common-key-systems
pub(crate) fn is_supported_key_system(key_system: &Utf16String) -> bool {
    const SUPPORTED_KEY_SYSTEMS: [&str; 1] = [
        // https://w3c.github.io/encrypted-media/#clear-key
        "org.w3.clearkey",
    ];

    SUPPORTED_KEY_SYSTEMS
        .iter()
        .any(|supported_key_system| *key_system == *supported_key_system)
}

pub(crate) fn key_system_from_string(key_system: &Utf16String) -> Box<dyn KeySystem> {
    if *key_system == "org.w3.clearkey" {
        return Box::new(ClearKeySystem);
    }

    unreachable!("the key system is supported")
}

use ak::Utf16String;

use super::encrypted_media_extensions::MediaKeyRestrictions;
use super::media_key_system_access::MediaKeySystemConfiguration;

pub(crate) trait KeySystem {
    fn supports_init_data_type(&self, init_data_type: &Utf16String) -> bool;
    fn supports_encryption_scheme(&self, encryption_scheme: &Utf16String) -> bool;
    fn supports_robustness(&self, robustness: &Utf16String) -> bool;
    fn definitely_supports_playback(
        &self,
        container: &str,
        media_types: &str,
        encryption_scheme: Option<&Utf16String>,
        robustness: &Utf16String,
        accumulated_configuration: &MediaKeySystemConfiguration,
        restrictions: &MediaKeyRestrictions,
    ) -> bool;
}

pub(crate) struct ClearKeySystem;

impl KeySystem for ClearKeySystem {
    // https://w3c.github.io/encrypted-media/#clear-key-behavior
    fn supports_init_data_type(&self, init_data_type: &Utf16String) -> bool {
        // Implementations SHOULD support the "keyids" type
        // TODO: Implementations MAY support any combination of registered Initialization Data Types
        // https://www.w3.org/TR/eme-initdata-registry/
        const REGISTERED_INIT_DATA_TYPES: [&str; 1] = ["keyids"];

        REGISTERED_INIT_DATA_TYPES
            .iter()
            .any(|registered_init_data_type| *init_data_type == *registered_init_data_type)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/encrypted-media/#clear-key-capabilities
    fn supports_encryption_scheme(&self, encryption_scheme: &Utf16String) -> bool {
        // encryptionScheme: Implementations MUST support the "cenc" scheme, and MAY support other schemes.
        *encryption_scheme == "cenc"
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/encrypted-media/#clear-key-capabilities
    fn supports_robustness(&self, robustness: &Utf16String) -> bool {
        // robustness: Only the empty string is supported.
        robustness.is_empty()
    }

    fn definitely_supports_playback(
        &self,
        _container: &str,
        _media_types: &str,
        _encryption_scheme: Option<&Utf16String>,
        _robustness: &Utf16String,
        _accumulated_configuration: &MediaKeySystemConfiguration,
        _restrictions: &MediaKeyRestrictions,
    ) -> bool {
        // FIXME: Do some checks here
        true
    }
}

//! EventCounts, https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#sec-event-counts

use core::cell::RefCell;
use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::{Utf16FlyString, Utf16String};
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Map, Trace, Value, Vm};

use crate::bindings::CallContext;
use crate::bindings::conversions::ToJs;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::maplike::Maplike;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_event_timing_for_each_event_type_considered_for_event_timing(
        context: *mut c_void,
        callback: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, usize),
    );
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#sec-event-counts
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct EventCounts {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    entries: RefCell<Vec<(Utf16String, u64)>>,
}

impl Wrappable for EventCounts {}

impl EventCounts {
    // https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#sec-modifications-HTML
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm) -> Ref<Self> {
        // Upon construction of a Performance object whose relevant global object is a Window, its eventCounts must be
        // initialized to a map containing 0s for all event types that the user agent supports from the list described in
        // Events exposed.
        unsafe extern "C" fn append(context: *mut c_void, event_type: usize) {
            // SAFETY: The context is the list below, and LibWeb lends a live fly string for the call.
            let entries = unsafe { &mut *context.cast::<Vec<(Utf16String, u64)>>() };
            entries.push((unsafe { Utf16FlyString::from_raw_borrowed(event_type) }.into(), 0));
        }
        let mut entries = Vec::new();
        // SAFETY: The list outlives the call.
        unsafe { web_event_timing_for_each_event_type_considered_for_event_timing((&raw mut entries).cast(), append) };
        allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            entries: RefCell::new(entries),
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn increment(&self, event_type: &Utf16String) {
        let mut entries = self.entries.borrow_mut();
        let entry = entries
            .iter_mut()
            .find(|entry| &entry.0 == event_type)
            .expect("eventCounts contains every event type considered for Event Timing");
        entry.1 += 1;
    }
}

impl Maplike for EventCounts {
    fn map_entries(&self, cx: &CallContext) -> Gc<Map> {
        let map_entries = Map::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm());
        for (key, value) in &*self.entries.borrow() {
            let key = key.clone().to_js(cx).expect("a string converts to a JS value");
            let value = value.to_js(cx).expect("an unsigned long long converts to a JS value");
            map_entries.map_set(cx.vm(), key, value);
        }
        map_entries
    }

    fn map_value(&self, cx: &CallContext, key: &Utf16String) -> Option<Value> {
        let entries = self.entries.borrow();
        let entry = entries.iter().find(|entry| &entry.0 == key)?;
        Some(entry.1.to_js(cx).expect("an unsigned long long converts to a JS value"))
    }
}

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};

/// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#sec-modifications-HTML
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct WindowEventTimingState {
    // entries to be queued, a list that stores PerformanceEventTiming objects, which will initially be empty.
    entries_to_be_queued: GcRefCell<Vec<Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>>>,
    // has dispatched input event, a boolean which is initially set to false.
    has_dispatched_input_event: Cell<bool>,
    // user interaction value, an integer which is initially set to a random integer between 100 and 10000.
    user_interaction_value: Cell<u64>,
    // pending key downs, a map of integers to PerformanceEventTimings which is initially empty.
    pending_key_downs: GcRefCell<Vec<(u32, Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>)>>,
    // pointer interaction value map, a map of integers which is initially empty.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pointer_interaction_value_map: RefCell<Vec<(i32, u64)>>,
    // pending pointer downs, a map of integers to PerformanceEventTimings which is initially empty.
    pending_pointer_downs: GcRefCell<Vec<(i32, Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>)>>,
    // is contextmenu triggered, a boolean which is initially set to false.
    is_contextmenu_triggered: Cell<bool>,
    // eventCounts, a map with entries of the form type → numEvents.
    // NB: This is created when it is first asked for.
    event_counts: Cell<Option<Ref<EventCounts>>>,
    // interactionCount, an integer which counts the total number of distinct user interactions, for which there was a
    // unique interactionId computed via computing interactionId.
    interaction_count: Cell<u64>,
}

static WINDOW_EVENT_TIMING_STATE_CLASS: EmbedderClass<WindowEventTimingState> =
    EmbedderClass::new("WindowEventTimingState");

impl EmbedderValue for WindowEventTimingState {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &WINDOW_EVENT_TIMING_STATE_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type WindowEventTimingStateRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<WindowEventTimingState>>;

impl WindowEventTimingState {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm) -> WindowEventTimingStateRef {
        // NB: The user interaction value is initially set to a random integer between 100 and 10000.
        let mut random_bytes = [0u8; 8];
        libcrypto_rust::fill_with_random(&mut random_bytes).expect("OpenSSL produces random bytes");
        let user_interaction_value = 100 + u64::from_ne_bytes(random_bytes) % 9901;

        WINDOW_EVENT_TIMING_STATE_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            entries_to_be_queued: GcRefCell::default(),
            has_dispatched_input_event: Cell::new(false),
            user_interaction_value: Cell::new(user_interaction_value),
            pending_key_downs: GcRefCell::default(),
            pointer_interaction_value_map: RefCell::default(),
            pending_pointer_downs: GcRefCell::default(),
            is_contextmenu_triggered: Cell::new(false),
            event_counts: Cell::new(None),
            interaction_count: Cell::new(0),
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn event_counts(&self, vm: &Vm) -> Ref<EventCounts> {
        if let Some(event_counts) = self.event_counts.get() {
            return event_counts;
        }
        let event_counts = EventCounts::create(vm);
        self.event_counts.set(Some(event_counts));
        event_counts
    }

    pub(crate) fn interaction_count(&self) -> u64 {
        self.interaction_count.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn has_dispatched_input_event(&self) -> bool {
        self.has_dispatched_input_event.get()
    }

    fn take_pending_key_down(&self, vm: &Vm, code: u32) -> Option<Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>> {
        let mut pending_key_downs = self.pending_key_downs.borrow_mut(vm);
        let index = pending_key_downs.iter().position(|(key, _)| *key == code)?;
        Some(pending_key_downs.remove(index).1)
    }

    fn take_pending_pointer_down(&self, vm: &Vm, pointer_id: i32) -> Option<Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>> {
        let mut pending_pointer_downs = self.pending_pointer_downs.borrow_mut(vm);
        let index = pending_pointer_downs.iter().position(|(key, _)| *key == pointer_id)?;
        Some(pending_pointer_downs.remove(index).1)
    }

    fn pending_key_down(&self, code: u32) -> Option<Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>> {
        self.pending_key_downs
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .find(|(key, _)| *key == code)
            .map(|(_, entry)| *entry)
    }

    fn set_pending_key_down(&self, vm: &Vm, code: u32, entry: Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>) {
        let mut pending_key_downs = self.pending_key_downs.borrow_mut(vm);
        match pending_key_downs.iter_mut().find(|(key, _)| *key == code) {
            Some(pending_key_down) => pending_key_down.1 = entry,
            None => pending_key_downs.push((code, entry)),
        }
    }

    fn pending_pointer_down(&self, pointer_id: i32) -> Option<Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>> {
        self.pending_pointer_downs
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .find(|(key, _)| *key == pointer_id)
            .map(|(_, entry)| *entry)
    }

    fn set_pending_pointer_down(&self, vm: &Vm, pointer_id: i32, entry: Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>) {
        let mut pending_pointer_downs = self.pending_pointer_downs.borrow_mut(vm);
        match pending_pointer_downs.iter_mut().find(|(key, _)| *key == pointer_id) {
            Some(pending_pointer_down) => pending_pointer_down.1 = entry,
            None => pending_pointer_downs.push((pointer_id, entry)),
        }
    }

    fn pointer_interaction_value(&self, pointer_id: i32) -> Option<u64> {
        self.pointer_interaction_value_map
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .find(|(key, _)| *key == pointer_id)
            .map(|(_, value)| *value)
    }

    fn set_pointer_interaction_value(&self, pointer_id: i32, value: u64) {
        let mut pointer_map = self.pointer_interaction_value_map.borrow_mut();
        match pointer_map.iter_mut().find(|(key, _)| *key == pointer_id) {
            Some(entry) => entry.1 = value,
            None => pointer_map.push((pointer_id, value)),
        }
    }

    fn remove_pointer_interaction_value(&self, pointer_id: i32) {
        self.pointer_interaction_value_map
            .borrow_mut()
            .retain(|(key, _)| *key != pointer_id);
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#increase-interaction-count
fn increase_interaction_count(state: &WindowEventTimingState) {
    // 1. Increase window's user interaction value value by a small number chosen by the user agent.
    state.user_interaction_value.set(state.user_interaction_value.get() + 7);

    // 2. Let interactionCount be window's interactionCount.
    // 3. Set interactionCount to interactionCount + 1.
    state.interaction_count.set(state.interaction_count.get() + 1);
}

// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#compute-interactionid
fn compute_interaction_id(vm: &Vm, event: &CppEvent, window: &CppWindow) -> u64 {
    // 1. If event's isTrusted attribute value is false, return 0.
    if !event.is_trusted() {
        return 0;
    }

    // 2. Let type be event's type attribute value.
    let r#type = event.r#type();
    // 3. If type is not one among keyup, compositionstart, input, pointercancel, pointerup, click, or contextmenu,
    //    return 0.
    if ![
        "keyup",
        "compositionstart",
        "input",
        "pointercancel",
        "pointerup",
        "click",
        "contextmenu",
    ]
    .iter()
    .any(|event_type| r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8(event_type))
    {
        return 0;
    }

    // 4. Let window be event's relevant global object.
    // NB: The window is passed in by the caller.
    let state = window.event_timing_state(vm);

    // 5. Let pendingKeyDowns be window's pending key downs.
    // 6. Let pointerMap be window's pointer interaction value map.
    // 7. Let pendingPointerDowns be window's pending pointer downs.

    // 8. If type is keyup:
    if r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("keyup") {
        let Some(keyboard_event) = CppKeyboardEvent::from_event(event) else {
            return 0;
        };

        // 1. If event's isComposing attribute value is true, return 0.
        if keyboard_event.is_composing() {
            return 0;
        }

        // 2. Let code be event's keyCode attribute value.
        let code = keyboard_event.key_code();

        // 3. If pendingKeyDowns[code] does not exist, return 0.
        // 4. Let entry be pendingKeyDowns[code].
        // 9. Remove pendingKeyDowns[code].
        let Some(entry) = state.take_pending_key_down(vm, code) else {
            return 0;
        };

        // 5. Increase interaction count on window.
        increase_interaction_count(&state);

        // 6. Let interactionId be window's user interaction value value.
        let interaction_id = state.user_interaction_value.get();

        // 7. Set entry's interactionId to interactionId.
        entry.set_interaction_id(interaction_id);

        // 8. Add entry to window's entries to be queued.
        state.entries_to_be_queued.borrow_mut(vm).push(entry);

        // 10. Return interactionId.
        return interaction_id;
    }

    // 9. If type is compositionstart:
    if r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("compositionstart") {
        // 1. For each entry in the values of pendingKeyDowns:
        // 2. Clear pendingKeyDowns.
        let mut pending_key_downs = state.pending_key_downs.borrow_mut(vm);
        for (_, entry) in pending_key_downs.drain(..) {
            // 1. Append entry to window's entries to be queued.
            state.entries_to_be_queued.borrow_mut(vm).push(entry);
        }

        // 3. Return 0.
        return 0;
    }

    // 10. If type is input:
    if r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("input") {
        // 1. If event is not an instance of InputEvent, return 0.
        // NOTE: This check is done to exclude Events for which the type is input but that are not about modified text
        //       content.
        let Some(input_event) = CppInputEvent::from_event(event) else {
            return 0;
        };

        // 2. If event's isComposing attribute value is false, return 0.
        if !input_event.is_composing() {
            return 0;
        }

        // 3. Increase interaction count on window.
        increase_interaction_count(&state);

        // 4. Return window's user interaction value.
        return state.user_interaction_value.get();
    }

    // 11. Otherwise (type is pointercancel, pointerup, click, or contextmenu):
    // 1. Let pointerId be event's pointerId attribute value.
    // AD-HOC: We dispatch click and contextmenu events as MouseEvents rather than PointerEvents, so they have no
    //         pointerId. They come from the mouse, so they use the pointerId of the mouse instead.
    let pointer_id = if let Some(pointer_event) = CppPointerEvent::from_event(event) {
        pointer_event.pointer_id()
    } else if is_mouse_event(event) {
        MOUSE_POINTER_ID
    } else {
        return 0;
    };

    // 2. If type is click:
    if r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("click") {
        // 1. If pointerMap[pointerId] does not exist, return 0.
        // 2. Let value be pointerMap[pointerId].
        let Some(value) = state.pointer_interaction_value(pointer_id) else {
            return 0;
        };

        // 3. Remove pointerMap[pointerId].
        state.remove_pointer_interaction_value(pointer_id);

        // 4. Return value.
        return value;
    }

    // 3. Assert that type is pointerup, pointercancel, or contextmenu.
    assert!(
        r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("pointerup")
            || r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("pointercancel")
            || r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("contextmenu")
    );

    // 4. If pendingPointerDowns[pointerId] does not exist:
    // 5. Let pointerDownEntry be pendingPointerDowns[pointerId].
    // 6. Assert that pointerDownEntry is a PerformanceEventTiming entry.
    // 9. Remove pendingPointerDowns[pointerId].
    let Some(pointer_down_entry) = state.take_pending_pointer_down(vm, pointer_id) else {
        // 1. If type is contextmenu, return window's user interaction value.
        if r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("contextmenu") {
            return state.user_interaction_value.get();
        }

        // 2. If type is pointerup and window's is contextmenu triggered flag is true:
        if r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("pointerup") && state.is_contextmenu_triggered.get() {
            // 1. Set window's is contextmenu triggered flag to false.
            state.is_contextmenu_triggered.set(false);

            // 2. Return window's user interaction value.
            return state.user_interaction_value.get();
        }

        // 3. Otherwise, return 0.
        return 0;
    };

    // 7. If type is pointerup or contextmenu:
    if r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("pointerup") || r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("contextmenu") {
        // 1. Increase interaction count on window.
        increase_interaction_count(&state);

        // 2. Set pointerMap[pointerId] to window's user interaction value.
        state.set_pointer_interaction_value(pointer_id, state.user_interaction_value.get());

        // 3. Set pointerDownEntry's interactionId to pointerMap[pointerId].
        pointer_down_entry.set_interaction_id(state.user_interaction_value.get());
    }

    // 8. Append pointerDownEntry to window’s entries to be queued.
    state.entries_to_be_queued.borrow_mut(vm).push(pointer_down_entry);

    // 10. If type is contextmenu, set window's is contextmenu triggered to true.
    if r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("contextmenu") {
        state.is_contextmenu_triggered.set(true);
    }

    // 11. If type is pointercancel, return 0.
    if r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("pointercancel") {
        return 0;
    }

    // 12. Return pointerMap[pointerId].
    state.pointer_interaction_value(pointer_id).unwrap_or(0)
}

// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#initialize-event-timing
fn initialize_event_timing(
    vm: &Vm,
    event: &CppEvent,
    processing_start: f64,
    interaction_id: u64,
) -> Ref<PerformanceEventTiming> {
    // 1. If the algorithm to determine if event should be considered for Event Timing returns false, then return null.
    // NB: The caller only initializes event timing for an event that is considered for Event Timing.

    // 2. Let timingEntry be a new PerformanceEventTiming object with event's relevant realm.
    // 3. Set timingEntry's name to event's type attribute value.
    // 4. Set timingEntry's entryType to "event".
    // 5. Set timingEntry's startTime to event's timeStamp attribute value.
    // 6. Set timingEntry's processingStart to processingStart.
    // 7. Set timingEntry's cancelable to event's cancelable attribute value.
    // 8. Set timingEntry's interactionId to interactionId.
    // 9. Return timingEntry.
    PerformanceEventTiming::create(
        vm,
        event.r#type(),
        event.time_stamp(),
        processing_start,
        event.cancelable(),
        interaction_id,
    )
}

// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#finalize-event-timing
fn finalize_event_timing(
    vm: &Vm,
    timing_entry: Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>,
    event: &CppEvent,
    relevant_global: &CppWindow,
    target_node: Option<CppCell>,
    target_selector: Utf16String,
    processing_end: f64,
) {
    // 1. If timingEntry is null, then return.
    // 2. Let relevantGlobal be target's relevant global object.
    // 3. If relevantGlobal does not implement Window, return.
    // NB: The caller has done these steps.
    let state = relevant_global.event_timing_state(vm);

    // 4. Set timingEntry's processingEnd to processingEnd.
    timing_entry.set_processing_end(processing_end);

    // 5. Assert that target implements Node.
    // NOTE: This assertion holds due to the types of events supported by the Event Timing API.
    // NB: Events of these types can also be dispatched at the Window or the Document, which have no element to time.

    // 6. Set timingEntry's eventTarget to target.
    // NOTE: This will set eventTarget to the last event target. So if retargeting occurs, the last target, closest to
    //       the root, will be used.
    timing_entry.set_event_target(vm, target_node);

    // 7. Set timingEntry's targetSelector to the result of running the algorithm to generate a CSS selector with
    //    target as input.
    timing_entry.set_target_selector(target_selector);

    // 8. If event's type attribute value is pointerdown:
    let r#type = event.r#type();
    if r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("pointerdown") {
        // 1. Let pendingPointerDowns be relevantGlobal's pending pointer downs.
        // 2. Let pointerId be event's pointerId.
        let pointer_id = CppPointerEvent::from_event(event).map_or(0, |pointer_event| pointer_event.pointer_id());

        // 3. If pendingPointerDowns[pointerId] exists:
        if let Some(previous_pointer_down_entry) = state.pending_pointer_down(pointer_id) {
            // 1. Let previousPointerDownEntry be pendingPointerDowns[pointerId].
            // 2. Add previousPointerDownEntry to relevantGlobal's entries to be queued.
            state
                .entries_to_be_queued
                .borrow_mut(vm)
                .push(previous_pointer_down_entry);
        }

        // 4. Set pendingPointerDowns[pointerId] to timingEntry.
        state.set_pending_pointer_down(vm, pointer_id, timing_entry);

        // 5. Set relevantGlobal's is contextmenu triggered to false.
        state.is_contextmenu_triggered.set(false);
    }
    // 9. Otherwise, if event's type attribute value is keydown:
    else if let Some(keyboard_event) = CppKeyboardEvent::from_event(event)
        && r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8("keydown")
    {
        // 1. If event's isComposing attribute value is true:
        if keyboard_event.is_composing() {
            // 1. Append timingEntry to relevantGlobal's entries to be queued.
            state.entries_to_be_queued.borrow_mut(vm).push(timing_entry);

            // 2. Return.
            return;
        }

        // 2. Let pendingKeyDowns be relevantGlobal's pending key downs.
        // 3. Let code be event's keyCode attribute value.
        let code = keyboard_event.key_code();

        // 4. If pendingKeyDowns[code] exists:
        if let Some(previous_key_down_entry) = state.pending_key_down(code) {
            // 1. Let previousKeyDownEntry be pendingKeyDowns[code].
            // 2. If code is not 229:
            if code != 229 {
                // 1. Increase relevantGlobal's user interaction value value by a small number chosen by the user
                //    agent.
                state.user_interaction_value.set(state.user_interaction_value.get() + 7);

                // 2. Set previousKeyDownEntry's interactionId to relevantGlobal's user interaction value.
                previous_key_down_entry.set_interaction_id(state.user_interaction_value.get());
            }
            // NOTE: 229 is a special case since it corresponds to IME keyboard events. Sometimes multiple of these
            //       are sent by the user agent, and they do not correspond to holding a key down repeatedly.

            // 3. Add previousKeyDownEntry to relevantGlobal's entries to be queued.
            state.entries_to_be_queued.borrow_mut(vm).push(previous_key_down_entry);
        }

        // 5. Set pendingKeyDowns[code] to timingEntry.
        state.set_pending_key_down(vm, code, timing_entry);
    }
    // 10. Otherwise:
    else {
        // 1. Append timingEntry to relevantGlobal's entries to be queued.
        state.entries_to_be_queued.borrow_mut(vm).push(timing_entry);
    }

    // AD-HOC: The duration of the entry is set by the next rendering update, which is asked for here in case nothing
    //         else asks for one.
    // SAFETY: The Window is live.
    unsafe { web_event_timing_request_frame(relevant_global.as_ptr()) };
}

// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#set-event-timing-entry-duration
fn set_event_timing_entry_duration(
    vm: &Vm,
    timing_entry: Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>,
    window: &CppWindow,
    rendering_timestamp: f64,
) {
    let state = window.event_timing_state(vm);

    // 1. If timingEntry's duration attribute value is nonzero, return.
    // AD-HOC: A duration that rounds to zero is a duration that has been set all the same. Otherwise, a pending
    //         pointerdown or keydown entry would be given a duration again by every later rendering update until its
    //         duration rounds to a nonzero value, and its event would be counted in eventCounts each time.
    if timing_entry.has_duration() {
        return;
    }

    let entry = AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceEventTiming(timing_entry);

    // 2. Let start be timingEntry's startTime attribute value.
    let start = entry.start_time();

    // 3. Set timingEntry's duration to a DOMHighResTimeStamp resulting from renderingTimestamp - start, with
    //    granularity of 8ms or less.
    timing_entry.set_duration(((rendering_timestamp - start) / 8.0).round() * 8.0);

    // 4. Let name be timingEntry's name attribute value.
    let name = entry.name();

    // 5. Perform the following steps to update the event counts:
    // 1. Let eventCounts be window's eventCounts.
    // 2. Assert that eventCounts contains name.
    // 3. Set eventCounts[name] to eventCounts[name] + 1.
    state.event_counts(vm).increment(&name);

    // 6. If window's has dispatched input event is false, and timingEntry's interactionId is not 0, run the following
    //    steps:
    if !state.has_dispatched_input_event.get() && timing_entry.interaction_id.get() != 0 {
        // 1. Let firstInputEntry be a copy of timingEntry.
        // 2. Set firstInputEntry's entryType to "first-input".
        let first_input_entry = AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceEventTiming(
            timing_entry.copy_with_entry_type(vm, Utf16String::from_utf8("first-input")),
        );

        // 3. Queue firstInputEntry.
        let timeline = PerformanceTimeline::of(vm, window.realm());
        timeline.queue_performance_entry(vm, &first_input_entry);
        timeline.add_performance_entry(vm, &first_input_entry, true);

        // 4. Set window's has dispatched input event to true.
        state.has_dispatched_input_event.set(true);
    }
}

fn has_pending_event_timing_entries(vm: &Vm, window: &CppWindow) -> bool {
    let state = window.event_timing_state(vm);
    if !state.entries_to_be_queued.borrow().is_empty() {
        return true;
    }
    state
        .pending_pointer_downs
        .borrow()
        .iter()
        .any(|(_, entry)| !entry.has_duration())
        || state
            .pending_key_downs
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .any(|(_, entry)| !entry.has_duration())
}

// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#dispatch-pending-event-timing-entries
fn dispatch_pending_event_timing_entries(vm: &Vm, window: &CppWindow) {
    // 1. Let window be doc's relevant global object.
    let state = window.event_timing_state(vm);

    // OPTIMIZATION: There is nothing to do while no event has been timed.
    if state.entries_to_be_queued.borrow().is_empty()
        && state.pending_pointer_downs.borrow().is_empty()
        && state.pending_key_downs.borrow().is_empty()
    {
        return;
    }

    // 2. Let renderingTimestamp be the current high resolution time.
    // SAFETY: The Window's global object is live.
    let rendering_timestamp = unsafe {
        web_high_resolution_time_current_high_resolution_time(window.realm().global_object().as_ptr().cast())
    };

    // 3. For each timingEntry in window's entries to be queued:
    // 4. Set window's entries to be queued to an empty list.
    let entries_to_be_queued = MarkedVec::new(vm);
    entries_to_be_queued.extend_from_slice(&state.entries_to_be_queued.borrow());
    state.entries_to_be_queued.borrow_mut(vm).clear();
    let timeline = PerformanceTimeline::of(vm, window.realm());
    for timing_entry in entries_to_be_queued.values().iter().copied() {
        // 1. Set event timing entry duration passing timingEntry, window, and renderingTimestamp.
        set_event_timing_entry_duration(vm, timing_entry, window, rendering_timestamp);

        // 2. If timingEntry's duration attribute value is greater than or equal to 16, then queue timingEntry.
        let entry = AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceEventTiming(timing_entry);
        if entry.duration() >= 16.0 {
            timeline.queue_performance_entry(vm, &entry);
            timeline.add_performance_entry(vm, &entry, true);
        }
    }

    // 5. For each pendingPointerDownEntry in the values from window's pending pointer downs:
    let pending_pointer_downs = MarkedVec::new(vm);
    for (_, entry) in state.pending_pointer_downs.borrow().iter() {
        pending_pointer_downs.push(*entry);
    }
    for pending_pointer_down_entry in pending_pointer_downs.values().iter().copied() {
        // 1. Set event timing entry duration passing pendingPointerDownEntry, window, and renderingTimestamp.
        set_event_timing_entry_duration(vm, pending_pointer_down_entry, window, rendering_timestamp);
    }

    // 6. For each pendingKeyDownEntry in the values from window's pending key downs:
    let pending_key_downs = MarkedVec::new(vm);
    for (_, entry) in state.pending_key_downs.borrow().iter() {
        pending_key_downs.push(*entry);
    }
    for pending_key_down_entry in pending_key_downs.values().iter().copied() {
        // 1. Set event timing entry duration passing pendingKeyDownEntry, window, and renderingTimestamp.
        set_event_timing_entry_duration(vm, pending_key_down_entry, window, rendering_timestamp);
    }
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#compute-interactionid
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_event_timing_compute_interaction_id(
    vm: &Vm,
    window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>,
    event: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Event>,
) -> u64 {
    let (window, event) = (CppWindow::from_lent(window), CppEvent::from_lent(event));
    compute_interaction_id(vm, &event, &window)
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#initialize-event-timing
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_event_timing_initialize_event_timing(
    vm: &Vm,
    event: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Event>,
    processing_start: f64,
    interaction_id: u64,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let event = CppEvent::from_lent(event);
    cell_into_abi(initialize_event_timing(vm, &event, processing_start, interaction_id))
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#finalize-event-timing
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_event_timing_finalize_event_timing(
    vm: &Vm,
    timing_entry: &InterfaceCell,
    event: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Event>,
    relevant_global: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>,
    target_node: Option<&LentCppCell<cpp_class::Node>>,
    target_selector: Utf16String,
    processing_end: f64,
) {
    let (timing_entry, event, relevant_global, target_node) = (
        timing_entry.object::<PerformanceEventTiming>(),
        CppEvent::from_lent(event),
        CppWindow::from_lent(relevant_global),
        target_node.map(CppCell::from_lent),
    );
    finalize_event_timing(
        vm,
        timing_entry,
        &event,
        &relevant_global,
        target_node,
        target_selector,
        processing_end,
    );
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_event_timing_has_pending_event_timing_entries(
    vm: &Vm,
    window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>,
) -> bool {
    let window = CppWindow::from_lent(window);
    has_pending_event_timing_entries(vm, &window)
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#dispatch-pending-event-timing-entries
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_event_timing_dispatch_pending_event_timing_entries(
    vm: &Vm,
    window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>,
) {
    let window = CppWindow::from_lent(window);
    dispatch_pending_event_timing_entries(vm, &window);
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#sec-modifications-HTML
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_event_timing_has_dispatched_input_event(
    vm: &Vm,
    window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>,
) -> bool {
    let window = CppWindow::from_lent(window);
    window.event_timing_state(vm).has_dispatched_input_event()
}

//! PerformanceEventTiming, https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#sec-performance-event-timing

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{GcRefCell, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::CppCell;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::css::css_rule::wrap_cpp_cell;
use crate::paint_timing::paint_timing::is_exposed_for_paint_timing;
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_entry::{AnyPerformanceEntry, PerformanceEntry};
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_observer::PerformanceObserverInit;

/// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#sec-performance-event-timing
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceEventTiming {
    // NB: An entry is "event", unless it is the copy of an entry that is queued as the first input.
    entry: PerformanceEntry,
    has_duration: Cell<bool>,
    processing_start: f64,
    processing_end: Cell<f64>,
    cancelable: bool,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#eventtarget
    event_target: GcRefCell<Option<CppCell>>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    target_selector: RefCell<Utf16String>,
    pub(crate) interaction_id: Cell<u64>,
}

impl Wrappable for PerformanceEventTiming {}

impl Inherits<PerformanceEntry> for PerformanceEventTiming {
    fn parent(&self) -> &PerformanceEntry {
        &self.entry
    }
}

impl PerformanceEventTiming {
    // https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#initialize-event-timing
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        name: Utf16String,
        start_time: f64,
        processing_start: f64,
        cancelable: bool,
        interaction_id: u64,
    ) -> Ref<Self> {
        // 2. Let timingEntry be a new PerformanceEventTiming object with event's relevant realm.
        // 3. Set timingEntry's name to event's type attribute value.
        // 4. Set timingEntry's entryType to "event".
        // 5. Set timingEntry's startTime to event's timeStamp attribute value.
        // 6. Set timingEntry's processingStart to processingStart.
        // 7. Set timingEntry's cancelable to event's cancelable attribute value.
        // 8. Set timingEntry's interactionId to interactionId.
        let timing_entry = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            entry: PerformanceEntry::new(name, Utf16String::from_utf8("event"), start_time, 0.0),
            has_duration: Cell::new(false),
            processing_start,
            processing_end: Cell::new(0.0),
            cancelable,
            event_target: GcRefCell::new(None),
            target_selector: RefCell::new(Utf16String::default()),
            interaction_id: Cell::new(interaction_id),
        });
        let any_entry = AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceEventTiming(timing_entry);
        any_entry.entry().set_object(any_entry);
        timing_entry
    }

    pub(crate) fn copy_with_entry_type(&self, vm: &Vm, entry_type: Utf16String) -> Ref<Self> {
        let entry = self.entry.object();
        let copy = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            entry: PerformanceEntry::new(entry.name(), entry_type, entry.start_time(), entry.duration()),
            has_duration: Cell::new(self.has_duration.get()),
            processing_start: self.processing_start,
            processing_end: Cell::new(self.processing_end.get()),
            cancelable: self.cancelable,
            event_target: GcRefCell::new(self.event_target.borrow().clone()),
            target_selector: RefCell::new(self.target_selector.borrow().clone()),
            interaction_id: Cell::new(self.interaction_id.get()),
        });
        let any_entry = AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceEventTiming(copy);
        any_entry.entry().set_object(any_entry);
        copy
    }

    pub(crate) fn processing_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.processing_start)
    }

    pub(crate) fn processing_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.processing_end.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn cancelable(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.cancelable)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#dom-performanceeventtiming-target
    pub(crate) fn target(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CppInterface>> {
        let event_target = self.event_target.borrow();

        // 1. If this's eventTarget is not exposed for paint timing given null, return null.
        let Some(event_target) = event_target
            .as_ref()
            .filter(|target| is_exposed_for_paint_timing(target))
        else {
            return Ok(None);
        };

        // 2. Return this's eventTarget.
        Ok(Some(wrap_cpp_cell(cx, event_target)))
    }

    pub(crate) fn target_selector(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.target_selector.borrow().clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn interaction_id(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        Ok(self.interaction_id.get())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#should-add-performanceeventtiming
    pub(crate) fn should_add_entry(&self, options: Option<&PerformanceObserverInit>) -> bool {
        // 1. If entry's entryType attribute value equals to "first-input", return true.
        let entry = self.entry.object();
        if entry.entry_type() == Utf16String::from_utf8("first-input") {
            return true;
        }

        // 2. Assert that entry's entryType attribute value equals "event".
        assert!(entry.entry_type() == Utf16String::from_utf8("event"));

        // 3. Let minDuration be computed as follows:
        let min_duration = match options.and_then(|options| options.duration_threshold) {
            // 1. If options is not present or if options's durationThreshold is not present, let minDuration be 104.
            None => 104.0,
            // 2. Otherwise, let minDuration be the maximum between 16 and options's durationThreshold value.
            Some(duration_threshold) => f64::max(16.0, duration_threshold),
        };

        // 4. If entry's duration attribute value is greater than or equal to minDuration, return true.
        // 5. Otherwise, return false.
        entry.duration() >= min_duration
    }

    pub(crate) fn has_duration(&self) -> bool {
        self.has_duration.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_duration(&self, duration: f64) {
        self.entry.set_duration(duration);
        self.has_duration.set(true);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_processing_end(&self, processing_end: f64) {
        self.processing_end.set(processing_end);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_event_target(&self, vm: &Vm, event_target: Option<CppCell>) {
        *self.event_target.borrow_mut(vm) = event_target;
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_target_selector(&self, target_selector: Utf16String) {
        *self.target_selector.borrow_mut() = target_selector;
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_interaction_id(&self, interaction_id: u64) {
        self.interaction_id.set(interaction_id);
    }
}

/*

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::UsvString;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, cell_into_abi};
use crate::domurl::url_search_params::URLSearchParams;
use crate::fetch::infrastructure::http::bodies::CppBody;
use crate::file_api::blob::AnyBlob;
use crate::xhr::form_data::FormData;

#[repr(u8)]
enum BodyInitKind {
    Blob = 0,
    Bytes = 1,
    FormData = 2,
    URLSearchParams = 3,
    String = 4,
}

#[repr(C)]
struct BodyInitAbi<'a> {
    kind: BodyInitKind,
    cell: *mut c_void,
    bytes: ak::Span<'a, u8>,
    string: usize,
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_fetch_safely_extract_body(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        object: *const BodyInitAbi<'_>,
        out_type: *mut usize,
    ) -> *mut c_void;
}

/// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#typedefdef-xmlhttprequestbodyinit
pub(crate) enum XMLHttpRequestBodyInit {
    Blob(AnyBlob),
    Bytes(Vec<u8>),
    FormData(Ref<FormData>),
    URLSearchParams(Ref<URLSearchParams>),
    String(UsvString),
}

/// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#body-with-type
pub(crate) struct BodyWithType {
    pub(crate) body: CppBody,
    pub(crate) r#type: Option<Utf16String>,
}

/// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#bodyinit-safely-extract
pub(crate) fn safely_extract_body(realm: Gc<Realm>, object: &XMLHttpRequestBodyInit) -> BodyWithType {
    let mut abi = BodyInitAbi {
        kind: BodyInitKind::Bytes,
        cell: core::ptr::null_mut(),
        bytes: ak::Span::new(&[]),
        string: 0,
    };
    match object {
        XMLHttpRequestBodyInit::Blob(blob) => {
            abi.kind = BodyInitKind::Blob;
            abi.cell = blob.clone().cell_into_abi();
        }
        XMLHttpRequestBodyInit::Bytes(bytes) => abi.bytes = ak::Span::new(bytes),
        XMLHttpRequestBodyInit::FormData(form_data) => {
            abi.kind = BodyInitKind::FormData;
            abi.cell = cell_into_abi(*form_data);
        }
        XMLHttpRequestBodyInit::URLSearchParams(url_search_params) => {
            abi.kind = BodyInitKind::URLSearchParams;
            abi.cell = cell_into_abi(*url_search_params);
        }
        XMLHttpRequestBodyInit::String(string) => {
            abi.kind = BodyInitKind::String;
            abi.string = string.as_utf16_string().raw_identity();
        }
    }
    let mut r#type = 0;
    // SAFETY: The realm and the object are live, the object is lent for the call, and LibWeb returns a live body and
    //         hands over 0 or the type.
    unsafe {
        let body = CppBody::from_raw(web_fetch_safely_extract_body(
            realm.as_ptr().cast(),
            &raw const abi,
            &raw mut r#type,
        ));
        BodyWithType {
            body,
            r#type: (r#type != 0).then(|| Utf16String::from_raw_owned(r#type)),
        }
    }
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_fetch_controller_create(global_object: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_fetch_controller_terminate(controller: *mut c_void);
    fn web_fetch_controller_abort(controller: *mut c_void, realm: *mut c_void);
    fn web_fetch_controller_has_report_timing_steps(controller: *mut c_void) -> bool;
    fn web_fetch_controller_report_timing(controller: *mut c_void, global_object: *mut c_void);

/// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CppFetchController(CppCell);

impl PartialEq for CppFetchController {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.as_ptr() == other.as_ptr()
    }
}

impl CppFetchController {
    pub(crate) fn create(global_object: Gc<Object>) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The global object is live, and LibWeb returns a new, live fetch controller.
        Self(unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(web_fetch_controller_create(global_object.as_ptr().cast())) })
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_lent(controller: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::FetchController>) -> Self {
        Self(CppCell::from_lent(controller))
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `controller` must be a live fetch controller.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_raw(controller: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live fetch controller.
        Self(unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(controller) })
    }

    pub(crate) fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.as_ptr()
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller-terminate
    pub(crate) fn terminate(&self) {
        // SAFETY: The fetch controller is live.
        unsafe { web_fetch_controller_terminate(self.as_ptr()) };
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller-abort
    pub(crate) fn abort(&self, realm: Gc<Realm>) {
        // SAFETY: The fetch controller and the realm are live.
        unsafe { web_fetch_controller_abort(self.as_ptr(), realm.as_ptr().cast()) };
    }

    pub(crate) fn has_report_timing_steps(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The fetch controller is live.
        unsafe { web_fetch_controller_has_report_timing_steps(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#finalize-and-report-timing
    pub(crate) fn report_timing(&self, global_object: Gc<Object>) {
        // SAFETY: The fetch controller and the global object are live.
        unsafe { web_fetch_controller_report_timing(self.as_ptr(), global_object.as_ptr().cast()) };
    }
}

#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct FetchTimingInfo {

    pub(crate) redirect_start_time: f64,
    pub(crate) redirect_end_time: f64,
    pub(crate) post_redirect_start_time: f64,

/// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-timing-info
pub(crate) struct CppFetchTimingInfo(NonNull<c_void>);

impl CppFetchTimingInfo {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `timing_info` must be a fetch timing info that LibWeb hands over a reference to.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn adopt(timing_info: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        Self(NonNull::new(timing_info).expect("LibWeb hands over a fetch timing info"))
    }

    pub(crate) fn read(&self) -> FetchTimingInfo {
        let mut values = FetchTimingInfo::default();
        // SAFETY: This holds a reference to the timing info, and LibWeb writes its values.
        unsafe { web_fetch_timing_info_read(self.0.as_ptr(), &raw mut values) };
        values
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#connection-timing-info-alpn-negotiated-protocol
    pub(crate) fn alpn_negotiated_protocol(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        unsafe extern "C" fn copy(context: *mut c_void, protocol: Span<'_, u8>) {
            // SAFETY: The context is the protocol below, and LibWeb lends the bytes for the call.
            *unsafe { &mut *context.cast::<Vec<u8>>() } = protocol.as_slice().to_vec();
        }
        let mut protocol = Vec::new();
        // SAFETY: This holds a reference to the timing info, and the protocol outlives the call.
        unsafe { web_fetch_timing_info_alpn_negotiated_protocol(self.0.as_ptr(), (&raw mut protocol).cast(), copy) };
        protocol
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-timing-info-server-timing-headers
    pub(crate) fn server_timing_headers(&self) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
        unsafe extern "C" fn append(context: *mut c_void, header: Span<'_, u8>) {
            // SAFETY: The context is the list below, and LibWeb lends the header for the call.
            unsafe { &mut *context.cast::<Vec<Vec<u8>>>() }.push(header.as_slice().to_vec());
        }
        let mut headers = Vec::new();
        // SAFETY: This holds a reference to the timing info, and the list outlives the call.
        unsafe {
            web_fetch_timing_info_for_each_server_timing_header(self.0.as_ptr(), (&raw mut headers).cast(), append);
        };
        headers
    }
}

impl Drop for CppFetchTimingInfo {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: This holds a reference to the timing info, which it lets go of.
        unsafe { web_fetch_timing_info_unref(self.0.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

unsafe extern "C" fn on_bytes(bytes: *mut c_void, lent: ak::Span<'_, u8>) {
    // SAFETY: bytes is the vector of the caller, and LibWeb lends the bytes for the call.
    unsafe { *bytes.cast::<Vec<u8>>() = lent.as_slice().to_vec() };
}

unsafe extern "C" fn on_header(headers: *mut c_void, name: ak::Span<'_, u8>, value: ak::Span<'_, u8>) {
    // SAFETY: headers is the list of the caller, and LibWeb lends the name and the value for the call.
    unsafe {
        (*headers.cast::<Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>>()).push((name.as_slice().to_vec(), value.as_slice().to_vec()));
    }
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `string` must be 0 or a raw string that LibWeb hands over.
unsafe fn string_if_not_null(string: usize) -> Option<Utf16String> {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a raw string that LibWeb hands over.
    (string != 0).then(|| unsafe { Utf16String::from_raw_owned(string) })
}

/// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response

        Self(CppCell::from_lent(response))
    }

    pub(crate) fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.0.as_ptr()
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error
    pub(crate) fn is_network_error(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The response is live.
        unsafe { web_fetch_response_is_network_error(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-aborted
    pub(crate) fn aborted(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The response is live.
        unsafe { web_fetch_response_aborted(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status
    pub(crate) fn status(&self) -> u16 {
        // SAFETY: The response is live.
        unsafe { web_fetch_response_status(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status-message
    pub(crate) fn status_message(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
        // SAFETY: The response is live, and the bytes outlive the call.
        unsafe { web_fetch_response_status_message(self.as_ptr(), (&raw mut bytes).cast(), on_bytes) };

    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-get
    pub(crate) fn get_header(&self, name: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-sort-and-combine
    pub(crate) fn sort_and_combine(&self) -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> {
        let mut headers = Vec::new();
        // SAFETY: The response is live, and the headers outlive the call.
        unsafe { web_fetch_response_sort_and_combine(self.as_ptr(), (&raw mut headers).cast(), on_header) };
        headers
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#header-list-extract-a-length
    pub(crate) fn extract_length(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        let mut length = 0;
        // SAFETY: The response is live, and the length outlives the call.
        unsafe { web_fetch_response_extract_length(self.as_ptr(), &raw mut length) }.then_some(length)
    }

    /// Whether the body has a content coding, i.e. Content-Encoding names a coding other than identity. That's read from
    /// the unfiltered headers, which still hold Content-Encoding when a CORS filter leaves it out.
    pub(crate) fn has_content_coding(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The response is live.
        unsafe { web_fetch_response_has_content_coding(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-extract-mime-type
    pub(crate) fn extract_mime_type(&self) -> Option<MimeType> {
        // SAFETY: The response is live, and LibWeb hands over 0 or the serialization of the MIME type.
        let serialized = unsafe { string_if_not_null(web_fetch_response_extract_mime_type(self.as_ptr())) }?;
        let code_points: Vec<char> = char::decode_utf16(serialized.to_utf16().iter().copied())
            .map(|code_point| code_point.expect("the serialization of a MIME type is well-formed"))
            .collect();
        Some(MimeType::parse(&code_points).expect("the serialization of a MIME type parses"))
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url
    pub(crate) fn url(&self, exclude_fragment: bool) -> Option<Utf16String> {
        // SAFETY: The response is live, and LibWeb hands over 0 or the serialization of the URL.
        unsafe { string_if_not_null(web_fetch_response_url(self.as_ptr(), exclude_fragment)) }
    }

    /// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-body
    pub(crate) fn has_body(&self) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: The response is live.
        unsafe { web_fetch_response_has_body(self.as_ptr()) }
    }

    pub(crate) fn network_error_message(&self) -> Option<Utf16String> {
        // SAFETY: The response is live, and LibWeb hands over 0 or the message.
        unsafe { string_if_not_null(web_fetch_response_network_error_message(self.as_ptr())) }
    }
}

//! The Fetch Standard, https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/

pub(crate) mod body_init;
pub(crate) mod infrastructure;

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::{InterfaceCell, cell_into_abi};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, MustNotThrow};
use crate::encoding::text_decoder_stream::TextDecoderStream;
use crate::streams::algorithms::{CancelAlgorithm, PullAlgorithm, StartAlgorithm};
use crate::streams::readable_stream::{ReadableStream, create_readable_stream, readable_stream_close};

/// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-body-textstream
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_body_text_stream(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, stream: Option<&InterfaceCell>) -> *mut c_void {
    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);

    // 1. If this is unusable, then throw a TypeError.
    // AD-HOC: This is implemented in the C++ caller

    // 2. If this's body is null:
    let Some(stream) = stream else {
        // 1. Let emptyStream be a new ReadableStream in this's relevant realm.
        // 2. Set up emptyStream.
        let empty_stream = create_readable_stream(
            &cx,
            StartAlgorithm::ReturnsUndefined,
            PullAlgorithm::ReturnsResolvedUndefined,
            CancelAlgorithm::ReturnsResolvedUndefined,
            None,
            None,
        )
        .must();

        // 3. Close emptyStream.
        readable_stream_close(vm, empty_stream);

        // 4. Return emptyStream.
        return cell_into_abi(empty_stream);
    };

    // 3. Let stream be this's body's stream.
    let stream = stream.object::<ReadableStream>();

    // 4. Let decoder be a new TextDecoderStream object in this's relevant realm.
    // 5. Set up decoder with UTF-8.
    let decoder = TextDecoderStream::set_up(&cx, encoding_rs::UTF_8, false, false);

    // 6. Return the result of stream, piped through decoder.
    cell_into_abi(ReadableStream::piped_through(
        stream,
        vm,
        decoder.transform(),
        false,
        false,
        false,
        None,
    ))
}

//! Blob, https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-section

use core::cell::{Ref as CellRef, RefCell};
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ops::Deref;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::{Utf16String, Utf16StringUnits};
use libjs_rust::api::{MarkedVec, Trace};

use super::file::File;
use crate::bindings::conversions::{BufferSource, UsvString};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_from_abi, cell_into_abi};
use crate::bindings::promise::{WebIdlPromise, promise_from_abi};
use crate::bindings::structured_data::{Serializable, SerializationReader, SerializationWriter};
