unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_blob_bytes_destroy(owner: *mut c_void);
    fn web_blob_get_stream(realm: *mut c_void, bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_blob_text(realm: *mut c_void, bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_blob_array_buffer(realm: *mut c_void, bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_blob_bytes(realm: *mut c_void, bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>) -> *mut c_void;
}

/// The enumeration EndingType of FileAPI/Blob.idl.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) enum EndingType {
    Transparent,
    Native,
}

/// The dictionary BlobPropertyBag of FileAPI/Blob.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) struct BlobPropertyBag {
    pub(crate) endings: EndingType,
    pub(crate) r#type: Utf16String,
}

/// An object of Blob or of File, which inherits from it.
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum AnyBlob {
    Blob(Ref<Blob>),
    File(Ref<File>),
}

impl Deref for AnyBlob {
    type Target = Blob;

    fn deref(&self) -> &Blob {
        match self {
            Self::Blob(blob) => blob,
            Self::File(file) => {
                let file: &File = file;
                file.parent()
            }
        }
    }
}

impl AnyBlob {
    /// The cell of the object, as LibWeb's C++ code holds it.
    pub(crate) fn cell_into_abi(self) -> *mut c_void {
        match self {
            Self::Blob(blob) => cell_into_abi(blob),
            Self::File(file) => cell_into_abi(file),
        }
    }
}

/// The union (BufferSource or Blob or USVString) of FileAPI/Blob.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum BlobPart {
    BufferSource(BufferSource),
    Blob(AnyBlob),
    USVString(#[gc(untraced)] UsvString),
}

/// Bytes that C++ owns for a Blob, as it hands them over: the owner, which web_blob_bytes_destroy() destroys, and the
/// bytes, which live as long as it.
#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct ForeignBytesAbi {
    pub(crate) owner: *mut c_void,
    pub(crate) data: *const u8,
    pub(crate) length: usize,
}

/// Bytes that a C++ Web::FileAPI::BlobBytes owns: those that C++ created the Blob with, or moved into immutable bytes
/// or shared memory.
struct ForeignBytes {
    owner: NonNull<c_void>,
    data: *const u8,
    length: usize,
}

impl ForeignBytes {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `bytes` must be bytes that C++ hands over, which nothing else destroys.
    unsafe fn from_abi(bytes: ForeignBytesAbi) -> Self {
        Self {
            owner: NonNull::new(bytes.owner).expect("C++ hands over the owner of the bytes"),
            data: bytes.data,
            length: bytes.length,
        }
    }

    fn as_slice(&self) -> &[u8] {
        // SAFETY: The owner keeps the bytes alive and unchanged for as long as it lives.
        unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.data, self.length) }
    }
}

impl Drop for ForeignBytes {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: The value owns the owner, which nothing uses after this.
        unsafe { web_blob_bytes_destroy(self.owner.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-byte-sequence
enum ByteSequence {
    Owned(Vec<u8>),
    Foreign(ForeignBytes),
}

impl ByteSequence {
    fn as_slice(&self) -> &[u8] {
        match self {
            Self::Owned(bytes) => bytes,
            Self::Foreign(bytes) => bytes.as_slice(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Blob {
    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-byte-sequence
    // NB: The bytes move into immutable bytes or shared memory the first time C++ shares them, and stay in shared
    //     memory once there.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    byte_sequence: RefCell<ByteSequence>,
    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-type
    #[gc(untraced)]
    r#type: Utf16String,
}

impl Wrappable for Blob {
    const OWNS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY: bool = true;
    const COUNTS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_WHEN_ALLOCATED: bool = true;

    fn external_memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        match &*self.byte_sequence.borrow() {
            ByteSequence::Owned(bytes) => bytes.capacity(),
            ByteSequence::Foreign(bytes) => bytes.as_slice().len(),
        }
    }
}

fn append_utf8(bytes: &mut Vec<u8>, string: &UsvString) {
    let length = string.utf8_length();
    bytes.reserve(length);
    // SAFETY: The spare capacity has room for the encoding, which encode_utf8() initializes before the length grows
    //         over it.
    unsafe {
        let written = string.encode_utf8(bytes.spare_capacity_mut());
        bytes.set_len(bytes.len() + written);
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#convert-line-endings-to-native
fn convert_line_endings_to_native(s: &str) -> String {
    // 1. Let native line ending be the code point U+000A LF.
    let native_line_ending = "\n";

    // 2. If the underlying platform’s conventions are to represent newlines as a carriage return and line feed
    //    sequence, set native line ending to the code point U+000D CR followed by the code point U+000A LF.
    // NOTE: this step is a no-op since LibWeb does not compile on Windows, which is the only platform we know of that
    //       that uses a carriage return and line feed sequence for line endings.

    let code_points = s.as_bytes();
    let collect_token = |position: &mut usize| {
        let token_start = *position;
        while *position < code_points.len() && code_points[*position] != b'\n' && code_points[*position] != b'\r' {
            *position += 1;
        }
        &s[token_start..*position]
    };

    // 3. Set result to the empty string.
    let mut result = String::with_capacity(s.len());

    // 4. Let position be a position variable for s, initially pointing at the start of s.
    let mut position = 0;

    // 5. Let token be the result of collecting a sequence of code points that are not equal to U+000A LF or U+000D CR
    //    from s given position.
    let token = collect_token(&mut position);

    // 6. Append token to result.
    result.push_str(token);

    // 7. While position is not past the end of s:
    while position < code_points.len() {
        // 1. If the code point at position within s equals U+000D CR:
        if code_points[position] == b'\r' {
            // 1. Append native line ending to result.
            result.push_str(native_line_ending);

            // 2. Advance position by 1.
            position += 1;

            // 3. If position is not past the end of s and the code point at position within s equals U+000A LF advance
            //    position by 1.
            if position < code_points.len() && code_points[position] == b'\n' {
                position += 1;
            }
        }
        // 2. Otherwise if the code point at position within s equals U+000A LF, advance position by 1 and append native
        //    line ending to result.
        else if code_points[position] == b'\n' {
            position += 1;
            result.push_str(native_line_ending);
        }

        // 3. Let token be the result of collecting a sequence of code points that are not equal to U+000A LF or U+000D
        //    CR from s given position.
        let token = collect_token(&mut position);

        // 4. Append token to result.
        result.push_str(token);
    }

    // 8. Return result.
    result
}

// https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#process-blob-parts
pub(crate) fn process_blob_parts(blob_parts: &MarkedVec<'_, BlobPart>, options: &BlobPropertyBag) -> Vec<u8> {
    // 1. Let bytes be an empty sequence of bytes.
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();

    // 2. For each element in parts:
    for element in blob_parts.values().iter() {
        match element {
            // 1. If element is a USVString, run the following sub-steps:
            BlobPart::USVString(string) => {
                // 1. Let s be element.
                // 2. If the endings member of options is "native", set s to the result of converting line endings
                //    to native of element.
                // 3. Append the result of UTF-8 encoding s to bytes.
                if options.endings == EndingType::Native {
                    bytes.extend_from_slice(convert_line_endings_to_native(&string.to_utf8()).as_bytes());
                } else {
                    append_utf8(&mut bytes, string);
                }
            }
            // 2. If element is a BufferSource, get a copy of the bytes held by the buffer source, and append those
            //    bytes to bytes.
            BlobPart::BufferSource(buffer_source) => {
                // SAFETY: Appending the bytes neither runs script nor allocates a cell.
                unsafe { buffer_source.with_bytes(|held_bytes| bytes.extend_from_slice(held_bytes)) };
            }
            // 3. If element is a Blob, append the bytes it represents to bytes.
            BlobPart::Blob(blob) => bytes.extend_from_slice(&blob.raw_bytes()),
        }
    }

    // 3. Return bytes.
    bytes
}

fn is_basic_latin(string: &Utf16String) -> bool {
    match string.as_units() {
        Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(bytes) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(bytes) => {
            bytes.iter().all(|&byte| (0x20..=0x7E).contains(&byte))
        }
        Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => code_units.iter().all(|&code_unit| (0x20..=0x7E).contains(&code_unit)),
    }
}

/// The type of a Blob or a File that is constructed with the type member of its options.
pub(crate) fn type_from_options(r#type: &Utf16String) -> Utf16String {
    // 1. If the type member is provided and is not the empty string, let t be set to the type dictionary member.
    //    If t contains any characters outside the range U+0020 to U+007E, then set t to the empty string and return
    //    from these substeps.
    if !is_basic_latin(r#type) {
        return Utf16String::default();
    }

    // 2. Convert every character in t to ASCII lowercase.
    to_ascii_lowercase(r#type)
}

/// Converts a string whose code units are all in the range U+0020 to U+007E to ASCII lowercase.
fn to_ascii_lowercase(string: &Utf16String) -> Utf16String {
    let lowercase: Vec<u8> = string
        .to_utf16()
        .iter()
        .map(|&code_unit| (code_unit as u8).to_ascii_lowercase())
        .collect();
    Utf16String::from_ascii(&lowercase)
}

impl Blob {
    pub(crate) fn new(bytes: Vec<u8>, r#type: Utf16String) -> Self {
        Self {
            byte_sequence: RefCell::new(ByteSequence::Owned(bytes)),
            r#type,
        }
    }

    /// A Blob that refers to bytes that C++ hands over.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `bytes` must be bytes that C++ hands over, which nothing else destroys.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn with_foreign_bytes(bytes: ForeignBytesAbi, r#type: Utf16String) -> Self {
        Self {
            // SAFETY: The caller hands over the bytes.
            byte_sequence: RefCell::new(ByteSequence::Foreign(unsafe { ForeignBytes::from_abi(bytes) })),
            r#type,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn raw_bytes(&self) -> CellRef<'_, [u8]> {
        CellRef::map(self.byte_sequence.borrow(), ByteSequence::as_slice)
    }

    pub(crate) fn foreign_bytes_owner(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        match &*self.byte_sequence.borrow() {
            ByteSequence::Owned(_) => core::ptr::null_mut(),
            ByteSequence::Foreign(bytes) => bytes.owner.as_ptr(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn type_string(&self) -> &Utf16String {
        &self.r#type
    }

    /// Makes the Blob refer to the same bytes in storage that C++ hands over, as it does when it moves them to shared
    /// memory.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `bytes` must be bytes that C++ hands over, which nothing else destroys.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn set_foreign_bytes(&self, bytes: ForeignBytesAbi) {
        // SAFETY: The caller hands over the bytes.
        let bytes = unsafe { ForeignBytes::from_abi(bytes) };
        *self.byte_sequence.borrow_mut() = ByteSequence::Foreign(bytes);
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#ref-for-dom-blob-blob
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        _: &mut CallContext,
        blob_parts: Option<MarkedVec<'_, BlobPart>>,
        options: BlobPropertyBag,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. If invoked with zero parameters, return a new Blob object consisting of 0 bytes, with size set to 0, and
        //    with type set to the empty string.
        // NB: The steps below do that for a Blob constructed with zero parameters, whose options are an empty
        //     dictionary.

        // 2. Let bytes be the result of processing blob parts given blobParts and options.
        let bytes = blob_parts.map_or_else(Vec::new, |blob_parts| process_blob_parts(&blob_parts, &options));

        // 3. If the type member of the options argument is not the empty string, run the following sub-steps:
        let r#type = if options.r#type.is_empty() {
            Utf16String::default()
        } else {
            type_from_options(&options.r#type)
        };

        // 4. Return a Blob object referring to bytes as its associated byte sequence, with its size set to the length
        //    of bytes, and its type set to the value of t from the substeps above.
        Ok(Self::new(bytes, r#type))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-size
    pub(crate) fn size(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        Ok(self.raw_bytes().len() as u64)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-type
    pub(crate) fn r#type(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.r#type.clone())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-slice
    pub(crate) fn slice(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        start: Option<i64>,
        end: Option<i64>,
        content_type: Option<Utf16String>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Blob>> {
        // 1. Let sliceStart, sliceEnd, and sliceContentType be null.
        // 2. If start is given, set sliceStart to start.
        // 3. If end is given, set sliceEnd to end.
        // 3. If contentType is given, set sliceContentType to contentType.
        // 4. Return the result of slice blob given this, sliceStart, sliceEnd, and sliceContentType.
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| {
            self.slice_blob(start, end, content_type.as_ref())
        }))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#slice-blob
    pub(crate) fn slice_blob(&self, start: Option<i64>, end: Option<i64>, content_type: Option<&Utf16String>) -> Blob {
        let bytes = self.raw_bytes();

        // 1. Let originalSize be blob’s size.
        let original_size = i64::try_from(bytes.len()).expect("a Blob has fewer than 2^63 bytes");

        // 2. The start parameter, if non-null, is a value for the start point of a slice blob call, and must be treated
        //    as a byte-order position, with the zeroth position representing the first byte. User agents must normalize
        //    start according to the following:
        let relative_start = match start {
            // a. If start is null, let relativeStart be 0.
            None => 0,
            // b. If start is negative, let relativeStart be max((originalSize + start), 0).
            Some(start) if start < 0 => (original_size + start).max(0),
            // c. Otherwise, let relativeStart be min(start, originalSize).
            Some(start) => start.min(original_size),
        };

        // 3. The end parameter, if non-null. is a value for the end point of a slice blob call. User agents must
        //    normalize end according to the following:
        let relative_end = match end {
            // a. If end is null, let relativeEnd be originalSize.
            None => original_size,
            // b. If end is negative, let relativeEnd be max((originalSize + end), 0).
            Some(end) if end < 0 => (original_size + end).max(0),
            // c. Otherwise, let relativeEnd be min(end, originalSize).
            Some(end) => end.min(original_size),
        };

        // 4. The contentType parameter, if non-null, is used to set the ASCII-encoded string in lower case representing
        //    the media type of the Blob. User agents must normalize contentType according to the following:
        let relative_content_type = match content_type {
            // a. If contentType is null, let relativeContentType be set to the empty string.
            None => Utf16String::default(),
            // b. Otherwise, let relativeContentType be set to contentType and run the substeps below:
            // 1. If relativeContentType contains any characters outside the range of U+0020 to U+007E, then set
            //    relativeContentType to the empty string and return from these substeps:
            Some(content_type) if !is_basic_latin(content_type) => Utf16String::default(),
            // 2. Convert every character in relativeContentType to ASCII lowercase.
            Some(content_type) => to_ascii_lowercase(content_type),
        };

        // 5. Let span be max((relativeEnd - relativeStart), 0).
        let span = (relative_end - relative_start).max(0);

        // 6. Return a new Blob object S with the following characteristics:
        // a. S refers to span consecutive bytes from blob’s associated byte sequence, beginning with the byte at
        //    byte-order position relativeStart.
        // b. S.size = span.
        // c. S.type = relativeContentType.
        let relative_start = usize::try_from(relative_start).expect("relativeStart is not negative");
        let span = usize::try_from(span).expect("span is not negative");
        Blob::new(
            bytes[relative_start..relative_start + span].to_vec(),
            relative_content_type,
        )
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dom-blob-stream
    pub(crate) fn stream(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<ReadableStream>> {
        // SAFETY: The realm is live, LibWeb copies the bytes, and it returns a new ReadableStream.
        unsafe {
            let stream = web_blob_get_stream(cx.realm().as_ptr().cast(), ak::Span::new(&self.raw_bytes()));
            Ok(cell_from_abi(stream))
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dom-blob-text
    pub(crate) fn text(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        // SAFETY: The realm is live, LibWeb copies the bytes, and it returns a new promise.
        Ok(unsafe {
            promise_from_abi(web_blob_text(
                cx.realm().as_ptr().cast(),
                ak::Span::new(&self.raw_bytes()),
            ))
        })
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dom-blob-arraybuffer
    pub(crate) fn array_buffer(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        // SAFETY: The realm is live, LibWeb copies the bytes, and it returns a new promise.
        Ok(unsafe {
            promise_from_abi(web_blob_array_buffer(
                cx.realm().as_ptr().cast(),
                ak::Span::new(&self.raw_bytes()),
            ))
        })
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dom-blob-textstream
    pub(crate) fn text_stream(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<ReadableStream>> {
        // 1. Let stream be the result of calling get stream on this.
        let stream = self.stream(cx)?;

        // 2. Let decoder be a new TextDecoderStream in this's relevant realm.
        // 3. Set up decoder with UTF-8.
        let decoder = TextDecoderStream::set_up(cx, encoding_rs::UTF_8, false, false);

        // 4. Return the result of calling stream, piped through decoder.
        Ok(ReadableStream::piped_through(
            stream,
            cx.vm(),
            decoder.transform(),
            false,
            false,
            false,
            None,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dom-blob-bytes
    pub(crate) fn bytes(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        // SAFETY: The realm is live, LibWeb copies the bytes, and it returns a new promise.
        Ok(unsafe {
            promise_from_abi(web_blob_bytes(
                cx.realm().as_ptr().cast(),
                ak::Span::new(&self.raw_bytes()),
            ))
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn serialize(&self, serialized: &mut SerializationWriter) {
        // FIXME: 1. Set serialized.[[SnapshotState]] to value’s snapshot state.

        // NON-STANDARD: FileAPI spec doesn't specify that type should be serialized, although
        //               to be conformant with other browsers this needs to be serialized.
        serialized.write_utf16_string(&self.r#type);

        // 2. Set serialized.[[ByteSequence]] to value’s underlying byte sequence.
        serialized.write_bytes(&self.raw_bytes());
    }

    pub(crate) fn deserialize(serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // FIXME: 1. Set value’s snapshot state to serialized.[[SnapshotState]].

        // NON-STANDARD: FileAPI spec doesn't specify that type should be deserialized, although
        //               to be conformant with other browsers this needs to be deserialized.
        let r#type = serialized.read_utf16_string()?;

        // 2. Set value’s underlying byte sequence to serialized.[[ByteSequence]].
        Ok(Self::new(serialized.read_bytes()?, r#type))
    }
}

impl Serializable for Blob {
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        _for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.serialize(serialized);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn deserialization_steps(_: &mut CallContext, serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        Self::deserialize(serialized)
    }
}

//! The C ABI through which LibWeb's C++ creates the Blob, File and FileList objects that it hands to script, and reads
//! those that it receives, which Libraries/LibWeb/FileAPI/Blob.h, File.h and FileList.h declare. A Blob cell can be that
//! of a File.

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::Vm;

use super::blob::{AnyBlob, Blob, BlobPropertyBag, EndingType, ForeignBytesAbi};
use super::file::{File, FilePropertyBag};
use super::file_list::FileList;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, InterfaceCell, allocate, cell_into_abi};

/// The Blob or File whose cell C++ lends, as a Blob.
fn blob_from_abi(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> &Blob {
    if let Some(blob) = cell.implementation_if::<Blob>() {
        return blob;
    }
    cell.implementation::<File>().parent()
}

/// The Blob or File whose cell C++ lends.
pub(crate) fn any_blob_from_abi(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> AnyBlob {
    match cell.object_if::<Blob>() {
        Some(blob) => AnyBlob::Blob(blob),
        None => AnyBlob::File(cell.object()),
    }
}

/// A new Blob that refers to the bytes that C++ hands over, with the type, a raw AK::Utf16String that C++ hands over.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `vm` must be the live VM, `bytes` bytes that C++ hands over, and `type` a raw string that C++ owns a reference to.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_blob_create(vm: &Vm, bytes: ForeignBytesAbi, r#type: Utf16String) -> *mut c_void {
    // SAFETY: The caller hands over the bytes and the string.
    let blob = unsafe { Blob::with_foreign_bytes(bytes, r#type) };
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| blob))
}

/// The byte sequence of the Blob or File, which lives until the object dies or C++ moves its bytes into immutable
/// bytes or shared memory.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_blob_byte_sequence(cell: &InterfaceCell, out_length: &mut usize) -> *const u8 {
    let bytes = blob_from_abi(cell).raw_bytes();
    *out_length = bytes.len();
    bytes.as_ptr()
}

/// The owner of the bytes of the Blob or File if C++ handed them over, or null.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_blob_foreign_bytes_owner(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> *mut c_void {
    blob_from_abi(cell).foreign_bytes_owner()
}

/// Makes the Blob or File refer to the same bytes in storage that C++ hands over.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `cell` must be the live cell of a Blob or a File, and `bytes` bytes that C++ hands over, which are those of the
/// object.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_blob_set_foreign_bytes(cell: &InterfaceCell, bytes: ForeignBytesAbi) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell and hands over the bytes.
    unsafe { blob_from_abi(cell).set_foreign_bytes(bytes) };
}

/// The type of the Blob or File, a raw AK::Utf16String that the call lends for as long as the object lives.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_blob_type(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> usize {
    blob_from_abi(cell).type_string().raw_identity()
}

/// The result of slice blob given the Blob or File, start, end and contentType, which are null unless `has_start`,
/// `has_end` and C++ passes a contentType, https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#slice-blob
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
#[allow(
    clippy::too_many_arguments,
    reason = "the arguments are the parameters of slice blob, which can each be null"
)]
pub extern "C" fn web_blob_slice(
    vm: &Vm,
    cell: &InterfaceCell,
    has_start: bool,
    start: i64,
    has_end: bool,
    end: i64,
    content_type: Option<Utf16String>,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let blob = blob_from_abi(cell);
    let sliced_blob = blob.slice_blob(
        has_start.then_some(start),
        has_end.then_some(end),
        content_type.as_ref(),
    );
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| sliced_blob))
}

/// Whether the cell of a Blob or a File is that of a File.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_blob_is_file(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> bool {
    cell.object_if::<File>().is_some()
}

/// A new File, as the File constructor creates it given one part of the bytes, the file name and the options with the
/// type, which are raw AK::Utf16Strings that C++ hands over, and the last modified date if `has_last_modified`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_file_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
    file_name: Utf16String,
    r#type: Utf16String,
    has_last_modified: bool,
    last_modified: i64,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let options = FilePropertyBag {
        parent: BlobPropertyBag {
            endings: EndingType::Transparent,
            r#type,
        },
        last_modified: has_last_modified.then_some(last_modified),
    };
    let file = File::create(bytes.as_slice().to_vec(), file_name, &options);
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| file))
}

/// The name of the File, a raw AK::Utf16String that the call lends for as long as the File lives.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_file_name(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> usize {
    cell.object::<File>().name_string().raw_identity()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_file_last_modified(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> i64 {
    cell.object::<File>().last_modified_value()
}

/// A new FileList with no files.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_file_list_create(vm: &Vm) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |defer_gc| FileList::new(defer_gc, &[])))
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_file_list_add_file(vm: &Vm, list: &InterfaceCell, file: &InterfaceCell) {
    let (list, file) = (list.object::<FileList>(), file.object::<File>());
    list.add_file(vm, file);
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_file_list_length(list: &InterfaceCell) -> u32 {
    list.object::<FileList>().file_count()
}

/// The cell of the File at the index of the FileList, or null if it has none there.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_file_list_item(list: &InterfaceCell, index: u32) -> *mut c_void {
    list.object::<FileList>()
        .file(index)
        .map_or(core::ptr::null_mut(), cell_into_abi)
}

//! FileList, https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section

use libjs_rust::api::{DeferGc, GcRefCell, MarkedVec, Trace, Vm};

use super::file::File;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::structured_data::{Serializable, SerializationReader, SerializationWriter};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct FileList {
    files: GcRefCell<Vec<Ref<File>>>,
}

impl Wrappable for FileList {}

impl FileList {
    pub(crate) fn new(_: &DeferGc<'_>, files: &[Ref<File>]) -> Self {
        Self {
            files: GcRefCell::new(files.to_vec()),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn add_file(&self, vm: &Vm, file: Ref<File>) {
        self.files.borrow_mut(vm).push(file);
    }

    pub(crate) fn file_count(&self) -> u32 {
        u32::try_from(self.files.borrow().len()).expect("a list has fewer than 2^32 files")
    }

    pub(crate) fn file(&self, index: u32) -> Option<Ref<File>> {
        self.files.borrow().get(index as usize).copied()
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-length
    pub(crate) fn length(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        Ok(self.file_count())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-item
    pub(crate) fn item(&self, _: &mut CallContext, index: u32) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<File>>> {
        Ok(self.file(index))
    }
}

impl Serializable for FileList {
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Set serialized.[[Files]] to an empty list.
        // 2. For each file in value, append the sub-serialization of file to serialized.[[Files]].
        // NB: The files are serialized in place, as they were before FileList was implemented in Rust, so that stored
        //     values keep the positions that their objects have in the memory of the serialization.
        let count = self.file_count();
        serialized.write_u64(u64::from(count));
        for index in 0..count {
            let file = self.file(index).expect("the list holds the file");
            serialized.write_object_in_place::<File>(cx, &file, for_storage)?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    fn deserialization_steps(cx: &mut CallContext, serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // 1. For each file of serialized.[[Files]], add the sub-deserialization of file to value.
        let count = serialized.read_u64()?;
        let files = MarkedVec::new(cx.vm());
        for _ in 0..count {
            files.push(serialized.read_object_in_place::<File>(cx)?);
        }

        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |defer_gc| Self::new(defer_gc, &files.values())))
    }
}

//! FileReaderSync, https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#FileReaderSync

use super::blob::AnyBlob;

// https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#FileReaderSync
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct FileReaderSync;

impl Wrappable for FileReaderSync {}

impl FileReaderSync {
    pub(crate) fn construct(_: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        Ok(Self)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-readAsArrayBufferSync
    pub(crate) fn read_as_array_buffer(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, blob: AnyBlob) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
        Ok(ArrayBuffer::create_from_bytes(
            cx.vm(),
            cx.realm(),
            &blob.raw_bytes(),
            ArrayBufferShared::No,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-readAsBinaryStringSync
    pub(crate) fn read_as_binary_string(&self, _: &mut CallContext, blob: AnyBlob) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(read_as(&blob, Type::BinaryString, None))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-readAsTextSync
    pub(crate) fn read_as_text(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        blob: AnyBlob,
        encoding: Option<Utf16String>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(read_as(&blob, Type::Text, encoding.as_ref()))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-readAsDataURLSync
    pub(crate) fn read_as_data_url(&self, _: &mut CallContext, blob: AnyBlob) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(read_as(&blob, Type::DataURL, None))
    }
}

fn read_as(blob: &AnyBlob, r#type: Type, encoding: Option<&Utf16String>) -> Utf16String {
    let blob_type = blob.type_string();
    match package_data(blob.raw_bytes().to_vec(), r#type, Some(blob_type), encoding) {
        PackagedData::String(string) => string,
        PackagedData::Bytes(_) => unreachable!("package data returns a string for a type other than ArrayBuffer"),
    }
}

/// The union (DOMString or ArrayBuffer) of FileAPI/FileReader.idl.
pub(crate) enum DOMStringOrArrayBuffer {
    DOMString(Utf16String),
    ArrayBuffer(Gc<ArrayBuffer>),
}

// https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dom-filereader-readystate
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum State {
    // The FileReader object has been constructed, and there are no pending reads. None of the read methods have been called.
    // This is the default state of a newly minted FileReader object, until one of the read methods have been called on it.
    Empty = 0,

    // A File or Blob is being read. One of the read methods is being processed, and no error has occurred during the read.
    Loading = 1,

    // The entire File or Blob has been read into memory, OR a file read error occurred, OR the read was aborted using abort().
    // The FileReader is no longer reading a File or Blob.
    // If readyState is set to DONE it means at least one of the read methods have been called on this FileReader.
    Done = 2,
}

/// The type that a read operation packages its bytes as.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum Type {
    ArrayBuffer,
    BinaryString,
    Text,
    DataURL,
}

/// What package data returns.
pub(crate) enum PackagedData {
    String(Utf16String),
    Bytes(Vec<u8>),
}

// https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-filereader
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct FileReader {
    event_target: CppEventTarget,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,

    // Internal state to handle aborting the FileReader.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pending_tasks: RefCell<Vec<TaskId>>,
    // The read operation being processed, which abort() terminates, and which a later read replaces.
    current_read: Cell<Option<ReadOperationRef>>,

    // A FileReader has an associated state, that is "empty", "loading", or "done". It is initially "empty".
    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filereader-state
    #[gc(untraced)]
    state: Cell<State>,

    // A FileReader has an associated result (null, a DOMString or an ArrayBuffer). It is initially null.
    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filereader-result
    #[gc(untraced)]
    result: RefCell<Option<PackagedData>>,

    // The result ArrayBuffer must keep a stable identity across accesses within a
    // world, so it is created lazily and cached per wrapper world. The cache holds
    // weak references (a dropped ArrayBuffer is unobservable) and is invalidated
    // whenever the result changes. See set_result().
    #[gc(untraced)]
    result_array_buffers: RefCell<Vec<(WrapperWorld, GcWeak<ArrayBuffer>)>>,
}

impl Wrappable for FileReader {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event_target.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for FileReader {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
}

/// The steps of a task that FileReader::queue_a_task() queues, with what they capture.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct QueuedSteps<C> {
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, C),
}

// SAFETY: The steps are a plain function, which holds no cells.
unsafe impl<C: Trace> Trace for QueuedSteps<C> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.captures.trace(visitor);
    }
}

/// The state of a read operation, https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#readOperation, which its steps keep across chunks.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct ReadOperation {
    reader: Ref<ReadableStreamDefaultReader>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    bytes: RefCell<Vec<u8>>,
    is_first_chunk: Cell<bool>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    progress_timer: Cell<Option<Instant>>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    r#type: Type,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    encoding_name: Option<Utf16String>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    blobs_type: Utf16String,
}

static READ_OPERATION_CLASS: EmbedderClass<ReadOperation> = EmbedderClass::new("FileReaderReadOperation");

impl EmbedderValue for ReadOperation {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &READ_OPERATION_CLASS;
}

type ReadOperationRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<ReadOperation>>;

fn to_utf8_string(string: &Utf16String) -> String {
    String::from_utf16_lossy(&string.to_utf16())
}

// https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-package-data
pub(crate) fn package_data(
    bytes: Vec<u8>,
    r#type: Type,
    mime_type: Option<&Utf16String>,
    encoding_name: Option<&Utf16String>,
) -> PackagedData {
    // A Blob has an associated package data algorithm, given bytes, a type, a optional mimeType, and a optional encodingName, which switches on type and runs the associated steps:
    match r#type {
        Type::DataURL => {
            // Return bytes as a DataURL [RFC2397] subject to the considerations below:
            // Use mimeType as part of the Data URL if it is available in keeping with the Data URL specification [RFC2397].
            // If mimeType is not available return a Data URL without a media-type. [RFC2397].
            // https://github.com/w3c/FileAPI/issues/104
            let mime_string = match mime_type {
                Some(mime_type) if !mime_type.is_empty() => to_utf8_string(mime_type),
                _ => String::from("application/octet-stream"),
            };
            let payload = to_utf8_string(&encode_base64(&bytes, Base64Alphabet::Base64, false));
            let url = liburl_rust::create_with_data(&mime_string, &payload, true);
            PackagedData::String(Utf16String::from_utf8(url.serialize(ExcludeFragment::No)))
        }
        Type::Text => {
            // 1. Let encoding be failure.
            let mut encoding: Option<&'static Encoding> = None;

            // 2. If the encodingName is present, set encoding to the result of getting an encoding from encodingName.
            if let Some(encoding_name) = encoding_name {
                encoding = encoding_for_label(encoding_name.as_units());
            }

            // 3. If encoding is failure, and mimeType is present:
            if encoding.is_none()
                && let Some(mime_type) = mime_type
            {
                // 1. Let type be the result of parse a MIME type given mimeType.
                let code_points: Vec<char> = char::decode_utf16(mime_type.to_utf16().iter().copied())
                    .map(|code_point| code_point.unwrap_or(char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER))
                    .collect();
                let maybe_type = MimeType::parse(&code_points);

                // 2. If type is not failure, set encoding to the result of getting an encoding from type’s parameters["charset"].
                if let Some(r#type) = maybe_type
                    && let Some((_, charset)) = r#type.parameters().find(|(name, _)| *name == "charset")
                {
                    encoding = Encoding::for_label(charset.as_bytes());
                }
            }

            // 4. If encoding is failure, then set encoding to UTF-8.
            // 5. Decode bytes using fallback encoding encoding, and return the result.
            let (decoded, _, _) = encoding.unwrap_or(UTF_8).decode(&bytes);
            PackagedData::String(Utf16String::from_utf8(&decoded))
        }
        // Return bytes. The binding wrapper performs the ArrayBuffer allocation
        // for the caller's realm.
        Type::ArrayBuffer => PackagedData::Bytes(bytes),
        Type::BinaryString => {
            // Return bytes as a binary string, in which every byte is represented by a code unit of equal value [0..255].
            let code_units: Vec<u16> = bytes.iter().map(|&byte| u16::from(byte)).collect();
            PackagedData::String(Utf16String::from_utf16(&code_units))
        }
    }
}

impl FileReader {
    fn new(realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Self {
        Self {
            event_target: CppEventTarget::new(),
            realm,
            pending_tasks: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            current_read: Cell::new(None),
            state: Cell::new(State::Empty),
            result: RefCell::new(None),
            result_array_buffers: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filereaderConstrctr
    pub(crate) fn construct(cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let reader = allocate(cx.vm(), |_| Self::new(cx.realm()));
        reader.event_target.set_owner(reader);
        Ok(reader)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dom-filereader-readystate
    pub(crate) fn ready_state(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u16> {
        Ok(self.state.get() as u16)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dom-filereader-result
    pub(crate) fn result(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<DOMStringOrArrayBuffer>> {
        let result = self.result.borrow();
        let Some(result) = &*result else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        match result {
            PackagedData::String(string) => Ok(Some(DOMStringOrArrayBuffer::DOMString(string.clone()))),
            PackagedData::Bytes(bytes) => {
                // Return the same ArrayBuffer for repeated accesses in this world; the ArrayBuffer
                // is created in the receiver's realm and its identity must be stable.
                let wrapper_world = wrapper_world_of(cx.vm(), cx.realm());
                let cached = self
                    .result_array_buffers
                    .borrow()
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(world, _)| *world == wrapper_world)
                    .and_then(|(_, array_buffer)| array_buffer.get());
                if let Some(cached) = cached {
                    return Ok(Some(DOMStringOrArrayBuffer::ArrayBuffer(cached)));
                }
                let array_buffer = ArrayBuffer::create_from_bytes(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), bytes, ArrayBufferShared::No);
                let mut result_array_buffers = self.result_array_buffers.borrow_mut();
                result_array_buffers.retain(|(world, _)| *world != wrapper_world);
                result_array_buffers.push((wrapper_world, GcWeak::new(cx.vm().heap(), array_buffer)));
                Ok(Some(DOMStringOrArrayBuffer::ArrayBuffer(array_buffer)))
            }
        }
    }

    fn set_result(&self, result: Option<PackagedData>) {
        *self.result.borrow_mut() = result;

        // Any previously handed-out ArrayBuffers belong to the old result.
        self.result_array_buffers.borrow_mut().clear();
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dom-filereader-error
    pub(crate) fn error(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CppInterface>> {
        // A FileReader has an associated error (null or a DOMException). It is initially null.
        // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filereader-error
        // NB: Nothing sets the error yet, so it stays null.
        Ok(None)
    }

    fn fire_event(&self, event_name: &str) {
        let event = CppEvent::create(self.realm, event_name, false, false, false);
        self.event_target.dispatch_event(&event);
    }

    fn queue_a_task<C: Trace + Copy + 'static>(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm, captures: C, steps: fn(&Vm, C)) {
        // To implement the requirement of removing queued tasks on an abort we keep track of a list of
        // task IDs which are pending evaluation. This allows an abort to go through the task queue to
        // remove those pending tasks.

        let id = queue_a_global_task(
            vm,
            this.realm.global_object(),
            TaskSource::FileReading,
            (this, QueuedSteps { captures, steps }),
            |vm, (this, task)| {
                let current_task = currently_running_task(this.realm);

                (task.steps)(vm, task.captures);

                this.pending_tasks.borrow_mut().retain(|id| *id != current_task);
            },
        );
        this.pending_tasks.borrow_mut().push(id);
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#readOperation
    fn read_operation(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        blob: &AnyBlob,
        r#type: Type,
        encoding_name: Option<Utf16String>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let realm = this.realm;
        let blobs_type = blob.type_string().clone();

        // 1. If fr’s state is "loading", throw an InvalidStateError DOMException.
        if this.state.get() == State::Loading {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidStateError",
                Utf16String::from_utf8("Read already in progress"),
            ));
        }

        // 2. Set fr’s state to "loading".
        this.state.set(State::Loading);

        // 3. Set fr’s result to null.
        this.set_result(None);

        // 4. Set fr’s error to null.
        // NB: The error is always null, see error().

        // 5. Let stream be the result of calling get stream on blob.
        let stream = blob.stream(&mut CallContext::new(vm, realm))?;

        // 6. Let reader be the result of getting a reader from stream.
        let reader = ReadableStream::get_a_reader(stream, vm)?;

        // 7. Let bytes be an empty byte sequence.
        let bytes = Vec::new();

        // 8. Let chunkPromise be the result of reading a chunk from stream with reader.
        let chunk_promise = ReadableStreamDefaultReader::read(&reader, &mut CallContext::new(vm, realm))?;

        // 9. Let isFirstChunk be true.
        let is_first_chunk = true;

        // 10. In parallel, while true:
        let state = READ_OPERATION_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| ReadOperation {
            reader,
            bytes: RefCell::new(bytes),
            is_first_chunk: Cell::new(is_first_chunk),
            progress_timer: Cell::new(None),
            r#type,
            encoding_name,
            blobs_type,
        });
        this.current_read.set(Some(state));

        queue_a_global_task(
            vm,
            realm.global_object(),
            TaskSource::FileReading,
            (*this, state, chunk_promise),
            |vm, (this, state, chunk_promise)| {
                with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(this.realm, || {
                    Self::process_next_chunk(vm, this, state, chunk_promise);
                });
            },
        );

        Ok(())
    }

    fn process_next_chunk(vm: &Vm, this: Ref<Self>, state: ReadOperationRef, chunk_promise: WebIdlPromise) {
        // 1. Wait for chunkPromise to be fulfilled or rejected.
        react_to_promise(
            vm,
            chunk_promise,
            (this, state),
            Some(|cx, (this, state), promise_value| {
                with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(this.realm, || {
                    Self::chunk_promise_fulfilled(cx.vm(), this, state, promise_value);
                });
                Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
            }),
            // 6. Otherwise, if chunkPromise is rejected with an error error, queue a task to run the following steps and abort this algorithm:
            Some(|cx, (this, state), _| {
                with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(this.realm, || {
                    if this.current_read.get() != Some(state) {
                        return;
                    }

                    Self::queue_a_task(this, cx.vm(), this, |_, this| {
                        // 1. Set fr’s state to "done".
                        this.state.set(State::Done);

                        // FIXME: 2. Set fr’s error to error.

                        // 3. Fire a progress event called error at fr.
                        this.fire_event("error");

                        // 4. If fr’s state is not "loading", fire a progress event called loadend at fr.
                        if this.state.get() != State::Loading {
                            this.fire_event("loadend");
                        }

                        // NOTE: Event handler for the error event could have started another load, if that happens the
                        //       loadend event for this load is not fired.
                    });
                });
                Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
            }),
        );
    }

    fn chunk_promise_fulfilled(vm: &Vm, this: Ref<Self>, state: ReadOperationRef, promise_value: Value) {
        if this.current_read.get() != Some(state) {
            return;
        }

        // 2. If chunkPromise is fulfilled, and isFirstChunk is true, queue a task to fire a progress event called loadstart at fr.
        // NOTE: ISSUE 2 We might change loadstart to be dispatched synchronously, to align with XMLHttpRequest behavior. [Issue #119]
        if state.is_first_chunk.get() {
            Self::queue_a_task(this, vm, this, |_, this| this.fire_event("loadstart"));
        }

        // 3. Set isFirstChunk to false.
        state.is_first_chunk.set(false);

        assert!(promise_value.is_object());
        let result = promise_value.as_object();

        let value = result.get(vm, &PropertyKey::from_utf8("value")).must();
        let done = result.get(vm, &PropertyKey::from_utf8("done")).must();

        let byte_sequence = if !done.as_bool() && value.is_object() {
            value
                .as_object()
                .downcast::<TypedArrayBase>()
                .filter(|typed_array| typed_array.kind() == TypedArrayKind::Uint8Array)
        } else {
            None
        };

        // 4. If chunkPromise is fulfilled with an object whose done property is false and whose value property is a Uint8Array object, run these steps:
        if let Some(byte_sequence) = byte_sequence {
            // 1. Let bs be the byte sequence represented by the Uint8Array object.
            // 2. Append bs to bytes.
            // SAFETY: Appending the bytes neither runs script nor allocates a cell.
            unsafe {
                BufferSource::TypedArray(byte_sequence)
                    .with_bytes(|bytes| state.bytes.borrow_mut().extend_from_slice(bytes));
            }

            // 3. If roughly 50ms have passed since these steps were last invoked, queue a task to fire a progress event called progress at fr.
            let now = Instant::now();
            let enough_time_passed = state
                .progress_timer
                .get()
                .is_none_or(|progress_timer| now - progress_timer >= Duration::from_millis(50));
            // WPT tests for this and expects no progress event to fire when there isn't any data.
            // See http://wpt.live/FileAPI/reading-data-section/filereader_events.any.html
            let contained_data = byte_sequence.array_length().length() > 0;
            if enough_time_passed && contained_data {
                Self::queue_a_task(this, vm, this, |_, this| this.fire_event("progress"));
                state.progress_timer.set(Some(now));
            }

            // 4. Set chunkPromise to the result of reading a chunk from stream with reader.
            let next_chunk_promise =
                ReadableStreamDefaultReader::read(&state.reader, &mut CallContext::new(vm, this.realm)).must();
            Self::process_next_chunk(vm, this, state, next_chunk_promise);
        }
        // 5. Otherwise, if chunkPromise is fulfilled with an object whose done property is true, queue a task to run the following steps and abort this algorithm:
        else if done.as_bool() {
            Self::queue_a_task(this, vm, (this, state), |_, (this, state)| {
                // 1. Set fr’s state to "done".
                this.state.set(State::Done);

                // 2. Let result be the result of package data given bytes, type, blob’s type, and encodingName.
                let bytes = core::mem::take(&mut *state.bytes.borrow_mut());
                let result = package_data(
                    bytes,
                    state.r#type,
                    Some(&state.blobs_type),
                    state.encoding_name.as_ref(),
                );

                // 3. If package data threw an exception error:
                // NB: Package data does not throw.

                // 4. Else:
                // 1. Set fr’s result to result.
                this.set_result(Some(result));

                // 2. Fire a progress event called load at the fr.
                this.fire_event("load");

                // 5. If fr’s state is not "loading", fire a progress event called loadend at the fr.
                if this.state.get() != State::Loading {
                    this.fire_event("loadend");
                }

                // NOTE: Event handler for the load or error events could have started another load, if that happens
                //       the loadend event for this load is not fired.
            });
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-readAsDataURL
    pub(crate) fn read_as_data_url(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext, blob: AnyBlob) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The readAsDataURL(blob) method, when invoked, must initiate a read operation for blob with DataURL.
        Self::read_operation(this, cx, &blob, Type::DataURL, None)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-readAsText
    pub(crate) fn read_as_text(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        blob: AnyBlob,
        encoding: Option<Utf16String>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The readAsText(blob, encoding) method, when invoked, must initiate a read operation for blob with Text and encoding.
        Self::read_operation(this, cx, &blob, Type::Text, encoding)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-readAsArrayBuffer
    pub(crate) fn read_as_array_buffer(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext, blob: AnyBlob) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The readAsArrayBuffer(blob) method, when invoked, must initiate a read operation for blob with ArrayBuffer.
        Self::read_operation(this, cx, &blob, Type::ArrayBuffer, None)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-readAsBinaryString
    pub(crate) fn read_as_binary_string(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext, blob: AnyBlob) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The readAsBinaryString(blob) method, when invoked, must initiate a read operation for blob with BinaryString.
        // NOTE: The use of readAsArrayBuffer() is preferred over readAsBinaryString(), which is provided for backwards compatibility.
        Self::read_operation(this, cx, &blob, Type::BinaryString, None)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-abort
    pub(crate) fn abort(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If this's state is "empty" or if this's state is "done" set this's result to null and terminate this algorithm.
        if self.state.get() == State::Empty || self.state.get() == State::Done {
            self.set_result(None);
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. If this's state is "loading" set this's state to "done" and set this's result to null.
        if self.state.get() == State::Loading {
            self.state.set(State::Done);
            self.set_result(None);
        }

        // 3. If there are any tasks from this on the file reading task source in an affiliated task queue, then remove those tasks from that task queue.
        let pending_tasks = self.pending_tasks.take();
        remove_tasks(self.realm, &pending_tasks);

        // 4. Terminate the algorithm for the read method being processed.
        self.current_read.set(None);

        // 5. Fire a progress event called abort at this.
        self.fire_event("abort");

        // 6. If this's state is not "loading", fire a progress event called loadend at this.
        if self.state.get() != State::Loading {
            self.fire_event("loadend");
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}

//! File, https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#file-section

use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{MarkedVec, Trace};

use super::blob::{Blob, BlobPart, BlobPropertyBag, process_blob_parts, type_from_options};
use crate::bindings::conversions::UsvString;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Wrappable};
use crate::bindings::structured_data::{Serializable, SerializationReader, SerializationWriter};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

/// The dictionary FilePropertyBag of FileAPI/File.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) struct FilePropertyBag {
    pub(crate) parent: BlobPropertyBag,
    pub(crate) last_modified: Option<i64>,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct File {
    blob: Blob,
    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-name
    #[gc(untraced)]
    name: Utf16String,
    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-lastModified
    #[gc(untraced)]
    last_modified: i64,
}

impl Wrappable for File {
    const OWNS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY: bool = true;
    const COUNTS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_WHEN_ALLOCATED: bool = true;

    fn external_memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.blob.external_memory_size()
    }
}

impl Inherits<Blob> for File {
    fn parent(&self) -> &Blob {
        &self.blob
    }
}

impl File {
    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#ref-for-dom-file-file
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        _: &mut CallContext,
        file_bits: MarkedVec<'_, BlobPart>,
        file_name: UsvString,
        options: FilePropertyBag,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Let bytes be the result of processing blob parts given fileBits and options.
        let bytes = process_blob_parts(&file_bits, &options.parent);

        Ok(Self::create(bytes, file_name.into_utf16_string(), &options))
    }

    /// Steps 2 to 4 of the File constructor, given the bytes that step 1 results in.
    pub(crate) fn create(bytes: Vec<u8>, file_name: Utf16String, options: &FilePropertyBag) -> Self {
        // 2. Let n be the fileName argument to the constructor.
        //    NOTE: Underlying OS filesystems use differing conventions for file name; with constructed files, mandating
        //          UTF-16 lessens ambiquity when file names are converted to byte sequences.
        let name = file_name;

        // 3. Process FilePropertyBag dictionary argument by running the following substeps:
        let r#type = type_from_options(&options.parent.r#type);

        // 3. If the lastModified member is provided, let d be set to the lastModified dictionary member. If it is not
        //    provided, set d to the current date and time represented as the number of milliseconds since the Unix
        //    Epoch (which is the equivalent of Date.now() [ECMA-262]).
        //    Note: Since ECMA-262 Date objects convert to long long values representing the number of milliseconds
        //          since the Unix Epoch, the lastModified member could be a Date object [ECMA-262].
        let last_modified = options.last_modified.unwrap_or_else(|| {
            let since_epoch = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default();
            i64::try_from(since_epoch.as_millis()).unwrap_or(i64::MAX)
        });

        // 4. Return a new File object F such that:
        //    2. F refers to the bytes byte sequence.
        //       NOTE: Spec started at 2 therefore keeping the same number sequence here.
        //    3. F.size is set to the number of total bytes in bytes.
        //    4. F.name is set to n.
        //    5. F.type is set to t.
        //    6. F.lastModified is set to d.
        Self {
            blob: Blob::new(bytes, r#type),
            name,
            last_modified,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn name_string(&self) -> &Utf16String {
        &self.name
    }

    pub(crate) fn last_modified_value(&self) -> i64 {
        self.last_modified
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-name
    pub(crate) fn name(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.name.clone())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-lastModified
    pub(crate) fn last_modified(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<i64> {
        Ok(self.last_modified)
    }
}

impl Serializable for File {
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        _for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Set serialized.[[SnapshotState]] to value’s snapshot state.
        // 2. Set serialized.[[ByteSequence]] to value’s underlying byte sequence.
        self.blob.serialize(serialized);

        // 3. Set serialized.[[Name]] to the value of value’s name attribute.
        serialized.write_utf16_string(&self.name);

        // 4. Set serialized.[[LastModified]] to the value of value’s lastModified attribute.
        serialized.write_i64(self.last_modified);

        Ok(())
    }

    fn deserialization_steps(_: &mut CallContext, serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Set value’s snapshot state to serialized.[[SnapshotState]].
        // 2. Set value’s underlying byte sequence to serialized.[[ByteSequence]].
        let blob = Blob::deserialize(serialized)?;

        // 3. Initialize the value of value’s name attribute to serialized.[[Name]].
        let name = serialized.read_utf16_string()?;

        // 4. Initialize the value of value’s lastModified attribute to serialized.[[LastModified]].
        let last_modified = serialized.read_i64()?;

        Ok(Self {
            blob,
            name,
            last_modified,
        })
    }
}

//! The entry points through which LibWeb's C++ code runs the Navigator steps of the Gamepad API, declared in
//! Libraries/LibWeb/Gamepad/NavigatorGamepad.cpp.

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::Vm;

use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::{LentCppCell, cpp_class};
use crate::bindings::global_object::CppWindow;
use crate::gamepad::gamepad::{GamepadDescription, GamepadDescriptionAbi, GamepadState, GamepadStateAbi};
use crate::gamepad::navigator_gamepad::{
    get_gamepads, handle_gamepad_connected, handle_gamepad_disconnected, handle_gamepad_updated,
};

/// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-navigator-getgamepads
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the live VM and live Windows.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_gamepad_get_gamepads(
    vm: &Vm,
    navigator_window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>,
    current_window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>,
    ctx: *mut c_void,
    on_gamepad: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void),
) -> bool {
    let (navigator_window, current_window) = (
        CppWindow::from_lent(navigator_window),
        CppWindow::from_lent(current_window),
    );
    let Ok(gamepads) = get_gamepads(vm, &navigator_window, &current_window) else {
        return false;
    };
    for index in 0..gamepads.len() {
        let gamepad = gamepads.get(index).flatten();
        let cell = gamepad.map_or(core::ptr::null_mut(), |gamepad| gamepad.as_ptr().cast());
        // SAFETY: The cell is live, and the caller roots it.
        unsafe { on_gamepad(ctx, cell) };
    }
    true
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#event-gamepadconnected
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the live VM, a live Window and a description that the caller lends for the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_gamepad_handle_gamepad_connected(
    vm: &Vm,
    window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>,
    description: *const GamepadDescriptionAbi<'_>,
) {
    // SAFETY: The caller lends the description.
    let (window, description) = unsafe { (CppWindow::from_lent(window), &*description) };
    handle_gamepad_connected(vm, &window, GamepadDescription::from_abi(description));
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-receives-new-button-or-axis-input-values
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the live VM, a live Window and a state that the caller lends for the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_gamepad_handle_gamepad_updated(
    vm: &Vm,
    window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>,
    state: *const GamepadStateAbi<'_>,
) {
    // SAFETY: The caller lends the state.
    let (window, state) = unsafe { (CppWindow::from_lent(window), &*state) };
    handle_gamepad_updated(vm, &window, GamepadState::from_abi(state));
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#event-gamepaddisconnected
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_gamepad_handle_gamepad_disconnected(
    vm: &Vm,
    window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>,
    handle: u32,
) {
    let window = CppWindow::from_lent(window);
    handle_gamepad_disconnected(vm, &window, handle);
}

use core::cell::Cell;

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-gamepadbutton
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct GamepadButton {
    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-pressed
    // A flag indicating that the button is pressed
    pressed: Cell<bool>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-touched
    // A flag indicating that the button is touched
    touched: Cell<bool>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-value
    // A double representing the button value scaled to the range [0 .. 1]
    value: Cell<f64>,
}

impl Wrappable for GamepadButton {}

impl GamepadButton {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm) -> Ref<Self> {
        allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            pressed: Cell::new(false),
            touched: Cell::new(false),
            value: Cell::new(0.0),
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn pressed(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.pressed.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn touched(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.touched.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn value(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.value.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_pressed(&self) -> bool {
        self.pressed.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_pressed(&self, pressed: bool) {
        self.pressed.set(pressed);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_touched(&self, touched: bool) {
        self.touched.set(touched);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_value(&self, value: f64) {
        self.value.set(value);
    }
}

/// The dictionary GamepadEventInit of Gamepad/GamepadEvent.idl.

    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) gamepad: Option<Ref<Gamepad>>,

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-gamepadevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct GamepadEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    gamepad: Option<Ref<Gamepad>>,
}

impl Wrappable for GamepadEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl GamepadEvent {
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: GamepadEventInit,
    ) -> Ref<GamepadEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.parent.bubbles,
            event_init.parent.cancelable,
            event_init.parent.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| GamepadEvent {
            event,
            gamepad: event_init.gamepad,
        });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: GamepadEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<GamepadEvent>> {
        Ok(Self::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &r#type, event_init_dict))
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    pub(crate) fn gamepad(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<Gamepad>>> {
        Ok(self.gamepad)
    }
}
