//! GamepadHapticActuator, https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#gamepadhapticactuator-interface

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, GcRefCell, Object, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::ToJs;
use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::CppCell;
use crate::bindings::global_object::{CppWindow, window_from_global_object};
use crate::bindings::interface::{
    Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_from_abi, with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks,
};
use crate::bindings::promise::{
    TaskSource, WebIdlPromise, deferred_invoke, promise_realm, queue_a_global_task, reject_promise_with_exception,
    resolve_promise,
};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::gamepad::gamepad::Gamepad;
use crate::html::visibility_state::VisibilityState;
use crate::platform::timer::CppTimer;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_gamepad_play_effect(
        window: *mut c_void,
        handle: u32,
        effect_type: u8,
        first_magnitude: u16,
        second_magnitude: u16,
        duration: u32,
    );
    fn web_gamepad_stop_effects(window: *mut c_void, handle: u32);
}

/// The enumeration GamepadHapticsResult of Gamepad/GamepadHapticActuator.idl.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum GamepadHapticsResult {
    Complete,
    Preempted,
}

impl GamepadHapticsResult {
    fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Complete => "complete",
            Self::Preempted => "preempted",
        }
    }
}

/// The enumeration GamepadHapticEffectType of Gamepad/GamepadHapticActuator.idl.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum GamepadHapticEffectType {
    DualRumble,
    TriggerRumble,
}

/// The dictionary GamepadEffectParameters of Gamepad/GamepadHapticActuator.idl.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct GamepadEffectParameters {
    pub(crate) duration: u64,
    pub(crate) start_delay: u64,
    pub(crate) strong_magnitude: f64,
    pub(crate) weak_magnitude: f64,
    pub(crate) left_trigger: f64,
    pub(crate) right_trigger: f64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct HapticsCompletionSteps {
    promise: WebIdlPromise,
    queue_on: Option<Gc<Object>>,
}

fn resolve_haptics_promise(vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise, result: GamepadHapticsResult) {
    let realm = promise_realm(promise);
    with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(realm, || {
        let result = Utf16String::from_ascii(result.as_str().as_bytes())
            .to_js(&CallContext::new(vm, realm))
            .expect("a string converts to a JS value");
        resolve_promise(vm, promise, result);
    });
}

impl HapticsCompletionSteps {
    fn run(self, vm: &Vm, result: GamepadHapticsResult) {
        match self.queue_on {
            Some(global) => {
                queue_a_global_task(
                    vm,
                    global,
                    TaskSource::Gamepad,
                    (self.promise, result),
                    |vm, (promise, result)| resolve_haptics_promise(vm, promise, result),
                );
            }
            None => resolve_haptics_promise(vm, self.promise, result),
        }
    }
}

// FIXME: What is a valid duration and startDelay? The spec doesn't define that.
//        Safari: clamps any duration above 5000ms to 5000ms and doesn't seem to clamp or reject any startDelay.
//        Chrome: rejects if duration + startDelay > 5000ms.
//        Firefox doesn't support vibration at the time of writing.
const MAX_VIBRATION_DURATION: u64 = 5000;

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#gamepadhapticactuator-interface
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct GamepadHapticActuator {
    gamepad: Ref<Gamepad>,
    window: CppWindow,
    document_became_hidden_observer: GcRefCell<Option<CppCell>>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-effects
    // Represents the effects supported by the actuator.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    effects: Vec<GamepadHapticEffectType>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-playingeffectpromise
    // The completion steps for playing some effect, or null if no effect is playing.
    playing_effect_completion_steps: GcRefCell<Option<HapticsCompletionSteps>>,
    playing_effect_timer: GcRefCell<Option<CppTimer>>,
}

impl Wrappable for GamepadHapticActuator {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.window.realm())
    }
}

unsafe extern "C" fn document_visibility_changed(vm: *mut c_void, actuator: *mut c_void, visible: bool) {
    // SAFETY: LibWeb passes the live VM.
    let vm = unsafe { &*vm.cast::<Vm>() };
    // SAFETY: The observer holds the actuator, whose cell it was given.
    let actuator: Ref<GamepadHapticActuator> = unsafe { cell_from_abi(actuator) };
    if !visible {
        GamepadHapticActuator::document_became_hidden(actuator, vm);
    }
}

fn gamepad_effect_magnitudes(r#type: GamepadHapticEffectType, params: &GamepadEffectParameters) -> (f64, f64) {
    match r#type {
        GamepadHapticEffectType::DualRumble => (params.strong_magnitude, params.weak_magnitude),
        GamepadHapticEffectType::TriggerRumble => (params.left_trigger, params.right_trigger),
    }
}

fn magnitude_to_u16(magnitude: f64) -> u16 {
    #[allow(
        clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
        clippy::cast_sign_loss,
        reason = "a valid magnitude is in the range [0 .. 1]"
    )]
    let magnitude = (magnitude * f64::from(u16::MAX)) as u16;
    magnitude
}

impl GamepadHapticActuator {
    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-constructing-a-gamepadhapticactuator
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, window: &CppWindow, gamepad: Ref<Gamepad>) -> Ref<Self> {
        // 1. Let gamepadHapticActuator be a newly created GamepadHapticActuator instance.
        // 2. Let supportedEffectsList be an empty list.
        let mut supported_effects_list = Vec::new();

        // 3. For each enum value type of GamepadHapticEffectType, if the user agent can send a command to initiate effects
        //    of that type on that actuator, append type to supportedEffectsList.
        if gamepad.description().supports_dual_rumble {
            supported_effects_list.push(GamepadHapticEffectType::DualRumble);
        }

        if gamepad.description().supports_trigger_rumble {
            supported_effects_list.push(GamepadHapticEffectType::TriggerRumble);
        }

        // 4. Set gamepadHapticActuator.[[effects]] to supportedEffectsList.
        let gamepad_haptic_actuator = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            gamepad,
            window: window.clone(),
            document_became_hidden_observer: GcRefCell::new(None),
            effects: supported_effects_list,
            playing_effect_completion_steps: GcRefCell::new(None),
            playing_effect_timer: GcRefCell::new(None),
        });

        let observer = window
            .associated_document()
            .observe_visibility_state(gamepad_haptic_actuator.as_ptr().cast(), document_visibility_changed);
        *gamepad_haptic_actuator.document_became_hidden_observer.borrow_mut(vm) = Some(observer);

        gamepad_haptic_actuator
    }

    pub(crate) fn effects(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<GamepadHapticEffectType>> {
        Ok(self.effects.clone())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-valid-effect
    fn is_valid_effect(r#type: GamepadHapticEffectType, params: &GamepadEffectParameters) -> bool {
        let is_in_unit_range = |value: f64| (0.0..=1.0).contains(&value);

        // 1. Given the value of GamepadHapticEffectType type, switch on:
        //    "dual-rumble"
        //          If params does not describe a valid dual-rumble effect, return false.
        //    "trigger-rumble"
        //          If params does not describe a valid trigger-rumble effect, return false.
        // 2. Return true
        match r#type {
            GamepadHapticEffectType::DualRumble => {
                // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-valid-dual-rumble-effect
                // Given GamepadEffectParameters params, a valid dual-rumble effect must have a valid duration, a valid
                // startDelay, and both the strongMagnitude and the weakMagnitude must be in the range [0 .. 1].
                let Some(total_duration) = params.duration.checked_add(params.start_delay) else {
                    return false;
                };

                if total_duration > MAX_VIBRATION_DURATION {
                    return false;
                }

                if !is_in_unit_range(params.strong_magnitude) {
                    return false;
                }

                if !is_in_unit_range(params.weak_magnitude) {
                    return false;
                }

                true
            }
            GamepadHapticEffectType::TriggerRumble => {
                // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-valid-trigger-rumble-effect
                // Given GamepadEffectParameters params, a valid trigger-rumble effect must have a valid duration, a valid
                // startDelay, and the strongMagnitude, weakMagnitude, leftTrigger, and rightTrigger must be in the range
                // [0 .. 1].
                let Some(total_duration) = params.duration.checked_add(params.start_delay) else {
                    return false;
                };

                if total_duration > MAX_VIBRATION_DURATION {
                    return false;
                }

                if !is_in_unit_range(params.strong_magnitude) {
                    return false;
                }

                if !is_in_unit_range(params.weak_magnitude) {
                    return false;
                }

                if !is_in_unit_range(params.left_trigger) {
                    return false;
                }

                if !is_in_unit_range(params.right_trigger) {
                    return false;
                }

                true
            }
        }
    }

    fn can_play_effect_with_type(&self, r#type: GamepadHapticEffectType) -> bool {
        // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#ref-for-dfn-play-effects-with-type-1
        // A GamepadHapticActuator can play effects with type type if type can be found in the [[effects]] list.
        self.effects.contains(&r#type)
    }

    fn current_document_is_hidden_or_inactive(vm: &Vm) -> bool {
        let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a binding runs in a realm");
        let window =
            window_from_global_object(realm.global_object()).expect("GamepadHapticActuator is only exposed on Window");
        let document = window.associated_document();
        !document.is_fully_active() || document.visibility_state() == VisibilityState::Hidden
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-gamepadhapticactuator-playeffect
    pub(crate) fn play_effect(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        promise: WebIdlPromise,
        r#type: GamepadHapticEffectType,
        params: GamepadEffectParameters,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. If params does not describe a valid effect of type type, return a promise rejected with a TypeError.
        if !Self::is_valid_effect(r#type, &params) {
            reject_promise_with_exception(vm, promise, Exception::type_error("Invalid effect"));
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Let document be the current settings object's relevant global object's associated Document.
        // 3. If document is null or document is not fully active or document's visibility state is "hidden", return a
        //    promise rejected with an "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
        if Self::current_document_is_hidden_or_inactive(vm) {
            reject_promise_with_exception(
                vm,
                promise,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "InvalidStateError",
                    Utf16String::from_utf8("Haptics are not allowed in a hidden document"),
                ),
            );
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 5. If this GamepadHapticActuator cannot play effects with type type, return a promise rejected with reason
        //    NotSupportedError.
        if !this.can_play_effect_with_type(r#type) {
            reject_promise_with_exception(
                vm,
                promise,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "NotSupportedError",
                    Utf16String::from_utf8("Gamepad does not support this effect"),
                ),
            );
            return Ok(());
        }

        let completion_steps = HapticsCompletionSteps {
            promise,
            queue_on: Some(promise_realm(promise).global_object()),
        };
        Self::play_effect_with_completion_steps(*this, vm, r#type, params, completion_steps);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-gamepadhapticactuator-reset
    pub(crate) fn reset(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext, promise: WebIdlPromise) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Let document be the current settings object's relevant global object's associated Document.
        // 2. If document is null or document is not fully active or document's visibility state is "hidden", return a
        //    promise rejected with an "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
        if Self::current_document_is_hidden_or_inactive(vm) {
            reject_promise_with_exception(
                vm,
                promise,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "InvalidStateError",
                    Utf16String::from_utf8("Haptics are not allowed in a hidden document"),
                ),
            );
            return Ok(());
        }

        Self::reset_with_completion_steps(
            *this,
            vm,
            HapticsCompletionSteps {
                promise,
                queue_on: None,
            },
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-gamepadhapticactuator-playeffect
    fn play_effect_with_completion_steps(
        this: Ref<Self>,
        vm: &Vm,
        r#type: GamepadHapticEffectType,
        params: GamepadEffectParameters,
        completion_steps: HapticsCompletionSteps,
    ) {
        // 4. If this.[[playingEffectPromise]] is not null:
        let playing_effect_completion_steps = this.playing_effect_completion_steps.borrow().clone();
        if let Some(effect_completion_steps) = playing_effect_completion_steps {
            // 1. Let effectPromise be this.[[playingEffectPromise]].
            // 2. Set this.[[playingEffectPromise]] to null.
            *this.playing_effect_completion_steps.borrow_mut(vm) = None;
            this.clear_playing_effect_timers(vm);

            // 3. Queue a global task on the gamepad task source with the relevant global object of this to resolve
            //    effectPromise with "preempted".
            effect_completion_steps.run(vm, GamepadHapticsResult::Preempted);
        }

        // 6. Let [[playingEffectPromise]] be a new promise.
        *this.playing_effect_completion_steps.borrow_mut(vm) = Some(completion_steps);

        // 7. Let playEffectTimestamp be the current high resolution time given the document's relevant global object.
        // NOTE: Unused.

        // 8. Do the following steps in parallel:
        deferred_invoke(vm, (this, r#type, params), |vm, (this, r#type, params)| {
            // 1. Issue a haptic effect to the actuator with type, params, and the playEffectTimestamp.
            Self::issue_haptic_effect(this, vm, r#type, params);
        });

        // 9. Return [[playingEffectPromise]].
    }

    fn effect_completed(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        // 2. When the effect completes, if this.[[playingEffectPromise]] is not null, queue a global task on the
        //    gamepad task source with the relevant global object of this to run the following steps:
        let playing_effect_completion_steps = this.playing_effect_completion_steps.borrow().clone();
        if let Some(completion_steps) = playing_effect_completion_steps {
            // 2. Resolve this.[[playingEffectPromise]] with "complete".
            completion_steps.run(vm, GamepadHapticsResult::Complete);

            // 3. Set this.[[playingEffectPromise]] to null.
            *this.playing_effect_completion_steps.borrow_mut(vm) = None;
            this.clear_playing_effect_timers(vm);
        }
    }

    fn reset_with_completion_steps(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm, reset_completion_steps: HapticsCompletionSteps) {
        // 4. If this.[[playingEffectPromise]] is not null, do the following steps in parallel:
        if this.playing_effect_completion_steps.borrow().is_none() {
            return;
        }

        deferred_invoke(
            vm,
            (this, reset_completion_steps),
            |vm, (this, reset_completion_steps)| {
                // 1. Let effectPromise be this.[[playingEffectPromise]].
                let effect_completion_steps = this.playing_effect_completion_steps.borrow().clone();

                // 2. Stop haptic effects on this's gamepad's actuator.
                this.stop_haptic_effects();

                // 3. If the effect has been successfully stopped, do:
                // AD-HOC: The stop command is sent to the UI process without waiting for a reply, so it is taken to have
                //         succeeded, matching other engines.
                //    1. If effectPromise and this.[[playingEffectPromise]] are still the same,
                //       set this.[[playingEffectPromise]] to null.
                let playing_effect_promise = this
                    .playing_effect_completion_steps
                    .borrow()
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(|steps| steps.promise);
                if effect_completion_steps.as_ref().map(|steps| steps.promise) == playing_effect_promise {
                    *this.playing_effect_completion_steps.borrow_mut(vm) = None;
                }

                //    2. Queue a global task on the gamepad task source with the relevant global object of this to resolve
                //       effectPromise with "preempted".
                if let Some(effect_completion_steps) = effect_completion_steps {
                    effect_completion_steps.run(vm, GamepadHapticsResult::Preempted);
                }

                // 4. Resolve resetResultPromise with "complete"
                reset_completion_steps.run(vm, GamepadHapticsResult::Complete);
            },
        );
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#handling-visibility-change
    fn document_became_hidden(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        // When the document's visibility state becomes "hidden", run these steps for each GamepadHapticActuator actuator:
        // 1. If actuator.[[playingEffectPromise]] is null, abort these steps.
        let playing_effect_completion_steps = this.playing_effect_completion_steps.borrow().clone();
        let Some(completion_steps) = playing_effect_completion_steps else {
            return;
        };

        // 2. Queue a global task on the gamepad task source with the relevant global object of actuator to run the
        //    following steps:
        // 2. Resolve actuator.[[playingEffectPromise]] with "preempted".
        completion_steps.run(vm, GamepadHapticsResult::Preempted);

        // 3. Set actuator.[[playingEffectPromise]] to null.
        *this.playing_effect_completion_steps.borrow_mut(vm) = None;
        this.clear_playing_effect_timers(vm);

        // 3. Stop haptic effects on actuator.
        this.stop_haptic_effects();
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-issue-a-haptic-effect
    fn issue_haptic_effect(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm, r#type: GamepadHapticEffectType, params: GamepadEffectParameters) {
        // To issue a haptic effect on an actuator, the user agent MUST send a command to the device to render an effect
        // of type and try to make it use the provided params. The user agent SHOULD use the provided playEffectTimestamp
        // for more precise playback timing when params.startDelay is not 0.0. The user agent MAY modify the effect to
        // increase compatibility. For example, an effect intended for a rumble motor may be transformed into a
        // waveform-based effect for a device that supports waveform haptics but lacks rumble motors.
        let timer = CppTimer::create_single_shot(
            vm,
            params.start_delay,
            (this, r#type, params),
            |vm, (this, r#type, params)| {
                let (first_magnitude, second_magnitude) = gamepad_effect_magnitudes(r#type, &params);
                this.play_gamepad_effect(
                    r#type,
                    magnitude_to_u16(first_magnitude),
                    magnitude_to_u16(second_magnitude),
                    u32::try_from(params.duration).expect("a valid duration fits in 32 bits"),
                );

                let timer = CppTimer::create_single_shot(vm, params.duration, (this, r#type), |vm, (this, r#type)| {
                    // Explicitly stop the rumble before completing, ensuring the stop signal is sent synchronously.
                    this.play_gamepad_effect(r#type, 0, 0, 0);
                    Self::effect_completed(this, vm);
                });
                *this.playing_effect_timer.borrow_mut(vm) = Some(timer);
            },
        );
        *this.playing_effect_timer.borrow_mut(vm) = Some(timer);
    }

    fn play_gamepad_effect(
        &self,
        r#type: GamepadHapticEffectType,
        first_magnitude: u16,
        second_magnitude: u16,
        duration: u32,
    ) {
        // SAFETY: The Window is live.
        unsafe {
            web_gamepad_play_effect(
                self.window.as_ptr(),
                self.gamepad.handle(),
                r#type as u8,
                first_magnitude,
                second_magnitude,
                duration,
            );
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-stop-haptic-effects
    fn stop_haptic_effects(&self) {
        // To stop haptic effects on an actuator, the user agent MUST send a command to the device to abort any effects
        // currently being played. If a haptic effect was interrupted, the actuator SHOULD return to a motionless state
        // as quickly as possible.
        // SAFETY: The Window is live.
        unsafe { web_gamepad_stop_effects(self.window.as_ptr(), self.gamepad.handle()) };
    }

    fn clear_playing_effect_timers(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        if let Some(timer) = self.playing_effect_timer.borrow_mut(vm).take() {
            timer.stop();
        }
    }
}

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct GamepadInputDescriptor {
    pub(crate) has_canonical_index: bool,
    pub(crate) canonical_index: u32,
    pub(crate) logical_minimum: i16,
    pub(crate) logical_maximum: i16,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct GamepadDescription {
    pub(crate) handle: u32,
    pub(crate) id: String,
    pub(crate) has_standard_mapping: bool,
    pub(crate) supports_dual_rumble: bool,
    pub(crate) supports_trigger_rumble: bool,
    pub(crate) axes: Vec<GamepadInputDescriptor>,
    pub(crate) buttons: Vec<GamepadInputDescriptor>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(crate) struct GamepadState {
    pub(crate) handle: u32,
    pub(crate) axis_values: Vec<i16>,
    pub(crate) button_values: Vec<i16>,
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct GamepadDescriptionAbi<'a> {
    handle: u32,
    id: ak::Span<'a, u8>,
    has_standard_mapping: bool,
    supports_dual_rumble: bool,
    supports_trigger_rumble: bool,
    axes: ak::Span<'a, GamepadInputDescriptor>,
    buttons: ak::Span<'a, GamepadInputDescriptor>,
}

#[repr(C)]
pub struct GamepadStateAbi<'a> {
    handle: u32,
    axis_values: ak::Span<'a, i16>,
    button_values: ak::Span<'a, i16>,
}

impl GamepadDescription {
    pub(crate) fn from_abi(description: &GamepadDescriptionAbi<'_>) -> Self {
        Self {
            handle: description.handle,
            id: String::from_utf8_lossy(description.id.as_slice()).into_owned(),
            has_standard_mapping: description.has_standard_mapping,
            supports_dual_rumble: description.supports_dual_rumble,
            supports_trigger_rumble: description.supports_trigger_rumble,
            axes: description.axes.as_slice().to_vec(),
            buttons: description.buttons.as_slice().to_vec(),
        }
    }

    fn to_abi(&self) -> GamepadDescriptionAbi<'_> {
        GamepadDescriptionAbi {
            handle: self.handle,
            id: ak::Span::new(self.id.as_bytes()),
            has_standard_mapping: self.has_standard_mapping,
            supports_dual_rumble: self.supports_dual_rumble,
            supports_trigger_rumble: self.supports_trigger_rumble,
            axes: ak::Span::new(&self.axes),
            buttons: ak::Span::new(&self.buttons),
        }
    }
}

impl GamepadState {
    pub(crate) fn from_abi(state: &GamepadStateAbi<'_>) -> Self {
        Self {
            handle: state.handle,
            axis_values: state.axis_values.as_slice().to_vec(),
            button_values: state.button_values.as_slice().to_vec(),
        }
    }

    fn to_abi(&self) -> GamepadStateAbi<'_> {
        GamepadStateAbi {
            handle: self.handle,
            axis_values: ak::Span::new(&self.axis_values),
            button_values: ak::Span::new(&self.button_values),
        }
    }
}

/// The enumeration GamepadMappingType of Gamepad/Gamepad.idl.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum GamepadMappingType {
    Empty,
    Standard,
    #[allow(dead_code, reason = "no gamepad uses the xr-standard mapping")]
    XrStandard,
}

    unsafe { web_high_resolution_time_current_high_resolution_time(window.realm().global_object().as_ptr().cast()) }

struct InitializedInputs {
    mapping: Vec<usize>,
    minimums: Vec<i16>,
    maximums: Vec<i16>,
    size: usize,

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-gamepad
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Gamepad {
    window: CppWindow,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    description: GamepadDescription,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-gamepad-id
    // An identification string for the gamepad. This string identifies the brand or style of connected gamepad device.
    // The exact format of the id string is left unspecified. It is RECOMMENDED that the user agent select a string
    // that identifies the product without uniquely identifying the device. For example, a USB gamepad may be
    // identified by its idVendor and idProduct values. Unique identifiers like serial numbers or Bluetooth device
    // addresses MUST NOT be included in the id string.
    id: Utf16String,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-gamepad-index
    // The index of the gamepad in the Navigator. When multiple gamepads are connected to a user agent, indices MUST be
    // assigned on a first-come, first-serve basis, starting at zero. If a gamepad is disconnected, previously assigned
    // indices MUST NOT be reassigned to gamepads that continue to be connected. However, if a gamepad is disconnected,
    // and subsequently the same or a different gamepad is then connected, the lowest previously used index MUST be
    // reused.
    index: usize,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-connected
    // A flag indicating that the device is connected to the system
    connected: Cell<bool>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-timestamp
    // The last time data for this Gamepad was updated
    timestamp: Cell<f64>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-axes
    // A sequence of double values representing the current state of axes exposed by this device.
    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-gamepad-axes
    // Array of values for all axes of the gamepad. All axis values MUST be linearly normalized to the range [-1 .. 1].
    // If the controller is perpendicular to the ground with the directional stick pointing up, -1 SHOULD correspond to
    // "forward" or "left", and 1 SHOULD correspond to "backward" or "right". Axes that are drawn from a 2D input
    // device SHOULD appear next to each other in the axes array, X then Y. It is RECOMMENDED that axes appear in
    // decreasing order of importance, such that element 0 and 1 typically represent the X and Y axis of a directional
    // stick. The same object MUST be returned until the user agent needs to return different values (or values in a
    // different order).
    // FIXME: Our current FrozenArray implementation only supports returning new objects everytime.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    axes: RefCell<Vec<f64>>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-axismapping
    // Mapping from unmapped axis index to an index in the axes array
    axis_mapping: Vec<usize>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-axisminimums
    // A list containing the minimum logical value for each axis
    // NOTE: While the Gamepad API internally uses u32 to represent raw axis values, SDL uses i16 for axes.
    axis_minimums: Vec<i16>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-axismaximums
    // A list containing the maximum logical value for each axis
    // NOTE: While the Gamepad API internally uses u32 to represent raw axis values, SDL uses i16 for axes.
    axis_maximums: Vec<i16>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-buttons
    // A sequence of GamepadButton objects representing the current state of buttons exposed by this device
    // Array of button states for all buttons of the gamepad. It is RECOMMENDED that buttons appear in decreasing
    // importance such that the primary button, secondary button, tertiary button, and so on appear as elements 0, 1,
    // 2, ... in the buttons array. The same object MUST be returned until the user agent needs to return different
    // values (or values in a different order).
    // FIXME: Our current FrozenArray implementation only supports returning new objects everytime.
    buttons: Vec<Ref<GamepadButton>>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-buttonmapping
    // Mapping from unmapped button index to an index in the buttons array
    button_mapping: Vec<usize>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-buttonminimums
    // A list containing the minimum logical value for each button.
    // NOTE: While the Gamepad API internally uses u32 to represent raw button values, SDL uses bool for buttons and
    //       i16 for axes. The left and right triggers are buttons in the Gamepad API.
    button_minimums: Vec<i16>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-buttonmaximums
    // A list containing the maximum logical value for each button
    button_maximums: Vec<i16>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-exposed
    // A flag indicating that the Gamepad object has been exposed to script
    exposed: Cell<bool>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-vibrationactuator
    vibration_actuator: Cell<Option<Ref<GamepadHapticActuator>>>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-gamepad-mapping
    // The mapping in use for this device. If the user agent has knowledge of the layout of the device, then it SHOULD
    // indicate that a mapping is in use by setting mapping to the corresponding GamepadMappingType value.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    mapping: GamepadMappingType,

    #[gc(untraced)]
    latest_state: RefCell<GamepadState>,
}

impl Wrappable for Gamepad {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.window.realm())
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-initializing-axes
fn initialize_axes(description: &GamepadDescription) -> InitializedInputs {
    // 1. Let inputCount be the number of axis inputs exposed by the device represented by gamepad.
    let inputs = &description.axes;

    // 2. Set gamepad.[[axisMinimums]] to a list of unsigned long values with size equal to inputCount containing minimum logical values for each of the axis inputs.
    // 3. Set gamepad.[[axisMaximums]] to a list of unsigned long values with size equal to inputCount containing maximum logical values for each of the axis inputs.
    let minimums = inputs.iter().map(|input| input.logical_minimum).collect();
    let maximums = inputs.iter().map(|input| input.logical_maximum).collect();
    let mut mapping = vec![0; inputs.len()];

    // 4. Let unmappedInputList be an empty list.
    let mut unmapped_input_list = Vec::new();

    // 5. Let mappedIndexList be an empty list.
    let mut mapped_index_list = Vec::new();

    // 6. Let axesSize be 0.
    let mut axes_size = 0;

    // 7. For each rawInputIndex of the range from 0 to inputCount − 1:
    for (raw_input_index, input) in inputs.iter().enumerate() {
        // 1. If the gamepad axis at index rawInputIndex represents a Standard Gamepad axis:
        if input.has_canonical_index {
            // 1. Let canonicalIndex be the canonical index for the axis.
            let canonical_index = input.canonical_index as usize;

            // 2. If mappedIndexList contains canonicalIndex, then append rawInputIndex to unmappedInputList.
            if mapped_index_list.contains(&canonical_index) {
                unmapped_input_list.push(raw_input_index);
            } else {
                // Otherwise:
                // 1. Set gamepad.[[axisMapping]][rawInputIndex] to canonicalIndex.
                mapping[raw_input_index] = canonical_index;

                // 2. Append canonicalIndex to mappedIndexList.
                mapped_index_list.push(canonical_index);

                // 3. If canonicalIndex + 1 is greater than axesSize, then set axesSize to canonicalIndex + 1.
                if canonical_index + 1 > axes_size {
                    axes_size = canonical_index + 1;
                }
            }
        } else {
            // Otherwise, append rawInputIndex to unmappedInputList.
            unmapped_input_list.push(raw_input_index);
        }
    }

    // 8. Let axisIndex be 0.
    let mut axis_index = 0;

    // 9. For each rawInputIndex of unmappedInputList:
    for raw_input_index in unmapped_input_list {
        // 1. While mappedIndexList contains axisIndex:
        while mapped_index_list.contains(&axis_index) {
            // 1. Increment axisIndex.
            axis_index += 1;
        }

        // 2. Set gamepad.[[axisMapping]][rawInputIndex] to axisIndex.
        mapping[raw_input_index] = axis_index;

        // 3. Append axisIndex to mappedIndexList.
        mapped_index_list.push(axis_index);

        // 4. If axisIndex + 1 is greater than axesSize, then set axesSize to axisIndex + 1.
        if axis_index + 1 > axes_size {
            axes_size = axis_index + 1;
        }
    }

    // NB: Instead of returning a list, the caller creates the axes from the size.
    // 10. Let axes be an empty list.
    // 11. For each axisIndex of the range from 0 to axesSize − 1, append 0 to axes.
    // 12. Return axes.
    InitializedInputs {
        mapping,
        minimums,
        maximums,
        size: axes_size,
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-initializing-buttons
fn initialize_buttons(description: &GamepadDescription) -> InitializedInputs {
    // 1. Let inputCount be the number of button inputs exposed by the device represented by gamepad.
    let inputs = &description.buttons;

    // 2. Set gamepad.[[buttonMinimums]] to be a list of unsigned long values with size equal to inputCount containing minimum logical values for each of the button inputs.
    // 3. Set gamepad.[[buttonMaximums]] to be a list of unsigned long values with size equal to inputCount containing maximum logical values for each of the button inputs.
    let minimums = inputs.iter().map(|input| input.logical_minimum).collect();
    let maximums = inputs.iter().map(|input| input.logical_maximum).collect();
    let mut mapping = vec![0; inputs.len()];

    // 4. Let unmappedInputList be an empty list.
    let mut unmapped_input_list = Vec::new();

    // 5. Let mappedIndexList be an empty list.
    let mut mapped_index_list = Vec::new();

    // 6. Let buttonsSize be 0.
    let mut buttons_size = 0;

    // 7. For each rawInputIndex of the range from 0 to inputCount − 1:
    for (raw_input_index, input) in inputs.iter().enumerate() {
        // 1. If the gamepad button at index rawInputIndex represents a Standard Gamepad button:
        if input.has_canonical_index {
            // 1. Let canonicalIndex be the canonical index for the button.
            let canonical_index = input.canonical_index as usize;

            // 2. If mappedIndexList contains canonicalIndex, then append rawInputIndex to unmappedInputList.
            if mapped_index_list.contains(&canonical_index) {
                unmapped_input_list.push(raw_input_index);
            } else {
                // Otherwise:
                // 1. Set gamepad.[[buttonMapping]][rawInputIndex] to canonicalIndex.
                mapping[raw_input_index] = canonical_index;

                // 2. Append canonicalIndex to mappedIndexList.
                mapped_index_list.push(canonical_index);

                // 3. If canonicalIndex + 1 is greater than buttonsSize, then set buttonsSize to canonicalIndex + 1.
                if canonical_index + 1 > buttons_size {
                    buttons_size = canonical_index + 1;
                }
            }
        } else {
            // Otherwise, append rawInputIndex to unmappedInputList.
            unmapped_input_list.push(raw_input_index);
        }

        // 2. Increment rawInputIndex.
    }

    // 8. Let buttonIndex be 0.
    let mut button_index = 0;

    // 9. For each rawInputIndex of unmappedInputList:
    for raw_input_index in unmapped_input_list {
        // 1. While mappedIndexList contains buttonIndex:
        while mapped_index_list.contains(&button_index) {
            // 1. Increment buttonIndex.
            button_index += 1;
        }

        // 2. Set gamepad.[[buttonMapping]][rawInputIndex] to buttonIndex.
        mapping[raw_input_index] = button_index;

        // 3. Append buttonIndex to mappedIndexList.
        mapped_index_list.push(button_index);

        // 4. If buttonIndex + 1 is greater than buttonsSize, then set buttonsSize to buttonIndex + 1.
        if button_index + 1 > buttons_size {
            buttons_size = button_index + 1;
        }
    }

    // NB: Instead of returning a list, the caller creates the buttons from the size.
    // 10. Let buttons be an empty list.
    // 11. For each buttonIndex of the range from 0 to buttonsSize − 1, append a new GamepadButton to buttons.
    // 12. Return buttons.
    InitializedInputs {
        mapping,
        minimums,
        maximums,
        size: buttons_size,
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-selecting-a-mapping
fn select_a_mapping(description: &GamepadDescription) -> GamepadMappingType {
    // 1. If the button and axis layout of the gamepad device corresponds with the Standard Gamepad layout, then
    //    return "standard".
    // 2. Return "".
    // NB: The UI process performs this check when it builds the description.
    if description.has_standard_mapping {
        GamepadMappingType::Standard
    } else {
        GamepadMappingType::Empty
    }
}

impl Gamepad {
    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-a-new-gamepad
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, window: &CppWindow, description: GamepadDescription) -> Ref<Self> {
        // 1. Let gamepad be a newly created Gamepad instance:
        //    1. Initialize gamepad's id attribute to an identification string for the gamepad.
        let id = Utf16String::from_utf8(&description.id);

        //    2. Initialize gamepad's index attribute to the result of selecting an unused gamepad index for gamepad.
        //    https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-selecting-an-unused-gamepad-index
        //    1. Let navigator be gamepad's relevant global object's Navigator object.
        //    The rest of the steps are implemented in navigator_gamepad.rs.
        //    NOTE: Gamepad is only exposed on Window.
        let index = select_an_unused_gamepad_index(vm, &navigator_gamepad(vm, window));

        //    3. Initialize gamepad's mapping attribute to the result of selecting a mapping for the gamepad device.
        let mapping = select_a_mapping(&description);

        //    4. Set gamepad.[[connected]] to true.
        //    5. Set gamepad.[[timestamp]] to the current high resolution time given gamepad's relevant global object.
        let timestamp = current_high_resolution_time(window);

        //    6. Set gamepad.[[axes]] to the result of initializing axes for gamepad.
        let axes = initialize_axes(&description);

        //    7. Set gamepad.[[buttons]] to the result of initializing buttons for gamepad.
        let buttons = initialize_buttons(&description);
        let button_objects = MarkedVec::with_capacity(vm, buttons.size);
        for _ in 0..buttons.size {
            button_objects.push(GamepadButton::create(vm));
        }

        let gamepad = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            window: window.clone(),
            description,
            id,
            index,
            connected: Cell::new(true),
            timestamp: Cell::new(timestamp),
            axes: RefCell::new(vec![0.0; axes.size]),
            axis_mapping: axes.mapping,
            axis_minimums: axes.minimums,
            axis_maximums: axes.maximums,
            buttons: button_objects.to_vec(),
            button_mapping: buttons.mapping,
            button_minimums: buttons.minimums,
            button_maximums: buttons.maximums,
            exposed: Cell::new(false),
            vibration_actuator: Cell::new(None),
            mapping,
            latest_state: RefCell::default(),
        });

        //    8. Set gamepad.[[vibrationActuator]] to the result of constructing a GamepadHapticActuator for gamepad.
        gamepad
            .vibration_actuator
            .set(Some(GamepadHapticActuator::create(vm, window, gamepad)));

        // 2. Return gamepad.
        gamepad
    }

    pub(crate) fn handle(&self) -> u32 {
        self.description.handle
    }

    pub(crate) fn description(&self) -> &GamepadDescription {
        &self.description
    }

    pub(crate) fn gamepad_index(&self) -> usize {
        self.index
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_exposed(&self) -> bool {
        self.exposed.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_exposed(&self, exposed: bool) {
        self.exposed.set(exposed);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_connected(&self, connected: bool) {
        self.connected.set(connected);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_timestamp(&self, timestamp: f64) {
        self.timestamp.set(timestamp);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_latest_state(&self, state: GamepadState) {
        *self.latest_state.borrow_mut() = state;
    }

    pub(crate) fn id(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.id.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn index(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<i32> {
        Ok(i32::try_from(self.index).expect("a gamepad index fits in a long"))
    }

    pub(crate) fn connected(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.connected.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn timestamp(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.timestamp.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn mapping(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<GamepadMappingType> {
        Ok(self.mapping)
    }

    pub(crate) fn axes(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<f64>> {
        Ok(self.axes.borrow().clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn buttons<'vm>(&self, cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, Ref<GamepadButton>>> {
        let buttons = MarkedVec::with_capacity(cx.vm(), self.buttons.len());
        buttons.extend_from_slice(&self.buttons);
        Ok(buttons)
    }

    pub(crate) fn vibration_actuator(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<GamepadHapticActuator>> {
        Ok(self
            .vibration_actuator
            .get()
            .expect("a gamepad has a vibration actuator once it is created"))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-map-and-normalize-axes
    fn map_and_normalize_axes(&self) {
        // 1. Let axisValues be a list of unsigned long values representing the most recent logical axis input values for
        //    each axis input of the device represented by gamepad.
        // NOTE: While the Gamepad API internally uses u32 to represent raw axis values, SDL uses i16 for axes.
        let latest_state = self.latest_state.borrow();
        let axis_values = &latest_state.axis_values;
        let mut axes = self.axes.borrow_mut();

        // 2. Let maxRawAxisIndex be the size of axisValues − 1.
        // 3. For each rawAxisIndex of the range from 0 to maxRawAxisIndex:
        for (raw_axis_index, &logical_value) in axis_values.iter().enumerate().take(self.axis_minimums.len()) {
            // 1. Let mappedIndex be gamepad.[[axisMapping]][rawAxisIndex].
            let mapped_index = self.axis_mapping[raw_axis_index];

            // 2. Let logicalValue be axisValues[rawAxisIndex].

            // 3. Let logicalMinimum be gamepad.[[axisMinimums]][rawAxisIndex].
            let logical_minimum = self.axis_minimums[raw_axis_index];

            // 4. Let logicalMaximum be gamepad.[[axisMaximums]][rawAxisIndex].
            let logical_maximum = self.axis_maximums[raw_axis_index];

            // 5. Let normalizedValue be 2 (logicalValue − logicalMinimum) / (logicalMaximum − logicalMinimum) − 1.
            // SAFETY: The function only computes with its arguments.
            let normalized_value =
                unsafe { web_gamepad_normalize_axis_value(logical_value, logical_minimum, logical_maximum) };

            // 6. Set gamepad.[[axes]][axisIndex] to be normalizedValue.
            // FIXME: axisIndex should be mappedIndex.
            axes[mapped_index] = normalized_value;
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-map-and-normalize-buttons
    fn map_and_normalize_buttons(&self) {
        // 1. Let buttonValues be a list of unsigned long values representing the most recent logical button input values
        //    for each button input of the device represented by gamepad.
        // NOTE: While the Gamepad API internally uses u32 to represent raw button values, SDL uses bool for buttons and
        //       i16 for axes. The left and right triggers are buttons in the Gamepad API.
        let latest_state = self.latest_state.borrow();
        let button_values = &latest_state.button_values;

        // 2. Let maxRawButtonIndex be the size of buttonValues − 1.
        // 3. For each rawButtonIndex of the range from 0 to maxRawButtonIndex:
        for (raw_button_index, &logical_value) in button_values.iter().enumerate().take(self.button_minimums.len()) {
            // 1. Let mappedIndex be gamepad.[[buttonMapping]][rawButtonIndex].
            let mapped_index = self.button_mapping[raw_button_index];

            // 2. Let logicalValue be buttonValues[rawButtonIndex].

            // 3. Let logicalMinimum be gamepad.[[buttonMinimums]][rawButtonIndex].
            let logical_minimum = self.button_minimums[raw_button_index];

            // 4. Let logicalMaximum be gamepad.[[buttonMaximums]][rawButtonIndex].
            let logical_maximum = self.button_maximums[raw_button_index];

            // 5. Let normalizedValue be (logicalValue − logicalMinimum) / (logicalMaximum − logicalMinimum).
            // SAFETY: The function only computes with its arguments.
            let value = unsafe { web_gamepad_normalize_button_value(logical_value, logical_minimum, logical_maximum) };

            // 6. Let button be gamepad.[[buttons]][mappedIndex].
            let button = self.buttons[mapped_index];

            // 7. Set button.[[value]] to normalizedValue.
            button.set_value(value);

            // 8. If the button has a digital switch to indicate a pure pressed or released state, set button.[[pressed]]
            //    to true if the button is pressed or false if it is not pressed.
            //    Otherwise, set button.[[pressed]] to true if the value is above the button press threshold or false if
            //    it is not above the threshold.
            // SAFETY: The function only computes with its arguments.
            button
                .set_pressed(unsafe { web_gamepad_is_button_pressed(logical_value, logical_minimum, logical_maximum) });

            // 9. If the button is capable of detecting touch, set button.[[touched]] to true if the button is currently being touched.
            //    Otherwise, set button.[[touched]] to button.[[pressed]].
            // FIXME: Support the PS4/PS5 controller which has a touchpad, which is a button that can be touched and not pressed in at the same time.
            button.set_touched(button.is_pressed());
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-update-gamepad-state
    pub(crate) fn update_gamepad_state(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        // 1. Let now be the current high resolution time given gamepad's relevant global object.
        let now = current_high_resolution_time(&this.window);
        let window = &this.window;

        // 2. Set gamepad.[[timestamp]] to now.
        this.timestamp.set(now);

        // 3. Run the steps to map and normalize axes for gamepad.
        this.map_and_normalize_axes();

        // 4. Run the steps to map and normalize buttons for gamepad.
        this.map_and_normalize_buttons();

        // FIXME: 5. Run the steps to record touches for gamepad.

        // 6. Let navigator be gamepad's relevant global object's Navigator object.
        let navigator = navigator_gamepad(vm, window);

        // 7. Let document be gamepad's relevant global object's associated Document; otherwise null.
        // 8. If document is null, abort these steps.
        // NB: A Window always has an associated Document.
        let document = window.associated_document();

        // AD-HOC: https://github.com/w3c/gamepad/pull/230 proposes a step here: "If document is a fully active descendant of
        //         a top-level traversable with user attention and gamepad contains a gamepad user gesture, then run the
        //         activation notification steps given document." The UI process runs it.

        // 9. If navigator.[[hasGamepadGesture]] is false and document is a fully active descendant of a top-level
        //    traversable with user attention and gamepad contains a gamepad user gesture:
        if !navigator.has_gamepad_gesture()
            && document.is_fully_active_descendant_of_a_top_level_traversable_with_user_attention()
            && this.contains_gamepad_user_gesture()
        {
            // 1. Set navigator.[[hasGamepadGesture]] to true.
            navigator.set_has_gamepad_gesture(true);

            // 2. For each connectedGamepad of navigator.[[gamepads]]:
            let gamepads = navigator.gamepads(vm);
            for connected_gamepad in gamepads.values().iter() {
                // 1. If connectedGamepad is not equal to null:
                let Some(connected_gamepad) = connected_gamepad else {
                    continue;
                };

                // 1. Set connectedGamepad.[[exposed]] to true.
                connected_gamepad.exposed.set(true);

                // 2. Set connectedGamepad.[[timestamp]] to now.
                connected_gamepad.timestamp.set(now);

                // 3. If document is not null and is fully active, then queue a global task on the gamepad task source
                //    to fire an event named gamepadconnected at gamepad's relevant global object using GamepadEvent
                //    with its gamepad attribute initialized to connectedGamepad.
                if document.is_fully_active() {
                    fire_a_gamepad_event(vm, window, "gamepadconnected", *connected_gamepad);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-gamepad-user-gesture
    fn contains_gamepad_user_gesture(&self) -> bool {
        // NB: The UI process uses the same algorithm to decide when to tell this process about its gamepads.
        let latest_state = self.latest_state.borrow();
        let description = self.description.to_abi();
        let state = latest_state.to_abi();
        // SAFETY: The description and the state are lent for the call.
        unsafe { web_gamepad_contains_gamepad_user_gesture(&raw const description, &raw const state) }
    }
}

//! The Navigator partial interface of the Gamepad API, https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#extensions-to-the-navigator-interface

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, GcRefCell, MarkedVec, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::global_object::CppWindow;
use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;
use crate::bindings::promise::{TaskSource, queue_a_global_task};
use crate::bindings::realm_data::realm_data;
use crate::dom::document::CppDocument;
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;
use crate::gamepad::gamepad::{Gamepad, GamepadDescription, GamepadState, current_high_resolution_time};
use crate::gamepad::gamepad_event::{GamepadEvent, GamepadEventInit};
use crate::permissions_policy::permissions_policy::PolicyControlledFeature;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_gamepad_did_start_using_gamepads(window: *mut c_void);
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#internal-slots
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct NavigatorGamepad {
    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-hasgamepadgesture
    // A flag indicating that a gamepad user gesture has been observed
    has_gamepad_gesture: Cell<bool>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-gamepads
    // Each Gamepad present at the index specified by its index attribute, or null for unassigned indices.
    gamepads: GcRefCell<Vec<Option<Ref<Gamepad>>>>,

    // Non-standard attribute to know which gamepads are available to the system. This is used to prevent duplicate
    // connections for the same gamepad ID (e.g. if the navigator object is initialized and checks for connected gamepads
    // and also receives a gamepad connected event)
    #[gc(untraced)]
    available_gamepads: RefCell<Vec<u32>>,
}

static NAVIGATOR_GAMEPAD_CLASS: EmbedderClass<NavigatorGamepad> = EmbedderClass::new("NavigatorGamepad");

impl EmbedderValue for NavigatorGamepad {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &NAVIGATOR_GAMEPAD_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type NavigatorGamepadRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<NavigatorGamepad>>;

pub(crate) fn navigator_gamepad(vm: &Vm, window: &CppWindow) -> NavigatorGamepadRef {
    let data = realm_data(vm, window.realm());
    if let Some(navigator) = data.navigator_gamepad.get() {
        return navigator;
    }
    let navigator = NAVIGATOR_GAMEPAD_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| NavigatorGamepad {
        has_gamepad_gesture: Cell::new(false),
        gamepads: GcRefCell::default(),
        available_gamepads: RefCell::default(),
    });
    data.navigator_gamepad.set(Some(navigator));
    navigator
}

pub(crate) fn fire_a_gamepad_event(vm: &Vm, window: &CppWindow, event_name: &str, gamepad: Ref<Gamepad>) {
    let event_init = GamepadEventInit {
        parent: EventInit {
            bubbles: false,
            cancelable: false,
            composed: false,
        },
        gamepad: Some(gamepad),
    };
    let event = GamepadEvent::create(vm, window.realm(), &Utf16String::from_utf8(event_name), event_init);
    window.as_event_target().dispatch_event(event.event());
}

pub(crate) struct NotAllowedToUseGamepads;

impl NavigatorGamepad {
    pub(crate) fn has_gamepad_gesture(&self) -> bool {
        self.has_gamepad_gesture.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_has_gamepad_gesture(&self, has_gamepad_gesture: bool) {
        self.has_gamepad_gesture.set(has_gamepad_gesture);
    }

    pub(crate) fn gamepads<'vm>(&self, vm: &'vm Vm) -> MarkedVec<'vm, Option<Ref<Gamepad>>> {
        let gamepads = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        gamepads.extend_from_slice(&self.gamepads.borrow());
        gamepads
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dom-navigator-getgamepads
pub(crate) fn get_gamepads<'vm>(
    vm: &'vm Vm,
    navigator_window: &CppWindow,
    current_window: &CppWindow,
) -> Result<MarkedVec<'vm, Option<Ref<Gamepad>>>, NotAllowedToUseGamepads> {
    let navigator = navigator_gamepad(vm, navigator_window);

    // 1. Let doc be the current global object's associated Document.
    let document = current_window.associated_document();

    // 2. If doc is null or doc is not fully active, then return an empty list.
    let gamepads = MarkedVec::new(vm);
    if !document.is_fully_active() {
        return Ok(gamepads);
    }

    // 3. If doc is not allowed to use the "gamepad" permission, then throw a "SecurityError" DOMException and abort these steps.
    if !document.is_allowed_to_use_feature(PolicyControlledFeature::Gamepad) {
        return Err(NotAllowedToUseGamepads);
    }

    // AD-HOC: Tell the UI process that this process consumes gamepad input.
    // SAFETY: The Window is live.
    unsafe { web_gamepad_did_start_using_gamepads(current_window.as_ptr()) };

    // 4. If this.[[hasGamepadGesture]] is false, then return an empty list.
    if !navigator.has_gamepad_gesture.get() {
        return Ok(gamepads);
    }

    // 5. Let now be the current high resolution time given the current global object.
    let now = current_high_resolution_time(current_window);

    // 6. Let gamepads be an empty list.
    // NOTE: Already done.

    // 7. For each gamepad of this.[[gamepads]]:
    for gamepad in navigator.gamepads.borrow().iter().copied() {
        // 1. If gamepad is not null and gamepad.[[exposed]] is false:
        if let Some(gamepad) = gamepad
            && !gamepad.is_exposed()
        {
            // 1. Set gamepad.[[exposed]] to true.
            gamepad.set_exposed(true);

            // 2. Set gamepad.[[timestamp]] to now.
            gamepad.set_timestamp(now);
        }

        // 2. Append gamepad to gamepads.
        gamepads.push(gamepad);
    }

    // 8. Return gamepads.
    Ok(gamepads)
}

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-selecting-an-unused-gamepad-index
pub(crate) fn select_an_unused_gamepad_index(vm: &Vm, navigator: &NavigatorGamepadRef) -> usize {
    let mut gamepads = navigator.gamepads.borrow_mut(vm);

    // 2. Let maxGamepadIndex be the size of navigator.[[gamepads]] − 1.
    // 3. For each gamepadIndex of the range from 0 to maxGamepadIndex:
    for (gamepad_index, gamepad) in gamepads.iter().enumerate() {
        // 1. If navigator.[[gamepads]][gamepadIndex] is null, then return gamepadIndex.
        if gamepad.is_none() {
            return gamepad_index;
        }
    }

    // 4. Append null to navigator.[[gamepads]].
    gamepads.push(None);

    // 5. Return the size of navigator.[[gamepads]] − 1.
    gamepads.len() - 1
}

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct GamepadConnection {
    window: CppWindow,
    document: CppDocument,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    description: GamepadDescription,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#event-gamepadconnected
pub(crate) fn handle_gamepad_connected(vm: &Vm, window: &CppWindow, description: GamepadDescription) {
    let navigator = navigator_gamepad(vm, window);

    // When a gamepad becomes available on the system, run the following steps:
    if navigator.available_gamepads.borrow().contains(&description.handle) {
        return;
    }

    // 1. Let document be the current global object's associated Document; otherwise null.
    // FIXME: We can't use the current global object here, since it's not executing in a scripting context.
    // NOTE: NavigatorGamepad is only available on Window.
    // NOTE: document is never null.
    let global = window.realm().global_object();
    let document = window.associated_document();

    // 2. If document is not null and is not allowed to use the "gamepad" permission, then abort these steps.
    if !document.is_allowed_to_use_feature(PolicyControlledFeature::Gamepad) {
        return;
    }

    navigator.available_gamepads.borrow_mut().push(description.handle);

    // 3. Queue a global task on the gamepad task source with the current global object to perform the following steps:
    let connection = GamepadConnection {
        window: window.clone(),
        document,
        description,
    };
    queue_a_global_task(vm, global, TaskSource::Gamepad, connection, |vm, connection| {
        // 1. Let gamepad be a new Gamepad representing the gamepad.
        let gamepad = Gamepad::create(vm, &connection.window, connection.description);

        // 2. Let navigator be gamepad's relevant global object's Navigator object.
        let navigator = navigator_gamepad(vm, &connection.window);

        // 3. Set navigator.[[gamepads]][gamepad.index] to gamepad.
        navigator.gamepads.borrow_mut(vm)[gamepad.gamepad_index()] = Some(gamepad);

        // 4. If navigator.[[hasGamepadGesture]] is true:
        if navigator.has_gamepad_gesture.get() {
            // 1. Set gamepad.[[exposed]] to true.
            gamepad.set_exposed(true);

            // 2. If document is not null and is fully active, then fire an event named gamepadconnected at gamepad's
            //    relevant global object using GamepadEvent with its gamepad attribute initialized to gamepad.
            if connection.document.is_fully_active() {
                fire_a_gamepad_event(vm, &connection.window, "gamepadconnected", gamepad);
            }
        }
    });
}

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct GamepadUpdate {
    window: CppWindow,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    state: GamepadState,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/#dfn-receives-new-button-or-axis-input-values
pub(crate) fn handle_gamepad_updated(vm: &Vm, window: &CppWindow, state: GamepadState) {
    // When the system receives new button or axis input values, run the following steps:
    if !navigator_gamepad(vm, window)
        .available_gamepads
        .borrow()
        .contains(&state.handle)
    {
        return;
    }

    // 2. Queue a global task on the gamepad task source with gamepad's relevant global object to update gamepad state
    //    for gamepad.
    // AD-HOC: Step 1 runs in the task. A newly available gamepad is created by an earlier task on the same task
    //         source, so input received before that task has run still reaches the gamepad.
    let global = window.realm().global_object();
    let update = GamepadUpdate {
        window: window.clone(),
        state,
    };
    queue_a_global_task(vm, global, TaskSource::Gamepad, update, |vm, update| {
        // 1. Let gamepad be the Gamepad object representing the device that received new button or axis input values.
        let navigator = navigator_gamepad(vm, &update.window);
        let gamepad = navigator
            .gamepads
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .copied()
            .find(|gamepad| gamepad.handle() == update.state.handle);
        let Some(gamepad) = gamepad else {
            return;
        };

        gamepad.set_latest_state(update.state);
        Gamepad::update_gamepad_state(gamepad, vm);
    });
}

pub(crate) fn handle_gamepad_disconnected(vm: &Vm, window: &CppWindow, handle: u32) {
    // When a gamepad becomes unavailable on the system, run the following steps:
    let navigator = navigator_gamepad(vm, window);
    let was_available = {
        let mut available_gamepads = navigator.available_gamepads.borrow_mut();
        let position = available_gamepads
            .iter()
            .position(|available_gamepad| *available_gamepad == handle);
        position.map(|position| available_gamepads.remove(position)).is_some()
    };

    if !was_available {
        return;
    }

    // 2. Queue a global task on the gamepad task source with gamepad's relevant global object to perform the
    //    following steps:
    // AD-HOC: Step 1 runs in the task. A newly available gamepad is created by an earlier task on the same task
    //         source, so a gamepad that becomes unavailable before that task has run is still removed.
    let global = window.realm().global_object();
    queue_a_global_task(
        vm,
        global,
        TaskSource::Gamepad,
        (window.clone(), handle),
        |vm, (window, handle)| {
            // 1. Let gamepad be the Gamepad representing the unavailable device.
            let navigator = navigator_gamepad(vm, &window);
            let gamepad = navigator
                .gamepads
                .borrow()
                .iter()
                .flatten()
                .copied()
                .find(|gamepad| gamepad.handle() == handle);
            let Some(gamepad) = gamepad else {
                return;
            };

            // 1. Set gamepad.[[connected]] to false.
            gamepad.set_connected(false);

            // 2. Let document be gamepad's relevant global object's associated Document; otherwise null.
            let document = window.associated_document();

            // 3. If gamepad.[[exposed]] is true and document is not null and is fully active, then fire an event named
            //    gamepaddisconnected at gamepad's relevant global object using GamepadEvent with its gamepad attribute
            //    initialized to gamepad.
            if gamepad.is_exposed() && document.is_fully_active() {
                fire_a_gamepad_event(vm, &window, "gamepaddisconnected", gamepad);
            }

            // 4. Let navigator be gamepad's relevant global object's Navigator object.
            // 5. Set navigator.[[gamepads]][gamepad.index] to null.
            let mut gamepads = navigator.gamepads.borrow_mut(vm);
            gamepads[gamepad.gamepad_index()] = None;

            // 6. While navigator.[[gamepads]] is not empty and the last item of navigator.[[gamepads]] is null, remove the
            //    last item of navigator.[[gamepads]].
            while gamepads.last().is_some_and(Option::is_none) {
                gamepads.pop();
            }
        },
    );
}

//! GeolocationCoordinates, https://w3c.github.io/geolocation/#coordinates_interface

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_into_abi};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

/// Web::Geolocation::CoordinatesData.
#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct CoordinatesData {
    accuracy: f64,
    latitude: f64,
    longitude: f64,
    has_altitude: bool,
    altitude: f64,
    has_altitude_accuracy: bool,
    altitude_accuracy: f64,
    has_heading: bool,
    heading: f64,
    has_speed: bool,
    speed: f64,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/geolocation/#coordinates_interface
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct GeolocationCoordinates {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    accuracy: f64,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    latitude: f64,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    longitude: f64,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    altitude: Option<f64>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    altitude_accuracy: Option<f64>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    heading: Option<f64>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    speed: Option<f64>,
}

impl Wrappable for GeolocationCoordinates {}

impl GeolocationCoordinates {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, data: &CoordinatesData) -> Ref<Self> {
        let optional = |has_value: bool, value: f64| has_value.then_some(value);
        allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            accuracy: data.accuracy,
            latitude: data.latitude,
            longitude: data.longitude,
            altitude: optional(data.has_altitude, data.altitude),
            altitude_accuracy: optional(data.has_altitude_accuracy, data.altitude_accuracy),
            heading: optional(data.has_heading, data.heading),
            speed: optional(data.has_speed, data.speed),
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn accuracy(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.accuracy)
    }

    pub(crate) fn latitude(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.latitude)
    }

    pub(crate) fn longitude(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.longitude)
    }

    pub(crate) fn altitude(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<f64>> {
        Ok(self.altitude)
    }

    pub(crate) fn altitude_accuracy(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<f64>> {
        Ok(self.altitude_accuracy)
    }

    pub(crate) fn heading(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<f64>> {
        Ok(self.heading)
    }

    pub(crate) fn speed(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<f64>> {
        Ok(self.speed)
    }
}

/// A new GeolocationCoordinates with the data.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_geolocation_create_geolocation_coordinates(vm: &Vm, data: &CoordinatesData) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(GeolocationCoordinates::create(vm, data))
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/geolocation/#dom-geolocationpositionerror-code
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u16)]
pub(crate) enum GeolocationPositionErrorCode {
    PermissionDenied = 1,
    PositionUnavailable = 2,
    Timeout = 3,
}

impl GeolocationPositionErrorCode {
    pub(crate) fn from_u16(code: u16) -> Self {
        match code {
            1 => Self::PermissionDenied,
            2 => Self::PositionUnavailable,
            3 => Self::Timeout,
            _ => unreachable!("LibWeb passes a GeolocationPositionErrorCode"),
        }
    }
}

//! GeolocationPositionError, https://w3c.github.io/geolocation/#dom-geolocationpositionerror

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::geolocation::geolocation_position_error_code::GeolocationPositionErrorCode;

// https://w3c.github.io/geolocation/#dom-geolocationpositionerror
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct GeolocationPositionError {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    code: GeolocationPositionErrorCode,
}

impl Wrappable for GeolocationPositionError {}

impl GeolocationPositionError {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, code: GeolocationPositionErrorCode) -> Ref<Self> {
        allocate(vm, |_| Self { code })
    }

    pub(crate) fn code(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u16> {
        Ok(self.code as u16)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/geolocation/#message-attribute
    pub(crate) fn message(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The message attribute is a developer-friendly textual description of the code attribute.
        let message: &[u8] = match self.code {
            GeolocationPositionErrorCode::PositionUnavailable => b"Position unavailable",
            GeolocationPositionErrorCode::PermissionDenied => b"Permission denied",
            GeolocationPositionErrorCode::Timeout => b"Timeout",
        };
        Ok(Utf16String::from_ascii(message))
    }
}

thread_local! {
    static NEXT_WATCH_ID: Cell<u32> = const { Cell::new(0) };

// https://w3c.github.io/geolocation/#dom-positionoptions
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PositionOptions {
    pub(crate) enable_high_accuracy: bool,
    pub(crate) timeout: u32,
    pub(crate) maximum_age: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct PositionRequestArguments {
    success_callback: CallbackFunction,
    error_callback: Option<CallbackFunction>,
    options: PositionOptions,
    watch_id: Option<u32>,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct WatchPositionData {
    success_callback: CallbackFunction,
    error_callback: Option<CallbackFunction>,
    options: PositionOptions,
    emulated_position_data_observer_id: Option<u64>,
    observed_document: Option<WeakCppDocument>,
}

/// Web::Geolocation::EmulatedPositionData.
#[repr(C)]
struct EmulatedPositionDataAbi {
    kind: u8,
    coordinates: *mut c_void,
    error_code: u16,
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/geolocation/#dfn-emulated-position-data
enum EmulatedPositionData {
    None,
    Coordinates(Ref<GeolocationCoordinates>),
    Error(GeolocationPositionErrorCode),
}
