    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrixreadonly-multiply
    pub(crate) fn multiply(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, other: DOMMatrixInit) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMMatrix>> {
        // 1. Let result be the resulting matrix initialized to the values of the current matrix.
        let result = self.copy();

        // 2. Perform a multiplySelf() transformation on result with the argument other.
        let other_object = DOMMatrix::from_dictionary(&other)?;
        result.parent().multiply_self_steps(other_object.parent());

        // 3. Return result.
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| result))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrixreadonly-flipx
    pub(crate) fn flip_x(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMMatrix>> {
        // 1. Let result be the resulting matrix initialized to the values of the current matrix.
        let result = self.copy();

        // 2. Post-multiply result with new DOMMatrix([-1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0]).
        let matrix = result.parent().matrix().multiplied(Matrix4::scale(-1.0, 1.0, 1.0));
        result.parent().set_matrix(matrix);

        // 3. Return result.
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| result))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrixreadonly-flipy
    pub(crate) fn flip_y(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMMatrix>> {
        // 1. Let result be the resulting matrix initialized to the values of the current matrix.
        let result = self.copy();

        // 2. Post-multiply result with new DOMMatrix([1, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0]).
        let matrix = result.parent().matrix().multiplied(Matrix4::scale(1.0, -1.0, 1.0));
        result.parent().set_matrix(matrix);

        // 3. Return result.
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| result))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrixreadonly-inverse
    pub(crate) fn inverse(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMMatrix>> {
        // 1. Let result be the resulting matrix initialized to the values of the current matrix.
        let result = self.copy();

        // 2. Perform a invertSelf() transformation on result.
        result.parent().invert_self_steps();

        // 3. Return result.
        // The current matrix is not modified.
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| result))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrixreadonly-transformpoint
    pub(crate) fn transform_point(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, point: DOMPointInit) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMPoint>> {
        // Let pointObject be the result of invoking create a DOMPoint from the dictionary point. Return the result of
        // invoking transform a point with a matrix, given pointObject and the current matrix. The passed argument
        // does not get modified.
        let point_object = DOMPointReadOnly::from_dictionary(&point);
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| self.transform_point_steps(&point_object)))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#transform-a-point-with-a-matrix
    pub(crate) fn transform_point_steps(&self, point: &DOMPointReadOnly) -> DOMPoint {
        // 1. Let x be point’s x coordinate.
        // 2. Let y be point’s y coordinate.
        // 3. Let z be point’s z coordinate.
        // 4. Let w be point’s w perspective.
        // 5. Let pointVector be a new column vector with the elements being x, y, z, and w, respectively.
        let point_vector = point.coordinates();

        // 6. Set pointVector to pointVector pre-multiplied by matrix.
        let [x, y, z, w] = self.matrix.get().map_vector4(point_vector);

        // 7. Let transformedPoint be a new DOMPoint object.
        // 8. Set transformedPoint’s x coordinate to pointVector’s first element.
        // 9. Set transformedPoint’s y coordinate to pointVector’s second element.
        // 10. Set transformedPoint’s z coordinate to pointVector’s third element.
        // 11. Set transformedPoint’s w perspective to pointVector’s fourth element.
        // 12. Return transformedPoint.
        DOMPoint::new(x, y, z, w)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrixreadonly-tofloat32array
    #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, reason = "a Float32Array holds floats")]
    pub(crate) fn to_float32_array(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<TypedArrayBase>> {
        // Returns the serialized 16 elements m11 to m44 of the current matrix in column-major order as Float32Array.
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = self
            .matrix
            .get()
            .to_column_major()
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|element| (*element as f32).to_ne_bytes())
            .collect();
        create_typed_array(cx, TypedArrayKind::Float32Array, &bytes)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrixreadonly-tofloat64array
    pub(crate) fn to_float64_array(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<TypedArrayBase>> {
        // Returns the serialized 16 elements m11 to m44 of the current matrix in column-major order as Float64Array.
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = self
            .matrix
            .get()
            .to_column_major()
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|element| element.to_ne_bytes())
            .collect();
        create_typed_array(cx, TypedArrayKind::Float64Array, &bytes)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dommatrixreadonly-stringification-behavior
    pub(crate) fn to_string(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        self.stringify().ok_or_else(|| {
            Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidStateError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Cannot stringify non-finite matrix values"),
            )
        })
    }

    /// The stringification behavior, which has no string for a matrix with a non-finite element.
    pub(crate) fn stringify(&self) -> Option<Utf16String> {
        let matrix = self.matrix.get();

        // 1. If one or more of m11 element through m44 element are a non-finite value, then throw an
        //    "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
        // NOTE: The CSS syntax cannot represent NaN or Infinity values.
        if !matrix.to_column_major().iter().all(|element| element.is_finite()) {
            return None;
        }

        // 2. Let string be the empty string.
        // 3. If is 2D is true, then:
        //     1. Append "matrix(" to string.
        //     2. Append ! ToString(m11 element) to string.
        //     3. Append ", " to string.
        //     4. Append ! ToString(m12 element) to string.
        //     5. Append ", " to string.
        //     6. Append ! ToString(m21 element) to string.
        //     7. Append ", " to string.
        //     8. Append ! ToString(m22 element) to string.
        //     9. Append ", " to string.
        //     10. Append ! ToString(m41 element) to string.
        //     11. Append ", " to string.
        //     12. Append ! ToString(m42 element) to string.
        //     13. Append ")" to string.
        // 4. Otherwise:
        //     1. Append "matrix3d(" to string.
        //     2. Append ! ToString(m11 element) to string.
        //     3. Append ", " to string.
        //     4. Append ! ToString(m12 element) to string.
        //     5. Append ", " to string.
        //     6. Append ! ToString(m13 element) to string.
        //     7. Append ", " to string.
        //     8. Append ! ToString(m14 element) to string.
        //     9. Append ", " to string.
        //     10. Append ! ToString(m21 element) to string.
        //     11. Append ", " to string.
        //     12. Append ! ToString(m22 element) to string.
        //     13. Append ", " to string.
        //     14. Append ! ToString(m23 element) to string.
        //     15. Append ", " to string.
        //     16. Append ! ToString(m24 element) to string.
        //     17. Append ", " to string.
        //     18. Append ! ToString(m41 element) to string.
        //     19. Append ", " to string.
        //     20. Append ! ToString(m42 element) to string.
        //     21. Append ", " to string.
        //     22. Append ! ToString(m43 element) to string.
        //     23. Append ", " to string.
        //     24. Append ! ToString(m44 element) to string.
        //     25. Append ")" to string.
        // NB: The steps leave out m31 to m34, which matrix3d() requires, so they are appended after m24.
        let (function, elements) = if self.is_2d.get() {
            let m = |row, column| matrix.element(row, column);
            ("matrix(", vec![m(1, 1), m(1, 2), m(2, 1), m(2, 2), m(4, 1), m(4, 2)])
        } else {
            ("matrix3d(", matrix.to_column_major().to_vec())
        };
        let numbers: Vec<String> = elements.into_iter().map(number_to_string).collect();
        let string = format!("{function}{})", numbers.join(", "));

        // 5. Return string.
        Some(Utf16String::from_ascii(string.as_bytes()))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-multiplyself, from step 2 on.
    pub(super) fn multiply_self_steps(&self, other_object: &DOMMatrixReadOnly) {
        // 2. The otherObject matrix gets post-multiplied to the current matrix.
        self.matrix.set(self.matrix.get().multiplied(other_object.matrix.get()));

        // 3. If is 2D of otherObject is false, set is 2D of the current matrix to false.
        if !other_object.is_2d.get() {
            self.is_2d.set(false);
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-premultiplyself, from step 2 on.
    pub(super) fn pre_multiply_self_steps(&self, other_object: &DOMMatrixReadOnly) {
        // 2. The otherObject matrix gets pre-multiplied to the current matrix.
        self.matrix.set(other_object.matrix.get().multiplied(self.matrix.get()));

        // 3. If is 2D of otherObject is false, set is 2D of the current matrix to false.
        if !other_object.is_2d.get() {
            self.is_2d.set(false);
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-translateself
    pub(crate) fn translate_self_steps(&self, tx: f64, ty: f64, tz: f64) {
        // 1. Post-multiply a translation transformation on the current matrix. The 3D translation matrix is described
        //    in CSS Transforms. [CSS3-TRANSFORMS]
        self.matrix
            .set(self.matrix.get().multiplied(Matrix4::translation(tx, ty, tz)));

        // 2. If tz is specified and not 0 or -0, set is 2D of the current matrix to false.
        if tz != 0.0 {
            self.is_2d.set(false);
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-scaleself
    pub(crate) fn scale_self_steps(
        &self,
        scale_x: f64,
        scale_y: Option<f64>,
        scale_z: f64,
        origin_x: f64,
        origin_y: f64,
        origin_z: f64,
    ) {
        // 1. Perform a translateSelf() transformation on the current matrix with the arguments originX, originY,
        //    originZ.
        self.translate_self_steps(origin_x, origin_y, origin_z);

        // 2. If scaleY is missing, set scaleY to the value of scaleX.
        let scale_y = scale_y.unwrap_or(scale_x);

        // 3. Post-multiply a non-uniform scale transformation on the current matrix. The 3D scale matrix is described
        //    in CSS Transforms with sx = scaleX, sy = scaleY and sz = scaleZ. [CSS3-TRANSFORMS]
        self.matrix
            .set(self.matrix.get().multiplied(Matrix4::scale(scale_x, scale_y, scale_z)));

        // 4. Negate originX, originY and originZ.
        // 5. Perform a translateSelf() transformation on the current matrix with the arguments originX, originY,
        //    originZ.
        self.translate_self_steps(-origin_x, -origin_y, -origin_z);

        // 6. If scaleZ is not 1, set is 2D of the current matrix to false.
        if scale_z != 1.0 {
            self.is_2d.set(false);
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-scale3dself
    pub(super) fn scale3d_self_steps(&self, scale: f64, origin_x: f64, origin_y: f64, origin_z: f64) {
        // 1. Apply a translateSelf() transformation to the current matrix with the arguments originX, originY,
        //    originZ.
        self.translate_self_steps(origin_x, origin_y, origin_z);

        // 2. Post-multiply a uniform 3D scale transformation (m11 = m22 = m33 = scale) on the current matrix. The 3D
        //    scale matrix is described in CSS Transforms with sx = sy = sz = scale. [CSS3-TRANSFORMS]
        self.matrix
            .set(self.matrix.get().multiplied(Matrix4::scale(scale, scale, scale)));

        // 3. Apply a translateSelf() transformation to the current matrix with the arguments -originX, -originY,
        //    -originZ.
        self.translate_self_steps(-origin_x, -origin_y, -origin_z);

        // 4. If scale is not 1, set is 2D of the current matrix to false.
        if scale != 1.0 {
            self.is_2d.set(false);
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-rotateself
    pub(super) fn rotate_self_steps(&self, rot_x: f64, rot_y: Option<f64>, rot_z: Option<f64>) {
        // 1. If rotY and rotZ are both missing, set rotZ to the value of rotX and set rotX and rotY to 0.
        let (rot_x, rot_y, rot_z) = match (rot_y, rot_z) {
            (None, None) => (0.0, Some(0.0), Some(rot_x)),
            _ => (rot_x, rot_y, rot_z),
        };

        // 2. If rotY is still missing, set rotY to 0.
        let rot_y = rot_y.unwrap_or(0.0);

        // 3. If rotZ is still missing, set rotZ to 0.
        let rot_z = rot_z.unwrap_or(0.0);

        // 4. If rotX or rotY are not 0 or -0, set is 2D of the current matrix to false.
        if rot_x != 0.0 || rot_y != 0.0 {
            self.is_2d.set(false);
        }

        let mut matrix = self.matrix.get();

        // 5. Post-multiply a rotation transformation on the current matrix around the vector 0, 0, 1 by the specified
        //    rotation rotZ in degrees. The 3D rotation matrix is described in CSS Transforms with alpha = rotZ in
        //    degrees. [CSS3-TRANSFORMS]
        matrix = matrix.multiplied(Matrix4::rotation([0.0, 0.0, 1.0], to_radians(rot_z)));

        // 6. Post-multiply a rotation transformation on the current matrix around the vector 0, 1, 0 by the specified
        //    rotation rotY in degrees. The 3D rotation matrix is described in CSS Transforms with alpha = rotY in
        //    degrees. [CSS3-TRANSFORMS]
        matrix = matrix.multiplied(Matrix4::rotation([0.0, 1.0, 0.0], to_radians(rot_y)));

        // 7. Post-multiply a rotation transformation on the current matrix around the vector 1, 0, 0 by the specified
        //    rotation rotX in degrees. The 3D rotation matrix is described in CSS Transforms with alpha = rotX in
        //    degrees. [CSS3-TRANSFORMS]
        matrix = matrix.multiplied(Matrix4::rotation([1.0, 0.0, 0.0], to_radians(rot_x)));

        self.matrix.set(matrix);
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-rotatefromvectorself
    pub(super) fn rotate_from_vector_self_steps(&self, x: f64, y: f64) {
        // 1. Post-multiply a rotation transformation on the current matrix. The rotation angle is determined by the
        //    angle between the vector (1,0)T and (x,y)T in the clockwise direction. If x and y should both be 0 or -0,
        //    the angle is specified as 0. The 2D rotation matrix is described in CSS Transforms where alpha is the
        //    angle between the vector (1,0)T and (x,y)T in degrees. [CSS3-TRANSFORMS]
        let angle = if x == 0.0 && y == 0.0 { 0.0 } else { math::atan2(y, x) };
        self.matrix
            .set(self.matrix.get().multiplied(Matrix4::rotation([0.0, 0.0, 1.0], angle)));
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-rotateaxisangleself
    pub(crate) fn rotate_axis_angle_self_steps(&self, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, angle: f64) {
        // 1. Post-multiply a rotation transformation on the current matrix around the specified vector x, y, z by the
        //    specified rotation angle in degrees. The 3D rotation matrix is described in CSS Transforms with alpha =
        //    angle in degrees. [CSS3-TRANSFORMS]
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-transforms-2/#funcdef-rotate3d
        // "A direction vector that cannot be normalized, such as [0,0,0], will cause the rotation to not be applied."
        let length = (x * x + y * y + z * z).sqrt();
        if length != 0.0 {
            let inverse_length = 1.0 / length;
            let axis = [x * inverse_length, y * inverse_length, z * inverse_length];
            self.matrix
                .set(self.matrix.get().multiplied(Matrix4::rotation(axis, to_radians(angle))));
        }

        // 2. If x or y are not 0 or -0, set is 2D of the current matrix to false.
        if x != 0.0 || y != 0.0 {
            self.is_2d.set(false);
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-skewxself
    pub(super) fn skew_x_self_steps(&self, sx: f64) {
        // 1. Post-multiply a skewX transformation on the current matrix by the specified angle sx in degrees. The 2D
        //    skewX matrix is described in CSS Transforms with alpha = sx in degrees. [CSS3-TRANSFORMS]
        let mut skew = Matrix4::identity();
        skew.set_element(2, 1, math::tan(to_radians(sx)));
        self.matrix.set(self.matrix.get().multiplied(skew));
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-skewyself
    pub(super) fn skew_y_self_steps(&self, sy: f64) {
        // 1. Post-multiply a skewX transformation on the current matrix by the specified angle sy in degrees. The 2D
        //    skewY matrix is described in CSS Transforms with beta = sy in degrees. [CSS3-TRANSFORMS]
        let mut skew = Matrix4::identity();
        skew.set_element(1, 2, math::tan(to_radians(sy)));
        self.matrix.set(self.matrix.get().multiplied(skew));
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-invertself
    pub(super) fn invert_self_steps(&self) {
        // 1. Invert the current matrix.
        match self.matrix.get().inverse() {
            Some(inverse) => self.matrix.set(inverse),
            // 2. If the current matrix is not invertible set all attributes to NaN and set is 2D to false.
            None => {
                self.matrix.set(Matrix4 {
                    elements: [[f64::NAN; 4]; 4],
                });
                self.is_2d.set(false);
            }
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-setmatrixvalue, from step 2 on.
    pub(super) fn set_matrix_value_steps(&self, matrix: Matrix4, is_2d_transform: bool) {
        // 2. Set is 2D to the value of 2dTransform.
        self.is_2d.set(is_2d_transform);

        // 3. Set m11 element through m44 element to the element values of matrix in column-major order.
        self.matrix.set(matrix);
    }
}

/// The elements of a Float32Array or a Float64Array, none for one that is detached or out of bounds.
fn typed_array_elements(array: Gc<TypedArrayBase>) -> Vec<f64> {
    let record = make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record(&array, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
    // NB: The offset of a view of a detached buffer, or of one that a resize left out of bounds, can be past the end of
    //     the buffer.
    if is_typed_array_out_of_bounds(&record) {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let byte_length = typed_array_byte_length(&record) as usize;
    let mut bytes = vec![0; byte_length];
    let byte_offset = array.byte_offset();
    array
        .viewed_array_buffer()
        .with_data_block(|data_block| data_block.copy_to(byte_offset, &mut bytes));
    if array.kind() == TypedArrayKind::Float32Array {
        let (elements, _) = bytes.as_chunks::<4>();
        elements
            .iter()
            .map(|element| f64::from(f32::from_ne_bytes(*element)))
            .collect()
    } else {
        let (elements, _) = bytes.as_chunks::<8>();
        elements.iter().map(|element| f64::from_ne_bytes(*element)).collect()
    }
}

/// A new typed array of the kind in the realm of the call context, which holds the bytes.
fn create_typed_array(cx: &CallContext, kind: TypedArrayKind, bytes: &[u8]) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<TypedArrayBase>> {
    let buffer = ArrayBuffer::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), bytes.len(), ArrayBufferShared::No)?;
    buffer.with_data_block(|data_block| data_block.overwrite(0, bytes));
    let element_count = 16;
    Ok(create_typed_array_on_buffer(
        cx.vm(),
        cx.realm(),
        kind,
        element_count,
        buffer,
    ))
}

/// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#parse-a-string-into-an-abstract-matrix, which throws a "SyntaxError"
/// DOMException for failure.
pub(crate) fn parse_transform_list(transform_list: &Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<(Matrix4, bool)> {
    let mut elements = [0.0; 16];
    let mut is_2d_transform = true;
    // SAFETY: The string is lent for the call.
    let parsed = unsafe {
        web_dom_matrix_parse_transform_list(transform_list.raw_identity(), &mut elements, &mut is_2d_transform)
    };
    if !parsed {
        return Err(Exception::syntax_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(
            b"Failed to parse CSS transform string.",
        )));
    }
    Ok((Matrix4::from_column_major(elements), is_2d_transform))
}

impl Serializable for DOMMatrixReadOnly {
    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        _for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        serialize_matrix(self, serialized);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
    fn deserialization_steps(_: &mut CallContext, serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        deserialize_matrix(serialized)
    }
}

/// The serialization steps for DOMMatrixReadOnly and DOMMatrix, https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
pub(crate) fn serialize_matrix(matrix: &DOMMatrixReadOnly, serialized: &mut SerializationWriter) {
    // NB: Is 2D is serialized first, so that the deserialization steps know how many elements follow.
    serialized.write_bool(matrix.is_2d.get());

    let elements = matrix.matrix.get();
    let m = |row, column| elements.element(row, column);

    // 1. If value’s is 2D is true:
    if matrix.is_2d.get() {
        // 1. Set serialized.[[M11]] to value’s m11 element.
        // 2. Set serialized.[[M12]] to value’s m12 element.
        // 3. Set serialized.[[M21]] to value’s m21 element.
        // 4. Set serialized.[[M22]] to value’s m22 element.
        // 5. Set serialized.[[M41]] to value’s m41 element.
        // 6. Set serialized.[[M42]] to value’s m42 element.
        // 7. Set serialized.[[Is2D]] to true.
        for element in [m(1, 1), m(1, 2), m(2, 1), m(2, 2), m(4, 1), m(4, 2)] {
            serialized.write_f64(element);
        }
    }
    // 2. Otherwise:
    else {
        // 1. Set serialized.[[M11]] to value’s m11 element.
        // 2. Set serialized.[[M12]] to value’s m12 element.
        // 3. Set serialized.[[M13]] to value’s m13 element.
        // 4. Set serialized.[[M14]] to value’s m14 element.
        // 5. Set serialized.[[M21]] to value’s m21 element.
        // 6. Set serialized.[[M22]] to value’s m22 element.
        // 7. Set serialized.[[M23]] to value’s m23 element.
        // 8. Set serialized.[[M24]] to value’s m24 element.
        // 9. Set serialized.[[M31]] to value’s m31 element.
        // 10. Set serialized.[[M32]] to value’s m32 element.
        // 11. Set serialized.[[M33]] to value’s m33 element.
        // 12. Set serialized.[[M34]] to value’s m34 element.
        // 13. Set serialized.[[M41]] to value’s m41 element.
        // 14. Set serialized.[[M42]] to value’s m42 element.
        // 15. Set serialized.[[M43]] to value’s m43 element.
        // 16. Set serialized.[[M44]] to value’s m44 element.
        // 17. Set serialized.[[Is2D]] to false.
        for element in elements.to_column_major() {
            serialized.write_f64(element);
        }
    }
}

/// The deserialization steps of DOMMatrixReadOnly and DOMMatrix, which give the matrix of the new object.
pub(crate) fn deserialize_matrix(serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<DOMMatrixReadOnly> {
    let is_2d = serialized.read_bool()?;

    // 1. If serialized.[[Is2D]] is true:
    if is_2d {
        // 1. Set value’s m11 element to serialized.[[M11]].
        // 2. Set value’s m12 element to serialized.[[M12]].
        // 3. Set value’s m13 element to 0.
        // 4. Set value’s m14 element to 0.
        // 5. Set value’s m21 element to serialized.[[M21]].
        // 6. Set value’s m22 element to serialized.[[M22]].
        // 7. Set value’s m23 element to 0.
        // 8. Set value’s m24 element to 0.
        // 9. Set value’s m31 element to 0.
        // 10. Set value’s m32 element to 0.
        // 11. Set value’s m33 element to 1.
        // 12. Set value’s m34 element to 0.
        // 13. Set value’s m41 element to serialized.[[M41]].
        // 14. Set value’s m42 element to serialized.[[M42]].
        // 15. Set value’s m43 element to 0.
        // 16. Set value’s m44 element to 1.
        // 17. Set value’s is 2D to true.
        let mut elements = [0.0; 6];
        for element in &mut elements {
            *element = serialized.read_f64()?;
        }
        return Ok(DOMMatrixReadOnly::create_2d_matrix(elements));
    }

    // 2. Otherwise:
    // 1. Set value’s m11 element to serialized.[[M11]].
    // 2. Set value’s m12 element to serialized.[[M12]].
    // 3. Set value’s m13 element to serialized.[[M13]].
    // 4. Set value’s m14 element to serialized.[[M14]].
    // 5. Set value’s m21 element to serialized.[[M21]].
    // 6. Set value’s m22 element to serialized.[[M22]].
    // 7. Set value’s m23 element to serialized.[[M23]].
    // 8. Set value’s m24 element to serialized.[[M24]].
    // 9. Set value’s m31 element to serialized.[[M31]].
    // 10. Set value’s m32 element to serialized.[[M32]].
    // 11. Set value’s m33 element to serialized.[[M33]].
    // 12. Set value’s m34 element to serialized.[[M34]].
    // 13. Set value’s m41 element to serialized.[[M41]].
    // 14. Set value’s m42 element to serialized.[[M42]].
    // 15. Set value’s m43 element to serialized.[[M43]].
    // 16. Set value’s m44 element to serialized.[[M44]].
    // 17. Set value’s is 2D to false.
    let mut elements = [0.0; 16];
    for element in &mut elements {
        *element = serialized.read_f64()?;
    }
    Ok(DOMMatrixReadOnly::create_3d_matrix(elements))
}

        Self { matrix }

        cx: &mut CallContext,

        Ok(Self::from_read_only(DOMMatrixReadOnly::from_init(cx, init)?))
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_matrix(cx: &mut CallContext, other: DOMMatrixInit) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // The fromMatrix(other) static method on DOMMatrix must create a DOMMatrix from the dictionary other.
        let matrix = Self::from_dictionary(&other)?;
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| matrix))

    /// Sets the element mRC of the 2D matrix to the value, as the setter of its attribute does.
    fn set_element(&self, row: usize, column: usize, value: f64) {
        let mut matrix = self.matrix.matrix();
        matrix.set_element(row, column, value);
        self.matrix.set_matrix(matrix);
    }

    /// Sets an element outside of the 2D matrix: the element to the new value and, if the new value is not the value
    /// of the identity matrix, is 2D to false.
    fn set_3d_element(&self, row: usize, column: usize, value: f64) {
        self.set_element(row, column, value);
        let identity_value = if row == column { 1.0 } else { 0.0 };
        if value != identity_value {
            self.matrix.set_is_2d(false);
        }
    }

    // NB: The mutable transformation methods return the current matrix, so they receive the object that they run on,
    //     which the bindings pass as they pass `&self` to the other methods.

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-multiplyself
    pub(crate) fn multiply_self(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        other: DOMMatrixInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // 1. Let otherObject be the result of invoking create a DOMMatrix from the dictionary other.
        let other_object = Self::from_dictionary(&other)?;

        // 2. The otherObject matrix gets post-multiplied to the current matrix.
        // 3. If is 2D of otherObject is false, set is 2D of the current matrix to false.
        this.matrix.multiply_self_steps(&other_object.matrix);

        // 4. Return the current matrix.
        Ok(*this)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-premultiplyself
    pub(crate) fn pre_multiply_self(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        other: DOMMatrixInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // 1. Let otherObject be the result of invoking create a DOMMatrix from the dictionary other.
        let other_object = Self::from_dictionary(&other)?;

        // 2. The otherObject matrix gets pre-multiplied to the current matrix.
        // 3. If is 2D of otherObject is false, set is 2D of the current matrix to false.
        this.matrix.pre_multiply_self_steps(&other_object.matrix);

        // 4. Return the current matrix.
        Ok(*this)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-translateself

        this: &Ref<Self>,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        tx: f64,
        ty: f64,
        tz: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        this.matrix.translate_self_steps(tx, ty, tz);

        Ok(*this)

    pub(crate) fn rotate_self(

        _: &mut CallContext,
        rot_x: f64,
        rot_y: Option<f64>,
        rot_z: Option<f64>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        this.matrix.rotate_self_steps(rot_x, rot_y, rot_z);

        // 8. Return the current matrix.
        Ok(*this)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-rotatefromvectorself
    pub(crate) fn rotate_from_vector_self(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        this.matrix.rotate_from_vector_self_steps(x, y);

        // 2. Return the current matrix.
        Ok(*this)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-rotateaxisangleself
    pub(crate) fn rotate_axis_angle_self(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
        z: f64,
        angle: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        this.matrix.rotate_axis_angle_self_steps(x, y, z, angle);

        // 3. Return the current matrix.
        Ok(*this)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-skewxself
    pub(crate) fn skew_x_self(this: &Ref<Self>, _: &mut CallContext, sx: f64) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        this.matrix.skew_x_self_steps(sx);

        // 2. Return the current matrix.
        Ok(*this)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-skewyself
    pub(crate) fn skew_y_self(this: &Ref<Self>, _: &mut CallContext, sy: f64) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        this.matrix.skew_y_self_steps(sy);

        // 2. Return the current matrix.
        Ok(*this)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-invertself
    pub(crate) fn invert_self(this: &Ref<Self>, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        this.matrix.invert_self_steps();

        // 3. Return the current matrix.
        Ok(*this)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dommatrix-setmatrixvalue
    pub(crate) fn set_matrix_value(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        transform_list: Utf16String,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // 1. Parse transformList into an abstract matrix, and let matrix and 2dTransform be the result. If the result
        //    is failure, then throw a "SyntaxError" DOMException.
        let (matrix, is_2d_transform) = parse_transform_list(&transform_list)?;

        // 2. Set is 2D to the value of 2dTransform.
        // 3. Set m11 element through m44 element to the element values of matrix in column-major order.
        this.matrix.set_matrix_value_steps(matrix, is_2d_transform);

        // 4. Return the current matrix.
        Ok(*this)
    }
}

impl Serializable for DOMMatrix {
    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        _for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        serialize_matrix(&self.matrix, serialized);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
    fn deserialization_steps(_: &mut CallContext, serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        Ok(Self::from_read_only(deserialize_matrix(serialized)?))
    }
}

//! https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dompointreadonly

use core::cell::Cell;

use libjs_rust::api::Trace;

pub(crate) use super::dictionaries::DOMPointInit;
use super::dom_matrix::DOMMatrix;
use super::dom_matrix_read_only::DOMMatrixInit;
use super::dom_point::DOMPoint;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::structured_data::{Serializable, SerializationReader, SerializationWriter};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct DOMPointReadOnly {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    x: Cell<f64>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    y: Cell<f64>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    z: Cell<f64>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    w: Cell<f64>,
}

impl Wrappable for DOMPointReadOnly {}

impl DOMPointReadOnly {
    pub(crate) fn new(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, w: f64) -> Self {
        Self {
            x: Cell::new(x),
            y: Cell::new(y),
            z: Cell::new(z),
            w: Cell::new(w),
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dompointreadonly-dompointreadonly
    pub(crate) fn construct(_: &mut CallContext, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, w: f64) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Let point be a new DOMPointReadOnly or DOMPoint object as appropriate.
        // 2. Set point’s variables x coordinate to x, y coordinate to y, z coordinate to z and w perspective to w.
        // 3. Return point.
        Ok(Self::new(x, y, z, w))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dompointreadonly-frompoint
    pub(crate) fn from_point(cx: &mut CallContext, other: DOMPointInit) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // The fromPoint(other) static method on DOMPointReadOnly must create a DOMPointReadOnly from the dictionary
        // other.
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| Self::from_dictionary(&other)))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#create-a-dompointreadonly-from-the-dictionary
    pub(crate) fn from_dictionary(other: &DOMPointInit) -> Self {
        // 1. Let point be a new DOMPointReadOnly or DOMPoint as appropriate.
        // 2. Set point’s variables x coordinate to other’s x dictionary member, y coordinate to other’s y dictionary
        //    member, z coordinate to other’s z dictionary member and w perspective to other’s w dictionary member.
        // 3. Return point.
        Self::new(other.x, other.y, other.z, other.w)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dompointreadonly-x
    pub(crate) fn x(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.x.get())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dompointreadonly-y
    pub(crate) fn y(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.y.get())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dompointreadonly-z
    pub(crate) fn z(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.z.get())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dompointreadonly-w
    pub(crate) fn w(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.w.get())
    }

    /// The coordinates x, y, z and w, in that order.
    pub(crate) fn coordinates(&self) -> [f64; 4] {
        [self.x.get(), self.y.get(), self.z.get(), self.w.get()]
    }

    pub(super) fn set_x_coordinate(&self, value: f64) {
        self.x.set(value);
    }

    pub(super) fn set_y_coordinate(&self, value: f64) {
        self.y.set(value);
    }

    pub(super) fn set_z_coordinate(&self, value: f64) {
        self.z.set(value);
    }

    pub(super) fn set_w_perspective(&self, value: f64) {
        self.w.set(value);
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-dompointreadonly-matrixtransform
    pub(crate) fn matrix_transform(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, matrix: DOMMatrixInit) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMPoint>> {
        // 1. Let matrixObject be the result of invoking create a DOMMatrix from the dictionary matrix.
        let matrix_object = DOMMatrix::from_dictionary(&matrix)?;

        // 2. Return the result of invoking transform a point with a matrix, given the current point and matrixObject.
        //    The current point does not get modified.
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| {
            matrix_object.parent().transform_point_steps(self)
        }))
    }
}

impl Serializable for DOMPointReadOnly {
    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        _for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        serialize_point(self, serialized);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
    fn deserialization_steps(_: &mut CallContext, serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        deserialize_point(serialized)
    }
}

/// The serialization steps for DOMPointReadOnly and DOMPoint, https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
pub(crate) fn serialize_point(point: &DOMPointReadOnly, serialized: &mut SerializationWriter) {
    // 1. Set serialized.[[X]] to value’s x coordinate.
    serialized.write_f64(point.x.get());

    // 2. Set serialized.[[Y]] to value’s y coordinate.
    serialized.write_f64(point.y.get());

    // 3. Set serialized.[[Z]] to value’s z coordinate.
    serialized.write_f64(point.z.get());

    // 4. Set serialized.[[W]] to value’s w perspective.
    serialized.write_f64(point.w.get());
}

/// The deserialization steps of DOMPointReadOnly and DOMPoint, which give the coordinates of the new point.
pub(crate) fn deserialize_point(serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<DOMPointReadOnly> {
    // 1. Set value’s x coordinate to serialized.[[X]].
    let x = serialized.read_f64()?;

    // 2. Set value’s y coordinate to serialized.[[Y]].
    let y = serialized.read_f64()?;

    // 3. Set value’s z coordinate to serialized.[[Z]].
    let z = serialized.read_f64()?;

    // 4. Set value’s w perspective to serialized.[[W]].
    let w = serialized.read_f64()?;

    Ok(DOMPointReadOnly::new(x, y, z, w))
}

//! https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#domquad

use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};

use super::dictionaries::DOMPointInit;
pub(crate) use super::dictionaries::DOMQuadInit;
use super::dictionaries::DOMRectInit;
use super::dom_point::DOMPoint;
use super::dom_rect::DOMRect;
use super::{nan_safe_maximum, nan_safe_minimum};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::structured_data::{Serializable, SerializationReader, SerializationWriter};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct DOMQuad {
    p1: Ref<DOMPoint>,
    p2: Ref<DOMPoint>,
    p3: Ref<DOMPoint>,
    p4: Ref<DOMPoint>,
}

impl Wrappable for DOMQuad {}

/// A new DOMPoint object with its attributes set to the values of the namesake dictionary members in the dictionary.
fn new_point(vm: &Vm, init: &DOMPointInit) -> Ref<DOMPoint> {
    allocate(vm, |_| DOMPoint::from_dictionary(init))
}

impl DOMQuad {
    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domquad-domquad
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        p1: DOMPointInit,
        p2: DOMPointInit,
        p3: DOMPointInit,
        p4: DOMPointInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Let point1 be a new DOMPoint object with its attributes set to the values of the namesake dictionary
        //    members in p1.
        let point1 = new_point(vm, &p1);

        // 2. Let point2 be a new DOMPoint object with its attributes set to the values of the namesake dictionary
        //    members in p2.
        let point2 = new_point(vm, &p2);

        // 3. Let point3 be a new DOMPoint object with its attributes set to the values of the namesake dictionary
        //    members in p3.
        let point3 = new_point(vm, &p3);

        // 4. Let point4 be a new DOMPoint object with its attributes set to the values of the namesake dictionary
        //    members in p4.
        let point4 = new_point(vm, &p4);

        // 5. Return a new DOMQuad with point 1 set to point1, point 2 set to point2, point 3 set to point3 and point 4
        //    set to point4.
        Ok(Self {
            p1: point1,
            p2: point2,
            p3: point3,
            p4: point4,
        })
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domquad-fromrect
    pub(crate) fn from_rect(cx: &mut CallContext, other: DOMRectInit) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // The fromRect(other) static method on DOMQuad must create a DOMQuad from the DOMRectInit dictionary other.
        let quad = Self::from_rect_dictionary(cx.vm(), &other);
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| quad))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#create-a-domquad-from-the-domrectinit-dictionary
    fn from_rect_dictionary(vm: &Vm, other: &DOMRectInit) -> Self {
        // 1. Let x, y, width and height be the value of other’s x, y, width and height dictionary members,
        //    respectively.
        let DOMRectInit { x, y, width, height } = *other;

        // 2. Let point1 be a new DOMPoint object with x coordinate set to x, y coordinate set to y, z coordinate set
        //    to 0 and w perspective set to 1.
        let point1 = allocate(vm, |_| DOMPoint::new(x, y, 0.0, 1.0));

        // 3. Let point2 be a new DOMPoint object with x coordinate set to x + width, y coordinate set to y, z
        //    coordinate set to 0 and w perspective set to 1.
        let point2 = allocate(vm, |_| DOMPoint::new(x + width, y, 0.0, 1.0));

        // 4. Let point3 be a new DOMPoint object with x coordinate set to x + width, y coordinate set to y + height, z
        //    coordinate set to 0 and w perspective set to 1.
        let point3 = allocate(vm, |_| DOMPoint::new(x + width, y + height, 0.0, 1.0));

        // 5. Let point4 be a new DOMPoint object with x coordinate set to x, y coordinate set to y + height, z
        //    coordinate set to 0 and w perspective set to 1.
        let point4 = allocate(vm, |_| DOMPoint::new(x, y + height, 0.0, 1.0));

        // 6. Return a new DOMQuad with point 1 set to point1, point 2 set to point2, point 3 set to point3 and point 4
        //    set to point4.
        Self {
            p1: point1,
            p2: point2,
            p3: point3,
            p4: point4,
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domquad-fromquad
    pub(crate) fn from_quad(cx: &mut CallContext, other: DOMQuadInit) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // The fromQuad(other) static method on DOMQuad must create a DOMQuad from the DOMQuadInit dictionary other.
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#create-a-domquad-from-the-domquadinit-dictionary
        // 1. Let point1 be the result of invoking create a DOMPoint from the dictionary p1 dictionary member of other,
        //    if it exists.
        let point1 = new_point(vm, &other.p1.unwrap_or_default());

        // 2. Let point2 be the result of invoking create a DOMPoint from the dictionary p2 dictionary member of other,
        //    if it exists.
        let point2 = new_point(vm, &other.p2.unwrap_or_default());

        // 3. Let point3 be the result of invoking create a DOMPoint from the dictionary p3 dictionary member of other,
        //    if it exists.
        let point3 = new_point(vm, &other.p3.unwrap_or_default());

        // 4. Let point4 be the result of invoking create a DOMPoint from the dictionary p4 dictionary member of other,
        //    if it exists.
        let point4 = new_point(vm, &other.p4.unwrap_or_default());

        // 5. Return a new DOMQuad with point 1 set to point1, point 2 set to point2, point 3 set to point3 and point 4
        //    set to point4.
        Ok(allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            p1: point1,
            p2: point2,
            p3: point3,
            p4: point4,
        }))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domquad-p1
    pub(crate) fn p1(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMPoint>> {
        // The p1 attribute must return point 1.
        Ok(self.p1)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domquad-p2
    pub(crate) fn p2(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMPoint>> {
        // The p2 attribute must return point 2.
        Ok(self.p2)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domquad-p3
    pub(crate) fn p3(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMPoint>> {
        // The p3 attribute must return point 3.
        Ok(self.p3)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domquad-p4
    pub(crate) fn p4(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMPoint>> {
        // The p4 attribute must return point 4.
        Ok(self.p4)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domquad-getbounds
    pub(crate) fn get_bounds(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<DOMRect>> {
        let [x1, y1, ..] = self.p1.parent().coordinates();
        let [x2, y2, ..] = self.p2.parent().coordinates();
        let [x3, y3, ..] = self.p3.parent().coordinates();
        let [x4, y4, ..] = self.p4.parent().coordinates();

        // 1. Let bounds be a DOMRect object.
        // 2. Let left be the NaN-safe minimum of point 1’s x coordinate, point 2’s x coordinate, point 3’s x
        //    coordinate and point 4’s x coordinate.
        let left = nan_safe_minimum(&[x1, x2, x3, x4]);

        // 3. Let top be the NaN-safe minimum of point 1’s y coordinate, point 2’s y coordinate, point 3’s y coordinate
        //    and point 4’s y coordinate.
        let top = nan_safe_minimum(&[y1, y2, y3, y4]);

        // 4. Let right be the NaN-safe maximum of point 1’s x coordinate, point 2’s x coordinate, point 3’s x
        //    coordinate and point 4’s x coordinate.
        let right = nan_safe_maximum(&[x1, x2, x3, x4]);

        // 5. Let bottom be the NaN-safe maximum of point 1’s y coordinate, point 2’s y coordinate, point 3’s y
        //    coordinate and point 4’s y coordinate.
        let bottom = nan_safe_maximum(&[y1, y2, y3, y4]);

        // 6. Set x coordinate of bounds to left, y coordinate of bounds to top, width dimension of bounds to right -
        //    left and height dimension of bounds to bottom - top.
        // 7. Return bounds.
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| {
            DOMRect::new(left, top, right - left, bottom - top)
        }))
    }
}

impl Serializable for DOMQuad {
    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // NB: The points are serialized in place, as they were before DOMQuad was implemented in Rust, so that stored
        //     values keep the positions that their objects have in the memory of the serialization.

        // 1. Set serialized.[[P1]] to the sub-serialization of value’s point 1.
        serialized.write_object_in_place::<DOMPoint>(cx, &self.p1, for_storage)?;

        // 2. Set serialized.[[P2]] to the sub-serialization of value’s point 2.
        serialized.write_object_in_place::<DOMPoint>(cx, &self.p2, for_storage)?;

        // 3. Set serialized.[[P3]] to the sub-serialization of value’s point 3.
        serialized.write_object_in_place::<DOMPoint>(cx, &self.p3, for_storage)?;

        // 4. Set serialized.[[P4]] to the sub-serialization of value’s point 4.
        serialized.write_object_in_place::<DOMPoint>(cx, &self.p4, for_storage)?;

        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
    fn deserialization_steps(cx: &mut CallContext, serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Set value’s point 1 to the sub-deserialization of serialized.[[P1]].
        let p1 = serialized.read_object_in_place::<DOMPoint>(cx)?;

        // 2. Set value’s point 2 to the sub-deserialization of serialized.[[P2]].
        let p2 = serialized.read_object_in_place::<DOMPoint>(cx)?;

        // 3. Set value’s point 3 to the sub-deserialization of serialized.[[P3]].
        let p3 = serialized.read_object_in_place::<DOMPoint>(cx)?;

        // 4. Set value’s point 4 to the sub-deserialization of serialized.[[P4]].
        let p4 = serialized.read_object_in_place::<DOMPoint>(cx)?;

        Ok(Self { p1, p2, p3, p4 })
    }
}

//! https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#domrectlist

use libjs_rust::api::{DeferGc, Trace};

use super::dom_rect::DOMRect;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct DOMRectList {
    rects: Vec<Ref<DOMRect>>,
}

impl Wrappable for DOMRectList {}

impl DOMRectList {
    pub(crate) fn new(_: &DeferGc<'_>, rects: &[Ref<DOMRect>]) -> Self {
        Self { rects: rects.to_vec() }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectlist-length
    pub(crate) fn length(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        // The length attribute must return the total number of DOMRect objects associated with the object.
        Ok(u32::try_from(self.rects.len()).expect("a list has fewer than 2^32 rectangles"))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectlist-item
    pub(crate) fn item(&self, _: &mut CallContext, index: u32) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<DOMRect>>> {
        // The item(index) method, when invoked, must return null when index is greater than or equal to the number of
        // DOMRect objects associated with the DOMRectList. Otherwise, the DOMRect object at index must be returned.
        // Indices are zero-based.
        Ok(self.rects.get(index as usize).copied())
    }
}

//! https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#domrectreadonly

use core::cell::Cell;

use libjs_rust::api::Trace;

pub(crate) use super::dictionaries::DOMRectInit;
use super::{nan_safe_maximum, nan_safe_minimum};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::structured_data::{Serializable, SerializationReader, SerializationWriter};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct DOMRectReadOnly {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    x: Cell<f64>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    y: Cell<f64>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    width: Cell<f64>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    height: Cell<f64>,
}

impl Wrappable for DOMRectReadOnly {}

impl DOMRectReadOnly {
    pub(crate) fn new(x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64) -> Self {
        Self {
            x: Cell::new(x),
            y: Cell::new(y),
            width: Cell::new(width),
            height: Cell::new(height),
        }
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectreadonly-domrectreadonly
    pub(crate) fn construct(_: &mut CallContext, x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Let rect be a new DOMRectReadOnly or DOMRect object as appropriate.
        // 2. Set rect’s variables x coordinate to x, y coordinate to y, width dimension to width and height dimension
        //    to height.
        // 3. Return rect.
        Ok(Self::new(x, y, width, height))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectreadonly-fromrect
    pub(crate) fn from_rect(cx: &mut CallContext, other: DOMRectInit) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // The fromRect(other) static method on DOMRectReadOnly must create a DOMRectReadOnly from the dictionary other.
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| Self::from_dictionary(&other)))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#create-a-domrectreadonly-from-the-dictionary
    pub(crate) fn from_dictionary(other: &DOMRectInit) -> Self {
        // 1. Let rect be a new DOMRectReadOnly or DOMRect as appropriate.
        // 2. Set rect’s variables x coordinate to other’s x dictionary member, y coordinate to other’s y dictionary
        //    member, width dimension to other’s width dictionary member and height dimension to other’s height
        //    dictionary member.
        // 3. Return rect.
        Self::new(other.x, other.y, other.width, other.height)
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectreadonly-x
    pub(crate) fn x(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.x.get())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectreadonly-y
    pub(crate) fn y(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.y.get())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectreadonly-width
    pub(crate) fn width(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.width.get())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectreadonly-height
    pub(crate) fn height(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.height.get())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectreadonly-top
    pub(crate) fn top(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The top attribute, on getting, must return the NaN-safe minimum of the y coordinate and the sum of the y
        // coordinate and the height dimension.
        Ok(nan_safe_minimum(&[self.y.get(), self.y.get() + self.height.get()]))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectreadonly-right
    pub(crate) fn right(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The right attribute, on getting, must return the NaN-safe maximum of the x coordinate and the sum of the x
        // coordinate and the width dimension.
        Ok(nan_safe_maximum(&[self.x.get(), self.x.get() + self.width.get()]))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectreadonly-bottom
    pub(crate) fn bottom(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The bottom attribute, on getting, must return the NaN-safe maximum of the y coordinate and the sum of the y
        // coordinate and the height dimension.
        Ok(nan_safe_maximum(&[self.y.get(), self.y.get() + self.height.get()]))
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#dom-domrectreadonly-left
    pub(crate) fn left(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The left attribute, on getting, must return the NaN-safe minimum of the x coordinate and the sum of the x
        // coordinate and the width dimension.
        Ok(nan_safe_minimum(&[self.x.get(), self.x.get() + self.width.get()]))
    }

    pub(super) fn set_x_coordinate(&self, value: f64) {
        self.x.set(value);
    }

    pub(super) fn set_y_coordinate(&self, value: f64) {
        self.y.set(value);
    }

    pub(super) fn set_width_dimension(&self, value: f64) {
        self.width.set(value);
    }

    pub(super) fn set_height_dimension(&self, value: f64) {
        self.height.set(value);
    }
}

impl Serializable for DOMRectReadOnly {
    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        _for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        serialize_rect(self, serialized);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
    fn deserialization_steps(_: &mut CallContext, serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        deserialize_rect(serialized)
    }
}

/// The serialization steps for DOMRectReadOnly and DOMRect, https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#structured-serialization
pub(crate) fn serialize_rect(rect: &DOMRectReadOnly, serialized: &mut SerializationWriter) {
    // 1. Set serialized.[[X]] to value’s x coordinate.
    serialized.write_f64(rect.x.get());

    // 2. Set serialized.[[Y]] to value’s y coordinate.
    serialized.write_f64(rect.y.get());

    // 3. Set serialized.[[Width]] to value’s width dimension.
    serialized.write_f64(rect.width.get());

    // 4. Set serialized.[[Height]] to value’s height dimension.
    serialized.write_f64(rect.height.get());
}

/// The deserialization steps of DOMRectReadOnly and DOMRect, which give the dimensions of the new rectangle.
pub(crate) fn deserialize_rect(serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<DOMRectReadOnly> {
    // 1. Set value’s x coordinate to serialized.[[X]].
    let x = serialized.read_f64()?;

    // 2. Set value’s y coordinate to serialized.[[Y]].
    let y = serialized.read_f64()?;

    // 3. Set value’s width dimension to serialized.[[Width]].
    let width = serialized.read_f64()?;

    // 4. Set value’s height dimension to serialized.[[Height]].
    let height = serialized.read_f64()?;

    Ok(DOMRectReadOnly::new(x, y, width, height))
}

//! The C ABI through which LibWeb's C++ creates the geometry objects that it returns to script, and reads and changes
//! the matrices of CSS Typed OM, which the headers in Libraries/LibWeb/Geometry declare. A cell is the cell of an
//! object of the interface that the name of the function says; a DOMMatrixReadOnly cell can be that of a DOMMatrix.

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::{MarkedVec, Vm};

use super::dom_matrix::DOMMatrix;
use super::dom_matrix_read_only::DOMMatrixReadOnly;
use super::dom_point::DOMPoint;
use super::dom_point_read_only::DOMPointReadOnly;
use super::dom_rect::DOMRect;
use super::dom_rect_list::DOMRectList;
use super::dom_rect_read_only::DOMRectReadOnly;
use super::matrix::{ColumnMajor, Matrix4};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, InterfaceCell, allocate, cell_into_abi};

/// The matrix of a DOMMatrixReadOnly or a DOMMatrix whose cell C++ lends.
fn matrix_from_abi(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> &DOMMatrixReadOnly {
    if let Some(matrix) = cell.implementation_if::<DOMMatrixReadOnly>() {
        return matrix;
    }
    cell.implementation::<DOMMatrix>().parent()
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_point_read_only_create(vm: &Vm, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, w: f64) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| DOMPointReadOnly::new(x, y, z, w)))
}

/// Stores the coordinates x, y, z and w of the point, in that order.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_point_coordinates(point: &InterfaceCell, out_coordinates: &mut [f64; 4]) {
    *out_coordinates = point.object::<DOMPoint>().parent().coordinates();
}

/// Sets the x and y coordinates of the point.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_point_set_x_and_y(point: &InterfaceCell, x: f64, y: f64) {
    point.object::<DOMPoint>().set_x_and_y(x, y);
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_point_create(vm: &Vm, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, w: f64) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| DOMPoint::new(x, y, z, w)))
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_rect_read_only_create(vm: &Vm, x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| DOMRectReadOnly::new(x, y, width, height)))
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_rect_create(vm: &Vm, x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| DOMRect::new(x, y, width, height)))
}

/// Sets the x coordinate, y coordinate, width dimension and height dimension of the rectangle.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_rect_set(rect: &InterfaceCell, x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64) {
    let rect = rect.implementation::<DOMRect>().parent();
    rect.set_x_coordinate(x);
    rect.set_y_coordinate(y);
    rect.set_width_dimension(width);
    rect.set_height_dimension(height);
}

/// A new DOMRectList of new DOMRects, whose x, y, width and height are the groups of four values of `rects`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_rect_list_create(vm: &Vm, rects: ak::Span<'_, [f64; 4]>) -> *mut c_void {
    // NB: Creating a rectangle can collect, so the rectangles created before it are kept in a MarkedVec until the
    //     list holds them.
    let created = MarkedVec::with_capacity(vm, rects.as_slice().len());
    for &[x, y, width, height] in rects.as_slice() {
        created.push(allocate(vm, |_| DOMRect::new(x, y, width, height)));
    }
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |defer_gc| DOMRectList::new(defer_gc, &created.values())))
}

/// A new DOMMatrix whose elements m11, m12, m13, m14, m21, ..., m44 are the values, in that order.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_matrix_create(vm: &Vm, elements: &[f64; 16], is_2d: bool) -> *mut c_void {
    let matrix = DOMMatrixReadOnly::new(Matrix4::from_column_major(*elements), is_2d);
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| DOMMatrix::from_read_only(matrix)))
}

/// A new DOMMatrix initialized to the values of the matrix.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_matrix_create_from_read_only(vm: &Vm, matrix: &InterfaceCell) -> *mut c_void {
    let matrix = matrix_from_abi(matrix);
    let copy = DOMMatrixReadOnly::new(matrix.matrix(), matrix.is_2d());
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| DOMMatrix::from_read_only(copy)))
}

/// Stores the elements m11, m12, m13, m14, m21, ..., m44 of the matrix, in that order.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_matrix_read_only_elements(matrix: &InterfaceCell, out_elements: &mut [f64; 16]) {
    *out_elements = matrix_from_abi(matrix).matrix().to_column_major();
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_matrix_read_only_is_2d(matrix: &InterfaceCell) -> bool {
    matrix_from_abi(matrix).is_2d()
}

/// Stores the stringification of the matrix, an AK::Utf16String that the caller adopts, unless an element of the
/// matrix is not finite, which has none.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_matrix_read_only_to_string(matrix: &InterfaceCell, out_string: &mut usize) -> bool {
    let Some(string) = matrix_from_abi(matrix).stringify() else {
        return false;
    };
    *out_string = string.into_raw();
    true
}

/// Sets the elements m11, m12, m13, m14, m21, ..., m44 of the matrix, in that order, and whether it is 2D.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_matrix_set_elements(matrix: &InterfaceCell, elements: &[f64; 16], is_2d: bool) {
    let matrix = matrix.implementation::<DOMMatrix>().parent();
    matrix.set_matrix(Matrix4::from_column_major(*elements));
    matrix.set_is_2d(is_2d);
}

/// Post-multiplies the other matrix to the matrix, as multiplySelf() does with the DOMMatrix of a dictionary.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_matrix_multiply_self(matrix: &InterfaceCell, other: &InterfaceCell) {
    let (matrix, other) = (matrix.object::<DOMMatrix>(), matrix_from_abi(other));
    matrix.parent().multiply_self_steps(other);
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_dom_matrix_rotate_axis_angle_self(matrix: &InterfaceCell, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, angle: f64) {
    matrix
        .object::<DOMMatrix>()
        .parent()
        .rotate_axis_angle_self_steps(x, y, z, angle);
}

//! The 4x4 matrices of the geometry interfaces, https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#4x4-abstract-matrix, whose
//! arithmetic is that of LibGfx, in doubles.

pub(crate) use libgfx_rust::DoubleMatrix4x4 as Matrix4;

/// The elements of a matrix as the specification names them. A Matrix4 stores its elements row by row, and the matrix
/// of the specification is column-major, so its element mRC is in row C and column R: m12 is in the first column of
/// the second row.
pub(crate) trait ColumnMajor {
    /// The matrix whose elements m11, m12, m13, m14, m21, ..., m44 are the values, in that order.
    fn from_column_major(elements: [f64; 16]) -> Self;

    /// The elements m11, m12, m13, m14, m21, ..., m44, in that order.
    fn to_column_major(&self) -> [f64; 16];

    /// The element mRC, for a row R and a column C from 1 to 4.
    fn element(&self, row: usize, column: usize) -> f64;

    fn set_element(&mut self, row: usize, column: usize, value: f64);
}

impl ColumnMajor for Matrix4 {
    fn from_column_major(elements: [f64; 16]) -> Self {
        let mut matrix = Self::identity();
        for (index, element) in elements.into_iter().enumerate() {
            matrix.elements[index % 4][index / 4] = element;
        }
        matrix
    }

    fn to_column_major(&self) -> [f64; 16] {
        core::array::from_fn(|index| self.elements[index % 4][index / 4])
    }

    fn element(&self, row: usize, column: usize) -> f64 {
        self.elements[column - 1][row - 1]
    }

    fn set_element(&mut self, row: usize, column: usize, value: f64) {
        self.elements[column - 1][row - 1] = value;
    }
}

/// Degrees in radians, as AK::to_radians() converts them.
pub(crate) fn to_radians(degrees: f64) -> f64 {
    degrees * core::f64::consts::PI / 180.0
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{ColumnMajor, Matrix4};

    #[test]
    fn column_major_elements_round_trip() {
        let elements: [f64; 16] = core::array::from_fn(|index| index as f64);
        let matrix = Matrix4::from_column_major(elements);
        // NB: The elements are numbered from 0 in column-major order, so m12, the second, is 1, and m21, the fifth, is
        //     4.
        assert_eq!(matrix.element(1, 2), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(matrix.element(2, 1), 4.0);
        assert_eq!(matrix.to_column_major(), elements);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_inverse_undoes_the_matrix() {
        let matrix = Matrix4::translation(10.0, 20.0, 30.0).multiplied(Matrix4::scale(2.0, 4.0, 8.0));
        let inverse = matrix.inverse().expect("the matrix is invertible");
        assert_eq!(matrix.multiplied(inverse), Matrix4::identity());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_singular_matrix_has_no_inverse() {
        assert_eq!(Matrix4::scale(0.0, 1.0, 1.0).inverse(), None);
    }
}

pub(crate) mod matrix;

/// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#nan-safe-minimum
pub(crate) fn nan_safe_minimum(values: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    // The NaN-safe minimum of a non-empty list of unrestricted double values is NaN if any member of the list is NaN,
    // or the minimum of the list otherwise.
    if values.iter().any(|value| value.is_nan()) {
        return f64::NAN;
    }
    // NB: The minimum of equal values is the one first in the list, as AK::min() gives it to C++, so that the sign of
    //     a zero does not change.
    let (last, rest) = values.split_last().expect("the list is not empty");
    rest.iter()
        .rev()
        .fold(*last, |minimum, value| if minimum < *value { minimum } else { *value })
}

/// https://drafts.fxtf.org/geometry/#nan-safe-maximum
pub(crate) fn nan_safe_maximum(values: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    // Analogously, the NaN-safe maximum of a non-empty list of unrestricted double values is NaN if any member of the
    // list is NaN, or the maximum of the list otherwise.
    if values.iter().any(|value| value.is_nan()) {
        return f64::NAN;
    }
    let (last, rest) = values.split_last().expect("the list is not empty");
    rest.iter()
        .rev()
        .fold(*last, |maximum, value| if *value < maximum { maximum } else { *value })
}

//! Performance, https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#sec-performance

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, MarkedVec, Realm, Trace, Value, Vm, utf16_formatted};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_high_resolution_time_current_high_resolution_time(global_object: *mut c_void) -> f64;
    fn web_high_resolution_time_get_time_origin_timestamp(global_object: *mut c_void) -> f64;

pub(crate) enum DOMStringOrPerformanceMeasureOptions {
    DOMString(Utf16String),
    PerformanceMeasureOptions(PerformanceMeasureOptions),
