// https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#sec-performance
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Performance {
    event_target: CppEventTarget,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    timing: Cell<Option<Ref<PerformanceTiming>>>,
    navigation: Cell<Option<Ref<PerformanceNavigation>>>,
}

impl Wrappable for Performance {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.realm)
    }

    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event_target.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for Performance {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
}

impl Performance {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Ref<Self> {
        let performance = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            event_target: CppEventTarget::new(),
            realm,
            timing: Cell::new(None),
            navigation: Cell::new(None),
        });
        performance.event_target.set_owner(performance);
        performance
    }

    pub(crate) fn event_target(&self) -> &CppEventTarget {
        &self.event_target
    }

    fn performance_timeline(&self, vm: &Vm) -> PerformanceTimelineRef {
        PerformanceTimeline::of(vm, self.realm)
    }

    fn window(&self) -> Option<CppWindow> {
        window_from_global_object(self.realm.global_object())
    }

    fn timing_object(&self, vm: &Vm) -> Ref<PerformanceTiming> {
        if let Some(timing) = self.timing.get() {
            return timing;
        }
        let window = self.window().expect("only a Window has a PerformanceTiming");
        let timing = allocate(vm, |_| PerformanceTiming::new(window));
        self.timing.set(Some(timing));
        timing
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performance-timing
    pub(crate) fn timing(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<PerformanceTiming>> {
        Ok(self.timing_object(cx.vm()))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performance-navigation
    pub(crate) fn navigation(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<PerformanceNavigation>> {
        if let Some(navigation) = self.navigation.get() {
            return Ok(navigation);
        }
        let window = self.window().expect("only a Window has a PerformanceNavigation");
        let navigation = allocate(cx.vm(), |_| PerformanceNavigation::new(window));
        self.navigation.set(Some(navigation));
        Ok(navigation)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#dom-performance-eventcounts
    pub(crate) fn event_counts(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<EventCounts>> {
        // The eventCounts attribute's getter returns this's relevant global object's eventCounts.
        let window = self.window().expect("only a Window has eventCounts");
        Ok(window.event_timing_state(cx.vm()).event_counts(cx.vm()))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#dom-performance-interactioncount
    pub(crate) fn interaction_count(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // The interactionCount attribute's getter returns this's relevant global object's interactionCount.
        let window = self.window().expect("only a Window has an interactionCount");
        Ok(window.event_timing_state(cx.vm()).interaction_count())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#timeorigin-attribute
    pub(crate) fn time_origin(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The timeOrigin attribute MUST return the number of milliseconds in the duration returned by get time origin timestamp for the relevant global object of this.
        // SAFETY: The global object is live.
        Ok(unsafe { web_high_resolution_time_get_time_origin_timestamp(self.realm.global_object().as_ptr().cast()) })
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#now-method
    pub(crate) fn now(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The now() method MUST return the number of milliseconds in the current high resolution time given this's relevant global object (a duration).
        // SAFETY: The global object is live.
        Ok(
            unsafe {
                web_high_resolution_time_current_high_resolution_time(self.realm.global_object().as_ptr().cast())
            },
        )
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/user-timing/#mark-method
    pub(crate) fn mark(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        mark_name: Utf16String,
        mark_options: PerformanceMarkOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<PerformanceMark>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Run the PerformanceMark constructor and let entry be the newly created object.
        let entry = run_the_performance_mark_constructor(cx, self.realm, mark_name, &mark_options)?;

        // 2. Queue entry.
        let timeline = self.performance_timeline(vm);
        timeline.queue_performance_entry(vm, &AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceMark(entry));

        // 3. Add entry to the performance entry buffer.
        timeline.add_performance_entry(vm, &AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceMark(entry), false);

        // 4. Return entry.
        Ok(entry)
    }

    pub(crate) fn clear_marks(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, mark_name: Option<Utf16String>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let timeline = self.performance_timeline(vm);
        let entry_type = Utf16String::from_utf8("mark");

        // 1. If markName is omitted, remove all PerformanceMark objects from the performance entry buffer.
        let Some(mark_name) = mark_name else {
            timeline.clear_performance_entry_buffer(vm, &entry_type);
            return Ok(());
        };

        // 2. Otherwise, remove all PerformanceMark objects listed in the performance entry buffer whose name is markName.
        timeline.remove_entries_from_performance_entry_buffer(vm, &entry_type, &mark_name);

        // 3. Return undefined.
        Ok(())
    }

    fn convert_name_to_timestamp(&self, vm: &Vm, name: &Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // 1. If the global object is not a Window object, throw a TypeError.
        if self.window().is_none() {
            return Err(Exception::TypeError(utf16_formatted(
                "'{}' is an attribute in the PerformanceTiming interface and thus can only be used in a Window context",
                &[name],
            )));
        }

        // 2. If name is navigationStart, return 0.
        if *name == Utf16String::from_utf8("navigationStart") {
            return Ok(0.0);
        }

        let timing = self.timing_object(vm);
        let mut cx = CallContext::new(vm, self.realm);

        // 3. Let startTime be the value of navigationStart in the PerformanceTiming interface.
        let start_time = timing.navigation_start(&mut cx)?;

        // 4. Let endTime be the value of name in the PerformanceTiming interface.
        let end_time = timing.attribute(&mut cx, name)?;

        // 5. If endTime is 0, throw an InvalidAccessError.
        if end_time == 0 {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidAccessError",
                utf16_formatted(
                    "The '{}' entry in the PerformanceTiming interface is equal to 0, meaning it hasn't happened yet",
                    &[name],
                ),
            ));
        }

        // 6. Return result of subtracting startTime from endTime.
        Ok(end_time.wrapping_sub(start_time) as f64)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/user-timing/#dfn-convert-a-mark-to-a-timestamp
    fn convert_mark_to_timestamp(&self, cx: &CallContext, mark: &DOMStringOrDouble) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        let mark_time_stamp = match mark {
            DOMStringOrDouble::DOMString(mark_string) => {
                // 1. If mark is a DOMString and it has the same name as a read only attribute in the PerformanceTiming interface, let end
                //    time be the value returned by running the convert a name to a timestamp algorithm with name set to the value of mark.
                if is_performance_timing_attribute(mark_string) {
                    return self.convert_name_to_timestamp(cx.vm(), mark_string);
                }

                // 2. Otherwise, if mark is a DOMString, let end time be the value of the startTime attribute from the most recent occurrence
                //    of a PerformanceMark object in the performance entry buffer whose name is mark. If no matching entry is found, throw a
                //    SyntaxError.
                let start_time = self
                    .performance_timeline(cx.vm())
                    .with_relevant_performance_entry_tuple(&Utf16String::from_utf8("mark"), |tuple| {
                        tuple
                            .performance_entry_buffer
                            .iter()
                            .rev()
                            .find(|entry| entry.name() == *mark_string)
                            .map(|entry| entry.start_time())
                    });

                return start_time.ok_or_else(|| {
                    Exception::syntax_error(utf16_formatted(
                        "No PerformanceMark object with name '{}' found in the performance timeline",
                        &[mark_string],
                    ))
                });
            }
            // 3. Otherwise, if mark is a DOMHighResTimeStamp:
            DOMStringOrDouble::Double(mark_time_stamp) => *mark_time_stamp,
        };

        // 1. If mark is negative, throw a TypeError.
        if mark_time_stamp < 0.0 {
            return Err(Exception::type_error(
                "Cannot have negative time values in PerformanceMark",
            ));
        }

        // 2. Otherwise, let end time be mark.
        Ok(mark_time_stamp)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/user-timing/#dom-performance-measure
    pub(crate) fn measure(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        measure_name: Utf16String,
        start_or_measure_options: DOMStringOrPerformanceMeasureOptions,
        end_mark: Option<Utf16String>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<PerformanceMeasure>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. If startOrMeasureOptions is a PerformanceMeasureOptions object and at least one of start, end, duration, and detail
        //    are present, run the following checks:
        let options = match &start_or_measure_options {
            DOMStringOrPerformanceMeasureOptions::PerformanceMeasureOptions(options) => Some(options),
            DOMStringOrPerformanceMeasureOptions::DOMString(_) => None,
        };
        if let Some(options) = options
            && (options.start.is_some()
                || options.end.is_some()
                || options.duration.is_some()
                || options.detail.is_some())
        {
            // 1. If endMark is given, throw a TypeError.
            if end_mark.is_some() {
                return Err(Exception::type_error(
                    "Cannot provide PerformanceMeasureOptions and endMark at the same time",
                ));
            }

            // 2. If startOrMeasureOptions's start and end members are both omitted, throw a TypeError.
            if options.start.is_none() && options.end.is_none() {
                return Err(Exception::type_error(
                    "PerformanceMeasureOptions must contain one or both of 'start' and 'end'",
                ));
            }

            // 3. If startOrMeasureOptions's start, duration, and end members are all present, throw a TypeError.
            if options.start.is_some() && options.end.is_some() && options.duration.is_some() {
                return Err(Exception::type_error(
                    "PerformanceMeasureOptions cannot contain 'start', 'duration' and 'end' properties all at once",
                ));
            }
        }

        // 2. Compute end time as follows:
        // 1. If endMark is given, let end time be the value returned by running the convert a mark to a timestamp algorithm passing
        //    in endMark.
        let end_time = if let Some(end_mark) = end_mark {
            self.convert_mark_to_timestamp(cx, &DOMStringOrDouble::DOMString(end_mark))?
        }
        // 2. Otherwise, if startOrMeasureOptions is a PerformanceMeasureOptions object, and if its end member is present, let end
        //    time be the value returned by running the convert a mark to a timestamp algorithm passing in startOrMeasureOptions's end.
        else if let Some(end) = options.and_then(|options| options.end.as_ref()) {
            self.convert_mark_to_timestamp(cx, end)?
        }
        // 3. Otherwise, if startOrMeasureOptions is a PerformanceMeasureOptions object, and if its start and duration members are
        //    both present:
        else if let Some((start, duration)) =
            options.and_then(|options| Some((options.start.as_ref()?, options.duration?)))
        {
            // 1. Let start be the value returned by running the convert a mark to a timestamp algorithm passing in start.
            let start = self.convert_mark_to_timestamp(cx, start)?;

            // 2. Let duration be the value returned by running the convert a mark to a timestamp algorithm passing in duration.
            let duration = self.convert_mark_to_timestamp(cx, &DOMStringOrDouble::Double(duration))?;

            // 3. Let end time be start plus duration.
            start + duration
        }
        // 4. Otherwise, let end time be the value that would be returned by the Performance object's now() method.
        else {
            self.now(cx)?
        };

        // 3. Compute start time as follows:
        // 1. If startOrMeasureOptions is a PerformanceMeasureOptions object, and if its start member is present, let start time be
        //    the value returned by running the convert a mark to a timestamp algorithm passing in startOrMeasureOptions's start.
        let start_time = if let Some(start) = options.and_then(|options| options.start.as_ref()) {
            self.convert_mark_to_timestamp(cx, start)?
        }
        // 2. Otherwise, if startOrMeasureOptions is a PerformanceMeasureOptions object, and if its duration and end members are
        //    both present:
        else if let Some((duration, end)) =
            options.and_then(|options| Some((options.duration?, options.end.as_ref()?)))
        {
            // 1. Let duration be the value returned by running the convert a mark to a timestamp algorithm passing in duration.
            let duration = self.convert_mark_to_timestamp(cx, &DOMStringOrDouble::Double(duration))?;

            // 2. Let end be the value returned by running the convert a mark to a timestamp algorithm passing in end.
            let end = self.convert_mark_to_timestamp(cx, end)?;

            // 3. Let start time be end minus duration.
            end - duration
        }
        // 3. Otherwise, if startOrMeasureOptions is a DOMString, let start time be the value returned by running the convert a mark
        //    to a timestamp algorithm passing in startOrMeasureOptions.
        else if let DOMStringOrPerformanceMeasureOptions::DOMString(start) = &start_or_measure_options {
            self.convert_mark_to_timestamp(cx, &DOMStringOrDouble::DOMString(start.clone()))?
        }
        // 4. Otherwise, let start time be 0.
        else {
            0.0
        };

        // NOTE: Step 4 (creating the entry) is done after determining values, as we set the values once during creation and never
        //       change them after.

        // 5. Set entry's name attribute to measureName.
        // NOTE: Will be done during construction.

        // 6. Set entry's entryType attribute to DOMString "measure".
        // NOTE: Already done via the `entry_type` virtual function.

        // 7. Set entry's startTime attribute to start time.
        // NOTE: Will be done during construction.

        // 8. Set entry's duration attribute to the duration from start time to end time. The resulting duration value MAY be negative.
        let duration = end_time - start_time;

        // 4. Create a new PerformanceMeasure object (entry).
        let mut detail = Value::NULL;
        if let Some(options_detail) = options.and_then(|options| options.detail)
            && !options_detail.is_null()
        {
            detail = structured_clone(&CallContext::new(vm, self.realm), options_detail, &[])?;
        }
        let entry = PerformanceMeasure::create(vm, measure_name, start_time, duration, detail);

        // 10. Queue entry.
        let timeline = self.performance_timeline(vm);
        timeline.queue_performance_entry(vm, &AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceMeasure(entry));

        // 11. Add entry to the performance entry buffer.
        timeline.add_performance_entry(vm, &AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceMeasure(entry), false);

        // 12. Return entry.
        Ok(entry)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/user-timing/#dom-performance-clearmeasures
    pub(crate) fn clear_measures(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, measure_name: Option<Utf16String>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let timeline = self.performance_timeline(vm);
        let entry_type = Utf16String::from_utf8("measure");

        // 1. If measureName is omitted, remove all PerformanceMeasure objects in the performance entry buffer.
        let Some(measure_name) = measure_name else {
            timeline.clear_performance_entry_buffer(vm, &entry_type);
            return Ok(());
        };

        // 2. Otherwise remove all PerformanceMeasure objects listed in the performance entry buffer whose name is measureName.
        timeline.remove_entries_from_performance_entry_buffer(vm, &entry_type, &measure_name);

        // 3. Return undefined.
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performance-clearresourcetimings
    pub(crate) fn clear_resource_timings(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Remove all PerformanceResourceTiming objects in the performance entry buffer.
        // 2. Set resource timing buffer current size to 0.
        self.performance_timeline(cx.vm())
            .clear_performance_entry_buffer(cx.vm(), &Utf16String::from_utf8("resource"));
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performance-setresourcetimingbuffersize
    pub(crate) fn set_resource_timing_buffer_size(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, max_size: u32) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Set resource timing buffer size limit to the maxSize parameter. If the maxSize parameter is less than
        //    resource timing buffer current size, no PerformanceResourceTiming objects are to be removed from the
        //    performance entry buffer.
        self.performance_timeline(cx.vm())
            .set_resource_timing_buffer_size_limit(max_size);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#getentries-method
    pub(crate) fn get_entries<'vm>(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, AnyPerformanceEntry>> {
        // Returns a PerformanceEntryList object returned by the filter buffer map by name and type algorithm with name and
        // type set to null.
        let entries = self
            .performance_timeline(cx.vm())
            .filter_buffer_map_by_name_and_type(cx, None, None);
        Ok(entries)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performance-getentriesbytype
    pub(crate) fn get_entries_by_type<'vm>(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
        r#type: Utf16String,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, AnyPerformanceEntry>> {
        // Returns a PerformanceEntryList object returned by filter buffer map by name and type algorithm with name set to null,
        // and type set to the method's input type parameter.
        let entries = self
            .performance_timeline(cx.vm())
            .filter_buffer_map_by_name_and_type(cx, None, Some(&r#type));
        Ok(entries)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performance-getentriesbyname
    pub(crate) fn get_entries_by_name<'vm>(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
        name: Utf16String,
        r#type: Option<Utf16String>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, AnyPerformanceEntry>> {
        // Returns a PerformanceEntryList object returned by filter buffer map by name and type algorithm with name set to the
        // method input name parameter, and type set to null if optional entryType is omitted, or set to the method's input type
        // parameter otherwise.
        let entries =
            self.performance_timeline(cx.vm())
                .filter_buffer_map_by_name_and_type(cx, Some(&name), r#type.as_ref());
        Ok(entries)
    }
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#barprop

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::{LentCppCell, cpp_class};
use crate::bindings::global_object::CppWindow;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Wrappable, allocate, cell_into_abi};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_html_bar_prop_window_browsing_context(window: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_html_bar_prop_top_level_browsing_context_is_popup(browsing_context: *mut c_void) -> bool;
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct BarProp {
    window: CppWindow,
}

impl Wrappable for BarProp {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.window.realm())
    }
}

impl BarProp {
    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#dom-barprop-visible
    pub(crate) fn visible(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let browsingContext be this's relevant global object's browsing context.
        // SAFETY: The Window is live.
        let browsing_context = unsafe { web_html_bar_prop_window_browsing_context(self.window.as_ptr()) };

        // 2. If browsingContext is null, then return true.
        if browsing_context.is_null() {
            return Ok(true);
        }

        // 3. Return the negation of browsingContext's top-level browsing context's is popup.
        // SAFETY: The browsing context is live.
        Ok(!unsafe { web_html_bar_prop_top_level_browsing_context_is_popup(browsing_context) })
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_bar_prop_create(vm: &Vm, window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>) -> *mut c_void {
    let window = CppWindow::from_lent(window);
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| BarProp { window }))
}

//! BeforeUnloadEvent, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#the-beforeunloadevent-interface

use core::cell::RefCell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::event_target::CppEvent;
use crate::bindings::interface::{InterfaceCell, Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::lent_string::{LentUtf16FlyString, LentUtf16String};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#beforeunloadevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct BeforeUnloadEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    return_value: RefCell<Utf16String>,
}

impl Wrappable for BeforeUnloadEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl BeforeUnloadEvent {
    fn create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, event_name: &Utf16String, event_init: &EventInit) -> Ref<BeforeUnloadEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.bubbles,
            event_init.cancelable,
            event_init.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| BeforeUnloadEvent {
            event,
            return_value: RefCell::new(Utf16String::from_utf8("")),
        });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#dom-beforeunloadevent-returnvalue
    pub(crate) fn return_value(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.return_value.borrow().clone())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#dom-beforeunloadevent-returnvalue
    pub(crate) fn set_return_value(&self, _: &mut CallContext, return_value: Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        *self.return_value.borrow_mut() = return_value;
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The Event of a new trusted BeforeUnloadEvent in the realm, for the implementation to fire.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_before_unload_event_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    r#type: LentUtf16FlyString<'_>,
    bubbles: bool,
    cancelable: bool,
    composed: bool,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let event_init = EventInit {
        bubbles,
        cancelable,
        composed,
    };
    let r#type: Utf16String = r#type.to_utf16_fly_string().into();
    let event = BeforeUnloadEvent::create(vm, realm, &r#type, &event_init);
    event.event().as_ptr()
}

/// The Event of a new BeforeUnloadEvent in the realm whose type is the empty string, for createEvent().
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_before_unload_event_create_for_create_event(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> *mut c_void {
    let event_init = EventInit {
        bubbles: false,
        cancelable: false,
        composed: false,
    };
    BeforeUnloadEvent::create(vm, realm, &Utf16String::from_utf8(""), &event_init)
        .event()
        .as_ptr()
}

/// The returnValue of the BeforeUnloadEvent, which the caller adopts.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_before_unload_event_return_value(event: &InterfaceCell) -> usize {
    let event = event.implementation::<BeforeUnloadEvent>();
    event.return_value.borrow().clone().into_raw()
}

/// Sets the returnValue of the BeforeUnloadEvent.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_before_unload_event_set_return_value(
    event: &InterfaceCell,
    return_value: LentUtf16String<'_>,
) {
    let event = event.implementation::<BeforeUnloadEvent>();
    *event.return_value.borrow_mut() = return_value.to_utf16_string();
}

//! BroadcastChannel, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html#broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
use core::ffi::{c_int, c_void};
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;

use liburl_rust::FfiOrigin;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_html_broadcast_channel_relevant_settings_object_origin(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        ctx: *mut c_void,
        on_origin: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const FfiOrigin),
    );
    fn web_html_broadcast_channel_set_strongly_referenced(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        event_target: *mut c_void,

/// A message that a BroadcastChannel posted, in this agent or in another process: what the tasks that steps 6 to 9 of
/// postMessage() queue read.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct BroadcastChannelMessage {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) storage_key: StorageKey,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) channel_name: Utf16String,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) source_origin: Origin,
    pub(crate) serialized: MessageRecord,
}

pub(crate) static BROADCAST_CHANNEL_MESSAGE_CLASS: EmbedderClass<BroadcastChannelMessage> =
    EmbedderClass::new("BroadcastChannelMessage");

impl EmbedderValue for BroadcastChannelMessage {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &BROADCAST_CHANNEL_MESSAGE_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type BroadcastChannelMessageRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<BroadcastChannelMessage>>;

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html#broadcastchannel
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct BroadcastChannel {
    event_target: CppEventTarget,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,

    // A BroadcastChannel object has a channel name and a closed flag.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    channel_name: Utf16String,
    closed_flag: Cell<bool>,

    #[gc(untraced)]
    origin: Origin,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    storage_key: StorageKey,
}

impl Wrappable for BroadcastChannel {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.realm)
    }

    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event_target.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for BroadcastChannel {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
}

impl EventListenerListChanged for BroadcastChannel {
    fn event_listener_list_changed(this: Ref<Self>) {
        this.update_strong_reference_from_relevant_global_object();
    }
}

/// The channels of the thread's agent, in creation order: references that do not keep them alive, which a collected
/// channel leaves empty. The empty ones are pruned once the list has grown to twice what was live after the last
/// pruning.
struct BroadcastChannels {
    channels: Vec<GcWeak<EmbedderCell<Wrapped<BroadcastChannel>>>>,
    live_after_pruning: usize,
}

impl BroadcastChannels {
    const CHANNELS_BEFORE_FIRST_PRUNING: usize = 128;

    fn add(&mut self, vm: &Vm, channel: Ref<BroadcastChannel>) {
        if self.channels.len() >= (2 * self.live_after_pruning).max(Self::CHANNELS_BEFORE_FIRST_PRUNING) {
            self.channels.retain(|channel| channel.get().is_some());
            self.live_after_pruning = self.channels.len();
        }
        self.channels.push(GcWeak::new(vm.heap(), channel));
    }
}

thread_local! {
    static BROADCAST_CHANNELS: RefCell<BroadcastChannels> = const {
        RefCell::new(BroadcastChannels {
            channels: Vec::new(),
            live_after_pruning: 0,
        })
    };
}

/// Forgets the channels of the thread's agent, whose references into its heap have to go before the heap does.
pub(crate) fn forget_broadcast_channels_of_agent() {
    BROADCAST_CHANNELS.with_borrow_mut(|channels| {
        channels.channels.clear();
        channels.live_after_pruning = 0;
    });
}

fn relevant_settings_object_origin(realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Origin {
    unsafe extern "C" fn on_origin(ctx: *mut c_void, ffi_origin: *const FfiOrigin) {
        // SAFETY: ctx is the origin below, and LibWeb lends the origin for the call.
        unsafe { *ctx.cast::<Option<Origin>>() = Some((*ffi_origin).to_origin()) };
    }

    let mut origin: Option<Origin> = None;
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the origin outlives the call.
    unsafe {
        web_html_broadcast_channel_relevant_settings_object_origin(
            realm.as_ptr().cast(),
            (&raw mut origin).cast(),
            on_origin,
        );
    }
    origin.expect("LibWeb lends the origin")
}

impl BroadcastChannel {
    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html#dom-broadcastchannel
    pub(crate) fn construct(cx: &mut CallContext, name: Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let realm = cx.realm();
        let channel = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            event_target: CppEventTarget::new(),
            realm,
            // 1. Set this's channel name to name.
            channel_name: name,
            // 2. Set this's closed flag to false.
            closed_flag: Cell::new(false),
            origin: relevant_settings_object_origin(realm),
            storage_key: obtain_a_storage_key_for_non_storage_purposes(&relevant_settings_object(
                realm.global_object(),
            )),
        });
        channel.event_target.set_owner(channel);
        channel.event_target.set_event_listener_list_changed_steps::<Self>();
        BROADCAST_CHANNELS.with_borrow_mut(|channels| channels.add(vm, channel));
        Ok(channel)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html#dom-broadcastchannel-name
    pub(crate) fn name(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The name getter steps are to return this's channel name.
        Ok(self.channel_name.clone())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html#eligible-for-messaging
    fn is_eligible_for_messaging(&self) -> bool {
        // A BroadcastChannel object is said to be eligible for messaging when its relevant global object is either:
        let relevant_global_object = relevant_global_object(self);

        // * a Window object whose associated Document is fully active, or
        if let Some(window) = window_from_global_object(relevant_global_object) {
            return window.associated_document().is_fully_active();
        }

        // * a WorkerGlobalScope object whose closing flag is false and is not suspendable.
        // FIXME: Suspendable worker
        if let Some(worker_global_scope) = worker_global_scope_from_global_object(relevant_global_object) {
            return !worker_global_scope.is_closing();
        }

        false
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html#broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts
    fn update_strong_reference_from_relevant_global_object(&self) {
        // While a BroadcastChannel object whose closed flag is false has an event listener registered for message or
        // messageerror events, there must be a strong reference from the BroadcastChannel object's relevant global object
        // to the BroadcastChannel object itself.
        let strongly_referenced = !self.closed_flag.get()
            && (self.event_target.has_event_listener("message")
                || self.event_target.has_event_listener("messageerror"));
        // SAFETY: The realm and the EventTarget are live.
        unsafe {
            web_html_broadcast_channel_set_strongly_referenced(
                self.realm.as_ptr().cast(),
                self.event_target.as_ptr(),
                strongly_referenced,
            );
        }
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html#dom-broadcastchannel-postmessage
    pub(crate) fn post_message(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext, message: Value) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If this is not eligible for messaging, then return.
        if !this.is_eligible_for_messaging() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. If this's closed flag is true, then throw an "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
        if this.closed_flag.get() {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidStateError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"BroadcastChannel.postMessage() on a closed channel"),
            ));
        }

        // 3. Let serialized be StructuredSerialize(message). Rethrow any exceptions.
        // AD-HOC: This message reaches agents through the browser process, also those in this process, which then reference
        //         the same [[ArrayBufferData]] rather than a copy.
        let serialized = structured_serialize_for_message(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), message)?;

        // 4. Let sourceOrigin be this's relevant settings object's origin.
        let source_origin = this.origin.clone();

        // 5. Let sourceStorageKey be the result of running obtain a storage key for non-storage purposes with this's relevant settings object.
        let source_storage_key = this.storage_key.clone();

        let message = BROADCAST_CHANNEL_MESSAGE_CLASS.allocate(cx.vm(), |defer_gc| BroadcastChannelMessage {
            storage_key: source_storage_key,
            channel_name: this.channel_name.clone(),
            source_origin,
            serialized: serialized.finish_message_record(defer_gc),
        });

        // Steps 6-9.
        Self::deliver_message_locally(cx.vm(), message, Some(*this));

        // SAFETY: The realm is live, the name and the bytes are lent for the call, and the call takes over the
        //         duplicated descriptor.
        unsafe {
            web_html_broadcast_channel_post_message_to_other_processes(
                this.realm.as_ptr().cast(),
                message.channel_name.raw_identity(),
                ak::Span::new(&message.serialized.bytes),
                message.serialized.duplicate_shared_store_lifeline(),
            );
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html#dom-broadcastchannel-postmessage
    pub(crate) fn deliver_message_locally(vm: &Vm, message: BroadcastChannelMessageRef, source: Option<Ref<Self>>) {
        // 6. Let destinations be a list of BroadcastChannel objects that match the following criteria:
        //    * They are eligible for messaging.
        //    * The result of running obtain a storage key for non-storage purposes with their relevant settings object equals sourceStorageKey.
        //    * Their channel name is this's channel name.
        // 7. Remove source from destinations.
        let destinations = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        BROADCAST_CHANNELS.with_borrow(|channels| {
            for channel in channels.channels.iter().filter_map(GcWeak::get) {
                if Some(channel) != source
                    && channel.is_eligible_for_messaging()
                    && channel.storage_key == message.storage_key
                    && channel.channel_name == message.channel_name
                {
                    destinations.push(channel);
                }
            }
        });

        // 8. Sort destinations such that all BroadcastChannel objects whose relevant agents are the same are sorted in creation order, oldest first.
        //    (This does not define a complete ordering. Within this constraint, user agents may sort the list in any implementation-defined manner.)
        // NB: The channels of the thread's agent are listed in creation order, so destinations already are.

        // 9. For each destination in destinations, queue a global task on the DOM manipulation task source given destination's relevant global object to perform the following steps:
        for destination in destinations.values().iter() {
            queue_a_global_task(
                vm,
                destination.realm.global_object(),
                TaskSource::DOMManipulation,
                (*destination, message),
                |vm, (destination, message)| Self::message_task_steps(destination, vm, &message),
            );
        }
    }

    fn message_task_steps(destination: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm, message: &BroadcastChannelMessage) {
        // 1. If destination's closed flag is true, then abort these steps.
        if destination.closed_flag.get() {
            return;
        }

        // 2. Let targetRealm be destination's relevant realm.
        let target_realm = destination.realm;
        let cx = CallContext::new(vm, target_realm);

        // 3. Let data be StructuredDeserialize(serialized, targetRealm).
        let data = structured_deserialize_message(&cx, &message.serialized);
        let Ok(data) = data else {
            //    If this throws an exception, catch it, fire an event named messageerror at destination, using MessageEvent, with its
            //    origin initialized to sourceOrigin, and then abort these steps.
            let event = MessageEvent::create(
                vm,
                target_realm,
                &Utf16String::from_utf8("messageerror"),
                MessageEventInit::new(vm),
                Some(message.source_origin.clone()),
            );
            destination.event_target.dispatch_event(event.event());
            return;
        };

        // 4. Fire an event named message at destination, using MessageEvent, with the data attribute initialized to data and
        //    its origin initialized to sourceOrigin.
        let mut event_init = MessageEventInit::new(vm);
        event_init.data = data;
        let event = MessageEvent::create(
            vm,
            target_realm,
            &Utf16String::from_utf8("message"),
            event_init,
            Some(message.source_origin.clone()),
        );
        destination.event_target.dispatch_event(event.event());
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-messaging.html#dom-broadcastchannel-close
    pub(crate) fn close(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The close() method steps are to set this's closed flag to true.
        self.closed_flag.set(true);

        self.update_strong_reference_from_relevant_global_object();
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvascompositing

use ak::Utf16String;

use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::canvas_2d::context::{CanvasKind, RenderingContext2D};
use crate::canvas_2d::drawing_state::{composite_operation_name, composite_operation_named};
use crate::canvas_2d::float;

impl<K: CanvasKind> RenderingContext2D<K> {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-globalalpha
    pub(crate) fn global_alpha(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(f64::from(self.drawing_state().global_alpha))
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-globalalpha
    pub(crate) fn set_global_alpha(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, alpha: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let alpha = float(alpha);
        // 1. If the given value is either infinite, NaN, or not in the range 0.0 to 1.0, then return.
        if !alpha.is_finite() || !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&alpha) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // 2. Otherwise, set this's global alpha to the given value.
        self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).global_alpha = alpha;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-globalcompositeoperation
    pub(crate) fn global_composite_operation(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        let operator = self.drawing_state().current_compositing_and_blending_operator;
        Ok(Utf16String::from_ascii(composite_operation_name(operator).as_bytes()))
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-globalcompositeoperation
    pub(crate) fn set_global_composite_operation(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        global_composite_operation: Utf16String,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If the given value is not identical to any of the values that the <blend-mode> or the <composite-mode>
        //    properties are defined to take, then return.
        // 2. Otherwise, set this's current compositing and blending operator to the given value.
        if let Some(operator) = composite_operation_named(&global_composite_operation) {
            self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm())
                .current_compositing_and_blending_operator = operator;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvasdrawimage

use ak::Utf16String;
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::commands::CanvasId;
use libgfx_rust::image_frame::ImageFrameHandle;
use libgfx_rust::{AffineTransform, FloatRect, IntSize, ScalingMode};

use super::image_bitmap::ImageBitmap;
use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::canvas_2d::canvas::{CanvasImageSourceKind, Usability, capture_video_frame};
use crate::canvas_2d::context::{CanvasKind, ContextState, RenderingContext2D};
use crate::canvas_2d::float;

/// The union CanvasImageSource of HTML/Canvas/CanvasDrawImage.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum CanvasImageSource {
    HTMLImageElement(CppInterface),
    SVGImageElement(CppInterface),
    HTMLVideoElement(CppInterface),
    HTMLCanvasElement(CppInterface),
    ImageBitmap(Ref<ImageBitmap>),
    OffscreenCanvas(CppInterface),
}

impl CanvasImageSource {
    /// The source and its kind, if it is implemented in C++.
    fn cpp_source(self) -> Option<(CppInterface, CanvasImageSourceKind)> {
        match self {
            Self::HTMLImageElement(source) => Some((source, CanvasImageSourceKind::HTMLImageElement)),
            Self::SVGImageElement(source) => Some((source, CanvasImageSourceKind::SVGImageElement)),
            Self::HTMLVideoElement(source) => Some((source, CanvasImageSourceKind::HTMLVideoElement)),
            Self::HTMLCanvasElement(source) => Some((source, CanvasImageSourceKind::HTMLCanvasElement)),
            Self::OffscreenCanvas(source) => Some((source, CanvasImageSourceKind::OffscreenCanvas)),
            Self::ImageBitmap(_) => None,
        }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#check-the-usability-of-the-image-argument
    /// Whether the image is good, or an exception.
    pub(crate) fn check_usability(self) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        let usability = match self.cpp_source() {
            Some((source, kind)) => kind.check_usability(source),
            None => {
                let Self::ImageBitmap(image_bitmap) = self else {
                    unreachable!("an image source that is not implemented in C++ is an ImageBitmap");
                };
                // FIXME: VideoFrame
                if image_bitmap.is_detached() {
                    Usability::InvalidState(Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Image bitmap is detached"))
                } else {
                    Usability::Good
                }
            }
        };
        match usability {
            Usability::Good => Ok(true),
            Usability::Bad => Ok(false),
            Usability::InvalidState(message) => Err(Exception::Dom("InvalidStateError", message)),
        }
    }

    /// The width and the height of the image, as the operations that do not take its size use them. An image without a
    /// natural size is sized against the default object size, the size of the canvas it is drawn into.
    pub(crate) fn size(self, default_object_size: IntSize) -> (i32, i32) {
        match self.cpp_source() {
            Some((source, kind)) => kind.size(source, default_object_size),
            None => {
                let Self::ImageBitmap(image_bitmap) = self else {
                    unreachable!("an image source that is not implemented in C++ is an ImageBitmap");
                };
                match image_bitmap.frame() {
                    Some(frame) => (frame.width(), frame.height()),
                    None => (
                        i32::try_from(image_bitmap.width_of_bitmap()).unwrap_or(i32::MAX),
                        i32::try_from(image_bitmap.height_of_bitmap()).unwrap_or(i32::MAX),
                    ),
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#the-image-argument-is-not-origin-clean
    pub(crate) fn is_not_origin_clean(self) -> bool {
        match self.cpp_source() {
            Some((source, kind)) => kind.is_not_origin_clean(source),
            None => {
                let Self::ImageBitmap(image_bitmap) = self else {
                    unreachable!("an image source that is not implemented in C++ is an ImageBitmap");
                };
                // image's bitmap's origin-clean flag is false.
                !image_bitmap.origin_clean()
            }
        }
    }

    /// The frame of an image, a canvas or an ImageBitmap, if it has one. A canvas is read back for it, which flushes
    /// the commands of every canvas.
    pub(crate) fn frame(self) -> Option<ImageFrameHandle> {
        match self {
            Self::ImageBitmap(image_bitmap) => image_bitmap.frame(),
            Self::HTMLVideoElement(_) => unreachable!("a video is drawn by its frames, which it holds"),
            _ => {
                let (source, kind) = self.cpp_source().expect("the image source is implemented in C++");
                kind.frame(source)
            }
        }
    }

    /// The frame to paint the source rectangle of the image from, and that rectangle in the frame's pixels. A vector
    /// image is rasterized at the size it is painted at, so that it stays sharp when it is scaled up.
    fn frame_for_painting(
        self,
        source_rect: FloatRect,
        destination_rect: FloatRect,
        transform: AffineTransform,
        canvas_size: IntSize,
    ) -> Option<(ImageFrameHandle, FloatRect)> {
        let (Self::HTMLImageElement(source) | Self::SVGImageElement(source)) = self else {
            return self.frame().map(|frame| (frame, source_rect));
        };
        let kind = self.cpp_source().expect("an image element is implemented in C++").1;
        let (natural_width, natural_height) = kind.size(source, canvas_size);
        if natural_width <= 0 || natural_height <= 0 {
            return kind.frame(source).map(|frame| (frame, source_rect));
        }
        let scale_x = destination_rect.width / source_rect.width * transform.x_scale();
        let scale_y = destination_rect.height / source_rect.height * transform.y_scale();
        if scale_x <= 1.0 && scale_y <= 1.0 {
            // A vector image without a natural size has no frame of its own, so it's rasterized at the size it's drawn
            // from.
            return kind
                .frame_rasterized_at(source, natural_width, natural_height)
                .map(|(frame, _)| (frame, source_rect));
        }

        // The image is rasterized at one scale in both directions, as the vector image would be fitted into a raster of
        // another aspect ratio rather than stretched. The raster is capped at the canvas's size, so that painting a
        // small part of an image enlarged can't allocate a raster much larger than the canvas.
        let scale = scale_x
            .max(scale_y)
            .min(canvas_size.width.max(natural_width) as f32 / natural_width as f32)
            .min(canvas_size.height.max(natural_height) as f32 / natural_height as f32);
        let raster_width = (natural_width as f32 * scale).ceil() as i32;
        let raster_height = (natural_height as f32 * scale).ceil() as i32;
        let (frame, rasterized) = kind.frame_rasterized_at(source, raster_width, raster_height)?;
        if !rasterized {
            return Some((frame, source_rect));
        }

        let frame_scale_x = frame.width() as f32 / natural_width as f32;
        let frame_scale_y = frame.height() as f32 / natural_height as f32;
        let frame_source_rect = FloatRect::new(
            source_rect.x * frame_scale_x,
            source_rect.y * frame_scale_y,
            source_rect.width * frame_scale_x,
            source_rect.height * frame_scale_y,
        );
        Some((frame, frame_source_rect))
    }
}

impl ContextState {
    /// 4.12.5.1.15 Drawing images, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#drawing-images
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the arguments of drawImage()")]
    pub(crate) fn draw_image_internal(
        &self,
        image: CanvasImageSource,
        mut source_x: f32,
        mut source_y: f32,
        mut source_width: f32,
        mut source_height: f32,
        mut destination_x: f32,
        mut destination_y: f32,
        mut destination_width: f32,
        mut destination_height: f32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
        let arguments = [
            source_x,
            source_y,
            source_width,
            source_height,
            destination_x,
            destination_y,
            destination_width,
            destination_height,
        ];
        if !arguments.iter().all(|argument| argument.is_finite()) {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Let usability be the result of checking the usability of image.
        // 3. If usability is bad, then return (without drawing anything).
        if !image.check_usability()? {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 4. Establish the source and destination rectangles as follows:
        //    If not specified, the dw and dh arguments must default to the values of sw and sh, interpreted such that
        //    one CSS pixel in the image is treated as one unit in the output bitmap's coordinate space.
        //    If the sx, sy, sw, and sh arguments are omitted, then they must default to 0, 0, the image's natural
        //    width in image pixels, and the image's natural height in image pixels, respectively.
        //    If the image has no natural dimensions, then the concrete object size must be used instead, as
        //    determined using the CSS "Concrete Object Size Resolution" algorithm, with the specified size having
        //    neither a definite width nor height, nor any additional constraints, the object's natural properties
        //    being those of the image argument, and the default object size being the size of the output bitmap.
        // NOTE: Implemented in drawImage() overloads
        if source_width < 0.0 {
            source_x += source_width;
            source_width = source_width.abs();
        }
        if source_height < 0.0 {
            source_y += source_height;
            source_height = source_height.abs();
        }
        if destination_width < 0.0 {
            destination_x += destination_width;
            destination_width = destination_width.abs();
        }
        if destination_height < 0.0 {
            destination_y += destination_height;
            destination_height = destination_height.abs();
        }

        //    The source rectangle is the rectangle whose corners are the four points (sx, sy), (sx+sw, sy),
        //    (sx+sw, sy+sh), (sx, sy+sh).
        let source_rect = FloatRect::new(source_x, source_y, source_width, source_height);
        //    The destination rectangle is the rectangle whose corners are the four points (dx, dy), (dx+dw, dy),
        //    (dx+dw, dy+dh), (dx, dy+dh).
        let destination_rect = FloatRect::new(destination_x, destination_y, destination_width, destination_height);
        // FIXME: When the source rectangle is outside the source image, the source rectangle must be clipped to the
        //        source image and the destination rectangle must be clipped in the same proportion.

        // 5. If one of the sw or sh arguments is zero, then return. Nothing is painted.
        if source_width == 0.0 || source_height == 0.0 {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 6. Paint the region of the image argument specified by the source rectangle on the region of the rendering
        //    context's output bitmap specified by the destination rectangle, after applying the current
        //    transformation matrix to the destination rectangle.
        let scaling_mode = if self.drawing_state().image_smoothing_enabled {
            // FIXME: Honor the image smoothing quality.
            ScalingMode::BilinearMipmap
        } else {
            ScalingMode::NearestNeighbor
        };

        // 7. If image is not origin-clean, then set the CanvasRenderingContext2D's origin-clean flag to false.
        let update_origin_clean = || {
            if image.is_not_origin_clean() {
                self.set_origin_clean(false);
            }
        };

        // A canvas is drawn by its id. A 2D source needs no eager synchronization: its recorded commands precede this
        // DrawCanvas in the shared ordered stream, so the replay sees them by construction. WebGL frames are presented
        // by a separate message and the source's registry surface is its live drawing buffer, so the source is
        // presented now and the DrawCanvas is flushed right after it, before a later WebGL frame can overtake the
        // reference.
        if let CanvasImageSource::HTMLCanvasElement(source) | CanvasImageSource::OffscreenCanvas(source) = image {
            let kind = image.cpp_source().expect("a canvas is implemented in C++").1;
            if let Some((source_canvas_id, source_is_2d)) = kind.canvas_id(source) {
                if self.recorder_is_ready() {
                    let state = self.drawing_state();
                    self.record(|recorder| {
                        recorder.draw_canvas(
                            CanvasId(source_canvas_id),
                            destination_rect,
                            source_rect,
                            scaling_mode,
                            &Self::compositing(&state),
                        );
                    });
                    drop(state);
                    self.did_draw();
                    if !source_is_2d {
                        self.record(|recorder| recorder.flush());
                    }
                }
                update_origin_clean();
                return Ok(());
            }
        }

        if let CanvasImageSource::HTMLVideoElement(video) = image {
            let Some(captured_frame) = capture_video_frame(video) else {
                return Ok(());
            };
            if self.recorder_is_ready() {
                let state = self.drawing_state();
                self.record(|recorder| {
                    recorder.draw_video_frame(
                        &captured_frame.hold,
                        captured_frame.sink_handle,
                        captured_frame.generation,
                        destination_rect,
                        source_rect,
                        scaling_mode,
                        &Self::compositing(&state),
                    );
                });
                drop(state);
                self.did_draw();
            }
            update_origin_clean();
            return Ok(());
        }

        let transform = self.drawing_state().transform;
        let Some((frame, source_rect)) =
            image.frame_for_painting(source_rect, destination_rect, transform, self.size())
        else {
            return Ok(());
        };

        // NOTE: Reading a canvas back for its frame may flush the shared command stream, so the recorder is readied
        //       only afterwards.
        if self.recorder_is_ready() {
            let state = self.drawing_state();
            self.record(|recorder| {
                recorder.draw_image_frame(
                    &frame,
                    destination_rect,
                    source_rect,
                    scaling_mode,
                    &Self::compositing(&state),
                );
            });
            drop(state);
            self.did_draw();
        }

        // 7. If image is not origin-clean, then set the CanvasRenderingContext2D's origin-clean flag to false.
        update_origin_clean();

        Ok(())
    }
}

impl<K: CanvasKind> RenderingContext2D<K> {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-drawimage
    pub(crate) fn draw_image(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        image: CanvasImageSource,
        dx: f64,
        dy: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // If not specified, the dw and dh arguments must default to the values of sw and sh, interpreted such that one
        // CSS pixel in the image is treated as one unit in the output bitmap's coordinate space.
        // If the sx, sy, sw, and sh arguments are omitted, then they must default to 0, 0, the image's natural
        // width in image pixels, and the image's natural height in image pixels, respectively.
        let (dx, dy) = (float(dx), float(dy));
        let (width, height) = image.size(self.size());
        let (width, height) = (int_to_float(width), int_to_float(height));
        self.draw_image_internal(image, 0.0, 0.0, width, height, dx, dy, width, height)
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-drawimage
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the arguments of drawImage()")]
    pub(crate) fn draw_image_with_size(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        image: CanvasImageSource,
        dx: f64,
        dy: f64,
        dw: f64,
        dh: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // If the sx, sy, sw, and sh arguments are omitted, then they must default to 0, 0, the image's natural
        // width in image pixels, and the image's natural height in image pixels, respectively.
        let (dx, dy, dw, dh) = (float(dx), float(dy), float(dw), float(dh));
        let (width, height) = image.size(self.size());
        let (width, height) = (int_to_float(width), int_to_float(height));
        self.draw_image_internal(image, 0.0, 0.0, width, height, dx, dy, dw, dh)
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-drawimage
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the arguments of drawImage()")]
    pub(crate) fn draw_image_with_source_rectangle(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        image: CanvasImageSource,
        sx: f64,
        sy: f64,
        sw: f64,
        sh: f64,
        dx: f64,
        dy: f64,
        dw: f64,
        dh: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.draw_image_internal(
            image,
            float(sx),
            float(sy),
            float(sw),
            float(sh),
            float(dx),
            float(dy),
            float(dw),
            float(dh),
        )
    }
}

#[allow(
    clippy::cast_precision_loss,
    reason = "a size of an image becomes a float, as the C++ had it"
)]
fn int_to_float(value: i32) -> f32 {
    value as f32
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvasdrawpath

use libgfx_rust::path::{Path, StrokeStyle};
use libgfx_rust::{AffineTransform, FloatPoint, WindingRule};

use super::path2d::Path2D;
use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::canvas_2d::context::{CanvasKind, RenderingContext2D};
use crate::canvas_2d::drawing_state::DrawingState;
use crate::canvas_2d::float;

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvasfillrule
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum CanvasFillRule {
    Nonzero,
    Evenodd,
}

impl From<CanvasFillRule> for WindingRule {
    fn from(fill_rule: CanvasFillRule) -> Self {
        match fill_rule {
            CanvasFillRule::Nonzero => Self::Nonzero,
            CanvasFillRule::Evenodd => Self::EvenOdd,
        }
    }
}

/// The path of a Path2D, which nothing changes while a context draws with it, as no script runs meanwhile.
fn path_of(path: &Ref<Path2D>) -> &Path {
    // SAFETY: No script runs while the context uses the path.
    unsafe { path.path_unguarded() }
}

/// Whether the point, in the coordinates that the transform maps from, is inside the path.
fn is_point_in_path_internal(
    path: &Path,
    transform: AffineTransform,
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    fill_rule: CanvasFillRule,
) -> bool {
    // NB: A transform that is not invertible maps every path onto a line or a point, which has no inside.
    let Some(inverse_transform) = transform.inverse() else {
        return false;
    };
    let point = inverse_transform.map_point(FloatPoint {
        x: float(x),
        y: float(y),
    });
    path.contains(point.x, point.y, WindingRule::from(fill_rule))
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#is-point-in-stroke-steps
fn is_point_in_stroke_internal(path: &Path, state: &DrawingState, x: f64, y: f64) -> bool {
    // 1. If x or y are infinite or NaN, then return false.
    if !x.is_finite() || !y.is_finite() {
        return false;
    }

    // 2. If the point given by the x and y coordinates, when treated as coordinates in the canvas coordinate space
    //    unaffected by the current transformation, is inside the path that results from tracing the intended path for
    //    path, using the nonzero winding rule, and using context's line styles as set by its CanvasPathDrawingStyles
    //    mixin, then return true. Points on the resulting path must be considered to be inside the path.
    // 3. Return false.
    let stroke = path.stroke_to_fill(&StrokeStyle {
        thickness: state.line_width,
        cap_style: state.cap_style(),
        join_style: state.join_style(),
        miter_limit: state.miter_limit,
        dash_array: state.dash_array(),
        dash_offset: state.line_dash_offset,
    });
    is_point_in_path_internal(&stroke, state.transform, x, y, CanvasFillRule::Nonzero)
}

impl<K: CanvasKind> RenderingContext2D<K> {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-beginpath
    pub(crate) fn begin_path(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.clear_path();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-fill
    pub(crate) fn fill(&self, _: &mut CallContext, fill_rule: CanvasFillRule) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let path = self.path().clone();
        self.fill_internal(&path, fill_rule.into());
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-fill
    pub(crate) fn fill_path2d(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        path: Ref<Path2D>,
        fill_rule: CanvasFillRule,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.fill_internal(path_of(&path), fill_rule.into());
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-stroke
    pub(crate) fn stroke(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let path = self.path().clone();
        self.stroke_internal(&path);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-stroke
    pub(crate) fn stroke_path2d(&self, _: &mut CallContext, path: Ref<Path2D>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.stroke_internal(path_of(&path));
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-clip
    pub(crate) fn clip(&self, _: &mut CallContext, fill_rule: CanvasFillRule) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let path = self.path().clone();
        self.clip_internal(&path, fill_rule.into());
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-clip
    pub(crate) fn clip_path2d(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        path: Ref<Path2D>,
        fill_rule: CanvasFillRule,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.clip_internal(path_of(&path), fill_rule.into());
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-ispointinpath
    pub(crate) fn is_point_in_path(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
        fill_rule: CanvasFillRule,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        let transform = self.drawing_state().transform;
        Ok(is_point_in_path_internal(&self.path(), transform, x, y, fill_rule))
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-ispointinpath
    pub(crate) fn is_point_in_path2d(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        path: Ref<Path2D>,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
        fill_rule: CanvasFillRule,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        let transform = self.drawing_state().transform;
        Ok(is_point_in_path_internal(path_of(&path), transform, x, y, fill_rule))
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-ispointinstroke
    pub(crate) fn is_point_in_stroke(&self, _: &mut CallContext, x: f64, y: f64) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The isPointInStroke(x, y) method steps are to return the result of the is point in stroke steps given this,
        // null, x, and y.
        Ok(is_point_in_stroke_internal(&self.path(), &self.drawing_state(), x, y))
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-ispointinstroke-path
    pub(crate) fn is_point_in_stroke_path2d(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        path: Ref<Path2D>,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The isPointInStroke(path, x, y) method steps are to return the result of the is point in stroke steps given
        // this, path, x, and y.
        Ok(is_point_in_stroke_internal(path_of(&path), &self.drawing_state(), x, y))
    }
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvasfillstrokestyles

use ak::Utf16String;

use super::canvas_draw_image::CanvasImageSource;
use super::canvas_gradient::CanvasGradient;
use super::canvas_pattern::CanvasPattern;
use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::canvas_2d::context::{CanvasKind, RenderingContext2D};
use crate::canvas_2d::drawing_state::{FillOrStrokeStyle, serialize_color};

/// The union (DOMString or CanvasGradient or CanvasPattern) of HTML/Canvas/CanvasFillStrokeStyles.idl, the value of
/// fillStyle and strokeStyle, whose members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) enum DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern {
    DOMString(Utf16String),
    CanvasGradient(Ref<CanvasGradient>),
    CanvasPattern(Ref<CanvasPattern>),
}

impl From<FillOrStrokeStyle> for DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern {
    fn from(style: FillOrStrokeStyle) -> Self {
        match style {
            FillOrStrokeStyle::Color(color) => Self::DOMString(serialize_color(color.srgb)),
            FillOrStrokeStyle::Gradient(gradient) => Self::CanvasGradient(gradient),
            FillOrStrokeStyle::Pattern(pattern) => Self::CanvasPattern(pattern),
        }
    }
}

impl<K: CanvasKind> RenderingContext2D<K> {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-strokestyle
    pub(crate) fn stroke_style(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern> {
        Ok(self.drawing_state().stroke_style.into())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-strokestyle
    pub(crate) fn set_stroke_style(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        style: DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let style = match style {
            // 1. If the given value is a string:
            DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern::DOMString(string) => {
                // 1. Let context be this's canvas attribute's value, if that is an element; otherwise null.

                // 2. Let parsedValue be the result of parsing the given value with context if non-null.
                // 3. If parsedValue is failure, then return.
                let Some(parsed_value) = self.parse_a_css_color_value(&string) else {
                    return Ok(());
                };

                // 4. Set this's stroke style to parsedValue.
                self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).stroke_style = FillOrStrokeStyle::Color(parsed_value);

                // 5. Return.
                return Ok(());
            }
            DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern::CanvasGradient(gradient) => FillOrStrokeStyle::Gradient(gradient),
            DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern::CanvasPattern(pattern) => {
                // 2. If the given value is a CanvasPattern object that is marked as not origin-clean, then set this's
                //    origin-clean flag to false.
                if pattern.is_not_origin_clean() {
                    self.set_origin_clean(false);
                }
                FillOrStrokeStyle::Pattern(pattern)
            }
        };

        // 3. Set this's stroke style to the given value.
        self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).stroke_style = style;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-fillstyle
    pub(crate) fn fill_style(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern> {
        Ok(self.drawing_state().fill_style.into())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-fillstyle
    pub(crate) fn set_fill_style(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        style: DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let style = match style {
            // 1. If the given value is a string:
            DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern::DOMString(string) => {
                // 1. Let context be this's canvas attribute's value, if that is an element; otherwise null.

                // 2. Let parsedValue be the result of parsing the given value with context if non-null.
                // 3. If parsedValue is failure, then return.
                let Some(parsed_value) = self.parse_a_css_color_value(&string) else {
                    return Ok(());
                };

                // 4. Set this's fill style to parsedValue.
                self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).fill_style = FillOrStrokeStyle::Color(parsed_value);

                // 5. Return.
                return Ok(());
            }
            DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern::CanvasGradient(gradient) => FillOrStrokeStyle::Gradient(gradient),
            DOMStringOrCanvasGradientOrCanvasPattern::CanvasPattern(pattern) => {
                // 2. If the given value is a CanvasPattern object that is marked as not origin-clean, then set this's
                //    origin-clean flag to false.
                if pattern.is_not_origin_clean() {
                    self.set_origin_clean(false);
                }
                FillOrStrokeStyle::Pattern(pattern)
            }
        };

        // 3. Set this's fill style to the given value.
        self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).fill_style = style;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createlineargradient
    pub(crate) fn create_linear_gradient(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        x0: f64,
        y0: f64,
        x1: f64,
        y1: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<CanvasGradient>> {
        Ok(CanvasGradient::create_linear(cx.vm(), x0, y0, x1, y1))
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createradialgradient
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the arguments of createRadialGradient()")]
    pub(crate) fn create_radial_gradient(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        x0: f64,
        y0: f64,
        r0: f64,
        x1: f64,
        y1: f64,
        r1: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<CanvasGradient>> {
        // If either of r0 or r1 are negative, then an "IndexSizeError" DOMException must be thrown.
        if r0 < 0.0 {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"The r0 passed is less than 0",
            )));
        }
        if r1 < 0.0 {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"The r1 passed is less than 0",
            )));
        }
        Ok(CanvasGradient::create_radial(cx.vm(), x0, y0, r0, x1, y1, r1))
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createconicgradient
    pub(crate) fn create_conic_gradient(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        start_angle: f64,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<CanvasGradient>> {
        Ok(CanvasGradient::create_conic(cx.vm(), start_angle, x, y))
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createpattern
    pub(crate) fn create_pattern(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        image: CanvasImageSource,
        repetition: Utf16String,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<CanvasPattern>>> {
        CanvasPattern::create_for_image(cx.vm(), &image, &repetition, self.context_attributes.color_space.into())
    }
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvasfilters

use std::rc::Rc;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libcompositing_rust::filter_bytes::filter_functions_graph;
use libgfx_rust::filter::Filter;

use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::canvas_2d::context::{CanvasKind, RenderingContext2D};

impl<K: CanvasKind> RenderingContext2D<K> {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-filter
    pub(crate) fn filter(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self
            .drawing_state()
            .filter_string
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| Utf16String::from_ascii(b"none")))
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-filter
    pub(crate) fn set_filter(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, filter: Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).filter = None;

        // 1. If the given value is "none", then set this's current filter to "none" and return.
        if filter == Utf16String::from_ascii(b"none") {
            self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).filter_string = None;
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Let parsedValue be the result of parsing the given values as a <filter-value-list>. If any
        //    property-independent style sheet syntax like 'inherit' or 'initial' is present, then this parsing must
        //    return failure.
        // 3. If parsedValue is failure, then return.
        // NB: LibWeb's C++ parses the value and resolves its lengths and colors, and leaves out the references to SVG
        //     filters, which are not implemented.
        let Some(functions) = self.canvas_handle().parse_filter(&filter, self.font_metrics_source()) else {
            return Ok(());
        };

        // 4. Set this's current filter to the given value.
        let graph = filter_functions_graph(functions.into_iter().map(Filter::from));
        let mut state = self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm());
        state.filter = graph.map(|graph| Rc::from(graph.serialize()));
        state.filter_string = Some(filter);
        Ok(())
    }
}
