//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvasgradient

use core::cell::RefCell;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::canvas_2d::{ColorStops, Paint};
use libgfx_rust::{Color, FloatPoint};
use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};

use super::color_stops::ColorStopList;
use super::predefined_color_space::PredefinedColorSpace;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// Parses the color as the CSS color value of a canvas without an element to resolve it against, which LibWeb's
    /// C++ does, and returns whether it is one. The color is given in each predefined color space, in the order of
    /// PredefinedColorSpace. The string is a borrowed AK::Utf16String.
    fn web_canvas_gradient_parse_color(color: usize, out_colors: *mut [Color; 4]) -> bool;
}

/// Where the colors of a gradient go, which the method of the context that created it decides. The points and the
/// radii are in the coordinates that a draw is transformed from.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum GradientGeometry {
    Linear {
        start_point: FloatPoint,
        end_point: FloatPoint,
    },
    Radial {
        start_center: FloatPoint,
        start_radius: f32,
        end_center: FloatPoint,
        end_radius: f32,
    },
    Conic {
        center: FloatPoint,
        start_angle: f32,
    },
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CanvasGradient {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    geometry: GradientGeometry,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    color_stops: RefCell<ColorStopList>,
}

impl Wrappable for CanvasGradient {}

#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    reason = "the gradient keeps its geometry in floats, as the C++ did"
)]
fn point(x: f64, y: f64) -> FloatPoint {
    FloatPoint {
        x: x as f32,
        y: y as f32,
    }
}

impl CanvasGradient {
    fn create(vm: &Vm, geometry: GradientGeometry) -> Ref<Self> {
        allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            geometry,
            color_stops: RefCell::new(ColorStopList::default()),
        })
    }

    /// The gradient of createLinearGradient(), https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createlineargradient
    pub(crate) fn create_linear(vm: &Vm, x0: f64, y0: f64, x1: f64, y1: f64) -> Ref<Self> {
        Self::create(
            vm,
            GradientGeometry::Linear {
                start_point: point(x0, y0),
                end_point: point(x1, y1),
            },
        )
    }

    /// The gradient of createRadialGradient(), whose radii the context has checked,
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createradialgradient
    #[allow(
        clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
        reason = "the gradient keeps its geometry in floats, as the C++ did"
    )]
    pub(crate) fn create_radial(vm: &Vm, x0: f64, y0: f64, r0: f64, x1: f64, y1: f64, r1: f64) -> Ref<Self> {
        Self::create(
            vm,
            GradientGeometry::Radial {
                start_center: point(x0, y0),
                start_radius: r0 as f32,
                end_center: point(x1, y1),
                end_radius: r1 as f32,
            },
        )
    }

    /// The gradient of createConicGradient(), https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createconicgradient
    #[allow(
        clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
        reason = "the gradient keeps its geometry in floats, as the C++ did"
    )]
    pub(crate) fn create_conic(vm: &Vm, start_angle: f64, x: f64, y: f64) -> Ref<Self> {
        Self::create(
            vm,
            GradientGeometry::Conic {
                center: point(x, y),
                start_angle: start_angle as f32,
            },
        )
    }

    /// Whether a draw with the gradient can change a pixel: whether one of its stops is not transparent.
    pub(crate) fn is_visible(&self) -> bool {
        self.color_stops
            .borrow()
            .colors(PredefinedColorSpace::Srgb)
            .iter()
            .any(|color| color.alpha() > 0)
    }

    /// The paint of a draw with the gradient in a context of the color space, which borrows the stops until the
    /// gradient changes.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Nothing may add a stop to the gradient while the paint is in use.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn paint_unguarded(&self, color_space: PredefinedColorSpace) -> Paint<'_> {
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the stops from changing while the paint borrows them.
        let color_stops = unsafe { self.color_stops.try_borrow_unguarded() }.expect("nothing adds a stop meanwhile");
        self.paint_with_color_stops(color_stops, color_space)
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#interpolation
    /// The color of the gradient at each stop is the color specified for that stop, converted to the context's color
    /// space.
    fn paint_with_color_stops<'a>(
        &self,
        color_stops: &'a ColorStopList,
        color_space: PredefinedColorSpace,
    ) -> Paint<'a> {
        let color_stops = ColorStops {
            colors: color_stops.colors(color_space),
            positions: color_stops.positions(),
        };
        match self.geometry {
            GradientGeometry::Linear { start_point, end_point } => Paint::LinearGradient {
                start_point,
                end_point,
                color_stops,
            },
            GradientGeometry::Radial {
                start_center,
                start_radius,
                end_center,
                end_radius,
            } => Paint::RadialGradient {
                start_center,
                start_radius,
                end_center,
                end_radius,
                color_stops,
            },
            GradientGeometry::Conic { center, start_angle } => Paint::ConicGradient {
                center,
                start_angle,
                color_stops,
            },
        }
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-canvasgradient-addcolorstop
    pub(crate) fn add_color_stop(&self, _: &mut CallContext, offset: f64, color: Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If the offset is less than 0 or greater than 1, then throw an "IndexSizeError" DOMException.
        if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&offset) {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"CanvasGradient color stop offset out of bounds",
            )));
        }

        // 2. Let parsed color be the result of parsing color.
        // https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value
        let mut parsed_color = [Color(0); 4];
        // SAFETY: The string is live for the call, and the colors are a local.
        let is_color = unsafe { web_canvas_gradient_parse_color(color.raw_identity(), &raw mut parsed_color) };

        // 3. If parsed color is failure, throw a "SyntaxError" DOMException.
        if !is_color {
            return Err(Exception::syntax_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"Could not parse color for CanvasGradient",
            )));
        }

        // 4. Place a new stop on the gradient, at offset offset relative to the whole gradient, and with the color
        //    parsed color.
        //    If multiple stops are added at the same offset on a gradient, then they must be placed in the order
        //    added, with the first one closest to the start of the gradient, and each subsequent one infinitesimally
        //    further along towards the end point (in effect causing all but the first and last stop added at each
        //    point to be ignored).
        #[allow(
            clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
            reason = "the gradient keeps its stops in floats, as the C++ did"
        )]
        self.color_stops.borrow_mut().add(offset as f32, parsed_color);

        Ok(())
    }
}

/*

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvasimagedata
//!
//! The rectangles of these operations are computed in 64 bits from the IDL longs that they take, so that no sum or
//! difference of them overflows, and every rectangle that reads or writes pixels is checked against the bounds of the
//! pixels it reads or writes.

use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::canvas_2d_recorder::AlphaType;
use libgfx_rust::{IntPoint, IntRect};
use libjs_rust::api::{ErrorKind, ErrorType};

use super::image_data::{ImageData, ImageDataSettings};
use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::canvas_2d::canvas::image_frame_from_pixels;
use crate::canvas_2d::context::{CanvasKind, ContextState, RenderingContext2D};

/// The size of a pixel of an ImageData and of a readback, whose pixels are RGBA8888.
const BYTES_PER_PIXEL: usize = 4;

/// The absolute magnitude of a size, with that of the smallest long, which a long cannot represent, being the largest.
fn absolute_magnitude(size: i32) -> u32 {
    if size == i32::MIN {
        i32::MAX.unsigned_abs()
    } else {
        size.unsigned_abs()
    }
}

fn index_size_error_for_zero_size() -> Exception {
    Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Width and height must not be zero"))
}

fn invalid_state_error(message: &[u8]) -> Exception {
    Exception::Dom("InvalidStateError", Utf16String::from_ascii(message))
}

/// A number of pixels or bytes that is known not to be negative.
fn to_usize(value: i64) -> usize {
    usize::try_from(value).expect("the number is not negative")
}

/// A coordinate or a size that is known to fit in an int.
fn to_i32(value: i64) -> i32 {
    i32::try_from(value).expect("the number fits in an int")
}

impl ContextState {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context2d-putimagedata-common
    /// The caller has readied the recorder.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the arguments of putImageData()")]
    fn put_pixels_from_an_image_data_onto_a_bitmap(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        image_data: Ref<ImageData>,
        dx: i32,
        dy: i32,
        dirty_x: i32,
        dirty_y: i32,
        dirty_width: i32,
        dirty_height: i32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let buffer be imageData's data attribute value's [[ViewedArrayBuffer]] internal slot.
        // 2. If IsDetachedBuffer(buffer) is true, then throw an "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
        if image_data.is_detached() {
            return Err(invalid_state_error(b"ImageData's underlying buffer is detached"));
        }

        let (width, height) = image_data.size();
        let (width, height) = (i64::from(width), i64::from(height));
        let (dx, dy) = (i64::from(dx), i64::from(dy));
        let (mut dirty_x, mut dirty_y) = (i64::from(dirty_x), i64::from(dirty_y));
        let (mut dirty_width, mut dirty_height) = (i64::from(dirty_width), i64::from(dirty_height));

        // 3. If dirtyWidth is negative, then let dirtyX be dirtyX+dirtyWidth, and let dirtyWidth be equal to the
        //    absolute magnitude of dirtyWidth.
        if dirty_width < 0 {
            dirty_x += dirty_width;
            dirty_width = -dirty_width;
        }
        // If dirtyHeight is negative, then let dirtyY be dirtyY+dirtyHeight, and let dirtyHeight be equal to the
        // absolute magnitude of dirtyHeight.
        if dirty_height < 0 {
            dirty_y += dirty_height;
            dirty_height = -dirty_height;
        }

        // 4. If dirtyX is negative, then let dirtyWidth be dirtyWidth+dirtyX, and let dirtyX be 0.
        if dirty_x < 0 {
            dirty_width += dirty_x;
            dirty_x = 0;
        }
        // If dirtyY is negative, then let dirtyHeight be dirtyHeight+dirtyY, and let dirtyY be 0.
        if dirty_y < 0 {
            dirty_height += dirty_y;
            dirty_y = 0;
        }

        // 5. If dirtyX+dirtyWidth is greater than the width attribute of the imageData argument, then let dirtyWidth
        //    be the value of that width attribute, minus the value of dirtyX.
        if dirty_x + dirty_width > width {
            dirty_width = width - dirty_x;
        }
        // If dirtyY+dirtyHeight is greater than the height attribute of the imageData argument, then let dirtyHeight
        // be the value of that height attribute, minus the value of dirtyY.
        if dirty_y + dirty_height > height {
            dirty_height = height - dirty_y;
        }

        // 6. If, after those changes, either dirtyWidth or dirtyHeight are negative or zero, then return without
        //    affecting any bitmaps.
        if dirty_width <= 0 || dirty_height <= 0 {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 7. For all integer values of x and y where dirtyX ≤ x < dirtyX+dirtyWidth and dirtyY ≤ y <
        //    dirtyY+dirtyHeight, set the pixel with coordinate (dx+x, dy+y) in bitmap to the color of the pixel at
        //    coordinate (x, y) in the imageData data structure's bitmap, converted from imageData's colorSpace to the
        //    color space of bitmap using 'relative-colorimetric' rendering intent.
        let Some(pixels) = image_data.pixels() else {
            return Err(invalid_state_error(
                b"ImageData's underlying buffer is detached or out-of-bounds",
            ));
        };
        // NB: A lost context, or a canvas without backing storage, has no bitmap to set pixels in.
        if !self.recorder_is_ready() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // NB: Only the pixels that land inside the output bitmap are set, so only those are copied. The source
        //     rectangle is also kept inside imageData here, whatever the steps above computed, before its pixels are
        //     read.
        let size = self.size();
        let source_left = dirty_x.max(-dx).max(0);
        let source_top = dirty_y.max(-dy).max(0);
        let source_right = (dirty_x + dirty_width).min(i64::from(size.width) - dx).min(width);
        let source_bottom = (dirty_y + dirty_height).min(i64::from(size.height) - dy).min(height);
        if source_left >= source_right || source_top >= source_bottom {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // NB: The destination rectangle is inside the output bitmap, so its coordinates fit in an int.
        let destination_rect = IntRect {
            x: to_i32(source_left + dx),
            y: to_i32(source_top + dy),
            width: to_i32(source_right - source_left),
            height: to_i32(source_bottom - source_top),
        };

        // NOTE: The ImageData buffer is mutable from script and the recorded draw is only serialized at flush time, so
        //       the dirty pixels are copied now. The copy is shareable, so that flushing to the Compositor passes the
        //       pixels by file descriptor instead of copying them again.
        let source_pitch = to_usize(width) * BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
        let first_row_offset = to_usize(source_top) * source_pitch + to_usize(source_left) * BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
        // SAFETY: The source rectangle is inside the width × height pixels of the ImageData, which pixels() vouched
        //         for, so its first pixel is too.
        let first_row = unsafe { NonNull::new_unchecked(pixels.as_ptr().add(first_row_offset)) };
        // SAFETY: The rows of the source rectangle are inside the pixels of the ImageData, and nothing runs script
        //         while they are copied.
        let Some(frame) = (unsafe {
            image_frame_from_pixels(
                first_row,
                source_pitch,
                destination_rect.width,
                destination_rect.height,
                image_data.predefined_color_space().into(),
            )
        }) else {
            return Err(cx
                .vm()
                .throw_completion::<()>(ErrorKind::InternalError, ErrorType::OutOfMemory, &[])
                .expect_err("throwing a completion throws")
                .into());
        };

        self.record(|recorder| {
            recorder.put_image_frame(
                &frame,
                IntPoint {
                    x: destination_rect.x,
                    y: destination_rect.y,
                },
            );
        });

        self.did_draw();

        Ok(())
    }
}

impl<K: CanvasKind> RenderingContext2D<K> {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createimagedata
    pub(crate) fn create_image_data(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        sw: i32,
        sh: i32,
        settings: ImageDataSettings,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<ImageData>> {
        // 1. If one or both of sw and sh are zero, then throw an "IndexSizeError" DOMException.
        if sw == 0 || sh == 0 {
            return Err(index_size_error_for_zero_size());
        }

        // 2. Let newImageData be a new ImageData object.
        // 3. Initialize newImageData given the absolute magnitude of sw, the absolute magnitude of sh, settings set to
        //    settings, and defaultColorSpace set to this's color space.
        // 4. Initialize the image data of newImageData to transparent black.
        // 5. Return newImageData.
        ImageData::create(
            cx,
            absolute_magnitude(sw),
            absolute_magnitude(sh),
            Some(&settings),
            Some(self.context_attributes.color_space),
        )
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createimagedata-imagedata
    pub(crate) fn create_image_data_from(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        image_data: Ref<ImageData>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<ImageData>> {
        // 1. Let newImageData be a new ImageData object.
        // 2. Initialize newImageData given the value of imageData's width attribute, the value of imageData's height
        //    attribute, and defaultColorSpace set to the value of imageData's colorSpace attribute.
        // 3. Initialize the image data of newImageData to transparent black.
        // 4. Return newImageData.
        let (width, height) = image_data.size();
        ImageData::create(cx, width, height, None, Some(image_data.predefined_color_space()))
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-getimagedata
    pub(crate) fn get_image_data(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        sx: i32,
        sy: i32,
        sw: i32,
        sh: i32,
        settings: ImageDataSettings,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<ImageData>> {
        // 1. If either the sw or sh arguments are zero, then throw an "IndexSizeError" DOMException.
        if sw == 0 || sh == 0 {
            return Err(index_size_error_for_zero_size());
        }

        // 2. If the CanvasRenderingContext2D's origin-clean flag is set to false, then throw a "SecurityError"
        //    DOMException.
        if !self.origin_clean() {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "SecurityError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"CanvasRenderingContext2D is not origin-clean"),
            ));
        }

        // ImageData initialization requires positive width and height
        // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/imagebitmap-and-animations.html#initialize-an-imagedata-object
        let (width, height) = (absolute_magnitude(sw), absolute_magnitude(sh));

        // 3. Let imageData be a new ImageData object.
        // 4. Initialize imageData given sw, sh, settings set to settings, and defaultColorSpace set to this's color
        //    space.
        let image_data = ImageData::create(
            cx,
            width,
            height,
            Some(&settings),
            Some(self.context_attributes.color_space),
        )?;

        // 5. Let the source rectangle be the rectangle whose corners are the four points (sx, sy), (sx+sw, sy),
        //    (sx+sw, sy+sh), (sx, sy+sh).
        // NOTE: The spec doesn't seem to define this behavior, but MDN does and the WPT tests assume it works this
        //       way. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/getImageData#sw
        let source_x = i64::from(sx) + i64::from(sw.min(0));
        let source_y = i64::from(sy) + i64::from(sh.min(0));
        let size = self.size();
        let left = source_x.max(0);
        let top = source_y.max(0);
        let right = (source_x + i64::from(width)).min(i64::from(size.width));
        let bottom = (source_y + i64::from(height)).min(i64::from(size.height));
        if left >= right || top >= bottom {
            return Ok(image_data);
        }
        let readback_rect = IntRect {
            x: to_i32(left),
            y: to_i32(top),
            width: to_i32(right - left),
            height: to_i32(bottom - top),
        };

        // NOTE: If reading back from the Compositor fails (no backing storage or no connection), it's like copying
        //       only transparent black pixels (which is a no-op).
        // NOTE: Internally we must use premultiplied alpha, but ImageData should hold unpremultiplied alpha. This
        //       conversion might result in a loss of precision, but is according to spec.
        //       See: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#premultiplied-alpha-and-the-2d-rendering-context
        // NB: The readback converts the pixels to the color space of imageData, which step 6 does below.
        let Some(readback) = self.read_pixels(
            readback_rect,
            AlphaType::Unpremultiplied,
            image_data.predefined_color_space().into(),
        ) else {
            return Ok(image_data);
        };

        // 6. Set the pixel values of imageData to be the pixels of this's output bitmap in the area specified by the
        //    source rectangle in the bitmap's coordinate space units, converted from this's color space to imageData's
        //    colorSpace using 'relative-colorimetric' rendering intent.
        // NB: The pixels of imageData are RGBA8888 and unpremultiplied.
        if !readback.has_unpremultiplied_rgba8888_pixels() {
            return Ok(image_data);
        }
        if readback.width() != readback_rect.width || readback.height() != readback_rect.height {
            return Ok(image_data);
        }
        let image_data_pixels = image_data.pixels().expect("a new ImageData has room for its pixels");

        // The readback only covers the part of the source rectangle that is inside the output bitmap.
        let destination_x = to_usize(left - source_x);
        let destination_y = to_usize(top - source_y);
        let destination_pitch = width as usize * BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
        let row_size = to_usize(i64::from(readback_rect.width)) * BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
        let rows = to_usize(i64::from(readback_rect.height));
        assert!(destination_x * BYTES_PER_PIXEL + row_size <= destination_pitch);
        assert!(destination_y + rows <= height as usize);
        assert!(row_size <= readback.pitch());
        for row in 0..rows {
            // SAFETY: The row is inside both the readback and the pixels of the new ImageData, as asserted above, and
            //         the two do not overlap.
            unsafe {
                let source = readback.pixels().as_ptr().add(row * readback.pitch());
                let destination = image_data_pixels
                    .as_ptr()
                    .add((destination_y + row) * destination_pitch + destination_x * BYTES_PER_PIXEL);
                core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(source, destination, row_size);
            }
        }

        // 7. Set the pixels values of imageData for areas of the source rectangle that are outside of the output
        //    bitmap to transparent black.
        // NOTE: No-op, already done during creation.

        // 8. Return imageData.
        Ok(image_data)
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-putimagedata-short
    pub(crate) fn put_image_data(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        image_data: Ref<ImageData>,
        dx: i32,
        dy: i32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The putImageData(imageData, dx, dy) method steps are to put pixels from an ImageData onto a bitmap, given
        // imageData, this's output bitmap, dx, dy, 0, 0, imageData's width, and imageData's height.
        let (width, height) = image_data.size();
        // NB: An ImageData's size fits in a long, as nothing creates a larger one.
        let (width, height) = (
            i32::try_from(width).unwrap_or(i32::MAX),
            i32::try_from(height).unwrap_or(i32::MAX),
        );
        self.put_pixels_from_an_image_data_onto_a_bitmap(cx, image_data, dx, dy, 0, 0, width, height)
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-putimagedata
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the arguments of putImageData()")]
    pub(crate) fn put_image_data_with_dirty_rectangle(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        image_data: Ref<ImageData>,
        dx: i32,
        dy: i32,
        dirty_x: i32,
        dirty_y: i32,
        dirty_width: i32,
        dirty_height: i32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The putImageData(imageData, dx, dy, dirtyX, dirtyY, dirtyWidth, dirtyHeight) method steps are to put pixels
        // from an ImageData onto a bitmap, given imageData, this's output bitmap, dx, dy, dirtyX, dirtyY, dirtyWidth,
        // and dirtyHeight.
        self.put_pixels_from_an_image_data_onto_a_bitmap(
            cx,
            image_data,
            dx,
            dy,
            dirty_x,
            dirty_y,
            dirty_width,
            dirty_height,
        )
    }
}

impl<K: CanvasKind> RenderingContext2D<K> {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-linewidth
    pub(crate) fn line_width(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // On getting, it must return the current value.
        Ok(f64::from(self.drawing_state().line_width))
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_line_width(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, line_width: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, zero, negative, infinite, and NaN values must be ignored, leaving the value unchanged;
        let line_width = float(line_width);
        if line_width <= 0.0 || !line_width.is_finite() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // other values must change the current value to the new value.
        self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).line_width = line_width;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn line_cap(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<CanvasLineCap> {

        self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).line_cap = line_cap;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-linejoin
    pub(crate) fn line_join(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<CanvasLineJoin> {
        Ok(self.drawing_state().line_join)
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_line_join(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, line_join: CanvasLineJoin) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).line_join = line_join;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-miterlimit
    pub(crate) fn miter_limit(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(f64::from(self.drawing_state().miter_limit))
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_miter_limit(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, miter_limit: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, zero, negative, infinite, and NaN values must be ignored, leaving the value unchanged;
        let miter_limit = float(miter_limit);
        if miter_limit <= 0.0 || !miter_limit.is_finite() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // other values must change the current value to the new value.
        self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).miter_limit = miter_limit;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-setlinedash
    pub(crate) fn set_line_dash(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, mut segments: Vec<f64>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If any value in segments is not finite (e.g. an Infinity or a NaN value), or if any value is negative
        //    (less than zero), then return (without throwing an exception; user agents could show a message on a
        //    developer console, though, as that would be helpful for debugging).
        if segments.iter().any(|segment| !segment.is_finite() || *segment < 0.0) {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. If the number of elements in segments is odd, then let segments be the concatenation of two copies of
        //    segments.
        if segments.len() % 2 == 1 {
            segments.extend_from_within(..);
        }

        // 3. Set the object's dash list to segments.
        self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).dash_list = segments;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-getlinedash
    pub(crate) fn get_line_dash(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<f64>> {
        // When the getLineDash() method is invoked, it must return a sequence whose values are the values of the
        // object's dash list, in the same order.
        Ok(self.drawing_state().dash_list.clone())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-linedashoffset
    pub(crate) fn line_dash_offset(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(f64::from(self.drawing_state().line_dash_offset))
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_line_dash_offset(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, line_dash_offset: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, infinite and NaN values must be ignored, leaving the value unchanged;
        let line_dash_offset = float(line_dash_offset);
        if !line_dash_offset.is_finite() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // other values must change the current value to the new value.
        self.drawing_state_mut(cx.vm()).line_dash_offset = line_dash_offset;
        Ok(())
    }
}

/*

//! The operations of the CanvasPath mixin, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvaspath, which
//! Path2D and the 2D contexts share. They build on a Path, with its rules for a path without a current point.
//!
//! The arithmetic is that of the C++ it replaces, in the same precision: the arguments of moveTo(), lineTo(),
//! quadraticCurveTo(), arc() and ellipse() are floats, and those of the rest are doubles that become floats where
//! they become points.

use ak::math;
use libgfx_rust::{FloatPoint, FloatSize};

use crate::ak_format::ak_formatted;

use crate::geometry::dictionaries::DOMPointInit;

/// The union (unrestricted double or DOMPointInit) of HTML/Canvas/CanvasPath.idl, a radius of roundRect(), whose
/// members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) enum UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInit {
    UnrestrictedDouble(f64),
    DOMPointInit(DOMPointInit),
}

/// The union (unrestricted double or DOMPointInit or sequence<(unrestricted double or DOMPointInit)>) of
/// HTML/Canvas/CanvasPath.idl, the radii of roundRect(), whose members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) enum UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInitOrUnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInitSequence {
    UnrestrictedDouble(f64),
    DOMPointInit(DOMPointInit),
    Sequence(Vec<UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInit>),
}

impl From<UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInit> for RoundRectRadius {
    fn from(radius: UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInit) -> Self {
        match radius {
            UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInit::UnrestrictedDouble(radius) => Self { x: radius, y: radius },
            UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInit::DOMPointInit(point) => Self { x: point.x, y: point.y },
        }
    }
}

/// The radii of roundRect() as a list, which step 2 of its steps makes of a single radius.
pub(crate) fn round_rect_radii(
    radii: UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInitOrUnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInitSequence,
) -> Vec<RoundRectRadius> {
    use UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInitOrUnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInitSequence as Radii;
    match radii {
        Radii::UnrestrictedDouble(radius) => vec![UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInit::UnrestrictedDouble(radius).into()],
        Radii::DOMPointInit(point) => vec![UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInit::DOMPointInit(point).into()],
        Radii::Sequence(radii) => radii.into_iter().map(RoundRectRadius::from).collect(),
    }
}

/// What the operations build on, which is a Path, or what the crate tests record.
pub(crate) trait PathSink {
    /// Whether the path has no current point.
    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool;
    fn last_point(&self) -> FloatPoint;
    fn move_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint);
    fn line_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint);
    fn quadratic_bezier_curve_to(&mut self, through: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint);
    fn cubic_bezier_curve_to(&mut self, c1: FloatPoint, c2: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint);
    fn elliptical_arc_to(
        &mut self,
        point: FloatPoint,
        radii: FloatSize,
        x_axis_rotation: f32,
        large_arc: bool,
        sweep: bool,
    );
    fn arc_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint, radius: f32, large_arc: bool, sweep: bool);
    fn close(&mut self);
}

impl PathSink for libgfx_rust::path::Path {
    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.is_empty()
    }

    fn last_point(&self) -> FloatPoint {
        self.last_point()
    }

    fn move_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint) {
        self.move_to(point);
    }

    fn line_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint) {
        self.line_to(point);
    }

    fn quadratic_bezier_curve_to(&mut self, through: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint) {
        self.quadratic_bezier_curve_to(through, point);
    }

    fn cubic_bezier_curve_to(&mut self, c1: FloatPoint, c2: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint) {
        self.cubic_bezier_curve_to(c1, c2, point);
    }

    fn elliptical_arc_to(
        &mut self,
        point: FloatPoint,
        radii: FloatSize,
        x_axis_rotation: f32,
        large_arc: bool,
        sweep: bool,
    ) {
        self.elliptical_arc_to(point, radii, x_axis_rotation, large_arc, sweep);
    }

    fn arc_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint, radius: f32, large_arc: bool, sweep: bool) {
        self.arc_to(point, radius, large_arc, sweep);
    }

    fn close(&mut self) {
        self.close();
    }
}

/// What an operation throws.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) enum CanvasPathError {
    /// The radius of arc(), an IndexSizeError.
    NegativeArcRadius(f32),
    /// The radius of arcTo(), an IndexSizeError.
    NegativeArcToRadius(f64),
    /// The radiusX of ellipse(), an IndexSizeError.
    NegativeMajorAxisRadius(f32),
    /// The radiusY of ellipse(), an IndexSizeError.
    NegativeMinorAxisRadius(f32),
    /// More than four radii, or none, for roundRect(), a RangeError.
    RoundRectRadiusCount,
    /// A negative radius for roundRect(), a RangeError.
    NegativeRoundRectRadius,
}

impl CanvasPathError {
    /// Whether the exception is a RangeError rather than an "IndexSizeError" DOMException.
    pub(crate) fn is_range_error(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::RoundRectRadiusCount | Self::NegativeRoundRectRadius)
    }

    pub(crate) fn message(self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::NegativeArcRadius(radius) => format!("The radius provided ({}) is negative.", ak_formatted(radius)),
            Self::NegativeArcToRadius(radius) => format!("The radius provided ({}) is negative.", ak_formatted(radius)),
            Self::NegativeMajorAxisRadius(radius) => {
                format!("The major-axis radius provided ({}) is negative.", ak_formatted(radius))
            }
            Self::NegativeMinorAxisRadius(radius) => {
                format!("The minor-axis radius provided ({}) is negative.", ak_formatted(radius))
            }
            Self::RoundRectRadiusCount => "roundRect: Can have between 1 and 4 radii".to_owned(),
            Self::NegativeRoundRectRadius => "roundRect: Radius can't be negative".to_owned(),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(not(test))]
impl From<CanvasPathError> for crate::bindings::Exception {
    fn from(error: CanvasPathError) -> Self {
        let message = ak::Utf16String::from_utf8(&error.message());
        if error.is_range_error() {
            Self::RangeError(message)
        } else {
            Self::index_size_error(message)
        }
    }
}

fn point(x: f32, y: f32) -> FloatPoint {
    FloatPoint { x, y }
}

#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, reason = "a point of a path is in floats")]
fn point_from_doubles(x: f64, y: f64) -> FloatPoint {
    point(x as f32, y as f32)
}

fn ensure_subpath(path: &mut impl PathSink, x: f32, y: f32) {
    if path.is_empty() {
        path.move_to(point(x, y));
    }
}

fn add_line_to_start_point(path: &mut impl PathSink, start_point: FloatPoint) {
    if path.is_empty() {
        path.move_to(start_point);
    } else {
        path.line_to(start_point);
    }
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-closepath
pub(crate) fn close_path(path: &mut impl PathSink) {
    // The closePath() method, when invoked, must do nothing if the object's path has no subpaths. Otherwise, it must
    // mark the last subpath as closed, create a new subpath whose first point is the same as the previous subpath's
    // first point, and finally add this new subpath to the path.
    if path.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    path.close();
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-moveto
pub(crate) fn move_to(path: &mut impl PathSink, x: f32, y: f32) {
    // 1. If either of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
    if !x.is_finite() || !y.is_finite() {
        return;
    }

    // 2. Create a new subpath with the specified point as its first (and only) point.
    path.move_to(point(x, y));
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-lineto
pub(crate) fn line_to(path: &mut impl PathSink, x: f32, y: f32) {
    // 1. If either of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
    if !x.is_finite() || !y.is_finite() {
        return;
    }

    if path.is_empty() {
        // 2. If the object's path has no subpaths, then ensure there is a subpath for (x, y).
        ensure_subpath(path, x, y);
    } else {
        // 3. Otherwise, connect the last point in the subpath to the given point (x, y) using a straight line, and
        //    then add the given point (x, y) to the subpath.
        path.line_to(point(x, y));
    }
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-quadraticcurveto
pub(crate) fn quadratic_curve_to(path: &mut impl PathSink, cpx: f32, cpy: f32, x: f32, y: f32) {
    // 1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
    if !cpx.is_finite() || !cpy.is_finite() || !x.is_finite() || !y.is_finite() {
        return;
    }

    // 2. Ensure there is a subpath for (cpx, cpy).
    ensure_subpath(path, cpx, cpy);

    // 3. Connect the last point in the subpath to the given point (x, y) using a quadratic Bézier curve with control
    //    point (cpx, cpy).
    // 4. Add the given point (x, y) to the subpath.
    path.quadratic_bezier_curve_to(point(cpx, cpy), point(x, y));
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-beziercurveto
pub(crate) fn bezier_curve_to(path: &mut impl PathSink, cp1x: f64, cp1y: f64, cp2x: f64, cp2y: f64, x: f64, y: f64) {
    // 1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
    if [cp1x, cp1y, cp2x, cp2y, x, y]
        .iter()
        .any(|argument| !argument.is_finite())
    {
        return;
    }

    // 2. Ensure there is a subpath for (cp1x, cp1y).
    let control_point_1 = point_from_doubles(cp1x, cp1y);
    ensure_subpath(path, control_point_1.x, control_point_1.y);

    // 3. Connect the last point in the subpath to the given point (x, y) using a cubic Bézier curve with control
    //    points (cp1x, cp1y) and (cp2x, cp2y).
    // 4. Add the point (x, y) to the subpath.
    path.cubic_bezier_curve_to(
        control_point_1,
        point_from_doubles(cp2x, cp2y),
        point_from_doubles(x, y),
    );
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-arc
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
pub(crate) fn arc(
    path: &mut impl PathSink,
    x: f32,
    y: f32,
    radius: f32,
    start_angle: f64,
    end_angle: f64,
    counterclockwise: bool,
) -> Result<(), CanvasPathError> {
    if radius < 0.0 && radius.is_finite() {
        return Err(CanvasPathError::NegativeArcRadius(radius));
    }
    ellipse(
        path,
        x,
        y,
        radius,
        radius,
        0.0,
        start_angle,
        end_angle,
        counterclockwise,
    )
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-ellipse
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
pub(crate) fn ellipse(
    path: &mut impl PathSink,
    x: f32,
    y: f32,
    radius_x: f32,
    radius_y: f32,
    rotation: f32,
    start_angle: f64,
    end_angle: f64,
    counterclockwise: bool,
) -> Result<(), CanvasPathError> {
    // 1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
    if [x, y, radius_x, radius_y, rotation]
        .iter()
        .any(|argument| !argument.is_finite())
        || !start_angle.is_finite()
        || !end_angle.is_finite()
    {
        return Ok(());
    }

    // 2. If either radiusX or radiusY are negative, then throw an "IndexSizeError" DOMException.
    if radius_x < 0.0 {
        return Err(CanvasPathError::NegativeMajorAxisRadius(radius_x));
    }
    if radius_y < 0.0 {
        return Err(CanvasPathError::NegativeMinorAxisRadius(radius_y));
    }

    if radius_x == 0.0 || radius_y == 0.0 {
        add_line_to_start_point(path, point(x, y));
        return Ok(());
    }

    // "If counterclockwise is false and endAngle − startAngle is greater than or equal to 2π, or, if counterclockwise
    // is true and startAngle − endAngle is greater than or equal to 2π, then the arc is the whole circumference of
    // this ellipse"
    // Also draw the full ellipse if making a non-zero whole number of turns.
    // NB: The angles are compared in double precision, as they were given, so that an arc of exactly 2π stays whole.
    let is_whole_circumference = (!counterclockwise && (end_angle - start_angle) >= core::f64::consts::TAU)
        || (counterclockwise && (start_angle - end_angle) >= core::f64::consts::TAU)
        || (start_angle != end_angle && (start_angle - end_angle) % core::f64::consts::TAU == 0.0);

    let tau = core::f32::consts::TAU;
    #[allow(
        clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
        reason = "the angles of an arc of a path are floats"
    )]
    let (start_angle, end_angle) = ((start_angle as f32) % tau, (end_angle as f32) % tau);

    // Then, figure out where the ends of the arc are.
    // To do so, we can pretend that the center of this ellipse is at (0, 0), and the whole coordinate system is
    // rotated `rotation` radians around the x axis, centered on `center`. The sign of the resulting relative
    // positions is just whether our angle is on one of the left quadrants.
    // NB: The C++ took the sine and the cosine of the rotation with the x87 instruction, in extended precision. Taken
    //     in double precision, they round to the same floats but in rare cases.
    let (sin_rotation, cos_rotation) = math::sincos(f64::from(rotation));
    #[allow(
        clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
        reason = "the C++ kept the sine and the cosine in floats"
    )]
    let (sin_rotation, cos_rotation) = (sin_rotation as f32, cos_rotation as f32);

    let resolve_point_with_angle = |angle: f32| {
        let tan_relative = math::tan(angle);
        let tan2 = tan_relative * tan_relative;

        let ab = radius_x * radius_y;
        let a2 = radius_x * radius_x;
        let b2 = radius_y * radius_y;
        let sqrt = (b2 + a2 * tan2).sqrt();

        let mut relative_x_position = ab / sqrt;
        let mut relative_y_position = ab * tan_relative / sqrt;

        // Make sure to set the correct sign
        // -1 if 0 ≤ θ < 90° or 270°< θ ≤ 360°
        //  1 if 90° < θ< 270°
        let sn = if math::cos(angle) >= 0.0 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
        relative_x_position *= sn;
        relative_y_position *= sn;

        // Now rotate it (back) around the center point by 'rotation' radians, then move it back to our actual origin.
        let relative_rotated_x_position = relative_x_position * cos_rotation - relative_y_position * sin_rotation;
        let relative_rotated_y_position = relative_x_position * sin_rotation + relative_y_position * cos_rotation;
        point(relative_rotated_x_position + x, relative_rotated_y_position + y)
    };

    let start_point = resolve_point_with_angle(start_angle);
    let end_point = resolve_point_with_angle(end_angle);

    let mut delta_theta = if counterclockwise {
        start_angle - end_angle
    } else {
        end_angle - start_angle
    };

    if delta_theta < 0.0 {
        delta_theta += core::f32::consts::PI * 2.0;
    }

    // 3. If canvasPath's path has any subpaths, then add a straight line from the last point in the subpath to the
    //    start point of the arc.
    add_line_to_start_point(path, start_point);

    let radii = FloatSize {
        width: radius_x,
        height: radius_y,
    };

    // NB: The whole circumference starts and ends at the start point, so it is added as two halves.
    if is_whole_circumference {
        let half_turn = if counterclockwise {
            -core::f32::consts::PI
        } else {
            core::f32::consts::PI
        };
        let opposite_point = resolve_point_with_angle(start_angle + half_turn);
        path.elliptical_arc_to(opposite_point, radii, rotation, false, !counterclockwise);
        path.elliptical_arc_to(start_point, radii, rotation, false, !counterclockwise);
        return Ok(());
    }

    // 4. Add the start and end points of the arc to the subpath, and connect them with an arc.
    path.elliptical_arc_to(
        end_point,
        radii,
        rotation,
        delta_theta > core::f32::consts::PI,
        !counterclockwise,
    );

    Ok(())
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-arcto
pub(crate) fn arc_to(
    path: &mut impl PathSink,
    x1: f64,
    y1: f64,
    x2: f64,
    y2: f64,
    radius: f64,
) -> Result<(), CanvasPathError> {
    // 1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
    if [x1, y1, x2, y2, radius].iter().any(|argument| !argument.is_finite()) {
        return Ok(());
    }

    // Point (x1, y1)
    let p1 = point_from_doubles(x1, y1);
    // Point (x2, y2)
    let p2 = point_from_doubles(x2, y2);

    // 2. Ensure there is a subpath for (x1, y1).
    ensure_subpath(path, p1.x, p1.y);

    // 3. If radius is negative, then throw an "IndexSizeError" DOMException.
    if radius < 0.0 {
        return Err(CanvasPathError::NegativeArcToRadius(radius));
    }

    // 4. Let the point (x0, y0) be the last point in the subpath, transformed by the inverse of the current
    //    transformation matrix (so that it is in the same coordinate system as the points passed to the method).
    // NB: A Path2D has no transformation matrix, and a context keeps its current default path in the coordinates of
    //     its current transformation matrix, so the last point is in that coordinate system already.
    // Point (x0, y0)
    let p0 = path.last_point();

    // 5. If the point (x0, y0) is equal to the point (x1, y1), or if the point (x1, y1) is equal to the point
    //    (x2, y2), or if radius is zero, then add the point (x1, y1) to the subpath, and connect that point to the
    //    previous point (x0, y0) by a straight line.
    if p0 == p1 || p1 == p2 || radius == 0.0 {
        path.line_to(p1);
        return Ok(());
    }

    let v1 = (p0.x - p1.x, p0.y - p1.y);
    let v2 = (p2.x - p1.x, p2.y - p1.y);
    let length = |vector: (f32, f32)| (vector.0 * vector.0 + vector.1 * vector.1).sqrt();
    let cos_theta = (v1.0 * v2.0 + v1.1 * v2.1) / (length(v1) * length(v2));
    // 6. Otherwise, if the points (x0, y0), (x1, y1), and (x2, y2) all lie on a single straight line, then add the
    //    point (x1, y1) to the subpath, and connect that point to the previous point (x0, y0) by a straight line.
    if cos_theta == -1.0 || cos_theta == 1.0 {
        path.line_to(p1);
        return Ok(());
    }

    // 7. Otherwise, let The Arc be the shortest arc given by circumference of the circle that has radius radius, and
    //    that has one point tangent to the half-infinite line that crosses the point (x0, y0) and ends at the point
    //    (x1, y1), and that has a different point tangent to the half-infinite line that ends at the point (x1, y1)
    //    and crosses the point (x2, y2). The points at which this circle touches these two lines are called the start
    //    and end tangent points respectively.
    let adjacent = radius / f64::from(math::tan(math::acos(cos_theta) / 2.0));
    let factor1 = adjacent / f64::from(length(v1));
    let x3 = f64::from(p1.x) + factor1 * f64::from(p0.x - p1.x);
    let y3 = f64::from(p1.y) + factor1 * f64::from(p0.y - p1.y);
    let start_tangent = point_from_doubles(x3, y3);

    let factor2 = adjacent / f64::from(length(v2));
    let x4 = f64::from(p1.x) + factor2 * f64::from(p2.x - p1.x);
    let y4 = f64::from(p1.y) + factor2 * f64::from(p2.y - p1.y);
    let end_tangent = point_from_doubles(x4, y4);

    // Connect the point (x0, y0) to the start tangent point by a straight line, adding the start tangent point to the
    // subpath.
    path.line_to(start_tangent);

    // NB: The arc is always small, since the tangent points are its end points and the lines meet at (x1, y1).
    let large_arc = false;
    let cross_product = v1.0 * v2.1 - v1.1 * v2.0;
    // NB: By the right-hand rule, true means clockwise.
    let sweep = cross_product < 0.0;

    // and then connect the start tangent point to the end tangent point by The Arc, adding the end tangent point to
    // the subpath.
    #[allow(
        clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
        reason = "the radius of an arc of a path is a float"
    )]
    path.arc_to(end_tangent, radius as f32, large_arc, sweep);
    Ok(())
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-rect
pub(crate) fn rect(path: &mut impl PathSink, x: f64, y: f64, w: f64, h: f64) {
    // 1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
    if [x, y, w, h].iter().any(|argument| !argument.is_finite()) {
        return;
    }

    // 2. Create a new subpath containing just the four points (x, y), (x+w, y), (x+w, y+h), (x, y+h), in that order,
    //    with those four points connected by straight lines.
    path.move_to(point_from_doubles(x, y));
    path.line_to(point_from_doubles(x + w, y));
    path.line_to(point_from_doubles(x + w, y + h));
    path.line_to(point_from_doubles(x, y + h));

    // 3. Mark the subpath as closed.
    path.close();

    // 4. Create a new subpath with the point (x, y) as the only point in the subpath.
    path.move_to(point_from_doubles(x, y));
}

/// A radius of roundRect(): both of a DOMPointInit, or a number twice. `CanvasRoundRectRadius` of
/// Libraries/LibWeb/HTML/Canvas/CanvasPath.h mirrors it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct RoundRectRadius {
    pub(crate) x: f64,
    pub(crate) y: f64,
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-roundrect, with the radii as a list.
pub(crate) fn round_rect(
    path: &mut impl PathSink,
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    w: f64,
    h: f64,
    radii: &[RoundRectRadius],
) -> Result<(), CanvasPathError> {
    // 1. If any of x, y, w, or h are infinite or NaN, then return.
    if [x, y, w, h].iter().any(|argument| !argument.is_finite()) {
        return Ok(());
    }

    // 2. If radii is an unrestricted double or DOMPointInit, then set radii to « radii ».
    // NB: The caller passes a list.

    // 3. If radii is not a list of size one, two, three, or four, then throw a RangeError.
    if radii.is_empty() || radii.len() > 4 {
        return Err(CanvasPathError::RoundRectRadiusCount);
    }

    // 4. Let normalizedRadii be an empty list.
    let mut normalized_radii = Vec::with_capacity(radii.len());

    // 5. For each radius of radii:
    for radius in radii {
        // 5.1.1. If radius["x"] or radius["y"] is infinite or NaN, then return.
        if !radius.x.is_finite() || !radius.y.is_finite() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 5.1.2. If radius["x"] or radius["y"] is negative, then throw a RangeError.
        if radius.x < 0.0 || radius.y < 0.0 {
            return Err(CanvasPathError::NegativeRoundRectRadius);
        }

        // 5.1.3. Otherwise, append radius to normalizedRadii.
        normalized_radii.push(*radius);

        // 5.2. If radius is a unrestricted double:
        // NB: The caller passes a number as a radius with x and y.
    }

    // 6. Let upperLeft, upperRight, lowerRight, and lowerLeft be null.
    // 7. If normalizedRadii's size is 4, then set upperLeft to normalizedRadii[0], set upperRight to
    //    normalizedRadii[1], set lowerRight to normalizedRadii[2], and set lowerLeft to normalizedRadii[3].
    // 8. If normalizedRadii's size is 3, then set upperLeft to normalizedRadii[0], set upperRight and lowerLeft to
    //    normalizedRadii[1], and set lowerRight to normalizedRadii[2].
    // 9. If normalizedRadii's size is 2, then set upperLeft and lowerRight to normalizedRadii[0] and set upperRight
    //    and lowerLeft to normalizedRadii[1].
    // 10. If normalizedRadii's size is 1, then set upperLeft, upperRight, lowerRight, and lowerLeft to
    //     normalizedRadii[0].
    let (mut upper_left, mut upper_right, mut lower_right, mut lower_left) = match *normalized_radii.as_slice() {
        [upper_left, upper_right, lower_right, lower_left] => (upper_left, upper_right, lower_right, lower_left),
        [upper_left, upper_right_and_lower_left, lower_right] => (
            upper_left,
            upper_right_and_lower_left,
            lower_right,
            upper_right_and_lower_left,
        ),
        [upper_left_and_lower_right, upper_right_and_lower_left] => (
            upper_left_and_lower_right,
            upper_right_and_lower_left,
            upper_left_and_lower_right,
            upper_right_and_lower_left,
        ),
        [all] => (all, all, all, all),
        _ => unreachable!("there are one to four radii"),
    };

    // 11. Corner curves must not overlap. Scale all radii to prevent this:
    // 11.1. Let top be upperLeft["x"] + upperRight["x"].
    let top = upper_left.x + upper_right.x;

    // 11.2. Let right be upperRight["y"] + lowerRight["y"].
    let right = upper_right.y + lower_right.y;

    // 11.3. Let bottom be lowerRight["x"] + lowerLeft["x"].
    let bottom = lower_right.x + lower_left.x;

    // 11.4. Let left be upperLeft["y"] + lowerLeft["y"].
    let left = upper_left.y + lower_left.y;

    // 11.5. Let scale be the minimum value of the ratios w / top, h / right, w / bottom, h / left.
    // NB: As AK::min(), which the C++ took it with, this keeps the first of two ratios unless the second is less.
    // INTEROP: The ratios are taken with the magnitudes of w and h, so that a rectangle with a negative width or
    //          height keeps its radii.
    let min = |a: f64, b: f64| if b < a { b } else { a };
    let (width, height) = (w.abs(), h.abs());
    let scale = min(min(width / top, height / right), min(width / bottom, height / left));

    // 11.6. If scale is less than 1, then set the x and y members of upperLeft, upperRight, lowerLeft, and
    //       lowerRight to their current values multiplied by scale.
    if scale < 1.0 {
        for radius in [&mut upper_left, &mut upper_right, &mut lower_left, &mut lower_right] {
            radius.x *= scale;
            radius.y *= scale;
        }
    }

    // 12. Create a new subpath:
    // INTEROP: When w or h is negative, the rectangle extends to the left of x or above y. The corner radii are then
    //          measured into the rectangle from its corners, and the arcs turn the other way when just one of them
    //          is negative.
    let x_direction = if w < 0.0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 };
    let y_direction = if h < 0.0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 };
    let large_arc = false;
    let sweep = x_direction * y_direction > 0.0;
    #[allow(
        clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
        reason = "the radii of an arc of a path are floats"
    )]
    let radii_of = |radius: RoundRectRadius| FloatSize {
        width: radius.x as f32,
        height: radius.y as f32,
    };

    // 12.1. Move to the point (x + upperLeft["x"], y).
    path.move_to(point_from_doubles(x + x_direction * upper_left.x, y));

    // 12.2. Draw a straight line to the point (x + w − upperRight["x"], y).
    path.line_to(point_from_doubles(x + w - x_direction * upper_right.x, y));

    // 12.3. Draw an arc to the point (x + w, y + upperRight["y"]).
    path.elliptical_arc_to(
        point_from_doubles(x + w, y + y_direction * upper_right.y),
        radii_of(upper_right),
        0.0,
        large_arc,
        sweep,
    );

    // 12.4. Draw a straight line to the point (x + w, y + h − lowerRight["y"]).
    path.line_to(point_from_doubles(x + w, y + h - y_direction * lower_right.y));

    // 12.5. Draw an arc to the point (x + w − lowerRight["x"], y + h).
    path.elliptical_arc_to(
        point_from_doubles(x + w - x_direction * lower_right.x, y + h),
        radii_of(lower_right),
        0.0,
        large_arc,
        sweep,
    );

    // 12.6. Draw a straight line to the point (x + lowerLeft["x"], y + h).
    path.line_to(point_from_doubles(x + x_direction * lower_left.x, y + h));

    // 12.7. Draw an arc to the point (x, y + h − lowerLeft["y"]).
    path.elliptical_arc_to(
        point_from_doubles(x, y + h - y_direction * lower_left.y),
        radii_of(lower_left),
        0.0,
        large_arc,
        sweep,
    );

    // 12.8. Draw a straight line to the point (x, y + upperLeft["y"]).
    path.line_to(point_from_doubles(x, y + y_direction * upper_left.y));

    // 12.9. Draw an arc to the point (x + upperLeft["x"], y).
    path.elliptical_arc_to(
        point_from_doubles(x + x_direction * upper_left.x, y),
        radii_of(upper_left),
        0.0,
        large_arc,
        sweep,
    );

    // 13. Mark the subpath as closed.
    path.close();

    // 14. Create a new subpath with the point (x, y) as the only point in the subpath.
    path.move_to(point_from_doubles(x, y));
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        CanvasPathError, PathSink, RoundRectRadius, arc, arc_to, close_path, ellipse, line_to, move_to, rect,
        round_rect,
    };
    use libgfx_rust::{FloatPoint, FloatSize};

    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
    enum Op {
        MoveTo(f32, f32),
        LineTo(f32, f32),
        Quadratic,
        Cubic,
        EllipticalArcTo {
            x: f32,
            y: f32,
            radii: (f32, f32),
            large_arc: bool,
            sweep: bool,
        },
        ArcTo {
            x: f32,
            y: f32,
            radius: f32,
            sweep: bool,
        },
        Close,
    }

    /// The operations that a path was given, with the rules of `Path` for its current point.
    #[derive(Default)]
    struct RecordingPath {
        ops: Vec<Op>,
        last_point: Option<FloatPoint>,
        subpath_start: FloatPoint,
    }

    impl PathSink for RecordingPath {
        fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
            self.last_point.is_none()
        }

        fn last_point(&self) -> FloatPoint {
            self.last_point.unwrap_or_default()
        }

        fn move_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint) {
            self.ops.push(Op::MoveTo(point.x, point.y));
            self.last_point = Some(point);
            self.subpath_start = point;
        }

        fn line_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint) {
            if self.is_empty() {
                return self.move_to(point);
            }
            self.ops.push(Op::LineTo(point.x, point.y));
            self.last_point = Some(point);
        }

        fn quadratic_bezier_curve_to(&mut self, _: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint) {
            self.ops.push(Op::Quadratic);
            self.last_point = Some(point);
        }

        fn cubic_bezier_curve_to(&mut self, _: FloatPoint, _: FloatPoint, point: FloatPoint) {
            self.ops.push(Op::Cubic);
            self.last_point = Some(point);
        }

        fn elliptical_arc_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint, radii: FloatSize, _: f32, large_arc: bool, sweep: bool) {
            self.ops.push(Op::EllipticalArcTo {
                x: point.x,
                y: point.y,
                radii: (radii.width, radii.height),
                large_arc,
                sweep,
            });
            self.last_point = Some(point);
        }

        fn arc_to(&mut self, point: FloatPoint, radius: f32, _: bool, sweep: bool) {
            self.ops.push(Op::ArcTo {
                x: point.x,
                y: point.y,
                radius,
                sweep,
            });
            self.last_point = Some(point);
        }

        fn close(&mut self) {
            if self.is_empty() {
                return;
            }
            self.ops.push(Op::Close);
            self.last_point = Some(self.subpath_start);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn points_that_are_not_finite_are_ignored() {
        let mut path = RecordingPath::default();
        move_to(&mut path, f32::NAN, 0.0);
        line_to(&mut path, 0.0, f32::INFINITY);
        close_path(&mut path);
        rect(&mut path, 0.0, 0.0, f64::NAN, 1.0);
        assert!(path.ops.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_line_without_a_subpath_starts_one() {
        let mut path = RecordingPath::default();
        line_to(&mut path, 1.0, 2.0);
        line_to(&mut path, 3.0, 4.0);
        assert_eq!(path.ops, [Op::MoveTo(1.0, 2.0), Op::LineTo(3.0, 4.0)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_rect_is_a_closed_subpath_followed_by_a_new_one() {
        let mut path = RecordingPath::default();
        rect(&mut path, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0);
        assert_eq!(
            path.ops,
            [
                Op::MoveTo(1.0, 2.0),
                Op::LineTo(4.0, 2.0),
                Op::LineTo(4.0, 6.0),
                Op::LineTo(1.0, 6.0),
                Op::Close,
                Op::MoveTo(1.0, 2.0),
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn negative_radii_throw() {
        let mut path = RecordingPath::default();
        assert_eq!(
            arc(&mut path, 0.0, 0.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, false),
            Err(CanvasPathError::NegativeArcRadius(-1.0))
        );
        assert_eq!(arc(&mut path, 0.0, 0.0, f32::NEG_INFINITY, 0.0, 1.0, false), Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(
            ellipse(&mut path, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, -2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, false),
            Err(CanvasPathError::NegativeMinorAxisRadius(-2.0))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            arc_to(&mut path, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0, 2.0, -0.5),
            Err(CanvasPathError::NegativeArcToRadius(-0.5))
        );
        // NB: arcTo() ensures there is a subpath before it checks the radius.
        assert_eq!(path.ops, [Op::MoveTo(1.0, 1.0)]);
        assert_eq!(
            CanvasPathError::NegativeArcToRadius(-0.5).message(),
            "The radius provided (-0.5) is negative."
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_ellipse_with_a_zero_radius_is_a_line_to_its_center() {
        let mut path = RecordingPath::default();
        move_to(&mut path, 1.0, 1.0);
        assert_eq!(ellipse(&mut path, 5.0, 6.0, 0.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, false), Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(path.ops, [Op::MoveTo(1.0, 1.0), Op::LineTo(5.0, 6.0)]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_whole_turn_is_the_whole_ellipse() {
        let mut path = RecordingPath::default();
        assert_eq!(
            arc(&mut path, 0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 0.0, core::f64::consts::TAU, false),
            Ok(())
        );
        let [
            Op::MoveTo(start_x, start_y),
            Op::EllipticalArcTo {
                x: opposite_x,
                large_arc: first_large_arc,
                sweep: first_sweep,
                radii,
                ..
            },
            Op::EllipticalArcTo {
                x: end_x,
                y: end_y,
                large_arc: second_large_arc,
                sweep: second_sweep,
                ..
            },
        ] = path.ops.as_slice()
        else {
            panic!("the arc is two elliptical arcs from its start: {:?}", path.ops);
        };
        assert_eq!((*start_x, *start_y), (10.0, 0.0));
        assert_eq!(*opposite_x, -10.0);
        assert_eq!((*end_x, *end_y), (10.0, 0.0));
        assert_eq!(*radii, (10.0, 10.0));
        assert!(!*first_large_arc && *first_sweep && !*second_large_arc && *second_sweep);
    }

    #[test]
    fn arc_to_with_collinear_points_is_a_line() {
        let mut path = RecordingPath::default();
        move_to(&mut path, 0.0, 0.0);
        assert_eq!(arc_to(&mut path, 1.0, 0.0, 2.0, 0.0, 1.0), Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(arc_to(&mut path, 3.0, 3.0, 4.0, 3.0, 0.0), Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(
            path.ops,
            [Op::MoveTo(0.0, 0.0), Op::LineTo(1.0, 0.0), Op::LineTo(3.0, 3.0)]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn arc_to_a_corner_is_a_line_and_an_arc_between_the_tangent_points() {
        let mut path = RecordingPath::default();
        move_to(&mut path, 0.0, 0.0);
        assert_eq!(arc_to(&mut path, 10.0, 0.0, 10.0, 10.0, 5.0), Ok(()));
        let [_, Op::LineTo(x3, y3), Op::ArcTo { x, y, radius, sweep }] = path.ops.as_slice() else {
            panic!("the corner is a line and an arc: {:?}", path.ops);
        };
        assert!((x3 - 5.0).abs() < 1e-5 && *y3 == 0.0);
        assert!((*x - 10.0).abs() < 1e-5 && (y - 5.0).abs() < 1e-5);
        assert!(*sweep);
        assert!((radius - 5.0).abs() < 1e-5);
    }

    #[test]
    fn round_rect_takes_one_to_four_radii() {
        let radius = RoundRectRadius { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 };
        let mut path = RecordingPath::default();
        assert_eq!(
            round_rect(&mut path, 0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 10.0, &[]),
            Err(CanvasPathError::RoundRectRadiusCount)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            round_rect(&mut path, 0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 10.0, &[radius; 5]),
            Err(CanvasPathError::RoundRectRadiusCount)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            round_rect(
                &mut path,
                0.0,
                0.0,
                10.0,
                10.0,
                &[radius, RoundRectRadius { x: -1.0, y: 0.0 }]
            ),
            Err(CanvasPathError::NegativeRoundRectRadius)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            round_rect(
                &mut path,
                0.0,
                0.0,
                10.0,
                10.0,
                &[radius, RoundRectRadius { x: f64::NAN, y: -1.0 }]
            ),
            Ok(())
        );
        assert!(path.ops.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn round_rect_assigns_three_radii_to_the_corners_and_scales_them_down() {
        let mut path = RecordingPath::default();
        let radii = [
            RoundRectRadius { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 },
            RoundRectRadius { x: 2.0, y: 2.0 },
            RoundRectRadius { x: 30.0, y: 30.0 },
        ];
        assert_eq!(round_rect(&mut path, 0.0, 0.0, 16.0, 16.0, &radii), Ok(()));
        // NB: The upper right and the lower right corners are 32 tall together, so every radius is halved.
        let arc_radii: Vec<_> = path
            .ops
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|op| match op {
                Op::EllipticalArcTo { radii, .. } => Some(*radii),
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(arc_radii, [(1.0, 1.0), (15.0, 15.0), (1.0, 1.0), (0.5, 0.5)]);
        assert_eq!(path.ops.first(), Some(&Op::MoveTo(0.5, 0.0)));
        assert_eq!(path.ops.last(), Some(&Op::MoveTo(0.0, 0.0)));
    }
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvaspattern

use core::cell::Cell;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::canvas_2d::Compositing;
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::canvas_2d_recorder::{AlphaType, ColorSpace, Recorder};
use libcompositing_rust::display_list::commands::Canvas2DPatternRepetition;
use libgfx_rust::image_frame::ImageFrameHandle;
use libgfx_rust::{AffineTransform, CompositingAndBlendingOperator, FloatRect, IntRect, IntSize, ScalingMode};
use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};

use super::canvas_draw_image::CanvasImageSource;
use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::canvas_2d::canvas::{CanvasImageSourceKind, capture_video_frame, video_transport};
use crate::geometry::dictionaries::{DOMMatrix2DInit, validate_and_fixup_2d};

/// The repetition that a value of the repetition argument of createPattern() names exactly, if it names one.
fn parse_repetition(repetition: &Utf16String) -> Option<Canvas2DPatternRepetition> {
    [
        ("repeat", Canvas2DPatternRepetition::Repeat),
        ("repeat-x", Canvas2DPatternRepetition::RepeatX),
        ("repeat-y", Canvas2DPatternRepetition::RepeatY),
        ("no-repeat", Canvas2DPatternRepetition::NoRepeat),
    ]
    .into_iter()
    .find(|(name, _)| *repetition == Utf16String::from_ascii(name.as_bytes()))
    .map(|(_, repetition)| repetition)
}

/// A copy of the frame of the video at its current playback position, in the color space, which it keeps. A pattern or
/// an ImageBitmap outlives any one video frame, so it reads the frame back instead of holding it.
pub(crate) fn read_back_current_video_frame(video: CppInterface, color_space: ColorSpace) -> Option<ImageFrameHandle> {
    let captured_frame = capture_video_frame(video)?;
    let transport = video_transport(video)?;
    let mut recorder = Recorder::new(transport);

    // A video has a size of its own, so no default object size applies to it.
    let (width, height) = CanvasImageSourceKind::HTMLVideoElement.size(video, IntSize::default());
    let frame_rect = IntRect {
        x: 0,
        y: 0,
        width,
        height,
    };
    // NB: The context only exists to be read back.
    let will_read_frequently = true;
    if width <= 0
        || height <= 0
        || !recorder.create_context(IntSize { width, height }, true, will_read_frequently, color_space)
    {
        return None;
    }

    #[allow(
        clippy::cast_precision_loss,
        reason = "the rectangle is in floats, as the C++ had it"
    )]
    let destination = FloatRect::new(0.0, 0.0, width as f32, height as f32);
    recorder.draw_video_frame(
        &captured_frame.hold,
        captured_frame.sink_handle,
        captured_frame.generation,
        destination,
        destination,
        ScalingMode::NearestNeighbor,
        &Compositing {
            compositing_and_blending_operator: CompositingAndBlendingOperator::Copy,
            ..Compositing::default()
        },
    );
    recorder.flush();
    let frame = recorder.read_back_pixels(frame_rect, AlphaType::Premultiplied, color_space);
    recorder.destroy_context();
    frame
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CanvasPattern {
    /// The frame of the image when createPattern() was called, if the image had one.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    image: Option<ImageFrameHandle>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    repetition: Canvas2DPatternRepetition,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    transform: Cell<Option<AffineTransform>>,
    /// Whether the pattern is marked as not origin-clean, as its image was.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    not_origin_clean: Cell<bool>,
}

impl Wrappable for CanvasPattern {}

impl CanvasPattern {
    /// The pattern of createPattern(), whose image and repetition the context has checked,
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createpattern
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, image: Option<ImageFrameHandle>, repetition: Canvas2DPatternRepetition) -> Ref<Self> {
        allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            image,
            repetition,
            transform: Cell::new(None),
            not_origin_clean: Cell::new(false),
        })
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-createpattern
    pub(crate) fn create_for_image(
        vm: &Vm,
        image: &CanvasImageSource,
        repetition: &Utf16String,
        color_space: ColorSpace,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<Self>>> {
        // 1. Let usability be the result of checking the usability of image.
        // 2. If usability is bad, then return null.
        // 3. Assert: usability is good.
        if !image.check_usability()? {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        // 4. If repetition is the empty string, then set it to "repeat".
        // 5. If repetition is not identical to one of "repeat", "repeat-x", "repeat-y", or "no-repeat", then throw a
        //    "SyntaxError" DOMException.
        let repetition = if repetition.is_empty() {
            Some(Canvas2DPatternRepetition::Repeat)
        } else {
            parse_repetition(repetition)
        };
        let Some(repetition) = repetition else {
            return Err(Exception::syntax_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"Repetition value is not valid",
            )));
        };

        // 6. Let pattern be a new CanvasPattern object with the image image and the repetition behavior given by
        //    repetition.
        let frame = match *image {
            // NB: The frame of a video is read back in the color space of the context, which a draw with the pattern
            //     converts it to anyway.
            CanvasImageSource::HTMLVideoElement(video) => read_back_current_video_frame(video, color_space),
            _ => image.frame(),
        };
        let pattern = Self::create(vm, frame, repetition);

        // 7. If image is not origin-clean, then mark pattern as not origin-clean.
        if image.is_not_origin_clean() {
            pattern.not_origin_clean.set(true);
        }

        // 8. Return pattern.
        Ok(Some(pattern))
    }

    pub(crate) fn image(&self) -> Option<&ImageFrameHandle> {
        self.image.as_ref()
    }

    /// Whether the pattern is marked as not origin-clean.
    pub(crate) fn is_not_origin_clean(&self) -> bool {
        self.not_origin_clean.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn repetition(&self) -> Canvas2DPatternRepetition {
        self.repetition
    }

    /// The transformation matrix of the pattern, which it has once setTransform() gave it one.
    pub(crate) fn transform(&self) -> Option<AffineTransform> {
        self.transform.get()
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-canvaspattern-settransform
    pub(crate) fn set_transform(&self, _: &mut CallContext, transform: DOMMatrix2DInit) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let matrix be the result of creating a DOMMatrix from the 2D dictionary transform.
        let matrix = validate_and_fixup_2d(&transform)?;

        // 2. If one or more of matrix's m11 element, m12 element, m21 element, m22 element, m41 element, or m42
        //    element are infinite or NaN, then return.
        if !matrix.is_finite() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 3. Reset the pattern's transformation matrix to matrix.
        self.transform.set(Some(matrix.to_affine_transform()));

        Ok(())
    }
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvasrect

use libgfx_rust::path::Path;
use libgfx_rust::{FloatPoint, FloatRect, WindingRule};

use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::canvas_2d::context::{CanvasKind, RenderingContext2D};
use crate::canvas_2d::float;

/// The outline of a rectangle, as a closed subpath that goes around it clockwise from its top left corner.
fn rect_path(x: f32, y: f32, width: f32, height: f32) -> Path {
    let mut path = Path::new();
    path.move_to(FloatPoint { x, y });
    path.line_to(FloatPoint { x: x + width, y });
    path.line_to(FloatPoint {
        x: x + width,
        y: y + height,
    });
    path.line_to(FloatPoint { x, y: y + height });
    path.line_to(FloatPoint { x, y });
    path
}

impl<K: CanvasKind> RenderingContext2D<K> {
    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-clearrect
    pub(crate) fn clear_rect(&self, _: &mut CallContext, x: f64, y: f64, w: f64, h: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let (x, y, w, h) = (float(x), float(y), float(w), float(h));

        // 1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
        if !x.is_finite() || !y.is_finite() || !w.is_finite() || !h.is_finite() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        let color = self.clear_color();
        if self.record_if_ready(|recorder| recorder.clear_rect(FloatRect::new(x, y, w, h), color)) {
            self.did_draw();
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-fillrect
    pub(crate) fn fill_rect(&self, _: &mut CallContext, x: f64, y: f64, w: f64, h: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.fill_internal(&rect_path(float(x), float(y), float(w), float(h)), WindingRule::EvenOdd);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-strokerect
    pub(crate) fn stroke_rect(&self, _: &mut CallContext, x: f64, y: f64, w: f64, h: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let (x, y, w, h) = (float(x), float(y), float(w), float(h));

        // 1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
        if !x.is_finite() || !y.is_finite() || !w.is_finite() || !h.is_finite() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Take the result of tracing the path described below, using the CanvasPathDrawingStyles interface's line
        //    styles, and fill it with this's stroke style.

        // If both w and h are zero, the path has a single subpath with just one point (x, y), and no lines, and this
        // method thus has no effect (the trace a path algorithm returns an empty path in that case).

        // If just one of either w or h is zero, then the path has a single subpath consisting of two points, with
        // coordinates (x, y) and (x+w, y+h), in that order, connected by a single straight line.

        // Otherwise, the path has a single subpath consisting of four points, with coordinates (x, y), (x+w, y),
        // (x+w, y+h), and (x, y+h), connected to each other in that order by straight lines.

        // INTEROP: The path is the closed outline of the rectangle in every case. Tracing it prunes zero-length
        //          lines, so a rectangle with just one of w and h zero strokes as a closed line, with joins and no
        //          caps, and a rectangle with both zero strokes nothing.
        let mut path = rect_path(x, y, w, h);
        path.close();
        self.stroke_internal(&path);
        Ok(())
    }
}
