//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#path2d

use core::cell::RefCell;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libgfx_rust::path::Path;
use libjs_rust::api::Trace;

use super::canvas_path::{
    self, UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInitOrUnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInitSequence, round_rect_radii,
};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::geometry::dictionaries::{DOMMatrix2DInit, validate_and_fixup_2d};

/// The union (Path2D or DOMString) of HTML/Path2D.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
pub(crate) enum Path2DOrDOMString {
    Path2D(Ref<Path2D>),
    DOMString(Utf16String),
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Path2D {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    path: RefCell<Path>,
}

impl Wrappable for Path2D {}

#[allow(
    clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
    reason = "these operations take floats, as the C++ did"
)]
fn float(number: f64) -> f32 {
    number as f32
}

impl Path2D {
    /// The path, which the 2D contexts fill, stroke and clip with.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Nothing may change the path while the reference is in use.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn path_unguarded(&self) -> &Path {
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the path from changing while it reads it.
        unsafe { self.path.try_borrow_unguarded() }.expect("nothing changes the path meanwhile")
    }

    fn build<R>(&self, function: impl FnOnce(&mut Path) -> R) -> R {
        function(&mut self.path.borrow_mut())
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-path2d
    pub(crate) fn construct(_: &mut CallContext, path: Option<Path2DOrDOMString>) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Let output be a new Path2D object.
        let output = Self {
            path: RefCell::new(Path::new()),
        };

        // 2. If path is not given, then return output.
        let Some(path) = path else {
            return Ok(output);
        };

        let path = match path {
            // 3. If path is a Path2D object, then add all subpaths of path to output and return output.
            //    (In other words, it returns a copy of the argument.)
            Path2DOrDOMString::Path2D(path) => {
                output.path.replace(path.path.borrow().clone());
                return Ok(output);
            }
            Path2DOrDOMString::DOMString(path) => path,
        };

        // 4. Let svgPath be the result of parsing and interpreting path according to SVG 2's rules for path data.
        //    [SVG]
        let svg_path = libweb_rust::gfx_path_from_path_data(path.as_units());

        if !svg_path.is_empty() {
            // 5. Let (x, y) be the last point in svgPath.
            let xy = svg_path.last_point();

            // 6. Add all the subpaths, if any, from svgPath to output.
            output.path.replace(svg_path);

            // 7. Create a new subpath in output with (x, y) as the only point in the subpath.
            output.build(|path| canvas_path::move_to(path, xy.x, xy.y));
        }

        // 8. Return output.
        Ok(output)
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-path2d-addpath
    pub(crate) fn add_path(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        path: Ref<Path2D>,
        transform: DOMMatrix2DInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The addPath(path, transform) method, when invoked on a Path2D object a, must run these steps:

        // 1. If the Path2D object path has no subpaths, then return.
        if path.path.borrow().is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Let matrix be the result of creating a DOMMatrix from the 2D dictionary transform.
        let matrix = validate_and_fixup_2d(&transform)?;

        // 3. If one or more of matrix's m11 element, m12 element, m21 element, m22 element, m41 element, or m42
        //    element are infinite or NaN, then return.
        if !matrix.is_finite() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 4. Create a copy of all the subpaths in path. Let c be this copy.
        // 5. Transform all the coordinates and lines in c by the transform matrix matrix.
        let copy = path.path.borrow().copy_transformed(matrix.to_affine_transform().values);

        // 6. Let (x, y) be the last point in the last subpath of c.
        let xy = copy.last_point();

        // 7. Add all the subpaths in c to a.
        // FIXME: Is this correct?
        self.build(|path| path.append_path(&copy));

        // 8. Create a new subpath in a with (x, y) as the only point in the subpath.
        self.build(|path| canvas_path::move_to(path, xy.x, xy.y));

        Ok(())
    }

    // The operations of the CanvasPath mixin, whose steps are in canvas_path.rs.

    pub(crate) fn close_path(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.build(canvas_path::close_path);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn move_to(&self, _: &mut CallContext, x: f64, y: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.build(|path| canvas_path::move_to(path, float(x), float(y)));
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn line_to(&self, _: &mut CallContext, x: f64, y: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.build(|path| canvas_path::line_to(path, float(x), float(y)));
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn quadratic_curve_to(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        cpx: f64,
        cpy: f64,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.build(|path| canvas_path::quadratic_curve_to(path, float(cpx), float(cpy), float(x), float(y)));
        Ok(())
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn bezier_curve_to(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        cp1x: f64,
        cp1y: f64,
        cp2x: f64,
        cp2y: f64,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.build(|path| canvas_path::bezier_curve_to(path, cp1x, cp1y, cp2x, cp2y, x, y));
        Ok(())
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn arc_to(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        x1: f64,
        y1: f64,
        x2: f64,
        y2: f64,
        radius: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // NB: A Path2D has no transformation matrix, so its points are in the coordinates that it was given.
        self.build(|path| canvas_path::arc_to(path, x1, y1, x2, y2, radius))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn rect(&self, _: &mut CallContext, x: f64, y: f64, w: f64, h: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.build(|path| canvas_path::rect(path, x, y, w, h));
        Ok(())
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn round_rect(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
        w: f64,
        h: f64,
        radii: UnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInitOrUnrestrictedDoubleOrDOMPointInitSequence,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let radii = round_rect_radii(radii);
        self.build(|path| canvas_path::round_rect(path, x, y, w, h, &radii))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn arc(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
        radius: f64,
        start_angle: f64,
        end_angle: f64,
        counterclockwise: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.build(|path| {
            canvas_path::arc(
                path,
                float(x),
                float(y),
                float(radius),
                start_angle,
                end_angle,
                counterclockwise,
            )
        })?;
        Ok(())
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn ellipse(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        x: f64,
        y: f64,
        radius_x: f64,
        radius_y: f64,
        rotation: f64,
        start_angle: f64,
        end_angle: f64,
        counterclockwise: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.build(|path| {
            canvas_path::ellipse(
                path,
                float(x),
                float(y),
                float(radius_x),
                float(radius_y),
                float(rotation),
                start_angle,
                end_angle,
                counterclockwise,
            )
        })?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#pluginarray

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::{LentCppCell, cpp_class};
use crate::bindings::global_object::CppWindow;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_into_abi};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::html::plugin::Plugin;
use crate::html::window::{PDF_VIEWER_PLUGIN_NAMES, with_pdf_viewer_plugin_objects};

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PluginArray {
    window: CppWindow,
}

impl Wrappable for PluginArray {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.window.realm())
    }
}

impl PluginArray {
    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#dom-pluginarray-refresh
    pub(crate) fn refresh(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The PluginArray interface's refresh() method steps are to do nothing.
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#pdf-viewing-support:support-named-properties
    pub(crate) fn supported_property_names(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> Vec<Utf16String> {
        // The PluginArray interface supports named properties. If the user agent's PDF viewer supported is true, then
        // they are the PDF viewer plugin names. Otherwise, they are the empty list.
        if !self.window.pdf_viewer_supported() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        PDF_VIEWER_PLUGIN_NAMES
            .into_iter()
            .map(Utf16String::from_utf8)
            .collect()
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#dom-pluginarray-length
    pub(crate) fn length(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        // The PluginArray interface's length getter steps are to return this's relevant global object's PDF viewer
        // plugin objects's size.
        Ok(with_pdf_viewer_plugin_objects(cx.vm(), &self.window, |plugins| {
            u32::try_from(plugins.len()).expect("there are five PDF viewer plugin objects")
        }))
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#dom-pluginarray-item
    pub(crate) fn item(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, index: u32) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<Plugin>>> {
        // 1. Let plugins be this's relevant global object's PDF viewer plugin objects.
        // 2. If index < plugins's size, then return plugins[index].
        // 3. Return null.
        Ok(with_pdf_viewer_plugin_objects(cx.vm(), &self.window, |plugins| {
            plugins.get(index as usize).copied()
        }))
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/system-state.html#dom-pluginarray-nameditem
    pub(crate) fn named_item(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, name: Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<Plugin>>> {
        // 1. For each Plugin plugin of this's relevant global object's PDF viewer plugin objects: if plugin's name is
        //    name, then return plugin.
        // 2. Return null.
        Ok(with_pdf_viewer_plugin_objects(cx.vm(), &self.window, |plugins| {
            plugins.iter().find(|plugin| plugin.name == name).copied()
        }))
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_plugin_array_create(vm: &Vm, window: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Window>) -> *mut c_void {
    let window = CppWindow::from_lent(window);
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| PluginArray { window }))
}

use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

/// The dictionary PopStateEventInit of HTML/PopStateEvent.idl.
pub(crate) struct PopStateEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) state: Value,
    pub(crate) has_ua_visual_transition: bool,
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#popstateevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PopStateEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    state: Value,
    has_ua_visual_transition: bool,
}

impl Wrappable for PopStateEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl PopStateEvent {
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: PopStateEventInit,
    ) -> Ref<PopStateEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.parent.bubbles,
            event_init.parent.cancelable,
            event_init.parent.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| PopStateEvent {
            event,
            state: event_init.state,
            has_ua_visual_transition: event_init.has_ua_visual_transition,
        });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: PopStateEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<PopStateEvent>> {
        Ok(Self::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &r#type, event_init_dict))
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#dom-popstateevent-state
    pub(crate) fn state(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        Ok(self.state)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#dom-popstateevent-hasuavisualtransition
    pub(crate) fn has_ua_visual_transition(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.has_ua_visual_transition)
    }
}

/// The Event of a new trusted PopStateEvent in the realm, for the implementation to fire.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_pop_state_event_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    r#type: LentUtf16FlyString<'_>,
    state: Value,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let event_init = PopStateEventInit {
        parent: EventInit {
            bubbles: false,
            cancelable: false,
            composed: false,
        },
        state,
        has_ua_visual_transition: false,
    };
    let r#type: Utf16String = r#type.to_utf16_fly_string().into();
    let event = PopStateEvent::create(vm, realm, &r#type, event_init);
    event.event().as_ptr()
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Bindings/Rust/src/html/port_channel.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! The channel between two MessagePorts in one process, which may be in the agents of different threads.
//!
//! As in WebKit's MessagePortChannel, the channel owns the queues, so that a message waits in the queue of its side no
//! matter who owns that side, and a port that is transferred leaves its messages where they are. Only plain data is ever
//! in it: nothing of a heap crosses, and the receiver makes its record from the plain data on its own thread. An end
//! holds a share of the channel, so either side can go first, and a wake only names a read hook that the event loop looks
//! up on the thread of the receiver, where it finds nothing if the port went away.
//!
//! A channel stops being one when an end leaves the process. Its peer then finds a transport handle on its side, and
//! changes over to that when it gets to it. This happens at most once: an end that goes away never comes back, and a
//! channel does not form again between ports that a transport connects.

use core::hash::{BuildHasher, Hasher};
use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};
use std::hash::RandomState;
use std::sync::{Arc, LazyLock, Mutex, MutexGuard, PoisonError};

use crate::html::message_port::{MessagePortTransport, TransportHandle};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::transfer_record::PortMessage;

/// Tells the owner of an end that there is something to read. Any thread may call it.
pub(crate) type Wake = Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>;

#[derive(Default)]
struct Side {
    /// The messages that wait for this side.
    queue: VecDeque<PortMessage>,
    wake: Option<Wake>,
    is_wake_pending: bool,
    /// The end of this side is gone, closed or out of this process, so nothing reaches it through the channel anymore.
    is_gone: bool,
    /// What this side changes over to, once the other side has left the process.
    transport: Option<TransportHandle>,
}

impl Side {
    fn has_news(&self, peer: &Side) -> bool {
        !self.queue.is_empty() || self.transport.is_some() || peer.is_gone
    }

    /// The wake to call once the channel is unlocked, unless the owner of this side has one on its way.
    fn wake_to_call(&mut self) -> Option<Wake> {
        if self.is_wake_pending {
            return None;
        }
        let wake = self.wake.clone()?;
        self.is_wake_pending = true;
        Some(wake)
    }
}

type Sides = [Side; 2];

fn lock(sides: &Mutex<Sides>) -> MutexGuard<'_, Sides> {
    sides.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}

/// What read() found.
pub(crate) enum PeerState {
    Connected,
    Gone,
    /// The peer has left the process, and this is how to reach it.
    Transport(TransportHandle),
}

/// One end of a channel, which is what a MessagePortTransport or a data holder owns. Dropping it closes the end, and
/// what the end has sent stays readable for the peer.
pub(crate) struct PortChannelEnd {
    sides: Arc<Mutex<Sides>>,
    index: usize,
}

impl PortChannelEnd {
    pub(crate) fn create_pair() -> (Self, Self) {
        let sides = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Sides::default()));
        (
            Self {
                sides: Arc::clone(&sides),
                index: 0,
            },
            Self { sides, index: 1 },
        )
    }

    /// An end that another process handed over: its queued messages, and how to reach the peer, if it is still there.
    pub(crate) fn from_elsewhere(messages: Vec<PortMessage>, transport: Option<TransportHandle>) -> Self {
        let (end, peer) = Self::create_pair();
        {
            let mut sides = lock(&end.sides);
            sides[0].queue = messages.into();
            sides[0].transport = transport;
        }
        drop(peer);
        end
    }

    fn peer_index(&self) -> usize {
        1 - self.index
    }

    /// Sets what tells the owner of this end that there is something to read, or nothing for an end on its way to another
    /// owner. Calls it if there is already something to read.
    pub(crate) fn set_wake(&self, wake: Option<Wake>) {
        let mut sides = lock(&self.sides);
        let has_news = sides[self.index].has_news(&sides[self.peer_index()]);
        let side = &mut sides[self.index];
        side.wake = wake;
        side.is_wake_pending = false;
        let wake = if has_news { side.wake_to_call() } else { None };
        drop(sides);
        if let Some(wake) = wake {
            wake();
        }
    }

    /// Whether a message sent now can arrive.
    pub(crate) fn is_open(&self) -> bool {
        let sides = lock(&self.sides);
        sides[self.index].transport.is_some() || !sides[self.peer_index()].is_gone
    }

    /// Adds the message to the queue of the peer. A message for a peer that is gone is dropped, and one that has to go
    /// over a transport comes back.
    pub(crate) fn send(&self, message: PortMessage) -> Result<(), PortMessage> {
        let mut sides = lock(&self.sides);
        if sides[self.index].transport.is_some() {
            return Err(message);
        }
        let peer = &mut sides[self.peer_index()];
        if peer.is_gone {
            drop(sides);
            drop(message);
            return Ok(());
        }
        peer.queue.push_back(message);
        let wake = peer.wake_to_call();
        drop(sides);
        if let Some(wake) = wake {
            wake();
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Takes all the messages that wait for this end, and tells what became of the peer.
    pub(crate) fn read(&self) -> (VecDeque<PortMessage>, PeerState) {
        let mut sides = lock(&self.sides);
        let peer_is_gone = sides[self.peer_index()].is_gone;
        let side = &mut sides[self.index];
        side.is_wake_pending = false;
        let messages = core::mem::take(&mut side.queue);
        let state = match side.transport.take() {
            Some(transport) => PeerState::Transport(transport),
            None if peer_is_gone => PeerState::Gone,
            None => PeerState::Connected,
        };
        (messages, state)
    }

    /// Moves the channel over to a transport as this end goes to another process, which gets what this returns: the
    /// messages that wait for this end, and the transport handle of its side, if the peer is still there.
    pub(crate) fn leave_process(self) -> (Vec<PortMessage>, Option<TransportHandle>) {
        let needs_new_transport = {
            let sides = lock(&self.sides);
            sides[self.index].transport.is_none() && !sides[self.peer_index()].is_gone
        };
        let new_transport = needs_new_transport.then(MessagePortTransport::create_paired_handles);

        // NB: The queue and the change over are one step: the peer can send until it finds its transport, and what it
        //     sends must be in the queue that goes along, or on that transport.
        let mut sides = lock(&self.sides);
        let peer_is_gone = sides[self.peer_index()].is_gone;
        let side = &mut sides[self.index];
        let messages: Vec<_> = core::mem::take(&mut side.queue).into();
        // NB: If the peer left the process at the same time, the transport that it made for this end is the one.
        if let Some(transport) = side.transport.take() {
            return (messages, Some(transport));
        }
        if peer_is_gone {
            return (messages, None);
        }
        let (own_handle, peer_handle) = new_transport.expect("a peer that is still there got a new transport");
        self.hand_peer_transport(sides, peer_handle);
        (messages, Some(own_handle))
    }

    /// Gives the peer the handle to change over to, and ends this side.
    fn hand_peer_transport(&self, mut sides: MutexGuard<'_, Sides>, handle: TransportHandle) {
        sides[self.index].is_gone = true;
        let peer = &mut sides[self.peer_index()];
        peer.transport = Some(handle);
        let wake = peer.wake_to_call();
        drop(sides);
        if let Some(wake) = wake {
            wake();
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for PortChannelEnd {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let mut sides = lock(&self.sides);
        let peer_index = self.peer_index();
        let side = &mut sides[self.index];
        let was_gone = core::mem::replace(&mut side.is_gone, true);
        side.wake = None;
        let queue = core::mem::take(&mut side.queue);
        let transport = side.transport.take();
        let wake = if was_gone {
            None
        } else {
            sides[peer_index].wake_to_call()
        };
        drop(sides);

        // NB: A message can hold ends of other channels, which lock these.
        drop(queue);
        drop(transport);
        if let Some(wake) = wake {
            wake();
        }
    }
}

/// An end on its way through the browser process, to a thread that its data holder does not reach directly. What reaches
/// the thread is a token, which finds the end here if it arrives in this process.
struct ParkedEnd {
    end: PortChannelEnd,
    /// The handle for the peer of the end, if the data holder also carries a transport, for the case that it arrives
    /// in another process.
    peer_transport: Option<TransportHandle>,
}

fn parked_ends() -> MutexGuard<'static, HashMap<u64, ParkedEnd>> {
    static PARKED_ENDS: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<u64, ParkedEnd>>> = LazyLock::new(Mutex::default);
    PARKED_ENDS.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}

/// Parks the end, and returns its token. If the end may arrive in another process, this also returns what the data
/// holder has to carry for that case.
pub(crate) fn park_end(end: PortChannelEnd, may_leave_process: bool) -> (u64, Option<TransportHandle>) {
    let (carried_transport, peer_transport) = if may_leave_process {
        let (carried_transport, peer_transport) = MessagePortTransport::create_paired_handles();
        (Some(carried_transport), Some(peer_transport))
    } else {
        (None, None)
    };
    let mut parked_ends = parked_ends();
    // NB: The token can arrive in another process, where it must not stand for an end of that process.
    let mut token = RandomState::new().build_hasher().finish();
    while token == 0 || parked_ends.contains_key(&token) {
        token = token.wrapping_add(1);
    }
    parked_ends.insert(token, ParkedEnd { end, peer_transport });
    (token, carried_transport)
}

/// The end that the token stands for, if it is still parked in this process.
pub(crate) fn claim_parked_end(token: u64) -> Option<PortChannelEnd> {
    let parked_end = parked_ends().remove(&token)?;
    Some(parked_end.end)
}

/// For an end that nobody in this process is going to claim: the peer goes on over the transport that the data holder
/// carries, if it has one, and otherwise finds its peer gone. An end that was claimed is left alone.
pub(crate) fn give_up_on_parked_end(token: u64) {
    let Some(ParkedEnd { end, peer_transport }) = parked_ends().remove(&token) else {
        return;
    };
    if let Some(peer_transport) = peer_transport {
        let sides = lock(&end.sides);
        end.hand_peer_transport(sides, peer_transport);
    }
}

//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#predefinedcolorspace

use libcompositing_rust::display_list::canvas_2d_recorder::ColorSpace;

/// In the order of Web::Bindings::PredefinedColorSpace, which C++ passes as its underlying value.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub(crate) enum PredefinedColorSpace {
    #[default]
    Srgb,
    SrgbLinear,
    DisplayP3,
    DisplayP3Linear,
}

impl PredefinedColorSpace {
    /// The color space whose underlying value C++ passes, if it is one.
    pub(crate) fn from_u8(value: u8) -> Option<Self> {
        match value {
            0 => Some(Self::Srgb),
            1 => Some(Self::SrgbLinear),
            2 => Some(Self::DisplayP3),
            3 => Some(Self::DisplayP3Linear),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

impl From<PredefinedColorSpace> for ColorSpace {
    fn from(color_space: PredefinedColorSpace) -> Self {
        match color_space {
            PredefinedColorSpace::Srgb => Self::Srgb,
            PredefinedColorSpace::SrgbLinear => Self::SrgbLinear,
            PredefinedColorSpace::DisplayP3 => Self::DisplayP3,
            PredefinedColorSpace::DisplayP3Linear => Self::DisplayP3Linear,
        }
    }
}

//! PromiseRejectionEvent, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#promiserejectionevent

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Object, Realm, Trace, Value, Vm};

use crate::bindings::event_target::CppEvent;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::lent_string::LentUtf16FlyString;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;

/// The dictionary PromiseRejectionEventInit of HTML/PromiseRejectionEvent.idl.
pub(crate) struct PromiseRejectionEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) promise: Gc<Object>,
    pub(crate) reason: Option<Value>,
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#promiserejectionevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PromiseRejectionEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    promise: Gc<Object>,
    reason: Value,
}

impl Wrappable for PromiseRejectionEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl PromiseRejectionEvent {
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: PromiseRejectionEventInit,
    ) -> Ref<PromiseRejectionEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.parent.bubbles,
            event_init.parent.cancelable,
            event_init.parent.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| PromiseRejectionEvent {
            event,
            promise: event_init.promise,
            reason: event_init.reason.unwrap_or(Value::UNDEFINED),
        });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: PromiseRejectionEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<PromiseRejectionEvent>> {
        Ok(Self::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &r#type, event_init_dict))
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#dom-promiserejectionevent-promise
    pub(crate) fn promise(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<Object>> {
        Ok(self.promise)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#dom-promiserejectionevent-reason
    pub(crate) fn reason(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        Ok(self.reason)
    }
}

/// The Event of a new trusted PromiseRejectionEvent in the realm, for the implementation to fire.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "C++ passes each member of the dictionary")]
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_promise_rejection_event_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    r#type: LentUtf16FlyString<'_>,
    bubbles: bool,
    cancelable: bool,
    composed: bool,
    promise: Gc<Object>,
    reason: Value,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let event_init = PromiseRejectionEventInit {
        parent: EventInit {
            bubbles,
            cancelable,
            composed,
        },
        promise,
        reason: Some(reason),
    };
    let r#type: Utf16String = r#type.to_utf16_fly_string().into();
    let event = PromiseRejectionEvent::create(vm, realm, &r#type, event_init);
    event.event().as_ptr()
}

// NB: A canonicalized SanitizerElementNamespace or SanitizerAttributeNamespace dictionary.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct SanitizerName {
    pub(crate) name: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) namespace_: Option<Utf16String>,

// NB: A canonicalized SanitizerElementNamespaceWithAttributes dictionary.

    pub(crate) attributes: Option<Vec<SanitizerName>>,

// NB: A canonicalized SanitizerConfig dictionary. Processing instructions are represented by their target.

    pub(crate) remove_elements: Option<Vec<SanitizerName>>,
