// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#sanitizer
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Sanitizer {
    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#sanitizer-configuration
    #[gc(untraced)]
    configuration: RefCell<SanitizerConfiguration>,
}

impl Wrappable for Sanitizer {}

impl Sanitizer {
    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-constructor
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        _: &mut CallContext,
        configuration: SanitizerConfigOrSanitizerPresets,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. If configuration is a SanitizerPresets string:
        //    1. Assert: configuration is "default".
        //    2. Set configuration to the built-in safe default configuration.
        let fresh_configuration = match configuration {
            SanitizerConfigOrSanitizerPresets::SanitizerConfig(config) => canonicalize_sanitizer_config(&config),
            SanitizerConfigOrSanitizerPresets::SanitizerPresets(preset) => {
                assert!(preset == SanitizerPresets::Default);
                built_in_safe_default_configuration().clone()
            }
        };

        // 2. Configure this given configuration and true.
        let canonical_configuration = configure_sanitizer_configuration(fresh_configuration, PermissiveDefaults::Yes)?;
        Ok(Self::new(canonical_configuration))
    }

    fn new(configuration: SanitizerConfiguration) -> Self {
        assert!(sanitizer_configuration_is_valid(&configuration));
        Self {
            configuration: RefCell::new(configuration),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_with_configuration(vm: &Vm, configuration: SanitizerConfiguration) -> Ref<Self> {
        allocate(vm, |_| Self::new(configuration))
    }

    pub(crate) fn configuration(&self) -> SanitizerConfiguration {
        self.configuration.borrow().clone()
    }
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#compare-sanitizer-items
fn compare_sanitizer_items(item_a: &SanitizerName, item_b: &SanitizerName) -> bool {
    // 1. Let namespaceA be itemA["namespace"].
    let namespace_a = &item_a.namespace_;

    // 2. Let namespaceB be itemB["namespace"].
    let namespace_b = &item_b.namespace_;

    // 3. If namespaceA is null:
    if namespace_a.is_none() {
        // 1. If namespaceB is not null, then return true.
        if namespace_b.is_some() {
            return true;
        }
    }
    // 4. Otherwise:
    else {
        // 1. If namespaceB is null, then return false.
        let Some(namespace_b) = namespace_b else {
            return false;
        };
        let namespace_a = namespace_a.as_ref().unwrap();

        // 2. If namespaceA is code unit less than namespaceB, then return true.
        if Utf16View::of_string(namespace_a)
            .code_units()
            .cmp(Utf16View::of_string(namespace_b).code_units())
            .is_lt()
        {
            return true;
        }

        // 3. If namespaceA is not namespaceB, then return false.
        if namespace_a != namespace_b {
            return false;
        }
    }

    // 5. If itemA["name"] is code unit less than itemB["name"], then return true.
    if Utf16View::of_string(&item_a.name)
        .code_units()
        .cmp(Utf16View::of_string(&item_b.name).code_units())
        .is_lt()
    {
        return true;
    }

    // 6. Return false.
    false
}

fn sort_sanitizer_items(list: &mut [SanitizerName]) {
    list.sort_unstable_by(sanitizer_item_order);
}
fn sanitizer_item_order(a: &SanitizerName, b: &SanitizerName) -> core::cmp::Ordering {
    if compare_sanitizer_items(a, b) {
        core::cmp::Ordering::Less
    } else if compare_sanitizer_items(b, a) {
        core::cmp::Ordering::Greater
    } else {
        core::cmp::Ordering::Equal
    }
}
fn sort_processing_instructions(list: &mut [Utf16String]) {
    list.sort_unstable_by(|a, b| {
        Utf16View::of_string(a)
            .code_units()
            .cmp(Utf16View::of_string(b).code_units())
    });
}

// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#create-a-set
fn create_a_set(list: &[SanitizerName]) -> Vec<SanitizerName> {
    let mut set = Vec::new();
    for item in list {
        if !set.contains(item) {
            set.push(item.clone());
        }
    }
    set
}
// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-difference
fn difference(a: &[SanitizerName], b: &[SanitizerName]) -> Vec<SanitizerName> {
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    for item in a {
        if !b.contains(item) {
            result.push(item.clone());
        }
    }
    result
}
// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-intersection
fn intersection(a: &[SanitizerName], b: &[SanitizerName]) -> Vec<SanitizerName> {
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    for item in a {
        if b.contains(item) {
            result.push(item.clone());
        }
    }
    result
}

impl Sanitizer {
    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-get
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<SanitizerConfig> {
        // NOTE: Outside of the get() method, the order of the Sanitizer's elements and attributes is unobservable. By
        //       explicitly sorting the result of this method, we give implementations the opportunity to optimize by,
        //       for example, using unordered sets internally.
        // 1. Let config be this's configuration.
        let mut config = self.configuration.borrow().clone();

        // 2. Assert: config is valid.
        assert!(sanitizer_configuration_is_valid(&config));

        // 3. If config["elements"] exists:
        if let Some(elements) = &mut config.elements {
            // 1. For each element of config["elements"]:
            for element in elements.iter_mut() {
                // 1. If element["attributes"] exists, then set element["attributes"] to the result of sorting
                //    element["attributes"], with compare sanitizer items.
                if let Some(list) = &mut element.attributes {
                    sort_sanitizer_items(list);
                }

                // 2. If element["removeAttributes"] exists, then set element["removeAttributes"] to the result of sorting
                //    element["removeAttributes"], with compare sanitizer items.
                if let Some(list) = &mut element.remove_attributes {
                    sort_sanitizer_items(list);
                }
            }

            // 2. Set config["elements"] to the result of sorting config["elements"], with compare sanitizer items.
            elements.sort_unstable_by(|a, b| sanitizer_item_order(&a.element, &b.element));
        }
        // 4. Otherwise:
        else {
            // 1. Set config["removeElements"] to the result of sorting config["removeElements"], with compare sanitizer
            //    items.
            sort_sanitizer_items(config.remove_elements.as_mut().unwrap());
        }

        // 5. If config["replaceWithChildrenElements"] exists, then set config["replaceWithChildrenElements"] to the result
        //    of sorting config["replaceWithChildrenElements"], with compare sanitizer items.
        if let Some(list) = &mut config.replace_with_children_elements {
            sort_sanitizer_items(list);
        }

        // 6. If config["processingInstructions"] exists, then set config["processingInstructions"] to the result of
        //    sorting config["processingInstructions"], with piA["target"] being code unit less than piB["target"].
        if let Some(list) = &mut config.processing_instructions {
            sort_processing_instructions(list);
        }
        // 7. Otherwise:
        else {
            // 1. Set config["removeProcessingInstructions"] to the result of sorting
            //    config["removeProcessingInstructions"], with piA["target"] being code unit less than piB["target"].
            sort_processing_instructions(config.remove_processing_instructions.as_mut().unwrap());
        }

        // 8. If config["attributes"] exists, then set config["attributes"] to the result of sorting config["attributes"]
        //    given compare sanitizer items.
        if let Some(list) = &mut config.attributes {
            sort_sanitizer_items(list);
        }
        // 9. Otherwise:
        else {
            // 1. Set config["removeAttributes"] to the result of sorting config["removeAttributes"] given compare
            //    sanitizer items.
            sort_sanitizer_items(config.remove_attributes.as_mut().unwrap());
        }

        // 10. Return config.
        Ok(sanitizer_configuration_to_bindings(&config))
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-allowelement
    pub(crate) fn allow_element(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        element_input: SanitizerElementWithAttributes,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let configuration be this's configuration.
        let mut configuration = self.configuration.borrow_mut();

        // 2. Assert: configuration is valid.
        assert!(sanitizer_configuration_is_valid(&configuration));

        // 3. Set element to the result of canonicalizing element.
        let mut element = canonicalize_sanitizer_element_with_attributes(&element_input);

        // 4. If configuration["elements"] exists:
        if configuration.elements.is_some() {
            // 1. Let modified be the result of removing element from configuration["replaceWithChildrenElements"].
            let modified = sanitizer_list_remove(&mut configuration.replace_with_children_elements, &element.element);

            // 2. If configuration["attributes"] exists:
            if let Some(attributes) = &configuration.attributes {
                // 1. If element["attributes"] exists:
                if let Some(list) = &element.attributes {
                    // 1. Set element["attributes"] to the result of creating a set from element["attributes"].
                    element.attributes = Some(create_a_set(list));

                    // 2. Set element["attributes"] to the difference of element["attributes"] and
                    //    configuration["attributes"].
                    element.attributes = Some(difference(element.attributes.as_ref().unwrap(), attributes));

                    // 3. If configuration["dataAttributes"] is true, then remove all items item from element["attributes"]
                    //    where item is a custom data attribute.
                    if configuration.data_attributes == Some(true) {
                        element
                            .attributes
                            .as_mut()
                            .unwrap()
                            .retain(|item| !is_custom_data_attribute(item));
                    }
                }

                // 2. If element["removeAttributes"] exists:
                if let Some(list) = &element.remove_attributes {
                    // 1. Set element["removeAttributes"] to the result of creating a set from element["removeAttributes"].
                    element.remove_attributes = Some(create_a_set(list));

                    // 2. Set element["removeAttributes"] to the intersection of element["removeAttributes"] and
                    //    configuration["attributes"].
                    element.remove_attributes =
                        Some(intersection(element.remove_attributes.as_ref().unwrap(), attributes));
                }
            }
            // 3. Otherwise:
            else {
                // 1. If element["attributes"] exists:
                if let Some(list) = &element.attributes {
                    // 1. Set element["attributes"] to the result of creating a set from element["attributes"].
                    element.attributes = Some(create_a_set(list));

                    // 2. Set element["attributes"] to the difference of element["attributes"] and
                    //    element["removeAttributes"] with default « ».
                    element.attributes = Some(difference(
                        element.attributes.as_ref().unwrap(),
                        element.remove_attributes.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[]),
                    ));

                    // 3. Remove element["removeAttributes"].
                    element.remove_attributes = None;

                    // 4. Set element["attributes"] to the difference of element["attributes"] and
                    //    configuration["removeAttributes"].
                    element.attributes = Some(difference(
                        element.attributes.as_ref().unwrap(),
                        configuration.remove_attributes.as_ref().unwrap(),
                    ));
                }

                // 2. If element["removeAttributes"] exists:
                if let Some(list) = &element.remove_attributes {
                    // 1. Set element["removeAttributes"] to the result of creating a set from element["removeAttributes"].
                    element.remove_attributes = Some(create_a_set(list));

                    // 2. Set element["removeAttributes"] to the difference of element["removeAttributes"] and
                    //    configuration["removeAttributes"].
                    element.remove_attributes = Some(difference(
                        element.remove_attributes.as_ref().unwrap(),
                        configuration.remove_attributes.as_ref().unwrap(),
                    ));
                }
            }

            // 4. If configuration["elements"] does not contain element:
            let elements = configuration.elements.as_mut().unwrap();
            let current_element = elements.iter().position(|item| item.element == element.element);
            if current_element.is_none() {
                // 1. Append element to configuration["elements"].
                elements.push(element);

                // 2. Return true.
                return Ok(true);
            }

            // 5. Let currentElement be the item in configuration["elements"] whose name member is element's name member
            //    and whose namespace member is element's namespace member.
            // 6. If element is equal to currentElement, then return modified.
            let current_element = current_element.unwrap();
            if element == elements[current_element] {
                return Ok(modified);
            }

            // 7. Remove element from configuration["elements"].
            elements.remove(current_element);

            // 8. Append element to configuration["elements"].
            elements.push(element);

            // 9. Return true.
            return Ok(true);
        }

        // 5. Otherwise:
        // 1. If element["attributes"] exists or element["removeAttributes"] with default « » is not empty, then return
        //    false.
        if element.attributes.is_some() || element.remove_attributes.as_ref().is_some_and(|list| !list.is_empty()) {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 2. Let modified be the result of removing element from configuration["replaceWithChildrenElements"].
        let modified = sanitizer_list_remove(&mut configuration.replace_with_children_elements, &element.element);

        // 3. If configuration["removeElements"] does not contain element, then return modified.
        if !configuration
            .remove_elements
            .as_ref()
            .unwrap()
            .contains(&element.element)
        {
            return Ok(modified);
        }

        // 4. Remove element from configuration["removeElements"].
        sanitizer_list_remove(&mut configuration.remove_elements, &element.element);

        // 5. Return true.
        Ok(true)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-removeelement
    pub(crate) fn remove_element(&self, _: &mut CallContext, element: SanitizerElement) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The removeElement(element) method steps are to return the result of removing element from this's
        // configuration.
        Ok(remove_an_element_from_sanitizer_config(
            &mut self.configuration.borrow_mut(),
            &canonicalize_sanitizer_element(&element),
        ))
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-replaceelementwithchildren
    pub(crate) fn replace_element_with_children(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        element_input: SanitizerElement,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let configuration be this's configuration.
        let mut configuration = self.configuration.borrow_mut();

        // 2. Assert: configuration is valid.
        assert!(sanitizer_configuration_is_valid(&configuration));

        // 3. Set element to the result of canonicalizing element.
        let element = canonicalize_sanitizer_element(&element_input);

        // 4. If the built-in non-replaceable elements list contains element, then return false.
        if built_in_non_replaceable_elements_list_contains(&element) {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 5. Let modified be the result of removing element from configuration["elements"].
        let mut modified = false;
        if let Some(elements) = &mut configuration.elements {
            let size = elements.len();
            elements.retain(|item| item.element != element);
            modified = size != elements.len();
        }

        // 6. If removing element from configuration["removeElements"] is true, then set modified to true.
        if sanitizer_list_remove(&mut configuration.remove_elements, &element) {
            modified = true;
        }

        // 7. If configuration["replaceWithChildrenElements"] does not contain element:
        if !sanitizer_list_contains(configuration.replace_with_children_elements.as_deref(), &element) {
            // 1. Append element to configuration["replaceWithChildrenElements"].
            configuration
                .replace_with_children_elements
                .get_or_insert_with(Vec::new)
                .push(element);

            // 2. Return true.
            return Ok(true);
        }

        // 8. Return modified.
        Ok(modified)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-allowattribute
    pub(crate) fn allow_attribute(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        attribute_input: SanitizerAttribute,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let configuration be this's configuration.
        let mut configuration = self.configuration.borrow_mut();

        // 2. Assert: configuration is valid.
        assert!(sanitizer_configuration_is_valid(&configuration));

        // 3. Set attribute to the result of canonicalizing attribute.
        let attribute = canonicalize_sanitizer_attribute(&attribute_input);

        // 4. If configuration["attributes"] exists:
        if configuration.attributes.is_some() {
            // 1. If configuration["dataAttributes"] is true and attribute is a custom data attribute, then return false.
            if configuration.data_attributes == Some(true) && is_custom_data_attribute(&attribute) {
                return Ok(false);
            }

            // 2. If configuration["attributes"] contains attribute, then return false.
            if configuration.attributes.as_ref().unwrap().contains(&attribute) {
                return Ok(false);
            }

            // 3. If configuration["elements"] exists:
            if let Some(elements) = &mut configuration.elements {
                // 1. For each element in configuration["elements"]:
                for element in elements {
                    // 1. If element["attributes"] with default « » contains attribute, then remove attribute from
                    //    element["attributes"].
                    sanitizer_list_remove(&mut element.attributes, &attribute);
                }
            }

            // 4. Append attribute to configuration["attributes"].
            configuration.attributes.as_mut().unwrap().push(attribute);

            // 5. Return true.
            return Ok(true);
        }

        // 5. Otherwise:
        // 1. If configuration["removeAttributes"] does not contain attribute, then return false.
        if !configuration.remove_attributes.as_ref().unwrap().contains(&attribute) {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 2. Remove attribute from configuration["removeAttributes"].
        sanitizer_list_remove(&mut configuration.remove_attributes, &attribute);

        // 3. Return true.
        Ok(true)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-removeattribute
    pub(crate) fn remove_attribute(&self, _: &mut CallContext, attribute: SanitizerAttribute) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The removeAttribute(attribute) method steps are to return the result of removing attribute from this's
        // configuration.
        Ok(remove_an_attribute_from_sanitizer_config(
            &mut self.configuration.borrow_mut(),
            &canonicalize_sanitizer_attribute(&attribute),
        ))
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-setcomments
    pub(crate) fn set_comments(&self, _: &mut CallContext, allow: bool) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let configuration be this's configuration.
        let mut configuration = self.configuration.borrow_mut();

        // 2. Assert: configuration is valid.
        assert!(sanitizer_configuration_is_valid(&configuration));

        // 3. If configuration["comments"] is allow, then return false.
        if configuration.comments == Some(allow) {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 4. Set configuration["comments"] to allow.
        configuration.comments = Some(allow);

        // 5. Return true.
        Ok(true)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-setdataattributes
    pub(crate) fn set_data_attributes(&self, _: &mut CallContext, allow: bool) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let configuration be this's configuration.
        let mut configuration = self.configuration.borrow_mut();

        // 2. Assert: configuration is valid.
        assert!(sanitizer_configuration_is_valid(&configuration));

        // 3. If configuration["attributes"] does not exist, then return false.
        if configuration.attributes.is_none() {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 4. If configuration["dataAttributes"] exists and is equal to allow, then return false.
        if configuration.data_attributes == Some(allow) {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 5. If allow is true:
        if allow {
            // 1. If configuration["elements"] exists:
            if let Some(elements) = &mut configuration.elements {
                // 1. For each element of configuration["elements"]:
                for element in elements {
                    // 1. If element["attributes"] exists, then remove all items item from element["attributes"] where item
                    //    is a custom data attribute.
                    if let Some(attributes) = &mut element.attributes {
                        attributes.retain(|item| !is_custom_data_attribute(item));
                    }

                    // AD-HOC: Do the same for element["removeAttributes"], which must stay a subset of
                    //         configuration["attributes"] for the configuration to remain valid.
                    if let Some(remove_attributes) = &mut element.remove_attributes {
                        remove_attributes.retain(|item| !is_custom_data_attribute(item));
                    }
                }
            }

            // 2. Remove all items item from configuration["attributes"] where item is a custom data attribute.
            configuration
                .attributes
                .as_mut()
                .unwrap()
                .retain(|item| !is_custom_data_attribute(item));
        }

        // 6. Set configuration["dataAttributes"] to allow.
        configuration.data_attributes = Some(allow);

        // 7. Return true.
        Ok(true)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-setjavascripturls
    pub(crate) fn set_javascript_urls(&self, _: &mut CallContext, allow: bool) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let configuration be this's configuration.
        let mut configuration = self.configuration.borrow_mut();

        // 2. Assert: configuration is valid.
        assert!(sanitizer_configuration_is_valid(&configuration));

        // 3. If configuration["javascriptURLs"] is allow, then return false.
        if configuration.javascript_urls == Some(allow) {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 4. Set configuration["javascriptURLs"] to allow.
        configuration.javascript_urls = Some(allow);

        // 5. Return true.
        Ok(true)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-allowprocessinginstruction
    pub(crate) fn allow_processing_instruction(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        pi_input: SanitizerPI,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let configuration be this's configuration.
        let mut configuration = self.configuration.borrow_mut();

        // 2. Assert: configuration is valid.
        assert!(sanitizer_configuration_is_valid(&configuration));

        // 3. Set pi to the result of canonicalizing pi.
        let pi = canonicalize_sanitizer_processing_instruction(&pi_input);

        // 4. If configuration["processingInstructions"] exists:
        if let Some(list) = &mut configuration.processing_instructions {
            // 1. If configuration["processingInstructions"] contains pi, then return false.
            if list.contains(&pi) {
                return Ok(false);
            }

            // 2. Append pi to configuration["processingInstructions"].
            list.push(pi);

            // 3. Return true.
            return Ok(true);
        }

        // 5. Otherwise:
        // 1. If configuration["removeProcessingInstructions"] contains pi:
        if configuration
            .remove_processing_instructions
            .as_ref()
            .unwrap()
            .contains(&pi)
        {
            // 1. Remove pi from configuration["removeProcessingInstructions"].
            configuration
                .remove_processing_instructions
                .as_mut()
                .unwrap()
                .retain(|item| *item != pi);

            // 2. Return true.
            return Ok(true);
        }

        // 2. Return false.
        Ok(false)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-removeprocessinginstruction
    pub(crate) fn remove_processing_instruction(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        pi_input: SanitizerPI,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let configuration be this's configuration.
        let mut configuration = self.configuration.borrow_mut();

        // 2. Assert: configuration is valid.
        assert!(sanitizer_configuration_is_valid(&configuration));

        // 3. Set pi to the result of canonicalizing pi.
        let pi = canonicalize_sanitizer_processing_instruction(&pi_input);

        // 4. If configuration["processingInstructions"] exists:
        if let Some(list) = &mut configuration.processing_instructions {
            // 1. If configuration["processingInstructions"] contains pi:
            if list.contains(&pi) {
                // 1. Remove pi from configuration["processingInstructions"].
                list.retain(|item| *item != pi);

                // 2. Return true.
                return Ok(true);
            }

            // 2. Return false.
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 5. Otherwise:
        // 1. If configuration["removeProcessingInstructions"] contains pi, then return false.
        if configuration
            .remove_processing_instructions
            .as_ref()
            .unwrap()
            .contains(&pi)
        {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 2. Append pi to configuration["removeProcessingInstructions"].
        configuration.remove_processing_instructions.as_mut().unwrap().push(pi);

        // 3. Return true.
        Ok(true)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-sanitizer-removeunsafe
    pub(crate) fn remove_unsafe(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The removeUnsafe() method steps are to return the result of removing unsafe from this's configuration.
        Ok(remove_unsafe_from_sanitizer_config(
            &mut self.configuration.borrow_mut(),
        ))
    }
}

//! StorageEvent, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#storageevent

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, GcRefCell, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::UsvString;
use crate::bindings::event_target::CppEvent;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;
use crate::html::storage::Storage;

/// The dictionary StorageEventInit of HTML/StorageEvent.idl.
pub(crate) struct StorageEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) key: Option<Utf16String>,
    pub(crate) old_value: Option<Utf16String>,
    pub(crate) new_value: Option<Utf16String>,
    pub(crate) url: UsvString,
    pub(crate) storage_area: Option<Ref<Storage>>,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct StorageEventState {
    key: Option<Utf16String>,
    old_value: Option<Utf16String>,
    new_value: Option<Utf16String>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    url: UsvString,
    storage_area: Option<Ref<Storage>>,
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#storageevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct StorageEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    state: GcRefCell<StorageEventState>,
}

impl Wrappable for StorageEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl StorageEvent {
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: StorageEventInit,
    ) -> Ref<StorageEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.parent.bubbles,
            event_init.parent.cancelable,
            event_init.parent.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| StorageEvent {
            event,
            state: GcRefCell::new(StorageEventState {
                key: event_init.key,
                old_value: event_init.old_value,
                new_value: event_init.new_value,
                url: event_init.url,
                storage_area: event_init.storage_area,
            }),
        });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: StorageEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<StorageEvent>> {
        Ok(Self::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &r#type, event_init_dict))
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    pub(crate) fn key(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Utf16String>> {
        Ok(self.state.borrow().key.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn old_value(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Utf16String>> {
        Ok(self.state.borrow().old_value.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn new_value(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Utf16String>> {
        Ok(self.state.borrow().new_value.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn url(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        Ok(self.state.borrow().url.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn storage_area(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<Storage>>> {
        Ok(self.state.borrow().storage_area)
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#dom-storageevent-initstorageevent
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the operation has these arguments")]
    pub(crate) fn init_storage_event(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        bubbles: bool,
        cancelable: bool,
        key: Option<Utf16String>,
        old_value: Option<Utf16String>,
        new_value: Option<Utf16String>,
        url: UsvString,
        storage_area: Option<Ref<Storage>>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The initStorageEvent(type, bubbles, cancelable, key, oldValue, newValue, url, storageArea) method must initialize
        // the event in a manner analogous to the similarly-named initEvent() method. [DOM]
        if self.event.dispatched() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        self.event.initialize_event(&r#type, bubbles, cancelable);
        *self.state.borrow_mut(cx.vm()) = StorageEventState {
            key,
            old_value,
            new_value,
            url,
            storage_area,
        };
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! Storage, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#storage-2

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, MarkedVec, Realm, Throw, Trace, Value, Visitor, Vm};
use liburl_rust::url::ExcludeFragment;

use crate::bindings::conversions::UsvString;
use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::{CppEnvironmentSettingsObject, relevant_settings_object};
use crate::bindings::global_object::{CppWindow, active_windows, relevant_global_object, window_from_global_object};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_from_abi};
use crate::bindings::promise::{TaskSource, queue_a_global_task};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;
use crate::html::storage_event::{StorageEvent, StorageEventInit};
use crate::storage_api::storage_bottle::StorageBottle;
use crate::storage_api::storage_key::{StorageKey, obtain_a_storage_key};
use crate::webidl::dom_exception::DOMExceptionFields;
use crate::webidl::quota_exceeded_error::{self, QuotaExceededErrorFields};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_html_window_storage(window: *mut c_void, storage_type: u8) -> *mut c_void;
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#concept-storage-type
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub(crate) enum StorageType {
    Local = 0,
    Session = 1,
}

impl StorageType {
    /// The storage type that LibWeb passes, an HTML::Storage::Type.
    pub(crate) fn from_abi(value: u8) -> Self {
        match value {
            0 => StorageType::Local,
            1 => StorageType::Session,
            _ => panic!("LibWeb passes a storage type"),
        }
    }
}

// SAFETY: A storage type holds no cells.
unsafe impl Trace for StorageType {
    fn trace(&self, _: &mut Visitor) {}
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#storage-2
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Storage {
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    storage_type: StorageType,
    map: StorageBottle,
}

impl Wrappable for Storage {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.realm)
    }
}

/// The key, values and URL of a change to a storage area, which the storage events for it carry.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct StorageChange {
    key: Option<Utf16String>,
    old_value: Option<Utf16String>,
    new_value: Option<Utf16String>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    url: UsvString,
}

static STORAGE_CHANGE_CLASS: EmbedderClass<StorageChange> = EmbedderClass::new("StorageChange");

impl EmbedderValue for StorageChange {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &STORAGE_CHANGE_CLASS;
}

/// The Storage object that the Window's localStorage or sessionStorage getter returns, if it does not throw.
fn window_storage(window: &CppWindow, storage_type: StorageType) -> Option<Ref<Storage>> {
    // SAFETY: The Window is live, and LibWeb returns null or the live cell of a Storage object.
    let storage = unsafe { web_html_window_storage(window.as_ptr(), storage_type as u8) };
    // SAFETY: A non-null pointer is the live cell of a Storage object.
    (!storage.is_null()).then(|| unsafe { cell_from_abi::<Storage>(storage) })
}

/// Fires the storage events for a change to a storage area of the type with the storage key, made by the script of
/// excluded_storage when the change was made in this process: steps 3 and 4 of broadcast.
///
/// NB: The map lives in the browser process and is mirrored here; the mirror tells the browser of a change made here,
///     and the browser relays it to every other process mirroring the map, where these steps run with no
///     excluded_storage. session_page is the page of the change's traversable navigable, for a "session" type.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "a change has these parts")]
pub(crate) fn dispatch_storage_events(
    vm: &Vm,
    storage_type: StorageType,
    storage_key: &StorageKey,
    session_page: Option<u64>,
    key: Option<Utf16String>,
    old_value: Option<Utf16String>,
    new_value: Option<Utf16String>,
    url: &str,
    excluded_storage: Option<Ref<Storage>>,
) {
    // 3. Let remoteStorages be all Storage objects excluding storage whose:
    let remote_storages = MarkedVec::new(vm);

    // AD-HOC: The specification defines this by iterating over created Storage objects. However, Storage objects are
    //         created lazily when accessed through window.localStorage or window.sessionStorage. This means that events
    //         will not be fired to Windows who have not had these properties accessed - which is not expected.
    //         See: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10135. To solve this, we instead iterate over all active
    //         windows, and initialize any storage objects as part of this loop.
    let windows = active_windows(vm);
    for window in windows.values().iter() {
        // * type is storage's type
        let Some(storage) = window_storage(window, storage_type) else {
            continue;
        };

        // "excluding storage"
        if Some(storage) == excluded_storage {
            continue;
        }

        // * relevant settings object's origin is same origin with storage's relevant settings object's origin
        // NB: A storage key is an origin, and two keys are equal when their origins are same origin. Compared as the
        //     keys the bottles are kept under, so the file: documents that share one bottle hear each other.
        if obtain_a_storage_key(&storage.relevant_settings_object()).as_ref() != Some(storage_key) {
            continue;
        }

        // * and, if type is "session", whose relevant settings object's associated Document's node navigable's
        //   traversable navigable is thisDocument's node navigable's traversable navigable.
        // NB: A page's documents all belong to one traversable, so the page stands for the traversable here.
        if storage_type == StorageType::Session {
            // NB: It is possible the remote storage may have not been fully teared down immediately at the point it's
            //     document is made inactive.
            if window.associated_document().navigable().is_none() {
                continue;
            }

            if session_page != Some(window.page_id()) {
                continue;
            }
        }

        remote_storages.push(storage);
    }

    if remote_storages.is_empty() {
        return;
    }

    let change = STORAGE_CHANGE_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| StorageChange {
        key,
        old_value,
        new_value,
        url: UsvString::from_utf8(url),
    });

    // 4. For each remoteStorage of remoteStorages: queue a global task on the DOM manipulation task source given
    //    remoteStorage's relevant global object to fire an event named storage at remoteStorage's relevant global
    //    object, using StorageEvent, with key initialized to key, oldValue initialized to oldValue, newValue
    //    initialized to newValue, url initialized to url, and storageArea initialized to remoteStorage.
    for &remote_storage in remote_storages.values().iter() {
        let global: &Storage = &remote_storage;
        queue_a_global_task(
            vm,
            relevant_global_object(global),
            TaskSource::DOMManipulation,
            (remote_storage, change),
            |vm, (remote_storage, change)| {
                let event_init = StorageEventInit {
                    parent: EventInit {
                        bubbles: false,
                        cancelable: false,
                        composed: false,
                    },
                    key: change.key.clone(),
                    old_value: change.old_value.clone(),
                    new_value: change.new_value.clone(),
                    url: change.url.clone(),
                    storage_area: Some(remote_storage),
                };
                let event =
                    StorageEvent::create(vm, remote_storage.realm, &Utf16String::from_utf8("storage"), event_init);
                remote_storage.window().as_event_target().dispatch_event(event.event());
            },
        );
    }
}

impl Storage {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, storage_type: StorageType, map: StorageBottle) -> Ref<Storage> {
        allocate(vm, |_| Storage {
            realm,
            storage_type,
            map,
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn map(&self) -> &StorageBottle {
        &self.map
    }

    /// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#relevant-settings-object
    fn relevant_settings_object(&self) -> CppEnvironmentSettingsObject {
        relevant_settings_object(relevant_global_object(self))
    }

    /// The Window that is the relevant global object.
    fn window(&self) -> CppWindow {
        window_from_global_object(relevant_global_object(self)).expect("a Storage belongs to a Window")
    }

    /// The serialization of the URL of the associated Document of the relevant global object.
    fn document_url(&self) -> String {
        self.window()
            .associated_document()
            .url()
            .serialize(ExcludeFragment::No)
            .to_owned()
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#dom-storage-length
    pub(crate) fn length(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        // The length getter steps are to return this's map's size.
        Ok(u32::try_from(self.map.size()).expect("the quota keeps a map below 2^32 entries"))
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#dom-storage-key
    pub(crate) fn key(&self, _: &mut CallContext, index: u32) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Utf16String>> {
        // 1. If index is greater than or equal to this's map's size, then return null.
        // 2. Let keys be the result of running get the keys on this's map.
        // NB: We combine these steps so we don't have to do two IPC calls and cause a race condition if the storage bottle
        //     changes size between them.
        let keys = self.map.keys();

        // 3. Return keys[index].
        Ok(keys.into_iter().nth(index as usize))
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#dom-storage-getitem
    pub(crate) fn get_item(&self, _: &mut CallContext, key: Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Utf16String>> {
        // 1. If this's map[key] does not exist, then return null.
        // 2. Return this's map[key].
        Ok(self.map.get(&key))
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#dom-storage-setitem
    pub(crate) fn set_item(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        key: Utf16String,
        value: Utf16String,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let oldValue be null.
        // 2. Let reorder be true.
        let mut reorder = true;

        // 3. If this's map[key] exists:
        //     1. Set oldValue to this's map[key].
        //     2. If oldValue is value, then return.
        //     3. Set reorder to false.
        // 4. If value cannot be stored, then throw a "QuotaExceededError" DOMException.
        // 5. Set this's map[key] to value.

        let url = this.document_url();
        let Ok(old_value) = this.map.set(&key, &value, &url) else {
            return Err(this.quota_exceeded_error(cx));
        };

        if let Some(old_value) = &old_value {
            if *old_value == value {
                return Ok(());
            }

            reorder = false;
        }

        // 6. If reorder is true, then reorder this.
        if reorder {
            this.reorder();
        }

        // 7. Broadcast this with key, oldValue, and value.
        Self::broadcast(this, cx.vm(), Some(key), old_value, Some(value), &url);

        Ok(())
    }

    fn quota_exceeded_error(&self, cx: &CallContext) -> Exception {
        let quota = self.map.quota().expect("a bottle that refuses a value has a quota");
        let fields = QuotaExceededErrorFields {
            dom_exception: DOMExceptionFields {
                name: Utf16String::from_utf8("QuotaExceededError"),
                message: Utf16String::from_utf8(&format!("Unable to store more than {quota} bytes in storage")),
            },
            quota: None,
            requested: None,
        };
        Exception::Thrown(Throw::new(Value::from_object(quota_exceeded_error::create(
            cx.realm(),
            &fields,
        ))))
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#dom-storage-removeitem
    pub(crate) fn remove_item(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext, key: Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If this's map[key] does not exist, then return.
        // 2. Set oldValue to this's map[key].
        let Some(old_value) = this.map.get(&key) else {
            return Ok(());
        };

        // 3. Remove this's map[key].
        let url = this.document_url();
        this.map.remove(&key, &url);

        // 4. Reorder this.
        this.reorder();

        // 5. Broadcast this with key, oldValue, and null.
        Self::broadcast(this, cx.vm(), Some(key), Some(old_value), None, &url);

        Ok(())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#dom-storage-clear
    pub(crate) fn clear(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If this's map is empty, then return.
        if this.map.size() == 0 {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 2. Clear this's map.
        let url = this.document_url();
        this.map.clear(&url);

        // 3. Broadcast this with null, null, and null.
        Self::broadcast(this, cx.vm(), None, None, None, &url);

        Ok(())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#concept-storage-reorder
    #[allow(
        clippy::unused_self,
        reason = "reordering is implementation-defined, and does nothing here"
    )]
    fn reorder(&self) {
        // To reorder a Storage object storage, reorder storage's map's entries in an implementation-defined manner.
        // NOTE: This basically means that we're not required to maintain any particular iteration order.
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html#concept-storage-broadcast
    fn broadcast(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        vm: &Vm,
        key: Option<Utf16String>,
        old_value: Option<Utf16String>,
        new_value: Option<Utf16String>,
        url: &str,
    ) {
        // 1. Let thisDocument be storage's relevant global object's associated Document.
        // 2. Let url be the serialization of thisDocument's URL.
        // NB: The caller serialized it, for the bottle; it is the same document's URL.

        // NB: The key the bottle is kept under, not the bare origin: Every file: document shares one bottle (see "obtain
        //     a storage key"), so each hears the others' changes. A window that has no key has no bottle to have written.
        let Some(storage_key) = obtain_a_storage_key(&this.relevant_settings_object()) else {
            return;
        };
        let session_page = (this.storage_type == StorageType::Session).then(|| this.window().page_id());

        // Steps 3 and 4.
        dispatch_storage_events(
            vm,
            this.storage_type,
            &storage_key,
            session_page,
            key,
            old_value,
            new_value,
            url,
            Some(*this),
        );
    }

    pub(crate) fn supported_property_names(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> Vec<Utf16String> {
        // The supported property names on a Storage object storage are the result of running get the keys on storage's
        // map.
        self.map.keys()
    }
}

fn object_into_abi<T>(object: Gc<T>) -> *mut c_void {
    object.as_ptr().cast()
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `object` must be a live object or null.
unsafe fn object_from_abi(object: *mut c_void) -> Option<Gc<Object>> {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live object or null.
    NonNull::new(object.cast::<Object>()).map(|object| unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(object) })
}

fn completion(result: RawNativeFunctionResult) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    Ok(result.into_completion()?)
}

/// The values of an array of objects, as the C ABI takes them.
pub(crate) fn objects_into_abi<T>(objects: &[Gc<T>]) -> Vec<*mut c_void> {
    objects.iter().map(|object| object_into_abi(*object)).collect()
}

/// An HTML::IPCSerializationRecord that C++ lends for a serialization to set.
pub(crate) struct IPCSerializationRecord(NonNull<c_void>);

impl IPCSerializationRecord {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `record` must be a record that C++ lends while this is used.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_raw(record: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        Self(NonNull::new(record).expect("C++ lends a record"))
    }

    /// Sets the record to the bytes, with the SharedArrayBuffers of its same-agent side table.
    pub(crate) fn set(self, data: &[u8], shared_array_buffers: &[Gc<ArrayBuffer>]) {
        let shared_array_buffers = objects_into_abi(shared_array_buffers);
        // SAFETY: The record is lent, the call borrows the bytes, and the buffers are live.
        unsafe {
            web_structured_serialize_set_ipc_record(
                self.0.as_ptr(),
                ak::Span::new(data),
                shared_array_buffers.as_ptr(),
                shared_array_buffers.len(),
            );
        }
    }
}

/// An HTML::StorageSerializationRecord that C++ lends for a serialization to set.
pub(crate) struct StorageSerializationRecord(NonNull<c_void>);

impl StorageSerializationRecord {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `record` must be a record that C++ lends while this is used.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_raw(record: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        Self(NonNull::new(record).expect("C++ lends a record"))
    }

    pub(crate) fn set(self, data: &[u8]) {
        // SAFETY: The record is lent, and the call borrows the bytes.
        unsafe { web_structured_serialize_set_storage_record(self.0.as_ptr(), ak::Span::new(data)) };
    }
}

/// An HTML::IPCSerializationRecord that C++ lends for a deserialization to read.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct ReceivedIPCSerializationRecord<'a> {
    raw: NonNull<c_void>,
    _lent: PhantomData<&'a c_void>,
}

impl<'a> ReceivedIPCSerializationRecord<'a> {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `record` must be a record that C++ lends for `'a`.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_raw(record: *const c_void) -> Self {
        Self {
            raw: NonNull::new(record.cast_mut()).expect("C++ lends a record"),
            _lent: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn data(self) -> &'a [u8] {
        let mut data = ak::Span::default();
        // SAFETY: The record is lent for 'a, and its bytes with it.
        unsafe { web_structured_serialize_ipc_record_data(self.raw.as_ptr(), &mut data) };
        data.as_slice()
    }

    /// The SharedArrayBuffer at the index of the record's same-agent side table, if there is one.
    pub(crate) fn shared_array_buffer(self, side_table_index: u32) -> Option<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
        // SAFETY: The record is lent. LibWeb returns a live object or null.
        let object = unsafe {
            object_from_abi(web_structured_serialize_ipc_record_shared_array_buffer(
                self.raw.as_ptr(),
                side_table_index,
            ))
        }?;
        Some(
            object
                .downcast::<ArrayBuffer>()
                .expect("the side table holds ArrayBuffers"),
        )
    }
}

/// AD-HOC: Gathers the pixels of the ImageBitmaps of the transfer list in one buffer of shared memory, whose index in
///         the shared memory of the record of the transfer is the buffer index. Without it, as when there is not enough
///         memory for it, the pixels travel inline.
pub(crate) fn gather_image_bitmap_pixels(
    transfer_list: &[Gc<Object>],
    buffer_index: u32,
) -> (ImageBitmapSharedPixels, Option<SharedMemory>) {
    let transfer_list = objects_into_abi(transfer_list);
    let (mut descriptor, mut size) = (0, 0);
    // SAFETY: The objects are live, and the call writes to the locals.
    let pixels = ImageBitmapSharedPixels(NonNull::new(unsafe {
        web_structured_serialize_gather_image_bitmap_pixels(
            transfer_list.as_ptr(),
            transfer_list.len(),
            buffer_index,
            &mut descriptor,
            &mut size,
        )
    }));
    if pixels.0.is_none() {
        return (pixels, None);
    }
    // SAFETY: The pixels keep the descriptor open.
    match unsafe { SharedMemory::duplicate(descriptor, size) } {
        Some(shared_memory) => (pixels, Some(shared_memory)),
        // NB: Without a descriptor for the record, the pixels travel inline.
        None => (ImageBitmapSharedPixels(None), None),
    }
}

/// data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(): the "DataCloneError" DOMException in the realm for a record that does
/// not hold what deserializing it reads.
pub(crate) fn data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(realm: Gc<Realm>, message: &str) -> Exception {
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the message is lent for the call.
    let result = completion(unsafe {
        web_structured_serialize_data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(
            realm.as_ptr().cast(),
            ak::Span::new(message.as_bytes()),
        )
    });
    match result {
        Err(exception) => exception,
        Ok(_) => unreachable!("the helper throws"),
    }
}

/// The shared memory that the ImageBitmaps of a record share their pixels through, mapped when one needs it.
pub(crate) struct SharedPixelBuffers<'a> {
    memory: &'a [SharedMemory],
    buffers: core::cell::Cell<Option<NonNull<c_void>>>,
}

impl<'a> SharedPixelBuffers<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn new(memory: &'a [SharedMemory]) -> Self {
        Self {
            memory,
            buffers: core::cell::Cell::new(None),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn as_raw(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        if let Some(buffers) = self.buffers.get() {
            return Some(buffers);
        }
        let descriptors: Vec<_> = self
            .memory
            .iter()
            .map(|memory| raw_descriptor(memory.descriptor.as_shared_memory()))
            .collect();
        let sizes: Vec<_> = self.memory.iter().map(|memory| memory.size).collect();
        // SAFETY: The call borrows the open descriptors and their sizes, and hands over the buffer list.
        let buffers = NonNull::new(unsafe {
            web_structured_serialize_shared_pixels_create(descriptors.as_ptr(), sizes.as_ptr(), descriptors.len())
        });
        self.buffers.set(buffers);
        buffers
    }
}

impl Drop for SharedPixelBuffers<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(buffers) = self.buffers.get() {
            // SAFETY: This owns the list. Each image keeps its own reference to the buffers it uses.
            unsafe { web_structured_serialize_shared_pixels_destroy(buffers.as_ptr()) };
        }
    }
}

//! The entry points through which LibWeb's C++ code runs structured serialization: the functions of
//! Libraries/LibWeb/HTML/StructuredSerialize.h, which keep their C++ signatures for the C++ code that calls them.

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, MarkedVec, Object, RawNativeFunctionResult, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr, Value, Vm};
use libwebcommon_rust::html::serialization_records::SerializationType;

use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::cpp::{
    IPCSerializationRecord, ReceivedIPCSerializationRecord, SerializedTransferRecord, StorageSerializationRecord,
    TransferredValues,
};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::memory::{DeserializationMemory, SerializationMemory};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::reader::StructuredSerializeReader;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::transfer_record::TransferRecord;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::writer::StructuredSerializeWriter;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::{
    AllowSharedArrayBuffers, structured_deserialize_internal, structured_deserialize_with_transfer,
    structured_serialize_internal, structured_serialize_with_transfer,
};

/// The completion of an algorithm, as the entry points return it to C++.
fn completion(cx: &CallContext, result: WebIdlResult<Value>) -> RawNativeFunctionResult {
    let result: ThrowCompletionOr<Value> = result.map_err(|exception| exception.throw(cx));
    RawNativeFunctionResult::from_completion(result)
}

/// StructuredSerializeInternal(value, forStorage) in the current realm, with a new memory.
fn structured_serialize_in_current_realm<'vm>(
    vm: &'vm Vm,
    serialized: &StructuredSerializeWriter<'vm>,
    value: Value,
    for_storage: bool,
    allow_shared_array_buffers: AllowSharedArrayBuffers,
) -> Result<(), RawNativeFunctionResult> {
    let memory = SerializationMemory::new(vm);
    // NB: Code outside of any script serializes values too, with no current realm. An object's exception is created in
    //     its realm then; a Symbol throws too, but only script serializes one.
    let realm = vm
        .current_realm()
        .or_else(|| value.is_object().then(|| value.as_object().shape().realm()));
    structured_serialize_internal(
        vm,
        realm,
        serialized,
        value,
        for_storage,
        &memory,
        allow_shared_array_buffers,
    )
    .map_err(|exception| {
        let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm.expect("what throws has a realm"));
        completion(&cx, Err(exception))
    })
}

/// StructuredSerialize, which runs in the current realm, and sets the record.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the VM and a record that C++ lends. The value must be live.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_structured_serialize(
    vm: &Vm,
    value: Value,
    allow_shared_array_buffers: u8,
    record: *mut c_void,
) -> RawNativeFunctionResult {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live value, and lends the record.
    let record = unsafe { IPCSerializationRecord::from_raw(record) };
    let serialized = StructuredSerializeWriter::new(vm, SerializationType::Ipc);
    if let Err(result) = structured_serialize_in_current_realm(
        vm,
        &serialized,
        value,
        false,
        AllowSharedArrayBuffers::from_abi(allow_shared_array_buffers),
    ) {
        return result;
    }
    serialized.finish_ipc_record(record);
    RawNativeFunctionResult::from_completion(Ok(Value::UNDEFINED))
}

/// StructuredSerializeForStorage, which runs in the current realm, and sets the record.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the VM and a record that C++ lends. The value must be live.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_structured_serialize_for_storage(
    vm: &Vm,
    value: Value,
    record: *mut c_void,
) -> RawNativeFunctionResult {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live value, and lends the record.
    let record = unsafe { StorageSerializationRecord::from_raw(record) };
    let serialized = StructuredSerializeWriter::new(vm, SerializationType::Storage);
    if let Err(result) = structured_serialize_in_current_realm(
        vm,
        &serialized,
        value,
        true,
        AllowSharedArrayBuffers::CrossOriginIsolatedOnly,
    ) {
        return result;
    }
    serialized.finish_storage_record(record);
    RawNativeFunctionResult::from_completion(Ok(Value::UNDEFINED))
}

/// StructuredDeserialize of the IPC record in the realm.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the VM, a live realm, and a record that C++ lends.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_structured_deserialize(
    vm: &Vm,
    target_realm: Gc<Realm>,
    record: *const c_void,
) -> RawNativeFunctionResult {
    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, target_realm);
    // SAFETY: The caller lends the record.
    let record = unsafe { ReceivedIPCSerializationRecord::from_raw(record) };
    let serialized = StructuredSerializeReader::new_ipc(target_realm, record);
    let memory = DeserializationMemory::new(vm);
    completion(&cx, structured_deserialize_internal(&cx, &serialized, &memory, false))
}

/// StructuredDeserialize of the bytes of the storage record in the realm, which throws a "DataCloneError" DOMException
/// for bytes after its value.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_structured_deserialize_for_storage(
    vm: &Vm,
    target_realm: Gc<Realm>,
    data: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
) -> RawNativeFunctionResult {
    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, target_realm);
    let result = StructuredSerializeReader::new_storage(target_realm, data.as_slice()).and_then(|serialized| {
        let memory = DeserializationMemory::new(vm);
        structured_deserialize_internal(&cx, &serialized, &memory, true)
    });
    completion(&cx, result)
}

/// StructuredSerializeWithTransfer in the realm, whose record the caller owns.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the VM, a live realm, and `count` live objects. The value must be live.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_structured_serialize_with_transfer(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    value: Value,
    transfer_list: *const *mut c_void,
    count: usize,
    out_record: &mut *mut c_void,
) -> RawNativeFunctionResult {
    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);
    let transfer_list_values = MarkedVec::with_capacity(vm, count);
    for index in 0..count {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes `count` live objects.
        transfer_list_values.push(unsafe {
            Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new((*transfer_list.add(index)).cast::<Object>()).expect("C++ passes objects"))
        });
    }
    let result = structured_serialize_with_transfer(&cx, value, &transfer_list_values.values());
    completion(
        &cx,
        result.map(|record| {
            *out_record = TransferRecord::into_cpp(record, vm).into_raw();
            Value::UNDEFINED
        }),
    )
}

/// StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer in the realm, which returns [[Deserialized]], and appends [[TransferredValues]] to
/// the list.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the VM, a live realm, and a record and a list that C++ lends.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_structured_deserialize_with_transfer(
    vm: &Vm,
    target_realm: Gc<Realm>,
    record: *mut c_void,
    transferred_values: *mut c_void,
) -> RawNativeFunctionResult {
    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, target_realm);
    // SAFETY: The caller lends the record and the list.
    let (record, transferred_values) = unsafe {
        (
            SerializedTransferRecord::from_raw(record),
            TransferredValues::from_raw(transferred_values),
        )
    };
    let record = TransferRecord::from_cpp(vm, record);
    let result = structured_deserialize_with_transfer(&cx, record);
    TransferRecord::discard(record);
    completion(
        &cx,
        result.map(|deserialize_record| {
            for value in deserialize_record.transferred_values.values().iter() {
                transferred_values.append(*value);
            }
            deserialize_record.deserialized
        }),
    )
}

/// # Safety
///
/// The callback must accept the context and an identifier of static storage.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_serializable_storage_registry(
    context: *mut c_void,
    append: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u16, ak::Span<'static, u8>),
) {
    for entry in super::serializable::STORAGE_INTERFACES {
        // SAFETY: The caller lends its context to its callback.
        unsafe { append(context, entry.interface_name, ak::Span::new(entry.identifier)) };
    }
}

//! The memories of structured serializations and deserializations.

use core::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::HashMap;

use libjs_rust::api::{MarkedVec, Value, Vm};

pub(crate) struct SerializationMemory<'vm> {
    values: MarkedVec<'vm, Value>,
    positions: RefCell<HashMap<u64, u32>>,
}

impl<'vm> SerializationMemory<'vm> {
    pub(crate) fn new(vm: &'vm Vm) -> Self {
        Self {
            values: MarkedVec::new(vm),
            positions: RefCell::new(HashMap::new()),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn get(&self, value: Value) -> Option<u32> {
        self.positions.borrow().get(&value.to_raw()).copied()
    }

    pub(crate) fn contains(&self, value: Value) -> bool {
        self.get(value).is_some()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set(&self, value: Value, index: u32) {
        if self.positions.borrow_mut().insert(value.to_raw(), index).is_none() {
            self.values.push(value);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn size(&self) -> u32 {
        u32::try_from(self.positions.borrow().len()).expect("a serialization has fewer than 2^32 values")
    }
}

pub(crate) struct DeserializationMemory<'vm> {
    values: MarkedVec<'vm, Value>,
}

impl<'vm> DeserializationMemory<'vm> {
    pub(crate) fn new(vm: &'vm Vm) -> Self {
        Self {
            values: MarkedVec::new(vm),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn size(&self) -> usize {
        self.values.len()
    }

    pub(crate) fn append(&self, value: Value) {
        self.values.push(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Value {
        self.values.get(index).expect("the memory has a value at the index")
    }

    pub(crate) fn set(&self, index: usize, value: Value) {
        self.values.set(index, value);
    }
}

/*

//! The record of a message that may reach agents in other processes, which Rust owns: the bytes of the values, the
//! SharedArrayBuffers that agents in this agent's realms share, the pin of the stores that the bytes name, and the
//! shared memory that hands the pixels of ImageBitmaps over.
//! C++ sees the record only when it is sent to or received from other processes.

use core::ffi::c_int;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    ArrayBuffer, DeferGc, Gc, OwnedSharedMemory, SharedStorePin, Trace, borrowed_from_raw_descriptor,
    duplicate_lifeline_from_raw_descriptor, lifeline_into_raw_descriptor,
};

pub(crate) struct SharedMemory {
    pub(crate) descriptor: OwnedSharedMemory,
    pub(crate) size: usize,
}

impl SharedMemory {
    /// A duplicate of a descriptor that C++ lends, unless it cannot be duplicated.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The descriptor must stay open for the call.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn duplicate(descriptor: c_int, size: usize) -> Option<Self> {
        // SAFETY: The caller keeps the descriptor open.
        let descriptor = unsafe { borrowed_from_raw_descriptor(descriptor) }
            .try_clone_to_owned()
            .ok()?;
        Some(Self { descriptor, size })
    }
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct MessageRecord {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) bytes: Vec<u8>,
    /// The same-agent side table, by index from the bytes.
    pub(crate) shared_array_buffers: Vec<Gc<ArrayBuffer>>,
    /// The shared memory of ImageBitmap pixels, by index from the data holders.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) shared_memory: Vec<SharedMemory>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) shared_store_pin: Option<SharedStorePin>,
}

impl MessageRecord {
    /// A record that another process sent, for the caller to allocate a cell with under the deferral. A lifeline that
    /// cannot be duplicated is left out, so that the stores it would keep may be gone, which deserializing throws for.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// Each descriptor must stay open for the call, and so must the one of the lifeline, if it is not negative.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn received(
        _: &DeferGc<'_>,
        bytes: &[u8],
        descriptors: &[c_int],
        sizes: &[usize],
        shared_store_lifeline: c_int,
    ) -> Self {
        let shared_memory = descriptors
            .iter()
            .zip(sizes)
            // SAFETY: The caller keeps the descriptors open.
            .map_while(|(&descriptor, &size)| unsafe { SharedMemory::duplicate(descriptor, size) })
            .collect();
        Self {
            bytes: bytes.to_vec(),
            shared_array_buffers: Vec::new(),
            shared_memory,
            // SAFETY: The caller keeps the descriptor open.
            shared_store_pin: (shared_store_lifeline >= 0)
                .then(|| unsafe { duplicate_lifeline_from_raw_descriptor(shared_store_lifeline) }.ok())
                .flatten()
                .map(SharedStorePin::Lifeline),
        }
    }

    /// The descriptor of a lifeline for the stores, which the caller owns, or a negative value for no lifeline, for
    /// sending the record to other processes.
    pub(crate) fn duplicate_shared_store_lifeline(&self) -> c_int {
        self.shared_store_pin
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(SharedStorePin::duplicate_lifeline)
            .map_or(-1, lifeline_into_raw_descriptor)
    }
}

impl Drop for MessageRecord {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(pin) = self.shared_store_pin.take() {
            pin.release();
        }
    }
}

/// HTML::ValueTag, the tags of the values of a record, which are part of the stable storage serialization format.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum ValueTag {
    UndefinedPrimitive = 1,
    NullPrimitive = 2,
    BooleanPrimitive = 3,
    NumberPrimitive = 4,
    StringPrimitive = 5,
    BigIntPrimitive = 6,
    BooleanObject = 7,
    NumberObject = 8,
    StringObject = 9,
    BigIntObject = 10,
    DateObject = 11,
    RegExpObject = 12,
    MapObject = 13,
    SetObject = 14,
    ArrayObject = 15,
    ErrorObject = 16,
    Object = 17,
    ObjectReference = 18,
    GrowableSharedArrayBuffer = 19,
    SharedArrayBuffer = 20,
    ResizeableArrayBuffer = 21,
    ArrayBuffer = 22,
    ArrayBufferView = 23,
    SerializableObject = 24,
    Int32Primitive = 25,
    EndObject = 0xFF,
}

impl ValueTag {
    /// The tag of a value with the raw value, if values can have it: only tags listed here decode as values, as
    /// value_tag_is_decodable() says. Empty and EndObject are reserved.
    fn decodable_from(raw_tag: u8) -> Option<Self> {
        Some(match raw_tag {
            1 => Self::UndefinedPrimitive,
            2 => Self::NullPrimitive,
            3 => Self::BooleanPrimitive,
            4 => Self::NumberPrimitive,
            5 => Self::StringPrimitive,
            6 => Self::BigIntPrimitive,
            7 => Self::BooleanObject,
            8 => Self::NumberObject,
            9 => Self::StringObject,
            10 => Self::BigIntObject,
            11 => Self::DateObject,
            12 => Self::RegExpObject,
            13 => Self::MapObject,
            14 => Self::SetObject,
            15 => Self::ArrayObject,
            16 => Self::ErrorObject,
            17 => Self::Object,
            18 => Self::ObjectReference,
            19 => Self::GrowableSharedArrayBuffer,
            20 => Self::SharedArrayBuffer,
            21 => Self::ResizeableArrayBuffer,
            22 => Self::ArrayBuffer,
            23 => Self::ArrayBufferView,
            24 => Self::SerializableObject,
            25 => Self::Int32Primitive,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }
}

/// The types of the data holders of a transfer, which only IPC carries.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum TransferType {
    MessagePort = 1,
    ArrayBuffer = 2,
    ResizableArrayBuffer = 3,
    ReadableStream = 4,
    WritableStream = 5,
    TransformStream = 6,
    ImageBitmap = 7,
    OffscreenCanvas = 8,
}

impl TransferType {
    fn from_u8(value: u8) -> Option<Self> {
        Some(match value {
            1 => Self::MessagePort,
            2 => Self::ArrayBuffer,
            3 => Self::ResizableArrayBuffer,
            4 => Self::ReadableStream,
            5 => Self::WritableStream,
            6 => Self::TransformStream,
            7 => Self::ImageBitmap,
            8 => Self::OffscreenCanvas,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }
}

/// A platform object that is a transferable object, which has a [[Detached]] internal slot.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum TransferablePlatformObject {
    MessagePort(Ref<MessagePort>),
    ReadableStream(Ref<ReadableStream>),
    WritableStream(Ref<WritableStream>),
    TransformStream(Ref<TransformStream>),
    ImageBitmap(Ref<ImageBitmap>),
    OffscreenCanvas(Gc<Object>),
}

impl TransferablePlatformObject {
    fn from_object(object: Gc<Object>) -> Option<Self> {
        if let Some(port) = implementation_if_wrapper(object) {
            return Some(Self::MessagePort(port));
        }
        if let Some(stream) = implementation_if_wrapper(object) {
            return Some(Self::ReadableStream(stream));
        }
        if let Some(stream) = implementation_if_wrapper(object) {
            return Some(Self::WritableStream(stream));
        }
        if let Some(stream) = implementation_if_wrapper(object) {
            return Some(Self::TransformStream(stream));
        }
        if let Some(image_bitmap) = implementation_if_wrapper(object) {
            return Some(Self::ImageBitmap(image_bitmap));
        }
        offscreen_canvas::is_offscreen_canvas(object).then_some(Self::OffscreenCanvas(object))
    }

    /// The identifier of the primary interface of the object.
    fn primary_interface(self) -> TransferType {
        match self {
            Self::MessagePort(_) => TransferType::MessagePort,
            Self::ReadableStream(_) => TransferType::ReadableStream,
            Self::WritableStream(_) => TransferType::WritableStream,
            Self::TransformStream(_) => TransferType::TransformStream,
            Self::ImageBitmap(_) => TransferType::ImageBitmap,
            Self::OffscreenCanvas(_) => TransferType::OffscreenCanvas,
        }
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#detached
    fn is_detached(self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::MessagePort(port) => port.detached().get(),
            Self::ReadableStream(stream) => stream.detached().get(),
            Self::WritableStream(stream) => stream.detached().get(),
            Self::TransformStream(stream) => stream.detached().get(),
            Self::ImageBitmap(image_bitmap) => image_bitmap.detached().get(),
            Self::OffscreenCanvas(object) => offscreen_canvas::is_detached(object),
        }
    }

    fn set_detached(self) {
        match self {
            Self::MessagePort(port) => port.detached().set(true),
            Self::ReadableStream(stream) => stream.detached().set(true),
            Self::WritableStream(stream) => stream.detached().set(true),
            Self::TransformStream(stream) => stream.detached().set(true),
            Self::ImageBitmap(image_bitmap) => image_bitmap.detached().set(true),
            // NB: The [[Detached]] internal slot of an OffscreenCanvas is its detached context mode, which its transfer
            //     steps set.
            Self::OffscreenCanvas(_) => {}
        }
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#transfer-steps
    fn transfer_steps(self, cx: &mut CallContext, data_holder: &mut TransferDataWriter) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        match self {
            Self::MessagePort(port) => MessagePort::transfer_steps(&port, cx, data_holder),
            Self::ReadableStream(stream) => ReadableStream::transfer_steps(&stream, cx, data_holder),
            Self::WritableStream(stream) => WritableStream::transfer_steps(&stream, cx, data_holder),
            Self::TransformStream(stream) => TransformStream::transfer_steps(&stream, cx, data_holder),
            Self::ImageBitmap(image_bitmap) => ImageBitmap::transfer_steps(&image_bitmap, cx, data_holder),
            Self::OffscreenCanvas(object) => offscreen_canvas::transfer_steps(object, data_holder),
        }
    }
}

/// Web::Bindings::InterfaceName of the interface that the type of a data holder identifies, if it identifies one.
fn transferable_interface_name(transfer_type: TransferType) -> Option<u16> {
    Some(match transfer_type {
        TransferType::MessagePort => MessagePort::INTERFACE_NAME,
        TransferType::ReadableStream => ReadableStream::INTERFACE_NAME,
        TransferType::WritableStream => WritableStream::INTERFACE_NAME,
        TransferType::TransformStream => TransformStream::INTERFACE_NAME,
        TransferType::ImageBitmap => ImageBitmap::INTERFACE_NAME,
        TransferType::OffscreenCanvas => offscreen_canvas::interface_name(),
        TransferType::ArrayBuffer | TransferType::ResizableArrayBuffer => return None,
    })
}

/// The wrapper of a new object of `T` in the realm of the data holder, after the transfer-receiving steps of `T`.
fn receive_transferred<T: Transferable>(cx: &CallContext, data_holder: &mut TransferDataReader) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    let mut cx = CallContext::new(cx.vm(), data_holder.realm());
    let object = T::transfer_receiving_steps(&mut cx, data_holder)?;
    Ok(Value::from_object(wrap(&cx, object)))
}

/// Error, followed by the native errors of LibJS, in the order of JS_ENUMERATE_NATIVE_ERRORS, which IPC records hold.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum ErrorType {
    Error,
    EvalError,
    InternalError,
    RangeError,
    ReferenceError,
    SyntaxError,
    TypeError,
    URIError,
}

const NATIVE_ERROR_TYPES: [(ErrorType, &str); 7] = [
    (ErrorType::EvalError, "EvalError"),
    (ErrorType::InternalError, "InternalError"),
    (ErrorType::RangeError, "RangeError"),
    (ErrorType::ReferenceError, "ReferenceError"),
    (ErrorType::SyntaxError, "SyntaxError"),
    (ErrorType::TypeError, "TypeError"),
    (ErrorType::URIError, "URIError"),
];

fn error_type_to_name(error_type: ErrorType) -> &'static str {
    if error_type == ErrorType::Error {
        return "Error";
    }
    NATIVE_ERROR_TYPES
        .iter()
        .find(|(native_error_type, _)| *native_error_type == error_type)
        .map(|(_, name)| *name)
        .expect("every error type has a name")
}

fn error_type_from_ipc(raw_error_type: u8) -> Option<ErrorType> {
    Some(match raw_error_type {
        0 => ErrorType::Error,
        1 => ErrorType::EvalError,
        2 => ErrorType::InternalError,
        3 => ErrorType::RangeError,
        4 => ErrorType::ReferenceError,
        5 => ErrorType::SyntaxError,
        6 => ErrorType::TypeError,
        7 => ErrorType::URIError,
        _ => return None,
    })
}
