        }
        // 5. Otherwise:
        else {
            // 1. Assert: transferable is a platform object that is a transferable object.
            let platform_object = platform_object.expect("transferable is a transferable object");
            assert!(transferable.is_platform_object());

            // 2. Let interfaceName be the identifier of the primary interface of transferable.
            let interface_name = platform_object.primary_interface();

            // 3. Set dataHolder.[[Type]] to interfaceName.
            data_holder.encode(&(interface_name as u8));

            // FIXME: 4. If transferable's primary interface is decorated with [SameAgentCluster], then restrict dataHolder to the same agent cluster.

            // 5. Perform the appropriate transfer steps for the interface identified by interfaceName, given transferable and dataHolder.
            let mut steps_cx = CallContext::new(vm, cx.realm());
            let mut writer = TransferDataWriter::new(&data_holder, cx.realm(), Some(&image_bitmap_pixels));
            platform_object.transfer_steps(&mut steps_cx, &mut writer)?;

            // 6. Set transferable.[[Detached]] to true.
            platform_object.set_detached();
        }

        // 6. Append dataHolder to transferDataHolders.
        transfer_data_holders.push(data_holder.finish());
    }

    // 6. Let result be { [[Serialized]]: serialized, [[TransferDataHolders]]: transferDataHolders, [[InterfaceNames]]: an empty ordered set, [[AgentCluster]]: null }.
    let result = TransferRecord::create(
        vm,
        |defer_gc| serialized.finish_message_record(defer_gc),
        transfer_data_holders,
    );

    // FIXME: 7. For each object → record of memory:
    //     1. If object is a platform object, then append record.[[Type]] to result.[[InterfaceNames]].
    //     2. If record.[[AgentCluster]] is not null, then restrict result to the same agent cluster.

    // 8. Return result.
    Ok(result)
}

/// The record that StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer returns,
/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#structureddeserializewithtransfer
pub(crate) struct DeserializedTransferRecord<'vm> {
    /// [[Deserialized]], the deserialized value.
    pub(crate) deserialized: Value,
    /// [[TransferredValues]], the transferred objects in the order of their data holders.
    pub(crate) transferred_values: MarkedVec<'vm, Gc<Object>>,
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#structureddeserializewithtransfer
pub(crate) fn structured_deserialize_with_transfer<'vm>(
    cx: &CallContext<'vm>,
    serialize_with_transfer_result: TransferRecordRef,
) -> WebIdlResult<DeserializedTransferRecord<'vm>> {
    let target_realm = cx.realm();

    // 1. Let memory be an empty map.
    let memory = DeserializationMemory::new(cx.vm());

    // FIXME: 2. If serializeWithTransferResult.[[AgentCluster]] is not null and targetRealm's corresponding agent cluster is not serializeWithTransferResult.[[AgentCluster]], then throw a "DataCloneError" DOMException.
    // FIXME: 3. For each interfaceName of serializeWithTransferResult.[[InterfaceNames]]:
    //     1. If the interface identified by interfaceName is not exposed in targetRealm, then throw a "DataCloneError" DOMException.

    // 4. Let transferredValues be a new empty List.
    let transferred_values = MarkedVec::new(cx.vm());

    let serialized = serialize_with_transfer_result.serialized.borrow();
    let serialized = serialized
        .as_ref()
        .ok_or_else(|| data_clone_error("Empty transfer record"))?;
    let shared_pixels = SharedPixelBuffers::new(&serialized.shared_memory);

    // 5. For each transferDataHolder of serializeWithTransferResult.[[TransferDataHolders]]:
    let transfer_data_holders = core::mem::take(&mut *serialize_with_transfer_result.data_holders.borrow_mut());
    for mut transfer_data_holder in transfer_data_holders {
        // NB: The transfer writes no empty data holder.
        if transfer_data_holder.bytes.is_empty() {
            return Err(data_clone_error("Empty transfer data holder"));
        }
        let mut data_holder =
            TransferDataReader::with_shared_pixels(&mut transfer_data_holder, target_realm, &shared_pixels);

        // 1. Let value be an uninitialized value.
        let value = structured_deserialize_with_transfer_internal(cx, &mut data_holder)?;

        // 5. Set memory[transferDataHolder] to value.
        memory.append(value);

        // 6. Append value to transferredValues.
        transferred_values.push(value.as_object());
    }

    // 6. Let deserialized be ? StructuredDeserialize(serializeWithTransferResult.[[Serialized]], targetRealm, memory).
    let serialized = StructuredSerializeReader::new_message(target_realm, serialized);
    let deserialized = with_temporary_execution_context(target_realm, || {
        structured_deserialize_internal(cx, &serialized, &memory, false)
    })?;

    // 7. Return { [[Deserialized]]: deserialized, [[TransferredValues]]: transferredValues }.
    Ok(DeserializedTransferRecord {
        deserialized,
        transferred_values,
    })
}

// AD-HOC: This non-standard overload is meant to extract just one transferrable value from a serialized transfer record.
//         It's primarily useful for an object's transfer receiving steps to deserialize a nested value.
pub(crate) fn structured_deserialize_with_transfer_internal(
    cx: &CallContext,
    data_holder: &mut TransferDataReader,
) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    let vm = cx.vm();
    let target_realm = cx.realm();

    let Some(transfer_type) = TransferType::from_u8(data_holder.read()?) else {
        return Err(data_clone_error("Unknown type transferred"));
    };

    // 1. Let value be an uninitialized value.
    #[allow(clippy::needless_late_init, reason = "the steps let value be uninitialized first")]
    let value: Value;

    // 2. If transferDataHolder.[[Type]] is "ArrayBuffer", then set value to a new ArrayBuffer object in targetRealm
    //    whose [[ArrayBufferData]] internal slot value is transferDataHolder.[[ArrayBufferData]], and
    //    whose [[ArrayBufferByteLength]] internal slot value is transferDataHolder.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]].
    // NOTE: In cases where the original memory occupied by [[ArrayBufferData]] is accessible during the deserialization,
    //       this step is unlikely to throw an exception, as no new memory needs to be allocated: the memory occupied by
    //       [[ArrayBufferData]] is instead just getting transferred into the new ArrayBuffer. This could be true, for example,
    //       when both the source and target realms are in the same process.
    if transfer_type == TransferType::ArrayBuffer {
        let bytes = data_holder.read_bytes()?;
        value = Value::from_object(array_buffer_from_bytes(vm, target_realm, bytes, ArrayBufferShared::No)?);
    }
    // 3. Otherwise, if transferDataHolder.[[Type]] is "ResizableArrayBuffer", then set value to a new ArrayBuffer object
    //     in targetRealm whose [[ArrayBufferData]] internal slot value is transferDataHolder.[[ArrayBufferData]], whose
    //     [[ArrayBufferByteLength]] internal slot value is transferDataHolder.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]], and whose
    //     [[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]] internal slot value is transferDataHolder.[[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]].
    // NOTE: For the same reason as the previous step, this step is also unlikely to throw an exception.
    else if transfer_type == TransferType::ResizableArrayBuffer {
        let bytes = data_holder.read_bytes()?;
        let max_byte_length = data_holder.read::<usize>()?;

        // NB: Creating a resizable buffer throws a RangeError if its byte length is greater than its max byte length.
        if max_byte_length < bytes.len() {
            return Err(data_clone_error("ArrayBuffer byte length exceeds its max byte length"));
        }

        let data = array_buffer_from_bytes(vm, target_realm, bytes, ArrayBufferShared::No)?;
        data.set_max_byte_length(max_byte_length);

        value = Value::from_object(data);
    }
    // 4. Otherwise:
    else {
        // 1. Let interfaceName be transferDataHolder.[[Type]].
        // NB: Step 3 of StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer checks that every transferred interface is exposed before any
        //     transfer-receiving steps run. The check runs here, per data holder, instead.
        let interface_name = transferable_interface_name(transfer_type).expect("the type names an interface");
        if !is_exposed(interface_name, target_realm) {
            return Err(data_clone_error("Unknown type transferred"));
        }

        // 2. Set value to a new instance of the interface identified by interfaceName, created in targetRealm.
        // 3. Perform the appropriate transfer-receiving steps for the interface identified by interfaceName given transferDataHolder and value.
        value = match transfer_type {
            TransferType::MessagePort => receive_transferred::<MessagePort>(cx, data_holder)?,
            TransferType::ReadableStream => receive_transferred::<ReadableStream>(cx, data_holder)?,
            TransferType::WritableStream => receive_transferred::<WritableStream>(cx, data_holder)?,
            TransferType::TransformStream => receive_transferred::<TransformStream>(cx, data_holder)?,
            TransferType::ImageBitmap => receive_transferred::<ImageBitmap>(cx, data_holder)?,
            TransferType::OffscreenCanvas => offscreen_canvas::create_from_transfer(data_holder)?,
            TransferType::ArrayBuffer | TransferType::ResizableArrayBuffer => {
                unreachable!("the type names an interface")
            }
        };
    }

    Ok(value)
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#structuredserialize
// AD-HOC: For a message that reaches agents in other processes, which names the stores of its SharedArrayBuffers. The
//         caller finishes the writer into a MessageRecord.
pub(crate) fn structured_serialize_for_message(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    value: Value,
) -> WebIdlResult<StructuredSerializeWriter<'_>> {
    let memory = SerializationMemory::new(vm);
    let serialized = StructuredSerializeWriter::new_for_message(vm);

    // 1. Return ? StructuredSerializeInternal(value, false).
    structured_serialize_internal(
        vm,
        Some(realm),
        &serialized,
        value,
        false,
        &memory,
        AllowSharedArrayBuffers::CrossOriginIsolatedOnly,
    )?;
    serialized.pin_named_stores();
    Ok(serialized)
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#structureddeserialize
// NB: In the realm of the call.
pub(crate) fn structured_deserialize_message(cx: &CallContext, serialized: &MessageRecord) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    let target_realm = cx.realm();
    let serialized = StructuredSerializeReader::new_message(target_realm, serialized);
    let memory = DeserializationMemory::new(cx.vm());
    with_temporary_execution_context(target_realm, || {
        structured_deserialize_internal(cx, &serialized, &memory, false)
    })
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#structuredserializeforstorage
pub(crate) fn structured_serialize_for_storage(cx: &CallContext, value: Value) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<u8>> {
    let vm = cx.vm();
    let memory = SerializationMemory::new(vm);
    let serialized = StructuredSerializeWriter::new(vm, SerializationType::Storage);

    // 1. Return ? StructuredSerializeInternal(value, true).
    structured_serialize_internal(
        vm,
        Some(cx.realm()),
        &serialized,
        value,
        true,
        &memory,
        AllowSharedArrayBuffers::CrossOriginIsolatedOnly,
    )?;
    Ok(serialized.into_storage_bytes())
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#structureddeserialize
// NB: The bytes of a storage record, which throws a "DataCloneError" DOMException for bytes after its value, in the realm
//     of the call.
pub(crate) fn structured_deserialize_for_storage(cx: &CallContext, serialized: &[u8]) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    let target_realm = cx.realm();
    let serialized = StructuredSerializeReader::new_storage(target_realm, serialized)?;
    let memory = DeserializationMemory::new(cx.vm());
    with_temporary_execution_context(target_realm, || {
        structured_deserialize_internal(cx, &serialized, &memory, true)
    })
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#structuredserializeinternal
pub(crate) fn structured_serialize_internal<'memory>(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Option<Gc<Realm>>,
    serialized: &StructuredSerializeWriter<'memory>,
    value: Value,
    for_storage: bool,
    memory: &SerializationMemory<'memory>,
    allow_shared_array_buffers: AllowSharedArrayBuffers,
) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
    let serializer = Serializer {
        vm,
        realm,
        serialized,
        memory,
        for_storage,
        allow_shared_array_buffers,
    };
    serializer.serialize(value)
}

pub(crate) fn structured_deserialize_internal(
    cx: &CallContext,
    serialized: &StructuredSerializeReader,
    memory: &DeserializationMemory,
    check_fully_consumed: bool,
) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    let deserializer = Deserializer { cx, serialized, memory };
    let value = deserializer.deserialize()?;

    // Nested sub-value decodes legitimately stop mid-record.
    if check_fully_consumed && serialized.serialization_type() == SerializationType::Storage && !serialized.is_at_end()
    {
        return Err(data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(
            cx.realm(),
            "Trailing data after structured serialize storage record",
        ));
    }

    Ok(value)
}

//! The record that a structured deserialization reads: the bytes of the values in the format of the record
//! (libwebcommon_rust::html::serialization_records), which C++ lends, and the SharedArrayBuffers that the record shares
//! beside them. What the deserialization reads that the record does not hold throws a "DataCloneError" DOMException in
//! the realm that it creates its values in.

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;
use std::sync::Arc;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{
    ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferShared, BigInt, DataBlock, DataBlockStorage, ExternalPrimitiveStorage, ForeignCellSlot,
    GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE, Gc, Realm, SharedBackingStore, Value, Vm,
};
use libwebcommon_rust::html::serialization_records::{DecodeError, DecodedString, RecordDecoder, SerializationType};

use crate::bindings::WebIdlResult;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::cpp::{
    ReceivedIPCSerializationRecord, data_clone_error_from_serialization_error,
};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::message_record::MessageRecord;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::serializable::{
    is_ipc_interface, serializable_interface_name_from_storage_identifier,
};
use crate::web_assembly::memory::buffer_of_shared_memory;

/// Where the record keeps the SharedArrayBuffers that it shares.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum SharedArrayBuffers<'a> {
    None,
    /// The side table of a record that C++ lends.
    Lent(ReceivedIPCSerializationRecord<'a>),
    Message(&'a MessageRecord),
}

pub(crate) struct StructuredSerializeReader<'a> {
    decoder: RecordDecoder<'a>,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    shared_array_buffers: SharedArrayBuffers<'a>,
}

impl<'a> StructuredSerializeReader<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn new_ipc(realm: Gc<Realm>, record: ReceivedIPCSerializationRecord<'a>) -> Self {
        Self {
            decoder: RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Ipc, record.data()).expect("an IPC record has no prologue"),
            realm,
            shared_array_buffers: SharedArrayBuffers::Lent(record),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn new_message(realm: Gc<Realm>, record: &'a MessageRecord) -> Self {
        Self {
            decoder: RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Ipc, &record.bytes).expect("an IPC record has no prologue"),
            realm,
            shared_array_buffers: SharedArrayBuffers::Message(record),
        }
    }

    /// The reader of the bytes of a storage record, which throws if they do not start with the prologue of the format.
    pub(crate) fn new_storage(realm: Gc<Realm>, data: &'a [u8]) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        let decoder = RecordDecoder::new(SerializationType::Storage, data)
            .map_err(|error| data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(realm, error.0))?;
        Ok(Self {
            decoder,
            realm,
            shared_array_buffers: SharedArrayBuffers::None,
        })
    }

    /// The realm that the deserialization creates its values in.
    pub(crate) fn realm(&self) -> Gc<Realm> {
        self.realm
    }

    pub(crate) fn serialization_type(&self) -> SerializationType {
        self.decoder.serialization_type()
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_at_end(&self) -> bool {
        self.decoder.is_at_end()
    }

    fn decoded<T>(&self, result: Result<T, DecodeError>) -> WebIdlResult<T> {
        result.map_err(|error| data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(self.realm, error.0))
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_u8(&self) -> WebIdlResult<u8> {
        self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_u8())
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_bool(&self) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_bool())
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_i32(&self) -> WebIdlResult<i32> {
        self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_i32())
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_u16(&self) -> WebIdlResult<u16> {
        self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_u16())
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_u32(&self) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_u32())
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_u64(&self) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_u64())
    }

    /// A u64 that is the size of something in memory.
    pub(crate) fn decode_size(&self) -> WebIdlResult<usize> {
        let size = self.decode_u64()?;
        self.decoded(
            usize::try_from(size)
                .map_err(|_| DecodeError("Structured serialize integer does not fit in native integer type")),
        )
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_i64(&self) -> WebIdlResult<i64> {
        self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_i64())
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_f64(&self) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_f64())
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_optional_f64(&self) -> WebIdlResult<Option<f64>> {
        if !self.decode_bool()? {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        Ok(Some(self.decode_f64()?))
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_optional_u64(&self) -> WebIdlResult<Option<u64>> {
        if !self.decode_bool()? {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        Ok(Some(self.decode_u64()?))
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_utf16_string(&self) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(match self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_utf16_string())? {
            DecodedString::Latin1(characters) => Utf16String::from_latin1(characters),
            DecodedString::Utf16(code_units) => Utf16String::from_utf16(&code_units),
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_optional_utf16_string(&self) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Utf16String>> {
        if !self.decode_bool()? {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        Ok(Some(self.decode_utf16_string()?))
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode_bytes(&self) -> WebIdlResult<&'a [u8]> {
        self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_bytes())
    }

    /// Bindings::InterfaceName, which a storage record holds as the identifier of the interface. It is the name of a
    /// serializable interface.
    pub(crate) fn decode_interface_name(&self) -> WebIdlResult<u16> {
        let interface_name = match self.serialization_type() {
            SerializationType::Ipc => {
                let interface_name = self.decode_u16()?;
                is_ipc_interface(interface_name).then_some(interface_name)
            }
            SerializationType::Storage => match self.decode_utf16_string()?.as_units() {
                ak::Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(identifier) => {
                    serializable_interface_name_from_storage_identifier(identifier)
                }
                ak::Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(_) | ak::Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(_) => None,
            },
        };
        self.decoded(interface_name.ok_or(DecodeError("Unknown structured serialize interface name")))
    }

    /// A new BigInt with the value that StructuredSerializeWriter::encode_big_int() wrote.
    pub(crate) fn decode_big_int(&self, vm: &Vm) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        let (is_negative, magnitude) = self.decoded(self.decoder.decode_big_int())?;
        Ok(Value::from_bigint(BigInt::create_from_magnitude_bytes_be(
            vm,
            is_negative,
            magnitude,
        )))
    }

    /// A new SharedArrayBuffer over the store that `id` names. A store is only found in the process of the agent that
    /// sent the message, as its bytes do not leave that process.
    pub(crate) fn array_buffer_from_shared_store(&self, vm: &Vm, id: u64) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        let store = SharedBackingStore::with_id(id).ok_or_else(|| {
            data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(self.realm, "SharedArrayBuffer is out of reach")
        })?;
        Ok(Value::from_object(ArrayBuffer::create_from_shared_store(
            vm, self.realm, store,
        )))
    }

    /// A new SharedArrayBuffer of the shared WebAssembly memory that `id` names: a fixed-length one of the byte length,
    /// or a growable one without. A memory is only found in the process of the agent that sent the message, as its
    /// bytes do not leave that process.
    pub(crate) fn array_buffer_of_web_assembly_memory(
        &self,
        vm: &Vm,
        id: u64,
        fixed_byte_length: Option<usize>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        buffer_of_shared_memory(vm, self.realm, id, fixed_byte_length)
            .map(Value::from_object)
            .ok_or_else(|| data_clone_error_from_serialization_error(self.realm, "SharedArrayBuffer is out of reach"))
    }

    /// A new SharedArrayBuffer that shares the storage of the buffer at the index of the record's same-agent side
    /// table, if there is such a buffer, and its storage can be shared.
    pub(crate) fn array_buffer_sharing_side_table_entry(
        &self,
        vm: &Vm,
        side_table_index: u32,
        byte_length: usize,
        preserve_growability: bool,
    ) -> Option<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
        let source_buffer = match self.shared_array_buffers {
            SharedArrayBuffers::None => return None,
            SharedArrayBuffers::Lent(record) => record.shared_array_buffer(side_table_index)?,
            SharedArrayBuffers::Message(record) => *record.shared_array_buffers.get(side_table_index as usize)?,
        };
        array_buffer_sharing_storage_with(vm, self.realm, source_buffer, byte_length, preserve_growability)
    }
}

fn foreign_cell_slot(cell: NonNull<c_void>) -> ForeignCellSlot {
    let slot = ForeignCellSlot::empty();
    // SAFETY: The cell is a live cell of the heap, which the slot then keeps alive.
    unsafe { slot.set(Some(cell)) };
    slot
}

// Returns None when the source storage cannot be aliased, allowing the caller to copy it.
fn array_buffer_sharing_storage_with(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    source_buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>,
    byte_length: usize,
    preserve_growability: bool,
) -> Option<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
    assert!(source_buffer.is_shared_array_buffer());
    let fixed_byte_length = (!preserve_growability).then_some(byte_length);
    let data_block = source_buffer.with_data_block(|source_block| match &source_block.byte_buffer {
        // Flatten alias chains to the actual owner. Keep this buffer's byte length because the owner's
        // storage may be larger (for example, a fixed-length view of growable WebAssembly.Memory).
        DataBlockStorage::External(external) => Some(DataBlock::external(
            ExternalPrimitiveStorage::new(
                foreign_cell_slot(external.owner()),
                external.handle(),
                fixed_byte_length,
            ),
            ArrayBufferShared::Yes,
        )),

        // AD-HOC: A fixed-length shared block is aliased by referencing the same store, so that the clone can itself be
        //         shared with an agent on another thread.
        DataBlockStorage::Shared(store) => Some(DataBlock::shared(Arc::clone(store))),

        DataBlockStorage::Owned(owned) => {
            // Zero-length buffers have no backing storage to share.
            if owned.handle() == GC_PRIMITIVE_STORAGE_NULL_HANDLE {
                return None;
            }
            // SAFETY: The source buffer is a live cell.
            let owner = unsafe { NonNull::new_unchecked(source_buffer.as_ptr().cast()) };
            Some(DataBlock::external(
                ExternalPrimitiveStorage::new(foreign_cell_slot(owner), owned.handle(), fixed_byte_length),
                ArrayBufferShared::Yes,
            ))
        }

        // A detached block has no storage to share.
        DataBlockStorage::Empty => None,
    })?;
    Some(ArrayBuffer::create_from_data_block(vm, realm, data_block))
}

//! The data holders of the transfer steps and the transfer-receiving steps,
//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#transferable-objects

use core::cell::RefCell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
pub(crate) use libipc_rust::cpp_connection::RawAttachment;
use libipc_rust::{Attachment, Decode, DecodeError, Decoder, Encode, EncodeError, Encoder};
use std::collections::VecDeque;

use crate::html::message_port::TransportHandle;
use crate::html::port_channel::{PortChannelEnd, claim_parked_end, park_end};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::transfer_record::PortMessage;

pub(crate) type ReceivePayload = unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, ak::Span<'_, u8>, *const RawAttachment, usize);

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_structured_serialize_transfer_data_holder_create(
        bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
        attachments: *const RawAttachment,
        count: usize,
    ) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_structured_serialize_transfer_data_holder_take(
        holder: *mut c_void,
        context: *mut c_void,
        receive: ReceivePayload,
    );
}

pub(crate) fn append_attachments(encoder: &mut Encoder, attachments: Vec<Attachment>) {
    for attachment in attachments {
        encoder.append_attachment(attachment);
    }
}

/// A channel end that a data holder carries.
pub(crate) enum CarriedChannelEnd {
    Held(PortChannelEnd),
    /// Parked in this process, under the token, for the data holder to go through the browser process. The transport is
    /// for a data holder that may arrive in another process.
    Parked(u64, Option<TransportHandle>),
}

impl CarriedChannelEnd {
    /// A data holder that is encoded leaves the process, as far as this end knows, so the end changes over to a transport.
    fn encode_owned(self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        let (token, messages, transport) = match self {
            Self::Held(end) => {
                let (messages, transport) = end.leave_process();
                (0, messages, transport)
            }
            Self::Parked(token, transport) => (token, Vec::new(), transport),
        };
        encoder.encode(&token)?;
        encoder.encode_size(messages.len())?;
        for message in messages {
            message.encode_into(encoder)?;
        }
        encoder.encode(&transport.is_some())?;
        if let Some(transport) = transport {
            transport.encode_into(encoder)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let token = decoder.decode::<u64>()?;
        let count = decoder.decode_size()?;
        let mut messages = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..count {
            messages.push(PortMessage::decode(decoder)?);
        }
        let transport = decoder
            .decode::<bool>()?
            .then(|| TransportHandle::decode(decoder))
            .transpose()?;
        if token != 0
            && let Some(end) = claim_parked_end(token)
        {
            return Ok(Self::Held(end));
        }
        Ok(Self::Held(PortChannelEnd::from_elsewhere(messages, transport)))
    }

    pub(crate) fn into_end(self) -> PortChannelEnd {
        match self {
            Self::Held(end) => end,
            Self::Parked(..) => unreachable!("a parked end is only ever encoded"),
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) struct TransferPayload {
    pub(crate) bytes: Vec<u8>,
    pub(crate) attachments: Vec<Attachment>,
    /// The channel ends of the MessagePorts that the data holder carries, which its readers take in the order its writers
    /// added them.
    pub(crate) channel_ends: VecDeque<CarriedChannelEnd>,
}

impl TransferPayload {
    pub(crate) fn new(bytes: Vec<u8>, attachments: Vec<Attachment>) -> Self {
        Self {
            bytes,
            attachments,
            channel_ends: VecDeque::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Parks the channel end of a data holder that goes through the browser process to a thread of a worker, and returns
    /// the token that settling it takes. This is for a holder with one end, of a new channel.
    pub(crate) fn park_channel_end(&mut self, may_leave_process: bool) -> u64 {
        let end = self
            .channel_ends
            .pop_front()
            .expect("the data holder of a new channel holds its end")
            .into_end();
        let (token, transport) = park_end(end, may_leave_process);
        self.channel_ends.push_back(CarriedChannelEnd::Parked(token, transport));
        token
    }

    /// The carrier of this data holder for C++, for which it is opaque. Encoding makes it fit to leave the process.
    pub(crate) fn into_cpp(self) -> *mut c_void {
        let mut encoder = Encoder::new();
        self.encode_owned(&mut encoder).expect("a data holder encodes");
        let (bytes, attachments) = encoder.finish();
        Self::new(bytes, attachments).with_raw(|bytes, attachments| {
            // SAFETY: C++ copies the lent bytes and takes all attachments.
            unsafe {
                web_structured_serialize_transfer_data_holder_create(bytes, attachments.as_ptr(), attachments.len())
            }
        })
    }

    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// C++ must hand over the holder and its attachments.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_cpp(holder: *mut c_void) -> Self {
        let mut payload = None;
        // SAFETY: The holder is handed over, and the callback fills the lent result slot.
        unsafe { web_structured_serialize_transfer_data_holder_take(holder, (&raw mut payload).cast(), Self::receive) };
        let payload: Self = payload.expect("C++ hands over the payload");
        // NB: What cannot be decoded holds nothing, which is what reading from it reports.
        let mut decoder = Decoder::new(&payload.bytes, payload.attachments);
        decoder
            .decode::<Self>()
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| Self::new(Vec::new(), Vec::new()))
    }

    pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn receive(
        context: *mut c_void,
        bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
        attachments: *const RawAttachment,
        count: usize,
    ) {
        // SAFETY: The caller lends this result slot and bytes, and transfers every raw attachment.
        let attachments = unsafe { RawAttachment::take_all(ak::slice_from_raw_parts(attachments, count)) };
        unsafe {
            *context.cast::<Option<Self>>() = Some(Self::new(bytes.as_slice().to_vec(), attachments));
        };
    }

    pub(crate) fn with_raw<R>(self, steps: impl FnOnce(ak::Span<'_, u8>, &[RawAttachment]) -> R) -> R {
        let attachments: Vec<_> = self
            .attachments
            .into_iter()
            .map(RawAttachment::from_attachment)
            .collect();
        steps(ak::Span::new(&self.bytes), &attachments)
    }
}

impl Encode for TransferPayload {
    fn encode(&self, _: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        Err(EncodeError::InvalidValue(
            "a transfer payload must move its attachments",
        ))
    }

    fn encode_owned(self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        encoder.encode(self.bytes.as_slice())?;
        encoder.encode_size(self.attachments.len())?;
        append_attachments(encoder, self.attachments);
        encoder.encode_size(self.channel_ends.len())?;
        for end in self.channel_ends {
            end.encode_owned(encoder)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Decode for TransferPayload {
    const MIN_ENCODED_SIZE: usize = 8;

    fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let bytes = decoder.decode::<Vec<u8>>()?;
        let count = decoder.decode::<u32>()? as usize;
        if count > decoder.remaining_attachments() {
            return Err(DecodeError::MissingAttachment);
        }
        let attachments = (0..count)
            .map(|_| decoder.take_attachment())
            .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
        let end_count = decoder.decode_size()?;
        let mut channel_ends = VecDeque::new();
        for _ in 0..end_count {
            channel_ends.push_back(CarriedChannelEnd::decode(decoder)?);
        }
        Ok(Self {
            bytes,
            attachments,
            channel_ends,
        })
    }
}

pub(crate) struct TransferDataHolder {
    encoder: RefCell<Encoder>,
    channel_ends: RefCell<VecDeque<CarriedChannelEnd>>,
}

impl TransferDataHolder {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            encoder: RefCell::new(Encoder::new()),
            channel_ends: RefCell::new(VecDeque::new()),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode<T: Encode + ?Sized>(&self, value: &T) {
        self.with_encoder(|encoder| encoder.encode(value));
    }

    pub(crate) fn with_encoder(&self, write: impl FnOnce(&mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError>) {
        write(&mut self.encoder.borrow_mut()).expect("a data holder encodes what it is given");
    }

    pub(crate) fn add_channel_end(&self, end: PortChannelEnd) {
        self.channel_ends.borrow_mut().push_back(CarriedChannelEnd::Held(end));
    }

    pub(crate) fn extend(&self, payload: TransferPayload) {
        let mut encoder = self.encoder.borrow_mut();
        encoder.append_bytes(&payload.bytes);
        append_attachments(&mut encoder, payload.attachments);
        self.channel_ends.borrow_mut().extend(payload.channel_ends);
    }

    pub(crate) fn finish(self) -> TransferPayload {
        let (bytes, attachments) = self.encoder.into_inner().finish();
        TransferPayload {
            bytes,
            attachments,
            channel_ends: self.channel_ends.into_inner(),
        }
    }
}

//! The result of StructuredSerializeWithTransfer,
//! https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#structuredserializewithtransfer

use core::cell::RefCell;
use core::ffi::{c_int, c_void};
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    ArrayBuffer, DeferGc, EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, GcRefCell, SharedStorePin, Trace, Vm,
    into_raw_descriptor, lifeline_into_raw_descriptor,
};

use super::cpp::{OwnedSerializedTransferRecord, SerializedTransferRecord, objects_into_abi};
use super::message_record::{MessageRecord, SharedMemory};
use super::transfer_data_holder::TransferPayload;
use libipc_rust::wire::File;

use libjs_rust::api::{AsSharedMemory, lifeline_from_raw_descriptor, owned_from_raw_descriptor, raw_descriptor};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_structured_serialize_validate_shared_memory(descriptor: c_int, size: usize) -> bool;
    fn web_structured_serialize_transfer_record_create(
        bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
        array_buffers: *const *mut c_void,
        array_buffer_count: usize,
        descriptors: *const c_int,
        sizes: *const usize,
        shared_memory_count: usize,
        shared_store_lifeline: c_int,
        holders: *const *mut c_void,
        holder_count: usize,
    ) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_structured_serialize_transfer_record_take(
        record: *mut c_void,
        context: *mut c_void,
        receive: unsafe extern "C" fn(
            *mut c_void,
            ak::Span<'_, u8>,
            *const *mut c_void,
            usize,
            *const c_int,
            *const usize,
            usize,
            c_int,
        ),
        append_holder: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void),
    );
}

/// The descriptor as what the record encodes, which takes it over.
fn file_from_raw_descriptor(raw: c_int) -> File {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    // SAFETY: The caller hands the descriptor over.
    let descriptor = unsafe { std::os::fd::FromRawFd::from_raw_fd(raw) };
    #[cfg(windows)]
    // SAFETY: The caller hands the descriptor over.
    let descriptor = unsafe { libipc_rust::transport_windows::OwnedDescriptor::from_raw(raw) };
    File(descriptor)
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct TransferRecord {
    pub(crate) serialized: GcRefCell<Option<MessageRecord>>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) data_holders: RefCell<Vec<TransferPayload>>,
}

static TRANSFER_RECORD_CLASS: EmbedderClass<TransferRecord> = EmbedderClass::new("SerializedTransferRecord");

impl EmbedderValue for TransferRecord {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &TRANSFER_RECORD_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type TransferRecordRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<TransferRecord>>;

/// A record on its way to a MessagePort, which is plain data that any thread can own: the bytes, the data holders, the
/// shared memory of ImageBitmap pixels, and the pin of the stores that the bytes name.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct PortMessage {
    bytes: Vec<u8>,
    data_holders: Vec<TransferPayload>,
    shared_memory: Vec<SharedMemory>,
    shared_store_pin: Option<SharedStorePin>,
}

impl PortMessage {
    pub(crate) fn encode_into(mut self, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        encoder.encode(self.bytes.as_slice())?;
        encoder.encode_owned(core::mem::take(&mut self.data_holders))?;
        encoder.encode_size(self.shared_memory.len())?;
        for memory in core::mem::take(&mut self.shared_memory) {
            encoder.encode(&true)?;
            encoder.encode(&(memory.size as u64))?;
            encoder.encode_owned(file_from_raw_descriptor(into_raw_descriptor(memory.descriptor)))?;
        }
        let shared_store_lifeline = self.shared_store_pin.take().and_then(SharedStorePin::into_lifeline);
        encoder.encode(&shared_store_lifeline.is_some())?;
        if let Some(lifeline) = shared_store_lifeline {
            encoder.encode_owned(file_from_raw_descriptor(lifeline_into_raw_descriptor(lifeline)))?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode(decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<Self, DecodeError> {
        let bytes = decoder.decode::<Vec<u8>>()?;
        let data_holders = decoder.decode::<Vec<TransferPayload>>()?;
        let count = decoder.decode_size()?;
        let mut shared_memory = Vec::new();
        let mut keep_prefix = true;
        for _ in 0..count {
            if !decoder.decode::<bool>()? {
                // Match importing an invalid C++ AnonymousBuffer: its missing descriptor truncates the side table.
                keep_prefix = false;
                continue;
            }
            let size = usize::try_from(decoder.decode::<u64>()?)
                .map_err(|_| DecodeError::InvalidValue("shared memory size does not fit"))?;
            let File(descriptor) = decoder.decode::<File>()?;
            #[cfg(unix)]
            let raw = std::os::fd::IntoRawFd::into_raw_fd(descriptor);
            #[cfg(windows)]
            let raw = descriptor.into_raw();
            // SAFETY: File hands its descriptor over to the shared-memory owner.
            let memory = SharedMemory {
                descriptor: unsafe { owned_from_raw_descriptor(raw) },
                size,
            };
            // The native backing size and seal checks must run before any bitmap or ArrayBuffer can map the claim.
            // SAFETY: The owner keeps the descriptor open for validation.
            if !unsafe {
                web_structured_serialize_validate_shared_memory(
                    raw_descriptor(memory.descriptor.as_shared_memory()),
                    size,
                )
            } {
                return Err(DecodeError::InvalidValue("invalid shared memory backing"));
            }
            if keep_prefix {
                shared_memory.push(memory);
            }
        }
        let shared_store_pin = decoder
            .decode::<bool>()?
            .then(|| decoder.decode::<File>())
            .transpose()?
            .map(|File(descriptor)| {
                #[cfg(unix)]
                let raw = std::os::fd::IntoRawFd::into_raw_fd(descriptor);
                #[cfg(windows)]
                let raw = descriptor.into_raw();
                // SAFETY: File hands its descriptor over to the lifeline.
                SharedStorePin::Lifeline(unsafe { lifeline_from_raw_descriptor(raw) })
            });
        Ok(Self {
            bytes,
            data_holders,
            shared_memory,
            shared_store_pin,
        })
    }
}

impl Drop for PortMessage {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(pin) = self.shared_store_pin.take() {
            pin.release();
        }
    }
}

impl TransferRecord {
    pub(crate) fn discard(record: TransferRecordRef) {
        record.serialized.replace(None);
        record.data_holders.borrow_mut().clear();
    }

    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        build: impl FnOnce(&DeferGc<'_>) -> MessageRecord,
        data_holders: Vec<TransferPayload>,
    ) -> TransferRecordRef {
        TRANSFER_RECORD_CLASS.allocate(vm, |defer_gc| Self {
            serialized: GcRefCell::new(Some(build(defer_gc))),
            data_holders: RefCell::new(data_holders),
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn into_cpp(record: TransferRecordRef, vm: &Vm) -> OwnedSerializedTransferRecord {
        DeferGc::scope(vm, |_defer_gc| {
            let mut message = record.serialized.replace(None).expect("a record is handed over once");
            let buffers = objects_into_abi(&message.shared_array_buffers);
            let (descriptors, sizes): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) = core::mem::take(&mut message.shared_memory)
                .into_iter()
                .map(|memory| (into_raw_descriptor(memory.descriptor), memory.size))
                .unzip();
            let shared_store_lifeline = message
                .shared_store_pin
                .take()
                .and_then(SharedStorePin::into_lifeline)
                .map_or(-1, lifeline_into_raw_descriptor);
            let holders: Vec<_> = record
                .data_holders
                .borrow_mut()
                .drain(..)
                .map(TransferPayload::into_cpp)
                .collect();
            // SAFETY: The call borrows bytes and live buffers, and takes every descriptor and holder. GC remains
            //         deferred until the C++ carrier roots the buffer aliases.
            unsafe {
                OwnedSerializedTransferRecord::from_raw(web_structured_serialize_transfer_record_create(
                    ak::Span::new(&message.bytes),
                    buffers.as_ptr(),
                    buffers.len(),
                    descriptors.as_ptr(),
                    sizes.as_ptr(),
                    descriptors.len(),
                    shared_store_lifeline,
                    holders.as_ptr(),
                    holders.len(),
                ))
            }
        })
    }

    /// The IPC encoding of a SerializedTransferRecord, without its same-agent SharedArrayBuffers.
    pub(crate) fn encode_into(record: TransferRecordRef, vm: &Vm, encoder: &mut Encoder) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
        Self::into_port_message(record, vm).encode_into(encoder)
    }

    /// What of the record can leave the heap of the sender. The side table of same-agent SharedArrayBuffers stays behind,
    /// as the bytes name those by the id of their store too.
    pub(crate) fn into_port_message(record: TransferRecordRef, vm: &Vm) -> PortMessage {
        DeferGc::scope(vm, |_| {
            let mut message = record.serialized.replace(None).expect("a record is handed over once");
            PortMessage {
                bytes: core::mem::take(&mut message.bytes),
                data_holders: core::mem::take(&mut *record.data_holders.borrow_mut()),
                shared_memory: core::mem::take(&mut message.shared_memory),
                shared_store_pin: message.shared_store_pin.take(),
            }
        })
    }

    /// The record of a message, in the heap of the receiver.
    pub(crate) fn from_port_message(vm: &Vm, mut message: PortMessage) -> TransferRecordRef {
        let holders = core::mem::take(&mut message.data_holders);
        Self::create(
            vm,
            |_| MessageRecord {
                bytes: core::mem::take(&mut message.bytes),
                shared_array_buffers: Vec::new(),
                shared_memory: core::mem::take(&mut message.shared_memory),
                shared_store_pin: message.shared_store_pin.take(),
            },
            holders,
        )
    }

    pub(crate) fn decode(vm: &Vm, decoder: &mut Decoder<'_>) -> Result<TransferRecordRef, DecodeError> {
        Ok(Self::from_port_message(vm, PortMessage::decode(decoder)?))
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_cpp(vm: &Vm, record: SerializedTransferRecord) -> TransferRecordRef {
        struct Received<'a> {
            defer_gc: &'a DeferGc<'a>,
            message: Option<MessageRecord>,
            holders: Vec<TransferPayload>,
        }

        unsafe extern "C" fn receive(
            context: *mut c_void,
            bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
            buffers: *const *mut c_void,
            buffer_count: usize,
            descriptors: *const c_int,
            sizes: *const usize,
            shared_memory_count: usize,
            shared_store_lifeline: c_int,
        ) {
            // SAFETY: from_cpp() lends the state under its allocation's deferral, and C++ lends every input slice.
            let received = unsafe { &mut *context.cast::<Received<'_>>() };
            #[cfg_attr(
                ladybird_gc_lints,
                expect(gc_container_on_stack, reason = "the collector is deferred while C++ lends them")
            )]
            let mut message = unsafe {
                MessageRecord::received(
                    received.defer_gc,
                    bytes.as_slice(),
                    ak::slice_from_raw_parts(descriptors, shared_memory_count),
                    ak::slice_from_raw_parts(sizes, shared_memory_count),
                    shared_store_lifeline,
                )
            };
            message.shared_array_buffers = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(buffers, buffer_count) }
                .iter()
                .map(|&buffer| {
                    // SAFETY: C++ lends live ArrayBuffers while the collector is deferred.
                    unsafe {
                        Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(buffer.cast::<ArrayBuffer>()).expect("C++ lends a buffer"))
                    }
                })
                .collect();
            received.message = Some(message);
        }

        unsafe extern "C" fn append(context: *mut c_void, holder: *mut c_void) {
            // SAFETY: from_cpp() lends the state, and C++ hands the holder over.
            unsafe {
                (*context.cast::<Received<'_>>())
                    .holders
                    .push(TransferPayload::from_cpp(holder));
            };
        }

        TRANSFER_RECORD_CLASS.allocate(vm, |defer_gc| {
            let mut received = Received {
                defer_gc,
                message: None,
                holders: Vec::new(),
            };
            // SAFETY: The record and the state are live, and the callbacks receive only the state and the contents.
            unsafe {
                web_structured_serialize_transfer_record_take(
                    record.as_raw(),
                    (&raw mut received).cast(),
                    receive,
                    append,
                );
            };
            Self {
                serialized: GcRefCell::new(received.message),
                data_holders: RefCell::new(received.holders),
            }
        })
    }
}

//! The record that a structured serialization writes: the bytes of the values in the format of the record
//! (libwebcommon_rust::html::serialization_records), and the SharedArrayBuffers that the record shares beside them.
//! C++ code and the UI process carry records without reading them, so a writer hands what it wrote over to LibWeb's
//! C++ record when it finishes, or to a MessageRecord that Rust keeps.

use core::cell::RefCell;
use std::sync::Arc;

use ak::{Utf16String, Utf16StringUnits};
use libjs_rust::api::{
    ArrayBuffer, BigInt, DataBlockStorage, DeferGc, Gc, MarkedVec, SharedByMessage, SharedStorePin, Vm,
};
use libwebcommon_rust::html::serialization_records::{RecordEncoder, SerializationType};

use crate::html::structured_serialize::cpp::{IPCSerializationRecord, StorageSerializationRecord};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::message_record::{MessageRecord, SharedMemory};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::serializable::serializable_interface_storage_identifier;
use crate::web_assembly::memory::shared_memory_of_buffer;

/// The record of a structured serialization, which the serialization writes its values to.
pub(crate) struct StructuredSerializeWriter<'vm> {
    encoder: RefCell<RecordEncoder>,
    /// The SharedArrayBuffers that an IPC record shares with a deserialization in the same agent, by their index in
    /// this same-agent side table.
    shared_array_buffers: MarkedVec<'vm, Gc<ArrayBuffer>>,
    /// The shared memory that a MessageRecord, which may reach agents in other processes, hands over beside its bytes.
    shared_memory: Option<RefCell<Vec<SharedMemory>>>,
    /// The stores and the shared WebAssembly memories that a message names, which only a record that may reach an agent
    /// on another thread has.
    stores_of_message: Option<RefCell<Vec<SharedByMessage>>>,
    shared_store_pin: RefCell<Option<SharedStorePin>>,
}

impl<'vm> StructuredSerializeWriter<'vm> {
    pub(crate) fn new(vm: &'vm Vm, serialization_type: SerializationType) -> Self {
        Self {
            encoder: RefCell::new(RecordEncoder::new(serialization_type)),
            shared_array_buffers: MarkedVec::new(vm),
            shared_memory: None,
            stores_of_message: None,
            shared_store_pin: RefCell::new(None),
        }
    }

    /// The writer of a message, which agents on other threads may receive, and which names the stores of its
    /// SharedArrayBuffers.
    pub(crate) fn new_for_message(vm: &'vm Vm) -> Self {
        Self {
            shared_memory: Some(RefCell::new(Vec::new())),
            stores_of_message: Some(RefCell::new(Vec::new())),
            ..Self::new(vm, SerializationType::Ipc)
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn serialization_type(&self) -> SerializationType {
        self.encoder.borrow().serialization_type()
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_u8(&self, value: u8) {
        self.encoder.borrow_mut().encode_u8(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_bool(&self, value: bool) {
        self.encoder.borrow_mut().encode_bool(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_i32(&self, value: i32) {
        self.encoder.borrow_mut().encode_i32(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_u16(&self, value: u16) {
        self.encoder.borrow_mut().encode_u16(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_u32(&self, value: u32) {
        self.encoder.borrow_mut().encode_u32(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_u64(&self, value: u64) {
        self.encoder.borrow_mut().encode_u64(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_i64(&self, value: i64) {
        self.encoder.borrow_mut().encode_i64(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_f64(&self, value: f64) {
        self.encoder.borrow_mut().encode_f64(value);
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_optional_f64(&self, value: Option<f64>) {
        self.encode_bool(value.is_some());
        if let Some(value) = value {
            self.encode_f64(value);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_optional_u64(&self, value: Option<u64>) {
        self.encode_bool(value.is_some());
        if let Some(value) = value {
            self.encode_u64(value);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_utf16_string(&self, string: &Utf16String) {
        self.encoder.borrow_mut().encode_utf16_string(string.as_units());
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_optional_utf16_string(&self, string: Option<&Utf16String>) {
        self.encode_bool(string.is_some());
        if let Some(string) = string {
            self.encode_utf16_string(string);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_bytes(&self, bytes: &[u8]) {
        self.encoder.borrow_mut().encode_bytes(bytes);
    }

    /// Bindings::InterfaceName, which a storage record holds as the identifier of the interface.
    pub(crate) fn encode_interface_name(&self, interface_name: u16) {
        match self.serialization_type() {
            SerializationType::Ipc => self.encode_u16(interface_name),
            SerializationType::Storage => {
                let identifier =
                    serializable_interface_storage_identifier(interface_name).expect("the interface is serializable");
                self.encoder
                    .borrow_mut()
                    .encode_utf16_string(Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(identifier));
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn encode_big_int(&self, big_int: Gc<BigInt>) {
        self.encoder
            .borrow_mut()
            .encode_big_int(big_int.is_negative(), &big_int.magnitude_to_bytes_be());
    }

    /// Puts the SharedArrayBuffer in the record's same-agent side table, and returns its index there.
    pub(crate) fn add_shared_array_buffer(&self, array_buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>) -> u32 {
        let index = u32::try_from(self.shared_array_buffers.len()).expect("a record shares fewer than 2^32 buffers");
        self.shared_array_buffers.push(array_buffer);
        index
    }

    /// Hands the shared memory over beside the record, and returns its index there.
    pub(crate) fn append_shared_memory(&self, shared_memory: SharedMemory) -> u32 {
        let mut list = self
            .shared_memory
            .as_ref()
            .expect("the record hands shared memory over")
            .borrow_mut();
        let index = u32::try_from(list.len()).expect("a record shares fewer than 2^32 buffers");
        list.push(shared_memory);
        index
    }

    /// The index that the next shared memory handed over beside the record gets.
    pub(crate) fn next_shared_memory_index(&self) -> u32 {
        let list = self
            .shared_memory
            .as_ref()
            .expect("the record hands shared memory over")
            .borrow();
        u32::try_from(list.len()).expect("a record shares fewer than 2^32 buffers")
    }

    /// Has the message keep the store of the SharedArrayBuffer alive, and returns the id that names the store, if the
    /// buffer has one, and the record is a message.
    pub(crate) fn name_store_of(&self, array_buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>) -> Option<u64> {
        let stores = self.stores_of_message.as_ref()?;
        let store = array_buffer.with_data_block(|data_block| match &data_block.byte_buffer {
            DataBlockStorage::Shared(store) => Some(Arc::clone(store)),
            _ => None,
        })?;
        let id = store.id();
        stores.borrow_mut().push(store);
        Some(id)
    }

    /// Has the message keep the shared WebAssembly memory alive that the SharedArrayBuffer is a buffer of, and returns
    /// the id that names the memory, if the buffer is one of a memory, and the record is a message.
    pub(crate) fn name_web_assembly_memory_of(&self, array_buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>) -> Option<u64> {
        let stores = self.stores_of_message.as_ref()?;
        let memory = shared_memory_of_buffer(array_buffer)?;
        let id = memory.id();
        stores.borrow_mut().push(memory);
        Some(id)
    }

    /// Gives the message its pin, if it names stores.
    pub(crate) fn pin_named_stores(&self) {
        let stores = self.stores_of_message.as_ref().map(RefCell::take).unwrap_or_default();
        if !stores.is_empty() {
            *self.shared_store_pin.borrow_mut() = Some(SharedStorePin::Counted(stores));
        }
    }

    /// Sets the IPC record that C++ lends to what the writer wrote.
    pub(crate) fn finish_ipc_record(self, record: IPCSerializationRecord) {
        assert_eq!(self.serialization_type(), SerializationType::Ipc);
        record.set(self.encoder.borrow().bytes(), &self.shared_array_buffers.values());
    }

    /// The MessageRecord that the writer wrote. Its SharedArrayBuffers are traced once it is in a cell, which the caller
    /// allocates under the deferral.
    pub(crate) fn finish_message_record(self, _: &DeferGc<'_>) -> MessageRecord {
        assert_eq!(self.serialization_type(), SerializationType::Ipc);
        let shared_memory = self.shared_memory.expect("the writer is a message's");
        MessageRecord {
            shared_store_pin: self.shared_store_pin.take(),
            bytes: self.encoder.into_inner().into_bytes(),
            shared_array_buffers: self.shared_array_buffers.values().to_vec(),
            shared_memory: shared_memory.into_inner(),
        }
    }

    /// The bytes of the storage record that the writer wrote, for Rust code that keeps them, as IndexedDB does.
    pub(crate) fn into_storage_bytes(self) -> Vec<u8> {
        assert_eq!(self.serialization_type(), SerializationType::Storage);
        assert!(
            self.shared_array_buffers.is_empty(),
            "a storage record shares no SharedArrayBuffer"
        );
        self.encoder.into_inner().into_bytes()
    }

    /// Sets the storage record that C++ lends to what the writer wrote.
    pub(crate) fn finish_storage_record(self, record: StorageSerializationRecord) {
        assert_eq!(self.serialization_type(), SerializationType::Storage);
        assert!(
            self.shared_array_buffers.is_empty(),
            "a storage record shares no SharedArrayBuffer"
        );
        record.set(self.encoder.borrow().bytes());
    }
}

use core::ffi::c_void;

/// The dictionary SubmitEventInit of HTML/SubmitEvent.idl.
pub(crate) struct SubmitEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) submitter: Option<CppInterface>,
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#submitevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct SubmitEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    submitter: Option<CppCell>,
}

impl Wrappable for SubmitEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl SubmitEvent {
    fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: &EventInit,
        submitter: Option<CppCell>,
    ) -> Ref<SubmitEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.bubbles,
            event_init.cancelable,
            event_init.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| SubmitEvent { event, submitter });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: SubmitEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<SubmitEvent>> {
        let submitter = event_init_dict.submitter.map(CppInterface::cell);
        Ok(Self::create(
            cx.vm(),
            cx.realm(),
            &r#type,
            &event_init_dict.parent,
            submitter,
        ))
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#dom-submitevent-submitter
    pub(crate) fn submitter(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CppInterface>> {
        Ok(self.submitter.as_ref().map(|submitter| wrap_cpp_cell(cx, submitter)))
    }
}

/// The Event of a new trusted SubmitEvent in the realm, for the implementation to fire.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_submit_event_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    r#type: LentUtf16FlyString<'_>,
    bubbles: bool,
    cancelable: bool,
    composed: bool,
    submitter: Option<&LentCppCell<cpp_class::Element>>,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let event_init = EventInit {
        bubbles,
        cancelable,
        composed,
    };
    let r#type: Utf16String = r#type.to_utf16_fly_string().into();
    let submitter = submitter.map(CppCell::from_lent);
    let event = SubmitEvent::create(vm, realm, &r#type, &event_init, submitter);
    event.event().as_ptr()
}

//! TextTrackCue, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#texttrackcue

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ops::Deref;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{GcRefCell, Trace};

use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::CppCell;
use crate::bindings::event_target::{CppEventTarget, GetTheParent};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, InterfaceCell, Ref, Wrappable};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::css::css_rule::wrap_cpp_cell;
use crate::web_vtt::vtt_cue::VTTCue;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_html_text_track_cue_timing_changed(track: *mut c_void);
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#texttrackcue
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct TextTrackCue {
    event_target: CppEventTarget,

    // The TextTrack whose text track list of cues the cue is in, if any.
    track: GcRefCell<Option<CppCell>>,

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#text-track-cue-identifier
    #[gc(untraced)]
    identifier: RefCell<Utf16String>,

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#text-track-cue-start-time
    start_time: Cell<f64>,

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#text-track-cue-end-time
    end_time: Cell<f64>,

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#text-track-cue-pause-on-exit-flag
    pause_on_exit: Cell<bool>,

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#text-track-cue-active-flag
    active: Cell<bool>,

    order_added: Cell<u64>,
}

impl Wrappable for TextTrackCue {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event_target.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for TextTrackCue {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
}

impl TextTrackCue {
    pub(crate) fn new(start_time: f64, end_time: f64) -> Self {
        Self {
            event_target: CppEventTarget::new(),
            track: GcRefCell::new(None),
            identifier: RefCell::new(Utf16String::from_utf8("")),
            start_time: Cell::new(start_time),
            end_time: Cell::new(end_time),
            pause_on_exit: Cell::new(false),
            active: Cell::new(false),
            order_added: Cell::new(0),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn event_target(&self) -> &CppEventTarget {
        &self.event_target
    }

    pub(crate) fn track_cell(&self) -> Option<CppCell> {
        self.track.borrow().clone()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_track_cell(&self, track: Option<CppCell>) {
        self.track.replace(track);
    }

    pub(crate) fn identifier(&self) -> Utf16String {
        self.identifier.borrow().clone()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_identifier(&self, identifier: Utf16String) {
        *self.identifier.borrow_mut() = identifier;
    }

    pub(crate) fn start_time_value(&self) -> f64 {
        self.start_time.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn end_time_value(&self) -> f64 {
        self.end_time.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn pause_on_exit_flag(&self) -> bool {
        self.pause_on_exit.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_active(&self) -> bool {
        self.active.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_active(&self, active: bool) {
        self.active.set(active);
    }

    pub(crate) fn order_added(&self) -> u64 {
        self.order_added.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_order_added(&self, order_added: u64) {
        self.order_added.set(order_added);
    }

    fn timing_changed(&self) {
        let Some(track) = self.track_cell() else {
            return;
        };
        // SAFETY: The TextTrack is live, which the cue keeps alive.
        unsafe { web_html_text_track_cue_timing_changed(track.as_ptr()) };
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-texttrackcue-track
    pub(crate) fn track(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CppInterface>> {
        // The track attribute, on getting, must return the TextTrack object of the text track in whose list of cues the
        // text track cue that the TextTrackCue object represents finds itself, if any; or null otherwise.
        Ok(self.track_cell().map(|track| wrap_cpp_cell(cx, &track)))
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-texttrackcue-id
    pub(crate) fn id(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The id attribute, on getting, must return the text track cue identifier of the text track cue that the
        // TextTrackCue object represents.
        Ok(self.identifier())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-texttrackcue-id
    pub(crate) fn set_id(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, the text track cue identifier must be set to the new value.
        self.set_identifier(value);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-texttrackcue-starttime
    pub(crate) fn start_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The startTime attribute, on getting, must return the text track cue start time of the text track cue that the
        // TextTrackCue object represents, in seconds.
        Ok(self.start_time.get())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-texttrackcue-starttime
    pub(crate) fn set_start_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, the text track cue start time must be set to the new value, interpreted in seconds; then, if the
        // TextTrackCue object's text track cue is in a text track's list of cues, and that text track is in a media
        // element's list of text tracks, and the media element's show poster flag is not set, then run the time marches
        // on steps for that media element.
        self.start_time.set(value);
        self.timing_changed();
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-texttrackcue-endtime
    pub(crate) fn end_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The endTime attribute, on getting, must return the text track cue end time of the text track cue that the
        // TextTrackCue object represents, in seconds.
        Ok(self.end_time.get())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-texttrackcue-endtime
    pub(crate) fn set_end_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, if the new value is negative Infinity or a Not-a-Number (NaN) value, then throw a TypeError
        // exception.
        if value == f64::NEG_INFINITY || value.is_nan() {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Value is negative infinity or NaN"));
        }

        // Otherwise, the text track cue end time must be set to the new value.
        self.end_time.set(value);

        // Then, if the TextTrackCue object's text track cue is in a text track's list of cues, and that text track is
        // in a media element's list of text tracks, and the media element's show poster flag is not set, then run the
        // time marches on steps for that media element.
        self.timing_changed();
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-texttrackcue-pauseonexit
    pub(crate) fn pause_on_exit(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The pauseOnExit attribute, on getting, must return true if the text track cue pause-on-exit flag of the text
        // track cue that the TextTrackCue object represents is set; or false otherwise.
        Ok(self.pause_on_exit.get())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-texttrackcue-pauseonexit
    pub(crate) fn set_pause_on_exit(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: bool) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, the text track cue pause-on-exit flag must be set if the new value is true, and must be unset
        // otherwise.
        self.pause_on_exit.set(value);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// An object of TextTrackCue or of an interface that inherits from it, as LibWeb's C++ code names it.
pub(crate) enum AnyTextTrackCue {
    TextTrackCue(Ref<TextTrackCue>),
    VTTCue(Ref<VTTCue>),
}

impl Deref for AnyTextTrackCue {
    type Target = TextTrackCue;

    fn deref(&self) -> &TextTrackCue {
        match self {
            Self::TextTrackCue(cue) => cue,
            Self::VTTCue(cue) => {
                let cue: &VTTCue = cue;
                cue.parent()
            }
        }
    }
}

impl AnyTextTrackCue {
    pub(crate) fn from_abi(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> Self {
        if let Some(cue) = cell.object_if::<VTTCue>() {
            return Self::VTTCue(cue);
        }
        Self::TextTrackCue(cell.object::<TextTrackCue>())
    }
}

//! ToggleEvent, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#toggleevent

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::{CppCell, LentCppCell, cpp_class};
use crate::bindings::event_target::CppEvent;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::lent_string::LentUtf16FlyString;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::css::css_rule::wrap_cpp_cell;
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;

/// The dictionary ToggleEventInit of HTML/ToggleEvent.idl.
pub(crate) struct ToggleEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) old_state: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) new_state: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) source: Option<CppInterface>,
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#toggleevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct ToggleEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    old_state: Utf16String,
    new_state: Utf16String,
    source: Option<CppCell>,
}

impl Wrappable for ToggleEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl ToggleEvent {
    fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: &EventInit,
        old_state: Utf16String,
        new_state: Utf16String,
        source: Option<CppCell>,
    ) -> Ref<ToggleEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.bubbles,
            event_init.cancelable,
            event_init.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| ToggleEvent {
            event,
            old_state,
            new_state,
            source,
        });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: ToggleEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<ToggleEvent>> {
        let source = event_init_dict.source.map(CppInterface::cell);
        Ok(Self::create(
            cx.vm(),
            cx.realm(),
            &r#type,
            &event_init_dict.parent,
            event_init_dict.old_state,
            event_init_dict.new_state,
            source,
        ))
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#dom-toggleevent-oldstate
    pub(crate) fn old_state(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.old_state.clone())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#dom-toggleevent-newstate
    pub(crate) fn new_state(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.new_state.clone())
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#dom-toggleevent-source
    pub(crate) fn source(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CppInterface>> {
        // The source getter steps are to return the result of retargeting source against this's currentTarget.
        Ok(self.source.as_ref().map(|source| {
            let source = self.event.retarget_against_current_target(source);
            wrap_cpp_cell(cx, &source)
        }))
    }
}

/// The Event of a new trusted ToggleEvent in the realm, for the implementation to fire.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "C++ passes each member of the dictionary")]
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_toggle_event_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    r#type: LentUtf16FlyString<'_>,
    bubbles: bool,
    cancelable: bool,
    composed: bool,
    old_state: LentUtf16FlyString<'_>,
    new_state: LentUtf16FlyString<'_>,
    source: Option<&LentCppCell<cpp_class::Element>>,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let event_init = EventInit {
        bubbles,
        cancelable,
        composed,
    };
    let r#type: Utf16String = r#type.to_utf16_fly_string().into();
    let old_state: Utf16String = old_state.to_utf16_fly_string().into();
    let new_state: Utf16String = new_state.to_utf16_fly_string().into();
    let source = source.map(CppCell::from_lent);
    let event = ToggleEvent::create(vm, realm, &r#type, &event_init, old_state, new_state, source);
    event.event().as_ptr()
}

use crate::css::css_rule::wrap_cpp_cell;

/// The dictionary TrackEventInit of HTML/TrackEvent.idl.
pub(crate) struct TrackEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) track: Option<CppInterface>,
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#trackevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct TrackEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    track: Option<CppCell>,
}

impl Wrappable for TrackEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl TrackEvent {
    fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: &EventInit,
        track: Option<CppCell>,
    ) -> Ref<TrackEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.bubbles,
            event_init.cancelable,
            event_init.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| TrackEvent { event, track });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: TrackEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<TrackEvent>> {
        let track = event_init_dict.track.map(CppInterface::cell);
        Ok(Self::create(
            cx.vm(),
            cx.realm(),
            &r#type,
            &event_init_dict.parent,
            track,
        ))
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-trackevent-track
    pub(crate) fn track(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CppInterface>> {
        Ok(self.track.as_ref().map(|track| wrap_cpp_cell(cx, track)))
    }
}

/// The Event of a new trusted TrackEvent in the realm, for the implementation to fire. The track is a VideoTrack, an
/// AudioTrack or a TextTrack.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_track_event_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    r#type: LentUtf16FlyString<'_>,
    track: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Cell>,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let event_init = EventInit {
        bubbles: false,
        cancelable: false,
        composed: false,
    };
    let r#type: Utf16String = r#type.to_utf16_fly_string().into();
    let track = CppCell::from_lent(track);
    let event = TrackEvent::create(vm, realm, &r#type, &event_init, Some(track));
    event.event().as_ptr()
}

//! VisibilityStateEntry, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#visibilitystateentry

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_into_abi};
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_entry::{AnyPerformanceEntry, PerformanceEntry};

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#visibilitystateentry
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct VisibilityStateEntry {
    entry: PerformanceEntry,
}

impl Wrappable for VisibilityStateEntry {}

impl Inherits<PerformanceEntry> for VisibilityStateEntry {
    fn parent(&self) -> &PerformanceEntry {
        &self.entry
    }
}

impl VisibilityStateEntry {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, visibility_state: Utf16String, timestamp: f64) -> Ref<Self> {
        let entry = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            // The name getter steps are to return this's visibility state.
            // The entryType getter steps are to return "visibility-state".
            // The startTime getter steps are to return this's timestamp.
            // The duration getter steps are to return zero.
            entry: PerformanceEntry::new(
                visibility_state,
                Utf16String::from_utf8("visibility-state"),
                timestamp,
                0.0,
            ),
        });
        let any_entry = AnyPerformanceEntry::VisibilityStateEntry(entry);
        any_entry.entry().set_object(any_entry);
        entry
    }
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#visibilitystateentry
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_html_create_visibility_state_entry(
    vm: &Vm,
    visibility_state: Utf16String,
    timestamp: f64,
) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(VisibilityStateEntry::create(vm, visibility_state, timestamp))
}
