        range.is_in_range(record.key())
    };

    let prev_requirements =
        |record: RecordInList<'_>, position: &Option<Rc<Key>>, object_store_position: &Option<Rc<Key>>| -> bool {
            // * If key is defined:
            if let Some(key) = &key {
                // * The record’s key is less than or equal to key.
                if !Key::less_than_or_equal(record.key(), key) {
                    return false;
                }
            }

            // * If primaryKey is defined:
            if let Some(primary_key) = &primary_key {
                let inner_record = record.index_record();
                let key = key.as_ref().expect("primaryKey is given with key");

                // * The record’s key is equal to key and the record’s value is less than or equal to primaryKey
                if Key::equals(&inner_record.key, key) {
                    if !Key::less_than_or_equal(&inner_record.value, primary_key) {
                        return false;
                    }
                }
                // * The record’s key is less than key.
                else if !Key::less_than(&inner_record.key, key) {
                    return false;
                }
            }

            // * If position is defined and source is an object store:
            if let Some(position) = position
                && source_is_object_store
            {
                // * The record’s key is less than position.
                if !Key::less_than(record.key(), position) {
                    return false;
                }
            }

            // * If position is defined and source is an index:
            if let Some(position) = position
                && source_is_index
            {
                let inner_record = record.index_record();
                let object_store_position = object_store_position
                    .as_ref()
                    .expect("a cursor of an index with a position has an object store position");

                // * The record’s key is equal to position and the record’s value is less than object store position
                if Key::equals(&inner_record.key, position) {
                    if !Key::less_than(&inner_record.value, object_store_position) {
                        return false;
                    }
                }
                // * The record’s key is less than position.
                else if !Key::less_than(&inner_record.key, position) {
                    return false;
                }
            }

            // * The record’s key is in range.
            range.is_in_range(record.key())
        };

    let prev_unique_requirements = |record: RecordInList<'_>, position: &Option<Rc<Key>>| -> bool {
        // * If key is defined:
        if let Some(key) = &key {
            // * The record’s key is less than or equal to key.
            if !Key::less_than_or_equal(record.key(), key) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        // * If position is defined:
        if let Some(position) = position {
            // * The record’s key is less than position.
            if !Key::less_than(record.key(), position) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        // * The record’s key is in range.
        range.is_in_range(record.key())
    };

    let records_of_source = |search: &mut dyn FnMut(
        &mut dyn DoubleEndedIterator<Item = RecordInList<'_>>,
    ) -> Option<FoundRecord>|
     -> Option<FoundRecord> {
        match source {
            RecordSource::ObjectStore(object_store) => {
                let records = object_store.records();
                search(&mut records.iter().map(RecordInList::ObjectStore))
            }
            RecordSource::Index(index) => {
                let records = index.records();
                search(&mut records.iter().map(RecordInList::Index))
            }
        }
    };

    // 9. While count is greater than 0:
    let mut found_record: Option<FoundRecord> = None;
    while count > 0 {
        // 1. Switch on direction:
        match direction {
            IDBCursorDirection::Next => {
                // Let found record be the first record in records which satisfy all of the following requirements:
                found_record = records_of_source(&mut |mut records| {
                    Iterator::find(&mut records, |record| {
                        next_requirements(*record, &position, &object_store_position)
                    })
                    .map(RecordInList::to_found_record)
                });
            }
            IDBCursorDirection::Nextunique => {
                // Let found record be the first record in records which satisfy all of the following requirements:
                found_record = records_of_source(&mut |mut records| {
                    Iterator::find(&mut records, |record| next_unique_requirements(*record, &position))
                        .map(RecordInList::to_found_record)
                });
            }
            IDBCursorDirection::Prev => {
                // Let found record be the last record in records which satisfy all of the following requirements:
                found_record = records_of_source(&mut |records| {
                    records
                        .rev()
                        .find(|record| prev_requirements(*record, &position, &object_store_position))
                        .map(RecordInList::to_found_record)
                });
            }
            IDBCursorDirection::Prevunique => {
                // Let temp record be the last record in records which satisfy all of the following requirements:
                let temp_record = records_of_source(&mut |records| {
                    records
                        .rev()
                        .find(|record| prev_unique_requirements(*record, &position))
                        .map(RecordInList::to_found_record)
                });

                // If temp record is defined, let found record be the first record in records whose key is equal to temp record’s key.
                found_record = None;
                if let Some(temp_record) = temp_record {
                    let temp_record_key = temp_record.key().clone();

                    found_record = records_of_source(&mut |mut records| {
                        Iterator::find(&mut records, |content_record| {
                            Key::equals(content_record.key(), &temp_record_key)
                        })
                        .map(RecordInList::to_found_record)
                    });
                }
            }
        }

        // 2. If found record is not defined, then:
        let Some(found) = &found_record else {
            // 1. Set cursor’s key to undefined.
            cursor.set_key(None);

            // 2. If source is an index, set cursor’s object store position to undefined.
            if source_is_index {
                cursor.set_object_store_position(None);
            }

            // 3. If cursor’s key only flag is false, set cursor’s value to undefined.
            if !cursor.key_only() {
                cursor.set_value(Some(Value::UNDEFINED));
            }

            // 4. Return null.
            return Ok(None);
        };

        // 3. Let position be found record’s key.
        position = Some(found.key().clone());

        // 4. If source is an index, let object store position be found record’s value.
        if let FoundRecord::Index(record) = found {
            object_store_position = Some(record.value.clone());
        }

        // 5. Decrease count by 1.
        count -= 1;
    }
    let found_record = found_record.expect("a record was found");

    // 10. Set cursor’s position to position.
    cursor.set_position(position);

    // 11. If source is an index, set cursor’s object store position to object store position.
    if source_is_index {
        cursor.set_object_store_position(object_store_position);
    }

    // 12. Set cursor’s key to found record’s key.
    cursor.set_key(Some(found_record.key().clone()));

    // 13. If cursor’s key only flag is false, then:
    if !cursor.key_only() {
        // 1. Let serialized be found record’s value if source is an object store, or found record’s referenced value otherwise.
        let serialized = match (&found_record, source) {
            (FoundRecord::ObjectStore(record), _) => record.value.clone(),
            (FoundRecord::Index(record), RecordSource::Index(index)) => index.referenced_value(record),
            (FoundRecord::Index(_), RecordSource::ObjectStore(_)) => {
                unreachable!("a record of an index is found in an index")
            }
        };

        // 2. Set cursor’s value to ! StructuredDeserialize(serialized, targetRealm)
        cursor.set_value(Some(deserialize_a_stored_record(cx, &serialized)?));
    }

    // 14. Set cursor’s got value flag to true.
    cursor.set_got_value(true);

    // 15. Return cursor.
    Ok(Some(cursor))
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#clear-an-object-store
pub(crate) fn clear_an_object_store(vm: &Vm, store: ObjectStoreRef) -> Value {
    // 1. Remove all records from store.
    store.clear_records(vm);

    // 2. In all indexes which reference store, remove all records.
    for index in store.indexes(vm).values().iter().copied() {
        Index::clear_records(index, vm);
    }

    // 3. Return undefined.
    Value::UNDEFINED
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#retrieve-a-key-from-an-object-store
pub(crate) fn retrieve_a_key_from_an_object_store(
    cx: &CallContext,
    store: ObjectStoreRef,
    range: &IDBKeyRange,
) -> Value {
    // 1. Let record be the first record in store’s list of records whose key is in range, if any.
    let record = store.first_in_range(range);

    // 2. If record was not found, return undefined.
    let Some(record) = record else {
        return Value::UNDEFINED;
    };

    // 3. Return the result of converting a key to a value with record’s key.
    convert_a_key_to_a_value(cx, &record.key)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum RecordKind {
    Key,
    Value,
    Record,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#retrieve-multiple-items-from-an-object-store
pub(crate) fn retrieve_multiple_items_from_an_object_store(
    cx: &CallContext,
    store: ObjectStoreRef,
    range: &IDBKeyRange,
    kind: RecordKind,
    direction: IDBCursorDirection,
    mut count: Option<u32>,
) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<Array>> {
    let vm = cx.vm();

    // 1. If count is not given or is 0 (zero), let count be infinity.
    if count == Some(0) {
        count = None;
    }

    // 2. Let records be an empty list of records.
    let mut records = Vec::new();

    // 3. If direction is "next" or "nextunique", set records to the first count of store’s list of records whose key is in range.
    if direction == IDBCursorDirection::Next || direction == IDBCursorDirection::Nextunique {
        records.extend(store.first_n_in_range(range, count));
    }

    // 4. If direction is "prev" or "prevunique", set records to the last count of store’s list of records whose key is in range.
    if direction == IDBCursorDirection::Prev || direction == IDBCursorDirection::Prevunique {
        records.extend(store.last_n_in_range(range, count));
    }

    // 5. Let list be an empty list.
    let list = Array::create(vm, cx.realm(), records.len() as u64, None).must();

    // 6. For each record of records, switching on kind:
    for (i, record) in records.iter().enumerate() {
        let property_key = PropertyKey::from_number(i as u64);
        match kind {
            RecordKind::Key => {
                // 1. Let key be the result of converting a key to a value with record’s key.
                let key = convert_a_key_to_a_value(cx, &record.key);

                // 2. Append key to list.
                list.create_data_property_or_throw(vm, &property_key, key).must();
            }
            RecordKind::Value => {
                // 1. Let serialized be record’s value.
                let serialized = &record.value;

                // 2. Let value be ! StructuredDeserialize(serialized, targetRealm).
                let entry = deserialize_a_stored_record(cx, serialized)?;

                // 3. Append value to list.
                list.create_data_property_or_throw(vm, &property_key, entry).must();
            }
            RecordKind::Record => {
                // 1. Let key be the record’s key.
                let key = record.key.clone();

                // 2. Let serialized be record’s value.
                let serialized = &record.value;

                // 3. Let value be ! StructuredDeserialize(serialized, targetRealm).
                let value = deserialize_a_stored_record(cx, serialized)?;

                // 4. Let recordSnapshot be a new record snapshot with its key set to key, value set to value, and primary key set to key.
                let record_snapshot = IDBRecord::create(vm, key.clone(), value, key);

                // 5. Append recordSnapshot to list.
                list.create_data_property_or_throw(vm, &property_key, record_snapshot.to_js(cx)?)
                    .must();
            }
        }
    }

    // 7. Return list.
    Ok(list)
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#retrieve-a-referenced-value-from-an-index
pub(crate) fn retrieve_a_referenced_value_from_an_index(
    cx: &CallContext,
    index: IndexRef,
    range: &IDBKeyRange,
) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    // 1. Let record be the first record in index’s list of records whose key is in range, if any.
    let record = index.first_in_range(range);

    // 2. If record was not found, return undefined.
    let Some(record) = record else {
        return Ok(Value::UNDEFINED);
    };

    // 3. Let serialized be record’s referenced value.
    let serialized = index.referenced_value(&record);

    // 4. Return ! StructuredDeserialize(serialized, targetRealm).
    deserialize_a_stored_record(cx, &serialized)
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#retrieve-a-value-from-an-index
pub(crate) fn retrieve_a_value_from_an_index(cx: &CallContext, index: IndexRef, range: &IDBKeyRange) -> Value {
    // 1. Let record be the first record in index’s list of records whose key is in range, if any.
    let record = index.first_in_range(range);

    // 2. If record was not found, return undefined.
    let Some(record) = record else {
        return Value::UNDEFINED;
    };

    // 3. Return the result of converting a key to a value with record’s value.
    convert_a_key_to_a_value(cx, &record.value)
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#queue-a-database-task
pub(crate) fn queue_a_database_task(vm: &Vm, steps: Function) {
    // To queue a database task, perform queue a task on the database access task source.
    crate::indexed_db::cpp::queue_a_task_on_the_database_access_task_source(vm, steps);
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#cleanup-indexed-database-transactions
pub(crate) fn cleanup_indexed_database_transactions(vm: &Vm, event_loop: &CppCell) -> bool {
    let mut has_matching_event_loop = false;

    Database::for_each_database(vm, |database| {
        for connection in database.associated_connections(vm).values().iter() {
            for transaction in connection.transactions(vm).values().iter() {
                let transaction = *transaction;

                // 2. For each transaction transaction with cleanup event loop matching the current event loop:
                if transaction.cleanup_event_loop() == Some(event_loop.as_ptr()) {
                    has_matching_event_loop = true;

                    // 1. Set transaction’s state to inactive.
                    assert!(transaction.state() == TransactionState::Active);
                    transaction.set_state(TransactionState::Inactive);

                    // https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#transaction-commit
                    // The implementation must attempt to commit an inactive transaction when all requests placed
                    // against the transaction have completed and their returned results handled, no new requests have
                    // been placed against the transaction, and the transaction has not been aborted

                    // FIXME: We skip committing if the transaction is waiting for prior writes.
                    //        Update the steps here text if this becomes explicit in the spec:
                    //         https://github.com/w3c/IndexedDB/issues/489#issuecomment-3994928473
                    if !transaction.request_list().execution_is_blocked() && transaction.request_list().is_empty() {
                        commit_a_transaction(vm, transaction);
                    }

                    // 2. Clear transaction’s cleanup event loop.
                    transaction.set_cleanup_event_loop(vm, None);
                }
            }
        }
    });

    // 1. If there are no transactions with cleanup event loop matching the current event loop, return false.
    // 3. Return true.
    has_matching_event_loop
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#is-a-potentially-valid-key-range
pub(crate) fn is_a_potentially_valid_key_range(cx: &CallContext, value: Value) -> bool {
    // 1. If value is a key range, return true.
    if key_range_from_value(value).is_some() {
        return true;
    }

    // 2. Let key be the result of converting a value to a key with value.
    // 3. If key is "invalid type" return false.
    // 4. Else return true.
    // AD-HOC: The type of value is checked instead, which is what decides whether the conversion returns
    //         "invalid type", so that the getters of an array's elements do not run twice.
    if value.is_number() || value.is_string() {
        return true;
    }
    if value.is_object() && value.as_object().downcast::<Date>().is_some() {
        return true;
    }
    if buffer_source_type_of(value).is_some() {
        return true;
    }
    if value.is_object() && value.is_array(cx.vm()).must() {
        return true;
    }
    false
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#retrieve-multiple-items-from-an-index
pub(crate) fn retrieve_multiple_items_from_an_index(
    target_cx: &CallContext,
    index: IndexRef,
    range: &IDBKeyRange,
    kind: RecordKind,
    direction: IDBCursorDirection,
    mut count: Option<u32>,
) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<Array>> {
    let vm = target_cx.vm();

    // 1. If count is not given or is 0 (zero), let count be infinity.
    if count == Some(0) {
        count = None;
    }

    // 2. Let records be an empty list of records.
    let mut records: Vec<IndexRecord> = Vec::new();

    // 3. Switching on direction:
    match direction {
        // "next"
        IDBCursorDirection::Next => {
            // 1. Set records to the first count of index’s list of records whose key is in range.
            records.extend(index.first_n_in_range(range, count));
        }
        // "nextunique"
        IDBCursorDirection::Nextunique => {
            // 1. Let rangeRecords be a list containing the index’s list of records whose key is in range.
            let range_records = index.first_n_in_range(range, None);

            // 2. Let rangeRecordsLength be rangeRecords’s size.
            let range_records_length = range_records.len();

            // 3. Let i be 0.
            let mut i = 0;

            // x. Append |rangeRecords[0]| to records.
            // FIXME: https://github.com/w3c/IndexedDB/issues/480
            if range_records_length > 0 {
                records.push(range_records[0].clone());
            }

            // 4. While i is less than rangeRecordsLength, then:
            while i + 1 < range_records_length {
                // 1. Increase i by 1.
                i += 1;

                // 2. if record’s size is equal to count, then break.
                if count.is_some_and(|count| records.len() == count as usize) {
                    break;
                }

                // 3. If the result of comparing two keys using the keys from |rangeRecords[i]| and |rangeRecords[i-1]| is equal, then continue.
                if Key::equals(&range_records[i].key, &range_records[i - 1].key) {
                    continue;
                }

                // 4. Else append |rangeRecords[i]| to records.
                records.push(range_records[i].clone());
            }
        }
        // "prev"
        IDBCursorDirection::Prev => {
            // 1. Set records to the last count of index’s list of records whose key is in range.
            records.extend(index.last_n_in_range(range, count));
        }
        // "prevunique"
        IDBCursorDirection::Prevunique => {
            // 1. Let rangeRecords be a list containing the index’s list of records whose key is in range.
            let range_records = index.first_n_in_range(range, None);

            // 2. Let rangeRecordsLength be rangeRecords’s size.
            let range_records_length = range_records.len();

            // 3. Let i be 0.
            let mut i = 0;

            // x. Append |rangeRecords[0]| to records.
            // FIXME: https://github.com/w3c/IndexedDB/issues/480
            if range_records_length > 0 {
                records.push(range_records[0].clone());
            }

            // 4. While i is less than rangeRecordsLength, then:
            while i + 1 < range_records_length {
                // 1. Increase i by 1.
                i += 1;

                // 2. if record’s size is equal to count, then break.
                if count.is_some_and(|count| records.len() == count as usize) {
                    break;
                }

                // 3. If the result of comparing two keys using the keys from |rangeRecords[i]| and |rangeRecords[i-1]| is equal, then continue.
                if Key::equals(&range_records[i].key, &range_records[i - 1].key) {
                    continue;
                }

                // 4. Else prepend |rangeRecords[i]| to records.
                records.insert(0, range_records[i].clone());
            }
        }
    }

    // 4. Let list be an empty list.
    let list = Array::create(vm, target_cx.realm(), records.len() as u64, None).must();

    // 5. For each record of records, switching on kind:
    for (i, record) in records.iter().enumerate() {
        let property_key = PropertyKey::from_number(i as u64);
        match kind {
            // "key"
            RecordKind::Key => {
                // 1. Let key be the result of converting a key to a value with record’s value.
                let key = convert_a_key_to_a_value(target_cx, &record.value);

                // 2. Append key to list.
                list.create_data_property_or_throw(vm, &property_key, key).must();
            }
            // "value"
            RecordKind::Value => {
                // 1. Let serialized be record’s referenced value.
                let serialized = index.referenced_value(record);

                // 2. Let value be ! StructuredDeserialize(serialized, targetRealm).
                let value = deserialize_a_stored_record(target_cx, &serialized)?;

                // 3. Append value to list.
                list.create_data_property_or_throw(vm, &property_key, value).must();
            }

            // "record"
            RecordKind::Record => {
                // 1. Let index key be the record’s key.
                let index_key = record.key.clone();

                // 2. Let key be the record’s value.
                let key = record.value.clone();

                // 3. Let serialized be record’s referenced value.
                let serialized = index.referenced_value(record);

                // 4. Let value be ! StructuredDeserialize(serialized, targetRealm).
                let value = deserialize_a_stored_record(target_cx, &serialized)?;

                // 5. Let recordSnapshot be a new record snapshot with its key set to index key, value set to value, and primary key set to key.
                let record_snapshot = IDBRecord::create(vm, index_key, value, key);

                // 6. Append recordSnapshot to list.
                list.create_data_property_or_throw(vm, &property_key, record_snapshot.to_js(target_cx)?)
                    .must();
            }
        }
    }

    // 6. Return list.
    Ok(list)
}

fn source_of_source_handle(source_handle: IDBRequestSource) -> (RecordSource, Ref<IDBTransaction>) {
    // 1. Let source be an index or an object store from sourceHandle.
    //    If sourceHandle is an index handle, then source is the index handle’s associated index.
    //    Otherwise, source is the object store handle’s associated object store.
    // 4. Let transaction be sourceHandle’s transaction.
    match source_handle {
        IDBRequestSource::Index(index) => (RecordSource::Index(index.index()), index.transaction_object()),
        IDBRequestSource::ObjectStore(object_store) => (
            RecordSource::ObjectStore(object_store.store()),
            object_store.transaction_object(),
        ),
        IDBRequestSource::Empty | IDBRequestSource::Cursor(_) => {
            unreachable!("the source handle is an index handle or an object store handle")
        }
    }
}

fn retrieve_multiple_items_operation(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    source: RecordSource,
    range: Ref<IDBKeyRange>,
    kind: RecordKind,
    direction: IDBCursorDirection,
    count: Option<u32>,
) -> Operation {
    match source {
        // 11. If source is an index, set operation to retrieve multiple items from an index with targetRealm, source, range, kind, direction, and count if given.
        RecordSource::Index(index) => create_operation(
            vm,
            (realm, index, range, NoCells(kind), NoCells(direction), count),
            |vm, &(realm, index, range, ref kind, ref direction, count)| {
                let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);
                Ok(Value::from_object(retrieve_multiple_items_from_an_index(
                    &cx,
                    index,
                    &range,
                    kind.0,
                    direction.0,
                    count,
                )?))
            },
        ),
        // 12. Else set operation to retrieve multiple items from an object store with targetRealm, source, range, kind, direction, and count if given.
        RecordSource::ObjectStore(object_store) => create_operation(
            vm,
            (realm, object_store, range, NoCells(kind), NoCells(direction), count),
            |vm, &(realm, object_store, range, ref kind, ref direction, count)| {
                let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);
                Ok(Value::from_object(retrieve_multiple_items_from_an_object_store(
                    &cx,
                    object_store,
                    &range,
                    kind.0,
                    direction.0,
                    count,
                )?))
            },
        ),
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#create-a-request-to-retrieve-multiple-items
pub(crate) fn create_a_request_to_retrieve_multiple_items(
    cx: &CallContext,
    source_handle: IDBRequestSource,
    kind: RecordKind,
    query_or_options: Value,
    mut count: Option<u32>,
) -> WebIdlResult<AnyIDBRequest> {
    let vm = cx.vm();

    // 1. Let source be an index or an object store from sourceHandle.
    //    If sourceHandle is an index handle, then source is the index handle’s associated index.
    //    Otherwise, source is the object store handle’s associated object store.
    let (source, transaction) = source_of_source_handle(source_handle);

    // 2. If source has been deleted, throw an "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
    // 3. If source is an index and source’s object store has been deleted, throw an "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
    let is_source_or_object_store_deleted = match source {
        RecordSource::ObjectStore(object_store) => object_store.is_deleted(),
        RecordSource::Index(index) => index.is_deleted() || index.object_store().is_deleted(),
    };
    if is_source_or_object_store_deleted {
        return Err(Exception::Dom(
            "InvalidStateError",
            Utf16String::from_utf8("Source or its object store has been deleted"),
        ));
    }

    // 4. Let transaction be sourceHandle’s transaction.
    // NB: source_of_source_handle() found the transaction with the source.

    // 5. If transaction’s state is not active, then throw a "TransactionInactiveError" DOMException.
    if !transaction.is_active() {
        return Err(Exception::Dom(
            "TransactionInactiveError",
            Utf16String::from_utf8("Transaction is not active while creating retrieve multiple items request"),
        ));
    }

    // 6. Let range be a key range.
    let range;

    // 7. Let direction be a cursor direction.
    let mut direction = IDBCursorDirection::Next;

    // 8. If running is a potentially valid key range with queryOrOptions is true, then:
    // AD-HOC: Check if query_or_options is null following https://github.com/w3c/IndexedDB/issues/475
    if query_or_options.is_nullish() || is_a_potentially_valid_key_range(cx, query_or_options) {
        // 1. Set range to the result of converting a value to a key range with queryOrOptions. Rethrow any exceptions.
        range = convert_a_value_to_a_key_range(cx, Some(query_or_options), false)?;

        // 2. Set direction to "next".
        direction = IDBCursorDirection::Next;
    }
    // 9. Else:
    else {
        // 1. Set range to the result of converting a value to a key range with queryOrOptions["query"]. Rethrow any exceptions.
        range = convert_a_value_to_a_key_range(
            cx,
            Some(query_or_options.get(vm, &PropertyKey::from_utf8("query"))?),
            false,
        )?;

        // 2. Set count to queryOrOptions["count"].
        count = Some(query_or_options.get(vm, &PropertyKey::from_utf8("count"))?.to_u32(vm)?);

        // 3. Set direction to queryOrOptions["direction"].
        let direction_value = query_or_options
            .get(vm, &PropertyKey::from_utf8("direction"))?
            .to_utf16_string(vm)?;
        if direction_value == Utf16String::from_utf8("next") {
            direction = IDBCursorDirection::Next;
        } else if direction_value == Utf16String::from_utf8("nextunique") {
            direction = IDBCursorDirection::Nextunique;
        } else if direction_value == Utf16String::from_utf8("prev") {
            direction = IDBCursorDirection::Prev;
        } else if direction_value == Utf16String::from_utf8("prevunique") {
            direction = IDBCursorDirection::Prevunique;
        }
    }

    // 10. Let operation be an algorithm to run.
    let operation = retrieve_multiple_items_operation(vm, cx.realm(), source, range, kind, direction, count);

    // 13. Return the result (an IDBRequest) of running asynchronously execute a request with sourceHandle and operation.
    Ok(asynchronously_execute_a_request(vm, source_handle, operation, None))
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#create-a-request-to-retrieve-multiple-items
pub(crate) fn create_a_request_to_retrieve_multiple_items_with_options(
    cx: &CallContext,
    source_handle: IDBRequestSource,
    kind: RecordKind,
    options: &IDBGetAllOptions,
) -> WebIdlResult<AnyIDBRequest> {
    let vm = cx.vm();

    // 1. Let source be an index or an object store from sourceHandle.
    //    If sourceHandle is an index handle, then source is the index handle’s associated index.
    //    Otherwise, source is the object store handle’s associated object store.
    let (source, transaction) = source_of_source_handle(source_handle);

    // 2. If source has been deleted, throw an "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
    // 3. If source is an index and source’s object store has been deleted, throw an "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
    let is_source_or_object_store_deleted = match source {
        RecordSource::ObjectStore(object_store) => object_store.is_deleted(),
        RecordSource::Index(index) => index.is_deleted() || index.object_store().is_deleted(),
    };
    if is_source_or_object_store_deleted {
        return Err(Exception::Dom(
            "InvalidStateError",
            Utf16String::from_utf8("Source or its object store has been deleted"),
        ));
    }

    // 4. Let transaction be sourceHandle’s transaction.
    // NB: source_of_source_handle() found the transaction with the source.

    // 5. If transaction’s state is not active, then throw a "TransactionInactiveError" DOMException.
    if !transaction.is_active() {
        return Err(Exception::Dom(
            "TransactionInactiveError",
            Utf16String::from_utf8("Transaction is not active while creating retrieve multiple items request"),
        ));
    }

    // 6. Let range be a key range.
    let range = convert_a_value_to_a_key_range(cx, Some(options.query), false)?;

    // 10. Let operation be an algorithm to run.
    let operation =
        retrieve_multiple_items_operation(vm, cx.realm(), source, range, kind, options.direction, options.count);

    // 13. Return the result (an IDBRequest) of running asynchronously execute a request with sourceHandle and operation.
    Ok(asynchronously_execute_a_request(vm, source_handle, operation, None))
}

pub(crate) fn convert_a_key_path_to_a_value(cx: &CallContext, key_path: &KeyPath) -> Value {
    let vm = cx.vm();
    match key_path {
        KeyPath::String(value) => Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(vm, value.clone())),
        KeyPath::Sequence(values) => {
            let list = MarkedVec::with_capacity(vm, values.len());
            for entry in values {
                list.push(Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(vm, entry.clone())));
            }
            Value::from_object(Array::create_from_list(vm, cx.realm(), &list))
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn set_idb_request_result(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, request: AnyIDBRequest, database: Ref<IDBDatabase>) {
    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);
    request.set_result(database.to_js(&cx).must());
}

/// The value of a special key path property of a Blob or a File, https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#key-path-construct
fn key_path_value_for_blob_or_file(cx: &CallContext, value: Value, identifier: &Utf16String) -> Option<Value> {
    if !value.is_object() {
        return None;
    }
    let object = value.as_object();
    if !is_host_instance_of(&object, Blob::wrapper_class()) {
        return None;
    }
    let blob = match implementation_if::<Blob>(object) {
        Some(blob) => AnyBlob::Blob(blob),
        None => AnyBlob::File(implementation_of::<File>(object)),
    };
    if *identifier == Utf16String::from_utf8("size") {
        #[allow(
            clippy::cast_precision_loss,
            reason = "the C++ converted the size to a double as well"
        )]
        return Some(Value::from_f64(blob.raw_bytes().len() as f64));
    }
    if *identifier == Utf16String::from_utf8("type") {
        return Some(Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(
            cx.vm(),
            blob.type_string().clone(),
        )));
    }

    if let AnyBlob::File(file) = blob {
        if *identifier == Utf16String::from_utf8("name") {
            return Some(Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(
                cx.vm(),
                file.name_string().clone(),
            )));
        }
        if *identifier == Utf16String::from_utf8("lastModified") {
            #[allow(
                clippy::cast_precision_loss,
                reason = "the C++ converted the time to a double as well"
            )]
            return Some(Value::from_f64(file.last_modified_value() as f64));
        }
    }

    None
}

//! Databases, https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#database-construct, and the connections associated with them

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, GcRefCell, GcWeak, MarkedVec, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;
use crate::indexed_db::idb_database::{ConnectionState, IDBDatabase};
use crate::indexed_db::idb_transaction::IDBTransaction;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::algorithms::queue_a_database_task;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::function::Function;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::object_store::ObjectStoreRef;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::storage::storage;
use crate::storage_api::storage_key::StorageKey;

type WeakConnection = GcWeak<EmbedderCell<crate::bindings::interface::Wrapped<IDBDatabase>>>;

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct PendingConnectionWait {
    #[gc(untraced = "the connections are weak")]
    connections: Vec<WeakConnection>,
    callback: Function,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#database-construct
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Database {
    #[gc(untraced = "the connections are weak")]
    associated_connections: RefCell<Vec<WeakConnection>>,
    pending_connection_wait: GcRefCell<Option<PendingConnectionWait>>,

    // A database has a name which identifies it within a specific storage key.
    name: Utf16String,

    // A database has a version. When a database is first created, its version is 0 (zero).
    version: Cell<u64>,

    // A database has at most one associated upgrade transaction, which is either null or an upgrade transaction, and is initially null.
    upgrade_transaction: Cell<Option<Ref<IDBTransaction>>>,

    // A database has zero or more object stores which hold the data stored in the database.
    object_stores: GcRefCell<Vec<ObjectStoreRef>>,
}

static DATABASE_CLASS: EmbedderClass<Database> = EmbedderClass::new("IndexedDBDatabase");

impl EmbedderValue for Database {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &DATABASE_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type DatabaseRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<Database>>;

impl Database {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, name: &Utf16String) -> DatabaseRef {
        DATABASE_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| Database {
            associated_connections: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            pending_connection_wait: GcRefCell::new(None),
            name: name.clone(),
            version: Cell::new(0),
            upgrade_transaction: Cell::new(None),
            object_stores: GcRefCell::new(Vec::new()),
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_version(&self, version: u64) {
        self.version.set(version);
    }

    pub(crate) fn version(&self) -> u64 {
        self.version.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn name(&self) -> Utf16String {
        self.name.clone()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_upgrade_transaction(&self, transaction: Option<Ref<IDBTransaction>>) {
        self.upgrade_transaction.set(transaction);
    }

    pub(crate) fn upgrade_transaction(&self) -> Option<Ref<IDBTransaction>> {
        self.upgrade_transaction.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn object_stores<'vm>(&self, vm: &'vm Vm) -> MarkedVec<'vm, ObjectStoreRef> {
        let object_stores = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        object_stores.extend_from_slice(&self.object_stores.borrow());
        object_stores
    }

    pub(crate) fn object_store_with_name(&self, name: &Utf16String) -> Option<ObjectStoreRef> {
        self.object_stores
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .find(|object_store| object_store.name() == *name)
            .copied()
    }

    pub(crate) fn add_object_store(this: DatabaseRef, vm: &Vm, object_store: ObjectStoreRef) {
        this.object_stores.borrow_mut(vm).push(object_store);
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove_object_store(this: DatabaseRef, vm: &Vm, object_store: ObjectStoreRef) {
        let mut object_stores = this.object_stores.borrow_mut(vm);
        if let Some(position) = object_stores.iter().position(|entry| *entry == object_store) {
            object_stores.remove(position);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn associate(&self, vm: &Vm, connection: Ref<IDBDatabase>) {
        self.associated_connections
            .borrow_mut()
            .push(GcWeak::new(vm.heap(), connection));
    }

    pub(crate) fn dissociate(&self, connection: Ref<IDBDatabase>) {
        self.associated_connections
            .borrow_mut()
            .retain(|entry| entry.get().is_some_and(|entry| entry != connection));
    }

    pub(crate) fn associated_connections<'vm>(&self, vm: &'vm Vm) -> MarkedVec<'vm, Ref<IDBDatabase>> {
        let connections = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        for connection in self.associated_connections.borrow().iter() {
            if let Some(connection) = connection.get() {
                connections.push(connection);
            }
        }
        connections
    }

    pub(crate) fn associated_connections_except<'vm>(
        &self,
        vm: &'vm Vm,
        connection: Ref<IDBDatabase>,
    ) -> MarkedVec<'vm, Ref<IDBDatabase>> {
        let connections = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        for associated_connection in self.associated_connections.borrow().iter() {
            if let Some(associated_connection) = associated_connection.get()
                && associated_connection != connection
            {
                connections.push(associated_connection);
            }
        }
        connections
    }

    pub(crate) fn for_key<'vm>(vm: &'vm Vm, key: &StorageKey) -> MarkedVec<'vm, DatabaseRef> {
        let databases = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        storage(vm).for_each_database_of_key(key, |database| databases.push(database));
        databases
    }

    pub(crate) fn for_key_and_name(vm: &Vm, key: &StorageKey, name: &Utf16String) -> Option<DatabaseRef> {
        storage(vm).database(key, name)
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_for_key_and_name(vm: &Vm, key: &StorageKey, name: &Utf16String) -> DatabaseRef {
        let value = Database::create(vm, name);
        storage(vm).set_database(vm, key, name, value);
        value
    }

    pub(crate) fn delete_for_key_and_name(vm: &Vm, key: &StorageKey, name: &Utf16String) {
        storage(vm).remove_database(vm, key, name);
    }

    pub(crate) fn for_each_database(vm: &Vm, mut visitor: impl FnMut(DatabaseRef)) {
        let databases = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        storage(vm).for_each_database(|database| databases.push(database));
        for database in databases.values().iter() {
            visitor(*database);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn wait_for_connections_to_close(&self, vm: &Vm, connections: &[Ref<IDBDatabase>], after_all: Function) {
        let all_closed = connections.iter().all(|entry| entry.state() == ConnectionState::Closed);

        if all_closed {
            queue_a_database_task(vm, after_all);
            return;
        }

        assert!(self.pending_connection_wait.borrow().is_none());
        let weak_connections = connections
            .iter()
            .map(|connection| GcWeak::new(vm.heap(), *connection))
            .collect();
        *self.pending_connection_wait.borrow_mut(vm) = Some(PendingConnectionWait {
            connections: weak_connections,
            callback: after_all,
        });
    }

    pub(crate) fn check_pending_connection_wait(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        let callback = {
            let wait = self.pending_connection_wait.borrow();
            let Some(wait) = &*wait else {
                return;
            };
            for connection in &wait.connections {
                if let Some(connection) = connection.get()
                    && connection.state() != ConnectionState::Closed
                {
                    return;
                }
            }
            wait.callback
        };

        // All connections are closed - invoke the callback and clear the wait
        *self.pending_connection_wait.borrow_mut(vm) = None;
        queue_a_database_task(vm, callback);
    }
}

//! GC::Function as the C++ implementation used it: steps that run later, which keep their captures alive until then.

use core::any::Any;
use core::marker::PhantomData;

use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, Trace, Value, Visitor, Vm};

use crate::bindings::WebIdlResult;

trait Steps: Trace {
    /// Takes the argument, an Option<A>, and runs the steps with it.
    fn call(&self, vm: &Vm, argument: &mut dyn Any);
}

struct CapturedSteps<C, A> {
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, &C, A),
}

// SAFETY: The steps are a plain function, which holds no cells.
unsafe impl<C: Trace, A> Trace for CapturedSteps<C, A> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.captures.trace(visitor);
    }
}

impl<C: Trace, A: 'static> Steps for CapturedSteps<C, A> {
    fn call(&self, vm: &Vm, argument: &mut dyn Any) {
        let argument = argument
            .downcast_mut::<Option<A>>()
            .and_then(Option::take)
            .expect("a function is called with an argument of its type");
        (self.steps)(vm, &self.captures, argument);
    }
}

pub(crate) struct FunctionCell(Box<dyn Steps>);

// SAFETY: The captures of the steps are all the cells this reaches.
unsafe impl Trace for FunctionCell {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.0.trace(visitor);
    }
}

static FUNCTION_CLASS: EmbedderClass<FunctionCell> = EmbedderClass::new("IndexedDBFunction");

impl EmbedderValue for FunctionCell {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &FUNCTION_CLASS;
}

/// A GC::Function<void(A)>.
pub(crate) struct FunctionWith<A> {
    cell: Gc<EmbedderCell<FunctionCell>>,
    _argument: PhantomData<fn(A)>,
}

impl<A> Clone for FunctionWith<A> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        *self
    }
}

impl<A> Copy for FunctionWith<A> {}

// SAFETY: The cell is all the function reaches.
unsafe impl<A> Trace for FunctionWith<A> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.cell.trace(visitor);
    }
}

/// A GC::Function<void()>.
pub(crate) type Function = FunctionWith<()>;

/// GC::create_function(), with captures that the function keeps alive.
pub(crate) fn create_function_with<A: 'static, C: Trace + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, &C, A),
) -> FunctionWith<A> {
    let cell = FUNCTION_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| {
        let steps: Box<dyn Steps> = Box::new(CapturedSteps { captures, steps });
        FunctionCell(steps)
    });
    FunctionWith {
        cell,
        _argument: PhantomData,
    }
}

pub(crate) fn create_function<C: Trace + 'static>(vm: &Vm, captures: C, steps: fn(&Vm, &C, ())) -> Function {
    create_function_with(vm, captures, steps)
}

impl<A: 'static> FunctionWith<A> {
    pub(crate) fn call(self, vm: &Vm, argument: A) {
        let mut argument = Some(argument);
        self.cell.0.call(vm, &mut argument);
        // NB: The function keeps its captures alive while it runs.
        core::hint::black_box(self.cell);
    }
}

pub(crate) fn call_function(vm: &Vm, function: Function) {
    function.call(vm, ());
}

/// A value that holds no cells, for the captures of a function: keys and plain data.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct NoCells<T>(pub(crate) T);

// SAFETY: The value holds no cells.
unsafe impl<T> Trace for NoCells<T> {
    fn trace(&self, _: &mut Visitor) {}
}

trait OperationSteps: Trace {
    fn call(&self, vm: &Vm) -> WebIdlResult<Value>;
}

struct CapturedOperation<C> {
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, &C) -> WebIdlResult<Value>,
}

// SAFETY: The steps are a plain function, which holds no cells.
unsafe impl<C: Trace> Trace for CapturedOperation<C> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.captures.trace(visitor);
    }
}

impl<C: Trace> OperationSteps for CapturedOperation<C> {
    fn call(&self, vm: &Vm) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        (self.steps)(vm, &self.captures)
    }
}

pub(crate) struct OperationCell(Box<dyn OperationSteps>);

// SAFETY: The captures of the steps are all the cells this reaches.
unsafe impl Trace for OperationCell {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.0.trace(visitor);
    }
}

static OPERATION_CLASS: EmbedderClass<OperationCell> = EmbedderClass::new("IndexedDBOperation");

impl EmbedderValue for OperationCell {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &OPERATION_CLASS;
}

/// A GC::Function<WebIDL::ExceptionOr<JS::Value>()>: the operation of a request.
pub(crate) type Operation = Gc<EmbedderCell<OperationCell>>;

/// GC::create_function() for an operation, with captures that it keeps alive.
pub(crate) fn create_operation<C: Trace + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, &C) -> WebIdlResult<Value>,
) -> Operation {
    OPERATION_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| {
        let steps: Box<dyn OperationSteps> = Box::new(CapturedOperation { captures, steps });
        OperationCell(steps)
    })
}

pub(crate) fn perform_operation(vm: &Vm, operation: Operation) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    let result = operation.0.call(vm);
    // NB: The operation keeps its captures alive while it runs.
    core::hint::black_box(operation);
    result
}

impl Function {
    /// The cell, for LibWeb's C++ code to hold until it runs the function.
    pub(crate) fn cell_as_ptr(self) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
        self.cell.as_ptr().cast()
    }

    /// The function whose cell cell_as_ptr() handed out.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The cell must be that of a function that takes no argument.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_cell(cell: Gc<EmbedderCell<FunctionCell>>) -> Self {
        Self {
            cell,
            _argument: PhantomData,
        }
    }
}

//! Indexes, https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#index-construct

use core::cell::{Cell, Ref, RefCell};
use core::cmp::Ordering;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, Trace, Vm};

use crate::indexed_db::idb_key_range::IDBKeyRange;
use crate::indexed_db::idb_record::{IndexRecord, StorageSerializationRecord};
use crate::indexed_db::internal::algorithms::KeyPath;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::key::Key;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::object_store::ObjectStoreRef;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::record_range::{KeyedRecord, record_range_for_key_range};

impl KeyedRecord for IndexRecord {
    fn key(&self) -> &Key {
        &self.key
    }
}

fn compare_index_records(a: &IndexRecord, b: &IndexRecord) -> Ordering {
    let key_comparison = Key::compare_two_keys(&a.key, &b.key);
    if key_comparison != 0 {
        return key_comparison.cmp(&0);
    }

    Key::compare_two_keys(&a.value, &b.value).cmp(&0)
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#index-construct
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Index {
    // An index [...] has a referenced object store.
    object_store: ObjectStoreRef,

    // The index has a list of records which hold the data stored in the index.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    records: RefCell<Vec<IndexRecord>>,

    // An index has a name, which is a name. At any one time, the name is unique within index’s referenced object store.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    name: RefCell<Utf16String>,

    // An index has a unique flag. When true, the index enforces that no two records in the index has the same key.
    unique: bool,

    // An index has a multiEntry flag. This flag affects how the index behaves when the result of evaluating the index’s key path yields an array key.
    multi_entry: bool,

    // The keys are derived from the referenced object store’s values using a key path.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    key_path: KeyPath,

    deleted: Cell<bool>,

    // NB: Whether the request that creates the index in its upgrade transaction has yet to be processed. Until then,
    //     storing records into the object store leaves the index alone.
    pending_creation: Cell<bool>,
}

static INDEX_CLASS: EmbedderClass<Index> = EmbedderClass::new("IndexedDBIndex");

impl EmbedderValue for Index {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &INDEX_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type IndexRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<Index>>;

impl Index {
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        store: ObjectStoreRef,
        name: &Utf16String,
        key_path: &KeyPath,
        unique: bool,
        multi_entry: bool,
    ) -> IndexRef {
        let index = INDEX_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| Index {
            object_store: store,
            records: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            name: RefCell::new(name.clone()),
            unique,
            multi_entry,
            key_path: key_path.clone(),
            deleted: Cell::new(false),
            pending_creation: Cell::new(false),
        });
        store.index_set_set(vm, name.clone(), index);
        index
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_name(this: IndexRef, vm: &Vm, name: Utf16String) {
        // NOTE: Update the key in the map so it still matches the name
        let old_value = this
            .object_store
            .index_set_take(vm, &this.name())
            .expect("the index is in its object store's index set");
        this.object_store.index_set_set(vm, name.clone(), old_value);

        *this.name.borrow_mut() = name;
    }

    pub(crate) fn name(&self) -> Utf16String {
        self.name.borrow().clone()
    }

    pub(crate) fn unique(&self) -> bool {
        self.unique
    }

    pub(crate) fn multi_entry(&self) -> bool {
        self.multi_entry
    }

    pub(crate) fn object_store(&self) -> ObjectStoreRef {
        self.object_store
    }

    pub(crate) fn records(&self) -> Ref<'_, Vec<IndexRecord>> {
        self.records.borrow()
    }

    pub(crate) fn key_path(&self) -> &KeyPath {
        &self.key_path
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_deleted(&self) -> bool {
        self.deleted.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_deleted(&self, deleted: bool) {
        self.deleted.set(deleted);
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_pending_creation(&self) -> bool {
        self.pending_creation.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_pending_creation(&self, pending_creation: bool) {
        self.pending_creation.set(pending_creation);
    }

    pub(crate) fn has_record_with_key(&self, key: &Key) -> bool {
        self.records
            .borrow()
            .binary_search_by(|record| Key::ordering(&record.key, key))
            .is_ok()
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#index-referenced-value
    pub(crate) fn referenced_value(&self, index_record: &IndexRecord) -> StorageSerializationRecord {
        // Records in an index are said to have a referenced value.
        // This is the value of the record in the index’s referenced object store which has a key equal to the index’s record’s value.
        let store_records = self.object_store.records();
        let position = store_records
            .binary_search_by(|record| Key::ordering(&record.key, &index_record.value))
            .expect("the referenced object store has a record with the index record's value as its key");
        store_records[position].value.clone()
    }

    pub(crate) fn clear_records(this: IndexRef, vm: &Vm) {
        let deleted = core::mem::take(&mut *this.records.borrow_mut());
        if let Some(log) = this.object_store.mutation_log()
            && !deleted.is_empty()
        {
            log.note_index_records_deleted(vm, this, deleted);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn first_in_range(&self, range: &IDBKeyRange) -> Option<IndexRecord> {
        let records = self.records.borrow();
        let record_range = record_range_for_key_range(&records, range);
        if record_range.start == record_range.end {
            return None;
        }
        Some(records[record_range.start].clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn first_n_in_range(&self, range: &IDBKeyRange, count: Option<u32>) -> Vec<IndexRecord> {
        let mut result = Vec::new();
        let records = self.records.borrow();
        let record_range = record_range_for_key_range(&records, range);
        for record in &records[record_range.start..record_range.end] {
            result.push(record.clone());

            if count.is_some_and(|count| result.len() >= count as usize) {
                break;
            }
        }

        result
    }

    pub(crate) fn last_n_in_range(&self, range: &IDBKeyRange, count: Option<u32>) -> Vec<IndexRecord> {
        let mut result = Vec::new();
        let records = self.records.borrow();
        let record_range = record_range_for_key_range(&records, range);
        for record in records[record_range.start..record_range.end].iter().rev() {
            result.push(record.clone());

            if count.is_some_and(|count| result.len() >= count as usize) {
                break;
            }
        }

        result
    }

    pub(crate) fn count_records_in_range(&self, range: &IDBKeyRange) -> u64 {
        let records = self.records.borrow();
        let record_range = record_range_for_key_range(&records, range);
        (record_range.end - record_range.start) as u64
    }

    pub(crate) fn store_a_record(this: IndexRef, vm: &Vm, record: &IndexRecord) {
        if let Some(log) = this.object_store.mutation_log() {
            log.note_index_record_stored(vm, this, record.clone());
        }

        // NOTE: The record is stored in index’s list of records such that the list is sorted primarily on the records keys, and secondarily on the records values, in ascending order.
        let mut records = this.records.borrow_mut();
        if records
            .last()
            .is_none_or(|last| compare_index_records(last, record) != Ordering::Greater)
        {
            records.push(record.clone());
            return;
        }

        let position = records.partition_point(|existing| compare_index_records(existing, record) == Ordering::Less);
        records.insert(position, record.clone());
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove_record(&self, record: &IndexRecord) {
        let mut records = self.records.borrow_mut();
        let position = records.partition_point(|existing| compare_index_records(existing, record) == Ordering::Less);
        if position < records.len() && compare_index_records(&records[position], record) == Ordering::Equal {
            records.remove(position);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove_records_with_value_in_range(this: IndexRef, vm: &Vm, range: &IDBKeyRange) {
        let log = this.object_store.mutation_log();
        let mut removed_records = Vec::new();
        let mut records = this.records.borrow_mut();
        let mut i = 0;
        while i < records.len() {
            if range.is_in_range(&records[i].value) {
                let removed_record = records.remove(i);
                if log.is_some() {
                    removed_records.push(removed_record);
                }
                continue;
            }
            i += 1;
        }
        drop(records);
        if !removed_records.is_empty() {
            log.expect("records are only collected for a mutation log")
                .note_index_records_deleted(vm, this, removed_records);
        }
    }
}

//! Key generators, https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#key-generator-construct

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#key-generator-construct

// The current number is always a positive integer less than or equal to 2^53 (9007199254740992) + 1.
pub(crate) const MAX_KEY_GENERATOR_VALUE: f64 = 9007199254740992.0;

pub(crate) struct KeyGenerator {
    // A key generator has a current number.
    // The current number is always a positive integer less than or equal to 2^53 (9007199254740992) + 1.
    // The initial value of a key generator's current number is 1, set when the associated object store is created.
    // The current number is incremented as keys are generated, and may be updated to a specific value by using explicit keys.
    current_number: u64,
}

impl KeyGenerator {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
        Self { current_number: 1 }
    }

    pub(crate) fn current_number(&self) -> u64 {
        self.current_number
    }

    pub(crate) fn increment(&mut self, amount: u64) {
        self.current_number += amount;
    }

    pub(crate) fn set(&mut self, value: u64) {
        self.current_number = value;
    }
}

//! Keys, https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#key-construct

use std::rc::Rc;

use core::cmp::Ordering;

use ak::{Utf16String, Utf16StringUnits};

// A key has an associated type which is one of: number, date, string, binary, or array.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub(crate) enum KeyType {
    Invalid,
    Number,
    Date,
    String,
    Binary,
    Array,
}

// A key also has an associated value, which will be either:
// * an unrestricted double if type is number or date,
// * a DOMString if type is string,
// * a byte sequence if type is binary,
// * a list of other keys if type is array.
pub(crate) enum KeyValue {
    Double(f64),
    String(Utf16String),
    Bytes(Vec<u8>),
    Keys(Vec<Rc<Key>>),
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#key-construct
pub(crate) struct Key {
    r#type: KeyType,
    value: KeyValue,
}

impl Key {
    pub(crate) fn create(r#type: KeyType, value: KeyValue) -> Rc<Key> {
        Rc::new(Key { r#type, value })
    }

    pub(crate) fn r#type(&self) -> KeyType {
        self.r#type
    }

    pub(crate) fn value(&self) -> &KeyValue {
        &self.value
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_invalid(&self) -> bool {
        self.r#type == KeyType::Invalid
    }

    pub(crate) fn value_as_double(&self) -> f64 {
        match self.value {
            KeyValue::Double(value) => value,
            _ => unreachable!("the key's value is a double"),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn value_as_string(&self) -> &Utf16String {
        match &self.value {
            KeyValue::String(value) => value,
            _ => unreachable!("the key's value is a string"),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn value_as_byte_buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
        match &self.value {
            KeyValue::Bytes(value) => value,
            _ => unreachable!("the key's value is a byte sequence"),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn value_as_vector(&self) -> &[Rc<Key>] {
        match &self.value {
            KeyValue::Keys(value) => value,
            _ => unreachable!("the key's value is a list of keys"),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn subkeys(&self) -> &[Rc<Key>] {
        assert_eq!(self.r#type, KeyType::Array);
        self.value_as_vector()
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_number(value: f64) -> Rc<Key> {
        Self::create(KeyType::Number, KeyValue::Double(value))
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_date(value: f64) -> Rc<Key> {
        Self::create(KeyType::Date, KeyValue::Double(value))
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_string(value: Utf16String) -> Rc<Key> {
        Self::create(KeyType::String, KeyValue::String(value))
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_binary(value: Vec<u8>) -> Rc<Key> {
        Self::create(KeyType::Binary, KeyValue::Bytes(value))
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_array(value: Vec<Rc<Key>>) -> Rc<Key> {
        Self::create(KeyType::Array, KeyValue::Keys(value))
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_invalid(value: &str) -> Rc<Key> {
        Self::create(KeyType::Invalid, KeyValue::String(Utf16String::from_utf8(value)))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#compare-two-keys
    pub(crate) fn compare_two_keys(a: &Key, b: &Key) -> i8 {
        // 1. Let ta be the type of a.
        let ta = a.r#type();

        // 2. Let tb be the type of b.
        let tb = b.r#type();

        // 3. If ta does not equal tb, then run these steps:
        if ta != tb {
            // 1. If ta is array, then return 1.
            if ta == KeyType::Array {
                return 1;
            }

            // 2. If tb is array, then return -1.
            if tb == KeyType::Array {
                return -1;
            }

            // 3. If ta is binary, then return 1.
            if ta == KeyType::Binary {
                return 1;
            }

            // 4. If tb is binary, then return -1.
            if tb == KeyType::Binary {
                return -1;
            }

            // 5. If ta is string, then return 1.
            if ta == KeyType::String {
                return 1;
            }

            // 6. If tb is string, then return -1.
            if tb == KeyType::String {
                return -1;
            }

            // 7. If ta is date, then return 1.
            if ta == KeyType::Date {
                return 1;
            }

            // 8. Assert: tb is date.
            assert_eq!(tb, KeyType::Date);

            // 9. Return -1.
            return -1;
        }

        // 4. Let va be the value of a.
        let va = &a.value;

        // 5. Let vb be the value of b.
        let vb = &b.value;

        // 6. Switch on ta:
        match ta {
            KeyType::Invalid => unreachable!("invalid keys are not compared"),
            // number
            // date
            KeyType::Number | KeyType::Date => {
                let (KeyValue::Double(a_value), KeyValue::Double(b_value)) = (va, vb) else {
                    unreachable!("the value of a number or a date key is a double");
                };

                // 1. If va is greater than vb, then return 1.
                if a_value > b_value {
                    return 1;
                }

                // 2. If va is less than vb, then return -1.
                if a_value < b_value {
                    return -1;
                }

                // 3. Return 0.
                0
            }
            // string
            KeyType::String => {
                let (KeyValue::String(a_value), KeyValue::String(b_value)) = (va, vb) else {
                    unreachable!("the value of a string key is a string");
                };

                // 1. If va is code unit less than vb, then return -1.
                if code_unit_less_than(a_value, b_value) {
                    return -1;
                }

                // 2. If vb is code unit less than va, then return 1.
                if code_unit_less_than(b_value, a_value) {
                    return 1;
                }

                // 3. Return 0.
                0
            }
            // binary
            KeyType::Binary => {
                let (KeyValue::Bytes(a_value), KeyValue::Bytes(b_value)) = (va, vb) else {
                    unreachable!("the value of a binary key is a byte sequence");
                };

                // 1. If va is byte less than vb, then return -1.
                if is_byte_less_than(a_value, b_value) {
                    return -1;
                }

                // 2. If vb is byte less than va, then return 1.
                if is_byte_less_than(b_value, a_value) {
                    return 1;
                }

                // 3. Return 0.
                0
            }
            // array
            KeyType::Array => {
                let (KeyValue::Keys(a_value), KeyValue::Keys(b_value)) = (va, vb) else {
                    unreachable!("the value of an array key is a list of keys");
                };

                // 1. Let length be the lesser of va’s size and vb’s size.
                let length = a_value.len().min(b_value.len());

                // 2. Let i be 0.
                let mut i = 0;

                // 3. While i is less than length, then:
                while i < length {
                    // 1. Let c be the result of recursively comparing two keys with va[i] and vb[i].
                    let c = Self::compare_two_keys(&a_value[i], &b_value[i]);

                    // 2. If c is not 0, return c.
                    if c != 0 {
                        return c;
                    }

                    // 3. Increase i by 1.
                    i += 1;
                }

                // 4. If va’s size is greater than vb’s size, then return 1.
                if a_value.len() > b_value.len() {
                    return 1;
                }

                // 5. If va’s size is less than vb’s size, then return -1.
                if a_value.len() < b_value.len() {
                    return -1;
                }

                // 6. Return 0.
                0
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn equals(a: &Key, b: &Key) -> bool {
        Self::compare_two_keys(a, b) == 0
    }

    pub(crate) fn less_than(a: &Key, b: &Key) -> bool {
        Self::compare_two_keys(a, b) < 0
    }

    pub(crate) fn greater_than(a: &Key, b: &Key) -> bool {
        Self::compare_two_keys(a, b) > 0
    }

    pub(crate) fn less_than_or_equal(a: &Key, b: &Key) -> bool {
        Self::compare_two_keys(a, b) <= 0
    }

    pub(crate) fn greater_than_or_equal(a: &Key, b: &Key) -> bool {
        Self::compare_two_keys(a, b) >= 0
    }

    /// compare two keys, as an Ordering.
    pub(crate) fn ordering(a: &Key, b: &Key) -> Ordering {
        Self::compare_two_keys(a, b).cmp(&0)
    }
}

// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit-less-than
fn code_unit_less_than(a: &Utf16String, b: &Utf16String) -> bool {
    code_unit_order(a, b) == Ordering::Less
}

/// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit-less-than, as an Ordering.
pub(crate) fn code_unit_order(a: &Utf16String, b: &Utf16String) -> Ordering {
    match (a.as_units(), b.as_units()) {
        (Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(a), Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(b)) => a.cmp(b),
        _ => a.to_utf16().cmp(&b.to_utf16()),
    }
}

// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#byte-less-than
fn is_byte_less_than(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {
    a < b
}
