//! The log of what a transaction changed in an object store, which an abort reverts

use std::rc::Rc;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, GcRefCell, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;
use crate::indexed_db::idb_database::IDBDatabase;
use crate::indexed_db::idb_record::{IndexRecord, ObjectStoreRecord};
use crate::indexed_db::internal::database::{Database, DatabaseRef};
use crate::indexed_db::internal::index::{Index, IndexRef};
use crate::indexed_db::internal::key::Key;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::object_store::ObjectStoreRef;

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/ has no notion of these changes: they are what DevTools reports of a transaction
// that commits, as Web::IndexedDB::TransactionChanges of LibWebCommon.
pub(crate) struct TransactionChange {
    pub(crate) database_name: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) object_store_name: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) key: Option<Rc<Key>>,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct TransactionChanges {
    pub(crate) added: Vec<TransactionChange>,
    pub(crate) changed: Vec<TransactionChange>,
    pub(crate) deleted: Vec<TransactionChange>,
}

impl TransactionChanges {
    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.added.is_empty() && self.changed.is_empty() && self.deleted.is_empty()
    }
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
enum Entry {
    ObjectStoreCreated,
    ObjectStoreDeleted,
    ObjectStoreRenamed {
        old_name: Utf16String,
    },
    IndexCreated {
        index: IndexRef,
    },
    IndexDeleted {
        index: IndexRef,
    },
    IndexRenamed {
        index: IndexRef,
        old_name: Utf16String,
    },
    KeyGeneratorChanged {
        old_value: u64,
    },
    RecordsDeleted {
        #[gc(untraced)]
        records: Vec<ObjectStoreRecord>,
    },
    RecordStored {
        #[gc(untraced)]
        key: Rc<Key>,
    },
    IndexRecordsDeleted {
        index: IndexRef,
        #[gc(untraced)]
        records: Vec<IndexRecord>,
    },
    IndexRecordStored {
        index: IndexRef,
        #[gc(untraced)]
        record: IndexRecord,
    },
}

// Tracks mutations to an object store and its indexes so they can be reverted on request failure
// (asynchronously execute a request step 5.4) or transaction abort (abort a transaction step 2).
//
// For upgrade transactions, this also tracks schema-level changes (store/index creation and deletion).
// Schema entries are always at the boundaries: ObjectStoreCreated is always first (if present),
// and ObjectStoreDeleted is always last (if present). Index schema entries appear in order between
// data mutations.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct MutationLog {
    entries: GcRefCell<Vec<Entry>>,
}

static MUTATION_LOG_CLASS: EmbedderClass<MutationLog> = EmbedderClass::new("IndexedDBMutationLog");

impl EmbedderValue for MutationLog {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &MUTATION_LOG_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type MutationLogRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<MutationLog>>;

impl MutationLog {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm) -> MutationLogRef {
        MUTATION_LOG_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| MutationLog {
            entries: GcRefCell::new(Vec::new()),
        })
    }

    fn append(&self, vm: &Vm, entry: Entry) {
        self.entries.borrow_mut(vm).push(entry);
    }

    // Schema-level entries (upgrade transactions only).
    pub(crate) fn note_object_store_created(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::ObjectStoreCreated);
    }

    pub(crate) fn note_object_store_deleted(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::ObjectStoreDeleted);
    }

    pub(crate) fn note_object_store_renamed(&self, vm: &Vm, old_name: Utf16String) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::ObjectStoreRenamed { old_name });
    }

    pub(crate) fn note_index_created(&self, vm: &Vm, index: IndexRef) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::IndexCreated { index });
    }

    pub(crate) fn note_index_deleted(&self, vm: &Vm, index: IndexRef) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::IndexDeleted { index });
    }

    pub(crate) fn note_index_renamed(&self, vm: &Vm, index: IndexRef, old_name: Utf16String) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::IndexRenamed { index, old_name });
    }

    // Record that the key generator value was changed, saving the old value for revert.
    pub(crate) fn note_key_generator_changed(&self, vm: &Vm, old_value: u64) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::KeyGeneratorChanged { old_value });
    }

    // Record that records were deleted from the object store, saving them for re-insertion on revert.
    pub(crate) fn note_records_deleted(&self, vm: &Vm, records: Vec<ObjectStoreRecord>) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::RecordsDeleted { records });
    }

    // Record that a new record was stored in the object store, saving the key for deletion on revert.
    pub(crate) fn note_record_stored(&self, vm: &Vm, key: Rc<Key>) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::RecordStored { key });
    }

    // Record that records were deleted from an index, saving them for re-insertion on revert.
    pub(crate) fn note_index_records_deleted(&self, vm: &Vm, index: IndexRef, records: Vec<IndexRecord>) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::IndexRecordsDeleted { index, records });
    }

    // Record that a new record was stored in an index, saving it for deletion on revert.
    pub(crate) fn note_index_record_stored(&self, vm: &Vm, index: IndexRef, record: IndexRecord) {
        self.append(vm, Entry::IndexRecordStored { index, record });
    }

    pub(crate) fn position(&self) -> usize {
        self.entries.borrow().len()
    }

    pub(crate) fn append_changes(
        &self,
        database_name: &Utf16String,
        object_store_name: &Utf16String,
        changes: &mut TransactionChanges,
    ) {
        let mut stored_keys: Vec<Rc<Key>> = Vec::new();
        let mut changed_keys: Vec<Rc<Key>> = Vec::new();
        let mut deleted_keys: Vec<Rc<Key>> = Vec::new();

        fn remove_key(keys: &mut Vec<Rc<Key>>, key: &Key) -> bool {
            match keys.iter().position(|existing| Key::equals(existing, key)) {
                Some(position) => {
                    keys.remove(position);
                    true
                }
                None => false,
            }
        }

        let change = |key: Option<Rc<Key>>| TransactionChange {
            database_name: database_name.clone(),
            object_store_name: object_store_name.clone(),
            key,
        };

        for entry in self.entries.borrow().iter() {
            match entry {
                Entry::ObjectStoreCreated => {
                    changes.added.push(change(None));
                }
                Entry::ObjectStoreDeleted => {
                    changes.deleted.push(change(None));
                }
                Entry::ObjectStoreRenamed { old_name } => {
                    changes.deleted.push(TransactionChange {
                        database_name: database_name.clone(),
                        object_store_name: old_name.clone(),
                        key: None,
                    });
                    changes.added.push(change(None));
                }
                Entry::IndexCreated { .. } | Entry::IndexDeleted { .. } | Entry::IndexRenamed { .. } => {}
                Entry::KeyGeneratorChanged { .. } => {}
                Entry::RecordsDeleted { records } => {
                    for record in records {
                        if remove_key(&mut stored_keys, &record.key) {
                            continue;
                        }
                        remove_key(&mut changed_keys, &record.key);
                        deleted_keys.push(record.key.clone());
                    }
                }
                Entry::RecordStored { key } => {
                    if remove_key(&mut deleted_keys, key) {
                        changed_keys.push(key.clone());
                        continue;
                    }
                    stored_keys.push(key.clone());
                }
                Entry::IndexRecordsDeleted { .. } | Entry::IndexRecordStored { .. } => {}
            }
        }

        for key in stored_keys {
            changes.added.push(change(Some(key)));
        }

        for key in changed_keys {
            changes.changed.push(change(Some(key)));
        }

        for key in deleted_keys {
            changes.deleted.push(change(Some(key)));
        }
    }

    // Undo all logged mutations in reverse order. Database and connection are required for schema entries.
    pub(crate) fn revert(&self, vm: &Vm, store: ObjectStoreRef, database: DatabaseRef, connection: Ref<IDBDatabase>) {
        self.revert_entries(vm, store, 0, Some((database, connection)));
    }

    // Undo logged mutations from the given position forward (used for per-request revert on failure).
    // Asserts that no schema entries are encountered.
    pub(crate) fn revert_from(&self, vm: &Vm, store: ObjectStoreRef, position: usize) {
        self.revert_entries(vm, store, position, None);
    }

    fn revert_entries(
        &self,
        vm: &Vm,
        store: ObjectStoreRef,
        from_position: usize,
        schema: Option<(DatabaseRef, Ref<IDBDatabase>)>,
    ) {
        // Temporarily clear the store's mutation log pointer so that the operations below
        // don't re-log into this log while we're reverting it.
        let saved_log = store.mutation_log();
        store.set_mutation_log(None);

        loop {
            let entry = {
                let mut entries = self.entries.borrow_mut(vm);
                if entries.len() <= from_position {
                    break;
                }
                entries.pop().expect("the log has an entry past the position")
            };
            match entry {
                Entry::ObjectStoreCreated => {
                    let (database, connection) = schema.expect("schema entries are reverted with the database");
                    Database::remove_object_store(database, vm, store);
                    connection.remove_from_object_store_set(vm, store);

                    // https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#abort-a-transaction
                    // Any object stores and indexes which were created during the transaction are now considered deleted
                    // for the purposes of other algorithms.
                    store.set_deleted(true);
                    for index in store.indexes(vm).values().iter() {
                        index.set_deleted(true);
                    }
                }
                Entry::ObjectStoreDeleted => {
                    let (database, connection) = schema.expect("schema entries are reverted with the database");
                    store.set_deleted(false);
                    for index in store.indexes(vm).values().iter() {
                        index.set_deleted(false);
                    }
                    Database::add_object_store(database, vm, store);
                    connection.add_to_object_store_set(vm, store);
                }
                Entry::IndexCreated { index } => {
                    assert!(schema.is_some(), "schema entries are reverted with the database");
                    index.object_store().index_set_remove(vm, &index.name());

                    // https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#abort-a-transaction
                    // Any object stores and indexes which were created during the transaction are now considered deleted
                    // for the purposes of other algorithms.
                    index.set_deleted(true);
                }
                Entry::IndexDeleted { index } => {
                    assert!(schema.is_some(), "schema entries are reverted with the database");
                    index.set_deleted(false);
                    index.object_store().index_set_set(vm, index.name(), index);
                }
                Entry::ObjectStoreRenamed { old_name } => {
                    store.set_name(old_name);
                }
                Entry::IndexRenamed { index, old_name } => {
                    Index::set_name(index, vm, old_name);
                }
                Entry::KeyGeneratorChanged { old_value } => {
                    store.key_generator().set(old_value);
                }
                Entry::RecordsDeleted { records } => {
                    for record in records {
                        store.store_a_record(vm, record);
                    }
                }
                Entry::RecordStored { key } => {
                    store.remove_record_with_key(&key);
                }
                Entry::IndexRecordsDeleted { index, records } => {
                    for record in &records {
                        Index::store_a_record(index, vm, record);
                    }
                }
                Entry::IndexRecordStored { index, record } => {
                    index.remove_record(&record);
                }
            }
        }

        store.set_mutation_log(saved_log);
    }
}

//! Object stores, https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#object-store-construct

use core::cell::{Cell, Ref, RefCell, RefMut};

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{DeferGc, EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, GcRefCell, MarkedVec, Trace, Vm};

use crate::indexed_db::idb_key_range::IDBKeyRange;
use crate::indexed_db::idb_record::ObjectStoreRecord;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::algorithms::KeyPath;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::database::{Database, DatabaseRef};
use crate::indexed_db::internal::index::IndexRef;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::key::{Key, KeyType};
use crate::indexed_db::internal::key_generator::{KeyGenerator, MAX_KEY_GENERATOR_VALUE};
use crate::indexed_db::internal::mutation_log::MutationLogRef;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::record_range::{KeyedRecord, record_range_for_key_range};

impl KeyedRecord for ObjectStoreRecord {
    fn key(&self) -> &Key {
        &self.key
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#object-store-construct
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct ObjectStore {
    // AD-HOC: An ObjectStore needs to know what Database it belongs to...
    database: DatabaseRef,

    // AD-HOC: An Index has referenced ObjectStores, we also need the reverse mapping
    indexes: GcRefCell<Vec<(Utf16String, IndexRef)>>,

    // An object store has a name, which is a name. At any one time, the name is unique within the database to which it belongs.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    name: RefCell<Utf16String>,

    // An object store optionally has a key path. If the object store has a key path it is said to use in-line keys. Otherwise it is said to use out-of-line keys.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    key_path: Option<KeyPath>,

    // An object store optionally has a key generator.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    key_generator: RefCell<Option<KeyGenerator>>,

    // An object store has a list of records
    #[gc(untraced)]
    records: RefCell<Vec<ObjectStoreRecord>>,

    deleted: Cell<bool>,

    // AD-HOC: Tracks mutations for revert on request failure or transaction abort.
    mutation_log: Cell<Option<MutationLogRef>>,
}

static OBJECT_STORE_CLASS: EmbedderClass<ObjectStore> = EmbedderClass::new("IndexedDBObjectStore");

impl EmbedderValue for ObjectStore {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &OBJECT_STORE_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type ObjectStoreRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<ObjectStore>>;

impl ObjectStore {
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        database: DatabaseRef,
        name: Utf16String,
        auto_increment: bool,
        key_path: Option<KeyPath>,
    ) -> ObjectStoreRef {
        let object_store = OBJECT_STORE_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| ObjectStore {
            database,
            indexes: GcRefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            name: RefCell::new(name),
            key_path,
            key_generator: RefCell::new(auto_increment.then(KeyGenerator::new)),
            records: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            deleted: Cell::new(false),
            mutation_log: Cell::new(None),
        });
        Database::add_object_store(database, vm, object_store);
        object_store
    }

    pub(crate) fn name(&self) -> Utf16String {
        self.name.borrow().clone()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_name(&self, name: Utf16String) {
        *self.name.borrow_mut() = name;
    }

    pub(crate) fn key_path(&self) -> Option<&KeyPath> {
        self.key_path.as_ref()
    }

    pub(crate) fn uses_inline_keys(&self) -> bool {
        self.key_path.is_some()
    }

    pub(crate) fn uses_out_of_line_keys(&self) -> bool {
        self.key_path.is_none()
    }

    pub(crate) fn key_generator(&self) -> RefMut<'_, KeyGenerator> {
        RefMut::map(self.key_generator.borrow_mut(), |generator| {
            generator.as_mut().expect("the object store has a key generator")
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn uses_a_key_generator(&self) -> bool {
        self.key_generator.borrow().is_some()
    }

    /// The index set, as a list of the indexes with their names, for the storage of a cell being built.
    pub(crate) fn index_set(&self, _: &DeferGc<'_>) -> Vec<(Utf16String, IndexRef)> {
        self.indexes.borrow().clone()
    }

    pub(crate) fn copy_index_set_into(&self, indexes: &mut Vec<(Utf16String, IndexRef)>) {
        indexes.clone_from(&self.indexes.borrow());
    }

    pub(crate) fn indexes<'vm>(&self, vm: &'vm Vm) -> MarkedVec<'vm, IndexRef> {
        let indexes = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        for (_, index) in self.indexes.borrow().iter() {
            indexes.push(*index);
        }
        indexes
    }

    pub(crate) fn index_set_get(&self, name: &Utf16String) -> Option<IndexRef> {
        self.indexes
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .find(|(index_name, _)| index_name == name)
            .map(|(_, index)| *index)
    }

    pub(crate) fn index_set_set(&self, vm: &Vm, name: Utf16String, index: IndexRef) {
        let mut indexes = self.indexes.borrow_mut(vm);
        if let Some(entry) = indexes.iter_mut().find(|(index_name, _)| *index_name == name) {
            entry.1 = index;
            return;
        }
        indexes.push((name, index));
    }

    pub(crate) fn index_set_take(&self, vm: &Vm, name: &Utf16String) -> Option<IndexRef> {
        let mut indexes = self.indexes.borrow_mut(vm);
        let position = indexes.iter().position(|(index_name, _)| index_name == name)?;
        Some(indexes.remove(position).1)
    }

    pub(crate) fn index_set_remove(&self, vm: &Vm, name: &Utf16String) {
        self.index_set_take(vm, name);
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_deleted(&self) -> bool {
        self.deleted.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_deleted(&self, deleted: bool) {
        self.deleted.set(deleted);
    }

    pub(crate) fn database(&self) -> DatabaseRef {
        self.database
    }

    pub(crate) fn records(&self) -> Ref<'_, Vec<ObjectStoreRecord>> {
        self.records.borrow()
    }

    // Mutation log access. The log is set externally by the readwrite transaction that owns it.
    pub(crate) fn mutation_log(&self) -> Option<MutationLogRef> {
        self.mutation_log.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_mutation_log(&self, log: Option<MutationLogRef>) {
        self.mutation_log.set(log);
    }

    pub(crate) fn mutation_log_position(&self) -> usize {
        match self.mutation_log.get() {
            None => 0,
            Some(log) => log.position(),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn revert_mutations_from(this: ObjectStoreRef, vm: &Vm, position: usize) {
        if let Some(log) = this.mutation_log.get() {
            log.revert_from(vm, this, position);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove_records_in_range(&self, vm: &Vm, range: &IDBKeyRange) {
        let mut records = self.records.borrow_mut();
        if records.is_empty() {
            return;
        }

        // Since records are sorted by key, records in range form a contiguous block.
        let record_range = record_range_for_key_range(&records, range);

        if record_range.start < record_range.end {
            let deleted: Vec<ObjectStoreRecord> = records.drain(record_range.start..record_range.end).collect();
            drop(records);
            if let Some(log) = self.mutation_log.get() {
                log.note_records_deleted(vm, deleted);
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove_record_with_key(&self, key: &Key) {
        let mut records = self.records.borrow_mut();
        if let Ok(index) = records.binary_search_by(|record| Key::ordering(&record.key, key)) {
            records.remove(index);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn has_record_with_key(&self, key: &Key) -> bool {
        self.records
            .borrow()
            .binary_search_by(|record| Key::ordering(&record.key, key))
            .is_ok()
    }

    pub(crate) fn store_a_record(&self, vm: &Vm, record: ObjectStoreRecord) {
        if let Some(log) = self.mutation_log.get() {
            log.note_record_stored(vm, record.key.clone());
        }

        // NOTE: The record is stored in the object store’s list of records such that the list is sorted according to the key of the records in ascending order.
        let mut records = self.records.borrow_mut();
        if records
            .last()
            .is_none_or(|last| Key::compare_two_keys(&last.key, &record.key) <= 0)
        {
            records.push(record);
            return;
        }

        let position = records.partition_point(|existing| Key::compare_two_keys(&existing.key, &record.key) < 0);
        records.insert(position, record);
    }

    pub(crate) fn count_records_in_range(&self, range: &IDBKeyRange) -> u64 {
        let records = self.records.borrow();
        let record_range = record_range_for_key_range(&records, range);
        (record_range.end - record_range.start) as u64
    }

    pub(crate) fn first_in_range(&self, range: &IDBKeyRange) -> Option<ObjectStoreRecord> {
        let records = self.records.borrow();
        let record_range = record_range_for_key_range(&records, range);
        if record_range.start == record_range.end {
            return None;
        }
        Some(records[record_range.start].clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn clear_records(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        let deleted_records = core::mem::take(&mut *self.records.borrow_mut());
        if let Some(log) = self.mutation_log.get()
            && !deleted_records.is_empty()
        {
            log.note_records_deleted(vm, deleted_records);
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#generate-a-key
    pub(crate) fn generate_a_key(&self, vm: &Vm) -> Result<u64, &'static str> {
        // 1. Let generator be store's key generator.
        let mut generator = self.key_generator();

        // 2. Let key be generator's current number.
        let key = generator.current_number();

        // 3. If key is greater than 2^53 (9007199254740992), then return failure.
        #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss, reason = "2^53 is a u64")]
        if key > MAX_KEY_GENERATOR_VALUE as u64 {
            return Err("Key is greater than 2^53 while trying to generate a key");
        }

        // 4. Increase generator's current number by 1.
        if let Some(log) = self.mutation_log.get() {
            log.note_key_generator_changed(vm, key);
        }
        generator.increment(1);

        // 5. Return key.
        Ok(key)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#possibly-update-the-key-generator
    pub(crate) fn possibly_update_the_key_generator(&self, vm: &Vm, key: &Key) {
        // 1. If the type of key is not number, abort these steps.
        if key.r#type() != KeyType::Number {
            return;
        }

        // 2. Let value be the value of key.
        let mut value = key.value_as_double();

        // 3. Set value to the minimum of value and 2^53 (9007199254740992).
        value = value.min(MAX_KEY_GENERATOR_VALUE);

        // 4. Set value to the largest integer not greater than value.
        value = value.floor();

        // 5. Let generator be store's key generator.
        let mut generator = self.key_generator();

        // 6. If value is greater than or equal to generator's current number, then set generator's current number to value + 1.
        #[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss, reason = "the current number is at most 2^53 + 1")]
        if value >= generator.current_number() as f64 {
            if let Some(log) = self.mutation_log.get() {
                log.note_key_generator_changed(vm, generator.current_number());
            }
            // NB: value + 1 is computed as an integer, as 2^53 + 1 does not fit in a double.
            #[allow(
                clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
                clippy::cast_sign_loss,
                reason = "value is an integer in the range of the current number"
            )]
            generator.set(value as u64 + 1);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn first_n_in_range(&self, range: &IDBKeyRange, count: Option<u32>) -> Vec<ObjectStoreRecord> {
        let mut result = Vec::new();
        let records = self.records.borrow();
        let record_range = record_range_for_key_range(&records, range);
        for record in &records[record_range.start..record_range.end] {
            result.push(record.clone());

            if count.is_some_and(|count| result.len() >= count as usize) {
                break;
            }
        }

        result
    }

    pub(crate) fn last_n_in_range(&self, range: &IDBKeyRange, count: Option<u32>) -> Vec<ObjectStoreRecord> {
        let mut result = Vec::new();
        let records = self.records.borrow();
        let record_range = record_range_for_key_range(&records, range);
        for record in records[record_range.start..record_range.end].iter().rev() {
            result.push(record.clone());

            if count.is_some_and(|count| result.len() >= count as usize) {
                break;
            }
        }

        result
    }
}

//! The records of a sorted list of records whose keys a key range selects

use crate::indexed_db::idb_key_range::IDBKeyRange;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::key::Key;

/// A record of an object store's or an index's list of records, which is sorted on its keys.
pub(crate) trait KeyedRecord {
    fn key(&self) -> &Key;
}

pub(crate) struct RecordRange {
    pub(crate) start: usize,
    pub(crate) end: usize,
}

fn first_record_index_with_key_at_or_after<R: KeyedRecord>(records: &[R], key: &Key, open: bool) -> usize {
    let mut low = 0;
    let mut high = records.len();

    while low < high {
        let middle = low + (high - low) / 2;
        let comparison = Key::compare_two_keys(records[middle].key(), key);
        if comparison < 0 || (comparison == 0 && open) {
            low = middle + 1;
        } else {
            high = middle;
        }
    }

    low
}

fn first_record_index_with_key_after<R: KeyedRecord>(records: &[R], key: &Key, open: bool, start: usize) -> usize {
    let mut low = start;
    let mut high = records.len();

    while low < high {
        let middle = low + (high - low) / 2;
        let comparison = Key::compare_two_keys(records[middle].key(), key);
        if comparison < 0 || (comparison == 0 && !open) {
            low = middle + 1;
        } else {
            high = middle;
        }
    }

    low
}

pub(crate) fn record_range_for_key_range<R: KeyedRecord>(records: &[R], range: &IDBKeyRange) -> RecordRange {
    let mut start = 0;
    let mut end = records.len();

    if let Some(lower) = range.lower_key() {
        start = first_record_index_with_key_at_or_after(records, lower, range.is_lower_open());
    }

    if let Some(upper) = range.upper_key() {
        end = first_record_index_with_key_after(records, upper, range.is_upper_open(), start);
    }

    RecordRange { start, end }
}

//! The request lists of transactions, https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#transaction-request-list, and of connection queues

use core::cell::Cell;

use libjs_rust::api::{DeferGc, GcRefCell, MarkedVec, Trace, Vm};

use crate::indexed_db::idb_request::{AnyIDBRequest, WeakIDBRequest};
use crate::indexed_db::internal::algorithms::queue_a_database_task;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::function::{Function, call_function};

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct Entry {
    #[gc(untraced = "the request is weak")]
    request: WeakIDBRequest,
    steps: Option<Function>,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct RequestList {
    entries: GcRefCell<Vec<Entry>>,
    on_all_processed: Cell<Option<Function>>,
    blocked: Cell<bool>,
    // Whether this is a connection queue's list, whose requests run one at a time, each until its steps complete.
    is_connection_queue: bool,
}

impl RequestList {
    pub(crate) fn new(_: &DeferGc<'_>) -> Self {
        Self {
            entries: GcRefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            on_all_processed: Cell::new(None),
            blocked: Cell::new(false),
            is_connection_queue: false,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn new_for_connection_queue(defer: &DeferGc<'_>) -> Self {
        Self {
            is_connection_queue: true,
            ..Self::new(defer)
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn enqueue(&self, vm: &Vm, request: AnyIDBRequest, steps: Function) {
        self.entries.borrow_mut(vm).push(Entry {
            request: WeakIDBRequest::new(vm, request),
            steps: Some(steps),
        });
        self.maybe_process_next_request(vm);
    }

    pub(crate) fn maybe_process_next_request(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        if self.blocked.get() {
            return;
        }

        let mut entries = self.entries.borrow_mut(vm);
        while entries.first().is_some_and(|entry| entry.request.get().is_none()) {
            entries.remove(0);
        }

        let mut steps_to_queue = None;
        for entry in entries.iter_mut() {
            let Some(request) = entry.request.get() else {
                continue;
            };
            // AD-HOC: The spec has a connection queue's request wait only until the requests before it are processed,
            //         and upgrading a database sets its request's processed flag before it fires upgradeneeded. So a
            //         request would run while the upgrade transaction is live. Instead, a request waits until the one
            //         before it has completed, which drops it from the queue.
            if request.processed() && !self.is_connection_queue {
                continue;
            }
            if request.aborted() {
                continue;
            }

            // If the steps are null here, the request is still executing, so we should wait until it is finished.
            let Some(steps) = entry.steps else {
                return;
            };

            steps_to_queue = Some(steps);
            entry.steps = None;
            break;
        }
        drop(entries);

        if let Some(steps) = steps_to_queue {
            queue_a_database_task(vm, steps);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn on_request_processed(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        if self.is_connection_queue {
            let mut entries = self.entries.borrow_mut(vm);
            if let Some(position) = entries.iter().position(|entry| entry.steps.is_none()) {
                entries.remove(position);
            }
        }
        self.maybe_process_next_request(vm);
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove(&self, vm: &Vm, request: AnyIDBRequest) {
        let mut entries = self.entries.borrow_mut(vm);
        if let Some(position) = entries.iter().position(|entry| entry.request.get() == Some(request)) {
            entries.remove(position);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.entries.borrow().is_empty()
    }

    pub(crate) fn block_execution(&self) {
        self.blocked.set(true);
    }

    pub(crate) fn execution_is_blocked(&self) -> bool {
        self.blocked.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn unblock_execution(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        self.blocked.set(false);
        self.maybe_process_next_request(vm);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_on_all_processed(&self, vm: &Vm, callback: Function) {
        self.on_all_processed.set(Some(callback));
        self.check_all_processed(vm);
    }

    pub(crate) fn clear_on_all_processed(&self) {
        self.on_all_processed.set(None);
    }

    pub(crate) fn check_all_processed(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        if self.on_all_processed.get().is_none() {
            return;
        }

        {
            let mut entries = self.entries.borrow_mut(vm);
            entries.retain(|entry| entry.request.get().is_some());

            for entry in entries.iter() {
                if !entry.request.get().expect("the request is live").processed() {
                    return;
                }
            }
        }

        let callback = self.on_all_processed.take().expect("a callback is set");
        call_function(vm, callback);
    }

    pub(crate) fn requests<'vm>(&self, vm: &'vm Vm) -> MarkedVec<'vm, AnyIDBRequest> {
        let requests = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        for entry in self.entries.borrow().iter() {
            if let Some(request) = entry.request.get() {
                requests.push(request);
            }
        }
        requests
    }
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2024-2025, stelar7 <dudedbz@gmail.com>
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

//! The databases of the agent, by their storage key and name, and the connection queues of those,
//! https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#connection-queues. They live as long as the thread of the agent.

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, GcRefCell, Trace, Vm};

use crate::indexed_db::internal::database::DatabaseRef;
use crate::indexed_db::internal::request_list::RequestList;
use crate::storage_api::storage_key::StorageKey;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn gc_root_create(cell: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn gc_root_destroy(root: *mut c_void);
}

// https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#connection-queues
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct ConnectionQueue {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    storage_key: StorageKey,
    name: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) request_list: RequestList,
}

static CONNECTION_QUEUE_CLASS: EmbedderClass<ConnectionQueue> = EmbedderClass::new("IndexedDBConnectionQueue");

impl EmbedderValue for ConnectionQueue {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &CONNECTION_QUEUE_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type ConnectionQueueRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<ConnectionQueue>>;

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct DatabasesOfKey {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    storage_key: StorageKey,
    databases: Vec<(Utf16String, DatabaseRef)>,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Storage {
    databases: GcRefCell<Vec<DatabasesOfKey>>,
    connection_queues: GcRefCell<Vec<ConnectionQueueRef>>,
}

static STORAGE_CLASS: EmbedderClass<Storage> = EmbedderClass::new("IndexedDBStorage");

impl EmbedderValue for Storage {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &STORAGE_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type StorageRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<Storage>>;

thread_local! {
    // NB: Keeping the root here lets the leak checker see it as reachable.
    static STORAGE: Cell<Option<(StorageRef, NonNull<c_void>)>> = const { Cell::new(None) };
}

/// The storage of the current thread's agent, created on first use.
pub(crate) fn storage(vm: &Vm) -> StorageRef {
    if let Some((storage, _)) = STORAGE.get() {
        return storage;
    }
    let storage = STORAGE_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| Storage {
        databases: GcRefCell::new(Vec::new()),
        connection_queues: GcRefCell::new(Vec::new()),
    });
    // NB: The storage lives as long as the agent of the thread, which roots its cell.
    // SAFETY: The cell is a live cell of the heap.
    let root = NonNull::new(unsafe { gc_root_create(storage.as_ptr().cast()) }).expect("a root is allocated");
    STORAGE.set(Some((storage, root)));
    storage
}

/// Releases the storage of the current thread's agent, which goes away with its heap.
pub(crate) fn shut_down_storage() {
    if let Some((_, root)) = STORAGE.take() {
        // SAFETY: The root is the one storage() created, and the heap it is in is alive.
        unsafe { gc_root_destroy(root.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

impl Storage {
    pub(crate) fn for_each_database(&self, mut visitor: impl FnMut(DatabaseRef)) {
        for databases_of_key in self.databases.borrow().iter() {
            for (_, database) in &databases_of_key.databases {
                visitor(*database);
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn for_each_database_of_key(&self, key: &StorageKey, mut visitor: impl FnMut(DatabaseRef)) {
        for databases_of_key in self.databases.borrow().iter() {
            if databases_of_key.storage_key != *key {
                continue;
            }
            for (_, database) in &databases_of_key.databases {
                visitor(*database);
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn database(&self, key: &StorageKey, name: &Utf16String) -> Option<DatabaseRef> {
        let databases = self.databases.borrow();
        let databases_of_key = databases.iter().find(|entry| entry.storage_key == *key)?;
        databases_of_key
            .databases
            .iter()
            .find(|(database_name, _)| database_name == name)
            .map(|(_, database)| *database)
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_database(&self, vm: &Vm, key: &StorageKey, name: &Utf16String, database: DatabaseRef) {
        let mut databases = self.databases.borrow_mut(vm);
        let databases_of_key = match databases.iter().position(|entry| entry.storage_key == *key) {
            Some(position) => &mut databases[position],
            None => {
                databases.push(DatabasesOfKey {
                    storage_key: key.clone(),
                    databases: Vec::new(),
                });
                databases.last_mut().expect("an entry was just added")
            }
        };
        if let Some(entry) = databases_of_key
            .databases
            .iter_mut()
            .find(|(database_name, _)| database_name == name)
        {
            entry.1 = database;
            return;
        }
        databases_of_key.databases.push((name.clone(), database));
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove_database(&self, vm: &Vm, key: &StorageKey, name: &Utf16String) {
        let mut databases = self.databases.borrow_mut(vm);
        let Some(databases_of_key) = databases.iter_mut().find(|entry| entry.storage_key == *key) else {
            return;
        };
        if let Some(position) = databases_of_key
            .databases
            .iter()
            .position(|(database_name, _)| database_name == name)
        {
            databases_of_key.databases.remove(position);
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#connection-queue
    pub(crate) fn connection_queue_for_key_and_name(
        &self,
        vm: &Vm,
        key: &StorageKey,
        name: &Utf16String,
    ) -> ConnectionQueueRef {
        if let Some(queue) = self
            .connection_queues
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .find(|queue| queue.storage_key == *key && queue.name == *name)
        {
            return *queue;
        }

        let new_queue = CONNECTION_QUEUE_CLASS.allocate(vm, |defer| ConnectionQueue {
            storage_key: key.clone(),
            name: name.clone(),
            request_list: RequestList::new_for_connection_queue(defer),
        });
        self.connection_queues.borrow_mut(vm).push(new_queue);
        new_queue
    }
}

//! InternalAnimationTimeline, the timeline whose time tests set.

use core::cell::RefCell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{CellRoot, Gc, Trace, Visitor, Vm};
use libweb_rust::web_animations::{TimelineDescription, TimelineRecordRef};

use crate::animations::animation::perform_host_effect;
use crate::animations::animation_timeline::{AnimationTimeline, finalize_timeline, timeline_object_of_record};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, cell_into_abi};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

pub(crate) struct InternalAnimationTimeline {
    timeline: AnimationTimeline,
}

// SAFETY: The timeline visits what it reaches.
unsafe impl Trace for InternalAnimationTimeline {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.timeline.trace(visitor);
    }
}

impl Inherits<AnimationTimeline> for InternalAnimationTimeline {
    fn parent(&self) -> &AnimationTimeline {
        &self.timeline
    }
}

impl Wrappable for InternalAnimationTimeline {
    const TRACED_ON_OWNER_THREAD_ONLY: bool = true;
    const FINALIZES: bool = true;

    fn finalize(object: Ref<Self>) {
        finalize_timeline(&object.timeline);
    }
}

impl InternalAnimationTimeline {
    pub(crate) fn from_timeline(timeline: AnimationTimeline) -> Self {
        Self { timeline }
    }

    pub(crate) fn timeline(&self) -> &AnimationTimeline {
        &self.timeline
    }

    /// Sets the time of the timeline, or the time a read of it observes, where `for_observation`.
    fn set_internal_time(&self, time: Option<f64>, for_observation: bool) {
        // NB: The animations the timeline updates stay alive through it, which can run script.
        let roots: RefCell<Vec<CellRoot<c_void>>> = RefCell::default();
        let keep_alive = |cell: NonNull<c_void>| {
            roots
                .borrow_mut()
                .push(CellRoot::new(unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(cell) }));
        };
        self.timeline
            .record()
            .set_internal_time(time, for_observation, &keep_alive, perform_host_effect);
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext, time: Option<f64>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.set_internal_time(time, false);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_time_for_observation(&self, _: &mut CallContext, time: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.set_internal_time(Some(time), true);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// A new timeline of the Internals interface associated with the host's `DOM::Document` `document`.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `vm` must be the live VM, and `document` a live document.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_internal_animation_timeline_create(vm: &Vm, document: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void {
    let document = NonNull::new(document).expect("a timeline is associated with a document");
    let record = TimelineRecordRef::new(document, TimelineDescription::Internal);
    let crate::animations::animation_timeline::AnyAnimationTimeline::InternalAnimationTimeline(object) =
        timeline_object_of_record(vm, &record)
    else {
        unreachable!("the record is of an internal timeline");
    };
    cell_into_abi(object)
}

//! LargestContentfulPaint, https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#sec-largest-contentful-paint-interface

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::{CppCell, LentCppCell, WeakCppCell, cpp_class};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_into_abi};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::css::css_rule::wrap_cpp_cell;
use crate::paint_timing::paint_timing::is_exposed_for_paint_timing;
use crate::paint_timing::paint_timing_mixin::{PaintTimingInfo, PaintTimingMixin, default_paint_timestamp};
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_entry::{AnyPerformanceEntry, PerformanceEntry};

/// https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#sec-largest-contentful-paint-interface
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct LargestContentfulPaint {
    entry: PerformanceEntry,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    paint_timing_mixin: PaintTimingMixin,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#largestcontentfulpaint-size
    size: u32,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#largestcontentfulpaint-loadtime
    load_time: f64,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#largestcontentfulpaint-id
    id: Utf16String,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#largestcontentfulpaint-url
    url: Utf16String,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#largestcontentfulpaint-element
    // NB: Held weakly, as the element getter returns null for an element that is not connected.
    element: WeakCppCell,
}

impl Wrappable for LargestContentfulPaint {}

impl Inherits<PerformanceEntry> for LargestContentfulPaint {
    fn parent(&self) -> &PerformanceEntry {
        &self.entry
    }
}

impl LargestContentfulPaint {
    // https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#create-a-largestcontentfulpaint-entry
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        paint_timing_info: PaintTimingInfo,
        size: u32,
        url: Utf16String,
        id: Utf16String,
        load_time: f64,
        element: &CppCell,
    ) -> Ref<Self> {
        let entry = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            // The name attribute's getter must return the empty string.
            // The startTime attribute's getter must return the value of this's renderTime.
            // The duration attribute's getter must return 0.
            entry: PerformanceEntry::new(
                Utf16String::default(),
                Utf16String::from_utf8("largest-contentful-paint"),
                default_paint_timestamp(&paint_timing_info),
                0.0,
            ),
            paint_timing_mixin: PaintTimingMixin::new(paint_timing_info),
            size,
            load_time,
            id,
            url,
            element: WeakCppCell::new(vm, element),
        });
        let any_entry = AnyPerformanceEntry::LargestContentfulPaint(entry);
        any_entry.entry().set_object(any_entry);
        entry
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#dom-largestcontentfulpaint-loadtime
    pub(crate) fn load_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The loadTime attribute must return the value of this's loadTime.
        Ok(self.load_time)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#dom-largestcontentfulpaint-rendertime
    pub(crate) fn render_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The renderTime attribute must return the default paint timestamp given this's paint timing info.
        Ok(default_paint_timestamp(self.paint_timing_mixin.paint_timing_info()))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#dom-largestcontentfulpaint-size
    pub(crate) fn size(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        // The size attribute must return the value of this's size.
        Ok(self.size)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#dom-largestcontentfulpaint-id
    pub(crate) fn id(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The id attribute must return the value of this's id.
        Ok(self.id.clone())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#dom-largestcontentfulpaint-url
    pub(crate) fn url(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The url attribute must return the value of this's url.
        Ok(self.url.clone())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#dom-largestcontentfulpaint-element
    pub(crate) fn element(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<CppInterface>> {
        // 1. If this's element is not exposed for paint timing given null, return null.
        let Some(element) = self.element.get().filter(is_exposed_for_paint_timing) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };

        // 2. Return this's element.
        Ok(Some(wrap_cpp_cell(cx, &element)))
    }

    pub(crate) fn paint_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.paint_timing_mixin.paint_time())
    }

    pub(crate) fn presentation_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<f64>> {
        Ok(self.paint_timing_mixin.presentation_time())
    }
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/largest-contentful-paint/#create-a-largestcontentfulpaint-entry
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_largest_contentful_paint_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    rendering_update_end_time: f64,
    has_presentation_time: bool,
    presentation_time: f64,
    size: u32,
    url: Utf16String,
    id: Utf16String,
    load_time: f64,
    element: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Element>,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let element = CppCell::from_lent(element);
    let paint_timing_info =
        PaintTimingInfo::from_abi(rendering_update_end_time, has_presentation_time, presentation_time);
    cell_into_abi(LargestContentfulPaint::create(
        vm,
        paint_timing_info,
        size,
        url,
        id,
        load_time,
        &element,
    ))
}

//! MediaStreamTrackEvent, https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-main/#mediastreamtrackevent

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Object, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::CppCell;
use crate::bindings::event_target::CppEvent;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::lent_string::LentUtf16FlyString;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_media_capture_media_stream_track_from_wrapper(wrapper: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_media_capture_media_stream_track_wrap(realm: *mut c_void, track: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
}

/// The dictionary MediaStreamTrackEventInit of MediaCapture/MediaStreamTrackEvent.idl.
pub(crate) struct MediaStreamTrackEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) track: CppInterface,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-main/#mediastreamtrackevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct MediaStreamTrackEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    track: CppCell,
}

impl Wrappable for MediaStreamTrackEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl MediaStreamTrackEvent {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `track` must be a live MediaStreamTrack.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: &EventInit,
        track: *mut c_void,
    ) -> Ref<MediaStreamTrackEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.bubbles,
            event_init.cancelable,
            event_init.composed,
        );
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live MediaStreamTrack.
        let track = unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(track) };
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| MediaStreamTrackEvent { event, track });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: MediaStreamTrackEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<MediaStreamTrackEvent>> {
        // SAFETY: The bindings converted the member to a wrapper of a MediaStreamTrack.
        let track = unsafe {
            web_media_capture_media_stream_track_from_wrapper(event_init_dict.track.wrapper().as_ptr().cast())
        };
        // SAFETY: LibWeb returns the live MediaStreamTrack that the wrapper wraps.
        Ok(unsafe { Self::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &r#type, &event_init_dict.parent, track) })
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    pub(crate) fn track(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<CppInterface> {
        // SAFETY: The realm and the MediaStreamTrack are live, and LibWeb returns the wrapper of the MediaStreamTrack.
        let wrapper =
            unsafe { web_media_capture_media_stream_track_wrap(cx.realm().as_ptr().cast(), self.track.as_ptr()) };
        // SAFETY: The wrapper is one of a MediaStreamTrack.
        Ok(unsafe { CppInterface::from_wrapper(Gc::<Object>::from_non_null(NonNull::new(wrapper.cast()).unwrap())) })
    }
}

/// The Event of a new trusted MediaStreamTrackEvent in the realm, for the implementation to fire.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The VM, the realm and the track must be live. The type is lent for the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_media_stream_track_event_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    r#type: LentUtf16FlyString<'_>,
    bubbles: bool,
    cancelable: bool,
    composed: bool,
    track: *mut c_void,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let event_init = EventInit {
        bubbles,
        cancelable,
        composed,
    };
    let r#type: Utf16String = r#type.to_utf16_fly_string().into();
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live MediaStreamTrack.
    let event = unsafe { MediaStreamTrackEvent::create(vm, realm, &r#type, &event_init, track) };
    event.event().as_ptr()
}

//! BufferedChangeEvent, https://w3c.github.io/media-source/#bufferedchangeevent-interface

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::Trace;

use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use crate::bindings::event_target::CppEvent;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;

/// The dictionary BufferedChangeEventInit of MediaSourceExtensions/BufferedChangeEvent.idl.
pub(crate) struct BufferedChangeEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    #[allow(dead_code, reason = "the attributes that return the ranges are not implemented")]
    pub(crate) added_ranges: Option<CppInterface>,
    #[allow(dead_code, reason = "the attributes that return the ranges are not implemented")]
    pub(crate) removed_ranges: Option<CppInterface>,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/media-source/#bufferedchangeevent-interface
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct BufferedChangeEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
}

impl Wrappable for BufferedChangeEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl BufferedChangeEvent {
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: BufferedChangeEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<BufferedChangeEvent>> {
        let event_init = event_init_dict.parent;
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            cx.realm(),
            &r#type,
            event_init.bubbles,
            event_init.cancelable,
            event_init.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(cx.vm(), |_| BufferedChangeEvent { event });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        Ok(object)
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }
}

//! PerformanceNavigationTiming, https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::{LentCppCell, cpp_class};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::dom::document::CppDocument;
use crate::fetch::infrastructure::fetch_timing_info::CppFetchTimingInfo;
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_entry::AnyPerformanceEntry;
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_timeline::PerformanceTimeline;
use crate::resource_timing::performance_resource_timing::{
    CacheState, PerformanceResourceTiming, ResponseBodyInfo, ResponseBodyInfoAbi,
};

/// https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-navigationtimingtype
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum NavigationTimingType {
    Navigate,
    Reload,
    BackForward,
}

impl NavigationTimingType {
    fn from_abi(navigation_type: u8) -> Self {
        match navigation_type {
            0 => Self::Navigate,
            1 => Self::Reload,
            2 => Self::BackForward,
            _ => unreachable!("C++ passes a navigation timing type"),
        }
    }
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceNavigationTiming {
    resource_timing: PerformanceResourceTiming,
    document: CppDocument,
    redirect_count: u16,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    navigation_type: NavigationTimingType,
}

impl Wrappable for PerformanceNavigationTiming {}

impl Inherits<PerformanceResourceTiming> for PerformanceNavigationTiming {
    fn parent(&self) -> &PerformanceResourceTiming {
        &self.resource_timing
    }
}

impl PerformanceNavigationTiming {
    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#performanceentry
    pub(crate) fn entry_type(&self) -> Utf16String {
        // The entryType getter step is to return the DOMString "navigation".
        Utf16String::from_utf8("navigation")
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#performanceentry
    pub(crate) fn start_time(&self) -> f64 {
        // The startTime getter step is to return a DOMHighResTimeStamp with a time value of 0.
        0.0
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#performanceentry
    pub(crate) fn duration(&self) -> f64 {
        // The duration getter step is to return a DOMHighResTimeStamp equal to the difference between loadEventEnd and
        // this's startTime.
        self.document.load_timing_info().load_event_end_time - self.start_time()
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#PerformanceResourceTiming
    pub(crate) fn redirect_start(&self) -> f64 {
        // 1. If this's redirect count is 0, return 0.
        if self.redirect_count == 0 {
            return 0.0;
        }

        // 2. Otherwise return this's redirectStart.
        self.resource_timing.resource_timing_redirect_start()
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#PerformanceResourceTiming
    pub(crate) fn redirect_end(&self) -> f64 {
        // 1. If this's redirect count is 0, return 0.
        if self.redirect_count == 0 {
            return 0.0;
        }

        // 2. Otherwise return this's redirectEnd.
        self.resource_timing.resource_timing_redirect_end()
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-unloadeventstart
    pub(crate) fn unload_event_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The unloadEventStart getter steps are to return this's previous document unload timing's unload event start
        // time.
        Ok(self.document.previous_document_unload_timing().unload_event_start_time)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-unloadeventend
    pub(crate) fn unload_event_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The unloadEventEnd getter steps are to return this's previous document unload timing's unload event end time.
        Ok(self.document.previous_document_unload_timing().unload_event_end_time)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-dominteractive
    pub(crate) fn dom_interactive(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The domInteractive getter steps are to return this's document load timing's DOM interactive time.
        Ok(self.document.load_timing_info().dom_interactive_time)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-domcontentloadedeventstart
    pub(crate) fn dom_content_loaded_event_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The domContentLoadedEventStart getter steps are to return this's document load timing's DOM content loaded
        // event start time.
        Ok(self.document.load_timing_info().dom_content_loaded_event_start_time)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-domcontentloadedeventend
    pub(crate) fn dom_content_loaded_event_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The domContentLoadedEventEnd getter steps are to return this's document load timing's DOM content loaded event
        // end time.
        Ok(self.document.load_timing_info().dom_content_loaded_event_end_time)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-domcomplete
    pub(crate) fn dom_complete(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The domComplete getter steps are to return this's document load timing's DOM complete time.
        Ok(self.document.load_timing_info().dom_complete_time)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-loadeventstart
    pub(crate) fn load_event_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The loadEventStart getter steps are to return this's document load timing's load event start time.
        Ok(self.document.load_timing_info().load_event_start_time)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-loadeventend
    pub(crate) fn load_event_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The loadEventEnd getter steps are to return this's document load timing's load event end time.
        Ok(self.document.load_timing_info().load_event_end_time)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-type
    pub(crate) fn r#type(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<NavigationTimingType> {
        // The type getter steps are to run the this's navigation type.
        Ok(self.navigation_type)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-redirectcount
    pub(crate) fn redirect_count(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u16> {
        // The redirectCount getter steps are to return this's redirect count.
        Ok(self.redirect_count)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigationtiming-criticalchrestart
    pub(crate) fn critical_ch_restart(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The criticalCHRestart getter steps are to return this's `Critical-CH` restart time.
        // FIXME: Implement the `Critical-CH` restart time.
        Ok(0.0)
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dfn-create-the-navigation-timing-entry
#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "these are the inputs of the algorithm")]
fn create_the_navigation_timing_entry(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    document: CppDocument,
    document_url: Utf16String,
    timing_info: CppFetchTimingInfo,
    redirect_count: u16,
    navigation_type: NavigationTimingType,
    cache_mode: Option<CacheState>,
    body_info: ResponseBodyInfo,
    response_status: u16,
) {
    // 1. Let global be document's relevant global object.
    // NB: The realm is that of global.

    // 2. Let navigationTimingEntry be a new PerformanceNavigationTiming object in global's realm.
    // 3. Setup the resource timing entry for navigationTimingEntry given "navigation", document's URL, fetchTiming,
    //    cacheMode, and bodyInfo.
    let resource_timing = PerformanceResourceTiming::setup_the_resource_timing_entry(
        realm,
        Utf16String::from_utf8("navigation"),
        document_url,
        timing_info,
        cache_mode,
        body_info,
        response_status,
        Utf16String::default(),
    );

    // 4. Set navigationTimingEntry's document load timing to document's load timing info
    // 5. Set navigationTimingEntry's previous document unload timing to document's previous document unload timing.
    // NB: The entry reads both from the document, which it keeps.
    // 6. Set navigationTimingEntry's redirect count to redirectCount.
    // 7. Set navigationTimingEntry's navigation type to navigationType.
    // 8. Set navigationTimingEntry's service worker timing to serviceWorkerTiming.
    // FIXME: Implement service worker timing.
    let navigation_timing_entry = allocate(vm, |_| PerformanceNavigationTiming {
        resource_timing,
        document: document.clone(),
        redirect_count,
        navigation_type,
    });
    let entry = AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceNavigationTiming(navigation_timing_entry);
    entry.entry().set_object(entry);

    // 9. Set document's navigation timing entry to navigationTimingEntry.
    document.set_navigation_timing_entry(navigation_timing_entry);

    // 10. Set navigationTimingEntry's `Critical-CH` restart time to criticalCHRestart.
    // FIXME: Implement the `Critical-CH` restart time.
    // 11. Set navigationTimingEntry's not restored reasons to the result of creating a NotRestoredReasons object given
    //     document's not restored reasons.
    // FIXME: Implement not restored reasons.

    // 12. Add navigationTimingEntry to global's performance entry buffer.
    PerformanceTimeline::of(vm, realm).add_performance_entry(vm, &entry, false);
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dfn-create-the-navigation-timing-entry
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `vm` must be the live VM, `realm` the live realm of the document's relevant global object, `document` a live
/// Document, `timing_info` a fetch timing info that LibWeb hands over a reference to, and `document_url` and the content
/// type of `body_info` raw AK::Utf16Strings that LibWeb hands over.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_navigation_timing_create_the_navigation_timing_entry(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    document: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::Document>,
    document_url: Utf16String,
    timing_info: *mut c_void,
    redirect_count: u16,
    navigation_type: u8,
    cache_mode: u8,
    body_info: ResponseBodyInfoAbi,
    response_status: u16,
) {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live Document, hands over the timing info and the strings.
    unsafe {
        create_the_navigation_timing_entry(
            vm,
            realm,
            CppDocument::from_lent(document),
            document_url,
            CppFetchTimingInfo::adopt(timing_info),
            redirect_count,
            NavigationTimingType::from_abi(navigation_type),
            CacheState::from_abi(cache_mode),
            body_info.into_body_info(),
            response_status,
        );
    }
}

//! PerformanceNavigation, https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#the-performancenavigation-interface

use libjs_rust::api::Trace;

use crate::bindings::global_object::CppWindow;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::navigation_timing::performance_navigation_timing::{NavigationTimingType, PerformanceNavigationTiming};

const TYPE_NAVIGATE: u16 = 0;
const TYPE_RELOAD: u16 = 1;
const TYPE_BACK_FORWARD: u16 = 2;

/// https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#the-performancenavigation-interface
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceNavigation {
    window: CppWindow,
}

impl Wrappable for PerformanceNavigation {}

impl PerformanceNavigation {
    pub(crate) fn new(window: CppWindow) -> Self {
        Self { window }
    }

    fn navigation_timing_entry(&self) -> Option<Ref<PerformanceNavigationTiming>> {
        self.window.associated_document().navigation_timing_entry()
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigation-type
    pub(crate) fn r#type(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u16> {
        // This attribute must return the type of the last non-redirect navigation. It must have one of the following
        // navigation type values.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(TYPE_NAVIGATE);
        };

        Ok(match entry.r#type(cx)? {
            NavigationTimingType::Navigate => TYPE_NAVIGATE,
            NavigationTimingType::Reload => TYPE_RELOAD,
            NavigationTimingType::BackForward => TYPE_BACK_FORWARD,
        })
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancenavigation-redirectcount
    pub(crate) fn redirect_count(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u16> {
        // This attribute must return the number of redirects since the last non-redirect navigation. If there is no
        // redirect or there is any redirect that is not from the same origin as the destination document, this attribute
        // must return zero.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };

        entry.redirect_count(cx)
    }
}
