//! PerformanceTiming, https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#the-performancetiming-interface

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::Trace;

use crate::bindings::global_object::CppWindow;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::dom::document::CppDocument;
use crate::navigation_timing::performance_navigation_timing::PerformanceNavigationTiming;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_high_resolution_time_estimated_monotonic_time_of_the_unix_epoch() -> f64;
    fn web_high_resolution_time_coarsen_time(timestamp: f64) -> f64;
}

type Attribute = fn(&PerformanceTiming, &mut CallContext<'_>) -> WebIdlResult<u64>;

const ATTRIBUTES: [(&str, Attribute); 21] = [
    ("connectEnd", PerformanceTiming::connect_end),
    ("connectStart", PerformanceTiming::connect_start),
    ("domainLookupEnd", PerformanceTiming::domain_lookup_end),
    ("domainLookupStart", PerformanceTiming::domain_lookup_start),
    ("domComplete", PerformanceTiming::dom_complete),
    (
        "domContentLoadedEventEnd",
        PerformanceTiming::dom_content_loaded_event_end,
    ),
    (
        "domContentLoadedEventStart",
        PerformanceTiming::dom_content_loaded_event_start,
    ),
    ("domInteractive", PerformanceTiming::dom_interactive),
    ("domLoading", PerformanceTiming::dom_loading),
    ("fetchStart", PerformanceTiming::fetch_start),
    ("loadEventEnd", PerformanceTiming::load_event_end),
    ("loadEventStart", PerformanceTiming::load_event_start),
    ("navigationStart", PerformanceTiming::navigation_start),
    ("redirectEnd", PerformanceTiming::redirect_end),
    ("redirectStart", PerformanceTiming::redirect_start),
    ("requestStart", PerformanceTiming::request_start),
    ("responseEnd", PerformanceTiming::response_end),
    ("responseStart", PerformanceTiming::response_start),
    ("secureConnectionStart", PerformanceTiming::secure_connection_start),
    ("unloadEventEnd", PerformanceTiming::unload_event_end),
    ("unloadEventStart", PerformanceTiming::unload_event_start),
];

fn attribute_named(name: &Utf16String) -> Option<Attribute> {
    ATTRIBUTES
        .iter()
        .find(|(attribute_name, _)| *name == Utf16String::from_utf8(attribute_name))
        .map(|(_, attribute)| *attribute)
}

pub(crate) fn is_performance_timing_attribute(name: &Utf16String) -> bool {
    attribute_named(name).is_some()
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#the-performancetiming-interface
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceTiming {
    window: CppWindow,
}

impl Wrappable for PerformanceTiming {}

// All time values are measured in milliseconds since midnight of January 1, 1970 (UTC).
fn monotonic_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(timestamp: f64) -> u64 {
    if timestamp == 0.0 {
        return 0;
    }

    // SAFETY: These read the clock.
    let wall_time = timestamp - unsafe { web_high_resolution_time_estimated_monotonic_time_of_the_unix_epoch() };
    let coarsened_time = unsafe { web_high_resolution_time_coarsen_time(wall_time) };
    #[expect(
        clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
        clippy::cast_sign_loss,
        reason = "C++ casts it to u64"
    )]
    let milliseconds = coarsened_time as u64;
    milliseconds
}

impl PerformanceTiming {
    pub(crate) fn new(window: CppWindow) -> Self {
        Self { window }
    }

    pub(crate) fn attribute(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, name: &Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        attribute_named(name).expect("the name is that of a PerformanceTiming attribute")(self, cx)
    }

    fn document(&self) -> CppDocument {
        self.window.associated_document()
    }

    fn navigation_timing_entry(&self) -> Option<Ref<PerformanceNavigationTiming>> {
        self.document().navigation_timing_entry()
    }

    // The document's time origin is its navigation start time, so a timestamp relative to it becomes monotonic by adding
    // that back. A fetch phase coinciding with navigation start is 0 relative to the time origin without being unset.
    fn fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(&self, relative_timestamp: f64) -> u64 {
        monotonic_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(
            relative_timestamp + self.document().load_timing_info().navigation_start_time,
        )
    }

    fn relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(&self, relative_timestamp: f64) -> u64 {
        if relative_timestamp == 0.0 {
            return 0;
        }

        self.fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(relative_timestamp)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-navigationstart
    pub(crate) fn navigation_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately after the user agent finishes prompting to unload the previous
        // document. If there is no previous document, this attribute must return the time the current document is created.
        Ok(monotonic_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(
            self.document().load_timing_info().navigation_start_time,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-unloadeventstart
    pub(crate) fn unload_event_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // If the previous document and the current document have the same origin, this attribute must return the time
        // immediately before the user agent starts the unload event of the previous document. If there is no previous
        // document or the previous document has a different origin than the current document, this attribute must return
        // zero.
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(
            self.document()
                .previous_document_unload_timing()
                .unload_event_start_time,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-unloadeventend
    pub(crate) fn unload_event_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // If the previous document and the current document have the same origin, this attribute must return the time
        // immediately after the user agent finishes the unload event of the previous document. If there is no previous
        // document or the previous document has a different origin than the current document or the unload is not yet
        // completed, this attribute must return zero.
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(
            self.document().previous_document_unload_timing().unload_event_end_time,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-redirectstart
    pub(crate) fn redirect_start(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // If there are HTTP redirects when navigating and if all the redirects are from the same origin, this attribute
        // must return the starting time of the fetch that initiates the redirect. Otherwise, this attribute must return
        // zero.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };

        if entry.redirect_count(cx)? == 0 {
            return Ok(0);
        }
        Ok(self.fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.redirect_start()))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-redirectend
    pub(crate) fn redirect_end(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // If there are HTTP redirects when navigating and all redirects are from the same origin, this attribute must
        // return the time immediately after receiving the last byte of the response of the last redirect. Otherwise, this
        // attribute must return zero.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };

        if entry.redirect_count(cx)? == 0 {
            return Ok(0);
        }
        Ok(self.fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.redirect_end()))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-fetchstart
    pub(crate) fn fetch_start(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // If the new resource is to be fetched using a "GET" request method, fetchStart must return the time immediately
        // before the user agent starts checking the HTTP cache. Otherwise, it must return the time when the user agent
        // starts fetching the resource.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };

        Ok(self.fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.parent().fetch_start(cx)?))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-domainlookupstart
    pub(crate) fn domain_lookup_start(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately before the user agent starts the domain name lookup for the
        // current document.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };
        Ok(self.fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.parent().domain_lookup_start(cx)?))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-domainlookupend
    pub(crate) fn domain_lookup_end(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately after the user agent finishes the domain name lookup for the
        // current document.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };
        Ok(self.fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.parent().domain_lookup_end(cx)?))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-connectstart
    pub(crate) fn connect_start(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately before the user agent start establishing the connection to the
        // server to retrieve the document.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };
        Ok(self.fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.parent().connect_start(cx)?))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-connectend
    pub(crate) fn connect_end(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately after the user agent finishes establishing the connection to
        // the server to retrieve the current document.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };
        Ok(self.fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.parent().connect_end(cx)?))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-secureconnectionstart
    pub(crate) fn secure_connection_start(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // When this attribute is available, if the scheme of the current page is "https", this attribute must return the
        // time immediately before the user agent starts the handshake process to secure the current connection. If this
        // attribute is available but HTTPS is not used, this attribute must return zero.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.parent().secure_connection_start(cx)?))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-requeststart
    pub(crate) fn request_start(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately before the user agent starts requesting the current document
        // from the server, or HTTP cache or from local resources.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };
        Ok(self.fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.parent().request_start(cx)?))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-responsestart
    pub(crate) fn response_start(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately after the user agent receives the first byte of the response
        // from the server, or HTTP cache or from local resources.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };
        Ok(self.fetch_phase_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.parent().response_start(cx)?))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-responseend
    pub(crate) fn response_end(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately after the user agent receives the last byte of the current
        // document or immediately before the transport connection is closed, whichever comes first.
        let Some(entry) = self.navigation_timing_entry() else {
            return Ok(0);
        };
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(entry.parent().response_end(cx)?))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-domloading
    pub(crate) fn dom_loading(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately before the user agent sets the current document readiness to
        // "loading".
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(self.document().load_timing_info().dom_loading_time))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-dominteractive
    pub(crate) fn dom_interactive(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately before the user agent sets the current document readiness to
        // "interactive".
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(self.document().load_timing_info().dom_interactive_time))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-domcontentloadedeventstart
    pub(crate) fn dom_content_loaded_event_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately before the user agent fires the DOMContentLoaded event at the
        // Document.
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(
            self.document().load_timing_info().dom_content_loaded_event_start_time,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-domcontentloadedeventend
    pub(crate) fn dom_content_loaded_event_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately after the document's DOMContentLoaded event completes.
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(
            self.document().load_timing_info().dom_content_loaded_event_end_time,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-domcomplete
    pub(crate) fn dom_complete(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately before the user agent sets the current document readiness to
        // "complete".
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(self.document().load_timing_info().dom_complete_time))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-loadeventstart
    pub(crate) fn load_event_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time immediately before the load event of the current document is fired. It must
        // return zero when the load event is not fired yet.
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(self.document().load_timing_info().load_event_start_time))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-performancetiming-loadeventend
    pub(crate) fn load_event_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        // This attribute must return the time when the load event of the current document is completed. It must return
        // zero when the load event is not fired or is not completed.
        Ok(self.relative_timestamp_to_wall_time_milliseconds(self.document().load_timing_info().load_event_end_time))
    }
}

use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::CppEnvironmentSettingsObject;
use crate::permissions::permissions::PermissionName;
use crate::permissions_api::permission_status::PermissionState;
use crate::permissions_api::permissions::permission_state;

// https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#permissions-integration
pub(crate) fn get_the_notifications_permission_state(settings: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject) -> PermissionState {
    // To get the notifications permission state, run these steps:

    // 1. Let permissionState be the result of getting the current permission state with "notifications".
    permission_state(PermissionName::Notifications, settings)

    // NB: Steps 2 and 3, which turn "prompt" into "default", belong to the permission getter: Every other caller wants
    //     the raw state.
}

// https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#action

// https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-notification
// This is the notification described as "notification" in the spec. Do not confuse it with "notification" as in the IDL which is just the JS wrapper.
// "A notification is an abstract representation of something that happened, such as the delivery of a message."
struct ConceptNotification {
    // FIXME: A notification has an associated service worker registration (null or a service worker registration). It is initially null.
    title: Utf16String,
    direction: NotificationDirection,
    language: Utf16String,
    body: Utf16String,
    navigation_url: Option<Url>,
    tag: Utf16String,
    data: Vec<u8>,
    timestamp: u64,
    #[allow(dead_code, reason = "the spec keeps the origin, which no step reads yet")]
    origin: Origin,
    renotify_preference: bool,
    silent_preference: Option<bool>,
    require_interaction_preference: bool,
    image_url: Option<Url>,
    icon_url: Option<Url>,
    badge_url: Option<Url>,

    // FIXME: add the resources from m_image_url, m_icon_url and m_badge_url

    // FIXME: A notification has an associated vibration pattern (a list). It is initially « ».
    actions: Vec<ConceptNotificationAction>,
}

// Where the notification is on its way to the platform. From Pending on it's in the page's list of notifications,
// which keeps it alive; Closed means it has left the list for good.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum State {
    Idle,
    Pending,
    Showing,
    Closing,
    Closed,
}

// https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#notifications
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Notification {
    event_target: CppEventTarget,

    #[gc(untraced)]
    notification: ConceptNotification,

    // The global the constructor ran in: Where the events fire, and whose window the notification belongs to.
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    window: Option<CppWindow>,

    #[gc(untraced)]
    state: Cell<State>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    id: Cell<u64>,

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#icon-resource
    icon: GcRefCell<Option<CppCell>>,
    // Bounds the wait for the icon: Past it, the notification shows without one.
    fetch_timeout: GcRefCell<Option<CppTimer>>,
}

impl Wrappable for Notification {
    const OWNS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY: bool = true;
    const COUNTS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_WHEN_ALLOCATED: bool = true;

    fn external_memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.notification.data.capacity()
    }

    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.realm)
    }

    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event_target.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for Notification {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
}

// The longest a notification waits for its icon before it shows without one.
const ICON_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS: u64 = 5_000;

fn parse_url(url: &UsvString, base_url: &Url) -> Option<Url> {
    basic_parse(url_input(url.units()), BasicParseOptions::new().base_url(base_url))
}

fn serialize_url_for_bindings(url: Option<&Url>) -> UsvString {
    url.map_or_else(
        || UsvString::from_ascii(b""),
        |url| UsvString::from_utf16_string(&Utf16String::from_utf8(url.serialize(ExcludeFragment::No))),
    )
}

fn notification_permission_from(permission_state: PermissionState) -> NotificationPermission {
    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#permissions-integration
    // 2. If permissionState is "prompt", then return "default".
    // 3. Return permissionState.
    match permission_state {
        PermissionState::Prompt => NotificationPermission::Default,
        PermissionState::Granted => NotificationPermission::Granted,
        PermissionState::Denied => NotificationPermission::Denied,
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct PermissionRequest {
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    global: Gc<Object>,
    promise: WebIdlPromise,
    deprecated_callback: Option<CallbackFunction>,
    settings: CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
}

impl Notification {
    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-notification-notification
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        title: Utf16String,
        options: NotificationOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let options = CreateNotificationOptions {
            direction: options.dir,
            language: options.lang,
            body: options.body,
            navigate: options.navigate,
            tag: options.tag,
            image: options.image,
            icon: options.icon,
            badge: options.badge,
            has_vibrate: options.vibrate.is_some(),
            timestamp: options.timestamp,
            renotify: options.renotify,
            silent: options.silent,
            require_interaction: options.require_interaction,
            data: options.data,
            actions: options.actions,
        };
        Self::create_with_global_scope(cx, title, options)
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#constructors
    fn create_with_global_scope(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        title: Utf16String,
        options: CreateNotificationOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let realm = cx.realm();
        let relevant_global_object = realm.global_object();
        let relevant_settings_object = relevant_settings_object(relevant_global_object);

        // 1. If this’s relevant global object is a ServiceWorkerGlobalScope object, then throw a TypeError.
        if is_service_worker_global_scope(relevant_global_object) {
            return Err(Exception::type_error(
                "This’s relevant global object is a ServiceWorkerGlobalScope object",
            ));
        }

        // 2. If options["actions"] is not empty, then throw a TypeError.
        if !options.actions.is_empty() {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Options `action` is not empty"));
        }

        // 3. Let notification be the result of creating a notification with a settings object given title, options, and this’s relevant settings object.
        let notification =
            Self::create_a_notification_with_a_settings_object(cx, title, options, &relevant_settings_object)?;

        // 4. Associate this with notification.
        let this_notification = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            event_target: CppEventTarget::new(),
            notification,
            realm,
            window: window_from_global_object(relevant_global_object),
            state: Cell::new(State::Idle),
            id: Cell::new(0),
            icon: GcRefCell::new(None),
            fetch_timeout: GcRefCell::new(None),
        });
        this_notification.event_target.set_owner(this_notification);

        // 5. Run these steps in parallel:
        // AD-HOC: The steps run from a task on the relevant global instead of in parallel: Showing crosses to the UI
        //         process asynchronously anyway, and a task keeps the permission read and the event firing on the main
        //         thread, after the constructor's caller has had its turn to attach event handlers.
        queue_a_global_task(
            vm,
            relevant_global_object,
            TaskSource::Unspecified,
            this_notification,
            |vm, this_notification| Self::run_steps_in_parallel_after_construction(this_notification, vm),
        );

        Ok(this_notification)
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#create-a-notification-with-a-settings-object
    fn create_a_notification_with_a_settings_object(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        title: Utf16String,
        options: CreateNotificationOptions,
        settings: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<ConceptNotification> {
        // 1. Let origin be settings’s origin.
        let origin = settings.origin();

        // 2. Let baseURL be settings’s API base URL.
        let base_url = settings.api_base_url();

        // 3. Let fallbackTimestamp be the number of milliseconds from the Unix epoch to settings’s current wall time,
        // rounded to the nearest integer.
        #[allow(
            clippy::cast_possible_truncation,
            clippy::cast_sign_loss,
            reason = "the conversion saturates, as AK::round_to() does"
        )]
        let fallback_timestamp = settings.current_wall_time().round_ties_even() as u64;

        // 4. Return the result of creating a notification given title, options, origin, baseURL, and fallbackTimestamp.
        Self::create_a_notification(cx, title, options, origin, &base_url, fallback_timestamp)
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#create-a-notification
    fn create_a_notification(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        title: Utf16String,
        options: CreateNotificationOptions,
        origin: Origin,
        base_url: &Url,
        fallback_timestamp: u64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<ConceptNotification> {
        // 1. Let notification be a new notification.

        // 2. If options["silent"] is true and options["vibrate"] exists, then throw a TypeError.
        if options.silent == Some(true) && options.has_vibrate {
            return Err(Exception::type_error(
                "options[\"vibrate\"] cannot be set when options[\"silent\"] is true.",
            ));
        }

        // 3. If options["renotify"] is true and options["tag"] is the empty string, then throw a TypeError.
        if options.renotify && options.tag.is_empty() {
            return Err(Exception::type_error(
                "options[\"tag\"] cannot be the empty string when options[\"renotify\"] is set to true.",
            ));
        }

        let mut notification = ConceptNotification {
            // 4. Set notification’s data to StructuredSerializeForStorage(options["data"]).
            data: structured_serialize_for_storage(cx, options.data)?,

            // 5. Set notification’s title to title.
            title,

            // 6. Set notification’s direction to options["dir"].
            direction: options.direction,

            // 7. Set notification’s language to options["lang"].
            language: options.language,

            // 8. Set notification’s origin to origin.
            origin,

            // 9. Set notification’s body to options["body"].
            body: options.body,

            // 10. If options["navigate"] exists, then parse it using baseURL, and if that does not return failure,
            // set notification’s navigation URL to the return value. (Otherwise notification’s navigation URL remains null.)
            navigation_url: options
                .navigate
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|navigate| parse_url(navigate, base_url)),

            // 11. Set notification’s tag to options["tag"].
            tag: options.tag,

            // 12. If options["image"] exists, then parse it using baseURL, and if that does not return failure,
            // set notification’s image URL to the return value. (Otherwise notification’s image URL is not set.)
            image_url: options.image.as_ref().and_then(|image| parse_url(image, base_url)),

            // 13. If options["icon"] exists, then parse it using baseURL, and if that does not return failure,
            // set notification’s icon URL to the return value. (Otherwise notification’s icon URL is not set.)
            icon_url: options.icon.as_ref().and_then(|icon| parse_url(icon, base_url)),

            // 14. If options["badge"] exists, then parse it using baseURL, and if that does not return failure,
            // set notification’s badge URL to the return value. (Otherwise notification’s badge URL is not set.)
            badge_url: options.badge.as_ref().and_then(|badge| parse_url(badge, base_url)),

            // FIXME: 15. If options["vibrate"] exists, then validate and normalize it and
            // set notification’s vibration pattern to the return value.

            // 16. If options["timestamp"] exists, then set notification’s timestamp to the value.
            // Otherwise, set notification’s timestamp to fallbackTimestamp.
            timestamp: options.timestamp.unwrap_or(fallback_timestamp),

            // 17. Set notification’s renotify preference to options["renotify"].
            renotify_preference: options.renotify,

            // 18. Set notification’s silent preference to options["silent"].
            silent_preference: options.silent,

            // 19. Set notification’s require interaction preference to options["requireInteraction"].
            require_interaction_preference: options.require_interaction,

            // 20. Set notification’s actions to « ».
            actions: Vec::new(),
        };

        // 21. For each entry in options["actions"], up to the maximum number of actions supported (skip any excess entries):
        for entry in options.actions {
            if notification.actions.len() >= Self::MAX_ACTIONS as usize {
                break;
            }

            // 1. Let action be a new notification action.
            let action = ConceptNotificationAction {
                // 2. Set action’s name to entry["action"].
                name: entry.action,

                // 3. Set action’s title to entry["title"].
                title: entry.title,

                // 4. If entry["navigate"] exists, then parse it using baseURL, and if that does not return failure,
                // set action’s navigation URL to the return value. (Otherwise action’s navigation URL remains null.)
                navigation_url: entry
                    .navigate
                    .as_ref()
                    .and_then(|navigate| parse_url(navigate, base_url)),

                // 5. If entry["icon"] exists, then parse it using baseURL, and if that does not return failure,
                // set action’s icon URL to the return value. (Otherwise action’s icon URL remains null.)
                icon_url: entry.icon.as_ref().and_then(|icon| parse_url(icon, base_url)),
            };

            // 6. Append action to notification’s actions.
            notification.actions.push(action);
        }

        // 22. Return notification.
        Ok(notification)
    }

    // Step 5 of https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#constructors
    fn run_steps_in_parallel_after_construction(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        let settings = relevant_settings_object(this.realm.global_object());

        // 1. If the result of getting the notifications permission state is not "granted", then queue a task to fire an
        //    event named error on this, and abort these steps.
        if get_the_notifications_permission_state(&settings) != PermissionState::Granted {
            Self::queue_task_to_fire_event(this, vm, "error");
            return;
        }

        // AD-HOC: The spec lets any document or worker show a notification. We refuse two cases until they're supported:
        //         A worker has no page to route the notification's events through, and a document whose origin differs
        //         from its top-level origin would have its notification attributed to the top-level site. Both get an
        //         error event, as if permission had been denied.
        if this.window.is_none() {
            Self::queue_task_to_fire_event(this, vm, "error");
            return;
        }
        if !settings
            .top_level_origin()
            .is_some_and(|top_level_origin| top_level_origin.is_same_origin(&settings.origin()))
        {
            Self::queue_task_to_fire_event(this, vm, "error");
            return;
        }

        // 2. Run the notification show steps for notification.
        Self::show_steps(this, vm);
    }

    fn window(&self) -> &CppWindow {
        self.window.as_ref().expect("a notification that is shown has a window")
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#notification-show-steps
    fn show_steps(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        // The notification joins the page's list now, rather than once it's displayed: The list is what keeps it alive
        // while its icon is on its way, and what lets the page withdraw it if the document goes away before then.
        // SAFETY: The window and the cell are live.
        this.id
            .set(unsafe { web_notifications_api_register_notification(this.window().as_ptr(), cell_into_abi(this)) });
        this.state.set(State::Pending);

        // 1. Run the fetch steps given notification and settings.
        // 2. Wait for any fetches to complete and notification's image resource, icon resource, and badge resource to
        //    be set (if any), as well as the icon resources for the notification's actions (if any).
        // AD-HOC: The wait for the fetch is bounded: An icon that hasn't arrived after a few seconds isn't worth holding
        //         the notification back for, so it then shows without one.
        let fetch_timeout = CppTimer::create_single_shot(vm, ICON_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, this, |vm, this| {
            if let Some(icon) = &*this.icon.borrow() {
                // SAFETY: The icon is live.
                unsafe { web_notifications_api_stop_icon_fetch(icon.as_ptr()) };
            }
            Self::display(this, vm);
        });
        *this.fetch_timeout.borrow_mut(vm) = Some(fetch_timeout);
        Self::run_the_fetch_steps(this, vm);
    }

    fn fetch_steps_done(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        let Some(fetch_timeout) = this.fetch_timeout.borrow().clone() else {
            return;
        };
        fetch_timeout.stop();
        Self::display(this, vm);
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-steps
    fn run_the_fetch_steps(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        // 1. If the notification platform supports images and notification's image URL is set, then fetch a notification
        //    resource given notification, notification's image URL, settings, and the following step given a resource
        //    resource: set notification's image resource to resource.
        // NB: No platform we show on takes an image.

        // 2. If the notification platform supports icons and notification's icon URL is set, then fetch a notification
        //    resource given notification, notification's icon URL, settings, and the following step given a resource
        //    resource: set notification's icon resource to resource.
        let Some(icon_url) = &this.notification.icon_url else {
            Self::fetch_steps_done(this, vm);
            return;
        };
        let settings = relevant_settings_object(this.realm.global_object());
        // SAFETY: The cell and the settings object are live, the URL is lent for the call, and LibWeb returns a live
        //         icon.
        let icon = unsafe {
            CppCell::from_raw(web_notifications_api_fetch_icon(
                cell_into_abi(this),
                settings.as_ptr(),
                &RustUrl::from_url(icon_url),
            ))
        };
        *this.icon.borrow_mut(vm) = Some(icon);

        // 3. If the notification platform supports badges and notification's badge URL is set, then fetch a notification
        //    resource given notification, notification's badge URL, settings, and the following step given a resource
        //    resource: set notification's badge resource to resource.
        // NB: No platform we show on takes a badge.

        // 4. If the notification platform supports actions and action icons, then for each entry of notification's
        //    actions: if entry's icon URL is non-null, then fetch a notification resource given notification, entry's
        //    icon URL, settings, and the following step given a resource resource: set entry's icon resource to resource.
        // NB: A non-persistent notification has no actions.
    }

    // Steps 3 to 8 of https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#notification-show-steps
    fn display(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        *this.fetch_timeout.borrow_mut(vm) = None;
        if this.state.get() != State::Pending {
            return;
        }

        // A document that went away while the icon was on its way gets no notification: The page may show another site
        // by now, and the notification would be attributed to that one.
        if !this.window().associated_document().is_fully_active() {
            this.abandon(vm);
            return;
        }

        // 3. Let shown be false.
        // 4. Let oldNotification be the notification in the list of notifications whose tag is not the empty string and is
        //    notification's tag, and whose origin is same origin with notification's origin, if any, and null otherwise.
        // 5. If oldNotification is non-null:
        //    1. Handle close events with oldNotification.
        //    2. If the notification platform supports replacement:
        //       1. Replace oldNotification with notification, in the list of notifications.
        //       2. Set shown to true.
        //    3. Otherwise, remove oldNotification from the list of notifications.
        // 6. If shown is false:
        //    1. Append notification to the list of notifications.
        //    2. Display notification on the device (e.g., by calling the appropriate notification platform API).
        // 7. If shown is false or oldNotification is non-null, and notification's renotify preference is true, then
        //    optionally alert the end user in a user-agent-defined manner (e.g., by playing a sound).
        // NB: Steps 4, 5 and 7 are the UI process's: It sees every page's notifications, so it finds oldNotification
        //     across pages, replaces it on the platform, and reports its close back through notification_closed().
        //     Here, the notification joins this page's part of the list and is sent off for display.
        this.state.set(State::Showing);
        let notification = &this.notification;
        let data = NotificationDataAbi {
            title: notification.title.raw_identity(),
            body: notification.body.raw_identity(),
            tag: notification.tag.raw_identity(),
            language: notification.language.raw_identity(),
            direction: notification.direction as u8,
            has_silent: notification.silent_preference.is_some(),
            silent: notification.silent_preference.unwrap_or(false),
            require_interaction: notification.require_interaction_preference,
            renotify: notification.renotify_preference,
        };
        let icon = this
            .icon
            .borrow()
            .as_ref()
            .map_or(core::ptr::null_mut(), CppCell::as_ptr);
        // SAFETY: The window and the icon are live, and the strings are lent for the call.
        unsafe { web_notifications_api_show_notification(this.window().as_ptr(), this.id.get(), &data, icon) };

        // 8. If notification is a non-persistent notification, then queue a task to fire an event named show on the
        //    Notification object representing notification.
        // NB: Fired from did_show(), once the platform has shown the notification: Until then the display can still fail,
        //     and a failure fires error instead.
    }

    fn document_ptr(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        self.window
            .as_ref()
            .map_or(core::ptr::null_mut(), |window| window.associated_document().as_ptr())
    }

    fn abandon(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        // Still on its way to the platform: Nothing has been shown, so there's nothing to tell the UI process.
        if self.state.get() == State::Pending {
            self.state.set(State::Closed);
            if let Some(fetch_timeout) = self.fetch_timeout.borrow_mut(vm).take() {
                fetch_timeout.stop();
            }
            if let Some(icon) = &*self.icon.borrow() {
                // SAFETY: The icon is live.
                unsafe { web_notifications_api_stop_icon_fetch(icon.as_ptr()) };
            }
            // SAFETY: The window is live.
            unsafe { web_notifications_api_unregister_notification(self.window().as_ptr(), self.id.get()) };
            return;
        }
        if self.state.get() != State::Showing && self.state.get() != State::Closing {
            return;
        }
        self.state.set(State::Closed);
        // SAFETY: The window is live.
        unsafe {
            web_notifications_api_unregister_notification(self.window().as_ptr(), self.id.get());
            web_notifications_api_abandon_notification(self.window().as_ptr(), self.id.get());
        }
    }

    fn did_show(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        if this.state.get() != State::Showing {
            return;
        }
        Self::queue_task_to_fire_event(this, vm, "show");
    }

    fn did_fail_to_show(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        // NB: The UI process forgets a notification it failed to show, so the close it was carrying out ends here.
        if this.state.get() == State::Closing {
            Self::did_close(this, vm);
            return;
        }
        if this.state.get() != State::Showing {
            return;
        }
        this.state.set(State::Closed);
        // SAFETY: The window is live.
        unsafe { web_notifications_api_unregister_notification(this.window().as_ptr(), this.id.get()) };
        Self::queue_task_to_fire_event(this, vm, "error");
    }

    // Step 2 of the non-persistent branch of https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#activating-a-notification
    fn did_click(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        if this.state.get() != State::Showing && this.state.get() != State::Closing {
            return;
        }

        // Otherwise, queue a task to run these steps:
        queue_a_global_task(
            vm,
            this.realm.global_object(),
            TaskSource::UserInteraction,
            this,
            |_, this| {
                // 1. Let intoFocus be the result of firing an event named click on the Notification object representing
                //    notification, with its cancelable attribute initialized to true.
                // NB: The user activated the notification, so the window gets transient activation first: That's what lets
                //     focus() work from within the event listener, as the spec encourages.
                if let Some(window) = &this.window {
                    window.give_transient_activation();
                }
                let event = CppEvent::create(this.realm, "click", false, true, false);
                let into_focus = this.event_target.dispatch_event(&event);

                // 2. If intoFocus is true, then the user agent should bring the notification's related browsing context's
                //    viewport into focus.
                if let Some(window) = &this.window {
                    // SAFETY: The window is live.
                    unsafe {
                        web_notifications_api_handle_notification_click(window.as_ptr(), this.id.get(), into_focus);
                    }
                }
            },
        );
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-notification-close
    pub(crate) fn close(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The close() method steps are to run the close steps for this's notification.
        self.close_steps();
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#close-steps
    fn close_steps(&self) {
        // 1. If the list of notifications does not contain notification, then abort these steps.
        // NB: A notification that's already on its way out (Closing) is left to the close the UI process is carrying out.
        if self.state.get() != State::Showing {
            return;
        }

        // 2. Handle close events with notification.
        // 3. Remove notification from the list of notifications.
        // NB: Both happen in did_close(), once the UI process has withdrawn the notification from the platform.
        self.state.set(State::Closing);
        // SAFETY: The window is live.
        unsafe { web_notifications_api_request_close_notification(self.window().as_ptr(), self.id.get()) };
    }

    // Steps 2 and 3 of https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#close-steps
    fn did_close(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        if this.state.get() != State::Showing && this.state.get() != State::Closing {
            return;
        }

        // 2. Handle close events with notification.
        // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#handle-close-events
        // 2. If notification is a non-persistent notification, then queue a task to fire an event named close on the
        //    Notification object representing notification.
        Self::queue_task_to_fire_event(this, vm, "close");

        // 3. Remove notification from the list of notifications.
        this.state.set(State::Closed);
        // SAFETY: The window is live.
        unsafe { web_notifications_api_unregister_notification(this.window().as_ptr(), this.id.get()) };
    }

    fn queue_task_to_fire_event(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm, event_name: &'static str) {
        queue_a_global_task(
            vm,
            this.realm.global_object(),
            TaskSource::Unspecified,
            (this, event_name),
            |_, (this, event_name)| {
                let event = CppEvent::create(this.realm, event_name, false, false, false);
                this.event_target.dispatch_event(&event);
            },
        );
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-notification-permission
    pub(crate) fn permission(cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<NotificationPermission> {
        // The static permission getter steps are to return the result of getting the notifications permission state.
        // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#permissions-integration
        // 1. Let permissionState be the result of getting the current permission state with "notifications".
        Ok(notification_permission_from(get_the_notifications_permission_state(
            &current_settings_object(cx.vm()),
        )))
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-notification-requestpermission
    pub(crate) fn request_permission(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        deprecated_callback: Option<CallbackFunction>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Let global be the current global object.
        let settings = current_settings_object(vm);
        let realm = settings.realm();
        let global = settings.global_object();

        // 2. Let promise be a new promise in this's relevant Realm.
        // NB: A static method has no "this"; the current realm is the one the call was made from.
        let promise = create_promise(vm, realm);

        // 3. Run these steps in parallel:
        //    1. Let permissionState be the result of requesting permission to use "notifications".
        //    2. Queue a global task on the DOM manipulation task source given global to run these steps:
        let request = PermissionRequest {
            realm,
            global,
            promise,
            deprecated_callback,
            settings: settings.clone(),
        };

        // AD-HOC: "Request permission to use" asks the user whenever the state is "prompt". We ask only from a document
        //         that is its own top-level site, and only while it has transient activation, which the request consumes.
        //         Any other request resolves with the state as it is, and nothing is stored, so the page may ask again
        //         from a click. (A document that isn't a secure context already reads "denied" from the permission
        //         state algorithm, so it never gets this far.) Each refusal is explained on the console.
        let current_state = get_the_notifications_permission_state(&settings);
        if current_state == PermissionState::Prompt {
            let window = window_from_global_object(global).expect("requestPermission() is exposed only to windows");
            let refuse = |message: &str| {
                realm.intrinsics().console_object(vm).console().output_debug_message(
                    ConsoleLogLevel::Error,
                    Utf16View::of_string(&Utf16String::from_utf8(message)),
                );
                Self::settle_permission_request(vm, request.clone());
                Ok(promise)
            };
            let is_its_own_top_level_site = settings.top_level_origin().is_some_and(|top_level_origin| {
                window.associated_document().origin().is_same_origin(&top_level_origin)
            });
            if !is_its_own_top_level_site {
                return refuse(
                    "Notification permission can only be requested from a document whose origin is the top-level origin.",
                );
            }
            if !window.has_transient_activation() {
                return refuse("Notification permission can only be requested while handling a user gesture.");
            }
            window.consume_user_activation();
        }
        request_permission_to_use(
            vm,
            PermissionName::Notifications,
            &settings,
            request,
            |vm, request, _| {
                Self::settle_permission_request(vm, request);
            },
        );

        // 4. Return promise.
        Ok(promise)
    }

    fn settle_permission_request(vm: &Vm, request: PermissionRequest) {
        // AD-HOC: "Request permission to use" reports "denied" for a prompt the user dismissed, though it stores nothing
        //         for it, and the page would then take a shrug for a refusal. The state the store holds once the
        //         answer is in is reported instead: "default" after a dismissal, so the page may ask again later.
        let permission_state = get_the_notifications_permission_state(&request.settings);
        let global = request.global;
        queue_a_global_task(
            vm,
            global,
            TaskSource::DOMManipulation,
            (request, permission_state as u8),
            |vm, (request, permission_state)| {
                let permission_state = match permission_state {
                    0 => PermissionState::Granted,
                    1 => PermissionState::Denied,
                    _ => PermissionState::Prompt,
                };
                with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(request.realm, || {
                    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, request.realm);
                    let permission = enumeration_value_to_js(
                        &cx,
                        match notification_permission_from(permission_state) {
                            NotificationPermission::Default => "default",
                            NotificationPermission::Denied => "denied",
                            NotificationPermission::Granted => "granted",
                        },
                    );

                    // 1. If deprecatedCallback is given, then invoke deprecatedCallback with « permissionState » and "report".
                    if let Some(deprecated_callback) = &request.deprecated_callback {
                        deprecated_callback.invoke_and_report(&[permission]);
                    }

                    // 2. Resolve promise with permissionState.
                    resolve_promise(vm, request.promise, permission);
                });
            },
        );
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#maximum-number-of-actions-supported
    // Two is what both desktop notification platforms show room for; persistent notifications, the only kind that
    // carries actions, aren't supported yet.
    const MAX_ACTIONS: u32 = 2;

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-notification-maxactions
    pub(crate) fn max_actions(_: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        Ok(Self::MAX_ACTIONS)
    }

    pub(crate) fn title(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.notification.title.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn dir(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<NotificationDirection> {
        Ok(self.notification.direction)
    }

    pub(crate) fn lang(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.notification.language.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn body(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.notification.body.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn navigate(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        Ok(serialize_url_for_bindings(self.notification.navigation_url.as_ref()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn tag(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.notification.tag.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn image(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        Ok(serialize_url_for_bindings(self.notification.image_url.as_ref()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn icon(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        Ok(serialize_url_for_bindings(self.notification.icon_url.as_ref()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn badge(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<UsvString> {
        Ok(serialize_url_for_bindings(self.notification.badge_url.as_ref()))
    }

    pub(crate) fn timestamp(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
        Ok(self.notification.timestamp)
    }

    pub(crate) fn renotify(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.notification.renotify_preference)
    }

    pub(crate) fn silent(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<bool>> {
        Ok(self.notification.silent_preference)
    }

    pub(crate) fn require_interaction(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.notification.require_interaction_preference)
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-notification-data
    pub(crate) fn data(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        // The data getter steps are to return StructuredDeserialize(this's notification's data, this's relevant Realm).
        // If this throws an exception, then return null.
        Ok(structured_deserialize_for_storage(cx, &self.notification.data).unwrap_or(Value::NULL))
    }

    // https://notifications.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-notification-actions
    pub(crate) fn actions(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<NotificationAction>> {
        // 1. Let frozenActions be an empty list of type NotificationAction.
        let mut frozen_actions = Vec::with_capacity(self.notification.actions.len());

        // 2. For each entry of this’s notification’s actions:
        for entry in &self.notification.actions {
            // 1. Let action be a new NotificationAction.
            let action = NotificationAction {
                // 2. Set action["action"] to entry’s name.
                action: entry.name.clone(),

                // 3. Set action["title"] to entry’s title.
                title: entry.title.clone(),

                // 4. If entry’s navigation URL is non-null, then set action["navigate"] to entry’s navigation URL, serialized.
                navigate: entry
                    .navigation_url
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(|url| serialize_url_for_bindings(Some(url))),

                // 5. If entry’s icon URL is non-null, then set action["icon"] to entry’s icon URL, serialized.
                icon: entry.icon_url.as_ref().map(|url| serialize_url_for_bindings(Some(url))),
            };

            // FIXME: 6. Call Object.freeze on action, to prevent accidental mutation by scripts.

            // 7. Append action to frozenActions.
            frozen_actions.push(action);
        }

        // 3. Return the result of create a frozen array from frozenActions.
        // NB: The bindings freeze the array they build from this sequence.
        Ok(frozen_actions)
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]

    notification.object::<Notification>().id.get()
}

/// Whether the notification still waits for its icon.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_notifications_api_is_pending(notification: &InterfaceCell) -> bool {
    notification.object::<Notification>().state.get() == State::Pending
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_notifications_api_icon_bytes_arrived(notification: &InterfaceCell) {
    let notification = notification.object::<Notification>();
    if let Some(fetch_timeout) = &*notification.fetch_timeout.borrow() {
        fetch_timeout.stop();
    }
}

/// The icon resource is set, or there is none.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]

    let notification = notification.object::<Notification>();
    Notification::fetch_steps_done(notification, vm);
}

    let notification = notification.object::<Notification>();
    notification.abandon(vm);
}

}

    let notification = notification.object::<Notification>();
    Notification::did_close(notification, vm);
}

//! PaintTimingMixin, https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#sec-PaintTimingMixin

/// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#paint-timing-info
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct PaintTimingInfo {
    /// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#paint-timing-info-rendering-update-end-time
    pub(crate) rendering_update_end_time: f64,
    /// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#paint-timing-info-implementation-defined-presentation-time
    pub(crate) implementation_defined_presentation_time: Option<f64>,
}

impl PaintTimingInfo {
    pub(crate) fn from_abi(
        rendering_update_end_time: f64,
        has_presentation_time: bool,
        implementation_defined_presentation_time: f64,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            rendering_update_end_time,
            implementation_defined_presentation_time: has_presentation_time
                .then_some(implementation_defined_presentation_time),
        }
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#default-paint-timestamp
pub(crate) fn default_paint_timestamp(paint_timing_info: &PaintTimingInfo) -> f64 {
    // To get the default paint timestamp for a paint timing info paintTimingInfo, return paintTimingInfo's
    // implementation-defined presentation time if it is non-null, otherwise paintTimingInfo's rendering update end time.
    paint_timing_info
        .implementation_defined_presentation_time
        .unwrap_or(paint_timing_info.rendering_update_end_time)
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#sec-PaintTimingMixin
pub(crate) struct PaintTimingMixin {
    // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#painttimingmixin-paint-timing-info
    // NB: Every object that includes this mixin is created with a paint timing info, so it is never null here.
    paint_timing_info: PaintTimingInfo,
}

impl PaintTimingMixin {
    pub(crate) fn new(paint_timing_info: PaintTimingInfo) -> Self {
        Self { paint_timing_info }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#dom-painttimingmixin-painttime
    pub(crate) fn paint_time(&self) -> f64 {
        // The paintTime attribute's getter step is to return this's paint timing info's rendering update end time.
        self.paint_timing_info.rendering_update_end_time
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#dom-painttimingmixin-presentationtime
    pub(crate) fn presentation_time(&self) -> Option<f64> {
        // The presentationTime attribute's getter step, if exists, is to return this's paint timing info's
        // implementation-defined presentation time.
        self.paint_timing_info.implementation_defined_presentation_time
    }

    pub(crate) fn paint_timing_info(&self) -> &PaintTimingInfo {
        &self.paint_timing_info
    }
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#exposed-for-paint-timing
pub(crate) fn is_exposed_for_paint_timing(node: &CppCell) -> bool {
    // NB: Given a null document. Only elements can be exposed for paint timing.

//! PerformancePaintTiming, https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#sec-PerformancePaintTiming

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_into_abi};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::paint_timing::paint_timing_mixin::{PaintTimingInfo, PaintTimingMixin, default_paint_timestamp};
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_entry::{AnyPerformanceEntry, PerformanceEntry};

/// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#sec-PerformancePaintTiming
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformancePaintTiming {
    entry: PerformanceEntry,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    paint_timing_mixin: PaintTimingMixin,
}

impl Wrappable for PerformancePaintTiming {}

impl Inherits<PerformanceEntry> for PerformancePaintTiming {
    fn parent(&self) -> &PerformanceEntry {
        &self.entry
    }
}

impl PerformancePaintTiming {
    // https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#report-paint-timing
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, paint_type: Utf16String, paint_timing_info: PaintTimingInfo) -> Ref<Self> {
        let new_entry = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            // 1. Set newEntry's name attribute to paintType.
            // 3. Set newEntry's startTime attribute to the default paint timestamp given paintTimingInfo.
            // 4. Set newEntry's duration attribute to 0.
            entry: PerformanceEntry::new(
                paint_type,
                Utf16String::from_utf8("paint"),
                default_paint_timestamp(&paint_timing_info),
                0.0,
            ),
            // 2. Set newEntry's paint timing info to paintTimingInfo.
            paint_timing_mixin: PaintTimingMixin::new(paint_timing_info),
        });
        let any_entry = AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformancePaintTiming(new_entry);
        any_entry.entry().set_object(any_entry);
        new_entry
    }

    pub(crate) fn paint_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.paint_timing_mixin.paint_time())
    }

    pub(crate) fn presentation_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<f64>> {
        Ok(self.paint_timing_mixin.presentation_time())
    }
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#report-paint-timing
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_paint_timing_create_performance_paint_timing(
    vm: &Vm,
    paint_type: Utf16String,
    rendering_update_end_time: f64,
    has_presentation_time: bool,
    presentation_time: f64,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let paint_timing_info =
        PaintTimingInfo::from_abi(rendering_update_end_time, has_presentation_time, presentation_time);
    cell_into_abi(PerformancePaintTiming::create(vm, paint_type, paint_timing_info))
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-queue-a-performanceentry, for an entry whose relevant global object

    entry: &InterfaceCell,
) {

}

) {

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{DeferGc, Trace};

use crate::performance_timeline::entry_types::SupportedEntryType;
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_entry::AnyPerformanceEntry;

// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-performance-entry-buffer-map
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceEntryTuple {
    /// The key of the tuple in the map.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) entry_type: Utf16String,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-performance-entry-buffer
    // A performance entry buffer to store PerformanceEntry objects, that is initially empty.
    pub(crate) performance_entry_buffer: Vec<AnyPerformanceEntry>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-maxbuffersize
    // An integer maxBufferSize, initialized to the registry value for this entry type.
    // NB: None is an infinite size.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) max_buffer_size: Option<u64>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-availablefromtimeline
    // A boolean availableFromTimeline, initialized to the registry value for this entry type.
    pub(crate) available_from_timeline: bool,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-dropped-entries-count
    // An integer dropped entries count that is initially 0.
    pub(crate) dropped_entries_count: u64,
}

impl PerformanceEntryTuple {
    pub(crate) fn new(_: &DeferGc<'_>, supported_entry_type: &SupportedEntryType) -> Self {
        Self {
            entry_type: Utf16String::from_utf8(supported_entry_type.entry_type),
            performance_entry_buffer: Vec::new(),
            max_buffer_size: supported_entry_type.max_buffer_size,
            available_from_timeline: supported_entry_type.available_from_timeline,
            dropped_entries_count: 0,
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-determine-if-a-performance-entry-buffer-is-full
    pub(crate) fn is_full(&mut self) -> bool {
        // 1. Let num current entries be the size of tuple's performance entry buffer.
        let num_current_entries = self.performance_entry_buffer.len() as u64;

        // 2. If num current entries is less than tuples's maxBufferSize, return false.
        if self
            .max_buffer_size
            .is_none_or(|max_buffer_size| num_current_entries < max_buffer_size)
        {
            return false;
        }

        // 3. Increase tuple's dropped entries count by 1.
        self.dropped_entries_count += 1;

        // 4. Return true.
        true
    }
}

//! PerformanceEntry, https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#the-performanceentry-interface

use core::cell::Cell;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{MarkedVec, ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value};

use crate::bindings::conversions::ToJs;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, InterfaceCell, Ref, Wrappable, wrap};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::event_timing::performance_event_timing::PerformanceEventTiming;
use crate::html::visibility_state_entry::VisibilityStateEntry;
use crate::largest_contentful_paint::largest_contentful_paint::LargestContentfulPaint;
use crate::navigation_timing::performance_navigation_timing::PerformanceNavigationTiming;
use crate::paint_timing::performance_paint_timing::PerformancePaintTiming;
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_observer::PerformanceObserverInit;
use crate::resource_timing::performance_resource_timing::PerformanceResourceTiming;
use crate::user_timing::performance_mark::PerformanceMark;
use crate::user_timing::performance_measure::PerformanceMeasure;

/// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceentry
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceEntry {
    name: Utf16String,
    entry_type: Utf16String,
    start_time: f64,
    duration: Cell<f64>,
    object: Cell<Option<AnyPerformanceEntry>>,
}

impl Wrappable for PerformanceEntry {}

impl PerformanceEntry {
    pub(crate) fn new(name: Utf16String, entry_type: Utf16String, start_time: f64, duration: f64) -> Self {
        Self {
            name,
            entry_type,
            start_time,
            duration: Cell::new(duration),
            object: Cell::new(None),
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-initialize-a-performanceentry
    pub(crate) fn initialize(start_time: f64, entry_type: Utf16String, name: Utf16String, end_time: f64) -> Self {
        // 1. Assert: entryType is defined in the entry type registry.
        // 2. Initialize entry’s startTime to startTime.
        // 3. Initialize entry’s entryType to entryType.
        // 4. Initialize entry’s name to name.
        // 5. Initialize entry’s end time to endTime.
        // NB: Neither the end time nor startTime change after this, so the result of the duration getter steps is kept
        //     instead: https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceentry-duration
        //     The getter steps for the duration attribute are to return 0 if this’s end time is 0; otherwise this’s end
        //     time - this’s startTime.
        let duration = if end_time == 0.0 { 0.0 } else { end_time - start_time };
        Self::new(name, entry_type, start_time, duration)
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_object(&self, object: AnyPerformanceEntry) {
        self.object.set(Some(object));
    }

    pub(crate) fn object(&self) -> AnyPerformanceEntry {
        self.object
            .get()
            .expect("every entry is part of an object of an interface that inherits from PerformanceEntry")
    }

    pub(crate) fn name(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.object().name())
    }

    pub(crate) fn entry_type(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.object().entry_type())
    }

    pub(crate) fn start_time(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.object().start_time())
    }

    pub(crate) fn duration(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.object().duration())
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_duration(&self, duration: f64) {
        self.duration.set(duration);
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum AnyPerformanceEntry {
    LargestContentfulPaint(Ref<LargestContentfulPaint>),
    PerformanceEventTiming(Ref<PerformanceEventTiming>),
    PerformanceMark(Ref<PerformanceMark>),
    PerformanceMeasure(Ref<PerformanceMeasure>),
    PerformanceNavigationTiming(Ref<PerformanceNavigationTiming>),
    PerformancePaintTiming(Ref<PerformancePaintTiming>),
    PerformanceResourceTiming(Ref<PerformanceResourceTiming>),
    VisibilityStateEntry(Ref<VisibilityStateEntry>),
}

macro_rules! for_each_entry {
    ($any:expr, $object:ident => $expression:expr) => {
        match $any {
            AnyPerformanceEntry::LargestContentfulPaint($object) => $expression,
            AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceEventTiming($object) => $expression,
            AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceMark($object) => $expression,
            AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceMeasure($object) => $expression,
            AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceNavigationTiming($object) => $expression,
            AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformancePaintTiming($object) => $expression,
            AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceResourceTiming($object) => $expression,
            AnyPerformanceEntry::VisibilityStateEntry($object) => $expression,
        }
    };
}

impl ToJs for AnyPerformanceEntry {
    fn to_js(self, cx: &CallContext) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        Ok(Value::from_object(for_each_entry!(self, object => wrap(cx, object))))
    }
}

impl AnyPerformanceEntry {
    pub(crate) fn from_abi(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> Self {
        if let Some(object) = cell.object_if() {
            return Self::LargestContentfulPaint(object);
        }
        if let Some(object) = cell.object_if() {
            return Self::PerformanceEventTiming(object);
        }
        if let Some(object) = cell.object_if() {
            return Self::PerformanceMark(object);
        }
        if let Some(object) = cell.object_if() {
            return Self::PerformanceMeasure(object);
        }
        if let Some(object) = cell.object_if() {
            return Self::PerformanceNavigationTiming(object);
        }
        if let Some(object) = cell.object_if() {
            return Self::PerformancePaintTiming(object);
        }
        if let Some(object) = cell.object_if() {
            return Self::PerformanceResourceTiming(object);
        }
        Self::VisibilityStateEntry(cell.object())
    }

    pub(crate) fn entry(&self) -> &PerformanceEntry {
        match self {
            Self::LargestContentfulPaint(object) => object.parent(),
            Self::PerformanceEventTiming(object) => object.parent(),
            Self::PerformanceMark(object) => object.parent(),
            Self::PerformanceMeasure(object) => object.parent(),
            Self::PerformanceNavigationTiming(object) => {
                let resource_timing: &PerformanceResourceTiming = object.parent();
                resource_timing.parent()
            }
            Self::PerformancePaintTiming(object) => object.parent(),
            Self::PerformanceResourceTiming(object) => object.parent(),
            Self::VisibilityStateEntry(object) => object.parent(),
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceentry-name
    pub(crate) fn name(&self) -> Utf16String {
        // This attribute must return the value it is initialized to.
        self.entry().name.clone()
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceentry-entrytype
    pub(crate) fn entry_type(&self) -> Utf16String {
        if let Self::PerformanceNavigationTiming(entry) = self {
            return entry.entry_type();
        }

        // This attribute must return the value it is initialized to.
        self.entry().entry_type.clone()
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceentry-starttime
    pub(crate) fn start_time(&self) -> f64 {
        if let Self::PerformanceNavigationTiming(entry) = self {
            return entry.start_time();
        }

        // This attribute must return the value it is initialized to.
        self.entry().start_time
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceentry-duration
    pub(crate) fn duration(&self) -> f64 {
        if let Self::PerformanceNavigationTiming(entry) = self {
            return entry.duration();
        }

        // The getter steps for the duration attribute are to return 0 if this’s end time is 0; otherwise this’s end time
        // - this’s startTime.
        // NB: initialize() keeps the result of these steps, and the specs that set the duration attribute keep theirs.
        self.entry().duration.get()
    }

    /// https://w3c.github.io/timing-entrytypes-registry/#dfn-should-add-entry
    pub(crate) fn should_add_entry(&self, options: Option<&PerformanceObserverInit>) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::PerformanceEventTiming(entry) => entry.should_add_entry(options),
            _ => true,
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn sort_in_chronological_order(entries: &MarkedVec<'_, AnyPerformanceEntry>) {
    entries
        .values_mut()
        .sort_by(|left, right| left.start_time().total_cmp(&right.start_time()));
}

// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-filter-buffer-by-name-and-type
pub(crate) fn filter_buffer_by_name_and_type<'vm>(
    cx: &CallContext<'vm>,
    buffer: &[AnyPerformanceEntry],
    name: Option<&Utf16String>,
    r#type: Option<&Utf16String>,
) -> MarkedVec<'vm, AnyPerformanceEntry> {
    // 1. Let result be an initially empty list.
    let result = MarkedVec::new(cx.vm());

    // 2. For each PerformanceEntry entry in buffer, run the following steps:
    for entry in buffer {
        // 1. If type is not null and if type is not identical to entry's entryType attribute, continue to next entry.
        if r#type.is_some_and(|r#type| *r#type != entry.entry_type()) {
            continue;
        }

        // 2. If name is not null and if name is not identical to entry's name attribute, continue to next entry.
        if name.is_some_and(|name| *name != entry.name()) {
            continue;
        }

        // 3. append entry to result.
        result.push(*entry);
    }

    // 3. Sort results's entries in chronological order with respect to startTime
    sort_in_chronological_order(&result);

    // 4. Return result.
    result
}

//! PerformanceObserverEntryList, https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#performanceobserverentrylist-interface

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, MarkedVec, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_entry::{AnyPerformanceEntry, filter_buffer_by_name_and_type};

// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#performanceobserverentrylist-interface
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceObserverEntryList {
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-entry-list
    entry_list: Vec<AnyPerformanceEntry>,
}

impl Wrappable for PerformanceObserverEntryList {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.realm)
    }
}

impl PerformanceObserverEntryList {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, entry_list: &MarkedVec<'_, AnyPerformanceEntry>) -> Ref<Self> {
        allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            realm,
            entry_list: entry_list.to_vec(),
        })
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceobserverentrylist-getentries
    pub(crate) fn get_entries<'vm>(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, AnyPerformanceEntry>> {
        // Returns a PerformanceEntryList object returned by filter buffer by name and type algorithm with this's entry list,
        // name and type set to null.
        let entries = filter_buffer_by_name_and_type(cx, &self.entry_list, None, None);
        Ok(entries)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceobserverentrylist-getentriesbytype
    pub(crate) fn get_entries_by_type<'vm>(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
        r#type: Utf16String,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, AnyPerformanceEntry>> {
        // Returns a PerformanceEntryList object returned by filter buffer by name and type algorithm with this's entry list,
        // name set to null, and type set to the method's input type parameter.
        let entries = filter_buffer_by_name_and_type(cx, &self.entry_list, None, Some(&r#type));
        Ok(entries)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceobserverentrylist-getentriesbyname
    pub(crate) fn get_entries_by_name<'vm>(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
        name: Utf16String,
        r#type: Option<Utf16String>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, AnyPerformanceEntry>> {
        // Returns a PerformanceEntryList object returned by filter buffer by name and type algorithm with this's entry list,
        // name set to the method input name parameter, and type set to null if optional entryType is omitted, or set to the
        // method's input type parameter otherwise.
        let entries = filter_buffer_by_name_and_type(cx, &self.entry_list, Some(&name), r#type.as_ref());
        Ok(entries)
    }
}
