//! PerformanceObserver, https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#the-performanceobserver-interface

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};

use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, GcRefCell, MarkedVec, PropertyKey, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value, Vm};

// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceobserverinit
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceObserverInit {
    pub(crate) entry_types: Option<Vec<Utf16String>>,
    pub(crate) r#type: Option<Utf16String>,
    pub(crate) buffered: Option<bool>,
    // https://w3c.github.io/event-timing/#sec-modifications-perf-timeline
    pub(crate) duration_threshold: Option<f64>,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-observer-type
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum ObserverType {
    Undefined,
    Single,
    Multiple,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceobserver
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceObserver {
    realm: Gc<Realm>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-observer-callback
    // A PerformanceObserverCallback observer callback set on creation.
    callback: CallbackFunction,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-observer-buffer
    // A PerformanceEntryList object called the observer buffer that is initially empty.
    observer_buffer: GcRefCell<Vec<AnyPerformanceEntry>>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-observer-type
    // A DOMString observer type which is initially "undefined".
    #[gc(untraced)]
    observer_type: Cell<ObserverType>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-requires-dropped-entries
    // A boolean requires dropped entries which is initially set to false.
    requires_dropped_entries: Cell<bool>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-options-list
    // A registered performance observer is a struct consisting of an observer member (a PerformanceObserver object)
    // and an options list member (a list of PerformanceObserverInit objects).
    // NOTE: This doesn't use a separate struct as methods such as disconnect() assume it can access an options list from `this`: a PerformanceObserver.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    options_list: RefCell<Vec<PerformanceObserverInit>>,
}

impl Wrappable for PerformanceObserver {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.realm)
    }
}

fn is_supported_entry_type(global_is_window: bool, r#type: &Utf16String) -> bool {
    supported_entry_types(global_is_window).any(|supported| *r#type == Utf16String::from_utf8(supported.entry_type))
}

impl PerformanceObserver {
    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceobserver-constructor
    pub(crate) fn construct(cx: &mut CallContext, callback: CallbackFunction) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |_| Self {
            realm: cx.realm(),
            callback,
            observer_buffer: GcRefCell::default(),
            observer_type: Cell::new(ObserverType::Undefined),
            requires_dropped_entries: Cell::new(false),
            options_list: RefCell::default(),
        }))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceobserver-observe
    pub(crate) fn observe(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        options: PerformanceObserverInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Let relevantGlobal be this's relevant global object.
        let relevant_global = PerformanceTimeline::of(vm, this.realm);

        // 2. If options's entryTypes and type members are both omitted, then throw a "TypeError".
        if options.entry_types.is_none() && options.r#type.is_none() {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Must specify one of entryTypes or type"));
        }

        // 3. If options's entryTypes is present and any other member is also present, then throw a "TypeError".
        if options.entry_types.is_some() && (options.r#type.is_some() || options.buffered.is_some()) {
            return Err(Exception::type_error(
                "Cannot specify type or buffered if entryTypes is specified",
            ));
        }

        // 4. Update or check this's observer type by running these steps:
        match this.observer_type.get() {
            // 1. If this's observer type is "undefined":
            ObserverType::Undefined => {
                // 1. If options's entryTypes member is present, then set this's observer type to "multiple".
                if options.entry_types.is_some() {
                    this.observer_type.set(ObserverType::Multiple);
                }

                // 2. If options's type member is present, then set this's observer type to "single".
                if options.r#type.is_some() {
                    this.observer_type.set(ObserverType::Single);
                }
            }
            // 2. If this's observer type is "single" and options's entryTypes member is present, then throw an
            //    "InvalidModificationError".
            ObserverType::Single => {
                if options.entry_types.is_some() {
                    return Err(Exception::Dom(
                        "InvalidModificationError",
                        Utf16String::from_utf8(
                            "Cannot change a PerformanceObserver from observing a single type to observing multiple types",
                        ),
                    ));
                }
            }
            // 3. If this's observer type is "multiple" and options's type member is present, then throw an
            //    "InvalidModificationError".
            ObserverType::Multiple => {
                if options.r#type.is_some() {
                    return Err(Exception::Dom(
                        "InvalidModificationError",
                        Utf16String::from_utf8(
                            "Cannot change a PerformanceObserver from observing multiple types to observing a single type",
                        ),
                    ));
                }
            }
        }

        // 5. Set this's requires dropped entries to true.
        this.requires_dropped_entries.set(true);

        let global_is_window = realm_is_window(this.realm);

        // 6. If this's observer type is "multiple", run the following steps:
        if this.observer_type.get() == ObserverType::Multiple {
            // 1. Let entry types be options's entryTypes sequence.
            let mut options = options;
            let entry_types = options
                .entry_types
                .as_mut()
                .expect("an observer of multiple types observes entryTypes");

            // 2. Remove all types from entry types that are not contained in relevantGlobal's frozen array of supported
            //    entry types. The user agent SHOULD notify developers if entry types is modified. For example, a console
            //    warning listing removed types might be appropriate.
            entry_types.retain(|r#type| is_supported_entry_type(global_is_window, r#type));

            // 3. If the resulting entry types sequence is an empty sequence, abort these steps.
            //    The user agent SHOULD notify developers when the steps are aborted to notify that registration has been
            //    aborted. For example, a console warning might be appropriate.
            if entry_types.is_empty() {
                return Ok(());
            }

            // 4. If the list of registered performance observer objects of relevantGlobal contains a registered
            //    performance observer whose observer is this, replace its options list with a list containing options as
            //    its only item.
            // 5. Otherwise, create and append a registered performance observer object to the list of registered
            //    performance observer objects of relevantGlobal, with observer set to this and options list set to a list
            //    containing options as its only item.
            *this.options_list.borrow_mut() = vec![options];
            relevant_global.register_performance_observer(vm, *this);
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 7. Otherwise, run the following steps:
        // 1. Assert that this's observer type is "single".
        assert!(this.observer_type.get() == ObserverType::Single);

        // 2. If options's type is not contained in the relevantGlobal's frozen array of supported entry types, abort
        //    these steps. The user agent SHOULD notify developers when this happens, for instance via a console warning.
        let r#type = options
            .r#type
            .clone()
            .expect("an observer of a single type observes type");
        if !is_supported_entry_type(global_is_window, &r#type) {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 3. If the list of registered performance observer objects of relevantGlobal contains a registered performance
        //    observer obs whose observer is this:
        if relevant_global.has_registered_performance_observer(*this) {
            // 1. If obs's options list contains a PerformanceObserverInit item currentOptions whose type is equal to
            //    options's type, replace currentOptions with options in obs's options list.
            let mut options_list = this.options_list.borrow_mut();
            if let Some(current_options) = options_list
                .iter_mut()
                .find(|current_options| current_options.r#type == options.r#type)
            {
                *current_options = options.clone();
            }
            // 2. Otherwise, append options to obs's options list.
            else {
                options_list.push(options.clone());
            }
        }
        // 4. Otherwise, create and append a registered performance observer object to the list of registered performance
        //    observer objects of relevantGlobal, with observer set to the this and options list set to a list containing
        //    options as its only item.
        else {
            *this.options_list.borrow_mut() = vec![options.clone()];
            relevant_global.register_performance_observer(vm, *this);
        }

        // 5. If options's buffered flag is set:
        if options.buffered == Some(true) {
            // 1. Let tuple be the relevant performance entry tuple of options's type and relevantGlobal.
            relevant_global.with_relevant_performance_entry_tuple(&r#type, |tuple| {
                // 2. For each entry in tuple's performance entry buffer:
                let mut observer_buffer = this.observer_buffer.borrow_mut(vm);
                for entry in &tuple.performance_entry_buffer {
                    // 1. If should add entry with entry and options as parameters returns true, append entry to the
                    //    observer buffer.
                    if entry.should_add_entry(Some(&options)) {
                        observer_buffer.push(*entry);
                    }
                }
            });

            // 3. Queue the PerformanceObserver task with relevantGlobal as input.
            relevant_global.queue_the_performance_observer_task(vm);
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceobserver-disconnect
    pub(crate) fn disconnect(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Remove this from the list of registered performance observer objects of relevant global object.
        PerformanceTimeline::of(vm, this.realm).unregister_performance_observer(vm, *this);

        // 2. Empty this's observer buffer.
        this.observer_buffer.borrow_mut(vm).clear();

        // 3. Empty this's options list.
        this.options_list.borrow_mut().clear();
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceobserver-takerecords
    pub(crate) fn take_records<'vm>(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, AnyPerformanceEntry>> {
        // The takeRecords() method must return a copy of this's observer buffer, and also empty this's observer buffer.
        let records = self.take_observer_buffer(cx.vm());
        Ok(records)
    }

    pub(crate) fn take_observer_buffer<'vm>(&self, vm: &'vm Vm) -> MarkedVec<'vm, AnyPerformanceEntry> {
        let records = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        let mut buffer = self.observer_buffer.borrow_mut(vm);
        records.extend_from_slice(&buffer);
        buffer.clear();
        drop(buffer);
        records
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dom-performanceobserver-supportedentrytypes
    pub(crate) fn supported_entry_types(cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        // When supportedEntryTypes’s attribute getter is called, run the following steps:
        // 1. Let globalObject be the environment settings object’s global object.
        // 2. Return globalObject’s frozen array of supported entry types.
        let data = realm_data(cx.vm(), cx.realm());
        if let Some(array) = data.performance_observer_supported_entry_types.get() {
            return Ok(Value::from_object(array));
        }
        let global_is_window = realm_is_window(cx.realm());
        let types: Vec<Utf16String> = supported_entry_types(global_is_window)
            .map(|supported| Utf16String::from_utf8(supported.entry_type))
            .collect();
        let array = frozen_array_to_js(cx, sequence_to_js(cx, types, |r#type| r#type.to_js(cx)))?;
        data.performance_observer_supported_entry_types
            .set(Some(array.as_object()));
        Ok(array)
    }

    pub(crate) fn realm(&self) -> Gc<Realm> {
        self.realm
    }

    pub(crate) fn requires_dropped_entries(&self) -> bool {
        self.requires_dropped_entries.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn unset_requires_dropped_entries(&self) {
        self.requires_dropped_entries.set(false);
    }

    pub(crate) fn options_list(&self) -> core::cell::Ref<'_, Vec<PerformanceObserverInit>> {
        self.options_list.borrow()
    }

    pub(crate) fn append_to_observer_buffer(&self, vm: &Vm, entry: AnyPerformanceEntry) {
        self.observer_buffer.borrow_mut(vm).push(entry);
    }

    pub(crate) fn invoke_callback(
        this: Ref<Self>,
        vm: &Vm,
        observer_entry_list: Ref<PerformanceObserverEntryList>,
        dropped_entries_count: Option<u64>,
    ) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()> {
        let cx = &CallContext::new(vm, this.realm);
        let callback_options = create_dictionary_object(cx);
        if let Some(dropped_entries_count) = dropped_entries_count {
            callback_options.create_data_property(
                vm,
                &PropertyKey::from_utf8("droppedEntriesCount"),
                dropped_entries_count.to_js(cx)?,
                None,
                None,
            )?;
        }
        let observer = Value::from_object(wrap(cx, this));
        this.callback.invoke(
            Some(observer),
            &[
                Value::from_object(wrap(cx, observer_entry_list)),
                observer,
                Value::from_object(callback_options),
            ],
        )?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! The performance timeline, https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#performance-timeline

use core::cell::Cell;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, GcRefCell, MarkedVec, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::CallContext;
use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::relevant_settings_object;
use crate::bindings::event_target::CppEvent;
use crate::bindings::interface::{
    Ref, realm_is_window, report_an_exception, with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks,
};
use crate::bindings::promise::{TaskSource, queue_a_global_task, queue_a_task};
use crate::bindings::realm_data::realm_data;
use crate::high_resolution_time::performance::Performance;
use crate::performance_timeline::entry_types::supported_entry_types;
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_entry::{
    AnyPerformanceEntry, filter_buffer_by_name_and_type, sort_in_chronological_order,
};
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_entry_tuple::PerformanceEntryTuple;
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_observer::PerformanceObserver;
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_observer_entry_list::PerformanceObserverEntryList;

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceTimeline {
    realm: Gc<Realm>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-windoworworkerglobalscope-performance
    performance: Cell<Option<Ref<Performance>>>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#performance-timeline
    // Each global object has:
    // - a performance observer task queued flag
    performance_observer_task_queued: Cell<bool>,

    // - a list of registered performance observer objects that is initially empty
    registered_performance_observer_objects: GcRefCell<Vec<Ref<PerformanceObserver>>>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-performance-entry-buffer-map
    // a performance entry buffer map map, keyed on a DOMString, representing the entry type to which the buffer belongs. The map's value is the following tuple:
    performance_entry_buffer_map: GcRefCell<Vec<PerformanceEntryTuple>>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#sec-extensions-performance-interface
    // Each ECMAScript global environment has:
    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-resource-timing-buffer-size-limit
    // A resource timing buffer size limit which should initially be 250 or greater.
    // The recommended minimum number of PerformanceResourceTiming objects is 250, though this may be changed by the
    // user agent. setResourceTimingBufferSize can be called to request a change to this limit.
    resource_timing_buffer_size_limit: Cell<u32>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-resource-timing-buffer-full-event-pending-flag
    // A resource timing buffer full event pending flag which is initially false.
    resource_timing_buffer_full_event_pending: Cell<bool>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-resource-timing-secondary-buffer-current-size
    // A resource timing secondary buffer current size which is initially 0.
    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-resource-timing-secondary-buffer
    // A resource timing secondary buffer to store PerformanceResourceTiming objects that is initially empty.
    resource_timing_secondary_buffer: GcRefCell<Vec<AnyPerformanceEntry>>,
}

static PERFORMANCE_TIMELINE_CLASS: EmbedderClass<PerformanceTimeline> = EmbedderClass::new("PerformanceTimeline");

impl EmbedderValue for PerformanceTimeline {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &PERFORMANCE_TIMELINE_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type PerformanceTimelineRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<PerformanceTimeline>>;

impl PerformanceTimeline {
    /// Every world of the global object shares its timeline.
    pub(crate) fn of(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> PerformanceTimelineRef {
        let realm = relevant_settings_object(realm.global_object()).realm();
        let data = realm_data(vm, realm);
        if let Some(timeline) = data.performance_timeline.get() {
            return timeline;
        }
        let timeline = PERFORMANCE_TIMELINE_CLASS.allocate(vm, |defer_gc| Self {
            realm,
            performance: Cell::new(None),
            performance_observer_task_queued: Cell::new(false),
            registered_performance_observer_objects: GcRefCell::default(),
            performance_entry_buffer_map: GcRefCell::new(
                supported_entry_types(realm_is_window(realm))
                    .map(|supported_entry_type| PerformanceEntryTuple::new(defer_gc, supported_entry_type))
                    .collect(),
            ),
            resource_timing_buffer_size_limit: Cell::new(250),
            resource_timing_buffer_full_event_pending: Cell::new(false),
            resource_timing_secondary_buffer: GcRefCell::default(),
        });
        data.performance_timeline.set(Some(timeline));
        timeline
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-windoworworkerglobalscope-performance
    pub(crate) fn performance(&self, vm: &Vm) -> Ref<Performance> {
        if let Some(performance) = self.performance.get() {
            return performance;
        }
        let performance = Performance::create(vm, self.realm);
        self.performance.set(Some(performance));
        performance
    }

    /// https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-relevant-performance-entry-tuple
    pub(crate) fn with_relevant_performance_entry_tuple<R>(
        &self,
        entry_type: &Utf16String,
        steps: impl FnOnce(&PerformanceEntryTuple) -> R,
    ) -> R {
        // 1. Let map be the performance entry buffer map associated with globalObject.
        // 2. Return the result of getting the value of an entry from map, given entryType as the key.
        let map = self.performance_entry_buffer_map.borrow();
        steps(Self::tuple_of(&map, entry_type))
    }

    fn with_relevant_performance_entry_tuple_mut<R>(
        &self,
        vm: &Vm,
        entry_type: &Utf16String,
        steps: impl FnOnce(&mut PerformanceEntryTuple) -> R,
    ) -> R {
        let mut map = self.performance_entry_buffer_map.borrow_mut(vm);
        let tuple = map
            .iter_mut()
            .find(|tuple| tuple.entry_type == *entry_type)
            .expect("the entry type is a supported entry type");
        steps(tuple)
    }

    fn tuple_of<'a>(map: &'a [PerformanceEntryTuple], entry_type: &Utf16String) -> &'a PerformanceEntryTuple {
        map.iter()
            .find(|tuple| tuple.entry_type == *entry_type)
            .expect("the entry type is a supported entry type")
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-queue-a-performanceentry
    pub(crate) fn queue_performance_entry(&self, vm: &Vm, new_entry: &AnyPerformanceEntry) {
        // 1. Let interested observers be an initially empty set of PerformanceObserver objects.
        let interested_observers = MarkedVec::new(vm);

        // 2. Let entryType be newEntry’s entryType value.
        let entry_type = new_entry.entry_type();

        // 3. Let relevantGlobal be newEntry's relevant global object.
        // NB: Already is `self`.

        // 4. For each registered performance observer regObs in relevantGlobal's list of registered performance observer
        //    objects:
        for registered_observer in self.registered_performance_observer_objects.borrow().iter() {
            // 1. If regObs's options list contains a PerformanceObserverInit options whose entryTypes member includes entryType
            //    or whose type member equals to entryType:
            let options_list = registered_observer.options_list();
            let options = options_list.iter().find(|options| match &options.entry_types {
                Some(entry_types) => entry_types.contains(&entry_type),
                None => options.r#type.as_ref() == Some(&entry_type),
            });

            if let Some(options) = options {
                // 1. If should add entry with newEntry and options returns true, append regObs's observer to interested observers.
                if new_entry.should_add_entry(Some(options)) {
                    interested_observers.push(*registered_observer);
                }
            }
        }

        // 5. For each observer in interested observers:
        for observer in interested_observers.values().iter() {
            // 1. Append newEntry to observer's observer buffer.
            observer.append_to_observer_buffer(vm, *new_entry);
        }

        // AD-HOC: Steps 6-9 are not here because other engines do not add to the performance entry buffer when queuing
        //         the performance observer task. The users of the Performance Timeline specification also do not expect
        //         this function to add to the entry buffer, instead queuing the observer task, then adding to the entry
        //         buffer separately.

        // OPTIMIZATION: The PerformanceObserver task delivers only what observers have buffered. An entry that no observer
        //               is interested in buffers nothing, so it doesn't queue the task. A document's initial visibility
        //               state entry, e.g., then doesn't queue a task for every new document.
        if interested_observers.is_empty() {
            return;
        }

        // 10. Queue the PerformanceObserver task with relevantGlobal as input.
        self.queue_the_performance_observer_task(vm);
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-queue-a-performanceentry
    // AD-HOC: This is a separate function because the users of this specification queues PerformanceObserver tasks and add
    //         to the entry buffer separately.
    pub(crate) fn add_performance_entry(
        &self,
        vm: &Vm,
        new_entry: &AnyPerformanceEntry,
        check_if_performance_buffer_is_full: bool,
    ) {
        // 6. Let tuple be the relevant performance entry tuple of entryType and relevantGlobal.
        self.with_relevant_performance_entry_tuple_mut(vm, &new_entry.entry_type(), |tuple| {
            // AD-HOC: We have a custom flag to always append to the buffer by default, as other performance specs do this by default
            //         (either they don't have a limit, or they check the limit themselves). This flag allows compatibility for specs
            //         that rely do and don't rely on this.
            let mut is_buffer_full = false;
            let mut should_add = true;

            if check_if_performance_buffer_is_full {
                // 7. Let isBufferFull be the return value of the determine if a performance entry buffer is full algorithm with tuple
                //    as input.
                is_buffer_full = tuple.is_full();

                // 8. Let shouldAdd be the result of should add entry with newEntry as input.
                should_add = new_entry.should_add_entry(None);
            }

            // 9. If isBufferFull is false and shouldAdd is true, append newEntry to tuple's performance entry buffer.
            if !is_buffer_full && should_add {
                tuple.performance_entry_buffer.push(*new_entry);
            }
        });
    }

    pub(crate) fn clear_performance_entry_buffer(&self, vm: &Vm, entry_type: &Utf16String) {
        self.with_relevant_performance_entry_tuple_mut(vm, entry_type, |tuple| tuple.performance_entry_buffer.clear());
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove_entries_from_performance_entry_buffer(
        &self,
        vm: &Vm,
        entry_type: &Utf16String,
        entry_name: &Utf16String,
    ) {
        self.with_relevant_performance_entry_tuple_mut(vm, entry_type, |tuple| {
            tuple
                .performance_entry_buffer
                .retain(|entry| entry.name() != *entry_name);
        });
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-filter-buffer-map-by-name-and-type
    pub(crate) fn filter_buffer_map_by_name_and_type<'vm>(
        &self,
        cx: &CallContext<'vm>,
        name: Option<&Utf16String>,
        r#type: Option<&Utf16String>,
    ) -> MarkedVec<'vm, AnyPerformanceEntry> {
        // 1. Let result be an initially empty list.
        let result = MarkedVec::new(cx.vm());

        // 2. Let map be the performance entry buffer map associated with the relevant global object of this.
        let map = self.performance_entry_buffer_map.borrow();

        // 3. Let tuple list be an empty list.
        // 4. If type is not null, append the result of getting the value of entry on map given type as key to tuple list.
        //    Otherwise, assign the result of get the values on map to tuple list.
        let tuple_list = map
            .iter()
            .filter(|tuple| r#type.is_none_or(|r#type| tuple.entry_type == *r#type));

        // 5. For each tuple in tuple list, run the following steps:
        for tuple in tuple_list {
            // 1. Let buffer be tuple's performance entry buffer.
            let buffer = &tuple.performance_entry_buffer;

            // 2. If tuple's availableFromTimeline is false, continue to the next tuple.
            if !tuple.available_from_timeline {
                continue;
            }

            // 3. Let entries be the result of running filter buffer by name and type with buffer, name and type as inputs.
            let entries = filter_buffer_by_name_and_type(cx, buffer, name, r#type);

            // 4. For each entry in entries, append entry to result.
            result.extend_from_slice(&entries.values());
        }

        // 6. Sort results's entries in chronological order with respect to startTime
        sort_in_chronological_order(&result);

        // 7. Return result.
        result
    }

    pub(crate) fn register_performance_observer(&self, vm: &Vm, observer: Ref<PerformanceObserver>) {
        if !self.has_registered_performance_observer(observer) {
            self.registered_performance_observer_objects
                .borrow_mut(vm)
                .push(observer);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn unregister_performance_observer(&self, vm: &Vm, observer: Ref<PerformanceObserver>) {
        self.registered_performance_observer_objects
            .borrow_mut(vm)
            .retain(|registered_observer| *registered_observer != observer);
    }

    pub(crate) fn has_registered_performance_observer(&self, observer: Ref<PerformanceObserver>) -> bool {
        self.registered_performance_observer_objects
            .borrow()
            .contains(&observer)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#dfn-queue-the-performanceobserver-task
    pub(crate) fn queue_the_performance_observer_task(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        // 1. If relevantGlobal's performance observer task queued flag is set, terminate these steps.
        if self.performance_observer_task_queued.get() {
            return;
        }

        // 2. Set relevantGlobal's performance observer task queued flag.
        self.performance_observer_task_queued.set(true);

        // 3. Queue a task that consists of running the following substeps. The task source for the queued task is the performance
        //    timeline task source.
        queue_a_global_task(
            vm,
            self.realm.global_object(),
            TaskSource::PerformanceTimeline,
            self.realm,
            |vm, realm| {
                with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(realm, || {
                    Self::of(vm, realm).run_performance_observer_task(vm);
                });
            },
        );
    }

    fn run_performance_observer_task(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        // 1. Unset performance observer task queued flag of relevantGlobal.
        self.performance_observer_task_queued.set(false);

        // 2. Let notifyList be a copy of relevantGlobal's list of registered performance observer objects.
        let notify_list = MarkedVec::new(vm);
        notify_list.extend_from_slice(&self.registered_performance_observer_objects.borrow());

        // 3. For each registered performance observer object registeredObserver in notifyList, run these steps:
        for registered_observer in notify_list.values().iter() {
            // 1. Let po be registeredObserver's observer.
            // 2. Let entries be a copy of po’s observer buffer.
            // 4. Empty po’s observer buffer.
            let entries = registered_observer.take_observer_buffer(vm);

            // 3. If entries is empty, return.
            // FIXME: Do they mean `continue`?
            if entries.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }

            // 5. Let observerEntryList be a new PerformanceObserverEntryList, with its entry list set to entries.
            let observer_entry_list = PerformanceObserverEntryList::create(vm, registered_observer.realm(), &entries);

            // 6. Let droppedEntriesCount be null.
            let mut dropped_entries_count = None;

            // 7. If po's requires dropped entries is set, perform the following steps:
            if registered_observer.requires_dropped_entries() {
                // 1. Set droppedEntriesCount to 0.
                let mut count = 0;

                // 2. For each PerformanceObserverInit item in registeredObserver's options list:
                let map = self.performance_entry_buffer_map.borrow();
                for item in registered_observer.options_list().iter() {
                    // 1. For each DOMString entryType that appears either as item's type or in item's entryTypes:
                    for r#type in item.r#type.iter().chain(item.entry_types.iter().flatten()) {
                        // 1. Let map be relevantGlobal's performance entry buffer map.
                        // 2. Let tuple be the result of getting the value of entry on map given entryType as key.
                        let tuple = Self::tuple_of(&map, r#type);

                        // 3. Increase droppedEntriesCount by tuple's dropped entries count.
                        count += tuple.dropped_entries_count;
                    }
                }
                dropped_entries_count = Some(count);

                // 3. Set po's requires dropped entries to false.
                registered_observer.unset_requires_dropped_entries();
            }

            // 8. Let callbackOptions be a PerformanceObserverCallbackOptions with its droppedEntriesCount set to
            //    droppedEntriesCount if droppedEntriesCount is not null, otherwise unset.
            // 9. Call po’s observer callback with observerEntryList as the first argument, with po as the second
            //    argument and as callback this value, and with callbackOptions as the third argument.
            //    If this throws an exception, report the exception.
            if let Err(throw) = PerformanceObserver::invoke_callback(
                *registered_observer,
                vm,
                observer_entry_list,
                dropped_entries_count,
            ) {
                report_an_exception(self.realm, throw.value());
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_resource_timing_buffer_size_limit(&self, value: u32) {
        self.resource_timing_buffer_size_limit.set(value);
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-add-a-performanceresourcetiming-entry
    pub(crate) fn add_resource_timing_entry(&self, vm: &Vm, new_entry: &AnyPerformanceEntry) {
        // 1. If can add resource timing entry returns true and resource timing buffer full event pending flag is false,
        //    run the following substeps:
        if self.can_add_resource_timing_entry() && !self.resource_timing_buffer_full_event_pending.get() {
            // a. Add new entry to the performance entry buffer.
            // b. Increase resource timing buffer current size by 1.
            self.add_performance_entry(vm, new_entry, false);

            // c. Return.
            return;
        }

        // 2. If resource timing buffer full event pending flag is false, run the following substeps:
        if !self.resource_timing_buffer_full_event_pending.get() {
            // a. Set resource timing buffer full event pending flag to true.
            self.resource_timing_buffer_full_event_pending.set(true);

            // b. Queue a task on the performance timeline task source to run fire a buffer full event.
            queue_a_task(vm, TaskSource::PerformanceTimeline, self.realm, |vm, realm| {
                with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(realm, || {
                    Self::of(vm, realm).fire_resource_timing_buffer_full_event(vm);
                });
            });
        }

        // 3. Add new entry to the resource timing secondary buffer.
        // 4. Increase resource timing secondary buffer current size by 1.
        self.resource_timing_secondary_buffer.borrow_mut(vm).push(*new_entry);
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-can-add-resource-timing-entry
    fn can_add_resource_timing_entry(&self) -> bool {
        // 1. If resource timing buffer current size is smaller than resource timing buffer size limit, return true.
        // 2. Return false.
        self.resource_timing_buffer_current_size() < self.resource_timing_buffer_size_limit.get() as usize
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-resource-timing-buffer-current-size
    fn resource_timing_buffer_current_size(&self) -> usize {
        // A resource timing buffer current size which is initially 0.
        self.with_relevant_performance_entry_tuple(&Utf16String::from_utf8("resource"), |tuple| {
            tuple.performance_entry_buffer.len()
        })
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-fire-a-buffer-full-event
    fn fire_resource_timing_buffer_full_event(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        // 1. While resource timing secondary buffer is not empty, run the following substeps:
        while !self.resource_timing_secondary_buffer.borrow().is_empty() {
            // 1. Let number of excess entries before be resource timing secondary buffer current size.
            let number_of_excess_entries_before = self.resource_timing_secondary_buffer.borrow().len();

            // 2. If can add resource timing entry returns false, then fire an event named resourcetimingbufferfull at the Performance object.
            if !self.can_add_resource_timing_entry() {
                let full_event = CppEvent::create(self.realm, "resourcetimingbufferfull", false, false, false);
                self.performance(vm).event_target().dispatch_event(&full_event);
            }

            // 3. Run copy secondary buffer.
            self.copy_resource_timing_secondary_buffer(vm);

            // 4. Let number of excess entries after be resource timing secondary buffer current size.
            let number_of_excess_entries_after = self.resource_timing_secondary_buffer.borrow().len();

            // 5. If number of excess entries before is lower than or equals number of excess entries after, then remove
            //    all entries from resource timing secondary buffer, set resource timing secondary buffer current size to
            //    0, and abort these steps.
            if number_of_excess_entries_before <= number_of_excess_entries_after {
                self.resource_timing_secondary_buffer.borrow_mut(vm).clear();
                break;
            }
        }

        // 2. Set resource timing buffer full event pending flag to false.
        self.resource_timing_buffer_full_event_pending.set(false);
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-copy-secondary-buffer
    fn copy_resource_timing_secondary_buffer(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        // 1. While resource timing secondary buffer is not empty and can add resource timing entry returns true,
        //    run the following substeps:
        while !self.resource_timing_secondary_buffer.borrow().is_empty() && self.can_add_resource_timing_entry() {
            // 1. Let entry be the oldest PerformanceResourceTiming in resource timing secondary buffer.
            // 2. Add entry to the end of performance entry buffer.
            // 3. Increment resource timing buffer current size by 1.
            // 4. Remove entry from resource timing secondary buffer.
            // 5. Decrement resource timing secondary buffer current size by 1.
            let mut secondary_buffer = self.resource_timing_secondary_buffer.borrow_mut(vm);
            let entry = secondary_buffer.remove(0);
            self.with_relevant_performance_entry_tuple_mut(vm, &Utf16String::from_utf8("resource"), |tuple| {
                tuple.performance_entry_buffer.push(entry);
            });
        }
    }
}

//! PermissionStatus, https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#permissionstatus-interface

use core::cell::Cell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::relevant_settings_object;
use crate::bindings::event_target::{CppEvent, CppEventTarget, GetTheParent};
use crate::bindings::global_object::window_from_global_object;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::promise::{TaskSource, queue_a_global_task};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::permissions::permissions::PermissionName;

use crate::permissions_api::permissions::{PermissionDescriptor, permission_query_algorithm, permission_state};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_html_window_or_worker_global_scope_register_permission_status(
        global_object: *mut c_void,
        status: *mut c_void,
    );
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dom-permissionstate
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum PermissionState {
    Granted,
    Denied,
    Prompt,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#permissionstatus-interface
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PermissionStatus {
    event_target: CppEventTarget,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,

    #[gc(untraced)]
    name: Utf16String,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    permission_name: PermissionName,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    state: Cell<PermissionState>,

    // https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-query
    #[gc(untraced)]
    query: PermissionDescriptor,
}

impl Wrappable for PermissionStatus {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.realm)
    }

    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event_target.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for PermissionStatus {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
}

impl PermissionStatus {
    // https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-create-a-permissionstatus
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, permission_desc: PermissionDescriptor) -> Ref<Self> {
        // 1. Let name be permissionDesc's name.
        let name = permission_desc.name.clone();

        // 2. Assert: The feature identified by name is supported by the user agent.
        let permission_name = PermissionName::from_name(&name).expect("the name is supported");

        // 3. Let status be a new instance of the permission result type identified by name:
        // FIXME: A permission result type is a PermissionStatus or one of its subtypes.
        // If unspecified, this defaults to PermissionStatus. No subtypes exist yet in Ladybird.
        // 1. Initialize status's [[query]] internal slot to permissionDesc.
        // 2. Initialize status's name to name.
        let status = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            event_target: CppEventTarget::new(),
            realm,
            name,
            permission_name,
            state: Cell::new(PermissionState::Prompt),
            query: permission_desc,
        });
        status.event_target.set_owner(status);

        // NB: The store tells every status when a permission changes, and the global keeps a status alive while it has a
        //     change listener.
        register_status(vm, status);
        // SAFETY: The global object and the EventTarget are live.
        unsafe {
            web_html_window_or_worker_global_scope_register_permission_status(
                realm.global_object().as_ptr().cast(),
                status.event_target.as_ptr(),
            );
        }

        // 4. Return status.
        status
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dom-permissionstatus-state
    pub(crate) fn state(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<PermissionState> {
        Ok(self.state.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_state(&self, state: PermissionState) {
        self.state.set(state);
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dom-permissionstatus-name
    pub(crate) fn name(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        Ok(self.name.clone())
    }

    pub(crate) fn query(&self) -> &PermissionDescriptor {
        &self.query
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#PermissionStatus-update
    pub(crate) fn update_from_store(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) {
        let global = this.realm.global_object();

        // 1. If this's relevant global object is a Window object, then:
        if let Some(window) = window_from_global_object(global) {
            // 1. Let document be status's relevant global object's associated Document.
            // 2. If document is null or document is not fully active, terminate this algorithm.
            if !window.associated_document().is_fully_active() {
                return;
            }
        }

        // NB: The store tells every status of a change, and only those whose state it moved run these steps.
        let settings = relevant_settings_object(global);
        if permission_state(this.permission_name, &settings) == this.state.get() {
            return;
        }

        // 2. Let query be status's [[query]] internal slot.
        let query = this.query();

        // 3. Run query's name's permission query algorithm, passing query and status.
        permission_query_algorithm(query, &this, &settings);

        // 4. Queue a task on the permissions task source to fire an event named change at status.
        queue_a_global_task(vm, global, TaskSource::Permissions, this, |_, this| {
            let event = CppEvent::create(this.realm, "change", false, false, false);
            this.event_target.dispatch_event(&event);
        });
    }
}

//! The statuses of the permission store, https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-permission-store

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};

use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, GcWeak, MarkedVec, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrapped};
use crate::permissions_api::permission_status::PermissionStatus;

thread_local! {
    static PERMISSION_STATUSES: RefCell<Vec<GcWeak<EmbedderCell<Wrapped<PermissionStatus>>>>> =
        const { RefCell::new(Vec::new()) };

    // The newest snapshot that the statuses of this agent have seen.
    static REVISION: Cell<Option<u64>> = const { Cell::new(None) };
}

pub(crate) fn register_status(vm: &Vm, status: Ref<PermissionStatus>) {
    PERMISSION_STATUSES.with_borrow_mut(|statuses| {
        // Pruning only when the vector would grow, and leaving it at most half full, keeps a registration amortized
        // constant time.
        if statuses.len() == statuses.capacity() {
            statuses.retain(|status| status.get().is_some());
            statuses.reserve(statuses.len());
        }
        statuses.push(GcWeak::new(vm.heap(), status));
    });
}

/// Reads the state of every status of the thread's agent again from the permission store, once the store has applied
/// the snapshot of the revision. Returns whether the statuses heard of a change.
pub(crate) fn update_statuses_of_this_agent(vm: &Vm, revision: u64, store_changed: bool) -> bool {
    // NB: The agent that got here first made the change, and the others still have to hear of it. An agent has heard of a
    //     revision only once its statuses have, which is not the case for one that it fetched without telling them.
    let is_unseen = REVISION.get().is_none_or(|seen| revision > seen);
    if is_unseen {
        REVISION.set(Some(revision));
    }
    if !store_changed && !is_unseen {
        return false;
    }

    // NB: Updating a status allocates, and a collection then could clear another status's weak reference, so every
    //     live status is rooted first.
    let statuses = MarkedVec::new(vm);
    PERMISSION_STATUSES.with_borrow_mut(|weak_statuses| {
        weak_statuses.retain(|status| status.get().is_some());
        for status in weak_statuses.iter().filter_map(GcWeak::get) {
            statuses.push(status);
        }
    });
    for status in statuses.values().iter() {
        PermissionStatus::update_from_store(*status, vm);
    }
    true
}

/// For an agent that goes away, whose statuses have to go with its heap.
pub(crate) fn forget_statuses_of_this_agent() {
    PERMISSION_STATUSES.with_borrow_mut(Vec::clear);
    REVISION.set(None);
}

//! Permissions, https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#permissions-interface

use core::cell::RefCell;
use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{
    EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, ErrorKind, ErrorType, Gc, Object, Throw, Trace, Value, Visitor, Vm,
};

#[cfg(web_idl_bindings)]
use crate::bindings::conversions::FromJs;
use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::{CppEnvironmentSettingsObject, relevant_settings_object};
use crate::bindings::global_object::window_from_global_object;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Wrappable, with_temporary_execution_context, wrap};
use crate::bindings::promise::{
    TaskSource, WebIdlPromise, exception_value, queue_a_global_task, reject_promise, resolve_promise,
};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::permissions::permissions::PermissionName;
use crate::permissions_api::permission_status::{PermissionState, PermissionStatus};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_permissions_api_permission_state(settings_object: *mut c_void, name: u8) -> u8;
    fn web_permissions_api_request_permission_to_use(
        settings_object: *mut c_void,
        name: u8,
        cell: *mut c_void,
        steps: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void, u8),
    );
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dom-permissiondescriptor
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct PermissionDescriptor {
    pub(crate) name: Utf16String,
}

impl PermissionName {
    pub(crate) fn from_name(name: &Utf16String) -> Option<Self> {
        if *name == "geolocation" {
            return Some(Self::Geolocation);
        }
        if *name == "microphone" {
            return Some(Self::Microphone);
        }
        if *name == "notifications" {
            return Some(Self::Notifications);
        }
        None
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-permission-state
pub(crate) fn permission_state(name: PermissionName, settings: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject) -> PermissionState {
    // SAFETY: The settings object is live.
    permission_state_from(unsafe { web_permissions_api_permission_state(settings.as_ptr(), name as u8) })
}

fn permission_state_from(state: u8) -> PermissionState {
    match state {
        0 => PermissionState::Granted,
        1 => PermissionState::Denied,
        2 => PermissionState::Prompt,
        _ => unreachable!("LibWeb returns a PermissionState"),
    }
}

/// Steps that run once with the state that requesting permission to use settled on.
trait DecisionSteps: Trace {
    fn run(&self, vm: &Vm, state: PermissionState);
}

struct CapturedDecisionSteps<C> {
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, C, PermissionState),
}

// SAFETY: The steps are a plain function, which holds no cells.
unsafe impl<C: Trace> Trace for CapturedDecisionSteps<C> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.captures.trace(visitor);
    }
}

impl<C: Trace + Clone + 'static> DecisionSteps for CapturedDecisionSteps<C> {
    fn run(&self, vm: &Vm, state: PermissionState) {
        (self.steps)(vm, self.captures.clone(), state);
    }
}

/// The cell that keeps the steps of a permission request and what they capture alive until the request settles.
struct PendingDecision(RefCell<Option<Box<dyn DecisionSteps>>>);

// SAFETY: The steps that have not run are all the cells this reaches.
unsafe impl Trace for PendingDecision {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        if let Some(steps) = &*self.0.borrow() {
            steps.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

static PENDING_DECISION_CLASS: EmbedderClass<PendingDecision> = EmbedderClass::new("PendingDecision");

impl EmbedderValue for PendingDecision {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &PENDING_DECISION_CLASS;
}

unsafe extern "C" fn run_pending_decision(vm: *mut c_void, cell: *mut c_void, state: u8) {
    // SAFETY: LibWeb passes the VM and the cell that request_permission_to_use() made, which it kept alive.
    let (vm, cell) = unsafe {
        (
            &*vm.cast::<Vm>(),
            PENDING_DECISION_CLASS
                .downcast(NonNull::new(cell).expect("LibWeb passes the cell"))
                .expect("LibWeb passes a PendingDecision"),
        )
    };
    // NB: The cell keeps what the steps capture alive while they run, and lets go of it once they have.
    cell.0
        .borrow()
        .as_ref()
        .expect("a permission request settles once")
        .run(vm, permission_state_from(state));
    cell.0.take();
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-request-permission-to-use
pub(crate) fn request_permission_to_use<C: Trace + Clone + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    name: PermissionName,
    settings: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, C, PermissionState),
) {
    let cell = PENDING_DECISION_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| {
        let steps: Box<dyn DecisionSteps> = Box::new(CapturedDecisionSteps { captures, steps });
        PendingDecision(RefCell::new(Some(steps)))
    });
    // SAFETY: The settings object and the cell are live.
    unsafe {
        web_permissions_api_request_permission_to_use(
            settings.as_ptr(),
            name as u8,
            cell.as_ptr().cast(),
            run_pending_decision,
        );
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#permissions-interface
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Permissions;

impl Wrappable for Permissions {}

fn convert_to_permission_descriptor(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> Result<PermissionDescriptor, Throw> {
    #[cfg(web_idl_bindings)]
    return PermissionDescriptor::from_js(vm, value);
    #[cfg(not(web_idl_bindings))]
    {
        let _ = (vm, value);
        unreachable!("converting to PermissionDescriptor requires the generated bindings")
    }
}

impl Permissions {
    // https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#query-method
    pub(crate) fn query(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        promise: WebIdlPromise,
        permission_desc: Gc<Object>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let relevant_realm = cx.realm();
        let relevant_global_object = relevant_realm.global_object();
        let current_realm = vm.current_realm().expect("query() runs in a realm");
        let current_global_object = current_realm.global_object();

        // 1. If this's relevant global object is a Window object, then:
        if window_from_global_object(relevant_global_object).is_some() {
            // 1. If the current settings object's associated Document is not fully active, return a promise rejected with an "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
            let window = window_from_global_object(current_global_object)
                .expect("the objects of a window are reachable only from windows");
            if !window.associated_document().is_fully_active() {
                let error = exception_value(
                    vm,
                    current_realm,
                    Exception::Dom(
                        "InvalidStateError",
                        Utf16String::from_ascii(b"The document is not fully active."),
                    ),
                );
                reject_promise(vm, promise, error);
                return Ok(());
            }
        }

        // 2. Let rootDesc be the object permissionDesc refers to, converted to an IDL value of type PermissionDescriptor.
        // 3. If the conversion throws an exception, return a promise rejected with that exception.
        let root_desc = match convert_to_permission_descriptor(vm, Value::from_object(permission_desc)) {
            Ok(root_desc) => root_desc,
            Err(throw) => {
                reject_promise(vm, promise, throw.value());
                return Ok(());
            }
        };

        // 4. If rootDesc["name"] is not supported, return a promise rejected with a TypeError.
        if PermissionName::from_name(&root_desc.name).is_none() {
            let Err(error) = vm.throw_completion::<()>(
                ErrorKind::TypeError,
                ErrorType::InvalidEnumerationValue,
                &[&root_desc.name, &"PermissionName"],
            ) else {
                unreachable!("throw_completion() throws")
            };
            reject_promise(vm, promise, error.value());
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 5. Let typedDescriptor be the object permissionDesc refers to, converted to an IDL value of rootDesc's name's permission descriptor type.
        // 6. If the conversion throws an exception, return a promise rejected with that exception.
        // FIXME: Support specific permission descriptor types. For now, we only support the base PermissionDescriptor.
        // AD-HOC: The base PermissionDescriptor isn't converted a second time: That would read name again, which could
        //         then name a permission that isn't supported.
        let typed_descriptor = root_desc;

        // 8. Return promise and continue in parallel:
        // FIXME: Continue in parallel.
        {
            // 1. Let status be create a PermissionStatus with typedDescriptor.
            let status = PermissionStatus::create(vm, relevant_realm, typed_descriptor);

            // 2. Let query be status's [[query]] internal slot.
            let query = status.query();

            // 3. Run query's name's permission query algorithm, passing query and status.
            // FIXME: For now, only the base PermissionDescriptor is supported so there is only one permission query algorithm.
            // NB: The status was registered for changes when it was created, so a change from here on reaches it.
            // AD-HOC: The state is read with this's relevant settings object, as the changes the status hears of later
            //         are, rather than with the current settings object that permission state defaults to.
            permission_query_algorithm(query, &status, &relevant_settings_object(relevant_global_object));

            // 4. Queue a global task on the permissions task source with this's relevant global object to resolve promise with status.
            queue_a_global_task(
                vm,
                relevant_global_object,
                TaskSource::Permissions,
                (relevant_realm, promise, status),
                |vm, (realm, promise, status)| {
                    with_temporary_execution_context(realm, || {
                        let wrapper = wrap(&CallContext::new(vm, realm), status);
                        resolve_promise(vm, promise, Value::from_object(wrapper));
                    });
                },
            );
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/permissions/#dfn-permission-query-algorithm
pub(crate) fn permission_query_algorithm(
    permission_desc: &PermissionDescriptor,
    status: &PermissionStatus,
    settings: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
) {
    // 1. Set status's state to permissionDesc's permission state.
    let name = PermissionName::from_name(&permission_desc.name).expect("the name is supported");
    status.set_state(permission_state(name, settings));
}

//! PictureInPictureEvent, https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#pictureinpictureevent

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Object, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::CppInterface;
use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::CppCell;
use crate::bindings::event_target::CppEvent;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::lent_string::LentUtf16FlyString;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_picture_in_picture_window_from_wrapper(wrapper: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_picture_in_picture_window_wrap(realm: *mut c_void, window: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
}

/// The dictionary PictureInPictureEventInit of PictureInPicture/PictureInPictureEvent.idl.
pub(crate) struct PictureInPictureEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) picture_in_picture_window: CppInterface,
}

// https://w3c.github.io/picture-in-picture/#pictureinpictureevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PictureInPictureEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    picture_in_picture_window: CppCell,
}

impl Wrappable for PictureInPictureEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

impl PictureInPictureEvent {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `window` must be a live PictureInPictureWindow.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: &EventInit,
        window: *mut c_void,
    ) -> Ref<PictureInPictureEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.bubbles,
            event_init.cancelable,
            event_init.composed,
        );
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a live PictureInPictureWindow.
        let picture_in_picture_window = unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(window) };
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| PictureInPictureEvent {
            event,
            picture_in_picture_window,
        });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: PictureInPictureEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<PictureInPictureEvent>> {
        // SAFETY: The bindings converted the member to a wrapper of a PictureInPictureWindow.
        let window = unsafe {
            web_picture_in_picture_window_from_wrapper(
                event_init_dict.picture_in_picture_window.wrapper().as_ptr().cast(),
            )
        };
        // SAFETY: LibWeb returns the live PictureInPictureWindow that the wrapper wraps.
        Ok(unsafe { Self::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &r#type, &event_init_dict.parent, window) })
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    pub(crate) fn picture_in_picture_window(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<CppInterface> {
        // SAFETY: The realm and the window are live, and LibWeb returns the wrapper of the window.
        let wrapper = unsafe {
            web_picture_in_picture_window_wrap(cx.realm().as_ptr().cast(), self.picture_in_picture_window.as_ptr())
        };
        // SAFETY: The wrapper is one of a PictureInPictureWindow.
        Ok(unsafe { CppInterface::from_wrapper(Gc::<Object>::from_non_null(NonNull::new(wrapper.cast()).unwrap())) })
    }
}

/// The Event of a new trusted PictureInPictureEvent in the realm, for the implementation to fire.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The VM, the realm and the window must be live. The type is lent for the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_picture_in_picture_event_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    r#type: LentUtf16FlyString<'_>,
    bubbles: bool,
    cancelable: bool,
    composed: bool,
    window: *mut c_void,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let event_init = EventInit {
        bubbles,
        cancelable,
        composed,
    };
    let r#type: Utf16String = r#type.to_utf16_fly_string().into();
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live PictureInPictureWindow.
    let event = unsafe { PictureInPictureEvent::create(vm, realm, &r#type, &event_init, window) };
    event.event().as_ptr()
}

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::CppCell;
use crate::bindings::promise::{pending_steps, run_pending_steps};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_platform_timer_create_single_shot(
        milliseconds: u64,
        cell: *mut c_void,
        steps: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void),
    ) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_platform_timer_stop(timer: *mut c_void);
}

#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CppTimer(CppCell);

impl CppTimer {
    pub(crate) fn create_single_shot<C: Trace + Clone + 'static>(
        vm: &Vm,
        milliseconds: u64,
        captures: C,
        steps: fn(&Vm, C),
    ) -> Self {
        let cell = pending_steps(vm, captures, steps);
        // SAFETY: The cell is live, and LibWeb returns a live timer.
        Self(unsafe {
            CppCell::from_raw(web_platform_timer_create_single_shot(
                milliseconds,
                cell,
                run_pending_steps,
            ))
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn stop(&self) {
        // SAFETY: The timer is live.
        unsafe { web_platform_timer_stop(self.0.as_ptr()) };
    }
}

//! https://w3c.github.io/requestidlecallback/#the-idledeadline-interface

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Wrappable, allocate, cell_into_abi};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_high_resolution_time_current_high_resolution_time(global_object: *mut c_void) -> f64;
    fn web_request_idle_callback_idle_deadline_deadline(global_object: *mut c_void) -> f64;
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct IdleDeadline {
    did_timeout: bool,
}

impl Wrappable for IdleDeadline {}

impl IdleDeadline {
    // https://w3c.github.io/requestidlecallback/#dom-idledeadline-timeremaining
    pub(crate) fn time_remaining(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        if self.did_timeout {
            return Ok(0.0);
        }

        // 1. Let now be a DOMHighResTimeStamp representing current high resolution time in milliseconds.
        let global = cx.realm().global_object();
        // SAFETY: The global object is live.
        let now = unsafe { web_high_resolution_time_current_high_resolution_time(global.as_ptr().cast()) };

        // 2. Let deadline be the result of calling IdleDeadline's get deadline time algorithm.
        // SAFETY: The global object is live.
        let deadline = unsafe { web_request_idle_callback_idle_deadline_deadline(global.as_ptr().cast()) };

        // 3. Let timeRemaining be deadline - now.
        let mut time_remaining = deadline - now;

        // 4. If timeRemaining is negative, set it to 0.
        if time_remaining < 0.0 {
            time_remaining = 0.0;
        }

        // 5. Return timeRemaining.
        // NB: Coarsened to milliseconds.
        Ok(time_remaining.ceil())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/requestidlecallback/#dom-idledeadline-didtimeout
    pub(crate) fn did_timeout(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.did_timeout)
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_idle_deadline_create(vm: &Vm, did_timeout: bool) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |_| IdleDeadline { did_timeout }))
}

//! PerformanceResourceTiming, https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, MarkedVec, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::ByteString;
use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::relevant_settings_object;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::lent_string::LentUtf16FlyString;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::fetch::infrastructure::fetch_timing_info::CppFetchTimingInfo;
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_entry::{AnyPerformanceEntry, PerformanceEntry};
use crate::performance_timeline::performance_timeline::PerformanceTimeline;

/// https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-renderblockingstatustype
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum RenderBlockingStatusType {
    Blocking,
    NonBlocking,
}

/// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-cache-state
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum CacheState {
    Local,
    Validated,
}

impl CacheState {
    pub(crate) fn from_abi(cache_state: u8) -> Option<Self> {
        match cache_state {
            0 => None,
            1 => Some(Self::Local),
            2 => Some(Self::Validated),
            _ => unreachable!("C++ passes a cache state"),
        }
    }
}

/// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#response-body-info
pub(crate) struct ResponseBodyInfo {
    pub(crate) encoded_size: u64,
    pub(crate) decoded_size: u64,
    pub(crate) content_type: Utf16String,
}

#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct ResponseBodyInfoAbi {
    encoded_size: u64,
    decoded_size: u64,
    content_type: usize,
}

impl ResponseBodyInfoAbi {
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The content type must be a raw string that C++ hands over.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn into_body_info(self) -> ResponseBodyInfo {
        ResponseBodyInfo {
            encoded_size: self.encoded_size,
            decoded_size: self.decoded_size,
            // SAFETY: The caller hands over the string.
            content_type: unsafe { Utf16String::from_raw_owned(self.content_type) },
        }
    }
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct PerformanceResourceTiming {
    entry: PerformanceEntry,
    initiator_type: Utf16String,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    timing_info: CppFetchTimingInfo,
    time_origin: f64,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    response_body_info: ResponseBodyInfo,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    cache_mode: Option<CacheState>,
    response_status: u16,
    delivery_type: Utf16String,
}

impl Wrappable for PerformanceResourceTiming {}

impl Inherits<PerformanceEntry> for PerformanceResourceTiming {
    fn parent(&self) -> &PerformanceEntry {
        &self.entry
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-convert-fetch-timestamp
pub(crate) fn convert_fetch_timestamp(time_stamp: f64, time_origin: f64) -> f64 {
    // 1. If ts is zero, return zero.
    if time_stamp == 0.0 {
        return 0.0;
    }

    // 2. Otherwise, return the relative high resolution coarse time given ts and global.
    time_stamp - time_origin
}

impl PerformanceResourceTiming {
    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dfn-setup-the-resource-timing-entry
    #[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "these are the inputs of the algorithm")]
    pub(crate) fn setup_the_resource_timing_entry(
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        initiator_type: Utf16String,
        requested_url: Utf16String,
        timing_info: CppFetchTimingInfo,
        cache_mode: Option<CacheState>,
        body_info: ResponseBodyInfo,
        response_status: u16,
        mut delivery_type: Utf16String,
    ) -> Self {
        // 1. Assert that cacheMode is the empty string, "local", or "validated".

        // 2. Let global be entry's relevant global object.
        // NB: The realm is that of global.
        let time_origin = relevant_settings_object(realm.global_object()).time_origin();

        // 3. Initialize entry given the result of converting timingInfo's start time given global, "resource",
        //    requestedURL, and the result of converting timingInfo's end time given global.
        let timing = timing_info.read();
        let entry = PerformanceEntry::initialize(
            convert_fetch_timestamp(timing.start_time, time_origin),
            Utf16String::from_utf8("resource"),
            requested_url,
            convert_fetch_timestamp(timing.end_time, time_origin),
        );

        // 4. Set entry's initiator type to initiatorType.
        // 5. Set entry's requested URL to requestedURL.
        // NB: The entry's name, which step 3 initialized, is its requested URL.
        // 6. Set entry's timing info to timingInfo.
        // 7. Set entry's resource info to bodyInfo.
        // 8. Set entry's cache mode to cacheMode.
        // 9. Set entry's response status to responseStatus.

        // 10. If deliveryType is the empty string and cacheMode is not, then set deliveryType to "cache".
        if delivery_type.is_empty() && cache_mode.is_some() {
            delivery_type = Utf16String::from_utf8("cache");
        }

        // 11. Set entry's delivery type to deliveryType.
        Self {
            entry,
            initiator_type,
            timing_info,
            time_origin,
            response_body_info: body_info,
            cache_mode,
            response_status,
            delivery_type,
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-initiatortype
    pub(crate) fn initiator_type(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The initiatorType getter steps are to return the initiator type for this.
        Ok(self.initiator_type.clone())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-deliverytype
    pub(crate) fn delivery_type(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The deliveryType getter steps are to return the delivery type for this.
        Ok(self.delivery_type.clone())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-nexthopprotocol
    pub(crate) fn next_hop_protocol(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<ByteString> {
        // The nextHopProtocol getter steps are to isomorphic decode this's timing info's final connection timing info's
        // ALPN negotiated protocol. See Recording connection timing info for more info.
        // NOTE: "final connection timing info" can be null, e.g. if this is the timing of a cross-origin resource and
        //       the Timing-Allow-Origin check fails. We return empty string in this case.
        Ok(ByteString::from_bytes(self.timing_info.alpn_negotiated_protocol()))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-workerstart
    pub(crate) fn worker_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The workerStart getter steps are to convert fetch timestamp for this's timing info's final service worker start
        // time and the relevant global object for this. See HTTP fetch for more info.
        Ok(convert_fetch_timestamp(
            self.timing_info.read().final_service_worker_start_time,
            self.time_origin,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-redirectstart
    pub(crate) fn redirect_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        if let AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceNavigationTiming(entry) = self.entry.object() {
            return Ok(entry.redirect_start());
        }
        Ok(self.resource_timing_redirect_start())
    }

    pub(crate) fn resource_timing_redirect_start(&self) -> f64 {
        // The redirectStart getter steps are to convert fetch timestamp for this's timing info's redirect start time and
        // the relevant global object for this. See HTTP-redirect fetch for more info.
        convert_fetch_timestamp(self.timing_info.read().redirect_start_time, self.time_origin)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-redirectend
    pub(crate) fn redirect_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        if let AnyPerformanceEntry::PerformanceNavigationTiming(entry) = self.entry.object() {
            return Ok(entry.redirect_end());
        }
        Ok(self.resource_timing_redirect_end())
    }

    pub(crate) fn resource_timing_redirect_end(&self) -> f64 {
        // The redirectEnd getter steps are to convert fetch timestamp for this's timing info's redirect end time and the
        // relevant global object for this. See HTTP-redirect fetch for more info.
        convert_fetch_timestamp(self.timing_info.read().redirect_end_time, self.time_origin)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-fetchstart
    pub(crate) fn fetch_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The fetchStart getter steps are to convert fetch timestamp for this's timing info's post-redirect start time and
        // the relevant global object for this. See HTTP fetch for more info.
        Ok(convert_fetch_timestamp(
            self.timing_info.read().post_redirect_start_time,
            self.time_origin,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-domainlookupstart
    pub(crate) fn domain_lookup_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The domainLookupStart getter steps are to convert fetch timestamp for this's timing info's final connection
        // timing info's domain lookup start time and the relevant global object for this. See Recording connection timing
        // info for more info.
        // NOTE: "final connection timing info" can be null, e.g. if this is the timing of a cross-origin resource and
        //       the Timing-Allow-Origin check fails. We return 0.0 in this case.
        let Some(connection_timing_info) = self.timing_info.read().final_connection_timing_info() else {
            return Ok(0.0);
        };

        Ok(convert_fetch_timestamp(
            connection_timing_info.domain_lookup_start_time,
            self.time_origin,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-domainlookupend
    pub(crate) fn domain_lookup_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The domainLookupEnd getter steps are to convert fetch timestamp for this's timing info's final connection timing
        // info's domain lookup end time and the relevant global object for this. See Recording connection timing info for
        // more info.
        // NOTE: "final connection timing info" can be null, e.g. if this is the timing of a cross-origin resource and
        //       the Timing-Allow-Origin check fails. We return 0.0 in this case.
        let Some(connection_timing_info) = self.timing_info.read().final_connection_timing_info() else {
            return Ok(0.0);
        };

            connection_timing_info.domain_lookup_end_time,
            self.time_origin,
        ))
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-connectstart
    pub(crate) fn connect_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The connectStart getter steps are to convert fetch timestamp for this's timing info's final connection timing
        // info's connection start time and the relevant global object for this. See Recording connection timing info for
        // more info.
        // NOTE: "final connection timing info" can be null, e.g. if this is the timing of a cross-origin resource and
        //       the Timing-Allow-Origin check fails. We return 0.0 in this case.
        let Some(connection_timing_info) = self.timing_info.read().final_connection_timing_info() else {

    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/resource-timing/#dom-performanceresourcetiming-connectend
    pub(crate) fn connect_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The connectEnd getter steps are to convert fetch timestamp for this's timing info's final connection timing
        // info's connection end time and the relevant global object for this. See Recording connection timing info for
        // more info.
        // NOTE: "final connection timing info" can be null, e.g. if this is the timing of a cross-origin resource and
        //       the Timing-Allow-Origin check fails. We return 0.0 in this case.
