//! Storage bottles, https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-bottle

use std::rc::Rc;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, Trace, Visitor, Vm};

use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::CppEnvironmentSettingsObject;
use crate::bindings::global_object::window_from_global_object;
pub(crate) use crate::storage_api::storage_area_mirror::QuotaExceeded;
use crate::storage_api::storage_area_mirror::{Requester, StorageAreaMirror, StorageEndpointType};
use crate::storage_api::storage_endpoint::StorageEndpoint;
use crate::storage_api::storage_key::{StorageKey, obtain_a_storage_key};

/// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-type
/// A storage type is "local" or "session".
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum StorageType {
    Local,
    Session,
}

/// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-bottle
///
/// NB: The bottle's map lives in the browser process; what a bottle here holds is this process's mirror of it, shared
///     with every other bottle in the process for the same area. Each bottle object is one storage proxy map over it.
pub(crate) struct StorageBottle {
    environment: CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
    environment_id: String,
    page_id: u64,
    // https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-bottle-quota
    // A storage bottle also has a quota, which is null or a number representing a conservative estimate of the total
    // amount of bytes it can hold. Null indicates the lack of a limit.
    quota: Option<u64>,
    mirror: Rc<StorageAreaMirror>,
}

// SAFETY: The settings object is the only cell a bottle holds.
unsafe impl Trace for StorageBottle {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.environment.trace(visitor);
    }
}

impl StorageBottle {
    fn create(environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject, endpoint: &StorageEndpoint, key: &StorageKey) -> Self {
        let window =
            window_from_global_object(environment.global_object()).expect("a storage bottle map is a Window's");
        let page_id = window.page_id();
        // Session storage is partitioned by the traversable, and a page's documents all belong to one traversable, so
        // a session bottle's mirror is found by its page as well as its storage key.
        let session_page = (endpoint.identifier == StorageEndpointType::SessionStorage).then_some(page_id);
        Self {
            environment: environment.clone(),
            environment_id: environment.id(),
            page_id,
            quota: endpoint.quota,
            mirror: StorageAreaMirror::obtain(endpoint.identifier, session_page, key, endpoint.quota),
        }
    }

    fn requester(&self) -> Requester<'_> {
        Requester {
            page_id: self.page_id,
            environment_id: &self.environment_id,
            environment: self.environment.as_ptr(),
        }
    }

    /// Loads the map now rather than on first access, so changes other processes make start arriving.
    pub(crate) fn connect(&self) {
        self.mirror.connect(&self.requester());
    }

    pub(crate) fn size(&self) -> usize {
        self.mirror.size(&self.requester())
    }

    /// https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-getting-the-keys
    pub(crate) fn keys(&self) -> Vec<Utf16String> {
        self.mirror.keys(&self.requester())
    }

    pub(crate) fn get(&self, key: &Utf16String) -> Option<Utf16String> {
        self.mirror.get(&self.requester(), key)
    }

    /// The value the key had, or the quota's refusal.
    pub(crate) fn set(
        &self,
        key: &Utf16String,
        value: &Utf16String,
        document_url: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<Utf16String>, QuotaExceeded> {
        self.mirror.set(&self.requester(), key, value, document_url)
    }

    pub(crate) fn remove(&self, key: &Utf16String, document_url: &str) {
        let _ = self.mirror.remove(&self.requester(), key, document_url);
    }

    pub(crate) fn clear(&self, document_url: &str) {
        self.mirror.clear(&self.requester(), document_url);
    }

    pub(crate) fn quota(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        self.quota
    }
}

type BottleMap = [Option<StorageBottle>; StorageEndpointType::COUNT];

// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-bucket
// A storage bucket is a place for storage endpoints to store data.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct StorageBucket {
    // A storage bucket has a bottle map of storage identifiers to storage bottles.
    bottle_map: BottleMap,
}

static STORAGE_BUCKET_CLASS: EmbedderClass<StorageBucket> = EmbedderClass::new("StorageBucket");

impl EmbedderValue for StorageBucket {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &STORAGE_BUCKET_CLASS;
}

impl StorageBucket {
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
        key: &StorageKey,
        storage_type: StorageType,
    ) -> Gc<EmbedderCell<Self>> {
        // 1. Let bucket be null.
        // 2. If type is "local", then set bucket to a new local storage bucket.
        // 3. Otherwise:
        //     1. Assert: type is "session".
        //     2. Set bucket to a new session storage bucket.
        STORAGE_BUCKET_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| {
            let mut bottle_map = core::array::from_fn(|_| None);

            // 4. For each endpoint of registered storage endpoints whose types contain type, set bucket’s bottle map[endpoint’s identifier] to a new storage bottle whose quota is endpoint’s quota.
            for endpoint in StorageEndpoint::registered_endpoints() {
                if endpoint.storage_type == storage_type {
                    bottle_map[endpoint.identifier as usize] = Some(StorageBottle::create(environment, &endpoint, key));
                }
            }

            // 5. Return bucket.
            StorageBucket { bottle_map }
        })
    }
}

/// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-storage-bottle-map
fn obtain_a_storage_bottle_map(
    storage_type: StorageType,
    environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
    identifier: StorageEndpointType,
) -> Option<StorageBottle> {
    // 1. Let shed be null.
    // 2. If type is "local", then set shed to the user agent’s storage shed.
    // 3. Otherwise:
    //     1. Assert: type is "session".
    //     2. Set shed to environment’s global object’s associated Document’s node navigable’s traversable navigable’s storage shed.
    // NB: Both sheds are kept by the browser process, in a StorageJar, which the bottle returned here mirrors. The
    //     bottle names environment, from which the browser process obtains the storage key itself.

    // 4. Let shelf be the result of running obtain a storage shelf, with shed, environment, and type.
    // 5. If shelf is failure, then return failure.
    let storage_key = obtain_a_storage_key(environment)?;

    // 6. Let bucket be shelf’s bucket map["default"].
    // 7. Let bottle be bucket’s bottle map[identifier].
    // NB: The bucket's bottle map holds a bottle for each registered storage endpoint whose types contain type, with
    //     that endpoint's quota.
    let endpoint = StorageEndpoint::registered_endpoints()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|endpoint| endpoint.identifier == identifier)
        .expect("the storage endpoint is registered");
    assert!(
        endpoint.storage_type == storage_type,
        "the endpoint supports the storage type"
    );

    // 8. Let proxyMap be a new storage proxy map whose backing map is bottle’s map.
    // 9. Append proxyMap to bottle’s proxy map reference set.
    // 10. Return proxyMap.
    Some(StorageBottle::create(environment, &endpoint, &storage_key))
}

/// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-local-storage-bottle-map
pub(crate) fn obtain_a_local_storage_bottle_map(
    environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
    identifier: StorageEndpointType,
) -> Option<StorageBottle> {
    // To obtain a local storage bottle map, given an environment settings object environment and storage identifier
    // identifier, return the result of running obtain a storage bottle map with "local", environment, and identifier.
    obtain_a_storage_bottle_map(StorageType::Local, environment, identifier)
}

/// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-session-storage-bottle-map
pub(crate) fn obtain_a_session_storage_bottle_map(
    environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
    identifier: StorageEndpointType,
) -> Option<StorageBottle> {
    // To obtain a session storage bottle map, given an environment settings object environment and storage identifier
    // identifier, return the result of running obtain a storage bottle map with "session", environment, and
    // identifier.
    obtain_a_storage_bottle_map(StorageType::Session, environment, identifier)
}

//! Storage endpoints, https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-endpoint

use core::ffi::c_void;

use crate::storage_api::storage_area_mirror::StorageEndpointType;
use crate::storage_api::storage_bottle::StorageType;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_storage_api_for_each_registered_endpoint(
        endpoints: *mut c_void,
        on_endpoint: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, u8, bool, bool, u64),
    );
}

// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-endpoint
//
// A storage endpoint is a local or session storage API that uses the infrastructure defined by this
// standard, most notably storage bottles, to keep track of its storage needs.
pub(crate) struct StorageEndpoint {
    // https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-endpoint-identifier
    // A storage endpoint has an identifier, which is a storage identifier.
    pub(crate) identifier: StorageEndpointType,

    // https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-endpoint-types
    // A storage endpoint also has types, which is a set of storage types.
    // NOTE: We do not implement this as a set as it is not necessary in the current implementation.
    pub(crate) storage_type: StorageType,

    // https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-endpoint-quota
    // A storage endpoint also has a quota, which is null or a number representing a recommended quota (in bytes) for each storage bottle corresponding to this storage endpoint.
    pub(crate) quota: Option<u64>,
}

unsafe extern "C" fn on_endpoint(
    endpoints: *mut c_void,
    identifier: u8,
    is_session: bool,
    has_quota: bool,
    quota: u64,
) {
    let identifier = match identifier {
        0 => StorageEndpointType::Caches,
        1 => StorageEndpointType::IndexedDB,
        2 => StorageEndpointType::LocalStorage,
        3 => StorageEndpointType::ServiceWorkerRegistrations,
        4 => StorageEndpointType::SessionStorage,
        _ => panic!("LibWeb passes a registered storage endpoint"),
    };
    // SAFETY: endpoints is the vector of the caller, which outlives the call.
    unsafe { &mut *endpoints.cast::<Vec<StorageEndpoint>>() }.push(StorageEndpoint {
        identifier,
        storage_type: if is_session {
            StorageType::Session
        } else {
            StorageType::Local
        },
        quota: has_quota.then_some(quota),
    });
}

impl StorageEndpoint {
    /// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#registered-storage-endpoints
    pub(crate) fn registered_endpoints() -> Vec<Self> {
        let mut endpoints = Vec::new();
        // SAFETY: The vector outlives the call, which copies the registered endpoints from LibWebCommon.
        unsafe { web_storage_api_for_each_registered_endpoint((&raw mut endpoints).cast(), on_endpoint) };
        endpoints
    }
}

//! Storage keys, https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-keys

#[cfg(not(test))]
use core::ffi::c_void;

#[cfg(not(test))]
use liburl_rust::FfiOrigin;
use liburl_rust::origin::Origin;

#[cfg(not(test))]
use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::CppEnvironmentSettingsObject;

#[cfg(not(test))]
unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_storage_api_obtain_a_storage_key(
        environment: *mut c_void,
        ctx: *mut c_void,
        on_origin: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const FfiOrigin),
    ) -> bool;
    fn web_storage_api_obtain_a_storage_key_for_non_storage_purposes(
        environment: *mut c_void,
        ctx: *mut c_void,
        on_origin: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const FfiOrigin),
    );
}

// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-keys
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct StorageKey {
    // A storage key is a tuple consisting of an origin (an origin). [HTML]
    // NOTE: This is expected to change; see Client-Side Storage Partitioning https://privacycg.github.io/storage-partitioning/.
    pub(crate) origin: Origin,
}

impl PartialEq for StorageKey {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        // To determine whether a storage key A equals storage key B, run these steps:
        // 1. If A’s origin is not same origin with B’s origin, then return false.
        // 2. Return true.
        self.origin.is_same_origin(&other.origin)
    }
}

#[cfg(not(test))]
unsafe extern "C" fn on_origin(ctx: *mut c_void, ffi_origin: *const FfiOrigin) {
    // SAFETY: ctx is the origin of the caller, and LibWeb lends the origin for the call.
    unsafe { *ctx.cast::<Option<Origin>>() = Some((*ffi_origin).to_origin()) };
}

/// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-storage-key
#[cfg(not(test))]
pub(crate) fn obtain_a_storage_key(environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject) -> Option<StorageKey> {
    let mut origin: Option<Origin> = None;
    // SAFETY: The environment settings object is live, and the origin outlives the call.
    unsafe { web_storage_api_obtain_a_storage_key(environment.as_ptr(), (&raw mut origin).cast(), on_origin) };
    origin.map(|origin| StorageKey { origin })
}

/// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-storage-key-for-non-storage-purposes
#[cfg(not(test))]
pub(crate) fn obtain_a_storage_key_for_non_storage_purposes(environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject) -> StorageKey {
    let mut origin: Option<Origin> = None;
    // SAFETY: The environment settings object is live, and the origin outlives the call.
    unsafe {
        web_storage_api_obtain_a_storage_key_for_non_storage_purposes(
            environment.as_ptr(),
            (&raw mut origin).cast(),
            on_origin,
        );
    }
    StorageKey {
        origin: origin.expect("LibWeb lends the origin of the storage key"),
    }
}

//! StorageManager, https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storagemanager

use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Object, PropertyKey, Realm, Trace, Value, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::ToJs;
use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::relevant_settings_object;
use crate::bindings::global_object::relevant_global_object;
use crate::bindings::interface::{
    Ref, Wrappable, allocate, create_dictionary_object, set_dictionary_member,
    with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks,
};
use crate::bindings::promise::{
    TaskSource, WebIdlPromise, create_promise, in_parallel, promise_realm, queue_a_global_task,
    reject_promise_with_exception, resolve_promise,
};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::storage_api::storage_shelf::obtain_a_local_storage_shelf;

/// The dictionary StorageEstimate of StorageAPI/StorageManager.idl.
pub(crate) struct StorageEstimate {
    pub(crate) usage: Option<u64>,
    pub(crate) quota: Option<u64>,
}

// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storagemanager
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct StorageManager {
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
}

impl Wrappable for StorageManager {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.realm)
    }
}

/// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#queue-a-storage-task
fn queue_a_storage_task<C: Trace + Copy + 'static>(vm: &Vm, global: Gc<Object>, captures: C, steps: fn(&Vm, C)) {
    // To queue a storage task given a global object global and a series of steps steps, queue a global task on the
    // storage task source with global and steps.
    queue_a_global_task(vm, global, TaskSource::Storage, captures, steps);
}

impl StorageManager {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Ref<StorageManager> {
        allocate(vm, |_| StorageManager { realm })
    }

    // https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-storagemanager-estimate
    pub(crate) fn estimate(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Let promise be a new promise.
        let promise = create_promise(vm, self.realm);

        // 2. Let global be this's relevant global object.
        let global = relevant_global_object(self);

        // 3. Let shelf be the result of running obtain a local storage shelf with this's relevant settings object.
        let shelf = obtain_a_local_storage_shelf(vm, &relevant_settings_object(global));

        // 4. If shelf is failure, then reject promise with a TypeError.
        let Some(shelf) = shelf else {
            reject_promise_with_exception(
                vm,
                promise,
                Exception::type_error("Failed to obtain local storage shelf."),
            );
            return Ok(promise);
        };

        // 5. Otherwise, run these steps in parallel:
        in_parallel(
            vm,
            self.realm,
            (promise, global, shelf),
            |vm, (promise, global, shelf)| {
                // 1. Let usage be storage usage for shelf.
                let usage = shelf.storage_usage();

                // 2. Let quota be storage quota for shelf.
                let quota = shelf.storage_quota();

                // 3. Let dictionary be a new StorageEstimate dictionary whose usage member is usage and quota member is quota.
                // 4. If there was an internal error while obtaining usage and quota, then queue a storage task with global to
                //    reject promise with a TypeError.
                // 5. Otherwise, queue a storage task with global to resolve promise with dictionary.
                queue_a_storage_task(vm, global, (promise, usage, quota), |vm, (promise, usage, quota)| {
                    let realm = promise_realm(promise);
                    with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(realm, || {
                        let dictionary = StorageEstimate {
                            usage: Some(usage),
                            quota: Some(quota),
                        };
                        resolve_promise(
                            vm,
                            promise,
                            storage_estimate_to_js(&CallContext::new(vm, realm), dictionary),
                        );
                    });
                });
            },
        );

        // 6. Return promise.
        Ok(promise)
    }
}

// NB: The generated conversion of StorageEstimate is only built with the bindings, so the dictionary is converted here.
fn storage_estimate_to_js(cx: &CallContext, dictionary: StorageEstimate) -> Value {
    let object = create_dictionary_object(cx);
    let members = [("usage", dictionary.usage), ("quota", dictionary.quota)];
    for (name, value) in members {
        if let Some(value) = value {
            let value = value.to_js(cx).expect("converting a number does not throw");
            set_dictionary_member(cx, object, &PropertyKey::from_utf8(name), value)
                .expect("defining a member of a new object does not throw");
        }
    }
    Value::from_object(object)
}

//! Storage shelves, https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-shelf

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::CppEnvironmentSettingsObject;
use crate::storage_api::storage_bottle::{StorageBucket, StorageType};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_storage_api_storage_usage(environment: *mut c_void) -> u64;
}

// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-shelf
// A storage shelf exists for each storage key within a storage shed. It holds a bucket map, which is a map of strings to storage buckets.
type BucketMap = Vec<(String, Gc<EmbedderCell<StorageBucket>>)>;

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct StorageShelf {
    environment: CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
    bucket_map: BucketMap,
}

static STORAGE_SHELF_CLASS: EmbedderClass<StorageShelf> = EmbedderClass::new("StorageShelf");

impl EmbedderValue for StorageShelf {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &STORAGE_SHELF_CLASS;
}

impl StorageShelf {
    // https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#create-a-storage-shelf
    fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
        key: &StorageKey,
        storage_type: StorageType,
    ) -> Gc<EmbedderCell<Self>> {
        // 1. Let shelf be a new storage shelf.
        STORAGE_SHELF_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| {
            // 2. Set shelf’s bucket map["default"] to the result of running create a storage bucket with type.
            let bucket_map = vec![(
                "default".to_owned(),
                StorageBucket::create(vm, environment, key, storage_type),
            )];
            // 3. Return shelf.
            StorageShelf {
                environment: environment.clone(),
                bucket_map,
            }
        })
    }

    /// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-usage
    pub(crate) fn storage_usage(&self) -> u64 {
        // The storage usage of a storage shelf is an implementation-defined rough estimate of the amount of bytes used
        // by it.
        // SAFETY: The environment settings object is live.
        unsafe { web_storage_api_storage_usage(self.environment.as_ptr()) }
    }

    /// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-quota
    #[allow(clippy::unused_self, reason = "every shelf has the same quota")]
    pub(crate) fn storage_quota(&self) -> u64 {
        // "The storage quota of a storage shelf is an implementation-defined conservative estimate of the total amount of
        //  bytes it can hold. This amount should be less than the total storage space on the device. It must not be a
        //  function of the available storage space on the device."
        // The bottles with a quota of their own (localStorage, sessionStorage) hold a few MiB each, and the rest (Cache
        // Storage, IndexedDB, service worker registrations) are unbounded, so the shelf reports the 10 GiB a site may
        // reasonably put in those. Nothing about the device goes into the figure.
        10 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
    }
}

/// https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-local-storage-shelf
pub(crate) fn obtain_a_local_storage_shelf(
    vm: &Vm,
    environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
) -> Option<Gc<EmbedderCell<StorageShelf>>> {
    // To obtain a local storage shelf, given an environment settings object environment, return the result of running
    // obtain a storage shelf with the user agent’s storage shed, environment, and "local".

    // FIXME: This should be implemented in a way that works for Workers.
    let key = obtain_a_storage_key(environment)?;

    // AD-HOC: The user agent's storage shed is kept by the browser process, in a StorageJar. This shelf is a transient
    //         helper for computing estimate()'s usage and quota — so a standalone shelf is functionally equivalent to
    //         the spec's requirement to obtain one from a shed.
    Some(StorageShelf::create(vm, environment, &key, StorageType::Local))
}

//! Miscellaneous abstract operations, https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#misc-abstract-ops

use libjs_rust::api::{ArrayBuffer, Gc, Must, Value, clone_array_buffer, construct, same_value};

use crate::bindings::conversions::{ArrayBufferView, BufferSource};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::html::structured_serialize::transfer_record::TransferRecord;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::{structured_deserialize_with_transfer, structured_serialize_with_transfer};

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#can-transfer-array-buffer
pub(crate) fn can_transfer_array_buffer(array_buffer: &ArrayBuffer) -> bool {
    // 1. Assert: O is an Object.
    // 2. Assert: O has an [[ArrayBufferData]] internal slot.

    // 3. If ! IsDetachedBuffer(O) is true, return false.
    if array_buffer.is_detached() {
        return false;
    }

    // 4. If SameValue(O.[[ArrayBufferDetachKey]], undefined) is false, return false.
    if !same_value(array_buffer.detach_key(), Value::UNDEFINED) {
        return false;
    }

    // 5. Return true.
    true
}

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#is-non-negative-number
pub(crate) fn is_non_negative_number(value: Value) -> bool {
    // 1. If v is not a Number, return false.
    if !value.is_number() {
        return false;
    }

    // 2. If v is NaN, return false.
    if value.is_nan() {
        return false;
    }

    // 3. If v < 0, return false.
    if value.as_f64() < 0.0 {
        return false;
    }

    // 4. Return true.
    true
}

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#transfer-array-buffer
pub(crate) fn transfer_array_buffer(cx: &CallContext, buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
    // 1. Assert: ! IsDetachedBuffer(O) is false.
    assert!(!buffer.is_detached());

    // 2. Let arrayBufferData be O.[[ArrayBufferData]].
    // 3. Let arrayBufferByteLength be O.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]].
    // 4. Perform ? DetachArrayBuffer(O).
    // NB: The data block is taken from the buffer as it is detached, so the transfer copies nothing.
    let block = buffer.detach_and_take_data_block(cx.vm())?;

    // 5. Return a new ArrayBuffer object, created in the current Realm, whose [[ArrayBufferData]] internal slot value
    //    is arrayBufferData and whose [[ArrayBufferByteLength]] internal slot value is arrayBufferByteLength.
    Ok(ArrayBuffer::create_from_data_block(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), block))
}

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-cloneasuint8array
pub(crate) fn clone_as_uint8_array(cx: &CallContext, view: ArrayBufferView) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    let vm = cx.vm();
    let extent = BufferSource::from(view).extent();

    // 1. Assert: O is an Object.
    // 2. Assert: O has an [[ViewedArrayBuffer]] internal slot.

    // 3. Assert: ! IsDetachedBuffer(O.[[ViewedArrayBuffer]]) is false.
    assert!(!extent.buffer.is_detached());

    // 4. Let buffer be ? CloneArrayBuffer(O.[[ViewedArrayBuffer]], O.[[ByteOffset]], O.[[ByteLength]], %ArrayBuffer%).
    let buffer = clone_array_buffer(vm, extent.buffer, extent.byte_offset, extent.byte_length)?;

    // 5. Let array be ! Construct(%Uint8Array%, « buffer »).
    let array = construct(
        vm,
        cx.realm().intrinsics().uint8_array_constructor(vm),
        &[Value::from_object(buffer)],
        None,
    )
    .must();

    // 6. Return array.
    Ok(Value::from_object(array))
}

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-structuredclone
pub(crate) fn structured_clone(cx: &CallContext, value: Value) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
    // 1. Let serialized be ? StructuredSerialize(v).
    // NB: StructuredSerializeWithTransfer with an empty transfer list is StructuredSerialize, in a record that Rust owns.
    let serialized = structured_serialize_with_transfer(cx, value, &[])?;

    // 2. Return ? StructuredDeserialize(serialized, the current Realm).
    let result = structured_deserialize_with_transfer(cx, serialized);
    TransferRecord::discard(serialized);
    Ok(result?.deserialized)
}

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-cancopydatablockbytes
pub(crate) fn can_copy_data_block_bytes_buffer(
    to_buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>,
    to_index: u64,
    from_buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>,
    from_index: u64,
    count: u64,
) -> bool {
    // 1. Assert: toBuffer is an Object.
    // 2. Assert: toBuffer has an [[ArrayBufferData]] internal slot.
    // 3. Assert: fromBuffer is an Object.
    // 4. Assert: fromBuffer has an [[ArrayBufferData]] internal slot.

    // 5. If toBuffer is fromBuffer, return false.
    if to_buffer == from_buffer {
        return false;
    }

    // 6. If ! IsDetachedBuffer(toBuffer) is true, return false.
    if to_buffer.is_detached() {
        return false;
    }

    // 7. If ! IsDetachedBuffer(fromBuffer) is true, return false.
    if from_buffer.is_detached() {
        return false;
    }

    // 8. If toIndex + count > toBuffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]], return false.
    if to_index + count > to_buffer.byte_length() as u64 {
        return false;
    }

    // 9. If fromIndex + count > fromBuffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]], return false.
    if from_index + count > from_buffer.byte_length() as u64 {
        return false;
    }

    // 10. Return true.
    true
}

//! The algorithms that streams and their controllers are set up with: one variant for each way the Streams Standard,
//! or a specification that sets a stream up, defines one, holding what its steps refer to. The steps of a variant are
//! next to the abstract operation that defines them.

use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, Gc, IteratorRecord, ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value};

use crate::bindings::callback::{CallbackFunction, PromiseCallbackFunction};
use crate::bindings::conversions::to_unrestricted_double;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, wrap};
use crate::bindings::promise::{WebIdlPromise, create_rejected_promise, create_resolved_promise};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::html::message_port::MessagePort;
use crate::streams::cpp::{CppPromiseAlgorithm, CppPromiseAlgorithmWithArgument};
use crate::streams::cross_realm_transform::{
    CrossRealmWritableState, cross_realm_transform_abort_algorithm, cross_realm_transform_cancel_algorithm,
    cross_realm_transform_close_algorithm, cross_realm_transform_pull_algorithm,
};
use crate::streams::generic_transform_stream::RustTransformSteps;
use crate::streams::readable_stream::{
    ReadableStream, readable_stream_from_iterable_cancel_algorithm, readable_stream_from_iterable_pull_algorithm,
};
use crate::streams::readable_stream_tee::{ByteTeeState, DefaultTeeState};
use crate::streams::transform_stream::{
    TransformStream, transform_stream_default_sink_abort_algorithm, transform_stream_default_sink_close_algorithm,
    transform_stream_default_sink_write_algorithm, transform_stream_default_source_cancel_algorithm,
    transform_stream_default_source_pull_algorithm,
};
use crate::streams::transform_stream_default_controller::{
    TransformStreamDefaultController, transform_stream_default_controller_enqueue,
};
use crate::streams::underlying_source::ReadableStreamController;
use crate::streams::writable_stream_default_controller::WritableStreamDefaultController;

/// A promise resolved with undefined in the realm of the context.
fn resolved_with_undefined(cx: &CallContext) -> WebIdlPromise {
    create_resolved_promise(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), Value::UNDEFINED)
}

/// The startAlgorithm of a stream, which its set-up runs once.
pub(crate) enum StartAlgorithm {
    /// An algorithm that returns undefined.
    ReturnsUndefined,
    /// An algorithm that returns the result of invoking `start` with argument list « controller » and callback this
    /// value `this_value`.
    Callback {
        start: CallbackFunction,
        this_value: Value,
        controller: Value,
    },
    /// An algorithm that returns the promise.
    ReturnsPromise(WebIdlPromise),
}

impl StartAlgorithm {
    pub(crate) fn run(self) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        match self {
            Self::ReturnsUndefined => Ok(Value::UNDEFINED),
            Self::Callback {
                start,
                this_value,
                controller,
            } => Ok(start.invoke(Some(this_value), &[controller])?),
            Self::ReturnsPromise(promise) => Ok(Value::from_object(promise.promise())),
        }
    }
}

/// The pullAlgorithm of a readable stream's controller, https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readablestreamdefaultcontroller-pullalgorithm
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum PullAlgorithm {
    /// An algorithm that returns a promise resolved with undefined.
    ReturnsResolvedUndefined,
    /// An algorithm that returns the result of invoking `pull` with argument list « controller » and callback this
    /// value `underlying_source`.
    Callback {
        pull: PromiseCallbackFunction,
        underlying_source: Value,
        controller: ReadableStreamController,
    },
    /// The pullAlgorithm of ReadableStreamFromIterable.
    FromIterable {
        stream: Ref<ReadableStream>,
        iterator_record: Gc<IteratorRecord>,
    },
    /// The pullAlgorithm of ReadableStreamDefaultTee.
    DefaultTee(Gc<EmbedderCell<DefaultTeeState>>),
    /// The pull1Algorithm or the pull2Algorithm of ReadableByteStreamTee.
    ByteTee {
        state: Gc<EmbedderCell<ByteTeeState>>,
        for_branch2: bool,
    },
    /// The pullAlgorithm of InitializeTransformStream.
    TransformStream(Ref<TransformStream>),
    /// The pullAlgorithm of SetUpCrossRealmTransformReadable.
    CrossRealm(Ref<MessagePort>),
    /// The pullAlgorithmWrapper of setting up a ReadableStream with byte reading support, given the pullAlgorithm that
    /// C++ set the stream up with, if any.
    WithByteReadingSupport(Option<CppPromiseAlgorithm>),
}

impl PullAlgorithm {
    /// Performs the algorithm, with the context of the realm of the stream.
    pub(crate) fn run(&self, cx: &CallContext) -> WebIdlPromise {
        match self {
            Self::ReturnsResolvedUndefined => resolved_with_undefined(cx),
            Self::Callback {
                pull,
                underlying_source,
                controller,
            } => pull.invoke(Some(*underlying_source), &[controller.to_js(cx)]),
            Self::FromIterable {
                stream,
                iterator_record,
            } => readable_stream_from_iterable_pull_algorithm(cx, *stream, *iterator_record),
            Self::DefaultTee(state) => DefaultTeeState::pull_algorithm(*state, cx),
            Self::ByteTee { state, for_branch2 } => {
                if *for_branch2 {
                    ByteTeeState::pull2_algorithm(*state, cx)
                } else {
                    ByteTeeState::pull1_algorithm(*state, cx)
                }
            }
            Self::TransformStream(stream) => transform_stream_default_source_pull_algorithm(cx, *stream),
            Self::CrossRealm(port) => cross_realm_transform_pull_algorithm(cx, *port),
            Self::WithByteReadingSupport(pull_algorithm) => {
                // 1. Let result be the result of running pullAlgorithm, if pullAlgorithm was given, or null otherwise.
                //    If this throws an exception e, return a promise rejected with e.
                // 2. If result is a Promise, then return result.
                if let Some(pull_algorithm) = pull_algorithm {
                    return pull_algorithm.call();
                }

                // 3. Return a promise resolved with undefined.
                resolved_with_undefined(cx)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The cancelAlgorithm of a readable stream's controller or of a TransformStreamDefaultController,
/// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readablestreamdefaultcontroller-cancelalgorithm
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum CancelAlgorithm {
    /// An algorithm that returns a promise resolved with undefined.
    ReturnsResolvedUndefined,
    /// An algorithm that takes an argument reason and returns the result of invoking `cancel` with argument list
    /// « reason » and callback this value `this_value`.
    Callback {
        cancel: PromiseCallbackFunction,
        this_value: Value,
    },
    /// The cancelAlgorithm of ReadableStreamFromIterable.
    FromIterable { iterator_record: Gc<IteratorRecord> },
    /// The cancel1Algorithm or the cancel2Algorithm of ReadableStreamDefaultTee.
    DefaultTee {
        state: Gc<EmbedderCell<DefaultTeeState>>,
        for_branch2: bool,
    },
    /// The cancel1Algorithm or the cancel2Algorithm of ReadableByteStreamTee.
    ByteTee {
        state: Gc<EmbedderCell<ByteTeeState>>,
        for_branch2: bool,
    },
    /// The cancelAlgorithm of InitializeTransformStream.
    TransformStream(Ref<TransformStream>),
    /// The cancelAlgorithm of SetUpCrossRealmTransformReadable.
    CrossRealm(Ref<MessagePort>),
    /// The cancelAlgorithmWrapper of setting up a ReadableStream with byte reading support or a TransformStream, given
    /// the cancelAlgorithm that C++ set the stream up with, if any.
    Wrapper(Option<CppPromiseAlgorithmWithArgument>),
}

impl CancelAlgorithm {
    /// Performs the algorithm given the reason, with the context of the realm of the stream.
    pub(crate) fn run(&self, cx: &CallContext, reason: Value) -> WebIdlPromise {
        match self {
            Self::ReturnsResolvedUndefined => resolved_with_undefined(cx),
            Self::Callback { cancel, this_value } => cancel.invoke(Some(*this_value), &[reason]),
            Self::FromIterable { iterator_record } => {
                readable_stream_from_iterable_cancel_algorithm(cx, *iterator_record, reason)
            }
            Self::DefaultTee { state, for_branch2 } => {
                if *for_branch2 {
                    DefaultTeeState::cancel2_algorithm(*state, cx, reason)
                } else {
                    DefaultTeeState::cancel1_algorithm(*state, cx, reason)
                }
            }
            Self::ByteTee { state, for_branch2 } => {
                if *for_branch2 {
                    ByteTeeState::cancel2_algorithm(*state, cx, reason)
                } else {
                    ByteTeeState::cancel1_algorithm(*state, cx, reason)
                }
            }
            Self::TransformStream(stream) => transform_stream_default_source_cancel_algorithm(cx, *stream, reason),
            Self::CrossRealm(port) => cross_realm_transform_cancel_algorithm(cx, *port, reason),
            Self::Wrapper(cancel_algorithm) => {
                // 1. Let result be the result of running cancelAlgorithm given reason, if cancelAlgorithm was given,
                //    or null otherwise. If this throws an exception e, return a promise rejected with e.
                // 2. If result is a Promise, then return result.
                if let Some(cancel_algorithm) = cancel_algorithm {
                    return cancel_algorithm.call(reason);
                }

                // 3. Return a promise resolved with undefined.
                resolved_with_undefined(cx)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The strategySizeAlgorithm of a controller, https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readablestreamdefaultcontroller-strategysizealgorithm
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum SizeAlgorithm {
    /// An algorithm that returns 1.
    ReturnsOne,
    /// An algorithm that returns the result of invoking strategy["size"] with argument list « chunk ».
    Strategy(CallbackFunction),
}

impl SizeAlgorithm {
    pub(crate) fn run(&self, cx: &CallContext, chunk: Value) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        match self {
            Self::ReturnsOne => Ok(Value::from_i32(1)),
            Self::Strategy(size) => {
                let size = size.invoke(None, &[chunk])?;
                Ok(Value::from_f64(to_unrestricted_double(cx.vm(), size)?))
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The writeAlgorithm of a WritableStreamDefaultController, https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#writablestreamdefaultcontroller-writealgorithm
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]

    /// An algorithm that returns a promise resolved with undefined.
    ReturnsResolvedUndefined,
    /// An algorithm that takes an argument chunk and returns the result of invoking `write` with argument list
    /// « chunk, controller » and callback this value `underlying_sink`.
    Callback {
        write: PromiseCallbackFunction,
        underlying_sink: Value,
        controller: Ref<WritableStreamDefaultController>,

            Self::ReturnsResolvedUndefined => resolved_with_undefined(cx),

            Self::CrossRealm(state) => CrossRealmWritableState::write_algorithm(*state, cx, chunk),
            Self::CppWrapper(write_algorithm) => write_algorithm.call(chunk),
        }
    }

/// The transformAlgorithm of a TransformStreamDefaultController, https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#transformstreamdefaultcontroller-transformalgorithm
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum TransformAlgorithm {
    /// An algorithm that takes an argument chunk and returns the result of invoking `transform` with argument list
    /// « chunk, controller » and callback this value `transformer`.
    Callback {
        transform: PromiseCallbackFunction,
        transformer: Value,
        controller: Ref<TransformStreamDefaultController>,
    },
    /// The transformAlgorithm of SetUpTransformStreamDefaultControllerFromTransformer for a transformer without a
    /// transform member, which enqueues the chunk.
    Enqueue(Ref<TransformStreamDefaultController>),
    /// The transformAlgorithmWrapper of setting up a TransformStream, given the transformAlgorithm that C++ set the
    /// stream up with.
    CppWrapper(CppPromiseAlgorithmWithArgument),
    /// The transformAlgorithmWrapper of setting up a TransformStream, given steps of an implementation in Rust.
    RustWrapper(RustTransformSteps),
}

impl TransformAlgorithm {
    /// Performs the algorithm given the chunk, with the context of the realm of the stream.
    pub(crate) fn run(&self, cx: &CallContext, chunk: Value) -> WebIdlPromise {
        match self {
            Self::Callback {
                transform,
                transformer,
                controller,
            } => {
                let controller = Value::from_object(wrap(cx, *controller));
                transform.invoke(Some(*transformer), &[chunk, controller])
            }
            Self::Enqueue(controller) => {
                // 1. Let result be TransformStreamDefaultControllerEnqueue(controller, chunk).
                // 2. If result is an abrupt completion, return a promise rejected with result.[[Value]].
                if let Err(exception) = transform_stream_default_controller_enqueue(cx, *controller, chunk) {
                    let reason = crate::bindings::promise::exception_value(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), exception);
                    return create_rejected_promise(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), reason);
                }

                // 3. Otherwise, return a promise resolved with undefined.
                resolved_with_undefined(cx)
            }
            // 1. Let result be the result of running transformAlgorithm given chunk. If this throws an exception e,
            //    return a promise rejected with e.
            // 2. If result is a Promise, then return result.
            Self::CppWrapper(transform_algorithm) => transform_algorithm.call(chunk),
            Self::RustWrapper(steps) => steps.transform(cx, chunk),
        }
    }
}

/// The flushAlgorithm of a TransformStreamDefaultController, https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#transformstreamdefaultcontroller-flushalgorithm
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum FlushAlgorithm {
    /// An algorithm that returns a promise resolved with undefined.
    ReturnsResolvedUndefined,
    /// An algorithm that returns the result of invoking `flush` with argument list « controller » and callback this
    /// value `transformer`.
    Callback {
        flush: PromiseCallbackFunction,
        transformer: Value,
        controller: Ref<TransformStreamDefaultController>,
    },
    /// The flushAlgorithmWrapper of setting up a TransformStream, given the flushAlgorithm that C++ set the stream up
    /// with, if any.
    CppWrapper(Option<CppPromiseAlgorithm>),
    /// The flushAlgorithmWrapper of setting up a TransformStream, given steps of an implementation in Rust.
    RustWrapper(RustTransformSteps),
}

impl FlushAlgorithm {
    /// Performs the algorithm, with the context of the realm of the stream.
    pub(crate) fn run(&self, cx: &CallContext) -> WebIdlPromise {
        match self {
            Self::ReturnsResolvedUndefined => resolved_with_undefined(cx),
            Self::Callback {
                flush,
                transformer,
                controller,
            } => {
                let controller = Value::from_object(wrap(cx, *controller));
                flush.invoke(Some(*transformer), &[controller])
            }
            Self::CppWrapper(flush_algorithm) => {
                // 1. Let result be the result of running flushAlgorithm, if flushAlgorithm was given, or null
                //    otherwise. If this throws an exception e, return a promise rejected with e.
                // 2. If result is a Promise, then return result.
                if let Some(flush_algorithm) = flush_algorithm {
                    return flush_algorithm.call();
                }

                // 3. Return a promise resolved with undefined.
                resolved_with_undefined(cx)
            }
            Self::RustWrapper(steps) => steps.flush(cx),
        }
    }
}

//! ByteLengthQueuingStrategy, https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#blqs-class

use libjs_rust::api::{
    FunctionObject, Gc, PropertyKey, RawNativeFunction, ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value, Vm, raw_native,
};

use crate::bindings::interface::Wrappable;
use crate::bindings::realm_data::realm_data;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::streams::queuing_strategy_init::QueuingStrategyInit;

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct ByteLengthQueuingStrategy {
    high_water_mark: f64,
}

impl Wrappable for ByteLengthQueuingStrategy {}

#[expect(
    clippy::unnecessary_wraps,
    reason = "the bindings call every method of an implementation for its WebIDL result, whether or not it can fail"
)]
impl ByteLengthQueuingStrategy {
    // https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#blqs-constructor
    pub(crate) fn construct(_: &mut CallContext, init: QueuingStrategyInit) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Set this.[[highWaterMark]] to init["highWaterMark"].
        Ok(Self {
            high_water_mark: init.high_water_mark,
        })
    }

    // https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#blqs-high-water-mark
    pub(crate) fn high_water_mark(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // The highWaterMark getter steps are:
        // 1. Return this.[[highWaterMark]].
        Ok(self.high_water_mark)
    }

    // https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#blqs-size
    pub(crate) fn size(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<FunctionObject>> {
        // 1. Return this's relevant global object's byte length queuing strategy size function.
        Ok(byte_length_queuing_strategy_size_function(cx))
    }
}

/// The byte length queuing strategy size function of the global object of the realm of the call context,
/// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#byte-length-queuing-strategy-size-function, which the first use in the realm
/// creates.
fn byte_length_queuing_strategy_size_function(cx: &CallContext) -> Gc<FunctionObject> {
    let data = realm_data(cx.vm(), cx.realm());
    if let Some(function) = data.byte_length_queuing_strategy_size_function.get() {
        return function;
    }

    // 1. Let steps be the following steps, given chunk:
    fn steps(vm: &Vm) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        let chunk = vm.argument(0);

        // 1. Return ? GetV(chunk, "byteLength").
        chunk.get(vm, &vm.names.byteLength)
    }

    // 2. Let F be ! CreateBuiltinFunction(steps, 1, "size", « », globalObject's relevant Realm).
    let function = RawNativeFunction::create(
        cx.vm(),
        raw_native!(steps),
        1,
        &PropertyKey::from_utf8("size"),
        Some(cx.realm()),
        None,
        None,
    );

    // 3. Set globalObject's byte length queuing strategy size function to a Function that represents a reference
    //    to F, with callback context equal to globalObject's relevant settings object.
    let function: Gc<FunctionObject> = function.upcast();
    data.byte_length_queuing_strategy_size_function.set(Some(function));
    function
}

//! The cells of LibWeb's C++ code that streams hold: the algorithms that C++ sets a stream up with, and the read
//! requests that C++ reads a stream with, which are defined in Streams/ReadableStream.cpp.

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Value};

use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::{CppCell, LentCppCell, cpp_class};
use crate::bindings::promise::{WebIdlPromise, promise_from_abi};

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// Calls a GC::Function<GC::Ref<WebIDL::Promise>()>.
    fn web_streams_call_promise_algorithm(function: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;

    /// Calls a GC::Function<GC::Ref<WebIDL::Promise>(JS::Value)>.
    fn web_streams_call_promise_algorithm_with_argument(function: *mut c_void, argument: u64) -> *mut c_void;

    /// Performs the chunk steps of a Streams::ReadRequest.
    fn web_streams_read_request_chunk_steps(read_request: *mut c_void, chunk: u64);

    /// Performs the close steps of a Streams::ReadRequest.
    fn web_streams_read_request_close_steps(read_request: *mut c_void);

    /// Performs the error steps of a Streams::ReadRequest.
    fn web_streams_read_request_error_steps(read_request: *mut c_void, error: u64);

    /// Calls a GC::Function<void(ByteBuffer)> with a copy of the bytes.
    fn web_streams_call_bytes_steps(function: *mut c_void, bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>);

    /// Calls a GC::Function<void(JS::Value)>.
    fn web_streams_call_value_steps(function: *mut c_void, value: u64);
}

/// A promise-returning algorithm with no arguments that C++ set a stream up with, a pullAlgorithm or a flushAlgorithm.
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CppPromiseAlgorithm(CppCell);

impl CppPromiseAlgorithm {
    pub(crate) fn from_lent(cell: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::PromiseAlgorithm>) -> Self {
        Self(CppCell::from_lent(cell))
    }

    pub(crate) fn call(&self) -> WebIdlPromise {
        // SAFETY: The cell is a live GC::Function<GC::Ref<WebIDL::Promise>()>, which returns a live promise.
        unsafe { promise_from_abi(web_streams_call_promise_algorithm(self.0.as_ptr())) }
    }
}

/// A promise-returning algorithm with an argument that C++ set a stream up with, a cancelAlgorithm or a
/// transformAlgorithm.
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CppPromiseAlgorithmWithArgument(CppCell);

impl CppPromiseAlgorithmWithArgument {
    pub(crate) fn from_lent(cell: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::PromiseAlgorithmWithArgument>) -> Self {
        Self(CppCell::from_lent(cell))
    }

    pub(crate) fn call(&self, argument: Value) -> WebIdlPromise {
        // SAFETY: The cell is a live GC::Function<GC::Ref<WebIDL::Promise>(JS::Value)>, which returns a live promise.
        unsafe {
            promise_from_abi(web_streams_call_promise_algorithm_with_argument(
                self.0.as_ptr(),
                argument.to_raw(),
            ))
        }
    }
}

//! Transferable streams, https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#transferrable-streams, which MessagePorts carry.

use core::cell::Cell;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, Must, NativeFunction, Object, PrimitiveString, PropertyKey, Realm,
    Trace, Value, Vm,
};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, allocate, implementation_of, wrap};
use crate::bindings::promise::{
    NativeSteps, WebIdlPromise, create_promise, create_rejected_promise_from_exception, create_resolved_promise,
    exception_value, reject_promise_with_exception, resolve_promise, upon_fulfillment,
};
use crate::bindings::structured_data::{TransferDataReader, TransferDataWriter};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, MustNotThrow, WebIdlResult};
use crate::html::message_event::MessageEvent;
use crate::html::message_port::MessagePort;
use crate::streams::algorithms::{
    AbortAlgorithm, CancelAlgorithm, CloseAlgorithm, PullAlgorithm, SizeAlgorithm, StartAlgorithm, WriteAlgorithm,
};

use crate::streams::readable_stream_default_controller::{
    ReadableStreamDefaultController, readable_stream_default_controller_close,
    readable_stream_default_controller_enqueue, readable_stream_default_controller_error,
    set_up_readable_stream_default_controller,
};
use crate::streams::writable_stream::{WritableStream, initialize_writable_stream};
use crate::streams::writable_stream_default_controller::{
    WritableStreamDefaultController, set_up_writable_stream_default_controller,
    writable_stream_default_controller_error_if_needed,
};

/// The steps of a port's message event handler, given the state of the transform and the data of the message.
type MessageSteps<C> = fn(&CallContext, C, Value);

/// The steps of a port's messageerror event handler, given the state of the transform.
type MessageErrorSteps<C> = fn(&CallContext, C);

/// Adds the handlers for the port's message and messageerror events, which are given the state.
fn add_handlers<C: Trace + Copy + 'static>(
    cx: &CallContext,
    port: Ref<MessagePort>,
    state: C,
    on_message: MessageSteps<C>,
    on_message_error: MessageErrorSteps<C>,
) {
    let realm = cx.realm();
    let on_message = NativeFunction::create(
        cx.vm(),
        NativeSteps {
            captures: (state, realm),
            steps: on_message,
        },
        |vm: &Vm, function: &NativeSteps<(C, Gc<Realm>), MessageSteps<C>>| {
            let (state, realm) = function.captures;
            // NB: The port's message event handler is called with a MessageEvent.
            let data = implementation_of::<MessageEvent>(vm.argument(0).as_object()).data_value();
            (function.steps)(&CallContext::new(vm, realm), state, data);
            Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
        },
        1,
        &PropertyKey::from_utf8(""),
        Some(realm),
        None,
        None,
    );
    let on_message_error = NativeFunction::create(
        cx.vm(),
        NativeSteps {
            captures: (state, realm),
            steps: on_message_error,
        },
        |vm: &Vm, function: &NativeSteps<(C, Gc<Realm>), MessageErrorSteps<C>>| {
            let (state, realm) = function.captures;
            (function.steps)(&CallContext::new(vm, realm), state);
            Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
        },
        1,
        &PropertyKey::from_utf8(""),
        Some(realm),
        None,
        None,
    );
    port.event_target()
        .add_event_listener(cx, "message", on_message.as_function_object_gc());
    port.event_target()
        .add_event_listener(cx, "messageerror", on_message_error.as_function_object_gc());
}

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-packandpostmessage
fn pack_and_post_message(cx: &CallContext, port: Ref<MessagePort>, r#type: &str, value: Value) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
    let vm = cx.vm();

    // 1. Let message be OrdinaryObjectCreate(null).
    let message = Object::create(vm, cx.realm(), None);

    // 2. Perform ! CreateDataProperty(message, "type", type).
    let r#type = Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create_from_ascii(vm, r#type.as_bytes()));
    message
        .create_data_property(vm, &vm.names.type_, r#type, None, None)
        .must();

    // 3. Perform ! CreateDataProperty(message, "value", value).
    message
        .create_data_property(vm, &vm.names.value, value, None, None)
        .must();

    // 4. Let targetPort be the port with which port is entangled, if any; otherwise let it be null.
    let target_port = port.entangled_port();

    // 5. Let options be «[ "transfer" → « » ]».
    // 6. Run the message port post message steps providing targetPort, message, and options.
    MessagePort::message_port_post_message_steps(port, cx, target_port, Value::from_object(message), &[])
}

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-packandpostmessagehandlingerror
fn pack_and_post_message_handling_error(
    cx: &CallContext,
    port: Ref<MessagePort>,
    r#type: &str,
    value: Value,
) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
    // 1. Let result be PackAndPostMessage(port, type, value).
    let result = pack_and_post_message(cx, port, r#type, value);

    // 2. If result is an abrupt completion,
    let Err(exception) = result else {
        // 3. Return result as a completion record.
        return Ok(());
    };
    let error = exception_value(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), exception);

    // 1. Perform ! CrossRealmTransformSendError(port, result.[[Value]]).
    cross_realm_transform_send_error(cx, port, error);

    // 3. Return result as a completion record.
    Err(Exception::Thrown(libjs_rust::api::Throw::new(error)))
}

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-crossrealmtransformsenderror
fn cross_realm_transform_send_error(cx: &CallContext, port: Ref<MessagePort>, error: Value) {
    // 1. Perform PackAndPostMessage(port, "error", error), discarding the result.
    let _ = pack_and_post_message(cx, port, "error", error);
}

/// The pullAlgorithm of SetUpCrossRealmTransformReadable.
pub(crate) fn cross_realm_transform_pull_algorithm(cx: &CallContext, port: Ref<MessagePort>) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Perform ! PackAndPostMessage(port, "pull", undefined).
    pack_and_post_message(cx, port, "pull", Value::UNDEFINED).must();

    // 2. Return a promise resolved with undefined.
    create_resolved_promise(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), Value::UNDEFINED)
}

/// The cancelAlgorithm of SetUpCrossRealmTransformReadable, and the abortAlgorithm of
/// SetUpCrossRealmTransformWritable.
pub(crate) fn cross_realm_transform_cancel_algorithm(
    cx: &CallContext,
    port: Ref<MessagePort>,
    reason: Value,
) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Let result be PackAndPostMessageHandlingError(port, "error", reason).
    let result = pack_and_post_message_handling_error(cx, port, "error", reason);

    // 2. Disentangle port.
    port.disentangle();

    // 3. If result is an abrupt completion, return a promise rejected with result.[[Value]].
    if let Err(exception) = result {
        return create_rejected_promise_from_exception(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), exception);
    }

    // 4. Otherwise, return a promise resolved with undefined.
    create_resolved_promise(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), Value::UNDEFINED)
}

/// The closeAlgorithm of SetUpCrossRealmTransformWritable.
pub(crate) fn cross_realm_transform_close_algorithm(cx: &CallContext, port: Ref<MessagePort>) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Perform ! PackAndPostMessage(port, "close", undefined).
    pack_and_post_message(cx, port, "close", Value::UNDEFINED).must();

    // 2. Disentangle port.
    port.disentangle();

    // 3. Return a promise resolved with undefined.
    create_resolved_promise(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), Value::UNDEFINED)
}

/// The abortAlgorithm of SetUpCrossRealmTransformWritable.
pub(crate) fn cross_realm_transform_abort_algorithm(
    cx: &CallContext,
    port: Ref<MessagePort>,
    reason: Value,
) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Let result be PackAndPostMessageHandlingError(port, "error", reason).
    // 2. Disentangle port.
    // 3. If result is an abrupt completion, return a promise rejected with result.[[Value]].
    // 4. Otherwise, return a promise resolved with undefined.
    cross_realm_transform_cancel_algorithm(cx, port, reason)
}

/// The type and the value of a message that a cross-realm transform received, ! Get(data, "type") and
/// ! Get(data, "value").
fn type_and_value_of_message(vm: &Vm, data: Value) -> (Gc<PrimitiveString>, Value) {
    // 2. Assert: data is an Object.
    assert!(data.is_object());
    let data = data.as_object();

    // 3. Let type be ! Get(data, "type").
    let r#type = data.get(vm, &vm.names.type_).must();

    // 4. Let value be ! Get(data, "value").
    let value = data.get(vm, &vm.names.value).must();

    // 5. Assert: type is a String.
    assert!(r#type.is_string());
    (r#type.as_string(), value)
}

/// A new "DataCloneError" DOMException, which a cross-realm transform errors with when a message cannot be received.
fn data_clone_error(cx: &CallContext) -> Value {
    exception_value(
        cx.vm(),
        cx.realm(),
        Exception::Dom(
            "DataCloneError",
            ak::Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Unable to transfer stream"),
        ),
    )
}

/// The state that the handlers and the algorithms of a cross-realm transform share.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct ReadableHandlerState {
    port: Ref<MessagePort>,
    controller: Ref<ReadableStreamDefaultController>,
}

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-setupcrossrealmtransformreadable
pub(crate) fn set_up_cross_realm_transform_readable(
    cx: &CallContext,
    stream: Ref<ReadableStream>,
    port: Ref<MessagePort>,
) {
    stream.set_realm(cx.realm());

    // 1. Perform ! InitializeReadableStream(stream).
    initialize_readable_stream(stream);

    // 2. Let controller be a new ReadableStreamDefaultController.
    let controller = allocate(cx.vm(), ReadableStreamDefaultController::new);
    let state = ReadableHandlerState { port, controller };

    // 3. Add a handler for port’s message event with the following steps:
    fn on_message(cx: &CallContext, state: ReadableHandlerState, data: Value) {
        let port = state.port;
        let controller = state.controller;

        // 1. Let data be the data of the message.
        // 2. Assert: data is an Object.
        // 3. Let type be ! Get(data, "type").
        // 4. Let value be ! Get(data, "value").
        // 5. Assert: type is a String.
        let (r#type, value) = type_and_value_of_message(cx.vm(), data);
        let r#type = r#type.to_utf8();

        // 6. If type is "chunk",
        if r#type == "chunk" {
            // 1. Perform ! ReadableStreamDefaultControllerEnqueue(controller, value).
            readable_stream_default_controller_enqueue(cx, controller, value).must();
        }
        // 7. Otherwise, if type is "close",
        else if r#type == "close" {
            // 1. Perform ! ReadableStreamDefaultControllerClose(controller).
            readable_stream_default_controller_close(cx, controller);

            // 2. Disentangle port.
            port.disentangle();
        }
        // 8. Otherwise, if type is "error",
        else if r#type == "error" {
            // 1. Perform ! ReadableStreamDefaultControllerError(controller, value).
            readable_stream_default_controller_error(cx, controller, value);

            // 2. Disentangle port.
            port.disentangle();
        }
    }

    // 4. Add a handler for port’s messageerror event with the following steps:
    fn on_message_error(cx: &CallContext, state: ReadableHandlerState) {
        let port = state.port;

        // 1. Let error be a new "DataCloneError" DOMException.
        let error = data_clone_error(cx);

        // 2. Perform ! CrossRealmTransformSendError(port, error).
        cross_realm_transform_send_error(cx, port, error);

        // 3. Perform ! ReadableStreamDefaultControllerError(controller, error).
        readable_stream_default_controller_error(cx, state.controller, error);

        // 4. Disentangle port.
        port.disentangle();
    }
    add_handlers(cx, port, state, on_message, on_message_error);

    // 5. Enable port’s port message queue.
    MessagePort::enable(port, cx.vm());

    // 6. Let startAlgorithm be an algorithm that returns undefined.
    let start_algorithm = StartAlgorithm::ReturnsUndefined;

    // 7. Let pullAlgorithm be the following steps:
    let pull_algorithm = PullAlgorithm::CrossRealm(port);

    // 8. Let cancelAlgorithm be the following steps, taking a reason argument:
    let cancel_algorithm = CancelAlgorithm::CrossRealm(port);

    // 9. Let sizeAlgorithm be an algorithm that returns 1.
    let size_algorithm = SizeAlgorithm::ReturnsOne;

    // 10. Perform ! SetUpReadableStreamDefaultController(stream, controller, startAlgorithm, pullAlgorithm,
    //     cancelAlgorithm, 0, sizeAlgorithm).
    set_up_readable_stream_default_controller(
        cx,
        stream,
        controller,
        start_algorithm,
        pull_algorithm,
        cancel_algorithm,
        0.0,
        size_algorithm,
    )
    .must();
}

/// The state that the handlers and the writeAlgorithm of SetUpCrossRealmTransformWritable share.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct CrossRealmWritableState {
    port: Ref<MessagePort>,
    controller: Ref<WritableStreamDefaultController>,
    // backpressurePromise
    backpressure_promise: Cell<Option<WebIdlPromise>>,
}

static CROSS_REALM_WRITABLE_STATE_CLASS: EmbedderClass<CrossRealmWritableState> =
    EmbedderClass::new("CrossRealmTransformWritable");

impl EmbedderValue for CrossRealmWritableState {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &CROSS_REALM_WRITABLE_STATE_CLASS;
}

impl CrossRealmWritableState {
    /// The writeAlgorithm of SetUpCrossRealmTransformWritable.
    pub(crate) fn write_algorithm(this: Gc<EmbedderCell<Self>>, cx: &CallContext, chunk: Value) -> WebIdlPromise {
        // 1. If backpressurePromise is undefined, set backpressurePromise to a promise resolved with undefined.
        let backpressure_promise = match this.backpressure_promise.get() {
            Some(backpressure_promise) => backpressure_promise,
            None => {
                let backpressure_promise = create_resolved_promise(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), Value::UNDEFINED);
                this.backpressure_promise.set(Some(backpressure_promise));
                backpressure_promise
            }
        };

        // AD-HOC: The steps below return a promise that they create when they run, but the error of
        //         PackAndPostMessageHandlingError has to reach the original ReadableStream, which WPT tests: the
        //         promise that reacting to backpressurePromise returns is the one that they reject or resolve.
        let reaction_promise = create_promise(cx.vm(), cx.realm());

        // 2. Return the result of reacting to backpressurePromise with the following fulfillment steps:
        upon_fulfillment(
            cx.vm(),
            backpressure_promise,
            (this, reaction_promise, chunk),
            |cx, (this, reaction_promise, chunk), _| {
                // 1. Set backpressurePromise to a new promise.
                this.backpressure_promise.set(Some(create_promise(cx.vm(), cx.realm())));

                // 2. Let result be PackAndPostMessageHandlingError(port, "chunk", chunk).
                let result = pack_and_post_message_handling_error(cx, this.port, "chunk", chunk);

                match result {
                    // 3. If result is an abrupt completion,
                    Err(exception) => {
                        // 1. Disentangle port.
                        this.port.disentangle();

                        // 2. Return a promise rejected with result.[[Value]].
                        reject_promise_with_exception(cx.vm(), reaction_promise, exception);
                    }
                    // 4. Otherwise, return a promise resolved with undefined.
                    Ok(()) => resolve_promise(cx.vm(), reaction_promise, Value::UNDEFINED),
                }
                Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
            },
        );
        reaction_promise
    }

    /// Resolves backpressurePromise with undefined and sets it to undefined, if it is not undefined.
    fn resolve_backpressure_promise(&self, vm: &Vm) {
        // 1. If backpressurePromise is not undefined,
        if let Some(backpressure_promise) = self.backpressure_promise.take() {
            // 1. Resolve backpressurePromise with undefined.
            // 2. Set backpressurePromise to undefined.
            resolve_promise(vm, backpressure_promise, Value::UNDEFINED);
        }
    }
}

// https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#abstract-opdef-setupcrossrealmtransformwritable
pub(crate) fn set_up_cross_realm_transform_writable(
    cx: &CallContext,
    stream: Ref<WritableStream>,
    port: Ref<MessagePort>,
) {
    // 1. Perform ! InitializeWritableStream(stream).
    initialize_writable_stream(cx.vm(), stream);

    // 2. Let controller be a new WritableStreamDefaultController.
    let controller = allocate(cx.vm(), WritableStreamDefaultController::new);

    // 3. Let backpressurePromise be a new promise.
    let state = CROSS_REALM_WRITABLE_STATE_CLASS.allocate(cx.vm(), |_| CrossRealmWritableState {
        port,
        controller,
        backpressure_promise: Cell::new(Some(create_promise(cx.vm(), cx.realm()))),
    });

    // 4. Add a handler for port’s message event with the following steps:
    fn on_message(cx: &CallContext, state: Gc<EmbedderCell<CrossRealmWritableState>>, data: Value) {
        // 1. Let data be the data of the message.
        // 2. Assert: data is an Object.
        // 3. Let type be ! Get(data, "type").
        // 4. Let value be ! Get(data, "value").
        // 5. Assert: type is a String.
        let (r#type, value) = type_and_value_of_message(cx.vm(), data);
        let r#type = r#type.to_utf8();

        // 6. If type is "pull",
        if r#type == "pull" {
            // 1. If backpressurePromise is not undefined,
            state.resolve_backpressure_promise(cx.vm());
        }
        // 7. Otherwise, if type is "error",
        else if r#type == "error" {
            // 1. Perform ! WritableStreamDefaultControllerErrorIfNeeded(controller, value).
            writable_stream_default_controller_error_if_needed(cx, state.controller, value);

            // 2. If backpressurePromise is not undefined,
            state.resolve_backpressure_promise(cx.vm());
        }
    }

    // 5. Add a handler for port’s messageerror event with the following steps:
    fn on_message_error(cx: &CallContext, state: Gc<EmbedderCell<CrossRealmWritableState>>) {
        // 1. Let error be a new "DataCloneError" DOMException.
        let error = data_clone_error(cx);

        // 2. Perform ! CrossRealmTransformSendError(port, error).
        cross_realm_transform_send_error(cx, state.port, error);

        // 3. Perform ! WritableStreamDefaultControllerErrorIfNeeded(controller, error).
        writable_stream_default_controller_error_if_needed(cx, state.controller, error);

        // 4. Disentangle port.
        state.port.disentangle();
    }
    add_handlers(cx, port, state, on_message, on_message_error);

    // 6. Enable port’s port message queue.
    MessagePort::enable(port, cx.vm());

    // 7. Let startAlgorithm be an algorithm that returns undefined.
    let start_algorithm = StartAlgorithm::ReturnsUndefined;

    // 8. Let writeAlgorithm be the following steps, taking a chunk argument:
    let write_algorithm = WriteAlgorithm::CrossRealm(state);

    // 9. Let closeAlgorithm be the following steps:
    let close_algorithm = CloseAlgorithm::CrossRealm(port);

    // 10. Let abortAlgorithm be the following steps, taking a reason argument:
    let abort_algorithm = AbortAlgorithm::CrossRealm(port);

    // 11. Let sizeAlgorithm be an algorithm that returns 1.
    let size_algorithm = SizeAlgorithm::ReturnsOne;

    // 12. Perform ! SetUpWritableStreamDefaultController(stream, controller, startAlgorithm, writeAlgorithm,
    //     closeAlgorithm, abortAlgorithm, 1, sizeAlgorithm).
    set_up_writable_stream_default_controller(
        cx,
        stream,
        controller,
        start_algorithm,
        write_algorithm,
        close_algorithm,
        abort_algorithm,
        1.0,
        size_algorithm,
    )
    .must();
}

/// Two new MessagePorts in the current realm, entangled with each other.
pub(crate) fn create_entangled_ports(cx: &CallContext) -> (Ref<MessagePort>, Ref<MessagePort>) {
    let port1 = MessagePort::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm());
    let port2 = MessagePort::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm());
    MessagePort::entangle(cx.vm(), port1, port2);
    (port1, port2)
}

/// Sets the data holder to ! StructuredSerializeWithTransfer(port, « port »).
pub(crate) fn serialize_message_port(cx: &CallContext, data_holder: &mut TransferDataWriter, port: Ref<MessagePort>) {
    data_holder
        .write_transferred_value(cx, Value::from_object(wrap(cx, port)))
        .must();
}

/// The MessagePort of ! StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer(dataHolder.[[port]], the current Realm).
pub(crate) fn deserialize_message_port(cx: &CallContext, data_holder: &mut TransferDataReader) -> Ref<MessagePort> {
    let deserialized = data_holder.read_transferred_value(cx).must();
    implementation_of(deserialized.as_object())
}

//! The C ABI through which the C++ classes of Streams/ReadableStream.h, Streams/TransformStream.h and
//! Streams/WritableStream.h set streams up and read them, for the specifications that LibWeb implements in C++.

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, RawNativeFunctionResult, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr, Value, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::BufferSource;
use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::{LentCppCell, cpp_class};
use crate::bindings::interface::{InterfaceCell, Ref, allocate, cell_into_abi};

use crate::bindings::{CallContext, MustNotThrow, WebIdlResult};
use crate::streams::algorithms::{CancelAlgorithm, FlushAlgorithm, TransformAlgorithm, WriteAlgorithm};
use crate::streams::cpp::{
    CppBytesSteps, CppPromiseAlgorithm, CppPromiseAlgorithmWithArgument, CppReadRequest, CppValueSteps,
};

    ReadableStream, ReadableStreamState, is_readable_stream_locked, readable_stream_cancel,
};

use crate::streams::readable_stream_default_reader::ReadableStreamDefaultReader;
