//! The builtins of the JS API, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#builtins, and the imported strings,
//! https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#instantiate-imported-strings

use core::ffi::c_void;
use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::rc::Rc;

use ak::{Utf16String, Utf16StringUnits};
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Must, Object, PrimitiveString, PropertyKey, Value, Vm};
use libwasm_engine::module::{Import, ImportDescription};
use libwasm_engine::runtime::{FunctionAddress, HostFunction, Store, Trap, Value as WasmValue};
use libwasm_engine::types::{GlobalType, HeapType, RefType, ValType};

use crate::bindings::conversions::UsvString;
use crate::web_assembly::exported_function::create_exported_function;
use crate::web_assembly::instance::function_type_in_store;
use crate::web_assembly::values::{EXTERNREF, to_js_value, to_webassembly_value};
use crate::web_assembly::{Agent, CompiledModule};

const JS_STRING_BUILTIN_SET_NAME: &str = "js-string";
const JS_STRING_BUILTIN_SET_QUALIFIED_NAME: &str = "wasm:js-string";

/// The funcTypes of the builtins, each in a recursion group of its own, as the types of a module that has nothing
/// else. The store gives types the same identity wherever they are equivalent, so an import matches the funcType of a
/// builtin exactly when the identity of its type is the identity of that funcType.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum BuiltinTypeIndex {
    // (rec (type (array (mut i16)))).0
    #[allow(
        dead_code,
        reason = "the array type is the type of the other types' array parameters"
    )]
    ArrayType,
    // (rec (type (func (param externref) (result (ref extern))))).0
    ExternrefToRefExtern,
    // (rec (type (func (param externref) (result i32)))).0
    ExternrefToI32,
    // (rec (type (func (param (ref null arrayType) i32 i32) (result (ref extern))))).0
    ArrayI32I32ToRefExtern,
    // (rec (type (func (param externref (ref null arrayType) i32) (result i32)))).0
    ExternrefArrayI32ToI32,
    // (rec (type (func (param i32) (result (ref extern))))).0
    I32ToRefExtern,
    // (rec (type (func (param externref i32) (result i32)))).0
    ExternrefI32ToI32,
    // (rec (type (func (param externref externref) (result (ref extern))))).0
    ExternrefExternrefToRefExtern,
    // (rec (type (func (param externref i32 i32) (result (ref extern))))).0
    ExternrefI32I32ToRefExtern,
    // (rec (type (func (param externref externref) (result i32)))).0
    ExternrefExternrefToI32,
}

pub(crate) const BUILTIN_TYPES_MODULE_BYTES: [u8; 75] = [
    // Magic and version.
    0x00, 0x61, 0x73, 0x6d, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, //
    // The type section: 65 bytes, 10 types.
    0x01, 0x41, 0x0a, //
    // array (mut i16)
    0x5e, 0x77, 0x01, //
    // func (param externref) (result (ref extern))
    0x60, 0x01, 0x6f, 0x01, 0x64, 0x6f, //
    // func (param externref) (result i32)
    0x60, 0x01, 0x6f, 0x01, 0x7f, //
    // func (param (ref null 0) i32 i32) (result (ref extern))
    0x60, 0x03, 0x63, 0x00, 0x7f, 0x7f, 0x01, 0x64, 0x6f, //
    // func (param externref (ref null 0) i32) (result i32)
    0x60, 0x03, 0x6f, 0x63, 0x00, 0x7f, 0x01, 0x7f, //
    // func (param i32) (result (ref extern))
    0x60, 0x01, 0x7f, 0x01, 0x64, 0x6f, //
    // func (param externref i32) (result i32)
    0x60, 0x02, 0x6f, 0x7f, 0x01, 0x7f, //
    // func (param externref externref) (result (ref extern))
    0x60, 0x02, 0x6f, 0x6f, 0x01, 0x64, 0x6f, //
    // func (param externref i32 i32) (result (ref extern))
    0x60, 0x03, 0x6f, 0x7f, 0x7f, 0x01, 0x64, 0x6f, //
    // func (param externref externref) (result i32)
    0x60, 0x02, 0x6f, 0x6f, 0x01, 0x7f,
];

/// The store-wide identity of the type at `type_index` of a module.
fn type_identity(vm: &Vm, module: &CompiledModule, type_index: u32) -> u32 {
    Agent::the(vm).store().module_type_identities_of(module)[type_index as usize]
}

type BuiltinSteps = fn(&Vm, &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap>;

struct Builtin {
    name: &'static str,
    function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex,
    steps: BuiltinSteps,
}

fn trap(message: &str) -> Trap {
    Trap::Host(message.to_string())
}

fn js_value_of(vm: &Vm, value: WasmValue) -> Value {
    to_js_value(vm, value, EXTERNREF).must()
}

fn string_reference(vm: &Vm, string: Gc<PrimitiveString>) -> WasmValue {
    to_webassembly_value(vm, Value::from_string(string), EXTERNREF).must()
}

fn string_reference_of_code_units(vm: &Vm, code_units: &[u16]) -> WasmValue {
    string_reference(vm, PrimitiveString::create(vm, Utf16String::from_utf16(code_units)))
}

fn i32_of(value: WasmValue) -> i32 {
    let WasmValue::I32(value) = value else {
        unreachable!("the funcType of the builtin has an i32 there");
    };
    value
}

fn unsigned_i32(value: WasmValue) -> u32 {
    i32_of(value) as u32
}

/// The code units of a string.
fn code_units_of(string: Gc<PrimitiveString>) -> Vec<u16> {
    let string = string.utf16_string();
    match string.as_units() {
        Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(characters) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(characters) => {
            characters.iter().map(|&character| u16::from(character)).collect()
        }
        Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(code_units) => code_units.to_vec(),
    }
}

/// The number of elements of an array, which is not null.
fn array_length(array: u64) -> u32 {
    // SAFETY: The array is the argument of a builtin whose funcType makes it a live array of i16s.
    unsafe { libwasm_engine::runtime::gc::array_length(array) }
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#abstract-opdef-unwrapstring
fn unwrap_string(vm: &Vm, v: WasmValue) -> Result<Gc<PrimitiveString>, Trap> {
    let value = js_value_of(vm, v);

    // 1. If v is not a String,
    if !value.is_string() {
        // 1. Throw a RuntimeError exception as if a trap was executed.
        return Err(trap("Expected a string"));
    }

    // 2. Return v
    Ok(value.as_string())
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#abstract-opdef-fromcharcode
fn from_char_code(v: i32) -> u16 {
    // 1. Assert: v is of type i32.
    // 2. Return ! Call(String.fromCharCode, undefined, « ToJSValue(v) »).
    v as u16
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#abstract-opdef-charcodeat
fn char_code_at(string: Gc<PrimitiveString>, index: u32) -> i32 {
    // 1. Assert: index is of type i32.
    // 2. Return ! Call(String.prototype.charCodeAt, string, « ToJSValue(index) »).
    i32::from(string.code_unit_at(index as usize))
}

#[allow(
    clippy::unnecessary_wraps,
    reason = "the steps of every builtin have the one type, and some can trap"
)]
mod js_string_builtins {
    use libjs_rust::api::{Must, PrimitiveString, Vm};
    use libwasm_engine::runtime::{Trap, Value as WasmValue};

    use super::{
        array_length, code_units_of, i32_of, js_value_of, string_reference, string_reference_of_code_units, trap,
        unsigned_i32, unwrap_string,
    };

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-cast
    pub(super) fn cast(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        // 1. Return ? UnwrapString(v)
        unwrap_string(vm, arguments[0])?;
        Ok(arguments[0])
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-test
    pub(super) fn test(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        // 1. If v is not a String,
        if !js_value_of(vm, arguments[0]).is_string() {
            // 1. Return 0.
            return Ok(WasmValue::I32(0));
        }

        // 2. Return 1.
        Ok(WasmValue::I32(1))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-fromcharcodearray
    pub(super) fn from_char_code_array(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        let WasmValue::Ref(array) = arguments[0] else {
            unreachable!("the funcType of the builtin has an array reference there");
        };
        // NB: The indices are unsigned, as everywhere else in WebAssembly.
        let start = unsigned_i32(arguments[1]);
        let end = unsigned_i32(arguments[2]);

        // 1. If array is null,
        if array == 0 {
            // 1. Throw a RuntimeError exception as if a trap was executed.
            return Err(trap("The array is null"));
        }

        // 2. Let length be the number of elements in array.
        let length = array_length(array);

        // 3. If start > end or end > length,
        if start > end || end > length {
            // 1. Throw a RuntimeError exception as if a trap was executed.
            return Err(trap("The range is out of the array's bounds"));
        }

        // 4. Let result be the empty string.
        let mut result = Vec::with_capacity((end - start) as usize);

        // 5. Let i be start.
        // 6. While i < end:
        for i in start..end {
            // 1. Let charCode be the value of the element stored at index i in array.
            // SAFETY: The array is a live array of i16s, and i is in its bounds.
            let char_code = unsafe { libwasm_engine::runtime::gc::array_element(array, i) } as i32;

            // 2. Let charCodeString be FromCharCode(charCode).
            // 3. Let result be the concatenation of result and charCodeString.
            // NB: FromCharCode() makes a string of one code unit, which is the code unit itself here.
            result.push(super::from_char_code(char_code));

            // 4. Set i to i + 1.
        }

        // 7. Return result.
        Ok(string_reference_of_code_units(vm, &result))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-intocharcodearray
    pub(super) fn into_char_code_array(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        let WasmValue::Ref(array) = arguments[1] else {
            unreachable!("the funcType of the builtin has an array reference there");
        };
        let start = unsigned_i32(arguments[2]);

        // 1. If array is null,
        if array == 0 {
            // 1. Throw a RuntimeError exception as if a trap was executed.
            return Err(trap("The array is null"));
        }

        // 2. Let string be ? UnwrapString(string).
        let string = unwrap_string(vm, arguments[0])?;

        // 3. Let stringLength be the length of string.
        let string_length = string.length_in_utf16_code_units();

        // 4. Let arrayLength be the number of elements in array.
        let array_length = array_length(array);

        // 5. If start + stringLength > arrayLength,
        if u64::from(start) + string_length as u64 > u64::from(array_length) {
            // 1. Throw a RuntimeError exception as if a trap was executed.
            return Err(trap("The string does not fit in the array"));
        }

        // 6. Let i be 0.
        // 7. While i < stringLength:
        for i in 0..string_length as u32 {
            // 1. Let charCode be CharCodeAt(string, i).
            let char_code = super::char_code_at(string, i);

            // 2. Set the element at index start + i in array to ToWebAssemblyValue(charCode, i32).
            // SAFETY: The array is a live array of i16s, and start + i is in its bounds.
            unsafe { libwasm_engine::runtime::gc::set_array_element(array, start + i, u64::from(char_code as u32)) };

            // 3. Set i to i + 1.
        }

        // 8. Return stringLength.
        Ok(WasmValue::I32(string_length as i32))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-fromcharcode
    pub(super) fn from_char_code(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        // 1. Return FromCharCode(v).
        Ok(string_reference_of_code_units(
            vm,
            &[super::from_char_code(i32_of(arguments[0]))],
        ))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-fromcodepoint
    pub(super) fn from_code_point(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        let v = unsigned_i32(arguments[0]);

        // 1. If v > 0x10ffff,
        if v > 0x10ffff {
            // 1. Throw a RuntimeError exception as if a trap was executed.
            return Err(trap("The code point is out of range"));
        }

        // 2. Return ! Call(String.fromCodePoint, undefined, « ToJSValue(v) »).
        // NB: A code point beyond the BMP is a surrogate pair, and a surrogate code point is a lone surrogate.
        if v < 0x10000 {
            return Ok(string_reference_of_code_units(vm, &[v as u16]));
        }
        let offset = v - 0x10000;
        Ok(string_reference_of_code_units(
            vm,
            &[0xd800 | (offset >> 10) as u16, 0xdc00 | (offset & 0x3ff) as u16],
        ))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-charcodeat
    pub(super) fn char_code_at(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        let index = unsigned_i32(arguments[1]);

        // 1. Let string be ? UnwrapString(string).
        let string = unwrap_string(vm, arguments[0])?;

        // 2. Let length be the length of string.
        let length = string.length_in_utf16_code_units();

        // 3. If index >= length,
        if index as usize >= length {
            // 1. Throw a RuntimeError exception as if a trap was executed.
            return Err(trap("The index is out of the string's bounds"));
        }

        // 4. Return CharCodeAt(string, index).
        Ok(WasmValue::I32(super::char_code_at(string, index)))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-codepointat
    pub(super) fn code_point_at(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        let index = unsigned_i32(arguments[1]) as usize;

        // 1. Let string be ? UnwrapString(string).
        let string = unwrap_string(vm, arguments[0])?;

        // 2. Let length be the length of string.
        let length = string.length_in_utf16_code_units();

        // 3. If index >= length,
        if index >= length {
            // 1. Throw a RuntimeError exception as if a trap was executed.
            return Err(trap("The index is out of the string's bounds"));
        }

        // 4. Return ! Call(String.prototype.codePointAt, string, « ToJSValue(index) »).
        // NB: A leading surrogate that a trailing one follows is the code point of the pair, and any other code unit
        //     is the code point of its value.
        let first = string.code_unit_at(index);
        if (0xd800..=0xdbff).contains(&first) && index + 1 < length {
            let second = string.code_unit_at(index + 1);
            if (0xdc00..=0xdfff).contains(&second) {
                let code_point = 0x10000 + ((u32::from(first) - 0xd800) << 10) + (u32::from(second) - 0xdc00);
                return Ok(WasmValue::I32(code_point as i32));
            }
        }
        Ok(WasmValue::I32(i32::from(first)))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-length
    pub(super) fn length(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        // 1. Let string be ? UnwrapString(v).
        let string = unwrap_string(vm, arguments[0])?;

        // 2. Return the length of string.
        Ok(WasmValue::I32(string.length_in_utf16_code_units() as i32))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-concat
    pub(super) fn concat(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        // 1. Let first be ? UnwrapString(first).
        let first = unwrap_string(vm, arguments[0])?;

        // 2. Let second be ? UnwrapString(second).
        let second = unwrap_string(vm, arguments[1])?;

        // 3. Return ! Call(String.prototype.concat, first, « second »).
        // NB: String.prototype.concat makes a rope, so code that appends piece by piece does not copy the string so far
        //     on every append. It throws a RangeError if the result would be too long, which traps here instead.
        if second.length_in_utf16_code_units() >= u32::MAX as usize - first.length_in_utf16_code_units() {
            return Err(trap("Invalid string length"));
        }
        let result = PrimitiveString::create_from_concatenation(vm, first, second).must();
        Ok(string_reference(vm, result))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-substring
    pub(super) fn substring(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        // NB: The indices are unsigned, as everywhere else in WebAssembly.
        let start = unsigned_i32(arguments[1]) as usize;
        let end = unsigned_i32(arguments[2]) as usize;

        // 1. Let string be ? UnwrapString(string).
        let string = unwrap_string(vm, arguments[0])?;

        // 2. Let length be the length of string.
        let length = string.length_in_utf16_code_units();

        // 3. If start > end or start > length,
        if start > end || start > length {
            // 1. Return the empty string.
            return Ok(string_reference(vm, vm.empty_string()));
        }

        // 4. Return ! Call(String.prototype.substring, string, « ToJSValue(start), ToJSValue(end) »).
        // NB: start <= end here, and String.prototype.substring clamps end to the length.
        let clamped_end = end.min(length);
        Ok(string_reference(
            vm,
            PrimitiveString::create_from_substring(vm, string, start, clamped_end - start),
        ))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-equals
    pub(super) fn equals(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        let first = js_value_of(vm, arguments[0]);
        let second = js_value_of(vm, arguments[1]);

        // 1. If first is not null and first is not a String,
        if !first.is_null() && !first.is_string() {
            // 1. Throw a RuntimeError exception as if a trap was executed.
            return Err(trap("Expected a string or null"));
        }

        // 2. If second is not null and second is not a String,
        if !second.is_null() && !second.is_string() {
            // 1. Throw a RuntimeError exception as if a trap was executed.
            return Err(trap("Expected a string or null"));
        }

        // 3. If IsStrictlyEqual(first, second) is true,
        let strictly_equal = if first.is_null() || second.is_null() {
            first.is_null() && second.is_null()
        } else {
            first.as_string().utf16_string() == second.as_string().utf16_string()
        };
        if strictly_equal {
            // 1. Return 1.
            return Ok(WasmValue::I32(1));
        }

        // 4. Return 0.
        Ok(WasmValue::I32(0))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#js-string-compare
    pub(super) fn compare(vm: &Vm, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<WasmValue, Trap> {
        // 1. Let first be ? UnwrapString(first).
        let first = code_units_of(unwrap_string(vm, arguments[0])?);

        // 2. Let second be ? UnwrapString(second).
        let second = code_units_of(unwrap_string(vm, arguments[1])?);

        // 3. If IsStrictlyEqual(first, second) is true,
        if first == second {
            // 1. Return 0.
            return Ok(WasmValue::I32(0));
        }

        // 4. If ! IsLessThan(first, second, true) is true,
        // NB: IsLessThan() compares two strings by their code units.
        if first < second {
            // 1. Return -1.
            return Ok(WasmValue::I32(-1));
        }

        // 5. Return 1.
        Ok(WasmValue::I32(1))
    }
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#string-builtins
const JS_STRING_BUILTINS: [Builtin; 13] = [
    Builtin {
        name: "cast",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ExternrefToRefExtern,
        steps: js_string_builtins::cast,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "test",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ExternrefToI32,
        steps: js_string_builtins::test,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "fromCharCodeArray",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ArrayI32I32ToRefExtern,
        steps: js_string_builtins::from_char_code_array,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "intoCharCodeArray",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ExternrefArrayI32ToI32,
        steps: js_string_builtins::into_char_code_array,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "fromCharCode",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::I32ToRefExtern,
        steps: js_string_builtins::from_char_code,
    },
    // INTEROP: The funcType of fromCodePoint has a (ref extern) result in other implementations, where the spec has an
    //          externref result.
    Builtin {
        name: "fromCodePoint",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::I32ToRefExtern,
        steps: js_string_builtins::from_code_point,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "charCodeAt",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ExternrefI32ToI32,
        steps: js_string_builtins::char_code_at,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "codePointAt",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ExternrefI32ToI32,
        steps: js_string_builtins::code_point_at,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "length",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ExternrefToI32,
        steps: js_string_builtins::length,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "concat",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ExternrefExternrefToRefExtern,
        steps: js_string_builtins::concat,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "substring",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ExternrefI32I32ToRefExtern,
        steps: js_string_builtins::substring,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "equals",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ExternrefExternrefToI32,
        steps: js_string_builtins::equals,
    },
    Builtin {
        name: "compare",
        function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex::ExternrefExternrefToI32,
        steps: js_string_builtins::compare,
    },
];

pub(crate) fn refers_to_a_builtin_set(builtin_set_name: &UsvString) -> bool {
    builtin_set_name.to_utf8() == JS_STRING_BUILTIN_SET_NAME
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#get-the-builtins-for-a-builtin-set
fn get_the_builtins_for_a_builtin_set(builtin_set_name: &UsvString) -> &'static [Builtin] {
    // 1. Return a list of (name, funcType, steps) for the set with name builtinSetName defined within this section.
    assert!(refers_to_a_builtin_set(builtin_set_name));
    &JS_STRING_BUILTINS
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#validate-builtin-set-names
fn validate_builtin_set_names(builtin_set_names: &[UsvString]) -> bool {
    // 1. If builtinSetNames contains any duplicates, return false.
    let mut seen_names = HashSet::new();
    if !builtin_set_names
        .iter()
        .all(|builtin_set_name| seen_names.insert(builtin_set_name.to_utf8()))
    {
        return false;
    }

    // 2. Return true.
    true
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#find-a-builtin
fn find_a_builtin(import: &Import, builtin_set_names: &[UsvString]) -> Option<&'static Builtin> {
    // 1. Assert: validate builtin set names builtinSetNames is true.
    assert!(validate_builtin_set_names(builtin_set_names));

    // 2. Let importModuleName be import[0].
    let import_module_name = &import.module;

    // 3. Let importName be import[1].
    let import_name = &import.name;

    // 4. For each builtinSetName of builtinSetNames,
    for builtin_set_name in builtin_set_names {
        // 1. If builtinSetName does not refer to a builtin set, then continue.
        if !refers_to_a_builtin_set(builtin_set_name) {
            continue;
        }

        // 2. Let builtinSetQualifiedName be builtinSetName prefixed with "wasm:".
        let builtin_set_qualified_name = JS_STRING_BUILTIN_SET_QUALIFIED_NAME;

        // 3. If importModuleName equals builtinSetQualifiedName,
        if import_module_name == builtin_set_qualified_name {
            // 1. Let builtins be the result of get the builtins for a builtin set builtinSetName.
            let builtins = get_the_builtins_for_a_builtin_set(builtin_set_name);

            // 2. For each builtin of builtins,
            for builtin in builtins {
                // 1. Let builtinName be builtin[0].
                // 2. If importName equals builtinName, return (builtinSetName, builtin).
                if import_name == builtin.name {
                    return Some(builtin);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // 5. Return null.
    None
}

/// Whether finding a builtin for the import and builtinSetNames does not return null.
pub(crate) fn import_refers_to_a_builtin(import: &Import, builtin_set_names: &[UsvString]) -> bool {
    find_a_builtin(import, builtin_set_names).is_some()
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#validate-an-import-for-builtins
fn validate_an_import_for_builtins(
    vm: &Vm,
    module: &CompiledModule,
    import: &Import,
    builtin_set_names: &[UsvString],
) -> bool {
    // 1. Assert: validate builtin set names builtinSetNames is true.
    assert!(validate_builtin_set_names(builtin_set_names));

    // 2. Let maybeBuiltin be the result of finding a builtin for import and builtinSetNames.
    let maybe_builtin = find_a_builtin(import, builtin_set_names);

    // 3. If maybeBuiltin is null, return true.
    let Some(maybe_builtin) = maybe_builtin else {
        return true;
    };

    // 4. Let importExternType be import[2].
    let import_extern_type = &import.description;

    // 5. Let builtinFuncType be maybeBuiltin[1][1].
    let builtin_func_type = maybe_builtin.function_type;

    // 6. Let builtinExternType be func |builtinFuncType|.
    // 7. Return match_externtype(builtinExternType, importExternType).
    // NB: The funcType of a builtin is final and has no supertypes, so it only matches the import's type if both are
    //     the same type.
    let ImportDescription::Function(type_index) = *import_extern_type else {
        return false;
    };
    let builtin_types_module = Agent::the(vm).builtin_types_module();
    type_identity(vm, module, type_index) == type_identity(vm, builtin_types_module, builtin_func_type as u32)
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#validate-builtins-and-imported-string-for-a-webassembly-module
pub(crate) fn validate_builtins_and_imported_strings(
    vm: &Vm,
    module: &CompiledModule,
    builtin_set_names: &[UsvString],
    imported_string_module: Option<&UsvString>,
) -> bool {
    // 1. If validating builtin set names for builtinSetNames is false, return false.
    if !validate_builtin_set_names(builtin_set_names) {
        return false;
    }

    let imported_string_module = imported_string_module.map(UsvString::to_utf8);

    // 2. For each import of module_imports(module),
    for import in &module.imports {
        // 1. If importedStringModule is not null and import[0] equals importedStringModule,
        if imported_string_module.as_ref() == Some(&import.module) {
            // 1. Let importExternType be import[2].
            let import_extern_type = &import.description;

            // 2. Let stringExternType be global ref extern.
            // 3. If match_externtype(stringExternType, importExternType) is false, return false
            // NB: An immutable global matches if (ref extern) is a subtype of the import's value type, which then is
            //     (ref extern) or externref.
            if !matches!(
                import_extern_type,
                ImportDescription::Global(GlobalType {
                    value: ValType::Ref(RefType {
                        heap: HeapType::Extern,
                        ..
                    }),
                    mutable: false,
                })
            ) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        // 2. Else,
        else {
            // 1. If validating an import for builtins with import and builtinSetNames is false, return false.
            if !validate_an_import_for_builtins(vm, module, import, builtin_set_names) {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }

    // 3. Return true.
    true
}

/// The steps of a builtin's host function, and the index of the builtin in its set.
struct BuiltinFunction {
    steps: BuiltinSteps,
    index: u32,
}

impl HostFunction for BuiltinFunction {
    fn call(&self, _: &mut Store, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<Vec<WasmValue>, Trap> {
        let vm = Agent::current().vm();
        (self.steps)(vm, arguments).map(|result| vec![result])
    }

    fn user_data(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        core::ptr::from_ref(&self.index).cast_mut().cast()
    }
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-builtin-function
fn create_a_builtin_function(
    vm: &Vm,
    function_type: BuiltinTypeIndex,
    steps: BuiltinSteps,
    index: u32,
) -> FunctionAddress {
    // 1. Let hostfunc be a host function which executes steps when called.
    let host_function = Rc::new(BuiltinFunction { steps, index });

    // 2. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
    // 3. Let (store, funcaddr) be func_alloc(store, funcType, hostfunc).
    // 4. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
    // 5. Return funcaddr.
    // NB: The index is the builtin's position in its set, which names the Exported Function made for it.
    let agent = Agent::the(vm);
    let ty = function_type_in_store(vm, agent.builtin_types_module(), function_type as u32);
    agent.store().allocate_host_function(ty, host_function)
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#instantiate-a-builtin-set
pub(crate) fn instantiate_a_builtin_set(vm: &Vm, builtin_set_name: &UsvString) -> Gc<Object> {
    let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("instantiating a builtin set runs in a realm");

    // 1. Let builtins be the result of get the builtins for a builtin set builtinSetName.
    let builtins = get_the_builtins_for_a_builtin_set(builtin_set_name);

    // 2. Let exportsObject be OrdinaryObjectCreate(null).
    let exports_object = Object::create(vm, realm, None);

    // 3. For each (name, funcType, steps) of builtins,
    for (index, builtin) in builtins.iter().enumerate() {
        // 1. Let funcaddr be the result of create a builtin function with funcType and steps.
        let funcaddr = create_a_builtin_function(vm, builtin.function_type, builtin.steps, index as u32);

        // 2. Let func be the result of creating a new Exported Function from funcaddr.
        let func = create_exported_function(vm, realm, funcaddr);

        // 3. Let value be func.
        let value = Value::from_object(func.upcast::<Object>());

        // 4. Let status be ! CreateDataProperty(exportsObject, name, value).
        let status = exports_object
            .create_data_property(vm, &PropertyKey::from_utf8(builtin.name), value, None, None)
            .must();

        // 5. Assert: status is true.
        assert!(status);
    }

    // 4. Return exportsObject.
    exports_object
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#instantiate-imported-strings
pub(crate) fn instantiate_imported_strings(
    vm: &Vm,
    module: &CompiledModule,
    imported_string_module: &UsvString,
) -> Gc<Object> {
    let realm = vm
        .current_realm()
        .expect("instantiating imported strings runs in a realm");

    // 1. Assert: importedStringModule is not null.
    let imported_string_module = imported_string_module.to_utf8();

    // 2. Let exportsObject be OrdinaryObjectCreate(null).
    let exports_object = Object::create(vm, realm, None);

    // 3. For each (moduleName, componentName, externtype) of module_imports(module),
    for import in &module.imports {
        // 1. If moduleName does not equal importedStringModule, then continue.
        if import.module != imported_string_module {
            continue;
        }

        // 2. Let stringConstant be componentName.
        let string_constant = Utf16String::from_utf8(&import.name);

        // 3. Let status be ! CreateDataProperty(exportsObject, stringConstant, stringConstant).
        let value = Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(vm, string_constant.clone()));
        let status = exports_object
            .create_data_property(vm, &PropertyKey::from(&string_constant), value, None, None)
            .must();

        // 4. Assert: status is true.
        assert!(status);
    }

    // 4. Return exportsObject.
    exports_object
}

//! The error types of the namespace, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#error-objects: objects implementing
//! the NativeError Object Structure, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-nativeerror-object-structure, whose prototypes and
//! constructors every realm has its own of.

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::{Utf16FlyString, Utf16String};
use libjs_rust::api::{
    Attribute, Error, Gc, HostFunction, JS_HOST_CLASS_FUNCTION, JS_HOST_CLASS_HAS_CONSTRUCTOR, JSCompletion,
    JSHostClass, JSHostFunctionHooks, JSObject, JSVM, Object, PrimitiveString, PropertyAttributes, Realm, Throw,
    ThrowCompletionOr, Value, Vm, completion_into_abi, get_function_realm, object_from_abi, vm_from_abi,
};

use crate::bindings::lent_string::LentUtf16String;
use crate::bindings::realm_data::realm_data;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum WebAssemblyError {
    Compile,
    Link,
    Runtime,
}

impl WebAssemblyError {
    pub(crate) const ALL: [Self; 3] = [Self::Compile, Self::Link, Self::Runtime];

    pub(crate) fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Compile => "CompileError",
            Self::Link => "LinkError",
            Self::Runtime => "RuntimeError",
        }
    }

    fn index(self) -> usize {
        self as usize
    }

    const fn of_index(index: usize) -> Self {
        match index {
            0 => Self::Compile,
            1 => Self::Link,
            _ => Self::Runtime,
        }
    }
}

const fn constructor_hooks<const ERROR: usize>() -> JSHostFunctionHooks {
    JSHostFunctionHooks {
        call: Some(call_native_error_constructor::<ERROR>),
        construct: Some(construct_native_error::<ERROR>),
        finalize: None,
    }
}

static CONSTRUCTOR_HOOKS: [JSHostFunctionHooks; 3] = [
    constructor_hooks::<{ WebAssemblyError::Compile as usize }>(),
    constructor_hooks::<{ WebAssemblyError::Link as usize }>(),
    constructor_hooks::<{ WebAssemblyError::Runtime as usize }>(),
];

static CONSTRUCTOR_CLASSES: [JSHostClass; 3] = [
    JSHostClass::new(
        JS_HOST_CLASS_FUNCTION,
        "CompileErrorConstructor",
        None,
        (&raw const CONSTRUCTOR_HOOKS[0]).cast(),
        JS_HOST_CLASS_HAS_CONSTRUCTOR,
    ),
    JSHostClass::new(
        JS_HOST_CLASS_FUNCTION,
        "LinkErrorConstructor",
        None,
        (&raw const CONSTRUCTOR_HOOKS[1]).cast(),
        JS_HOST_CLASS_HAS_CONSTRUCTOR,
    ),
    JSHostClass::new(
        JS_HOST_CLASS_FUNCTION,
        "RuntimeErrorConstructor",
        None,
        (&raw const CONSTRUCTOR_HOOKS[2]).cast(),
        JS_HOST_CLASS_HAS_CONSTRUCTOR,
    ),
];

/// The NativeError prototype and constructor of the error type in the realm, which the first use in the realm
/// creates.
fn prototype_and_constructor(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, error: WebAssemblyError) -> (Gc<Object>, Gc<Object>) {
    let data = realm_data(vm, realm);
    let index = error.index();
    if let (Some(prototype), Some(constructor)) = (
        data.webassembly_error_prototypes[index].get(),
        data.webassembly_error_constructors[index].get(),
    ) {
        return (prototype, constructor);
    }

    let name = Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create_from_utf8(vm, error.name()));
    let attributes = PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::WRITABLE | Attribute::CONFIGURABLE);

    // 20.5.6.3 Properties of the NativeError Prototype Objects, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-nativeerror-prototype-objects
    let prototype = Object::create(vm, realm, Some(realm.intrinsics().error_prototype(vm)));
    prototype.define_direct_property(vm, &vm.names.name, name, attributes);
    let empty = Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(vm, Utf16String::default()));
    prototype.define_direct_property(vm, &vm.names.message, empty, attributes);

    // 20.5.6.2 Properties of the NativeError Constructors, https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-nativeerror-constructors
    // SAFETY: The class is of kind JS_HOST_CLASS_FUNCTION, and the constructor has no host data.
    let constructor = unsafe {
        HostFunction::create_without_own_properties(
            vm,
            realm,
            &CONSTRUCTOR_CLASSES[index],
            Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(error.name()),
            Some(realm.intrinsics().error_constructor(vm).upcast()),
            None,
        )
    }
    .upcast::<Object>();
    constructor.define_direct_property(
        vm,
        &vm.names.prototype,
        Value::from_object(prototype),
        PropertyAttributes::new(0),
    );
    let configurable = PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE);
    constructor.define_direct_property(vm, &vm.names.name, name, configurable);
    constructor.define_direct_property(vm, &vm.names.length, Value::from_i32(1), configurable);

    prototype.define_direct_property(vm, &vm.names.constructor, Value::from_object(constructor), attributes);

    data.webassembly_error_prototypes[index].set(Some(prototype));
    data.webassembly_error_constructors[index].set(Some(constructor));
    (prototype, constructor)
}

/// The constructor of the error type in the realm.
pub(crate) fn error_constructor(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, error: WebAssemblyError) -> Gc<Object> {
    prototype_and_constructor(vm, realm, error).1
}

/// A new error of the type in the realm, with the message.
pub(crate) fn create_webassembly_error(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, error: WebAssemblyError, message: &str) -> Gc<Error> {
    let (prototype, _) = prototype_and_constructor(vm, realm, error);
    let object = Error::create_with_prototype(vm, realm, prototype);
    object.set_message(vm, Utf16String::from_utf8(message));
    object
}

/// What throwing a new error of the type in the realm, with the message, throws.
pub(crate) fn throw_webassembly_error(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, error: WebAssemblyError, message: &str) -> Throw {
    Throw::new(Value::from_object(
        create_webassembly_error(vm, realm, error, message).upcast::<Object>(),
    ))
}

// 20.5.6.1.1 NativeError ( message [ , options ] ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-nativeerror
unsafe extern "C" fn call_native_error_constructor<const ERROR: usize>(
    function: *mut JSObject,
    vm: *mut JSVM,
) -> JSCompletion {
    // 1. If NewTarget is undefined, let newTarget be the active function object; else let newTarget be NewTarget.
    // SAFETY: The runtime passes the live function and the VM.
    unsafe { construct_native_error::<ERROR>(function, vm, function) }
}

// 20.5.6.1.1 NativeError ( message [ , options ] ), https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-nativeerror
unsafe extern "C" fn construct_native_error<const ERROR: usize>(
    _function: *mut JSObject,
    vm: *mut JSVM,
    new_target: *mut JSObject,
) -> JSCompletion {
    // SAFETY: The runtime passes the VM and the live new target.
    let (vm, new_target) = unsafe { (vm_from_abi(vm), object_from_abi(new_target)) };
    completion_into_abi(native_error(vm, new_target, WebAssemblyError::of_index(ERROR)).map(Value::from_object))
}

fn native_error(vm: &Vm, new_target: Gc<Object>, error: WebAssemblyError) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<Object>> {
    let message = vm.argument(0);
    let options = vm.argument(1);

    // 2. Let O be ? OrdinaryCreateFromConstructor(newTarget, "%NativeError.prototype%", « [[ErrorData]] »).
    // NB: The intrinsic default prototype is that of the error type in the realm of newTarget, which the realm's data
    //     keeps, not its intrinsics.
    // https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-getprototypefromconstructor
    // 2. Let proto be ? Get(constructor, "prototype").
    let mut prototype = new_target.get(vm, &vm.names.prototype)?;

    // 3. If Type(proto) is not Object, then
    if !prototype.is_object() {
        // a. Let realm be ? GetFunctionRealm(constructor).
        let realm = get_function_realm(
            vm,
            new_target
                .downcast::<libjs_rust::api::FunctionObject>()
                .expect("the new target of a construction is a function"),
        )?;

        // b. Set proto to realm's intrinsic object named intrinsicDefaultProto.
        prototype = Value::from_object(prototype_and_constructor(vm, realm, error).0);
    }
    let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a constructor runs in a realm");
    let object = Error::create_with_prototype(vm, realm, prototype.as_object());

    // 3. If message is not undefined, then
    if !message.is_undefined() {
        // a. Let msg be ? ToString(message).
        let message = message.to_utf16_string(vm)?;

        // b. Perform CreateNonEnumerableDataPropertyOrThrow(O, "message", msg).
        object.create_non_enumerable_data_property_or_throw(
            vm,
            &vm.names.message,
            Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(vm, message)),
        );
    }

    // 4. Perform ? InstallErrorCause(O, options).
    object.install_error_cause(vm, options)?;

    // 5. Return O.
    Ok(object.upcast())
}

/// A CompileError with the message in the realm, for C++ code that throws one: the CSP check of
/// HostEnsureCanCompileWasmBytes.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_web_assembly_create_compile_error(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    message: LentUtf16String<'_>,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let message = message.to_utf16_string();
    let (prototype, _) = prototype_and_constructor(vm, realm, WebAssemblyError::Compile);
    let error = Error::create_with_prototype(vm, realm, prototype);
    error.set_message(vm, message);
    error.as_ptr().cast()
}

//! Exception, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#exceptions

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{CompactTraceback, Error, Gc, MarkedVec, Realm, Trace, Value, Vm};
use libwasm_engine::runtime::TagInstance;

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate, wrap};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception as WebIdlException, WebIdlResult};
use crate::web_assembly::tag::Tag;
use crate::web_assembly::values::{to_js_value, to_webassembly_value};
use crate::web_assembly::{
    Agent, CellReference, EntityRef, WasmValues, host_object, implementation_of_value, set_host_object,
};

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dictdef-exceptionoptions
pub(crate) struct ExceptionOptions {
    pub(crate) trace_stack: bool,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Exception {
    // [[Address]]
    address: CellReference,
    // [[Type]]
    // NB: The payload of an exception never changes, so getArg() reads [[Payload]] from the store.
    tag: EntityRef<TagInstance>,
    // [[Stack]]
    #[gc(untraced)]
    stack: Option<Utf16String>,
}

impl Wrappable for Exception {}

impl Exception {
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-exception-exception
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        exception_tag: Ref<Tag>,
        payload: MarkedVec<'_, Value>,
        options: ExceptionOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let agent = Agent::the(vm);

        // 1. Let JSTagAddr be the result of getting the JavaScript exception tag.
        // 2. If exceptionTag.[[Address]] is equal to JSTagAddr,
        //     1. Throw a TypeError.
        if exception_tag.address() == agent.js_tag() {
            return Err(WebIdlException::type_error(
                "Cannot construct an exception with the JavaScript tag",
            ));
        }

        // 3. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
        // 4. Let [types] → [] be tag_type(store, exceptionTag.[[Address]]).
        let types = agent.store().tag(exception_tag.address()).ty.params.clone();

        // 5. If types's size is not payload's size,
        //     1. Throw a TypeError.
        if types.len() != payload.len() {
            return Err(WebIdlException::TypeError(Utf16String::from_utf8(&format!(
                "The tag takes {} values, not {}",
                types.len(),
                payload.len()
            ))));
        }

        // 6. Let wasmPayload be « ».
        // NB: The converted values may refer to new cells, which the cell of the values keeps alive until they are in
        //     the exception.
        let wasm_payload = WasmValues::allocate(vm);
        let payload_traces = WasmValues::traces_of(vm, &types);

        // 7. For each value and resultType of payload and types, paired linearly,
        for (index, &result_type) in types.iter().enumerate() {
            // 1. If resultType is v128 or exnref,
            //     1. Throw a TypeError.
            // 2. Append ? ToWebAssemblyValue(value, resultType) to wasmPayload.
            // NB: ToWebAssemblyValue throws the TypeError for v128 and exnref.
            let value = to_webassembly_value(
                vm,
                payload.get(index).expect("the payload has a value per type"),
                result_type,
            )?;
            wasm_payload.push(value, payload_traces[index]);
        }

        // 8. Let (store, exceptionAddr) be exn_alloc(store, exceptionTag.[[Address]], wasmPayload).
        // 9. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
        let exception = agent
            .store()
            .allocate_exception_with_values(exception_tag.address(), &wasm_payload.values());
        // NB: Using the Gc after the allocation keeps the payload where the conservative scan finds it until it is in
        //     the exception.
        core::hint::black_box(wasm_payload);

        // 10. Initialize this from exceptionAddr.
        // 11. If options["traceStack"] is true,
        //     1. Set this.[[Stack]] to either a DOMString representation of the current call stack or undefined.
        // 12. Otherwise,
        //     1. Set this.[[Stack]] to undefined.
        let stack = options.trace_stack.then(|| {
            let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a constructor runs in a realm");
            Error::create(vm, realm).stack_string(CompactTraceback::No)
        });
        Ok(Self::initialize(vm, exception, stack))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#initialize-an-exception-object
    fn initialize(vm: &Vm, exception: u64, stack: Option<Utf16String>) -> Ref<Self> {
        // 1. Let map be the surrounding agent's associated exception object cache.
        // 2. Assert: map[exnAddr] doesn't exist.
        let cell = exception as *mut u8;
        assert!(host_object::<()>(cell).is_none());

        // 3. Set exn.[[Address]] to exnAddr.
        // 4. Set map[exnAddr] to exn.
        // 5. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
        // 6. Let tagaddr be exn_tag(store, exnAddr).
        // 7. Let payload be exn_read(store, exnAddr).
        // 8. Set exn.[[Type]] to tagaddr.
        // 9. Set exn.[[Payload]] to payload.
        let tag = Agent::the(vm).store().exception(exception).tag;
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            address: CellReference(exception),
            tag: EntityRef(tag),
            stack,
        });
        set_host_object(cell, object);
        object
    }

    /// The wrapper of the Exception object of the exception in the realm,
    /// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-an-exception-object
    pub(crate) fn wrapper_of_address(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, exception: u64) -> Value {
        // 1. Let map be the surrounding agent's associated exception object cache.
        // 2. If map[exnAddr] exists,
        //     1. Return map[exnAddr].
        // 3. Let exn be a new Exception.
        // 4. Initialize exn from exnAddr.
        let object = host_object(exception as *mut u8).unwrap_or_else(|| Self::initialize(vm, exception, None));
        Value::from_object(wrap(&CallContext::new(vm, realm), object))
    }

    /// The [[Address]] of the Exception object that the value is, if it is the wrapper of one.
    pub(crate) fn address_of_value(value: Value) -> Option<u64> {
        implementation_of_value::<Self>(value).map(|exception| exception.address.0)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-exception-getarg
    pub(crate) fn get_arg(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, exception_tag: Ref<Tag>, index: u32) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let store = Agent::the(vm).store();

        // 1. If this.[[Type]] is not equal to exceptionTag.[[Address]],
        //     1. Throw a TypeError.
        if self.tag.0 != exception_tag.address() {
            return Err(WebIdlException::type_error("The exception does not have this tag"));
        }

        // 2. Let payload be this.[[Payload]].
        let payload = store.exception_values(self.address.0);

        // 3. If index ≥ payload's size,
        //     1. Throw a RangeError.
        let Some(&value) = payload.get(index as usize) else {
            return Err(WebIdlException::RangeError(Utf16String::from_utf8(&format!(
                "The exception has {} values",
                payload.len()
            ))));
        };

        // 4. Let [types] → [] be tag_type(store, exceptionTag.[[Address]]).
        // 5. If types[index] matches v128 or exnref,
        //     1. Throw a TypeError.
        // 6. Return ToJSValue(payload[index]).
        // NB: ToJSValue throws the TypeError for v128 and exnref.
        let ty = store.tag(exception_tag.address()).ty.params[index as usize];
        Ok(to_js_value(vm, value, ty)?)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-exception-is
    pub(crate) fn is(&self, _: &mut CallContext, exception_tag: Ref<Tag>) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. If this.[[Type]] is not equal to exceptionTag.[[Address]],
        //     1. Return false.
        // 2. Return true.
        Ok(self.tag.0 == exception_tag.address())
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-exception-stack
    pub(crate) fn stack(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Utf16String>> {
        // 1. Return this.[[Stack]].
        Ok(self.stack.clone())
    }
}

//! Exported Functions, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#exported-function, and the host functions that
//! JavaScript functions become when a module imports them, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-host-function

use core::ffi::c_void;
use std::rc::Rc;

use ak::{Utf16FlyString, Utf16String};
use libjs_rust::api::{
    Attribute, DeferGc, ErrorKind, ErrorType, FunctionObject, Gc, MarkedVec, Must, NativeFunction, Object,
    PrimitiveString, PropertyAttributes, PropertyKey, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value, Visitor, Vm, call,
    get_iterator_from_method_impl, iterator_to_list,
};

use libwasm_engine::runtime::{
    FunctionAddress, FunctionInstance, FunctionKind, HostCallback, HostFunction, Store, Trap, Value as WasmValue,
};

use crate::web_assembly::exception::Exception;

    EXTERNREF, matches_v128_or_exnref, results_to_js_value, to_js_value, to_webassembly_value,

    Agent, EntityRef, WasmValues, gc_visitor_visit_cell, host_object, set_host_object, throw_of_trap,

/// The internal slots of an Exported Function: its [[FunctionAddress]], and the type of its function.
struct ExportedFunction {
    function: EntityRef<FunctionInstance>,
    ty: FuncType,
    use_stack_slots: bool,
}

const STACK_SLOT_CAPACITY: usize = 8;

// SAFETY: The type holds no cells, so the function is the one cell the slots reach.
unsafe impl Trace for ExportedFunction {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        self.function.trace(visitor);
    }
}

/// The value of the function's [[FunctionAddress]] internal slot, if it has one and is therefore an Exported Function.
pub(crate) fn exported_function_address(function: Gc<Object>) -> Option<FunctionAddress> {
    NativeFunction::captures_if::<ExportedFunction>(&function).map(|function| function.function.0)
}

/// The name of the WebAssembly function, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#name-of-the-webassembly-function
fn name_of_webassembly_function(store: &Store, function: FunctionAddress) -> Utf16FlyString {
    // 1. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
    // 2. Let funcinst be store.funcs[funcaddr].
    let index = match &store.function(function).kind {
        // 3. If funcinst is of the form {type functype, hostcode hostfunc},
        //     1. Assert: hostfunc is a JavaScript object and IsCallable(hostfunc) is true.
        //     2. Let index be the index of the host function funcaddr.
        // SAFETY: The data of the browser's host functions, the steps of a JavaScript function or of a builtin, is the
        //         index of the host function.
        FunctionKind::Host(steps) => unsafe { *steps.user_data().cast::<u32>() },
        // 4. Otherwise,
        //     1. Let moduleinst be funcinst.module.
        //     2. Assert: funcaddr is contained in moduleinst.funcaddrs.
        //     3. Let index be the index of moduleinst.funcaddrs where funcaddr is found.
        FunctionKind::Wasm { index, .. } => *index,
    };

    // 5. Return ! ToString(index).
    Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(&index.to_string())
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#a-new-exported-function
pub(crate) fn create_exported_function(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, function: FunctionAddress) -> Gc<NativeFunction> {
    if let Some(object) = host_object::<NativeFunction>(function.cell()) {
        return object;
    }

    // 5. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
    let store = Agent::the(vm).store();
    let ty = store.function(function).ty.clone();
    let arity = ty.params.len() as i32;
    let name = name_of_webassembly_function(store, function);
    let use_stack_slots = matches!(store.function(function).kind, FunctionKind::Wasm { .. })
        && ty.params.len() <= STACK_SLOT_CAPACITY
        && ty.results.len() <= STACK_SLOT_CAPACITY
        && ty
            .params
            .iter()
            .chain(&ty.results)
            .all(|ty| matches!(ty, ValType::I32 | ValType::I64 | ValType::F32 | ValType::F64));

    // NB: The function has its name on call stacks too, as a HostFunction of the C++ API would.
    let object = NativeFunction::create_with_name(
        vm,
        realm,
        &name,
        ExportedFunction {
            function: EntityRef(function),
            ty,
            use_stack_slots,
        },
        |vm: &Vm, function: &ExportedFunction| call_an_exported_function(vm, function),
    );
    let configurable = PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::CONFIGURABLE);
    object.define_direct_property(vm, &vm.names.length, Value::from_i32(arity), configurable);
    let name_value = Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create(vm, Utf16String::from(&name)));
    object.define_direct_property(vm, &vm.names.name, name_value, configurable);
    object.set_initial_name(name);

    set_host_object(function.cell(), object);

    object
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#call-an-exported-function
fn call_an_exported_function(vm: &Vm, function: &ExportedFunction) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    // 1. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
    // 2. Let functype be func_type(store, funcaddr).
    // 3. Let func parameters → results be the expansion of functype.
    // NB: The slots keep functype, which never changes.
    let FuncType {
        params: parameters,
        results,
    } = &function.ty;

    // Numeric values need no GC roots. Keep small signatures on the stack and pass their slots directly to the
    // engine, avoiding the traced containers and temporary vectors of the general path. Convert arguments in
    // JavaScript order even though the engine's operand stack stores them in reverse order: conversion can run JS.
    if function.use_stack_slots {
        let mut argument_slots = [0; STACK_SLOT_CAPACITY];
        for (i, &ty) in parameters.iter().enumerate() {
            let value = to_webassembly_value(vm, vm.argument(i), ty)?;
            argument_slots[parameters.len() - i - 1] = value.to_slots().0[0];
        }
        let mut result_slots = [0; STACK_SLOT_CAPACITY];
        Agent::the(vm)
            .store()
            .invoke_slots(
                function.function.0,
                &argument_slots[..parameters.len()],
                &mut result_slots[..results.len()],
            )
            .map_err(|trap| throw_of_trap(vm, trap))?;
        let mut values = [WasmValue::I32(0); STACK_SLOT_CAPACITY];
        for (i, &ty) in results.iter().enumerate() {
            values[i] = WasmValue::from_slots(ty, &result_slots[results.len() - i - 1..]);
        }
        return results_to_js_value(vm, &values[..results.len()], results);
    }

    // 4. If any type in parameters or results matches v128 or exnref, throw a TypeError.
    // Note: the above error is thrown each time the [[Call]] method is invoked.
    if parameters.iter().chain(results).any(|&ty| matches_v128_or_exnref(ty)) {
        return vm.throw_completion_with_message(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            "Cannot call a WebAssembly function with v128 or exnref parameters or results from JavaScript".to_string(),
        );
    }

    // 5. Let args be « ».
    // NB: The converted arguments may refer to new cells, which the cell of the arguments keeps alive during the call.
    let args = WasmValues::allocate(vm);
    let arg_traces = WasmValues::traces_of(vm, parameters);

    // 6. Let i be 0.
    // 7. For each t of parameters,
    for (i, &t) in parameters.iter().enumerate() {
        // 1. If argValues's size > i, let arg be argValues[i].
        // 2. Otherwise, let arg be undefined.
        let arg = vm.argument(i);

        // 3. Append ? ToWebAssemblyValue(arg, t) to args.
        let arg = to_webassembly_value(vm, arg, t)?;
        args.push(arg, arg_traces[i]);

        // 4. Set i to i + 1.
    }

    // NB: The results may refer to new cells, which the cell of the results keeps alive from when the call returns them.
    let ret = WasmValues::allocate(vm);

    // 8. Let (store, ret) be the result of func_invoke(store, funcaddr, args).
    // 9. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
    let result = Agent::the(vm).store().invoke(function.function.0, &args.values());
    // NB: Using the Gc after the call keeps the arguments where the conservative scan finds them until it has returned.
    core::hint::black_box(args);

    // 10. If ret is error, throw an exception. This exception should be a WebAssembly RuntimeError exception, unless
    //     otherwise indicated by the WebAssembly error mapping.
    // 11. If ret is of the form exception exnaddr, then
    // NB: throw_of_trap() throws what an error or an exception throws.
    match result {
        Ok(values) => ret.set(vm, values, results),
        Err(trap) => return Err(throw_of_trap(vm, trap)),
    }

    // 12. Let outArity be the size of ret.
    // 13. If outArity is 0, return undefined.
    // 14. Otherwise, if outArity is 1, return ToJSValue(ret[0]).
    // 15. Otherwise,
    //     1. Let values be « ».
    //     2. For each r of ret,
    //         1. Append ToJSValue(r) to values.
    //     3. Return CreateArrayFromList(values).
    let result = results_to_js_value(vm, &ret.values(), results);
    // NB: Using the Gc after the conversion keeps the results where the conservative scan finds them until it is done.
    core::hint::black_box(ret);
    result
}

/// The steps of a host function that a JavaScript function becomes, and the index of the host function.
struct HostFunctionSteps {
    function: Gc<FunctionObject>,
    ty: FuncType,
    index: u32,
    use_stack_arguments: bool,
}

impl HostFunction for HostFunctionSteps {
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-host-function
    // NB: The store the engine passes is the agent's. The JavaScript function reaches it through the agent as well,
    //     and may call back into WebAssembly, so the steps reach it the same way and never through both at once.
    fn call(&self, _: &mut Store, arguments: &[WasmValue]) -> Result<Vec<WasmValue>, Trap> {
        let agent = Agent::current();
        let vm = agent.vm();
        // FIXME: The settings steps around the call.
        let result = run_a_host_function(vm, self.function, &self.ty, arguments, self.use_stack_arguments);

        let throw = match result {
            Ok(results) => return Ok(results),
            Err(throw) => throw,
        };
        let value = throw.value();

        if let Some(exception) = Exception::address_of_value(value) {
            return Err(Trap::UncaughtException(exception));
        }

        // 3. Otherwise,
        //     1. Let type be the JavaScript exception tag.
        //     2. Let payload be ! ToWebAssemblyValue(v, externref).
        //     3. Let (store, address) be exn_alloc(store, type, « payload »).
        // NB: The exception is v again once it leaves WebAssembly.
        let payload = to_webassembly_value(vm, value, EXTERNREF).must();
        Err(Trap::UncaughtException(
            agent.store().allocate_exception_with_values(agent.js_tag(), &[payload]),
        ))
    }

    fn visit_edges(&self, visitor: &StoreVisitor) {
        // SAFETY: The visitor is live while it visits, and the function is a cell of its heap.
        unsafe { gc_visitor_visit_cell(visitor.raw(), self.function.as_ptr().cast()) };
    }

    fn user_data(&self) -> *mut c_void {
        core::ptr::from_ref(&self.index).cast_mut().cast()
    }
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#run-a-host-function
fn run_a_host_function(
    vm: &Vm,
    function: Gc<FunctionObject>,
    functype: &FuncType,
    arguments: &[WasmValue],
    use_stack_arguments: bool,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Vec<WasmValue>> {
    // 1. Let func parameters → results be the expansion of functype.
    let FuncType {
        params: parameters,
        results,
    } = functype;

    // 2. If any type in parameters or results matches v128 or exnref, throw a TypeError.
    if parameters.iter().chain(results).any(|&ty| matches_v128_or_exnref(ty)) {
        return vm.throw_completion_with_message(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            "Cannot call a JavaScript function with v128 or exnref parameters or results from WebAssembly".to_string(),
        );
    }

    let callee = Value::from_object(function.upcast::<Object>());

    // OPTIMIZATION: These conversions produce only Numbers, so the arguments need no GC roots.
    let ret = if use_stack_arguments {
        // 3. Let jsArguments be « ».
        let mut js_arguments = [Value::UNDEFINED; STACK_SLOT_CAPACITY];

        // 4. For each arg of arguments,
        for (i, (arg, &parameter)) in arguments.iter().zip(parameters).enumerate() {
            // 1. Append ToJSValue(arg) to jsArguments.
            js_arguments[i] = to_js_value(vm, *arg, parameter)?;
        }

        // 5. Let ret be ? Call(func, undefined, jsArguments).
        call(vm, callee, Value::UNDEFINED, &js_arguments[..arguments.len()])?
    } else {
        // 3. Let jsArguments be « ».
        let js_arguments = MarkedVec::with_capacity(vm, arguments.len());

        // 4. For each arg of arguments,
        for (arg, &parameter) in arguments.iter().zip(parameters) {
            // 1. Append ToJSValue(arg) to jsArguments.
            js_arguments.push(to_js_value(vm, *arg, parameter)?);
        }

        // 5. Let ret be ? Call(func, undefined, jsArguments).
        call(vm, callee, Value::UNDEFINED, &js_arguments.values())?
    };

    // 6. Let resultsSize be results's size.
    // 7. If resultsSize is 0, return « ».
    if results.is_empty() {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }

    // 8. Otherwise, if resultsSize is 1, return « ? ToWebAssemblyValue(ret, results[0]) ».
    if results.len() == 1 {
        let value = to_webassembly_value(vm, ret, results[0])?;
        // OPTIMIZATION: No further conversion or GC allocation can occur before the engine receives this value.
        return Ok(vec![value]);
    }

    // NB: Converting subsequent results can collect garbage, so keep earlier reference results in a traced cell.
    let converted = WasmValues::allocate(vm);
    let result_traces = WasmValues::traces_of(vm, results);

    // 9. Otherwise,
    {
        // 1. Let method be ? GetMethod(ret, %Symbol.iterator%).
        let method = ret.get_method(vm, &PropertyKey::from(vm.well_known_symbols().iterator))?;

        // 2. If method is undefined, throw a TypeError.
        let Some(method) = method else {
            return vm.throw_completion(
                ErrorKind::TypeError,
                ErrorType::NotIterable,
                &[&ret.to_utf16_string_without_side_effects()],
            );
        };

        // 3. Let values be ? IteratorToList(? GetIteratorFromMethod(ret, method)).
        let iterator = get_iterator_from_method_impl(vm, ret, method)?;
        let values = iterator_to_list(vm, &iterator)?;

        // 4. Let wasmValues be a new, empty list.
        // 5. If values's size is not resultsSize, throw a TypeError exception.
        if values.len() != results.len() {
            return vm.throw_completion_with_message(
                ErrorKind::TypeError,
                format!(
                    "Invalid number of return values for multi-value wasm return of {} objects",
                    results.len()
                ),
            );
        }

        // 6. For each value and resultType in values and results, paired linearly,
        for (index, &result_type) in results.iter().enumerate() {
            // 1. Append ? ToWebAssemblyValue(value, resultType) to wasmValues.
            let value = to_webassembly_value(
                vm,
                values.get(index).expect("the list has a value per result"),
                result_type,
            )?;
            converted.push(value, result_traces[index]);
        }

        // 7. Return wasmValues.
    }
    Ok(converted.take())
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-host-function
pub(crate) fn create_host_function(vm: &Vm, function: Gc<FunctionObject>, ty: FuncType, index: u32) -> FunctionAddress {
    // 1. Assert: IsCallable(func).
    // 2. Let stored settings be the incumbent settings object.
    // 3. Let hostfunc be a host function which performs the following steps when called with arguments arguments:
    // NB: The function's entity visits what the steps hold, which keeps the JavaScript function alive with it. Until
    //     the entity holds them, nothing collects garbage.
    // 4. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
    // 6. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
    DeferGc::scope(vm, |_| {
        #[cfg_attr(
            ladybird_gc_lints,
            expect(
                gc_container_on_stack,
                reason = "the function's entity visits the steps through HostFunction::visit_edges()"
            )
        )]
        let steps: HostCallback = Rc::new(HostFunctionSteps {
            function,
            use_stack_arguments: ty.params.len() <= STACK_SLOT_CAPACITY
                && ty
                    .params
                    .iter()
                    .all(|ty| matches!(ty, ValType::I32 | ValType::F32 | ValType::F64)),
            ty: ty.clone(),
            index,
        });
        Agent::the(vm).store().allocate_host_function(ty, steps)
    })
}

fn throw_type_error(message: &str) -> JSCompletion {
    let vm = Agent::current().vm();
    completion_into_abi(vm.throw_completion_with_message::<()>(ErrorKind::TypeError, message.to_string()))
}

}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-new-exported-gc-object
pub(crate) fn create_exported_gc_object(vm: &Vm, reference: u64) -> Gc<Object> {
    // 1. Assert: objectaddr is a struct or array address.
    // 2. Let map be the current agent's associated exported GC object cache.
    // 3. If map[objectaddr] exists, return map[objectaddr].
    let cell = reference as *mut u8;
    if let Some(object) = host_object::<Object>(cell) {
        return object;
    }

    // 4. Let object be a new Exported GC Object, with [[ObjectAddress]] set to objectaddr and [[ObjectKind]] set to
    //    objectKind.
    let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a conversion runs in a realm");
    // SAFETY: The class is of kind JS_HOST_CLASS_OBJECT, and the host data is the live cell of the struct or array.
    let object = unsafe {
        HostObject::create(
            vm,
            realm,
            &EXPORTED_GC_OBJECT_CLASS,
            None,
            None,
            Some(NonNull::new_unchecked(cell.cast())),
        )
    }
    .upcast::<Object>();
    // NB: [[IsExtensible]] is always false, which caches of property additions rely on the shape to tell.
    object.set_non_extensible(vm);

    // 5. Set map[objectaddr] to object.
    set_host_object(cell, object);

    // 6. Return object.
    object
}

/// The value of the object's [[ObjectAddress]] internal slot, if it has one and is therefore an Exported GC Object.
pub(crate) fn exported_gc_object_address(object: Gc<Object>) -> Option<u64> {
    if !is_host_instance_of(&object, &EXPORTED_GC_OBJECT_CLASS) {
        return None;
    }
    host_data_of(&object).map(|cell| cell.as_ptr() as u64)
}

//! Global, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#globals

use libjs_rust::api::{Trace, Value, Vm};
use libwasm_engine::runtime::{GlobalAddress, GlobalInstance};
use libwasm_engine::types::{GlobalType, HeapType, RefType, ValType};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::web_assembly::values::{default_webassembly_value, to_js_value, to_webassembly_value};
use crate::web_assembly::{Agent, EntityRef, host_object, implementation_of_value, set_host_object};

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#enumdef-valuetype
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum ValueType {
    I32,
    I64,
    F32,
    F64,
    V128,
    Externref,
    Anyfunc,
}

impl ValueType {
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#tovaluetype
    pub(crate) fn to_value_type(self) -> ValType {
        let reference = |heap| ValType::Ref(RefType { nullable: true, heap });
        match self {
            Self::I32 => ValType::I32,
            Self::I64 => ValType::I64,
            Self::F32 => ValType::F32,
            Self::F64 => ValType::F64,
            Self::V128 => ValType::V128,
            Self::Anyfunc => reference(HeapType::Func),
            Self::Externref => reference(HeapType::Extern),
        }
    }
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dictdef-globaldescriptor
pub(crate) struct GlobalDescriptor {
    pub(crate) value: ValueType,
    pub(crate) mutable: bool,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Global {
    // [[Global]]
    address: EntityRef<GlobalInstance>,
}

impl Wrappable for Global {}

impl Global {
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-global-global
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        descriptor: GlobalDescriptor,
        v: Option<Value>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Let mutable be descriptor["mutable"].
        let mutable = descriptor.mutable;

        // 2. Let valuetype be ToValueType(descriptor["value"]).
        let value_type = descriptor.value.to_value_type();

        //     1. Throw a TypeError.
        if value_type == ValType::V128 {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("V128 is not supported as a global value type"));
        }

        // 4. If v is missing,
        //     1. Let value be DefaultValue(valuetype).
        //     2. Assert: value is not error.
        // 5. Otherwise,
        //     1. Let value be ? ToWebAssemblyValue(v, valuetype).
        let value = match v {
            None => default_webassembly_value(vm, value_type).expect("ToValueType gives types with a default value"),
            Some(v) => to_webassembly_value(vm, v, value_type)?,
        };

        // 6. If mutable is true, let globaltype be var valuetype; otherwise, let globaltype be const valuetype.
        // 7. Let store be the current agent’s associated store.
        // 8. Let (store, globaladdr) be global_alloc(store, globaltype, value).
        // 9. Set the current agent’s associated store to store.
        let global = Agent::the(vm).store().allocate_global(
            GlobalType {
                value: value_type,
                mutable,
            },
            value,
        );

        // 10. Initialize this from globaladdr.
        Ok(Self::initialize(vm, global))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#initialize-a-global-object
    fn initialize(vm: &Vm, global: GlobalAddress) -> Ref<Self> {
        assert!(host_object::<()>(global.cell()).is_none());

        let object = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            address: EntityRef(global),
        });

        set_host_object(global.cell(), object);
        object
    }

    /// The Global object of the global, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-global-object
    pub(crate) fn from_address(vm: &Vm, global: GlobalAddress) -> Ref<Self> {
        if let Some(object) = host_object(global.cell()) {
            return object;
        }

        Self::initialize(vm, global)
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_value(value: Value) -> Option<Ref<Self>> {
        implementation_of_value(value)
    }

    pub(crate) fn address(&self) -> GlobalAddress {
        self.address.0
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#getglobalvalue
    fn get_global_value(&self, cx: &CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        // 1. Let store be the current agent’s associated store.
        // 2. Let globaladdr be global.[[Global]].
        // 3. Let globaltype be global_type(store, globaladdr).
        let global = Agent::the(cx.vm()).store().global(self.address());

        if global.ty.value == ValType::V128 {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("V128 is not supported as a global value type"));
        }

        // 5. Let value be global_read(store, globaladdr).
        Ok(to_js_value(cx.vm(), global.get(), global.ty.value)?)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-global-value
    pub(crate) fn value(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        self.get_global_value(cx)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-global-value
    pub(crate) fn set_value(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, value: Value) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let store be the current agent’s associated store.
        // 2. Let globaladdr be this.[[Global]].
        // 3. Let mut valuetype be global_type(store, globaladdr).
        let ty = Agent::the(cx.vm()).store().global(self.address()).ty;

        if ty.value == ValType::V128 {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Cannot set the value of a V128 global"));
        }

        // 5. If mut is const, throw a TypeError.
        if !ty.mutable {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Cannot set the value of a const global"));
        }

        // 6. Let value be ? ToWebAssemblyValue(the given value, valuetype).
        let value = to_webassembly_value(cx.vm(), value, ty.value)?;

        // 7. Let store be global_write(store, globaladdr, value).
        // 8. If store is error, throw a RangeError exception.
        // 9. Set the current agent’s associated store to store.
        // NB: Writing cannot fail, as the value has the global's type.
        Agent::the(cx.vm()).store().global_mut(self.address()).set(value);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-global-valueof
    pub(crate) fn value_of(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        self.get_global_value(cx)
    }
}

//! Instance, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#instances

use core::cell::RefCell;

use ak::Utf16FlyString;
use libjs_rust::api::{
    Attribute, EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, ErrorKind, ErrorType, Gc, IntegrityLevel, MarkedVec, Must,
    Object, PropertyAttributes, PropertyKey, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value, Visitor, Vm,
};
use libwasm_engine::module::ImportDescription;
use libwasm_engine::runtime::{ExternValue, Instance as CoreInstance, InstanceAddress};
use libwasm_engine::types::{FuncType, GlobalType, HeapType, RefType, ValType};

use crate::bindings::conversions::UsvString;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, wrap};
use crate::bindings::realm_data::wrapper_world_of;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};

    create_exported_function, create_host_function, exported_function_address,
};
