#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Instance {
    // [[Instance]]
    instance: EntityRef<CoreInstance>,
    // [[Exports]]
    exports: Gc<Object>,
}

impl Wrappable for Instance {}

/// The imports of a module, which keep the entities they are alive while they wait for an instance to hold them: the
/// host functions and globals made for the imports are referenced from nowhere else, reading the imports runs user
/// code (getters, valueOf) that may collect garbage, and an asynchronous instantiation holds them until its task runs.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Imports(pub(crate) RefCell<Vec<ExternValue>>);

static IMPORTS_CLASS: EmbedderClass<Imports> = EmbedderClass::new("WebAssemblyImports");

impl EmbedderValue for Imports {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &IMPORTS_CLASS;
}

// SAFETY: Visits the cell of every entity of the list.
unsafe impl Trace for Imports {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        for &import in self.0.borrow().iter() {
            match import {
                ExternValue::Function(address) => EntityRef(address).trace(visitor),
                ExternValue::Table(address) => EntityRef(address).trace(visitor),
                ExternValue::Memory(address) => EntityRef(address).trace(visitor),
                ExternValue::Global(address) => EntityRef(address).trace(visitor),
                ExternValue::Tag(address) => EntityRef(address).trace(visitor),
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Imports {
    pub(crate) fn push(&self, import: ExternValue) {
        self.0.borrow_mut().push(import);
    }
}

/// A value type of the module, in the store's terms (see Store::module_type_identities()).
pub(crate) fn value_type_in_store(vm: &Vm, module: &CompiledModule, ty: ValType) -> ValType {
    let ValType::Ref(RefType {
        nullable,
        heap: HeapType::Concrete(index),
    }) = ty
    else {
        return ty;
    };
    let identities = Agent::the(vm).store().module_type_identities_of(module);
    ValType::Ref(RefType {
        nullable,
        heap: HeapType::Concrete(identities[index as usize]),
    })
}

/// The function type at `type_index` of the module, in the store's terms.
pub(crate) fn function_type_in_store(vm: &Vm, module: &CompiledModule, type_index: u32) -> FuncType {
    let ty = module.types[type_index as usize]
        .as_func()
        .expect("the type of a function import is a function type");
    FuncType {
        params: ty
            .params
            .iter()
            .map(|&ty| value_type_in_store(vm, module, ty))
            .collect(),
        results: ty
            .results
            .iter()
            .map(|&ty| value_type_in_store(vm, module, ty))
            .collect(),
    }
}

/// The global type of the module, in the store's terms.
pub(crate) fn global_type_in_store(vm: &Vm, module: &CompiledModule, ty: GlobalType) -> GlobalType {
    GlobalType {
        value: value_type_in_store(vm, module, ty.value),
        mutable: ty.mutable,
    }
}

fn link_error<T>(vm: &Vm, message: &str) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T> {
    let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("reading the imports runs in a realm");
    Err(throw_webassembly_error(vm, realm, WebAssemblyError::Link, message))
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#read-the-imports
pub(crate) fn read_the_imports(
    vm: &Vm,
    module: &CompiledModule,
    import_object: Option<Gc<Object>>,
    builtin_set_names: &[UsvString],
    imported_string_module: Option<&UsvString>,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<EmbedderCell<Imports>>> {
    // 1. If module_imports(module) is not empty, and importObject is missing, throw a TypeError exception.
    if !module.imports.is_empty() && import_object.is_none() {
        return vm.throw_completion_with_message(
            ErrorKind::TypeError,
            "ImportObject must be provided when module has imports".to_string(),
        );
    }

    // 2. Let builtinOrStringImports be the ordered map «[ ]».
    // NB: The keys are UTF-8, as the module names of imports are.
    let builtin_or_string_imports = MarkedVec::<(String, Gc<Object>)>::new(vm);
    let contains_key = |key: &str| {
        builtin_or_string_imports
            .values()
            .iter()
            .any(|(builtin_or_string_import, _)| builtin_or_string_import == key)
    };

    // 3. For each builtinSetName of builtinSetNames,
    for builtin_set_name in builtin_set_names {
        // 3.1. Let builtinSetQualifiedName be builtinSetName prefixed with "wasm:"
        let builtin_set_qualified_name = format!("wasm:{}", builtin_set_name.to_utf8());

        // 3.2. Assert: builtinOrStringImports does not contain builtinSetQualifiedName
        assert!(!contains_key(&builtin_set_qualified_name));

        // 3.3. If builtinSetName does not refer to a builtin set, then continue.
        if !refers_to_a_builtin_set(builtin_set_name) {
            continue;
        }

        // 3.4. Let exportsObject be the result of instantiate a builtin set with builtinSetName
        let exports_object = instantiate_a_builtin_set(vm, builtin_set_name);

        // 3.5. Set builtinOrStringImports[builtinSetQualifiedName] to exportsObject
        builtin_or_string_imports.push((builtin_set_qualified_name, exports_object));
    }

    // 4. If importedStringModule is not null,
    if let Some(imported_string_module) = imported_string_module {
        // 4.1. Let exportsObject be the result of instantiate imported strings with module and importedStringModule
        let exports_object = instantiate_imported_strings(vm, module, imported_string_module);

        // 4.2. Set builtinOrStringImports[importedStringModule] to exportsObject
        let imported_string_module = imported_string_module.to_utf8();
        let existing = builtin_or_string_imports
            .values()
            .iter()
            .position(|(builtin_or_string_import, _)| *builtin_or_string_import == imported_string_module);
        match existing {
            Some(index) => builtin_or_string_imports.set(index, (imported_string_module, exports_object)),
            None => builtin_or_string_imports.push((imported_string_module, exports_object)),
        }
    }

    // 5. Let imports be « ».
    let imports = IMPORTS_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| Imports::default());
    // NB: A module without an import object has no imports (step 1).
    let Some(import_object) = import_object else {
        return Ok(imports);
    };
    let mut imported_function_count = 0;

    // 6. For each (moduleName, componentName, externtype) of module_imports(module),
    for import in &module.imports {
        let module_name = PropertyKey::from(Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(&import.module));
        let component_name = PropertyKey::from(Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(&import.name));

        let builtin_or_string_import = builtin_or_string_imports
            .values()
            .iter()
            .find(|(builtin_or_string_import, _)| *builtin_or_string_import == import.module)
            .map(|&(_, exports_object)| exports_object);
        let value = match builtin_or_string_import {
            // 6.1. If builtinOrStringImports[moduleName] exists,
            Some(builtin_or_string_import) => {
                // 6.1.1. Let o be builtinOrStringImports[moduleName].
                let mut value = Value::from_object(builtin_or_string_import);

                // 6.1.2. If o is not an Object or if ? HasProperty(o, componentName) is false,
                if !value.is_object() || !value.as_object().has_property(vm, &component_name)? {
                    // 6.1.2.1. Set o to ? Get(importObject, moduleName).
                    value = import_object.get(vm, &module_name)?;
                }
                value
            }
            // 6.2. Else,
            None => {
                // 6.2.1. Let o be ? Get(importObject, moduleName).
                import_object.get(vm, &module_name)?
            }
        };

        // 6.3. If o is not an Object, throw a TypeError exception.
        if !value.is_object() {
            return vm.throw_completion(
                ErrorKind::TypeError,
                ErrorType::IsNotAEvaluatedFrom,
                &[
                    &value.to_utf16_string_without_side_effects(),
                    &"Object",
                    &format!("[wasm import object][\"{}\"]", import.module),
                ],
            );
        }

        // 6.4. Let v be ? Get(o, componentName).
        let v = value.as_object().get(vm, &component_name)?;

        match &import.description {
            // 6.5. If externtype is of the form func functype,
            ImportDescription::Function(type_index) => {
                // 6.5.1. If IsCallable(v) is false, throw a LinkError exception.
                if !v.is_function() {
                    let message = ErrorType::IsNotAEvaluatedFrom.message(&[
                        &v.to_utf16_string_without_side_effects(),
                        &"function",
                        &format!("[wasm import object][\"{}\"]", import.name),
                    ]);
                    return link_error(vm, &String::from_utf16_lossy(&message.to_utf16()));
                }

                // 6.5.2. If v has a [[FunctionAddress]] internal slot, and therefore is an Exported Function,
                //     6.5.2.1. Let funcaddr be the value of v's [[FunctionAddress]] internal slot.
                // 6.5.3. Otherwise,
                //     6.5.3.1. Create a host function from v and functype, and let funcaddr be the result.
                //     6.5.3.2. Let index be the number of external functions in imports. This value index is known as the index of the host function funcaddr.
                let function = exported_function_address(v.as_object()).unwrap_or_else(|| {
                    create_host_function(
                        vm,
                        v.as_function(),
                        function_type_in_store(vm, module, *type_index),
                        imported_function_count,
                    )
                });

                // 6.5.4. Let externfunc be the external value func funcaddr.
                // 6.5.5. Append externfunc to imports.
                imports.push(ExternValue::Function(function));
                imported_function_count += 1;
            }
            // 6.6. If externtype is of the form global mut valtype,
            ImportDescription::Global(ty) => {
                let ty = global_type_in_store(vm, module, *ty);
                // 6.6.1. If v implements Global,
                //     6.6.1.1. Let globaladdr be v.[[Global]].
                let global = if let Some(global) = Global::from_value(v) {
                    global.address()
                }
                // 6.6.2. Otherwise,
                else {
                    // 6.6.2.1. If valtype is i64 and v is not a BigInt, throw a LinkError exception.
                    if ty.value == ValType::I64 && !v.is_bigint() {
                        return link_error(vm, "Import resolution attempted to use a non-BigInt for an i64 global");
                    }
                    // 6.6.2.2. If valtype is one of i32, f32 or f64 and v is not a Number, throw a LinkError exception.
                    if matches!(ty.value, ValType::I32 | ValType::F32 | ValType::F64) && !v.is_number() {
                        return link_error(
                            vm,
                            "Import resolution attempted to use a non-Number for a numeric global",
                        );
                    }
                    // 6.6.2.3. If valtype is v128, throw a LinkError exception.
                    if ty.value == ValType::V128 {
                        return link_error(vm, "Import resolution attempted to use a value for a V128 global");
                    }
                    // 6.6.2.4. If mut is var, throw a LinkError exception.
                    if ty.mutable {
                        return link_error(vm, "Import resolution attempted to use a value for a mutable global");
                    }
                    // 6.6.2.5. Let value be ToWebAssemblyValue(v, valtype). If this throws a TypeError, catch it, and throw
                    //          a LinkError exception.
                    let Ok(value) = to_webassembly_value(vm, v, ty.value) else {
                        return link_error(
                            vm,
                            "Import resolution attempted to use a value of the wrong type for a global",
                        );
                    };
                    // 6.6.2.6. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
                    // 6.6.2.7. Let (store, globaladdr) be global_alloc(store, const valtype, value).
                    // 6.6.2.8. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
                    Agent::the(vm).store().allocate_global(
                        GlobalType {
                            value: ty.value,
                            mutable: false,
                        },
                        value,
                    )
                };

                // 6.6.3. Let externglobal be global globaladdr.
                // 6.6.4. Append externglobal to imports.
                imports.push(ExternValue::Global(global));
            }
            // 6.7. If externtype is of the form mem memtype,
            ImportDescription::Memory(_) => {
                // 6.7.1. If v does not implement Memory, throw a LinkError exception.
                let Some(memory) = Memory::from_value(v) else {
                    return link_error(vm, "Expected an instance of WebAssembly.Memory for a memory import");
                };

                // 6.7.2. Let externmem be the external value mem v.[[Memory]].
                // 6.7.3. Append externmem to imports.
                imports.push(ExternValue::Memory(memory.address()));
            }
            // 6.8. If externtype is of the form table tabletype,
            ImportDescription::Table(_) => {
                // 6.8.1. If v does not implement Table, throw a LinkError exception.
                let Some(table) = Table::from_value(v) else {
                    return link_error(vm, "Expected an instance of WebAssembly.Table for a table import");
                };

                // 6.8.2. Let tableaddr be v.[[Table]].
                // 6.8.3. Let externtable be the external value table tableaddr.
                // 6.8.4. Append externtable to imports.
                imports.push(ExternValue::Table(table.address()));
            }
            // 6.9. If externtype is of the form tag attribute functype,
            ImportDescription::Tag(_) => {
                // 6.9.1. Assert: attribute is exception.
                // 6.9.2. If v does not implement Tag, throw a LinkError exception.
                let Some(tag) = Tag::from_value(v) else {
                    return link_error(vm, "Expected an instance of WebAssembly.Tag for a tag import");
                };

                // 6.9.3. Let tagaddr be v.[[Address]].
                // 6.9.4. Let externtag be the external value tag tagaddr.
                // 6.9.5. Append externtag to imports.
                imports.push(ExternValue::Tag(tag.address()));
            }
        }
    }

    // 7. Return imports.
    Ok(imports)
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/index.html#instantiate-the-core-of-a-webassembly-module
pub(crate) fn instantiate_the_core_of_a_webassembly_module(
    vm: &Vm,
    module: &CompiledModule,
    imports: &Imports,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<InstanceAddress> {
    // 1. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
    // 2. Let result be module_instantiate(store, module, imports).
    // 3. If result is error, throw an appropriate exception type:
    //     * A LinkError exception for most cases which occur during linking.
    //     * If the error came when running the start function, throw a RuntimeError for most errors which occur from
    //       WebAssembly, or the error object propagated from inner ECMAScript code.
    //     * Another error type if appropriate, for example an out-of-memory exception, as documented in the
    //       WebAssembly error mapping.
    // 4. Let (store, instance) be result.
    // 5. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
    // 6. Return instance.
    let imports = imports.0.borrow().clone();
    Agent::the(vm)
        .store()
        .instantiate(module.clone(), &imports)
        .map_err(|error| throw_of_instantiation_error(vm, error))
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-an-exports-object
fn create_an_exports_object(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, instance: InstanceAddress) -> Gc<Object> {
    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);
    let exports_object = Object::create(vm, realm, None);
    let attributes = PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::WRITABLE | Attribute::ENUMERABLE | Attribute::CONFIGURABLE);

    // NB: Creating the object of an export may reach the store, so nothing of it stays borrowed across the loop.
    let module = Agent::the(vm).store().instance(instance).module.clone();
    for export in &module.exports {
        let Some(value) = Agent::the(vm).store().instance(instance).export(&export.name) else {
            continue;
        };
        let value = match value {
            ExternValue::Function(function) => {
                Value::from_object(create_exported_function(vm, realm, function).upcast::<Object>())
            }
            ExternValue::Global(global) => Value::from_object(wrap(&cx, Global::from_address(vm, global))),
            ExternValue::Memory(memory) => Value::from_object(wrap(&cx, Memory::from_address(vm, memory))),
            ExternValue::Table(table) => Value::from_object(wrap(&cx, Table::from_address(vm, table))),
            ExternValue::Tag(tag) => Value::from_object(wrap(&cx, Tag::from_address(vm, realm, tag))),
        };
        exports_object.define_direct_property(
            vm,
            &PropertyKey::from(Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(&export.name)),
            value,
            attributes,
        );
    }

    exports_object.set_integrity_level(vm, IntegrityLevel::Frozen).must();
    exports_object
}

impl Instance {
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-instance-instance
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        module_object: Ref<Module>,
        import_object: Option<Gc<Object>>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Let builtinSetNames be moduleObject.[[BuiltinSets]].
        let builtin_set_names = module_object.builtin_sets();

        // 2. Let importedStringModule be moduleObject.[[ImportedStringModule]].
        let imported_string_module = module_object.imported_string_module();

        // 3. Let module be moduleObject.[[Module]].
        let module = module_object.compiled_module().clone();

        // 4. Read the imports of module with imports importObject, builtinSetNames, and importedStringModule, and let
        //    imports be the result.
        let imports = read_the_imports(vm, &module, import_object, builtin_set_names, imported_string_module)?;

        // 5. Instantiate the core of a WebAssembly module module with imports, and let instance be the result.
        let instance = instantiate_the_core_of_a_webassembly_module(vm, &module, &imports)?;

        // 6. Initialize this from module and instance.
        Ok(Self::initialize(vm, cx.realm(), instance))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#initialize-an-instance-object
    pub(crate) fn initialize(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, instance: InstanceAddress) -> Self {
        // NB: An instance's exports, like its memories and tables, belong to the realm it was created in.
        Self {
            instance: EntityRef(instance),
            exports: create_an_exports_object(vm, realm, instance),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn address(&self) -> InstanceAddress {
        self.instance.0
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-instance-exports
    pub(crate) fn exports(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<Object>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        assert!(
            wrapper_world_of(vm, cx.realm()) == wrapper_world_of(vm, self.exports.shape().realm()),
            "Reading a WebAssembly instance's exports from another world"
        );
        Ok(self.exports)
    }
}

//! Memory, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#memories, and its shared memories,
//! https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/
//!
//! A Memory object belongs to the agent, as its memory does, while its [[BufferObject]] belongs to a realm: the object
//! has a buffer object of its own in every realm that asks for one, and holds each as the internal slot the
//! specification gives it: "[[BufferObject]] : an ArrayBuffer whose Data Block is identified with the above memory
//! address".

use core::ptr::NonNull;
use std::sync::Arc;

use ak::Utf16String;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferShared, DataBlock, DataBlockStorage, ExternalPrimitiveStorage, ForeignCellSlot, Gc,
    GcRefCell, IntegrityLevel, MarkedVec, Must, PrimitiveString, RawNativeFunctionResult, Realm, ThrowCompletionOr,
    Trace, Value, Vm, detach_array_buffer, same_value,
};
use libwasm_engine::runtime::MemoryAddress;
use libwasm_engine::runtime::memory::{MemoryInstance, SharedMemory};
use libwasm_engine::types::{AddressType, Limits, MemoryType};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_if_abi};
use crate::bindings::structured_data::{Serializable, SerializationReader, SerializationWriter};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::web_assembly::{Agent, EntityRef, PAGE_SIZE, host_object, set_host_object};

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dictdef-memorydescriptor
pub(crate) struct MemoryDescriptor {
    pub(crate) initial: u32,
    pub(crate) maximum: Option<u32>,
    pub(crate) shared: bool,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Memory {
    // [[Memory]]
    address: EntityRef<MemoryInstance>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    shared: bool,
    // [[BufferObject]], one per realm.
    buffer_objects: GcRefCell<Vec<Gc<ArrayBuffer>>>,
}

impl Wrappable for Memory {}

fn detach_key(vm: &Vm) -> Value {
    Value::from_string(PrimitiveString::create_from_utf8(vm, "WebAssembly.Memory"))
}

impl Memory {
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-memory-memory
    pub(crate) fn construct(cx: &mut CallContext, descriptor: MemoryDescriptor) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/index.html#dom-memory-memory
        // 1. Let initial be descriptor["initial"].
        let initial = descriptor.initial;

        // 2. If descriptor["maximum"] exists, let maximum be descriptor["maximum"]; otherwise, let maximum be empty.
        let maximum = descriptor.maximum;

        // 3. If maximum is not empty and maximum < initial, throw a RangeError exception.
        if maximum.is_some_and(|maximum| maximum < initial) {
            return Err(Exception::range_error("Initial is larger than maximum."));
        }

        // 4. Let share be shared if descriptor["shared"] is true and unshared otherwise.
        let share = descriptor.shared;

        // 5. If share is shared and maximum is empty, throw a TypeError exception.
        if share && maximum.is_none() {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Maximum has to be specified for shared memory."));
        }

        // 6. Let memtype be ({ min initial, max maximum }, share).
        let memtype = MemoryType {
            limits: Limits {
                min: u64::from(initial),
                max: maximum.map(u64::from),
                address_type: AddressType::I32,
                shared: share,
            },
        };

        // 7. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
        // 8. Let (store, memaddr) be mem_alloc(store, memtype). If allocation fails, throw a RangeError exception.
        // 9. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
        let memory = Agent::the(cx.vm())
            .store()
            .allocate_memory(memtype)
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::range_error("Wasm Memory allocation failed"))?;

        // 10. Initialize this from memaddr.
        Ok(Self::initialize(cx.vm(), memory))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#initialize-a-memory-object
    fn initialize(vm: &Vm, memory: MemoryAddress) -> Ref<Self> {
        // 1. Let map be the surrounding agent's associated Memory object cache.
        assert!(host_object::<()>(memory.cell()).is_none());

        // NB: The buffer of a realm is created when the realm first asks for it.
        let shared = Agent::the(vm).store().memory(memory).ty.limits.shared;
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            address: EntityRef(memory),
            shared,
            buffer_objects: GcRefCell::default(),
        });

        set_host_object(memory.cell(), object);
        object
    }

    /// The Memory object of the memory, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-memory-object
    pub(crate) fn from_address(vm: &Vm, memory: MemoryAddress) -> Ref<Self> {
        // 1. Let map be the surrounding agent's associated Memory object cache.
        if let Some(object) = host_object(memory.cell()) {
            return object;
        }

        Self::initialize(vm, memory)
    }

    pub(crate) fn address(&self) -> MemoryAddress {
        self.address.0
    }

    /// A new Memory object of the surrounding agent for a shared memory, which another agent may have created. The
    /// agents share the bytes of the memory and its size, and each of them has Memory objects of its own for it.
    fn sharing(vm: &Vm, shared: Arc<SharedMemory>) -> Ref<Self> {
        let memory = Agent::the(vm).store().allocate_memory_sharing(shared);
        Self::initialize(vm, memory)
    }

    fn size(&self, vm: &Vm) -> usize {
        Agent::the(vm).store().memory(self.address()).size()
    }

    fn external_storage(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm, fixed_length: bool) -> ExternalPrimitiveStorage {
        let handle = Agent::the(vm).store().memory(this.address()).primitive_storage_handle();
        let owner = ForeignCellSlot::empty();
        // SAFETY: The memory object is a live cell of the heap, which the slot then keeps alive.
        unsafe { owner.set(Some(NonNull::new_unchecked(this.as_ptr().cast()))) };
        ExternalPrimitiveStorage::new(owner, handle, fixed_length.then(|| this.size(vm)))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/index.html#create-a-fixed-length-memory-buffer
    fn create_a_fixed_length_memory_buffer(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Gc<ArrayBuffer> {
        // 3. If share is shared,
        if this.shared {
            // 1. Let block be a Shared Data Block which is identified with the underlying memory of memaddr.
            // 2. Let buffer be a new SharedArrayBuffer with the internal slots [[ArrayBufferData]] and [[ArrayBufferByteLength]].
            // 3. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferData]] to block.
            // 4. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]] to the length of block.
            // NOTE: ArrayBufferByteLength should contain the original size regardless of growth.
            let block = DataBlock::external(Self::external_storage(this, vm, true), ArrayBufferShared::Yes);
            let buffer = ArrayBuffer::create_from_data_block(vm, realm, block);

            // 5. Perform ! SetIntegrityLevel(buffer, "frozen").
            buffer.set_integrity_level(vm, IntegrityLevel::Frozen).must();

            return buffer;
        }

        // 4. Otherwise,
        //     1. Let block be a Data Block which is identified with the underlying memory of memaddr.
        //     3. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferData]] to block.
        //     4. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]] to the length of block.
        let block = DataBlock::external(Self::external_storage(this, vm, true), ArrayBufferShared::No);
        let buffer = ArrayBuffer::create_from_data_block(vm, realm, block);
        buffer.set_detach_key(detach_key(vm));
        buffer
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-resizable-memory-buffer
    fn create_a_resizable_memory_buffer(
        this: Ref<Self>,
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        max_size: u64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
        // 3. If maxsize > (65536 x 65536),
        if max_size > 65536 * PAGE_SIZE {
            // 1. Throw a RangeError exception.
            return Err(Exception::range_error(
                "Maximum memory length exceeds 65536 * 65536 bytes",
            ));
        }

        // https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/index.html#create-a-resizable-memory-buffer
        // 5. If share is shared,
        if this.shared {
            // 1. Let block be a Shared Data Block which is identified with the underlying memory of memaddr.
            // 2. Let buffer be a new SharedArrayBuffer with the internal slots [[ArrayBufferData]], [[ArrayBufferByteLength]], and [[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]].
            // 3. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferData]] to block.
            // AD-HOC: The threads proposal uses the memory type's minimum for both shared and
            //         non-shared memories, but the upstream spec uses the memory instance's current
            //         size. We assume the upstream spec is correct for both cases.
            // 4. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]] to min.
            let block = DataBlock::external(Self::external_storage(this, vm, false), ArrayBufferShared::Yes);
            let buffer = ArrayBuffer::create_from_data_block(vm, realm, block);

            // 5. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]] to maxsize.
            buffer.set_max_byte_length(max_size as usize);

            // 6. Perform ! SetIntegrityLevel(buffer, "frozen").
            buffer.set_integrity_level(vm, IntegrityLevel::Frozen).must();

            // AD-HOC: Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferDetachKey]] to "WebAssembly.Memory".
            //         SharedArrayBuffers can't be detached, but this allows us to bail early from HostGrowSharedArrayBuffer
            //         for SharedArrayBuffers not associated with a WebAssembly memory.
            buffer.set_detach_key(detach_key(vm));

            // 7. Return buffer.
            return Ok(buffer);
        }

        // 6. Otherwise,
        // 1. Let block be a Data Block which is identified with the underlying memory of memaddr.
        // 4. Let buffer be a new ArrayBuffer with the internal slots [[ArrayBufferData]], [[ArrayBufferByteLength]], [[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]], and [[ArrayBufferDetachKey]].
        // 5. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferData]] to block.
        // 2. Let length be the length of block.
        // 6. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]] to length.
        let block = DataBlock::external(Self::external_storage(this, vm, false), ArrayBufferShared::No);
        let buffer = ArrayBuffer::create_from_data_block(vm, realm, block);

        // 7. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]] to maxsize.
        buffer.set_max_byte_length(max_size as usize);

        // 8. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferDetachKey]] to "WebAssembly.Memory".
        buffer.set_detach_key(detach_key(vm));

        // 9. Return buffer.
        Ok(buffer)
    }

    /// The [[BufferObject]] of the memory in the realm, which the realm's first use creates.
    fn buffer_object(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Gc<ArrayBuffer> {
        let buffer = this
            .buffer_objects
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .find(|buffer| buffer.shape().realm() == realm);
        if let Some(buffer) = buffer {
            // AD-HOC: Any agent with a shared memory can grow it, and nothing refreshes the memory buffers of the
            //         other agents then. So this is where an agent finds out that the size changed. A fixed-length
            //         buffer keeps its length, and a new one takes its place, as refreshing the memory buffer does.
            let is_stale = this.shared && buffer.is_fixed_length() && buffer.byte_length() != this.size(vm);
            if !is_stale {
                return buffer;
            }
        }
        let buffer = Self::create_a_fixed_length_memory_buffer(this, vm, realm);
        this.set_buffer_object(vm, buffer);
        buffer
    }

    /// Sets the [[BufferObject]] of the memory in the realm of the buffer.
    fn set_buffer_object(&self, vm: &Vm, buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>) {
        let realm = buffer.shape().realm();
        let mut buffer_objects = self.buffer_objects.borrow_mut(vm);
        buffer_objects.retain(|other| other.shape().realm() != realm);
        buffer_objects.push(buffer);
    }

    fn has_buffer_object(&self, buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>) -> bool {
        self.buffer_objects.borrow().contains(&buffer)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-memory-grow
    pub(crate) fn grow(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext, delta: u32) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        // 1. Let memaddr be this.[[Memory]].
        Self::grow_the_memory_buffer(*this, cx.vm(), u64::from(delta))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#grow-the-memory-buffer
    fn grow_the_memory_buffer(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm, delta: u64) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        // 1. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
        // 5. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
        let previous_size = Agent::the(vm)
            .store()
            .memory_mut(this.address())
            .grow(delta)
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                Exception::range_error("Memory.grow() grows past the stated limit of the memory instance")
            })?;

        refresh_the_memory_buffer(vm, this);

        Ok(previous_size as u32)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/index.html#dom-memory-tofixedlengthbuffer
    pub(crate) fn to_fixed_length_buffer(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let realm = cx.realm();

        // 1. Let buffer be this.[[BufferObject]].
        let buffer = Self::buffer_object(*this, vm, realm);

        // 2. Let memaddr be this.[[Memory]].
        // 3. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(buffer) is false,
        if !this.shared {
            // 1. If IsFixedLengthArrayBuffer(buffer) is true, return buffer.
            if buffer.is_fixed_length() {
                return Ok(buffer);
            }

            // 2. Otherwise,
            // 1. Let fixedBuffer be the result of creating a fixed length memory buffer from memaddr.
            let fixed_buffer = Self::create_a_fixed_length_memory_buffer(*this, vm, realm);

            // 2. Perform ! DetachArrayBuffer(buffer, "WebAssembly.Memory").
            detach_array_buffer(vm, buffer, Some(detach_key(vm))).must();

            // 3. Set this.[[BufferObject]] to fixedBuffer.
            this.set_buffer_object(vm, fixed_buffer);

            // 4. Return fixedBuffer.
            return Ok(fixed_buffer);
        }

        // 4. Otherwise,
        // 1. Let map be the surrounding agent's associated Memory object cache.
        // 2. Assert: map[memaddr] exists.
        // 3. Let newMemory be map[memaddr].
        let new_memory: Ref<Self> = host_object(this.address().cell()).expect("the memory has a Memory object");

        // 4. Let newBufferObject be newMemory.[[BufferObject]].
        let new_buffer_object = Self::buffer_object(new_memory, vm, realm);

        // 5. Set this.[[BufferObject]] to newBufferObject.
        this.set_buffer_object(vm, new_buffer_object);

        // 6. Return newBufferObject.
        Ok(new_buffer_object)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-memory-toresizablebuffer
    pub(crate) fn to_resizable_buffer(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let realm = cx.realm();

        // 1. Let buffer be this.[[BufferObject]].
        let buffer = Self::buffer_object(*this, vm, realm);

        // 2. If IsFixedLengthArrayBuffer(buffer) is false, return buffer.
        if !buffer.is_fixed_length() {
            return Ok(buffer);
        }

        // 3. Let memaddr be this.[[Memory]].
        // 4. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
        // 5. Let memtype be mem_type(store, memaddr).
        let maximum = Agent::the(vm).store().memory(this.address()).ty.limits.max;

        // 6. If memtype has a max,
        //        1. Let maxsize be the max value in memtype.
        // 7. Otherwise,
        //        1. Let maxsize be 65536 x 65536.
        let max_size = max_size_of_memory_buffer(maximum);

        // 8. Let resizableBuffer be the result of creating a resizable memory buffer from memaddr and maxsize.
        let resizable_buffer = Self::create_a_resizable_memory_buffer(*this, vm, realm, max_size)?;

        // https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/index.html#dom-memory-toresizablebuffer
        // 5. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(buffer) is false,
        // 9. Perform ! DetachArrayBuffer(buffer, "WebAssembly.Memory").
        if !buffer.is_shared_array_buffer() {
            detach_array_buffer(vm, buffer, Some(detach_key(vm))).must();
        }

        // 10. Set this.[[BufferObject]] to resizableBuffer.
        this.set_buffer_object(vm, resizable_buffer);

        // 11. Return resizeableBuffer.
        Ok(resizable_buffer)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/#dom-memory-buffer
    pub(crate) fn buffer(this: &Ref<Self>, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let realm = cx.realm();

        // 1. Let memaddr be this.[[Memory]].
        // 2. Let block be a Data Block which is identified with the underlying memory of memaddr.
        // 3. If block is a Shared Data Block,
        if this.shared {
            // 1. Let map be the surrounding agent's associated Memory object cache.
            // 2. Assert: map[memaddr] exists.
            // 3. Let newMemory be map[memaddr].
            let new_memory: Ref<Self> = host_object(this.address().cell()).expect("the memory has a Memory object");

            // 4. Let newBufferObject be newMemory.[[BufferObject]].
            let new_buffer_object = Self::buffer_object(new_memory, vm, realm);

            // 5. Set this.[[BufferObject]] to newBufferObject.
            this.set_buffer_object(vm, new_buffer_object);

            // 6. Return newBufferObject.
            return Ok(new_buffer_object);
        }

        // 4. Otherwise,
        // 1. Return this.[[BufferObject]].
        Ok(Self::buffer_object(*this, vm, realm))
    }
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#refresh-the-memory-buffer
pub(crate) fn refresh_the_memory_buffer(vm: &Vm, memory: Ref<Memory>) {
    // 1. Let map be the surrounding agent's associated Memory object cache.
    // 2. Assert: map[memaddr] exists.
    // 3. Let memory be map[memaddr].
    // 4. Let buffer be memory.[[BufferObject]].
    // NB: Replacing a buffer changes the list, so the loop runs over a copy of it.
    let buffer_objects = MarkedVec::new(vm);
    buffer_objects.extend_from_slice(&memory.buffer_objects.borrow());
    for &buffer in buffer_objects.values().iter() {
        // 5. If IsFixedLengthArrayBuffer(buffer) is true,
        if buffer.is_fixed_length() {
            // https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/index.html#refresh-the-memory-buffer
            // 1. If IsSharedArrayBuffer(buffer) is false,
            if !buffer.is_shared_array_buffer() {
                // 1. Perform ! DetachArrayBuffer(buffer, "WebAssembly.Memory").
                detach_array_buffer(vm, buffer, Some(detach_key(vm))).must();
            }

            // 2. Let newBuffer be the result of creating a fixed length memory buffer from memaddr.
            // 3. Set memory.[[BufferObject]] to newBuffer.
            let new_buffer = Memory::create_a_fixed_length_memory_buffer(memory, vm, buffer.shape().realm());
            memory.set_buffer_object(vm, new_buffer);
        } else {
            // 1. Let block be a Data Block which is identified with the underlying memory of memaddr.
            // AD-HOC: Neither the main spec nor the threads proposal specify that the Data Block should be Shared for
            //         shared Wasm memories, but we do in fact want a Shared Data Block in that case.
            let is_shared = if buffer.is_shared_array_buffer() {
                ArrayBufferShared::Yes
            } else {
                ArrayBufferShared::No
            };

            // 2. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferData]] to block.
            // 3. Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]] to the length of block.
            buffer.set_data_block(
                vm,
                DataBlock::external(Memory::external_storage(memory, vm, false), is_shared),
            );
        }
    }
}

/// The Memory object whose [[BufferObject]] the buffer is, if its [[ArrayBufferDetachKey]] is "WebAssembly.Memory".
fn memory_of_buffer(vm: &Vm, buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>) -> Option<Ref<Memory>> {
    if !same_value(buffer.detach_key(), detach_key(vm)) {
        return None;
    }
    // 3. For each memaddr → mem in all Memory object caches,
    //     1. If SameValue(mem.[[BufferObject]], buffer) is true,
    // NB: The memory whose [[BufferObject]] the buffer is owns the buffer's storage.
    let owner = buffer.with_data_block(|block| match &block.byte_buffer {
        DataBlockStorage::External(storage) => Some(storage.owner()),
        _ => None,
    })?;
    // SAFETY: The owner of external storage is a live cell.
    let memory = unsafe { cell_if_abi::<Memory>(owner.as_ptr()) }?;
    // 2. Assert: buffer is the [[BufferObject]] of exactly one value in map.
    assert!(memory.has_buffer_object(buffer));
    Some(memory)
}

/// The steps that HostResizeArrayBuffer and HostGrowSharedArrayBuffer share: whether the buffer is that of a memory,
/// and if it is, growing the memory to the new length.
fn grow_memory_of_buffer(vm: &Vm, buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>, new_length: usize) -> ThrowCompletionOr<bool> {
    let Some(memory) = memory_of_buffer(vm, buffer) else {
        return Ok(false);
    };
    let byte_length = buffer.byte_length();

    // 1. Assert: buffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]] modulo 65536 is 0.
    assert_eq!(byte_length as u64 % PAGE_SIZE, 0);

    // 2. Let lengthDelta be newLength - buffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]].
    // 3. If lengthDelta < 0 or lengthDelta modulo 65536 is not 0,
    if new_length < byte_length || !((new_length - byte_length) as u64).is_multiple_of(PAGE_SIZE) {
        // 1. Throw a RangeError exception.
        return vm.throw_completion_with_message(
            libjs_rust::api::ErrorKind::RangeError,
            "WebAssembly.Memory buffers must be resized by a multiple of the page size".to_string(),
        );
    }

    // 4. Let delta be lengthDelta ÷ 65536.
    let delta = (new_length - byte_length) as u64 / PAGE_SIZE;

    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, buffer.shape().realm());

    // AD-HOC: Another agent can grow a shared memory after the byte length was read above, and delta pages more would
    //         then give more than newLength. So a shared memory grows to newLength. If it has more than that by now,
    //         newLength is less than its length, which is an error as above.
    let shared = Agent::the(vm).store().memory(memory.address()).shared().cloned();
    if let Some(shared) = shared {
        if !shared.grow_to(new_length as u64 / PAGE_SIZE) {
            return Err(
                Exception::range_error("Cannot grow the buffer of the WebAssembly.Memory to this length").throw(&cx),
            );
        }
        refresh_the_memory_buffer(vm, memory);
        return Ok(true);
    }

    // 5. Grow the memory buffer associated with memaddr by delta.
    Memory::grow_the_memory_buffer(memory, vm, delta).map_err(|exception| exception.throw(&cx))?;
    Ok(true)
}

/// HostResizeArrayBuffer(buffer, newLength), https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#HostResizeArrayBuffer, which
/// writes whether it handled the buffer.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_web_assembly_host_resize_array_buffer(
    vm: &Vm,
    buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>,
    new_length: usize,
    handled: &mut bool,
) -> RawNativeFunctionResult {
    // 1. If buffer.[[ArrayBufferDetachKey]] is "WebAssembly.Memory",
    //     4. Return handled.
    // 2. Otherwise, return unhandled.
    let result = grow_memory_of_buffer(vm, buffer, new_length);
    if let Ok(was_handled) = result {
        *handled = was_handled;
    }
    RawNativeFunctionResult::from_completion(result.map(|_| Value::UNDEFINED))
}

/// HostGrowSharedArrayBuffer(buffer, newLength), https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/#abstract-operation-hostgrowsharedarraybuffer,
/// which writes whether it handled the buffer.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_web_assembly_host_grow_shared_array_buffer(
    vm: &Vm,
    buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>,
    new_length: usize,
    handled: &mut bool,
) -> RawNativeFunctionResult {
    // AD-HOC: If buffer.[[ArrayBufferDetachKey]] is "WebAssembly.Memory",
    let current_byte_length = buffer.byte_length();
    let result = grow_memory_of_buffer(vm, buffer, new_length).and_then(|was_handled| {
        if !was_handled {
            // AD-HOC: Otherwise, return unhandled.
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 4. If newLength < buffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLength]] or newLength > buffer.[[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]], throw a RangeError exception.
        // NB: The step cannot throw. Step 3.1.3 threw for a newLength below the byte length, and the buffer's
        //     [[ArrayBufferMaxByteLength]] is the memory's maximum, past which step 3.1.5 failed to grow.
        if new_length < current_byte_length {
            return vm.throw_completion(
                libjs_rust::api::ErrorKind::RangeError,
                libjs_rust::api::ErrorType::ByteLengthLessThanPreviousByteLength,
                &[&new_length, &current_byte_length],
            );
        }
        if new_length > buffer.max_byte_length() {
            return vm.throw_completion(
                libjs_rust::api::ErrorKind::RangeError,
                libjs_rust::api::ErrorType::ByteLengthExceedsMaxByteLength,
                &[&new_length, &buffer.max_byte_length()],
            );
        }

        // FIXME: 5. Let agentRecord be the surrounding agent’s Agent Record.
        // FIXME: 6. Let isLittleEndian be agentRecord.[[LittleEndian]] .
        // FIXME: 7. Let event be an implementation defined ReadModifyWriteSharedMemory event, whose [[Order]] is "SeqCst", [[Payload]] is NumericToRawBytes(Bigint, newLength, isLittleEndian), [[Block]] is buffer.[[ArrayBufferByteLengthData]], [[ByteIndex]] is 0, and [[ElementSize]] is 8.
        // FIXME: 8. Let eventsRecord be the EventsRecord in agentRecord.[[CandidateExecution]].[[EventsRecords]] that corresponds to the surrounding agent’s signifier agentRecord.[[Signifier]].
        // FIXME: 9. Append event to eventsRecord.[[EventsList]].
        // NB: Another agent with the memory may have grown it further by now.
        assert!(buffer.byte_length() >= new_length);

        // 10. Return handled.
        Ok(true)
    });
    if let Ok(was_handled) = result {
        *handled = was_handled;
    }
    RawNativeFunctionResult::from_completion(result.map(|_| Value::UNDEFINED))
}

/// The maxsize of a memory buffer: that of a memory type with the maximum, or 65536 × 65536 without one.
fn max_size_of_memory_buffer(maximum: Option<u64>) -> u64 {
    maximum.unwrap_or(65536).saturating_mul(PAGE_SIZE)
}

/// The shared memory that the SharedArrayBuffer is a buffer of, if it is one of a memory. That is so for the
/// [[BufferObject]] of a Memory object, and for every clone of one that shares its Data Block.
pub(crate) fn shared_memory_of_buffer(buffer: Gc<ArrayBuffer>) -> Option<Arc<SharedMemory>> {
    if !buffer.is_shared_array_buffer() {
        return None;
    }
    let handle = buffer.with_data_block(|block| match &block.byte_buffer {
        DataBlockStorage::External(storage) => Some(storage.handle()),
        _ => None,
    })?;
    SharedMemory::with_primitive_storage_handle(handle)
}

/// A new SharedArrayBuffer of the realm for the shared memory that `id` names, which the message of another agent
/// carries. A fixed-length buffer has the byte length that the buffer of the sender had, and a growable one has the size
/// of the memory, which it grows. Returns None for a memory that is out of reach, as that of another process is, or one
/// that is smaller than the buffer.
pub(crate) fn buffer_of_shared_memory(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    id: u64,
    fixed_byte_length: Option<usize>,
) -> Option<Gc<ArrayBuffer>> {
    let shared = SharedMemory::with_id(id)?;
    let maximum = shared.ty().limits.max;
    // NB: The Memory object owns the storage of the buffer, and is how the agent grows the memory of a growable one.
    let memory = Memory::sharing(vm, shared);
    let Some(byte_length) = fixed_byte_length else {
        let max_size = max_size_of_memory_buffer(maximum);
        if max_size > 65536 * PAGE_SIZE {
            return None;
        }
        // NB: The buffer is the [[BufferObject]] of the Memory object, as a resizable memory buffer is, so that the
        //     agent grows the memory through it. Unlike one, it is not frozen: a deserialization creates an ordinary
        //     SharedArrayBuffer.
        let block = DataBlock::external(Memory::external_storage(memory, vm, false), ArrayBufferShared::Yes);
        let buffer = ArrayBuffer::create_from_data_block(vm, realm, block);
        buffer.set_max_byte_length(max_size as usize);
        buffer.set_detach_key(detach_key(vm));
        memory.set_buffer_object(vm, buffer);
        return Some(buffer);
    };
    // NB: A memory only grows, so it holds every byte of a buffer that an agent had of it.
    if byte_length > memory.size(vm) {
        return None;
    }
    let owner = ForeignCellSlot::empty();
    // SAFETY: The memory object is a live cell of the heap, which the slot then keeps alive.
    unsafe { owner.set(Some(NonNull::new_unchecked(memory.as_ptr().cast()))) };
    let handle = Agent::the(vm)
        .store()
        .memory(memory.address())
        .primitive_storage_handle();
    let storage = ExternalPrimitiveStorage::new(owner, handle, Some(byte_length));
    Some(ArrayBuffer::create_from_data_block(
        vm,
        realm,
        DataBlock::external(storage, ArrayBufferShared::Yes),
    ))
}

impl Serializable for Memory {
    // INTEROP: No specification has steps to serialize a Memory object yet, but all engines serialize a shared one, and
    //          web-platform-tests cover it. A shared memory serializes as a record that names it, which keeps the
    //          memory within its agent cluster and requires the cross-origin isolated capability, as the record of a
    //          SharedArrayBuffer does. A memory that is not shared cannot be serialized.
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let Some(shared) = Agent::the(vm).store().memory(self.address()).shared().cloned() else {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "DataCloneError",
                Utf16String::from_utf8("Cannot serialize a WebAssembly.Memory that is not shared"),
            ));
        };
        if for_storage {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "DataCloneError",
                Utf16String::from_utf8("WebAssembly.Memory instances may not be serialized for storage"),
            ));
        }
        let this: Ref<Self> = host_object(self.address().cell()).expect("the memory has a Memory object");
        let buffer = Self::buffer_object(this, vm, cx.realm());
        serialized.write_shared_web_assembly_memory(shared.id(), buffer)?;
        // NB: The buffer of the new Memory object is of the kind that the buffer of this one is.
        serialized.write_bool(buffer.is_fixed_length());
        Ok(())
    }

    // INTEROP: See the serialization steps. Each deserialization creates a new Memory object for the memory.
    fn deserialization_steps(cx: &mut CallContext, serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let id = serialized.read_shared_web_assembly_memory_id()?;
        let has_fixed_length_buffer = serialized.read_bool()?;
        // NB: The memory of another process is out of reach, as its bytes do not leave that process.
        let Some(shared) = SharedMemory::with_id(id) else {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "DataCloneError",
                Utf16String::from_utf8("WebAssembly.Memory is out of reach"),
            ));
        };
        let max_size = max_size_of_memory_buffer(shared.ty().limits.max);
        let memory = Self::sharing(cx.vm(), shared);
        if !has_fixed_length_buffer {
            let buffer = Self::create_a_resizable_memory_buffer(memory, cx.vm(), cx.realm(), max_size)?;
            memory.set_buffer_object(cx.vm(), buffer);
        }
        Ok(memory)
    }
}

impl Memory {
    /// The Memory object that the value is, if it is the wrapper of one.
    pub(crate) fn from_value(value: Value) -> Option<Ref<Self>> {
        crate::web_assembly::implementation_of_value::<Self>(value)
    }
}

//! The WebAssembly JavaScript Interface, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/, its Web API,
//! https://webassembly.github.io/spec/web-api/, and its ESM integration,
//! https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/, on the engine of Libraries/LibWasm/Engine.
//!
//! The engine's entities (functions, tables, memories, globals, tags and instances) and its exceptions and GC objects
//! are cells of the agent's heap. The store keeps none of them alive: each lives while an object that stands for it,
//! or another entity, refers to it. The engine has each cell keep the object that stands for it alive in turn
//! (`set_host_object()`), which makes that object the cell's entry in the agent's object caches: the object stays the
//! same one for as long as both live, and both go away together.

)]

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#page-size
pub(crate) const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 65536;

unsafe extern "C" {

    fn gc_heap_defer_gc(heap: *mut c_void);
    fn gc_heap_undefer_gc(heap: *mut c_void);
    fn gc_heap_collect_garbage(heap: *mut c_void, collection_type: i32, print_report: bool);
    fn gc_heap_did_allocate_external_memory(heap: *mut c_void, size: usize);
    fn gc_root_create(cell: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn gc_root_destroy(root: *mut c_void);
    pub(crate) fn gc_visitor_visit_cell(visitor: *mut c_void, cell: *mut c_void);
    fn gc_primitive_storage_reserve(
        size: usize,
        capacity: usize,
        zero_fill: bool,

fn gc_interface(heap: *mut c_void) -> GcInterface {
    GcInterface {
        heap,
        gc_get_layout,
        gc_allocator_create,
        gc_allocator_set_traced_on_owner_thread_only,
        gc_heap_allocate_cell,
        gc_heap_defer_gc,

        gc_root_destroy,
        gc_visitor_visit_cell,
        gc_primitive_storage_reserve,
        gc_primitive_storage_resize,
        gc_primitive_storage_free,
        gc_primitive_storage_data,
    }

/// An entity of the store, which keeps its cell alive where it is traced.
pub(crate) struct EntityRef<T>(pub(crate) Handle<T>);

impl<T> Clone for EntityRef<T> {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        *self
    }
}

impl<T> Copy for EntityRef<T> {}

// SAFETY: The handle is the address of the entity's cell, which this visits.
unsafe impl<T: Entity + 'static> Trace for EntityRef<T> {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        // SAFETY: The visitor is live while it traces, and the cell is a cell of its heap.
        unsafe { gc_visitor_visit_cell(visitor.as_raw().cast(), self.0.cell().cast()) };
    }
}

/// An exception, a GC object, or another reference that is the address of a cell, which keeps the cell alive where it
/// is traced.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct CellReference(pub(crate) u64);

// SAFETY: The reference is the address of its cell, which this visits.
unsafe impl Trace for CellReference {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        // SAFETY: The visitor is live while it traces, and the reference is the address of a cell of its heap.
        unsafe { gc_visitor_visit_cell(visitor.as_raw().cast(), self.0 as *mut c_void) };
    }
}

/// How many values a WasmValues holds in its cell before it moves them to memory of their own.
const INLINE_WASM_VALUES: usize = 4;

/// How the collector follows each of some values, as the store's trace_of() says.
pub(crate) type WasmValueTraces = SmallVec<[u8; INLINE_WASM_VALUES]>;

/// Values of the store, which may be references that keep cells alive where they are traced. Each is traced as the type
/// it was made for says, which a function reference needs, as it points into its function's cell. They live in a cell of
/// their own, which a Gc in a local keeps alive. As allocating the cell can collect garbage, it is allocated empty,
/// before there are values for it to keep alive.
/// NB: Calls between JavaScript and WebAssembly that pass references make such cells, and the collector counts only the
///     bytes of cells towards the next collection. Keeping the few values of a call in the cell makes the collector see
///     what the call allocated, which it would not if they were in memory of their own.
pub(crate) struct WasmValues {
    values: RefCell<SmallVec<[WasmValue; INLINE_WASM_VALUES]>>,
    traces: RefCell<WasmValueTraces>,
}

static WASM_VALUES_CLASS: EmbedderClass<WasmValues> = EmbedderClass::new("WasmValues");

impl EmbedderValue for WasmValues {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &WASM_VALUES_CLASS;
}

impl WasmValues {
    pub(crate) fn allocate(vm: &Vm) -> Gc<EmbedderCell<WasmValues>> {
        WASM_VALUES_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| WasmValues {
            values: RefCell::default(),
            traces: RefCell::default(),
        })
    }

    /// How the collector follows values of `types`, for push().
    pub(crate) fn traces_of(vm: &Vm, types: &[ValType]) -> WasmValueTraces {
        let store = Agent::the(vm).store();
        types.iter().map(|&ty| store.trace_of(ty)).collect()
    }

    /// Appends a value, which the collector follows as `trace` says.
    pub(crate) fn push(&self, value: WasmValue, trace: u8) {
        self.values.borrow_mut().push(value);
        self.traces.borrow_mut().push(trace);
    }

    /// Replaces the values with ones of the types `types`.
    pub(crate) fn set(&self, vm: &Vm, values: Vec<WasmValue>, types: &[ValType]) {
        *self.traces.borrow_mut() = Self::traces_of(vm, types);
        *self.values.borrow_mut() = SmallVec::from_vec(values);
    }

    pub(crate) fn values(&self) -> core::cell::Ref<'_, [WasmValue]> {
        core::cell::Ref::map(self.values.borrow(), |values| values.as_slice())
    }

    pub(crate) fn take(&self) -> Vec<WasmValue> {
        self.traces.take();
        self.values.take().into_vec()
    }
}

// SAFETY: Every reference among the values is traced as the type it was made for says.
unsafe impl Trace for WasmValues {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        let wasm_visitor = libwasm_engine::runtime::heap::Visitor::new(visitor.as_raw().cast());
        let (values, traces) = (self.values.borrow(), self.traces.borrow());
        debug_assert_eq!(values.len(), traces.len());
        for (value, &trace) in values.iter().zip(traces.iter()) {
            if let WasmValue::Ref(bits) = *value {
                wasm_visitor.visit_value(bits, trace);
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The surrounding agent's associated store, and the agent's caches of the objects that are not the host objects of
/// cells: the boxes of the host value cache, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#host-value-cache
pub(crate) struct Agent {
    vm: NonNull<Vm>,
    // NB: The store must not move once it is attached to the heap.
    store: Box<UnsafeCell<Store>>,
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#javascript-exception-tag
    js_tag: TagAddress,
    // NB: The root of the tag's cell, which lives as long as the agent.
    _js_tag_root: NonNull<c_void>,
    // NB: The module whose types are the funcTypes of the builtins, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#builtins
    builtin_types_module: OnceCell<CompiledModule>,
    // NB: An entry whose box is gone is stale. Stale entries go once there are as many of them as live ones.
    extern_value_boxes: RefCell<HashMap<u64, GcWeak<EmbedderCell<ExternValueBox>>>>,
    live_extern_value_boxes_after_pruning: Cell<usize>,
}

thread_local! {
    static AGENT: Cell<Option<&'static Agent>> = const { Cell::new(None) };
}

impl Agent {
    /// The agent of the current thread, which the first use on it creates. Each thread is one agent with one VM and one
    /// heap, which outlive it: shut_down() ends it before they go.
    pub(crate) fn the(vm: &Vm) -> &'static Agent {
        if let Some(agent) = AGENT.get() {
            return agent;
        }
        let store_cell = Box::new(UnsafeCell::new(Store::with_heap(Some(gc_interface(
            vm.heap().raw().cast(),
        )))));
        // SAFETY: Nothing else has the store yet.
        let store = unsafe { &mut *store_cell.get() };
        store.attach_to_heap();

        // NB: An interrupt of the agent's VM has to stop the store's code too.
        // SAFETY: The word is in the boxed store, which does not move, and shut_down() clears it before the store goes.
        unsafe { vm.set_wasm_stack_limit_word(store.stack_limit_word()) };
        store.agent_waiter = Some(vm.agent_waiter().clone());

        // NB: The store is the agent's, whose [[CanBlock]] decides whether memory.atomic.wait may block.
        store.can_block = libjs_rust::api::agent_can_suspend(vm);

        let js_tag = store.allocate_tag(FuncType {
            params: vec![EXTERNREF],
            results: Vec::new(),
        });
        // NB: The tag lives as long as the agent, which roots its cell.
        // SAFETY: The cell is a live cell of the heap.
        let js_tag_root = NonNull::new(unsafe { gc_root_create(js_tag.cell().cast()) }).expect("a root is allocated");

        // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#memory-objects
        // Whenever memory.grow is executed, refresh the memory buffer of the memory's Memory object, if it has one.
        store.memory_grow_callback = Some(Rc::new(|memory| {
            let agent = AGENT.get().expect("a store's callbacks run on the thread of its agent");
            if let Some(object) = host_object::<EmbedderCell<Wrapped<Memory>>>(memory.cell()) {
                refresh_the_memory_buffer(agent.vm(), object);
            }
        }));

        let agent: &'static Agent = Box::leak(Box::new(Agent {
            vm: NonNull::from(vm),
            store: store_cell,
            js_tag,
            _js_tag_root: js_tag_root,
            builtin_types_module: OnceCell::new(),
            extern_value_boxes: RefCell::default(),
            live_extern_value_boxes_after_pruning: Cell::new(0),
        }));
        AGENT.set(Some(agent));
        agent
    }

    /// Ends the agent of the current thread, if it has one, while its heap is alive. The store and the root of the
    /// JavaScript exception tag point into the heap, and whatever cells of the store remain go with the heap.
    pub(crate) fn shut_down() {
        let Some(agent) = AGENT.take() else {
            return;
        };
        // SAFETY: Null is always allowed.
        unsafe { agent.vm().set_wasm_stack_limit_word(std::ptr::null()) };
        // SAFETY: The root belongs to the agent, which is going away, and the heap it is in is alive.
        unsafe { gc_root_destroy(agent._js_tag_root.as_ptr()) };
        // SAFETY: the() leaked this box, and AGENT held the only way to reach the agent.
        drop(unsafe { Box::from_raw(std::ptr::from_ref(agent).cast_mut()) });
    }

    /// The agent of the current thread, which must have one.
    pub(crate) fn current() -> &'static Agent {
        AGENT.get().expect("the thread has an agent")
    }

    pub(crate) fn vm(&self) -> &'static Vm {
        // SAFETY: The VM of the thread outlives its agent.
        unsafe { self.vm.as_ref() }
    }

    /// The store, which a call into it can be on the stack below. It belongs to the thread of the agent, and is reached
    /// the way the engine's C interface reaches it, through a pointer, for as long as any one use lasts: a caller keeps
    /// the reference no longer than that, as the JavaScript and WebAssembly that run in between reach the store through
    /// the agent as well.
    #[allow(
        clippy::mut_from_ref,
        reason = "the store is the agent's, as an embedder of the engine holds it"
    )]
    pub(crate) fn store(&self) -> &mut Store {
        // SAFETY: The agent lives as long as the thread, which is the only one that uses its store.
        unsafe { &mut *self.store.get() }
    }

    pub(crate) fn js_tag(&self) -> TagAddress {
        self.js_tag
    }

    pub(crate) fn builtin_types_module(&self) -> &CompiledModule {
        self.builtin_types_module.get_or_init(|| {
            Arc::new(
                libwasm_engine::compile(&builtins::BUILTIN_TYPES_MODULE_BYTES)
                    .expect("the funcTypes of the builtins are a valid module"),
            )
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn extern_value_box(&self, value: Value) -> Option<Gc<EmbedderCell<ExternValueBox>>> {
        self.extern_value_boxes
            .borrow()
            .get(&value.to_raw())
            .and_then(GcWeak::get)
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_extern_value_box(&self, value: Value, value_box: Gc<EmbedderCell<ExternValueBox>>) {
        let mut boxes = self.extern_value_boxes.borrow_mut();
        if boxes.len() >= 2 * self.live_extern_value_boxes_after_pruning.get() + 16 {
            boxes.retain(|_, weak| weak.get().is_some());
            self.live_extern_value_boxes_after_pruning.set(boxes.len());
        }
        boxes.insert(value.to_raw(), GcWeak::new(self.vm().heap(), value_box));
    }
}

/// The object that the cell keeps alive as the one that stands for it, if it has one (`set_host_object()`).
pub(crate) fn host_object<T>(cell: *mut u8) -> Option<Gc<T>> {
    // SAFETY: The cell is a live cell of the runtime.
    let object = unsafe { libwasm_engine::runtime::heap::host_object(cell.cast()) };
    // SAFETY: Each kind of cell keeps one kind of object, which its cache stores as a cell of that type.
    NonNull::new(object.cast::<T>()).map(|object| unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(object) })
}

/// Has the cell keep the object alive as the one that stands for it, for as long as the cell lives.
pub(crate) fn set_host_object<T>(cell: *mut u8, object: Gc<T>) {
    // SAFETY: The cell is a live cell of the runtime, and the object a cell of the same heap.
    unsafe { libwasm_engine::runtime::heap::set_host_object(cell, object.as_ptr().cast()) };
}

/// The object of the interface that the value is the wrapper of, if it is one.
pub(crate) fn implementation_of_value<T: Interface>(value: Value) -> Option<Ref<T>> {
    if !value.is_object() {
        return None;
    }
    implementation_if_wrapper(value.as_object())
}

/// A copy of the bytes held by a buffer, which the algorithms compile: their stableBytes.
pub(crate) fn stable_bytes_of(bytes: BufferSource) -> Vec<u8> {
    // SAFETY: Copying the bytes neither runs script nor allocates a cell.
    unsafe { bytes.with_bytes(<[u8]>::to_vec) }
}

/// What a compiled WebAssembly module is to its objects: the module, which threads can share.
pub(crate) type CompiledModule = Arc<CoreModule>;

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#compile-a-webassembly-module
/// https://webassembly.github.io/content-security-policy/js-api/#compile-a-webassembly-module
pub(crate) fn compile_a_webassembly_module(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    bytes: &[u8],
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<CompiledModule> {
    host_ensure_can_compile_wasm_bytes(realm)?;

    match libwasm_engine::compile(bytes) {
        Ok(module) => Ok(Arc::new(module)),
        Err(error) => Err(throw_webassembly_error(
            vm,
            realm,
            WebAssemblyError::Compile,
            &error.to_string(),
        )),
    }
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// EnsureCSPDoesNotBlockWasmByteCompilation(realm), which completes with nothing, or throws a CompileError.
    fn web_bindings_ensure_csp_does_not_block_wasm_byte_compilation(
        realm: *mut c_void,
    ) -> libjs_rust::api::RawNativeFunctionResult;
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/content-security-policy/js-api/#abstract-opdef-hostensurecancompilewasmbytes
pub(crate) fn host_ensure_can_compile_wasm_bytes(realm: Gc<Realm>) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()> {
    // 2. Perform EnsureCSPDoesNotBlockWasmByteCompilation(realm)
    // This algorithm does not return a value, but raises a CompileError exception if the operation cannot complete
    // successfully.
    // SAFETY: The realm is live.
    unsafe { web_bindings_ensure_csp_does_not_block_wasm_byte_compilation(realm.as_ptr().cast()) }
        .into_completion()
        .map(|_| ())
}

/// How instantiating a module or calling a function of the store failed, as the exception it throws,
/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#error-objects
pub(crate) fn throw_of_trap(vm: &Vm, trap: Trap) -> Throw {
    let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("WebAssembly code runs in a realm");
    let agent = Agent::the(vm);
    match trap {
        // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#stack-overflow
        // 6.1. Whenever a stack overflow occurs in WebAssembly code, the same class of exception is thrown as for a stack overflow in JavaScript.
        Trap::StackExhausted => {
            thrown(vm.throw_completion(ErrorKind::InternalError, ErrorType::CallStackSizeExceeded, &[]))
        }
        Trap::UncaughtException(exception) => {
            // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#call-an-exported-function
            // 11. If ret is of the form exception exnaddr, then
            //     1. Let tagaddr be exn_tag(store, exnaddr).
            //     2. Let payload be exn_read(store, exnaddr).
            //     3. Let jsTagAddr be the result of getting the JavaScript exception tag.
            let store = agent.store();
            let tagaddr = store.exception(exception).tag;

            //     4. If tagaddr is equal to jsTagAddr,
            if tagaddr == agent.js_tag() {
                //     1. Throw ToJSValue(payload[0]).
                let payload = store.exception_values(exception)[0];
                return Throw::new(to_js_value(vm, payload, EXTERNREF).unwrap_or_else(|throw| throw.value()));
            }

            //     5. Otherwise,
            //         1. Let exception be a new Exception created from exnaddr.
            //         2. Throw exception.
            Throw::new(Exception::wrapper_of_address(vm, realm, exception))
        }
        // FIXME: Use the convoluted mapping of errors defined in the spec.
        trap => throw_webassembly_error(
            vm,
            realm,
            WebAssemblyError::Runtime,
            &format!("Wasm execution trapped (WIP): {}", trap.message()),
        ),
    }
}

pub(crate) fn throw_of_instantiation_error(vm: &Vm, error: InstantiationError) -> Throw {
    match error {
        InstantiationError::Link(message) => throw_webassembly_error(
            vm,
            vm.current_realm().expect("instantiation runs in a realm"),
            WebAssemblyError::Link,
            &message,
        ),
        InstantiationError::Trap(trap) => throw_of_trap(vm, trap),
    }
}

fn thrown(completion: ThrowCompletionOr<()>) -> Throw {
    match completion {
        Err(throw) => throw,
        Ok(()) => unreachable!("throwing a completion throws"),
    }
}
