/// The fields that a WebAssembly Module Record has besides those of a Cyclic Module Record.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
struct WebAssemblyModuleRecord {
    // [[Instance]]
    instance: Cell<Option<Ref<Instance>>>,
    // [[ModuleSource]]
    module_source: Ref<Module>,
    // AD-HOC: The export name list, which never changes.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    export_name_list: Vec<Utf16FlyString>,
}

static WEBASSEMBLY_MODULE_RECORD_CLASS: EmbedderClass<WebAssemblyModuleRecord> =
    EmbedderClass::new("WebAssemblyModuleRecord");

impl EmbedderValue for WebAssemblyModuleRecord {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &WEBASSEMBLY_MODULE_RECORD_CLASS;
}

static WEBASSEMBLY_MODULE_HOOKS: JSHostModuleHooks = JSHostModuleHooks {
    get_exported_names: Some(get_exported_names),
    resolve_export: Some(resolve_export),
    initialize_environment: Some(initialize_environment),
    execute_module: Some(execute_module),
};

static WEBASSEMBLY_MODULE_CLASS: JSHostClass = JSHostClass::new(
    JS_HOST_CLASS_MODULE,
    "WebAssemblyModule",
    None,
    (&raw const WEBASSEMBLY_MODULE_HOOKS).cast(),
    0,
);

fn is_webassembly_module_record(module: &ModuleRecord) -> bool {
    host_module_class_of(module).is_some_and(|class| core::ptr::eq(class, &raw const WEBASSEMBLY_MODULE_CLASS))
}

fn data_of_webassembly_module_record(module: &ModuleRecord) -> Gc<EmbedderCell<WebAssemblyModuleRecord>> {
    let module = module
        .downcast_ref::<HostModule>()
        .expect("a WebAssembly Module Record is a host module");
    let data = module
        .host_data()
        .get()
        .expect("a WebAssembly Module Record has its fields");
    // SAFETY: The host data of a WebAssembly Module Record is the cell of its fields.
    unsafe { WEBASSEMBLY_MODULE_RECORD_CLASS.downcast(data) }.expect("a WebAssembly Module Record has its fields")
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `module` must be a live WebAssembly Module Record.
unsafe fn module_record_from_abi<'a>(module: *mut JSModule) -> &'a ModuleRecord {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live module.
    unsafe { &*module.cast::<ModuleRecord>() }
}

fn link_error<T>(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, message: &str) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T> {
    Err(throw_webassembly_error(vm, realm, WebAssemblyError::Link, message))
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/index.html#parse-a-webassembly-module
fn parse_a_webassembly_module(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    bytes: &[u8],
    filename: String,
    host_defined: ForeignCellSlot,
) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Gc<HostModule>> {
    // NB: The hooks of the record reach the store through the agent of the thread, which this ensures there is.
    Agent::the(vm);

    // 1. Let stableBytes be a copy of the bytes held by the buffer bytes.
    let stable_bytes = bytes.to_vec();

    // 2. Compile the WebAssembly module stableBytes and store the result as module.
    // 3. If module is error, throw a CompileError exception.
    // NOTE:  When integrating with the JS String Builtins proposal, builtinSetNames should be passed in the following
    //        step as « "js-string" » and importedStringModule as null.
    let module = compile_a_webassembly_module(vm, realm, &stable_bytes)?;

    // 5. Let requestedModules be a set.
    let mut requested_modules: Vec<ModuleRequest> = Vec::new();

    // 6. For each (moduleName, name, type) in module_imports(module.[[Module]]),
    for import in &module.imports {
        // 1. If moduleName starts with the prefix "wasm-js:",
        if import.module.starts_with("wasm-js:") {
            // 1. Throw a LinkError exception.
            return link_error(vm, realm, "Import with invalid module name");
        }

        // 2. If name starts with the prefix "wasm:" or "wasm-js:",
        if import.name.starts_with("wasm:") || import.name.starts_with("wasm-js:") {
            // 1. Throw a LinkError exception.
            return link_error(vm, realm, "Import with invalid name");
        }

        // NOTE: The following step only applies when integrating with the JS String Builtins proposal.
        // FIXME: 3. If Find a builtin with (moduleName, name, type) and builtins module.[[BuiltinSets]] is not null,
        //           then continue.

        // 4. Append moduleName to requestedModules.
        let module_name = Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(&import.module);
        if !requested_modules
            .iter()
            .any(|request| request.module_specifier == module_name)
        {
            requested_modules.push(ModuleRequest::new(module_name));
        }
    }

    // 7. For each (name, type) in module_exports(module.[[Module]])
    for export in &module.exports {
        // 1. If name starts with the prefix "wasm:" or "wasm-js:",
        if export.name.starts_with("wasm:") || export.name.starts_with("wasm-js:") {
            // 1. Throw a LinkError exception.
            return link_error(vm, realm, "Export with invalid name");
        }
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/index.html#export-name-list
    // 1. Let module be record’s [[ModuleSource]] internal slot.
    // 2. Let exports be an empty list.
    // 3. For each(name, type) in module_exports(module.[[Module]])
    //     1. Append name to the end of exports.
    // 4. Return exports.
    let export_name_list = module
        .exports
        .iter()
        .map(|export| Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(&export.name))
        .collect();

    // 4. Construct a WebAssembly module object from module and bytes, and let module be the result.
    let module_source = allocate(vm, |_| Module::new(module, stable_bytes, Vec::new(), None));

    // 8. Let moduleRecord be { [[Instance]]: ~empty~, [[Realm]]: realm, [[Environment]]: ~empty~,
    //                          [[Namespace]]: ~empty~, [[ModuleSource]]: module, [[HostDefined]]: hostDefined,
    //                          [[Status]]: "new", [[EvaluationError]]: undefined, [[DFSIndex]]: undefined,
    //                          [[DFSAncestorIndex]]: undefined, [[RequestedModules]]: requestedModules,
    //                          [[LoadedModules]]: « », [[CycleRoot]]: ~empty~, [[HasTLA]]: false,
    //                          [[AsyncEvaluation]]: false, [[TopLevelCapability]]: ~empty~ [[AsyncParentModules]]: « »,
    //                          [[PendingAsyncDependencies]]: ~empty~, }.
    let data = WEBASSEMBLY_MODULE_RECORD_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| WebAssemblyModuleRecord {
        instance: Cell::new(None),
        module_source,
        export_name_list,
    });
    let host_data = ForeignCellSlot::empty();
    // SAFETY: The fields are a live cell of the heap, which the slot then keeps alive.
    unsafe { host_data.set(Some(NonNull::new_unchecked(data.as_ptr().cast()))) };
    let module_record = HostModule::create(
        vm,
        realm,
        &WEBASSEMBLY_MODULE_CLASS,
        filename,
        requested_modules,
        host_defined,
        host_data,
    );

    // 9. Set module.[[ModuleRecord]] to moduleRecord.
    // NB: Nothing reads [[ModuleRecord]], which would keep the record alive from the module object.

    // 10. Return moduleRecord.
    Ok(module_record)
}

/// Parses a WebAssembly module, https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/index.html#parse-a-webassembly-module,
/// for HTML's create a WebAssembly module script, and writes the WebAssembly Module Record.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The pointers must be the VM, a live realm, `length` readable bytes, `filename_length` bytes of UTF-8, a live cell
/// or null, and a writable module pointer.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_web_assembly_parse_a_webassembly_module(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    bytes: *const u8,
    length: usize,
    filename: *const u8,
    filename_length: usize,
    host_defined: *mut c_void,
    module_record: *mut *mut c_void,
) -> RawNativeFunctionResult {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes the VM, a live realm, and the bytes.
    let (bytes, filename) = unsafe {
        (
            ak::slice_from_raw_parts(bytes, length),
            String::from_utf8_lossy(ak::slice_from_raw_parts(filename, filename_length)).into_owned(),
        )
    };
    let host_defined_slot = ForeignCellSlot::empty();
    // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell or null, which the slot then keeps alive.
    unsafe { host_defined_slot.set(NonNull::new(host_defined)) };
    let result = parse_a_webassembly_module(vm, realm, bytes, filename, host_defined_slot).map(|record| {
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a writable module pointer.
        unsafe { *module_record = record.as_ptr().cast() };
        Value::UNDEFINED
    });
    RawNativeFunctionResult::from_completion(result)
}

fn append_to_string_sink(sink: &JSStringSink, name: &Utf16FlyString) {
    let code_units = name.to_utf16();
    let append = sink.append.expect("a string sink appends");
    // SAFETY: The sink takes the code units for the call.
    unsafe { append(sink.context, code_units.as_ptr(), code_units.len()) };
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/index.html#get-exported-names
unsafe extern "C" fn get_exported_names(module: *mut JSModule, names: *mut JSStringSink) {
    // 1. Let record be this WebAssembly Module Record.
    // SAFETY: The runtime passes the record and a sink that outlives the call.
    let (record, names) = unsafe { (module_record_from_abi(module), &*names) };

    // 2. Return the export name list of record.
    for name in &data_of_webassembly_module_record(record).export_name_list {
        append_to_string_sink(names, name);
    }
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/index.html#resolve-export
unsafe extern "C" fn resolve_export(
    module: *mut JSModule,
    export_name: *const u16,
    export_name_length: usize,
    out: *mut JSResolvedBinding,
) {
    // 1. Let record be this WebAssembly Module Record.
    // SAFETY: The runtime passes the record, the code units of the name, and an out record.
    let (record, export_name, out) = unsafe {
        (
            module_record_from_abi(module),
            Utf16FlyString::from_utf16(if export_name_length == 0 {
                &[]
            } else {
                ak::slice_from_raw_parts(export_name, export_name_length)
            }),
            &mut *out,
        )
    };

    // 2. If the export name list of record contains exportName, return { [[Module]]: record, [[BindingName]]: exportName }.
    if data_of_webassembly_module_record(record)
        .export_name_list
        .contains(&export_name)
    {
        out.module = module;
        out.r#type = JS_RESOLVED_BINDING_BINDING_NAME;
        append_to_string_sink(&out.binding_name, &export_name);
        return;
    }

    // 3. Otherwise, return null.
    out.r#type = JS_RESOLVED_BINDING_NULL;
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/index.html#module-declaration-environment-setup
unsafe extern "C" fn initialize_environment(module: *mut JSModule) -> JSCompletion {
    let vm = Agent::current().vm();

    // 1. Let record be this WebAssembly Module Record.
    // SAFETY: The runtime passes the record.
    let record = unsafe { module_record_from_abi(module) };

    // 2. Let env be NewModuleEnvironment(null).
    let environment = ModuleEnvironment::create(vm, None);

    // 3. Set record.[[Environment]] to env.
    record.set_environment(environment);

    // 4. For each name in the export name list of record,
    for name in &data_of_webassembly_module_record(record).export_name_list {
        // 1. Perform !env.CreateImmutableBinding(name, true).
        environment.create_immutable_binding(vm, name, true).must();
    }

    completion_into_abi(Ok(()))
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/index.html#module-execution
unsafe extern "C" fn execute_module(module: *mut JSModule, capability: *mut JSPromiseCapability) -> JSCompletion {
    // 1. Assert: promiseCapability was not provided.
    assert!(capability.is_null());

    // 2. Let record be this WebAssembly Module Record.
    // SAFETY: The runtime passes the record.
    let record = unsafe { module_record_from_abi(module) };
    completion_into_abi(execute_webassembly_module_record(Agent::current().vm(), record))
}

fn execute_webassembly_module_record(vm: &Vm, record: &ModuleRecord) -> ThrowCompletionOr<()> {
    let record_data = data_of_webassembly_module_record(record);
    let realm = record.realm();

    // 3. Let module be record.[[ModuleSource]].[[Module]].
    let module = record_data.module_source.compiled_module().clone();

    // 4. Let imports be « ».
    let imports = libjs_rust::api::Root::new(vm, Imports::default());
    let mut imported_function_count = 0;

    // 5. For each (importedModuleName, name, importtype) in module_imports(module),
    for import in &module.imports {
        // NOTE: The following step only applies when integrating with the JS String Builtins proposal.
        // FIXME: 1. If Find a builtin with (importedModuleName, name) and builtins module.[[BuiltinSets]] is not null, then continue.

        // 2. Let importedModule be GetImportedModule(record, importedModuleName).
        let imported_module = record
            .as_cyclic_module()
            .expect("a host module is a Cyclic Module Record")
            .get_imported_module(&ModuleRequest::new(Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(&import.module)));

        // 3. Let resolution be importedModule.ResolveExport(name).
        let resolution = imported_module.resolve_export(vm, &Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(&import.name));

        // 4. Assert: resolution is a ResolvedBinding Record, as validated during environment initialization.
        assert!(resolution.is_valid());

        // 5. Let resolvedModule be resolution.\[[Module]].
        let resolved_module = resolution.module.expect("a resolved binding has a module");

        // 6. Let resolvedName be resolution.[[BindingName]].
        let resolved_name = &resolution.export_name;

        // 7. If resolvedModule is a WebAssembly Module Record,
        if is_webassembly_module_record(&resolved_module) {
            // 1. If resolvedModule.[[Instance]] is ~empty~, throw a {LinkError} exception.
            let Some(resolved_instance) = data_of_webassembly_module_record(&resolved_module).instance.get() else {
                return link_error(vm, realm, "Module has not been instantiated");
            };

            // 2. Assert: resolvedModule.[[Instance]] is a WebAssembly Instance object.
            // 3. Assert: resolvedModule.[[ModuleSource]] is a WebAssembly Module object.
            // 4. Let module be resolvedModule.[[ModuleSource]].[[Module]].
            // 5. Let externval be instance_export(resolvedModule.[[Instance]], resolvedName).
            // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/core/appendix/embedding.html#embed-instance-export
            // 6. Assert: externval is not error.
            let externval = Agent::the(vm)
                .store()
                .instance(resolved_instance.address())
                .export(&String::from_utf16_lossy(&resolved_name.to_utf16()))
                .expect("a WebAssembly module record exports what its export name list names");

            // 7. Assert: module_exports(module) contains an element (resolvedName, type).
            // 8. Let externtype be the value of type for the element (resolvedName, type) in module_exports(module).
            // 9. If importtype is not an extern subtype of externtype, throw a LinkError exception.
            // NB: Instantiation checks the type of every import, and throws that LinkError.

            // 10. Append externval to imports.
            imports.get().push(externval);
        }
        // 8. Otherwise,
        else {
            // 1. Let env be resolvedModule.[[Environment]].
            let environment = resolved_module
                .environment()
                .expect("a linked module has an environment");

            // 2. Let v be ?env.GetBindingValue(resolvedName, true).
            let v = environment.get_binding_value(vm, resolved_name, true)?;

            let import = match &import.description {
                // 3. If importtype is of the form func functype,
                ImportDescription::Function(type_index) => {
                    // 1. If IsCallable(v) is false, throw a LinkError exception.
                    if !v.is_function() {
                        let message = ErrorType::NotAFunction.message(&[&v.to_utf16_string_without_side_effects()]);
                        return link_error(vm, realm, &String::from_utf16_lossy(&message.to_utf16()));
                    }

                    // 2. If v has a [[FunctionAddress]] internal slot, and therefore is an Exported Function,
                    //     1. Let funcaddr be the value of v’s [[FunctionAddress]] internal slot.
                    // 3. Otherwise,
                    //     1. Create a host function from v and functype, and let funcaddr be the result.
                    //     2. Let index be the number of external functions in imports, defining the index of the host function funcaddr.
                    let function = exported_function_address(v.as_object()).unwrap_or_else(|| {
                        create_host_function(
                            vm,
                            v.as_function(),
                            function_type_in_store(vm, &module, *type_index),
                            imported_function_count,
                        )
                    });

                    // 4. Let externfunc be the external value func funcaddr.
                    // 5. Append externfunc to imports.
                    ExternValue::Function(function)
                }

                // 4. If importtype is of the form global mut valtype,
                ImportDescription::Global(ty) => {
                    let GlobalType {
                        value: valtype,
                        mutable,
                    } = global_type_in_store(vm, &module, *ty);

                    // 1. Let store be the surrounding agent’s associated store.
                    // 2. If v implements Global,
                    let global = if let Some(global) = Global::from_value(v) {
                        // 1. Let globaladdr be v.[[Global]].
                        let global = global.address();

                        // 2. Let targetmut valuetype be global_type(store, globaladdr).
                        let target_is_mutable = Agent::the(vm).store().global(global).ty.mutable;

                        // 3. If mut is const and targetmut is var, throw a LinkError exception.
                        if !mutable && target_is_mutable {
                            return link_error(vm, realm, "Mutable globals are not supported for immutable imports");
                        }
                        global
                    }
                    // 3. Otherwise,
                    else {
                        // AD-HOC: If valtype is i64 and v is a Number, throw a LinkError exception.
                        if valtype == ValType::I64 && v.is_number() {
                            return link_error(
                                vm,
                                realm,
                                "Import resolution attempted to cast a Number to a BigInteger",
                            );
                        }

                        // AD-HOC: If valtype is not i64 and v is a BigInt, throw a LinkError exception.
                        if valtype != ValType::I64 && v.is_bigint() {
                            return link_error(
                                vm,
                                realm,
                                "Import resolution attempted to cast a BigInteger to a Number",
                            );
                        }

                        // 1. If valtype is v128, throw a LinkError exception.
                        if valtype == ValType::V128 {
                            return link_error(vm, realm, "V128 is not supported as a global value type");
                        }

                        // 2. If mut is var, throw a LinkError exception.
                        if mutable {
                            return link_error(vm, realm, "Variable global value types are not supported");
                        }

                        // 3. Let value be ?ToWebAssemblyValue(v, valtype).
                        let value = to_webassembly_value(vm, v, valtype)?;

                        // 4. Let(store, globaladdr) be global_alloc(store, mut valtype, value).
                        // 5. Set the surrounding agent’s associated store to store.
                        Agent::the(vm).store().allocate_global(
                            GlobalType {
                                value: valtype,
                                mutable,
                            },
                            value,
                        )
                    };

                    // 4. Let externglobal be global globaladdr.
                    // 5. Append externglobal to imports.
                    ExternValue::Global(global)
                }

                // 5. If importtype is of the form mem memtype,
                ImportDescription::Memory(_) => {
                    // 1. If v does not implement Memory, throw a LinkError exception.
                    let Some(memory) = Memory::from_value(v) else {
                        return link_error(
                            vm,
                            realm,
                            "Expected an instance of WebAssembly.Memory for a memory import",
                        );
                    };

                    // 2. Let externmem be the external value mem v.[[Memory]].
                    // 3. Append externmem to imports.
                    ExternValue::Memory(memory.address())
                }

                // 6. If importtype is of the form table tabletype,
                ImportDescription::Table(_) => {
                    // 1. If v does not implement Table, throw a LinkError exception.
                    let Some(table) = Table::from_value(v) else {
                        return link_error(
                            vm,
                            realm,
                            "Expected an instance of WebAssembly.Table for a table import",
                        );
                    };

                    // 2. Let tableaddr be v.[[Table]].
                    // 3. Let externtable be the external value table tableaddr.
                    // 4. Append externtable to imports.
                    ExternValue::Table(table.address())
                }

                // 7. If importtype is of the form tag attribute functype,
                ImportDescription::Tag(_) => {
                    // 1. Assert: attribute is exception.
                    // 2. If v does not implement Tag, throw a LinkError exception.
                    let Some(tag) = Tag::from_value(v) else {
                        return link_error(vm, realm, "Expected an instance of WebAssembly.Tag for a tag import");
                    };

                    // 3. Let tagaddr be v.[[Address]].
                    // 4. Let externtag be the external value tag tagaddr.
                    // 5. Append externtag to imports.
                    ExternValue::Tag(tag.address())
                }
            };
            imports.get().push(import);
        }

        if matches!(import.description, ImportDescription::Function(_)) {
            imported_function_count += 1;
        }
    }

    // 6. Instantiate the core of a WebAssembly module module with imports, and let instance be the result.
    let instance_address = instantiate_the_core_of_a_webassembly_module(vm, &module, imports.get())?;

    // 7. Set record.[[Instance]] to instance.
    let instance = allocate(vm, |_| Instance::initialize(vm, realm, instance_address));
    record_data.instance.set(Some(instance));

    let environment = record.environment().expect("an evaluated module has an environment");

    // 8. For each (name, externtype) of module_exports(module),
    // NB: Converting a global's value may reach the store, so nothing of it stays borrowed across the conversion.
    for export in &module.exports {
        let name = Utf16FlyString::from_utf8(&export.name);
        let externval = Agent::the(vm)
            .store()
            .instance(instance_address)
            .export(&export.name)
            .expect("an instance has every export of its module");

        // 1. If externtype is of the form global mut globaltype,
        if let ExternValue::Global(global) = externval {
            // 1. Assert: externval is of the form global globaladdr.
            // 2. Let global globaladdr be externval.
            // 3. Let global_value be global_read(store, globaladdr).
            let (global_value, globaltype) = {
                let global = Agent::the(vm).store().global(global);
                (global.get(), global.ty.value)
            };

            // 4. If globaltype is not v128,
            if globaltype != ValType::V128 {
                // NOTE: The condition above leaves unsupported JS values as uninitialized in TDZ and therefore as a
                //       reference error on access. When integrating with shared globals, they may be excluded here
                //       similarly to v128 above.

                // 1. Perform !record.[[Environment]].InitializeBinding(name, ToJSValue(global_value)).
                let value = to_js_value(vm, global_value, globaltype)?;
                environment
                    .initialize_binding(vm, &name, value, InitializeBindingHint::Normal)
                    .must();

                // FIXME: 2. If mut is var, then associate all future mutations of globaladdr with the ECMA-262 binding record
                //        for name in record.[[Environment]], such that record.[[Environment]].GetBindingValue(resolution.[[BindingName]], true)
                //        always returns ToJSValue(global_read(store, globaladdr)) for the current surrounding agent’s associated store store.
            }
        }
        // 2. Otherwise,
        else {
            // 1. Perform !record.[[Environment]].InitializeBinding(name, !Get(instance.[[Exports]], name)).
            let exports = instance
                .exports(&mut crate::bindings::CallContext::new(vm, realm))
                .ok()
                .expect("an instance has its exports");
            let value = exports
                .get(vm, &libjs_rust::api::PropertyKey::from(name.clone()))
                .must();
            environment
                .initialize_binding(vm, &name, value, InitializeBindingHint::Normal)
                .must();
        }
    }

    // NOTE: The linking semantics here for Wasm to Wasm modules are identical to the WebAssembly JS API semantics as if
    //       passing the the exports object as the imports object in instantiation. When linking Wasm module imports to
    //       JS module exports, the JS API semantics are exactly followed as well. It is only in the case of importing
    //       Wasm from JS that WebAssembly.Global unwrapping is observable on the WebAssembly Module Record Environment
    //       Record.

    Ok(())
}

//! Module, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#modules

use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferShared, Gc, MarkedVec, Realm, Trace, Value};
use libwasm_engine::module::{ExternalKind, ImportDescription};

use crate::bindings::conversions::{BufferSource, UsvString};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable};
use crate::bindings::structured_data::{Serializable, SerializationReader, SerializationWriter};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::web_assembly::builtins::{import_refers_to_a_builtin, validate_builtins_and_imported_strings};
use crate::web_assembly::errors::{WebAssemblyError, throw_webassembly_error};
use crate::web_assembly::web_assembly::WebAssemblyCompileOptions;
use crate::web_assembly::{CompiledModule, compile_a_webassembly_module, implementation_of_value, stable_bytes_of};

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// The current Realm's corresponding agent cluster, as the ID it has if it has one.
    fn web_bindings_current_agent_cluster(agent_cluster: *mut u64) -> bool;

    /// The realm's corresponding agent cluster, as the ID it has if it has one.
    fn web_bindings_agent_cluster_of_realm(realm: *mut c_void, agent_cluster: *mut u64) -> bool;
}

fn current_agent_cluster() -> Option<u64> {
    let mut agent_cluster = 0;
    // SAFETY: The agent cluster is written if there is one.
    unsafe { web_bindings_current_agent_cluster(&raw mut agent_cluster) }.then_some(agent_cluster)
}

fn agent_cluster_of_realm(realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut agent_cluster = 0;
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the agent cluster is written if there is one.
    unsafe { web_bindings_agent_cluster_of_realm(realm.as_ptr().cast(), &raw mut agent_cluster) }
        .then_some(agent_cluster)
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#enumdef-importexportkind
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum ImportExportKind {
    Function,
    Table,
    Memory,
    Global,
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dictdef-moduleexportdescriptor
pub(crate) struct ModuleExportDescriptor {
    pub(crate) name: UsvString,
    pub(crate) kind: ImportExportKind,
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dictdef-moduleimportdescriptor
pub(crate) struct ModuleImportDescriptor {
    pub(crate) module: UsvString,
    pub(crate) name: UsvString,
    pub(crate) kind: ImportExportKind,
}

fn import_export_kind(kind: ExternalKind) -> Option<ImportExportKind> {
    match kind {
        ExternalKind::Function => Some(ImportExportKind::Function),
        ExternalKind::Table => Some(ImportExportKind::Table),
        ExternalKind::Memory => Some(ImportExportKind::Memory),
        ExternalKind::Global => Some(ImportExportKind::Global),
        ExternalKind::Tag => None,
    }
}

fn kind_of_import(description: &ImportDescription) -> ExternalKind {
    match description {
        ImportDescription::Function(_) => ExternalKind::Function,
        ImportDescription::Table(_) => ExternalKind::Table,
        ImportDescription::Memory(_) => ExternalKind::Memory,
        ImportDescription::Global(_) => ExternalKind::Global,
        ImportDescription::Tag(_) => ExternalKind::Tag,
    }
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Module {
    // [[Module]]
    #[gc(untraced)]
    module: CompiledModule,
    // [[Bytes]]
    // NB: The compiled module can't provide these, as the validator quickens the code in its own copy of the bytes.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    bytes: Vec<u8>,
    // [[BuiltinSets]]
    #[gc(untraced)]
    builtin_sets: Vec<UsvString>,
    // [[ImportedStringModule]]
    #[gc(untraced)]
    imported_string_module: Option<UsvString>,
}

impl Wrappable for Module {}

impl Module {
    /// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#construct-a-webassembly-module-object
    pub(crate) fn new(
        module: CompiledModule,
        bytes: Vec<u8>,
        builtin_sets: Vec<UsvString>,
        imported_string_module: Option<UsvString>,
    ) -> Self {
        // 1. Let moduleObject be a new Module.
        // 2. Set moduleObject.[[Module]] to module.
        // 3. Set moduleObject.[[Bytes]] to bytes.
        // 4. Set moduleObject.[[BuiltinSets]] to builtinSetNames.
        // 5. Set moduleObject.[[ImportedStringModule]] to importedStringModule.
        // 6. Return moduleObject.
        Self {
            module,
            bytes,
            builtin_sets,
            imported_string_module,
        }
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-module-module
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        bytes: BufferSource,
        options: WebAssemblyCompileOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Let stableBytes be a copy of the bytes held by the buffer bytes.
        let stable_bytes = stable_bytes_of(bytes);

        // 2. Compile the WebAssembly module stableBytes and store the result as module.
        // 3. If module is error, throw a CompileError exception.
        let module = compile_a_webassembly_module(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &stable_bytes)?;

        // 4. Let builtinSetNames be options["builtins"].
        let builtin_set_names = options.builtins;

        // 5. Let importedStringModule be options["importedStringConstants"].
        let imported_string_module = options.imported_string_constants;

        // 6. If validating builtins and imported strings for module with builtinSetNames and importedStringModule returns
        //    false, throw a CompileError exception.
        if !validate_builtins_and_imported_strings(
            cx.vm(),
            &module,
            &builtin_set_names,
            imported_string_module.as_ref(),
        ) {
            return Err(throw_webassembly_error(
                cx.vm(),
                cx.realm(),
                WebAssemblyError::Compile,
                "Invalid builtin or imported string",
            )
            .into());
        }

        // 7. Set this.[[Module]] to module.
        // 8. Set this.[[Bytes]] to stableBytes.
        // 9. Set this.[[BuiltinSets]] to builtinSetNames.
        // 10. Set this.[[ImportedStringModule]] to importedStringModule.
        Ok(Self::new(
            module,
            stable_bytes,
            builtin_set_names,
            imported_string_module,
        ))
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_value(value: Value) -> Option<Ref<Self>> {
        implementation_of_value(value)
    }

    pub(crate) fn compiled_module(&self) -> &CompiledModule {
        &self.module
    }

    pub(crate) fn builtin_sets(&self) -> &[UsvString] {
        &self.builtin_sets
    }

    pub(crate) fn imported_string_module(&self) -> Option<&UsvString> {
        self.imported_string_module.as_ref()
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/index.html#dom-module-exports
    pub(crate) fn exports(_: &mut CallContext, module_object: Ref<Self>) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<ModuleExportDescriptor>> {
        // 1. Let module be moduleObject.[[Module]].
        // 2. Let exports be « ».
        // 3. For each (name, type) of module_exports(module),
        let exports = module_object
            .module
            .exports
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|export| {
                // 3.1. Let kind be the string value of the extern type type.
                // FIXME: Exporting tags.
                let kind = import_export_kind(export.kind)?;

                // 3.2. Let obj be «[ "name" → name, "kind" → kind ]».
                // 3.3. Append obj to exports.
                Some(ModuleExportDescriptor {
                    name: UsvString::from_utf8(&export.name),
                    kind,
                })
            })
            .collect();

        // 4. Return exports.
        Ok(exports)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-module-imports
    pub(crate) fn imports(_: &mut CallContext, module_object: Ref<Self>) -> WebIdlResult<Vec<ModuleImportDescriptor>> {
        // 1. Let module be moduleObject.[[Module]].
        let module = &module_object.module;

        // 2. Let builtinSetNames be moduleObject.[[BuiltinSets]].
        let builtin_set_names = &module_object.builtin_sets;

        // 3. Let importedStringModule be moduleObject.[[ImportedStringModule]].
        let imported_string_module = module_object.imported_string_module.as_ref().map(UsvString::to_utf8);

        // 4. Let imports be « ».
        // 5. For each (moduleName, name, type) of module_imports(module),
        let imports = module
            .imports
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|import| {
                // 1. If find a builtin for (moduleName, name, type) and builtinSetNames is not null, then continue.
                if import_refers_to_a_builtin(import, builtin_set_names) {
                    return None;
                }

                // 2. If importedStringModule is not null and moduleName equals importedStringModule, then continue.
                if imported_string_module.as_ref() == Some(&import.module) {
                    return None;
                }

                // 3. Let kind be the string value of the extern type type.
                // FIXME: Importing tags.
                let kind = import_export_kind(kind_of_import(&import.description))?;

                // 4. Let obj be «[ "module" → moduleName, "name" → name, "kind" → kind ]».
                // 5. Append obj to imports.
                Some(ModuleImportDescriptor {
                    module: UsvString::from_utf8(&import.module),
                    name: UsvString::from_utf8(&import.name),
                    kind,
                })
            })
            .collect();

        // 6. Return imports.
        Ok(imports)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/threads/js-api/index.html#dom-module-customsections
    pub(crate) fn custom_sections<'vm>(
        cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
        module_object: Ref<Self>,
        section_name: Utf16String,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, Gc<ArrayBuffer>>> {
        // 1. Let bytes be moduleObject.[[Bytes]].
        // 2. Let customSections be « ».
        let module = &module_object.module;
        let custom_sections = MarkedVec::new(cx.vm());

        // 3. For each custom section customSection of bytes, interpreted according to the module grammar,
        for section in &module.custom_sections {
            if Utf16String::from_utf8(&section.name) != section_name {
                continue;
            }
            // 3.3.1. Append a new ArrayBuffer containing a copy of the bytes in bytes for the range matched by this customsec production to customSections.
            let contents = &module.bytes[section.contents.start as usize..section.contents.end as usize];
            custom_sections.push(ArrayBuffer::create_from_bytes(
                cx.vm(),
                cx.realm(),
                contents,
                ArrayBufferShared::No,
            ));
        }

        // 4. Return customSections.
        Ok(custom_sections)
    }
}

impl Serializable for Module {
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/web-api/#ref-for-serialization-steps
    fn serialization_steps(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
        for_storage: bool,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If forStorage is true, throw a "DataCloneError" DOMException.
        if for_storage {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "DataCloneError",
                Utf16String::from_utf8("WebAssembly Module instances may not be serialized for storage"),
            ));
        }

        // 2. Set serialized.[[Bytes]] to the sub-serialization of value.[[Bytes]].
        serialized.write_bytes(&self.bytes);

        // 3. Set serialized.[[AgentCluster]] to the current Realm’s corresponding agent cluster.
        serialized.write_optional_u64(current_agent_cluster());

        // AD-HOC: Recompiling needs the options the module was compiled with, or its builtins and imported strings
        //         would turn into ordinary imports.
        serialized.write_u64(self.builtin_sets.len() as u64);
        for builtin_set in &self.builtin_sets {
            serialized.write_utf16_string(builtin_set.as_utf16_string());
        }
        serialized.write_bool(self.imported_string_module.is_some());
        if let Some(imported_string_module) = &self.imported_string_module {
            serialized.write_utf16_string(imported_string_module.as_utf16_string());
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/web-api/#ref-for-deserialization-steps
    fn deserialization_steps(cx: &mut CallContext, serialized: &mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<Self> {
        // 1. Let bytes be the sub-deserialization of serialized.[[Bytes]].
        // 2. Set value.[[Bytes]] to bytes.
        let bytes = serialized.read_bytes()?;

        // 3. If targetRealm’s corresponding agent cluster is not serialized.[[AgentCluster]], then throw a "DataCloneError" DOMException.
        let agent_cluster = serialized.read_optional_u64()?;
        if agent_cluster.is_none() || agent_cluster != agent_cluster_of_realm(cx.realm()) {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "DataCloneError",
                Utf16String::from_utf8("Cannot deserialize WebAssembly Module outside its agent cluster"),
            ));
        }

        // AD-HOC: See the serialization steps.
        let builtin_set_count = serialized.read_u64()?;
        let mut builtin_sets = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..builtin_set_count {
            builtin_sets.push(UsvString::from_utf16_string(&serialized.read_utf16_string()?));
        }
        let imported_string_module = if serialized.read_bool()? {
            Some(UsvString::from_utf16_string(&serialized.read_utf16_string()?))
        } else {
            None
        };

        // 4. Compile a WebAssembly module from bytes and set value.[[Module]] to the result.
        let module = compile_a_webassembly_module(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &bytes)?;
        Ok(Self::new(module, bytes, builtin_sets, imported_string_module))
    }
}

//! Table, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#tables

use libjs_rust::api::{BigInt, Trace, Value, Vm};
use libwasm_engine::runtime::{TableAddress, TableInstance, Value as WasmValue};
use libwasm_engine::types::{AddressType as CoreAddressType, HeapType, Limits, RefType, TableType, ValType};

use crate::bindings::conversions::to_unsigned_long_enforcing_range;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};
use crate::web_assembly::values::{default_webassembly_value, to_js_value, to_webassembly_value};
use crate::web_assembly::{Agent, EntityRef, host_object, implementation_of_value, set_host_object};

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#enumdef-addresstype
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum AddressType {
    I32,
    I64,
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#enumdef-tablekind
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum TableKind {
    Externref,
    Anyfunc,
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dictdef-tabledescriptor
pub(crate) struct TableDescriptor {
    pub(crate) element: TableKind,
    pub(crate) initial: Value,
    pub(crate) maximum: Option<Value>,
    pub(crate) address: Option<AddressType>,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Table {
    // [[Table]]
    address: EntityRef<TableInstance>,
}

impl Wrappable for Table {}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#addressvaluetou64
fn address_value_to_u64(vm: &Vm, value: Value, address64: bool) -> WebIdlResult<u64> {
    if address64 {
        let n = value.to_bigint(vm)?;

        return n
            .to_u64_if_exact()
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::type_error("The table address value is out of range"));
    }

    Ok(u64::from(to_unsigned_long_enforcing_range(vm, value)?))
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#u64toaddressvalue
fn u64_to_address_value(vm: &Vm, value: u64, address64: bool) -> Value {
    if address64 {
        return Value::from_bigint(BigInt::create_from_u64(vm, value));
    }

    Value::from_f64(value as f64)
}

impl Table {
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-table-table
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        descriptor: TableDescriptor,
        value: Option<Value>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Let elementtype be ToValueType(descriptor["element"]).
        // NB: The TableKind enumeration only has reference types.
        let element = RefType {
            nullable: true,
            heap: match descriptor.element {
                TableKind::Externref => HeapType::Extern,
                TableKind::Anyfunc => HeapType::Func,
            },
        };

        // 3. If descriptor["address"] exists, let addrtype be descriptor["address"]; otherwise, let addrtype be "i32".
        let address64 = descriptor.address == Some(AddressType::I64);

        // 4. Let initial be ? AddressValueToU64(descriptor["initial"], addrtype).
        let initial = address_value_to_u64(vm, descriptor.initial, address64)?;

        let maximum = descriptor
            .maximum
            .map(|maximum| address_value_to_u64(vm, maximum, address64))
            .transpose()?;

        if maximum.is_some_and(|maximum| maximum < initial) {
            return Err(Exception::range_error(
                "Maximum should not be less than initial in table type",
            ));
        }

        // 8. If value is missing,
        //     1. Let ref be DefaultValue(elementtype).
        //     2. Assert: ref is not error.
        // 9. Otherwise,
        //     1. Let ref be ? ToWebAssemblyValue(value, elementtype).
        let reference = Self::value_or_default(vm, ValType::Ref(element), value)?
            .expect("ToValueType gives types with a default value");

        // 11. Let (store, tableaddr) be table_alloc(store, type, ref). If allocation fails, throw a RangeError exception.
        // 12. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
        let table = Agent::the(vm)
            .store()
            .allocate_table(
                TableType {
                    element,
                    limits: Limits {
                        min: initial,
                        max: maximum,
                        address_type: if address64 {
                            CoreAddressType::I64
                        } else {
                            CoreAddressType::I32
                        },
                        shared: false,
                    },
                },
                reference,
            )
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::range_error("Wasm Table allocation failed"))?;

        // 13. Initialize this from tableaddr.
        Ok(Self::initialize(vm, table))
    }

    /// Returns `None` where DefaultValue(ty) is an error.
    fn value_or_default(vm: &Vm, ty: ValType, value: Option<Value>) -> WebIdlResult<Option<u64>> {
        Ok(match value {
            None => default_webassembly_value(vm, ty).map(reference_of),
            Some(value) => Some(reference_of(to_webassembly_value(vm, value, ty)?)),
        })
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#initialize-a-table-object
    fn initialize(vm: &Vm, table: TableAddress) -> Ref<Self> {
        // 2. Assert: map[tableaddr] doesn't exist.
        assert!(host_object::<()>(table.cell()).is_none());

        // 3. Set table.[[Table]] to tableaddr.
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            address: EntityRef(table),
        });

        // 4. Set map[tableaddr] to table.
        set_host_object(table.cell(), object);
        object
    }

    /// The Table object of the table, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-table-object
    pub(crate) fn from_address(vm: &Vm, table: TableAddress) -> Ref<Self> {
        if let Some(object) = host_object(table.cell()) {
            return object;
        }

        Self::initialize(vm, table)
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_value(value: Value) -> Option<Ref<Self>> {
        implementation_of_value(value)
    }

    pub(crate) fn address(&self) -> TableAddress {
        self.address.0
    }

    fn ty(&self, vm: &Vm) -> TableType {
        Agent::the(vm).store().table(self.address()).ty
    }

    fn is_address64(&self, vm: &Vm) -> bool {
        self.ty(vm).limits.address_type == CoreAddressType::I64
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-table-grow
    pub(crate) fn grow(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, delta: Value, value: Option<Value>) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 3. Let initialSize be table_size(store, tableaddr).
        let ty = self.ty(vm);
        let address64 = ty.limits.address_type == CoreAddressType::I64;

        let delta = address_value_to_u64(vm, delta, address64)?;

        // 6. If value is missing,
        //     1. Let ref be DefaultValue(elementtype).
        //     2. If ref is error, throw a TypeError exception.
        // 7. Otherwise,
        //     1. Let ref be ? ToWebAssemblyValue(value, elementtype).
        let reference = Self::value_or_default(vm, ValType::Ref(ty.element), value)?
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::type_error("The table's element type has no default value"))?;

        // 10. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to result.
        let initial_size = Agent::the(vm)
            .store()
            .table_mut(self.address())
            .grow(delta, reference)
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::range_error("Failed to grow table"))?;

        Ok(u64_to_address_value(vm, initial_size, address64))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-table-length
    pub(crate) fn length(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        let length = Agent::the(vm).store().table(self.address()).elements.len() as u64;

        Ok(u64_to_address_value(vm, length, self.is_address64(vm)))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-table-get
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, index: Value) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 3. Let (addrtype, limits, elementtype) be table_type(store, tableaddr).
        let ty = self.ty(vm);

        if matches!(ty.element.heap, HeapType::Exn | HeapType::NoExn) {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Cannot get an exnref table element"));
        }

        let index = address_value_to_u64(vm, index, ty.limits.address_type == CoreAddressType::I64)?;

        // 6. Let result be table_read(store, tableaddr, index64).
        // 7. If result is error, throw a RangeError exception.
        let reference = usize::try_from(index)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|index| {
                Agent::the(vm)
                    .store()
                    .table(self.address())
                    .elements
                    .get(index)
                    .copied()
            })
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::range_error("Table element index out of range"))?;

        Ok(to_js_value(vm, WasmValue::Ref(reference), ValType::Ref(ty.element))?)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-table-set
    pub(crate) fn set(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, index: Value, value: Option<Value>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 3. Let (addrtype, limits, elementtype) be table_type(store, tableaddr).
        let ty = self.ty(vm);

        if matches!(ty.element.heap, HeapType::Exn | HeapType::NoExn) {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("Cannot set an exnref table element"));
        }

        let index = address_value_to_u64(vm, index, ty.limits.address_type == CoreAddressType::I64)?;

        // 6. If value is missing,
        //     1. Let ref be DefaultValue(elementtype).
        //     2. If ref is error, throw a TypeError exception.
        // 7. Otherwise,
        //     1. Let ref be ? ToWebAssemblyValue(value, elementtype).
        let reference = Self::value_or_default(vm, ValType::Ref(ty.element), value)?
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::type_error("The table's element type has no default value"))?;

        // 8. Let store be table_write(store, tableaddr, index64, ref).
        // 9. If store is error, throw a RangeError exception.
        // 10. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
        let element = usize::try_from(index)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|index| Agent::the(vm).store().table_mut(self.address()).elements.get_mut(index))
            .ok_or_else(|| Exception::range_error("Table element index out of range"))?;
        *element = reference;
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn reference_of(value: WasmValue) -> u64 {
    match value {
        WasmValue::Ref(reference) => reference,
        _ => unreachable!("a table holds references"),
    }
}

//! Tag, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#tags

use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Trace, Value, Vm};
use libwasm_engine::runtime::{TagAddress, TagInstance};
use libwasm_engine::types::FuncType;

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::realm_data::realm_data;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::web_assembly::global::ValueType;
use crate::web_assembly::{Agent, EntityRef, host_object, implementation_of_value, set_host_object};

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dictdef-tagtype
pub(crate) struct TagType {
    pub(crate) parameters: Vec<ValueType>,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Tag {
    // [[Address]]
    address: EntityRef<TagInstance>,
}

impl Wrappable for Tag {}

impl Tag {
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-tag-tag
    pub(crate) fn construct(cx: &mut CallContext, r#type: TagType) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // 1. Let parameters be type["parameters"].
        // 2. Let wasmParameters be «».
        // 3. For each type of parameters,
        //     1. Append ToValueType(type) to wasmParameters.
        let parameters = r#type
            .parameters
            .iter()
            .map(|parameter| parameter.to_value_type())
            .collect();

        // 4. Let store be the surrounding agent's associated store.
        // 5. Let (store, tagAddress) be tag_alloc(store, « wasmParameters » → « »).
        // 6. Set the surrounding agent's associated store to store.
        let tag = Agent::the(cx.vm()).store().allocate_tag(FuncType {
            params: parameters,
            results: Vec::new(),
        });

        // 7. Initialize this from tagAddress.
        Ok(Self::initialize(cx.vm(), tag))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#initialize-a-tag-object
    fn initialize(vm: &Vm, tag: TagAddress) -> Ref<Self> {
        // 1. Let map be the surrounding agent's associated tag object cache.
        // 3. Set tag.[[Address]] to tagAddress.
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            address: EntityRef(tag),
        });

        // 4. Set map[tagAddress] to tag.
        set_host_object(tag.cell(), object);
        object
    }

    /// The Tag object of the tag in the realm, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-tag-object
    pub(crate) fn from_address(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>, tag: TagAddress) -> Ref<Self> {
        // NB: The JavaScript exception tag lives as long as the agent, while a Tag object belongs to the realm it is
        //     first wrapped in, so every realm has a Tag object of its own for it.
        if tag == Agent::the(vm).js_tag() {
            let data = realm_data(vm, realm);
            if let Some(object) = data.webassembly_js_tag.get() {
                return object;
            }
            let object = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
                address: EntityRef(tag),
            });
            data.webassembly_js_tag.set(Some(object));
            return object;
        }

        // 1. Let map be the surrounding agent's associated tag object cache.
        // 2. If map[tagAddress] exists,
        //     1. Return map[tagAddress].
        if let Some(object) = host_object(tag.cell()) {
            return object;
        }

        // 3. Let tag be a new Tag.
        // 4. Initialize tag from tagAddress.
        // 5. Return tag.
        Self::initialize(vm, tag)
    }

    pub(crate) fn from_value(value: Value) -> Option<Ref<Self>> {
        implementation_of_value(value)
    }

    pub(crate) fn address(&self) -> TagAddress {
        self.address.0
    }
}

/*

//! The conversions between JavaScript values and WebAssembly values, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#tojsvalue
//!
//! References are encoded so that their kind shows in their low bits: an i31 has bit 0 set, and a host value has bits
//! 1:0 equal to 0b10. A host value is the address of a cell with bit 1 set, which keeps the cell alive wherever
//! WebAssembly keeps the reference. Functions, structs, arrays and exceptions are the addresses of their cells.

use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{
    Array, BigInt, CellHeader, CellKind, EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, ErrorKind, Gc, Object,
    ThrowCompletionOr, Trace, Value, Vm,
};
use libwasm_engine::runtime::Value as WasmValue;
use libwasm_engine::types::{HeapType, RefType, ValType};

use crate::web_assembly::Agent;
use crate::web_assembly::exported_function::{create_exported_function, exported_function_address};
use crate::web_assembly::gc_object::{create_exported_gc_object, exported_gc_object_address};

const I31_REFERENCE_BIT: u64 = 0b01;
const HOST_REFERENCE_TAG: u64 = 0b10;
const REFERENCE_TAG_MASK: u64 = 0b11;

/// A JavaScript value that is not a cell, boxed so that WebAssembly can refer to it as a host value.
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct ExternValueBox {
    value: Value,
}

static EXTERN_VALUE_BOX_CLASS: EmbedderClass<ExternValueBox> = EmbedderClass::new("ExternValueBox");

impl EmbedderValue for ExternValueBox {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &EXTERN_VALUE_BOX_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) const EXTERNREF: ValType = ValType::Ref(RefType {
    nullable: true,
    heap: HeapType::Extern,
});

/// Whether a type matches v128 or exnref, whose values have no JavaScript value.
pub(crate) fn matches_v128_or_exnref(ty: ValType) -> bool {
    matches!(
        ty,
        ValType::V128
            | ValType::Ref(RefType {
                heap: HeapType::Exn | HeapType::NoExn,
                ..
            })
    )
}

fn host_reference_of(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> u64 {
    let cell = if value.is_cell() {
        value.as_cell().as_ptr().cast::<u8>()
    } else {
        // NB: A value gets the same box while references to the box keep it alive, so that it converts to the same
        //     reference.
        let agent = Agent::the(vm);
        let value_box = agent.extern_value_box(value).unwrap_or_else(|| {
            let value_box = EXTERN_VALUE_BOX_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| ExternValueBox { value });
            agent.set_extern_value_box(value, value_box);
            value_box
        });
        value_box.as_ptr().cast::<u8>()
    };
    cell as u64 | HOST_REFERENCE_TAG
}

fn value_of_host_reference(reference: u64) -> Value {
    let address = (reference & !REFERENCE_TAG_MASK) as *mut CellHeader;
    // SAFETY: A host reference is the address of a live cell, which starts with its header.
    let kind = unsafe { (*address).kind };
    // SAFETY: The kind of the cell says what it is.
    unsafe {
        match kind {
            CellKind::Object => Value::from_object(Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new_unchecked(address.cast::<Object>()))),
            CellKind::PrimitiveString => Value::from_string(Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new_unchecked(address.cast()))),
            CellKind::Symbol => Value::from_symbol(Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new_unchecked(address.cast()))),
            CellKind::BigInt => Value::from_bigint(Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new_unchecked(address.cast()))),
            CellKind::Other => {
                let value_box: Gc<EmbedderCell<ExternValueBox>> =
                    Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new_unchecked(address.cast()));
                value_box.value
            }
            CellKind::Accessor => unreachable!("an accessor is no JavaScript value"),
        }
    }
}

fn i31_reference_of(value: Value) -> Option<u64> {
    const I31_MINIMUM: f64 = -((1 << 30) as f64);
    const I31_MAXIMUM: f64 = ((1 << 30) - 1) as f64;
    if !value.is_number() {
        return None;
    }
    let number = value.as_f64();
    if !(I31_MINIMUM..=I31_MAXIMUM).contains(&number)
        || number != number.trunc()
        || (number == 0.0 && number.is_sign_negative())
    {
        return None;
    }
    Some((u64::from((number as i32 as u32) & 0x7fff_ffff) << 1) | I31_REFERENCE_BIT)
}

fn value_of_i31_reference(reference: u64) -> i32 {
    // The value is in bits 31:1, so an arithmetic shift of the low 32 bits sign-extends it.
    (reference as u32 as i32) >> 1
}

/// The internal form of a JavaScript value as a reference of the any hierarchy: an i31 reference for a Number in its
/// range, the struct or array of an Exported GC Object, and otherwise a host reference.
fn internalized_reference_of(vm: &Vm, value: Value) -> u64 {
    if let Some(reference) = i31_reference_of(value) {
        return reference;
    }
    if value.is_object()
        && let Some(address) = exported_gc_object_address(value.as_object())
    {
        return address;
    }
    host_reference_of(vm, value)
}

/// Whether a reference type is of the func hierarchy, whose references are functions.
fn is_function_reference_type(vm: &Vm, heap: HeapType) -> bool {
    match heap {
        HeapType::Concrete(identity) => Agent::the(vm).store().is_function_type(identity),
        HeapType::Func | HeapType::NoFunc => true,
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn type_error<T>(vm: &Vm, message: &str) -> ThrowCompletionOr<T> {
    vm.throw_completion_with_message(ErrorKind::TypeError, message.to_string())
}

// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#towebassemblyvalue
fn to_webassembly_reference(vm: &Vm, value: Value, ty: RefType) -> ThrowCompletionOr<u64> {
    // If v is null: if the type is nullable, return ref.null of its heap type, and otherwise throw a TypeError.
    if value.is_null() {
        if !ty.nullable {
            return type_error(vm, "Cannot convert null to a non-nullable reference");
        }
        return Ok(0);
    }

    match ty.heap {
        HeapType::Exn | HeapType::NoExn => {
            return type_error(vm, "Cannot convert a JavaScript value to an exception reference");
        }
        HeapType::NoFunc | HeapType::NoExtern | HeapType::None | HeapType::Bottom => {
            return type_error(vm, "Only null converts to a bottom reference type");
        }
        // NB: An externref keeps the bits of the anyref it externalizes.
        HeapType::Extern => return Ok(internalized_reference_of(vm, value)),
        _ => {}
    }

    // If the type is of the func hierarchy, only an Exported Function of a matching type converts, to its function.
    if is_function_reference_type(vm, ty.heap) {
        if value.is_function()
            && let Some(address) = exported_function_address(value.as_object())
        {
            let store = Agent::the(vm).store();
            let reference = store.function_reference(address);
            if store.reference_matches(reference, ty.heap) {
                return Ok(reference);
            }
        }
        return type_error(vm, "Cannot convert the value to a function reference of this type");
    }

    // Otherwise the type is of the any hierarchy: the internal form of v converts if it matches the type.
    let reference = internalized_reference_of(vm, value);
    if !Agent::the(vm).store().reference_matches(reference, ty.heap) {
        return type_error(vm, "Cannot convert the value to a reference of this type");
    }
    Ok(reference)
}

/// ToWebAssemblyValue(v, type), https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#towebassemblyvalue, for a type in the store's
/// terms (see Store::module_type_identities()).
pub(crate) fn to_webassembly_value(vm: &Vm, value: Value, ty: ValType) -> ThrowCompletionOr<WasmValue> {
    Ok(match ty {
        ValType::I64 => WasmValue::I64(value.to_bigint_int64(vm)?),
        ValType::I32 => WasmValue::I32(value.to_i32(vm)?),
        ValType::F64 => WasmValue::F64(value.to_double(vm)?.to_bits()),
        ValType::F32 => WasmValue::F32((value.to_double(vm)? as f32).to_bits()),
        ValType::V128 => return type_error(vm, "Cannot convert a javascript value to a vector value"),
        ValType::Ref(ty) => WasmValue::Ref(to_webassembly_reference(vm, value, ty)?),
    })
}

/// DefaultValue(valuetype), https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#defaultvalue
/// Returns `None` where it is an error.
pub(crate) fn default_webassembly_value(vm: &Vm, ty: ValType) -> Option<WasmValue> {
    // 1. If valuetype equals externref, return ! ToWebAssemblyValue(undefined, valuetype).
    if ty
        == ValType::Ref(RefType {
            nullable: true,
            heap: HeapType::Extern,
        })
    {
        return Some(WasmValue::Ref(host_reference_of(vm, Value::UNDEFINED)));
    }

    // 2. Return val_default(valuetype).
    // NB: A non-nullable reference type has no default value.
    match ty {
        ValType::Ref(RefType { nullable: false, .. }) => None,
        _ => Some(WasmValue::default_for(ty)),
    }
}

/// ToJSValue(w), https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#tojsvalue, for a value of the type, which is in the store's
/// terms.
pub(crate) fn to_js_value(vm: &Vm, value: WasmValue, ty: ValType) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    let reference = match (value, ty) {
        (WasmValue::I64(value), _) => return Ok(Value::from_bigint(BigInt::create_from_i64(vm, value))),
        (WasmValue::I32(value), _) => return Ok(Value::from_i32(value)),
        (WasmValue::F64(bits), _) => return Ok(Value::from_f64(f64::from_bits(bits))),
        (WasmValue::F32(bits), _) => return Ok(Value::from_f64(f64::from(f32::from_bits(bits)))),
        (WasmValue::V128(_), _) => return type_error(vm, "Cannot convert a vector value to a javascript value"),
        (WasmValue::Ref(reference), _) => reference,
    };
    let ValType::Ref(ty) = ty else {
        unreachable!("a reference has a reference type");
    };

    if matches!(ty.heap, HeapType::Exn | HeapType::NoExn) {
        return type_error(vm, "Cannot convert an exception reference to a javascript value");
    }

    // 1. If w is of the form ref.null t, return null.
    if reference == 0 {
        return Ok(Value::NULL);
    }

    // 2. If w is of the form ref.func funcaddr, return the result of creating a new Exported Function from funcaddr.
    if is_function_reference_type(vm, ty.heap) {
        let function = Agent::the(vm)
            .store()
            .function_from_reference(reference)
            .expect("a function reference that is not null is a function");
        let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a conversion runs in a realm");
        return Ok(Value::from_object(
            create_exported_function(vm, realm, function).upcast::<Object>(),
        ));
    }

    // 3. If w is of the form ref.i31 u31, return 𝔽(signed_31(u31)).
    if reference & I31_REFERENCE_BIT != 0 {
        return Ok(Value::from_i32(value_of_i31_reference(reference)));
    }

    // 4. If w is of the form ref.host hostaddr, return the result of retrieving a host value from hostaddr.
    // NB: An externref of a host value keeps the bits of the host reference.
    if reference & REFERENCE_TAG_MASK == HOST_REFERENCE_TAG {
        return Ok(value_of_host_reference(reference));
    }

    // 5. If w is of the form ref.struct structaddr or ref.array arrayaddr, return the result of creating a new Exported
    //    GC Object from it.
    Ok(Value::from_object(create_exported_gc_object(vm, reference)))
}

/// The JavaScript value of the results of a call: undefined for none, the one result, or an array of them.
pub(crate) fn results_to_js_value(vm: &Vm, results: &[WasmValue], types: &[ValType]) -> ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
    match results {
        [] => Ok(Value::UNDEFINED),
        [result] => to_js_value(vm, *result, types[0]),
        _ => {
            let values = libjs_rust::api::MarkedVec::with_capacity(vm, results.len());
            for (result, ty) in results.iter().zip(types) {
                values.push(to_js_value(vm, *result, *ty)?);
            }
            let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("a conversion runs in a realm");
            Ok(Value::from_object(
                Array::create_from(vm, realm, &values.values()).upcast::<Object>(),
            ))
        }
    }
}

//! The WebAssembly namespace, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#webassembly-namespace, and its streaming
//! functions, https://webassembly.github.io/spec/web-api/index.html#streaming-modules

    Attribute, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, Object, PropertyAttributes, PropertyKey, RawNativeFunctionResult,
    Realm, Trace, Value, Visitor, Vm,
};

use crate::bindings::conversions::ToJs;

    resolve_promise,
