/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dictdef-webassemblyinstantiatedsource
pub(crate) struct WebAssemblyInstantiatedSource {
    pub(crate) module: Ref<Module>,
    pub(crate) instance: Ref<Instance>,
}

impl WebAssemblyInstantiatedSource {
    fn into_js(self, cx: &CallContext) -> libjs_rust::api::ThrowCompletionOr<Value> {
        // NB: The generated bindings convert the dictionary, which a build of the crate on its own leaves out.
        #[cfg(web_idl_bindings)]
        return ToJs::to_js(self, cx);
        #[cfg(not(web_idl_bindings))]
        {
            let _ = (self, cx);
            unreachable!("only the generated bindings resolve a promise with the dictionary")
        }
    }
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dictdef-webassemblycompileoptions
#[derive(Clone, Default, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct WebAssemblyCompileOptions {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) imported_string_constants: Option<UsvString>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) builtins: Vec<UsvString>,
}

static COMPILE_OPTIONS_CLASS: EmbedderClass<WebAssemblyCompileOptions> =
    EmbedderClass::new("WebAssemblyCompileOptions");

impl EmbedderValue for WebAssemblyCompileOptions {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &COMPILE_OPTIONS_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) struct WebAssembly;

/// The bytes that asynchronously compiling a module compiles in parallel, the options it compiles them with, and what
/// compiling them results in.
struct CompileJob {
    bytes: RefCell<Vec<u8>>,
    options: RefCell<WebAssemblyCompileOptions>,
    result: RefCell<Option<Result<CompiledModule, Value>>>,
}

// SAFETY: The exception that compiling the bytes throws is the one cell the job holds.
unsafe impl Trace for CompileJob {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        if let Some(Err(exception)) = &*self.result.borrow() {
            exception.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

static COMPILE_JOB_CLASS: EmbedderClass<CompileJob> = EmbedderClass::new("WebAssemblyCompileJob");

impl EmbedderValue for CompileJob {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &COMPILE_JOB_CLASS;
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#asynchronously-compile-a-webassembly-module
fn asynchronously_compile_a_webassembly_module(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    bytes: Vec<u8>,
    options: WebAssemblyCompileOptions,
    task_source: TaskSource,
) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Let promise be a new Promise.
    let promise = create_promise(vm, realm);

    // 2. Run the following steps in parallel:
    let job = COMPILE_JOB_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| CompileJob {
        bytes: RefCell::new(bytes),
        options: RefCell::new(options),
        result: RefCell::new(None),
    });
    in_parallel(
        vm,
        realm,
        (promise, job, task_source),
        |vm, (promise, job, task_source)| {
            // 1. Compile the WebAssembly module bytes and store the result as module.
            let realm = vm.current_realm().expect("the steps run in the realm of the promise");
            let result = compile_a_webassembly_module(vm, realm, &job.bytes.borrow()).map_err(|throw| throw.value());
            *job.result.borrow_mut() = Some(result);

            // 2. Queue a task on taskSource, if provided, to perform the following steps:
            queue_a_task(vm, task_source, (promise, job), |vm, (promise, job)| {
                let realm = crate::bindings::promise::promise_realm(promise);
                with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(realm, || {
                    // 1. If module is error, reject promise with a CompileError exception and return.
                    let module = match job.result.take().expect("the module is compiled before the task runs") {
                        Ok(module) => module,
                        Err(exception) => {
                            reject_promise(vm, promise, exception);
                            return;
                        }
                    };

                    let options = job.options.take();

                    // 2. Let builtinSetNames be options["builtins"].
                    let builtin_set_names = options.builtins;

                    // 3. Let importedStringModule be options["importedStringConstants"].
                    let imported_string_module = options.imported_string_constants;

                    // 4. If validating builtins and imported strings for module with builtinSetNames and importedStringModule is
                    //    false, reject promise with a CompileError exception.
                    if !validate_builtins_and_imported_strings(
                        vm,
                        &module,
                        &builtin_set_names,
                        imported_string_module.as_ref(),
                    ) {
                        let throw = throw_webassembly_error(
                            vm,
                            realm,
                            WebAssemblyError::Compile,
                            "Invalid builtin or imported string",
                        );
                        reject_promise(vm, promise, throw.value());
                    }
                    // 5. Otherwise,
                    else {
                        // 1. Construct a WebAssembly module object from module, bytes, builtinSetNames, importedStringModule, and
                        //    let moduleObject be the result.
                        let bytes = job.bytes.take();
                        let module_object = allocate(vm, |_| {
                            Module::new(module, bytes, builtin_set_names, imported_string_module)
                        });

                        // 2. Resolve promise with moduleObject.
                        let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);
                        resolve_promise(vm, promise, Value::from_object(wrap(&cx, module_object)));
                    }
                });
            });
        },
    );

    // 3. Return promise.
    promise
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#asynchronously-instantiate-a-webassembly-module
fn asynchronously_instantiate_a_webassembly_module(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    module_object: Ref<Module>,
    import_object: Option<Gc<Object>>,
) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Let promise be a new promise.
    let promise = create_promise(vm, realm);

    // 2. Let module be moduleObject.[[Module]].
    let module = module_object.compiled_module().clone();

    // 3. Let builtinSetNames be moduleObject.[[BuiltinSets]].
    let builtin_set_names = module_object.builtin_sets();

    // 4. Let importedStringModule be moduleObject.[[ImportedStringModule]].
    let imported_string_module = module_object.imported_string_module();

    // 5. Read the imports of module with imports importObject, builtinSetNames and importedStringModule, and let imports
    //    be the result. If this operation throws an exception, catch it, reject promise with the exception, and return
    //    promise.
    let imports = match read_the_imports(vm, &module, import_object, builtin_set_names, imported_string_module) {
        Ok(imports) => imports,
        Err(throw) => {
            reject_promise(vm, promise, throw.value());
            return promise;
        }
    };

    // 6. Run the following steps in parallel:
    //   1. Queue a task to perform the following steps: Note: Implementation-specific work may be performed here.
    queue_a_task(
        vm,
        TaskSource::Unspecified,
        (promise, module_object, imports),
        |vm, (promise, module_object, imports)| {
            let realm = crate::bindings::promise::promise_realm(promise);
            with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(realm, || {
                let module = module_object.compiled_module().clone();

                // 1. Instantiate the core of a WebAssembly module module with imports, and let instance be the result.
                //    If this throws an exception, catch it, reject promise with the exception, and terminate these substeps.
                let instance = match instantiate_the_core_of_a_webassembly_module(vm, &module, &imports) {
                    Ok(instance) => instance,
                    Err(throw) => {
                        reject_promise(vm, promise, throw.value());
                        return;
                    }
                };

                // 2. Let instanceObject be a new Instance.
                // 3. Initialize instanceObject from module and instance. If this throws an exception, catch it, reject promise with the exception, and terminate these substeps.
                let instance_object = allocate(vm, |_| Instance::initialize(vm, realm, instance));

                // 4. Resolve promise with instanceObject.
                let cx = CallContext::new(vm, realm);
                resolve_promise(vm, promise, Value::from_object(wrap(&cx, instance_object)));
            });
        },
    );

    // 7. Return promise.
    promise
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#instantiate-a-promise-of-a-module
fn instantiate_a_promise_of_a_module(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    promise_of_module: WebIdlPromise,
    import_object: Option<Gc<Object>>,
) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // 1. Let promise be a new Promise.
    let promise = create_promise(vm, realm);

    // FIXME: Spec should use react to promise here instead of separate upon fulfillment and upon rejection steps

    react_to_promise(
        vm,
        promise_of_module,
        (promise, import_object),
        // 2. Upon fulfillment of promiseOfModule with value module:
        Some(|cx: &CallContext, (promise, import_object), module_value: Value| {
            let module_object = Module::from_value(module_value).expect("the promise is fulfilled with a Module");

            // 1. Instantiate the WebAssembly module module importing importObject, and let innerPromise be the result.
            let realm = crate::bindings::promise::promise_realm(promise);
            let inner_promise =
                asynchronously_instantiate_a_webassembly_module(cx.vm(), realm, module_object, import_object);

            react_to_promise(
                cx.vm(),
                inner_promise,
                (promise, module_object),
                // 2. Upon fulfillment of innerPromise with value instance.
                Some(|cx: &CallContext, (promise, module_object), instance_value: Value| {
                    let instance = crate::web_assembly::implementation_of_value::<Instance>(instance_value)
                        .expect("the promise is fulfilled with an Instance");

                    // 1. Let result be the WebAssemblyInstantiatedSource value «[ "module" → module, "instance" → instance ]».
                    let result = WebAssemblyInstantiatedSource {
                        module: module_object,
                        instance,
                    }
                    .into_js(&CallContext::new(
                        cx.vm(),
                        crate::bindings::promise::promise_realm(promise),
                    ))?;

                    // 2. Resolve promise with result.
                    resolve_promise(cx.vm(), promise, result);
                    Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
                }),
                // 3. Upon rejection of innerPromise with reason reason.
                Some(|cx: &CallContext, (promise, _), reason: Value| {
                    // 1. Reject promise with reason.
                    reject_promise(cx.vm(), promise, reason);
                    Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
                }),
            );
            Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
        }),
        // 3. Upon rejection of promiseOfModule with reason reason:
        Some(|cx: &CallContext, (promise, _), reason: Value| {
            // 1. Reject promise with reason.
            reject_promise(cx.vm(), promise, reason);
            Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
        }),
    );

    // 4. Return promise.
    promise
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    /// Steps 1 to 8 of compiling a potential WebAssembly response: the checks of the Response object, then consuming
    /// its body as an ArrayBuffer, whose promise, a WebIDL::Promise, it writes. Throws the TypeError of a check that
    /// fails.
    fn web_bindings_consume_webassembly_response(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        unwrapped_source: u64,
        body_promise: *mut *mut c_void,
    ) -> RawNativeFunctionResult;
}

/// https://webassembly.github.io/spec/web-api/index.html#compile-a-potential-webassembly-response
fn compile_a_potential_webassembly_response(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    source: WebIdlPromise,
    options: WebAssemblyCompileOptions,
) -> WebIdlPromise {
    // Note: This algorithm accepts a Response object, or a promise for one, and compiles and instantiates the resulting bytes of the response.
    //       This compilation can be performed in the background and in a streaming manner.
    //       If the Response is not CORS-same-origin, does not represent an ok status, or does not match the `application/wasm` MIME type,
    //       the returned promise will be rejected with a TypeError; if compilation or instantiation fails,
    //       the returned promise will be rejected with a CompileError or other relevant error type, depending on the cause of failure.

    // 1. Let returnValue be a new promise
    let return_value = create_promise(vm, realm);

    // NB: The reactions hold the options in a cell of their own, as what they capture is traced.
    let options = COMPILE_OPTIONS_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| options);

    react_to_promise(
        vm,
        source,
        (return_value, options),
        // 2. Upon fulfillment of source with value unwrappedSource:
        Some(|cx: &CallContext, (return_value, options), unwrapped_source: Value| {
            let realm = crate::bindings::promise::promise_realm(return_value);
            let mut body_promise = core::ptr::null_mut();
            // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the promise is written before the completion is normal.
            let consumed = unsafe {
                web_bindings_consume_webassembly_response(
                    realm.as_ptr().cast(),
                    unwrapped_source.to_raw(),
                    &raw mut body_promise,
                )
            }
            .into_completion();
            if let Err(throw) = consumed {
                reject_promise(cx.vm(), return_value, throw.value());
                return Ok(Value::UNDEFINED);
            }
            // SAFETY: LibWeb wrote the WebIDL::Promise of the body.
            let body_promise = unsafe { crate::bindings::promise::promise_from_abi(body_promise) };

            react_to_promise(
                cx.vm(),
                body_promise,
                (return_value, options),
                // 9. Upon fulfillment of bodyPromise with value bodyArrayBuffer:
                Some(|cx: &CallContext, (return_value, options), body_array_buffer: Value| {
                    // 1. Let stableBytes be a copy of the bytes held by the buffer bodyArrayBuffer.
                    let bytes = crate::bindings::conversions::buffer_source_type_of(body_array_buffer)
                        .expect("a body consumed as an ArrayBuffer is one");
                    let stable_bytes = stable_bytes_of(bytes);

                    // 2. Asynchronously compile the WebAssembly module stableBytes using the networking task source and options
                    //    and resolve returnValue with the result.
                    let realm = crate::bindings::promise::promise_realm(return_value);
                    let result = asynchronously_compile_a_webassembly_module(
                        cx.vm(),
                        realm,
                        stable_bytes,
                        (*options).clone(),
                        TaskSource::Networking,
                    );
                    resolve_promise(cx.vm(), return_value, Value::from_object(result.promise()));
                    Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
                }),
                // 10. Upon rejection of bodyPromise with reason reason:
                Some(|cx: &CallContext, (return_value, _), reason: Value| {
                    // 1. Reject returnValue with reason.
                    reject_promise(cx.vm(), return_value, reason);
                    Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
                }),
            );
            Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
        }),
        // 3. Upon rejection of source with reason reason:
        Some(|cx: &CallContext, (return_value, _), reason: Value| {
            // 1. Reject returnValue with reason.
            reject_promise(cx.vm(), return_value, reason);
            Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
        }),
    );

    // 4. Return returnValue.
    return_value
}

impl WebAssembly {
    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#error-objects
    pub(crate) fn initialize(cx: &mut CallContext, namespace_object: Gc<Object>) {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Let namespaceObject be the namespace object.
        // 2. For each error of « "CompileError", "LinkError", "RuntimeError" »,
        // 2.1. Let constructor be a new object, implementing the NativeError Object Structure, with NativeError set to error.
        // 2.2. ! DefineMethodProperty(namespaceObject, error, constructor, false).
        let attributes = PropertyAttributes::new(Attribute::WRITABLE | Attribute::CONFIGURABLE);
        for error in WebAssemblyError::ALL {
            let constructor = error_constructor(vm, cx.realm(), error);
            namespace_object.define_direct_property(
                vm,
                &PropertyKey::from_utf8(error.name()),
                Value::from_object(constructor),
                attributes,
            );
        }
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-webassembly-jstag
    pub(crate) fn js_tag(cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Tag>> {
        // 1. Let JSTagAddr be the result of getting the JavaScript exception tag.
        // 2. Let JSTagObject be the result of creating a Tag object from JSTagAddr.
        // 3. Return JSTagObject.
        let tag = Agent::the(cx.vm()).js_tag();
        Ok(Tag::from_address(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), tag))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-webassembly-validate
    pub(crate) fn validate(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        bytes: BufferSource,
        options: WebAssemblyCompileOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // 1. Let stableBytes be a copy of the bytes held by the buffer bytes.
        let stable_bytes = stable_bytes_of(bytes);

        // 2. Compile stableBytes as a WebAssembly module and store the results as module.
        let module = libwasm_engine::compile(&stable_bytes);

        // 3. If module is error, return false.
        let Ok(module) = module else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        let module: CompiledModule = Arc::new(module);

        // 4. Let builtinSetNames be options["builtins"].
        let builtin_set_names = &options.builtins;

        // 5. Let importedStringModule be options["importedStringConstants"].
        let imported_string_module = options.imported_string_constants.as_ref();

        // 6. If validating builtins and imported strings for module with builtinSetNames and importedStringModule returns
        //    false, return false.
        if !validate_builtins_and_imported_strings(cx.vm(), &module, builtin_set_names, imported_string_module) {
            return Ok(false);
        }

        // 7. Return true.
        Ok(true)
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-webassembly-compile
    pub(crate) fn compile(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        bytes: BufferSource,
        options: WebAssemblyCompileOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        // 1. Let stableBytes be a copy of the bytes held by the buffer bytes.
        let stable_bytes = stable_bytes_of(bytes);

        // 2. Asynchronously compile a WebAssembly module from stableBytes using options and return the result.
        Ok(asynchronously_compile_a_webassembly_module(
            cx.vm(),
            cx.realm(),
            stable_bytes,
            options,
            TaskSource::Unspecified,
        ))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/web-api/index.html#dom-webassembly-compilestreaming
    pub(crate) fn compile_streaming(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        source: WebIdlPromise,
        options: WebAssemblyCompileOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        // The compileStreaming(source, options) method, when invoked, returns the result of compiling a potential
        // WebAssembly response with source using options.
        Ok(compile_a_potential_webassembly_response(
            cx.vm(),
            cx.realm(),
            source,
            options,
        ))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-webassembly-instantiate
    // https://webassembly.github.io/content-security-policy/js-api/#dom-webassembly-instantiate
    pub(crate) fn instantiate_bytes(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        bytes: BufferSource,
        import_object: Option<Gc<Object>>,
        options: WebAssemblyCompileOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let realm = cx.realm();

        // 1. Let stableBytes be a copy of the bytes held by the buffer bytes.
        let stable_bytes = stable_bytes_of(bytes);

        // 2. Perform HostEnsureCanCompileWasmBytes()
        crate::web_assembly::host_ensure_can_compile_wasm_bytes(realm)?;

        // 3. Asynchronously compile a WebAssembly module from stableBytes using options and let promiseOfModule be the
        //    result.
        let promise_of_module =
            asynchronously_compile_a_webassembly_module(vm, realm, stable_bytes, options, TaskSource::Unspecified);

        // 4. Instantiate promiseOfModule with imports importObject and return the result.
        Ok(instantiate_a_promise_of_a_module(
            vm,
            realm,
            promise_of_module,
            import_object,
        ))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#dom-webassembly-instantiate-moduleobject-importobject
    pub(crate) fn instantiate_module(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        module_object: Ref<Module>,
        import_object: Option<Gc<Object>>,
        _: Option<Value>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        // 1. Asynchronously instantiate the WebAssembly module moduleObject importing importObject, and return the result.
        Ok(asynchronously_instantiate_a_webassembly_module(
            cx.vm(),
            cx.realm(),
            module_object,
            import_object,
        ))
    }

    // https://webassembly.github.io/spec/web-api/index.html#dom-webassembly-instantiatestreaming
    pub(crate) fn instantiate_streaming(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        source: WebIdlPromise,
        import_object: Option<Gc<Object>>,
        options: WebAssemblyCompileOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        // The instantiateStreaming(source, importObject, options) method, when invoked, performs the following steps:

        // 1. Let promiseOfModule be the result of compiling a potential WebAssembly response with source using options.
        let promise_of_module = compile_a_potential_webassembly_response(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), source, options);

        // 2. Return the result of instantiating the promise of a module promiseOfModule with imports importObject.
        Ok(instantiate_a_promise_of_a_module(
            cx.vm(),
            cx.realm(),
            promise_of_module,
            import_object,
        ))
    }
}

// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#AnalyserNode
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct AnalyserNode {
    node: AudioNode,
    fft_size: Cell<u32>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    fft: RefCell<Option<FFT>>,
    max_decibels: Cell<f64>,
    min_decibels: Cell<f64>,
    smoothing_time_constant: Cell<f64>,

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#previous-block
    #[gc(untraced)]
    previous_block: RefCell<Vec<f32>>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    time_domain_ring: RefCell<Option<AudioFrameRing>>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    history: RefCell<Vec<f32>>,
    history_write_index: Cell<usize>,
    history_valid_frames: Cell<usize>,

    // Frequency data computed within the current render quantum, per the spec's requirement
    // that repeated getter calls in one quantum return identical data.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    cached_frequency_data: RefCell<Vec<f32>>,
    frequency_data_cache_time: Cell<Option<f64>>,
}

impl Inherits<AudioNode> for AnalyserNode {
    fn parent(&self) -> &AudioNode {
        &self.node
    }
}

impl Wrappable for AnalyserNode {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.node.cpp_parent()
    }

    const FINALIZES: bool = true;

    fn finalize(node: Ref<Self>) {
        node.node.finalize_node();
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for AnalyserNode {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
}

// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-analysernode-fftsize
// The maximum allowed fftSize; the node must keep this many past sample-frames around so
// that growing fftSize immediately exposes older data.
const MAX_FFT_SIZE: u32 = 32768;

pub(crate) struct AnalyserOptions {
    pub parent: AudioNodeOptions,
    pub fft_size: u32,
    pub max_decibels: f64,
    pub min_decibels: f64,
    pub smoothing_time_constant: f64,
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_audio_analyser_create_ring(callbacks: *mut AudioFrameRingCallbacks) -> FfiSharedCppObject;
}

impl AnalyserNode {
    pub(crate) fn create(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        context: AnyBaseAudioContext,
        options: &AnalyserOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // When the constructor is called with a BaseAudioContext c and an option object option, the user agent
        // MUST initialize the AudioNode this, with context and options as arguments.
        let node = allocate(cx.vm(), |defer_gc| Self {
            node: AudioNode::new(defer_gc, context, 2),
            fft_size: Cell::new(options.fft_size),
            fft: RefCell::new(None),
            max_decibels: Cell::new(options.max_decibels),
            min_decibels: Cell::new(options.min_decibels),
            smoothing_time_constant: Cell::new(options.smoothing_time_constant),
            previous_block: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            time_domain_ring: RefCell::new(None),
            history: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            history_write_index: Cell::new(0),
            history_valid_frames: Cell::new(0),
            cached_frequency_data: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            frequency_data_cache_time: Cell::new(None),
        });
        node.node.set_this(AnyAudioNode::AnalyserNode(node));
        node.node.event_target().set_owner(node);
        node.set_fft_size_without_validation(options.fft_size);

        // Default options for channel count and interpretation
        // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#AnalyserNode
        let default_options = AudioNodeDefaultOptions {
            channel_count: 2,
            channel_count_mode: ChannelCountMode::Max,
            channel_interpretation: ChannelInterpretation::Speakers,
        };

        // FIXME: Set tail-time to no
        node.node
            .initialize_audio_node_options(cx, &options.parent, &default_options)?;
        node.history.borrow_mut().resize(MAX_FFT_SIZE as usize, 0.);
        let mut callbacks = std::mem::MaybeUninit::uninit();
        let ring = unsafe { web_audio_analyser_create_ring(callbacks.as_mut_ptr()) };
        let callbacks = unsafe { callbacks.assume_init() };
        *node.time_domain_ring.borrow_mut() = Some(AudioFrameRing {
            owner: SharedCppObject {
                pointer: ring.pointer,
                retain: ring.retain,
                release: ring.release,
            },
            callbacks,
        });
        node.node.queue_render_node_creation(unsafe {
            create_analyser_render_node(
                node.node.node_id(),
                BaseAudioContext::RENDER_QUANTUM_SIZE as usize,
                ring,
                callbacks,
            )
        });
        Ok(node)
    }

    #[allow(clippy::needless_range_loop, reason = "preserve the C++ frame traversal")]
    fn drain_time_domain_ring(&self) {
        let ring = self.time_domain_ring.borrow();
        let Some(ring) = &*ring else {
            return;
        };

        // Ring pops are destructive, so everything the render thread has produced is folded into
        // the control-side history of the last MAX_FFT_SIZE sample-frames. Keeping the full
        // maximum window around means growing fftSize immediately exposes older data, as the
        // spec requires.
        let mut chunk = [0.; 1024];
        loop {
            let frame_count = ring.try_pop(&mut chunk);
            if frame_count == 0 {
                break;
            }
            let mut history = self.history.borrow_mut();
            for frame in 0..frame_count {
                history[self.history_write_index.get()] = chunk[frame];
                self.history_write_index
                    .set((self.history_write_index.get() + 1) % history.len());
            }
            self.history_valid_frames
                .set(history.len().min(self.history_valid_frames.get() + frame_count));
        }
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#current-time-domain-data
    fn current_time_domain_data(&self) -> Vec<f32> {
        // The input signal must be down-mixed to mono as if channelCount is 1, channelCountMode is "max" and
        // channelInterpretation is "speakers". This is independent of the settings for the AnalyserNode itself.
        // NB: The rendering thread down-mixes samples before writing them to the history ring.
        self.drain_time_domain_ring();

        // The most recent fftSize frames are used for the down-mixing operation.
        let mut result = vec![0.; self.fft_size.get() as usize];
        let frames_available = (self.fft_size.get() as usize).min(self.history_valid_frames.get());
        let history = self.history.borrow();
        for frame in 0..frames_available {
            let history_index =
                (self.history_write_index.get() + history.len() - frames_available + frame) % history.len();
            result[self.fft_size.get() as usize - frames_available + frame] = history[history_index];
        }
        result
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#blackman-window
    fn apply_a_blackman_window(&self, x: &[f32]) -> Vec<f32> {
        let a: f32 = 0.16;
        let a0 = 0.5f32 * (1. - a);
        let a1: f32 = 0.5;
        let a2 = a * 0.5f32;
        let n = self.fft_size.get();
        let w = |index: u32| {
            a0 - a1 * math::cos(2. * std::f32::consts::PI * index as f32 / n as f32)
                + a2 * math::cos(4. * std::f32::consts::PI * index as f32 / n as f32)
        };
        let mut x_hat = vec![0.; self.fft_size.get() as usize];

        // FIXME: Naive
        for i in 0..self.fft_size.get() as usize {
            x_hat[i] = x[i] * w(i as u32);
        }
        x_hat
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#smoothing-over-time
    fn smoothing_over_time(&self, current_block: &[f32]) -> Vec<f32> {
        // 1. Let X^−1[k] be the result of this operation on the previous block. The previous block is defined as being
        //    the buffer computed by the previous smoothing over time operation, or an array of N zeros if this is the
        //    first time we are smoothing over time.
        let mut previous_block = self.previous_block.borrow_mut();
        if previous_block.len() != current_block.len() {
            previous_block.clear();
            previous_block.resize(current_block.len(), 0.);
        }

        // 2. Let τ be the value of the smoothingTimeConstant attribute for this AnalyserNode.
        let tau = self.smoothing_time_constant.get() as f32;

        // 3. Let X[k] be the result of applying a Fourier transform of the current block.
        let mut result = vec![0.; current_block.len()];

        // 4. Then the smoothed value, X^[k], is computed by X^[k] = τ * X^−1[k] + (1 − τ) * |X[k]|
        //    If X^[k] is NaN, positive infinity or negative infinity, set X^[k] = 0.
        for i in 0..current_block.len() {
            let mut smoothed = tau * previous_block[i] + (1.0f32 - tau) * current_block[i].abs();
            if !smoothed.is_finite() {
                smoothed = 0.;
            }
            result[i] = smoothed;
        }
        *previous_block = result.clone();
        result
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#conversion-to-db
    fn conversion_to_db(&self, x_hat: &[f32]) -> Vec<f32> {
        // Y[k] = 20 log10 X^[k]   for k = 0,…,N−1
        let mut result = Vec::with_capacity(x_hat.len());
        for x in x_hat {
            // NB: 20 * log10(0) is -∞. The byte-domain conversion clamps this later.
            if *x > 0. {
                result.push(20.0f32 * math::log10(*x));
            } else {
                result.push(f32::NEG_INFINITY);
            }
        }
        result
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#current-frequency-data
    fn current_frequency_data(&self) -> Vec<f32> {
        // If another call to getFloatFrequencyData() or getByteFrequencyData() occurs within the same render quantum
        // as a previous call, the current frequency data is not updated with the same data. Instead, the previously
        // computed data is returned.
        // AD-HOC: The control thread cannot observe render quantum boundaries directly; the context's currentTime,
        //         which advances as quanta are rendered, stands in for the quantum stamp.
        let current_time = self.node.context_value().current_time_value();
        if self.frequency_data_cache_time.get() == Some(current_time) {
            return self.cached_frequency_data.borrow().clone();
        }

        // 1. Compute the current time-domain data.
        let time_domain_data = self.current_time_domain_data();

        // 2. Apply a Blackman window to the time domain input data.
        let windowed_input = self.apply_a_blackman_window(&time_domain_data);

        // 3. Apply a Fourier transform to the windowed time domain input data to get real and imaginary frequency data.
        let frequency_domain_data = apply_a_fourier_transform(
            self.fft.borrow().as_ref().unwrap(),
            &windowed_input,
            self.fft_size.get() as usize / 2,
        );

        // 4. Smooth over time the frequency domain data.
        let smoothed_data = self.smoothing_over_time(&frequency_domain_data);

        // 5. Convert to dB.
        let result = self.conversion_to_db(&smoothed_data);
        *self.cached_frequency_data.borrow_mut() = result.clone();
        self.frequency_data_cache_time.set(Some(current_time));
        result
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-analysernode-getfloatfrequencydata
    pub(crate) fn get_float_frequency_data(&self, _: &mut CallContext, array: Gc<TypedArrayBase>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // Write the current frequency data into array. If array has fewer elements than the frequencyBinCount,
        // the excess elements will be dropped. If array has more elements than the frequencyBinCount, the
        // excess elements will be ignored. The most recent fftSize frames are used in computing the frequency data.
        let data = self.current_frequency_data();
        let record = make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record(&array, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
        if is_typed_array_out_of_bounds(&record) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let count = typed_array_length(&record).min(self.fft_size.get() as usize / 2);
        overwrite_float32_array(&array, &data[..count]);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-analysernode-getbytefrequencydata
    pub(crate) fn get_byte_frequency_data(&self, _: &mut CallContext, array: Gc<TypedArrayBase>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let data = self.current_frequency_data();
        let mut byte_data = Vec::with_capacity(data.len());

        // For getByteFrequencyData(), the 𝑌[𝑘] is clipped to lie between minDecibels and maxDecibels
        // and then scaled to fit in an unsigned byte such that minDecibels is represented by the
        // value 0 and maxDecibels is represented by the value 255.
        let delta_db = (self.max_decibels.get() - self.min_decibels.get()) as f32;
        for mut x in data {
            x = if f64::from(x) < self.min_decibels.get() {
                self.min_decibels.get() as f32
            } else {
                x
            };
            x = if self.max_decibels.get() < f64::from(x) {
                self.max_decibels.get() as f32
            } else {
                x
            };
            byte_data.push((255. * (f64::from(x) - self.min_decibels.get()) / f64::from(delta_db)) as u8);
        }

        // Write the current frequency data into array. If array’s byte length is less than frequencyBinCount,
        // the excess elements will be dropped. If array’s byte length is greater than the frequencyBinCount ,
        // the excess elements will be ignored. The most recent fftSize frames are used in computing the frequency data.
        let record = make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record(&array, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
        if is_typed_array_out_of_bounds(&record) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let count = typed_array_length(&record).min(self.fft_size.get() as usize / 2);
        array
            .viewed_array_buffer()
            .overwrite(array.byte_offset(), &byte_data[..count]);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-analysernode-getfloattimedomaindata
    pub(crate) fn get_float_time_domain_data(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        array: Gc<TypedArrayBase>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // Write the current time-domain data (waveform data) into array. If array has fewer elements than the
        // value of fftSize, the excess elements will be dropped. If array has more elements than the value of
        // fftSize, the excess elements will be ignored. The most recent fftSize frames are written (after downmixing).
        let data = self.current_time_domain_data();
        let record = make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record(&array, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
        if is_typed_array_out_of_bounds(&record) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let count = typed_array_length(&record).min(self.fft_size.get() as usize);
        overwrite_float32_array(&array, &data[..count]);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-analysernode-getbytetimedomaindata
    pub(crate) fn get_byte_time_domain_data(&self, _: &mut CallContext, array: Gc<TypedArrayBase>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // Write the current time-domain data (waveform data) into array. If array’s byte length is less than
        // fftSize, the excess elements will be dropped. If array’s byte length is greater than the fftSize,
        // the excess elements will be ignored. The most recent fftSize frames are used in computing the byte data.
        let data = self.current_time_domain_data();
        let mut byte_data = Vec::with_capacity(data.len());
        assert_eq!(data.len(), self.fft_size.get() as usize);
        for sample in data {
            let mut x = 128. * (1. + sample);
            x = if x < 0. { 0. } else { x };
            x = if 255. < x { 255. } else { x };
            byte_data.push(x as u8);
        }
        let record = make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record(&array, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
        if is_typed_array_out_of_bounds(&record) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let count = typed_array_length(&record).min(self.fft_size.get() as usize);
        array
            .viewed_array_buffer()
            .overwrite(array.byte_offset(), &byte_data[..count]);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-analysernode-fftsize
    fn set_fft_size_without_validation(&self, fft_size: u32) {
        // reset previous block to 0s
        *self.previous_block.borrow_mut() = vec![0.; fft_size as usize / 2];
        self.frequency_data_cache_time.set(None);
        self.fft_size.set(fft_size);
        *self.fft.borrow_mut() = Some(FFT::new(fft_size as usize));

        // Note that increasing fftSize does mean that the current time-domain data must be expanded
        // to include past frames that it previously did not. This means that the AnalyserNode
        // effectively MUST keep around the last 32768 sample-frames and the current time-domain
        // data is the most recent fftSize sample-frames out of that.
        // NB: The history ring holds MAX_FFT_SIZE frames.
    }

    #[allow(clippy::manual_range_contains, reason = "preserve the C++ validation")]
    pub(crate) fn set_fft_size(&self, _: &mut CallContext, fft_size: u32) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        if fft_size < 32 || fft_size > MAX_FFT_SIZE || !fft_size.is_power_of_two() {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "IndexSizeError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Analyser node fftSize not a power of 2 between 32 and 32768"),
            ));
        }
        self.set_fft_size_without_validation(fft_size);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_max_decibels(&self, _: &mut CallContext, max_decibels: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        if self.min_decibels.get() >= max_decibels {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "IndexSizeError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Analyser node minDecibels greater than maxDecibels"),
            ));
        }
        self.max_decibels.set(max_decibels);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_min_decibels(&self, _: &mut CallContext, min_decibels: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        if min_decibels >= self.max_decibels.get() {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "IndexSizeError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Analyser node minDecibels greater than maxDecibels"),
            ));
        }
        self.min_decibels.set(min_decibels);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_smoothing_time_constant(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        smoothing_time_constant: f64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        if smoothing_time_constant > 1. || smoothing_time_constant < 0. {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "IndexSizeError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Analyser node smoothingTimeConstant not between 0.0 and 1.0"),
            ));
        }
        self.smoothing_time_constant.set(smoothing_time_constant);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn validate_options(options: &AnalyserOptions) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        if options.min_decibels >= options.max_decibels {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "IndexSizeError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Analyser node minDecibels greater than maxDecibels"),
            ));
        }
        if options.smoothing_time_constant > 1. || options.smoothing_time_constant < 0. {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "IndexSizeError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Analyser node smoothingTimeConstant not between 0.0 and 1.0"),
            ));
        }
        if options.fft_size < 32 || options.fft_size > MAX_FFT_SIZE || !options.fft_size.is_power_of_two() {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "IndexSizeError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Analyser node fftSize not a power of 2 between 32 and 32768"),
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        context: AnyBaseAudioContext,
        options: AnalyserOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        Self::validate_options(&options)?;
        Self::create(cx, context, &options)
    }

    pub(crate) fn fft_size(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        Ok(self.fft_size.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn max_decibels(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.max_decibels.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn min_decibels(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.min_decibels.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn smoothing_time_constant(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.smoothing_time_constant.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn frequency_bin_count(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        Ok(self.fft_size.get() / 2)
    }
}

// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#fourier-transform
//
// Returns `bin_count` (= fftSize / 2) magnitude values normalized by fftSize, per the spec's
// `(1/N) * |X[k]|` convention. The caller is expected to have applied a window already.
#[allow(clippy::manual_memcpy, reason = "preserve the C++ input copy loop")]
fn apply_a_fourier_transform(fft: &FFT, input: &[f32], bin_count: usize) -> Vec<f32> {
    let mut magnitudes = vec![0.; bin_count];
    if input.is_empty() {
        return magnitudes;
    }
    let n = input.len();
    let mut re = vec![0.; n];
    let mut im = vec![0.; n];
    for i in 0..n {
        re[i] = input[i];
    }
    fft.transform(&mut re, &mut im, FFTDirection::Forward);
    let inv_n = 1.0f32 / n as f32;
    for k in 0..bin_count.min(n) {
        magnitudes[k] = (re[k] * re[k] + im[k] * im[k]).sqrt() * inv_n;
    }
    magnitudes
}

use libjs_rust::api::{
    ArrayBufferOrder, TypedArrayBase, is_typed_array_out_of_bounds, make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record,
    typed_array_length,
};

// Utilities for moving sample data in and out of the Float32Arrays exposed by the Web Audio API. A Float32Array's
// contents can change from JavaScript at any time, so audio data destined for the rendering thread is always snapshotted
// into an owned buffer first.

// The current element length of a Float32Array, or 0 if it is out of bounds of its backing ArrayBuffer.
pub(crate) fn float32_array_length(array: &TypedArrayBase) -> usize {
    let record = make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record(array, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
    if is_typed_array_out_of_bounds(&record) {
        return 0;
    }
    typed_array_length(&record)
}

// Snapshots the live contents of a Float32Array into an owned buffer.
pub(crate) fn copy_float32_array(array: &TypedArrayBase) -> Vec<f32> {
    let length = float32_array_length(array);
    let mut values = vec![0.; length];
    let bytes = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(values.as_mut_ptr().cast::<u8>(), length * size_of::<f32>()) };
    array.viewed_array_buffer().copy_to(array.byte_offset(), bytes);
    values
}

// Overwrites the leading elements of a Float32Array with the given samples.
pub(crate) fn overwrite_float32_array(array: &TypedArrayBase, values: &[f32]) {
    let bytes = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(values.as_ptr().cast::<u8>(), size_of_val(values)) };
    array.viewed_array_buffer().overwrite(array.byte_offset(), bytes);
}

// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#AudioBufferSourceNode
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct AudioBufferSourceNode {
    node: AudioScheduledSourceNode,
    buffer: Cell<Option<Ref<AudioBuffer>>>,
    playback_rate: Ref<AudioParam>,
    detune: Ref<AudioParam>,
    r#loop: Cell<bool>,
    loop_start: Cell<f64>,
    loop_end: Cell<f64>,

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-buffer-set-slot
    buffer_set: Cell<bool>,
}

impl Inherits<AudioScheduledSourceNode> for AudioBufferSourceNode {
    fn parent(&self) -> &AudioScheduledSourceNode {
        &self.node
    }
}

impl Wrappable for AudioBufferSourceNode {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.node.cpp_parent()
    }

    const FINALIZES: bool = true;

    fn finalize(node: Ref<Self>) {
        node.node.parent().finalize_node();
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for AudioBufferSourceNode {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
}

pub(crate) struct AudioBufferSourceOptions {
    pub buffer: Option<Option<Ref<AudioBuffer>>>,
    pub playback_rate: f32,
    pub detune: f32,
    pub r#loop: bool,
    pub loop_start: f64,
    pub loop_end: f64,
}

impl AudioBufferSourceNode {
    fn queue_parameters_update(&self, buffer: Option<Arc<AudioBufferContents>>, update_buffer: bool) {
        self.node
            .parent()
            .context_value()
            .queue_control_message(ControlMessage::NodeMessage(NodeMessage::SetBufferSourceParameters(
                SetBufferSourceParameters {
                    node_id: self.node.parent().node_id(),
                    r#loop: self.r#loop.get(),
                    loop_start: self.loop_start.get(),
                    loop_end: self.loop_end.get(),
                    buffer,
                    update_buffer,
                },
            )));
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-buffer
    pub(crate) fn set_buffer(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, buffer: Option<Ref<AudioBuffer>>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let new buffer be the AudioBuffer or null value to be assigned to buffer.
        let new_buffer = buffer;

        // 2. If new buffer is not null and [[buffer set]] is true, throw an InvalidStateError and abort these steps.
        if new_buffer.is_some() && self.buffer_set.get() {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidStateError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Buffer has already been set"),
            ));
        }

        // 3. If new buffer is not null, set [[buffer set]] to true.
        if new_buffer.is_some() {
            self.buffer_set.set(true);
        }

        // 4. Assign new buffer to the buffer attribute.
        self.buffer.set(new_buffer);

        // 5. If start() has previously been called on this node, perform the operation acquire the content on buffer.
        if self.node.source_started() {
            self.queue_parameters_update(
                self.buffer
                    .get()
                    .and_then(|buffer| AudioBuffer::acquire_contents(buffer, cx.vm())),
                true,
            );
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-buffer
    pub(crate) fn buffer(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<AudioBuffer>>> {
        Ok(self.buffer.get())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-playbackrate
    pub(crate) fn playback_rate(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<AudioParam>> {
        Ok(self.playback_rate)
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-detune
    pub(crate) fn detune(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<AudioParam>> {
        Ok(self.detune)
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-loop
    pub(crate) fn r#loop(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.r#loop.get())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-loop
    pub(crate) fn set_loop(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: bool) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.r#loop.set(value);
        self.queue_parameters_update(None, false);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-loopstart
    pub(crate) fn loop_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.loop_start.get())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-loopstart
    pub(crate) fn set_loop_start(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.loop_start.set(value);
        self.queue_parameters_update(None, false);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-loopend
    pub(crate) fn loop_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.loop_end.get())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-loopend
    pub(crate) fn set_loop_end(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.loop_end.set(value);
        self.queue_parameters_update(None, false);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-start
    pub(crate) fn start(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        when: f64,
        offset: Option<f64>,
        duration: Option<f64>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If this AudioBufferSourceNode internal slot [[source started]] is true, an InvalidStateError exception MUST be thrown.
        if self.node.source_started() {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidStateError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"AudioBufferSourceNode has already been started"),
            ));
        }

        // 2. Check for any errors that must be thrown due to parameter constraints described below. If any exception is thrown during this step, abort those steps.
        // A RangeError exception MUST be thrown if when is negative.
        if when < 0. {
            return Err(Exception::range_error("when must not be negative"));
        }

        // A RangeError exception MUST be thrown if offset is negative
        if offset.is_some_and(|offset| offset < 0.) {
            return Err(Exception::range_error("offset must not be negative"));
        }

        // A RangeError exception MUST be thrown if duration is negative.
        if duration.is_some_and(|duration| duration < 0.) {
            return Err(Exception::range_error("duration must not be negative"));
        }

        // 3. Set the internal slot [[source started]] on this AudioBufferSourceNode to true.
        self.node.set_source_started(true);

        // 4. Queue a control message to start the AudioBufferSourceNode, including the parameter values in the message.
        // 5. Acquire the contents of the buffer if the buffer has been set.
        let mut contents = None;
        if let Some(buffer) = self.buffer.get() {
            contents = AudioBuffer::acquire_contents(buffer, cx.vm());
        }
        self.node
            .parent()
            .context_value()
            .queue_control_message(ControlMessage::NodeMessage(NodeMessage::StartBufferSource(
                StartBufferSource {
                    node_id: self.node.parent().node_id(),
                    when,
                    offset: offset.unwrap_or(0.),
                    duration,
                    buffer: contents,
                },
            )));
        self.node
            .parent()
            .context_value()
            .add_playing_source(cx.vm(), self.node.parent().this());

        // 6. Send a control message to the associated AudioContext to start running its rendering thread only when all the following conditions are met:
        //    1. The context’s [[control thread state]] is suspended.
        //    2. The context is allowed to start.
        //    3. [[suspended by user]] flag is false.
        // AD-HOC: Sources in an OfflineAudioContext are scheduled by start() and rendered by startRendering().
        if let AnyBaseAudioContext::AudioContext(context) = self.node.parent().context_value()
            && context.parent().control_state() == AudioContextState::Suspended
            && context.allowed_to_start()
            && !context.suspended_by_user()
            // AD-HOC: As in resume(), only start rendering while the context's document is fully active.
            && context.parent().document_is_fully_active()
        {
            // AD-HOC: Record startup now so another source started in the same task cannot request it again.
            context.parent().set_control_state(AudioContextState::Running);
            context.run_control_message_to_resume(cx.vm(), None);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffersourcenode-audiobuffersourcenode
    pub(crate) fn create(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        context: AnyBaseAudioContext,
        options: &AudioBufferSourceOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // When the constructor is called with a BaseAudioContext c and an option object option, the user agent
        // MUST initialize the AudioNode this, with context and options as arguments.

        let node = allocate(cx.vm(), |defer_gc| Self {
            node: AudioScheduledSourceNode::new(defer_gc, context),
            buffer: Cell::new(None),
            playback_rate: AudioParam::create(
                cx.vm(),
                context,
                None,
                options.playback_rate,
                f32::MIN,
                f32::MAX,
                AutomationRate::KRate,
                FixedAutomationRate::Yes,
            ),
            detune: AudioParam::create(
                cx.vm(),
                context,
                None,
                options.detune,
                f32::MIN,
                f32::MAX,
                AutomationRate::KRate,
                FixedAutomationRate::Yes,
            ),
            r#loop: Cell::new(options.r#loop),
            loop_start: Cell::new(options.loop_start),
            loop_end: Cell::new(options.loop_end),
            buffer_set: Cell::new(false),
        });
        node.node.parent().set_this(AnyAudioNode::AudioBufferSourceNode(node));
        node.node.parent().event_target().set_owner(node);
        node.playback_rate.set_owner(AnyAudioNode::AudioBufferSourceNode(node));
        node.detune.set_owner(AnyAudioNode::AudioBufferSourceNode(node));

        node.set_buffer(cx, options.buffer.flatten())?;

        // Default options for channel count and interpretation
        // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#AudioBufferSourceNode
        let default_options = AudioNodeDefaultOptions {
            channel_count: 2,
            channel_count_mode: ChannelCountMode::Max,
            channel_interpretation: ChannelInterpretation::Speakers,
        };

        // FIXME: Set tail-time to no
        node.node
            .parent()
            .initialize_audio_node_options(cx, &AudioNodeOptions::default(), &default_options)?;
        node.node
            .parent()
            .queue_render_node_creation(create_audio_buffer_source_render_node(
                node.node.parent().node_id(),
                BaseAudioContext::RENDER_QUANTUM_SIZE as usize,
                Arc::clone(node.playback_rate.render_param()),
                Arc::clone(node.detune.render_param()),
            ));
        node.queue_parameters_update(None, false);
        Ok(node)
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        context: AnyBaseAudioContext,
        options: AudioBufferSourceOptions,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        Self::create(cx, context, &options)
    }
}
