#![allow(
    clippy::needless_range_loop,
    clippy::collapsible_if,
    reason = "preserve the C++ channel and cache traversal order"
)]

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::ptr::NonNull;
use std::sync::Arc;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{
    ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferOrder, ArrayBufferShared, DataBlock, EmbedderCell, ErrorKind, ErrorType,
    ExternalPrimitiveStorage, ForeignCellSlot, Gc, GcWeak, Trace, TypedArrayBase, TypedArrayKind, Vm,
    create_typed_array_on_buffer, detach_array_buffer, make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record,
};
use libjs_rust::api::{OutOfMemory, OwnedBackingStore};
use libjs_rust::api::{is_typed_array_out_of_bounds, typed_array_byte_length};
use libweb_rust::web_audio::rendering::audio_data::AudioBufferContents;

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, Wrapped, allocate, cell_into_abi};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};

pub(crate) struct AudioBufferOptions {
    pub(crate) number_of_channels: u32,
    pub(crate) length: u32,
    pub(crate) sample_rate: f32,
}

// The sample data lives in the primitive storage cage, so an out-of-bounds access through a channel's Float32Array
// is masked back into the cage instead of reaching memory outside it. The AudioBuffer owns the storage, and the
// ArrayBuffer handed to script holds an owner edge back to the AudioBuffer, so the storage outlives every view.
struct Channel {
    data: OwnedBackingStore,
}

// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#AudioBuffer
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct AudioBuffer {
    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-number-of-channels-slot
    // The number of audio channels for this AudioBuffer, which is an unsigned long.
    //
    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-internal-data-slot
    // A data block holding the audio sample data.
    #[gc(untraced)]
    channels: RefCell<Vec<Channel>>, // [[internal data]] / [[number_of_channels]]
    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#audio-buffer-copying
    #[gc(untraced)]
    contents: RefCell<Option<Arc<AudioBufferContents>>>,

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-length-slot
    // The length of each channel of this AudioBuffer, which is an unsigned long.
    length: u32, // [[length]]
    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-sample-rate-slot
    // The sample-rate, in Hz, of this AudioBuffer, a float.
    sample_rate: f32, // [[sample rate]]
}

impl Wrappable for AudioBuffer {
    const OWNS_EXTERNAL_MEMORY: bool = true;

    fn external_memory_size(&self) -> usize {
        let channels = self.channels.borrow();
        let mut size = channels.capacity() * size_of::<Channel>();
        for channel in &*channels {
            size = size.saturating_add(channel.data.capacity());
        }
        size
    }
}

// The ArrayBuffer is tracked next to the view because it can outlive it: script is free to keep `array.buffer` and
// drop the array. The buffer is what projects the channel's storage, so it is the one that decides how long that
// storage must stay put, and the one that has to be detached when the content is acquired.
struct AudioBufferChannelView {
    view: GcWeak<TypedArrayBase>,
    array_buffer: GcWeak<ArrayBuffer>,
}

struct AudioBufferChannelDataCacheEntry {
    buffer: GcWeak<EmbedderCell<Wrapped<AudioBuffer>>>,
    channel: u32,
    views: Vec<AudioBufferChannelView>,
}

thread_local! { static AUDIO_BUFFER_CHANNEL_DATA_CACHES: RefCell<Vec<AudioBufferChannelDataCacheEntry>> = const { RefCell::new(Vec::new()) }; }
fn prune_audio_buffer_channel_data_caches(caches: &mut Vec<AudioBufferChannelDataCacheEntry>) {
    caches.retain(|entry| entry.buffer.get().is_some());
}

fn cache_for<'a>(
    caches: &'a mut Vec<AudioBufferChannelDataCacheEntry>,
    vm: &Vm,
    buffer: Ref<AudioBuffer>,
    channel: u32,
) -> &'a mut AudioBufferChannelDataCacheEntry {
    prune_audio_buffer_channel_data_caches(caches);
    for index in 0..caches.len() {
        if caches[index].buffer.get() == Some(buffer) && caches[index].channel == channel {
            return &mut caches[index];
        }
    }
    caches.push(AudioBufferChannelDataCacheEntry {
        buffer: GcWeak::new(vm.heap(), buffer),
        channel,
        views: Vec::new(),
    });
    caches.last_mut().unwrap()
}

fn prune_live_channel_views(views: &mut Vec<AudioBufferChannelView>) {
    views.retain(|entry| entry.array_buffer.get().is_some());
}

impl AudioBuffer {
    pub(crate) fn construct(cx: &mut CallContext, options: AudioBufferOptions) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. If any of the values in options lie outside its nominal range, throw a NotSupportedError exception and abort the following steps.
        super::base_audio_context::BaseAudioContext::verify_audio_options_inside_nominal_range(
            options.number_of_channels,
            options.length,
            options.sample_rate,
        )?;
        if options.length as usize > i32::MAX as usize / size_of::<f32>() {
            return Err(vm
                .throw_completion::<()>(ErrorKind::RangeError, ErrorType::InvalidLength, &[&"typed array"])
                .unwrap_err()
                .into());
        }

        // 2. Let b be a new AudioBuffer object.
        // 3. Respectively assign the values of the attributes numberOfChannels, length, sampleRate of the AudioBufferOptions passed in the
        //    constructor to the internal slots [[number of channels]], [[length]], [[sample rate]].
        // 4. Set the internal slot [[internal data]] of this AudioBuffer to the result of calling CreateByteDataBlock([[length]] * [[number of channels]]).
        Self::create(vm, options.number_of_channels, options.length, options.sample_rate).map_err(|_| {
            vm.throw_completion::<()>(ErrorKind::InternalError, ErrorType::OutOfMemory, &[])
                .unwrap_err()
                .into()
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        number_of_channels: u32,
        length: u32,
        sample_rate: f32,
    ) -> Result<Ref<Self>, OutOfMemory> {
        let buffer = allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            channels: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            contents: RefCell::new(None),
            length,
            sample_rate,
        });
        let channel_byte_length = length as usize * size_of::<f32>();
        let mut channels = buffer.channels.borrow_mut();
        channels
            .try_reserve_exact(number_of_channels as usize)
            .map_err(|_| OutOfMemory)?;
        for _i in 0..number_of_channels {
            channels.push(Channel {
                data: OwnedBackingStore::create_zeroed(channel_byte_length)?,
            });
        }
        drop(channels);
        vm.heap().did_allocate_external_memory(buffer.external_memory_size());
        Ok(buffer)
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#acquire-the-content
    pub(crate) fn acquire_contents(this: Ref<Self>, vm: &Vm) -> Option<Arc<AudioBufferContents>> {
        // NB: contents is populated exactly while the channel arrays are detached because step 4 below has not run yet.
        //     The snapshot then still holds the buffer's content and script has had no way to modify it, so it can be
        //     handed out again as-is. This is what makes a sequence of acquisitions with no intervening getChannelData(),
        //     e.g. one AudioBuffer played by many AudioBufferSourceNodes, free of allocations and copying.
        //     https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#audio-buffer-copying
        if let Some(contents) = &*this.contents.borrow() {
            return Some(Arc::clone(contents));
        }

        // 1. If any of the AudioBuffer's ArrayBuffers are detached, return true, abort these steps, and return a
        //    zero-length channel data buffer to the invoker.
        let detached = AUDIO_BUFFER_CHANNEL_DATA_CACHES.with_borrow(|caches| {
            for cache in caches {
                if cache.buffer.get() != Some(this) {
                    continue;
                }
                for entry in &cache.views {
                    if entry.array_buffer.get().is_some_and(|buffer| buffer.is_detached()) {
                        return true;
                    }
                }
            }
            false
        });
        if detached {
            return None;
        }

        // 2. Detach all ArrayBuffers for arrays previously returned by getChannelData() on this AudioBuffer.
        // 3. Retain the underlying [[internal data]] from those ArrayBuffers and return references to them to the invoker.
        let mut channels = Vec::with_capacity(this.channels.borrow().len());
        for channel in &*this.channels.borrow() {
            let mut samples = vec![0_f32; this.length as usize];
            if !samples.is_empty() {
                unsafe {
                    std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(
                        channel.data.data(),
                        samples.as_mut_ptr().cast::<u8>(),
                        samples.len() * size_of::<f32>(),
                    );
                }
            }
            channels.push(samples);
        }
        AUDIO_BUFFER_CHANNEL_DATA_CACHES.with_borrow(|caches| {
            for cache in caches {
                if cache.buffer.get() != Some(this) {
                    continue;
                }
                for entry in &cache.views {
                    if let Some(array_buffer) = entry.array_buffer.get() {
                        detach_array_buffer(vm, array_buffer, None).expect("channel ArrayBuffers can be detached");
                    }
                }
            }
        });
        *this.contents.borrow_mut() = Some(Arc::new(AudioBufferContents {
            channels,
            sample_rate: this.sample_rate,
        }));
        vm.heap()
            .did_allocate_external_memory(this.channels.borrow().len() * this.length as usize * size_of::<f32>());

        // 4. Attach ArrayBuffers containing copies of the data to the AudioBuffer, to be returned by the next call to
        //    getChannelData().
        // NB: Performed lazily by attach_acquired_channels().
        this.contents.borrow().clone()
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#audio-buffer-copying
    pub(crate) fn attach_acquired_channels(this: Ref<Self>) {
        // The pending final step of acquiring this buffer's content: fresh arrays holding a copy of the acquired sample
        // data are attached the first time script reaches for the channel data again. Whoever acquired the content keeps
        // using the snapshot, so writes through the new arrays cannot change what is already playing.
        let mut contents = this.contents.borrow_mut();
        let Some(snapshot) = &*contents else {
            return;
        };
        let channels = this.channels.borrow();
        assert_eq!(snapshot.channels.len(), channels.len());
        for i in 0..channels.len() {
            let samples = &snapshot.channels[i];
            if !samples.is_empty() {
                unsafe {
                    std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(
                        samples.as_ptr().cast::<u8>(),
                        channels[i].data.data(),
                        samples.len() * size_of::<f32>(),
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        *contents = None;

        // Every view of the storage was detached when the content was acquired, and the storage needs fresh views over it.
        // So, drop the cached ones instead of handing a detached array back to the next caller.
        AUDIO_BUFFER_CHANNEL_DATA_CACHES.with_borrow_mut(|caches| {
            for cache in caches {
                if cache.buffer.get() == Some(this) {
                    cache.views.clear();
                }
            }
        });
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-samplerate
    pub(crate) fn sample_rate(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f32> {
        // The sample-rate for the PCM audio data in samples per second. This MUST return the value of [[sample rate]].
        Ok(self.sample_rate)
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-length
    pub(crate) fn length(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        // Length of the PCM audio data in sample-frames. This MUST return the value of [[length]].
        Ok(self.length)
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-duration
    pub(crate) fn duration(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        // Duration of the PCM audio data in seconds.
        // This is computed from the [[sample rate]] and the [[length]] of the AudioBuffer by performing a division between the [[length]] and the [[sample rate]].
        Ok(f64::from(self.length) / f64::from(self.sample_rate))
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-numberofchannels
    pub(crate) fn number_of_channels(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        // The number of discrete audio channels. This MUST return the value of [[number of channels]].
        Ok(self.channels.borrow().len() as u32)
    }

    pub(crate) fn channel_data(&self, channel: u32) -> WebIdlResult<(*mut u8, usize)> {
        let channels = self.channels.borrow();
        if channel as usize >= channels.len() {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"Channel index is out of range",
            )));
        }
        let data = &channels[channel as usize].data;
        Ok((data.data(), data.size()))
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-getchanneldata
    pub(crate) fn get_channel_data(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        channel: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<TypedArrayBase>> {
        if channel as usize >= this.channels.borrow().len() {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"Channel index is out of range",
            )));
        }

        // This is where the deferred final step of acquiring the content runs: script is reaching for the channel data
        // again, so the copies of the acquired samples become this buffer's internal data before anything reads them.
        Self::attach_acquired_channels(*this);
        let realm = cx.realm();
        AUDIO_BUFFER_CHANNEL_DATA_CACHES.with_borrow_mut(|caches| {
            let cache = cache_for(caches, cx.vm(), *this, channel);
            prune_live_channel_views(&mut cache.views);
            for entry in &cache.views {
                if let Some(view) = entry.view.get() {
                    if view.shape().realm() == realm {
                        return Ok(view);
                    }
                }
            }

            // The ArrayBuffer projects this AudioBuffer's channel storage instead of owning a copy of it, and names the
            // AudioBuffer as the owner of that storage. The GC then traces the AudioBuffer through the ArrayBuffer, so the
            // samples cannot be freed while script still holds a view of them.
            let channels = this.channels.borrow();
            let channel_storage = &channels[channel as usize].data;
            let owner = ForeignCellSlot::empty();
            unsafe {
                owner.set(NonNull::new(cell_into_abi(*this)));
            }
            let storage = ExternalPrimitiveStorage::new(owner, channel_storage.handle(), Some(channel_storage.size()));
            let array_buffer = ArrayBuffer::create_from_data_block(
                cx.vm(),
                realm,
                DataBlock::external(storage, ArrayBufferShared::No),
            );
            let view = create_typed_array_on_buffer(
                cx.vm(),
                realm,
                TypedArrayKind::Float32Array,
                this.length as usize,
                array_buffer,
            );
            cache.views.try_reserve(1).map_err(|_| {
                cx.vm()
                    .throw_completion::<()>(ErrorKind::InternalError, ErrorType::OutOfMemory, &[])
                    .unwrap_err()
            })?;
            cache.views.push(AudioBufferChannelView {
                view: GcWeak::new(cx.vm().heap(), view),
                array_buffer: GcWeak::new(cx.vm().heap(), array_buffer),
            });
            Ok(view)
        })
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-copyfromchannel
    pub(crate) fn copy_from_channel(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        destination: Gc<TypedArrayBase>,
        channel_number: u32,
        buffer_offset: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The copyFromChannel() method copies the samples from the specified channel of the AudioBuffer to the destination array.
        //
        // Let buffer be the AudioBuffer with Nb frames, let Nf be the number of elements in the destination array, and k be the value
        // of bufferOffset. Then the number of frames copied from buffer to destination is max(0,min(Nb−k,Nf)). If this is less than Nf,
        // then the remaining elements of destination are not modified.
        let vm = cx.vm();
        if destination.viewed_array_buffer().is_shared_array_buffer() {
            return Err(vm
                .throw_completion::<()>(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::SharedArrayBuffer, &[&"Float32Array"])
                .unwrap_err()
                .into());
        }
        if destination.viewed_array_buffer().is_detached() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let channels = self.channels.borrow();
        if channel_number as usize >= channels.len() {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"Channel index is out of range",
            )));
        }
        let channel = &channels[channel_number as usize];
        let channel_length = self.length as usize;
        if buffer_offset as usize >= channel_length {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let destination_record = make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record(&destination, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
        let destination_length = if is_typed_array_out_of_bounds(&destination_record) {
            0
        } else {
            typed_array_byte_length(&destination_record) / size_of::<f32>()
        };
        let count = destination_length.min(channel_length - buffer_offset as usize);
        let destination_bytes = destination.viewed_array_buffer();
        if count != 0 {
            destination_bytes.with_data_block(|destination_block| unsafe {
                std::ptr::copy(
                    channel
                        .data
                        .data()
                        .wrapping_add(buffer_offset as usize * size_of::<f32>()),
                    destination_block.data_at(destination.byte_offset()),
                    count * size_of::<f32>(),
                );
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiobuffer-copytochannel
    pub(crate) fn copy_to_channel(
        this: &Ref<Self>,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        source: Gc<TypedArrayBase>,
        channel_number: u32,
        buffer_offset: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The copyToChannel() method copies the samples to the specified channel of the AudioBuffer from the source array.
        //
        // A UnknownError may be thrown if source cannot be copied to the buffer.
        //
        // Let buffer be the AudioBuffer with Nb frames, let Nf be the number of elements in the source array, and k be the value
        // of bufferOffset. Then the number of frames copied from source to the buffer is max(0,min(Nb−k,Nf)). If this is less than Nf,
        // then the remaining elements of buffer are not modified.
        let vm = cx.vm();
        if source.viewed_array_buffer().is_shared_array_buffer() {
            return Err(vm
                .throw_completion::<()>(ErrorKind::TypeError, ErrorType::SharedArrayBuffer, &[&"Float32Array"])
                .unwrap_err()
                .into());
        }
        if source.viewed_array_buffer().is_detached() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        if channel_number as usize >= this.channels.borrow().len() {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_ascii(
                b"Channel index is out of range",
            )));
        }
        Self::attach_acquired_channels(*this);
        let channels = this.channels.borrow();
        let channel = &channels[channel_number as usize];
        let channel_length = this.length as usize;
        if buffer_offset as usize >= channel_length {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let source_record = make_typed_array_with_buffer_witness_record(&source, ArrayBufferOrder::SeqCst);
        let source_length = if is_typed_array_out_of_bounds(&source_record) {
            0
        } else {
            typed_array_byte_length(&source_record) / size_of::<f32>()
        };
        let count = source_length.min(channel_length - buffer_offset as usize);
        let source_bytes = source.viewed_array_buffer();
        if count != 0 {
            source_bytes.with_data_block(|source_block| unsafe {
                std::ptr::copy(
                    source_block.data_at(source.byte_offset()),
                    channel
                        .data
                        .data()
                        .wrapping_add(buffer_offset as usize * size_of::<f32>()),
                    count * size_of::<f32>(),
                );
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

    // FIXME: Reject these promises with InvalidStateError when the document unloads.

    pending_resume_promises: GcRefCell<Vec<WebIdlPromise>>,

impl Inherits<BaseAudioContext> for AudioContext {

    }

impl Wrappable for AudioContext {
    const TRACED_ON_OWNER_THREAD_ONLY: bool = true;

        self.context.cpp_parent()
    }

    const FINALIZES: bool = true;

    fn finalize(context: Ref<Self>) {
        context.context.shutdown_audio_worklet();
        if let Some(renderer) = &*context.renderer.borrow() {
            renderer.stop();
            renderer.set_client(None);
        }
    }

        None
    }

struct RendererClient {

impl RealtimeAudioRendererClient for RendererClient {
    fn sources_ended(&self, nodes: &[u64]) {

impl AudioContext {
    fn this(&self) -> Ref<Self> {
        let AnyBaseAudioContext::AudioContext(context) = self.context.this() else {
            unreachable!()
        };
        context
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiocontext-audiocontext
    pub(crate) fn construct(cx: &mut CallContext, context_options: AudioContextOptions) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let window =
            window_from_global_object(cx.realm().global_object()).expect("an AudioContext is constructed on a Window");
        let global = unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(window.as_event_target().as_ptr()) };

        // If the current settings object’s responsible document is NOT fully active, throw an InvalidStateError and abort these steps.
        // FIXME: Not all settings objects currently return a responsible document.
        //        Therefore we only fail this check if responsible document is not null.
        unsafe extern "C" {
            fn web_audio_context_responsible_document_is_fully_active(global: *mut c_void) -> bool;
        }
        if !unsafe { web_audio_context_responsible_document_is_fully_active(global.as_ptr()) } {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidStateError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Document is not fully active"),
            ));
        }

        // AD-HOC: The spec doesn't currently require the sample rate to be validated here,
        //         but other browsers do perform a check and there is a WPT test that expects this.
        if let Some(sample_rate) = context_options.sample_rate {
            BaseAudioContext::verify_sample_rate(sample_rate)?;
        }

        // 1. Let context be a new AudioContext object.
        let context = allocate(cx.vm(), |defer_gc| Self {
            context: BaseAudioContext::new(defer_gc, global, 0.),
            base_latency: 0.,
            output_latency: 0.,
            pending_resume_promises: GcRefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            suspended_by_user: Cell::new(false),
            renderer: RefCell::new(None),
        });
        context
            .context
            .initialize(cx.vm(), AnyBaseAudioContext::AudioContext(context));
        context.context.event_target().set_owner(context);
        context.context.listener.set(Some(AudioListener::create(
            cx.vm(),
            AnyBaseAudioContext::AudioContext(context),
        )));
        context.context.destination.set(Some(AudioDestinationNode::create(
            cx,
            AnyBaseAudioContext::AudioContext(context),
            2,
        )?));

        // 2. Set a [[control thread state]] to suspended on context.
        context.context.set_control_state(AudioContextState::Suspended);

        // 3. Set a [[rendering thread state]] to suspended on context.
        context.context.set_rendering_state(AudioContextState::Suspended);

        // FIXME: 4. Let messageChannel be a new MessageChannel.
        // FIXME: 5. Let controlSidePort be the value of messageChannel’s port1 attribute.
        // FIXME: 6. Let renderingSidePort be the value of messageChannel’s port2 attribute.
        // FIXME: 7. Let serializedRenderingSidePort be the result of StructuredSerializeWithTransfer(renderingSidePort, « renderingSidePort »).
        // FIXME: 8. Set this audioWorklet's port to controlSidePort.
        // FIXME: 9. Queue a control message to set the MessagePort on the AudioContextGlobalScope, with serializedRenderingSidePort.
        // 10. If contextOptions is given, apply the options:
        // 1. If sinkId is specified, let sinkId be the value of contextOptions.sinkId and run the following substeps:
        // 2. Set the internal latency of context according to contextOptions.latencyHint, as described in latencyHint.
        // FIXME: Determine optimal settings for contextOptions.latencyHint.
        // 3: If contextOptions.sampleRate is specified, set the sampleRate of context to this value.
        if let Some(sample_rate) = context_options.sample_rate {
            context.context.set_sample_rate(sample_rate);
        } else {
            // Otherwise, follow these substeps:
            // FIXME: 1. If sinkId is the empty string or a type of AudioSinkOptions, use the sample rate of the default output device. Abort these substeps.
            // FIXME: 2. If sinkId is a DOMString, use the sample rate of the output device identified by sinkId. Abort these substeps.
            // If contextOptions.sampleRate differs from the sample rate of the output device, the user agent MUST resample the audio output to match the sample rate of the output device.
            context.context.set_sample_rate(44100.);
        }

        // AD-HOC: Ensure a sample rate is always set, even when no options were passed at all.
        if context.context.sample_rate_value() == 0. {
            context.context.set_sample_rate(44100.);
        }

        // 11. If context is allowed to start, send a control message to start processing.
        if context.allowed_to_start() {
            // AD-HOC: Record startup now so a source started before the statechange task cannot request it again.
            context.context.set_control_state(AudioContextState::Running);

            // FIXME: 1. Let document be the current settings object's relevant global object's associated Document.
            // 2. Attempt to acquire system resources to use a following audio output device based on [[sink ID]] for
            //    rendering.
            context.start_rendering_audio_graph(cx.vm());

            // 2. Set this [[rendering thread state]] to running on the AudioContext.
            context.context.set_rendering_state(AudioContextState::Running);

            // 3. Queue a media element task to execute the following steps:
            context
                .context
                .queue_a_media_element_task(cx.vm(), context, |_, context| {
                    // 1. Set the state attribute of the AudioContext to "running".
                    context.context.set_state(AudioContextState::Running);

                    // 2. Fire an event named statechange at the AudioContext.
                    context.context.dispatch_statechange();
                });
        }

        // 12. Return context.
        Ok(context)
    }

    pub(crate) fn document_became_inactive(&self) {
        // Release the audio output device and the GC roots held by the renderer's callbacks, so a context belonging to a
        // navigated-away document stops playing and can eventually be collected.
        self.context.shutdown_audio_worklet();
        if let Some(renderer) = &*self.renderer.borrow() {
            renderer.stop();
            renderer.set_client(None);
        }
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-baseaudiocontext-currenttime
    pub(crate) fn current_time_value(&self) -> f64 {
        // This is the time in seconds of the sample frame immediately following the last sample-frame in the block of
        // audio most recently processed by the context's rendering graph.
        if let Some(renderer) = &*self.renderer.borrow() {
            return renderer.frames_rendered() as f64 / f64::from(self.context.sample_rate_value());
        }
        0.
    }

    pub(crate) fn base_latency(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.base_latency)
    }

    pub(crate) fn output_latency(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.output_latency)
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiocontext-getoutputtimestamp
    pub(crate) fn get_output_timestamp(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<AudioTimestamp> {
        let renderer = self.renderer.borrow();

        // If the context's rendering graph has not yet processed a block of audio, then
        // getOutputTimestamp call returns an AudioTimestamp instance with both members
        // containing zero.
        if renderer.as_ref().is_none_or(|renderer| renderer.frames_rendered() == 0) {
            return Ok(AudioTimestamp {
                context_time: Some(0.),
                performance_time: Some(0.),
            });
        }

        // FIXME: performanceTime should be the moment the sample frame at contextTime was rendered by the output device.
        //        We sample performance.now() when getOutputTimestamp() is called instead of caching a timestamp when the
        //        renderer produced that block, so the returned pair does not describe a single output instant.
        Ok(AudioTimestamp {
            context_time: Some(renderer.as_ref().unwrap().output_time_played()),
            performance_time: Some(unsafe {
                web_audio_realtime_context_performance_now(self.context.global_event_target().as_ptr())
            }),
        })
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#allowed-to-start
    pub(crate) fn allowed_to_start(&self) -> bool {
        // NB: Autoplay permission governs the first start of this context.
        self.renderer.borrow().is_some()
            || unsafe { web_audio_context_is_allowed_to_start(self.context.global_event_target().as_ptr()) }
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiocontext-resume
    pub(crate) fn resume(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, promise: WebIdlPromise) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If this’s relevant global object’s associated Document is not fully active then return a promise rejected with "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
        if !self.context.document_is_fully_active() {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidStateError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Document is not fully active"),
            ));
        }

        // 2. Let promise be a new Promise.
        // NB: The bindings create the promise.

        // 3. If the [[control thread state]] on the AudioContext is closed reject the promise with InvalidStateError, abort these steps, returning promise.
        if self.context.control_state() == AudioContextState::Closed {
            reject_promise_with_exception(
                cx.vm(),
                promise,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "InvalidStateError",
                    Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Audio context is already closed."),
                ),
            );
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 4. Set [[suspended by user]] to false.
        self.suspended_by_user.set(false);

        // FIXME: 5. If the context’s state attribute is "suspended" and the context’s [[control thread state]] is "interrupted", then:
        // FIXME: 5.1. Queue a media element task to execute the following steps:
        // FIXME: 5.1.1. Set the state attribute of the AudioContext to "interrupted".
        // FIXME: 5.1.2. Set the [[state before interruption]] slot to "running".
        // FIXME: 5.1.3. Queue a media element task to fire an event named statechange at the AudioContext.
        // FIXME: 5.2. Reject the promise with InvalidStateError, abort these steps, returning promise.

        // 6. If the context is not allowed to start, append promise to [[pending promises]] and [[pending resume promises]] and abort these steps, returning promise.
        if !self.allowed_to_start() {
            self.context.pending_promises.borrow_mut(cx.vm()).push(promise);
            self.pending_resume_promises.borrow_mut(cx.vm()).push(promise);
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 7. Set the [[control thread state]] on the AudioContext to running.
        self.context.set_control_state(AudioContextState::Running);

        // 8. Queue a control message to resume the AudioContext with promise.
        self.run_control_message_to_resume(cx.vm(), Some(promise));

        // 9. Return promise.
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn suspended_by_user(&self) -> bool {
        self.suspended_by_user.get()
    }

    fn settle_pending_resume_promises(&self, vm: &Vm, mut settle: impl FnMut(WebIdlPromise)) {
        let mut resumes = self.pending_resume_promises.borrow_mut(vm);
        if resumes.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        for &promise in resumes.iter() {
            settle(promise);
            let mut pending = self.context.pending_promises.borrow_mut(vm);
            if let Some(index) = pending.iter().position(|pending| *pending == promise) {
                pending.remove(index);
            }
        }
        resumes.clear();
    }

    pub(crate) fn run_control_message_to_resume(&self, vm: &Vm, promise: Option<WebIdlPromise>) {
        // 1. Let promise be the promise passed into this algorithm.

        // 2. Attempt to acquire system resources.
        // NB: The renderer acquires resources when starting the graph in step 4.
        // 3. Set the [[rendering thread state]] on the AudioContext to running.
        self.context.set_rendering_state(AudioContextState::Running);

        // 4. Start rendering the audio graph.
        let started = self.start_rendering_audio_graph(vm);

        // 5. In case of failure, queue a media element task to execute the following steps:
        if !started {
            self.context.queue_a_media_element_task(vm, self.this(), |vm, context| {
                // 5.1. Reject all promises from [[pending resume promises]] in order, then clear [[pending resume promises]].
                for promise in &*context.pending_resume_promises.borrow() {
                    with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(promise_realm(*promise), || {
                        reject_promise(vm, *promise, Value::NULL);
                    });

                    // 5.2. Additionally, remove those promises from [[pending promises]].
                    let mut pending = context.context.pending_promises.borrow_mut(vm);
                    if let Some(index) = pending.iter().position(|pending| pending == promise) {
                        pending.remove(index);
                    }
                }
                context.pending_resume_promises.borrow_mut(vm).clear();
            });
        }

        // 6. queue a media element task to execute the following steps:
        self.context
            .queue_a_media_element_task(vm, (self.this(), promise), |vm, (context, promise)| {
                // 6.1. If the [[render quantum size]] of the AudioContext is 0, set it to the actual hardware render quantum size chosen during resource acquisition.
                // NB: This implementation always uses a fixed quantum size.

                // 6.2. Resolve all promises from [[pending resume promises]] in order.
                // 6.3. Clear [[pending resume promises]]. Additionally, remove those promises from [[pending promises]].
                with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(context.context.realm(), || {
                    context
                        .settle_pending_resume_promises(vm, |promise| resolve_promise(vm, promise, Value::UNDEFINED));

                    // 6.4. Resolve promise.
                    if let Some(promise) = promise {
                        resolve_promise(vm, promise, Value::UNDEFINED);
                    }

                    // 6.5. If the state attribute of the AudioContext is not already "running":
                    if context.context.state_value() != AudioContextState::Running {
                        // 6.5.1. Set the state attribute of the AudioContext to "running".
                        context.context.set_state(AudioContextState::Running);

                        // 6.5.2. Queue a media element task to fire an event named statechange at the AudioContext.
                        context.context.queue_a_media_element_task(vm, context, |_, context| {
                            context.context.dispatch_statechange();
                        });
                    }
                });
            });
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiocontext-suspend
    pub(crate) fn suspend(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, promise: WebIdlPromise) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If this’s relevant global object’s associated Document is not fully active then return a promise rejected with "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
        if !self.context.document_is_fully_active() {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidStateError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Document is not fully active"),
            ));
        }

        // 2. Let promise be a new Promise.
        // NB: The bindings create the promise.

        // 3. If the [[control thread state]] on the AudioContext is closed reject the promise with InvalidStateError, abort these steps, returning promise.
        if self.context.control_state() == AudioContextState::Closed {
            reject_promise_with_exception(
                cx.vm(),
                promise,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "InvalidStateError",
                    Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Audio context is already closed."),
                ),
            );
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 4. Append promise to [[pending promises]].
        self.context.pending_promises.borrow_mut(cx.vm()).push(promise);

        // 5. Set [[suspended by user]] to true.
        self.suspended_by_user.set(true);

        // 6. Set the [[control thread state]] on the AudioContext to suspended.
        self.context.set_control_state(AudioContextState::Suspended);

        // 7. Queue a control message to suspend the AudioContext with promise.
        self.run_control_message_to_suspend(cx.vm(), promise);

        // 8. Return promise.
        Ok(())
    }

    fn run_control_message_to_suspend(&self, vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise) {
        // 1. Let promise be the promise passed into this algorithm.

        // 2. Attempt to release system resources.
        if let Some(renderer) = &*self.renderer.borrow() {
            renderer.suspend();
            renderer.set_client(None);
        }

        // FIXME: 3. If the [[rendering thread state]] on the AudioContext is "interrupted", queue a media element task to set the [[state before interruption]] slot to "suspended".

        // 4. Set the [[rendering thread state]] on the AudioContext to "suspended".
        self.context.set_rendering_state(AudioContextState::Suspended);

        // 5. Queue a media element task to execute the following steps:
        self.context
            .queue_a_media_element_task(vm, (self.this(), promise), |vm, (context, promise)| {
                with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(promise_realm(promise), || {
                    // 5.1. Resolve promise.
                    resolve_promise(vm, promise, Value::UNDEFINED);

                    // AD-HOC: The spec omits removing a settled suspension promise from [[pending promises]].
                    context
                        .context
                        .pending_promises
                        .borrow_mut(vm)
                        .retain(|pending| *pending != promise);

                    // 5.2. If the state attribute of the AudioContext is not already "suspended":
                    if context.context.state_value() != AudioContextState::Suspended {
                        // 5.2.1. Set the state attribute of the AudioContext to "suspended".
                        context.context.set_state(AudioContextState::Suspended);

                        // 5.2.2. Queue a media element task to fire an event named statechange at the AudioContext.
                        context.context.queue_a_media_element_task(vm, context, |_, context| {
                            context.context.dispatch_statechange();
                        });
                    }
                });
            });
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiocontext-close
    pub(crate) fn close(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, promise: WebIdlPromise) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. If this’s relevant global object’s associated Document is not fully active then return a promise rejected with "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
        if !self.context.document_is_fully_active() {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidStateError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Document is not fully active"),
            ));
        }

        // 2. Let promise be a new Promise.
        // NB: The bindings create the promise.

        // 3. If the [[control thread state]] flag on the AudioContext is closed reject the promise with InvalidStateError, abort these steps, returning promise.
        if self.context.control_state() == AudioContextState::Closed {
            reject_promise_with_exception(
                cx.vm(),
                promise,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "InvalidStateError",
                    Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Audio context is already closed."),
                ),
            );
            return Ok(());
        }

        // 4. Set the [[control thread state]] flag on the AudioContext to closed.
        self.context.set_control_state(AudioContextState::Closed);

        // 5. Queue a control message to close the AudioContext.
        self.run_control_message_to_close(cx.vm(), promise);

        // 6. Return promise.
        Ok(())
    }

    fn run_control_message_to_close(&self, vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise) {
        // 1. Attempt to release system resources.
        self.context.shutdown_audio_worklet();
        if let Some(renderer) = &*self.renderer.borrow() {
            renderer.stop();
            renderer.set_client(None);
        }

        // 2. Set the [[rendering thread state]] to suspended.
        // NOTE: This will stop rendering.
        self.context.set_rendering_state(AudioContextState::Suspended);

        // 3. If this control message is being run in a reaction to the document being unloaded, abort this algorithm.
        // NOTE: There is no need to notify the control thread in this case.
        // NB: Document teardown releases the renderer directly.
        // 4. queue a media element task to execute the following steps:
        self.context
            .queue_a_media_element_task(vm, (self.this(), promise), |vm, (context, promise)| {
                with_temporary_execution_context_and_callbacks(promise_realm(promise), || {
                    // AD-HOC: As in Chromium and Firefox, reject resumes still waiting for autoplay permission.
                    // This context can no longer start once it closes.
                    context.settle_pending_resume_promises(vm, |promise| {
                        reject_promise_with_exception(
                            vm,
                            promise,
                            Exception::Dom(
                                "InvalidStateError",
                                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Audio context closed before it could resume."),
                            ),
                        );
                    });

                    // 4.1. Resolve promise.
                    resolve_promise(vm, promise, Value::UNDEFINED);

                    // 4.2. If the state attribute of the AudioContext is not already "closed":
                    if context.context.state_value() != AudioContextState::Closed {
                        // 4.2.1. Set the state attribute of the AudioContext to "closed".
                        context.context.set_state(AudioContextState::Closed);

                        // 4.2.2. queue a media element task to fire an event named statechange at the AudioContext.
                        context.context.queue_a_media_element_task(vm, context, |_, context| {
                            context.context.dispatch_statechange();
                        });
                    }
                });
            });
    }

    fn start_rendering_audio_graph(&self, vm: &Vm) -> bool {
        if let Some(renderer) = &*self.renderer.borrow() {
            self.set_renderer_client(vm, renderer);
            renderer.resume();
            return true;
        }

        let factory = unsafe { web_audio_output_factory_create(self.context.global_event_target().as_ptr()) };
        let renderer = RealtimeAudioRenderer::new(
            Arc::clone(self.context.control_message_queue()),
            self.context.destination_value().parent().node_id(),
            self.context.sample_rate_value(),
            BaseAudioContext::RENDER_QUANTUM_SIZE as usize,
            SharedCppObject {
                pointer: factory.pointer,
                retain: factory.retain,
                release: factory.release,
            },
        );
        self.set_renderer_client(vm, &renderer);
        *self.renderer.borrow_mut() = Some(Arc::clone(&renderer));
        renderer.start_rendering();
        true
    }

    // The renderer's callback captures a GC root on this context, keeping it alive while it renders. That root is released
    // by clearing the callbacks when the context is suspended, closed, or its document becomes inactive, so this is called
    // again to re-establish it whenever rendering resumes.
    fn set_renderer_client(&self, vm: &Vm, renderer: &RealtimeAudioRenderer) {
        renderer.set_client(Some(Rc::new(RendererClient {
            vm: NonNull::from(vm),
            context: CellRoot::new(self.this()),
        })));
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiocontext-createmediaelementsource
    pub(crate) fn create_media_element_source(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        media_element: CppInterface,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<MediaElementAudioSourceNode>> {
        MediaElementAudioSourceNode::create(cx, self.this(), media_element)
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiocontext-createmediastreamsource
    pub(crate) fn create_media_stream_source(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        media_stream: CppInterface,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<MediaStreamAudioSourceNode>> {
        MediaStreamAudioSourceNode::create(cx, self.this(), &MediaStreamAudioSourceOptions { media_stream })
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiocontext-createmediastreamdestination
    pub(crate) fn create_media_stream_destination(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode>> {
        MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode::create(cx, self.this(), &AudioNodeOptions::default())
    }
}

use super::base_audio_context::{AnyBaseAudioContext, BaseAudioContext};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, Exception, WebIdlResult};

// https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#AudioDestinationNode
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct AudioDestinationNode {
    node: AudioNode,
}

impl Inherits<AudioNode> for AudioDestinationNode {
    fn parent(&self) -> &AudioNode {
        &self.node
    }
}

impl Wrappable for AudioDestinationNode {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.node.cpp_parent()
    }

    const FINALIZES: bool = true;

    fn finalize(node: Ref<Self>) {
        node.node.finalize_node();
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for AudioDestinationNode {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
}

impl AudioDestinationNode {
    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audiodestinationnode-maxchannelcount
    pub(crate) fn max_channel_count(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        Ok(self.max_channel_count_value())
    }

    fn max_channel_count_value(&self) -> u32 {
        // The maximum number of channels that the channelCount attribute can be set to. An AudioDestinationNode
        // representing the audio hardware end-point (the normal case) can potentially output more than 2 channels of
        // audio if the audio hardware is multi-channel. maxChannelCount is the maximum number of channels that this
        // hardware is capable of supporting.
        // NB: For an OfflineAudioContext, channelCount may not be changed, so the maximum equals the channel count the
        //     context was constructed with. For an AudioContext, we follow the recommendation from the spec's privacy
        //     considerations that maxChannelCount be set to two (stereo) instead of exposing the audio hardware's
        //     actual capabilities.
        if matches!(self.node.context_value(), AnyBaseAudioContext::OfflineAudioContext(_)) {
            return self.node.channel_count_value();
        }
        2
    }

    pub(crate) fn create(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        context: AnyBaseAudioContext,
        channel_count: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        let node = allocate(cx.vm(), |defer_gc| Self {
            node: AudioNode::new(defer_gc, context, channel_count),
        });
        node.node.set_this(AnyAudioNode::AudioDestinationNode(node));
        node.node.event_target().set_owner(node);

        // Default options for channel count and interpretation
        // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#AudioDestinationNode
        let default_options = AudioNodeDefaultOptions {
            channel_count,
            channel_count_mode: ChannelCountMode::Explicit,
            channel_interpretation: ChannelInterpretation::Speakers,
        };

        // FIXME: Set tail-time to no
        node.node
            .initialize_audio_node_options(cx, &AudioNodeOptions::default(), &default_options)?;
        node.node.queue_render_node_creation(create_destination_render_node(
            node.node.node_id(),
            BaseAudioContext::RENDER_QUANTUM_SIZE as usize,
            channel_count as usize,
        ));
        Ok(node)
    }

    // https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#dom-audionode-channelcount
    pub(crate) fn set_channel_count_override(&self, _: &mut CallContext, channel_count: u32) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        if channel_count == self.node.channel_count_value() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        // The behavior depends on whether the destination node is the destination of an AudioContext
        // or OfflineAudioContext:

        // AudioContext: The channel count MUST be between 1 and maxChannelCount. An IndexSizeError
        // exception MUST be thrown for any attempt to set the count outside this range.
        // NB: Setting the count to zero throws NotSupportedError through AudioNode's channelCount validation below,
        //     taking precedence over the range check here.
        if matches!(self.node.context_value(), AnyBaseAudioContext::AudioContext(_)) {
            if channel_count > self.max_channel_count_value() {
                return Err(Exception::Dom(
                    "IndexSizeError",
                    Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Channel index is out of range"),
                ));
            }
        }

        // OfflineAudioContext: This value may not be changed; a NotSupportedError exception MUST be thrown if
        // channelCount is changed to a different value.
        if matches!(self.node.context_value(), AnyBaseAudioContext::OfflineAudioContext(_)) {
            return Err(Exception::Dom(
                "InvalidStateError",
                Utf16String::from_ascii(b"Cannot change channel count in an OfflineAudioContext"),
            ));
        }
        self.node.set_channel_count_impl(channel_count)
    }
}

#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]

    context: AnyBaseAudioContext,
    channel_count: Cell<u32>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    channel_count_mode: Cell<ChannelCountMode>,
    #[gc(untraced)]

    output_connections: GcRefCell<Vec<AudioNodeConnection>>,

}

impl Wrappable for AudioNode {

    }

    const FINALIZES: bool = true;

    fn finalize(node: Ref<Self>) {
        node.finalize_node();
    }
}

impl GetTheParent for AudioNode {
    fn get_the_parent(&self) -> Option<CppEventTarget> {
        None
    }
