//! Where the pixels of a 2D texture image are in the client memory that GL unpacks it from, and what
//! UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL and UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL do to them, as arithmetic on plain bytes that the tests of
//! the crate cover without the JS runtime.

use core::ops::Range;

use super::constants::{
    GL_ALPHA, GL_BYTE, GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT, GL_FLOAT, GL_FLOAT_32_UNSIGNED_INT_24_8_REV, GL_HALF_FLOAT, GL_INT,
    GL_LUMINANCE, GL_LUMINANCE_ALPHA, GL_RED, GL_RED_INTEGER, GL_RG, GL_RG_INTEGER, GL_RGB, GL_RGB_INTEGER, GL_RGBA,
    GL_RGBA_INTEGER, GL_SHORT, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, GL_UNSIGNED_INT, GL_UNSIGNED_INT_2_10_10_10_REV,
    GL_UNSIGNED_INT_5_9_9_9_REV, GL_UNSIGNED_INT_10F_11F_11F_REV, GL_UNSIGNED_INT_24_8, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT,
    GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_4_4_4_4, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_5_5_1, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_6_5,
};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct PixelUnpackState {
    pub(crate) alignment: usize,
    pub(crate) row_length: usize,
    pub(crate) skip_pixels: usize,
    pub(crate) skip_rows: usize,
}

impl Default for PixelUnpackState {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            alignment: 4,
            row_length: 0,
            skip_pixels: 0,
            skip_rows: 0,
        }
    }
}

/// Whether the pixels of a row of a 2D image that is `width` pixels wide lie inside the row of client memory that they
/// are unpacked from. A negative width is left for the operation to reject.
pub(crate) fn is_valid_2d_pixel_unpack_state(width: i32, unpack_state: &PixelUnpackState) -> bool {
    let Ok(width) = usize::try_from(width) else {
        return true;
    };
    let data_store_width = if unpack_state.row_length == 0 {
        width
    } else {
        unpack_state.row_length
    };
    unpack_state
        .skip_pixels
        .checked_add(width)
        .is_some_and(|unpacked_row_end| unpacked_row_end <= data_store_width)
}

/// How many bytes of client memory a 2D image is unpacked from, counted from the start of that memory.
pub(crate) fn required_2d_texture_data_size(
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    format: u32,
    r#type: u32,
    unpack_state: &PixelUnpackState,
) -> Option<usize> {
    if !is_valid_2d_pixel_unpack_state(width, unpack_state) {
        return None;
    }
    let width = usize::try_from(width).ok()?;
    let height = usize::try_from(height).ok()?;
    if width == 0 || height == 0 {
        return Some(0);
    }
    let pixel_size = texel_layout(format, r#type)?.bytes_per_pixel;
    let alignment = unpack_state.alignment;
    if !matches!(alignment, 1 | 2 | 4 | 8) {
        return None;
    }
    let pixels_per_row = if unpack_state.row_length == 0 {
        width
    } else {
        unpack_state.row_length
    };
    let row_byte_length = pixels_per_row.checked_mul(pixel_size)?.checked_add(alignment - 1)? / alignment * alignment;
    let skipped_rows_size = unpack_state.skip_rows.checked_mul(row_byte_length)?;
    let skipped_pixels_size = unpack_state.skip_pixels.checked_mul(pixel_size)?;
    let remaining_rows_size = (height - 1).checked_mul(row_byte_length)?;
    let final_row_size = width.checked_mul(pixel_size)?;
    skipped_rows_size
        .checked_add(skipped_pixels_size)?
        .checked_add(remaining_rows_size)?
        .checked_add(final_row_size)
}

/// https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/1.0/#PIXEL_STORAGE_PARAMETERS
///
/// A 2D image that texImage2D or texSubImage2D unpacks from an ArrayBufferView, and how it is flipped and
/// premultiplied on the way.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct ImageUnpackConversion {
    pub(crate) width: i32,
    pub(crate) height: i32,
    pub(crate) format: u32,
    pub(crate) r#type: u32,
    pub(crate) unpack_state: PixelUnpackState,
    pub(crate) flip_y: bool,
    pub(crate) premultiply_alpha: bool,
}

impl ImageUnpackConversion {
    /// Converts the pixels where they are, so that GL unpacks the converted image with the same pixel unpack state.
    /// The bytes between the rows and before the first pixel stay as they are, and bytes that do not hold the whole
    /// image are left for GL to report the error of.
    pub(crate) fn convert(&self, bytes: &mut [u8]) {
        let Some(texel_layout) = texel_layout(self.format, self.r#type) else {
            return;
        };
        let Some(rows) = ImageRows::new(self, texel_layout.bytes_per_pixel) else {
            return;
        };
        if rows.end > bytes.len() {
            return;
        }

        if self.premultiply_alpha && texel_layout.alpha_premultiplication != AlphaPremultiplication::Unneeded {
            for row in 0..rows.count {
                premultiply_alpha_of_row(&mut bytes[rows.bytes_of(row)], texel_layout);
            }
        }
        if self.flip_y {
            flip_rows(bytes, &rows);
        }
    }
}

/// Where the rows of the pixels of an image are. A row is followed by the padding that UNPACK_ALIGNMENT asks for, and
/// by the pixels past the image when UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH is wider than the image.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct ImageRows {
    start_of_first_row: usize,
    stride: usize,
    byte_length: usize,
    count: usize,
    end: usize,
}

impl ImageRows {
    /// `None` for an image without pixels, and for one whose rows overlap.
    fn new(image: &ImageUnpackConversion, bytes_per_pixel: usize) -> Option<Self> {
        let width = usize::try_from(image.width).ok().filter(|&width| width > 0)?;
        let count = usize::try_from(image.height).ok().filter(|&height| height > 0)?;
        let unpack_state = &image.unpack_state;

        let pixels_per_row = if unpack_state.row_length == 0 {
            width
        } else {
            unpack_state.row_length
        };
        let stride = pixels_per_row
            .checked_mul(bytes_per_pixel)?
            .checked_next_multiple_of(unpack_state.alignment)?;
        let byte_length = width.checked_mul(bytes_per_pixel)?;
        if byte_length > stride {
            return None;
        }
        let start_of_first_row = unpack_state
            .skip_rows
            .checked_mul(stride)?
            .checked_add(unpack_state.skip_pixels.checked_mul(bytes_per_pixel)?)?;
        let end = stride
            .checked_mul(count - 1)?
            .checked_add(start_of_first_row)?
            .checked_add(byte_length)?;
        Some(Self {
            start_of_first_row,
            stride,
            byte_length,
            count,
            end,
        })
    }

    fn bytes_of(&self, row: usize) -> Range<usize> {
        let start = self.start_of_first_row + row * self.stride;
        start..start + self.byte_length
    }
}

fn flip_rows(bytes: &mut [u8], rows: &ImageRows) {
    for upper_row in 0..rows.count / 2 {
        let lower_row = rows.count - 1 - upper_row;
        let (bytes_up_to_lower_row, bytes_from_lower_row) = bytes.split_at_mut(rows.bytes_of(lower_row).start);
        bytes_up_to_lower_row[rows.bytes_of(upper_row)].swap_with_slice(&mut bytes_from_lower_row[..rows.byte_length]);
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum ComponentType {
    UnsignedByte,
    Byte,
    UnsignedShort,
    Short,
    UnsignedInt,
    Int,
    HalfFloat,
    Float,
}

impl ComponentType {
    fn size(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::UnsignedByte | Self::Byte => 1,
            Self::UnsignedShort | Self::Short | Self::HalfFloat => 2,
            Self::UnsignedInt | Self::Int | Self::Float => 4,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum AlphaPremultiplication {
    /// The texel has no alpha, or no color for alpha to be multiplied into.
    Unneeded,
    /// Each component is a number of the type, and alpha is the last of them.
    IntoComponentsBeforeAlpha(ComponentType),
    UnsignedShort4444,
    UnsignedShort5551,
    UnsignedInt2101010Rev,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct TexelLayout {
    bytes_per_pixel: usize,
    alpha_premultiplication: AlphaPremultiplication,
}

/// Formats and types that no upload takes together may have a layout: GL rejects the upload whatever its pixels are.
fn texel_layout(format: u32, r#type: u32) -> Option<TexelLayout> {
    let format_is_rgba = matches!(format, GL_RGBA | GL_RGBA_INTEGER);
    let packed_texel = |bytes_per_pixel, alpha_premultiplication_of_rgba| TexelLayout {
        bytes_per_pixel,
        alpha_premultiplication: if format_is_rgba {
            alpha_premultiplication_of_rgba
        } else {
            AlphaPremultiplication::Unneeded
        },
    };
    match r#type {
        GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_4_4_4_4 => return Some(packed_texel(2, AlphaPremultiplication::UnsignedShort4444)),
        GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_5_5_1 => return Some(packed_texel(2, AlphaPremultiplication::UnsignedShort5551)),
        GL_UNSIGNED_INT_2_10_10_10_REV => return Some(packed_texel(4, AlphaPremultiplication::UnsignedInt2101010Rev)),
        GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_6_5 => return Some(packed_texel(2, AlphaPremultiplication::Unneeded)),
        GL_UNSIGNED_INT_10F_11F_11F_REV | GL_UNSIGNED_INT_5_9_9_9_REV | GL_UNSIGNED_INT_24_8 => {
            return Some(packed_texel(4, AlphaPremultiplication::Unneeded));
        }
        GL_FLOAT_32_UNSIGNED_INT_24_8_REV => return Some(packed_texel(8, AlphaPremultiplication::Unneeded)),
        _ => {}
    }

    let component_type = match r#type {
        GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE => ComponentType::UnsignedByte,
        GL_BYTE => ComponentType::Byte,
        GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT => ComponentType::UnsignedShort,
        GL_SHORT => ComponentType::Short,
        GL_UNSIGNED_INT => ComponentType::UnsignedInt,
        GL_INT => ComponentType::Int,
        GL_HALF_FLOAT => ComponentType::HalfFloat,
        GL_FLOAT => ComponentType::Float,
        _ => return None,
    };
    let (component_count, alpha_premultiplication) = match format {
        GL_ALPHA | GL_LUMINANCE | GL_RED | GL_RED_INTEGER | GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT => (1, AlphaPremultiplication::Unneeded),
        GL_RG | GL_RG_INTEGER => (2, AlphaPremultiplication::Unneeded),
        GL_RGB | GL_RGB_INTEGER => (3, AlphaPremultiplication::Unneeded),
        GL_LUMINANCE_ALPHA => (2, AlphaPremultiplication::IntoComponentsBeforeAlpha(component_type)),
        GL_RGBA | GL_RGBA_INTEGER => (4, AlphaPremultiplication::IntoComponentsBeforeAlpha(component_type)),
        _ => return None,
    };
    Some(TexelLayout {
        bytes_per_pixel: component_count * component_type.size(),
        alpha_premultiplication,
    })
}

fn premultiply_alpha_of_row(row: &mut [u8], texel_layout: TexelLayout) {
    let bytes_per_pixel = texel_layout.bytes_per_pixel;
    match texel_layout.alpha_premultiplication {
        AlphaPremultiplication::Unneeded => {}
        AlphaPremultiplication::IntoComponentsBeforeAlpha(component_type) => match component_type {
            ComponentType::UnsignedByte => premultiply_components_before_alpha::<1, u8>(row, bytes_per_pixel),
            ComponentType::Byte => premultiply_components_before_alpha::<1, i8>(row, bytes_per_pixel),
            ComponentType::UnsignedShort => premultiply_components_before_alpha::<2, u16>(row, bytes_per_pixel),
            ComponentType::Short => premultiply_components_before_alpha::<2, i16>(row, bytes_per_pixel),
            ComponentType::UnsignedInt => premultiply_components_before_alpha::<4, u32>(row, bytes_per_pixel),
            ComponentType::Int => premultiply_components_before_alpha::<4, i32>(row, bytes_per_pixel),
            ComponentType::HalfFloat => premultiply_components_before_alpha::<2, HalfFloat>(row, bytes_per_pixel),
            ComponentType::Float => premultiply_components_before_alpha::<4, f32>(row, bytes_per_pixel),
        },
        AlphaPremultiplication::UnsignedShort4444 => replace_numbers_of_row(row, premultiplied_unsigned_short_4444),
        AlphaPremultiplication::UnsignedShort5551 => replace_numbers_of_row(row, premultiplied_unsigned_short_5551),
        AlphaPremultiplication::UnsignedInt2101010Rev => {
            replace_numbers_of_row(row, premultiplied_unsigned_int_2_10_10_10_rev);
        }
    }
}

/// A number of `SIZE` bytes in the byte order of the platform, which is that of the typed arrays of script and that GL
/// unpacks.
trait NativeEndianNumber<const SIZE: usize>: Copy {
    fn from_bytes(bytes: [u8; SIZE]) -> Self;
    fn to_bytes(self) -> [u8; SIZE];
}

trait ColorComponent<const SIZE: usize>: NativeEndianNumber<SIZE> {
    fn multiplied_by_alpha(self, alpha: Self) -> Self;
}

macro_rules! native_endian_numbers {
    ($($number:ty),*) => {$(
        impl NativeEndianNumber<{ size_of::<$number>() }> for $number {
            fn from_bytes(bytes: [u8; size_of::<$number>()]) -> Self {
                Self::from_ne_bytes(bytes)
            }

            fn to_bytes(self) -> [u8; size_of::<$number>()] {
                self.to_ne_bytes()
            }
        }
    )*};
}

native_endian_numbers!(u8, i8, u16, i16, u32, i32, f32);

/// `color` and `alpha` count up to `maximum`, which stands for 1.
fn product_of_unsigned_normalized(color: u64, alpha: u64, maximum: u64) -> u64 {
    (color * alpha + maximum / 2) / maximum
}

/// `color` and `alpha` count from `-maximum` to `maximum`, which stand for -1 and 1. The one number below `-maximum`
/// stands for -1 as well.
fn product_of_signed_normalized(color: i64, alpha: i64, maximum: i64) -> i64 {
    let product = color.max(-maximum) * alpha.max(-maximum);
    let magnitude = (product.abs() + maximum / 2) / maximum;
    magnitude * product.signum()
}

macro_rules! unsigned_normalized_color_components {
    ($($number:ty),*) => {$(
        impl ColorComponent<{ size_of::<$number>() }> for $number {
            fn multiplied_by_alpha(self, alpha: Self) -> Self {
                let product = product_of_unsigned_normalized(self.into(), alpha.into(), Self::MAX.into());
                Self::try_from(product).expect("a product of two numbers up to 1 is up to 1")
            }
        }
    )*};
}

macro_rules! signed_normalized_color_components {
    ($($number:ty),*) => {$(
        impl ColorComponent<{ size_of::<$number>() }> for $number {
            fn multiplied_by_alpha(self, alpha: Self) -> Self {
                let product = product_of_signed_normalized(self.into(), alpha.into(), Self::MAX.into());
                Self::try_from(product).expect("a product of two numbers from -1 to 1 is from -1 to 1")
            }
        }
    )*};
}

// NB: An integer format has no range that stands for 1, so its alpha is premultiplied as though it were normalized.
unsigned_normalized_color_components!(u8, u16, u32);
signed_normalized_color_components!(i8, i16, i32);

impl ColorComponent<4> for f32 {
    fn multiplied_by_alpha(self, alpha: Self) -> Self {
        self * alpha
    }
}

const F32_SIGN_BIT: u32 = 0x8000_0000;
const F32_EXPONENT_BIAS: u32 = 127;
const F32_MANTISSA_BITS: u32 = 23;
const F32_INFINITY_BITS: u32 = 0x7f80_0000;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct HalfFloat(u16);

impl NativeEndianNumber<2> for HalfFloat {
    fn from_bytes(bytes: [u8; 2]) -> Self {
        Self(u16::from_ne_bytes(bytes))
    }

    fn to_bytes(self) -> [u8; 2] {
        self.0.to_ne_bytes()
    }
}

impl ColorComponent<2> for HalfFloat {
    fn multiplied_by_alpha(self, alpha: Self) -> Self {
        // NB: The product of two half floats is exact in an f32, so it is rounded once.
        Self::from_f32(self.to_f32() * alpha.to_f32())
    }
}

impl HalfFloat {
    const SIGN_BIT: u16 = 0x8000;
    const EXPONENT_BIAS: u32 = 15;
    const MANTISSA_BITS: u32 = 10;
    const MANTISSA_MASK: u16 = 0x3ff;
    const MAXIMUM_EXPONENT: u32 = 0x1f;
    const INFINITY: u16 = 0x7c00;
    const QUIET_NAN: u16 = 0x7e00;

    fn to_f32(self) -> f32 {
        const SUBNORMAL_STEP: f32 = 1.0 / 16_777_216.0;
        let sign = u32::from(self.0 & Self::SIGN_BIT) << 16;
        let exponent = u32::from(self.0 >> Self::MANTISSA_BITS) & Self::MAXIMUM_EXPONENT;
        let mantissa = self.0 & Self::MANTISSA_MASK;
        let mantissa_of_f32 = u32::from(mantissa) << (F32_MANTISSA_BITS - Self::MANTISSA_BITS);
        let magnitude = match exponent {
            0 => (f32::from(mantissa) * SUBNORMAL_STEP).to_bits(),
            Self::MAXIMUM_EXPONENT => F32_INFINITY_BITS | mantissa_of_f32,
            _ => ((exponent + F32_EXPONENT_BIAS - Self::EXPONENT_BIAS) << F32_MANTISSA_BITS) | mantissa_of_f32,
        };
        f32::from_bits(sign | magnitude)
    }

    /// Rounds to the nearest half float, and to the one with an even mantissa between two.
    fn from_f32(value: f32) -> Self {
        const SMALLEST_MAGNITUDE_ABOVE_THE_RANGE: u32 = (F32_EXPONENT_BIAS + 16) << F32_MANTISSA_BITS;
        const SMALLEST_NORMAL_MAGNITUDE: u32 = (F32_EXPONENT_BIAS + 1 - HalfFloat::EXPONENT_BIAS) << F32_MANTISSA_BITS;
        // NB: The step between the f32s from this one to twice it is that of the subnormal half floats, so the f32
        //     addition rounds a subnormal magnitude to one of them.
        const SUBNORMAL_ROUNDING_ADDEND: u32 = (F32_EXPONENT_BIAS - 1) << F32_MANTISSA_BITS;
        const DROPPED_MANTISSA_BITS: u32 = F32_MANTISSA_BITS - HalfFloat::MANTISSA_BITS;

        let bits = value.to_bits();
        let sign = ((bits >> 16) as u16) & Self::SIGN_BIT;
        let magnitude = bits & !F32_SIGN_BIT;
        let half_magnitude = if magnitude >= SMALLEST_MAGNITUDE_ABOVE_THE_RANGE {
            if magnitude > F32_INFINITY_BITS {
                Self::QUIET_NAN
            } else {
                Self::INFINITY
            }
        } else if magnitude < SMALLEST_NORMAL_MAGNITUDE {
            let sum = f32::from_bits(magnitude) + f32::from_bits(SUBNORMAL_ROUNDING_ADDEND);
            (sum.to_bits() - SUBNORMAL_ROUNDING_ADDEND) as u16
        } else {
            let mantissa_is_odd = (magnitude >> DROPPED_MANTISSA_BITS) & 1;
            let rebiased = magnitude - ((F32_EXPONENT_BIAS - Self::EXPONENT_BIAS) << F32_MANTISSA_BITS);
            // NB: A carry out of the mantissa increments the exponent, up to that of infinity.
            let rounded = rebiased + (1 << (DROPPED_MANTISSA_BITS - 1)) - 1 + mantissa_is_odd;
            (rounded >> DROPPED_MANTISSA_BITS) as u16
        };
        Self(sign | half_magnitude)
    }
}

fn premultiply_components_before_alpha<const SIZE: usize, C: ColorComponent<SIZE>>(
    row: &mut [u8],
    bytes_per_pixel: usize,
) {
    for pixel in row.chunks_exact_mut(bytes_per_pixel) {
        let Some((alpha, colors)) = pixel.as_chunks_mut::<SIZE>().0.split_last_mut() else {
            continue;
        };
        let alpha = C::from_bytes(*alpha);
        for color in colors {
            *color = C::from_bytes(*color).multiplied_by_alpha(alpha).to_bytes();
        }
    }
}

fn replace_numbers_of_row<const SIZE: usize, N: NativeEndianNumber<SIZE>>(
    row: &mut [u8],
    replacement: impl Fn(N) -> N,
) {
    for number in row.as_chunks_mut::<SIZE>().0 {
        *number = replacement(N::from_bytes(*number)).to_bytes();
    }
}

/// Red, green, blue and alpha from the most significant bits on.
fn premultiplied_unsigned_short_4444(texel: u16) -> u16 {
    let alpha = u64::from(texel & 0xf);
    let premultiplied = |shift: u32| {
        let color = u64::from((texel >> shift) & 0xf);
        (product_of_unsigned_normalized(color, alpha, 0xf) as u16) << shift
    };
    premultiplied(12) | premultiplied(8) | premultiplied(4) | (texel & 0xf)
}

/// Red, green and blue in five bits each and alpha in the least significant bit.
fn premultiplied_unsigned_short_5551(texel: u16) -> u16 {
    if texel & 1 == 0 { 0 } else { texel }
}

/// Red, green and blue in ten bits each and alpha in the two most significant bits, from the least significant bits on.
fn premultiplied_unsigned_int_2_10_10_10_rev(texel: u32) -> u32 {
    let alpha = u64::from(texel >> 30);
    let premultiplied = |shift: u32| {
        let color = u64::from((texel >> shift) & 0x3ff);
        (product_of_unsigned_normalized(color, alpha, 0b11) as u32) << shift
    };
    premultiplied(0) | premultiplied(10) | premultiplied(20) | (texel & 0xc000_0000)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::web_gl::constants::GL_DEPTH_STENCIL;

    fn image(width: i32, height: i32, format: u32, r#type: u32) -> ImageUnpackConversion {
        ImageUnpackConversion {
            width,
            height,
            format,
            r#type,
            unpack_state: PixelUnpackState {
                alignment: 1,
                ..PixelUnpackState::default()
            },
            flip_y: false,
            premultiply_alpha: false,
        }
    }

    fn flipped(image: ImageUnpackConversion) -> ImageUnpackConversion {
        ImageUnpackConversion { flip_y: true, ..image }
    }

    fn premultiplied(image: ImageUnpackConversion) -> ImageUnpackConversion {
        ImageUnpackConversion {
            premultiply_alpha: true,
            ..image
        }
    }

    fn with_unpack_state(image: ImageUnpackConversion, unpack_state: PixelUnpackState) -> ImageUnpackConversion {
        ImageUnpackConversion { unpack_state, ..image }
    }

    fn converted(image: ImageUnpackConversion, bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut bytes = bytes.to_vec();
        image.convert(&mut bytes);
        bytes
    }

    fn converted_numbers<const SIZE: usize, N: NativeEndianNumber<SIZE>>(
        image: ImageUnpackConversion,
        numbers: &[N],
    ) -> Vec<N> {
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = numbers.iter().flat_map(|number| number.to_bytes()).collect();
        let converted_bytes = converted(image, &bytes);
        converted_bytes
            .as_chunks::<SIZE>()
            .0
            .iter()
            .map(|bytes| N::from_bytes(*bytes))
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_rows_of_an_image_follow_the_pixel_unpack_state() {
        let rows = |width, height, bytes_per_pixel, unpack_state| {
            let image = with_unpack_state(image(width, height, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE), unpack_state);
            ImageRows::new(&image, bytes_per_pixel)
        };
        let unpack_state = |alignment, row_length, skip_pixels, skip_rows| PixelUnpackState {
            alignment,
            row_length,
            skip_pixels,
            skip_rows,
        };

        assert_eq!(
            rows(3, 2, 3, unpack_state(4, 0, 0, 0)),
            Some(ImageRows {
                start_of_first_row: 0,
                stride: 12,
                byte_length: 9,
                count: 2,
                end: 21,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(rows(3, 2, 3, unpack_state(1, 0, 0, 0)).unwrap().stride, 9);
        assert_eq!(rows(3, 2, 3, unpack_state(8, 0, 0, 0)).unwrap().stride, 16);
        assert_eq!(rows(3, 2, 4, unpack_state(8, 0, 0, 0)).unwrap().stride, 16);
        assert_eq!(
            rows(2, 3, 4, unpack_state(4, 5, 2, 1)),
            Some(ImageRows {
                start_of_first_row: 28,
                stride: 20,
                byte_length: 8,
                count: 3,
                end: 76,
            })
        );

        assert_eq!(rows(0, 2, 4, unpack_state(4, 0, 0, 0)), None);
        assert_eq!(rows(2, 0, 4, unpack_state(4, 0, 0, 0)), None);
        assert_eq!(rows(-1, 2, 4, unpack_state(4, 0, 0, 0)), None);
        assert_eq!(rows(3, 2, 4, unpack_state(4, 2, 0, 0)), None);
        assert_eq!(rows(2, 2, 4, unpack_state(0, 0, 0, 0)), None);
        assert_eq!(rows(2, 2, 4, unpack_state(4, 0, 0, usize::MAX)), None);
        assert_eq!(rows(2, 2, 4, unpack_state(4, 0, usize::MAX, 0)), None);
        assert_eq!(rows(i32::MAX, i32::MAX, 8, unpack_state(8, usize::MAX / 8, 0, 0)), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn flipping_swaps_the_pixels_of_rows_and_keeps_padding_and_skipped_bytes() {
        let rgb = image(2, 3, GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE);
        let aligned_to_four = with_unpack_state(rgb, PixelUnpackState::default());
        #[rustfmt::skip]
        let bytes = [
            1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 0xa0, 0xa1,
            7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 0xa2, 0xa3,
            13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18,
        ];
        #[rustfmt::skip]
        let expected = [
            13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 0xa0, 0xa1,
            7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 0xa2, 0xa3,
            1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6,
        ];
        assert_eq!(converted(flipped(aligned_to_four), &bytes), expected);
        assert_eq!(converted(premultiplied(aligned_to_four), &bytes), bytes);
        assert_eq!(converted(aligned_to_four, &bytes), bytes);

        let one_byte_pixels = image(1, 4, GL_ALPHA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE);
        assert_eq!(converted(flipped(one_byte_pixels), &[1, 2, 3, 4]), [4, 3, 2, 1]);
        assert_eq!(
            converted(flipped(image(4, 1, GL_ALPHA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE)), &[1, 2, 3, 4]),
            [1, 2, 3, 4]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn flipping_and_premultiplying_leave_the_pixels_around_a_sub_image_as_they_are() {
        let sub_image = with_unpack_state(
            image(2, 2, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE),
            PixelUnpackState {
                alignment: 4,
                row_length: 3,
                skip_pixels: 1,
                skip_rows: 1,
            },
        );
        let outside = [9, 9, 9, 0];
        let transparent = [255, 255, 255, 0];
        let one_fifth_opaque = [200, 100, 50, 51];
        let opaque = [10, 20, 30, 255];
        let bytes = [
            outside,
            outside,
            outside,
            outside,
            one_fifth_opaque,
            transparent,
            outside,
            opaque,
            opaque,
        ]
        .concat();
        let expected = [
            outside,
            outside,
            outside,
            outside,
            opaque,
            opaque,
            outside,
            [40, 20, 10, 51],
            [0, 0, 0, 0],
        ]
        .concat();
        assert_eq!(converted(flipped(premultiplied(sub_image)), &bytes), expected);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bytes_that_do_not_hold_the_whole_image_are_left_as_they_are() {
        let rgba = flipped(premultiplied(image(1, 2, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE)));
        let too_few_bytes = [255, 255, 255, 0, 1, 2, 3];
        assert_eq!(converted(rgba, &too_few_bytes), too_few_bytes);

        let more_bytes = [255, 255, 255, 0, 1, 2, 3, 255, 7];
        assert_eq!(converted(rgba, &more_bytes), [1, 2, 3, 255, 0, 0, 0, 0, 7]);

        let unknown_type = flipped(image(1, 2, GL_RGBA, 0x1234));
        assert_eq!(converted(unknown_type, &[1, 2]), [1, 2]);
        let unknown_format = flipped(image(1, 2, 0x1234, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE));
        assert_eq!(converted(unknown_format, &[1, 2]), [1, 2]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unsigned_bytes_are_premultiplied_where_the_format_has_alpha() {
        let premultiplied_pixel =
            |format, pixel: &[u8]| converted(premultiplied(image(1, 1, format, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE)), pixel);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_pixel(GL_RGBA, &[200, 100, 50, 51]), [40, 20, 10, 51]);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_pixel(GL_RGBA, &[255, 255, 255, 0]), [0, 0, 0, 0]);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_pixel(GL_RGBA, &[1, 128, 255, 255]), [1, 128, 255, 255]);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_pixel(GL_RGBA, &[255, 1, 3, 128]), [128, 1, 2, 128]);
        assert_eq!(
            premultiplied_pixel(GL_RGBA_INTEGER, &[200, 100, 50, 51]),
            [40, 20, 10, 51]
        );
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_pixel(GL_LUMINANCE_ALPHA, &[200, 51]), [40, 51]);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_pixel(GL_ALPHA, &[51]), [51]);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_pixel(GL_RGB, &[200, 100, 51]), [200, 100, 51]);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_pixel(GL_RG, &[200, 51]), [200, 51]);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_pixel(GL_LUMINANCE, &[51]), [51]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn wider_and_signed_components_are_premultiplied_as_normalized_numbers() {
        let rgba = |r#type| premultiplied(image(1, 1, GL_RGBA, r#type));
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<2, u16>(rgba(GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT), &[65535, 1000, 3, 13107]),
            [13107, 200, 1, 13107]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<4, u32>(rgba(GL_UNSIGNED_INT), &[u32::MAX, 1000, 0, u32::MAX / 5]),
            [u32::MAX / 5, 200, 0, u32::MAX / 5]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<1, i8>(rgba(GL_BYTE), &[127, -127, -128, 64]),
            [64, -64, -64, 64]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<1, i8>(rgba(GL_BYTE), &[100, -100, 0, -127]),
            [-100, 100, 0, -127]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<2, i16>(rgba(GL_SHORT), &[32767, -32767, 1000, 6553]),
            [6553, -6553, 200, 6553]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<4, i32>(rgba(GL_INT), &[i32::MAX, i32::MIN, 1000, i32::MAX / 5]),
            [i32::MAX / 5, -(i32::MAX / 5), 200, i32::MAX / 5]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<2, u16>(
                premultiplied(image(1, 1, GL_RGBA_INTEGER, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT)),
                &[65535, 0, 0, 0]
            ),
            [0, 0, 0, 0]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn floats_are_premultiplied_by_multiplication() {
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<4, f32>(premultiplied(image(1, 1, GL_RGBA, GL_FLOAT)), &[1.0, 0.5, -2.0, 0.25]),
            [0.25, 0.125, -0.5, 0.25]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<4, f32>(premultiplied(image(1, 1, GL_LUMINANCE_ALPHA, GL_FLOAT)), &[0.75, 0.5]),
            [0.375, 0.5]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<4, f32>(premultiplied(image(1, 1, GL_RGB, GL_FLOAT)), &[0.75, 0.5, 0.25]),
            [0.75, 0.5, 0.25]
        );

        let one = 0x3c00;
        let half = 0x3800;
        let quarter = 0x3400;
        let three_quarters = 0x3a00;
        let three_sixteenths = 0x3200;
        let eighth = 0x3000;
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<2, u16>(
                premultiplied(image(1, 1, GL_RGBA, GL_HALF_FLOAT)),
                &[one, three_quarters, half, quarter]
            ),
            [quarter, three_sixteenths, eighth, quarter]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<2, u16>(
                premultiplied(image(1, 1, GL_LUMINANCE_ALPHA, GL_HALF_FLOAT)),
                &[one, half]
            ),
            [half, half]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn half_floats_convert_to_and_from_f32s() {
        let to_f32 = |bits| HalfFloat(bits).to_f32();
        assert_eq!(to_f32(0x0000).to_bits(), 0.0f32.to_bits());
        assert_eq!(to_f32(0x8000).to_bits(), (-0.0f32).to_bits());
        assert_eq!(to_f32(0x3c00), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(to_f32(0xc000), -2.0);
        assert_eq!(to_f32(0x7bff), 65504.0);
        assert_eq!(to_f32(0x0400), 1.0 / 16384.0);
        assert_eq!(to_f32(0x0001), 1.0 / 16_777_216.0);
        assert_eq!(to_f32(0x03ff), 1023.0 / 16_777_216.0);
        assert_eq!(to_f32(0x7c00), f32::INFINITY);
        assert_eq!(to_f32(0xfc00), f32::NEG_INFINITY);
        assert!(to_f32(0x7e00).is_nan());

        let from_f32 = |value| HalfFloat::from_f32(value).0;
        assert_eq!(from_f32(0.0), 0x0000);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(-0.0), 0x8000);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(1.0), 0x3c00);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(-2.0), 0xc000);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(65504.0), 0x7bff);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(65519.0), 0x7bff);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(65520.0), 0x7c00);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(1.0e10), 0x7c00);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(f32::INFINITY), 0x7c00);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(f32::NEG_INFINITY), 0xfc00);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(f32::NAN) & 0x7e00, 0x7e00);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(1.0 / 16384.0), 0x0400);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(1.0 / 16_777_216.0), 0x0001);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(1.0 / 33_554_432.0), 0x0000);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(3.0 / 33_554_432.0), 0x0002);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(1.0 / 1.0e10), 0x0000);
        // Between two half floats, the one with the even mantissa.
        assert_eq!(from_f32(1.0 + 1.0 / 2048.0), 0x3c00);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(1.0 + 3.0 / 2048.0), 0x3c02);
        assert_eq!(from_f32(1.0 + 1.0 / 2048.0 + 1.0 / 65536.0), 0x3c01);

        for bits in (0..=0xffff_u16).filter(|&bits| !HalfFloat(bits).to_f32().is_nan()) {
            assert_eq!(from_f32(to_f32(bits)), bits);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn packed_texels_are_premultiplied_by_their_alpha_bits() {
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_unsigned_short_4444(0xfa56), 0x6426);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_unsigned_short_4444(0xfff0), 0x0000);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_unsigned_short_4444(0x123f), 0x123f);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_unsigned_short_4444(0xf008), 0x8008);

        assert_eq!(premultiplied_unsigned_short_5551(0xfc01), 0xfc01);
        assert_eq!(premultiplied_unsigned_short_5551(0xfffe), 0x0000);

        let texel = |red: u32, green: u32, blue: u32, alpha: u32| (alpha << 30) | (blue << 20) | (green << 10) | red;
        assert_eq!(
            premultiplied_unsigned_int_2_10_10_10_rev(texel(1023, 300, 0, 2)),
            texel(682, 200, 0, 2)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            premultiplied_unsigned_int_2_10_10_10_rev(texel(1023, 1023, 1023, 0)),
            texel(0, 0, 0, 0)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            premultiplied_unsigned_int_2_10_10_10_rev(texel(5, 6, 7, 3)),
            texel(5, 6, 7, 3)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            premultiplied_unsigned_int_2_10_10_10_rev(texel(1000, 2, 1, 1)),
            texel(333, 1, 0, 1)
        );

        let premultiplied_texels = |format, r#type, texels: &[u16]| {
            converted_numbers(premultiplied(image(texels.len() as i32, 1, format, r#type)), texels)
        };
        assert_eq!(
            premultiplied_texels(GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_4_4_4_4, &[0xfa56, 0xfff0]),
            [0x6426, 0x0000]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            premultiplied_texels(GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_5_5_1, &[0xfc01, 0xfffe]),
            [0xfc01, 0x0000]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            premultiplied_texels(GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_6_5, &[0xfffe, 0x0000]),
            [0xfffe, 0x0000]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<4, u32>(
                premultiplied(image(1, 1, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_INT_2_10_10_10_REV)),
                &[texel(1023, 300, 0, 2)]
            ),
            [texel(682, 200, 0, 2)]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            converted_numbers::<4, u32>(
                premultiplied(image(1, 1, GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_INT_10F_11F_11F_REV)),
                &[texel(1023, 300, 0, 2)]
            ),
            [texel(1023, 300, 0, 2)]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_texel_layout_takes_as_many_bytes_as_gl_unpacks() {
        let bytes_per_pixel = |format, r#type| texel_layout(format, r#type).map(|layout| layout.bytes_per_pixel);
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_LUMINANCE_ALPHA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_LUMINANCE, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE), Some(1));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_ALPHA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE), Some(1));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_4_4_4_4), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_5_5_1), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_6_5), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGBA, GL_FLOAT), Some(16));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_LUMINANCE_ALPHA, GL_HALF_FLOAT), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGBA_INTEGER, GL_UNSIGNED_INT), Some(16));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGB_INTEGER, GL_SHORT), Some(6));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RG, GL_HALF_FLOAT), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RG_INTEGER, GL_INT), Some(8));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RED, GL_BYTE), Some(1));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RED_INTEGER, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_INT_2_10_10_10_REV), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_INT_10F_11F_11F_REV), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_INT_5_9_9_9_REV), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT, GL_UNSIGNED_INT), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT, GL_FLOAT), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_DEPTH_STENCIL, GL_UNSIGNED_INT_24_8), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(
            bytes_per_pixel(GL_DEPTH_STENCIL, GL_FLOAT_32_UNSIGNED_INT_24_8_REV),
            Some(8)
        );
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(GL_RGBA, 0x1234), None);
        assert_eq!(bytes_per_pixel(0x1234, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_size_of_an_image_follows_from_its_dimensions() {
        let default = PixelUnpackState::default();
        assert_eq!(
            required_2d_texture_data_size(16, 16, GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, &default),
            Some(768)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            required_2d_texture_data_size(3, 2, GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, &default),
            Some(21)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            required_2d_texture_data_size(5, 2, GL_RGB, GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_6_5, &default),
            Some(22)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_size_of_an_image_includes_what_the_unpack_state_skips() {
        let unpack_state = PixelUnpackState {
            alignment: 8,
            row_length: 10,
            skip_pixels: 2,
            skip_rows: 3,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            required_2d_texture_data_size(4, 2, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, &unpack_state),
            Some(184)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_image_whose_rows_overlap_has_no_size() {
        let unpack_state = PixelUnpackState {
            row_length: 8,
            skip_pixels: 5,
            ..PixelUnpackState::default()
        };
        assert!(!is_valid_2d_pixel_unpack_state(4, &unpack_state));
        assert_eq!(
            required_2d_texture_data_size(4, 2, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, &unpack_state),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_image_whose_size_overflows_has_none() {
        for unpack_state in [
            PixelUnpackState {
                row_length: usize::MAX,
                skip_pixels: usize::MAX,
                ..PixelUnpackState::default()
            },
            PixelUnpackState {
                skip_rows: usize::MAX,
                ..PixelUnpackState::default()
            },
            PixelUnpackState {
                row_length: 2,
                skip_pixels: 1,
                skip_rows: usize::MAX / 8,
                ..PixelUnpackState::default()
            },
        ] {
            assert_eq!(
                required_2d_texture_data_size(1, 1, GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, &unpack_state),
                None
            );
        }
    }
}

//! The entry points of the recorder that are written by hand: the GL functions that GLFunctions.json marks as
//! custom, because their arguments do not serialize the way their signature suggests, and the commands that are no
//! GL functions.

use std::rc::Rc;

use libcompositing_rust::webgl::vocabulary::{commands, sync_calls};
use libcompositing_rust::webgl::wire::{DataSpan, InlineData, WireStruct, resolve_data_span};

use super::recorder::{Proxy, bytes_of_mut, copy_reply_data, until_nul};
use super::transport::{ReadPixelsResult, SharedMemory, Transport};
use crate::web_gl::constants::{GL_INVALID_VALUE, GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY};

fn pack_strings(strings: &[&[u8]]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut packed_strings = Vec::new();
    for string in strings {
        packed_strings.extend_from_slice(until_nul(string));
        packed_strings.push(0);
    }
    packed_strings
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct FrameUpload {
    /// `None` uploads the frame at its own size.
    pub(crate) destination_size: Option<(i32, i32)>,
    pub(crate) flip_y: bool,
    pub(crate) premultiply_alpha: bool,
}

impl FrameUpload {
    fn destination_width(self) -> i32 {
        self.destination_size.map_or(0, |(width, _)| width)
    }

    fn destination_height(self) -> i32 {
        self.destination_size.map_or(0, |(_, height)| height)
    }
}

impl<T: Transport> Proxy<T> {
    fn string_count(&self, strings: &[&[u8]]) -> Option<i32> {
        let count = i32::try_from(strings.len()).ok();
        if count.is_none() && !self.is_lost() {
            self.set_pending_local_error(GL_INVALID_VALUE);
        }
        count
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_size(&self, width: i32, height: i32) {
        self.record(&commands::SetDrawingBufferSize { width, height });
    }

    #[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the arguments of the GL function")]
    pub(crate) fn read_pixels_into_pixel_pack_buffer(
        &self,
        x: i32,
        y: i32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        offset: i64,
    ) {
        self.record(&commands::ReadPixelsIntoPixelPackBuffer {
            x,
            y,
            width,
            height,
            format,
            r#type,
            offset,
        });
    }

    #[expect(
        clippy::too_many_arguments,
        reason = "the arguments of the GL function, and the frame"
    )]
    pub(crate) fn tex_image2d_from_bitmap(
        &self,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        internalformat: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        frame: T::Frame,
        upload: FrameUpload,
    ) {
        if self.is_lost() {
            return;
        }
        let bitmap_index = self.append_pending_frame(frame);
        self.record(&commands::TexImage2DFromBitmap {
            target,
            level,
            internalformat,
            format,
            r#type,
            bitmap_index,
            has_explicit_destination_size: upload.destination_size.is_some(),
            destination_width: upload.destination_width(),
            destination_height: upload.destination_height(),
            flip_y: upload.flip_y,
            premultiply_alpha: upload.premultiply_alpha,
            ..commands::TexImage2DFromBitmap::ZEROED
        });
    }

    #[expect(
        clippy::too_many_arguments,
        reason = "the arguments of the GL function, and the frame"
    )]
    pub(crate) fn tex_sub_image2d_from_bitmap(
        &self,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        xoffset: i32,
        yoffset: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        frame: T::Frame,
        upload: FrameUpload,
    ) {
        if self.is_lost() {
            return;
        }
        let bitmap_index = self.append_pending_frame(frame);
        self.record(&commands::TexSubImage2DFromBitmap {
            target,
            level,
            xoffset,
            yoffset,
            format,
            r#type,
            bitmap_index,
            has_explicit_destination_size: upload.destination_size.is_some(),
            destination_width: upload.destination_width(),
            destination_height: upload.destination_height(),
            flip_y: upload.flip_y,
            premultiply_alpha: upload.premultiply_alpha,
            ..commands::TexSubImage2DFromBitmap::ZEROED
        });
    }

    #[expect(
        clippy::too_many_arguments,
        reason = "the arguments of the GL function, and the frame"
    )]
    pub(crate) fn tex_image3d_from_bitmap(
        &self,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        internalformat: i32,
        depth: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        frame: T::Frame,
        upload: FrameUpload,
    ) {
        if self.is_lost() {
            return;
        }
        let bitmap_index = self.append_pending_frame(frame);
        self.record(&commands::TexImage3DFromBitmap {
            target,
            level,
            internalformat,
            depth,
            format,
            r#type,
            bitmap_index,
            has_explicit_destination_size: upload.destination_size.is_some(),
            destination_width: upload.destination_width(),
            destination_height: upload.destination_height(),
            flip_y: upload.flip_y,
            premultiply_alpha: upload.premultiply_alpha,
            ..commands::TexImage3DFromBitmap::ZEROED
        });
    }

    #[expect(
        clippy::too_many_arguments,
        reason = "the arguments of the GL function, and the frame"
    )]
    pub(crate) fn tex_sub_image3d_from_bitmap(
        &self,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        xoffset: i32,
        yoffset: i32,
        zoffset: i32,
        depth: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        frame: T::Frame,
        upload: FrameUpload,
    ) {
        if self.is_lost() {
            return;
        }
        let bitmap_index = self.append_pending_frame(frame);
        self.record(&commands::TexSubImage3DFromBitmap {
            target,
            level,
            xoffset,
            yoffset,
            zoffset,
            depth,
            format,
            r#type,
            bitmap_index,
            has_explicit_destination_size: upload.destination_size.is_some(),
            destination_width: upload.destination_width(),
            destination_height: upload.destination_height(),
            flip_y: upload.flip_y,
            premultiply_alpha: upload.premultiply_alpha,
            ..commands::TexSubImage3DFromBitmap::ZEROED
        });
    }

    /// The source is all of `source`, whatever it contains.
    pub(crate) fn shader_source(&self, shader: u32, source: &[u8]) {
        let source_data = InlineData::NulTerminated(source);
        self.record_with_data(
            &commands::ShaderSource {
                shader,
                source: DataSpan::following::<commands::ShaderSource>(source_data),
            },
            source_data,
        );
    }

    pub(crate) fn transform_feedback_varyings(&self, program: u32, varyings: &[&[u8]], buffer_mode: u32) {
        let Some(count) = self.string_count(varyings) else {
            return;
        };
        let packed_varyings = pack_strings(varyings);
        let varyings_data = InlineData::Bytes(&packed_varyings);
        self.record_with_data(
            &commands::TransformFeedbackVaryings {
                program,
                count,
                varyings: DataSpan::following::<commands::TransformFeedbackVaryings>(varyings_data),
                buffer_mode,
            },
            varyings_data,
        );
    }

    /// Leaves `uniform_indices` as it is when the context is lost or has an error for the names.
    pub(crate) fn get_uniform_indices(&self, program: u32, uniform_names: &[&[u8]], uniform_indices: &mut [u32]) {
        assert!(uniform_indices.len() >= uniform_names.len());
        let Some(uniform_count) = self.string_count(uniform_names) else {
            return;
        };
        let packed_names = pack_strings(uniform_names);
        let names_data = InlineData::Bytes(&packed_names);
        let request = sync_calls::GetUniformIndicesRequest {
            program,
            uniform_count,
            uniform_names: DataSpan::following::<sync_calls::GetUniformIndicesRequest>(names_data),
        };
        self.sync_call(&request, names_data, |reply, reply_bytes| {
            copy_reply_data(
                reply_bytes,
                reply.uniform_indices,
                bytes_of_mut(&mut uniform_indices[..uniform_names.len()]),
            );
        });
    }

    /// Without the NUL that ends it, and empty when the context is lost.
    pub(crate) fn get_string(&self, name: u32) -> Rc<[u8]> {
        if let Some(string) = self.cached_string(name) {
            return string;
        }
        let request = sync_calls::GetStringRequest { name };
        let string = self.sync_call(&request, InlineData::NONE, |reply, reply_bytes| {
            let string = resolve_data_span(reply_bytes, reply.value);
            assert!(
                string.last() == Some(&0),
                "the replayer ends the string that it returns with a NUL"
            );
            Rc::<[u8]>::from(until_nul(string))
        });
        match string {
            Some(string) => {
                self.cache_string(name, Rc::clone(&string));
                string
            }
            None => Rc::from([]),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_vertex_attrib_pointerv_robust_angle(&self, index: u32, pname: u32) -> i64 {
        let request = sync_calls::GetVertexAttribPointervRobustANGLERequest { index, pname };
        self.sync_call(&request, InlineData::NONE, |reply, _| reply.pointer)
            .unwrap_or(0)
    }

    /// `use_pixels` does not run when the context is lost or when there is no memory to read into, which is a GL
    /// error of the context.
    #[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the arguments of the GL function")]
    pub(crate) fn read_pixels_robust_angle(
        &self,
        x: i32,
        y: i32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        buf_size: i32,
        use_pixels: impl FnOnce(ReadPixelsResult, &[u8]),
    ) {
        if self.is_lost() {
            return;
        }
        let transport = self.transport();
        let shared_pixels = match usize::try_from(buf_size) {
            Ok(size) if size > 0 => {
                let Some(shared_pixels) = transport.create_shared_memory(size) else {
                    self.set_pending_local_error(GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY);
                    return;
                };
                Some(shared_pixels)
            }
            _ => None,
        };

        self.flush_commands();
        let result =
            transport.read_pixels_robust_angle(x, y, width, height, format, r#type, buf_size, shared_pixels.as_ref());
        if self.is_lost() {
            return;
        }
        let pixels = match (&shared_pixels, usize::try_from(result.length)) {
            (Some(shared_pixels), Ok(length)) if length > 0 => {
                assert!(
                    length <= shared_pixels.len(),
                    "the replayer reads no more pixels than it has room for"
                );
                // SAFETY: The memory is mapped and at least `length` bytes long, and the replayer, which is the only
                //         other user of it, has answered the call and does not write to it any more.
                unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(shared_pixels.as_ptr(), length) }
            }
            _ => &[],
        };
        use_pixels(result, pixels);
    }

    /// False when the context is lost, when the replayer refuses, or when there is no memory to read into, which is a
    /// GL error of the context.
    pub(crate) fn read_buffer_sub_data(
        &self,
        target: u32,
        offset: i64,
        size: usize,
        use_data: impl FnOnce(&[u8]),
    ) -> bool {
        if self.is_lost() {
            return false;
        }
        if size == 0 {
            return true;
        }
        let Ok(size_for_replayer) = i64::try_from(size) else {
            self.set_pending_local_error(GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY);
            return false;
        };
        let transport = self.transport();
        let Some(shared_data) = transport.create_shared_memory(size) else {
            self.set_pending_local_error(GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY);
            return false;
        };

        self.flush_commands();
        if !transport.read_buffer_sub_data(target, offset, size_for_replayer, &shared_data) {
            return false;
        }
        if self.is_lost() {
            return false;
        }
        assert!(size <= shared_data.len());
        // SAFETY: The memory is mapped and at least `size` bytes long, and the replayer, which is the only other
        //         user of it, has answered the call and does not write to it any more.
        use_data(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(shared_data.as_ptr(), size) });
        true
    }
}

/*

//! The recorder of one WebGL context: it takes the place of GL for the implementation of the context, writes what
//! is asked of it as records into a buffer that it shares with the replayer, and publishes them in batches. A call
//! that returns something is a synchronous round trip, which everything recorded before it is flushed for.

use core::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
use core::ptr;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::rc::Rc;

use libcompositing_rust::webgl::vocabulary::{CommandType, MAX_COMMAND_STRUCT_SIZE};
use libcompositing_rust::webgl::wire::{
    Command, DataSpan, HEADER_SIZE, InlineData, Record, SyncReply, SyncRequest, encode_sync_request,
    padded_record_size, resolve_data_span,
};
use libcompositing_rust::webgl::{DEFAULT_SHARED_DATA_REGION_CAPACITY, SHARED_DATA_REGION_OFFSET};

use super::transport::{SharedMemory, Transport};
use crate::web_gl::constants::GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY;

pub(crate) const MAX_PENDING_COMMAND_BYTES: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;

/// Each frame that waits for a flush holds the descriptor of its pixels.
pub(crate) const MAX_PENDING_FRAMES: usize = 64;

/// What is kept free in the region of records for the command that names a frame, before the frame is added to the
/// pending ones. Making room only when the command is recorded could flush in between, and that flush would publish
/// the frame with the wrong batch.
const RESERVED_RECORD_SIZE_FOR_FRAME_COMMAND: usize = 256;
const _: () = assert!(HEADER_SIZE + MAX_COMMAND_STRUCT_SIZE <= RESERVED_RECORD_SIZE_FOR_FRAME_COMMAND);

pub(crate) struct Proxy<T: Transport> {
    transport: RefCell<Rc<T>>,
    lost: Cell<bool>,
    pending_local_error: Cell<u32>,
    next_object_id: Cell<u32>,

    // NB: A call of the transport can mark the context lost, which calls back into the recorder. So nothing below is
    //     borrowed across one: a number is in a Cell, and a vector is taken out of its Cell for as long as it is used.
    shared_command_buffer: RefCell<Option<T::SharedMemory>>,
    /// The start of the shared command buffer, which `shared_command_buffer` keeps mapped, or null without one.
    shared_command_buffer_start: Cell<*mut u8>,
    shared_data_capacity: Cell<usize>,
    wanted_shared_data_capacity: usize,
    shared_data_cursor: Cell<usize>,
    /// Where the records that are not published yet start.
    shared_data_flush_base: Cell<usize>,
    last_published_flush_sequence_number: Cell<u64>,

    /// The records of a context that could not get a shared command buffer.
    out_of_line_commands: Cell<Vec<u8>>,
    pending_frames: Cell<Vec<T::Frame>>,
    sync_request_bytes: Cell<Vec<u8>>,
    sync_reply_bytes: Cell<Vec<u8>>,
    /// By GL name. The strings do not change while a context lives.
    string_cache: RefCell<Vec<(u32, Rc<[u8]>)>>,

    transport_calls_are_deferred: Cell<bool>,
    deferred_record_count: Cell<usize>,
    deferred_flush_is_due: Cell<bool>,
    /// The record that had no room at the cursor while the calls of the transport that make room were deferred.
    deferred_record: Cell<Vec<u8>>,
    /// Memory made before the data of a record was borrowed, for a record that the region is too small for.
    memory_for_deferred_oversized_record: Cell<Option<T::SharedMemory>>,
    /// That memory, with the record written to it, and the size of the record.
    deferred_oversized_record: Cell<Option<(T::SharedMemory, usize)>>,
}

impl<T: Transport> Proxy<T> {
    pub(crate) fn new(transport: T) -> Self {
        Self::with_shared_data_capacity(transport, DEFAULT_SHARED_DATA_REGION_CAPACITY)
    }

    pub(super) fn with_shared_data_capacity(transport: T, shared_data_capacity: usize) -> Self {
        let proxy = Self {
            transport: RefCell::new(Rc::new(transport)),
            lost: Cell::new(false),
            pending_local_error: Cell::new(0),
            next_object_id: Cell::new(1),
            shared_command_buffer: RefCell::new(None),
            shared_command_buffer_start: Cell::new(ptr::null_mut()),
            shared_data_capacity: Cell::new(0),
            wanted_shared_data_capacity: shared_data_capacity,
            shared_data_cursor: Cell::new(0),
            shared_data_flush_base: Cell::new(0),
            last_published_flush_sequence_number: Cell::new(0),
            out_of_line_commands: Cell::new(Vec::new()),
            pending_frames: Cell::new(Vec::new()),
            sync_request_bytes: Cell::new(Vec::new()),
            sync_reply_bytes: Cell::new(Vec::new()),
            string_cache: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
            transport_calls_are_deferred: Cell::new(false),
            deferred_record_count: Cell::new(0),
            deferred_flush_is_due: Cell::new(false),
            deferred_record: Cell::new(Vec::new()),
            memory_for_deferred_oversized_record: Cell::new(None),
            deferred_oversized_record: Cell::new(None),
        };
        proxy.initialize_shared_command_buffer();
        proxy
    }

    /// Nothing that was recorded for the lost context reaches the new one.
    pub(crate) fn restore(&self, transport: T) {
        self.transport.replace(Rc::new(transport));
        self.lost.set(false);
        self.out_of_line_commands.take();
        self.pending_frames.take();
        self.string_cache.borrow_mut().clear();
        self.initialize_shared_command_buffer();
    }

    pub(super) fn transport(&self) -> Rc<T> {
        assert!(
            !self.transport_calls_are_deferred.get(),
            "the WebGL transport is not called while the data of a command is borrowed"
        );
        Rc::clone(&self.transport.borrow())
    }

    fn initialize_shared_command_buffer(&self) {
        self.shared_data_cursor.set(0);
        self.shared_data_flush_base.set(0);
        self.last_published_flush_sequence_number.set(0);

        let transport = self.transport();
        let buffer = transport.create_shared_memory(SHARED_DATA_REGION_OFFSET + self.wanted_shared_data_capacity);
        match &buffer {
            Some(buffer) => {
                assert!(buffer.len() > SHARED_DATA_REGION_OFFSET);
                assert!(buffer.as_ptr().cast::<AtomicU64>().is_aligned());
                transport.set_shared_command_buffer(buffer);
                self.shared_command_buffer_start.set(buffer.as_ptr());
                self.shared_data_capacity.set(buffer.len() - SHARED_DATA_REGION_OFFSET);
            }
            None => {
                self.shared_command_buffer_start.set(ptr::null_mut());
                self.shared_data_capacity.set(0);
            }
        }
        // NB: The pointer above is into the new buffer already, so the old one is not used once it is unmapped here.
        self.shared_command_buffer.replace(buffer);
    }

    fn has_shared_command_buffer(&self) -> bool {
        !self.shared_command_buffer_start.get().is_null()
    }

    fn executed_flush_sequence_number(&self) -> u64 {
        // SAFETY: Only called with a shared command buffer, which is mapped, larger than a u64 and aligned for one.
        //         The replayer writes the number as an atomic as well.
        unsafe { &*self.shared_command_buffer_start.get().cast::<AtomicU64>() }.load(Ordering::Acquire)
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_lost(&self) {
        self.lost.set(true);
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_lost(&self) -> bool {
        self.lost.get()
    }

    pub(crate) fn canvas_id(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        self.transport().canvas_id()
    }

    pub(super) fn allocate_object_id(&self) -> u32 {
        let id = self.next_object_id.get();
        self.next_object_id.set(id + 1);
        id
    }

    pub(super) fn set_pending_local_error(&self, error: u32) {
        if self.pending_local_error.get() == 0 {
            self.pending_local_error.set(error);
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn take_pending_local_error(&self) -> u32 {
        self.pending_local_error.replace(0)
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(super) fn record<C: Command>(&self, command: &C) {
        self.record_bytes(C::TYPE, command.as_bytes(), InlineData::NONE);
    }

    #[inline]
    pub(super) fn record_with_data<C: Command>(&self, command: &C, inline_data: InlineData<'_>) {
        self.record_bytes(C::TYPE, command.as_bytes(), inline_data);
    }

    fn record_bytes(&self, command_type: CommandType, payload: &[u8], inline_data: InlineData<'_>) {
        if self.lost.get() {
            return;
        }
        let transport_calls_are_deferred = self.transport_calls_are_deferred.get();
        if transport_calls_are_deferred {
            // NB: What is deferred runs once the record is made. After a second record it would run in the wrong
            //     order: a record that had no room after a record that was made after it.
            assert!(
                self.deferred_record_count.replace(1) == 0,
                "one command is recorded with borrowed data"
            );
        }
        let Some(record) = Record::new(command_type, payload, inline_data) else {
            self.set_pending_local_error(GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY);
            return;
        };

        if !self.has_shared_command_buffer() {
            let mut commands = self.out_of_line_commands.take();
            record.append_to(&mut commands);
            let flush_is_due = commands.len() >= MAX_PENDING_COMMAND_BYTES;
            self.out_of_line_commands.set(commands);
            if flush_is_due {
                self.flush_commands_or_defer();
            }
            return;
        }

        if transport_calls_are_deferred {
            self.rewind_shared_data_cursor_if_all_published_commands_executed();
            if record.size() > self.shared_data_capacity.get() - self.shared_data_cursor.get() {
                let memory = self
                    .memory_for_deferred_oversized_record
                    .take()
                    .filter(|memory| record.size() > self.shared_data_capacity.get() && record.size() <= memory.len());
                if let Some(memory) = memory {
                    // SAFETY: The memory has room for the record, and holds neither its payload nor its data.
                    unsafe { record.write_to(memory.as_ptr()) };
                    self.deferred_oversized_record.set(Some((memory, record.size())));
                    return;
                }
                self.deferred_record.set(record.encoded());
                return;
            }
        } else if record.size() > self.shared_data_capacity.get() {
            self.send_oversized_record(&record);
            return;
        } else {
            self.rewind_shared_data_cursor_if_all_published_commands_executed();
            self.ensure_shared_data_capacity(record.size());
            if self.lost.get() {
                return;
            }
        }

        // SAFETY: The destination has room for the record, which was just made sure of, and neither the payload nor
        //         the data is in the region of records.
        self.write_at_shared_data_cursor(record.size(), |destination| unsafe { record.write_to(destination) });
    }

    fn record_encoded(&self, record: &[u8]) {
        if self.lost.get() {
            return;
        }
        if record.len() > self.shared_data_capacity.get() {
            self.flush_commands();
            self.transport().send_commands(record, &[]);
            return;
        }
        self.rewind_shared_data_cursor_if_all_published_commands_executed();
        self.ensure_shared_data_capacity(record.len());
        if self.lost.get() {
            return;
        }
        // SAFETY: The destination has room for the record, which was just made sure of, and the record is not in
        //         the region of records.
        self.write_at_shared_data_cursor(record.len(), |destination| unsafe {
            ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(record.as_ptr(), destination, record.len());
        });
    }

    fn write_at_shared_data_cursor(&self, record_size: usize, write_record_to: impl FnOnce(*mut u8)) {
        let cursor = self.shared_data_cursor.get();
        assert!(record_size <= self.shared_data_capacity.get() - cursor);
        // SAFETY: The region of records is mapped and has the bytes from the cursor on. The replayer does not read
        //         the region past what was published.
        let destination = unsafe {
            self.shared_command_buffer_start
                .get()
                .add(SHARED_DATA_REGION_OFFSET + cursor)
        };
        write_record_to(destination);
        let cursor = cursor + record_size;
        self.shared_data_cursor.set(cursor);
        if cursor - self.shared_data_flush_base.get() >= MAX_PENDING_COMMAND_BYTES {
            self.flush_commands_or_defer();
        }
    }

    fn flush_commands_or_defer(&self) {
        if self.transport_calls_are_deferred.get() {
            self.deferred_flush_is_due.set(true);
        } else {
            self.flush_commands();
        }
    }

    fn send_oversized_record(&self, record: &Record<'_>) {
        self.flush_commands();
        let transport = self.transport();
        let Some(memory) = transport.create_shared_memory(record.size()) else {
            transport.send_commands(&record.encoded(), &[]);
            return;
        };
        // SAFETY: The memory has room for the record, and holds neither its payload nor its data.
        unsafe { record.write_to(memory.as_ptr()) };
        transport.send_commands_written_to(&memory, record.size(), &[]);
    }

    /// Runs `record`, which records one command with data that is borrowed from memory of script, without a call of
    /// the transport while it runs, as nothing else may run while the data is borrowed: the calls that the record
    /// needs are made before and after it.
    ///
    /// `data_size_hint` is how many bytes of data the command is expected to carry. Room for a record with as many is
    /// made before the data is borrowed. A record that there is no room for then, whatever the hint was, is copied,
    /// and the copy is put into the stream once the data is given back.
    pub(crate) fn record_with_borrowed_data<R>(&self, data_size_hint: usize, record: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R {
        if !self.lost.get() && self.has_shared_command_buffer() {
            // NB: Which command it is going to be is not known here, so room is made for the largest struct. A
            //     record that the region is too small for even with the smallest struct is sent on its own, and
            //     needs no room.
            let capacity = self.shared_data_capacity.get();
            let smallest_record_size = padded_record_size(1, data_size_hint);
            let largest_record_size = data_size_hint
                .checked_add(1)
                .and_then(|data_size| padded_record_size(MAX_COMMAND_STRUCT_SIZE, data_size));
            if let (Some(smallest_record_size), Some(largest_record_size)) = (smallest_record_size, largest_record_size)
            {
                if smallest_record_size <= capacity {
                    self.rewind_shared_data_cursor_if_all_published_commands_executed();
                    self.ensure_shared_data_capacity(largest_record_size.min(capacity));
                } else {
                    self.memory_for_deferred_oversized_record
                        .set(self.transport().create_shared_memory(largest_record_size));
                }
            }
        }

        assert!(!self.transport_calls_are_deferred.replace(true));
        self.deferred_record_count.set(0);
        let result = {
            let _deferral = EndOfDeferral(&self.transport_calls_are_deferred);
            record()
        };

        self.memory_for_deferred_oversized_record.take();
        if let Some((memory, size)) = self.deferred_oversized_record.take() {
            self.flush_commands();
            self.transport().send_commands_written_to(&memory, size, &[]);
        }
        let deferred_record = self.deferred_record.take();
        if !deferred_record.is_empty() {
            self.record_encoded(&deferred_record);
        }
        if self.deferred_flush_is_due.replace(false) {
            self.flush_commands();
        }
        result
    }

    fn rewind_shared_data_cursor_if_all_published_commands_executed(&self) {
        let cursor = self.shared_data_cursor.get();
        if cursor == 0 || cursor != self.shared_data_flush_base.get() {
            return;
        }
        if self.executed_flush_sequence_number() >= self.last_published_flush_sequence_number.get() {
            self.shared_data_cursor.set(0);
            self.shared_data_flush_base.set(0);
        }
    }

    /// When the region is full, everything in it is published and the recorder waits for the replayer to have
    /// executed it, which loses the context if the replayer never will.
    fn ensure_shared_data_capacity(&self, record_size: usize) {
        let capacity = self.shared_data_capacity.get();
        assert!(record_size <= capacity);
        if record_size <= capacity - self.shared_data_cursor.get() {
            return;
        }

        self.flush_commands();
        assert!(self.shared_data_cursor.get() == self.shared_data_flush_base.get());
        if self.executed_flush_sequence_number() < self.last_published_flush_sequence_number.get() {
            if !self.transport().wait_until_published_commands_executed() {
                self.set_lost();
                return;
            }
            assert!(self.executed_flush_sequence_number() >= self.last_published_flush_sequence_number.get());
        }
        self.shared_data_cursor.set(0);
        self.shared_data_flush_base.set(0);
    }

    pub(crate) fn flush_commands(&self) {
        if self.has_shared_command_buffer() {
            let cursor = self.shared_data_cursor.get();
            let flush_base = self.shared_data_flush_base.get();
            if cursor == flush_base {
                return;
            }
            let flush_sequence_number = self.last_published_flush_sequence_number.get() + 1;
            self.last_published_flush_sequence_number.set(flush_sequence_number);
            self.shared_data_flush_base.set(cursor);
            let frames = self.pending_frames.take();
            self.transport().send_commands_from_shared_buffer(
                flush_base as u64,
                (cursor - flush_base) as u64,
                flush_sequence_number,
                &frames,
            );
            self.keep_capacity_of_pending_frames(frames);
            return;
        }

        let mut commands = self.out_of_line_commands.take();
        if commands.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let frames = self.pending_frames.take();
        self.transport().send_commands(&commands, &frames);
        commands.clear();
        self.out_of_line_commands.set(commands);
        self.keep_capacity_of_pending_frames(frames);
    }

    fn keep_capacity_of_pending_frames(&self, mut sent_frames: Vec<T::Frame>) {
        sent_frames.clear();
        self.pending_frames.set(sent_frames);
    }

    /// Returns the index that the command which uses the frame names it by.
    pub(super) fn append_pending_frame(&self, frame: T::Frame) -> u32 {
        if self.with_pending_frames(|frames| frames.len()) >= MAX_PENDING_FRAMES {
            self.flush_commands();
        }
        if self.has_shared_command_buffer() {
            self.ensure_shared_data_capacity(RESERVED_RECORD_SIZE_FOR_FRAME_COMMAND);
        }
        self.with_pending_frames(|frames| {
            let frame_index = u32::try_from(frames.len()).expect("the frames of a message are fewer than 4 billion");
            frames.push(frame);
            frame_index
        })
    }

    fn with_pending_frames<O>(&self, use_frames: impl FnOnce(&mut Vec<T::Frame>) -> O) -> O {
        let mut frames = self.pending_frames.take();
        let output = use_frames(&mut frames);
        self.pending_frames.set(frames);
        output
    }

    /// `None` when the context is lost before or by the call, and when the stream cannot carry the request, which is
    /// a GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY error of the context.
    pub(super) fn sync_call<R: SyncRequest, O>(
        &self,
        request: &R,
        inline_data: InlineData<'_>,
        read_reply: impl FnOnce(R::Reply, &[u8]) -> O,
    ) -> Option<O> {
        if self.lost.get() {
            return None;
        }
        self.flush_commands();

        let mut request_bytes = self.sync_request_bytes.take();
        let mut reply_bytes = self.sync_reply_bytes.take();
        let output = if encode_sync_request(&mut request_bytes, request, inline_data) {
            reply_bytes.clear();
            self.transport().sync_call(&request_bytes, &mut reply_bytes);
            if reply_bytes.is_empty() {
                self.set_lost();
            }
            (!self.lost.get()).then(|| read_reply(R::Reply::from_reply_bytes(&reply_bytes), reply_bytes.as_slice()))
        } else {
            self.set_pending_local_error(GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY);
            None
        };
        self.sync_request_bytes.set(request_bytes);
        self.sync_reply_bytes.set(reply_bytes);
        output
    }

    pub(super) fn cached_string(&self, name: u32) -> Option<Rc<[u8]>> {
        let string_cache = self.string_cache.borrow();
        let (_, string) = string_cache.iter().find(|(cached_name, _)| *cached_name == name)?;
        Some(Rc::clone(string))
    }

    pub(super) fn cache_string(&self, name: u32, string: Rc<[u8]>) {
        self.string_cache.borrow_mut().push((name, string));
    }

    pub(crate) fn present_canvas_for_compositing(&self, preserve_drawing_buffer: bool) {
        self.flush_commands();
        self.transport().present_canvas(preserve_drawing_buffer);
    }

    pub(crate) fn clear_drawing_buffer(&self) {
        if self.lost.get() {
            return;
        }
        self.flush_commands();
        self.transport().clear_drawing_buffer();
    }

    pub(crate) fn read_back_drawing_buffer(
        &self,
        x: i32,
        y: i32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
    ) -> Option<T::DrawingBufferPixels> {
        if self.lost.get() {
            return None;
        }
        self.flush_commands();
        self.transport().read_back_drawing_buffer(x, y, width, height)
    }
}

/// Ends the deferral of the calls of the transport however the record ends, unwinding included.
struct EndOfDeferral<'a>(&'a Cell<bool>);

impl Drop for EndOfDeferral<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.0.set(false);
    }
}

impl<T: Transport> Drop for Proxy<T> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.transport().destroy_context();
    }
}

/// The product of the factors that GLFunctions.json gives for the size of a pointer argument.
pub(super) fn payload_size(factors: &[i64]) -> usize {
    factors
        .iter()
        .try_fold(1usize, |size, &factor| size.checked_mul(usize::try_from(factor).ok()?))
        .expect("the size of the data of a WebGL command is validated before the command is recorded")
}

pub(super) fn leading_bytes(bytes: &[u8], size: usize) -> &[u8] {
    bytes
        .get(..size)
        .expect("the data of a WebGL command is as large as the command says")
}

pub(super) fn leading_bytes_mut(bytes: &mut [u8], size: usize) -> &mut [u8] {
    bytes
        .get_mut(..size)
        .expect("the buffer for the output of a WebGL call is as large as the call says")
}

pub(super) fn gen_count(ids: &[u32]) -> i32 {
    i32::try_from(ids.len()).expect("the objects that one WebGL command creates are counted by a GLsizei")
}

/// The replayer ends a string at its first NUL.
pub(super) fn until_nul(string: &[u8]) -> &[u8] {
    let length = string.iter().position(|&byte| byte == 0).unwrap_or(string.len());
    &string[..length]
}

/// # Safety
///
/// The type has no padding, and every bit pattern is a value of it.
pub(crate) unsafe trait PlainNumber: Copy + 'static {}
// SAFETY: The types are primitive numbers.
unsafe impl PlainNumber for u8 {}
// SAFETY: As above.
unsafe impl PlainNumber for i32 {}
// SAFETY: As above.
unsafe impl PlainNumber for u32 {}
// SAFETY: As above.
unsafe impl PlainNumber for f32 {}
// SAFETY: As above.
unsafe impl PlainNumber for i64 {}

pub(crate) fn bytes_of<N: PlainNumber>(numbers: &[N]) -> &[u8] {
    // SAFETY: Per the contract of PlainNumber the numbers are their bytes, all of which are initialized.
    unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(numbers.as_ptr().cast::<u8>(), size_of_val(numbers)) }
}

pub(super) fn bytes_of_mut<N: PlainNumber>(numbers: &mut [N]) -> &mut [u8] {
    // SAFETY: Per the contract of PlainNumber the numbers are their bytes, and any bytes written are numbers.
    unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts_mut(numbers.as_mut_ptr().cast::<u8>(), size_of_val(numbers)) }
}

pub(super) fn copy_reply_data(reply: &[u8], span: DataSpan, destination: &mut [u8]) {
    let data = resolve_data_span(reply, span);
    assert!(
        data.len() <= destination.len(),
        "the replayer returns no more data than a WebGL call asks for"
    );
    destination[..data.len()].copy_from_slice(data);
}
