    pub(crate) fn create_query(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<WebGLQuery>> {
        let mut handle = [0];
        self.proxy.gen_queries(&mut handle);
        Ok(WebGLQuery::create(cx.vm(), self, handle[0]))
    }

    pub(crate) fn delete_query(&self, _: &mut CallContext, query: Option<Ref<WebGLQuery>>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(query) = query else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let Some(handle) = self.handle_for_deletion_of(query) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.proxy.delete_queries(1, &[handle]);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn active_query_binding(&self, target: u32) -> Option<&Binding<WebGLQuery>> {
        match target {
            GL_ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED => Some(&self.any_samples_passed),
            GL_ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED_CONSERVATIVE => Some(&self.any_samples_passed_conservative),
            GL_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_PRIMITIVES_WRITTEN => Some(&self.transform_feedback_primitives_written),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn begin_query(&self, _: &mut CallContext, target: u32, query: Ref<WebGLQuery>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(query_handle) = self.handle_of(query) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        if let Some(active_query_binding) = self.active_query_binding(target) {
            active_query_binding.set(Some(query));
        }
        self.proxy.begin_query(target, query_handle);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn end_query(&self, _: &mut CallContext, target: u32) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        if let Some(active_query_binding) = self.active_query_binding(target) {
            active_query_binding.set(None);
        }
        self.proxy.end_query(target);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_query(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        pname: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<WebGLQuery>>> {
        if pname != GL_CURRENT_QUERY {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_ENUM);
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let Some(active_query_binding) = self.active_query_binding(target) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_ENUM);
            return Ok(None);
        };
        Ok(active_query_binding.get())
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_query_parameter(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        query: Ref<WebGLQuery>,
        pname: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        let Some(query_handle) = self.handle_of(query) else {
            return Ok(Value::NULL);
        };
        let mut result = [0];
        self.proxy
            .get_query_objectuiv_robust_angle(query_handle, pname, 1, &mut result);
        let [result] = result;
        Ok(match pname {
            GL_QUERY_RESULT => Value::from_f64(f64::from(result)),
            GL_QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE => Value::from_bool(result == GL_TRUE),
            _ => Value::NULL,
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_sampler(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<WebGLSampler>> {
        let mut handle = [0];
        self.proxy.gen_samplers(&mut handle);
        Ok(WebGLSampler::create(cx.vm(), self, handle[0]))
    }

    pub(crate) fn delete_sampler(&self, _: &mut CallContext, sampler: Option<Ref<WebGLSampler>>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(sampler) = sampler else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let Some(handle) = self.handle_for_deletion_of(sampler) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.proxy.delete_samplers(1, &[handle]);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn bind_sampler(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        unit: u32,
        sampler: Option<Ref<WebGLSampler>>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let mut sampler_handle = 0;
        if let Some(sampler) = sampler {
            let Some(handle) = self.handle_of(sampler) else {
                return Ok(());
            };
            sampler_handle = handle;
        }
        self.proxy.bind_sampler(unit, sampler_handle);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn is_sampler_parameter_name(&self, pname: u32) -> bool {
        match pname {
            GL_TEXTURE_COMPARE_FUNC
            | GL_TEXTURE_COMPARE_MODE
            | GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER
            | GL_TEXTURE_MAX_LOD
            | GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER
            | GL_TEXTURE_MIN_LOD
            | GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_R
            | GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S
            | GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_T => true,
            GL_TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY_EXT => self.extension_enabled("EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic"),
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn sampler_parameteri(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        sampler: Ref<WebGLSampler>,
        pname: u32,
        param: i32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(sampler_handle) = self.handle_of(sampler) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        if !self.is_sampler_parameter_name(pname) {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_ENUM);
            return Ok(());
        }
        self.proxy.sampler_parameteri(sampler_handle, pname, param);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn sampler_parameterf(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        sampler: Ref<WebGLSampler>,
        pname: u32,
        param: f32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(sampler_handle) = self.handle_of(sampler) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        if !self.is_sampler_parameter_name(pname) {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_ENUM);
            return Ok(());
        }
        self.proxy.sampler_parameterf(sampler_handle, pname, param);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn fence_sync(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        condition: u32,
        flags: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Ref<WebGLSync>>> {
        let sync_handle = self.proxy.fence_sync(condition, flags);
        Ok(Some(WebGLSync::create(cx.vm(), self, sync_handle)))
    }

    pub(crate) fn delete_sync(&self, _: &mut CallContext, sync: Option<Ref<WebGLSync>>) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(sync) = sync else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let Ok(sync_handle) = sync.sync_handle_for_deletion(self) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return Ok(());
        };
        let Some(sync_handle) = sync_handle else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.proxy.delete_sync(sync_handle);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn client_wait_sync(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        sync: Ref<WebGLSync>,
        flags: u32,
        timeout: u64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        let Ok(sync_handle) = sync.sync_handle(self) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return Ok(GL_WAIT_FAILED);
        };
        Ok(self.proxy.client_wait_sync(sync_handle, flags, timeout))
    }

    pub(crate) fn wait_sync(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        sync: Ref<WebGLSync>,
        flags: u32,
        timeout: i64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Ok(sync_handle) = sync.sync_handle(self) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return Ok(());
        };
        // NB: GL has an unsigned timeout, whose largest value is what TIMEOUT_IGNORED, which is -1 here, stands for.
        self.proxy.wait_sync(sync_handle, flags, timeout.cast_unsigned());
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_sync_parameter(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        sync: Ref<WebGLSync>,
        pname: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        let Ok(sync_handle) = sync.sync_handle(self) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return Ok(Value::NULL);
        };
        let mut result = [0];
        self.proxy.get_synciv(sync_handle, pname, 1, &mut result);
        let [result] = result;
        Ok(Value::from_i32(result))
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_transform_feedback(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<WebGLTransformFeedback>> {
        let mut handle = [0];
        self.proxy.gen_transform_feedbacks(&mut handle);
        Ok(WebGLTransformFeedback::create(cx.vm(), self, handle[0]))
    }

    pub(crate) fn delete_transform_feedback(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        tf: Option<Ref<WebGLTransformFeedback>>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(transform_feedback) = tf else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let Some(handle) = self.handle_for_deletion_of(transform_feedback) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.proxy.delete_transform_feedbacks(1, &[handle]);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn bind_transform_feedback(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        tf: Option<Ref<WebGLTransformFeedback>>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let mut transform_feedback_handle = 0;
        if let Some(transform_feedback) = tf {
            let Some(handle) = self.handle_of(transform_feedback) else {
                return Ok(());
            };
            transform_feedback_handle = handle;
        }
        self.proxy.bind_transform_feedback(target, transform_feedback_handle);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn begin_transform_feedback(&self, _: &mut CallContext, primitive_mode: u32) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.proxy.begin_transform_feedback(primitive_mode);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn end_transform_feedback(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.proxy.end_transform_feedback();
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn transform_feedback_varyings(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        program: Ref<WebGLProgram>,
        varyings: Vec<Utf16String>,
        buffer_mode: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(program_handle) = self.handle_of_program_or_shader(program) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let varyings: Vec<Vec<u8>> = varyings.iter().map(utf8_bytes).collect();
        let varyings: Vec<&[u8]> = varyings.iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
        self.proxy
            .transform_feedback_varyings(program_handle, &varyings, buffer_mode);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn pause_transform_feedback(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.proxy.pause_transform_feedback();
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn resume_transform_feedback(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.proxy.resume_transform_feedback();
        Ok(())
    }

    fn buffer_handle_for_indexed_binding(&self, target: u32, buffer: Option<Ref<WebGLBuffer>>) -> Option<u32> {
        let Some(buffer) = buffer else {
            return Some(0);
        };
        let buffer_handle = self.handle_of(buffer)?;
        if !buffer.kind_allows_binding_to(target) {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return None;
        }

        // NB: GL reports a target that these do not bind buffers to, and binds nothing to it.
        if let Some(kind_of_buffers_at_target) = BufferKind::of_buffers_at_indexed_target(target) {
            buffer.was_bound_as(kind_of_buffers_at_target);
        }
        Some(buffer_handle)
    }

    pub(crate) fn bind_buffer_base(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        index: u32,
        buffer: Option<Ref<WebGLBuffer>>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(buffer_handle) = self.buffer_handle_for_indexed_binding(target, buffer) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.proxy.bind_buffer_base(target, index, buffer_handle);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn bind_buffer_range(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        index: u32,
        buffer: Option<Ref<WebGLBuffer>>,
        offset: i64,
        size: i64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(buffer_handle) = self.buffer_handle_for_indexed_binding(target, buffer) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.proxy.bind_buffer_range(target, index, buffer_handle, offset, size);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_uniform_indices(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        program: Ref<WebGLProgram>,
        uniform_names: Vec<Utf16String>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Vec<u32>>> {
        let Some(program_handle) = self.handle_of_program_or_shader(program) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let uniform_names: Vec<Vec<u8>> = uniform_names.iter().map(utf8_bytes).collect();
        let uniform_names: Vec<&[u8]> = uniform_names.iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
        let mut uniform_indices = vec![0; uniform_names.len()];
        self.proxy
            .get_uniform_indices(program_handle, &uniform_names, &mut uniform_indices);
        Ok(Some(uniform_indices))
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_active_uniforms(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        program: Ref<WebGLProgram>,
        uniform_indices: Vec<u32>,
        pname: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        let Some(program_handle) = self.handle_of_program_or_shader(program) else {
            return Ok(Value::NULL);
        };
        let Ok(uniform_count) = i32::try_from(uniform_indices.len()) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_VALUE);
            return Ok(Value::NULL);
        };
        let mut params = vec![0; uniform_indices.len()];
        self.proxy.get_active_uniformsiv(
            program_handle,
            uniform_count,
            bytes_of(&uniform_indices),
            pname,
            &mut params,
        );

        let params_as_values = MarkedVec::with_capacity(cx.vm(), params.len());
        for param in params {
            params_as_values.push(match pname {
                GL_UNIFORM_TYPE | GL_UNIFORM_SIZE => Value::from_f64(f64::from(param.cast_unsigned())),
                GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_INDEX | GL_UNIFORM_OFFSET | GL_UNIFORM_ARRAY_STRIDE | GL_UNIFORM_MATRIX_STRIDE => {
                    Value::from_i32(param)
                }
                GL_UNIFORM_IS_ROW_MAJOR => Value::from_bool(param.cast_unsigned() == GL_TRUE),
                _ => {
                    self.set_error(GL_INVALID_ENUM);
                    return Ok(Value::NULL);
                }
            });
        }
        Ok(Value::from_object(Array::create_from_list(
            cx.vm(),
            self.realm(),
            &params_as_values,
        )))
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_uniform_block_index(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        program: Ref<WebGLProgram>,
        uniform_block_name: Utf16String,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        let Some(program_handle) = self.handle_of_program_or_shader(program) else {
            return Ok(GL_INVALID_INDEX);
        };
        Ok(self
            .proxy
            .get_uniform_block_index(program_handle, &utf8_bytes(&uniform_block_name)))
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_active_uniform_block_parameter(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        program: Ref<WebGLProgram>,
        uniform_block_index: u32,
        pname: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        let Some(program_handle) = self.handle_of_program_or_shader(program) else {
            return Ok(Value::NULL);
        };
        match pname {
            GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_BINDING | GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_DATA_SIZE | GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_ACTIVE_UNIFORMS => {
                let mut result = [0];
                self.proxy.get_active_uniform_blockiv_robust_angle(
                    program_handle,
                    uniform_block_index,
                    pname,
                    1,
                    &mut result,
                );
                let [result] = result;
                Ok(Value::from_i32(result))
            }
            GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_ACTIVE_UNIFORM_INDICES => {
                let mut num_active_uniforms = [0];
                self.proxy.get_active_uniform_blockiv_robust_angle(
                    program_handle,
                    uniform_block_index,
                    GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_ACTIVE_UNIFORMS,
                    1,
                    &mut num_active_uniforms,
                );
                let [num_active_uniforms] = num_active_uniforms;
                let mut active_uniform_indices = vec![0; element_count_from_gl(num_active_uniforms)];
                self.proxy.get_active_uniform_blockiv_robust_angle(
                    program_handle,
                    uniform_block_index,
                    GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_ACTIVE_UNIFORM_INDICES,
                    num_active_uniforms,
                    &mut active_uniform_indices,
                );
                let active_uniform_indices: Vec<u32> =
                    active_uniform_indices.into_iter().map(i32::cast_unsigned).collect();
                Ok(self.uint32_array(cx, &active_uniform_indices))
            }
            GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_REFERENCED_BY_VERTEX_SHADER | GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_REFERENCED_BY_FRAGMENT_SHADER => {
                let mut result = [0];
                self.proxy.get_active_uniform_blockiv_robust_angle(
                    program_handle,
                    uniform_block_index,
                    pname,
                    1,
                    &mut result,
                );
                let [result] = result;
                Ok(Value::from_bool(result.cast_unsigned() == GL_TRUE))
            }
            _ => {
                self.set_error(GL_INVALID_ENUM);
                Ok(Value::NULL)
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn get_active_uniform_block_name(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        program: Ref<WebGLProgram>,
        uniform_block_index: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Option<Utf16String>> {
        let Some(program_handle) = self.handle_of_program_or_shader(program) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let mut uniform_block_name_length = [0];
        self.proxy.get_active_uniform_blockiv_robust_angle(
            program_handle,
            uniform_block_index,
            GL_UNIFORM_BLOCK_NAME_LENGTH,
            1,
            &mut uniform_block_name_length,
        );
        let [uniform_block_name_length] = uniform_block_name_length;
        let mut uniform_block_name = vec![0; element_count_from_gl(uniform_block_name_length)];
        if uniform_block_name.is_empty() {
            return Ok(Some(Utf16String::from_ascii(b"")));
        }
        self.proxy.get_active_uniform_block_name(
            program_handle,
            uniform_block_index,
            uniform_block_name_length,
            &mut uniform_block_name,
        );
        let length_without_nul = uniform_block_name.len() - 1;
        Ok(Some(utf16_string_from_gl_string(
            &uniform_block_name[..length_without_nul],
        )))
    }

    pub(crate) fn uniform_block_binding(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        program: Ref<WebGLProgram>,
        uniform_block_index: u32,
        uniform_block_binding: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(program_handle) = self.handle_of_program_or_shader(program) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.proxy
            .uniform_block_binding(program_handle, uniform_block_index, uniform_block_binding);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn create_vertex_array(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<WebGLVertexArrayObject>> {
        let mut handle = [0];
        self.proxy.gen_vertex_arrays(&mut handle);
        Ok(WebGLVertexArrayObject::create(cx.vm(), self, handle[0]))
    }

    pub(crate) fn delete_vertex_array(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        vertex_array: Option<Ref<WebGLVertexArrayObject>>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(vertex_array) = vertex_array else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let Some(handle) = self.handle_for_deletion_of(vertex_array) else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.proxy.delete_vertex_arrays(1, &[handle]);
        let is_current_vertex_array = matches!(
            self.current_vertex_array.get(),
            Some(VertexArrayBinding::WebGL2(current_vertex_array))
                if current_vertex_array.as_ptr() == vertex_array.as_ptr()
        );
        if is_current_vertex_array {
            self.current_vertex_array.set(None);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_vertex_array(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        vertex_array: Option<Ref<WebGLVertexArrayObject>>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        let Some(vertex_array) = vertex_array else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        let Some(handle) = self.handle_for_query_of(vertex_array) else {
            return Ok(false);
        };
        Ok(self.proxy.is_vertex_array(handle))
    }

    pub(crate) fn bind_vertex_array(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        array: Option<Ref<WebGLVertexArrayObject>>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let mut array_handle = 0;
        if let Some(array) = array {
            let Some(handle) = self.handle_of(array) else {
                return Ok(());
            };
            array_handle = handle;
        }
        self.proxy.bind_vertex_array(array_handle);
        self.current_vertex_array.set(array.map(VertexArrayBinding::WebGL2));
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/2.0/#3.7
//!
//! The operations of a WebGL 2 context that it has more overloads of than a WebGL 1 context.

use super::buffer_source::{destination_bytes, list_bytes, source_bytes, write_checked};
use super::constants::{GL_INVALID_ENUM, GL_INVALID_OPERATION, GL_INVALID_VALUE, GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY};
use super::pixel_unpacking::is_valid_2d_pixel_unpack_state;
use super::state::{RenderingContext, WebGL2};
use super::types::Float32List;
use super::web_gl_rendering_context_overloads::{Int32List, TexImageSource};

use crate::bindings::conversions::ArrayBufferView;
use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::webidl::buffers::AllowSharedBufferSource;

#[expect(
    clippy::too_many_arguments,
    reason = "the operations have the arguments of the GL functions"
)]
impl RenderingContext<WebGL2> {
    pub(crate) fn buffer_data_with_size(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        size: i64,
        usage: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.proxy.buffer_data(target, size, None, usage);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn buffer_data(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        src_data: Option<AllowSharedBufferSource>,
        usage: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/1.0/#5.14.5
        // If the passed data is null then an INVALID_VALUE error is generated.
        let Some(src_data) = src_data else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_VALUE);
            return Ok(());
        };
        let Ok(bytes) = source_bytes(src_data.into(), 0, 0) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_VALUE);
            return Ok(());
        };
        let size = i64::from(bytes.gl_size());
        // SAFETY: Recording the command neither runs script nor allocates a cell.
        unsafe {
            self.upload_through_nullable_pointer(&bytes, |bytes| {
                self.proxy.buffer_data(target, size, bytes, usage);
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn buffer_data_with_offset(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        src_data: ArrayBufferView,
        usage: u32,
        src_offset: u64,
        length: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Ok(bytes) = source_bytes(src_data.into(), src_offset, length) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_VALUE);
            return Ok(());
        };
        let size = i64::from(bytes.gl_size());
        // SAFETY: Recording the command neither runs script nor allocates a cell.
        unsafe {
            self.upload_through_nullable_pointer(&bytes, |bytes| {
                self.proxy.buffer_data(target, size, bytes, usage);
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn buffer_sub_data(

    pub(crate) fn tex_image2d(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        internalformat: i32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
        border: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        pixels: Option<ArrayBufferView>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(pixels) = pixels else {
            self.proxy.tex_image2d_robust_angle(
                target,
                level,
                internalformat,
                width,
                height,
                border,
                format,
                r#type,
                0,
                None,
            );
            return Ok(());
        };

        let Ok(texture_data) = self.texture_data_for_2d_upload(pixels, 0, width, height, format, r#type) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return Ok(());
        };
        let buf_size = texture_data.gl_size();
        // SAFETY: Recording the command neither runs script nor allocates a cell.
        unsafe {
            self.upload_texture_data(&texture_data, |texture_data| {
                self.proxy.tex_image2d_robust_angle(
                    target,
                    level,
                    internalformat,
                    width,
                    height,
                    border,
                    format,
                    r#type,
                    buf_size,
                    texture_data,
                );
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn tex_image2d_with_source(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        internalformat: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        source: TexImageSource,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some((frame, upload)) = self.read_texture_image_source(&source, format, r#type)? else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.proxy
            .tex_image2d_from_bitmap(target, level, internalformat, format, r#type, frame, upload);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn tex_image2d_with_size_and_source(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        internalformat: i32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
        border: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        source: TexImageSource,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/es3.0/html/glTexImage2D.xhtml
        // border: This value must be 0.
        if border != 0 {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_VALUE);
            return Ok(());
        }

        let Some((frame, mut upload)) = self.read_texture_image_source(&source, format, r#type)? else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        upload.destination_size = Some((width, height));
        self.proxy
            .tex_image2d_from_bitmap(target, level, internalformat, format, r#type, frame, upload);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn tex_image2d_with_offset(

        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,

        else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return Ok(());
        };
        let buf_size = texture_data.gl_size();
        // SAFETY: Recording the command neither runs script nor allocates a cell.
        unsafe {
            self.upload_texture_data(&texture_data, |texture_data| {
                self.proxy.tex_image2d_robust_angle(
                    target,
                    level,
                    internalformat,
                    width,
                    height,
                    border,
                    format,
                    r#type,
                    buf_size,
                    texture_data,
                );
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn tex_sub_image2d(

    pub(crate) fn tex_sub_image2d_with_source(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        xoffset: i32,
        yoffset: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        source: TexImageSource,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {

        };
        self.proxy
            .tex_sub_image2d_from_bitmap(target, level, xoffset, yoffset, format, r#type, frame, upload);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn tex_sub_image2d_with_size_and_source(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        xoffset: i32,
        yoffset: i32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        source: TexImageSource,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some((frame, mut upload)) = self.read_texture_image_source(&source, format, r#type)? else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        upload.destination_size = Some((width, height));
        self.proxy
            .tex_sub_image2d_from_bitmap(target, level, xoffset, yoffset, format, r#type, frame, upload);
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn tex_sub_image2d_with_offset(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        xoffset: i32,
        yoffset: i32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        src_data: ArrayBufferView,
        src_offset: u64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Ok(texture_data) = self.texture_data_for_2d_upload(src_data, src_offset, width, height, format, r#type)
        else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return Ok(());
        };
        let buf_size = texture_data.gl_size();
        // SAFETY: Recording the command neither runs script nor allocates a cell.
        unsafe {
            self.upload_texture_data(&texture_data, |texture_data| {
                self.proxy.tex_sub_image2d_robust_angle(
                    target,
                    level,
                    xoffset,
                    yoffset,
                    width,
                    height,
                    format,
                    r#type,
                    buf_size,
                    texture_data,
                );
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn compressed_tex_image2d(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,
        level: i32,
        internalformat: u32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
        border: i32,
        src_data: ArrayBufferView,
        src_offset: u64,
        src_length_override: u32,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        if !self
            .enabled_compressed_texture_formats
            .borrow()
            .contains(&internalformat)
        {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_ENUM);
            return Ok(());
        }
        let Ok(bytes) = source_bytes(src_data.into(), src_offset, src_length_override) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_VALUE);
            return Ok(());
        };
        let size = bytes.gl_size();
        // SAFETY: Recording the command neither runs script nor allocates a cell.
        unsafe {
            self.upload(&bytes, |bytes| {
                self.proxy.compressed_tex_image2d_robust_angle(
                    target,
                    level,
                    internalformat,
                    width,
                    height,
                    border,
                    size,
                    size,
                    bytes,
                );
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn compressed_tex_sub_image2d(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        target: u32,

        xoffset: i32,

        height: i32,
        format: u32,

            return Ok(());

            self.upload(&bytes, |bytes| {

                    target, level, xoffset, yoffset, width, height, format, size, size, bytes,
                );
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn uniform_matrix2fv(
        &self,

            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_VALUE);
            return Ok(());

            .uniform_matrix2fv(location_handle, count, transpose, values.as_bytes());
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/1.0/index.html#5.14.12
    pub(crate) fn read_pixels(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        x: i32,
        y: i32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        pixels: Option<ArrayBufferView>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        let Some(view) = pixels else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_VALUE);
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.read_pixels_with_offset(cx, x, y, width, height, format, r#type, view, 0)
    }

    /// https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/2.0/#4.7.10
    pub(crate) fn read_pixels_with_offset(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        x: i32,
        y: i32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        dst_data: ArrayBufferView,
        dst_offset: u64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // If a WebGLBuffer is bound to the PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER target, generates an INVALID_OPERATION error.
        if self.pixel_pack_buffer_binding.get().is_some() {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return Ok(());
        }

        // If pixel store parameter constraints are not met, generates an INVALID_OPERATION error.
        // If dstData doesn't have enough space for the read operation starting at dstOffset, generate
        // INVALID_OPERATION.
        let Ok(destination_bytes) = destination_bytes(&dst_data, dst_offset) else {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return Ok(());
        };

        let Ok(buf_size) = i32::try_from(destination_bytes.len()) else {
            self.set_error(GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY);
            return Ok(());
        };
        self.proxy
            .read_pixels_robust_angle(x, y, width, height, format, r#type, buf_size, |_, pixels| {
                if pixels.is_empty() {
                    return;
                }
                if write_checked(&dst_data, pixels, destination_bytes.start).is_err() {
                    self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
                }
            });
        Ok(())
    }

    /// https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/2.0/#4.7.10
    pub(crate) fn read_pixels_into_pack_buffer(
        &self,
        _: &mut CallContext,
        x: i32,
        y: i32,
        width: i32,
        height: i32,
        format: u32,
        r#type: u32,
        offset: i64,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // If no WebGLBuffer is bound to the PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER target, generates an INVALID_OPERATION error.
        if self.pixel_pack_buffer_binding.get().is_none() {
            self.set_error(GL_INVALID_OPERATION);
            return Ok(());
        }

        self.proxy
            .read_pixels_into_pixel_pack_buffer(x, y, width, height, format, r#type, offset);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/*

use core::ffi::c_void;
use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};
use std::hash::{BuildHasherDefault, DefaultHasher};

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, GcRefCell, Realm, Trace, Visitor, Vm};

use crate::bindings::callback::PromiseCallbackFunction;
use crate::bindings::environment_settings_object::CppEnvironmentSettingsObject;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, cell_from_abi};
use crate::bindings::promise::{pending_steps, run_pending_steps};
use crate::web_locks::lock_manager::LockManager;
use crate::web_locks::lock_request::LockRequestRef;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_locks_environment_lock_manager(environment: *mut c_void) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_locks_queue_task(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        cell: *mut c_void,
        steps: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void),
    );
    fn web_locks_queue_callback_task(
        callback: *mut c_void,
        cell: *mut c_void,
        steps: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *mut c_void),
    );
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct LockRequestQueue(pub(crate) GcRefCell<VecDeque<LockRequestRef>>);

static LOCK_REQUEST_QUEUE_CLASS: EmbedderClass<LockRequestQueue> = EmbedderClass::new("LockRequestQueue");

impl EmbedderValue for LockRequestQueue {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &LOCK_REQUEST_QUEUE_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type LockRequestQueueRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<LockRequestQueue>>;

// NB: A fixed hasher keeps the order of query()'s pending list the same from run to run.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct LockRequestQueueMap(
    pub(crate) HashMap<Utf16String, LockRequestQueueRef, BuildHasherDefault<DefaultHasher>>,
);

// SAFETY: Only the map's values contain cells.
unsafe impl Trace for LockRequestQueueMap {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        for queue in self.0.values() {
            queue.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

impl LockRequestQueueMap {
    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#get-the-lock-request-queue
    pub(crate) fn get_lock_request_queue(&mut self, vm: &Vm, name: &Utf16String) -> LockRequestQueueRef {
        // 1. If queueMap[name] does not exist, set queueMap[name] to a new empty lock request queue.
        let queue = *self.0.entry(name.clone()).or_insert_with(|| {
            LOCK_REQUEST_QUEUE_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| LockRequestQueue(GcRefCell::new(VecDeque::new())))
        });

        // 2. Return queueMap[name].
        queue
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#obtain-a-lock-manager
pub(crate) fn obtain_lock_manager(environment: &CppEnvironmentSettingsObject) -> Ref<LockManager> {
    // 1. Let map be the result of obtaining a local storage bottle map given environment and "web-locks".
    // 2. If map is failure, then return failure.
    // 3. Let bottle be map’s associated storage bottle.
    // 4. Return bottle’s associated lock manager.

    // FIXME: Spec issue: Storing and obtaining a lock manager in the environment's storage is currently not well
    //        defined. So we store a single instance per environment for now. See:
    //        https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#issue-73644ca1
    // SAFETY: The environment is live, and its settings object keeps its manager alive.
    unsafe { cell_from_abi(web_locks_environment_lock_manager(environment.as_ptr())) }
}

pub(crate) fn queue_web_locks_task<C: Trace + Clone + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, C),
) {
    let cell = pending_steps(vm, captures, steps);
    // SAFETY: LibWeb retains the realm and the traced captures until the task runs.
    unsafe { web_locks_queue_task(realm.as_ptr().cast(), cell, run_pending_steps) };
}

pub(crate) fn queue_web_locks_callback_task<C: Trace + Clone + 'static>(
    vm: &Vm,
    callback: &PromiseCallbackFunction,
    captures: C,
    steps: fn(&Vm, C),
) {
    let cell = pending_steps(vm, captures, steps);
    // SAFETY: LibWeb retains the callback and the traced captures until the task runs.
    unsafe { web_locks_queue_callback_task(callback.as_ptr(), cell, run_pending_steps) };
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum LockMode {
    Shared,
    #[default]
    Exclusive,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct LockOptions {
    pub(crate) mode: LockMode,
    pub(crate) if_available: bool,
    pub(crate) steal: bool,
    pub(crate) signal: Option<Ref<AbortSignal>>,
}

pub(crate) struct LockManagerSnapshot {
    pub(crate) held: Option<Vec<LockInfo>>,
    pub(crate) pending: Option<Vec<LockInfo>>,
}

impl LockManagerSnapshot {
    fn into_js(self, cx: &CallContext) -> Value {
        // NB: The generated bindings convert the dictionary, which a build of the crate on its own leaves out.
        #[cfg(web_idl_bindings)]
        return ToJs::to_js(self, cx).expect("a lock manager snapshot converts to a JS value");
        #[cfg(not(web_idl_bindings))]
        {
            let _ = (self, cx);
            unreachable!("only the generated bindings resolve a promise with the dictionary")
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) struct LockInfo {
    pub(crate) name: Option<Utf16String>,
    pub(crate) mode: Option<LockMode>,
    pub(crate) client_id: Option<Utf16String>,
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct LockManager {
    pub(crate) held_lock_set: GcRefCell<Vec<LockDataRef>>,
    pub(crate) lock_request_queue_map: GcRefCell<LockRequestQueueMap>,
    environment: CppEnvironmentSettingsObject,
    pub(crate) realm: Gc<Realm>,
}

impl Wrappable for LockManager {
    fn relevant_realm(&self) -> Option<Gc<Realm>> {
        Some(self.realm)
    }
}

impl LockManager {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> Ref<Self> {
        allocate(vm, |_| Self {
            held_lock_set: GcRefCell::default(),
            lock_request_queue_map: GcRefCell::default(),
            environment: relevant_settings_object(realm.global_object()),
            realm,
        })
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#dom-lockmanager-request
    pub(crate) fn request(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        name: Utf16String,
        options: Option<LockOptions>,
        callback: PromiseCallbackFunction,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        let vm = cx.vm();
        let realm = self.realm;

        // 1. If options was not passed, then let options be a new LockOptions dictionary with default members.
        let options = options.unwrap_or_default();
        let signal = options.signal;

        // 2. Let environment be this’s relevant settings object.
        let environment = &self.environment;

        // 3. If environment’s relevant global object’s associated Document is not fully active, then return a promise
        //    rejected with a "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
        if let Some(window) = window_from_global_object(environment.global_object())
            && !window.associated_document().is_fully_active()
        {
            return Ok(create_rejected_promise_from_exception(
                vm,
                realm,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "InvalidStateError",
                    Utf16String::from_utf8("Document is not fully active"),
                ),
            ));
        }

        // 4. Let manager be the result of obtaining a lock manager given environment. If that returned failure, then
        //    return a promise rejected with a "SecurityError" DOMException.
        let manager = obtain_lock_manager(environment);

        // 5. If name starts with U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS (-), then return a promise rejected with a "NotSupportedError"
        //    DOMException.
        let starts_with_hyphen = match name.as_units() {
            Utf16StringUnits::Ascii(units) | Utf16StringUnits::Latin1(units) => units.first() == Some(&b'-'),
            Utf16StringUnits::Utf16(units) => units.first() == Some(&u16::from(b'-')),
        };
        if starts_with_hyphen {
            return Ok(create_rejected_promise_from_exception(
                vm,
                realm,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "NotSupportedError",
                    Utf16String::from_utf8("Lock names starting with '-' are reserved"),
                ),
            ));
        }

        // 6. If both options["steal"] and options["ifAvailable"] are true, then return a promise rejected with a
        //    "NotSupportedError" DOMException.
        if options.steal && options.if_available {
            return Ok(create_rejected_promise_from_exception(
                vm,
                realm,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "NotSupportedError",
                    Utf16String::from_utf8("Lock options 'steal' and 'ifAvailable' cannot both be true"),
                ),
            ));
        }

        // 7. If options["steal"] is true and options["mode"] is not "exclusive", then return a promise rejected with a
        //    "NotSupportedError" DOMException.
        if options.steal && options.mode != LockMode::Exclusive {
            return Ok(create_rejected_promise_from_exception(
                vm,
                realm,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "NotSupportedError",
                    Utf16String::from_utf8("Lock option 'steal' can only be used with exclusive locks"),
                ),
            ));
        }

        // 8. If options["signal"] exists, and either of options["steal"] or options["ifAvailable"] is true, then return
        //    a promise rejected with a "NotSupportedError" DOMException.
        if signal.is_some() && (options.steal || options.if_available) {
            return Ok(create_rejected_promise_from_exception(
                vm,
                realm,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "NotSupportedError",
                    Utf16String::from_utf8("Lock option 'signal' cannot be combined with 'steal' or 'ifAvailable'"),
                ),
            ));
        }

        // 9. If options["signal"] exists and is aborted, then return a promise rejected with options["signal"]'s abort
        //    reason.
        if let Some(signal) = &signal
            && signal.aborted()
        {
            return Ok(create_rejected_promise(vm, realm, signal.reason()));
        }

        // 10. Let promise be a new promise.
        let promise = create_promise(vm, realm);

        // 11. Request a lock with promise, the current agent, environment’s id, manager, callback, name,
        //     options["mode"], options["ifAvailable"], options["steal"], and options["signal"].
        Self::request_lock(
            manager,
            vm,
            promise,
            callback,
            name,
            options.mode,
            options.if_available,
            options.steal,
            signal,
        );

        // 12. Return promise.
        Ok(promise)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#dom-lockmanager-query
    pub(crate) fn query(&self, cx: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<WebIdlPromise> {
        let vm = cx.vm();

        // 1. Let environment be this’s relevant settings object.
        let environment = &self.environment;

        // 2. If environment’s relevant global object’s associated Document is not fully active, then return a promise
        //    rejected with a "InvalidStateError" DOMException.
        if let Some(window) = window_from_global_object(environment.global_object())
            && !window.associated_document().is_fully_active()
        {
            return Ok(create_rejected_promise_from_exception(
                vm,
                self.realm,
                Exception::Dom(
                    "InvalidStateError",
                    Utf16String::from_utf8("Document is not fully active"),
                ),
            ));
        }

        // 3. Let manager be the result of obtaining a lock manager given environment. If that returned failure, then
        //    return a promise rejected with a "SecurityError" DOMException.
        let manager = obtain_lock_manager(environment);

        // 4. Let promise be a new promise.
        let promise = create_promise(vm, self.realm);

        // 5. Enqueue the steps to snapshot the lock state for manager with promise to the lock task queue.
        queue_web_locks_task(vm, self.realm, (manager, promise), |vm, (manager, promise)| {
            manager.snapshot_lock_state(vm, promise);
        });

        // 6. Return promise.
        Ok(promise)
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#request-a-lock
    #[allow(
        clippy::too_many_arguments,
        reason = "the specification gives the algorithm these parameters"
    )]
    fn request_lock(
        manager: Ref<Self>,
        vm: &Vm,
        promise: WebIdlPromise,
        callback: PromiseCallbackFunction,
        name: Utf16String,
        mode: LockMode,
        if_available: bool,
        steal: bool,
        signal: Option<Ref<AbortSignal>>,
    ) -> LockRequestRef {
        // 1. Let request be a new lock request (agent, clientId, manager, name, mode, callback, promise, signal).
        let request = LOCK_REQUEST_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| LockRequest {
            client_id: Utf16String::from_utf8(&manager.environment.id()),
            manager,
            name,
            mode,
            callback,
            promise,
            signal,
            abort_algorithm_id: Cell::new(None),
        });

        // 2. If signal is present, then add the algorithm signal to abort the request request with signal to signal.
        if let Some(signal) = &request.signal {
            let algorithm = NativeFunction::create(
                vm,
                (request, *signal),
                |vm, (request, signal): &(LockRequestRef, Ref<AbortSignal>)| {
                    LockRequest::signal_to_abort_request(*request, vm, signal);
                    Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
                },
                0,
                &PropertyKey::from_utf8(""),
                Some(manager.realm),
                None,
                None,
            );
            request
                .abort_algorithm_id
                .set(signal.add_abort_algorithm(vm, AbortAlgorithm::Rust(algorithm)));
        }

        // 3. Enqueue the following steps to the lock task queue:
        queue_web_locks_task(
            vm,
            manager.realm,
            (manager, request, if_available, steal),
            |vm, (manager, request, if_available, steal)| {
                // 1. Let queueMap be manager’s lock request queue map.
                let queue_map = &manager.lock_request_queue_map;

                // 2. Let queue be the result of getting the lock request queue from queueMap for name.
                let queue = queue_map.borrow_mut(vm).get_lock_request_queue(vm, &request.name);

                // 3. Let held be manager’s held lock set.
                let held = &manager.held_lock_set;

                // 4. If steal is true, then run these steps:
                if steal {
                    // 1. For each lock of held:
                    let mut i = 0;
                    while i < held.borrow().len() {
                        let lock = held.borrow()[i];

                        // 1. If lock’s name is name, then run these steps:
                        if lock.name == request.name {
                            // 1. Remove lock from held.
                            held.borrow_mut(vm).remove(i);

                            // 2. Reject lock’s released promise with an "AbortError" DOMException.
                            reject_promise_with_exception(
                                vm,
                                lock.released_promise,
                                Exception::Dom("AbortError", Utf16String::from_utf8("Lock was stolen")),
                            );
                        } else {
                            i += 1;
                        }
                    }

                    // 2. Prepend request in queue.
                    queue.0.borrow_mut(vm).push_front(request);
                }
                // 5. Otherwise, run these steps:
                else {
                    // 1. If ifAvailable is true and request is not grantable, then enqueue the following steps on
                    //    callback’s relevant settings object’s responsible event loop:
                    if if_available && !LockRequest::is_grantable(request, vm) {
                        queue_web_locks_callback_task(vm, &request.callback, request, |vm, request| {
                            // 1. Let r be the result of invoking callback with null as the only argument.
                            let r = request.callback.invoke(None, &[Value::NULL]);

                            // 2. Resolve promise with r and abort these steps.
                            resolve_promise(vm, request.promise, Value::from_object(r.promise()));
                        });

                        // AD-HOC: Abort the enclosing queue steps so an unavailable request is not also granted later.
                        return;
                    }

                    // 2. Enqueue request in queue.
                    queue.0.borrow_mut(vm).push_back(request);
                }

                // 6. Process the lock request queue queue.
                Self::process_lock_request_queue(vm, queue);
            },
        );

        // 4. Return request.
        request
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#process-the-lock-request-queue
    pub(crate) fn process_lock_request_queue(vm: &Vm, queue: LockRequestQueueRef) {
        // 1. Assert: these steps are running on the lock task queue.

        // 2. For each request of queue:
        while let Some(request) = { queue.0.borrow().front().copied() } {
            // 1. If request is not grantable, then return.
            // NOTE: Only the first item in a queue is grantable. Therefore, if something is not grantable then all the
            //       following items are automatically not grantable.
            if !LockRequest::is_grantable(request, vm) {
                return;
            }

            // 2. Remove request from queue.
            queue.0.borrow_mut(vm).pop_front();

            // FIXME: 3. Let agent be request’s agent.

            // 4. Let manager be request’s manager.
            let manager = request.manager;

            // 5. Let clientId be request’s clientId.
            let client_id = request.client_id.clone();

            // 6. Let name be request’s name.
            let name = request.name.clone();

            // 7. Let mode be request’s mode.
            let mode = request.mode;

            // 8. Let callback be request’s callback.
            let callback = request.callback.clone();

            // 9. Let p be request’s promise.
            let p = request.promise;

            // 10. Let signal be request’s signal.
            let signal = request.signal;

            // 11. Let waiting be a new promise.
            let waiting = create_promise(vm, manager.realm);

            // 12. Let lock be a new lock with agent agent, clientId clientId, manager manager, mode mode, name name,
            //     released promise p, and waiting promise waiting.
            let lock = LOCK_DATA_CLASS.allocate(vm, |_| LockData {
                client_id,
                manager,
                name,
                mode,
                released_promise: p,
                waiting_promise: waiting,
            });

            // 13. Append lock to manager’s held lock set.
            manager.held_lock_set.borrow_mut(vm).push(lock);

            // 14. Enqueue the following steps on callback’s relevant settings object’s responsible event loop:
            queue_web_locks_callback_task(
                vm,
                &callback,
                (manager, request, lock, signal, callback.clone(), waiting),
                |vm, (manager, request, lock, signal, callback, waiting)| {
                    // 1. If signal is present, then run these steps:
                    if let Some(signal) = &signal {
                        // 1. If signal is aborted, then run these steps:
                        if signal.aborted() {
                            // 1. Enqueue the following step to the lock task queue:
                            queue_web_locks_task(vm, manager.realm, lock, |vm, lock| {
                                // 1. Release the lock lock.
                                LockData::release_lock(lock, vm);
                            });

                            // 2. Return.
                            return;
                        }

                        // 2. Remove the algorithm signal to abort the request request from signal.
                        if let Some(id) = request.abort_algorithm_id.get() {
                            signal.remove_abort_algorithm(vm, id);
                        }
                    }

                    // 2. Let r be the result of invoking callback with a new Lock object associated with lock as the
                    //    only argument.
                    let cx = CallContext::new(vm, manager.realm);
                    let r = callback.invoke(None, &[Value::from_object(wrap(&cx, Lock::create(vm, lock)))]);

                    // 3. Resolve waiting with r.
                    resolve_promise(vm, waiting, Value::from_object(r.promise()));
                },
            );

            react_to_promise(
                vm,
                waiting,
                lock,
                Some(LockData::waiting_promise_settled),
                Some(LockData::waiting_promise_settled),
            );
        }
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#snapshot-the-lock-state
    fn snapshot_lock_state(&self, vm: &Vm, promise: WebIdlPromise) {
        // 1. Assert: these steps are running on the lock task queue.

        // 2. Let pending be a new list.
        let mut pending = Vec::new();

        // 3. For each queue of manager’s lock request queue map’s values:
        for queue in self.lock_request_queue_map.borrow().0.values() {
            // 1. For each request of queue:
            for request in queue.0.borrow().iter() {
                // 1. Append «[ "name" → request’s name, "mode" → request’s mode, "clientId" → request’s clientId ]»
                //    to pending.
                pending.push(LockInfo {
                    name: Some(request.name.clone()),
                    mode: Some(request.mode),
                    client_id: Some(request.client_id.clone()),
                });
            }
        }

        // 4. Let held be a new list.
        let mut held = Vec::new();

        // 5. For each lock of manager’s held lock set:
        for lock in self.held_lock_set.borrow().iter() {
            // 1. Append «[ "name" → lock’s name, "mode" → lock’s mode, "clientId" → lock’s clientId ]» to held.
            held.push(LockInfo {
                name: Some(lock.name.clone()),
                mode: Some(lock.mode),
                client_id: Some(lock.client_id.clone()),
            });
        }

        // 6. Resolve promise with «[ "held" → held, "pending" → pending ]».
        let snapshot = LockManagerSnapshot {
            held: Some(held),
            pending: Some(pending),
        };
        let cx = CallContext::new(vm, self.realm);
        resolve_promise(vm, promise, snapshot.into_js(&cx));
    }
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_web_locks_create_lock_manager(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(LockManager::create(vm, realm))
}

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

use core::cell::Cell;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::callback::PromiseCallbackFunction;
use crate::bindings::interface::Ref;
use crate::bindings::promise::{WebIdlPromise, reject_promise};
use crate::dom::abort_signal::AbortSignal;
use crate::web_locks::abstract_operations::queue_web_locks_task;
use crate::web_locks::lock_manager::{LockManager, LockMode};

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct LockRequest {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) client_id: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) manager: Ref<LockManager>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) name: Utf16String,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) mode: LockMode,
    pub(crate) callback: PromiseCallbackFunction,
    pub(crate) promise: WebIdlPromise,
    pub(crate) signal: Option<Ref<AbortSignal>>,
    pub(crate) abort_algorithm_id: Cell<Option<u64>>,
}

pub(crate) static LOCK_REQUEST_CLASS: EmbedderClass<LockRequest> = EmbedderClass::new("LockRequest");

impl EmbedderValue for LockRequest {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &LOCK_REQUEST_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type LockRequestRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<LockRequest>>;

impl LockRequest {
    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#abort-the-request
    pub(crate) fn abort_request(this: LockRequestRef, vm: &Vm) {
        // 1. Assert: these steps are running on the lock task queue.

        // 2. Let manager be request’s manager.
        let manager = this.manager;

        // 3. Let name be request’s name.
        let name = &this.name;

        // 4. Let queueMap be manager’s lock request queue map.
        let queue_map = &manager.lock_request_queue_map;

        // 5. Let queue be the result of getting the lock request queue from queueMap for name.
        let queue = queue_map.borrow_mut(vm).get_lock_request_queue(vm, name);

        // 6. Remove request from queue.
        queue.0.borrow_mut(vm).retain(|request| *request != this);

        // 7. Process the lock request queue queue.
        LockManager::process_lock_request_queue(vm, queue);
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#signal-to-abort-the-request
    pub(crate) fn signal_to_abort_request(this: LockRequestRef, vm: &Vm, signal: &AbortSignal) {
        // 1. Enqueue the steps to abort the request request to the lock task queue.
        queue_web_locks_task(vm, this.manager.realm, this, |vm, request| {
            Self::abort_request(request, vm);
        });

        // 2. Reject request’s promise with signal’s abort reason.
        reject_promise(vm, this.promise, signal.reason());
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#grantable
    pub(crate) fn is_grantable(this: LockRequestRef, vm: &Vm) -> bool {
        // 1. Let manager be request’s manager.
        let manager = this.manager;

        // 2. Let queueMap be manager’s lock request queue map.
        let queue_map = &manager.lock_request_queue_map;

        // 3. Let name be request’s name.
        let name = &this.name;

        // 4. Let queue be the result of getting the lock request queue from queueMap for name.
        let queue = queue_map.borrow_mut(vm).get_lock_request_queue(vm, name);

        // 5. Let held be manager’s held lock set
        let held = manager.held_lock_set.borrow();

        // 6. Let mode be request’s mode
        let mode = this.mode;

        // 7. If queue is not empty and request is not the first item in queue, then return false.
        if queue.0.borrow().front().is_some_and(|request| *request != this) {
            return false;
        }

        // 8. If mode is "exclusive", then return true if no lock in held has name equal to name, and false otherwise.
        if mode == LockMode::Exclusive {
            return !held.iter().any(|lock| &lock.name == name);
        }

        // 9. Otherwise, mode is "shared"; return true if no lock in held has mode "exclusive" and has name equal to
        //    name, and false otherwise.
        !held
            .iter()
            .any(|lock| lock.mode == LockMode::Exclusive && &lock.name == name)
    }
}

/*

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{EmbedderCell, EmbedderClass, EmbedderValue, Gc, Trace, Value, Vm};

use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::promise::{WebIdlPromise, resolve_promise};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::web_locks::abstract_operations::queue_web_locks_task;
use crate::web_locks::lock_manager::{LockManager, LockMode};

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct Lock {
    lock: LockDataRef,
}

impl Wrappable for Lock {}

impl Lock {
    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, lock: LockDataRef) -> Ref<Self> {
        allocate(vm, |_| Self { lock })
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#dom-lock-name
    pub(crate) fn name(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<Utf16String> {
        // The name getter’s steps are to return the associated lock’s name.
        Ok(self.lock.name.clone())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#dom-lock-mode
    pub(crate) fn mode(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<LockMode> {
        // The mode getter’s steps are to return the associated lock’s mode.
        Ok(self.lock.mode)
    }
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct LockData {
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) client_id: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) manager: Ref<LockManager>,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) name: Utf16String,
    #[gc(untraced)]
    pub(crate) mode: LockMode,
    pub(crate) released_promise: WebIdlPromise,
    pub(crate) waiting_promise: WebIdlPromise,
}

pub(crate) static LOCK_DATA_CLASS: EmbedderClass<LockData> = EmbedderClass::new("LockData");

impl EmbedderValue for LockData {
    const CLASS: &'static EmbedderClass<Self> = &LOCK_DATA_CLASS;
}

pub(crate) type LockDataRef = Gc<EmbedderCell<LockData>>;

impl LockData {
    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#release-the-lock
    pub(crate) fn release_lock(this: LockDataRef, vm: &Vm) {
        // 1. Assert: these steps are running on the lock task queue.

        // 2. Let manager be lock’s manager.
        let manager = this.manager;

        // 3. Let queueMap be manager’s lock request queue map.
        let queue_map = &manager.lock_request_queue_map;

        // 4. Let name be lock’s resource name.
        let name = &this.name;

        // 5. Let queue be the result of getting the lock request queue from queueMap for name.
        let queue = queue_map.borrow_mut(vm).get_lock_request_queue(vm, name);

        // 6. Remove lock from the manager’s held lock set.
        manager.held_lock_set.borrow_mut(vm).retain(|lock| *lock != this);

        // 7. Process the lock request queue queue.
        LockManager::process_lock_request_queue(vm, queue);
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/#concept-lock
    pub(crate) fn waiting_promise_settled(cx: &CallContext, lock: LockDataRef, _: Value) -> WebIdlResult<Value> {
        // When lock lock’s waiting promise settles (fulfills or rejects), enqueue the following steps on the lock task
        // queue:
        queue_web_locks_task(cx.vm(), lock.manager.realm, lock, |vm, lock| {
            // 1. Release the lock lock.
            Self::release_lock(lock, vm);

            // 2. Resolve lock’s released promise with lock’s waiting promise.
            resolve_promise(
                vm,
                lock.released_promise,
                Value::from_object(lock.waiting_promise.promise()),
            );
        });
        Ok(Value::UNDEFINED)
    }
}

use core::ffi::c_void;

// Each node names its parent by index, with index zero reserved for the fragment.
#[repr(C)]
struct DomNode {
    parent: usize,
    kind: Kind,
    value: usize,
    classes: usize,
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_vtt_create_fragment(document: *mut c_void, nodes: *const DomNode, length: usize) -> *mut c_void;
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum Kind {
    Text,
    Timestamp,
    Class,
    Italic,
    Bold,
    Underline,
    Ruby,
    RubyText,
    Voice,
    Language,
}

impl Kind {
    fn from_tag(name: &[u16]) -> Option<Self> {
        // The longest recognized tag name is four ASCII characters.
        if name.len() > 4 {
            return None;
        }
        Some(match String::from_utf16(name).ok()?.as_str() {
            "c" => Self::Class,
            "i" => Self::Italic,
            "b" => Self::Bold,
            "u" => Self::Underline,
            "ruby" => Self::Ruby,
            "rt" => Self::RubyText,
            "v" => Self::Voice,
            "lang" => Self::Language,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }
}

struct Node {
    kind: Kind,
    parent: usize,
    value: Utf16String,
    classes: Utf16String,
}

fn normalized_annotation(input: &[u16]) -> Utf16String {
    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#consume-an-html-character-reference
    // AD-HOC: WebVTT says this context is 'not "as part of an attribute"' for missing semicolons. All three other
    // browser engines keep "&notit;" literal in voice annotations, so decode annotations in the attribute context.
    let decoded = decode_character_references(input, CharacterReferenceContext::Attribute);
    let words: Vec<_> = decoded
        .split(|unit| is_ascii_whitespace((*unit).into()))
        .filter(|word| !word.is_empty())
        .collect();
    Utf16String::from_utf16(&words.join(&u16::from(b' ')))
}

fn timestamp(input: &[u16]) -> Option<Utf16String> {
    let mut lexer = GenericLexer::new(input);
    collect_a_webvtt_timestamp(&mut lexer)?;
    if !lexer.is_eof() {
        return None;
    }
    // Keep the digits so rounding a floating-point time cannot change the milliseconds.
    let mut parts = input.split(|unit| *unit == u16::from(b':'));
    let first = parts.next()?;
    let second = parts.next()?;
    let mut formatted = Vec::new();
    if let Some(seconds) = parts.next() {
        let first_nonzero = first
            .iter()
            .position(|unit| *unit != u16::from(b'0'))
            .unwrap_or(first.len() - 1);
        let hours = &first[first_nonzero..];
        if hours.len() == 1 {
            formatted.push(u16::from(b'0'));
        }
        formatted.extend_from_slice(hours);
        formatted.push(u16::from(b':'));
        formatted.extend_from_slice(second);
        formatted.push(u16::from(b':'));
        formatted.extend_from_slice(seconds);
    } else {
        formatted.extend("00:".encode_utf16());
        formatted.extend_from_slice(input);
    }
    Some(Utf16String::from_utf16(&formatted))
}

enum Token<'a> {
    Text(Utf16String),
    Start {
        name: &'a [u16],
        classes: Vec<&'a [u16]>,
        annotation: Utf16String,
    },
    End(&'a [u16]),
    Timestamp(&'a [u16]),
}

fn take_until<'a>(input: &mut &'a [u16], delimiter: impl Fn(u16) -> bool) -> &'a [u16] {
    let end = input.iter().position(|&unit| delimiter(unit)).unwrap_or(input.len());
    let (value, rest) = input.split_at(end);
    *input = rest;
    value
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-cue-text-tokenizer
fn next_token<'a>(input: &mut &'a [u16]) -> Token<'a> {
    // 2. Let tokenizer state be WebVTT data state.
    // NB: A run of data ends immediately before the next tag. Only ampersands enter the HTML character reference state.
    if !input.starts_with(&[u16::from(b'<')]) {
        let text = take_until(input, |unit| unit == u16::from(b'<'));
        return Token::Text(Utf16String::from_utf16(&decode_character_references(
            text,
            CharacterReferenceContext::Data,
        )));
    }

    // WebVTT tag state
    *input = &input[1..];
    let mut tag = take_until(input, |unit| unit == u16::from(b'>'));
    if !input.is_empty() {
        *input = &input[1..];
    }

    // WebVTT end tag state
    if let Some(name) = tag.strip_prefix(&[u16::from(b'/')]) {
        return Token::End(name);
    }
    // WebVTT timestamp tag state
    if tag.first().is_some_and(|unit| (0x30..=0x39).contains(unit)) {
        return Token::Timestamp(tag);
    }

    // WebVTT start tag state
    // NB: CR belongs to the name or class. The annotation itself uses all ASCII whitespace.
    let ends_name_or_class = |unit| matches!(unit, 0x09 | 0x0a | 0x0c | 0x20 | 0x2e);
    let name = take_until(&mut tag, ends_name_or_class);

    // WebVTT start tag class state
    let mut classes = Vec::new();
    while let Some(rest) = tag.strip_prefix(&[u16::from(b'.')]) {
        tag = rest;
        classes.push(take_until(&mut tag, ends_name_or_class));
    }

    // WebVTT start tag annotation state
    let annotation = normalized_annotation(tag);
    Token::Start {
        name,
        classes,
        annotation,
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-cue-text-parsing-rules
fn parse(mut input: &[u16]) -> Vec<Node> {
    // 3. Let result be a list of WebVTT Node Objects, initially empty.
    let mut result: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
    // 4. Let current be the WebVTT Internal Node Object result.
    let mut current = 0;
    // NB: For getCueAsHTML(), the DOM's lang attributes represent the language scopes.

    // 7. Loop: If position is past the end of input, return result and abort these steps.
    while !input.is_empty() {
        // 8. Let token be the result of invoking the WebVTT cue text tokenizer.
        // 9. Run the appropriate steps given the type of token:
        match next_token(&mut input) {
            Token::Text(value) => {
                // Append the newly created WebVTT Text Object to current.
                result.push(Node {
                    kind: Kind::Text,
                    parent: current,
                    value,
                    classes: Utf16String::default(),
                });
            }
            Token::Start {
                name,
                mut classes,
                annotation,
            } => {
                let Some(kind) = Kind::from_tag(name) else {
                    continue;
                };
                // If current is a WebVTT Ruby Object, then attach a WebVTT Ruby Text Object.
                if kind == Kind::RubyText && (current == 0 || result[current - 1].kind != Kind::Ruby) {
                    continue;
                }
                // Set the new object's list of applicable classes to the list of classes in the token,
                // excluding any classes that are the empty string.
                classes.retain(|class| !class.is_empty());
                let classes = Utf16String::from_utf16(&classes.join(&u16::from(b' ')));
                let value = if matches!(kind, Kind::Voice | Kind::Language) {
                    annotation
                } else {
                    Utf16String::default()
                };
                // Append the newly created node object to current.
                result.push(Node {
                    kind,
                    parent: current,
                    value,
                    classes,
                });
                // Let current be the newly created node object.
                current = result.len();
            }
            Token::End(name) => {
                if current == 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let node = &result[current - 1];
                if let Some(kind) = Kind::from_tag(name) {
                    if kind == node.kind {
                        current = node.parent;
                    } else if kind == Kind::Ruby && node.kind == Kind::RubyText {
                        current = result[node.parent - 1].parent;
                    }
                }
            }
            Token::Timestamp(text) => {
                // Collect a WebVTT timestamp.
                if let Some(value) = timestamp(text) {
                    result.push(Node {
                        kind: Kind::Timestamp,
                        parent: current,
                        value,
                        classes: Utf16String::default(),
                    });
                }
            }
        }
    }
    result
}

pub(super) fn create_fragment(cx: &CallContext, text: &Utf16String) -> CppInterface {
    let nodes = parse(&text.to_utf16());
    let dom: Vec<_> = nodes
        .iter()
        .map(|node| DomNode {
            parent: node.parent,
            kind: node.kind,
            value: node.value.raw_identity(),
            classes: node.classes.raw_identity(),
        })
        .collect();
    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttcue-getcueashtml
    // AD-HOC: The spec uses the entry document. Use the cue's document so borrowing the method across windows
    // preserves the owner document of the fragment and all of its children.
    let window = window_from_global_object(cx.realm().global_object()).expect("VTTCue is exposed only on Window");
    let document = window.associated_document();
    // SAFETY: The document and the strings in nodes stay live while LibWeb builds and returns the fragment.
    let fragment = unsafe { CppCell::from_raw(web_vtt_create_fragment(document.as_ptr(), dom.as_ptr(), dom.len())) };
    wrap_cpp_cell(cx, &fragment)
}

//! The C ABI through which LibWeb's C++ code parses WebVTT files and creates VTTCue objects for the cues in them,
//! which Libraries/LibWeb/WebVTT/Parser.cpp and Libraries/LibWeb/WebVTT/VTTCue.cpp declare.

use core::ffi::c_void;

use libjs_rust::api::Vm;

use crate::bindings::interface::cell_into_abi;
use crate::bindings::lent_string::LentUtf16String;
use crate::web_vtt::parser::parse_webvtt_file;
use crate::web_vtt::vtt_cue::VTTCue;

/// https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttcue-vttcue
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_vtt_cue_create(
    vm: &Vm,
    start_time: f64,
    end_time: f64,
    text: LentUtf16String<'_>,
) -> *mut c_void {
    let text = text.to_utf16_string();
    let Ok(cue) = VTTCue::create(vm, start_time, end_time, text) else {
        unreachable!("C++ creates cues whose end time is neither negative infinity nor NaN");
    };
    cell_into_abi(cue)
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-parser
///
/// Parses the bytes and passes each cue to `on_cue`, with the identifier and the text, whose references the callee
/// adopts. Returns false if the file does not start with the WebVTT file signature.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `bytes` must point to `length` bytes, and `on_cue` must be safe to call with `ctx`.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_vtt_parse_webvtt_file(
    bytes: *const u8,
    length: usize,
    ctx: *mut c_void,
    on_cue: unsafe extern "C" fn(ctx: *mut c_void, identifier: usize, start_time: f64, end_time: f64, text: usize),
) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes `length` bytes.
    let bytes = unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(bytes, length) };
    let Some(cues) = parse_webvtt_file(bytes) else {
        return false;
    };
    for cue in cues {
        let identifier = cue.identifier.into_raw();
        let text = cue.text.into_raw();
        // SAFETY: The caller passes a callback that is safe to call with the context.
        unsafe { on_cue(ctx, identifier, cue.start_time, cue.end_time, text) };
    }
    true
}
