//! The WebVTT parser, https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-parser

use ak::character_types::is_ascii_digit;
use ak::{GenericLexer, Utf16String};
use libwebcommon_rust::infra::character_types::is_ascii_whitespace;

const LINE_FEED: u16 = b'\n' as u16;
const CARRIAGE_RETURN: u16 = b'\r' as u16;
const REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER: u16 = 0xFFFD;

/// A cue that the parser collected, which LibWeb creates a VTTCue for.
pub(crate) struct ParsedCue {
    pub(crate) identifier: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) start_time: f64,
    pub(crate) end_time: f64,
    pub(crate) text: Utf16String,
}

fn contains(haystack: &[u16], needle: &[u16]) -> bool {
    haystack.windows(needle.len()).any(|window| window == needle)
}

fn utf16(string: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
    string.encode_utf16().collect()
}

fn skip_whitespace(lexer: &mut GenericLexer<'_, u16>) {
    lexer.ignore_while(|code_unit| is_ascii_whitespace(code_unit.into()));
}

fn collect_ascii_digits<'a>(lexer: &mut GenericLexer<'a, u16>) -> &'a [u16] {
    lexer.consume_while(|code_unit| is_ascii_digit(code_unit.into()))
}

fn interpret_as_base_ten_integer(digits: &[u16]) -> u64 {
    digits.iter().fold(0u64, |value, digit| {
        value.wrapping_mul(10).wrapping_add(u64::from(digit - u16::from(b'0')))
    })
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#collect-a-webvtt-timestamp
pub(super) fn collect_a_webvtt_timestamp(lexer: &mut GenericLexer<'_, u16>) -> Option<f64> {
    // 1. Let input and position be the same variables as those of the same name in the algorithm that invoked these
    //    steps.

    // 2. Let most significant units be minutes.
    let mut most_significant_units_are_hours = false;

    // 3. If position is past the end of input, return an error and abort these steps.
    let code_unit = lexer.peek()?;

    // 4. If the character indicated by position is not an ASCII digit, then return an error and abort these steps.
    if !is_ascii_digit(code_unit.into()) {
        return None;
    }

    // 5. Collect a sequence of code points that are ASCII digits, and let string be the collected substring.
    let mut string = collect_ascii_digits(lexer);

    // 6. Interpret string as a base-ten integer. Let value1 be that integer.
    let mut value1 = interpret_as_base_ten_integer(string);

    // 7. If string is not exactly two characters in length, or if value1 is greater than 59, let most significant units
    //    be hours.
    if string.len() != 2 || value1 > 59 {
        most_significant_units_are_hours = true;
    }

    // 8. If position is beyond the end of input or if the character at position is not a U+003A COLON character (:),
    //    then return an error and abort these steps. Otherwise, move position forwards one character.
    if !lexer.consume_specific(u16::from(b':')) {
        return None;
    }

    // 9. Collect a sequence of code points that are ASCII digits, and let string be the collected substring.
    string = collect_ascii_digits(lexer);

    // 10. If string is not exactly two characters in length, return an error and abort these steps.
    if string.len() != 2 {
        return None;
    }

    // 11. Interpret string as a base-ten integer. Let value2 be that integer.
    let mut value2 = interpret_as_base_ten_integer(string);
    let value3;

    // 12. If most significant units is hours, or if position is not beyond the end of input and the character at
    //     position is a U+003A COLON character (:), run these substeps:
    if most_significant_units_are_hours || lexer.peek() == Some(u16::from(b':')) {
        // 1. If position is beyond the end of input or if the character at position is not a U+003A COLON character
        //    (:), then return an error and abort these steps. Otherwise, move position forwards one character.
        if !lexer.consume_specific(u16::from(b':')) {
            return None;
        }

        // 2. Collect a sequence of code points that are ASCII digits, and let string be the collected substring.
        string = collect_ascii_digits(lexer);

        // 3. If string is not exactly two characters in length, return an error and abort these steps.
        if string.len() != 2 {
            return None;
        }

        // 4. Interpret string as a base-ten integer. Let value3 be that integer.
        value3 = interpret_as_base_ten_integer(string);
    }
    // Otherwise (if most significant units is not hours, and either position is beyond the end of input, or the
    // character at position is not a U+003A COLON character (:)), let value3 have the value of value2, then value2 have
    // the value of value1, then let value1 equal zero.
    else {
        value3 = value2;
        value2 = value1;
        value1 = 0;
    }

    // 13. If position is beyond the end of input or if the character at position is not a U+002E FULL STOP character
    //     (.), then return an error and abort these steps. Otherwise, move position forwards one character.
    if !lexer.consume_specific(u16::from(b'.')) {
        return None;
    }

    // 14. Collect a sequence of code points that are ASCII digits, and let string be the collected substring.
    string = collect_ascii_digits(lexer);

    // 15. If string is not exactly three characters in length, return an error and abort these steps.
    if string.len() != 3 {
        return None;
    }

    // 16. Interpret string as a base-ten integer. Let value4 be that integer.
    let value4 = interpret_as_base_ten_integer(string);

    // 17. If value2 is greater than 59 or if value3 is greater than 59, return an error and abort these steps.
    if value2 > 59 || value3 > 59 {
        return None;
    }

    // 18. Let result be value1×60×60 + value2×60 + value3 + value4∕1000.
    let result = (value1 as f64 * 60.0 * 60.0) + (value2 as f64 * 60.0) + value3 as f64 + (value4 as f64 / 1000.0);

    // 19. Return result.
    Some(result)
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#collect-webvtt-cue-timings-and-settings
fn collect_webvtt_cue_timings_and_settings(input: &[u16], cue: &mut ParsedCue) -> bool {
    // 1. Let input be the string being parsed.
    // 2. Let position be a pointer into input, initially pointing at the start of the string.
    let mut lexer = GenericLexer::new(input);

    // 3. Skip whitespace.
    skip_whitespace(&mut lexer);

    // 4. Collect a WebVTT timestamp. If that algorithm fails, then abort these steps and return failure. Otherwise, let
    //    cue's text track cue start time be the collected time.
    let Some(start_time) = collect_a_webvtt_timestamp(&mut lexer) else {
        return false;
    };
    cue.start_time = start_time;

    // 5. Skip whitespace.
    skip_whitespace(&mut lexer);

    // 6. If the character at position is not a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-) then abort these steps and return
    //    failure. Otherwise, move position forwards one character.
    // 7. If the character at position is not a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-) then abort these steps and return
    //    failure. Otherwise, move position forwards one character.
    // 8. If the character at position is not a U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN character (>) then abort these steps and return
    //    failure. Otherwise, move position forwards one character.
    if !lexer.consume_specific(u16::from(b'-'))
        || !lexer.consume_specific(u16::from(b'-'))
        || !lexer.consume_specific(u16::from(b'>'))
    {
        return false;
    }

    // 9. Skip whitespace.
    skip_whitespace(&mut lexer);

    // 10. Collect a WebVTT timestamp. If that algorithm fails, then abort these steps and return failure. Otherwise, let
    //     cue's text track cue end time be the collected time.
    let Some(end_time) = collect_a_webvtt_timestamp(&mut lexer) else {
        return false;
    };
    cue.end_time = end_time;

    // FIXME: 11. Let remainder be the trailing substring of input starting at position.
    // FIXME: 12. Parse the WebVTT cue settings from remainder using regions for cue.
    true
}

fn is_block_keyword(buffer: &[u16], keyword: &str) -> bool {
    let keyword = utf16(keyword);
    let Some(remainder) = buffer.strip_prefix(keyword.as_slice()) else {
        return false;
    };
    remainder.iter().all(|&code_unit| is_ascii_whitespace(code_unit.into()))
}

struct Parser<'a> {
    input: &'a [u16],
    lexer: GenericLexer<'a, u16>,
    seen_cue: bool,
}

impl<'a> Parser<'a> {
    fn new(input: &'a [u16]) -> Self {
        Self {
            input,
            lexer: GenericLexer::new(input),
            seen_cue: false,
        }
    }

    fn collect_a_sequence_of_code_points_that_are_not_line_feeds(&mut self) -> &'a [u16] {
        self.lexer.consume_while(|code_unit| code_unit != LINE_FEED)
    }

    fn collect_a_sequence_of_line_feeds(&mut self) {
        self.lexer.ignore_while(|code_unit| code_unit == LINE_FEED);
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#collect-a-webvtt-block
    fn collect_a_webvtt_block(&mut self, in_header: bool) -> Option<ParsedCue> {
        // 1. Let input, position, seen cue and regions be the same variables as those of the same name in the algorithm
        //    that invoked these steps.

        // 2. Let line count be zero.
        let mut line_count = 0usize;

        // 3. Let previous position be position.
        let mut previous_position = self.lexer.tell();

        // 4. Let line be the empty string.
        // 5. Let buffer be the empty string.
        let mut buffer: Vec<u16> = Vec::new();

        // 6. Let seen EOF be false.
        let mut seen_eof = false;

        // 7. Let seen arrow be false.
        let mut seen_arrow = false;

        // 8. Let cue be null.
        let mut cue: Option<ParsedCue> = None;

        // FIXME: 9. Let stylesheet be null.
        // FIXME: 10. Let region be null.

        let arrow = utf16("-->");

        // 11. Loop: Run these substeps in a loop:
        loop {
            // 1. Collect a sequence of code points that are not U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters. Let line be those
            //    characters, if any.
            let line = self.collect_a_sequence_of_code_points_that_are_not_line_feeds();

            // 2. Increment line count by 1.
            line_count += 1;

            // 3. If position is past the end of input, let seen EOF be true. Otherwise, the character indicated by
            //    position is a U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character; advance position to the next character in input.
            if self.lexer.is_eof() {
                seen_eof = true;
            } else {
                self.lexer.ignore(1);
            }

            // 4. If line contains the three-character substring "-->" (U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, U+003E
            //    GREATER-THAN SIGN), then run these substeps:
            if contains(line, &arrow) {
                // 1. If in header is not set and at least one of the following conditions are true:
                //    - line count is 1
                //    - line count is 2 and seen arrow is false
                //    ...then run these substeps:
                if !in_header && (line_count == 1 || (line_count == 2 && !seen_arrow)) {
                    // 1. Let seen arrow be true.
                    seen_arrow = true;

                    // 2. Let previous position be position.
                    previous_position = self.lexer.tell();

                    // 3. Cue creation: Let cue be a new WebVTT cue and initialize it as follows:
                    //    Let cue's text track cue identifier be buffer.
                    //    FIXME: Initialize the remaining cue fields once cue settings are supported.
                    let mut new_cue = ParsedCue {
                        identifier: Utf16String::from_utf16(&buffer),
                        start_time: 0.0,
                        end_time: 0.0,
                        text: Utf16String::from_utf8(""),
                    };

                    // 4. Collect WebVTT cue timings and settings from line using regions for cue. If that fails, let
                    //    cue be null. Otherwise, let buffer be the empty string and let seen cue be true.
                    if collect_webvtt_cue_timings_and_settings(line, &mut new_cue) {
                        cue = Some(new_cue);
                        buffer.clear();
                        self.seen_cue = true;
                    } else {
                        cue = None;
                    }
                }
                // Otherwise, let position be previous position and break out of loop.
                else {
                    self.lexer.retreat(self.lexer.tell() - previous_position);
                    break;
                }
            }
            // 5. Otherwise, if line is the empty string, break out of loop.
            else if line.is_empty() {
                break;
            }
            // 6. Otherwise, run these substeps:
            else {
                // 1. If in header is not set and line count is 2, run these substeps:
                if !in_header && line_count == 2 {
                    // 1. If seen cue is false and buffer starts with the substring "STYLE" (U+0053 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER
                    //    S, U+0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T, U+0059 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y, U+004C LATIN CAPITAL LETTER
                    //    L, U+0045 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER E), and the remaining characters in buffer (if any) are all
                    //    ASCII whitespace, then run these substeps:
                    // 2. Otherwise, if seen cue is false and buffer starts with the substring "REGION" (U+0052 LATIN
                    //    CAPITAL LETTER R, U+0045 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER E, U+0047 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER G, U+0049 LATIN
                    //    CAPITAL LETTER I, U+004F LATIN CAPITAL LETTER O, U+004E LATIN CAPITAL LETTER N), and the
                    //    remaining characters in buffer (if any) are all ASCII whitespace, then run these substeps:
                    if !self.seen_cue && (is_block_keyword(&buffer, "STYLE") || is_block_keyword(&buffer, "REGION")) {
                        // FIXME: Create the CSS style sheet or WebVTT region.
                        // Let buffer be the empty string.
                        buffer.clear();
                    }
                }

                // 2. If buffer is not the empty string, append a U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character to buffer.
                if !buffer.is_empty() {
                    buffer.push(LINE_FEED);
                }

                // 3. Append line to buffer.
                buffer.extend_from_slice(line);

                // 4. Let previous position be position.
                previous_position = self.lexer.tell();
            }

            // 7. If seen EOF is true, break out of loop.
            if seen_eof {
                break;
            }
        }

        // 12. If cue is not null, let the cue text of cue be buffer, and return cue.
        if let Some(mut cue) = cue {
            cue.text = Utf16String::from_utf16(&buffer);
            return Some(cue);
        }

        // FIXME: 13. Otherwise, if stylesheet is not null, then Parse a stylesheet from buffer. If it returned a list of
        //            rules, assign the list as stylesheet's CSS rules; otherwise, set stylesheet's CSS rules to an
        //            empty list. Finally, return stylesheet.
        // FIXME: 14. Otherwise, if region is not null, then collect WebVTT region settings from buffer using region for
        //            the results. Construct a WebVTT Region Object from region, and return it.

        // 15. Otherwise, return null.
        None
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-parser-algorithm
    fn parse(&mut self) -> Option<Vec<ParsedCue>> {
        let mut output = Vec::new();

        // 2. Let position be a pointer into input, initially pointing at the start of the string.
        // 3. Let seen cue be false.

        // 4. If input is less than six characters long, then abort these steps. The file does not start with the
        //    correct WebVTT file signature and was therefore not successfully processed.
        if self.input.len() < 6 {
            return None;
        }

        // 5. If input is exactly six characters long but does not exactly equal "WEBVTT", then abort these steps. The
        //    file does not start with the correct WebVTT file signature and was therefore not successfully processed.
        // 6. If input is more than six characters long but the first six characters do not exactly equal "WEBVTT", or
        //    the seventh character is not a U+0020 SPACE character, a U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab) character, or a
        //    U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character, then abort these steps. The file does not start with the correct WebVTT
        //    file signature and was therefore not successfully processed.
        if !self.input.starts_with(&utf16("WEBVTT")) {
            return None;
        }
        if self.input.len() > 6 && !matches!(self.input[6], 0x20 | 0x09 | LINE_FEED) {
            return None;
        }

        // 7. Collect a sequence of code points that are not U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters.
        self.collect_a_sequence_of_code_points_that_are_not_line_feeds();

        // 8. If position is past the end of input, then abort these steps. The file was successfully processed, but it
        //    contains no useful data and so no WebVTT cues were added to output.
        if self.lexer.is_eof() {
            return Some(output);
        }

        // 9. The character indicated by position is a U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character. Advance position to the next
        //    character in input.
        self.lexer.ignore(1);

        // 10. If position is past the end of input, then abort these steps. The file was successfully processed, but it
        //     contains no useful data and so no WebVTT cues were added to output.
        if self.lexer.is_eof() {
            return Some(output);
        }

        // 11. Header: If the character indicated by position is not a U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character, then collect a
        //     WebVTT block with the in header flag set. Otherwise, advance position to the next character in input.
        if self.lexer.peek() == Some(LINE_FEED) {
            self.lexer.ignore(1);
        } else {
            self.collect_a_webvtt_block(true);
        }

        // 12. Collect a sequence of code points that are U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters.
        self.collect_a_sequence_of_line_feeds();

        // FIXME: 13. Let regions be an empty text track list of regions.

        // 14. Block loop: While position doesn't point past the end of input:
        while !self.lexer.is_eof() {
            // 1. Collect a WebVTT block, and let block be the returned value.
            let block = self.collect_a_webvtt_block(false);

            // 2. If block is a WebVTT cue, add block to the text track list of cues output.
            if let Some(block) = block {
                output.push(block);
            }

            // FIXME: 3. Otherwise, if block is a CSS style sheet, add block to stylesheets.
            // FIXME: 4. Otherwise, if block is a WebVTT region object, add block to regions.

            // 5. Collect a sequence of code points that are U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters.
            self.collect_a_sequence_of_line_feeds();
        }

        // 15. End: The file has ended. Abort these steps. The WebVTT parser has finished. The file was successfully
        //     processed.
        Some(output)
    }
}

/// https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-parser
///
/// Returns None if the file does not start with the WebVTT file signature.
pub(crate) fn parse_webvtt_file(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<ParsedCue>> {
    // A WebVTT parser, given an input byte stream, a text track list of cues output, and a collection of CSS style
    // sheets stylesheets, must decode the byte stream using the UTF-8 decode algorithm, and then must parse the
    // resulting string according to the WebVTT parser algorithm below.
    let decoded = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes);
    let decoded = decoded.strip_prefix('\u{FEFF}').unwrap_or(&decoded);

    // 1. Let input be the string being parsed, after conversion to Unicode, and with the following transformations
    //    applied:
    //    - Replace all U+0000 NULL characters by U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTERs.
    //    - Replace each U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED (CRLF) character pair by a single U+000A LINE FEED
    //      (LF) character.
    //    - Replace all remaining U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN characters by U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters.
    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(decoded.len());
    let mut code_units = decoded.encode_utf16().peekable();
    while let Some(code_unit) = code_units.next() {
        match code_unit {
            0 => input.push(REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER),
            CARRIAGE_RETURN => {
                code_units.next_if_eq(&LINE_FEED);
                input.push(LINE_FEED);
            }
            _ => input.push(code_unit),
        }
    }

    Parser::new(&input).parse()
}

    pub(crate) fn create(vm: &Vm, start_time: f64, end_time: f64, text: Utf16String) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<VTTCue>> {
        // 1. Create a new WebVTT cue. Let cue be that WebVTT cue.
        // 2. Let cue’s text track cue start time be the value of the startTime argument.
        // 3. If the value of the endTime argument is negative Infinity or a Not-a-Number (NaN) value, then throw a
        //    TypeError exception. Otherwise, let cue’s text track cue end time be the value of the endTime argument.
        // NB: The cue is allocated below, once nothing can throw.
        if end_time == f64::NEG_INFINITY || end_time.is_nan() {
            return Err(Exception::type_error("End time is negative infinity or NaN"));
        }

        let cue = allocate(vm, |_| VTTCue {
            // 4. Let cue’s cue text be the value of the text argument, and let the rules for extracting the chapter
            //    title be the WebVTT rules for extracting the chapter title.
            // FIXME: let the rules for extracting the chapter title be the WebVTT rules for extracting the chapter
            //        title.
            text: RefCell::new(text),

            // 5. Let cue’s text track cue identifier be the empty string.
            // 6. Let cue’s text track cue pause-on-exit flag be false.
            cue: TextTrackCue::new(start_time, end_time),

            // 7. Let cue’s WebVTT cue region be null.
            region: Cell::new(None),

            // 8. Let cue’s WebVTT cue writing direction be horizontal.
            writing_direction: Cell::new(WritingDirection::Horizontal),

            // 9. Let cue’s WebVTT cue snap-to-lines flag be true.
            snap_to_lines: Cell::new(true),

            // 10. Let cue’s WebVTT cue line be auto.
            line: Cell::new(LineAndPositionSetting::AutoKeyword(AutoKeyword::Auto)),

            // 11. Let cue’s WebVTT cue line alignment be start alignment.
            line_alignment: Cell::new(LineAlignSetting::Start),

            // 12. Let cue’s WebVTT cue position be auto.
            position: Cell::new(LineAndPositionSetting::AutoKeyword(AutoKeyword::Auto)),

            // 13. Let cue’s WebVTT cue position alignment be auto.
            position_alignment: Cell::new(PositionAlignSetting::Auto),

            // 14. Let cue’s WebVTT cue size be 100.
            size: Cell::new(100.0),

            // 15. Let cue’s WebVTT cue text alignment be center alignment.
            text_alignment: Cell::new(AlignSetting::Center),
        });
        cue.cue.event_target().set_owner(cue);

        // 16. Return the VTTCue object representing cue.
        Ok(cue)
    }

        // Otherwise, the WebVTT region width must be set to the new value.
        self.width.set(value);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-lines
    pub(crate) fn lines(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<u32> {
        Ok(self.lines.get())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-lines
    pub(crate) fn set_lines(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: u32) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        self.lines.set(value);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-regionanchorx
    pub(crate) fn region_anchor_x(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.anchor_x.get())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-regionanchorx
    pub(crate) fn set_region_anchor_x(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, if the new value is negative or greater than 100, then an IndexSizeError exception must be thrown.
        if !(0.0..=100.0).contains(&value) {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_utf8(
                "Value is negative or greater than 100",
            )));
        }

        // Otherwise, the WebVTT region anchor X distance must be set to the new value.
        self.anchor_x.set(value);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-regionanchory
    pub(crate) fn region_anchor_y(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.anchor_y.get())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-regionanchory
    pub(crate) fn set_region_anchor_y(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, if the new value is negative or greater than 100, then an IndexSizeError exception must be thrown.
        if !(0.0..=100.0).contains(&value) {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_utf8(
                "Value is negative or greater than 100",
            )));
        }

        // Otherwise, the WebVTT region anchor Y distance must be set to the new value.
        self.anchor_y.set(value);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-viewportanchorx
    pub(crate) fn viewport_anchor_x(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.viewport_anchor_x.get())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-viewportanchorx
    pub(crate) fn set_viewport_anchor_x(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, if the new value is negative or greater than 100, then an IndexSizeError exception must be thrown.
        if !(0.0..=100.0).contains(&value) {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_utf8(
                "Value is negative or greater than 100",
            )));
        }

        // Otherwise, the WebVTT region viewport anchor X distance must be set to the new value.
        self.viewport_anchor_x.set(value);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-viewportanchory
    pub(crate) fn viewport_anchor_y(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.viewport_anchor_y.get())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-viewportanchory
    pub(crate) fn set_viewport_anchor_y(&self, _: &mut CallContext, value: f64) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // On setting, if the new value is negative or greater than 100, then an IndexSizeError exception must be thrown.
        if !(0.0..=100.0).contains(&value) {
            return Err(Exception::index_size_error(Utf16String::from_utf8(
                "Value is negative or greater than 100",
            )));
        }

        // Otherwise, the WebVTT region viewport anchor Y distance must be set to the new value.
        self.viewport_anchor_y.set(value);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-scroll
    pub(crate) fn scroll(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<ScrollSetting> {
        Ok(self.scroll_setting.get())
    }

    // https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#dom-vttregion-scroll

use libjs_rust::api::{ArrayBuffer, Gc};

use crate::bindings::conversions::{ArrayBufferView, BufferSource};

/// The union of WebIDL/Buffers.idl, whose members the bindings convert.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum AllowSharedBufferSource {
    ArrayBuffer(Gc<ArrayBuffer>),
    SharedArrayBuffer(Gc<ArrayBuffer>),
    ArrayBufferView(ArrayBufferView),
}

impl From<AllowSharedBufferSource> for BufferSource {
    fn from(source: AllowSharedBufferSource) -> Self {
        match source {
            AllowSharedBufferSource::ArrayBuffer(buffer) | AllowSharedBufferSource::SharedArrayBuffer(buffer) => {
                Self::ArrayBuffer(buffer)
            }
            AllowSharedBufferSource::ArrayBufferView(view) => view.into(),
        }
    }
}

//! The serialization steps of DOMException, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMException, which LibWeb implements in
//! C++ (Libraries/LibWeb/WebIDL/DOMException.cpp).

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Object, Realm};

use crate::bindings::WebIdlResult;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::reader::StructuredSerializeReader;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::writer::StructuredSerializeWriter;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_dom_exception_name_and_message(exception: *mut c_void, name: &mut usize, message: &mut usize);
    fn web_dom_exception_create(realm: *mut c_void, name: usize, message: usize) -> *mut c_void;
}

/// The name and the message of a DOMException.
pub(crate) struct DOMExceptionFields {
    pub(crate) name: Utf16String,
    pub(crate) message: Utf16String,
}

impl DOMExceptionFields {
    /// The fields of the DOMException, or of an object of an interface that inherits from it.
    pub(crate) fn of(exception: Gc<Object>) -> Self {
        let (mut name, mut message) = (0, 0);
        // SAFETY: The object is a live DOMException.
        unsafe { web_dom_exception_name_and_message(exception.as_ptr().cast(), &mut name, &mut message) };
        // SAFETY: LibWeb hands over the strings.
        unsafe {
            Self {
                name: Utf16String::from_raw_owned(name),
                message: Utf16String::from_raw_owned(message),
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A new DOMException with the fields, created in the realm.
pub(crate) fn create(realm: Gc<Realm>, fields: &DOMExceptionFields) -> Gc<Object> {
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the call borrows the strings.
    let exception = unsafe {
        web_dom_exception_create(
            realm.as_ptr().cast(),
            fields.name.raw_identity(),
            fields.message.raw_identity(),
        )
    };
    // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live object.
    unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(exception.cast()).expect("LibWeb creates the exception")) }
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMException
pub(crate) fn serialization_steps(value: &DOMExceptionFields, serialized: &StructuredSerializeWriter) {
    // 1. Set serialized.[[Name]] to value’s name.
    serialized.encode_utf16_string(&value.name);

    // 2. Set serialized.[[Message]] to value’s message.
    serialized.encode_utf16_string(&value.message);

    // FIXME: 3. User agents should attach a serialized representation of any interesting accompanying data which are not yet specified, notably the stack property, to serialized.
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMException
pub(crate) fn deserialization_steps(serialized: &StructuredSerializeReader) -> WebIdlResult<DOMExceptionFields> {
    // 1. Set value’s name to serialized.[[Name]].
    let name = serialized.decode_utf16_string()?;

    // 2. Set value’s message to serialized.[[Message]].
    let message = serialized.decode_utf16_string()?;

    // FIXME: 3. If any other data is attached to serialized, then deserialize and attach it to value.

    Ok(DOMExceptionFields { name, message })
}

//! The serialization steps of QuotaExceededError, https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#quotaexceedederror, which LibWeb
//! implements in C++ (Libraries/LibWeb/WebIDL/QuotaExceededError.cpp).

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Object, Realm};

use super::dom_exception::{self, DOMExceptionFields};
use crate::bindings::WebIdlResult;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::reader::StructuredSerializeReader;
use crate::html::structured_serialize::writer::StructuredSerializeWriter;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_quota_exceeded_error_quota_and_requested(
        error: *mut c_void,
        has_quota: &mut bool,
        quota: &mut f64,
        has_requested: &mut bool,
        requested: &mut f64,
    );
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the fields of the error pass one by one")]
    fn web_quota_exceeded_error_create(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        name: usize,
        message: usize,
        has_quota: bool,
        quota: f64,
        has_requested: bool,
        requested: f64,
    ) -> *mut c_void;
}

/// The fields of a QuotaExceededError: those of a DOMException, its quota and its requested.
pub(crate) struct QuotaExceededErrorFields {
    pub(crate) dom_exception: DOMExceptionFields,
    pub(crate) quota: Option<f64>,
    pub(crate) requested: Option<f64>,
}

impl QuotaExceededErrorFields {
    /// The fields of the QuotaExceededError.
    pub(crate) fn of(error: Gc<Object>) -> Self {
        let (mut has_quota, mut quota, mut has_requested, mut requested) = (false, 0.0, false, 0.0);
        // SAFETY: The object is a live QuotaExceededError.
        unsafe {
            web_quota_exceeded_error_quota_and_requested(
                error.as_ptr().cast(),
                &mut has_quota,
                &mut quota,
                &mut has_requested,
                &mut requested,
            );
        }
        Self {
            dom_exception: DOMExceptionFields::of(error),
            quota: has_quota.then_some(quota),
            requested: has_requested.then_some(requested),
        }
    }
}

/// A new QuotaExceededError with the fields, created in the realm.
pub(crate) fn create(realm: Gc<Realm>, fields: &QuotaExceededErrorFields) -> Gc<Object> {
    // SAFETY: The realm is live, and the call borrows the strings.
    let error = unsafe {
        web_quota_exceeded_error_create(
            realm.as_ptr().cast(),
            fields.dom_exception.name.raw_identity(),
            fields.dom_exception.message.raw_identity(),
            fields.quota.is_some(),
            fields.quota.unwrap_or_default(),
            fields.requested.is_some(),
            fields.requested.unwrap_or_default(),
        )
    };
    // SAFETY: LibWeb returns a live object.
    unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(error.cast()).expect("LibWeb creates the error")) }
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-quotaexceedederror⑦
pub(crate) fn serialization_steps(value: &QuotaExceededErrorFields, serialized: &StructuredSerializeWriter) {
    // 1. Run the DOMException serialization steps given value and serialized.
    dom_exception::serialization_steps(&value.dom_exception, serialized);

    // 2. Set serialized.[[Quota]] to value’s quota.
    serialized.encode_optional_f64(value.quota);

    // 3. Set serialized.[[Requested]] to value’s requested.
    serialized.encode_optional_f64(value.requested);
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#ref-for-quotaexceedederror⑦
pub(crate) fn deserialization_steps(serialized: &StructuredSerializeReader) -> WebIdlResult<QuotaExceededErrorFields> {
    // 1. Run the DOMException deserialization steps given serialized and value.
    let dom_exception = dom_exception::deserialization_steps(serialized)?;

    // 2. Set value’s quota to serialized.[[Quota]].
    let quota = serialized.decode_optional_f64()?;

    // 3. Set value’s requested to serialized.[[Requested]].
    let requested = serialized.decode_optional_f64()?;

    Ok(QuotaExceededErrorFields {
        dom_exception,
        quota,
        requested,
    })
}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Bindings/Rust/src/webrtc/rtc_encoded_audio_frame.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{ArrayBuffer, Gc, Object, Realm, Value};

use crate::bindings::structured_data::{SerializationReader, SerializationWriter};
use crate::bindings::{Exception, WebIdlResult};

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Default)]
struct OptionalField<T> {
    present: bool,
    value: T,
}

impl<T: Default> From<Option<T>> for OptionalField<T> {
    fn from(value: Option<T>) -> Self {
        Self {
            present: value.is_some(),
            value: value.unwrap_or_default(),
        }
    }
}

// Matches RTCEncodedAudioFrameFields in WebRTC/RTCEncodedAudioFrame.cpp. Serialization takes ownership of
// the string reference and borrows the span; deserialization lends both.
#[repr(C)]
struct RawFields<'a> {
    synchronization_source: OptionalField<u32>,
    payload_type: OptionalField<u8>,
    contributing_sources: OptionalField<ak::Span<'a, u32>>,
    rtp_timestamp: OptionalField<u32>,
    receive_time: OptionalField<f64>,
    capture_time: OptionalField<f64>,
    sender_capture_time_offset: OptionalField<f64>,
    mime_type: OptionalField<usize>,
    sequence_number: OptionalField<i16>,
    audio_level: OptionalField<f64>,
}

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_rtc_encoded_audio_frame_with_fields(
        frame: *mut c_void,
        state: *mut c_void,
        steps: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void, *const RawFields<'_>),
    ) -> *mut c_void;
    fn web_rtc_encoded_audio_frame_create(realm: *mut c_void, fields: &RawFields<'_>, data: *mut c_void)
    -> *mut c_void;
}

fn data_clone_error(message: &[u8]) -> Exception {
    Exception::Dom("DataCloneError", Utf16String::from_ascii(message))
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webrtc-encoded-transform/#RTCEncodedAudioFrame-serialization
pub(crate) fn serialization_steps(
    frame: Gc<Object>,
    serialized: &mut SerializationWriter,
    for_storage: bool,
) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
    // 1. If forStorage is true, then throw a DataCloneError.
    if for_storage {
        return Err(data_clone_error(b"RTCEncodedAudioFrame is not storable"));
    }

    unsafe extern "C" fn write_metadata(state: *mut c_void, fields: *const RawFields<'_>) {
        // SAFETY: The caller lends the writer and the frame's fields for this call.
        let (serialized, fields) = unsafe { (&mut *state.cast::<SerializationWriter>(), &*fields) };
        serialized.write_bool(fields.synchronization_source.present);
        if fields.synchronization_source.present {
            serialized.write_u32(fields.synchronization_source.value);
        }
        serialized.write_bool(fields.payload_type.present);
        if fields.payload_type.present {
            serialized.write_u8(fields.payload_type.value);
        }
        serialized.write_bool(fields.contributing_sources.present);
        if fields.contributing_sources.present {
            let sources = fields.contributing_sources.value.as_slice();
            serialized.write_u64(sources.len() as u64);
            for source in sources {
                serialized.write_u32(*source);
            }
        }
        serialized.write_bool(fields.rtp_timestamp.present);
        if fields.rtp_timestamp.present {
            serialized.write_u32(fields.rtp_timestamp.value);
        }
        serialized.write_bool(fields.receive_time.present);
        if fields.receive_time.present {
            serialized.write_f64(fields.receive_time.value);
        }
        serialized.write_bool(fields.capture_time.present);
        if fields.capture_time.present {
            serialized.write_f64(fields.capture_time.value);
        }
        serialized.write_bool(fields.sender_capture_time_offset.present);
        if fields.sender_capture_time_offset.present {
            serialized.write_f64(fields.sender_capture_time_offset.value);
        }
        serialized.write_bool(fields.mime_type.present);
        if fields.mime_type.present {
            // SAFETY: C++ hands over a reference to the string.
            let mime_type = unsafe { Utf16String::from_raw_owned(fields.mime_type.value) };
            serialized.write_utf16_string(&mime_type);
        }
        serialized.write_bool(fields.sequence_number.present);
        if fields.sequence_number.present {
            serialized.write_i32(i32::from(fields.sequence_number.value));
        }
        serialized.write_bool(fields.audio_level.present);
        if fields.audio_level.present {
            serialized.write_f64(fields.audio_level.value);
        }
    }

    // 2. Set serialized.[[metadata]] to an internal representation of value's metadata.
    // SAFETY: The frame is live, and the callback only writes its borrowed metadata.
    let data = unsafe {
        web_rtc_encoded_audio_frame_with_fields(
            frame.as_ptr().cast(),
            core::ptr::from_mut(serialized).cast(),
            write_metadata,
        )
    };
    // SAFETY: The frame owns the live ArrayBuffer returned by C++.
    let data = unsafe { Gc::<Object>::from_non_null(NonNull::new(data.cast()).expect("a frame has data")) };
    // 3. Set serialized.[[data]] to the sub-serialization of value.[[data]].
    serialized.write_value(Value::from_object(data))
}

fn read_optional<T>(
    serialized: &mut SerializationReader,
    read: impl FnOnce(&mut SerializationReader) -> WebIdlResult<T>,
) -> WebIdlResult<Option<T>> {
    if serialized.read_bool()? {
        Ok(Some(read(serialized)?))
    } else {
        Ok(None)
    }
}

// https://w3c.github.io/webrtc-encoded-transform/#RTCEncodedAudioFrame-serialization
pub(crate) fn deserialization_steps(
    realm: Gc<Realm>,
    serialized: &mut SerializationReader,
) -> WebIdlResult<Gc<Object>> {
    // 1. Set value's metadata to the platform object representation of serialized.[[metadata]].
    let synchronization_source = read_optional(serialized, |s| s.read_u32())?;
    let payload_type = read_optional(serialized, |s| s.read_u8())?;
    let contributing_sources = read_optional(serialized, |serialized| {
        let count = serialized.read_u64()?;
        let mut sources = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..count {
            sources.push(serialized.read_u32()?);
        }
        Ok(sources)
    })?;
    let rtp_timestamp = read_optional(serialized, |s| s.read_u32())?;
    let receive_time = read_optional(serialized, |s| s.read_f64())?;
    let capture_time = read_optional(serialized, |s| s.read_f64())?;
    let sender_capture_time_offset = read_optional(serialized, |s| s.read_f64())?;
    let mime_type = read_optional(serialized, |s| s.read_utf16_string())?;
    let sequence_number = read_optional(serialized, |s| {
        i16::try_from(s.read_i32()?).map_err(|_| data_clone_error(b"Invalid RTCEncodedAudioFrame sequence number"))
    })?;
    let audio_level = read_optional(serialized, |s| s.read_f64())?;
    let fields = RawFields {
        synchronization_source: synchronization_source.into(),
        payload_type: payload_type.into(),
        contributing_sources: contributing_sources.as_deref().map(ak::Span::new).into(),
        rtp_timestamp: rtp_timestamp.into(),
        receive_time: receive_time.into(),
        capture_time: capture_time.into(),
        sender_capture_time_offset: sender_capture_time_offset.into(),
        mime_type: mime_type.as_ref().map(Utf16String::raw_identity).into(),
        sequence_number: sequence_number.into(),
        audio_level: audio_level.into(),
    };

    // 2. Set value.[[data]] to the sub-deserialization of serialized.[[data]].
    let data = serialized.read_value()?;
    let data = data
        .is_object()
        .then(|| data.as_object())
        .and_then(|object| object.downcast::<ArrayBuffer>())
        .ok_or_else(|| data_clone_error(b"RTCEncodedAudioFrame.[[data]] did not deserialize to an ArrayBuffer"))?;
    // SAFETY: The realm and buffer are live; C++ borrows the metadata and copies it into the new frame.
    let frame = unsafe { web_rtc_encoded_audio_frame_create(realm.as_ptr().cast(), &fields, data.as_ptr().cast()) };
    // SAFETY: C++ returns the live wrapper of the new frame.
    Ok(unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(frame.cast()).expect("LibWeb creates the frame")) })
}

//! The C ABI through which LibWeb's C++ creates FormData objects, reads their entry lists and creates entries.

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Vm};

use super::form_data::{Entry, FormData, FormDataEntryValue, StringOrBlob, create_an_entry};
use super::xml_http_request::{NullOrFailureOrBytes, SyncSendRef, XMLHttpRequest};
use crate::bindings::conversions::UsvString;
use crate::bindings::cpp_cell::{LentCppCell, cpp_class};
use crate::bindings::interface::{InterfaceCell, Ref, allocate, cell_from_abi, cell_into_abi};
use crate::fetch::infrastructure::fetch_controller::CppFetchController;
use crate::fetch::infrastructure::http::response_view::CppResponseView;
use crate::file_api::exports::any_blob_from_abi;

#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct EntryValueAbi {
    file: *mut c_void,
    string: usize,
}

#[repr(C)]
pub(crate) struct EntryAbi {
    name: usize,
    value: EntryValueAbi,
}

impl EntryValueAbi {
    fn from_value(value: &FormDataEntryValue) -> Self {
        match value {
            FormDataEntryValue::File(file) => Self {
                file: cell_into_abi(*file),
                string: 0,
            },
            FormDataEntryValue::USVString(string) => Self {
                file: core::ptr::null_mut(),
                string: string.as_utf16_string().clone().into_raw(),
            },
        }
    }
}

impl EntryAbi {
    fn from_entry((name, value): &Entry) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.as_utf16_string().clone().into_raw(),
            value: EntryValueAbi::from_value(value),
        }
    }

    /// The entry that C++ hands over.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The entry must be one that C++ hands over: its strings are raw strings that it owns a reference to, and its file
    /// is the live cell of a File.
    unsafe fn into_entry(self) -> Entry {
        // SAFETY: The caller hands over the name.
        let name = unsafe { Utf16String::from_raw_owned(self.name) };
        let value = if self.value.file.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: The caller hands over the string.
            let string = unsafe { Utf16String::from_raw_owned(self.value.string) };
            FormDataEntryValue::USVString(UsvString::from_utf16_string(&string))
        } else {
            // SAFETY: The caller passes a live cell of a File.
            FormDataEntryValue::File(unsafe { cell_from_abi(self.value.file) })
        };
        (UsvString::from_utf16_string(&name), value)
    }
}

/// A new FormData whose entry list is the entries that C++ hands over.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `vm` must be the live VM, and `entries` entries that C++ hands over, whose files it keeps alive for the call.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_form_data_create(vm: &Vm, entries: ak::Span<'_, EntryAbi>) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(allocate(vm, |defer_gc| {
        let entry_list = entries
            .as_slice()
            .iter()
            .map(|entry| {
                // SAFETY: The caller hands over the entries, each of which is read once.
                unsafe { core::ptr::read(entry).into_entry() }
            })
            .collect();
        FormData::new(defer_gc, entry_list)
    }))
}

/// The size of the entry list of the FormData.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_form_data_entry_count(cell: &InterfaceCell) -> usize {
    let form_data: Ref<FormData> = cell.object();
    form_data.entry_list().len()
}

/// The entry at the index in the entry list of the FormData. C++ owns its strings.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_form_data_entry(cell: &InterfaceCell, index: usize) -> EntryAbi {
    let form_data: Ref<FormData> = cell.object();
    EntryAbi::from_entry(&form_data.entry_list()[index])
}

/// The value of the first entry named `name`, a raw AK::Utf16String that C++ hands over. C++ owns the string of the
/// value.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_form_data_value_named(
    cell: &InterfaceCell,
    name: Utf16String,
    out_value: &mut EntryValueAbi,
) -> bool {
    let (form_data, name): (Ref<FormData>, _) = (cell.object(), name);
    let Some(value) = form_data.value_named(&UsvString::from_utf16_string(&name)) else {
        return false;
    };
    *out_value = EntryValueAbi::from_value(&value);
    true
}

/// Creates an entry with the name and the Blob or File `blob`, or the string if `blob` is null. C++ hands over the raw
/// AK::Utf16Strings and owns those of the entry,
/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#create-an-entry
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_html_create_an_entry(
    vm: &Vm,
    name: Utf16String,
    blob: Option<&InterfaceCell>,
    string: Utf16String,
) -> EntryAbi {
    let value = match blob {
        Some(blob) => StringOrBlob::Blob(any_blob_from_abi(blob)),
        None => StringOrBlob::String(string),
    };
    EntryAbi::from_entry(&create_an_entry(vm, &name, value, None))
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_xhr_create(vm: &Vm, realm: Gc<Realm>) -> *mut c_void {
    cell_into_abi(XMLHttpRequest::create(vm, realm))
}

/// https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-xmlhttprequest-send
///
/// # Safety
///
/// `sync_send` must be the live flags of the send() of the XMLHttpRequest.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_xhr_process_response_consume_body(
    _vm: &Vm,
    xhr: &InterfaceCell,
    sync_send: *mut c_void,
    response: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::ResponseView>,
    kind: u8,
    bytes: ak::Span<'_, u8>,
) {
    let (xhr, response) = (xhr.object::<XMLHttpRequest>(), CppResponseView::from_lent(response));
    // SAFETY: The caller passes the live flags of its send().
    let sync_send = unsafe { sync_send_from_abi(sync_send) };
    let null_or_failure_or_bytes = match kind {
        0 => NullOrFailureOrBytes::Null,
        1 => NullOrFailureOrBytes::Failure,
        _ => NullOrFailureOrBytes::Bytes(bytes.as_slice()),
    };
    xhr.process_response_consume_body(&sync_send, response, null_or_failure_or_bytes);
}

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn web_rust_xhr_fetch_stopped(
    vm: &Vm,
    xhr: &InterfaceCell,
    fetch_controller: &LentCppCell<cpp_class::FetchController>,
) {
    let (xhr, fetch_controller) = (
        xhr.object::<XMLHttpRequest>(),
        CppFetchController::from_lent(fetch_controller),
    );
    XMLHttpRequest::fetch_stopped(xhr, vm, fetch_controller);
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `sync_send` must be the live flags of a send().
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn web_rust_xhr_sync_send_is_over(sync_send: *mut c_void) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes the live flags of a send().
    unsafe { sync_send_from_abi(sync_send) }.is_over()
}

/// # Safety
///
/// `sync_send` must be the live flags of a send().
unsafe fn sync_send_from_abi(sync_send: *mut c_void) -> SyncSendRef {
    // SAFETY: The caller passes the live flags of a send().
    unsafe { Gc::from_non_null(NonNull::new(sync_send.cast()).expect("C++ passes the flags of a send()")) }
}

//! FormData, https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-formdata

use core::cell;
use core::ffi::c_void;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{DeferGc, GcRefCell, MarkedVec, RawNativeFunctionResult, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::conversions::{CppInterface, UsvString};
use crate::bindings::interface::{Inherits, Ref, Wrappable, allocate, cell_from_abi};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::file_api::blob::{AnyBlob, BlobPropertyBag, EndingType};
use crate::file_api::file::{File, FilePropertyBag};

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn web_form_data_create_from_form(
        realm: *mut c_void,
        form: *mut c_void,
        submitter: *mut c_void,
        out_form_data: &mut *mut c_void,
    ) -> RawNativeFunctionResult;
}

/// https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#formdataentryvalue
#[derive(Clone, Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) enum FormDataEntryValue {
    File(Ref<File>),
    USVString(UsvString),
}

/// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#form-entry
pub(crate) type Entry = (UsvString, FormDataEntryValue);

pub(crate) enum StringOrBlob {
    String(Utf16String),
    Blob(AnyBlob),
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#create-an-entry
pub(crate) fn create_an_entry(vm: &Vm, name: &Utf16String, value: StringOrBlob, filename: Option<UsvString>) -> Entry {
    // 1. Set name to the result of converting name into a scalar value string.
    let name = UsvString::from_utf16_string(name);

    let value = match value {
        // 2. If value is a string, then set value to the result of converting value into a scalar value string.
        StringOrBlob::String(string) => FormDataEntryValue::USVString(UsvString::from_utf16_string(&string)),
        // 3. Otherwise:
        StringOrBlob::Blob(blob) => {
            // 1. If value is not a File object, then set value to a new File object, representing the same bytes, whose
            //    name attribute value is "blob".
            let file = match blob {
                AnyBlob::File(file) => file,
                AnyBlob::Blob(blob) => {
                    let options = file_property_bag(blob.type_string().clone(), None);
                    let file = File::create(blob.raw_bytes().to_vec(), Utf16String::from_ascii(b"blob"), &options);
                    allocate(vm, |_| file)
                }
            };

            // 2. If filename is given, then set value to a new File object, representing the same bytes, whose name
            //    attribute is filename.
            let file = match filename {
                Some(filename) => {
                    let blob = file.parent();
                    let options = file_property_bag(blob.type_string().clone(), Some(file.last_modified_value()));
                    let file = File::create(blob.raw_bytes().to_vec(), filename.into_utf16_string(), &options);
                    allocate(vm, |_| file)
                }
                None => file,
            };

            FormDataEntryValue::File(file)
        }
    };

    // 4. Return an entry whose name is name and whose value is value.
    (name, value)
}

fn file_property_bag(r#type: Utf16String, last_modified: Option<i64>) -> FilePropertyBag {
    FilePropertyBag {
        parent: BlobPropertyBag {
            endings: EndingType::Transparent,
            r#type,
        },
        last_modified,
    }
}

#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct FormData {
    // https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-formdata-entry-list
    entry_list: GcRefCell<Vec<Entry>>,
}

impl Wrappable for FormData {}

impl FormData {
    pub(crate) fn new(_: &DeferGc<'_>, entry_list: Vec<Entry>) -> Self {
        Self {
            entry_list: GcRefCell::new(entry_list),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn entry_list(&self) -> cell::Ref<'_, Vec<Entry>> {
        self.entry_list.borrow()
    }

    // https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-formdata
    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        form: Option<CppInterface>,
        submitter: Option<CppInterface>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<Self>> {
        // 1. If form is given, then:
        // NB: C++ runs the substeps and creates the object.
        let Some(form) = form else {
            return Ok(allocate(cx.vm(), |defer_gc| Self::new(defer_gc, Vec::new())));
        };
        let submitter = submitter.map_or(core::ptr::null_mut(), |submitter| submitter.wrapper().as_ptr().cast());
        let mut form_data = core::ptr::null_mut();
        // SAFETY: The realm and the wrappers are live.
        unsafe {
            web_form_data_create_from_form(
                cx.realm().as_ptr().cast(),
                form.wrapper().as_ptr().cast(),
                submitter,
                &mut form_data,
            )
        }
        .into_completion()?;
        // SAFETY: C++ creates a FormData when it does not throw.
        Ok(unsafe { cell_from_abi(form_data) })
    }

    // https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-formdata-append
    pub(crate) fn append(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let value be value if given; otherwise blobValue.
        // 2. Let entry be the result of creating an entry with name, value, and filename if given.
        let entry = create_an_entry(
            cx.vm(),
            name.as_utf16_string(),
            StringOrBlob::String(value.into_utf16_string()),
            None,
        );

        // 3. Append entry to this’s entry list.
        self.entry_list.borrow_mut(cx.vm()).push(entry);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-formdata-append-blob
    pub(crate) fn append_blob(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        name: UsvString,
        blob_value: AnyBlob,
        filename: Option<UsvString>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let value be value if given; otherwise blobValue.
        // 2. Let entry be the result of creating an entry with name, value, and filename if given.
        let entry = create_an_entry(
            cx.vm(),
            name.as_utf16_string(),
            StringOrBlob::Blob(blob_value),
            filename,
        );

        // 3. Append entry to this’s entry list.
        self.entry_list.borrow_mut(cx.vm()).push(entry);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-formdata-delete
    pub(crate) fn delete(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // The delete(name) method steps are to remove all entries whose name is name from this’s entry list.
        self.entry_list
            .borrow_mut(cx.vm())
            .retain(|(entry_name, _)| *entry_name != name);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-formdata-get
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, _: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<Option<FormDataEntryValue>> {
        // 1. If there is no entry whose name is name in this’s entry list, then return null.
        // 2. Return the value of the first entry whose name is name from this’s entry list.
        Ok(self.value_named(&name))
    }

    pub(crate) fn value_named(&self, name: &UsvString) -> Option<FormDataEntryValue> {
        self.entry_list
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .find(|(entry_name, _)| entry_name == name)
            .map(|(_, value)| value.clone())
    }

    // https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-formdata-getall
    pub(crate) fn get_all<'vm>(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext<'vm>,
        name: UsvString,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<MarkedVec<'vm, FormDataEntryValue>> {
        // 1. If there is no entry whose name is name in this’s entry list, then return the empty list.
        // 2. Return the values of all entries whose name is name, in order, from this’s entry list.
        let values = MarkedVec::new(cx.vm());
        for (_, value) in self
            .entry_list
            .borrow()
            .iter()
            .filter(|(entry_name, _)| *entry_name == name)
        {
            values.push(value.clone());
        }
        Ok(values)
    }

    // https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-formdata-has
    pub(crate) fn has(&self, _: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        // The has(name) method steps are to return true if there is an entry whose name is name in this’s entry list; otherwise false.
        Ok(self.value_named(&name).is_some())
    }

    // https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-formdata-set
    pub(crate) fn set(&self, cx: &mut CallContext, name: UsvString, value: UsvString) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let value be value if given; otherwise blobValue.
        // 2. Let entry be the result of creating an entry with name, value, and filename if given.
        let entry = create_an_entry(
            cx.vm(),
            name.as_utf16_string(),
            StringOrBlob::String(value.into_utf16_string()),
            None,
        );
        self.set_entry(cx.vm(), entry);
        Ok(())
    }

    // https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-formdata-set-blob
    pub(crate) fn set_blob(
        &self,
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        name: UsvString,
        blob_value: AnyBlob,
        filename: Option<UsvString>,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<()> {
        // 1. Let value be value if given; otherwise blobValue.
        // 2. Let entry be the result of creating an entry with name, value, and filename if given.
        let entry = create_an_entry(
            cx.vm(),
            name.as_utf16_string(),
            StringOrBlob::Blob(blob_value),
            filename,
        );
        self.set_entry(cx.vm(), entry);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn set_entry(&self, vm: &Vm, entry: Entry) {
        let mut entry_list = self.entry_list.borrow_mut(vm);

        // 3. If there are entries in this’s entry list whose name is name, then replace the first such entry with entry
        //    and remove the others.
        if let Some(first) = entry_list.iter().position(|(entry_name, _)| *entry_name == entry.0) {
            let mut index = 0;
            entry_list.retain(|(entry_name, _)| {
                let keep = index <= first || *entry_name != entry.0;
                index += 1;
                keep
            });
            entry_list[first] = entry;
        }
        // 4. Otherwise, append entry to this’s entry list.
        else {
            entry_list.push(entry);
        }
    }
}

// NB: The conversion of a FormDataEntryValue to a JS value is in the generated bindings.
#[cfg(web_idl_bindings)]
impl crate::bindings::iterable::PairIterable for FormData {
    type Key = UsvString;
    type Value = FormDataEntryValue;
    type Target = Ref<FormData>;

    fn iteration_target(
        _: &CallContext,
        wrapper: libjs_rust::api::Gc<libjs_rust::api::Object>,
        _: crate::bindings::iterable::IterationKind,
    ) -> Self::Target {
        crate::bindings::interface::implementation_of(wrapper)
    }

    fn value_pairs_to_iterate_over(
        target: &Self::Target,
    ) -> impl core::ops::Deref<Target = [(UsvString, FormDataEntryValue)]> + '_ {
        // The value pairs to iterate over are this’s entry list’s entries with the key being the name and the value
        // being the value.
        cell::Ref::map(target.entry_list.borrow(), Vec::as_slice)
    }
}

//! ProgressEvent, https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-progressevent

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use ak::Utf16String;
use libjs_rust::api::{Gc, Realm, Trace, Vm};

use crate::bindings::event_target::CppEvent;
use crate::bindings::interface::{Ref, Wrappable, allocate};
use crate::bindings::{CallContext, WebIdlResult};
use crate::dom::event::EventInit;

// https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dictdef-progresseventinit
pub(crate) struct ProgressEventInit {
    pub(crate) parent: EventInit,
    pub(crate) length_computable: bool,
    pub(crate) loaded: f64,
    pub(crate) total: f64,
}

// https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-progressevent
#[derive(Trace)]
#[gc(crate = libjs_rust)]
pub(crate) struct ProgressEvent {
    event: CppEvent,
    length_computable: bool,
    loaded: f64,
    total: f64,
}

impl Wrappable for ProgressEvent {
    fn cpp_parent(&self) -> Option<NonNull<c_void>> {
        self.event.as_cpp_parent()
    }
}

// https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-progressevent
impl ProgressEvent {
    pub(crate) fn create(
        vm: &Vm,
        realm: Gc<Realm>,
        event_name: &Utf16String,
        event_init: ProgressEventInit,
    ) -> Ref<ProgressEvent> {
        let event = CppEvent::create_for_owner(
            realm,
            event_name,
            event_init.parent.bubbles,
            event_init.parent.cancelable,
            event_init.parent.composed,
        );
        let object = allocate(vm, |_| ProgressEvent {
            event,
            length_computable: event_init.length_computable,
            loaded: event_init.loaded,
            total: event_init.total,
        });
        object.event.set_owner(object);
        object
    }

    pub(crate) fn construct(
        cx: &mut CallContext,
        r#type: Utf16String,
        event_init_dict: ProgressEventInit,
    ) -> WebIdlResult<Ref<ProgressEvent>> {
        Ok(Self::create(cx.vm(), cx.realm(), &r#type, event_init_dict))
    }

    pub(crate) fn event(&self) -> &CppEvent {
        &self.event
    }

    pub(crate) fn length_computable(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<bool> {
        Ok(self.length_computable)
    }

    pub(crate) fn loaded(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.loaded)
    }

    pub(crate) fn total(&self, _: &mut CallContext) -> WebIdlResult<f64> {
        Ok(self.total)
    }
}

//! XMLHttpRequestEventTarget, https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlhttprequesteventtarget

use core::ffi::c_void;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

use libjs_rust::api::Trace;

// https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlhttprequesteventtarget
#[derive(Trace)]

unsafe extern "C" fn on_bytes(bytes: *mut c_void, lent: ak::Span<'_, u8>) {
    // SAFETY: bytes is the vector of the caller, and LibWeb lends the bytes for the call.
    unsafe { *bytes.cast::<Vec<u8>>() = lent.as_slice().to_vec() };
}

unsafe extern "C" fn on_label(label: *mut c_void, lent: ak::Span<'_, u8>) {
    // SAFETY: label is the label of the caller, and LibWeb lends the label for the call.
    unsafe { *label.cast::<Option<Vec<u8>>>() = Some(lent.as_slice().to_vec()) };
}

// https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlhttprequestresponsetype
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]

    Empty,
    Arraybuffer,
    Blob,
    Document,
    Json,
    Text,
}

pub(crate) enum DocumentOrXMLHttpRequestBodyInit {
    Document(CppInterface),
    Blob(AnyBlob),
    BufferSource(BufferSource),
    FormData(Ref<FormData>),
    URLSearchParams(Ref<URLSearchParams>),
    USVString(UsvString),
}

// https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-xmlhttprequest-state
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum State {
    Unsent = 0,
    Opened = 1,
    HeadersReceived = 2,
    Loading = 3,
    Done = 4,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Response {
    NetworkError { message: &'static str, aborted: bool },
    Fetched(CppResponseView),
}

// SAFETY: A response that the fetch handed over is the only cell this reaches.
unsafe impl Trace for Response {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        if let Self::Fetched(response) = self {
            response.trace(visitor);
        }
    }
}

impl Response {
    fn network_error(message: &'static str) -> Self {
        Self::NetworkError {
            message,
            aborted: false,
        }
    }

    fn aborted_network_error() -> Self {
        Self::NetworkError {
            message: "Fetch was aborted",
            aborted: true,
        }
    }

    fn fetched(&self) -> Option<&CppResponseView> {
        match self {
            Self::NetworkError { .. } => None,
            Self::Fetched(response) => Some(response),
        }
    }

    fn is_network_error(&self) -> bool {
        self.fetched().is_none_or(CppResponseView::is_network_error)
    }

    fn aborted(&self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::NetworkError { aborted, .. } => *aborted,
            Self::Fetched(response) => response.aborted(),
        }
    }

    fn has_body(&self) -> bool {
        self.fetched().is_some_and(CppResponseView::has_body)
    }

    fn network_error_message(&self) -> Option<Utf16String> {
        match self {
            Self::NetworkError { message, .. } => Some(Utf16String::from_ascii(message.as_bytes())),
            Self::Fetched(response) => response.network_error_message(),
        }
    }

    fn extract_length(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        self.fetched().and_then(CppResponseView::extract_length)
    }

    /// The length progress events report: the extracted length, or 0 (unknown) for a body with a content coding.
    ///
    /// AD-HOC: The spec reports the extracted length. But a content-coded body's bytes count as received once they're
    ///         decoded, while its Content-Length counts the encoded bytes, so the received length could pass it — and
    ///         neither says how much of the body is left. So the length of such a body is unknown, and its progress events
    ///         aren't length-computable.
    ///         https://github.com/whatwg/xhr/issues/403
    fn progress_length(&self) -> u64 {
        if self.has_content_coding() {
            return 0;
        }
        self.extract_length().unwrap_or(0)
    }

    fn has_content_coding(&self) -> bool {
        self.fetched().is_some_and(CppResponseView::has_content_coding)
    }
}

/// https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#response-object
enum ResponseObject {
    Null,
    Document(CppCell),
    Blob(Ref<Blob>),
}

// SAFETY: The Document and the Blob are the only cells this reaches.
unsafe impl Trace for ResponseObject {
    fn trace(&self, visitor: &mut Visitor) {
        match self {
            Self::Null => {}
            Self::Document(document) => document.trace(visitor),
            Self::Blob(blob) => blob.trace(visitor),
        }
    }
}

    wrapper_world: WrapperWorld,
    object: Value,
}
