namespace Web::CSS::ComputedValuesFFI {

struct StyleRecordGroups;

}

namespace Web::CSS {

class InstalledStyle;

template<typename StyleGroup>
StyleGroup const& style_record_group(ComputedValuesFFI::StyleRecordGroups const* record);

}

namespace Web::DOM {

// Either an Element or a PseudoElement
// FIXME: Figure out const-correctness for the Element.
class WEB_API AbstractElement {
public:
    AbstractElement(GC::Ref<Element>, Optional<CSS::PseudoElement> = {}, Utf16FlyString highlight_name = {});
    AbstractElement(Element const&, Optional<CSS::PseudoElement> = {}, Utf16FlyString highlight_name = {});

    Document& document() const;

    Element& element() { return m_element; }
    Element const& element() const { return m_element; }
    Optional<CSS::PseudoElement> pseudo_element() const { return m_pseudo_element; }
    Utf16FlyString const& highlight_name() const { return m_highlight_name; }
    bool is_custom_highlight() const { return m_pseudo_element == CSS::PseudoElement::Highlight && !m_highlight_name.is_empty(); }

    Layout::NodeWithStyle* layout_node(Layout::BegunRead const& read);
    Layout::NodeWithStyle const* layout_node(Layout::BegunRead const& read) const { return const_cast<AbstractElement*>(this)->layout_node(read); }

    Layout::NodeWithStyle* unsafe_layout_node(Layout::BegunRead const& read);
    Layout::NodeWithStyle const* unsafe_layout_node(Layout::BegunRead const& read) const { return const_cast<AbstractElement*>(this)->unsafe_layout_node(read); }

    struct TreeCountingFunctionResolutionContext {
        size_t sibling_count;
        size_t sibling_index;
    };
    TreeCountingFunctionResolutionContext tree_counting_function_resolution_context() const;

    GC::Ptr<Element const> parent_element() const;
    Element* flat_tree_parent_element() const;
    Optional<AbstractElement> element_to_inherit_style_from() const;
    GC::Ptr<Node> root();

    [[nodiscard]] CSS::ComputedStyleRecordView computed_style() const;
    [[nodiscard]] CSS::StyleRecordID style_record_identity() const;
    [[nodiscard]] CSS::InstalledStyle const& installed_style() const;
    [[nodiscard]] bool has_style() const { return !!style_record_identity(); }
    [[nodiscard]] CSS::ComputedValuesFFI::StyleRecordGroups const* style_record_groups() const;
    template<typename StyleGroup>
    StyleGroup const* style_group() const
    {
        auto const* groups = style_record_groups();
        if (!groups)
            return nullptr;
        return &CSS::style_record_group<StyleGroup>(groups);
    }
    GC::Ptr<CSS::CSSStyleProperties const> inline_style() const;

    void set_custom_property_data(RefPtr<CSS::CustomPropertyData const>);
    void replace_custom_property_data(Badge<CSS::StyleComputer>, RefPtr<CSS::CustomPropertyData const>, CSS::IsAnimationOverlay);
    [[nodiscard]] RefPtr<CSS::CustomPropertyData const> custom_property_data() const;
    // Whether the environment `custom_property_data()` answers is the overlay of what this element's own animations
    // sample. A child that inherits all of its parent's custom properties holds its parent's overlay itself, which is
    // not an animation of the child's.
    [[nodiscard]] bool custom_property_data_is_animation_overlay() const;
    RefPtr<CSS::StyleValue const> get_custom_property(Utf16FlyString const& name) const;

    void visit(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor) const;

    Utf16String debug_description() const;
    bool operator==(AbstractElement const&) const = default;

    CSS::StyleScope const& style_scope() const;

    void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor&) const;

private:
    GC::Ref<Element> m_element;
    Optional<CSS::PseudoElement> m_pseudo_element;
    Utf16FlyString m_highlight_name;
};

}

template<>
struct AK::Traits<Web::DOM::AbstractElement> : public DefaultTraits<Web::DOM::AbstractElement> {
    static unsigned hash(Web::DOM::AbstractElement const& key)
    {
        return pair_int_hash(pair_int_hash(ptr_hash(&key.element()), key.pseudo_element().has_value() ? to_underlying(key.pseudo_element().value()) : -1), key.highlight_name().hash());
    }
};

#pragma once

#include <LibJS/Forward.h>
#include <LibWeb/Bindings/Wrappable.h>
#include <LibWeb/Forward.h>
#include <LibWebCommon/WebIDL/Types.h>

namespace Web::DOM {

// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-range-bp
struct BoundaryPoint {
    GC::Ref<Node> node;
    WebIDL::UnsignedLong offset;
};

// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#abstractrange
class WEB_API AbstractRange : public Bindings::GCAllocatedWrappable {
    WEB_WRAPPABLE(AbstractRange, Bindings::GCAllocatedWrappable);

public:
    static constexpr GC::MemberOffset start_container_offset() { return GC_FIELD_OFFSET(AbstractRange, m_start_container); }
    static constexpr GC::MemberOffset end_container_offset() { return GC_FIELD_OFFSET(AbstractRange, m_end_container); }
    virtual ~AbstractRange() override;

    BoundaryPoint start() const { return { m_start_container, m_start_offset }; }
    GC::Ref<Node> start_container() const { return m_start_container; }
    WebIDL::UnsignedLong start_offset() const { return m_start_offset; }

    BoundaryPoint end() const { return { m_end_container, m_end_offset }; }
    GC::Ref<Node> end_container() const { return m_end_container; }
    WebIDL::UnsignedLong end_offset() const { return m_end_offset; }

    // https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#range-collapsed
    bool collapsed() const
    {
        // A range is collapsed if its start node is its end node and its start offset is its end offset.
        return start_container() == end_container() && start_offset() == end_offset();
    }

    bool operator==(AbstractRange const& other) const
    {
        return start_container() == other.start_container()
            && start_offset() == other.start_offset()
            && end_container() == other.end_container()
            && end_offset() == other.end_offset();
    }

protected:
    AbstractRange(GC::Ref<Node> start_container, WebIDL::UnsignedLong start_offset, GC::Ref<Node> end_container, WebIDL::UnsignedLong end_offset);

    virtual void visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor&) override;

    GC::NonnullMember<Node> m_start_container;
    WebIDL::UnsignedLong m_start_offset;

    GC::NonnullMember<Node> m_end_container;
    WebIDL::UnsignedLong m_end_offset;
};

}

/*

#include <LibWeb/DOM/AccessibilityChangeTracker.h>

namespace Web::DOM {

void AccessibilityChangeTracker::begin(i64 document_id, bool whole_tree)
{
    m_whole_tree = whole_tree || needs_whole_tree(document_id);
    if (m_whole_tree)
        m_states.clear();
    m_document_id = document_id;
    ++m_build;
    m_known_at_begin = m_states.size();
    m_known_noted = 0;
}

bool AccessibilityChangeTracker::note(WebView::AccessibilityNodeData const& data, u64 record_version, Optional<u64> geometry_version)
{
    auto it = m_states.find(data.id);
    if (it == m_states.end()) {
        m_states.set(data.id, {});
        it = m_states.find(data.id);
    } else if (it->value.build != m_build) {
        ++m_known_noted;
        auto const& state = it->value;
        auto unchanged = !m_whole_tree && record_version != 0 && state.record_version == record_version
            && geometry_version.has_value() && state.geometry_version == geometry_version
            && state.parent_id == data.parent_id && state.child_ids == data.child_ids && state.bounds == data.bounds
            && state.is_focused == data.is_focused && state.caret_offset == data.caret_offset
            && state.selection_start == data.selection_start && state.selection_end == data.selection_end;
        if (unchanged) {
            it->value.build = m_build;
            return false;
        }
    }
    auto& state = it->value;
    state.record_version = record_version;
    state.geometry_version = geometry_version;
    state.parent_id = data.parent_id;
    state.child_ids = data.child_ids;
    state.bounds = data.bounds;
    state.is_focused = data.is_focused;
    state.caret_offset = data.caret_offset;
    state.selection_start = data.selection_start;
    state.selection_end = data.selection_end;
    state.build = m_build;
    return true;
}

Vector<i64> AccessibilityChangeTracker::end()
{
    // Only when fewer of the nodes noted last time were noted this time are any of them gone.
    Vector<i64> removed_ids;
    if (m_known_noted == m_known_at_begin)
        return removed_ids;
    for (auto const& [id, state] : m_states) {
        if (state.build != m_build)
            removed_ids.append(id);
    }
    for (auto id : removed_ids)
        m_states.remove(id);
    return removed_ids;
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/DOM/AccessibilityChangeTracker.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/HashMap.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/Vector.h>
#include <LibGfx/Rect.h>
#include <LibWebCommon/WebView/AccessibilityNodeData.h>

namespace Web::DOM {

// Remembers what was last handed over of each node of a document's accessibility tree, so that a build can hand over
// only the nodes whose data changed since then, and the IDs of the nodes that are gone: see Document::
// build_accessibility_tree_change(). Each consumer of the tree keeps its own.
class AccessibilityChangeTracker {
public:
    struct Change {
        bool is_whole_tree { false };
        // In tree order.
        Vector<WebView::AccessibilityNodeData> nodes;
        Vector<i64> removed_ids;
    };

    // Whether the next build has to hand over the whole tree: the first for a document.
    bool needs_whole_tree(i64 document_id) const { return m_document_id != document_id; }

    // For Document::build_accessibility_tree_change(): A build begins, notes each node it reaches, and ends.
    void begin(i64 document_id, bool whole_tree);
    // Returns whether the node goes in the change. A node's data is the same as last time when its kept record and
    // geometry have the same versions (see Document::kept_accessibility_record()) and every field computed again on
    // each build is the same; a geometry version that isn't known counts as changed.
    bool note(WebView::AccessibilityNodeData const&, u64 record_version, Optional<u64> geometry_version);
    // Returns the IDs of the nodes noted last time but not this time.
    Vector<i64> end();

private:
    struct NodeState {
        u64 record_version { 0 };
        Optional<u64> geometry_version;
        i64 parent_id { -1 };
        Vector<i64> child_ids;
        Gfx::IntRect bounds;
        bool is_focused { false };
        i32 caret_offset { -1 };
        i32 selection_start { -1 };
        i32 selection_end { -1 };
        u64 build { 0 };
    };

    Optional<i64> m_document_id;
    HashMap<i64, NodeState> m_states;
    u64 m_build { 0 };
    size_t m_known_at_begin { 0 };
    size_t m_known_noted { 0 };
    bool m_whole_tree { false };
};

}

// A frame element has no ARIA role, so the tree names it with a token of its own — the way Blink's Role::kIframe and
// Gecko's roles::INTERNAL_FRAME (an OuterDocAccessible) stand apart from the ARIA roles.
static bool is_frame_element(Element const& element)
{
    return is<HTML::HTMLIFrameElement>(element) || is<HTML::HTMLFrameElement>(element);
}

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(AccessibilityTreeNode);

// The advance of one code point shaped on its own — which is what a per-character offset table wants, kerning and
// ligatures across the character boundary aside.
static float glyph_advance(Gfx::Font const& font, u32 code_point)
{
    auto string = Utf16String::from_code_point(code_point);
    return font.width(string.utf16_view());
}

static String aria_live_name(ARIA::AriaLive live)
{
    switch (live) {
    case ARIA::AriaLive::Assertive:
        return "assertive"_string;
    case ARIA::AriaLive::Off:
        return "off"_string;
    case ARIA::AriaLive::Polite:
        return "polite"_string;
    }
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

GC::Ref<AccessibilityTreeNode> AccessibilityTreeNode::create(DOM::Node const* value)
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<AccessibilityTreeNode>(value);
}

AccessibilityTreeNode::AccessibilityTreeNode(GC::Ptr<DOM::Node const> value)
    : m_value(value)
{
    m_children = {};
}

void AccessibilityTreeNode::serialize_tree_as_json(JsonObjectSerializer<Utf16StringBuilder>& object, Document const& document) const
{
    if (value()->is_document()) {
        VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
    } else if (value()->is_element()) {
        auto const* element = static_cast<DOM::Element const*>(value().ptr());

        // The tree's membership was decided when it was built (Node::build_accessibility_tree()), and a select's
        // options and optgroups are in it without passing Element::include_in_accessibility_tree() — they have no
        // layout node while the popup is closed. So, don't re-check membership here.
        MUST(object.add("type"sv, "element"sv));

        auto role = element->role_or_default();
        bool has_role = role.has_value() && !ARIA::is_abstract_role(*role);

        auto name = MUST(element->accessible_name(document));
        MUST(object.add("name"sv, name.utf16_view()));
        auto description = MUST(element->accessible_description(document));
        MUST(object.add("description"sv, description.utf16_view()));

        if (has_role)
            MUST(object.add("role"sv, ARIA::role_name(*role).utf16_view()));
        else if (is_frame_element(*element))
            MUST(object.add("role"sv, "iframe"sv));
        else
            MUST(object.add("role"sv, ""sv));
    } else if (value()->is_text()) {
        MUST(object.add("type"sv, "text"sv));

        auto const* text_node = static_cast<DOM::Text const*>(value().ptr());
        MUST(object.add("name"sv, text_node->data().utf16_view()));
        MUST(object.add("role"sv, "text leaf"sv));
    }

    MUST(object.add("id"sv, value()->unique_id().value()));

    if (value()->has_child_nodes()) {
        auto node_children = MUST(object.add_array("children"sv));
        for (auto& child : children()) {
            if (child->value()->is_uninteresting_whitespace_node())
                continue;
            JsonObjectSerializer<Utf16StringBuilder> child_object = MUST(node_children.add_object());
            child->serialize_tree_as_json(child_object, document);
            MUST(child_object.finish());
        }
        MUST(node_children.finish());
    }
}

// The viewport-relative box a node reports. A display:contents element has no layout node, so getBoundingClientRect()
// gives it an empty rect while its children are laid out in its parent's box; the union of its child elements' boxes
// stands in — the way Blink (AXNodeObject::GetRelativeBounds) and Gecko (LocalAccessible::BoundsInAppUnits) build it.
// Text directly inside such an element contributes no box of its own, so whenever the union would miss content, the
// nearest laid-out ancestor's box — which is known to contain all of it — is reported instead.
static Gfx::IntRect accessibility_bounds(Layout::BegunRead const& read, Element const& element)
{
    if (element.layout_node(read))
        return element.get_bounding_client_rect().to_type<int>();

    Gfx::IntRect united;
    bool has_bare_text = false;
    for (auto const* child = element.first_child(); child; child = child->next_sibling()) {
        if (auto const* child_element = as_if<Element>(*child)) {
            // A child that isn't rendered at all (display:none, so no layout node and not display:contents) has no box,
            // and neither does anything inside it. Left in, its text would count as bare text below and pull the
            // nearest laid-out ancestor's box into the union.
            if (!child_element->layout_node(read) && !child_element->has_display_contents())
                continue;
            auto rect = accessibility_bounds(read, *child_element);
            if (!rect.is_empty())
                united = united.is_empty() ? rect : united.united(rect);
        } else if (child->is_text() && !child->is_uninteresting_whitespace_node()) {
            has_bare_text = true;
        }
    }
    if (!united.is_empty() && !has_bare_text)
        return united;

    for (auto ancestor = element.parent_element(); ancestor; ancestor = ancestor->parent_element()) {
        if (ancestor->layout_node(read))
            return ancestor->get_bounding_client_rect().to_type<int>();
    }
    return united;
}

// The union of a text node's rendered fragments in viewport space, through the Element::get_bounding_client_rect()
// transform — so a text leaf's box sits in the same space as every element's. That's the box Blink, WebKit and
// Gecko report for a text leaf (LayoutText::LocalBoundingBoxRectForAccessibility unions its line-box rects;
// AccessibilityRenderObject::boundingBoxRect takes RenderText::absoluteQuads; LocalAccessible::ParentRelativeBounds
// unions the text frame's in-flow rects). Empty when the text renders no fragment.
static Optional<CSSPixelRect> text_bounding_client_rect(Document const& document, Layout::Node const& layout_node)
{
    Layout::RustFFI::FfiViewportMapping viewport_mapping {};
    if (!document.can_compute_client_rects_without_accumulated_visual_contexts_update(layout_node))
        viewport_mapping = Painting::viewport_mapping(document);
    Optional<CSSPixelRect> united;
    Layout::RustFFI::layout_script_text_range_rects(
        layout_node.document_host(), Layout::Node::slot_id(&layout_node),
        to_underlying(Painting::SelectionState::Full), 0, 0, 0, NumericLimits<size_t>::max(),
        viewport_mapping, &united, [](void* context, CSSPixelRect rect) {
            auto& united = *static_cast<Optional<CSSPixelRect>*>(context);
            united = united.has_value() ? united->united(rect) : rect;
        });
    return united;
}

// The name and description that the accessibility tree reports for an element.
Document::CachedAccessibleText AccessibilityTreeNode::compute_accessible_text(Element const& element, Document const& document)
{
    Document::CachedAccessibleText text;
    // aria-label and aria-labelledby win over an option's own label/text — and accessible_name() resolves them
    // even though the option has no layout node. For an option with neither, accessible_name() is unreliable
    // (the option renders only in a popup) — so fall back to its label attribute or text.
    if (auto const* option = as_if<HTML::HTMLOptionElement>(element)) {
        auto has_aria_name = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_label).has_value()
            || element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_labelled_by).has_value();
        if (has_aria_name)
            text.name = MUST(element.accessible_name(document)).to_utf8();
        else if (auto label = option->label(); !label.is_empty())
            text.name = label.to_utf8();
        else
            text.name = option->text().to_utf8();
    } else if (auto const* group = as_if<HTML::HTMLOptGroupElement>(element)) {
        // Like an option, an optgroup only renders inside the popup, so accessible_name() comes back empty.
        if (auto label = group->attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::label); label.has_value())
            text.name = label->to_utf8();
    } else {
        text.name = MUST(element.accessible_name(document)).to_utf8();
    }
    if (auto trimmed = text.name.bytes_as_string_view().trim_whitespace(); trimmed != text.name.bytes_as_string_view())
        text.name = MUST(String::from_utf8(trimmed));
    text.description = MUST(element.accessible_description(document)).to_utf8();
    if (text.description.is_empty()) {
        if (auto desc = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_description); desc.has_value())
            text.description = desc.release_value().to_utf8();
    }
    return text;
}

// Fills in where each character of a text leaf renders, relative to the text's own top-left; where its lines break and
// how tall they are; and, once its lines are known, its bounds. Any layout can change all of that, with nothing changing
// in the text node itself, so it's computed again on every build of the tree.
// Returns whether the geometry came from the lines layout rendered the text on, rather than from font metrics alone.
static bool fill_text_geometry(WebView::AccessibilityNodeData& node_data, DOM::Text const& text_node, Gfx::Font const* font, Document const& document, Layout::BegunRead const& read)
{
    // Compute per-character (x, y) offsets and line-break positions. Visual lines give the DOM offsets
    // of each rendered line of this text node; the caret rect at a line's first offset gives that line's
    // origin and height. Text that renders no lines falls back to a single-line font-metrics computation.
    auto utf8 = node_data.name.bytes_as_string_view();
    Utf8View view { utf8 };

    auto* layout = text_node.layout_node(read);

    // The caret rect at a DOM offset is document-absolute and spans the height of the text on the line the offset
    // renders on, which is what a line's geometry is read from here.
    auto line_rect_at_offset = [&](size_t offset) -> Optional<CSSPixelRect> {
        if (!layout)
            return {};
        Compositing::RustFFI::NodeSlotId const no_slot { Compositing::RustFFI::INVALID_NODE_SLOT_INDEX };
        Layout::RustFFI::FfiCaret caret;
        Layout::RustFFI::layout_script_caret(layout->document_host(),
            { .node = Layout::Node::slot_id(layout), .offset = offset, .downstream = true, .child_before = no_slot, .child_before_length = 0, .child_after = no_slot },
            {}, &caret);
        if (!caret.found)
            return {};
        return caret.rect;
    };

    Vector<Layout::RustFFI::FfiVisualLine> lines;
    if (layout) {
        Layout::RustFFI::render_state_text_visual_lines(layout->document_host(), Layout::Node::slot_id(layout), &lines,
            [](void* context, Layout::RustFFI::FfiVisualLine line) {
                static_cast<Vector<Layout::RustFFI::FfiVisualLine>*>(context)->append(line);
            });
    }
    struct RenderedLine {
        Layout::RustFFI::FfiVisualLine line;
        CSSPixelRect rect;
    };
    Vector<RenderedLine> rendered_lines;
    for (auto const& line : lines) {
        if (auto rect = line_rect_at_offset(line.start_offset); rect.has_value())
            rendered_lines.append({ line, *rect });
    }

    if (!rendered_lines.is_empty()) {
        if (auto own_box = text_bounding_client_rect(document, *layout); own_box.has_value())
            node_data.bounds = own_box->to_type<int>();

        // Report positions relative to the text's own top-left (its leftmost line's left edge and its
        // topmost line's top): Caret rects are document-absolute, so the offsets don't move with scrolling,
        // and node_data.bounds' top-left is that same point in viewport space — so bounds' top-left plus an
        // offset is where the character is on screen.
        auto text_origin = rendered_lines.first().rect.top_left();
        for (auto const& rendered : rendered_lines) {
            text_origin.set_x(min(text_origin.x(), rendered.rect.x()));
            text_origin.set_y(min(text_origin.y(), rendered.rect.y()));
        }
        auto text_utf16 = text_node.data().utf16_view();

        // The document-absolute x where each DOM offset's character starts, and where each fragment's text
        // ends, from the glyph runs layout shaped the text into.
        struct CharacterXPositions {
            Vector<Optional<float>> start_x;
            Vector<Optional<float>> fragment_end_x;
        };
        CharacterXPositions x_positions;
        x_positions.start_x.resize(text_utf16.length_in_code_units() + 1);
        x_positions.fragment_end_x.resize(text_utf16.length_in_code_units() + 1);
        Layout::RustFFI::layout_script_text_character_x_positions(
            layout->document_host(), Layout::Node::slot_id(layout), &x_positions,
            [](void* context, size_t offset, float x, bool is_fragment_end) {
                auto& positions = *static_cast<CharacterXPositions*>(context);
                auto& list = is_fragment_end ? positions.fragment_end_x : positions.start_x;
                if (offset < list.size())
                    list[offset] = x;
            });
        auto origin_x = text_origin.x().to_float();
        auto known_x = [&](Vector<Optional<float>> const& list, size_t offset) -> Optional<float> {
            if (offset >= list.size() || !list[offset].has_value())
                return {};
            return *list[offset] - origin_x;
        };

        // Where the rendered text last reached: the position of the characters no line renders.
        Optional<Gfx::IntPoint> rendered_end;
        for (auto const& [line, line_rect] : rendered_lines) {
            auto line_top_y = static_cast<i32>(line_rect.y().to_int() - text_origin.y().to_int());
            auto line_left_x = static_cast<i32>(line_rect.x().to_int() - text_origin.x().to_int());
            auto line_height = static_cast<i32>(line_rect.height().to_int());
            // A visual line's offsets index the DOM data(), which is what node_data.name and text_utf16
            // hold. Collapsed whitespace renders on no line: a line starts past any leading run, and its
            // end_offset excludes the run hanging at a soft wrap.
            auto line_character_start = text_utf16.code_point_offset_of(line.start_offset);
            auto line_character_end = text_utf16.code_point_offset_of(line.end_offset);
            // Entry N is character N's position, so the characters no line renders take the position the
            // rendered text last reached (a leading run: the first line's start), and the first line starts
            // at character 0, leading run included.
            auto gap_position = rendered_end.value_or(Gfx::IntPoint { line_left_x, line_top_y });
            while (node_data.character_offsets.size() < line_character_start)
                node_data.character_offsets.append(gap_position);
            node_data.line_break_character_offsets.append(node_data.line_break_character_offsets.is_empty() ? 0 : static_cast<i32>(line_character_start));
            node_data.line_heights.append(line_height);
            // Each character's x is where layout's glyph run puts it. A character layout gives no position
            // to (whitespace that collapsed away) takes no width: It sits where the next positioned character
            // on the line starts, or where the line ends. Only a line layout positions nothing on (e.g. vertical
            // text) falls back to advancing each character by its own width, shaped on its own.
            auto utf8_start = view.byte_offset_of(line_character_start);
            auto utf8_end = view.byte_offset_of(line_character_end);
            Utf8View line_view { utf8.substring_view(utf8_start, utf8_end - utf8_start) };
            Vector<u32> line_code_points;
            Vector<Optional<float>> line_x;
            size_t code_unit_offset = line.start_offset;
            for (u32 code_point : line_view) {
                line_code_points.append(code_point);
                line_x.append(known_x(x_positions.start_x, code_unit_offset));
                code_unit_offset += code_point > 0xFFFF ? 2 : 1;
            }
            auto line_end_x = known_x(x_positions.fragment_end_x, line.end_offset);
            bool layout_positions_line = line_end_x.has_value() || any_of(line_x, [](auto const& x) { return x.has_value(); });

            float end_x = static_cast<float>(line_left_x);
            if (layout_positions_line) {
                Optional<float> next_x = line_end_x;
                for (size_t i = line_x.size(); i-- > 0;) {
                    if (line_x[i].has_value())
                        next_x = line_x[i];
                    else
                        line_x[i] = next_x;
                }
                Optional<float> previous_x;
                for (auto& x : line_x) {
                    if (!x.has_value())
                        x = previous_x.value_or(static_cast<float>(line_left_x));
                    previous_x = x;
                }
                end_x = line_end_x.value_or(previous_x.value_or(static_cast<float>(line_left_x)));
            } else {
                for (size_t i = 0; i < line_x.size(); ++i) {
                    line_x[i] = end_x;
                    end_x += font ? glyph_advance(*font, line_code_points[i]) : 0.0f;
                }
            }
            for (auto const& x : line_x)
                node_data.character_offsets.append(Gfx::IntPoint { static_cast<i32>(*x), line_top_y });
            rendered_end = Gfx::IntPoint { static_cast<i32>(end_x), line_top_y };
        }
        // A trailing run that renders on no line, likewise.
        while (rendered_end.has_value() && node_data.character_offsets.size() < view.length())
            node_data.character_offsets.append(*rendered_end);
        return true;
    }
    if (font) {
        // Fallback: single-line font-metrics computation.
        node_data.line_break_character_offsets.append(0);
        node_data.line_heights.append(node_data.bounds.height());
        float cumulative = 0;
        for (u32 code_point : view) {
            node_data.character_offsets.append(Gfx::IntPoint { static_cast<i32>(cumulative), 0 });
            cumulative += glyph_advance(*font, code_point);
        }
    }
    return false;
}

// What layout computes a text node's character geometry from, or nothing when that can't be told.
static Optional<Document::CachedTextGeometry> text_geometry_sources(Layout::Node const& layout)
{
    Document::CachedTextGeometry geometry;
    auto known = Layout::RustFFI::layout_script_text_geometry_sources(
        layout.document_host(), Layout::Node::slot_id(&layout), &geometry,
        [](void* context, Layout::RustFFI::InlineContent const* line_content, i32 x, i32 y) {
            static_cast<Document::CachedTextGeometry*>(context)->sources.append({ line_content, x, y });
        });
    if (!known)
        return {};
    return geometry;
}

// Keeps the geometry just computed into the node's data, with what layout computed it from, and returns the version it
// gets: or nothing, when it can't be kept.
static Optional<u64> keep_text_geometry(WebView::AccessibilityNodeData const& node_data, DOM::Text const& text_node, Document const& document, Document::CachedTextGeometry geometry)
{
    geometry.character_offsets = node_data.character_offsets;
    geometry.line_break_character_offsets = node_data.line_break_character_offsets;
    geometry.line_heights = node_data.line_heights;
    if (auto version = document.cache_text_geometry(text_node, move(geometry)))
        return version;
    return {};
}

// The fields that can change with nothing changing in the node itself or its style: its bounds and text geometry,
// which any layout can move, and whether it has the focus. They're computed again even for a node whose other fields
// are kept from the last build.
static Optional<u64> fill_volatile_fields(WebView::AccessibilityNodeData& node_data, DOM::Node const& node, Document const& document, Layout::BegunRead const& read)
{
    node_data.bounds = {};
    node_data.is_focused = false;
    node_data.character_offsets.clear();
    node_data.line_break_character_offsets.clear();
    node_data.line_heights.clear();
    if (auto const* element = as_if<DOM::Element>(node)) {
        node_data.bounds = accessibility_bounds(read, *element);
        node_data.is_focused = element->is_focused();
        return 0;
    }
    auto const* text_node = as_if<DOM::Text>(node);
    if (!text_node)
        return 0;
    auto parent = text_node->parent_element();
    if (!parent)
        return 0;
    node_data.bounds = accessibility_bounds(read, *parent);
    if (!parent->style_group<CSS::ComputedValues::FontValues>() || !parent->style_group<CSS::ComputedValues::InheritedTextValues>())
        return 0;
    Gfx::Font const* font = nullptr;
    if (auto layout = parent->layout_node(read))
        font = &layout->first_available_font();

    // Text geometry is the costliest part of a build, so keep it for as long as the lines it came from stay the same.
    // Only its bounds are read again: They're viewport-relative, so scrolling moves them.
    auto* text_layout = text_node->layout_node(read);
    auto geometry = text_layout ? text_geometry_sources(*text_layout) : Optional<Document::CachedTextGeometry> {};
    if (geometry.has_value()) {
        if (auto const* kept = document.cached_text_geometry(*text_node); kept && kept->sources == geometry->sources) {
            if (auto own_box = text_bounding_client_rect(document, *text_layout); own_box.has_value())
                node_data.bounds = own_box->to_type<int>();
            node_data.character_offsets = kept->character_offsets;
            node_data.line_break_character_offsets = kept->line_break_character_offsets;
            node_data.line_heights = kept->line_heights;
            return kept->version;
        }
    }
    if (!fill_text_geometry(node_data, *text_node, font, document, read) || !geometry.has_value())
        return {};
    return keep_text_geometry(node_data, *text_node, document, geometry.release_value());
}

static bool should_skip_child_in_node_data(AccessibilityTreeNode const& child)
{
    if (child.value()->is_uninteresting_whitespace_node())
        return true;
    if (child.value()->is_text()) {
        for (auto* ancestor = child.value()->parent(); ancestor; ancestor = ancestor->parent()) {
            if (is<HTML::HTMLHeadElement>(*ancestor))
                return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

void AccessibilityTreeNode::serialize_tree_as_node_data(Vector<WebView::AccessibilityNodeData>& out, Document const& document, Layout::BegunRead const& read, i64 parent_id, AccessibilityChangeTracker* tracker) const
{
    // Each node comes out before its subtree, and its children in order: a depth-first walk. It's done with a stack of
    // its own rather than by recursion, since a page's DOM can be many thousands of levels deep, and a frame per level
    // would exhaust the thread's stack.
    // The nodes still to serialize, each with its parent's ID at the same index of pending_parent_ids.
    GC::RootVector<GC::Ref<AccessibilityTreeNode const>> pending_nodes;
    Vector<i64> pending_parent_ids;
    pending_nodes.append(*this);
    pending_parent_ids.append(parent_id);
    while (!pending_nodes.is_empty()) {
        auto node = pending_nodes.take_last();
        auto node_parent_id = pending_parent_ids.take_last();
        auto id = node->serialize_node_as_node_data(out, document, read, node_parent_id, tracker);
        auto children = node->children();
        for (size_t i = children.size(); i > 0; --i) {
            if (should_skip_child_in_node_data(*children[i - 1]))
                continue;
            pending_nodes.append(*children[i - 1]);
            pending_parent_ids.append(id);
        }
    }
}

i64 AccessibilityTreeNode::serialize_node_as_node_data(Vector<WebView::AccessibilityNodeData>& out, Document const& document, Layout::BegunRead const& read, i64 parent_id, AccessibilityChangeTracker* tracker) const
{
    WebView::AccessibilityNodeData node_data;
    node_data.parent_id = parent_id;

    // While an assistive technology consumes the tree, it's rebuilt after every change to the page. So keep what each
    // node's data holds from one build to the next until a change to the node or its style could alter it, and compute
    // again just the fields that can change without one.
    auto keeps_records = document.page().accessibility_interested();
    // What a change tracker tells this build of the node from the last one by: see AccessibilityChangeTracker::note().
    u64 record_version = 0;
    Optional<u64> geometry_version;
    if (auto kept = keeps_records ? document.kept_accessibility_record(*value()) : Document::KeptAccessibilityRecord {}; kept.data) {
        node_data = *kept.data;
        record_version = kept.version;
        geometry_version = fill_volatile_fields(node_data, *value(), document, read);
    } else {
        if (!value()->is_text())
            geometry_version = 0;
        bool text_geometry_from_lines = false;
        if (value()->is_element()) {
            auto const& element = static_cast<DOM::Element const&>(*value());

            node_data.id = static_cast<i64>(element.unique_id().value());
            // role_or_default() already applies the presentational-role conflict rules: a none/presentation role on an
            // element that's focusable or carries a global ARIA attribute is ignored, and the implicit role comes back in
            // its place — as Blink/WebKit/Gecko do in AXObject::DetermineAriaRole() / AccessibilityNodeObject::
            // determineAriaRoleAttribute() / nsAccessibilityService::CreateAccessible() before they fall back to the
            // element's own implicit role.
            auto role = element.role_or_default();
            if (role.has_value() && !ARIA::is_abstract_role(*role))
                node_data.role = ARIA::role_name(*role).to_utf8();
            else if (is_frame_element(element))
                node_data.role = "iframe"_string;

            // While an assistive technology consumes the tree, it's rebuilt after every change to the page, so keep each
            // element's name and description from one build to the next until a change could alter them.
            Document::CachedAccessibleText text;
            if (!document.page().accessibility_interested() || document.accessibility_caches_bypassed()) {
                text = compute_accessible_text(element, document);
            } else if (auto const* cached = document.cached_accessible_text(element)) {
                text = *cached;
            } else {
                text = compute_accessible_text(element, document);
                document.cache_accessible_text(element, text);
            }
            node_data.name = move(text.name);
            node_data.description = move(text.description);
            node_data.bounds = accessibility_bounds(read, element);

            // aria-level is a heading's level only on a heading. On a treeitem, row or listitem it's the item's depth,
            // which the bridges expose as a hierarchical level (the ATK "level" object attribute, AXDisclosureLevel) and
            // never as the node's value — the split WebKit (AccessibilityNodeObject::headingLevel() vs. AXCoreObject::
            // hierarchicalLevel()), Blink (AXNodeObject::HeadingLevel() vs. AXNodeObject::HierarchicalLevel()) and Gecko
            // (HTMLHeadingAccessible vs. GroupPosition().level) all make. On any other role aria-level is an author error
            // and is ignored. A treeitem's depth isn't computed from its nesting yet, as Blink's HierarchicalLevel() does.
            if (auto level = element.aria_level(); level.has_value() && role.has_value()) {
                if (auto parsed = level->to_number<i32>(); parsed.has_value() && *parsed >= 1) {
                    if (*role == ARIA::Role::heading)
                        node_data.heading_level = *parsed;
                    else if (*role == ARIA::Role::treeitem || *role == ARIA::Role::row || *role == ARIA::Role::listitem)
                        node_data.hierarchical_level = *parsed;
                }
            }

            // https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-live
            // Only assertive, polite, and off are aria-live values. Any other value is ignored and the property treated as
            // not present (ARIA 1.2, Handling Author Errors), so the role's implicit value applies. WebKit does the same
            // (defaultLiveRegionStatusForRole(), with liveRegionStatusIsEnabled() admitting only polite and assertive);
            // Blink and Gecko instead pass an unknown value through as the platform's live attribute for the AT to judge
            // (AXObject::LiveRegionStatus(), nsAccUtils::SetLiveContainerAttributes()) — an attribute our bridges don't
            // expose. Here the value only decides whether a change is announced, and at which priority.
            auto live = ARIA::AriaData::parse_aria_live(element.aria_live());
            if (!live.has_value() && role.has_value())
                live = ARIA::implicit_aria_live_for_role(*role);
            if (live.has_value())
                node_data.live = aria_live_name(*live);

            // https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-disabled
            auto aria_disabled = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_disabled);
            if (element.is_actually_disabled() || (aria_disabled.has_value() && aria_disabled.value() == "true"sv))
                node_data.is_disabled = true;

            if (auto const* cell = as_if<HTML::HTMLTableCellElement>(element)) {
                node_data.column_span = static_cast<i32>(cell->col_span());
                node_data.row_span = static_cast<i32>(cell->row_span());

                // The cell's column index: the col_span sum of the cells before it in its row. Its row index isn't
                // serialized — both bridges derive it from the row's position in the tree.
                auto row_result = cell->closest("tr"_utf16);
                if (!row_result.is_exception() && row_result.value()) {
                    auto const* row = row_result.value();
                    i32 col_index = 0;
                    for (auto const* prev = row->first_child(); prev && prev != cell; prev = prev->next_sibling()) {
                        if (auto const* prev_cell = as_if<HTML::HTMLTableCellElement>(prev))
                            col_index += static_cast<i32>(prev_cell->col_span());
                    }
                    node_data.cell_column_index = col_index;
                }
            }

            if (auto const* table = as_if<HTML::HTMLTableElement>(element)) {
                auto rows = table->rows();
                node_data.table_row_count = static_cast<i32>(rows->length());
                // Column count: maximum over all rows of summed col_span.
                i32 max_cols = 0;
                for (u32 i = 0; i < rows->length(); ++i) {
                    auto* row = rows->item(i);
                    if (!row)
                        continue;
                    i32 cols = 0;
                    for (auto const* c = row->first_child(); c; c = c->next_sibling()) {
                        if (auto const* cell = as_if<HTML::HTMLTableCellElement>(c))
                            cols += static_cast<i32>(cell->col_span());
                    }
                    max_cols = max(max_cols, cols);
                }
                node_data.table_column_count = max_cols;

                for (auto const* c = table->first_child(); c; c = c->next_sibling()) {
                    if (c->is_element()
                        && static_cast<DOM::Element const&>(*c).tag_name().equals_ignoring_ascii_case("caption"sv)) {
                        node_data.table_caption_id = static_cast<i64>(c->unique_id().value());
                        break;
                    }
                }

                if (auto summary = table->get_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::summary); summary.has_value())
                    node_data.table_summary = summary.release_value().to_utf8();

                // Column headers: first row's th cells (or any row with explicit scope=col). Row headers: first th cell in
                // each row (or any cell with scope=row).
                node_data.column_header_ids.resize(max_cols, true);
                for (i32 c = 0; c < max_cols; ++c)
                    node_data.column_header_ids[c] = -1;
                node_data.row_header_ids.resize(rows->length(), true);
                for (u32 r = 0; r < rows->length(); ++r)
                    node_data.row_header_ids[r] = -1;

                for (u32 row_index = 0; row_index < rows->length(); ++row_index) {
                    auto* row = rows->item(row_index);
                    if (!row)
                        continue;
                    i32 col_index = 0;
                    for (auto const* c = row->first_child(); c; c = c->next_sibling()) {
                        auto const* cell = as_if<HTML::HTMLTableCellElement>(c);
                        if (!cell)
                            continue;
                        auto cell_id = static_cast<i64>(cell->unique_id().value());
                        auto tag = cell->tag_name();
                        auto scope_attr = cell->get_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::scope).value_or({});
                        auto scope = scope_attr.utf16_view();
                        bool is_th = tag.equals_ignoring_ascii_case("th"sv);
                        if (is_th && (scope == "col"sv || (scope.is_empty() && row_index == 0))) {
                            if (col_index < max_cols)
                                node_data.column_header_ids[col_index] = cell_id;
                        }
                        if (is_th && (scope == "row"sv || (scope.is_empty() && col_index == 0))) {
                            if (row_index < node_data.row_header_ids.size())
                                node_data.row_header_ids[row_index] = cell_id;
                        }
                        col_index += static_cast<i32>(cell->col_span());
                    }
                }
            }

            // The text a control now holds, which AT reads back as its value. A password field's is the mask the field
            // renders — one U+25CF BLACK CIRCLE per code point, as text_transform.rs draws it — never the text typed,
            // so an AT's caret and selection offsets stay valid without the password reaching every AT client. That's
            // the rendered text WebKit (AccessibilityRenderObject::secureFieldValue()) and Blink (AXNodeObject::
            // GetValueForControl() masks with the text-security character) hand out; Gecko (HTMLTextFieldAccessible::
            // Value()) exposes no value for a password field at all.
            if (auto const* input = as_if<HTML::HTMLInputElement>(element)) {
                using TAS = HTML::HTMLInputElement::TypeAttributeState;
                auto type = input->type_state();
                if (type == TAS::Text || type == TAS::Search || type == TAS::Email || type == TAS::Telephone
                    || type == TAS::URL) {
                    node_data.value = input->value().to_utf8();
                } else if (type == TAS::Password) {
                    node_data.is_password = true;
                    node_data.value = MUST(String::repeated(0x25CF, input->value().length_in_code_points()));
                }
            } else if (auto const* text_area = as_if<HTML::HTMLTextAreaElement>(element)) {
                node_data.value = text_area->value().to_utf8();
            }

            // AtkValue fields for numeric-value elements.
            if (auto const* progress = as_if<HTML::HTMLProgressElement>(element)) {
                node_data.value_numeric = progress->value();
                node_data.value_minimum = 0.0;
                node_data.value_maximum = progress->max();
            } else if (auto const* meter = as_if<HTML::HTMLMeterElement>(element)) {
                node_data.value_numeric = meter->value();
                node_data.value_minimum = meter->min();
                node_data.value_maximum = meter->max();
            } else if (auto const* input = as_if<HTML::HTMLInputElement>(element)) {
                if (input->value_as_number_applies()) {
                    // NB: An input whose value is not a number, such as an empty one, has a NaN valueAsNumber.
                    if (auto number = input->value_as_number(); !isnan(number))
                        node_data.value_numeric = number;
                    if (auto min_attr = input->get_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::min); min_attr.has_value()) {
                        if (auto parsed = min_attr->to_number<double>(); parsed.has_value())
                            node_data.value_minimum = *parsed;
                    }
                    if (auto max_attr = input->get_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::max); max_attr.has_value()) {
                        if (auto parsed = max_attr->to_number<double>(); parsed.has_value())
                            node_data.value_maximum = *parsed;
                    }
                    if (auto step_attr = input->get_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::step); step_attr.has_value()) {
                        if (auto parsed = step_attr->to_number<double>(); parsed.has_value())
                            node_data.value_step = *parsed;
                    }
                }
            }

            // AtkSelection state. An <option> carries the state in the host language; anything else, such as a
            // role="option" element, carries it in aria-selected.
            // https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-selected
            if (auto const* option = as_if<HTML::HTMLOptionElement>(element)) {
                node_data.is_selected = option->selected();
            } else if (auto aria_selected = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_selected); aria_selected.has_value()) {
                node_data.is_selected = aria_selected.value() == "true"sv;
            }

            // A checkbox or radio button carries the state in the host language, which wins over aria-checked. Any other
            // element (including an input whose role's been overridden to one that's checkable) takes it from aria-checked.
            if (auto const* input = as_if<HTML::HTMLInputElement>(element);
                input && (input->type_state() == HTML::HTMLInputElement::TypeAttributeState::Checkbox || input->type_state() == HTML::HTMLInputElement::TypeAttributeState::RadioButton)) {
                if (input->indeterminate())
                    node_data.checked_state = WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::CheckedState::Mixed;
                else
                    node_data.checked_state = input->checked()
                        ? WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::CheckedState::Checked
                        : WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::CheckedState::Unchecked;
            } else if (auto aria_checked = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_checked); aria_checked.has_value()) {
                auto value = aria_checked.value();
                if (value == "true"sv)
                    node_data.checked_state = WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::CheckedState::Checked;
                else if (value == "false"sv)
                    node_data.checked_state = WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::CheckedState::Unchecked;
                else if (value == "mixed"sv)
                    node_data.checked_state = WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::CheckedState::Mixed;
            }

            if (auto const* details = as_if<HTML::HTMLDetailsElement>(element)) {
                node_data.expanded_state = details->has_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::open)
                    ? WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::ExpandedState::Expanded
                    : WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::ExpandedState::Collapsed;
            } else if (auto aria_expanded = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_expanded);
                aria_expanded.has_value()) {
                auto value = aria_expanded.value();
                if (value == "true"sv)
                    node_data.expanded_state = WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::ExpandedState::Expanded;
                else if (value == "false"sv)
                    node_data.expanded_state = WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::ExpandedState::Collapsed;
            }

            // Editable/multi-line/read-only for text inputs and textareas and contenteditable.
            auto is_readonly_attr = element.has_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::readonly);
            auto is_required_attr = element.has_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::required);
            if (auto const* input = as_if<HTML::HTMLInputElement>(element)) {
                // Only text-like inputs are "editable"; checkbox/radio/button/submit, etc., are form controls but not
                // text-editable. AT-SPI2's EDITABLE state refers specifically to text editing.
                using TAS = HTML::HTMLInputElement::TypeAttributeState;
                auto type = input->type_state();
                bool is_text_type = type == TAS::Text || type == TAS::Search || type == TAS::Email
                    || type == TAS::Password || type == TAS::Telephone || type == TAS::URL || type == TAS::Number;
                if (is_text_type && !is_readonly_attr)
                    node_data.is_editable = true;
                if (is_text_type && is_readonly_attr)
                    node_data.is_read_only = true;
                if (is_required_attr)
                    node_data.is_required = true;
            } else if (is<HTML::HTMLTextAreaElement>(element)) {
                if (!is_readonly_attr)
                    node_data.is_editable = true;
                if (is_readonly_attr)
                    node_data.is_read_only = true;
                if (is_required_attr)
                    node_data.is_required = true;
                node_data.is_multi_line = true;
            } else if (element.is_editable_or_editing_host()) {
                node_data.is_editable = true;
                node_data.is_multi_line = true; // contenteditable elements default to multi-line.
            }

            // A disabled control cannot be edited, whichever branch above decided it was editable.
            if (node_data.is_disabled)
                node_data.is_editable = false;

            // aria-* overrides.
            if (auto ro = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_read_only);
                ro.has_value() && ro.value() == "true"sv) {
                node_data.is_read_only = true;
                node_data.is_editable = false;
            }
            if (auto req = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_required);
                req.has_value() && req.value() == "true"sv)
                node_data.is_required = true;
            if (auto ml = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_multi_line);
                ml.has_value() && ml.value() == "true"sv)
                node_data.is_multi_line = true;

            if (auto invalid = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_invalid);
                invalid.has_value() && invalid.value() != "false"sv
                && !invalid.value().is_empty())
                node_data.is_invalid = true;

            if (auto const* select = as_if<HTML::HTMLSelectElement>(element)) {
                if (select->has_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::multiple))
                    node_data.is_multi_selectable = true;
            }
            if (auto ms = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_multi_selectable);
                ms.has_value() && ms.value() == "true"sv)
                node_data.is_multi_selectable = true;

            if (auto aria_pressed = element.get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::aria_pressed); aria_pressed.has_value()) {
                auto value = aria_pressed.value();
                if (value == "true"sv)
                    node_data.pressed_state = WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::PressedState::Pressed;
                else if (value == "false"sv)
                    node_data.pressed_state = WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::PressedState::NotPressed;
                else if (value == "mixed"sv)
                    node_data.pressed_state = WebView::AccessibilityNodeData::PressedState::Mixed;
            }

            // Visited links.
            if (auto const* anchor = as_if<HTML::HTMLAnchorElement>(element)) {
                (void)anchor;
            }

            if (auto accesskey = element.get_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::accesskey); accesskey.has_value())
                node_data.keybinding = accesskey.release_value().to_utf8();

            if (auto const* anchor = as_if<HTML::HTMLAnchorElement>(element))
                node_data.url = anchor->href().to_utf8();
            else if (auto const* area = as_if<HTML::HTMLAreaElement>(element))
                node_data.url = area->href().to_utf8();

            if (auto const* html_element = as_if<HTML::HTMLHtmlElement>(element)) {
                if (auto lang = html_element->get_attribute(HTML::AttributeNames::lang); lang.has_value())
                    node_data.language = lang.release_value().to_utf8();
            }

            // Only the element that has the focus is focused — not the body that activeElement falls back to when nothing
            // does. Focus is on the document then, and the bridges hand the AT the document root, as Gecko, WebKit, and
            // Blink do (FocusManager::FocusedDOMNode() / AccessibilityNodeObject::isFocused() / AXNodeObject::IsFocused()).
            node_data.is_focused = element.is_focused();
        } else if (value()->is_text()) {
            auto const& text_node = static_cast<DOM::Text const&>(*value());
            node_data.id = static_cast<i64>(text_node.unique_id().value());
            node_data.role = "text leaf"_string;
            node_data.name = text_node.data().to_utf8();

            // A text leaf's box is the union of its rendered lines, set below once those are known. Until then — and for
            // good when the text renders no line — the parent element's box stands in.
            if (auto parent = text_node.parent_element()) {
                node_data.bounds = accessibility_bounds(read, *parent);

                // Read text formatting from the parent element's computed style. Text leaves inherit all their formatting
                // from their containing element. So this covers the common case: mixed inline text and formatting changes.
                // <p>Hello <b>world</b>: "Hello " and "world" are separate text leaves with different computed_properties.
                auto const* font_values = parent->style_group<CSS::ComputedValues::FontValues>();
                auto const* text_values = parent->style_group<CSS::ComputedValues::InheritedTextValues>();
                auto const* text_reset_values = parent->style_group<CSS::ComputedValues::TextResetValues>();
                auto const* background_values = parent->style_group<CSS::ComputedValues::BackgroundValues>();
                if (font_values && text_values) {
                    Gfx::Font const* font = nullptr;
                    if (auto layout = parent->layout_node(read)) {
                        font = &layout->first_available_font();
                        node_data.font_family = font->family().to_string();
                    }
                    node_data.font_size = MUST(String::formatted("{}", font_values->font_size.to_double()));
                    node_data.font_weight = MUST(String::formatted("{}", font_values->font_weight));

                    switch (font_values->font_style_keyword()) {
                    case CSS::FontStyleKeyword::Italic:
                        node_data.font_style = "italic"_string;
                        break;
                    case CSS::FontStyleKeyword::Oblique:
                        node_data.font_style = "oblique"_string;
                        break;
                    default:
                        node_data.font_style = "normal"_string;
                        break;
                    }

                    StringBuilder decoration_builder;
                    for (auto line : text_reset_values ? text_reset_values->decoration_lines() : ReadonlySpan<CSS::TextDecorationLine> {}) {
                        if (!decoration_builder.is_empty())
                            decoration_builder.append(' ');
                        switch (line) {
                        case CSS::TextDecorationLine::Underline:
                            decoration_builder.append("underline"sv);
                            break;
                        case CSS::TextDecorationLine::LineThrough:
                            decoration_builder.append("line-through"sv);
                            break;
                        case CSS::TextDecorationLine::Overline:
                            decoration_builder.append("overline"sv);
                            break;
                        case CSS::TextDecorationLine::Blink:
                            decoration_builder.append("blink"sv);
                            break;
                        default:
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    node_data.text_decoration = decoration_builder.is_empty()
                        ? "none"_string
                        : MUST(decoration_builder.to_string());

                    auto fg = text_values->color_value();
                    node_data.color = MUST(String::from_byte_string(fg.to_byte_string_without_alpha()));
                    auto bg = background_values ? background_values->background_color_value(fg) : Color::Transparent;
                    if (bg.alpha() > 0)
                        node_data.background_color = MUST(String::from_byte_string(bg.to_byte_string_without_alpha()));

                    text_geometry_from_lines = fill_text_geometry(node_data, text_node, font, document, read);
                }
            }
        }
        if (keeps_records) {
            record_version = document.cache_accessibility_record(*value(), node_data);
            // Keep the text's geometry with its record right away, so the next build reuses it rather than computing it
            // again.
            if (text_geometry_from_lines) {
                auto const& text_node = static_cast<DOM::Text const&>(*value());
                if (auto* text_layout = text_node.layout_node(read)) {
                    if (auto sources = text_geometry_sources(*text_layout); sources.has_value())
                        geometry_version = keep_text_geometry(node_data, text_node, document, sources.release_value());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    node_data.parent_id = parent_id;

    // Populate caret offset and selection range from the DOM Selection — for any node (element or text) that contains
    // it. This is what AtkText::get_caret_offset and get_n_selections report.
    if (auto selection = document.get_selection()) {
        auto* focus_node = selection->focus_node().ptr();
        auto* anchor_node = selection->anchor_node().ptr();
        if (focus_node && focus_node == value().ptr()) {
            // DOM offsets into text nodes are UTF-16 code-unit offsets — but AT-SPI2 expects Unicode character offsets.
            // For ASCII and BMP, those two match; but they diverge for astral-plane code points (emoji, etc.) — where
            // one code point occupies two UTF-16 code units. So, convert using Utf16View::code_point_offset_of.
            auto utf16_offset_to_character_offset = [focus_node](u32 utf16_offset) -> i32 {
                if (!focus_node->is_text())
                    return static_cast<i32>(utf16_offset);
                auto const& text = static_cast<DOM::Text const&>(*focus_node).data();
                return static_cast<i32>(text.utf16_view().code_point_offset_of(utf16_offset));
            };
            node_data.caret_offset = utf16_offset_to_character_offset(selection->focus_offset());
            if (!selection->is_collapsed() && anchor_node == focus_node) {
                auto anchor_character_offset = utf16_offset_to_character_offset(selection->anchor_offset());
                node_data.selection_start = min(node_data.caret_offset, anchor_character_offset);
                node_data.selection_end = max(node_data.caret_offset, anchor_character_offset);
            }
        }
    }

    auto my_id = node_data.id;

    for (auto const& child : children()) {
        if (should_skip_child_in_node_data(*child))
            continue;
        node_data.child_ids.append(static_cast<i64>(child->value()->unique_id().value()));
    }

    if (!tracker || tracker->note(node_data, record_version, geometry_version))
        out.append(move(node_data));
    return my_id;
}

void AccessibilityTreeNode::visit_edges(Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_value);
    visitor.visit(m_children);
}

}

#include <LibWeb/CSS/FontFaceSet.h>

#include <LibWeb/CSS/StyleEngineInput.h>
#include <LibWeb/CSS/StyleSheetState.h>
#include <LibWeb/DOM/AdoptedStyleSheets.h>
#include <LibWeb/DOM/Document.h>
#include <LibWeb/DOM/ShadowRoot.h>

namespace Web::DOM {

GC::Ref<WebIDL::ObservableArray> AdoptedStyleSheetsAccess::adopted_style_sheets(Document& document)
{
    return document.adopted_style_sheets();
}

GC::Ref<WebIDL::ObservableArray> AdoptedStyleSheetsAccess::adopted_style_sheets(ShadowRoot& shadow_root)
{
    return shadow_root.adopted_style_sheets();
}

// NB: The engine holds each sheet once. A sheet that the array holds more than once is placed at its last occurrence,
//     where its rules win the cascade.
static Optional<u32> last_index_of(WebIDL::ObservableArray& adopted_style_sheets, CSS::StyleSheetState& style_sheet, u32 skipped_index)
{
    for (auto index = adopted_style_sheets.length(); index > 0;) {
        --index;
        if (index == skipped_index)
            continue;
        if (auto value = adopted_style_sheets.element_value(index); value.has_value() && CSS::css_style_sheet_from_value(*value) == &style_sheet)
            return index;
    }
    return {};
}

// The first sheet after index that the engine places there, which is one that does not occur again later.
static CSS::StyleSheetState* first_sheet_after(WebIDL::ObservableArray& adopted_style_sheets, u32 index, u32 skipped_index)
{
    for (auto next_index = index + 1; next_index < adopted_style_sheets.length(); ++next_index) {
        if (next_index == skipped_index)
            continue;
        if (auto value = adopted_style_sheets.element_value(next_index); value.has_value()) {
            auto* style_sheet = CSS::css_style_sheet_from_value(*value);
            if (style_sheet && last_index_of(adopted_style_sheets, *style_sheet, skipped_index) == next_index)
                return style_sheet;
        }
    }
    return nullptr;
}

GC::Ref<WebIDL::ObservableArray> create_adopted_style_sheets_list(Node& document_or_shadow_root)
{
    auto& realm = document_or_shadow_root.document().relevant_settings_object().realm();
    auto adopted_style_sheets = WebIDL::ObservableArray::create(realm);
    adopted_style_sheets->set_convert_to_idl_value_callback(GC::create_function(realm.heap(), GC::captures(document_or_shadow_root), [](Node& document_or_shadow_root, JS::Value value) -> WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> {
        auto style_sheet = CSS::css_style_sheet_from_value(value);
        if (!style_sheet)
            return document_or_shadow_root.vm().throw_completion<JS::TypeError>(JS::ErrorType::NotAnObjectOfType, "CSSStyleSheet");

        // NB: These are the steps of the set an indexed value algorithm, which runs after the delete algorithm for
        //     the value it replaces. That delete algorithm has no effect that script can observe, so checking first
        //     is not observable either, and keeps a rejected replacement from detaching the sheet that stays.
        // The set an indexed value algorithm for adoptedStyleSheets, given value and index, is the following:
        // 1. If value’s constructed flag is not set, or its constructor document is not equal to this
        //    DocumentOrShadowRoot's node document, throw a "NotAllowedError" DOMException.
        if (!style_sheet->constructed())
            return WebIDL::NotAllowedError::create("StyleSheet's constructed flag is not set."_utf16);
        if (!style_sheet->constructed() || style_sheet->constructor_document().ptr() != &document_or_shadow_root.document())
            return WebIDL::NotAllowedError::create("Sharing a StyleSheet between documents is not allowed."_utf16);
        return {};
    }));
    adopted_style_sheets->set_on_set_an_indexed_value_callback(GC::create_function(realm.heap(), GC::captures(document_or_shadow_root, adopted_style_sheets), [](Node& document_or_shadow_root, GC::Ref<WebIDL::ObservableArray>& adopted_style_sheets, u32 index, JS::Value& value) -> WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> {
        auto style_sheet = CSS::css_style_sheet_from_value(value);
        VERIFY(style_sheet);

        // Adopted sheets are not in any StyleSheetList, so nothing else announces them to the
        // engine. Observable array operations can write displaced entries before the insertion
        // point, so preserve their final order by attaching before the entry currently following
        // this index.
        if (auto last_index = last_index_of(adopted_style_sheets, *style_sheet, index); last_index.has_value() && *last_index > index)
            return {};
        CSS::record_stylesheet_attached(*style_sheet, document_or_shadow_root, first_sheet_after(adopted_style_sheets, index, index));
        CSS::Invalidation::invalidate_style_after_adopting_style_sheet(document_or_shadow_root, *style_sheet);
        return {};
    }));
    adopted_style_sheets->set_on_delete_an_indexed_value_callback(GC::create_function(realm.heap(), GC::captures(document_or_shadow_root, adopted_style_sheets), [](Node& document_or_shadow_root, GC::Ref<WebIDL::ObservableArray>& adopted_style_sheets, JS::Value value, u32 index) -> WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> {
        // NB: Object.defineProperty() bypasses the set callback, so script can put any value in the array, including a
        //     sheet that the list could not have adopted, such as the sheet of a style element. Its attachment is not
        //     the list's to change.
        auto* style_sheet = CSS::css_style_sheet_from_value(value);
        if (!style_sheet || !style_sheet->constructed() || style_sheet->constructor_document().ptr() != &document_or_shadow_root.document())
            return {};

        // NB: The deleted value is still at index.
        auto last_index = last_index_of(adopted_style_sheets, *style_sheet, index);
        if (!last_index.has_value()) {
            CSS::record_stylesheet_detached(*style_sheet, document_or_shadow_root);
            CSS::Invalidation::invalidate_style_after_removing_adopted_style_sheet(document_or_shadow_root, *style_sheet);
            return {};
        }
        if (*last_index > index)
            return {};
        CSS::record_stylesheet_attached(*style_sheet, document_or_shadow_root, first_sheet_after(adopted_style_sheets, *last_index, index));
        CSS::Invalidation::invalidate_style_after_adopting_style_sheet(document_or_shadow_root, *style_sheet);
        return {};
    }));

    // The indexed callbacks run before the backing list changes. Font matching needs the resulting sheet order.
    if (document_or_shadow_root.is_document()) {
        adopted_style_sheets->set_on_backing_list_changed(GC::create_function(realm.heap(), GC::captures(document_or_shadow_root.document()), [](Document& document) {
            document.fonts()->synchronize_css_connected_font_order();
        }));
    }
    return adopted_style_sheets;
}

void for_each_adopted_style_sheet(WebIDL::ObservableArray& adopted_style_sheets, Function<void(CSS::StyleSheetState&)> const& callback)
{
    adopted_style_sheets.for_each_element_value([&](JS::Value value) {
        if (auto style_sheet = CSS::css_style_sheet_from_value(value))
            callback(*style_sheet);
    });
}

/*

#include <LibWeb/DOM/AnchorNameMap.h>
#include <LibWeb/DOM/Document.h>
#include <LibWeb/DOM/Element.h>
#include <LibWeb/Layout/NodeArena.h>

namespace Web::DOM {

void AnchorNameMap::register_name(Utf16FlyString const& name, GC::Ref<Element> element, Optional<CSS::StyleNodeID> scope_host)
{
    auto& elements = m_map.ensure(name);
    if (elements.contains_slow(element))
        return;

    // Insert in tree order so that .last() is always the last element in tree order.
    auto index = elements.find_first_index_if([&](auto& existing) {
        return element->is_before(existing);
    });
    if (index.has_value())
        elements.insert(*index, element);
    else
        elements.append(element);

    publish(name, element->document(), scope_host);
}

void AnchorNameMap::unregister_name(Utf16FlyString const& name, GC::Ref<Element> element, Optional<CSS::StyleNodeID> scope_host)
{
    auto it = m_map.find(name);
    if (it == m_map.end())
        return;
    it->value.remove_first_matching([&](auto& e) { return e == element; });
    if (it->value.is_empty())
        m_map.remove(it);
    publish(name, element->document(), scope_host);
}

void AnchorNameMap::publish(Utf16FlyString const& name, Document& document, Optional<CSS::StyleNodeID> scope_host) const
{
    // A shadow host whose identity is already retired has left the tree with its shadow root, and the
    // arena forgot the scope with the identity. Naming it anyway would name the document tree.
    if (scope_host.has_value() && !scope_host->value())
        return;

    auto it = m_map.find(name);
    auto* arena = document.layout_node_arena_if_created();
    if (!arena) {
        // Nothing was published to a document without an arena, so there is nothing to withdraw. A
        // name to publish creates it: a document that registers a name is one that lays out.
        if (it == m_map.end())
            return;
        arena = &document.layout_node_arena();
    }

    Vector<u32, 4> style_nodes;
    if (it != m_map.end()) {
        style_nodes.ensure_capacity(it->value.size());
        for (auto const& element : it->value)
            style_nodes.unchecked_append(element->style_node_id().value());
    }
    Layout::RustFFI::render_state_set_anchor_name_elements(
        arena->host(),
        scope_host.value_or(CSS::StyleNodeID {}).value(),
        name.raw_identity(),
        style_nodes.span());
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/DOM/AnchorNameMap.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026, Jelle Raaijmakers <jelle@ladybird.org>
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/HashMap.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/Utf16FlyString.h>
#include <LibGC/Ptr.h>
#include <LibWeb/CSS/StyleEngineIdentifiers.h>
#include <LibWeb/Forward.h>

namespace Web::DOM {

// https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#typedef-anchor-name
//
// The elements a name is registered on are published to the layout arena as they change, because an
// anchor query happens during layout. A map belongs to one tree scope, which the arena names by the
// shadow host of the scope's root, or by nothing for the document tree.
class AnchorNameMap {
public:
    // `scope_host` is empty for the document tree, and otherwise the identity of the shadow host
    // of the map's root.
    void register_name(Utf16FlyString const& name, GC::Ref<Element>, Optional<CSS::StyleNodeID> scope_host);
    void unregister_name(Utf16FlyString const& name, GC::Ref<Element>, Optional<CSS::StyleNodeID> scope_host);

    template<typename Visitor>
    void visit_edges(Visitor& visitor) { visitor.visit(m_map); }

private:
    void publish(Utf16FlyString const& name, Document&, Optional<CSS::StyleNodeID> scope_host) const;

    HashMap<Utf16FlyString, Vector<GC::Ref<Element>>> m_map;
};

}

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(Attr);

GC::Ref<Attr> Attr::create(Document& document, Utf16FlyString local_name, Utf16String value, GC::Ptr<Element> owner_element)
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<Attr>(document, QualifiedName(move(local_name), Optional<Utf16FlyString> {}, Optional<Utf16FlyString> {}), move(value), owner_element);
}

GC::Ref<Attr> Attr::create(Document& document, QualifiedName qualified_name, Utf16String value, GC::Ptr<Element> owner_element)
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<Attr>(document, move(qualified_name), move(value), owner_element);
}

GC::Ref<Attr> Attr::clone(Document& document) const
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<Attr>(document, m_qualified_name, value(), nullptr);
}

Attr::Attr(Document& document, QualifiedName qualified_name, Utf16String value, GC::Ptr<Element> owner_element)
    : Node(document, NodeType::ATTRIBUTE_NODE)
    , m_qualified_name(move(qualified_name))
    , m_value(move(value))
    , m_owner_element(owner_element)
{
}

void Attr::visit_edges(Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_owner_element);
}

Element* Attr::owner_element()
{
    return m_owner_element.ptr();
}

Element const* Attr::owner_element() const
{
    return m_owner_element.ptr();
}

void Attr::set_owner_element(Element* owner_element)
{
    m_owner_element = owner_element;
}

Utf16String Attr::value() const
{
    if (auto* element = owner_element()) {
        auto index = element->find_attribute_index_ns(namespace_uri(), local_name());
        VERIFY(index.has_value());
        return element->m_attributes->at(*index).value;
    }
    return m_value;
}

void Attr::detach_from_element(Utf16String value)
{
    m_value = move(value);
    m_owner_element = nullptr;
}

// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#set-an-existing-attribute-value
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> Attr::set_value(Utf16String value)
{
    // 1. If attribute’s element is null, then set attribute’s value to value and return.
    if (!owner_element()) {
        m_value = move(value);
        return {};
    }

    // 2. Let element be attribute’s element.
    auto const& element = *owner_element();

    // 3. Let verifiedValue be the result of calling get Trusted Types-compliant attribute value with
    //    attribute’s local name, attribute’s namespace, element, and value.
    auto verified_value = TRY(TrustedTypes::get_trusted_types_compliant_attribute_value(
        local_name(),
        namespace_uri(),
        element,
        value));

    // 4. If attribute’s element is null, then set attribute’s value to verifiedValue, and return.
    if (!owner_element()) {
        m_value = move(verified_value);
        return {};
    }

    // 5. Change attribute to verifiedValue.
    change_attribute(move(verified_value));

    return {};
}

// https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-change
void Attr::change_attribute(Utf16String value)
{
    if (auto* element = owner_element()) {
        element->change_attribute_value(*this, move(value));
        return;
    }
    m_value = move(value);
}

}
