GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(NetworkBodyPump);

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-http-network-fetch
// NB: Step 9 of HTTP-network fetch. Steps 10 to 13 run in create_body_from_channel(), when the body's view is made.
GC::Ref<NetworkBodyPump> NetworkBodyPump::create(RefPtr<Infrastructure::FetchParams const> fetch_params, Engine::FetchBodyDeliveryGate::NavigationHold navigation_hold, RefPtr<HTTP::MemoryCache> http_cache)
{
    // 9. Let buffer be an empty byte sequence.
    // NB: The buffer is the FetchByteChannel; its watermarks are the user-agent-chosen lower and upper limits.
    static constexpr Engine::FetchByteChannel::Watermarks network_body_watermarks { .low = 256 * KiB, .high = 1 * MiB };
    auto delivery_gate = Engine::FetchBodyDeliveryGate::create(navigation_hold);
    auto channel = Engine::FetchByteChannel::create(network_body_watermarks, delivery_gate->create_channel_sink());
    delivery_gate->grant_credit(channel->initial_credit());

    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<NetworkBodyPump>(move(fetch_params), move(channel), move(delivery_gate), move(http_cache));
}

NetworkBodyPump::NetworkBodyPump(RefPtr<Infrastructure::FetchParams const> fetch_params, NonnullRefPtr<Engine::FetchByteChannel> channel, NonnullRefPtr<Engine::FetchBodyDeliveryGate> delivery_gate, RefPtr<HTTP::MemoryCache> http_cache)
    : m_fetch_params(move(fetch_params))
    , m_fetch_controller(m_fetch_params ? m_fetch_params->controller().ptr() : nullptr)
    , m_channel(move(channel))
    , m_delivery_gate(move(delivery_gate))
    , m_http_cache(move(http_cache))
{
}

NetworkBodyPump::~NetworkBodyPump() = default;

void NetworkBodyPump::set_response(NonnullRefPtr<Infrastructure::Response> response)
{
    m_response = move(response);
    if (m_network_complete)
        m_response->set_body_sizes(m_encoded_body_size, m_decoded_body_size);
}

void NetworkBodyPump::visit_edges(Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_fetch_controller);
}

// This implements the transmission steps of HTTP-network fetch.
// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-http-network-fetch
void NetworkBodyPump::handle_network_data(Requests::ResponseData data)
{
    // 1. Run these steps, but abort when fetchParams is canceled:
    // AD-HOC: A stopped fetch is not canceled, but takes no more of its body either.
    if (m_fetch_params && !m_fetch_params->control_block().is_ongoing()) {
        m_channel->cancel();
        return;
    }

    // 1. If one or more bytes have been transmitted from response’s message body, then:
    auto bytes = data.bytes();
    if (bytes.is_empty())
        return;

    // 1. Let bytes be the transmitted bytes.

    // FIXME: 2. Let codings be the result of extracting header list values given `Content-Encoding` and response’s header list.
    // FIXME: 3. Let filteredCoding be "@unknown".
    // FIXME: 4. If codings is null or failure, then set filteredCoding to the empty string.
    // FIXME: 5. Otherwise, if codings’s size is greater than 1, then set filteredCoding to "multiple".
    // FIXME: 6. Otherwise, if codings[0] is the empty string, or it is supported by the user agent, and is a
    //           byte-case-insensitive match for an entry listed in the HTTP Content Coding Registry, then set
    //           filteredCoding to the result of byte-lowercasing codings[0].
    // FIXME: 7. Set response’s body info’s content encoding to filteredCoding.
    // FIXME: 8. Increase response’s body info’s encoded size by bytes’s length.
    // FIXME: 9. Set bytes to the result of handling content codings given codings and bytes.
    // FIXME: 11. If bytes is failure, then terminate fetchParams’s controller.

    if (m_delivery_gate->did_deliver(bytes.size()) == Engine::FetchBodyDeliveryGate::DeliveryResult::Rejected)
        return;

    // 10. Increase response’s body info’s decoded size by bytes’s length.
    // NB: The response's body info is updated once the network completes.
    m_decoded_body_size += bytes.size();

    // 12. Append bytes to buffer. (Steps 12 and 13 live in FetchByteChannel's writes.)
    auto const* file_backed = data.file_backed_slice();
    if (file_backed) {
        m_channel->write(file_backed->slice);
        m_channel->keep_whole_body(file_backed->payload);
    } else {
        m_channel->write_copy(bytes);
    }

    if (m_http_cache && !m_cache_body_replaces_network_buffer && !m_cache_body_too_large_for_memory) {
        if (file_backed && m_cache_buffer.is_empty()) {
            if (!m_cache_body.has_value())
                m_cache_body = file_backed->payload;
        } else if (!http_memory_cache_can_hold_body_in_memory(m_decoded_body_size)) {
            // NB: A mapped file of the whole body may still arrive, which the cache can hold.
            m_cache_body_too_large_for_memory = true;
            m_cache_buffer.clear();
            m_cache_body.clear();
        } else {
            if (m_cache_body.has_value()) {
                m_cache_buffer.append(m_cache_body->bytes());
                m_cache_body.clear();
            }
            m_cache_buffer.append(bytes);
        }
    }
}

void NetworkBodyPump::handle_network_complete(Optional<i64> request_server_encoded_body_size)
{
    m_delivery_gate->detach_transport();
    m_network_complete = true;
    // AD-HOC: RequestServer reports the encoded size of an HTTP body once it has been received. Other schemes have no
    //         content coding, so their encoded size is their decoded size.
    if (request_server_encoded_body_size.has_value())
        m_encoded_body_size = static_cast<u64>(max<i64>(*request_server_encoded_body_size, 0));
    else
        m_encoded_body_size = m_decoded_body_size;
    if (m_response)
        m_response->set_body_sizes(m_encoded_body_size, m_decoded_body_size);
    finalize_cache_entry();
    if (auto delivery_id = m_channel->delivery_id(); delivery_id.has_value()) {
        Engine::Event::EndOfBody end_of_body {
            .delivery_id = *delivery_id,
            .end_time = HighResolutionTime::unsafe_shared_current_time(),
        };
        auto* engine_record = m_fetch_params->engine_record();
        VERIFY(engine_record);
        engine_record->event_sink().handle_event(move(end_of_body));
    }
    m_channel->close();
}

void NetworkBodyPump::handle_network_error(StringView error_message)
{
    m_delivery_gate->detach_transport();
    if (WebDriver::BiDi::network_events_enabled() && m_fetch_params)
        WebDriver::BiDi::network_fetch_error(*m_fetch_params, error_message);
    abandon_cache_entry(HTTP::MemoryCache::StoredResponse::Keep);
    m_channel->error({ .message = MUST(ByteBuffer::copy(error_message.bytes())) });
}

void NetworkBodyPump::handle_network_teardown(Requests::Request::TeardownReason reason)
{
    m_delivery_gate->detach_transport();
    switch (reason) {
    case Requests::Request::TeardownReason::Stopped:
        (void)m_channel->cancel();
        break;
    case Requests::Request::TeardownReason::Transferred:
        (void)m_channel->transfer_out();
        break;
    }
    abandon_cache_entry(HTTP::MemoryCache::StoredResponse::Keep);
}

void NetworkBodyPump::set_cached_response_body(Core::ImmutableBytes body)
{
    if (!m_http_cache)
        return;

    m_cache_buffer.clear();
    m_cache_body = move(body);
    m_cache_body_replaces_network_buffer = true;
    m_cache_body_too_large_for_memory = false;
}

void NetworkBodyPump::finalize_cache_entry()
{
    if (!m_http_cache || !m_fetch_params)
        return;

    auto request = m_fetch_params->request();
    if (m_fetch_params->is_canceled() || !m_response || request->cache_mode() == HTTP::CacheMode::NoStore) {
        abandon_cache_entry(HTTP::MemoryCache::StoredResponse::Keep);
        return;
    }

    // NB: The cache cannot hold this response, which still replaces the one it has stored.
    if (m_cache_body_too_large_for_memory) {
        abandon_cache_entry(HTTP::MemoryCache::StoredResponse::Retire);
        return;
    }

    auto response_body = m_cache_body.has_value()
        ? m_cache_body.release_value()
        : Core::ImmutableBytes::adopt(move(m_cache_buffer));
    m_http_cache->finalize_entry(request->current_url(), request->method(), request->header_list(), m_response->status(), m_response->header_list(), move(response_body));
    evict_http_memory_cache_entries_over_limits();

    m_http_cache.clear();
    m_cache_body.clear();
}

void NetworkBodyPump::abandon_cache_entry(HTTP::MemoryCache::StoredResponse stored_response)
{
    if (m_http_cache && m_fetch_params && m_response) {
        auto request = m_fetch_params->request();
        m_http_cache->abandon_entry(request->current_url(), request->method(), request->header_list(), m_response->header_list(), stored_response);
    }

    m_http_cache.clear();
    m_cache_buffer.clear();
    m_cache_body.clear();
}

}

#pragma once

#include <AK/ByteBuffer.h>

#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Engine/FetchByteChannel.h>
#include <LibWeb/Forward.h>

namespace Web::Fetch::Fetching {

// The producer half of a streamed response body: memory-cache accumulation, and the writes into the channel the
// stream pulls from.
class WEB_API NetworkBodyPump final : public JS::Cell {
    GC_CELL(NetworkBodyPump, JS::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(NetworkBodyPump);

public:
    [[nodiscard]] static GC::Ref<NetworkBodyPump> create(RefPtr<Infrastructure::FetchParams const>, Engine::FetchBodyDeliveryGate::NavigationHold, RefPtr<HTTP::MemoryCache>);

    virtual ~NetworkBodyPump() override;

    [[nodiscard]] NonnullRefPtr<Engine::FetchByteChannel> const& channel() const { return m_channel; }
    [[nodiscard]] NonnullRefPtr<Engine::FetchBodyDeliveryGate> const& delivery_gate() const { return m_delivery_gate; }

    // The pump records the body's sizes in the response once the body completes.
    void set_response(NonnullRefPtr<Fetch::Infrastructure::Response>);

    void handle_network_data(Requests::ResponseData);
    void set_cached_response_body(Core::ImmutableBytes);

    // Each of these detaches the delivery gate before it closes, errors, cancels or transfers the body's channel.
    void handle_network_complete(Optional<i64> request_server_encoded_body_size = {});
    void handle_network_error(StringView error_message);
    void handle_network_teardown(Requests::Request::TeardownReason);

private:
    NetworkBodyPump(RefPtr<Infrastructure::FetchParams const>, NonnullRefPtr<Engine::FetchByteChannel>, NonnullRefPtr<Engine::FetchBodyDeliveryGate>, RefPtr<HTTP::MemoryCache>);

    virtual void visit_edges(Visitor& visitor) override;

    // Drops a pending memory-cache entry that matches the response's request, for a body that will not finish arriving.
    void abandon_cache_entry(HTTP::MemoryCache::StoredResponse);
    void finalize_cache_entry();

    RefPtr<Infrastructure::FetchParams const> m_fetch_params;
    // The controller of m_fetch_params, which the pump keeps alive with them.
    GC::Ptr<Infrastructure::FetchController> m_fetch_controller;
    RefPtr<Fetch::Infrastructure::Response> m_response;

    NonnullRefPtr<Engine::FetchByteChannel> m_channel;
    NonnullRefPtr<Engine::FetchBodyDeliveryGate> m_delivery_gate;

    RefPtr<HTTP::MemoryCache> m_http_cache;

    // Whole-response buffer retained only when m_http_cache is non-null, for finalize_entry().
    ByteBuffer m_cache_buffer;
    Optional<Core::ImmutableBytes> m_cache_body;
    bool m_cache_body_replaces_network_buffer { false };
    bool m_cache_body_too_large_for_memory { false };

    u64 m_encoded_body_size { 0 };
    u64 m_decoded_body_size { 0 };
    bool m_network_complete { false };
};

}

#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibJS/Runtime/VM.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Fetching/PendingResponse.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Infrastructure/FetchController.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Infrastructure/FetchParams.h>
#include <LibWeb/Platform/EventLoopPlugin.h>

namespace Web::Fetch::Fetching {

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(PendingResponse);

GC::Ref<PendingResponse> PendingResponse::create(GC::Ref<Infrastructure::FetchController> fetch_controller)
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<PendingResponse>(fetch_controller);
}

GC::Ref<PendingResponse> PendingResponse::create(GC::Ref<Infrastructure::FetchController> fetch_controller, NonnullRefPtr<Infrastructure::Response> response)
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<PendingResponse>(fetch_controller, move(response));
}

GC::Ref<PendingResponse> PendingResponse::create(Infrastructure::FetchParams const& fetch_params)
{
    return create(fetch_params.controller());
}

GC::Ref<PendingResponse> PendingResponse::create(Infrastructure::FetchParams const& fetch_params, NonnullRefPtr<Infrastructure::Response> response)
{
    return create(fetch_params.controller(), move(response));
}

PendingResponse::PendingResponse(GC::Ref<Infrastructure::FetchController> fetch_controller, RefPtr<Infrastructure::Response> response)
    : m_fetch_controller(fetch_controller)
    , m_response(move(response))
{
    m_fetch_controller->add_pending_response({}, *this);
}

void PendingResponse::visit_edges(JS::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_callback);
    visitor.visit(m_fetch_controller);
}

void PendingResponse::when_loaded(Callback callback)
{
    VERIFY(!m_callback);
    m_callback = callback;
    if (m_response)
        run_callback();
}

void PendingResponse::resolve(NonnullRefPtr<Infrastructure::Response> response)
{
    VERIFY(!m_response);
    m_response = move(response);
    if (m_callback)
        run_callback();
}

void PendingResponse::run_callback()
{
    VERIFY(m_callback);
    VERIFY(m_response);
    Platform::EventLoopPlugin::the().deferred_invoke(GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(*this), [](PendingResponse& self) {
        VERIFY(self.m_callback);
        VERIFY(self.m_response);
        // NB: The callback runs only once, so let go of it as it runs. A pending response can live for as long as its
        //     fetch streams, and the callback would otherwise keep what it captured alive all that time.
        auto callback = exchange(self.m_callback, nullptr);
        callback->function()(*self.m_response);
        self.m_fetch_controller->remove_pending_response({}, self);
    }));
}

}

/*

#pragma once

#include <LibGC/Ptr.h>
#include <LibJS/Forward.h>
#include <LibJS/Heap/Cell.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Infrastructure/HTTP/Responses.h>
#include <LibWeb/Forward.h>

namespace Web::Fetch::Fetching {

// Non-standard wrapper around a possibly pending Infrastructure::Response.
// This is needed to fit the asynchronous nature of ResourceLoader into the synchronous expectations
// of the Fetch spec - we run 'in parallel' as a deferred_invoke(), which is still on the main thread;
// therefore we use callbacks to run portions of the spec that require waiting for an HTTP load.
class PendingResponse : public JS::Cell {
    GC_CELL(PendingResponse, JS::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(PendingResponse);

public:
    using Callback = GC::Ref<GC::Function<void(NonnullRefPtr<Infrastructure::Response>)>>;

    [[nodiscard]] static GC::Ref<PendingResponse> create(GC::Ref<Infrastructure::FetchController>);
    [[nodiscard]] static GC::Ref<PendingResponse> create(GC::Ref<Infrastructure::FetchController>, NonnullRefPtr<Infrastructure::Response>);
    [[nodiscard]] static GC::Ref<PendingResponse> create(Infrastructure::FetchParams const&);
    [[nodiscard]] static GC::Ref<PendingResponse> create(Infrastructure::FetchParams const&, NonnullRefPtr<Infrastructure::Response>);

    void when_loaded(Callback);
    void resolve(NonnullRefPtr<Infrastructure::Response>);
    bool is_resolved() const { return m_response != nullptr; }

private:
    PendingResponse(GC::Ref<Infrastructure::FetchController>, RefPtr<Infrastructure::Response> = {});

    virtual void visit_edges(JS::Cell::Visitor&) override;

    void run_callback();

    GC::Ptr<GC::Function<void(NonnullRefPtr<Infrastructure::Response>)>> m_callback;
    GC::Ref<Infrastructure::FetchController> m_fetch_controller;
    RefPtr<Infrastructure::Response> m_response;
};

}

#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Engine/EngineCommand.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Fetching/PreloadWaitHandle.h>

namespace Web::Fetch::Fetching {

NonnullRefPtr<PreloadWaitHandle> PreloadWaitHandle::create()
{
    return adopt_ref(*new PreloadWaitHandle);
}

// NB: This can run as the heap sweeps the callback that holds the handle, so it touches no GC object and only posts.
PreloadWaitHandle::~PreloadWaitHandle()
{
    if (auto const* armed = m_state.get_pointer<Armed>())
        armed->fetch_executor->post(Engine::Command::PreloadWaitAbandoned { armed->fetch_id });
}

void PreloadWaitHandle::arm(Engine::FetchId fetch_id, Engine::FetchExecutor& fetch_executor)
{
    VERIFY(m_state.has<Unarmed>());
    m_state = Armed { fetch_id, fetch_executor };
}

void PreloadWaitHandle::disarm()
{
    m_state = Disarmed {};
}

}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/Fetch/Fetching/PreloadWaitHandle.h
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

#pragma once

#include <AK/NonnullRefPtr.h>
#include <AK/RefCounted.h>
#include <AK/Variant.h>
#include <AK/Weakable.h>
#include <LibGC/Forward.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Engine/FetchExecutor.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Engine/Ids.h>

namespace Web::Fetch::Fetching {

// Held by the callback that resolves a fetch's wait for a preloaded response. Destroyed while armed, it posts the
// abandonment of the wait to the fetch's engine.
class PreloadWaitHandle final
    : public RefCounted<PreloadWaitHandle>
    , public Weakable<PreloadWaitHandle> {
public:
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;

    [[nodiscard]] static NonnullRefPtr<PreloadWaitHandle> create();
    ~PreloadWaitHandle();

    // The fetch's main fetch waits from now on. A handle is armed at most once, and never after it is disarmed.
    void arm(Engine::FetchId, Engine::FetchExecutor&);
    // From now on the handle posts nothing.
    void disarm();

private:
    PreloadWaitHandle() = default;

    struct Unarmed { };
    struct Armed {
        Engine::FetchId fetch_id;
        NonnullRefPtr<Engine::FetchExecutor> fetch_executor;
    };
    struct Disarmed { };
    Variant<Unarmed, Armed, Disarmed> m_state { Unarmed {} };
};

}

namespace Web::Fetch {

struct ResponseObjectHolder final : public JS::Cell {
    GC_CELL(ResponseObjectHolder, JS::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(ResponseObjectHolder);

    virtual void visit_edges(JS::Cell::Visitor& visitor) override
    {
        Base::visit_edges(visitor);
        visitor.visit(response_object);
    }

    GC::Ptr<Response> response_object;
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(ResponseObjectHolder);

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#deserialize-a-serialized-abort-reason
static JS::Value deserialize_serialized_abort_reason(JS::Realm& realm, Infrastructure::FetchController const& controller)
{
    // 1. Let fallbackError be an "AbortError" DOMException.
    auto fallback_error = WebIDL::AbortError::create(realm, "Fetch was aborted"_utf16);
    auto fallback_error_value = throw_completion(realm, fallback_error).value();

    // 2. Let deserializedError be fallbackError.
    JS::Value deserialized_error = fallback_error_value;

    // 3. If abortReason is non-null, then set deserializedError to StructuredDeserialize(abortReason, realm).
    //    If that threw an exception or returned undefined, then set deserializedError to fallbackError.
    if (controller.serialized_abort_reason().has_value()) {
        auto deserialized_error_or_exception = HTML::structured_deserialize(realm.vm(), controller.serialized_abort_reason().value(), realm);
        if (!deserialized_error_or_exception.is_exception() && !deserialized_error_or_exception.value().is_undefined())
            deserialized_error = deserialized_error_or_exception.value();
    }

    // 4. Return deserializedError.
    return deserialized_error;
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-global-fetch
GC::Ref<WebIDL::Promise> fetch(JS::Realm& realm, RequestInfo const& input, Bindings::RequestInit const& init)
{
    auto& vm = realm.vm();

    // 1. Let p be a new promise.
    auto promise_capability = WebIDL::create_promise(realm);

    // 2. Let requestObject be the result of invoking the initial value of Request as constructor with input and init
    //    as arguments. If this throws an exception, reject p with it and return p.
    auto exception_or_request_object = Request::create_with_settings(HTML::principal_realm_settings_object(realm), input, init);
    if (exception_or_request_object.is_exception()) {
        WebIDL::reject_promise_with_exception(promise_capability, exception_or_request_object.release_error());
        return promise_capability;
    }
    auto request_object = exception_or_request_object.release_value();

    // 3. Let request be requestObject’s request.
    auto request = request_object->request();

    // 4. If requestObject’s signal is aborted, then:
    if (request_object->signal()->aborted()) {
        // 1. Abort the fetch() call with p, request, null, and requestObject’s signal’s abort reason.
        abort_fetch(*promise_capability, request_object, nullptr, request_object->signal()->reason());

        // 2. Return p.
        return promise_capability;
    }

    // 5. Let globalObject be request’s client’s global object.
    auto& global_object = Fetching::resolve_client(request)->global_object();

    // FIXME: 6. If globalObject is a ServiceWorkerGlobalScope object, then set request’s service-workers mode to "none".
    (void)global_object;

    // 7. Let responseObject be null.
    auto response_object_holder = GC::Heap::the().allocate<ResponseObjectHolder>();

    // 8. Let relevantRealm be this’s relevant Realm.
    // NOTE: This assumes that the running execution context is for the fetch() function call.
    auto& relevant_realm = HTML::relevant_realm(*vm.running_execution_context().function);

    // 9. Let locallyAborted be false.
    // NOTE: This lets us reject promises with predictable timing, when the request to abort comes from the same thread
    //       as the call to fetch.
    auto locally_aborted = Fetching::RefCountedFlag::create(false);

    // 10. Let controller be null.
    auto controller_holder = Infrastructure::FetchControllerHolder::create();

    // NOTE: Step 11 is done out of order so that the controller is non-null when we capture the GCPtr by copy in the abort algorithm lambda.
    //       This is not observable, AFAICT.

    // 12. Set controller to the result of calling fetch given request and processResponse given response being these
    //     steps:
    auto process_response = GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(locally_aborted, promise_capability, request_object, response_object_holder, controller_holder, relevant_realm), [](auto& locally_aborted, auto& promise_capability, auto& request_object, auto& response_object_holder, auto& controller_holder, auto& relevant_realm, GC::Ref<Infrastructure::ResponseView> response) {
        // 1. If locallyAborted is true, then abort these steps.
        if (locally_aborted->value())
            return;

        // AD-HOC: Promise reactions need an execution context and incumbent callback settings.
        HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext execution_context { relevant_realm, HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext::CallbacksEnabled::Yes };

        // 2. If response’s aborted flag is set, then:
        if (response->aborted()) {
            // 1. Let deserializedError be the result of deserialize a serialized abort reason given controller’s
            //    serialized abort reason and relevantRealm.
            auto deserialized_error = deserialize_serialized_abort_reason(relevant_realm, *controller_holder->controller());

            // 2. Abort the fetch() call with p, request, responseObject, and deserializedError.
            abort_fetch(*promise_capability, request_object, response_object_holder->response_object, deserialized_error);

            // 3. Abort these steps.
            return;
        }

        // 3. If response is a network error, then reject p with a TypeError and abort these steps.
        if (response->is_network_error()) {
            auto message = response->network_error_message().value_or("Response is a network error"_string);
            WebIDL::reject_promise(relevant_realm, promise_capability, JS::TypeError::create(relevant_realm, Utf16String::from_utf8(message)));
            return;
        }

        // 4. Set responseObject to the result of creating a Response object, given response, "immutable", and
        //    relevantRealm.
        response_object_holder->response_object = Response::create(response, Headers::Guard::Immutable);

        // 5. Resolve p with responseObject.
        auto response_value = Bindings::wrap(
            Bindings::host_defined_wrapper_world(relevant_realm),
            relevant_realm,
            GC::Ref { *response_object_holder->response_object });
        WebIDL::resolve_promise(relevant_realm, promise_capability, response_value);
    });
    Infrastructure::FetchAlgorithms::Input fetch_algorithms_input { Engine::BodyIntent::DeliverStreamToConsumerAgent };
    fetch_algorithms_input.process_response = process_response;
    // AD-HOC: Request holds its body's source and length, and requestObject its stream, which fetching reads. Its
    //         reader is acquired here, not when fetching reads the stream, so that script cannot lock the stream first.
    if (auto body = request_object->body_impl())
        fetch_algorithms_input.request_body_reader = Infrastructure::FetchAlgorithms::RequestBodyReader { *body, MUST(body->stream()->get_a_reader()) };
    controller_holder->set_controller(Fetching::fetch(realm, request, Infrastructure::FetchAlgorithms::create(move(fetch_algorithms_input))));

    // 11. Add the following abort steps to requestObject’s signal:
    (void)request_object->signal()->add_abort_algorithm(GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(locally_aborted, controller_holder, promise_capability, request_object, response_object_holder, relevant_realm), [](auto& locally_aborted, auto& controller_holder, auto& promise_capability, auto& request_object, auto& response_object_holder, auto& relevant_realm) {
        dbgln_if(WEB_FETCH_DEBUG, "Fetch: Request object signal's abort algorithm called");

        // 1. Set locallyAborted to true.
        locally_aborted->set_value(true);

        // 2. Assert: controller is non-null.
        VERIFY(controller_holder->controller());

        // 3. Abort controller with requestObject’s signal’s abort reason.
        controller_holder->controller()->abort(relevant_realm, request_object->signal()->reason());

        // AD-HOC: An execution context is required for Promise functions.
        HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext execution_context { relevant_realm, HTML::TemporaryExecutionContext::CallbacksEnabled::Yes };

        // 4. Abort the fetch() call with p, request, responseObject, and requestObject’s signal’s abort reason.
        abort_fetch(*promise_capability, request_object, response_object_holder->response_object, request_object->signal()->reason());
    }));

    // 13. Return p.
    return promise_capability;
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#abort-fetch
// NB: request is given as the Request object holding its body's stream.
void abort_fetch(WebIDL::Promise const& promise, GC::Ref<Request> request_object, GC::Ptr<Response> response_object, JS::Value error)
{
    dbgln_if(WEB_FETCH_DEBUG, "Fetch: Aborting fetch with: request @ {}, error = {}", request_object->request().ptr(), error);

    // 1. Reject promise with error.
    // NOTE: This is a no-op if promise has already fulfilled.
    WebIDL::reject_promise(promise, error);

    // 2. If request’s body is non-null and is readable, then cancel request’s body with error.
    if (auto body = request_object->body_impl(); body && body->stream()->is_readable()) {
        // NOTE: Cancel here is different than the cancel method of stream and refers to https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readablestream-cancel
        body->stream()->cancel(error);
    }

    // 3. If responseObject is null, then return.
    if (response_object == nullptr)
        return;

    // 4. Let response be responseObject’s response.
    auto response = response_object->response();

    // 5. If response’s body is non-null and is readable, then error response’s body with error.
    if (response->body()) {
        auto stream = response->body()->stream();
        if (stream->is_readable()) {
            stream->error(error);
        }
    }
}

}

#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibJS/Runtime/Completion.h>
#include <LibJS/Runtime/VM.h>
#include <LibTextCodec/Decoder.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Headers.h>

namespace Web::Fetch {

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(Headers);

GC::Ref<Headers> Headers::create(NonnullRefPtr<HTTP::HeaderList> header_list)
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<Headers>(move(header_list));
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-headers
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<GC::Ref<Headers>> Headers::create_from_init(Optional<HeadersInit> const& init)
{
    // The new Headers(init) constructor steps are:
    auto headers = create(HTTP::HeaderList::create());

    // 1. Set this’s guard to "none".
    headers->m_guard = Guard::None;

    // 2. If init is given, then fill this with init.
    if (init.has_value())
        TRY(headers->fill(*init));

    return headers;
}

Headers::Headers(NonnullRefPtr<HTTP::HeaderList> header_list)
    : m_header_list(move(header_list))
{
}

Headers::~Headers() = default;

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-headers-append
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> Headers::append(String const& name_string, String const& value_string)
{
    // The append(name, value) method steps are to append (name, value) to this.
    auto header = HTTP::Header::isomorphic_encode(name_string, value_string);
    TRY(append(move(header)));
    return {};
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-headers-delete
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> Headers::delete_(String const& name)
{
    // The delete(name) method steps are:

    // 1. If validating (name, ``) for headers returns false, then return.
    // NOTE: Passing a dummy header value ought not to have any negative repercussions.
    auto header = HTTP::Header::isomorphic_encode(name, ""sv);
    if (!TRY(validate(header)))
        return {};

    // 2. If this’s guard is "request-no-cors", name is not a no-CORS-safelisted request-header name, and name is not a privileged no-CORS request-header name, then return.
    if (m_guard == Guard::RequestNoCORS && !Infrastructure::is_no_cors_safelisted_request_header_name(name) && !Infrastructure::is_privileged_no_cors_request_header_name(name))
        return {};

    // 3. If this’s header list does not contain name, then return.
    if (!m_header_list->contains(name))
        return {};

    // 4. Delete name from this’s header list.
    m_header_list->delete_(name);

    // 5. If this’s guard is "request-no-cors", then remove privileged no-CORS request-headers from this.
    if (m_guard == Guard::RequestNoCORS)
        remove_privileged_no_cors_request_headers();

    return {};
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-headers-get
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<Optional<String>> Headers::get(String const& name)
{
    // The get(name) method steps are:

    // 1. If name is not a header name, then throw a TypeError.
    if (!HTTP::is_header_name(name))
        return WebIDL::SimpleException { WebIDL::SimpleExceptionType::TypeError, "Invalid header name"_utf16 };

    // 2. Return the result of getting name from this’s header list.
    auto byte_buffer = m_header_list->get(name);
    return byte_buffer.has_value() ? TextCodec::isomorphic_decode(*byte_buffer) : Optional<String> {};
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-headers-getsetcookie
Vector<String> Headers::get_set_cookie()
{
    // The getSetCookie() method steps are:
    auto values = Vector<String> {};

    // 1. If this’s header list does not contain `Set-Cookie`, then return « ».
    if (!m_header_list->contains("Set-Cookie"sv))
        return values;

    // 2. Return the values of all headers in this’s header list whose name is a byte-case-insensitive match for
    //    `Set-Cookie`, in order.
    for (auto const& header : *m_header_list) {
        if (header.name.equals_ignoring_ascii_case("Set-Cookie"sv))
            values.append(TextCodec::isomorphic_decode(header.value));
    }
    return values;
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-headers-has
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<bool> Headers::has(String const& name)
{
    // The has(name) method steps are:

    // 1. If name is not a header name, then throw a TypeError.
    if (!HTTP::is_header_name(name))
        return WebIDL::SimpleException { WebIDL::SimpleExceptionType::TypeError, "Invalid header name"_utf16 };

    // 2. Return true if this’s header list contains name; otherwise false.
    return m_header_list->contains(name);
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-headers-set
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> Headers::set(String const& name, String const& value)
{
    // The set(name, value) method steps are:

    // 1. Normalize value.
    auto normalized_value = HTTP::normalize_header_value(value);

    auto header = HTTP::Header::isomorphic_encode(name, normalized_value);

    // 2. If validating (name, value) for headers returns false, then return.
    if (!TRY(validate(header)))
        return {};

    // 3. If this’s guard is "request-no-cors" and (name, value) is not a no-CORS-safelisted request-header, then return.
    if (m_guard == Guard::RequestNoCORS && !Infrastructure::is_no_cors_safelisted_request_header(header))
        return {};

    // 4. Set (name, value) in this’s header list.
    m_header_list->set(move(header));

    // 5. If this’s guard is "request-no-cors", then remove privileged no-CORS request-headers from this.
    if (m_guard == Guard::RequestNoCORS)
        remove_privileged_no_cors_request_headers();

    return {};
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-iterable, Step 4
void Headers::for_each(ForEachCallback callback)
{
    // The value pairs to iterate over are the return value of running sort and combine with this’s header list.
    auto value_pairs_to_iterate_over = [&]() {
        return m_header_list->sort_and_combine();
    };

    // 1-5. Are done in the generated wrapper code.

    // 6. Let pairs be idlObject’s list of value pairs to iterate over.
    auto pairs = value_pairs_to_iterate_over();

    // 7. Let i be 0.
    size_t i = 0;

    // 8. While i < pairs’s size:
    while (i < pairs.size()) {
        // 1. Let pair be pairs[i].
        auto const& pair = pairs[i];

        // 2. Invoke idlCallback with « pair’s value, pair’s key, idlObject » and with thisArg as the callback this value.
        if (callback(TextCodec::isomorphic_decode(pair.name), TextCodec::isomorphic_decode(pair.value)) == IterationDecision::Break)
            break;

        // 3. Set pairs to idlObject’s current list of value pairs to iterate over. (It might have changed.)
        pairs = value_pairs_to_iterate_over();

        // 4. Set i to i + 1.
        ++i;
    }
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#headers-validate
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<bool> Headers::validate(HTTP::Header const& header) const
{
    // To validate a header (name, value) for a Headers object headers:
    auto const& [name, value] = header;

    // 1. If name is not a header name or value is not a header value, then throw a TypeError.
    if (!HTTP::is_header_name(name))
        return WebIDL::SimpleException { WebIDL::SimpleExceptionType::TypeError, "Invalid header name"_utf16 };
    if (!HTTP::is_header_value(value))
        return WebIDL::SimpleException { WebIDL::SimpleExceptionType::TypeError, "Invalid header value"_utf16 };

    // 2. If headers’s guard is "immutable", then throw a TypeError.
    if (m_guard == Guard::Immutable)
        return WebIDL::SimpleException { WebIDL::SimpleExceptionType::TypeError, "Headers object is immutable"_utf16 };

    // 3. If headers’s guard is "request" and (name, value) is a forbidden request-header, then return false.
    if (m_guard == Guard::Request && HTTP::is_forbidden_request_header(header))
        return false;

    // 4. If headers’s guard is "response" and name is a forbidden response-header name, then return false.
    if (m_guard == Guard::Response && HTTP::is_forbidden_response_header_name(name))
        return false;

    // 5. Return true.
    return true;
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-headers-append
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> Headers::append(HTTP::Header header)
{
    // To append a header (name, value) to a Headers object headers, run these steps:
    auto& [name, value] = header;

    // 1. Normalize value.
    value = HTTP::normalize_header_value(value);

    // 2. If validating (name, value) for headers returns false, then return.
    if (!TRY(validate(header)))
        return {};

    // 3. If headers’s guard is "request-no-cors":
    if (m_guard == Guard::RequestNoCORS) {
        // 1. Let temporaryValue be the result of getting name from headers’s header list.
        auto temporary_value = m_header_list->get(name);

        // 2. If temporaryValue is null, then set temporaryValue to value.
        if (!temporary_value.has_value()) {
            temporary_value = value;
        }
        // 3. Otherwise, set temporaryValue to temporaryValue, followed by 0x2C 0x20, followed by value.
        else {
            temporary_value = ByteString::formatted("{}, {}", *temporary_value, value);
        }

        auto temporary_header = HTTP::Header {
            .name = name,
            .value = temporary_value.release_value(),
        };

        // 4. If (name, temporaryValue) is not a no-CORS-safelisted request-header, then return.
        if (!Infrastructure::is_no_cors_safelisted_request_header(temporary_header))
            return {};
    }

    // 4. Append (name, value) to headers’s header list.
    m_header_list->append(move(header));

    // 5. If headers’s guard is "request-no-cors", then remove privileged no-CORS request-headers from headers.
    if (m_guard == Guard::RequestNoCORS)
        remove_privileged_no_cors_request_headers();

    return {};
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-headers-fill
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> Headers::fill(HeadersInit const& object)
{
    // To fill a Headers object headers with a given object object, run these steps:
    return object.visit(
        // 1. If object is a sequence, then for each header of object:
        [&](Vector<Vector<String>> const& object) -> WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> {
            for (auto const& entry : object) {
                // 1. If header's size is not 2, then throw a TypeError.
                if (entry.size() != 2)
                    return WebIDL::SimpleException { WebIDL::SimpleExceptionType::TypeError, "Array must contain header key/value pair"_utf16 };

                // 2. Append (header[0], header[1]) to headers.
                auto header = HTTP::Header::isomorphic_encode(entry[0], entry[1]);
                TRY(append(move(header)));
            }
            return {};
        },
        // 2. Otherwise, object is a record, then for each key → value of object, append (key, value) to headers.
        [&](OrderedHashMap<String, String> const& object) -> WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> {
            for (auto const& entry : object) {
                auto header = HTTP::Header::isomorphic_encode(entry.key, entry.value);
                TRY(append(move(header)));
            }
            return {};
        });
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-headers-remove-privileged-no-cors-request-headers
void Headers::remove_privileged_no_cors_request_headers()
{
    // To remove privileged no-CORS request-headers from a Headers object (headers), run these steps:

    static constexpr Array privileged_no_cors_request_header_names = {
        "Range"sv,
    };

    // 1. For each headerName of privileged no-CORS request-header names:
    for (auto const& header_name : privileged_no_cors_request_header_names) {
        // 1. Delete headerName from headers’s header list.
        m_header_list->delete_(header_name);
    }
}

}

using HeadersInit = Variant<Vector<Vector<String>>, OrderedHashMap<String, String>>;

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#headers-class
class Headers final : public Bindings::GCAllocatedWrappable {
    WEB_WRAPPABLE(Headers, Bindings::GCAllocatedWrappable);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(Headers);

public:
    enum class Guard {
        Immutable,
        Request,
        RequestNoCORS,
        Response,
        None,
    };

    [[nodiscard]] static GC::Ref<Headers> create(NonnullRefPtr<HTTP::HeaderList>);
    static WebIDL::ExceptionOr<GC::Ref<Headers>> create_from_init(Optional<HeadersInit> const& init);

    virtual ~Headers() override;

    [[nodiscard]] NonnullRefPtr<HTTP::HeaderList> const& header_list() const { return m_header_list; }
    void set_header_list(NonnullRefPtr<HTTP::HeaderList> header_list) { m_header_list = move(header_list); }

    [[nodiscard]] Guard guard() const { return m_guard; }
    void set_guard(Guard guard) { m_guard = guard; }

    WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> fill(HeadersInit const&);
    WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> append(HTTP::Header);

    // JS API functions
    WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> append(String const& name, String const& value);
    WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> delete_(String const& name);
    WebIDL::ExceptionOr<Optional<String>> get(String const& name);
    [[nodiscard]] Vector<String> get_set_cookie();
    WebIDL::ExceptionOr<bool> has(String const& name);
    WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> set(String const& name, String const& value);

    using ForEachCallback = Function<IterationDecision(String const&, String const&)>;
    void for_each(ForEachCallback);

private:
    friend class HeadersIterator;

    explicit Headers(NonnullRefPtr<HTTP::HeaderList>);

    WebIDL::ExceptionOr<bool> validate(HTTP::Header const&) const;
    void remove_privileged_no_cors_request_headers();

    // https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-headers-header-list
    // A Headers object has an associated header list (a header list), which is initially empty.
    NonnullRefPtr<HTTP::HeaderList> m_header_list;

    // https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-headers-guard
    // A Headers object also has an associated guard, which is a headers guard. A headers guard is "immutable", "request", "request-no-cors", "response" or "none".
    Guard m_guard { Guard::None };
};

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(HeadersIterator);

static constexpr JSHostClass headers_iterator_host_class = JS::make_host_class(JS_HOST_CLASS_OBJECT, "HeadersIterator"sv, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, 0);

HeadersIterator::HeadersIterator(Headers const& headers, JS::Object::PropertyKind iteration_kind)
    : m_headers(headers)
    , m_iteration_kind(iteration_kind)
{
}

HeadersIterator::~HeadersIterator() = default;

GC::Ref<JS::HostObject> HeadersIterator::create(JS::Realm& realm, Headers const& headers, JS::Object::PropertyKind iteration_kind)
{
    static auto const& prototype_name = "HeadersIterator"_utf16_fly_string;
    auto iterator = realm.create<HeadersIterator>(headers, iteration_kind);
    auto& prototype = Bindings::ensure_web_prototype<Bindings::HeadersIteratorPrototype>(realm, prototype_name);
    return JS::HostObject::create(realm, headers_iterator_host_class, prototype, {}, iterator);
}

void HeadersIterator::visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_headers);
}

// https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-iterable, Step 2
GC::Ref<JS::Object> HeadersIterator::next(JS::Realm& realm)
{
    // The value pairs to iterate over are the return value of running sort and combine with this’s header list.
    auto value_pairs_to_iterate_over = [&]() {
        return m_headers->m_header_list->sort_and_combine();
    };

    auto pairs = value_pairs_to_iterate_over();

    if (m_index >= pairs.size())
        return JS::create_iterator_result_object(realm, JS::js_undefined(), true);

    auto const& pair = pairs[m_index++];
    auto pair_name = TextCodec::isomorphic_decode(pair.name);
    auto pair_value = TextCodec::isomorphic_decode(pair.value);

    switch (m_iteration_kind) {
    case JS::Object::PropertyKind::Key:
        return JS::create_iterator_result_object(realm, JS::PrimitiveString::create(vm(), Utf16String::from_utf8(pair_name)), false);
    case JS::Object::PropertyKind::Value:
        return JS::create_iterator_result_object(realm, JS::PrimitiveString::create(vm(), Utf16String::from_utf8(pair_value)), false);
    case JS::Object::PropertyKind::KeyAndValue: {
        auto array = JS::Array::create_from(realm, { JS::PrimitiveString::create(vm(), Utf16String::from_utf8(pair_name)), JS::PrimitiveString::create(vm(), Utf16String::from_utf8(pair_value)) });
        return JS::create_iterator_result_object(realm, array, false);
    }
    default:
        VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
        return JS::create_iterator_result_object(realm, JS::js_undefined(), true);
    }
}

// What fetching reads from a request's client.
struct ClientContext {
    enum class GlobalKind : u8 {
        Window,
        Worker,
        Other,
    };

    enum class IsSecureContext : u8 {
        No,
        Yes,
    };

    // Whether the global object is a Window whose navigable is non-null and has no parent.
    enum class IsWindowOfATopLevelNavigable : u8 {
        No,
        Yes,
    };

    URL::Origin origin;
    URL::Origin site_for_cookies;
    URL::URL creation_url;
    Optional<URL::URL> top_level_creation_url;
    Optional<URL::Origin> top_level_origin;
    GlobalKind global_kind { GlobalKind::Other };
    IsWindowOfATopLevelNavigable is_window_of_a_top_level_navigable { IsWindowOfATopLevelNavigable::No };
    HasCrossSiteAncestor has_cross_site_ancestor { HasCrossSiteAncestor::No };
    HTML::CanUseCrossOriginIsolatedAPIs cross_origin_isolated_capability { HTML::CanUseCrossOriginIsolatedAPIs::No };
    IsSecureContext is_secure_context { IsSecureContext::No };
    MixedContent::ProhibitsMixedSecurityContexts prohibits_mixed_security_contexts { MixedContent::ProhibitsMixedSecurityContexts::DoesNotRestrictMixedSecurityContexts };

    // The cache mode while loading of the associated Document, if the global object is a Window.
    HTTP::CacheMode cache_mode_while_loading { HTTP::CacheMode::Default };

    double time_origin { 0 };

    // The navigable of the Window that is the global object, if it has one and this process hosts the Window.
    Optional<HTML::CrossProcessId> navigable_id;

    // The URL a "client" referrer is determined from, or none for no referrer.
    Optional<URL::URL> referrer_source;

    // The URL the content blocker treats as the source of a request that is not for a document.
    URL::URL content_blocker_source_url;

    NonnullRefPtr<KeepaliveQuotaAccountant> keepalive_quota_accountant;
};

// A request's client context, taken when the fetch started, or, for a client another process hosts, made from what
// that process serialized.
struct WEB_API ClientContextSnapshot final : public AtomicRefCounted<ClientContextSnapshot>
    , public ClientContext {
    explicit ClientContextSnapshot(ClientContext context)
        : ClientContext(move(context))
    {
    }
};

// What fetching reads from a request's reserved client.
struct ReservedClientContext {
    using IsSecureContext = ClientContext::IsSecureContext;

    enum class TargetBrowsingContext : u8 {
        None,
        TopLevel,
        Nested,
    };

    // The active document of the parent of the target browsing context's navigable.
    struct Parent {
        Optional<URL::Origin> active_document_origin;
        HasCrossSiteAncestor active_document_has_cross_site_ancestor { HasCrossSiteAncestor::No };
    };

    // A reserved client that is an environment but not a settings object.
    struct Environment {
        TargetBrowsingContext target_browsing_context { TargetBrowsingContext::None };
        Optional<Parent> parent;
    };

    // A reserved client that is a settings object.
    struct SettingsObject {
        URL::Origin origin;
        HasCrossSiteAncestor has_cross_site_ancestor { HasCrossSiteAncestor::No };
    };

    URL::URL creation_url;
    Optional<URL::URL> top_level_creation_url;
    Optional<URL::Origin> top_level_origin;
    IsSecureContext is_secure_context { IsSecureContext::No };
    Variant<Environment, SettingsObject> kind;
};

// A request's reserved client context as it was when the reserved client was set.
struct WEB_API ReservedClientContextSnapshot final : public AtomicRefCounted<ReservedClientContextSnapshot>
    , public ReservedClientContext {
    explicit ReservedClientContextSnapshot(ReservedClientContext context)
        : ReservedClientContext(move(context))
    {
    }
};

#include <LibGC/Heap.h>
#include <LibJS/Runtime/VM.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Infrastructure/FetchAlgorithms.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Infrastructure/HTTP/Bodies.h>
#include <LibWeb/Streams/ReadableStreamDefaultReader.h>

namespace Web::Fetch::Infrastructure {

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(FetchAlgorithms);

GC::Ref<FetchAlgorithms> FetchAlgorithms::create(Input input)
{
    auto has_consuming_intent = input.body_intent == Engine::BodyIntent::ConsumeForCallback || input.body_intent == Engine::BodyIntent::SyncAccumulate;
    VERIFY(has_consuming_intent || !input.process_response_consume_body);

    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<FetchAlgorithms>(
        input.body_intent,
        input.process_request_body_chunk_length,
        input.process_request_end_of_body,
        input.process_early_hints_response,
        input.process_response,
        input.process_response_end_of_body,
        input.process_response_consume_body,
        move(input.request_body_reader));
}

FetchAlgorithms::FetchAlgorithms(
    Engine::BodyIntent body_intent,
    ProcessRequestBodyChunkLengthHeapFunction process_request_body_chunk_length,
    ProcessRequestEndOfBodyHeapFunction process_request_end_of_body,
    ProcessEarlyHintsResponseHeapFunction process_early_hints_response,
    ProcessResponseHeapFunction process_response,
    ProcessResponseEndOfBodyHeapFunction process_response_end_of_body,
    ProcessResponseConsumeBodyHeapFunction process_response_consume_body,
    Optional<RequestBodyReader> request_body_reader)
    : m_body_intent(body_intent)
    , m_process_request_body_chunk_length(process_request_body_chunk_length)
    , m_process_request_end_of_body(process_request_end_of_body)
    , m_process_early_hints_response(process_early_hints_response)
    , m_process_response(process_response)
    , m_process_response_end_of_body(process_response_end_of_body)
    , m_process_response_consume_body(process_response_consume_body)
    , m_request_body_reader(move(request_body_reader))
{
}

void FetchAlgorithms::visit_edges(JS::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_process_request_body_chunk_length);
    visitor.visit(m_process_request_end_of_body);
    visitor.visit(m_process_early_hints_response);
    visitor.visit(m_process_response);
    visitor.visit(m_process_response_end_of_body);
    visitor.visit(m_process_response_consume_body);
    if (m_request_body_reader.has_value()) {
        visitor.visit(m_request_body_reader->body);
        visitor.visit(m_request_body_reader->reader);
    }
}

#pragma once

#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <LibCore/ImmutableBytes.h>
#include <LibGC/Function.h>
#include <LibGC/Ptr.h>
#include <LibJS/Heap/Cell.h>
#include <LibWeb/Export.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Engine/BodyIntent.h>
#include <LibWeb/Forward.h>

namespace Web::Fetch::Infrastructure {

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-elsewhere-fetch
class WEB_API FetchAlgorithms : public JS::Cell {
    GC_CELL(FetchAlgorithms, JS::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(FetchAlgorithms);

public:
    struct ConsumeBodyFailureTag { };
    using BodyBytes = Variant<Empty, ConsumeBodyFailureTag, Core::ImmutableBytes>;

    using ProcessRequestBodyChunkLengthFunction = Function<void(u64)>;
    using ProcessRequestEndOfBodyFunction = Function<void()>;
    using ProcessEarlyHintsResponseFunction = Function<void(GC::Ref<Infrastructure::ResponseView>)>;
    using ProcessResponseFunction = Function<void(GC::Ref<Infrastructure::ResponseView>)>;
    using ProcessResponseEndOfBodyFunction = Function<void(GC::Ref<Infrastructure::ResponseView>)>;
    using ProcessResponseConsumeBodyFunction = Function<void(GC::Ref<Infrastructure::ResponseView>, BodyBytes)>;

    using ProcessRequestBodyChunkLengthHeapFunction = GC::Ptr<GC::Function<ProcessRequestBodyChunkLengthFunction::FunctionType>>;
    using ProcessRequestEndOfBodyHeapFunction = GC::Ptr<GC::Function<ProcessRequestEndOfBodyFunction::FunctionType>>;
    using ProcessEarlyHintsResponseHeapFunction = GC::Ptr<GC::Function<ProcessEarlyHintsResponseFunction::FunctionType>>;
    using ProcessResponseHeapFunction = GC::Ptr<GC::Function<ProcessResponseFunction::FunctionType>>;
    using ProcessResponseEndOfBodyHeapFunction = GC::Ptr<GC::Function<ProcessResponseEndOfBodyFunction::FunctionType>>;
    using ProcessResponseConsumeBodyHeapFunction = GC::Ptr<GC::Function<ProcessResponseConsumeBodyFunction::FunctionType>>;

    // A request body whose stream is the only place its bytes are, with the reader fetch() acquired for that stream.
    struct RequestBodyReader {
        GC::Ref<Body> body;
        GC::Ref<Streams::ReadableStreamDefaultReader> reader;
    };

    struct Input {
        explicit Input(Engine::BodyIntent body_intent)
            : body_intent(body_intent)
        {
        }

        Engine::BodyIntent body_intent;
        ProcessRequestBodyChunkLengthHeapFunction process_request_body_chunk_length;
        ProcessRequestEndOfBodyHeapFunction process_request_end_of_body;
        ProcessEarlyHintsResponseHeapFunction process_early_hints_response;
        ProcessResponseHeapFunction process_response;
        ProcessResponseEndOfBodyHeapFunction process_response_end_of_body;
        ProcessResponseConsumeBodyHeapFunction process_response_consume_body;
        Optional<RequestBodyReader> request_body_reader;
    };

    [[nodiscard]] static GC::Ref<FetchAlgorithms> create(Input);

    Engine::BodyIntent body_intent() const { return m_body_intent; }
    Optional<RequestBodyReader> const& request_body_reader() const { return m_request_body_reader; }
    ProcessRequestBodyChunkLengthHeapFunction process_request_body_chunk_length() const { return m_process_request_body_chunk_length; }
    ProcessRequestEndOfBodyHeapFunction process_request_end_of_body() const { return m_process_request_end_of_body; }
    ProcessEarlyHintsResponseHeapFunction process_early_hints_response() const { return m_process_early_hints_response; }
    ProcessResponseHeapFunction process_response() const { return m_process_response; }
    ProcessResponseEndOfBodyHeapFunction process_response_end_of_body() const { return m_process_response_end_of_body; }
    ProcessResponseConsumeBodyHeapFunction process_response_consume_body() const { return m_process_response_consume_body; }

    virtual void visit_edges(JS::Cell::Visitor&) override;

private:
    FetchAlgorithms(
        Engine::BodyIntent,
        ProcessRequestBodyChunkLengthHeapFunction process_request_body_chunk_length,
        ProcessRequestEndOfBodyHeapFunction process_request_end_of_body,
        ProcessEarlyHintsResponseHeapFunction process_early_hints_response,
        ProcessResponseHeapFunction process_response,
        ProcessResponseEndOfBodyHeapFunction process_response_end_of_body,
        ProcessResponseConsumeBodyHeapFunction process_response_consume_body,
        Optional<RequestBodyReader> request_body_reader);

    Engine::BodyIntent m_body_intent;
    ProcessRequestBodyChunkLengthHeapFunction m_process_request_body_chunk_length;
    ProcessRequestEndOfBodyHeapFunction m_process_request_end_of_body;
    ProcessEarlyHintsResponseHeapFunction m_process_early_hints_response;
    ProcessResponseHeapFunction m_process_response;
    ProcessResponseEndOfBodyHeapFunction m_process_response_end_of_body;
    ProcessResponseConsumeBodyHeapFunction m_process_response_consume_body;
    Optional<RequestBodyReader> m_request_body_reader;
};

/*

#pragma once

#include <AK/AtomicRefCounted.h>
#include <AK/Badge.h>
#include <AK/NonnullRefPtr.h>
#include <AK/Optional.h>
#include <AK/RefPtr.h>
#include <LibGC/Forward.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Engine/BodyIntent.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Engine/FetchTimingSeed.h>
#include <LibWeb/Fetch/Infrastructure/FetchTimingInfo.h>

namespace Web::Fetch::Infrastructure {

class FetchController;

// The state of a fetch that its controller and its fetch params share.
class FetchControlBlock : public AtomicRefCounted<FetchControlBlock> {
public:
    GC_HOLDS_NO_CELL_EDGES;

    enum class State : u8 {
        Ongoing,
        Terminated,
        Aborted,
        Stopped,
    };

    [[nodiscard]] static NonnullRefPtr<FetchControlBlock> create() { return adopt_ref(*new FetchControlBlock); }

    [[nodiscard]] State state() const { return m_state; }
    void set_state(Badge<FetchController>, State state) { m_state = state; }

    // https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-params-aborted
    [[nodiscard]] bool is_aborted() const
    {
        // A fetch params fetchParams is aborted if its controller’s state is "aborted".
        return m_state == State::Aborted;
    }

    // https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-params-canceled
    [[nodiscard]] bool is_canceled() const
    {
        // A fetch params fetchParams is canceled if its controller’s state is "aborted" or "terminated".
        return m_state == State::Aborted || m_state == State::Terminated;
    }

    [[nodiscard]] bool is_ongoing() const { return m_state == State::Ongoing; }
    [[nodiscard]] bool is_stopped() const { return m_state == State::Stopped; }

    [[nodiscard]] RefPtr<FetchTimingInfo> full_timing_info() const { return m_full_timing_info; }
    void set_full_timing_info(NonnullRefPtr<FetchTimingInfo> full_timing_info) { m_full_timing_info = move(full_timing_info); }

    // The agent's timing state, which only the thread of the agent that started the fetch reads and writes.

    // The timing info the agent has of its latest response handover.
    [[nodiscard]] RefPtr<FetchTimingInfo> agent_timing_info() const { return m_agent_timing_info; }
    // Makes the agent's timing info from the fields a response handover gives it, the network phases settled last and
    // the fetch's end time.
    NonnullRefPtr<FetchTimingInfo> hand_over_timing(Engine::FetchTimingSeed const& seed)
    {
        auto timing_info = FetchTimingInfo::create(seed);
        if (m_network_phases.has_value())
            timing_info->set_network_phases(*m_network_phases);
        timing_info->set_end_time(m_end_time);
        m_agent_timing_info = timing_info;
        return timing_info;
    }
    // Gives the network phases a load of the fetch settled to the agent's timing info, and to that of later handovers.
    void settle_network_phases(Engine::FetchNetworkPhases network_phases)
    {
        if (m_agent_timing_info)
            m_agent_timing_info->set_network_phases(network_phases);
        m_network_phases = move(network_phases);
    }
    // The end time last set for the fetch, or 0, which the agent's timing info has, as do those of later handovers.
    [[nodiscard]] HighResolutionTime::DOMHighResTimeStamp end_time() const { return m_end_time; }
    void set_end_time(HighResolutionTime::DOMHighResTimeStamp end_time)
    {
        if (m_agent_timing_info)
            m_agent_timing_info->set_end_time(end_time);
        m_end_time = end_time;
    }

    [[nodiscard]] Engine::BodyIntent body_intent() const { return m_body_intent; }
    void set_body_intent(Badge<FetchController>, Engine::BodyIntent body_intent)
    {
        VERIFY(!m_response_arrived);
        m_body_intent = body_intent;
    }

    // AD-HOC: Whether this fetch's response has arrived, from the network or at main fetch. From then on,
    //         consume_a_preloaded_resource() no longer changes the fetch's body intent or task destination.
    void set_response_arrived() { m_response_arrived = true; }
    [[nodiscard]] bool response_arrived() const { return m_response_arrived; }

    [[nodiscard]] bool has_started_request() const { return m_has_started_request; }
    void set_has_started_request() { m_has_started_request = true; }

    [[nodiscard]] bool requires_network() const { return m_requires_network; }
    void set_requires_network() { m_requires_network = true; }

private:
    FetchControlBlock() = default;

    // https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller-state
    // state (default "ongoing")
    //    "ongoing", "terminated", or "aborted"
    State m_state { State::Ongoing };

    // https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller-full-timing-info
    // full timing info (default null)
    //    Null or a fetch timing info.
    RefPtr<FetchTimingInfo> m_full_timing_info;

    // The agent's timing state, which only the thread of the agent that started the fetch reads and writes.
    RefPtr<FetchTimingInfo> m_agent_timing_info;
    Optional<Engine::FetchNetworkPhases> m_network_phases;
    HighResolutionTime::DOMHighResTimeStamp m_end_time { 0 };

    Engine::BodyIntent m_body_intent { Engine::BodyIntent::DrainAndDiscard };
    bool m_response_arrived { false };
    bool m_has_started_request { false };
    bool m_requires_network { false };
};

}

#include <LibGC/Heap.h>

namespace Web::Fetch::Infrastructure {

extern "C" {

// Called by Bindings/Rust/src/fetch/infrastructure/fetch_controller.rs.
FetchController* web_fetch_controller_create(JSObject* global_object);
void web_fetch_controller_terminate(FetchController*);
void web_fetch_controller_abort(FetchController*, void* realm);
bool web_fetch_controller_has_report_timing_steps(FetchController*);

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(FetchController);

FetchController::FetchController(FetchControllerRegistry& registry)
    : m_registry(registry)
    , m_token(registry.add({}, *this))
    , m_control_block(FetchControlBlock::create())
{
}

GC::Ref<FetchController> FetchController::create(FetchControllerRegistry& registry)
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<FetchController>(registry);
}

void FetchController::visit_edges(JS::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_realm);
    visitor.visit(m_report_timing_steps);
    if (m_awaited_end_of_body.has_value())
        visitor.visit(m_awaited_end_of_body->steps);
    visitor.visit(m_next_manual_redirect_steps);
    visitor.visit(m_algorithms);
    visitor.visit(m_task_destination);
    visitor.visit(m_page);
    visitor.visit(m_pending_preloaded_response);
    visitor.visit(m_stop_steps);
    visitor.visit(m_pending_responses);
}

void FetchController::finalize()
{
    // A discarded response can leave an ongoing controller without a stop or end-of-body task.
    end_rendering_pending_operation(this);
    Base::finalize();
    if (m_registry)
        m_registry->remove({}, m_token);
}

void FetchController::set_algorithms(Badge<FetchParams>, GC::Ref<FetchAlgorithms const> algorithms)
{
    VERIFY(!m_algorithms);
    m_algorithms = algorithms;
    m_control_block->set_body_intent({}, algorithms->body_intent());
}

void FetchController::retarget(TaskDestination task_destination, Engine::BodyIntent body_intent)
{
    m_task_destination = move(task_destination);
    m_control_block->set_body_intent({}, body_intent);
}

void FetchController::set_original_fetch_params(Badge<FetchParams>, FetchParams const& fetch_params)
{
    m_original_fetch_params = fetch_params;
}

void FetchController::set_network_observation(Badge<FetchParams>, NonnullRefPtr<NetworkObservation> network_observation)
{
    VERIFY(!m_network_observation);
    m_network_observation = move(network_observation);
}

void FetchController::report_webdriver_bidi_fetch_error(StringView error_text) const
{
    if (!WebDriver::BiDi::network_events_enabled())
        return;
    if (auto fetch_params = m_original_fetch_params.strong_ref())
        WebDriver::BiDi::network_fetch_error(*fetch_params, error_text);
}

void FetchController::cancel_webdriver_bidi_network_interception() const
{
    if (!WebDriver::BiDi::is_active())
        return;
    if (auto fetch_params = original_fetch_params())
        WebDriver::BiDi::cancel_network_interception(*fetch_params);
}

RefPtr<FetchParams> FetchController::original_fetch_params() const
{
    return m_original_fetch_params.strong_ref();
}

void FetchController::set_request(Badge<FetchParams>, NonnullRefPtr<Request> request)
{
    VERIFY(!m_request);
    m_request = move(request);
}

NonnullRefPtr<Request> FetchController::request() const
{
    VERIFY(m_request);
    return *m_request;
}

GC::Ref<FetchAlgorithms const> FetchController::algorithms() const
{
    VERIFY(m_algorithms);
    return *m_algorithms;
}

GC::Ref<Page> FetchController::page() const
{
    VERIFY(m_page);
    return *m_page;
}

void FetchController::set_report_timing_steps(GC::Ref<GC::Function<void(JS::Object&)>> report_timing_steps)
{
    m_report_timing_steps = report_timing_steps;
}

void FetchController::set_next_manual_redirect_steps(GC::Ref<GC::Function<void()>> next_manual_redirect_steps)
{
    m_next_manual_redirect_steps = next_manual_redirect_steps;
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#finalize-and-report-timing
void FetchController::report_timing(JS::Object& global) const
{
    // 1. Assert: this’s report timing steps is not null.
    VERIFY(m_report_timing_steps);

    // 2. Call this’s report timing steps with global.
    m_report_timing_steps->function()(global);
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller-process-the-next-manual-redirect
void FetchController::process_next_manual_redirect() const
{
    // 1. Assert: controller’s next manual redirect steps are not null.
    VERIFY(m_next_manual_redirect_steps);

    // 2. Call controller’s next manual redirect steps.
    m_next_manual_redirect_steps->function()();
}

void FetchController::resolve_redirect(Engine::Command::ResolveRedirect::Resolution resolution)
{
    auto continuation_id = exchange(m_redirect_continuation_id, {});
    if (!continuation_id.has_value())
        return;

    VERIFY(m_started_fetch.has_value());
    Engine::Command::ResolveRedirect resolve {
        .fetch_id = m_started_fetch->fetch_id,
        .continuation_id = *continuation_id,
        .resolution = move(resolution),
    };
    m_started_fetch->fetch_executor->post(move(resolve));
}

void FetchController::when_body_ends(Engine::DeliveryId delivery_id, GC::Ptr<GC::Function<void(HighResolutionTime::DOMHighResTimeStamp)>> steps)
{
    if (m_fetch_ended)
        return;
    m_awaited_end_of_body = AwaitedEndOfBody { delivery_id, steps };
}

void FetchController::did_end_body(Engine::Event::EndOfBody const& end_of_body)
{
    if (!m_awaited_end_of_body.has_value() || m_awaited_end_of_body->delivery_id != end_of_body.delivery_id)
        return;
    auto awaited = m_awaited_end_of_body.release_value();
    if (awaited.steps)
        awaited.steps->function()(end_of_body.end_time);
}

void FetchController::did_end_fetch()
{
    m_fetch_ended = true;
    m_awaited_end_of_body.clear();

    VERIFY(m_started_fetch.has_value());
    if (auto* registry = m_registry.ptr())
        registry->release_fetch(m_started_fetch->fetch_id);
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#extract-full-timing-info
NonnullRefPtr<FetchTimingInfo> FetchController::extract_full_timing_info() const
{
    // 1. Assert: this’s full timing info is not null.
    auto full_timing_info = m_control_block->full_timing_info();
    VERIFY(full_timing_info);

    // 2. Return this’s full timing info.
    return full_timing_info.release_nonnull();
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller-abort
void FetchController::abort(JS::Realm& realm, Optional<JS::Value> error)
{
    // 1. Set controller’s state to "aborted".
    m_control_block->set_state({}, State::Aborted);
    report_webdriver_bidi_fetch_error("Fetch was aborted"sv);
    cancel_webdriver_bidi_network_interception();

    // 2. Let fallbackError be an "AbortError" DOMException.
    auto fallback_error = WebIDL::AbortError::create("Fetch was aborted"_utf16);
    auto fallback_error_value = throw_completion(realm, fallback_error).value();

    // 3. Set error to fallbackError if it is not given.
    if (!error.has_value())
        error = fallback_error_value;

    // 4. Let serializedError be StructuredSerialize(error). If that threw an exception, catch it, and let serializedError be StructuredSerialize(fallbackError).
    // 5. Set controller’s serialized abort reason to serializedError
    auto structured_serialize = [&realm](JS::Value error, JS::Value fallback_error) {
        auto serialized_value_or_error = HTML::structured_serialize(realm.vm(), error);
        return serialized_value_or_error.is_error()
            ? HTML::structured_serialize(realm.vm(), fallback_error).value()
            : serialized_value_or_error.value();
    };
    m_serialized_abort_reason = structured_serialize(error.value(), fallback_error_value);

    stop_request();
}

// https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller-terminate
void FetchController::terminate()
{
    // To terminate a fetch controller controller, set controller’s state to "terminated".
    m_control_block->set_state({}, State::Terminated);
    report_webdriver_bidi_fetch_error("Fetch was terminated"sv);
    cancel_webdriver_bidi_network_interception();

    stop_request();
}

void FetchController::set_started_fetch(Engine::FetchId fetch_id, Engine::FetchExecutor& fetch_executor)
{
    VERIFY(!m_started_fetch.has_value());
    m_started_fetch = StartedFetch { fetch_id, fetch_executor };
}

Optional<Engine::FetchId> FetchController::started_fetch_id() const
{
    if (!m_started_fetch.has_value())
        return {};
    return m_started_fetch->fetch_id;
}

Engine::FetchExecutor& FetchController::started_fetch_executor() const
{
    VERIFY(m_started_fetch.has_value());
    return *m_started_fetch->fetch_executor;
}

void FetchController::stop_fetch()
{
    if (m_control_block->is_canceled())
        return;

    m_control_block->set_state({}, State::Stopped);
    report_webdriver_bidi_fetch_error("Fetch was stopped"sv);
    cancel_webdriver_bidi_network_interception();

    // AD-HOC: Some HTML elements need to stop an ongoing fetching process without causing any network error to be raised
    //         (which abort() and terminate() will both do). This is tricky because the fetch process runs across several
    //         nested Platform::EventLoopPlugin::deferred_invoke() invocations. For now, we "stop" the fetch process by
    //         cancelling any queued fetch tasks and then ignoring any callbacks.
    auto ongoing_fetch_tasks = move(m_ongoing_fetch_tasks);

    HTML::current_event_loop().task_queue().remove_tasks_matching([&](auto const& task) {
        return ongoing_fetch_tasks.remove_all_matching([&](u64, HTML::TaskID task_id) {
            return task.id() == task_id;
        });
    });

    if (m_algorithms)
        m_algorithms = FetchAlgorithms::create(FetchAlgorithms::Input { m_control_block->body_intent() });

    stop_request();

    if (auto stop_steps = m_stop_steps) {
        m_stop_steps = nullptr;
        stop_steps->function()();
    }
}

static Engine::EngineCommand stop_command(FetchControlBlock::State state, Engine::FetchId fetch_id)
{
    switch (state) {
    case FetchControlBlock::State::Aborted:
        return Engine::Command::Abort { fetch_id };
    case FetchControlBlock::State::Terminated:
        return Engine::Command::Terminate { fetch_id };
    case FetchControlBlock::State::Stopped:
        return Engine::Command::Stop { fetch_id };
    case FetchControlBlock::State::Ongoing:
        break;
    }
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

// Posts the command that stops the network request of a fetch that is no longer ongoing, to the executor the fetch was
// started on.
void FetchController::stop_request()
{
    end_rendering_pending_operation(this);
    VERIFY(!m_control_block->is_ongoing());
    m_awaited_end_of_body.clear();

    if (!m_started_fetch.has_value())
        return;
    m_started_fetch->fetch_executor->post(stop_command(state(), m_started_fetch->fetch_id));
}

void FetchController::fetch_task_queued(u64 fetch_task_id, HTML::TaskID event_id)
{
    m_ongoing_fetch_tasks.set(fetch_task_id, event_id);
}

void FetchController::fetch_task_complete(u64 fetch_task_id)
{
    m_ongoing_fetch_tasks.remove(fetch_task_id);
}

void FetchController::add_pending_response(Badge<Fetching::PendingResponse>, GC::Ref<Fetching::PendingResponse> pending_response)
{
    VERIFY(!m_pending_responses.contains_slow(pending_response));
    m_pending_responses.append(pending_response);
}

void FetchController::remove_pending_response(Badge<Fetching::PendingResponse>, GC::Ref<Fetching::PendingResponse> pending_response)
{
    m_pending_responses.remove_first_matching([&](auto entry) { return entry == pending_response; });
}

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(FetchControllerHolder);

FetchControllerHolder::FetchControllerHolder() = default;

GC::Ref<FetchControllerHolder> FetchControllerHolder::create()
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<FetchControllerHolder>();
}

void FetchControllerHolder::visit_edges(JS::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_controller);
}

FetchController* web_fetch_controller_create(JSObject* global_object)
{
    auto& relevant_agent = HTML::relevant_agent(*JS::HostABI::object_from_abi(global_object));
    return FetchController::create(relevant_agent.fetch_controller_registry).ptr();
}

void web_fetch_controller_terminate(FetchController* controller)
{
    controller->terminate();
}

void web_fetch_controller_abort(FetchController* controller, void* realm)
{
    controller->abort(*static_cast<JS::Realm*>(realm), {});
}

bool web_fetch_controller_has_report_timing_steps(FetchController* controller)
{
    return controller->has_report_timing_steps();
}

void web_fetch_controller_report_timing(FetchController* controller, JSObject* global_object)
{
    controller->report_timing(*JS::HostABI::object_from_abi(global_object));
}

}
