    void set_user_agent_initiated(UserAgentInitiated user_agent_initiated) { m_user_agent_initiated = user_agent_initiated; }

    [[nodiscard]] Utf16String const& navigable_target_name() const { return m_navigable_target_name; }
    void set_navigable_target_name(Utf16String navigable_target_name) { m_navigable_target_name = move(navigable_target_name); }

private:
    DocumentState();

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-document
    // NOTE: We store the document's unique ID rather than a pointer to the document, because DocumentState is
    //       decoupled from the document's lifetime (LocalNavigable owns the document directly).
    Optional<UniqueNodeID> m_document_id;

    // AD-HOC: Stable identity used to preserve shared document states across canonical UI history and WebContent process swaps.
    CrossProcessId m_cross_process_id;

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-history-policy-container
    Variant<SerializedPolicyContainer, Client> m_history_policy_container { Client::Tag };

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-request-referrer
    Fetch::Infrastructure::Request::ReferrerType m_request_referrer { Fetch::Infrastructure::Request::Referrer::Client };

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-request-referrer-policy
    ReferrerPolicy::ReferrerPolicy m_request_referrer_policy { ReferrerPolicy::DEFAULT_REFERRER_POLICY };

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-initiator-origin
    Optional<URL::Origin> m_initiator_origin;

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-origin
    Optional<URL::Origin> m_origin;

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-about-base-url
    Optional<URL::URL> m_about_base_url = {};

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-resource
    DocumentResource m_resource {};

    HTTP::Cookie::SameSiteStatus m_navigation_same_site_status { HTTP::Cookie::SameSiteStatus::CrossSite };

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-reload-pending
    bool m_reload_pending { false };

    // AD-HOC: Whether the pending reload bypasses the HTTP cache, as the user can ask one to. HTML leaves that to the
    //         user agent: "When a user requests a reload of a navigable, user agents may provide a mechanism for
    //         ignoring any caches when reloading."
    //         https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/speculative-loading.html#nav-traversal-ui
    bool m_reload_bypasses_cache { false };

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-ever-populated
    bool m_ever_populated { false };

    // AD-HOC: Not one of the spec's document state fields. It's whether the navigation that created the entry had no
    //         source document, recorded so a traversal back to the entry can replay it. Blink and Gecko keep the same
    //         on their entries: Blink an absent FrameNavigationEntry::initiator_origin(), Gecko a system principal as
    //         SessionHistoryInfo::GetTriggeringPrincipal().
    UserAgentInitiated m_user_agent_initiated { UserAgentInitiated::No };

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-nav-target-name
    Utf16String m_navigable_target_name;
};

}

#include <LibGC/Heap.h>

#include <LibWeb/TrustedTypes/TrustedTypePolicy.h>
#include <LibWeb/XML/XMLDocumentBuilder.h>
#include <LibXML/Parser/Parser.h>

namespace Web::HTML {

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(DOMParser);

GC::Ref<DOMParser> DOMParser::create()
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<DOMParser>();
}

DOMParser::~DOMParser() = default;

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-domparser-parsefromstring
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<GC::Root<DOM::Document>> DOMParser::parse_from_string(JS::Realm& realm, TrustedTypes::TrustedHTMLOrString string, Bindings::DOMParserSupportedType type)
{
    // 1. Let compliantString to the result of invoking the Get Trusted Type compliant string algorithm with
    //    TrustedHTML, this's relevant global object, string, "DOMParser parseFromString", and "script".
    auto const compliant_string = TRY(TrustedTypes::get_trusted_type_compliant_string(
        TrustedTypes::TrustedTypeName::TrustedHTML,
        realm.global_object(),
        move(string),
        TrustedTypes::InjectionSink::DOMParser_parseFromString,
        TrustedTypes::Script.view()));

    // 2. Let document be a new Document, whose content type is type and url is this's relevant global object's associated Document's URL.
    GC::Ptr<DOM::Document> document;
    auto& associated_document = HTML::relevant_window(realm.global_object()).associated_document();

    // 3. Switch on type:
    if (type == Bindings::DOMParserSupportedType::Text_Html) {
        // -> "text/html"
        document = HTML::HTMLDocument::create(associated_document.page(), associated_document.relevant_global_event_target(), associated_document.url());
        document->set_content_type(Bindings::idl_enum_to_string(type));
        document->set_document_type(DOM::Document::Type::HTML);

        // 1. Parse HTML from a string given document and compliantString.
        [[maybe_unused]] auto wrapper = Bindings::wrap(Bindings::host_defined_wrapper_world(realm), realm, GC::Ref { *document });
        document->parse_html_from_a_string(compliant_string.utf16_view());
    } else {
        // -> Otherwise
        document = DOM::Document::create(associated_document.page(), associated_document.relevant_global_event_target(), associated_document.url());
        document->set_content_type(Bindings::idl_enum_to_string(type));
        document->set_document_type(DOM::Document::Type::XML);

        // 1. Create an XML parser parse, associated with document, and with XML scripting support disabled.
        auto const utf8_complaint_string = compliant_string.to_utf8_but_should_be_ported_to_utf16();
        XML::Parser parser(utf8_complaint_string, { .preserve_comments = true, .resolve_named_html_entity = resolve_named_html_entity });
        XMLDocumentBuilder builder { *document, XMLScriptingSupport::Disabled };
        // 2. Parse compliantString using parser.
        auto result = parser.parse_with_listener(builder);
        // 3. If the previous step resulted in an XML well-formedness or XML namespace well-formedness error, then:
        if (result.is_error() || builder.has_error()) {
            // NOTE: The XML parsing can produce nodes before it hits an error, just remove them.
            // 1. Assert: document has no child nodes.
            document->remove_all_children(true);
            // 2. Let root be the result of creating an element given document, "parsererror", and "http://www.mozilla.org/newlayout/xml/parsererror.xml".
            auto root = DOM::create_element(*document, "parsererror"_utf16_fly_string, "http://www.mozilla.org/newlayout/xml/parsererror.xml"_utf16_fly_string).release_value_but_fixme_should_propagate_errors();
            // FIXME: 3. Optionally, add attributes or children to root to describe the nature of the parsing error.
            // 4. Append root to document.
            MUST(document->append_child(*root));
        }
    }

    // AD-HOC: Setting the origin to match that of the associated document matches the behavior of existing browsers
    //         and avoids a crash, since we expect the origin to always be set.
    // Spec issue: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11429
    document->set_origin(associated_document.origin());

    // 3. Return document.
    return document;
}

}

extern "C" void* web_dom_string_list_create(JSVM*, ReadonlySpan<FlatPtr> strings);

GC::Ref<DOMStringList> DOMStringList::create(Vector<Utf16String> strings)
{
    Vector<FlatPtr> raw_strings;
    raw_strings.ensure_capacity(strings.size());
    for (auto& string : strings)
        raw_strings.unchecked_append(move(string).into_raw());

    return GC::Ref { *static_cast<DOMStringList*>(web_dom_string_list_create(JS::HostABI::vm_to_abi(JS::VM::the()), raw_strings.span())) };
}

}

bool DragDataStore::has_text_item() const
{
    for (auto const& item : m_item_list) {
        if (item.kind == DragDataStoreItem::Kind::Text && item.type_string == u"text/plain"sv)
            return true;

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(ElementInternals);

GC::Ref<ElementInternals> ElementInternals::create(HTMLElement& target_element)
{
    return GC::Heap::the().allocate<ElementInternals>(target_element);
}

ElementInternals::ElementInternals(HTMLElement& target_element)
    : m_target_element(target_element)
{
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#dom-elementinternals-shadowroot
GC::Ptr<DOM::ShadowRoot> ElementInternals::shadow_root() const
{
    // 1. Let target be this's target element.
    auto target = m_target_element;

    // 2. If target is not a shadow host, then return null.
    if (!target->is_shadow_host())
        return nullptr;

    // 3. Let shadow be target's shadow root.
    auto shadow = target->shadow_root();

    // 4. If shadow's available to element internals is false, then return null.
    if (!shadow->available_to_element_internals())
        return nullptr;

    // 5. Return shadow.
    return shadow;
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#dom-elementinternals-setformvalue
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> ElementInternals::set_form_value(ElementInternalsFormValue value, Optional<ElementInternalsFormValue> state)
{
    // 1. Let element be this's target element.
    auto element = m_target_element;

    // 2. If element is not a form-associated custom element, then throw a "NotSupportedError" DOMException.
    if (!element->is_form_associated_custom_element())
        return WebIDL::NotSupportedError::create("Element is not a form-associated custom element"_utf16);

    // 3. Set target element's submission value to value if value is not a FormData object, or to a clone of value's entry list otherwise.
    auto submission_value = value.visit(
        [](GC::Ref<FileAPI::File> file) -> FormAssociatedElement::FACESubmissionValue {
            return file;
        },
        [](Utf16String const& string) -> FormAssociatedElement::FACESubmissionValue {
            return string;
        },
        [](GC::Ref<XHR::FormData> form_data) -> FormAssociatedElement::FACESubmissionValue {
            return form_data->entry_list();
        },
        [](Empty const& empty) -> FormAssociatedElement::FACESubmissionValue {
            return empty;
        });

    element->set_face_submission_value({}, submission_value);

    // 4. If the state argument of the function is omitted, set element's state to its submission value.
    if (!state.has_value()) {
        element->set_face_state({}, submission_value);
    }

    // 5. Otherwise, if state is a FormData object, set element's state to a clone of state's entry list.
    // 6. Otherwise, set element's state to state.
    else {
        auto state_value = state.value().visit(
            [](GC::Ref<FileAPI::File> file) -> FormAssociatedElement::FACESubmissionValue {
                return GC::Ref { *file };
            },
            [](Utf16String const& string) -> FormAssociatedElement::FACESubmissionValue {
                return string;
            },
            [](GC::Ref<XHR::FormData> form_data) -> FormAssociatedElement::FACESubmissionValue {
                return form_data->entry_list();
            },
            [](Empty const& empty) -> FormAssociatedElement::FACESubmissionValue {
                return empty;
            });

        element->set_face_state({}, state_value);
    }

    return {};
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#dom-elementinternals-form
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<GC::Ptr<HTMLFormElement>> ElementInternals::form() const
{
    // Form-associated custom elements don't have form IDL attribute. Instead, their ElementInternals object has a form IDL attribute.
    // On getting, it must throw a "NotSupportedError" DOMException if the target element is not a form-associated custom element.
    // Otherwise, it must return the element's form owner, or null if there isn't one.
    if (!m_target_element->is_form_associated_custom_element())
        return WebIDL::NotSupportedError::create("Element is not a form-associated custom element"_utf16);

    return m_target_element->form();
}

static bool validity_flags_has_one_or_more_true_values(ValidityStateFlags const& flags)
{
    return flags.value_missing
        || flags.type_mismatch
        || flags.pattern_mismatch
        || flags.too_long
        || flags.too_short
        || flags.range_underflow
        || flags.range_overflow
        || flags.step_mismatch
        || flags.bad_input
        || flags.custom_error;
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#dom-elementinternals-setvalidity
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<void> ElementInternals::set_validity(ValidityStateFlags const& flags, Optional<Utf16String> message, GC::Ptr<HTMLElement> anchor)
{
    // 1. Let element be this's target element.
    auto element = m_target_element;

    // 2. If element is not a form-associated custom element, then throw a "NotSupportedError" DOMException.
    if (!element->is_form_associated_custom_element())
        return WebIDL::NotSupportedError::create("Element is not a form-associated custom element"_utf16);

    // 3. If flags contains one or more true values and message is not given or is the empty string, then throw a TypeError.
    if (validity_flags_has_one_or_more_true_values(flags) && (!message.has_value() || message->is_empty())) {
        return WebIDL::SimpleException {
            WebIDL::SimpleExceptionType::TypeError,
            "Invalid flag(s) and empty message"_utf16
        };
    }

    // 4. For each entry flag → value of flags, set element's validity flag with the name flag to value.
    element->set_face_validity_flags({}, flags);

    // 5. Set element's validation message to the empty string if message is not given or all of element's validity flags are false, or to message otherwise.
    Utf16String validation_message;
    if (message.has_value() && validity_flags_has_one_or_more_true_values(flags))
        validation_message = message.release_value();

    element->set_face_validation_message({}, validation_message);

    // 6. If element's customError validity flag is true, then set element's custom validity error message to element's
    //    validation message. Otherwise, set element's custom validity error message to the empty string.
    element->set_custom_validity_error_message({}, flags.custom_error ? validation_message : Utf16String {});

    // 7. If anchor is not given, then set it to element.
    if (!anchor) {
        anchor = element;
    }

    // 8. Otherwise, if anchor is not a shadow-including inclusive descendant of element, then throw a "NotFoundError" DOMException.
    else if (!anchor->is_shadow_including_inclusive_descendant_of(element)) {
        return WebIDL::NotFoundError::create("Anchor is not a shadow-including descendant of element"_utf16);
    }

    // 9. Set element's validation anchor to anchor.
    element->set_face_validation_anchor({}, anchor);

    // AD-HOC: Updating the validity flags changes which validity pseudo-classes match.
    CSS::Invalidation::invalidate_style_after_validity_change(*element);
    return {};
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#dom-elementinternals-willvalidate
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<bool> ElementInternals::will_validate() const
{
    // The willValidate attribute of ElementInternals interface, on getting, must throw a "NotSupportedError" DOMException if
    // the target element is not a form-associated custom element. Otherwise, it must return true if the target element is a
    // candidate for constraint validation, and false otherwise.
    if (!m_target_element->is_form_associated_custom_element())
        return WebIDL::NotSupportedError::create("Element is not a form-associated custom element"_utf16);

    return m_target_element->is_candidate_for_constraint_validation();
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#dom-elementinternals-validity
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<GC::Ref<ValidityState const>> ElementInternals::validity() const
{
    // The validity attribute of ElementInternals interface, on getting, must throw a "NotSupportedError" DOMException if
    // the target element is not a form-associated custom element. Otherwise, it must return a ValidityState object that
    // represents the validity states of the target element. This object is live.
    if (!m_target_element->is_form_associated_custom_element())
        return WebIDL::NotSupportedError::create("Element is not a form-associated custom element"_utf16);

    return ValidityState::create(m_target_element);
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#dom-elementinternals-validationmessage
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<Utf16String> ElementInternals::validation_message() const
{
    // 1. Let element be this's target element.
    auto element = m_target_element;

    // 2. If element is not a form-associated custom element, then throw a "NotSupportedError" DOMException.
    if (!element->is_form_associated_custom_element())
        return WebIDL::NotSupportedError::create("Element is not a form-associated custom element"_utf16);

    // 3. Return element's validation message.
    return element->face_validation_message();
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#dom-elementinternals-checkvalidity
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<bool> ElementInternals::check_validity() const
{
    // 1. Let element be this ElementInternals's target element.
    auto element = m_target_element;

    // 2. If element is not a form-associated custom element, then throw a "NotSupportedError" DOMException.
    if (!element->is_form_associated_custom_element())
        return WebIDL::NotSupportedError::create("Element is not a form-associated custom element"_utf16);

    // 3. Run the check validity steps on element.
    return element->check_validity_steps();
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#dom-elementinternals-reportvalidity
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<bool> ElementInternals::report_validity() const
{
    // 1. Let element be this ElementInternals's target element
    auto element = m_target_element;

    // 2. If element is not a form-associated custom element, then throw a "NotSupportedError" DOMException.
    if (!element->is_form_associated_custom_element())
        return WebIDL::NotSupportedError::create("Element is not a form-associated custom element"_utf16);

    // 3. Run the report validity steps on element.
    return element->report_validity_steps();
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#dom-elementinternals-labels
WebIDL::ExceptionOr<GC::Ptr<DOM::NodeList>> ElementInternals::labels()
{
    // Form-associated custom elements don't have a labels IDL attribute. Instead, their ElementInternals object has a labels IDL attribute.
    // On getting, it must throw a "NotSupportedError" DOMException if the target element is not a form-associated custom element.
    // Otherwise, it must return that NodeList object, and that same value must always be returned.
    if (!m_target_element->is_form_associated_custom_element())
        return WebIDL::NotSupportedError::create("Element is not a form-associated custom element"_utf16);

    return m_target_element->labels();
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#dom-elementinternals-states
GC::Ptr<CustomStateSet> ElementInternals::states()
{
    // The states getter steps are to return this's target element's states set.
    return m_target_element->ensure_custom_state_set();
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#get-the-content-attribute
Optional<Utf16String> ElementInternals::get_attribute(Utf16FlyString const& content_attribute) const
{
    // 1. If elementInternals's target element's internal content attribute map[the reflected content attribute name]
    //    does not exist, then return null.
    // 2. Return elementInternals's target element's internal content attribute map[the reflected content attribute
    //    name].
    return m_target_element->internal_content_attribute(content_attribute);
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#set-the-content-attribute
void ElementInternals::set_attribute_value(Utf16FlyString const& content_attribute, Utf16String const& value)
{
    // Set elementInternals's target element's internal content attribute map[the reflected content attribute name]
    // to value.
    m_target_element->internal_content_attribute_map().set(content_attribute, value);
    did_change_default_aria_semantics();
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#delete-the-content-attribute
void ElementInternals::remove_attribute(Utf16FlyString const& content_attribute)
{
    // Remove elementInternals's target element's internal content attribute map[the reflected content attribute
    // name].
    m_target_element->internal_content_attribute_map().remove(content_attribute);
    did_change_default_aria_semantics();
}

// AD-HOC: A change to the internal content attribute map changes the default ARIA semantics of the target element, so
//         ask the client to rebuild the accessibility tree, as a DOM mutation does in Node::queue_mutation_record().
void ElementInternals::did_change_default_aria_semantics()
{
    auto& page = m_target_element->document().page();
    if (page.accessibility_interested()) {
        // Default ARIA semantics can change the element's role, and so its descendants' roles, as its role attribute can.
        m_target_element->document().invalidate_cached_accessibility_data(*m_target_element, ARIA::AttributeNames::role);
        page.client().page_did_change_accessibility_tree();
    }
}

#define __ENUMERATE_ARIA_ATTRIBUTE(name, attribute)                       \
    Optional<Utf16String> ElementInternals::name() const                  \
    {                                                                     \
        return get_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::name);                 \
    }                                                                     \
                                                                          \
    void ElementInternals::set_##name(Optional<Utf16String> const& value) \
    {                                                                     \
        if (value.has_value())                                            \
            set_attribute_value(ARIA::AttributeNames::name, *value);      \
        else                                                              \
            remove_attribute(ARIA::AttributeNames::name);                 \
    }
ENUMERATE_ARIA_ATTRIBUTES
#undef __ENUMERATE_ARIA_ATTRIBUTE

#define __ENUMERATE_ARIA_ATTRIBUTE(attribute, referencing_attribute)    \
    GC::Ptr<DOM::Element> ElementInternals::attribute() const           \
    {                                                                   \
        return m_##attribute.ptr();                                     \
    }                                                                   \
                                                                        \
    void ElementInternals::set_##attribute(GC::Ptr<DOM::Element> value) \
    {                                                                   \
        m_##attribute = value;                                          \
    }
ENUMERATE_ARIA_ELEMENT_REFERENCING_ATTRIBUTES
#undef __ENUMERATE_ARIA_ATTRIBUTE

#define __ENUMERATE_ARIA_ATTRIBUTE(attribute, referencing_attribute)                       \
    Optional<Vector<GC::Weak<DOM::Element>> const&> ElementInternals::attribute() const    \
    {                                                                                      \
        if (!m_##attribute.has_value())                                                    \
            return {};                                                                     \
        return *m_##attribute;                                                             \
    }                                                                                      \
                                                                                           \
    void ElementInternals::set_##attribute(Optional<Vector<GC::Weak<DOM::Element>>> value) \
    {                                                                                      \
        m_##attribute = move(value);                                                       \
    }
ENUMERATE_ARIA_ELEMENT_LIST_REFERENCING_ATTRIBUTES
#undef __ENUMERATE_ARIA_ATTRIBUTE

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#attr-associated-element
GC::Ptr<DOM::Element> ElementInternals::get_the_attribute_associated_element(Utf16FlyString const& content_attribute, GC::Ptr<DOM::Element> explicitly_set_attribute_element) const
{
    // 1. Let element be the result of running reflectedTarget's get the element.
    auto const& element = get_the_element();

    // 2. Let contentAttributeValue be the result of running reflectedTarget's get the content attribute.
    auto content_attribute_value = get_attribute(content_attribute);

    return DOM::get_the_attribute_associated_element(element, content_attribute_value, explicitly_set_attribute_element);
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#attr-associated-elements
Optional<GC::RootVector<GC::Ref<DOM::Element>>> ElementInternals::get_the_attribute_associated_elements(Utf16FlyString const& content_attribute, Optional<Vector<GC::Weak<DOM::Element>> const&> explicitly_set_attribute_elements) const
{
    // 2. Let element be the result of running reflectedTarget's get the element.
    auto const& element = get_the_element();

    return DOM::get_the_attribute_associated_elements(
        element, [&] { return get_attribute(content_attribute); }, explicitly_set_attribute_elements);
}

void ElementInternals::visit_edges(GC::Cell::Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_target_element);
}

namespace Web::Bindings {

struct PerElementInternalsReflectedArrayCache {
    HashMap<Utf16FlyString, WrapperWorldWeakValueCache<JS::Array>> arrays_by_attribute;
};

static GC::WeakHashMap<HTML::ElementInternals, PerElementInternalsReflectedArrayCache>& reflected_element_array_caches()
{
    static NeverDestroyed<GC::WeakHashMap<HTML::ElementInternals, PerElementInternalsReflectedArrayCache>> caches;
    return *caches;
}

static WrapperWorldWeakValueCache<JS::Array>& reflected_element_array_cache_for(HTML::ElementInternals& element_internals, Utf16FlyString const& reflected_attribute)
{
    auto& per_element_internals = reflected_element_array_caches().ensure(element_internals);
    return per_element_internals.arrays_by_attribute.ensure(reflected_attribute);
}

GC::Ptr<JS::Array> cached_reflected_element_array(HTML::ElementInternals& element_internals, WrapperWorld const& wrapper_world, Utf16FlyString const& reflected_attribute)
{
    return reflected_element_array_cache_for(element_internals, reflected_attribute).get(wrapper_world);
}

void set_cached_reflected_element_array(HTML::ElementInternals& element_internals, WrapperWorld const& wrapper_world, Utf16FlyString const& reflected_attribute, GC::Ptr<JS::Array> array)
{
    reflected_element_array_cache_for(element_internals, reflected_attribute).set(wrapper_world, array);
}

[Exposed=Window]
interface ElementInternals {
    // Shadow root access
    readonly attribute ShadowRoot? shadowRoot;

    // Form-associated custom elements
    undefined setFormValue((File or USVString or FormData)? value,
                            optional (File or USVString or FormData)? state);

    readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;

    undefined setValidity(optional ValidityStateFlags flags = {},
                          optional DOMString message,
                          optional HTMLElement anchor);
    readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
    readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
    readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
    boolean checkValidity();
    boolean reportValidity();

    readonly attribute NodeList labels;

    // Custom state pseudo-class
    [SameObject] readonly attribute CustomStateSet states;
};

ElementInternals includes ARIAMixin;

    boolean valueMissing = false;
    boolean typeMismatch = false;
    boolean patternMismatch = false;
    boolean tooLong = false;
    boolean tooShort = false;
    boolean rangeUnderflow = false;
    boolean rangeOverflow = false;
    boolean stepMismatch = false;
    boolean badInput = false;
    boolean customError = false;
};

namespace Web::HTML {

extern "C" {
// Defined in Bindings/Rust/src/html/error_event.rs.
DOM::Event* web_rust_error_event_create(JSVM*, void* realm, FlatPtr type, bool bubbles, bool cancelable, bool composed, FlatPtr message, FlatPtr filename, u32 lineno, u32 colno, JSValue error);
void web_rust_error_event_attributes(Bindings::RustInterfaceCell* event, FlatPtr* message, FlatPtr* filename, u32* lineno, u32* colno, JSValue* error);
}

GC::Ref<DOM::Event> create_error_event(JS::Realm& realm, Utf16FlyString const& type, DOM::EventInit const& event_init, ErrorInformation const& error_information)
{
    return *web_rust_error_event_create(JS::HostABI::vm_to_abi(realm.vm()), &realm, type.raw_identity(), event_init.bubbles, event_init.cancelable, event_init.composed,
        error_information.message.raw_identity(), error_information.filename.raw_identity(), static_cast<u32>(error_information.lineno), static_cast<u32>(error_information.colno), JS::HostABI::value_to_abi(error_information.error));
}

bool is_error_event(DOM::Event const& event)
{
    return Bindings::rust_event_owner(event, Bindings::InterfaceName::ErrorEvent);
}

Optional<ErrorInformation> error_event_information(DOM::Event const& event)
{
    auto* owner = Bindings::rust_event_owner(event, Bindings::InterfaceName::ErrorEvent);
    if (!owner)
        return {};

    FlatPtr message = 0;
    FlatPtr filename = 0;
    u32 lineno = 0;
    u32 colno = 0;
    JSValue error {};
    web_rust_error_event_attributes(owner, &message, &filename, &lineno, &colno, &error);
    return ErrorInformation {
        .message = Utf16String::adopt_raw(message),
        .filename = Utf16String::adopt_raw(filename),
        .error = JS::HostABI::value_from_abi(error),
        .lineno = lineno,
        .colno = colno,
    };
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#extract-error
ErrorInformation extract_error_information(JS::VM& vm, JS::Value exception)
{
    // 1. Let attributes be an empty map keyed by IDL attributes.
    ErrorInformation attributes;

    // 2. Set attributes[error] to exception.
    attributes.error = exception;

    // 3. Set attributes[message], attributes[filename], attributes[lineno], and attributes[colno] to
    //    implementation-defined values derived from exception.
    // NB: An Error's or a DOMException's message is prefixed with its name, as Error.prototype.toString() does.
    auto prefix_with_name = [](Utf16String name, Utf16String message) {
        if (message.is_empty())
            return name;
        if (name.is_empty())
            return message;
        return Utf16String::formatted("{}: {}", name, message);
    };

    attributes.message = [&] {
        if (auto object = exception.as_if<JS::Object>()) {
            // NB: A DOMException's name and message are accessors on its prototype.
            if (auto const* dom_exception = Bindings::dom_exception_from_object(*object))
                return prefix_with_name(dom_exception->name().to_utf16_string(), dom_exception->message().to_utf16_string());

            // NB: Whatever script threw must not get to run here, so stay away from the traps of a proxy. What is left is
            //     a module namespace object whose binding of that name is not initialized yet.
            if (auto has_message = object->is_proxy() ? false : object->has_own_property(vm.names.message); !has_message.is_error() && has_message.value()) {
                auto message = object->get_without_side_effects(vm.names.message).to_utf16_string_without_side_effects();
                if (is<JS::Error>(*object)) {
                    auto name = object->get_without_side_effects(vm.names.name);
                    if (name.is_string())
                        return prefix_with_name(name.to_utf16_string_without_side_effects(), move(message));
                }
                return message;
            }
        }

        return Utf16String::formatted("Uncaught exception: {}", exception);
    }();

    // FIXME: This offset is relative to the javascript source. Other browsers appear to do it relative
    //        to the entire source document! Calculate that somehow.

    // NB: Take the throw site even when an Error's traceback gives the location, so the VM stops keeping it alive.
    auto throw_site = vm.take_throw_site_of(exception);

    // NB: If we got an Error object, then try and extract the information from the location the object was made. Only
    //     the script-visible frames count, so the location does not change while a debugger is attached.
    bool has_location = false;
    if (auto object = exception.as_if<JS::Object>(); object && object->error_data()) {
        for (auto const& frame : object->error_data()->script_visible_traceback()) {
            auto source_range = frame.source_range();
            if (source_range.start.line != 0 || source_range.start.column != 0) {
                attributes.filename = source_range.filename();
                attributes.lineno = source_range.start.line;
                attributes.colno = source_range.start.column;
                has_location = true;
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    if (has_location)
        return attributes;

    // NB: Otherwise, if a throw statement threw it, take the location from there. That includes an Error whose stack
    //     has no frames, as with Error.stackTraceLimit set to 0.
    if (throw_site.has_value()) {
        attributes.filename = throw_site->filename();
        attributes.lineno = throw_site->start.line;
        attributes.colno = throw_site->start.column;
    }
    // NB: Otherwise, we fall back to try and find the location of the invocation of the function itself.
    else if (auto source_range = vm.innermost_source_range(); source_range.has_value()) {
        attributes.filename = source_range->filename();
        attributes.lineno = source_range->start.line;
        attributes.colno = source_range->start.column;
    }

    // 4. Return attributes.
    return attributes;
}

}

    visitor.visit(listener);

class EventHandler final : public JS::Cell {
    GC_CELL(EventHandler, JS::Cell);
    GC_DECLARE_ALLOCATOR(EventHandler);

public:
    explicit EventHandler(Utf16String);
    explicit EventHandler(WebIDL::CallbackType&);

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-handler-listener
    // NB: This comes first, so that it fills the padding at the end of the cell header.
    GC::Member<DOM::DOMEventListener> listener;

    // https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-handler-value
    // NOTE: This does not contain Empty as part of the optimization of not allocating all event handler attributes up front.
    // FIXME: The string should actually be an "internal raw uncompiled handler" struct. This struct is just the uncompiled source code plus a source location for reporting parse errors.
    //        https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#internal-raw-uncompiled-handler
    Variant<Utf16String, GC::Ptr<WebIDL::CallbackType>> value;

private:
    virtual void visit_edges(Cell::Visitor&) override;
};

// Whether the keyframes of `effect` animate a property a clock tick cannot sample: a custom property, or one that changes
// the layout tree's shape or what the main thread observes of an element's box.
static bool animates_what_a_tick_cannot(Animations::EffectRef const& effect)
{
    auto const& keyframe_set = effect.keyframe_set();
    return keyframe_set && keyframe_set.facts().animates_what_a_tick_cannot;
}

// Whether the keyframes of `effect` animate a property that the children of its target inherit.
static bool animates_an_inherited_property(Animations::EffectRef const& effect)
{
    auto const& keyframe_set = effect.keyframe_set();
    return keyframe_set && keyframe_set.facts().animates_an_inherited_property;
}

// Whether no box shows anything of the animation of `effect` on `target`: the target has no box, as under
// `display: none`, or it is `display: contents`, and the effect animates neither one of its pseudo-elements nor what its
// children inherit, or those have no boxes either.
static bool no_box_shows(Animations::EffectRef const& effect, DOM::Element const& target, Layout::BegunRead const& read)
{
    if (target.unsafe_layout_node(read))
        return false;
    if (!target.has_display_contents() || (!effect.pseudo_element_type().has_value() && !animates_an_inherited_property(effect)))
        return true;
    // The pseudo-elements and children of a `display: contents` element are laid out where the nearest element above it
    // with a box lays out its own.
    for (auto const* ancestor = target.flat_tree_parent_element(); ancestor; ancestor = ancestor->flat_tree_parent_element()) {
        if (ancestor->unsafe_layout_node(read))
            return false;
        if (!ancestor->has_display_contents())
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// Whether a tick can sample the animation of `effect` on `target`.
static bool tick_can_sample(DOM::Document const& document, Animations::EffectRef const& effect, DOM::Element const& target, Layout::BegunRead const& read)
{
    // The root element and the body paint the background the canvas may take over, which only the host resolves.
    auto const* layout_node = target.unsafe_layout_node(read);
    return !effect.pseudo_element_type().has_value() && target.namespace_uri() == Namespace::HTML
        && &target != document.document_element() && &target != document.body()
        && layout_node && Painting::has_committed_box(*layout_node) && !animates_what_a_tick_cannot(effect);
}

// NB: An animation of a scroll timeline that finished runs again as the scroll goes back.
static bool runs_for_clock_plan(Animations::RustFFI::AnimationPlayState play_state, bool on_scroll_timeline)
{
    return play_state == Animations::RustFFI::AnimationPlayState::Running || (on_scroll_timeline && play_state == Animations::RustFFI::AnimationPlayState::Finished);
}

// The compositor runs these on its own, so the render clock does not sample them.
static bool runs_on_compositor(Animations::EffectRef const& effect)
{
    return effect.is_compositor_driven() || effect.is_compositor_replaced();
}

// Whether the render clock may hover what is under the pointer while a task runs. LIBWEB_HOVER_LANE=0 turns it off.
bool hover_lane_is_enabled()
{
    static bool const enabled = [] {
        auto value = getenv("LIBWEB_HOVER_LANE");
        return !value || StringView { value, strlen(value) } != "0"sv;
    }();
    return enabled;
}

// The page's cursor, as a hover of the render clock asks it to show the cursor of what it hovers, on the Render
// thread.
static Layout::RustFFI::FfiPageCursor ffi_page_cursor(PageCursor& cursor)
{
    return {
        .cursor = &cursor,
        .retain = [](void const* cursor) { static_cast<PageCursor const*>(cursor)->ref(); },
        .release = [](void const* cursor) { static_cast<PageCursor const*>(cursor)->unref(); },
        .request = [](void const* cursor, u8 css_cursor) {
            auto& page_cursor = const_cast<PageCursor&>(*static_cast<PageCursor const*>(cursor));
            page_cursor.request(css_to_gfx_cursor(static_cast<CSS::CursorPredefined>(css_cursor))); },
    };
}

// What tells the document's page the link a hover of the render clock is over, on the Render thread.
static Layout::RustFFI::FfiHoverLinkReporter ffi_hover_link_reporter(DOM::Document& document)
{
    document.update_hover_link_base();
    return {
        .reporter = &document.hover_link_reporter(),
        .retain = [](void const* reporter) { static_cast<HoverLinkReporter const*>(reporter)->ref(); },
        .release = [](void const* reporter) { static_cast<HoverLinkReporter const*>(reporter)->unref(); },
        .is_link = [](void const* reporter, u32 element) { return static_cast<HoverLinkReporter const*>(reporter)->is_link(element); },
        .report = [](void const* reporter, u32 element) { const_cast<HoverLinkReporter&>(*static_cast<HoverLinkReporter const*>(reporter)).report(element); },
        .withdraw = [](void const* reporter) { const_cast<HoverLinkReporter&>(*static_cast<HoverLinkReporter const*>(reporter)).withdraw(); },
    };
}

bool seal_clock_plan(DOM::Document& document, bool may_plan, u64 update_serial)
{
    auto* arena = document.layout_node_arena_if_created();
    if (!arena)
        return false;
    if (may_plan) {
        // The plan reads the boxes of the elements it names and seals its round from the document's layout.
        Layout::ForcedReadScope read { document };
        // The elements whose running animations a tick samples, the timestamp at which the sampled animations of the
        // document timeline have all ended, after which only a scroll moves anything, and the scroll timelines a tick
        // samples where the compositor has scrolled to. The ticks go on past the events of the animations, which the
        // main thread sends as it gets to them.
        Vector<u32> elements;
        // OPTIMIZATION: Hash sets keep a plan over thousands of animated elements from scanning lists for each one.
        HashTable<u32> element_set;
        double last_end = -AK::Infinity<double>;
        Vector<Animations::RustFFI::TimelineCell const*> scroll_timelines;
        HashTable<u32> held_elements;
        auto plan = [&] {
            if (!document.is_fully_active() || document.hidden() || !document.window())
                return false;
            auto timeline = document.timeline();
            auto timeline_time = timeline.current_time();
            if (!timeline_time.has_value() || timeline_time->type != Animations::RustFFI::TimeValueType::Milliseconds)
                return false;
            auto plan_animation = [&](Animations::AnimationRef const& animation, Animations::TimelineView const* scroll_timeline, Animations::EffectRef const& effect, DOM::Element const& target) {
                // NB: The record decides what the plan makes of the animation as far as its timing goes. One whose play
                //     is pending holds still, and the ticks sample nothing of its element.
                auto planned = Animations::RustFFI::animations_animation_clock_plan(&animation.record());
                if (planned.kind == Animations::RustFFI::FfiClockPlanAnimationKind::Held) {
                    if (!effect.pseudo_element_type().has_value())
                        held_elements.set(target.style_node_id().value());
                    return true;
                }
                // NB: Nor does a tick move one it cannot, as one of a scroll timeline with nothing to scroll, or one that a
                //     tick cannot follow.
                if (planned.kind == Animations::RustFFI::FfiClockPlanAnimationKind::NotTicked)
                    return false;
                // What the compositor runs, what the main thread does not sample per frame either, or what no box shows,
                // a tick does not sample.
                bool const tick_samples = !runs_on_compositor(effect) && !effect.can_skip_per_frame_style_update() && !no_box_shows(effect, target, read);
                if (tick_samples && !tick_can_sample(document, effect, target, read))
                    return false;
                // NB: The plan takes the scroll timelines a tick follows as they are when it is sealed.
                if (scroll_timeline && (scroll_timelines.is_empty() || scroll_timelines.last() != &scroll_timeline->record()))
                    scroll_timelines.append(&scroll_timeline->record());
                if (!tick_samples)
                    return true;
                if (!scroll_timeline)
                    last_end = max(last_end, timeline_time->value + (planned.active_end.value - planned.local_time.value) / animation.playback_rate());
                auto element = target.style_node_id().value();
                if (element_set.set(element) == HashSetResult::InsertedNewEntry)
                    elements.append(element);
                return true;
            };
            for (auto const& associated_timeline : document.associated_animation_timelines()) {
                Animations::TimelineView const* scroll_timeline = associated_timeline.is_scroll_timeline() ? &associated_timeline : nullptr;
                // OPTIMIZATION: Every animation the plan runs is one an update of its timeline may change.
                auto associated_animations = Animations::associated_animations_of(associated_timeline);
                for (auto const& animation : Animations::animations_needing_update_of(associated_timeline)) {
                    if (!associated_animations.contains(animation))
                        continue;
                    if (!runs_for_clock_plan(animation.play_state(), scroll_timeline != nullptr))
                        continue;
                    auto effect = animation.effect();
                    auto* target = effect.has_value() ? effect->target() : nullptr;
                    if (!target || &target->document() != &document || !target->is_connected())
                        continue;
                    // A tick moves the document's timeline and the scroll timelines alone.
                    bool const on_a_ticked_timeline = associated_timeline == timeline || scroll_timeline;
                    if (on_a_ticked_timeline && plan_animation(animation, scroll_timeline, *effect, *target))
                        continue;
                    // The boxes of an element with an animation a tick cannot sample show what the host's frame shows
                    // of it, while the ticks sample the others on.
                    if (!effect->pseudo_element_type().has_value())
                        held_elements.set(target->style_node_id().value());
                }
            }
            elements.remove_all_matching([&](auto element) { return held_elements.contains(element); });
            return !elements.is_empty();
        };
        bool const animates = plan();
        if (!animates) {
            elements.clear();
            last_end = -AK::Infinity<double>;
        }
        // The lane's ticks may also follow the pointer, and hover what is under it while a task runs.
        Optional<Layout::RustFFI::FfiHoverPlanInputs> hover;
        Vector<u32> effect_timing_nodes;
        Vector<Animations::RustFFI::AnimationEffectId> effect_timing_identities;
        Vector<Animations::RustFFI::EffectTimingSnapshot> effect_timings;
        if (hover_lane_is_enabled() && document.is_fully_active() && !document.hidden() && document.window()) {
            // A hover decides over the transitions the host runs as they run, where the host runs them without
            // sampling them, which leaves the timing the engine holds of them behind.
            // OPTIMIZATION: An animation whose effect produces nothing leaves the animations associated with its
            //               target, and one an update of its timeline may change is among those its timeline keeps,
            //               so look only at those, not at every animation associated with a timeline. Those of
            //               timelines the document is not associated with, or of none, are left out as before.
            auto const associated_timelines = document.associated_animation_timelines();
            HashTable<Animations::RustFFI::TimelineCell const*> timelines;
            for (auto const& timeline : associated_timelines)
                timelines.set(&timeline.record());
            auto add_effect_timing = [&](Animations::AnimationRef const& animation) {
                auto effect = animation.effect();
                auto* target = effect.has_value() ? effect->target() : nullptr;
                if (!target || effect->pseudo_element_type().has_value() || !target->style_node_id()
                    || !effect->can_skip_per_frame_style_update()
                    || !timelines.contains(Animations::RustFFI::animations_animation_timeline(&animation.record())))
                    return;
                // NB: The record decides the timing the hover runs the animation with.
                effect_timing_nodes.append(target->style_node_id().value());
                effect_timing_identities.append(effect->id());
                effect_timings.append(Animations::RustFFI::animations_animation_hover_timing(&animation.record()));
            };
            auto target_associated_animations = Animations::associated_animations_of(document.document_animations());
            for (auto const& animation : target_associated_animations)
                add_effect_timing(animation);
            // NB: A transition started provisionally runs on its timeline before its target observes it.
            for (auto const& timeline : associated_timelines) {
                auto associated_animations = Animations::associated_animations_of(timeline);
                for (auto const& animation : Animations::animations_needing_update_of(timeline)) {
                    if (associated_animations.contains(animation) && !target_associated_animations.contains(animation))
                        add_effect_timing(animation);
                }
            }
            Optional<Web::EventHandler::SelectionDragForLanes> selection_drag;
            if (auto navigable = document.navigable())
                selection_drag = navigable->event_handler().selection_drag_for_lanes(read);
            auto scrollport = selection_drag.has_value() ? selection_drag->scrollport.value_or(CSSPixelRect {}) : CSSPixelRect {};
            hover = Layout::RustFFI::FfiHoverPlanInputs {
                .device_pixels_per_css_pixel = document.page().client().device_pixels_per_css_pixel(),
                .chrome_metrics = document.page().chrome_metrics(),
                .page_cursor = ffi_page_cursor(document.page().cursor()),
                .link_reporter = ffi_hover_link_reporter(document),
                .effect_timing_nodes = effect_timing_nodes.data(),
                .effect_timing_identities = effect_timing_identities.data(),
                .effect_timings = effect_timings.data(),
                .effect_timing_count = effect_timings.size(),
                .selection_drag_anchor = selection_drag.has_value() ? selection_drag->anchor.value() : 0,
                .selection_drag_anchor_offset = selection_drag.has_value() ? selection_drag->anchor_offset : 0,
                .selection_drag_anchor_child = selection_drag.has_value() ? selection_drag->anchor_child.value() : 0,
                .selection_drag_scrollport = {
                    .x = scrollport.x().to_float(),
                    .y = scrollport.y().to_float(),
                    .width = scrollport.width().to_float(),
                    .height = scrollport.height().to_float(),
                },
            };
        }
        if (animates || hover.has_value()) {
            auto time_origin = document.relevant_settings_object().time_origin();
            Layout::RustFFI::render_state_seal_clock_plan(arena->host(), read, elements.data(), elements.size(), time_origin, last_end, scroll_timelines.data(), scroll_timelines.size(), hover.has_value() ? &*hover : nullptr, update_serial);
            return true;
        }
    }
    Layout::RustFFI::document_host_drop_clock_plan(arena->host(), update_serial);
    return false;
}

}

GC_DEFINE_ALLOCATOR(EventLoop);

EventLoop::EventLoop(Type type)
    : m_type(type)
{
    if (m_type == Type::Window) {
        // The threads a window's rendering runs on only read what the host lends them and never touch the heap
        // themselves. This makes that a debug assertion (and a collection there a verification failure) for whatever
        // C++ code they call.
        Layout::RustFFI::stage_thread_set_thread_setup([] { GC::forbid_heap_access_on_this_thread(); });
    }
    m_task_queue = GC::Heap::the().allocate<TaskQueue>(*this);

    m_rendering_task_function = GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(*this), [](EventLoop& self) {
        VERIFY(self.m_rendering_task_queued);
        self.m_rendering_task_queued = false;
        self.update_the_rendering();
    });
}

EventLoop::~EventLoop() = default;

String EventLoop::take_rendering_trace()
{
    StringBuilder builder;
    for (auto const& line : m_rendering_trace.value_or({})) {
        builder.append(line.text);
        if (line.repeats > 1)
            builder.appendff(" x{}", line.repeats);
        builder.append('\n');
    }
    m_rendering_trace.clear();
    return builder.to_string_without_validation();
}

void EventLoop::note_rendering_trace_event(StringView event)
{
    if (!m_rendering_trace.has_value())
        return;
    if (!m_rendering_trace->is_empty() && m_rendering_trace->last().text == event) {
        ++m_rendering_trace->last().repeats;
        return;
    }
    m_rendering_trace->append({ MUST(String::from_utf8(event)) });
}

void note_rendering_trace_event(StringView event)
{
    main_thread_event_loop().note_rendering_trace_event(event);
}

void EventLoop::visit_edges(Visitor& visitor)
{
    Base::visit_edges(visitor);
    visitor.visit(m_reached_step_1_tasks);
    visitor.visit(m_task_queue);
    m_microtask_queue.for_each([&](auto& task) { visitor.visit(task); });
    visitor.visit(m_currently_running_task);
    visitor.visit(m_backup_incumbent_realm_stack);
    visitor.visit(m_rendering_task_function);
    visitor.visit(m_system_event_loop_timer);
    visitor.visit(m_idle_period_timer);
    visitor.visit(m_navigables_with_frames_in_flight);
    visitor.visit(m_navigables_with_clock_lanes);
}

void EventLoop::schedule()
{
    m_turn_requested_without_a_task = true;
    schedule_for_queued_task();
}

void EventLoop::schedule_for_queued_task()
{
    if (!m_system_event_loop_timer) {
        m_system_event_loop_timer = Platform::Timer::create_single_shot(GC::Heap::the(), AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(0), GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(*this), [](EventLoop& self) {
            self.process();
        }));
    }

    if (!m_system_event_loop_timer->is_active())
        m_system_event_loop_timer->restart();
}

void EventLoop::destroy_once_script_has_finished()
{
    m_destruction_requested = true;
    schedule();
}

bool EventLoop::destroy_if_requested()
{
    // NB: A paused event loop has script waiting further up the stack, as a spinning one has.
    if (!m_destruction_requested || m_spin_depth > 0 || execution_paused())
        return false;
    if (auto on_destroyed = move(m_on_destroyed))
        on_destroyed();
    return true;
}

EventLoop& main_thread_event_loop()
{
    return *static_cast<HTML::Agent*>(Bindings::main_thread_vm().agent())->event_loop;
}

EventLoop& current_event_loop()
{
    return *surrounding_agent().event_loop;
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#spin-the-event-loop
void EventLoop::spin_until(GC::Ref<GC::Function<bool()>> goal_condition)
{
    // FIXME: The spec wants us to do the rest of the enclosing algorithm (i.e. the caller)
    //    in the context of the currently running task on entry. That's not possible with this implementation.
    // 1. Let task be the event loop's currently running task.
    // 2. Let task source be task's source.

    // 3. Let old stack be a copy of the JavaScript execution context stack.
    // 4. Empty the JavaScript execution context stack.
    auto& vm = this->vm();
    vm.save_execution_context_stack();
    vm.clear_execution_context_stack();

    // AD-HOC: A rendering update whose style update flies finishes first, as a pause that updates the rendering
    //         finishes it: the tasks the nested event loop runs come after the whole of it.
    finish_rendering_update_in_flight();

    // 5. Perform a microtask checkpoint.
    perform_a_microtask_checkpoint();

    // 6. In parallel:
    //    1. Wait until the condition goal is met.
    //    2. Queue a task on task source to:
    //       1. Replace the JavaScript execution context stack with old stack.
    //       2. Perform any steps that appear after this spin the event loop instance in the original algorithm.
    //       NOTE: This is achieved by returning from the function.

    ++m_spin_depth;
    ScopeGuard leave_spin = [this] {
        --m_spin_depth;
        if (m_destruction_requested)
            schedule();
    };
    Platform::EventLoopPlugin::the().spin_until(GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(*this, goal_condition), [](auto& self, auto& goal_condition) {
        if (goal_condition->function()())
            return true;
        if (self.m_task_queue->has_runnable_tasks()) {
            self.schedule();
            // FIXME: Remove the platform event loop plugin so that this doesn't look out of place
            Core::EventLoop::current().wake();
        }
        return goal_condition->function()();
    }));

    vm.restore_execution_context_stack();

    // 7. Stop task, allowing whatever algorithm that invoked it to resume.
    // NOTE: This is achieved by returning from the function.
}

void EventLoop::process()
{
    m_turn_requested_without_a_task = false;

    if (destroy_if_requested() || execution_paused())
        return;

    // OPTIMIZATION: A trip through the platform event loop costs more than a small task does, so run the tasks that are
    //               ready here for a short while. Each turn is one turn of the processing model with one task, so this
    //               is not visible to the page. The platform event loop gets its turn as soon as anything was posted to
    //               it. What it would only learn from the kernel waits for no longer than this deadline. A nested event
    //               loop goes back after every task, to check what it is waiting for.
    static constexpr auto maximum_time_between_platform_event_loop_turns = AK::Duration::from_microseconds(100);
    auto const turn_deadline = MonotonicTime::now() + maximum_time_between_platform_event_loop_turns;
    bool has_runnable_tasks = false;
    for (;;) {
        has_runnable_tasks = run_one_turn_of_the_processing_model();
        if (!has_runnable_tasks || execution_paused() || m_spin_depth > 0)
            break;
        if (Core::ThreadEventQueue::current().has_pending_events() || MonotonicTime::now() >= turn_deadline)
            break;
    }

    if (destroy_if_requested())
        return;

    // If there are eligible tasks in the queue, schedule a new round of processing. :^)
    if (has_runnable_tasks || (!m_microtask_queue.is_empty() && !m_performing_a_microtask_checkpoint)) {
        schedule();
        return;
    }

    // NB: A task that the turns above have run may have armed the timer for itself. What asked for a turn without
    //     queueing a task still gets one.
    if (m_system_event_loop_timer && !m_turn_requested_without_a_task)
        m_system_event_loop_timer->stop();
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-loop-processing-model
// Answers whether the event loop has a runnable task after this turn.
bool EventLoop::run_one_turn_of_the_processing_model()
{
    if (Core::StatsLog::the())
        begin_rendering_pending_task();
    ScopeGuard pending_task = [] {
        if (Core::StatsLog::the())
            end_rendering_pending_task();
    };

    // 1. Let oldestTask and taskStartTime be null.
    GC::Ptr<Task> oldest_task;
    [[maybe_unused]] double task_start_time = 0;

    m_task_generation++;

    // AD-HOC: A rendering update's style update and recording fly beside the tasks after it, and each is taken in
    //         once it has finished, between two tasks.
    take_finished_frames_in();

    // Some algorithms request that steps or states only occur once the event loop has reached step 1.
    // Invoke a set of tasks that these algorithms request us to in order to achieve this.
    GC::RootVector reached_step_1_tasks { move(m_reached_step_1_tasks) };
    for (auto& reached_step_1_task : reached_step_1_tasks)
        reached_step_1_task->function()();

    // 2. If the event loop has a task queue with at least one runnable task, then:
    // NB: Looking for the first runnable task once answers this as well.

    // 1. Let taskQueue be one such task queue, chosen in an implementation-defined manner.
    auto task_queue = m_task_queue;

    // 2. Set taskStartTime to the unsafe shared current time.
    task_start_time = HighResolutionTime::unsafe_shared_current_time();

    // 3. Set oldestTask to the first runnable task in taskQueue, and remove it from taskQueue.
    oldest_task = task_queue->take_first_runnable();

    // AD-HOC: Beside an idle event loop, whose rendering updates run a document's animations, the render clock's lanes
    //         only hover what is under the pointer.
    if (!oldest_task && !task_queue->has_runnable_tasks())
        note_clock_lanes(ClockAnimations::Hold);

    if (oldest_task) {
        // FIXME: 4. If oldestTask's document is not null, then record task start time given taskStartTime and oldestTask's document.

        // AD-HOC: While a task runs, the render clock's lanes tick the animations the last rendering update planned for.
        //         A task that runs beside a rendering update in flight comes after the whole of it.
        if (oldest_task->source() != Task::Source::Rendering) {
            note_clock_lanes(ClockAnimations::Run);
            note_script_ran_beside_rendering_update_in_flight();
        }

        // 5. Set the event loop's currently running task to oldestTask.
        m_currently_running_task = oldest_task.ptr();
        // NB: A task that spins the event loop runs other tasks in the middle of its own, so each restores what it found.
        TemporaryChange timer_nesting_level_for_microtasks { m_timer_nesting_level_for_microtasks, oldest_task->timer_nesting_level() };

        // 6. Perform oldestTask's steps.
        oldest_task->execute();

        // 7. Set the event loop's currently running task back to null.
        m_currently_running_task = nullptr;

        // 8. Perform a microtask checkpoint.
        perform_a_microtask_checkpoint();
    }

    // 3. Let taskEndTime be the unsafe shared current time. [HRT]
    [[maybe_unused]] auto task_end_time = HighResolutionTime::unsafe_shared_current_time();

    if (oldest_task && oldest_task->source() != Task::Source::Rendering) {
        auto task_duration = task_end_time - task_start_time;
        auto task_duration_microseconds = rendering_scheduler_duration_microseconds(task_duration);
        ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.tasks_between_updates;
        m_rendering_scheduler_counters.task_microseconds_between_updates += task_duration_microseconds;
        switch (oldest_task->source()) {
        case Task::Source::PostedMessage:
            ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.posted_message_tasks_between_updates;
            m_rendering_scheduler_counters.posted_message_task_microseconds_between_updates += task_duration_microseconds;
            break;
        case Task::Source::TimerTask:
            ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.timer_tasks_between_updates;
            m_rendering_scheduler_counters.timer_task_microseconds_between_updates += task_duration_microseconds;
            break;
        case Task::Source::Networking:
            ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.networking_tasks_between_updates;
            m_rendering_scheduler_counters.networking_task_microseconds_between_updates += task_duration_microseconds;
            break;
        case Task::Source::DOMManipulation:
            ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.dom_manipulation_tasks_between_updates;
            m_rendering_scheduler_counters.dom_manipulation_task_microseconds_between_updates += task_duration_microseconds;
            break;
        default:
            break;
        }
    }

    // 4. If oldestTask is not null, then:
    if (oldest_task) {
        // FIXME: 1. Let top-level browsing contexts be an empty set.
        // FIXME: 2. For each environment settings object settings of oldestTask's script evaluation environment settings object set:
        // FIXME: 2.1. Let global be settings's global object.
        // FIXME: 2.2. If global is not a Window object, then continue.
        // FIXME: 2.3. If global's browsing context is null, then continue.
        // FIXME: 2.4. Let tlbc be global's browsing context's top-level browsing context.
        // FIXME: 2.5. If tlbc is not null, then append it to top-level browsing contexts.
        // FIXME: 3. Report long tasks, passing in taskStartTime, taskEndTime, top-level browsing contexts, and oldestTask.
        // FIXME: 4. If oldestTask's document is not null, then record task end time given taskEndTime and oldestTask's document.
    }

    bool has_runnable_tasks = m_task_queue->has_runnable_tasks();

    // 5. If this is a window event loop that has no runnable task in this event loop's task queues, then:
    // NB: A callback that asks for the next one through a task still waits, as a page would otherwise spin while idle.
    static constexpr double minimum_time_between_idle_periods_in_ms = 1;
    bool idle_period_may_start = !m_idle_period_timer || !m_idle_period_timer->is_active()
        || (m_idle_callback_requested_outside_idle_period && HighResolutionTime::unsafe_shared_current_time() - m_last_idle_period_start_time >= minimum_time_between_idle_periods_in_ms);
    if (m_type == Type::Window && !has_runnable_tasks && m_may_have_idle_callbacks && idle_period_may_start) {
        auto windows = same_loop_windows();
        bool has_idle_callbacks = false;
        bool has_callbacks_of_hidden_document = false;
        for (auto& window : windows) {
            if (!window->has_idle_callbacks())
                continue;
            if (window->associated_document().hidden()) {
                has_callbacks_of_hidden_document = true;
                continue;
            }
            has_idle_callbacks = true;
            break;
        }
        // NB: same_loop_windows() leaves out a document that is not fully active, whose callbacks wait for it to come back.
        bool has_callbacks_of_inactive_document = any_of(m_documents, [](auto const& document) {
            return document && !document->is_fully_active() && document->window() && document->window()->has_idle_callbacks();
        });
        // OPTIMIZATION: Nothing is looked at here again until an idle callback is asked for.
        m_may_have_idle_callbacks = has_idle_callbacks || has_callbacks_of_hidden_document || has_callbacks_of_inactive_document;
        if (has_idle_callbacks) {
            // NB: Delay the next idle period until this one's 50 ms budget has elapsed. Callbacks registered
            //     during an idle period belong to the next one; immediately starting it lets self-scheduling
            //     callbacks spin continuously even when they have no work to do. A callback requested from
            //     anything but an idle callback starts an idle period right away (see did_request_idle_callback()).
            m_idle_callback_requested_outside_idle_period = false;
            if (!m_idle_period_timer) {
                m_idle_period_timer = Platform::Timer::create_single_shot(GC::Heap::the(), AK::Duration::from_milliseconds(50), GC::create_function(GC::Heap::the(), GC::captures(*this), [](EventLoop& self) {
                    self.schedule();
                }));
            }
            m_idle_period_timer->restart();

            // 1. Set this event loop's last idle period start time to the unsafe shared current time.
            m_last_idle_period_start_time = HighResolutionTime::unsafe_shared_current_time();

            // 2. Let computeDeadline be the following steps:
            // Implemented in EventLoop::compute_deadline()

            // 3. For each win of the same-loop windows for this event loop, perform the start an idle period algorithm for win with the following step: return the result of calling computeDeadline, coarsened given win's relevant settings object's cross-origin isolated capability. [REQUESTIDLECALLBACK]
            for (auto& window : windows)
                window->start_an_idle_period();
            has_runnable_tasks = m_task_queue->has_runnable_tasks();
        }
    }

    return has_runnable_tasks;
}

void EventLoop::request_rendering_update()
{
    ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.update_requests;
    if (m_running_rendering_task)
        ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.update_requests_while_rendering;

    if (m_rendering_update_requested || m_rendering_task_queued) {
        ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.coalesced_update_requests;
        note_rendering_trace_event(m_running_rendering_task ? "request while rendering, coalesced"sv : "request, coalesced"sv);
        return;
    }
    note_rendering_trace_event(m_running_rendering_task ? "request while rendering"sv : "request"sv);

    m_rendering_update_requested = true;
}

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-loop-processing-model
bool EventLoop::rendering_opportunity(HighResolutionTime::DOMHighResTimeStamp frame_time, RenderingOpportunitySource source)
{
    ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.opportunities_received;
    if (source == RenderingOpportunitySource::Watchdog)
        ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.watchdog_opportunities;
    note_rendering_trace_event(source == RenderingOpportunitySource::Watchdog ? "opportunity (watchdog)"sv : "opportunity"sv);

    // FIXME: 1. Wait until at least one navigable whose active document's relevant agent's event loop is eventLoop might have a rendering opportunity.

    // 2. Set eventLoop's last render opportunity time to the unsafe shared current time.
    advance_last_render_opportunity_time(frame_time);

    // AD-HOC: A nested event loop can deliver a timer while a rendering update is running. Keep the request pending
    //         so the PageClient can schedule it for the next opportunity instead of queueing a second rendering task.
    if (m_running_rendering_task)
        return false;

    m_rendering_update_requested = false;

    if (m_rendering_task_queued)
        return true;

    // 3. For each navigable that has a rendering opportunity, queue a global task on the rendering task source given navigable's active window to update the rendering:
    bool has_eligible_navigable = false;
    for (auto& navigable : all_local_navigables()) {
        if (!navigable.is_local_root())
            continue;
        if (!navigable.has_a_rendering_opportunity())
            continue;

        auto document = navigable.active_document();
        if (!document)
            continue;
        if (document->is_decoded_svg())
            continue;

        has_eligible_navigable = true;
        break;
    }

    if (!has_eligible_navigable)
        return false;

    // AD-HOC: One rendering update services every document in this event loop, so queue one event-loop task for the
    //         opportunity instead of one global task per page local root.
    VERIFY(!m_rendering_task_queued);
    m_rendering_task_queued = true;
    m_rendering_task_queued_time = MonotonicTime::now();
    queue_a_task(Task::Source::Rendering, this, nullptr, *m_rendering_task_function);
    ++m_rendering_scheduler_counters.opportunities_that_queued_a_task;
    return true;
}

void EventLoop::advance_last_render_opportunity_time(HighResolutionTime::DOMHighResTimeStamp frame_time)
{
    // INTEROP: Compositor-provided display timestamps match the shared monotonic clock. Clamp delayed or out-of-order
    //          opportunities so rendering timestamps remain monotonic and never describe a future frame.
    auto now = HighResolutionTime::unsafe_shared_current_time();
    m_last_render_opportunity_time = max(m_last_render_opportunity_time, min(frame_time, now));
}

static InputRoutingDecision input_routing_decision_for_finished_input_event(EventResult result)
{
    switch (result) {
    case EventResult::Accepted:
        return InputRoutingDecision::FinishedAccepted;
    case EventResult::Handled:
        return InputRoutingDecision::FinishedHandled;
    case EventResult::Dropped:
        return InputRoutingDecision::FinishedDropped;
    case EventResult::Cancelled:
        return InputRoutingDecision::FinishedCancelled;
    }
    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
}

void EventLoop::process_input_events() const
{
    auto process_input_events_queue = [&](Page& page) {
        auto& page_client = page.client();
        auto& input_events_queue = page_client.input_event_queue();

        // Process events only for this page, collecting others to re-enqueue
        Queue<Web::QueuedInputEvent> events_for_other_pages;

        auto record_routing = [&](u64 event_id, InputRoutingDecision decision) {
            page.input_trace().record({ .input_event_id = event_id, .stage = InputTraceStage::WebContent, .decision = decision });
        };
        auto finish_handling_input_event = [&](u64 event_id, EventResult result, InputRoutingDecision decision) {
            record_routing(event_id, decision);
            page_client.report_finished_handling_input_event(page_client.id(), event_id, result);
        };
        auto finish_handling_coalesced_input_events = [&](QueuedInputEvent const& event) {
            for (auto coalesced_event_id : event.coalesced_event_ids)
                finish_handling_input_event(coalesced_event_id, EventResult::Dropped, InputRoutingDecision::CoalescedIntoLaterEvent);
        };

        while (!input_events_queue.is_empty()) {
            auto event = input_events_queue.dequeue();

            // Skip events that are not intended for this page
            if (event.page_id != page_client.id()) {
                events_for_other_pages.enqueue(move(event));
                continue;
            }

            // A key event goes to the tab's focused navigable. Other events go to the local root given by the event's
            // navigable ID, or the page's traversable if it has none.
            GC::Ptr<LocalNavigable> root;
            if (event.event.has<Web::KeyEvent>())
                root = page.hosted_focused_navigable();
            else if (event.navigable_id.has_value())
                root = as_if<LocalNavigable>(page.navigable_with_id(*event.navigable_id).ptr());
            else if (page.has_local_traversable())
                root = page.local_traversable();

            if (!root) {
                finish_handling_coalesced_input_events(event);
                finish_handling_input_event(input_event_id(event.event), EventResult::Dropped, InputRoutingDecision::DroppedWithoutLocalRoot);
                continue;
            }

            // AD-HOC: The screen showed the hover of a newer pointer move than a mouse event that reached the queue
            //         before the task the hover of a clock lane took that move beside, which the host keeps where it
            //         took in what the lanes did: the pointer never moves back to where the event says it was. A move
            //         or leave is dropped, as the queue coalesces the moves it holds, and the newer move's own event
            //         follows. Any other event is handled, without moving the hover or the pointer.
            bool input_is_outdated = false;
            if (auto const* mouse_event = event.event.get_pointer<Web::MouseEvent>(); mouse_event && (!mouse_event->pointer_data.ptr() || mouse_event->pointer_data.ptr()->pointer_type == PointerType::Mouse)) {
                auto document = root->active_document();
                auto* arena = document ? document->layout_node_arena_if_created() : nullptr;
                input_is_outdated = arena && Layout::RustFFI::document_host_mouse_event_is_outdated(arena->host(), mouse_event->id);
                // A move with a button held is a drag's, whose script hears every move: it is handled, as outdated.
                if (input_is_outdated && mouse_event->buttons == 0 && first_is_one_of(mouse_event->type, Web::MouseEvent::Type::MouseMove, Web::MouseEvent::Type::MouseLeave)) {
                    finish_handling_coalesced_input_events(event);
                    finish_handling_input_event(mouse_event->id, EventResult::Dropped, InputRoutingDecision::DroppedOutdatedPointerMove);
                    continue;
                }
            }
            root->event_handler().set_handling_outdated_input(input_is_outdated);
            auto const* handled_mouse_event = event.event.get_pointer<Web::MouseEvent>();
            root->event_handler().set_handling_input_event_id(handled_mouse_event ? handled_mouse_event->id : 0);
            ScopeGuard end_outdated_input = [&] {
                root->event_handler().set_handling_outdated_input(false);
                root->event_handler().set_handling_input_event_id(0);
            };

            Optional<RemoteInputEventTarget> remote_target;
            auto result = event.event.visit(
                [&](Web::KeyEvent const& key_event) {
                    switch (key_event.type) {
                    case Web::KeyEvent::Type::KeyDown:
                        return page.handle_keydown(key_event.key, key_event.modifiers, key_event.code_point, key_event.repeat, key_event.should_insert_text, key_event.async_scroll_performed_default_action, key_event.editing_commands, key_event.native_editing_binding_resolved, key_event.user_input_scroll_count_with_nothing_to_scroll);
                    case Web::KeyEvent::Type::KeyUp:
                        return page.handle_keyup(key_event.key, key_event.modifiers, key_event.code_point, key_event.repeat);
                    }
                    VERIFY_NOT_REACHED();
                },
                [&](Web::MouseEvent const& mouse_event) {
                    if (auto* pointer = mouse_event.pointer_data.ptr(); pointer && pointer->pointer_type != PointerType::Mouse)
                        return root->event_handler().handle_pointer_event(mouse_event, page.device_to_css_point(mouse_event.position), page.device_to_css_point(mouse_event.screen_position), &remote_target);
                    switch (mouse_event.type) {
                    case Web::MouseEvent::Type::MouseDown:
                        return page.handle_mousedown(*root, mouse_event.position, mouse_event.screen_position, mouse_event.button, mouse_event.buttons, mouse_event.modifiers, mouse_event.click_count, mouse_event.scrollbar_dragged_by_compositor, &remote_target);
                    case Web::MouseEvent::Type::MouseUp:
                        return page.handle_mouseup(*root, mouse_event.position, mouse_event.screen_position, mouse_event.button, mouse_event.buttons, mouse_event.modifiers, &remote_target);
