#pragma once

#include <AK/Types.h>

namespace Web::HTML {

// https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parser-scripting-mode
enum class ParserScriptingMode : u8 {
    // Scripts are processed when inserted, respecting async and defer attributes and blocking the parser when encountering a classic script.
    Normal,

    // Scripts are disabled, and the noscript element can represent fallback content.
    Disabled,

    // Scripts are enabled, however they are marked as already started, essentially preventing them from executing.
    // This is the default mode of the HTML fragment parsing algorithm.
    Inert,

    // Scripts are executed as soon as they are inserted into the document as part of a the HTML fragment parsing
    // algorithm, ignoring async and defer attributes. This mode is used by createContextualFragment().
    Fragment,
};

// Whether the HTML fragment parsing algorithm may try the fragment fast path. Callers that have already tried it skip it.
enum class FragmentFastPath : u8 {
    Allow,
    Skip,
};

}

FILE: Libraries/LibWeb/HTML/Parser/Rust/build.rs
/*
 * Copyright (c) 2026-present, the Ladybird developers.
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause
 */

//! Build script that generates a DAFSA (Deterministic Acyclic Finite State Automaton)
//! for named character reference matching.

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::rc::Rc;

const FFI_HEADER: &str = "HTMLTokenizerRustFFI.h";

fn main() {
    let manifest_dir = env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").unwrap();
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var("OUT_DIR").unwrap());
    let target_pointer_size = env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_POINTER_WIDTH")
        .unwrap()
        .parse::<usize>()
        .unwrap()
        / 8;

    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=cbindgen.toml");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=src");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=FFI_OUTPUT_DIR");

    let ffi_out_dir = env::var("FFI_OUTPUT_DIR")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| out_dir.clone());

    cbindgen::generate(&manifest_dir).map_or_else(
        |error| match error {
            cbindgen::Error::ParseSyntaxError { .. } => {}
            e => panic!("{e:?}"),
        },
        |bindings| {
            bindings.write_to_file(out_dir.join(FFI_HEADER));
            if ffi_out_dir != out_dir {
                bindings.write_to_file(ffi_out_dir.join(FFI_HEADER));
            }
        },
    );

    let tag_names_header = Path::new(&manifest_dir).join("../../TagNames.h");
    let attr_names_header = Path::new(&manifest_dir).join("../../AttributeNames.h");
    let svg_tag_names_header = Path::new(&manifest_dir).join("../../../SVG/TagNames.h");
    let mathml_tag_names_header = Path::new(&manifest_dir).join("../../../MathML/TagNames.h");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", tag_names_header.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", attr_names_header.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", svg_tag_names_header.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", mathml_tag_names_header.display());
    let tag_names = parse_enumerate_macro(
        &fs::read_to_string(&tag_names_header).expect("Failed to read TagNames.h"),
        "__ENUMERATE_HTML_TAG",
    );
    let attribute_names = parse_enumerate_macro(
        &fs::read_to_string(&attr_names_header).expect("Failed to read AttributeNames.h"),
        "__ENUMERATE_HTML_ATTRIBUTE",
    );
    let svg_tag_names = parse_enumerate_macro(
        &fs::read_to_string(&svg_tag_names_header).expect("Failed to read SVG TagNames.h"),
        "__ENUMERATE_SVG_TAG",
    );
    let mathml_tag_names = parse_enumerate_macro(
        &fs::read_to_string(&mathml_tag_names_header).expect("Failed to read MathML TagNames.h"),
        "__ENUMERATE_MATHML_TAG",
    );
    emit_known_names(
        &out_dir.join("known_names_generated.rs"),
        &tag_names,
        &svg_tag_names,
        &mathml_tag_names,
        &attribute_names,
        target_pointer_size,
    );

    let json_path = Path::new(&manifest_dir).join("../Entities.json");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", json_path.display());

    let json_str = fs::read_to_string(&json_path).expect("Failed to read Entities.json");
    let entities = parse_entities_json(&json_str);

    // Build DAFSA.
    let mut builder = DafsaBuilder::new();
    for (name, _, _) in &entities {
        builder.insert(name);
    }
    builder.minimize(0);
    builder.calc_numbers();

    // Verify minimal perfect hashing (no collisions).
    let mut seen: Vec<bool> = vec![false; entities.len() + 1];
    for (name, _, _) in &entities {
        let idx = builder.get_unique_index(name).unwrap();
        assert!(!seen[idx], "Hash collision at index {idx} for '{name}'");
        seen[idx] = true;
    }

    // Build codepoints lookup table indexed by unique_index.
    let mut index_to_codepoints = vec![(0u32, 0u32); entities.len()];
    for (name, first, second) in &entities {
        let idx = builder.get_unique_index(name).unwrap();
        index_to_codepoints[idx - 1] = (*first, *second);
    }

    // Extract DAFSA layers.
    let root = &builder.root;
    let root_ref = root.borrow();

    let mut first_layer: Vec<u16> = Vec::new();
    let mut first_to_second_layer: Vec<(u64, u16)> = Vec::new();

    let mut first_layer_tally: u16 = 0;
    let mut second_layer_offset: u16 = 0;

    for c in 0u8..128 {
        if root_ref.children[c as usize].is_none() {
            continue;
        }
        assert!(c.is_ascii_alphabetic());
        let child = root_ref.children[c as usize].as_ref().unwrap();
        let child_ref = child.borrow();

        first_layer.push(first_layer_tally);
        first_layer_tally += child_ref.number;

        let mask = child_ref.get_ascii_alphabetic_bit_mask();
        first_to_second_layer.push((mask, second_layer_offset));
        second_layer_offset += child_ref.num_direct_children() as u16;
    }
    assert_eq!(first_layer.len(), 52);

    // BFS to build DAFSA node array.
    // Following the C++ write_node_data three-phase approach:
    type NodePtr = Rc<RefCell<Node>>;
    let mut queue: Vec<NodePtr> = Vec::new();
    let mut child_indexes: HashMap<*const RefCell<Node>, u16> = HashMap::new();

    // Phase 1: Queue root's children (first-layer nodes = 52 A-Z/a-z).
    // This assigns temporary child_indexes for first-layer children.
    queue_children(root, &mut queue, &mut child_indexes, 1);

    // Phase 2: Clear indexes and re-process. For each first-layer child,
    // queue ITS children (second-layer nodes) and assign their child_indexes.
    child_indexes.clear();
    let mut first_available_index: u16 = 1; // 0 is reserved (dummy node)
    let first_layer_count = queue.len();
    for i in 0..first_layer_count {
        let node = Rc::clone(&queue[i]);
        first_available_index = queue_children(&node, &mut queue, &mut child_indexes, first_available_index);
    }
    // Remove first-layer nodes from queue, keep only second-layer+ nodes.
    let second_layer_nodes: Vec<NodePtr> = queue.drain(first_layer_count..).collect();
    queue.clear();
    queue.extend(second_layer_nodes);

    // Phase 3: BFS remaining nodes, writing node data.
    let mut node_data: Vec<NodeData> = Vec::new();
    let mut qi = 0;
    #[allow(unused_assignments)]
    while qi < queue.len() {
        let node = Rc::clone(&queue[qi]);
        qi += 1;
        first_available_index = write_children_data(
            &node,
            &mut node_data,
            &mut queue,
            &mut child_indexes,
            first_available_index,
        );
    }

    // Build second_layer entries with child_indexes from phase 2.
    let mut second_layer: Vec<SecondLayerEntry> = Vec::new();
    for c in 0u8..128 {
        if root_ref.children[c as usize].is_none() {
            continue;
        }
        let first_child = root_ref.children[c as usize].as_ref().unwrap();
        let first_child_ref = first_child.borrow();
        let mut tally: u8 = 0;
        for cc in 0u8..128 {
            if first_child_ref.children[cc as usize].is_none() {
                continue;
            }
            let second_child = first_child_ref.children[cc as usize].as_ref().unwrap();
            let second_child_ref = second_child.borrow();
            let key = Rc::as_ptr(second_child);
            let ci = child_indexes.get(&key).copied().unwrap_or(0);
            let children_len = second_child_ref.num_direct_children();
            second_layer.push(SecondLayerEntry {
                child_index: ci,
                number: tally,
                children_len,
                end_of_word: second_child_ref.is_terminal,
            });
            tally = tally.wrapping_add(second_child_ref.number as u8);
        }
    }
    drop(root_ref);

    // Generate output file.
    let out_dir = env::var("OUT_DIR").unwrap();
    let out_path = Path::new(&out_dir).join("named_character_references.rs");
    let mut out = String::new();

    out.push_str("// Auto-generated by build.rs -- do not edit!\n\n");

    // Second codepoint enum.
    out.push_str("#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\n");
    out.push_str("#[repr(u8)]\n");
    out.push_str("pub enum SecondCodepoint {\n");
    out.push_str("    None = 0,\n");
    out.push_str("    CombiningLongSolidusOverlay = 1,\n");
    out.push_str("    CombiningLongVerticalLineOverlay = 2,\n");
    out.push_str("    HairSpace = 3,\n");
    out.push_str("    CombiningDoubleLowLine = 4,\n");
    out.push_str("    CombiningReverseSolidusOverlay = 5,\n");
    out.push_str("    VariationSelector1 = 6,\n");
    out.push_str("    LatinSmallLetterJ = 7,\n");
    out.push_str("    CombiningMacronBelow = 8,\n");
    out.push_str("}\n\n");

    out.push_str("impl SecondCodepoint {\n");
    out.push_str("    pub fn value(self) -> u32 {\n");
    out.push_str("        match self {\n");
    out.push_str("            SecondCodepoint::None => 0,\n");
    out.push_str("            SecondCodepoint::CombiningLongSolidusOverlay => 0x0338,\n");
    out.push_str("            SecondCodepoint::CombiningLongVerticalLineOverlay => 0x20D2,\n");
    out.push_str("            SecondCodepoint::HairSpace => 0x200A,\n");
    out.push_str("            SecondCodepoint::CombiningDoubleLowLine => 0x0333,\n");
    out.push_str("            SecondCodepoint::CombiningReverseSolidusOverlay => 0x20E5,\n");
    out.push_str("            SecondCodepoint::VariationSelector1 => 0xFE00,\n");
    out.push_str("            SecondCodepoint::LatinSmallLetterJ => 0x006A,\n");
    out.push_str("            SecondCodepoint::CombiningMacronBelow => 0x0331,\n");
    out.push_str("        }\n");
    out.push_str("    }\n");
    out.push_str("}\n\n");

    // Struct definitions.
    out.push_str("#[derive(Clone, Copy)]\n");
    out.push_str("pub struct DafsaNode {\n");
    out.push_str("    pub character: u8,\n");
    out.push_str("    pub number: u8,\n");
    out.push_str("    pub end_of_word: bool,\n");
    out.push_str("    pub child_index: u16,\n");
    out.push_str("    pub children_len: u8,\n");
    out.push_str("}\n\n");

    out.push_str("#[derive(Clone, Copy)]\n");
    out.push_str("pub struct SecondLayerNode {\n");
    out.push_str("    pub child_index: u16,\n");
    out.push_str("    pub number: u8,\n");
    out.push_str("    pub children_len: u8,\n");
    out.push_str("    pub end_of_word: bool,\n");
    out.push_str("}\n\n");

    // Codepoints lookup table.
    out.push_str(&format!(
        "pub static CODEPOINTS_LOOKUP: [(u32, SecondCodepoint); {}] = [\n",
        index_to_codepoints.len()
    ));
    for (first, second) in &index_to_codepoints {
        let variant = second_codepoint_variant(*second);
        out.push_str(&format!("    ({first:#06X}, SecondCodepoint::{variant}),\n"));
    }
    out.push_str("];\n\n");

    // DAFSA nodes array (with dummy node at index 0).
    out.push_str(&format!(
        "pub static DAFSA_NODES: [DafsaNode; {}] = [\n",
        node_data.len() + 1
    ));
    out.push_str("    DafsaNode { character: 0, number: 0, end_of_word: false, child_index: 0, children_len: 0 },\n");
    for nd in &node_data {
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "    DafsaNode {{ character: b'{}', number: {}, end_of_word: {}, child_index: {}, children_len: {} }},\n",
            escape_byte(nd.character),
            nd.number,
            nd.end_of_word,
            nd.child_index,
            nd.children_len
        ));
    }
    out.push_str("];\n\n");

    // First layer.
    out.push_str(&format!("pub static FIRST_LAYER: [u16; {}] = [\n", first_layer.len()));
    for n in &first_layer {
        out.push_str(&format!("    {n},\n"));
    }
    out.push_str("];\n\n");

    // First-to-second layer links.
    out.push_str(&format!(
        "pub static FIRST_TO_SECOND_LAYER: [(u64, u16); {}] = [\n",
        first_to_second_layer.len()
    ));
    for (mask, offset) in &first_to_second_layer {
        out.push_str(&format!("    ({mask:#018X}, {offset}),\n"));
    }
    out.push_str("];\n\n");

    // Second layer nodes.
    out.push_str(&format!(
        "pub static SECOND_LAYER: [SecondLayerNode; {}] = [\n",
        second_layer.len()
    ));
    for sl in &second_layer {
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "    SecondLayerNode {{ child_index: {}, number: {}, children_len: {}, end_of_word: {} }},\n",
            sl.child_index, sl.number, sl.children_len, sl.end_of_word
        ));
    }
    out.push_str("];\n\n");

    // Total entity count.
    out.push_str(&format!("pub const ENTITY_COUNT: usize = {};\n", entities.len()));

    fs::write(&out_path, &out).expect("Failed to write generated file");
}

fn parse_enumerate_macro(source: &str, macro_name: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let needle = format!("{macro_name}(");
    let names = source
        .lines()
        .filter_map(|line| {
            let rest = &line[line.find(&needle)? + needle.len()..];
            let comma = rest.find(',')?;
            let identifier = rest[..comma].trim().to_string();
            let rest = &rest[comma + 1..];
            let rest = &rest[rest.find('"')? + 1..];
            Some((identifier, rest[..rest.find('"')?].to_string()))
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    assert!(!names.is_empty(), "No entries found for {macro_name}");
    names
}

fn needs_static(name: &str, target_pointer_size: usize) -> bool {
    name.len() >= target_pointer_size || !name.is_ascii()
}

fn emit_known_names(
    out_path: &Path,
    tag_names: &[(String, String)],
    svg_tag_names: &[(String, String)],
    mathml_tag_names: &[(String, String)],
    attribute_names: &[(String, String)],
    target_pointer_size: usize,
) {
    let mut out = String::from("// Auto-generated by build.rs. Do not edit.\n\n");
    out.push_str("#[cfg(not(test))]\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nunsafe extern \"C\" {\n");
    for (identifier, name) in tag_names {
        if needs_static(name, target_pointer_size) {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    pub(crate) static ladybird_html_tag_name_{identifier}: usize;\n"
            ));
        }
    }
    for (identifier, name) in attribute_names {
        if needs_static(name, target_pointer_size) {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    pub(crate) static ladybird_html_attribute_name_{identifier}: usize;\n"
            ));
        }
    }
    emit_known_name_externs(&mut out, svg_tag_names, "svg", target_pointer_size);
    emit_known_name_externs(&mut out, mathml_tag_names, "mathml", target_pointer_size);
    out.push_str("}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmacro_rules! tag_name {\n");
    let mut emitted_names = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    emit_test_known_name_macro_arms(&mut out, tag_names, &mut emitted_names);
    emit_test_known_name_macro_arms(&mut out, svg_tag_names, &mut emitted_names);
    emit_test_known_name_macro_arms(&mut out, mathml_tag_names, &mut emitted_names);
    out.push_str("}\n\n#[cfg(not(test))]\nmacro_rules! tag_name {\n");
    let mut emitted_names = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    emit_known_name_macro_arms(&mut out, tag_names, "tag", target_pointer_size, &mut emitted_names);
    emit_known_name_macro_arms(&mut out, svg_tag_names, "svg", target_pointer_size, &mut emitted_names);
    emit_known_name_macro_arms(
        &mut out,
        mathml_tag_names,
        "mathml",
        target_pointer_size,
        &mut emitted_names,
    );
    out.push_str("}\npub(crate) use tag_name;\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmacro_rules! attribute_name {\n");
    emit_test_known_name_macro_arms(&mut out, attribute_names, &mut std::collections::HashSet::new());
    out.push_str("}\n\n#[cfg(not(test))]\nmacro_rules! attribute_name {\n");
    emit_known_name_macro_arms(
        &mut out,
        attribute_names,
        "attribute",
        target_pointer_size,
        &mut std::collections::HashSet::new(),
    );
    out.push_str("}\npub(crate) use attribute_name;\n");
    emit_tag_ids(&mut out, &[tag_names, svg_tag_names, mathml_tag_names]);
    emit_known_attribute_name_lookup(&mut out, attribute_names);
    fs::write(out_path, out).expect("Failed to write known_names_generated.rs");
}

/// Emits a small number for every known tag name, the `tag_id!` macro that gives the number of a name, and
/// `tag_id_for_name`, which finds the number of a name the tokenizer has read.
fn emit_tag_ids(out: &mut String, tag_name_lists: &[&[(String, String)]]) {
    let names: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> = tag_name_lists
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|names| names.iter().map(|(_, name)| name.as_str()))
        .collect();
    // NB: 0 is the id of every name that isn't a known one.
    let ids: Vec<(&str, usize)> = names.iter().copied().zip(1..).collect();

    out.push_str(&format!(
        "\npub(crate) const TAG_SET_WORD_COUNT: usize = {};\n\nmacro_rules! tag_id {{\n",
        (ids.len() + 1).div_ceil(64)
    ));
    for (name, id) in &ids {
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "    (\"{name}\") => {{ $crate::token::TagId::from_index({id}) }};\n"
        ));
    }
    out.push_str("}\npub(crate) use tag_id;\n\n");

    // NB: Names are told apart by their length and first byte before any of them is compared in full, which leaves
    //     only a few to compare with.
    let mut by_length_and_first_byte = std::collections::BTreeMap::<(usize, u8), Vec<(&str, usize)>>::new();
    for (name, id) in &ids {
        by_length_and_first_byte
            .entry((name.len(), name.as_bytes()[0]))
            .or_default()
            .push((name, *id));
    }
    out.push_str("pub(crate) fn tag_id_for_name(name: &[u8]) -> crate::token::TagId {\n");
    out.push_str(
        "    let Some(&first_byte) = name.first() else {\n        return crate::token::TagId::UNKNOWN;\n    };\n",
    );
    out.push_str("    match (name.len(), first_byte) {\n");
    for ((length, first_byte), names) in &by_length_and_first_byte {
        out.push_str(&format!("        ({length}, {first_byte}) => match name {{\n"));
        for (name, id) in names {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "            b\"{name}\" => crate::token::TagId::from_index({id}),\n"
            ));
        }
        out.push_str("            _ => crate::token::TagId::UNKNOWN,\n        },\n");
    }
    out.push_str("        _ => crate::token::TagId::UNKNOWN,\n    }\n}\n");
}

/// Emits `known_attribute_name`, which finds the known attribute name that has the bytes it is given.
fn emit_known_attribute_name_lookup(out: &mut String, attribute_names: &[(String, String)]) {
    let names: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> = attribute_names.iter().map(|(_, name)| name.as_str()).collect();
    // NB: As with tag names, the length and first byte of a name leave only a few known names to compare it with.
    let mut by_length_and_first_byte = std::collections::BTreeMap::<(usize, u8), Vec<&str>>::new();
    for name in names {
        by_length_and_first_byte
            .entry((name.len(), name.as_bytes()[0]))
            .or_default()
            .push(name);
    }
    out.push_str("\npub(crate) fn known_attribute_name(name: &[u8]) -> Option<crate::token::KnownName> {\n");
    out.push_str("    let &first_byte = name.first()?;\n");
    out.push_str("    match (name.len(), first_byte) {\n");
    for ((length, first_byte), names) in &by_length_and_first_byte {
        out.push_str(&format!("        ({length}, {first_byte}) => match name {{\n"));
        for name in names {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "            b\"{name}\" => Some(attribute_name!(\"{name}\")),\n"
            ));
        }
        out.push_str("            _ => None,\n        },\n");
    }
    out.push_str("        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n");
}

fn emit_known_name_externs(out: &mut String, names: &[(String, String)], prefix: &str, target_pointer_size: usize) {
    for (identifier, name) in names {
        if needs_static(name, target_pointer_size) {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    pub(crate) static ladybird_{prefix}_tag_name_{identifier}: usize;\n"
            ));
        }
    }
}

fn emit_test_known_name_macro_arms(
    out: &mut String,
    names: &[(String, String)],
    emitted_names: &mut std::collections::HashSet<String>,
) {
    for (_, name) in names {
        if emitted_names.insert(name.clone()) {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    (\"{name}\") => {{ $crate::token::KnownName::from_literal(\"{name}\") }};\n"
            ));
        }
    }
}

fn emit_known_name_macro_arms(
    out: &mut String,
    names: &[(String, String)],
    prefix: &str,
    target_pointer_size: usize,
    emitted_names: &mut std::collections::HashSet<String>,
) {
    for (identifier, name) in names {
        if !emitted_names.insert(name.clone()) {
            continue;
        }
        if !needs_static(name, target_pointer_size) {
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    (\"{name}\") => {{ $crate::token::KnownName::from_raw(ak::utf16_short_string_raw(\"{name}\").unwrap()) }};\n"
            ));
        } else {
            let symbol_prefix = match prefix {
                "tag" => "html_tag",
                "attribute" => "html_attribute",
                "svg" => "svg_tag",
                "mathml" => "mathml_tag",
                _ => unreachable!(),
            };
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "    (\"{name}\") => {{ $crate::token::KnownName::from_raw(unsafe {{ $crate::known_names::ladybird_{symbol_prefix}_name_{identifier} }}) }};\n"
            ));
        }
    }
}

fn escape_byte(b: u8) -> String {
    if b == b'\'' {
        "\\'".to_string()
    } else if b == b'\\' {
        "\\\\".to_string()
    } else if b.is_ascii_graphic() || b == b' ' {
        String::from(b as char)
    } else {
        format!("\\x{b:02X}")
    }
}

fn second_codepoint_variant(cp: u32) -> &'static str {
    match cp {
        0 => "None",
        0x0338 => "CombiningLongSolidusOverlay",
        0x20D2 => "CombiningLongVerticalLineOverlay",
        0x200A => "HairSpace",
        0x0333 => "CombiningDoubleLowLine",
        0x20E5 => "CombiningReverseSolidusOverlay",
        0xFE00 => "VariationSelector1",
        0x006A => "LatinSmallLetterJ",
        0x0331 => "CombiningMacronBelow",
        _ => panic!("Unknown second codepoint: {cp:#X}"),
    }
}

// Minimal JSON parser for Entities.json.
fn parse_entities_json(json: &str) -> Vec<(String, u32, u32)> {
    let mut entities = Vec::new();
    let bytes = json.as_bytes();
    let len = bytes.len();
    let mut i = 0;

    while i < len && bytes[i] != b'{' {
        i += 1;
    }
    i += 1;

    loop {
        while i < len && bytes[i].is_ascii_whitespace() {
            i += 1;
        }
        if i >= len || bytes[i] == b'}' {
            break;
        }
        if bytes[i] == b',' {
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }

        // Parse key.
        assert_eq!(bytes[i], b'"');
        i += 1;
        let key_start = i;
        while i < len && bytes[i] != b'"' {
            if bytes[i] == b'\\' {
                i += 1;
            }
            i += 1;
        }
        let key = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[key_start..i]).unwrap().to_string();
        i += 1;

        // Skip ':'.
        while i < len && bytes[i].is_ascii_whitespace() {
            i += 1;
        }
        assert_eq!(bytes[i], b':');
        i += 1;

        // Skip to inner '{'.
        while i < len && bytes[i] != b'{' {
            i += 1;
        }
        i += 1;

        // Parse inner object for "codepoints".
        let mut codepoints: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
        while i < len && bytes[i] != b'}' {
            if bytes[i] == b'"' {
                i += 1;
                let field_start = i;
                while i < len && bytes[i] != b'"' {
                    i += 1;
                }
                let field_name = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[field_start..i]).unwrap();
                i += 1;

                while i < len && bytes[i].is_ascii_whitespace() {
                    i += 1;
                }
                assert_eq!(bytes[i], b':');
                i += 1;
                while i < len && bytes[i].is_ascii_whitespace() {
                    i += 1;
                }

                if field_name == "codepoints" {
                    assert_eq!(bytes[i], b'[');
                    i += 1;
                    loop {
                        while i < len && (bytes[i].is_ascii_whitespace() || bytes[i] == b',') {
                            i += 1;
                        }
                        if i >= len || bytes[i] == b']' {
                            i += 1;
                            break;
                        }
                        let num_start = i;
                        while i < len && bytes[i].is_ascii_digit() {
                            i += 1;
                        }
                        let num_str = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[num_start..i]).unwrap();
                        codepoints.push(num_str.parse().unwrap());
                    }
                } else {
                    // Skip value.
                    if bytes[i] == b'"' {
                        i += 1;
                        while i < len && bytes[i] != b'"' {
                            if bytes[i] == b'\\' {
                                i += 1;
                            }
                            i += 1;
                        }
                        i += 1;
                    } else if bytes[i] == b'[' {
                        let mut depth = 1;
                        i += 1;
                        while i < len && depth > 0 {
                            if bytes[i] == b'[' {
                                depth += 1;
                            } else if bytes[i] == b']' {
                                depth -= 1;
                            }
                            i += 1;
                        }
                    }
                }
            } else {
                i += 1;
            }
        }
        i += 1;

        let name = key.strip_prefix('&').unwrap_or(&key).to_string();
        let first = codepoints.first().copied().unwrap_or(0);
        let second = if codepoints.len() > 1 { codepoints[1] } else { 0 };
        entities.push((name, first, second));
    }

    entities.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));
    entities
}

// DAFSA builder using Rc<RefCell<Node>> for shared ownership.

type NodeRc = Rc<RefCell<Node>>;

struct Node {
    children: Vec<Option<NodeRc>>, // 128 slots
    is_terminal: bool,
    number: u16,
}

struct SecondLayerEntry {
    child_index: u16,
    number: u8,
    children_len: u8,
    end_of_word: bool,
}

struct NodeData {
    character: u8,
    number: u8,
    end_of_word: bool,
    child_index: u16,
    children_len: u8,
}

impl Node {
    fn new_rc() -> NodeRc {
        Rc::new(RefCell::new(Node {
            children: (0..128).map(|_| Option::None).collect(),
            is_terminal: false,
            number: 0,
        }))
    }

    fn calc_numbers(&mut self) {
        self.number = if self.is_terminal { 1 } else { 0 };
        for child in self.children.iter().flatten() {
            child.borrow_mut().calc_numbers();
            self.number += child.borrow().number;
        }
    }

    fn num_direct_children(&self) -> u8 {
        let mut n = 0u8;
        for c in &self.children {
            if c.is_some() {
                n += 1;
            }
        }
        n
    }

    fn get_ascii_alphabetic_bit_mask(&self) -> u64 {
        let mut mask = 0u64;
        for i in 0..128u8 {
            if self.children[i as usize].is_some() {
                mask |= 1u64 << ascii_alphabetic_to_index(i);
            }
        }
        mask
    }

    /// Hash based on child identities (Rc pointer) and terminal status.
    fn structure_hash(&self) -> u64 {
        let mut h: u64 = if self.is_terminal { 1 } else { 0 };
        for (i, child) in self.children.iter().enumerate() {
            if let Some(c) = child {
                h = h.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(i as u64);
                h = h.wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(Rc::as_ptr(c) as u64);
            }
        }
        h
    }

    /// Check structural equality via Rc pointer identity.
    fn structure_eq(&self, other: &Node) -> bool {
        if self.is_terminal != other.is_terminal {
            return false;
        }
        for i in 0..128 {
            match (&self.children[i], &other.children[i]) {
                (None, None) => {}
                (Some(a), Some(b)) => {
                    if !Rc::ptr_eq(a, b) {
                        return false;
                    }
                }
                _ => return false,
            }
        }
        true
    }
}

fn ascii_alphabetic_to_index(c: u8) -> u8 {
    if c <= b'Z' { c - b'A' } else { c - b'a' + 26 }
}

struct UncheckedNode {
    parent: NodeRc,
    character: u8,
}

struct DafsaBuilder {
    root: NodeRc,
    minimized_nodes: HashMap<u64, Vec<NodeRc>>,
    unchecked_nodes: Vec<UncheckedNode>,
    previous_word: String,
}

impl DafsaBuilder {
    fn new() -> Self {
        DafsaBuilder {
            root: Node::new_rc(),
            minimized_nodes: HashMap::new(),
            unchecked_nodes: Vec::new(),
            previous_word: String::new(),
        }
    }

    fn insert(&mut self, word: &str) {
        assert!(
            word > self.previous_word.as_str(),
            "Words must be inserted in sorted order: '{word}' <= '{}'",
            self.previous_word
        );

        let common_prefix_len = word
            .bytes()
            .zip(self.previous_word.bytes())
            .take_while(|(a, b)| a == b)
            .count();

        self.minimize(common_prefix_len);

        let node: NodeRc = if self.unchecked_nodes.is_empty() {
            Rc::clone(&self.root)
        } else {
            let last = &self.unchecked_nodes[self.unchecked_nodes.len() - 1];
            let parent = last.parent.borrow();
            Rc::clone(parent.children[last.character as usize].as_ref().unwrap())
        };

        let remaining = &word[common_prefix_len..];
        let mut current = node;
        for c in remaining.bytes() {
            let new_child = Node::new_rc();
            {
                let mut current_ref = current.borrow_mut();
                assert!(current_ref.children[c as usize].is_none());
                current_ref.children[c as usize] = Some(Rc::clone(&new_child));
            }
            self.unchecked_nodes.push(UncheckedNode {
                parent: Rc::clone(&current),
                character: c,
            });
            current = new_child;
        }
        current.borrow_mut().is_terminal = true;

        self.previous_word = word.to_string();
    }

    fn minimize(&mut self, down_to: usize) {
        while self.unchecked_nodes.len() > down_to {
            let unchecked = self.unchecked_nodes.pop().unwrap();
            let parent = &unchecked.parent;
            let child = {
                let parent_ref = parent.borrow();
                Rc::clone(parent_ref.children[unchecked.character as usize].as_ref().unwrap())
            };

            let hash = child.borrow().structure_hash();
            let mut found_replacement: Option<NodeRc> = Option::None;

            if let Some(bucket) = self.minimized_nodes.get(&hash) {
                for existing in bucket {
                    if child.borrow().structure_eq(&existing.borrow()) {
                        found_replacement = Some(Rc::clone(existing));
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }

            if let Some(replacement) = found_replacement {
                parent.borrow_mut().children[unchecked.character as usize] = Some(replacement);
            } else {
                self.minimized_nodes.entry(hash).or_default().push(Rc::clone(&child));
            }
        }
    }

    fn calc_numbers(&mut self) {
        self.root.borrow_mut().calc_numbers();
    }

    fn get_unique_index(&self, word: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        let mut index: usize = 0;
        let mut current = Rc::clone(&self.root);

        for c in word.bytes() {
            let next = {
                let node = current.borrow();
                let child = node.children[c as usize].as_ref()?;
                for sibling_c in 0u8..128 {
                    if let Some(sibling) = &node.children[sibling_c as usize]
                        && sibling_c < c
                    {
                        index += sibling.borrow().number as usize;
                    }
                }
                Rc::clone(child)
            };
            if next.borrow().is_terminal {
                index += 1;
            }
            current = next;
        }

        Some(index)
    }
}

fn queue_children(
    node: &NodeRc,
    queue: &mut Vec<NodeRc>,
    child_indexes: &mut HashMap<*const RefCell<Node>, u16>,
    first_available_index: u16,
) -> u16 {
    let mut current = first_available_index;
    let node_ref = node.borrow();
    for c in 0..128u8 {
        if let Some(child) = &node_ref.children[c as usize] {
            let key = Rc::as_ptr(child);
            if let std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) = child_indexes.entry(key) {
                let num_children = child.borrow().num_direct_children();
                if num_children > 0 {
                    entry.insert(current);
                    current += num_children as u16;
                }
                queue.push(Rc::clone(child));
            }
        }
    }
    current
}

fn write_children_data(
    node: &NodeRc,
    node_data: &mut Vec<NodeData>,
    queue: &mut Vec<NodeRc>,
    child_indexes: &mut HashMap<*const RefCell<Node>, u16>,
    first_available_index: u16,
) -> u16 {
    let mut current = first_available_index;
    let mut unique_index_tally: u8 = 0;
    let node_ref = node.borrow();
    for c in 0..128u8 {
        if let Some(child) = &node_ref.children[c as usize] {
            let key = Rc::as_ptr(child);
            let child_ref = child.borrow();
            let num_children = child_ref.num_direct_children();

            if let std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) = child_indexes.entry(key) {
                if num_children > 0 {
                    entry.insert(current);
                    current += num_children as u16;
                }
                queue.push(Rc::clone(child));
            }

            node_data.push(NodeData {
                character: c,
                number: unique_index_tally,
                end_of_word: child_ref.is_terminal,
                child_index: child_indexes.get(&key).copied().unwrap_or(0),
                children_len: num_children,
            });

            unique_index_tally = unique_index_tally.wrapping_add(child_ref.number as u8);
        }
    }
    current
}

/*

use crate::scan;
use ak::Utf16View;
use std::ops::Range;

/// A string of code units, in either of the two forms the engine's own strings have: one byte per code unit while
/// every code unit is below U+0100, and UTF-16 otherwise.
///
/// The tokenizer's input stream is one of these, and so is everything the tokenizer reads out of it. Most documents
/// only have code units below U+0100. A string is widened the first time it is given a code unit that doesn't fit.
/// Both forms are indexed by code unit, so offsets into a string stay the same when that happens.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub enum CodeUnits {
    Latin1(Vec<u8>),
    Utf16(Vec<u16>),
}

/// Where a run of code units is in the input.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct InputRun {
    pub range: Range<usize>,
    /// Whether every code unit of the run is known to be ASCII.
    pub is_ascii: bool,
}

/// A `Utf16View` as the host is handed one. Exactly one pointer is non-null unless the view is empty, and what it
/// points at is only readable until the call it is passed to returns.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct RustFfiHtmlUtf16View {
    pub latin1: *const u8,
    pub utf16: *const u16,
    pub length: usize,
}

impl From<Utf16View<'_>> for RustFfiHtmlUtf16View {
    fn from(view: Utf16View<'_>) -> Self {
        match view {
            Utf16View::Latin1(code_units) => Self {
                latin1: code_units.as_ptr(),
                utf16: std::ptr::null(),
                length: code_units.len(),
            },
            Utf16View::Utf16(code_units) => Self {
                latin1: std::ptr::null(),
                utf16: code_units.as_ptr(),
                length: code_units.len(),
            },
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
impl RustFfiHtmlUtf16View {
    /// What a test's stand-in for the host was handed, as text.
    pub(crate) fn to_test_string(self) -> String {
        let code_units = if self.length == 0 {
            Vec::new()
        } else if !self.latin1.is_null() {
            Utf16View::Latin1(unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.latin1, self.length) }).to_utf16()
        } else {
            unsafe { ak::slice_from_raw_parts(self.utf16, self.length) }.to_vec()
        };
        String::from_utf16(&code_units).unwrap()
    }
}

/// Whether any code unit is something other than the ASCII whitespace the tree builder ignores for "frameset-ok".
pub fn contains_non_whitespace(view: Utf16View<'_>) -> bool {
    match view {
        Utf16View::Latin1(code_units) => scan::contains_non_whitespace(code_units),
        Utf16View::Utf16(code_units) => scan::contains_non_whitespace(code_units),
    }
}

impl Default for CodeUnits {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::Latin1(Vec::new())
    }
}

impl From<Vec<u8>> for CodeUnits {
    fn from(code_units: Vec<u8>) -> Self {
        Self::Latin1(code_units)
    }
}

impl From<Vec<u16>> for CodeUnits {
    fn from(code_units: Vec<u16>) -> Self {
        Self::Utf16(code_units)
    }
}

impl CodeUnits {
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => code_units.len(),
            Self::Utf16(code_units) => code_units.len(),
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len() == 0
    }

    /// The code unit at `offset`, which must be inside the input.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn code_unit_at(&self, offset: usize) -> u16 {
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => u16::from(code_units[offset]),
            Self::Utf16(code_units) => code_units[offset],
        }
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn get(&self, offset: usize) -> Option<u16> {
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => code_units.get(offset).copied().map(u16::from),
            Self::Utf16(code_units) => code_units.get(offset).copied(),
        }
    }

    pub fn slice_from(&self, start: usize) -> Utf16View<'_> {
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => Utf16View::Latin1(&code_units[start..]),
            Self::Utf16(code_units) => Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units[start..]),
        }
    }

    pub fn slice(&self, range: Range<usize>) -> Utf16View<'_> {
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => Utf16View::Latin1(&code_units[range]),
            Self::Utf16(code_units) => Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units[range]),
        }
    }

    pub fn append(&mut self, code_units: Utf16View<'_>) {
        self.insert(self.len(), code_units);
    }

    pub fn insert(&mut self, offset: usize, code_units: Utf16View<'_>) {
        if self.is_empty() {
            *self = match code_units {
                Utf16View::Latin1(code_units) => Self::Latin1(code_units.to_vec()),
                Utf16View::Utf16(code_units) => Self::Utf16(code_units.to_vec()),
            };
            return;
        }
        match (&mut *self, code_units) {
            (Self::Latin1(input), Utf16View::Latin1(code_units)) => {
                input.splice(offset..offset, code_units.iter().copied());
            }
            (Self::Utf16(input), Utf16View::Latin1(code_units)) => {
                input.splice(offset..offset, code_units.iter().copied().map(u16::from));
            }
            (Self::Utf16(input), Utf16View::Utf16(code_units)) => {
                input.splice(offset..offset, code_units.iter().copied());
            }
            (Self::Latin1(input), Utf16View::Utf16(code_units)) => {
                let mut widened = Vec::with_capacity(input.len() + code_units.len());
                widened.extend(input[..offset].iter().copied().map(u16::from));
                widened.extend_from_slice(code_units);
                widened.extend(input[offset..].iter().copied().map(u16::from));
                *self = Self::Utf16(widened);
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn to_utf16(&self) -> Vec<u16> {
        self.slice_from(0).to_utf16()
    }

    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self::Latin1(Vec::new())
    }

    pub fn as_slice(&self) -> Utf16View<'_> {
        self.slice_from(0)
    }

    pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => code_units.capacity(),
            Self::Utf16(code_units) => code_units.capacity(),
        }
    }

    /// Empties the string. A one-byte string keeps its buffer.
    pub fn clear(&mut self) {
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => code_units.clear(),
            // NB: An empty string is always in the one-byte form, so that what is written to it next stays at one
            //     byte per code unit if it can.
            Self::Utf16(_) => *self = Self::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Takes the string out, and leaves an empty one.
    pub fn take(&mut self) -> Self {
        std::mem::take(self)
    }

    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn push_ascii(&mut self, byte: u8) {
        debug_assert!(byte.is_ascii());
        match self {
            Self::Latin1(code_units) => code_units.push(byte),
            Self::Utf16(code_units) => code_units.push(u16::from(byte)),
        }
    }

    pub fn push_ascii_str(&mut self, string: &str) {
        debug_assert!(string.is_ascii());
        self.append(Utf16View::Latin1(string.as_bytes()));
    }

    /// Appends code units as they are. Unlike `append()`, a string that is empty keeps its buffer.
    pub fn push_slice(&mut self, code_units: Utf16View<'_>) {
        match (&mut *self, code_units) {
            (Self::Latin1(string), Utf16View::Latin1(code_units)) => string.extend_from_slice(code_units),
            (Self::Utf16(string), Utf16View::Utf16(code_units)) => string.extend_from_slice(code_units),
            (Self::Utf16(string), Utf16View::Latin1(code_units)) => {
                string.extend(code_units.iter().copied().map(u16::from));
            }
            // NB: Input stored as UTF-16 is mostly code units that fit in a byte, which keeps this at a byte each
            //     and in the buffer it already has.
            (Self::Latin1(string), Utf16View::Utf16(code_units))
                if code_units.iter().all(|&code_unit| code_unit <= 0xFF) =>
            {
                string.extend(code_units.iter().map(|&code_unit| code_unit as u8));
            }
            (Self::Latin1(string), Utf16View::Utf16(code_units)) => {
                let mut widened = Vec::with_capacity(string.len() + code_units.len());
                widened.extend(string.iter().copied().map(u16::from));
                widened.extend_from_slice(code_units);
                *self = Self::Utf16(widened);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Appends a code point. A surrogate is replaced with U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn push_code_point(&mut self, code_point: u32) {
        if let Self::Latin1(code_units) = self
            && code_point < 0x100
        {
            code_units.push(code_point as u8);
            return;
        }
        self.push_wide_code_point(code_point);
    }

    fn push_wide_code_point(&mut self, code_point: u32) {
        if let Self::Latin1(code_units) = self {
            *self = Self::Utf16(code_units.iter().copied().map(u16::from).collect());
        }
        let Self::Utf16(code_units) = self else {
            unreachable!();
        };
        match code_point {
            0xD800..=0xDFFF => code_units.push(0xFFFD),
            0..=0xFFFF => code_units.push(code_point as u16),
            _ => {
                let offset = code_point - 0x10000;
                code_units.push(0xD800 | (offset >> 10) as u16);
                code_units.push(0xDC00 | (offset & 0x3FF) as u16);
            }
        }
    }
}

impl PartialEq for CodeUnits {
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.as_slice() == other.as_slice()
    }
}

impl Eq for CodeUnits {}

impl PartialEq<str> for CodeUnits {
    fn eq(&self, other: &str) -> bool {
        self.as_slice() == *other
    }
}

impl PartialEq<&str> for CodeUnits {
    fn eq(&self, other: &&str) -> bool {
        self.as_slice() == **other
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn code_units(input: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
        input.encode_utf16().collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn one_byte_input_stays_one_byte() {
        let mut input = CodeUnits::default();
        input.append(Utf16View::Latin1(b"<p>"));
        input.append(Utf16View::Latin1(b"caf\xe9"));
        input.insert(3, Utf16View::Latin1(b"un "));
        assert!(matches!(input, CodeUnits::Latin1(_)));
        assert_eq!(input.to_utf16(), code_units("<p>un caf\u{e9}"));
        assert_eq!(input.code_unit_at(9), 0xe9);
        assert_eq!(input.get(10), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn wide_code_units_widen_the_input_in_place() {
        let mut input = CodeUnits::default();
        input.append(Utf16View::Latin1(b"<p>caf\xe9</p>"));
        input.insert(7, Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units(" \u{2014} \u{1f600}")));
        assert!(matches!(input, CodeUnits::Utf16(_)));
        assert_eq!(input.to_utf16(), code_units("<p>caf\u{e9} \u{2014} \u{1f600}</p>"));
        input.append(Utf16View::Latin1(b"\xe9"));
        assert_eq!(input.code_unit_at(input.len() - 1), 0xe9);
    }

    #[test]
    fn code_points_are_pushed_at_one_byte_each_until_one_doesnt_fit() {
        let mut string = CodeUnits::new();
        string.push_ascii(b'a');
        string.push_code_point(0xe9);
        assert!(matches!(string, CodeUnits::Latin1(_)));
        string.push_code_point(0x2014);
        string.push_code_point(0x1f600);
        string.push_code_point(0xd83d);
        string.push_ascii_str("ok");
        string.push_slice(Utf16View::Latin1(b"\xe9"));
        string.push_slice(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units("\u{2014}")));
        assert!(matches!(string, CodeUnits::Utf16(_)));
        assert_eq!(string, "a\u{e9}\u{2014}\u{1f600}\u{fffd}ok\u{e9}\u{2014}");
        string.clear();
        string.push_slice(Utf16View::Latin1(b"a"));
        assert!(matches!(string, CodeUnits::Latin1(_)));
        string.push_slice(Utf16View::Utf16(&code_units("\u{2014}")));
        assert_eq!(string, "a\u{2014}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn strings_compare_by_code_unit_whatever_form_they_are_in() {
        let narrow = CodeUnits::from(b"caf\xe9".to_vec());
        let wide = CodeUnits::from(code_units("caf\u{e9}"));
        assert_eq!(narrow, wide);
        assert_eq!(narrow, "caf\u{e9}");
        assert_ne!(narrow, "cafe");
        assert_ne!(wide, "caf");
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_input_takes_the_form_of_what_it_is_given() {
        let mut input = CodeUnits::from(Vec::<u16>::new());
        input.append(Utf16View::Latin1(b"abc"));
        assert!(matches!(input, CodeUnits::Latin1(_)));
    }
}

/*

//! Named character reference matching using a DAFSA (Deterministic Acyclic Finite
//! State Automaton) with minimal perfect hashing. The DAFSA data is generated at
//! build time by build.rs from Entities.json.

include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/named_character_references.rs"));

fn ascii_alphabetic_to_index(c: u8) -> u8 {
    if c <= b'Z' { c - b'A' } else { c - b'a' + 26 }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum SearchState {
    Init,
    FirstToSecondLayer { mask: u64, offset: u16 },
    DafsaChildren { start_index: u16, len: u8 },
}

/// Incremental matcher for named character references using the DAFSA.
///
/// Feed characters one at a time via `try_consume_code_point()`. After each
/// rejected character (returns false), call `code_points()` to get the longest
/// match found so far, and `overconsumed_code_points()` to know how many
/// characters were consumed past the longest match.
pub struct NamedCharacterReferenceMatcher {
    search_state: SearchState,
    last_matched_unique_index: u16,
    pending_unique_index: u16,
    overconsumed_code_points: u8,
    ends_with_semicolon: bool,
}

impl NamedCharacterReferenceMatcher {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            search_state: SearchState::Init,
            last_matched_unique_index: 0,
            pending_unique_index: 0,
            overconsumed_code_points: 0,
            ends_with_semicolon: false,
        }
    }

    /// Feed one code point to the matcher. Returns true if the character was
    /// consumed (there may still be longer matches), false if no further
    /// matches are possible.
    pub fn try_consume_code_point(&mut self, c: u32) -> bool {
        if c > 0x7F {
            return false;
        }
        self.try_consume_ascii_char(c as u8)
    }

    fn try_consume_ascii_char(&mut self, c: u8) -> bool {
        match self.search_state {
            SearchState::Init => {
                if !c.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
                    return false;
                }
                let index = ascii_alphabetic_to_index(c) as usize;
                self.search_state = SearchState::FirstToSecondLayer {
                    mask: FIRST_TO_SECOND_LAYER[index].0,
                    offset: FIRST_TO_SECOND_LAYER[index].1,
                };
                self.pending_unique_index = FIRST_LAYER[index];
                self.overconsumed_code_points += 1;
                true
            }
            SearchState::FirstToSecondLayer { mask, offset } => {
                if !c.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
                    return false;
                }
                let bit_index = ascii_alphabetic_to_index(c);
                if ((1u64 << bit_index) & mask) == 0 {
                    return false;
                }

                // Count set bits below bit_index to find the node's position.
                let lower_mask = (1u64 << bit_index) - 1;
                let char_index = (mask & lower_mask).count_ones() as u16;
                let node = &SECOND_LAYER[(offset + char_index) as usize];

                self.pending_unique_index += node.number as u16;
                self.overconsumed_code_points += 1;
                if node.end_of_word {
                    self.pending_unique_index += 1;
                    self.last_matched_unique_index = self.pending_unique_index;
                    self.ends_with_semicolon = c == b';';
                    self.overconsumed_code_points = 0;
                }
                self.search_state = SearchState::DafsaChildren {
                    start_index: node.child_index,
                    len: node.children_len,
                };
                true
            }
            SearchState::DafsaChildren { start_index, len } => {
                for i in 0..len as u16 {
                    let node = &DAFSA_NODES[(start_index + i) as usize];
                    if node.character == c {
                        self.pending_unique_index += node.number as u16;
                        self.overconsumed_code_points += 1;
                        if node.end_of_word {
                            self.pending_unique_index += 1;
                            self.last_matched_unique_index = self.pending_unique_index;
                            self.ends_with_semicolon = c == b';';
                            self.overconsumed_code_points = 0;
                        }
                        self.search_state = SearchState::DafsaChildren {
                            start_index: node.child_index,
                            len: node.children_len,
                        };
                        return true;
                    }
                }
                false
            }
        }
    }

    /// Returns the codepoints for the longest match found, or None if no match.
    /// Returns (first_codepoint, second_codepoint). second is 0 if there is no second codepoint.
    pub fn code_points(&self) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
        if self.last_matched_unique_index == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let entry = &CODEPOINTS_LOOKUP[(self.last_matched_unique_index - 1) as usize];
        Some((entry.0, entry.1.value()))
    }

    /// Number of characters consumed past the longest match.
    pub fn overconsumed_code_points(&self) -> u8 {
        self.overconsumed_code_points
    }

    /// Whether the longest match ended with a semicolon.
    pub fn last_match_ends_with_semicolon(&self) -> bool {
        self.ends_with_semicolon
    }
}

impl Default for NamedCharacterReferenceMatcher {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

//! The scanner of the fragment fast path.
//!
//! Markup given to innerHTML is very often a small subset of what goes in a body: a few kinds of elements, properly
//! nested, with quoted attribute values and no character references. The scanner reads such markup once and writes
//! down what the tree builder would have made of it as a flat list of operations, which the host then builds nodes
//! from without a tokenizer or a tree builder. Anything else is turned down before the host has made a single node,
//! and goes to the general parser.

use crate::code_units::RustFfiHtmlUtf16View;
use crate::known_names::known_attribute_name;
use crate::known_names::tag_id;
use crate::known_names::tag_id_for_name;
use crate::scan;
use crate::scan::CodeUnit;
use crate::token::TagId;
use crate::token::TagSet;
use crate::token::tag_set;
use std::cell::Cell;

#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperationKind {
    /// Make an element and the attributes at `start..start + length` of the attribute list, and append it to the
    /// innermost open element. It is then the innermost open element.
    OpenElement,
    /// The same for an element that takes no children, which is not left open.
    AppendVoidElement,
    /// Close the innermost open element.
    CloseElement,
    /// Append a text node with the code units at `start..start + length` of the input.
    AppendText,
}

#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperation {
    pub kind: RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperationKind,
    /// Whether the text of `AppendText` is all ASCII.
    pub is_ascii: bool,
    pub start: u32,
    pub length: u32,
    /// The identity of the `Utf16FlyString` with the local name of the element to make.
    pub tag_name: usize,
}

/// An attribute of an element to make. The name and the value are ranges of code units of the input.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct RustFfiHtmlFragmentAttribute {
    /// The identity of the `Utf16FlyString` with the name if it is one the engine knows, and otherwise 0.
    pub known_name: usize,
    pub name_start: u32,
    pub name_length: u32,
    pub value_start: u32,
    pub value_length: u32,
    pub value_is_ascii: bool,
}

/// What the scanner made of a fragment. `tape` is null if the fragment is not for the fast path, and otherwise must
/// be given to `rust_html_fragment_tape_release` once the operations have been read.
#[repr(C)]
pub struct RustFfiHtmlFragmentScan {
    pub tape: *mut RustHtmlFragmentTape,
    pub operations: *const RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperation,
    pub operation_count: usize,
    pub attributes: *const RustFfiHtmlFragmentAttribute,
    pub attribute_count: usize,
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct RustHtmlFragmentTape {
    operations: Vec<RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperation>,
    attributes: Vec<RustFfiHtmlFragmentAttribute>,
    open_elements: Vec<TagId>,
}

thread_local! {
    // NB: One tape is kept between fragments, so that scanning a fragment does not allocate.
    static SPARE_TAPE: Cell<Option<Box<RustHtmlFragmentTape>>> = const { Cell::new(None) };
}

// NB: A tape that an unusually large fragment grew past these sizes is freed, so that the spare one stays small.
const MAX_SPARE_TAPE_OPERATIONS: usize = 4096;
const MAX_SPARE_TAPE_ATTRIBUTES: usize = 4096;

fn keep_as_spare_tape(tape: Box<RustHtmlFragmentTape>) {
    if tape.operations.capacity() <= MAX_SPARE_TAPE_OPERATIONS
        && tape.attributes.capacity() <= MAX_SPARE_TAPE_ATTRIBUTES
    {
        SPARE_TAPE.set(Some(tape));
    }
}

/// Scans a fragment for the fast path.
///
/// # Safety
/// `input` must point at `input.length` readable code units.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_html_fragment_scan(input: RustFfiHtmlUtf16View) -> RustFfiHtmlFragmentScan {
    let mut tape = SPARE_TAPE.take().unwrap_or_default();
    // SAFETY: The caller promises that `input` points at `input.length` code units.
    let accepted = unsafe {
        if input.length == 0 {
            scan::<u8>(&[], &mut tape)
        } else if !input.latin1.is_null() {
            scan(ak::slice_from_raw_parts(input.latin1, input.length), &mut tape)
        } else {
            scan(ak::slice_from_raw_parts(input.utf16, input.length), &mut tape)
        }
    };
    if !accepted {
        keep_as_spare_tape(tape);
        return RustFfiHtmlFragmentScan {
            tape: std::ptr::null_mut(),
            operations: std::ptr::null(),
            operation_count: 0,
            attributes: std::ptr::null(),
            attribute_count: 0,
        };
    }
    RustFfiHtmlFragmentScan {
        operations: tape.operations.as_ptr(),
        operation_count: tape.operations.len(),
        attributes: tape.attributes.as_ptr(),
        attribute_count: tape.attributes.len(),
        tape: Box::into_raw(tape),
    }
}

/// Gives back the tape of a scan whose operations have been read.
///
/// # Safety
/// `tape` must be the tape of a `RustFfiHtmlFragmentScan` that has not been released yet.
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn rust_html_fragment_tape_release(tape: *mut RustHtmlFragmentTape) {
    // SAFETY: The caller promises that `tape` came from `rust_html_fragment_scan` and is released once.
    keep_as_spare_tape(unsafe { Box::from_raw(tape) });
}

/// Defines the tags the fast path takes, and the fly string of each.
///
/// Keep this subset deliberately small. Adding a tag requires checking its in-body tree-builder rules, its insertion
/// steps, and interactions with every other supported tag. A supported tag must not have children changed steps,
/// since the host links children below a new element without running them.
macro_rules! supported_tags {
    ($($name:tt),+ $(,)?) => {
        const SUPPORTED_TAGS: &TagSet = tag_set![$($name),+];

        /// The identity of the `Utf16FlyString` of every supported tag, by tag id.
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        fn tag_names() -> &'static [usize; TAG_ID_COUNT] {
            static TAG_NAMES: std::sync::OnceLock<[usize; TAG_ID_COUNT]> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
            TAG_NAMES.get_or_init(|| {
                let mut tag_names = [0; TAG_ID_COUNT];
                $(tag_names[tag_id!($name).index()] = crate::known_names::tag_name!($name).raw_identity();)+
                tag_names
            })
        }
    };
}

#[cfg(not(test))]
const TAG_ID_COUNT: usize = crate::known_names::TAG_SET_WORD_COUNT * 64;

supported_tags![
    "a", "article", "aside", "b", "big", "br", "button", "code", "div", "em", "footer", "header", "i", "input",
    "label", "li", "main", "nav", "ol", "s", "section", "small", "span", "strike", "strong", "tt", "u", "ul",
];

const MAX_OPEN_ELEMENTS: usize = 128;
const MAX_ATTRIBUTES: usize = 64;

/// The whitespace between the parts of a tag.
fn is_tag_whitespace(code_unit: u16) -> bool {
    matches!(code_unit, 0x09 | 0x0A | 0x0C | 0x20)
}

fn equals_ascii<T: CodeUnit>(code_units: &[T], ascii: &[u8]) -> bool {
    code_units.len() == ascii.len()
        && code_units
            .iter()
            .zip(ascii)
            .all(|(&code_unit, &byte)| code_unit.into() == u16::from(byte))
}

fn scan<T: CodeUnit>(input: &[T], tape: &mut RustHtmlFragmentTape) -> bool {
    tape.operations.clear();
    tape.attributes.clear();
    tape.open_elements.clear();
    // NB: The tape has offsets into the input as 32-bit numbers.
    if u32::try_from(input.len()).is_err() {
        return false;
    }
    Scanner {
        input,
        offset: 0,
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        tag_names: tag_names(),
        tape,
    }
    .scan()
}

struct Scanner<'a, T> {
    input: &'a [T],
    offset: usize,
    #[cfg(not(test))]
    tag_names: &'static [usize; TAG_ID_COUNT],
    tape: &'a mut RustHtmlFragmentTape,
}

impl<'a, T: CodeUnit> Scanner<'a, T> {
    fn scan(&mut self) -> bool {
        while self.offset < self.input.len() {
            let scanned = if self.peek() != u16::from(b'<') {
                self.scan_text()
            } else {
                self.offset += 1;
                if self.consume(b'/') {
                    self.scan_end_tag()
                } else {
                    self.scan_start_tag()
                }
            };
            if !scanned {
                return false;
            }
        }
        self.tape.open_elements.is_empty()
    }

    fn scan_text(&mut self) -> bool {
        // NB: Character references and input preprocessing use the general parser, which also replaces a surrogate
        //     that isn't half of a pair with U+FFFD. The run ends at all of those, so it has to end at a tag or at the
        //     end of the input.
        let run = scan::data_run(&self.input[self.offset..]);
        let end = self.offset + run.length;
        if end < self.input.len() && self.input[end].into() != u16::from(b'<') {
            return false;
        }
        self.tape.operations.push(RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperation {
            kind: RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperationKind::AppendText,
            is_ascii: run.is_ascii,
            start: self.offset as u32,
            length: run.length as u32,
            tag_name: 0,
        });
        self.offset = end;
        true
    }

    fn scan_end_tag(&mut self) -> bool {
        let Some(tag) = self.scan_supported_tag() else {
            return false;
        };
        self.skip_whitespace();
        if !self.consume(b'>') || self.tape.open_elements.pop() != Some(tag) {
            return false;
        }
        self.tape.operations.push(RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperation {
            kind: RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperationKind::CloseElement,
            is_ascii: false,
            start: 0,
            length: 0,
            tag_name: 0,
        });
        true
    }

    fn scan_start_tag(&mut self) -> bool {
        let Some(tag) = self.scan_supported_tag() else {
            return false;
        };
        let open_elements = &self.tape.open_elements;

        // Leave implicit closing of anchors, buttons, and list items to the general parser.
        if (tag == tag_id!("a") || tag == tag_id!("button")) && open_elements.contains(&tag) {
            return false;
        }
        if tag == tag_id!("li") {
            for &ancestor in open_elements.iter().rev() {
                if ancestor == tag_id!("li") {
                    return false;
                }
                // A nested list stops the in-body rule from closing an outer list item.
                if ancestor == tag_id!("ul") || ancestor == tag_id!("ol") {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if open_elements.len() >= MAX_OPEN_ELEMENTS {
            return false;
        }

        let first_attribute = self.tape.attributes.len();
        loop {
            self.skip_whitespace();
            if self.peek() == u16::from(b'>') || self.peek() == u16::from(b'/') {
                break;
            }
            if !self.scan_attribute(tag, first_attribute) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        let is_void = tag == tag_id!("br") || tag == tag_id!("input");
        if self.consume(b'/') && !is_void {
            return false;
        }
        if !self.consume(b'>') {
            return false;
        }

        self.tape.operations.push(RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperation {
            kind: if is_void {
                RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperationKind::AppendVoidElement
            } else {
                RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperationKind::OpenElement
            },
            is_ascii: false,
            start: first_attribute as u32,
            length: (self.tape.attributes.len() - first_attribute) as u32,
            tag_name: self.tag_name(tag),
        });
        if !is_void {
            self.tape.open_elements.push(tag);
        }
        true
    }

    /// Scans one attribute of a start tag of `tag`, whose attributes so far start at `first_attribute`.
    fn scan_attribute(&mut self, tag: TagId, first_attribute: usize) -> bool {
        let input = self.input;
        let name_start = self.offset;
        let name = self.scan_name();
        // NB: Customized built-in elements are made by the general parser.
        if name.is_empty()
            || equals_ascii(name, b"is")
            || self.tape.attributes.len() - first_attribute >= MAX_ATTRIBUTES
        {
            return false;
        }
        // NB: The tokenizer drops an attribute whose name the tag already has, which the general parser sees to.
        let is_duplicate = self.tape.attributes[first_attribute..].iter().any(|attribute| {
            let start = attribute.name_start as usize;
            input[start..start + attribute.name_length as usize] == *name
        });
        if is_duplicate {
            return false;
        }

        self.skip_whitespace();
        let mut value = scan::Run {
            length: 0,
            is_ascii: true,
        };
        let mut value_start = self.offset;
        if self.consume(b'=') {
            self.skip_whitespace();
            let quote = self.peek();
            if quote != u16::from(b'\'') && quote != u16::from(b'"') {
                return false;
            }
            self.offset += 1;
            value_start = self.offset;
            // NB: As with text, the run ends at everything that the general parser has to see to, so it has to end at
            //     the closing quote.
            value = scan::quoted_attribute_value_run(&input[value_start..], quote as u8);
            self.offset = value_start + value.length;
            if !self.consume(quote as u8) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        // NB: Other input types have insertion steps or children the fast path doesn't cover.
        let value_code_units = &input[value_start..value_start + value.length];
        if tag == tag_id!("input")
            && equals_ascii(name, b"type")
            && !equals_ascii(value_code_units, b"text")
            && !equals_ascii(value_code_units, b"checkbox")
        {
            return false;
        }

        self.tape.attributes.push(RustFfiHtmlFragmentAttribute {
            known_name: known_attribute_name_identity(name),
            name_start: name_start as u32,
            name_length: name.len() as u32,
            value_start: value_start as u32,
            value_length: value.length as u32,
            value_is_ascii: value.is_ascii,
        });
        true
    }

    fn scan_supported_tag(&mut self) -> Option<TagId> {
        let name = self.scan_name();
        let tag = tag_id_for_name(scan::ascii_name_bytes(name, &mut [0; 32])?);
        (tag != TagId::UNKNOWN && SUPPORTED_TAGS.contains(tag)).then_some(tag)
    }

    /// Scans a tag name or an attribute name of lowercase ASCII letters, digits and hyphens. Other names are for the
    /// general parser, which is what finding no name where one has to be leads to.
    fn scan_name(&mut self) -> &'a [T] {
        let input = self.input;
        let start = self.offset;
        while matches!(self.peek(), 0x61..=0x7A | 0x30..=0x39 | 0x2D) {
            self.offset += 1;
        }
        &input[start..self.offset]
    }

    fn tag_name(&self, tag: TagId) -> usize {
        #[cfg(not(test))]
        {
            self.tag_names[tag.index()]
        }
        // NB: There are no fly strings in the standalone tests, which get the tag id in place of one.
        #[cfg(test)]
        {
            tag.index()
        }
    }

    /// The code unit at the offset, or U+0000 NULL at the end of the input. Nothing the scanner takes has a NULL in it.
    fn peek(&self) -> u16 {
        self.input.get(self.offset).map_or(0, |&code_unit| code_unit.into())
    }

    fn consume(&mut self, byte: u8) -> bool {
        if self.offset == self.input.len() || self.peek() != u16::from(byte) {
            return false;
        }
        self.offset += 1;
        true
    }

    fn skip_whitespace(&mut self) {
        while is_tag_whitespace(self.peek()) {
            self.offset += 1;
        }
    }
}

fn known_attribute_name_identity<T: CodeUnit>(name: &[T]) -> usize {
    #[cfg(not(test))]
    {
        scan::ascii_name_bytes(name, &mut [0; 32])
            .and_then(known_attribute_name)
            .map_or(0, |name| name.raw_identity())
    }
    // NB: There are no fly strings in the standalone tests, which only tell known names from other names.
    #[cfg(test)]
    {
        usize::from(
            scan::ascii_name_bytes(name, &mut [0; 32])
                .and_then(known_attribute_name)
                .is_some(),
        )
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::RustFfiHtmlFragmentOperationKind::*;
    use super::*;

    /// What the scanner makes of `input`, as one line per operation, or `None` if it turns the input down.
    fn scan_to_text<T: CodeUnit>(input: &[T]) -> Option<String> {
        let mut tape = RustHtmlFragmentTape::default();
        if !scan(input, &mut tape) {
            return None;
        }
        let text_of = |start: u32, length: u32| {
            let code_units: Vec<u16> = input[start as usize..(start + length) as usize]
                .iter()
                .map(|&code_unit| code_unit.into())
                .collect();
            String::from_utf16(&code_units).unwrap()
        };
        let mut text = String::new();
        for operation in &tape.operations {
            match operation.kind {
                OpenElement | AppendVoidElement => {
                    text.push_str(if operation.kind == OpenElement { "open" } else { "void" });
                    text.push_str(&format!(" #{}", operation.tag_name));
                    let attributes = &tape.attributes[operation.start as usize..][..operation.length as usize];
                    for attribute in attributes {
                        text.push_str(&format!(
                            " {}{}={:?}{}",
                            text_of(attribute.name_start, attribute.name_length),
                            if attribute.known_name != 0 { "!" } else { "" },
                            text_of(attribute.value_start, attribute.value_length),
                            if attribute.value_is_ascii { "" } else { "~" },
                        ));
                    }
                }
                CloseElement => text.push_str("close"),
                AppendText => text.push_str(&format!(
                    "text {:?}{}",
                    text_of(operation.start, operation.length),
                    if operation.is_ascii { "" } else { "~" }
                )),
            }
            text.push('\n');
        }
        Some(text)
    }

    fn scan_str(input: &str) -> Option<String> {
        let utf16: Vec<u16> = input.encode_utf16().collect();
        let from_utf16 = scan_to_text(&utf16);
        if let Some(latin1) = utf16
            .iter()
            .map(|&code_unit| u8::try_from(code_unit).ok())
            .collect::<Option<Vec<u8>>>()
        {
            assert_eq!(scan_to_text(&latin1), from_utf16, "Latin-1 and UTF-16 input scan alike");
        }
        from_utf16
    }

    fn accepts(input: &str) -> bool {
        scan_str(input).is_some()
    }

    #[test]
    fn elements_attributes_and_text_become_operations() {
        let div = tag_id!("div").index();
        let input = tag_id!("input").index();
        assert_eq!(
            scan_str("a<div class=\"x y\" data-id='7' hidden>caf\u{E9}<input type = \"checkbox\" /></div >").unwrap(),
            format!(
                "text \"a\"\nopen #{div} class!=\"x y\" data-id=\"7\" hidden!=\"\"\ntext \"caf\u{E9}\"~\n\
                 void #{input} type!=\"checkbox\"\nclose\n"
            )
        );
        assert_eq!(scan_str("").unwrap(), "");
        assert_eq!(scan_str("x > y").unwrap(), "text \"x > y\"\n");
    }

    #[test]
    fn markup_the_tree_builder_takes_as_written_is_accepted() {
        for input in [
            "<br>",
            "<br/>",
            "<input>",
            "<li><ul><li></li></ul></li>",
            "<a><b></b></a><a></a>",
            "<div title='a<b>\"'></div>",
            "<div\n\tclass=''\x0C></div\n>",
        ] {
            assert!(accepts(input), "{input:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn markup_for_the_general_parser_is_turned_down() {
        for input in [
            "a &amp; b",
            "a\rb",
            "a\0b",
            "<p>x</p>",
            "<my-element></my-element>",
            "<DIV></DIV>",
            "<div>",
            "</div>",
            "<div></span>",
            "<div/>",
            "</br>",
            "<div",
            "<div class='a",
            "<div class=a></div>",
            "<div Class='a'></div>",
            "<div class='a' class='b'></div>",
            "<div class='a&amp;b'></div>",
            "<div class='a\rb'></div>",
            "<div is='x'></div>",
            "<a><b><a></a></b></a>",
            "<button><button></button></button>",
            "<li><li></li></li>",
            "<ul><li><b><li></li></b></li></ul>",
            "<input type='radio'>",
            "<input type>",
            "<!-- comment -->",
        ] {
            assert!(!accepts(input), "{input:?}");
        }
        let too_deep = "<div>".repeat(MAX_OPEN_ELEMENTS + 1) + &"</div>".repeat(MAX_OPEN_ELEMENTS + 1);
        assert!(!accepts(&too_deep));
        assert!(accepts(&too_deep["<div>".len()..too_deep.len() - "</div>".len()]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn surrogates_are_taken_in_pairs_only() {
        let code_units = |text: &str, surrogate: &[u16]| {
            let mut code_units: Vec<u16> = text.encode_utf16().collect();
            let offset = code_units
                .iter()
                .position(|&code_unit| code_unit == u16::from(b'?'))
                .unwrap();
            code_units.splice(offset..offset + 1, surrogate.iter().copied());
            code_units
        };
        for text in ["a?b", "<div title='a?b'></div>"] {
            assert!(scan_to_text(&code_units(text, &[0xD83D, 0xDE00])).is_some());
            assert!(scan_to_text(&code_units(text, &[0xD83D])).is_none());
            assert!(scan_to_text(&code_units(text, &[0xDE00])).is_none());
            assert!(scan_to_text(&code_units(text, &[0xDE00, 0xD83D])).is_none());
        }
        assert_eq!(
            scan_to_text(&code_units("?", &[0xD83D, 0xDE00])).unwrap(),
            "text \"\u{1F600}\"~\n"
        );
    }
}
